title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1 to G144
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1 Α (A): the first letter of the alphabet; figuratively, only (from its use as a numeral) the first. Origin: of Hebrew origin; KJV: --Alpha

G2 Ἀαρών (Aarṓn): Aaron, the brother of Moses. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H175); KJV: Aaron

G3 Ἀβαδδών (Abaddṓn): a destroying angel. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H11); KJV: Abaddon

G4 ἀβαρής (abarḗs): weightless, i.e. (figuratively) not burdensome. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G922 (βάρος); KJV: from being burdensome

G5 Ἀββᾶ (Abbâ): father as a vocative. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H2); KJV: Abba

G6 Ἄβελ (Ábel): Abel, the son of Adam. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1893); KJV: Abel

G7 Ἀβιά (Abiá): Abijah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H29); KJV: Abia

G8 Ἀβιαθάρ (Abiathár): Abiathar, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H54); KJV: Abiathar

G9 Ἀβιληνή (Abilēnḗ): Abilene, a region of Syria. Origin: of foreign origin (compare H58); KJV: Abilene

G10 Ἀβιούδ (Abioúd): Abihud, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H31); KJV: Abiud

G11 Ἀβραάμ (Abraám): Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H85); KJV: Abraham

G12 ἄβυσσος (ábyssos): depthless, i.e. (specially) (infernal) "abyss". Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a variation of G1037 (βυθός); KJV: deep, (bottomless) pit

G13 Ἄγαβος (Ágabos): Agabus, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H2285); KJV: Agabus

G14 ἀγαθοεργέω (agathoergéō): to work good. Origin: from G18 (ἀγαθός) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: do good

G15 ἀγαθοποιέω (agathopoiéō): to be a well-doer (as a favor or a duty). Origin: from G17 (ἀγαθοποιός); KJV: (when) do good (well)

G16 ἀγαθοποιΐα (agathopoiḯa): well-doing, i.e. virtue. Origin: from G17 (ἀγαθοποιός); KJV: well-doing

G17 ἀγαθοποιός (agathopoiós): a well-doer, i.e. virtuous. Origin: from G18 (ἀγαθός) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: them that do well

G18 ἀγαθός (agathós): "good" (in any sense, often as noun). Origin: a primary word; KJV: benefit, good(-s, things), well

G19 ἀγαθωσύνη (agathōsýnē): goodness, i.e. virtue or beneficence. Origin: from G18 (ἀγαθός); KJV: goodness

G20 ἀγαλλίασις (agallíasis): exultation; specially, welcome. Origin: from G21 (ἀγαλλιάω); KJV: gladness, (exceeding) joy

G21 ἀγαλλιάω (agalliáō): properly, to jump for joy, i.e. exult. Origin: from agan (much) and G242 (ἅλλομαι); KJV: be (exceeding) glad, with exceeding joy, rejoice (greatly)

G22 ἄγαμος (ágamos): unmarried. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1062 (γάμος); KJV: unmarried

G23 ἀγανακτέω (aganaktéō): akin to the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); to be greatly afflicted, i.e. (figuratively) indignant. Origin: from (much) and (grief; KJV: be much (sore) displeased, have (be moved with, with) indignation

G24 ἀγανάκτησις (aganáktēsis): indignation. Origin: from G23 (ἀγανακτέω); KJV: indignation

G25 ἀγαπάω (agapáō): to love (in a social or moral sense). Origin: perhaps from (much) (or compare G5689); KJV: (be-)love(-ed)

G26 ἀγάπη (agápē): love, i.e. affection or benevolence; specially (plural) a love-feast. Origin: from G25 (ἀγαπάω); KJV: (feast of) charity(-ably), dear, love

G27 ἀγαπητός (agapētós): beloved. Origin: from G25 (ἀγαπάω); KJV: (dearly, well) beloved, dear

G28 Ἄγαρ (Ágar): Hagar, the concubine of Abraham. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1904); KJV: Hagar

G29 ἀγγαρεύω (angareúō): properly, to be a courier, i.e. (by implication) to press into public service. Origin: of foreign origin (compare H104); KJV: compel (to go)

G30 ἀγγεῖον (angeîon): compare the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); a receptacle. Origin: from (a pail, perhaps as bent; KJV: vessel

G31 ἀγγελία (angelía): an announcement, i.e. (by implication) precept. Origin: from G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: message

G32 ἄγγελος (ángelos): compare G34 (ἀγέλη)) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor. Origin: from (probably derived from G71 (ἄγω); KJV: angel, messenger

G33 ἄγε (áge): properly, lead, i.e. come on. Origin: imperative of G71 (ἄγω); KJV: go to

G34 ἀγέλη (agélē): a drove. Origin: from G71 (ἄγω) (compare G32 (ἄγγελος)); KJV: herd

G35 ἀγενεαλόγητος (agenealógētos): unregistered as to birth. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1075 (γενεαλογέω); KJV: without descent

G36 ἀγενής (agenḗs): properly, without kin, i.e. (of unknown descent, and by implication) ignoble. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1085 (γένος); KJV: base things

G37 ἁγιάζω (hagiázō): to make holy, i.e. (ceremonially) purify or consecrate; (mentally) to venerate. Origin: from G40 (ἅγιος); KJV: hallow, be holy, sanctify

G38 ἁγιασμός (hagiasmós): properly, purification, i.e. (the state) purity; concretely (by Hebraism) a purifier. Origin: from G37 (ἁγιάζω); KJV: holiness, sanctification

G39 ἅγιον (hágion): a sacred thing (i.e. spot). Origin: neuter of G40 (ἅγιος); KJV: holiest (of all), holy place, sanctuary

G40 ἅγιος (hágios): sacred (physically, pure, morally blameless or religious, ceremonially, consecrated). Origin: from (an awful thing) (compare G53 (ἁγνός), G2282 (θάλπω)); KJV: (most) holy (one, thing), saint

G41 ἁγιότης (hagiótēs): sanctity (i.e. properly, the state). Origin: from G40 (ἅγιος); KJV: holiness

G42 ἁγιωσύνη (hagiōsýnē): sacredness (i.e. properly, the quality). Origin: from G40 (ἅγιος); KJV: holiness

G43 ἀγκάλη (ankálē): an arm (as curved). Origin: from (a bend, "ache"); KJV: arm

G44 ἄγκιστρον (ánkistron): a hook (as bent). Origin: from the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη); KJV: hook

G45 ἄγκυρα (ánkyra): an "anchor" (as crooked). Origin: from the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη); KJV: anchor

G46 ἄγναφος (ágnaphos): properly, unfulled, i.e. (by implication) new (cloth). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the same as G1102 (γναφεύς); KJV: new

G47 ἁγνεία (hagneía): cleanliness (the quality), i.e. (specially) chastity. Origin: from G53 (ἁγνός); KJV: purity

G48 ἁγνίζω (hagnízō): to make clean, i.e. (figuratively) sanctify (ceremonially or morally). Origin: from G53 (ἁγνός); KJV: purify (self)

G49 ἁγνισμός (hagnismós): a cleansing (the act), i.e. (ceremonially) lustration. Origin: from G48 (ἁγνίζω); KJV: purification

G50 ἀγνοέω (agnoéō): not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: (be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown

G51 ἀγνόημα (agnóēma): a thing ignored, i.e. shortcoming. Origin: from G50 (ἀγνοέω); KJV: error

G52 ἄγνοια (ágnoia): ignorance (properly, the quality). Origin: from G50 (ἀγνοέω); KJV: ignorance

G53 ἁγνός (hagnós): properly, clean, i.e. (figuratively) innocent, modest, perfect. Origin: from the same as G40 (ἅγιος); KJV: chaste, clean, pure

G54 ἁγνότης (hagnótēs): cleanness (the state), i.e. (figuratively) blamelessness. Origin: from G53 (ἁγνός); KJV: pureness

G55 ἁγνῶς (hagnōs): purely, i.e. honestly. Origin: adverb from G53 (ἁγνός); KJV: sincerely

G56 ἀγνωσία (agnōsía): ignorance (properly, the state). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1108 (γνῶσις); KJV: ignorance, not the knowledge

G57 ἄγνωστος (ágnōstos): unknown. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1110 (γνωστός); KJV: unknown

G58 ἀγορά (agorá): probably akin to G1453 (ἐγείρω)); properly, the town-square (as a place of public resort); by implication, a market or thoroughfare. Origin: from (to gather; KJV: market(-place), street

G59 ἀγοράζω (agorázō): properly, to go to market, i.e. (by implication) to purchase; specially, to redeem. Origin: from G58 (ἀγορά); KJV: buy, redeem

G60 ἀγοραῖος (agoraîos): relating to the market-place, i.e. forensic (times); by implication, vulgar. Origin: from G58 (ἀγορά); KJV: baser sort, low

G61 ἄγρα (ágra): (abstractly) a catching (of fish); also (concretely) a haul (of fish). Origin: from G71 (ἄγω); KJV: draught

G62 ἀγράμματος (agrámmatos): unlettered, i.e. illiterate. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1121 (γράμμα); KJV: unlearned

G63 ἀγραυλέω (agrauléō): to camp out. Origin: from G68 (ἀγρός) and G832 (αὐλέω) (in the sense of G833 (αὐλή)); KJV: abide in the field

G64 ἀγρεύω (agreúō): to hunt, i.e. (figuratively) to entrap. Origin: from G61 (ἄγρα); KJV: catch

G65 ἀγριέλαιος (agriélaios): an oleaster. Origin: from G66 (ἄγριος) and G1636 (ἐλαία); KJV: olive tree (which is) wild

G66 ἄγριος (ágrios): wild (as pertaining to the country), literally (natural) or figuratively (fierce). Origin: from G68 (ἀγρός); KJV: wild, raging

G67 Ἀγρίππας (Agríppas): wild-horse tamer; Agrippas, one of the Herods. Origin: apparently from G66 (ἄγριος) and G2462 (ἵππος); KJV: Agrippa

G68 ἀγρός (agrós): a field (as a drive for cattle); genitive case, the country; specially, a farm, i.e. hamlet. Origin: from G71 (ἄγω); KJV: country, farm, piece of ground, land

G69 ἀγρυπνέω (agrypnéō): to be sleepless, i.e. keep awake. Origin: ultimately from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G5258 (ὕπνος); KJV: watch

G70 ἀγρυπνία (agrypnía): sleeplessness, i.e. a keeping awake. Origin: from G69 (ἀγρυπνέω); KJV: watch

G71 ἄγω (ágō): properly, to lead; by implication, to bring, drive, (reflexively) go, (specially) pass (time), or (figuratively) induce. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be, bring (forth), carry, (let) go, keep, lead away, be open

G72 ἀγωγή (agōgḗ): a bringing up, i.e. mode of living. Origin: reduplicated from G71 (ἄγω); KJV: manner of life

G73 ἀγών (agṓn): properly, a place of assembly (as if led), i.e. (by implication) a contest (held there); figuratively, an effort or anxiety. Origin: from G71 (ἄγω); KJV: conflict, contention, fight, race

G74 ἀγωνία (agōnía): a struggle (properly, the state), i.e. (figuratively) anguish. Origin: from G73 (ἀγών); KJV: agony

G75 ἀγωνίζομαι (agōnízomai): to struggle, literally (to compete for a prize), figuratively (to contend with an adversary), or genitive case (to endeavor to accomplish something). Origin: from G73 (ἀγών); KJV: fight, labor fervently, strive

G76 Ἀδάμ (Adám): Adam, the first man; typically (of Jesus) man (as his representative). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H121); KJV: Adam

G77 ἀδάπανος (adápanos): and G1160 (δαπάνη); costless, i.e. gratuitous. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle); KJV: without expense

G78 Ἀδδί (Addí): Addi, an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H5716); KJV: Addi

G79 ἀδελφή (adelphḗ): a sister (naturally or ecclesiastically). Origin: feminine of G80 (ἀδελφός); KJV: sister

G80 ἀδελφός (adelphós): a brother (literally or figuratively) near or remote (much like G1 (Α)). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a connective particle) and (the womb); KJV: brother

G81 ἀδελφότης (adelphótēs): brotherhood (properly, the feeling of brotherliness), i.e. the (Christian) fraternity. Origin: from G80 (ἀδελφός); KJV: brethren, brotherhood

G82 ἄδηλος (ádēlos): hidden, figuratively, indistinct. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1212 (δῆλος); KJV: appear not, uncertain

G83 ἀδηλότης (adēlótēs): uncertainty. Origin: from G82 (ἄδηλος); KJV: X uncertain

G84 ἀδήλως (adḗlōs): uncertainly. Origin: adverb from G82 (ἄδηλος); KJV: uncertainly

G85 ἀδημονέω (adēmonéō): to be in distress (of mind). Origin: from a derivative of (to be sated to loathing); KJV: be full of heaviness, be very heavy

G86 ᾅδης (háidēs): properly, unseen, i.e. "Hades" or the place (state) of departed souls. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as negative particle) and G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: grave, hell

G87 ἀδιάκριτος (adiákritos): properly, undistinguished, i.e. (actively) impartial. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1252 (διακρίνω); KJV: without partiality

G88 ἀδιάλειπτος (adiáleiptos): unintermitted, i.e. permanent. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G1223 (διά) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: without ceasing, continual

G89 ἀδιαλείπτως (adialeíptōs): uninterruptedly, i.e. without omission (on an appropriate occasion). Origin: adverb from G88 (ἀδιάλειπτος); KJV: without ceasing

G90 ἀδιαφθορία (adiaphthoría): incorruptibleness, i.e. (figuratively) purity (of doctrine). Origin: from a derivative of a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1311 (διαφθείρω); KJV: uncorruptness

G91 ἀδικέω (adikéō): to be unjust, i.e. (actively) do wrong (morally, socially or physically). Origin: from G94 (ἄδικος); KJV: hurt, injure, be an offender, be unjust, (do, suffer, take) wrong

G92 ἀδίκημα (adíkēma): a wrong done. Origin: from G91 (ἀδικέω); KJV: evil doing, iniquity, matter of wrong

G93 ἀδικία (adikía): (legal) injustice (properly, the quality, by implication, the act); morally, wrongfulness (of character, life or act). Origin: from G94 (ἄδικος); KJV: iniquity, unjust, unrighteousness, wrong

G94 ἄδικος (ádikos): unjust; by extension wicked; by implication, treacherous; specially, heathen. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1349 (δίκη); KJV: unjust, unrighteous

G95 ἀδίκως (adíkōs): unjustly. Origin: adverb from G94 (ἄδικος); KJV: wrongfully

G96 ἀδόκιμος (adókimos): unapproved, i.e. rejected; by implication, worthless (literally or morally). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1384 (δόκιμος); KJV: castaway, rejected, reprobate

G97 ἄδολος (ádolos): and G1388 (δόλος); undeceitful, i.e. (figuratively) unadulterated. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle); KJV: sincere

G98 Ἀδραμυττηνός (Adramyttēnós): Adramyttene or belonging to Adramyttium. Origin: from (a place in Asia Minor); KJV: of Adramyttium

G99 Ἀδρίας (Adrías): the Adriatic sea (including the Ionian). Origin: from (a place near its shore); KJV: Adria

G100 ἁδρότης (hadrótēs): plumpness, i.e. (figuratively) liberality. Origin: from (stout); KJV: abundance

G101 ἀδυνατέω (adynatéō): to be unable, i.e. (passively) impossible. Origin: from G102 (ἀδύνατος); KJV: be impossible

G102 ἀδύνατος (adýnatos): unable, i.e. weak (literally or figuratively); passively, impossible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1415 (δυνατός); KJV: could not do, impossible, impotent, not possible, weak

G103 ᾄδω (áidō): to sing. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: sing

G104 ἀεί (aeí): "ever," by qualification regularly; by implication, earnestly. Origin: from an obsolete primary noun (apparently meaning continued duration); KJV: always, ever

G105 ἀετός (aetós): an eagle (from its wind-like flight). Origin: from the same as G109 (ἀήρ); KJV: eagle

G106 ἄζυμος (ázymos): unleavened, i.e. (figuratively) uncorrupted; (in the neutral plural) specially (by implication) the Passover week. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2219 (ζύμη); KJV: unleavened (bread)

G107 Ἀζώρ (Azṓr): Azor, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H5809); KJV: Azorigin

G108 Ἄζωτος (Ázōtos): Azotus (i.e. Ashdod), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H795); KJV: Azotus

G109 ἀήρ (aḗr): by analogy, to blow); "air" (as naturally circumambient). Origin: from (to breathe unconsciously, i.e. respire; KJV: air

G110 ἀθανασία (athanasía): deathlessness. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2288 (θάνατος); KJV: immortality

G111 ἀθέμιτος (athémitos): from the base of G5087 (τίθημι)); illegal; by implication, flagitious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of (statute; KJV: abominable, unlawful thing

G112 ἄθεος (átheos): godless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2316 (θεός); KJV: without God

G113 ἄθεσμος (áthesmos): lawless, i.e. (by implication) criminal. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι) (in the sense of enacting); KJV: wicked

G114 ἀθετέω (athetéō): to set aside, i.e. (by implication) to disesteem, neutralize or violate. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: cast off, despise, disannul, frustrate, bring to nought, reject

G115 ἀθέτησις (athétēsis): cancellation (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G114 (ἀθετέω); KJV: disannulling, put away

G116 Ἀθῆναι (Athēnai): Athenæ, the capitol of Greece. Origin: plural of (the goddess of wisdom, who was reputed to have founded the city); KJV: Athens

G117 Ἀθηναῖος (Athēnaîos): an Athenæan or inhabitant of Athenæ. Origin: from G116 (Ἀθῆναι); KJV: Athenian

G118 ἀθλέω (athléō): to contend in the competitive games. Origin: from (a contest in the public lists); KJV: strive

G119 ἄθλησις (áthlēsis): a struggle (figuratively). Origin: from G118 (ἀθλέω); KJV: fight

G120 ἀθυμέω (athyméō): to be spiritless, i.e. disheartened. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: be dismayed

G121 ἄθωος (áthōos): not guilty. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and probably a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι) (meaning a penalty); KJV: innocent

G122 αἴγειος (aígeios): belonging to a goat. Origin: from (a goat); KJV: goat

G123 αἰγιαλός (aigialós): a beach (on which the waves dash). Origin: from (to rush) and G251 (ἅλς) (in the sense of the sea; KJV: shore

G124 Αἰγύπτιος (Aigýptios): an Ægyptian or inhabitant of Ægyptus. Origin: from G125 (Αἴγυπτος); KJV: Egyptian

G125 Αἴγυπτος (Aígyptos): Ægyptus, the land of the Nile. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Egypt

G126 ἀΐδιος (aḯdios): everduring (forward and backward, or forward only). Origin: from G104 (ἀεί); KJV: eternal, everlasting

G127 αἰδώς (aidṓs): bashfulness, i.e. (towards men), modesty or (towards God) awe. Origin: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1492 (εἴδω) (through the idea of downcast eyes); KJV: reverence, shamefacedness

G128 Αἰθίοψ (Aithíops): an Æthiopian (as a blackamoor). Origin: from (to scorch) and (the face, from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); KJV: Ethiopian

G129 αἷμα (haîma): blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: blood

G130 αἱματεκχυσία (haimatekchysía): an effusion of blood. Origin: from G129 (αἷμα) and a derivative of G1632 (ἐκχέω); KJV: shedding of blood

G131 αἱμοῤῥέω (haimorrhéō): to flow blood, i.e. have a hæmorrhage. Origin: from G129 (αἷμα) and G4482 (ῥέω); KJV: diseased with an issue of blood

G132 Αἰνέας (Ainéas): Ænĕas, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Æneas

G133 αἴνεσις (aínesis): a praising (the act), i.e. (specially) a thank(-offering). Origin: from G134 (αἰνέω); KJV: praise

G134 αἰνέω (ainéō): to praise (God). Origin: from G136 (αἶνος); KJV: praise

G135 αἴνιγμα (aínigma): an obscure saying ("enigma"), i.e. (abstractly) obscureness. Origin: from a derivative of G136 (αἶνος) (in its primary sense); KJV: X darkly

G136 αἶνος (aînos): properly, a story, but used in the sense of G1868 (ἔπαινος); praise (of God). Origin: apparently a prime word; KJV: praise

G137 Αἰνών (Ainṓn): Ænon, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (a derivative of G5869, place of springs); KJV: Ænon

G138 αἱρέομαι (hairéomai): to take for oneself, i.e. to prefer. Origin: probably akin to G142 (αἴρω); KJV: choose

G139 αἵρεσις (haíresis): properly, a choice, i.e. (specially) a party or (abstractly) disunion. Origin: from G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: heresy (which is the Greek word itself), sect

G140 αἱρετίζω (hairetízō): to make a choice. Origin: from a derivative of G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: choose

G141 αἱρετικός (hairetikós): a schismatic. Origin: from the same as G140 (αἱρετίζω); KJV: heretic (the Greek word itself)

G142 αἴρω (aírō): to lift up; by implication, to take up or away; figuratively, to raise (the voice), keep in suspense (the mind), specially, to sail away (i.e. weigh anchor); by Hebraism (compare H05375) to expiate sin. Origin: a primary root; KJV: away with, bear (up), carry, lift up, loose, make to doubt, put away, remove, take (away, up)

G143 αἰσθάνομαι (aisthánomai): to apprehend (properly, by the senses). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: perceive

G144 αἴσθησις (aísthēsis): perception, i.e. (figuratively) discernment. Origin: from G143 (αἰσθάνομαι); KJV: judgment

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G145 to G288
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G145 αἰσθητήριον (aisthētḗrion): properly, an organ of perception, i.e. (figuratively) judgment. Origin: from a derivative of G143 (αἰσθάνομαι); KJV: senses

G146 αἰσχροκερδής (aischrokerdḗs): sordid. Origin: from G150 (αἰσχρός) and (gain); KJV: given to (greedy of) filthy lucre

G147 αἰσχροκερδῶς (aischrokerdōs): sordidly. Origin: adverb from G146 (αἰσχροκερδής); KJV: for filthy lucre's sake

G148 αἰσχρολογία (aischrología): vile conversation. Origin: from G150 (αἰσχρός) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: filthy communication

G149 αἰσχρόν (aischrón): a shameful thing, i.e. indecorum. Origin: neuter of G150 (αἰσχρός); KJV: shame

G150 αἰσχρός (aischrós): shameful, i.e. base (specially, venal). Origin: from the same as G153 (αἰσχύνομαι); KJV: filthy

G151 αἰσχρότης (aischrótēs): shamefulness, i.e. obscenity. Origin: from G150 (αἰσχρός); KJV: filthiness

G152 αἰσχύνη (aischýnē): shame or disgrace (abstractly or concretely). Origin: from G153 (αἰσχύνομαι); KJV: dishonesty, shame

G153 αἰσχύνομαι (aischýnomai): to feel shame (for oneself). Origin: from (disfigurement, i.e. disgrace); KJV: be ashamed

G154 αἰτέω (aitéō): to ask (in genitive case). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: ask, beg, call for, crave, desire, require

G155 αἴτημα (aítēma): a thing asked or (abstractly) an asking. Origin: from G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: petition, request, required

G156 αἰτία (aitía): a cause (as if asked for), i.e. (logical) reason (motive, matter), (legal) crime (alleged or proved). Origin: from the same as G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: accusation, case, cause, crime, fault, (wh-)ere(-fore)

G157 αἰτίαμα (aitíama): a thing charged. Origin: from a derivative of G156 (αἰτία); KJV: complaint

G158 αἴτιον (aítion): a reason or crime (like G156 (αἰτία)). Origin: neuter of G159 (αἴτιος); KJV: cause, fault

G159 αἴτιος (aítios): causative, i.e. (concretely) a causer. Origin: from the same as G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: author

G160 αἰφνίδιος (aiphnídios): unexpected, i.e. (adverbially) suddenly. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5316 (φαίνω) (compare G1810 (ἐξαίφνης)) (meaning non-apparent); KJV: sudden, unawares

G161 αἰχμαλωσία (aichmalōsía): captivity. Origin: from G164 (αἰχμάλωτος); KJV: captivity

G162 αἰχμαλωτεύω (aichmalōteúō): to capture (like G163 (αἰχμαλωτίζω)). Origin: from G164 (αἰχμάλωτος); KJV: lead captive

G163 αἰχμαλωτίζω (aichmalōtízō): to make captive. Origin: from G164 (αἰχμάλωτος); KJV: lead away captive, bring into captivity

G164 αἰχμάλωτος (aichmálōtos): properly, a prisoner of war, i.e. (genitive case) a captive. Origin: from (a spear) and a derivative of the same as G259 (ἅλωσις); KJV: captive

G165 αἰών (aiṓn): properly, an age; by extension, perpetuity (also past); by implication, the world; specially (Jewish) a Messianic period (present or future). Origin: from the same as G104 (ἀεί); KJV: age, course, eternal, (for) ever(-more), (n-)ever, (beginning of the , while the) world (began, without end)

G166 αἰώνιος (aiṓnios): perpetual (also used of past time, or past and future as well). Origin: from G165 (αἰών); KJV: eternal, for ever, everlasting, world (began)

G167 ἀκαθαρσία (akatharsía): impurity (the quality), physically or morally. Origin: from G169 (ἀκάθαρτος); KJV: uncleanness

G168 ἀκαθάρτης (akathártēs): impurity (the state), morally. Origin: from G169 (ἀκάθαρτος); KJV: filthiness

G169 ἀκάθαρτος (akáthartos): impure (ceremonially, morally (lewd) or specially, (demonic)). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2508 (καθαίρω) (meaning cleansed); KJV: foul, unclean

G170 ἀκαιρέομαι (akairéomai): to be inopportune (for oneself), i.e. to fail of a proper occasion. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2540 (καιρός) (meaning unseasonable); KJV: lack opportunity

G171 ἀκαίρως (akaírōs): inopportunely. Origin: adverb from the same as G170 (ἀκαιρέομαι); KJV: out of season

G172 ἄκακος (ákakos): not bad, i.e. (objectively) innocent or (subjectively) unsuspecting. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2556 (κακός); KJV: harmless, simple

G173 ἄκανθα (ákantha): a thorn. Origin: probably from the same as G188 (ἀκμήν); KJV: thorn

G174 ἀκάνθινος (akánthinos): thorny. Origin: from G173 (ἄκανθα); KJV: of thorns

G175 ἄκαρπος (ákarpos): barren (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2590 (καρπός); KJV: without fruit, unfruitful

G176 ἀκατάγνωστος (akatágnōstos): unblamable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2607 (καταγινώσκω); KJV: that cannot be condemned

G177 ἀκατακάλυπτος (akatakályptos): unveiled. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: uncovered

G178 ἀκατάκριτος (akatákritos): without (legal) trial. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2632 (κατακρίνω); KJV: uncondemned

G179 ἀκατάλυτος (akatálytos): indissoluble, i.e. (figuratively) permanent. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2647 (καταλύω); KJV: endless

G180 ἀκατάπαυστος (akatápaustos): unrefraining. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2664 (καταπαύω); KJV: that cannot cease

G181 ἀκαταστασία (akatastasía): instability, i.e. disorder. Origin: from G182 (ἀκατάστατος); KJV: commotion, confusion, tumult

G182 ἀκατάστατος (akatástatos): inconstant. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2525 (καθίστημι); KJV: unstable

G183 ἀκατάσχετος (akatáschetos): unrestrainable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2722 (κατέχω); KJV: unruly

G184 Ἀκελδαμά (Akeldamá): corresponding to H02506 and H01818); Akeldama, a place near Jerusalem. Origin: of Chaldee origin (meaning field of blood; KJV: Aceldama

G185 ἀκέραιος (akéraios): unmixed, i.e. (figuratively) innocent. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767 (κεράννυμι); KJV: harmless, simple

G186 ἀκλινής (aklinḗs): not leaning, i.e. (figuratively) firm. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: without wavering

G187 ἀκμάζω (akmázō): to make a point, i.e. (figuratively) mature. Origin: from the same as G188 (ἀκμήν); KJV: be fully ripe

G188 ἀκμήν (akmḗn): adverbially, just now, i.e. still. Origin: accusative case of a noun ("acme") akin to (a point) and meaning the same; KJV: yet

G189 ἀκοή (akoḗ): hearing (the act, the sense or the thing heard). Origin: from G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: audience, ear, fame, which ye heard, hearing, preached, report, rumor

G190 ἀκολουθέω (akolouthéō): properly, to be in the same way with, i.e. to accompany (specially, as a disciple). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and (a road); KJV: follow, reach

G191 ἀκούω (akoúō): to hear (in various senses). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: give (in the) audience (of), come (to the ears), (shall) hear(-er, -ken), be noised, be reported, understand

G192 ἀκρασία (akrasía): want of self-restraint. Origin: from G193 (ἀκρατής); KJV: excess, incontinency

G193 ἀκρατής (akratḗs): powerless, i.e. without self-control. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2904 (κράτος); KJV: incontinent

G194 ἄκρατος (ákratos): undiluted. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2767 (κεράννυμι); KJV: without mixture

G195 ἀκρίβεια (akríbeia): exactness. Origin: from the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος); KJV: perfect manner

G196 ἀκριβέστατος (akribéstatos): most exact. Origin: superlative of (a derivative of the same as G206 (ἄκρον)); KJV: most straitest

G197 ἀκριβέστερον (akribésteron): (adverbially) more exactly. Origin: neuter of the comparative of the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος); KJV: more perfect(-ly)

G198 ἀκριβόω (akribóō): to be exact, i.e. ascertain. Origin: from the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος); KJV: enquire diligently

G199 ἀκριβῶς (akribōs): exactly. Origin: adverb from the same as G196 (ἀκριβέστατος); KJV: circumspectly, diligently, perfect(-ly)

G200 ἀκρίς (akrís): a locust (as pointed, or as lighting on the top of vegetation). Origin: apparently from the same as G206 (ἄκρον); KJV: locust

G201 ἀκροατήριον (akroatḗrion): an audience-room. Origin: from G202 (ἀκροατής); KJV: place of hearing

G202 ἀκροατής (akroatḗs): apparently an intensive of G191 (ἀκούω)); a hearer (merely). Origin: from (to listen; KJV: hearer

G203 ἀκροβυστία (akrobystía): the prepuce; by implication, an uncircumcised (i.e. gentile, figuratively, unregenerate) state or person. Origin: from G206 (ἄκρον) and probably a modified form of (the penis or male sexual organ); KJV: not circumcised, uncircumcised (with G2192 (ἔχω)), uncircumcision

G204 ἀκρογωνιαῖος (akrogōniaîos): belonging to the extreme corner. Origin: from G206 (ἄκρον) and G1137 (γωνία); KJV: chief corner

G205 ἀκροθίνιον (akrothínion): properly (in the plural) the top of the heap, i.e. (by implication) best of the booty. Origin: from G206 (ἄκρον) and (a heap); KJV: spoils

G206 ἄκρον (ákron): the extremity. Origin: neuter of an adjective probably akin to the base of G188 (ἀκμήν); KJV: one end… other, tip, top, uttermost participle

G207 Ἀκύλας (Akýlas): Akulas, an Israelite. Origin: probably for Latin aquila (an eagle); KJV: Aquila

G208 ἀκυρόω (akyróō): to invalidate. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2964 (κυρόω); KJV: disannul, make of none effect

G209 ἀκωλύτως (akōlýtōs): in an unhindered manner, i.e. freely. Origin: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2967 (κωλύω); KJV: no man forbidding him

G210 ἄκων (ákōn): unwilling. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1635 (ἑκών); KJV: against the will

G211 ἀλάβαστρον (alábastron): properly, an "alabaster" box, i.e. (by extension) a perfume vase (of any material). Origin: neuter of (of uncertain derivation), the name of a stone; KJV: (alabaster) box

G212 ἀλαζονεία (alazoneía): braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) self-confidence. Origin: from G213 (ἀλαζών); KJV: boasting, pride

G213 ἀλαζών (alazṓn): braggart. Origin: from (vagrancy); KJV: boaster

G214 ἀλαλάζω (alalázō): to vociferate, i.e. (by implication) to wail; figuratively, to clang. Origin: from ( a shout, "halloo"); KJV: tinkle, wail

G215 ἀλάλητος (alálētos): unspeakable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: unutterable, which cannot be uttered

G216 ἄλαλος (álalos): mute. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: dumb

G217 ἅλας (hálas): salt; figuratively, prudence. Origin: from G251 (ἅλς); KJV: salt

G218 ἀλείφω (aleíphō): to oil (with perfume). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as particle of union) and the base of G3045 (λιπαρός); KJV: anoint

G219 ἀλεκτοροφωνία (alektorophōnía): cock-crow, i.e. the third night-watch. Origin: from G220 (ἀλέκτωρ) and G5456 (φωνή); KJV: cockcrowing

G220 ἀλέκτωρ (aléktōr): a cock or male fowl. Origin: from (to ward off); KJV: cock

G221 Ἀλεξανδρεύς (Alexandreús): an Alexandreian or inhabitant of Alexandria. Origin: from (the city so called); KJV: of Alexandria, Alexandrian

G222 Ἀλεξανδρῖνος (Alexandrînos): Alexandrine, or belonging to Alexandria. Origin: from the same as G221 (Ἀλεξανδρεύς); KJV: of Alexandria

G223 Ἀλέξανδρος (Aléxandros): man-defender; Alexander, the name of three Israelites and one other man. Origin: from the same as (the first part of) G220 (ἀλέκτωρ) and G435 (ἀνήρ); KJV: Alexander

G224 ἄλευρον (áleuron): flour. Origin: from (to grind); KJV: meal

G225 ἀλήθεια (alḗtheia): truth. Origin: from G227 (ἀληθής); KJV: true, X truly, truth, verity

G226 ἀληθεύω (alētheúō): to be true (in doctrine and profession). Origin: from G227 (ἀληθής); KJV: speak (tell) the truth

G227 ἀληθής (alēthḗs): true (as not concealing). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2990 (λανθάνω); KJV: true, truly, truth

G228 ἀληθινός (alēthinós): truthful. Origin: from G227 (ἀληθής); KJV: true

G229 ἀλήθω (alḗthō): to grind. Origin: from the same as G224 (ἄλευρον); KJV: grind

G230 ἀληθῶς (alēthōs): truly. Origin: adverb from G227 (ἀληθής); KJV: indeed, surely, of a surety, truly, of a (in) truth, verily, very

G231 ἁλιεύς (halieús): a sailor (as engaged on the salt water), i.e. (by implication) a fisher. Origin: from G251 (ἅλς); KJV: fisher(-man)

G232 ἁλιεύω (halieúō): to be a fisher, i.e. (by implication) to fish. Origin: from G231 (ἁλιεύς); KJV: go a-fishing

G233 ἁλίζω (halízō): to salt. Origin: from G251 (ἅλς); KJV: salt

G234 ἀλίσγεμα (alísgema): (ceremonially) defilement. Origin: from (to soil); KJV: pollution

G235 ἀλλά (allá): properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations). Origin: neuter plural of G243 (ἄλλος); KJV: and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet

G236 ἀλλάσσω (allássō): to make different. Origin: from G243 (ἄλλος); KJV: change

G237 ἀλλαχόθεν (allachóthen): from elsewhere. Origin: from G243 (ἄλλος); KJV: some other way

G238 ἀλληγορέω (allēgoréō): to allegorize. Origin: from G243 (ἄλλος) and (to harangue (compare G58 (ἀγορά))); KJV: be an allegory (the Greek word itself)

G239 ἀλληλουϊα (allēlouïa): praise ye Jah!, an adoring exclamation. Origin: of Hebrew origin (imperative of H1984 and H3050); KJV: alleluiah

G240 ἀλλήλων (allḗlōn): one another. Origin: Genitive plural from G243 (ἄλλος) reduplicated; KJV: each other, mutual, one another, (the other), (them-, your-)selves, (selves) together (sometimes with G3326 (μετά) or G4314 (πρός))

G241 ἀλλογενής (allogenḗs): foreign, i.e. not a Jew. Origin: from G243 (ἄλλος) and G1085 (γένος); KJV: stranger

G242 ἅλλομαι (hállomai): to jump; figuratively, to gush. Origin: middle voice of apparently a primary verb; KJV: leap, spring up

G243 ἄλλος (állos): "else," i.e. different (in many applications). Origin: a primary word; KJV: more, one (another), (an-, some an-)other(-s, -wise)

G244 ἀλλοτριεπίσκοπος (allotriepískopos): overseeing others' affairs, i.e. a meddler (specially, in Gentile customs). Origin: from G245 (ἀλλότριος) and G1985 (ἐπίσκοπος); KJV: busybody in other men's matters

G245 ἀλλότριος (allótrios): another's, i.e. not one's own; by extension foreign, not akin, hostile. Origin: from G243 (ἄλλος); KJV: alien, (an-)other (man's, men's), strange(-r)

G246 ἀλλόφυλος (allóphylos): foreign, i.e. (specially) Gentile. Origin: from G243 (ἄλλος) and G5443 (φυλή); KJV: one of another nation

G247 ἄλλως (állōs): differently. Origin: adverb from G243 (ἄλλος); KJV: otherwise

G248 ἀλοάω (aloáō): to tread out grain. Origin: from the same as G257 (ἅλων); KJV: thresh, tread out the corn

G249 ἄλογος (álogos): irrational. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: brute, unreasonable

G250 ἀλόη (alóē): aloes (the gum). Origin: of foreign origin (compare G174 (ἀκάνθινος)); KJV: aloes

G251 ἅλς (háls): "salt". Origin: a primary word; KJV: salt

G252 ἁλυκός (halykós): briny. Origin: from G251 (ἅλς); KJV: salt

G253 ἀλυπότερος (alypóteros): more without grief. Origin: comparative of a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3077 (λύπη); KJV: less sorrowful

G254 ἅλυσις (hálysis): a fetter or manacle. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: bonds, chain

G255 ἀλυσιτελής (alysitelḗs): gainless, i.e. (by implication) pernicious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G3081 (λυσιτελεῖ); KJV: unprofitable

G256 Ἀλφαῖος (Alphaîos): Alphæus, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H2501); KJV: Alpheus

G257 ἅλων (hálōn): a threshing-floor (as rolled hard), i.e. (figuratively) the grain (and chaff, as just threshed). Origin: probably from the base of G1507 (εἱλίσσω); KJV: floor

G258 ἀλώπηξ (alṓpēx): a fox, i.e. (figuratively) a cunning person. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: fox

G259 ἅλωσις (hálōsis): capture, be taken. Origin: from a collateral form of G138 (αἱρέομαι);

G260 ἅμα (háma): properly, at the "same" time, but freely used as a preposition or adverb denoting close association. Origin: a primary particle; KJV: also, and, together, with(-al)

G261 ἀμαθής (amathḗs): ignorant. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3129 (μανθάνω); KJV: unlearned

G262 ἀμαράντινος (amarántinos): "amaranthine", i.e. (by implication) fadeless. Origin: from G263 (ἀμάραντος); KJV: that fadeth not away

G263 ἀμάραντος (amárantos): unfading, i.e. (by implication) perpetual. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3133 (μαραίνω); KJV: that fadeth not away

G264 ἁμαρτάνω (hamartánō): properly, to miss the mark (and so not share in the prize), i.e. (figuratively) to err, especially (morally) to sin. Origin: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G3313 (μέρος); KJV: for your faults, offend, sin, trespass

G265 ἁμάρτημα (hamártēma): a sin (properly concrete). Origin: from G264 (ἁμαρτάνω); KJV: sin

G266 ἁμαρτία (hamartía): a sin (properly abstract). Origin: from G264 (ἁμαρτάνω); KJV: offence, sin(-ful)

G267 ἀμάρτυρος (amártyros): unattested. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a form of G3144 (μάρτυς); KJV: without witness

G268 ἁμαρτωλός (hamartōlós): sinful, i.e. a sinner. Origin: from G264 (ἁμαρτάνω); KJV: sinful, sinner

G269 ἄμαχος (ámachos): peaceable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3163 (μάχη); KJV: not a brawler

G270 ἀμάω (amáō): properly, to collect, i.e. (by implication) reap. Origin: from G260 (ἅμα); KJV: reap down

G271 ἀμέθυστος (améthystos): the "amethyst" (supposed to prevent intoxication). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3184 (μεθύω); KJV: amethyst

G272 ἀμελέω (ameléō): to be careless of. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3199 (μέλω); KJV: make light of, neglect, be negligent, no regard

G273 ἄμεμπτος (ámemptos): irreproachable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3201 (μέμφομαι); KJV: blameless, faultless, unblamable

G274 ἀμέμπτως (amémptōs): faultlessly. Origin: adverb from G273 (ἄμεμπτος); KJV: blameless, unblamably

G275 ἀμέριμνος (amérimnos): not anxious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3308 (μέριμνα); KJV: without care(-fulness), secure

G276 ἀμετάθετος (ametáthetos): unchangeable, or (neuter as abstract) unchangeability. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3346 (μετατίθημι); KJV: immutable(-ility)

G277 ἀμετακίνητος (ametakínētos): immovable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3334 (μετακινέω); KJV: unmovable

G278 ἀμεταμέλητος (ametamélētos): irrevocable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3338 (μεταμέλλομαι); KJV: without repentance, not to be repented of

G279 ἀμετανόητος (ametanóētos): unrepentant. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3340 (μετανοέω); KJV: impenitent

G280 ἄμετρος (ámetros): immoderate. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3358 (μέτρον); KJV: (thing) without measure

G281 ἀμήν (amḗn): properly, firm, i.e. (figuratively) trustworthy; adverbially, surely (often as interjection, so be it). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H543); KJV: amen, verily

G282 ἀμήτωρ (amḗtōr): motherless, i.e. of unknown maternity. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3384 (μήτηρ); KJV: without mother

G283 ἀμίαντος (amíantos): unsoiled, i.e. (figuratively) pure. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3392 (μιαίνω); KJV: undefiled

G284 Ἀμιναδάβ (Aminadáb): Aminadab, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5992); KJV: Aminadab

G285 ἄμμος (ámmos): sand (as heaped on the beach). Origin: perhaps from G260 (ἅμα); KJV: sand

G286 ἀμνός (amnós): a lamb. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: lamb

G287 ἀμοιβή (amoibḗ): requital. Origin: from (to exchange); KJV: requite

G288 ἄμπελος (ámpelos): a vine (as coiling about a support). Origin: probably from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and that of G257 (ἅλων); KJV: vine

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G289 to G430
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G289 ἀμπελουργός (ampelourgós): a vine-worker, i.e. pruner. Origin: from G288 (ἄμπελος) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: vine-dresser

G290 ἀμπελών (ampelṓn): a vineyard. Origin: from G288 (ἄμπελος); KJV: vineyard

G291 Ἀμπλίας (Amplías): Amplias, a Roman Christian. Origin: contracted for Latin ampliatus (enlarged); KJV: Amplias

G292 ἀμύνομαι (amýnomai): to ward off (for oneself), i.e. protect. Origin: middle voice of a primary verb; KJV: defend

G293 ἀμφίβληστρον (amphíblēstron): a (fishing) net (as thrown about the fish). Origin: from a compound of the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: net

G294 ἀμφιέννυμι (amphiénnymi): to enrobe. Origin: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and (to invest); KJV: clothe

G295 Ἀμφίπολις (Amphípolis): a city surrounded by a river; Amphipolis, a place in Macedonia. Origin: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: Amphipolis

G296 ἄμφοδον (ámphodon): a fork in the road. Origin: from the base of G297 (ἀμφότερος) and G3598 (ὁδός); KJV: where two ways meet

G297 ἀμφότερος (amphóteros): (in plural) both. Origin: comparative of (around); KJV: both

G298 ἀμώμητος (amṓmētos): unblamable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3469 (μωμάομαι); KJV: blameless

G299 ἄμωμος (ámōmos): unblemished (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3470 (μῶμος); KJV: without blame (blemish, fault, spot), faultless, unblamable

G300 Ἀμών (Amṓn): Amon, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H526); KJV: Amon

G301 Ἀμώς (Amṓs): Amos, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H531); KJV: Amos

G302 ἄν (án): Origin: a primary particle, denoting a supposition, wish, possibility or uncertainty KJV: (what-, where-, wither-, who-)soever

G303 ἀνά (aná): properly, up; but (by extension) used (distributively) severally, or (locally) at (etc.). Origin: a primary preposition and adverb; KJV: and, apiece, by, each, every (man), in, through

G304 ἀναβαθμός (anabathmós): a stairway. Origin: from G305 (ἀναβαίνω) (compare G898 (βαθμός)); KJV: stairs

G305 ἀναβαίνω (anabaínō): to go up (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: arise, ascend (up), climb (go, grow, rise, spring) up, come (up)

G306 ἀναβάλλομαι (anabállomai): to put off (for oneself). Origin: middle voice from G303 (ἀνά) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: defer

G307 ἀναβιβάζω (anabibázō): to cause to go up, i.e. haul (a net). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: draw

G308 ἀναβλέπω (anablépō): to look up; by implication, to recover sight. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: look (up), see, receive sight

G309 ἀνάβλεψις (anáblepsis): restoration of sight. Origin: from G308 (ἀναβλέπω); KJV: recovery of sight

G310 ἀναβοάω (anaboáō): to halloo. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G994 (βοάω); KJV: cry (aloud, out)

G311 ἀναβολή (anabolḗ): a putting off. Origin: from G306 (ἀναβάλλομαι); KJV: delay

G312 ἀναγγέλλω (anangéllō): to announce (in detail). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: declare, rehearse, report, show, speak, tell

G313 ἀναγεννάω (anagennáō): to beget or (by extension) bear (again). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G1080 (γεννάω); KJV: beget, (bear) X (again)

G314 ἀναγινώσκω (anaginṓskō): to know again, i.e. (by extension) to read. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: read

G315 ἀναγκάζω (anankázō): to necessitate. Origin: from G318 (ἀνάγκη); KJV: compel, constrain

G316 ἀναγκαῖος (anankaîos): necessary; by implication, close (of kin). Origin: from G318 (ἀνάγκη); KJV: near, necessary, necessity, needful

G317 ἀναγκαστῶς (anankastōs): compulsorily. Origin: adverb from a derivative of G315 (ἀναγκάζω); KJV: by constraint

G318 ἀνάγκη (anánkē): constraint (literally or figuratively); by implication, distress. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη); KJV: distress, must needs, (of) necessity(-sary), needeth, needful

G319 ἀναγνωρίζομαι (anagnōrízomai): to make (oneself) known. Origin: middle voice from G303 (ἀνά) and G1107 (γνωρίζω); KJV: be made known

G320 ἀνάγνωσις (anágnōsis): (the act of) reading. Origin: from G314 (ἀναγινώσκω); KJV: reading

G321 ἀνάγω (anágō): to lead up; by extension to bring out; specially, to sail away. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring (again, forth, up again), depart, launch (forth), lead (up), loose, offer, sail, set forth, take up

G322 ἀναδείκνυμι (anadeíknymi): to exhibit, i.e. (by implication) to indicate, appoint. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: appoint, shew

G323 ἀνάδειξις (anádeixis): (the act of) exhibition. Origin: from G322 (ἀναδείκνυμι); KJV: shewing

G324 ἀναδέχομαι (anadéchomai): to entertain (as a guest). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: receive

G325 ἀναδίδωμι (anadídōmi): to hand over. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: deliver

G326 ἀναζάω (anazáō): to recover life (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2198 (ζάω); KJV: (be a-)live again, revive

G327 ἀναζητέω (anazētéō): to search out. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2212 (ζητέω); KJV: seek

G328 ἀναζώννυμι (anazṓnnymi): to gird afresh. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2224 (ζώννυμι); KJV: gird up

G329 ἀναζωπυρέω (anazōpyréō): to re-enkindle. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a compound of the base of G2226 (ζῶον) and G4442 (πῦρ); KJV: stir up

G330 ἀναθάλλω (anathállō): to revive. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and (to flourish); KJV: flourish again

G331 ἀνάθεμα (anáthema): a (religious) ban or (concretely) excommunicated (thing or person). Origin: from G394 (ἀνατίθεμαι); KJV: accused, anathema, curse, X great

G332 ἀναθεματίζω (anathematízō): to declare or vow under penalty of execration. Origin: from G331 (ἀνάθεμα); KJV: (bind under a) curse, bind with an oath

G333 ἀναθεωρέω (anatheōréō): to look again (i.e. attentively) at (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2334 (θεωρέω); KJV: behold, consider

G334 ἀνάθημα (anáthēma): a votive offering. Origin: from G394 (ἀνατίθεμαι) (like G331 (ἀνάθεμα), but in a good sense); KJV: gift

G335 ἀναίδεια (anaídeia): impudence, i.e. (by implication) importunity. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle (compare G427 (ἄνευ))) and G127 (αἰδώς); KJV: importunity

G336 ἀναίρεσις (anaíresis): (the act of) killing. Origin: from G337 (ἀναιρέω); KJV: death

G337 ἀναιρέω (anairéō): to take up, i.e. adopt; by implication, to take away (violently), i.e. abolish, murder. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and (the active of) G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: put to death, kill, slay, take away, take up

G338 ἀναίτιος (anaítios): innocent. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G159 (αἴτιος) (in the sense of G156 (αἰτία)); KJV: blameless, guiltless

G339 ἀνακαθίζω (anakathízō): properly, to set up, i.e. (reflexively) to sit up. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2523 (καθίζω); KJV: sit up

G340 ἀνακαινίζω (anakainízō): to restore. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of G2537 (καινός); KJV: renew

G341 ἀνακαινόω (anakainóō): to renovate. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of G2537 (καινός); KJV: renew

G342 ἀνακαίνωσις (anakaínōsis): renovation. Origin: from G341 (ἀνακαινόω); KJV: renewing

G343 ἀνακαλύπτω (anakalýptō): to unveil. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of reversal) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: open, (un-)taken away

G344 ἀνακάμπτω (anakámptō): to turn back. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2578 (κάμπτω); KJV: (re-)turn

G345 ἀνακεῖμαι (anakeîmai): to recline (as a corpse or at a meal). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: guest, lean, lie, sit (down, at meat), at the table

G346 ἀνακεφαλαίομαι (anakephalaíomai): to sum up. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2775 (κεφαλαιόω) (in its original sense); KJV: briefly comprehend, gather together in one

G347 ἀνακλίνω (anaklínō): to lean back. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: lay, (make) sit down

G348 ἀνακόπτω (anakóptō): to beat back, i.e. check. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: hinder

G349 ἀνακράζω (anakrázō): to scream up (aloud). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2896 (κράζω); KJV: cry out

G350 ἀνακρίνω (anakrínō): properly, to scrutinize, i.e. (by implication) investigate, interrogate, determine. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: ask, question, discern, examine, judge, search

G351 ἀνάκρισις (anákrisis): a (judicial) investigation. Origin: from G350 (ἀνακρίνω); KJV: examination

G352 ἀνακύπτω (anakýptō): to unbend, i.e. rise; figuratively, be elated. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of reversal) and G2955 (κύπτω); KJV: lift up, look up

G353 ἀναλαμβάνω (analambánō): to take up. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: receive up, take (in, unto, up)

G354 ἀνάληψις (análēpsis): ascension. Origin: from G353 (ἀναλαμβάνω); KJV: taking up

G355 ἀναλίσκω (analískō): properly, to use up, i.e. destroy. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a form of the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: consume

G356 ἀναλογία (analogía): proportion. Origin: from a compound of G303 (ἀνά) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: proportion

G357 ἀναλογίζομαι (analogízomai): to estimate, i.e. (figuratively) contemplate. Origin: middle voice from G356 (ἀναλογία); KJV: consider

G358 ἄναλος (ánalos): saltless, i.e. insipid. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G251 (ἅλς); KJV: X lose saltness

G359 ἀνάλυσις (análysis): departure. Origin: from G360 (ἀναλύω); KJV: departure

G360 ἀναλύω (analýō): to break up, i.e. depart (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: depart, return

G361 ἀναμάρτητος (anamártētos): sinless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G264 (ἁμαρτάνω); KJV: that is without sin

G362 ἀναμένω (anaménō): to await. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: wait for

G363 ἀναμιμνήσκω (anamimnḗskō): to remind; (reflexively) to recollect. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3403 (μιμνήσκω); KJV: call to mind, (bring to , call to, put in), remember(-brance)

G364 ἀνάμνησις (anámnēsis): recollection. Origin: from G363 (ἀναμιμνήσκω); KJV: remembrance (again)

G365 ἀνανεόω (ananeóō): to renovate, i.e. reform. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of G3501 (νέος); KJV: renew

G366 ἀνανήφω (ananḗphō): to become sober again, i.e. (figuratively) regain (one's) senses. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3525 (νήφω); KJV: recover self

G367 Ἀνανίας (Ananías): Ananias, the name of three Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2608); KJV: Ananias

G368 ἀναντίῤῥητος (anantírrhētos): indisputable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: cannot be spoken against

G369 ἀναντιῤῥήτως (anantirrhḗtōs): promptly. Origin: adverb from G368 (ἀναντίῤῥητος); KJV: without gainsaying

G370 ἀνάξιος (anáxios): unfit. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G514 (ἄξιος); KJV: unworthy

G371 ἀναξίως (anaxíōs): irreverently. Origin: adverb from G370 (ἀνάξιος); KJV: unworthily

G372 ἀνάπαυσις (anápausis): intermission; by implication, recreation. Origin: from G373 (ἀναπαύω); KJV: rest

G373 ἀναπαύω (anapaúō): (reflexively) to repose (literally or figuratively (be exempt), remain); by implication, to refresh. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3973 (παύω); KJV: take ease, refresh, (give, take) rest

G374 ἀναπείθω (anapeíthō): to incite. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3982 (πείθω); KJV: persuade

G375 ἀναπέμπω (anapémpō): to send up or back. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3992 (πέμπω); KJV: send (again)

G376 ἀνάπηρος (anápēros): crippled. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of intensity) and (maimed); KJV: maimed

G377 ἀναπίπτω (anapíptō): to fall back, i.e. lie down, lean back. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: lean, sit down (to meat)

G378 ἀναπληρόω (anaplēróō): to complete; by implication, to occupy, supply; figuratively, to accomplish (by coincidence ot obedience). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4137 (πληρόω); KJV: fill up, fulfill, occupy, supply

G379 ἀναπολόγητος (anapológētos): indefensible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G626 (ἀπολογέομαι); KJV: without an excuse, inexcusable

G380 ἀναπτύσσω (anaptýssō): to unroll (a scroll or volume). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of reversal) and G4428 (πτύσσω); KJV: open

G381 ἀνάπτω (anáptō): to enkindle. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G681 (ἅπτω); KJV: kindle, light

G382 ἀναρίθμητος (anaríthmētos): unnumbered, i.e. without number. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G705 (ἀριθμέω); KJV: innumerable

G383 ἀνασείω (anaseíō): figuratively, to excite. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4579 (σείω); KJV: move, stir up

G384 ἀνασκευάζω (anaskeuázō): properly, to pack up (baggage), i.e. (by implication, and figuratively) to upset. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) (in the sense of reversal) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος); KJV: subvert

G385 ἀνασπάω (anaspáō): to take up or extricate. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4685 (σπάω); KJV: draw up, pull out

G386 ἀνάστασις (anástasis): a standing up again, i.e. (literally) a resurrection from death (individual, genitive case or by implication, (its author)), or (figuratively) a (moral) recovery (of spiritual truth). Origin: from G450 (ἀνίστημι); KJV: raised to life again, resurrection, rise from the dead, that should rise, rising again

G387 ἀναστατόω (anastatóō): properly, to drive out of home, i.e. (by implication) to disturb (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a derivative of G450 (ἀνίστημι) (in the sense of removal); KJV: trouble, turn upside down, make an uproar

G388 ἀνασταυρόω (anastauróō): to recrucify (figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4717 (σταυρόω); KJV: crucify afresh

G389 ἀναστενάζω (anastenázō): to sigh deeply. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4727 (στενάζω); KJV: sigh deeply

G390 ἀναστρέφω (anastréphō): to overturn; also to return; by implication, to busy oneself, i.e. remain, live. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: abide, behave self, have conversation, live, overthrow, pass, return, be used

G391 ἀναστροφή (anastrophḗ): behavior. Origin: from G390 (ἀναστρέφω); KJV: conversation

G392 ἀνατάσσομαι (anatássomai): to arrange. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the middle voice of G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: set in order

G393 ἀνατέλλω (anatéllō): to (cause to) arise. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G5056 (τέλος); KJV: (a-, make to) rise, at the rising of, spring (up), be up

G394 ἀνατίθεμαι (anatíthemai): to set forth (for oneself), i.e propound. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the middle voice of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: communicate, declare

G395 ἀνατολή (anatolḗ): a rising of light, i.e. dawn (figuratively); by implication, the east (also in plural). Origin: from G393 (ἀνατέλλω); KJV: dayspring, east, rising

G396 ἀνατρέπω (anatrépō): to overturn (figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: overthrow, subvert

G397 ἀνατρέφω (anatréphō): to rear (physically or mentally). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: bring up, nourish (up)

G398 ἀναφαίνω (anaphaínō): to show, i.e. (reflexively) appear, or (passively) to have pointed out. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: (should) appear, discover

G399 ἀναφέρω (anaphérō): to take up (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bear, bring (carry, lead) up, offer (up)

G400 ἀναφωνέω (anaphōnéō): to exclaim. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G5455 (φωνέω); KJV: speak out

G401 ἀνάχυσις (anáchysis): properly, effusion, i.e. (figuratively) license. Origin: from a comparative of G303 (ἀνά) and (to pour); KJV: excess

G402 ἀναχωρέω (anachōréō): to retire. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G5562 (χωρέω); KJV: depart, give place, go (turn) aside, withdraw self

G403 ἀνάψυξις (anápsyxis): properly, a recovery of breath, i.e. (figuratively) revival. Origin: from G404 (ἀναψύχω); KJV: revival

G404 ἀναψύχω (anapsýchō): properly, to cool off, i.e. (figuratively) relieve. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G5594 (ψύχω); KJV: refresh

G405 ἀνδραποδιστής (andrapodistḗs): an enslaver (as bringing men to his feet). Origin: from a derivative of a compound of G435 (ἀνήρ) and G4228 (πούς); KJV: menstealer

G406 Ἀνδρέας (Andréas): manly; Andreas, an Israelite. Origin: from G435 (ἀνήρ); KJV: Andrew

G407 ἀνδρίζομαι (andrízomai): to act manly. Origin: middle voice from G435 (ἀνήρ); KJV: quit like men

G408 Ἀνδρόνικος (Andrónikos): man of victory; Andronicos, an Israelite. Origin: from G435 (ἀνήρ) and G3534 (νῖκος); KJV: Adronicus

G409 ἀνδροφόνος (androphónos): a murderer. Origin: from G435 (ἀνήρ) and G5408 (φόνος); KJV: manslayer

G410 ἀνέγκλητος (anénklētos): unaccused, i.e. (by implication) irreproachable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1458 (ἐγκαλέω); KJV: blameless

G411 ἀνεκδιήγητος (anekdiḗgētos): not expounded in full, i.e. indescribable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1555 (ἐκδιηγέομαι); KJV: unspeakable

G412 ἀνεκλάλητος (aneklálētos): not spoken out, i.e. (by implication) unutterable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1583 (ἐκλαλέω); KJV: unspeakable

G413 ἀνέκλειπτος (anékleiptos): not left out, i.e. (by implication) inexhaustible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1587 (ἐκλείπω); KJV: that faileth not

G414 ἀνεκτότερος (anektóteros): more endurable. Origin: comparative of a derivative of G430 (ἀνέχομαι); KJV: more tolerable

G415 ἀνελεήμων (aneleḗmōn): merciless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G1655 (ἐλεήμων); KJV: unmerciful

G416 ἀνεμίζω (anemízō): to toss with the wind. Origin: from G417 (ἄνεμος); KJV: drive with the wind

G417 ἄνεμος (ánemos): wind; (plural) by implication, (the four) quarters (of the earth). Origin: from the base of G109 (ἀήρ); KJV: wind

G418 ἀνένδεκτος (anéndektos): unadmitted, i.e. (by implication) not supposable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of the same as G1735 (ἐνδέχεται); KJV: impossible

G419 ἀνεξερεύνητος (anexereúnētos): not searched out, i.e. (by implication) inscrutable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G1830 (ἐξερευνάω); KJV: unsearchable

G420 ἀνεξίκακος (anexíkakos): enduring of ill, i.e. forbearing. Origin: from G430 (ἀνέχομαι) and G2556 (κακός); KJV: patient

G421 ἀνεξιχνίαστος (anexichníastos): not tracked out, i.e. (by implication) untraceable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G2487 (ἴχνος); KJV: past finding out; unsearchable

G422 ἀνεπαίσχυντος (anepaíschyntos): not ashamed, i.e. irreprehensible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G153 (αἰσχύνομαι); KJV: --that needeth not to be ashamed

G423 ἀνεπίληπτος (anepílēptos): not arrested, i.e. (by implication) inculpable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G1949 (ἐπιλαμβάνομαι); KJV: blameless, unrebukeable

G424 ἀνέρχομαι (anérchomai): to ascend. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: go up

G425 ἄνεσις (ánesis): relaxation or (figuratively) relief. Origin: from G447 (ἀνίημι); KJV: eased, liberty, rest

G426 ἀνετάζω (anetázō): to investigate (judicially). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and (to test); KJV: (should have) examined(-d)

G427 ἄνευ (áneu): without. Origin: a primary particle; KJV: without

G428 ἀνεύθετος (aneúthetos): not well set, i.e. inconvenient. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2111 (εὔθετος); KJV: not commodious

G429 ἀνευρίσκω (aneurískō): to find out. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2147 (εὑρίσκω); KJV: find

G430 ἀνέχομαι (anéchomai): to hold oneself up against, i.e. (figuratively) put up with. Origin: middle voice from G303 (ἀνά) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: bear with, endure, forbear, suffer

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G431 to G573
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G431 ἀνεψιός (anepsiós): properly, akin, i.e. (specially) a cousin. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and an obsolete (a brood); KJV: sister's son

G432 ἄνηθον (ánēthon): dill. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: anise

G433 ἀνήκω (anḗkō): to attain to, i.e. (figuratively) be proper. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2240 (ἥκω); KJV: convenient, be fit

G434 ἀνήμερος (anḗmeros): savage. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (lame); KJV: fierce

G435 ἀνήρ (anḗr): a man (properly as an individual male). Origin: a primary word (compare G444 (ἄνθρωπος)); KJV: fellow, husband, man, sir

G436 ἀνθίστημι (anthístēmi): to stand against, i.e. oppose. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: resist, withstand

G437 ἀνθομολογέομαι (anthomologéomai): to confess in turn, i.e. respond in praise. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and the middle voice of G3670 (ὁμολογέω); KJV: give thanks

G438 ἄνθος (ánthos): a blossom. Origin: a primary word; KJV: flower

G439 ἀνθρακιά (anthrakiá): a bed of burning coals. Origin: from G440 (ἄνθραξ); KJV: fire of coals

G440 ἄνθραξ (ánthrax): a live coal. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: coal of fire

G441 ἀνθρωπάρεσκος (anthrōpáreskos): man-courting, i.e. fawning. Origin: from G444 (ἄνθρωπος) and G700 (ἀρέσκω); KJV: men-pleaser

G442 ἀνθρώπινος (anthrṓpinos): human. Origin: from G444 (ἄνθρωπος); KJV: human, common to man, man(-kind), (man-)kind, men's, after the manner of men

G443 ἀνθρωποκτόνος (anthrōpoktónos): a manslayer. Origin: from G444 (ἄνθρωπος) and (to kill); KJV: murderer

G444 ἄνθρωπος (ánthrōpos): from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); man-faced, i.e. a human being. Origin: from G435 (ἀνήρ) and (the countenance; KJV: certain, man

G445 ἀνθυπατεύω (anthypateúō): to act as proconsul. Origin: from G446 (ἀνθύπατος); KJV: be the deputy

G446 ἀνθύπατος (anthýpatos): instead of the highest officer, i.e. (specially) a Roman proconsul. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and a superlative of G5228 (ὑπέρ); KJV: deputy

G447 ἀνίημι (aníēmi): to let up, i.e. (literally) slacken or (figuratively) desert, desist from. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and (to send); KJV: forbear, leave, loose

G448 ἀνίλεως (aníleōs): inexorable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2436 (ἵλεως); KJV: without mercy

G449 ἄνιπτος (ániptos): without ablution. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3538 (νίπτω); KJV: unwashen

G450 ἀνίστημι (anístēmi): to stand up (literal or figurative, transitive or intransitive). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: arise, lift up, raise up (again), rise (again), stand up(-right)

G451 Ἄννα (Ánna): Anna, an Israelitess. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2584); KJV: Anna

G452 Ἄννας (Ánnas): Annas (i.e. G367 (Ἀνανίας)), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2608); KJV: Annas

G453 ἀνόητος (anóētos): unintelligent; by implication, sensual. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: fool(-ish), unwise

G454 ἄνοια (ánoia): stupidity; by implication, rage. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3563 (νοῦς); KJV: folly, madness

G455 ἀνοίγω (anoígō): to open up (literally or figuratively, in various applications). Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and (to open); KJV: open

G456 ἀνοικοδομέω (anoikodoméō): to rebuild. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and G3618 (οἰκοδομέω); KJV: build again

G457 ἄνοιξις (ánoixis): opening (throat). Origin: from G455 (ἀνοίγω); KJV: X open

G458 ἀνομία (anomía): illegality, i.e. violation of law or (genitive case) wickedness. Origin: from G459 (ἄνομος); KJV: iniquity, X transgress(-ion of) the law, unrighteousness

G459 ἄνομος (ánomos): lawless, i.e. (negatively) not subject to (the Jewish) law; (by implication, a Gentile), or (positively) wicked. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3551 (νόμος); KJV: without law, lawless, transgressor, unlawful, wicked

G460 ἀνόμως (anómōs): lawlessly, i.e. (specially) not amenable to (the Jewish) law. Origin: adverb from G459 (ἄνομος); KJV: without law

G461 ἀνορθόω (anorthóō): to straighten up. Origin: from G303 (ἀνά) and a derivative of the base of G3717 (ὀρθός); KJV: lift (set) up, make straight

G462 ἀνόσιος (anósios): wicked. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3741 (ὅσιος); KJV: unholy

G463 ἀνοχή (anochḗ): self-restraint, i.e. tolerance. Origin: from G430 (ἀνέχομαι); KJV: forbearance

G464 ἀνταγωνίζομαι (antagōnízomai): to struggle against (figuratively) ("antagonize"). Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G75 (ἀγωνίζομαι); KJV: strive against

G465 ἀντάλλαγμα (antállagma): an equivalent or ransom. Origin: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω); KJV: in exchange

G466 ἀνταναπληρόω (antanaplēróō): to supplement. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G378 (ἀναπληρόω); KJV: fill up

G467 ἀνταποδίδωμι (antapodídōmi): to requite (good or evil). Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G591 (ἀποδίδωμι); KJV: recompense, render, repay

G468 ἀνταπόδομα (antapódoma): a requital (properly, the thing). Origin: from G467 (ἀνταποδίδωμι); KJV: recompense

G469 ἀνταπόδοσις (antapódosis): requital (properly, the act). Origin: from G467 (ἀνταποδίδωμι); KJV: reward

G470 ἀνταποκρίνομαι (antapokrínomai): to contradict or dispute. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G611 (ἀποκρίνομαι); KJV: answer again, reply against

G471 ἀντέπω (antépō): to refute or deny. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G2036 (ἔπω); KJV: gainsay, say against

G472 ἀντέχομαι (antéchomai): to hold oneself opposite to, i.e. (by implication) adhere to; by extension to care for. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and the middle voice of G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: hold fast, hold to, support

G473 ἀντί (antí): opposite, i.e. instead or because of (rarely in addition to). Origin: a primary particle; KJV: for, in the room of

G474 ἀντιβάλλω (antibállō): to bandy. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: have

G475 ἀντιδιατίθεμαι (antidiatíthemai): to set oneself opposite, i.e. be disputatious. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G1303 (διατίθεμαι); KJV: that oppose themselves

G476 ἀντίδικος (antídikos): an opponent (in a lawsuit); specially, Satan (as the arch-enemy). Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G1349 (δίκη); KJV: adversary

G477 ἀντίθεσις (antíthesis): opposition, i.e. a conflict (of theories). Origin: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: opposition

G478 ἀντικαθίστημι (antikathístēmi): to set down (troops) against, i.e. withstand. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G2525 (καθίστημι); KJV: resist

G479 ἀντικαλέω (antikaléō): to invite in return. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: bid again

G480 ἀντίκειμαι (antíkeimai): to lie opposite, i.e. be adverse (figuratively, repugnant) to. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: adversary, be contrary, oppose

G481 ἀντικρύ (antikrý): opposite. Origin: prolonged from G473 (ἀντί); KJV: over against

G482 ἀντιλαμβάνομαι (antilambánomai): to take hold of in turn, i.e. succor; also to participate. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and the middle voice of G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: help, partaker, support

G483 ἀντιλέγω (antilégō): to dispute, refuse. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: answer again, contradict, deny, gainsay(-er), speak against

G484 ἀντίληψις (antílēpsis): relief. Origin: from G482 (ἀντιλαμβάνομαι); KJV: help

G485 ἀντιλογία (antilogía): dispute, disobedience. Origin: from a derivative of G483 (ἀντιλέγω); KJV: contradiction, gainsaying, strife

G486 ἀντιλοιδορέω (antiloidoréō): to rail in reply. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G3058 (λοιδορέω); KJV: revile again

G487 ἀντίλυτρον (antílytron): a redemption-price. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G3083 (λύτρον); KJV: ransom

G488 ἀντιμετρέω (antimetréō): to mete in return. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G3354 (μετρέω); KJV: measure again

G489 ἀντιμισθία (antimisthía): requital, correspondence. Origin: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G3408 (μισθός); KJV: recompense

G490 Ἀντιόχεια (Antiócheia): Antiochia, a place in Syria. Origin: from (a Syrian king); KJV: Antioch

G491 Ἀντιοχεύς (Antiocheús): an Antiochian or inhabitant of Antiochia. Origin: from G490 (Ἀντιόχεια); KJV: of Antioch

G492 ἀντιπαρέρχομαι (antiparérchomai): to go along opposite. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G3928 (παρέρχομαι); KJV: pass by on the other side

G493 Ἀντίπας (Antípas): Antipas, a Christian. Origin: contracted for a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and a derivative of G3962 (πατήρ); KJV: Antipas

G494 Ἀντιπατρίς (Antipatrís): Antipatris, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as G493 (Ἀντίπας); KJV: Antipatris

G495 ἀντιπέραν (antipéran): on the opposite side. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G4008 (πέραν); KJV: over against

G496 ἀντιπίπτω (antipíptō): to oppose. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G4098 (πίπτω) (including its alternate); KJV: resist

G497 ἀντιστρατεύομαι (antistrateúomai): (figuratively) to attack, i.e. (by implication) destroy. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G4754 (στρατεύομαι); KJV: war against

G498 ἀντιτάσσομαι (antitássomai): to range oneself against, i.e. oppose. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and the middle voice of G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: oppose themselves, resist

G499 ἀντίτυπον (antítypon): corresponding ("antitype"), i.e. a representative, counterpart. Origin: neuter of a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G5179 (τύπος); KJV: (like) figure (whereunto)

G500 ἀντίχριστος (antíchristos): an opponent of the Messiah. Origin: from G473 (ἀντί) and G5547 (Χριστός); KJV: antichrist

G501 ἀντλέω (antléō): to bale up (properly, bilge water), i.e. dip water (with a bucket, pitcher, etc.). Origin: from (the hold of a ship); KJV: draw (out)

G502 ἄντλημα (ántlēma): a baling-vessel. Origin: from G501 (ἀντλέω); KJV: thing to draw with

G503 ἀντοφθαλμέω (antophthalméō): to face. Origin: from a compound of G473 (ἀντί) and G3788 (ὀφθαλμός); KJV: bear up into

G504 ἄνυδρος (ánydros): waterless, i.e. dry. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5204 (ὕδωρ); KJV: dry, without water

G505 ἀνυπόκριτος (anypókritos): undissembled, i.e. sincere. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5271 (ὑποκρίνομαι); KJV: without dissimulation (hypocrisy), unfeigned

G506 ἀνυπότακτος (anypótaktos): unsubdued, i.e. insubordinate (in fact or temper). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5293 (ὑποτάσσω); KJV: disobedient, that is not put under, unruly

G507 ἄνω (ánō): upward or on the top. Origin: adverb from G473 (ἀντί); KJV: above, brim, high, up

G508 ἀνώγεον (anṓgeon): above the ground, i.e. (properly) the second floor of a building; used for a dome or a balcony on the upper story. Origin: from G507 (ἄνω) and G1093 (γῆ); KJV: upper room

G509 ἄνωθεν (ánōthen): from above; by analogy, from the first; by implication, anew. Origin: from G507 (ἄνω); KJV: from above, again, from the beginning (very first), the top

G510 ἀνωτερικός (anōterikós): superior, i.e. (locally) more remote. Origin: from G511 (ἀνώτερος); KJV: upper

G511 ἀνώτερος (anṓteros): upper, i.e. (neuter as adverb) to a more conspicuous place, in a former part of the book. Origin: comparative degree of G507 (ἄνω); KJV: above, higher

G512 ἀνωφελής (anōphelḗs): useless or (neuter) inutility. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G5624 (ὠφέλιμος); KJV: unprofitable(-ness)

G513 ἀξίνη (axínē): compare G4486 (ῥήγνυμι)); an axe. Origin: probably from (to break; KJV: axe

G514 ἄξιος (áxios): deserving, comparable or suitable (as if drawing praise). Origin: probably from G71 (ἄγω); KJV: due reward, meet, (un-)worthy

G515 ἀξιόω (axióō): to deem entitled or fit. Origin: from G514 (ἄξιος); KJV: desire, think good, count (think) worthy

G516 ἀξίως (axíōs): appropriately. Origin: adverb from G514 (ἄξιος); KJV: as becometh, after a godly sort, worthily(-thy)

G517 ἀόρατος (aóratos): invisible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3707 (ὁρατός); KJV: invisible (thing)

G518 ἀπαγγέλλω (apangéllō): to announce. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: bring word (again), declare, report, shew (again), tell

G519 ἀπάγχομαι (apánchomai): akin to the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); to strangle oneself off (i.e. to death). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to choke; KJV: hang himself

G520 ἀπάγω (apágō): to take off (in various senses). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring, carry away, lead (away), put to death, take away

G521 ἀπαίδευτος (apaídeutos): uninstructed, i.e. (figuratively) stupid. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3811 (παιδεύω); KJV: unlearned

G522 ἀπαίρω (apaírō): to lift off, i.e. remove. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G142 (αἴρω); KJV: take (away)

G523 ἀπαιτέω (apaitéō): to demand back. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: ask again, require

G524 ἀπαλγέω (apalgéō): to grieve out, i.e. become apathetic. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to smart); KJV: be past feeling

G525 ἀπαλλάσσω (apallássō): to change away, i.e. release, (reflexively) remove. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω); KJV: deliver, depart

G526 ἀπαλλοτριόω (apallotrióō): to estrange away, i.e. (passively and figuratively) to be non-participant. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G245 (ἀλλότριος); KJV: alienate, be alien

G527 ἀπαλός (apalós): soft. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: tender

G528 ἀπαντάω (apantáō): to meet away, i.e. encounter. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί); KJV: meet

G529 ἀπάντησις (apántēsis): a (friendly) encounter. Origin: from G528 (ἀπαντάω); KJV: meet

G530 ἅπαξ (hápax): one (or a single) time (numerically or conclusively). Origin: probably from G537 (ἅπας); KJV: once

G531 ἀπαράβατος (aparábatos): not passing away, i.e. untransferable (perpetual). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3845 (παραβαίνω); KJV: unchangeable

G532 ἀπαρασκεύαστος (aparaskeúastos): unready. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G3903 (παρασκευάζω); KJV: unprepared

G533 ἀπαρνέομαι (aparnéomai): to deny utterly, i.e. disown, abstain. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G720 (ἀρνέομαι); KJV: deny

G534 ἀπάρτι (apárti): from now, i.e. henceforth (already). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G737 (ἄρτι); KJV: from henceforth

G535 ἀπαρτισμός (apartismós): completion. Origin: from a derivative of G534 (ἀπάρτι); KJV: finishing

G536 ἀπαρχή (aparchḗ): a beginning of sacrifice, i.e. the (Jewish) first-fruit (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G756 (ἄρχομαι); KJV: first-fruits

G537 ἅπας (hápas): absolutely all or (singular) every one. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and G3956 (πᾶς); KJV: all (things), every (one), whole

G538 ἀπατάω (apatáō): to cheat, i.e. delude. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: deceive

G539 ἀπάτη (apátē): delusion. Origin: from G538 (ἀπατάω); KJV: deceit(-ful, -fulness), deceivableness(-ving)

G540 ἀπάτωρ (apátōr): fatherless, i.e. of unrecorded paternity. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3962 (πατήρ); KJV: without father

G541 ἀπαύγασμα (apaúgasma): an off-flash, i.e. effulgence. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G826 (αὐγάζω); KJV: brightness

G542 ἀπείδω (apeídō): to see fully. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the same as G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: see

G543 ἀπείθεια (apeítheia): disbelief (obstinate and rebellious). Origin: from G545 (ἀπειθής); KJV: disobedience, unbelief

G544 ἀπειθέω (apeithéō): to disbelieve (wilfully and perversely). Origin: from G545 (ἀπειθής); KJV: not believe, disobedient, obey not, unbelieving

G545 ἀπειθής (apeithḗs): unpersuadable, i.e. contumacious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3982 (πείθω); KJV: disobedient

G546 ἀπειλέω (apeiléō): to menace; by implication, to forbid. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: threaten

G547 ἀπειλή (apeilḗ): a menace. Origin: from G546 (ἀπειλέω); KJV: X straitly, threatening

G548 ἄπειμι (ápeimi): to be away. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: be absent

G549 ἄπειμι (ápeimi): to go away. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to go); KJV: go

G550 ἀπειπόμην (apeipómēn): to say off for oneself, i.e. disown. Origin: reflexive past of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G2036 (ἔπω); KJV: renounce

G551 ἀπείραστος (apeírastos): untried, i.e. not temptable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G3987 (πειράω); KJV: not to be tempted

G552 ἄπειρος (ápeiros): inexperienced, i.e. ignorant. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G3984 (πεῖρα); KJV: unskilful

G553 ἀπεκδέχομαι (apekdéchomai): to expect fully. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1551 (ἐκδέχομαι); KJV: look (wait) for

G554 ἀπεκδύομαι (apekdýomai): to divest wholly oneself, or (for oneself) despoil. Origin: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G1562 (ἐκδύω); KJV: put off, spoil

G555 ἀπέκδυσις (apékdysis): divestment. Origin: from G554 (ἀπεκδύομαι); KJV: putting off

G556 ἀπελαύνω (apelaúnō): to dismiss. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1643 (ἐλαύνω); KJV: drive

G557 ἀπελεγμός (apelegmós): refutation, i.e. (by implication) contempt. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω); KJV: nought

G558 ἀπελεύθερος (apeleútheros): one freed away, i.e. a freedman. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1658 (ἐλεύθερος); KJV: freeman

G559 Ἀπελλῆς (Apellēs): Apelles, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Apelles

G560 ἀπελπίζω (apelpízō): to hope out, i.e. fully expect. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1679 (ἐλπίζω); KJV: hope for again

G561 ἀπέναντι (apénanti): from in front, i.e. opposite, before or against. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1725 (ἔναντι); KJV: before, contrary, over against, in the presence of

G562 ἀπέραντος (apérantos): unfinished, i.e. (by implication) interminable. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a secondary derivative of G4008 (πέραν); KJV: endless

G563 ἀπερισπάστως (aperispástōs): undistractedly, i.e. free from (domestic) solicitude. Origin: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative participle) and a presumed derivative of G4049 (περισπάω); KJV: without distraction

G564 ἀπερίτμητος (aperítmētos): uncircumcised (figuratively). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4059 (περιτέμνω); KJV: uncircumcised

G565 ἀπέρχομαι (apérchomai): to go off (i.e. depart), aside (i.e. apart) or behind (i.e. follow), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: come, depart, go (aside, away, back, out, … ways), pass away, be past

G566 ἀπέχει (apéchei): it is sufficient. Origin: third person singular present indicative active of G568 (ἀπέχω) used impersonally; KJV: it is enough

G567 ἀπέχομαι (apéchomai): to hold oneself off, i.e. refrain. Origin: middle voice (reflexively) of G568 (ἀπέχω); KJV: abstain

G568 ἀπέχω (apéchō): (actively) to have out, i.e. receive in full; (intransitively) to keep (oneself) away, i.e. be distant (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: be, have, receive

G569 ἀπιστέω (apistéō): to be unbelieving, i.e. (transitively) disbelieve, or (by implication) disobey. Origin: from G571 (ἄπιστος); KJV: believe not
