G570 ἀπιστία (apistía): faithlessness, i.e. (negatively) disbelief (lack of Christian faith), or (positively) unfaithfulness (disobedience). Origin: from G571 (ἄπιστος); KJV: unbelief

G571 ἄπιστος (ápistos): (actively) disbelieving, i.e. without Christian faith (specially, a heathen); (passively) untrustworthy (person), or incredible (thing). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4103 (πιστός); KJV: that believeth not, faithless, incredible thing, infidel, unbeliever(-ing)

G572 ἁπλότης (haplótēs): singleness, i.e. (subjectively) sincerity (without dissimulation or self-seeking), or (objectively) generosity (copious bestowal). Origin: from G573 (ἁπλοῦς); KJV: bountifulness, liberal(-ity), simplicity, singleness

G573 ἁπλοῦς (haploûs): properly, folded together, i.e. single (figuratively, clear). Origin: probably from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and the base of G4120 (πλέκω); KJV: single

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G574 to G711
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G574 ἁπλῶς (haplōs): bountifully. Origin: adverb from G573 (ἁπλοῦς) (in the objective sense of G572 (ἁπλότης)); KJV: --liberally

G575 ἀπό (apó): "off," i.e. away (from something near), in various senses (of place, time, or relation; literal or figurative). Origin: a primary particle; KJV: (X here-)after, ago, at, because of, before, by (the space of), for(-th), from, in, (out) of, off, (up-)on(-ce), since, with

G576 ἀποβαίνω (apobaínō): literally, to disembark; figuratively, to eventuate. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: become, go out, turn

G577 ἀποβάλλω (apobállō): to throw off; figuratively, to lose. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: cast away

G578 ἀποβλέπω (apoblépō): to look away from everything else, i.e. (figuratively) intently regard. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: have respect

G579 ἀπόβλητος (apóblētos): cast off, i.e. (figuratively) such as to be rejected. Origin: from G577 (ἀποβάλλω); KJV: be refused

G580 ἀποβολή (apobolḗ): rejection; figuratively, loss. Origin: from G577 (ἀποβάλλω); KJV: casting away, loss

G581 ἀπογενόμενος (apogenómenos): absent, i.e. deceased (figuratively, renounced). Origin: past participle of a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: being dead

G582 ἀπογραφή (apographḗ): an enrollment; by implication, an assessment. Origin: from G583 (ἀπογράφω); KJV: taxing

G583 ἀπογράφω (apográphō): to write off (a copy or list), i.e. enrol. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1125 (γράφω); KJV: tax, write

G584 ἀποδείκνυμι (apodeíknymi): to show off, i.e. exhibit; figuratively, to demonstrate, i.e. accredit. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: (ap-)prove, set forth, shew

G585 ἀπόδειξις (apódeixis): manifestation. Origin: from G584 (ἀποδείκνυμι); KJV: demonstration

G586 ἀποδεκατόω (apodekatóō): to tithe (as debtor or creditor). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1183 (δεκατόω); KJV: (give, pay, take) tithe

G587 ἀπόδεκτος (apódektos): accepted, i.e. agreeable. Origin: from G588 (ἀποδέχομαι); KJV: acceptable

G588 ἀποδέχομαι (apodéchomai): to take fully, i.e. welcome (persons), approve (things). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: accept, receive (gladly)

G589 ἀποδημέω (apodēméō): to go abroad, i.e. visit a foreign land. Origin: from G590 (ἀπόδημος); KJV: go (travel) into a far country, journey

G590 ἀπόδημος (apódēmos): absent from one's own people, i.e. a foreign traveller. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: taking a far journey

G591 ἀποδίδωμι (apodídōmi): to give away, i.e. up, over, back, etc. (in various applications). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: deliver (again), give (again), (re-)pay(-ment be made), perform, recompense, render, requite, restore, reward, sell, yield

G592 ἀποδιορίζω (apodiorízō): to disjoin (by a boundary, figuratively, a party). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of G223 (Ἀλέξανδρος) and G3724 (ὁρίζω); KJV: separate

G593 ἀποδοκιμάζω (apodokimázō): to disapprove, i.e. (by implication) to repudiate. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G1381 (δοκιμάζω); KJV: disallow, reject

G594 ἀποδοχή (apodochḗ): acceptance. Origin: from G588 (ἀποδέχομαι); KJV: acceptation

G595 ἀπόθεσις (apóthesis): a laying aside (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G659 (ἀποτίθημι); KJV: putting away (off)

G596 ἀποθήκη (apothḗkē): a repository, i.e. granary. Origin: from G659 (ἀποτίθημι); KJV: barn, garner

G597 ἀποθησαυρίζω (apothēsaurízō): to treasure away. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2343 (θησαυρίζω); KJV: lay up in store

G598 ἀποθλίβω (apothlíbō): to crowd (from every side). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2346 (θλίβω); KJV: press

G599 ἀποθνήσκω (apothnḗskō): to die off (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2348 (θνήσκω); KJV: be dead, death, die, lie a-dying, be slain (X with)

G600 ἀποκαθίστημι (apokathístēmi): to reconstitute (in health, home or organization). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2525 (καθίστημι); KJV: restore (again)

G601 ἀποκαλύπτω (apokalýptō): to take off the cover, i.e. disclose. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: reveal

G602 ἀποκάλυψις (apokálypsis): disclosure. Origin: from G601 (ἀποκαλύπτω); KJV: appearing, coming, lighten, manifestation, be revealed, revelation

G603 ἀποκαραδοκία (apokaradokía): intense anticipation. Origin: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and a compound of (the head) and G1380 (δοκέω) (in the sense of watching); KJV: earnest expectation

G604 ἀποκαταλλάσσω (apokatallássō): to reconcile fully. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2644 (καταλλάσσω); KJV: reconcile

G605 ἀποκατάστασις (apokatástasis): reconstitution. Origin: from G600 (ἀποκαθίστημι); KJV: restitution

G606 ἀπόκειμαι (apókeimai): to be reserved; figuratively, to await. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: be appointed, (be) laid up

G607 ἀποκεφαλίζω (apokephalízō): to decapitate. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2776 (κεφαλή); KJV: behead

G608 ἀποκλείω (apokleíō): to close fully. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2808 (κλείω); KJV: shut up

G609 ἀποκόπτω (apokóptō): to amputate; reflexively (by irony) to mutilate (the privy parts). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: cut off

G610 ἀπόκριμα (apókrima): a judicial decision. Origin: from G611 (ἀποκρίνομαι) (in its original sense of judging); KJV: sentence

G611 ἀποκρίνομαι (apokrínomai): to conclude for oneself, i.e. (by implication) to respond; by Hebraism (compare H06030) to begin to speak (where an address is expected). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and ; KJV: answer

G612 ἀπόκρισις (apókrisis): a response. Origin: from G611 (ἀποκρίνομαι); KJV: answer

G613 ἀποκρύπτω (apokrýptō): to conceal away (i.e. fully); figuratively, to keep secret. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2928 (κρύπτω); KJV: hide

G614 ἀπόκρυφος (apókryphos): secret; by implication, treasured. Origin: from G613 (ἀποκρύπτω); KJV: hid, kept secret

G615 ἀποκτείνω (apokteínō): to kill outright; figuratively, to destroy. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to slay); KJV: put to death, kill, slay

G616 ἀποκυέω (apokyéō): to breed forth, i.e. (by transference) to generate (figuratively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2949 (κῦμα); KJV: beget, produce

G617 ἀποκυλίω (apokylíō): to roll away. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2947 (κυλιόω); KJV: roll away (back)

G618 ἀπολαμβάνω (apolambánō): to receive (specially, in full, or as a host); also to take aside. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: receive, take

G619 ἀπόλαυσις (apólausis): full enjoyment. Origin: from a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to enjoy); KJV: enjoy(-ment)

G620 ἀπολείπω (apoleípō): to leave behind (passively, remain); by implication, to forsake. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: leave, remain

G621 ἀπολείχω (apoleíchō): to lick clean. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to "lick"); KJV: lick

G622 ἀπόλλυμι (apóllymi): to destroy fully (reflexively, to perish, or lose), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3639 (ὄλεθρος); KJV: destroy, die, lose, mar, perish

G623 Ἀπολλύων (Apollýōn): a destroyer (i.e. Satan). Origin: active participle of G622 (ἀπόλλυμι); KJV: Apollyon

G624 Ἀπολλωνία (Apollōnía): from G622 (ἀπόλλυμι)); Apollonia, a place in Macedonia. Origin: from the pagan deity (i.e. the sun; KJV: Apollonia

G625 Ἀπολλῶς (Apollōs): Apollos, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the same as G624 (Ἀπολλωνία); KJV: Apollos

G626 ἀπολογέομαι (apologéomai): to give an account (legal plea) of oneself, i.e. exculpate (self). Origin: middle voice from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: answer (for self), make defence, excuse (self), speak for self

G627 ἀπολογία (apología): a plea ("apology"). Origin: from the same as G626 (ἀπολογέομαι); KJV: answer (for self), clearing of self, defence

G628 ἀπολούω (apoloúō): to wash fully, i.e. (figuratively) have remitted (reflexively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3068 (λούω); KJV: wash (away)

G629 ἀπολύτρωσις (apolýtrōsis): (the act) ransom in full, i.e. (figuratively) riddance, or (specially) Christian salvation. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3083 (λύτρον); KJV: deliverance, redemption

G630 ἀπολύω (apolýō): to free fully, i.e. (literally) relieve, release, dismiss (reflexively, depart), or (figuratively) let die, pardon or (specially) divorce. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: (let) depart, dismiss, divorce, forgive, let go, loose, put (send) away, release, set at liberty

G631 ἀπομάσσομαι (apomássomai): to scrape away. Origin: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and (to squeeze, knead, smear); KJV: wipe off

G632 ἀπονέμω (aponémō): to apportion, i.e. bestow. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G3551 (νόμος); KJV: give

G633 ἀπονίπτω (aponíptō): to wash off (reflexively, one's own hands symbolically). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3538 (νίπτω); KJV: wash

G634 ἀποπίπτω (apopíptō): to fall off. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall

G635 ἀποπλανάω (apoplanáō): to lead astray (figuratively); passively, to stray (from truth). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4105 (πλανάω); KJV: err, seduce

G636 ἀποπλέω (apopléō): to set sail. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4126 (πλέω); KJV: sail away

G637 ἀποπλύνω (apoplýnō): to rinse off. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4150 (πλύνω); KJV: wash

G638 ἀποπνίγω (apopnígō): to stifle (by drowning or overgrowth). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4155 (πνίγω); KJV: choke

G639 ἀπορέω (aporéō): to have no way out, i.e. be at a loss (mentally). Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: (stand in) doubt, be perplexed

G640 ἀπορία (aporía): a (state of) quandary. Origin: from the same as G639 (ἀπορέω); KJV: perplexity

G641 ἀποῤῥίπτω (aporrhíptō): to hurl off, i.e. precipitate (oneself). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4496 (ῥίπτω); KJV: cast

G642 ἀπορφανίζω (aporphanízō): to bereave wholly, i.e. (figuratively) separate (from intercourse). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G3737 (ὀρφανός); KJV: take

G643 ἀποσκευάζω (aposkeuázō): to pack up (one's) baggage. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος); KJV: take up… carriages

G644 ἀποσκίασμα (aposkíasma): a shading off, i.e. obscuration. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4639 (σκιά); KJV: shadow

G645 ἀποσπάω (apospáō): to drag forth, i.e. (literally) unsheathe (a sword), or relatively (with a degree of force implied) retire (personally or factiously). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4685 (σπάω); KJV: (with-)draw (away), after we were gotten from

G646 ἀποστασία (apostasía): defection from truth (properly, the state) ("apostasy"). Origin: feminine of the same as G647 (ἀποστάσιον); KJV: falling away, forsake

G647 ἀποστάσιον (apostásion): properly, something separative, i.e. (specially) divorce. Origin: neuter of a (presumed) adjective from a derivative of G868 (ἀφίστημι); KJV: (writing of) divorcement

G648 ἀποστεγάζω (apostegázō): to unroof. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a derivative of G4721 (στέγη); KJV: uncover

G649 ἀποστέλλω (apostéllō): set apart, i.e. (by implication) to send out (properly, on a mission) literally or figuratively. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: put in, send (away, forth, out), set (at liberty)

G650 ἀποστερέω (aposteréō): to despoil. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to deprive); KJV: defraud, destitute, kept back by fraud

G651 ἀποστολή (apostolḗ): commission, i.e. (specially) apostolate. Origin: from G649 (ἀποστέλλω); KJV: apostleship

G652 ἀπόστολος (apóstolos): a delegate; specially, an ambassador of the Gospel; officially a commissioner of Christ ("apostle") (with miraculous powers). Origin: from G649 (ἀποστέλλω); KJV: apostle, messenger, he that is sent

G653 ἀποστοματίζω (apostomatízō): to speak off-hand (properly, dictate), i.e. to catechize (in an invidious manner). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and a (presumed) derivative of G4750 (στόμα); KJV: provoke to speak

G654 ἀποστρέφω (apostréphō): to turn away or back (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: bring again, pervert, turn away (from)

G655 ἀποστυγέω (apostygéō): to detest utterly. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός); KJV: abhor

G656 ἀποσυνάγωγος (aposynágōgos): excommunicated. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G4864 (συναγωγή); KJV: (put) out of the synagogue(-s)

G657 ἀποτάσσομαι (apotássomai): literally, to say adieu (by departing or dismissing); figuratively, to renounce. Origin: middle voice from G575 (ἀπό) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: bid farewell, forsake, take leave, send away

G658 ἀποτελέω (apoteléō): to complete entirely, i.e. consummate. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5055 (τελέω); KJV: finish

G659 ἀποτίθημι (apotíthēmi): to put away (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: cast off, lay apart (aside, down), put away (off)

G660 ἀποτινάσσω (apotinássō): to brush off. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to jostle); KJV: shake off

G661 ἀποτίνω (apotínō): to pay in full. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5099 (τίνω); KJV: repay

G662 ἀποτολμάω (apotolmáō): to venture plainly. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5111 (τολμάω); KJV: be very bold

G663 ἀποτομία (apotomía): (figuratively) decisiveness, i.e. rigor. Origin: from the base of G664 (ἀποτόμως); KJV: severity

G664 ἀποτόμως (apotómōs): abruptly, i.e. peremptorily. Origin: adverb from a derivative of a comparative of G575 (ἀπό) and (to cut); KJV: sharply(-ness)

G665 ἀποτρέπω (apotrépō): to deflect, i.e. (reflexively) avoid. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: turn away

G666 ἀπουσία (apousía): a being away. Origin: from the participle of G548 (ἄπειμι); KJV: absence

G667 ἀποφέρω (apophérō): to bear off (literally or relatively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bring, carry (away)

G668 ἀποφεύγω (apopheúgō): (figuratively) to escape. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5343 (φεύγω); KJV: escape

G669 ἀποφθέγγομαι (apophthéngomai): to enunciate plainly, i.e. declare. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5350 (φθέγγομαι); KJV: say, speak forth, utterance

G670 ἀποφορτίζομαι (apophortízomai): to unload. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the middle voice of G5412 (φορτίζω); KJV: unlade

G671 ἀπόχρησις (apóchrēsis): the act of using up, i.e. consumption. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G5530 (χράομαι); KJV: using

G672 ἀποχωρέω (apochōréō): to go away. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5562 (χωρέω); KJV: depart

G673 ἀποχωρίζω (apochōrízō): to rend apart; reflexively, to separate. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5563 (χωρίζω); KJV: depart (asunder)

G674 ἀποψύχω (apopsýchō): to breathe out, i.e. faint. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G5594 (ψύχω); KJV: hearts failing

G675 Ἄππιος (Áppios): (in the genitive, i.e. possessive case) of Appius, the name of a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Appii

G676 ἀπρόσιτος (aprósitos): inaccessible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of a comparative of G4314 (πρός) and (to go); KJV: which no man can approach

G677 ἀπρόσκοπος (apróskopos): actively, inoffensive, i.e. not leading into sin; passively, faultless, i.e. not led into sin. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4350 (προσκόπτω); KJV: none (void of, without) offence

G678 ἀπροσωπολήπτως (aprosōpolḗptōs): in a way not accepting the person, i.e. impartially. Origin: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of a presumed compound of G4383 (πρόσωπον) and G2983 (λαμβάνω) (compare G4381 (προσωπολήπτης)); KJV: without respect of persons

G679 ἄπταιστος (áptaistos): not stumbling, i.e. (figuratively) without sin. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4417 (πταίω); KJV: from falling

G680 ἅπτομαι (háptomai): properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations). Origin: reflexive of G681 (ἅπτω); KJV: touch

G681 ἅπτω (háptō): properly, to fasten to, i.e. (specially) to set on fire. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: kindle, light

G682 Ἀπφία (Apphía): Apphia, a woman of Collosæ. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Apphia

G683 ἀπωθέομαι (apōthéomai): to push off, figuratively, to reject. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the middle voice of or (to shove); KJV: cast away, put away (from), thrust away (from)

G684 ἀπώλεια (apṓleia): ruin or loss (physical, spiritual or eternal). Origin: from a presumed derivative of G622 (ἀπόλλυμι); KJV: damnable(-nation), destruction, die, perdition, X perish, pernicious ways, waste

G685 ἀρά (ará): properly, prayer (as lifted to Heaven), i.e. (by implication) imprecation. Origin: probably from G142 (αἴρω); KJV: curse

G686 ἄρα (ára): a particle denoting an inference more or less decisive (as follows). Origin: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of drawing a conclusion); KJV: haply, (what) manner (of man), no doubt, perhaps, so be, then, therefore, truly, wherefore

G687 ἆρα (âra): Origin: a form of G686 (ἄρα), denoting an interrogation to which a negative answer is presumed KJV: therefore

G688 Ἀραβία (Arabía): Arabia, a region of Asia. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6152); KJV: Arabia

G689 Ἀράμ (Arám): Aram (i.e. Ram), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7410); KJV: Aram

G690 Ἄραψ (Áraps): an Arab or native of Arabia. Origin: from G688 (Ἀραβία); KJV: Arabian

G691 ἀργέω (argéō): to be idle, i.e. (figuratively) to delay. Origin: from G692 (ἀργός); KJV: linger

G692 ἀργός (argós): inactive, i.e. unemployed; (by implication) lazy, useless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: barren, idle, slow

G693 ἀργύρεος (argýreos): made of silver. Origin: from G696 (ἄργυρος); KJV: (of) silver

G694 ἀργύριον (argýrion): silvery, i.e. (by implication) cash; specially, a silverling (i.e. drachma or shekel). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G696 (ἄργυρος); KJV: money, (piece of) silver (piece)

G695 ἀργυροκόπος (argyrokópos): a beater (i.e. worker) of silver. Origin: from G696 (ἄργυρος) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: silversmith

G696 ἄργυρος (árgyros): silver (the metal, in the articles or coin). Origin: from (shining); KJV: silver

G697 Ἄρειος Πάγος (Áreios Págos): rock of Ares, a place in Athens. Origin: from (the name of the Greek deity of war) and a derivative of G4078 (πήγνυμι); KJV: Areopagus, Mars' Hill

G698 Ἀρεοπαγίτης (Areopagítēs): an Areopagite or member of the court held on Mars' Hill. Origin: from G697 (Ἄρειος Πάγος); KJV: Areopagite

G699 ἀρεσκεία (areskeía): complaisance. Origin: from a derivative of G700 (ἀρέσκω); KJV: pleasing

G700 ἀρέσκω (aréskō): to be agreeable (or by implication, to seek to be so). Origin: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (through the idea of exciting emotion); KJV: please

G701 ἀρεστός (arestós): agreeable; by implication, fit. Origin: from G700 (ἀρέσκω); KJV: (things that) please(-ing), reason

G702 Ἀρέτας (Arétas): Aretas, an Arabian. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Aretas

G703 ἀρέτη (arétē): properly, manliness (valor), i.e. excellence (intrinsic or attributed). Origin: from the same as G730 (ἄῤῥην); KJV: praise, virtue

G704 ἀρήν (arḗn): a lamb (as a male). Origin: perhaps the same as G730 (ἄῤῥην); KJV: lamb

G705 ἀριθμέω (arithméō): to enumerate or count. Origin: from G706 (ἀριθμός); KJV: number

G706 ἀριθμός (arithmós): a number (as reckoned up). Origin: from G142 (αἴρω); KJV: number

G707 Ἀριμαθαία (Arimathaía): Arimathæa (or Ramah), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7414); KJV: Arimathæa

G708 Ἀρίσταρχος (Arístarchos): best ruling; Aristarchus, a Macedonian. Origin: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: Aristarchus

G709 ἀριστάω (aristáō): to take the principle meal. Origin: from G712 (ἄριστον); KJV: dine

G710 ἀριστερός (aristerós): the left hand (as second-best). Origin: apparently a comparative of the same as G712 (ἄριστον); KJV: left (hand)

G711 Ἀριστόβουλος (Aristóboulos): best counselling; Aristoboulus, a Christian. Origin: from the same as G712 (ἄριστον) and G1012 (βουλή); KJV: Aristobulus

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G712 to G846
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G712 ἄριστον (áriston): the best meal (or breakfast; perhaps from ("early")), i.e. luncheon. Origin: apparently neuter of a superlative from the same as G730 (ἄῤῥην); KJV: dinner

G713 ἀρκετός (arketós): satisfactory. Origin: from G714 (ἀρκέω); KJV: enough, suffice (-ient)

G714 ἀρκέω (arkéō): properly, to ward off, i.e. (by implication) to avail (figuratively, be satisfactory). Origin: apparently a primary verb (but probably akin to G142 (αἴρω) through the idea of raising a barrier); KJV: be content, be enough, suffice, be sufficient

G715 ἄρκτος (árktos): a bear (as obstructing by ferocity). Origin: probably from G714 (ἀρκέω); KJV: bear

G716 ἅρμα (hárma): a chariot (as raised or fitted together (compare G719 (ἁρμός))). Origin: probably from G142 (αἴρω) (perhaps with G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) prefixed); KJV: chariot

G717 Ἀρμαγεδδών (Armageddṓn): Armageddon (or Har-Meggiddon), a symbolic name. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2022 and H4023); KJV: Armageddon

G718 ἁρμόζω (harmózō): to joint, i.e. (figuratively) to woo (reflexively, to betroth). Origin: from G719 (ἁρμός); KJV: espouse

G719 ἁρμός (harmós): an articulation (of the body). Origin: from the same as G716 (ἅρμα); KJV: joint

G720 ἀρνέομαι (arnéomai): to contradict, i.e. disavow, reject, abnegate. Origin: perhaps from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the middle voice of G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: deny, refuse

G721 ἀρνίον (arníon): a lambkin. Origin: diminutive from G704 (ἀρήν); KJV: lamb

G722 ἀροτριόω (arotrióō): to plow. Origin: from G723 (ἄροτρον); KJV: plough

G723 ἄροτρον (árotron): a plow. Origin: from (to till); KJV: plough

G724 ἁρπαγή (harpagḗ): pillage (properly abstract). Origin: from G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: extortion, ravening, spoiling

G725 ἁρπαγμός (harpagmós): plunder (properly concrete). Origin: from G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: robbery

G726 ἁρπάζω (harpázō): to seize (in various applications). Origin: from a derivative of G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: catch (away, up), pluck, pull, take (by force)

G727 ἅρπαξ (hárpax): rapacious. Origin: from G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: extortion, ravening

G728 ἀῤῥαβών (arrhabṓn): a pledge, i.e. part of the purchase-money or property given in advance as security for the rest. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6162); KJV: earnest

G729 ἄῤῥαφος (árrhaphos): unsewed, i.e. of a single piece. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of the same as G4476 (ῥαφίς); KJV: without seam

G730 ἄῤῥην (árrhēn): male (as stronger for lifting). Origin: probably from G142 (αἴρω); KJV: male, man

G731 ἄῤῥητος (árrhētos): unsaid, i.e. (by implication) inexpressible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the same as G4490 (ῥητῶς); KJV: unspeakable

G732 ἄῤῥωστος (árrhōstos): infirm. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4517 (ῥώννυμι); KJV: sick (folk, -ly)

G733 ἀρσενοκοίτης (arsenokoítēs): a sodomite. Origin: from G730 (ἄῤῥην) and G2845 (κοίτη); KJV: abuser of (that defile) self with mankind

G734 Ἀρτεμάς (Artemás): gift of Artemis; Artemas (or Artemidorus), a Christian. Origin: contracted from a compound of G735 (Ἄρτεμις) and G1435 (δῶρον); KJV: Artemas

G735 Ἄρτεμις (Ártemis): prompt; Artemis, the name of a Grecian goddess borrowed by the Asiatics for one of their deities. Origin: probably from the same as G736 (ἀρτέμων); KJV: Diana

G736 ἀρτέμων (artémōn): properly, something ready (or else more remotely from G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)); something hung up), i.e. (specially) the topsail (rather foresail or jib) of a vessel. Origin: from a derivative of G737 (ἄρτι); KJV: mainsail

G737 ἄρτι (árti): just now. Origin: adverb from a derivative of G142 (αἴρω) (compare G740 (ἄρτος)) through the idea of suspension; KJV: this day (hour), hence(-forth), here(-after), hither(-to), (even) now, (this) present

G738 ἀρτιγέννητος (artigénnētos): just born, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert. Origin: from G737 (ἄρτι) and G1084 (γεννητός); KJV: new born

G739 ἄρτιος (ártios): fresh, i.e. (by implication) complete. Origin: from G737 (ἄρτι); KJV: perfect

G740 ἄρτος (ártos): bread (as raised) or a loaf. Origin: from G142 (αἴρω); KJV: (shew-)bread, loaf

G741 ἀρτύω (artýō): to prepare, i.e. spice (with stimulating condiments). Origin: from a presumed derivative of G142 (αἴρω); KJV: season

G742 Ἀρφαξάδ (Arphaxád): Arphaxad, a post-diluvian patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H775); KJV: Arphaxad

G743 ἀρχάγγελος (archángelos): a chief angel. Origin: from G757 (ἄρχω) and G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: archangel

G744 ἀρχαῖος (archaîos): original or primeval. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή); KJV: (them of) old (time)

G745 Ἀρχέλαος (Archélaos): people-ruling; Archelaus, a Jewish king. Origin: from G757 (ἄρχω) and G2994 (Λαοδικεύς); KJV: Archelaus

G746 ἀρχή (archḗ): (properly abstract) a commencement, or (concretely) chief (in various applications of order, time, place, or rank). Origin: from G756 (ἄρχομαι); KJV: beginning, corner, (at the, the) first (estate), magistrate, power, principality, principle, rule

G747 ἀρχηγός (archēgós): a chief leader. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: author, captain, prince

G748 ἀρχιερατικός (archieratikós): high-priestly. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a derivative of G2413 (ἱερός); KJV: of the high-priest

G749 ἀρχιερεύς (archiereús): the high-priest (literally, of the Jews, typically, Christ); by extension a chief priest. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G2409 (ἱερεύς); KJV: chief (high) priest, chief of the priests

G750 ἀρχιποίμην (archipoímēn): a head shepherd. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G4166 (ποιμήν); KJV: chief shepherd

G751 Ἄρχιππος (Árchippos): horse-ruler; Archippus, a Christian. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G2462 (ἵππος); KJV: Archippus

G752 ἀρχισυνάγωγος (archisynágōgos): director of the synagogue services. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G4864 (συναγωγή); KJV: (chief) ruler of the synagogue

G753 ἀρχιτέκτων (architéktōn): a chief constructor, i.e. "architect". Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G5045 (τέκτων); KJV: masterbuilder

G754 ἀρχιτελώνης (architelṓnēs): a principle tax-gatherer. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and G5057 (τελώνης); KJV: chief among the publicans

G755 ἀρχιτρίκλινος (architríklinos): director of the entertainment. Origin: from G746 (ἀρχή) and a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G2827 (κλίνω) (a dinner-bed, because composed of three couches); KJV: governor (ruler) of the feast

G756 ἄρχομαι (árchomai): to commence (in order of time). Origin: middle voice of G757 (ἄρχω) (through the implication, of precedence); KJV: (rehearse from the) begin(-ning)

G757 ἄρχω (árchō): to be first (in political rank or power). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: reign (rule) over

G758 ἄρχων (árchōn): a first (in rank or power). Origin: present participle of G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: chief (ruler), magistrate, prince, ruler

G759 ἄρωμα (árōma): an aromatic. Origin: from G142 (αἴρω) (in the sense of sending off scent); KJV: (sweet) spice

G760 Ἀσά (Asá): Asa, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H609); KJV: Asa

G761 ἀσάλευτος (asáleutos): unshaken, i.e. (by implication) immovable (figuratively). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4531 (σαλεύω); KJV: which cannot be moved, unmovable

G762 ἄσβεστος (ásbestos): not extinguished, i.e. (by implication) perpetual. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4570 (σβέννυμι); KJV: not to be quenched, unquenchable

G763 ἀσέβεια (asébeia): impiety, i.e. (by implication) wickedness. Origin: from G765 (ἀσεβής); KJV: ungodly(-liness)

G764 ἀσεβέω (asebéō): to be (by implied act) impious or wicked. Origin: from G765 (ἀσεβής); KJV: commit (live, that after should live) ungodly

G765 ἀσεβής (asebḗs): irreverent, i.e. (by extension) impious or wicked. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι); KJV: ungodly (man)

G766 ἀσέλγεια (asélgeia): licentiousness (sometimes including other vices). Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed (of uncertain derivation, but apparently meaning continent); KJV: filthy, lasciviousness, wantonness

G767 ἄσημος (ásēmos): unmarked, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω); KJV: mean

G768 Ἀσήρ (Asḗr): Aser (i.e. Asher), an Israelite tribe. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H836); KJV: Aser

G769 ἀσθένεια (asthéneia): feebleness (of mind or body); by implication, malady; morally, frailty. Origin: from G772 (ἀσθενής); KJV: disease, infirmity, sickness, weakness

G770 ἀσθενέω (asthenéō): to be feeble (in any sense). Origin: from G772 (ἀσθενής); KJV: be diseased, impotent folk (man), (be) sick, (be, be made) weak

G771 ἀσθένημα (asthénēma): a scruple of conscience. Origin: from G770 (ἀσθενέω); KJV: infirmity

G772 ἀσθενής (asthenḗs): strengthless (in various applications, literal, figurative and moral). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G4599 (σθενόω); KJV: more feeble, impotent, sick, without strength, weak(-er, -ness, thing)

G773 Ἀσία (Asía): Asia, i.e. Asia Minor, or (usually) only its western shore. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Asia

G774 Ἀσιανός (Asianós): an Asian (i.e. Asiatic) or an inhabitant of Asia. Origin: from G773 (Ἀσία); KJV: of Asia

G775 Ἀσιάρχης (Asiárchēs): an Asiarch or president of the public festivities in a city of Asia Minor. Origin: from G773 (Ἀσία) and G746 (ἀρχή); KJV: chief of Asia

G776 ἀσιτία (asitía): fasting (the state). Origin: from G777 (ἄσιτος); KJV: abstinence

G777 ἄσιτος (ásitos): without (taking) food. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4621 (σῖτος); KJV: fasting

G778 ἀσκέω (askéō): to elaborate, i.e. (figuratively) train (by implication, strive). Origin: probably from the same as G4632 (σκεῦος); KJV: exercise

G779 ἀσκός (askós): a leathern (or skin) bag used as a bottle. Origin: from the same as G778 (ἀσκέω); KJV: bottle

G780 ἀσμένως (asménōs): with pleasure. Origin: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237 (ἡδονή); KJV: gladly

G781 ἄσοφος (ásophos): unwise. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4680 (σοφός); KJV: fool

G782 ἀσπάζομαι (aspázomai): to enfold in the arms, i.e. (by implication) to salute, (figuratively) to welcome. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and a presumed form of G4685 (σπάω); KJV: embrace, greet, salute, take leave

G783 ἀσπασμός (aspasmós): a greeting (in person or by letter). Origin: from G782 (ἀσπάζομαι); KJV: greeting, salutation

G784 ἄσπιλος (áspilos): unblemished (physically or morally). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4695 (σπιλόω); KJV: without spot, unspotted

G785 ἀσπίς (aspís): a buckler (or round shield); used of a serpent (as coiling itself), probably the "asp". Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: asp

G786 ἄσπονδος (áspondos): literally, without libation (which usually accompanied a treaty), i.e. (by implication) truceless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4689 (σπένδω); KJV: implacable, truce-breaker

G787 ἀσσάριον (assárion): an assarius or as, a Roman coin. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: farthing

G788 ἆσσον (âsson): more nearly, i.e. very near. Origin: neuter comparative of the base of G1451 (ἐγγύς); KJV: close

G789 Ἄσσος (Ássos): Assus, a city of Asia MInor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Assos

G790 ἀστατέω (astatéō): to be non-stationary, i.e. (figuratively) homeless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: have no certain dwelling-place

G791 ἀστεῖος (asteîos): urbane, i.e. (by implication) handsome. Origin: from (a city); KJV: fair

G792 ἀστήρ (astḗr): a star (as strown over the sky), literally or figuratively. Origin: probably from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι); KJV: star

G793 ἀστήρικτος (astḗriktos): unfixed, i.e. (figuratively) vacillating. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4741 (στηρίζω); KJV: unstable

G794 ἄστοργος (ástorgos): hard-hearted towards kindred. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of (to cherish affectionately); KJV: without natural affection

G795 ἀστοχέω (astochéō): to miss the mark, i.e. (figuratively) deviate from truth. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (an aim); KJV: err, swerve

G796 ἀστραπή (astrapḗ): lightning; by analogy, glare. Origin: from G797 (ἀστράπτω); KJV: lightning, bright shining

G797 ἀστράπτω (astráptō): to flash as lightning. Origin: probably from G792 (ἀστήρ); KJV: lighten, shine

G798 ἄστρον (ástron): properly, a constellation; put for a single star (natural or artificial). Origin: neuter from G792 (ἀστήρ); KJV: star

G799 Ἀσύγκριτος (Asýnkritos): incomparable; Asyncritus, a Christian. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4793 (συγκρίνω); KJV: Asyncritos

G800 ἀσύμφωνος (asýmphōnos): inharmonious (figuratively). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4859 (σύμφωνος); KJV: agree not

G801 ἀσύνετος (asýnetos): unintelligent; by implication, wicked. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G4908 (συνετός); KJV: foolish, without understanding

G802 ἀσύνθετος (asýnthetos): properly, not agreed, i.e. treacherous to compacts. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G4934 (συντίθεμαι); KJV: covenant-breaker

G803 ἀσφάλεια (aspháleia): security (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G804 (ἀσφαλής); KJV: certainty, safety

G804 ἀσφαλής (asphalḗs): secure (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and sphallo (to "fail"); KJV: certain(-ty), safe, sure

G805 ἀσφαλίζω (asphalízō): to render secure. Origin: from G804 (ἀσφαλής); KJV: make fast (sure)

G806 ἀσφαλῶς (asphalōs): securely (literally or figuratively). Origin: adverb from G804 (ἀσφαλής); KJV: assuredly, safely

G807 ἀσχημονέω (aschēmonéō): to be (i.e. act) unbecoming. Origin: from G809 (ἀσχήμων); KJV: behave self uncomely (unseemly)

G808 ἀσχημοσύνη (aschēmosýnē): an indecency; by implication, the pudenda. Origin: from G809 (ἀσχήμων); KJV: shame, that which is unseemly

G809 ἀσχήμων (aschḗmōn): properly, shapeless, i.e. (figuratively) inelegant. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of its congener G4976 (σχῆμα)); KJV: uncomely

G810 ἀσωτία (asōtía): properly, unsavedness, i.e. (by implication) profligacy. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G4982 (σώζω); KJV: excess, riot

G811 ἀσώτως (asṓtōs): dissolutely. Origin: adverb from the same as G810 (ἀσωτία); KJV: riotous

G812 ἀτακτέω (ataktéō): to be (i.e. act) irregular. Origin: from G813 (ἄτακτος); KJV: behave self disorderly

G813 ἄτακτος (átaktos): unarranged, i.e. (by implication) insubordinate (religiously). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: unruly

G814 ἀτάκτως (atáktōs): Origin: adverb from G813 (ἄτακτος), irregularly (morally) KJV: disorderly

G815 ἄτεκνος (áteknos): childless. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5043 (τέκνον); KJV: childless, without children

G816 ἀτενίζω (atenízō): to gaze intently. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a particle of union) and (to stretch); KJV: behold earnestly (stedfastly), fasten (eyes), look (earnestly, stedfastly, up stedfastly), set eyes

G817 ἄτερ (áter): aloof, i.e. apart from (literally or figuratively). Origin: a particle probably akin to G427 (ἄνευ); KJV: in the absence of, without

G818 ἀτιμάζω (atimázō): to render infamous, i.e. (by implication) contemn or maltreat. Origin: from G820 (ἄτιμος); KJV: despise, dishonour, suffer shame, entreat shamefully

G819 ἀτιμία (atimía): infamy, i.e. (subjectively) comparative indignity, (objectively) disgrace. Origin: from G820 (ἄτιμος); KJV: dishonour, reproach, shame, vile

G820 ἄτιμος (átimos): (negatively) unhonoured or (positively) dishonoured. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: despised, without honour, less honourable (comparative degree)

G821 ἀτιμόω (atimóō): used like G818 (ἀτιμάζω), to maltreat. Origin: from G820 (ἄτιμος); KJV: handle shamefully

G822 ἀτμίς (atmís): mist. Origin: from the same as G109 (ἀήρ); KJV: vapour

G823 ἄτομος (átomos): uncut, i.e. (by implication) indivisible (an "atom" of time). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος); KJV: moment

G824 ἄτοπος (átopos): out of place, i.e. (figuratively) improper, injurious, wicked. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5117 (τόπος); KJV: amiss, harm, unreasonable

G825 Ἀττάλεια (Attáleia): Attaleia, a place in Pamphylia. Origin: from (a king of Pergamus); KJV: Attalia

G826 αὐγάζω (augázō): to beam forth (figuratively). Origin: from G827 (αὐγή); KJV: shine

G827 αὐγή (augḗ): a ray of light, i.e. (by implication) radiance, dawn. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: break of day

G828 Αὐγοῦστος (Augoûstos): Augustus, a title of the Roman emperor. Origin: from Latin ("august"); KJV: Augustus

G829 αὐθάδης (authádēs): self-pleasing, i.e. arrogant. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and the base of G2237 (ἡδονή); KJV: self-willed

G830 αὐθαίρετος (authaíretos): self-chosen, i.e. (by implication) voluntary. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G140 (αἱρετίζω); KJV: of own accord, willing of self

G831 αὐθεντέω (authentéō): to act of oneself, i.e. (figuratively) dominate. Origin: from a compound of G846 (αὐτός) and an obsolete (a worker); KJV: usurp authority over

G832 αὐλέω (auléō): to play the flute. Origin: from G836 (αὐλός); KJV: pipe

G833 αὐλή (aulḗ): a yard (as open to the wind); by implication, a mansion. Origin: from the same as G109 (ἀήρ); KJV: court, (sheep-)fold, hall, palace

G834 αὐλητής (aulētḗs): a flute-player. Origin: from G832 (αὐλέω); KJV: minstrel, piper

G835 αὐλίζομαι (aulízomai): to pass the night (properly, in the open air). Origin: middle voice from G833 (αὐλή); KJV: abide, lodge

G836 αὐλός (aulós): a flute (as blown). Origin: from the same as G109 (ἀήρ); KJV: pipe

G837 αὐξάνω (auxánō): to grow ("wax"), i.e. enlarge (literal or figurative, active or passive). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb; KJV: grow (up), (give the) increase

G838 αὔξησις (aúxēsis): growth. Origin: from G837 (αὐξάνω); KJV: increase

G839 αὔριον (aúrion): properly, fresh, i.e. (adverb with ellipsis of G2250 (ἡμέρα)) to-morrow. Origin: from a derivative of the same as G109 (ἀήρ) (meaning a breeze, i.e. the morning air); KJV: (to-)morrow, next day

G840 αὐστηρός (austērós): rough (properly as a gale), i.e. (figuratively) severe. Origin: from a (presumed) derivative of the same as G109 (ἀήρ) (meaning blown); KJV: austere

G841 αὐτάρκεια (autárkeia): self-satisfaction, i.e. (abstractly) contentedness, or (concretely) a competence. Origin: from G842 (αὐτάρκης); KJV: contentment, sufficiency

G842 αὐτάρκης (autárkēs): self-complacent, i.e. contented. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and G714 (ἀρκέω); KJV: content

G843 αὐτοκατάκριτος (autokatákritos): self-condemned. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and a derivative or G2632 (κατακρίνω); KJV: condemned of self

G844 αὐτόματος (autómatos): self-moved ("automatic"), i.e. spontaneous. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and the same as G3155 (μάτην); KJV: of own accord, of self

G845 αὐτόπτης (autóptēs): self-seeing, i.e. an eye-witness. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: eye-witness

G846 αὐτός (autós): the reflexive pronoun self, used (alone or in the comparative G1438 (ἑαυτοῦ)) of the third person , and (with the proper personal pronoun) of the other persons. Origin: from the particle (perhaps akin to the base of G109 (ἀήρ) through the idea of a baffling wind) (backward); KJV: her, it(-self), one, the other, (mine) own, said, (self-), the) same, ((him-, my-, thy- )self, (your-)selves, she, that, their(-s), them(-selves), there(-at, - by, -in, -into, -of, -on, -with), they, (these) things, this (man), those, together, very, which

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G847 to G990
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G847 αὐτοῦ (autoû): properly, belonging to the same spot, i.e. in this (or that) place. Origin: genitive (i.e. possessive) of G846 (αὐτός), used as an adverb of location; KJV: (t-)here

G848 αὑτοῦ (hautoû): self (in some oblique case or reflexively, relation). Origin: contracted for G1438 (ἑαυτοῦ); KJV: her (own), (of) him(-self), his (own), of it, thee, their (own), them(-selves), they

G849 αὐτόχειρ (autócheir): self-handed, i.e. doing personally. Origin: from G846 (αὐτός) and G5495 (χείρ); KJV: with … own hands

G850 αὐχμηρός (auchmērós): properly, dirty, i.e. (by implication) obscure. Origin: from (probably from a base akin to that of G109 (ἀήρ)) (dust, as dried by wind); KJV: dark

G851 ἀφαιρέω (aphairéō): to remove (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: cut (smite) off, take away

G852 ἀφανής (aphanḗs): non-apparent). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: that is not manifest

G853 ἀφανίζω (aphanízō): to render unapparent, i.e. (actively) consume (becloud), or (passively) disappear (be destroyed). Origin: from G852 (ἀφανής); KJV: corrupt, disfigure, perish, vanish away

G854 ἀφανισμός (aphanismós): disappearance, i.e. (figuratively) abrogation. Origin: from G853 (ἀφανίζω); KJV: vanish away

G855 ἄφαντος (áphantos): non-manifested, i.e. invisible. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: vanished out of sight

G856 ἀφεδρών (aphedrṓn): a place of sitting apart, i.e. a privy. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: draught

G857 ἀφειδία (apheidía): unsparingness, i.e. austerity (asceticism). Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5339 (φείδομαι); KJV: neglecting

G858 ἀφελότης (aphelótēs): smoothness, i.e. (figuratively) simplicity. Origin: from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and (in the sense of a stone as stubbing the foot); KJV: singleness

G859 ἄφεσις (áphesis): freedom; (figuratively) pardon. Origin: from G863 (ἀφίημι); KJV: deliverance, forgiveness, liberty, remission

G860 ἁφή (haphḗ): probably a ligament (as fastening). Origin: from G680 (ἅπτομαι); KJV: joint

G861 ἀφθαρσία (aphtharsía): incorruptibility; genitive, unending existence; (figuratively) genuineness. Origin: from G862 (ἄφθαρτος); KJV: immortality, incorruption, sincerity

G862 ἄφθαρτος (áphthartos): undecaying (in essence or continuance). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5351 (φθείρω); KJV: not (in-, un-)corruptible, immortal

G863 ἀφίημι (aphíēmi): an intensive form of , to go); to send forth, in various applications (as follow). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and (to send; KJV: cry, forgive, forsake, lay aside, leave, let (alone, be, go, have), omit, put (send) away, remit, suffer, yield up

G864 ἀφικνέομαι (aphiknéomai): to go (i.e. spread) forth (by rumor). Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and the base of G2425 (ἱκανός); KJV: come abroad

G865 ἀφιλάγαθος (aphilágathos): hostile to virtue. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5358 (φιλάγαθος); KJV: despiser of those that are good

G866 ἀφιλάργυρος (aphilárgyros): unavaricious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5366 (φιλάργυρος); KJV: without covetousness, not greedy of filthy lucre

G867 ἄφιξις (áphixis): properly, arrival, i.e. (by implication) departure. Origin: from G864 (ἀφικνέομαι); KJV: departing

G868 ἀφίστημι (aphístēmi): to remove, i.e. (actively) instigate to revolt; usually (reflexively) to desist, desert, etc. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: depart, draw (fall) away, refrain, withdraw self

G869 ἄφνω (áphnō): unawares, i.e. unexpectedly. Origin: adverb from G852 (ἀφανής) (contraction); KJV: suddenly

G870 ἀφόβως (aphóbōs): fearlessly. Origin: adverb from a compound of G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5401 (φόβος); KJV: without fear

G871 ἀφομοιόω (aphomoióō): to assimilate closely. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3666 (ὁμοιόω); KJV: make like

G872 ἀφοράω (aphoráō): to consider attentively. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: look

G873 ἀφορίζω (aphorízō): to set off by boundary, i.e. (figuratively) limit, exclude, appoint, etc. Origin: from G575 (ἀπό) and G3724 (ὁρίζω); KJV: divide, separate, sever

G874 ἀφορμή (aphormḗ): a starting-point, i.e. (figuratively) an opportunity. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G3729 (ὁρμάω); KJV: occasion

G875 ἀφρίζω (aphrízō): to froth at the mouth (in epilepsy). Origin: from G876 (ἀφρός); KJV: foam

G876 ἀφρός (aphrós): froth, i.e. slaver. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: foaming

G877 ἀφροσύνη (aphrosýnē): senselessness, i.e. (euphemistically) egotism; (morally) recklessness. Origin: from G878 (ἄφρων); KJV: folly, foolishly(-ness)

G878 ἄφρων (áphrōn): properly, mindless, i.e. stupid, (by implication) ignorant, (specially) egotistic, (practically) rash, or (morally) unbelieving. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5424 (φρήν); KJV: fool(-ish), unwise

G879 ἀφυπνόω (aphypnóō): properly, to become awake, i.e. (by implication) to drop (off) in slumber. Origin: from a compound of G575 (ἀπό) and G5258 (ὕπνος); KJV: fall asleep

G880 ἄφωνος (áphōnos): voiceless, i.e. mute (by nature or choice); figuratively, unmeaning. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5456 (φωνή); KJV: dumb, without signification

G881 Ἀχάζ (Acház): Achaz, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H271); KJV: Achaz

G882 Ἀχαΐα (Achaḯa): Achaia (i.e. Greece), a country of Europe. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Achaia

G883 Ἀχαϊκός (Achaïkós): an Achaian; Achaicus, a Christian. Origin: from G882 (Ἀχαΐα); KJV: Achaicus

G884 ἀχάριστος (acháristos): thankless, i.e. ungrateful. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a presumed derivative of G5483 (χαρίζομαι); KJV: unthankful

G885 Ἀχείμ (Acheím): Achim, an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H3137); KJV: Achim

G886 ἀχειροποίητος (acheiropoíētos): unmanufactured, i.e. inartificial. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5499 (χειροποίητος); KJV: made without (not made with) hands

G887 ἀχλύς (achlýs): dimness of sight, i.e. (probably) a cataract. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: mist

G888 ἀχρεῖος (achreîos): useless, i.e. (euphemistically) unmeritorious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and a derivative of G5534 (χρή) (compare G5532 (χρεία)); KJV: unprofitable

G889 ἀχρειόω (achreióō): to render useless, i.e. spoil. Origin: from G888 (ἀχρεῖος); KJV: become unprofitable

G890 ἄχρηστος (áchrēstos): inefficient, i.e. (by implication) detrimental. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5543 (χρηστός); KJV: unprofitable

G891 ἄχρι (áchri): (of time) until or (of place) up to. Origin: akin to G206 (ἄκρον) (through the idea of a terminus); KJV: as far as, for, in(-to), till, (even, un-)to, until, while

G892 ἄχυρον (áchyron): chaff (as diffusive). Origin: perhaps remotely from (to shed forth); KJV: chaff

G893 ἀψευδής (apseudḗs): veracious. Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5579 (ψεῦδος); KJV: that cannot lie

G894 ἄψινθος (ápsinthos): wormwood (as a type of bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: wormwood

G895 ἄψυχος (ápsychos): lifeless, i.e. inanimate (mechanical). Origin: from G1 (Α) (as a negative particle) and G5590 (ψυχή); KJV: without life

G896 Βάαλ (Báal): Baal, a Phœnician deity (used as a symbol of idolatry). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1168); KJV: Baal

G897 Βαβυλών (Babylṓn): Babylon, the capitol of Chaldæa (literally or figuratively (as a type of tyranny)). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H894); KJV: Babylon

G898 βαθμός (bathmós): a step, i.e. (figuratively) grade (of dignity). Origin: from the same as G899 (βάθος); KJV: degree

G899 βάθος (báthos): profundity, i.e. (by implication) extent; (figuratively) mystery. Origin: from the same as G901 (βαθύς); KJV: deep(-ness, things), depth

G900 βαθύνω (bathýnō): to deepen. Origin: from G901 (βαθύς); KJV: deep

G901 βαθύς (bathýs): profound (as going down), literally or figuratively. Origin: from the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: deep, very early

G902 βαΐον (baḯon): a palm twig (as going out far). Origin: a diminutive of a derivative probably of the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: branch

G903 Βαλαάμ (Balaám): Balaam, a Mesopotamian (symbolic of a false teacher). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1109); KJV: Balaam

G904 Βαλάκ (Balák): Balak, a Moabite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1111); KJV: Balac

G905 βαλάντιον (balántion): a pouch (for money). Origin: probably remotely from G906 (βάλλω) (as a depository); KJV: bag, purse

G906 βάλλω (bállō): to throw (in various applications, more or less violent or intense). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: arise, cast (out), X dung, lay, lie, pour, put (up), send, strike, throw (down), thrust

G907 βαπτίζω (baptízō): to immerse, submerge; to make whelmed (i.e. fully wet); used only (in the New Testament) of ceremonial ablution, especially (technically) of the ordinance of Christian baptism. Origin: from a derivative of G911 (βάπτω); KJV: Baptist, baptize, wash

G908 βάπτισμα (báptisma): baptism (technically or figuratively). Origin: from G907 (βαπτίζω); KJV: baptism

G909 βαπτισμός (baptismós): ablution (ceremonial or Christian). Origin: from G907 (βαπτίζω); KJV: baptism, washing

G910 Βαπτιστής (Baptistḗs): a baptizer, as an epithet of Christ's forerunner. Origin: from G907 (βαπτίζω); KJV: Baptist

G911 βάπτω (báptō): to whelm, i.e. cover wholly with a fluid; in the New Testament only in a qualified or special sense, i.e. (literally) to moisten (a part of one's person), or (by implication) to stain (as with dye). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: dip

G912 Βαραββᾶς (Barabbâs): son of Abba; Bar-abbas, an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1347 and H5); KJV: Barabbas

G913 Βαράκ (Barák): Barak, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1301); KJV: Barak

G914 Βαραχίας (Barachías): Barachias (i.e. Berechijah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1296); KJV: Barachias

G915 βάρβαρος (bárbaros): a foreigner (i.e. non-Greek). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: barbarian(-rous)

G916 βαρέω (baréō): to weigh down (figuratively). Origin: from G926 (βαρύς); KJV: burden, charge, heavy, press

G917 βαρέως (baréōs): heavily (figuratively). Origin: adverb from G926 (βαρύς); KJV: dull

G918 Βαρθολομαῖος (Bartholomaîos): son of Tolmai; Bar-tholomæus, a Christian apostle. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H8526); KJV: Bartholomeus

G919 Βαριησοῦς (Bariēsoûs): son of Jesus (or Joshua); Bar-jesus, an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H3091); KJV: Barjesus

G920 Βαριωνᾶς (Bariōnâs): son of Jonas (or Jonah); Bar-jonas, an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H3124); KJV: Bar-jona

G921 Βαρνάβας (Barnábas): son of Nabas (i.e. prophecy); Barnabas, an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H5029); KJV: Barnabas

G922 βάρος (báros): compare G899 (βάθος)); weight; in the New Testament only, figuratively, a load, abundance, authority. Origin: probably from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going down; KJV: burden(-some), weight

G923 Βαρσαβᾶς (Barsabâs): son of Sabas (or Tsaba); Bar-sabas, the name of two Israelites. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and probably H6634); KJV: Barsabas

G924 Βαρτιμαῖος (Bartimaîos): son of Timæus (or the unclean); Bar-timæus, an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1247 and H2931); KJV: Bartimæus

G925 βαρύνω (barýnō): to burden (figuratively). Origin: from G926 (βαρύς); KJV: overcharge

G926 βαρύς (barýs): weighty, i.e. (fig) burdensome, grave. Origin: from the same as G922 (βάρος); KJV: grievous, heavy, weightier

G927 βαρύτιμος (barýtimos): highly valuable. Origin: from G926 (βαρύς) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: very precious

G928 βασανίζω (basanízō): to torture. Origin: from G931 (βάσανος); KJV: pain, toil, torment, toss, vex

G929 βασανισμός (basanismós): torture. Origin: from G928 (βασανίζω); KJV: torment

G930 βασανιστής (basanistḗs): a torturer. Origin: from G928 (βασανίζω); KJV: tormentor

G931 βάσανος (básanos): a touch-stone, i.e. (by analogy) torture. Origin: perhaps remotely from the same as G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of going to the bottom); KJV: torment

G932 βασιλεία (basileía): properly, royalty, i.e. (abstractly) rule, or (concretely) a realm (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G935 (βασιλεύς); KJV: kingdom, + reign

G933 βασίλειον (basíleion): a palace. Origin: neuter of G934 (βασίλειος); KJV: king's court

G934 βασίλειος (basíleios): kingly (in nature). Origin: from G935 (βασιλεύς); KJV: royal

G935 βασιλεύς (basileús): a sovereign (abstractly, relatively, or figuratively). Origin: probably from G939 (βάσις) (through the notion of a foundation of power); KJV: king

G936 βασιλεύω (basileúō): to rule (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G935 (βασιλεύς); KJV: king, reign

G937 βασιλικός (basilikós): regal (in relation), i.e. (literally) belonging to (or befitting) the sovereign (as land, dress, or a courtier), or (figuratively) preeminent. Origin: from G935 (βασιλεύς); KJV: king's, nobleman, royal

G938 βασίλισσα (basílissa): a queen. Origin: feminine from G936 (βασιλεύω); KJV: queen

G939 βάσις (básis): a pace ("base"), i.e. (by implication) the foot. Origin: from (to walk); KJV: foot

G940 βασκαίνω (baskaínō): to malign, i.e. (by extension) to fascinate (by false representations). Origin: akin to G5335 (φάσκω); KJV: bewitch

G941 βαστάζω (bastázō): to lift, literally or figuratively (endure, declare, sustain, receive, etc.). Origin: perhaps remotely derived from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of removal); KJV: bear, carry, take up

G942 βάτος (bátos): a brier shrub. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: bramble, bush

G943 βάτος (bátos): a bath, or measure for liquids. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1324); KJV: measure

G944 βάτραχος (bátrachos): a frog. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: frog

G945 βαττολογέω (battologéō): to stutter, i.e. (by implication) to prate tediously. Origin: from (a proverbial stammerer) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: use vain repetitions

G946 βδέλυγμα (bdélygma): a detestation, i.e. (specially) idolatry. Origin: from G948 (βδελύσσω); KJV: abomination

G947 βδελυκτός (bdelyktós): detestable, i.e. (specially) idolatrous. Origin: from G948 (βδελύσσω); KJV: abominable

G948 βδελύσσω (bdelýssō): to be disgusted, i.e. (by implication) detest (especially of idolatry). Origin: from a (presumed) derivative of (to stink); KJV: abhor, abominable

G949 βέβαιος (bébaios): stable (literally or figuratively). Origin: from the base of G939 (βάσις) (through the idea of basality); KJV: firm, of force, stedfast, sure

G950 βεβαιόω (bebaióō): to stabilitate (figuratively). Origin: from G949 (βέβαιος); KJV: confirm, (e-)stablish

G951 βεβαίωσις (bebaíōsis): stabiliment. Origin: from G950 (βεβαιόω); KJV: confirmation

G952 βέβηλος (bébēlos): accessible (as by crossing the door-way), i.e. (by implication, of Jewish notions) heathenish, wicked. Origin: from the base of G939 (βάσις) and (a threshold); KJV: profane (person)

G953 βεβηλόω (bebēlóō): to desecrate. Origin: from G952 (βέβηλος); KJV: profane

G954 Βεελζεβούλ (Beelzeboúl): dung-god; Beelzebul, a name of Satan. Origin: of Chaldee origin (by parody on H1176); KJV: Beelzebub

G955 Βελίαλ (Belíal): worthlessness; Belial, as an epithet of Satan. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1100); KJV: Belial

G956 βέλος (bélos): a missile, i.e. spear or arrow. Origin: from G906 (βάλλω); KJV: dart

G957 βελτίον (beltíon): better. Origin: neuter of a compound of a derivative of G906 (βάλλω) (used for the comparative of G18 (ἀγαθός)); KJV: very well

G958 Βενιαμίν (Beniamín): Benjamin, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1144); KJV: Benjamin

G959 Βερνίκη (Berníkē): victorious; Bernice, a member of the Herodian family. Origin: from a provincial form of G5342 (φέρω) and G3529 (νίκη); KJV: Bernice

G960 Βέροια (Béroia): Berœa, a place in Macedonia. Origin: perhaps a provincial from a derivative of G4008 (πέραν) (Perœa, i.e. the region beyond the coast-line); KJV: Berea

G961 Βεροιαῖος (Beroiaîos): a Berœoean or native of Berœa. Origin: from G960 (Βέροια); KJV: of Berea

G962 Βηθαβαρά (Bēthabará): ferry-house; Bethabara (i.e. Bethabarah), a place on the Jordan. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1004 and H5679); KJV: Bethabara

G963 Βηθανία (Bēthanía): date-house; Beth-any, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Chaldee origin; KJV: Bethany

G964 Βηθεσδά (Bēthesdá): house of kindness; Beth-esda, a pool in Jerusalem. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H1004 and H2617); KJV: Bethesda

G965 Βηθλεέμ (Bēthleém): Bethleem (i.e. Beth-lechem), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1036); KJV: Bethlehem

G966 Βηθσαϊδά (Bēthsaïdá): fishing-house; Bethsaida, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H1004 and H6719); KJV: Bethsaida

G967 Βηθφαγή (Bēthphagḗ): fig-house; Beth-phage, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H1004 and H6291); KJV: Bethphage

G968 βῆμα (bēma): a step, i.e. foot-breath; by implication, a rostrum, i.e. a tribunal. Origin: from the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: judgment-seat, set (foot) on, throne

G969 βήρυλλος (bḗryllos): a "beryl". Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: beryl

G970 βία (bía): force. Origin: probably akin to G979 (βίος) (through the idea of vital activity); KJV: violence

G971 βιάζω (biázō): to force, i.e. (reflexively) to crowd oneself (into), or (passively) to be seized. Origin: from G979 (βίος); KJV: press, suffer violence

G972 βίαιος (bíaios): violent. Origin: from G970 (βία); KJV: mighty

G973 βιαστής (biastḗs): a forcer, i.e. (figuratively) energetic. Origin: from G971 (βιάζω); KJV: violent

G974 βιβλιαρίδιον (bibliarídion): a booklet. Origin: a diminutive of G975 (βιβλίον); KJV: little book

G975 βιβλίον (biblíon): a roll. Origin: a diminutive of G976 (βίβλος); KJV: bill, book, scroll, writing

G976 βίβλος (bíblos): Origin: properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing KJV: book

G977 βιβρώσκω (bibrṓskō): to eat. Origin: a reduplicated and prolonged form of an obsolete primary verb (perhaps causative of G1006 (βόσκω)); KJV: eat

G978 Βιθυνία (Bithynía): Bithynia, a region of Asia. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Bithynia

G979 βίος (bíos): life, i.e. (literally) the present state of existence; by implication, the means of livelihood. Origin: a primary word; KJV: good, life, living

G980 βιόω (bióō): to spend existence. Origin: from G979 (βίος); KJV: live

G981 βίωσις (bíōsis): living (properly, the act, by implication, the mode). Origin: from G980 (βιόω); KJV: manner of life

G982 βιωτικός (biōtikós): relating to the present existence. Origin: from a derivative of G980 (βιόω); KJV: of (pertaining to, things that pertain to) this life

G983 βλαβερός (blaberós): injurious. Origin: from G984 (βλάπτω); KJV: hurtful

G984 βλάπτω (bláptō): properly, to hinder, i.e. (by implication) to injure. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: hurt

G985 βλαστάνω (blastánō): to germinate; by implication, to yield fruit. Origin: from (a sprout); KJV: bring forth, bud, spring (up)

G986 Βλάστος (Blástos): Blastus, an officer of Herod Agrippa. Origin: perhaps the same as the base of G985 (βλαστάνω); KJV: Blastus

G987 βλασφημέω (blasphēméō): to vilify; specially, to speak impiously. Origin: from G989 (βλάσφημος); KJV: (speak) blaspheme(-er, -mously, -my), defame, rail on, revile, speak evil

G988 βλασφημία (blasphēmía): vilification (especially against God). Origin: from G989 (βλάσφημος); KJV: blasphemy, evil speaking, railing

G989 βλάσφημος (blásphēmos): scurrilious, i.e. calumnious (against men), or (specially) impious (against God). Origin: from a derivative of G984 (βλάπτω) and G5345 (φήμη); KJV: blasphemer(-mous), railing

G990 βλέμμα (blémma): vision (properly concrete; by implication, abstract). Origin: from G991 (βλέπω); KJV: seeing

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G991 to G1148
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G991 βλέπω (blépō): to look at (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: behold, beware, lie, look (on, to), perceive, regard, see, sight, take heed

G992 βλητέος (blētéos): fit to be cast (i.e. applied). Origin: from G906 (βάλλω); KJV: must be put

G993 Βοανεργές (Boanergés): sons of commotion; Boanerges, an epithet of two of the apostles. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H1123 and H7266); KJV: Boanerges

G994 βοάω (boáō): to halloo, i.e. shout (for help or in a tumultuous way). Origin: apparently a prolonged form of a primary verb; KJV: cry

G995 βοή (boḗ): a halloo, i.e. call (for aid, etc.). Origin: from G994 (βοάω); KJV: cry

G996 βοήθεια (boḗtheia): aid; specially, a rope or chain for frapping a vessel. Origin: from G998 (βοηθός); KJV: help

G997 βοηθέω (boēthéō): to aid or relieve. Origin: from G998 (βοηθός); KJV: help, succor

G998 βοηθός (boēthós): a succorer. Origin: from G995 (βοή) and theo (to run); KJV: helper

G999 βόθυνος (bóthynos): a hole (in the ground); specially, a cistern. Origin: akin to G900 (βαθύνω); KJV: ditch, pit

G1000 βολή (bolḗ): a throw (as a measure of distance). Origin: from G906 (βάλλω); KJV: cast

G1001 βολίζω (bolízō): to heave the lead. Origin: from G1002 (βολίς); KJV: sound

G1002 βολίς (bolís): a missile, i.e. javelin. Origin: from G906 (βάλλω); KJV: dart

G1003 Βοόζ (Boóz): Booz, (i.e. Boaz), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1162); KJV: Booz

G1004 βόρβορος (bórboros): mud. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: mire

G1005 βοῤῥᾶς (borrhâs): the north (properly, wind). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: north

G1006 βόσκω (bóskō): to pasture; by extension to, fodder; reflexively, to graze. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb (compare G977 (βιβρώσκω), G1016 (βοῦς)); KJV: feed, keep

G1007 Βοσόρ (Bosór): Bosor (i.e. Beor), a Moabite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1160); KJV: Bosor

G1008 βοτάνη (botánē): herbage (as if for grazing). Origin: from G1006 (βόσκω); KJV: herb

G1009 βότρυς (bótrys): a bunch (of grapes). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: (vine) cluster (of the vine)

G1010 βουλευτής (bouleutḗs): an adviser, i.e. (specially) a councillor or member of the Jewish Sanhedrin. Origin: from G1011 (βουλεύω); KJV: counsellor

G1011 βουλεύω (bouleúō): to advise, i.e. (reflexively) deliberate, or (by implication) resolve. Origin: from G1012 (βουλή); KJV: consult, take counsel, determine, be minded, purpose

G1012 βουλή (boulḗ): volition, i.e. (objectively) advice, or (by implication) purpose. Origin: from G1014 (βούλομαι); KJV: + advise, counsel, will

G1013 βούλημα (boúlēma): a resolve. Origin: from G1014 (βούλομαι); KJV: purpose, will

G1014 βούλομαι (boúlomai): to "will," i.e. (reflexively) be willing. Origin: middle voice of a primary verb; KJV: be disposed, minded, intend, list, (be, of own) will (-ing)

G1015 βουνός (bounós): a hillock. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: hill

G1016 βοῦς (boûs): an ox (as grazing), i.e. an animal of that species ("beef"). Origin: probably from the base of G1006 (βόσκω); KJV: ox

G1017 βραβεῖον (brabeîon): an award (of arbitration), i.e. (specially) a prize in the public games. Origin: from (an umpire of uncertain derivation); KJV: prize

G1018 βραβεύω (brabeúō): to arbitrate, i.e. (genitive case) to govern (figuratively, prevail). Origin: from the same as G1017 (βραβεῖον); KJV: rule

G1019 βραδύνω (bradýnō): to delay. Origin: from G1021 (βραδύς); KJV: be slack, tarry

G1020 βραδυπλοέω (bradyploéō): to sail slowly. Origin: from G1021 (βραδύς) and a prolonged form of G4126 (πλέω); KJV: sail slowly

G1021 βραδύς (bradýs): slow; figuratively, dull. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: slow

G1022 βραδύτης (bradýtēs): tardiness. Origin: from G1021 (βραδύς); KJV: slackness

G1023 βραχίων (brachíōn): the arm, i.e. (figuratively) strength. Origin: properly, comparative of G1024 (βραχύς), but apparently in the sense of (to wield); KJV: arm

G1024 βραχύς (brachýs): short (of time, place, quantity, or number). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: few words, little (space, while)

G1025 βρέφος (bréphos): an infant (properly, unborn) literally or figuratively. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: babe, (young) child, infant

G1026 βρέχω (bréchō): to moisten (especially by a shower). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: (send) rain, wash

G1027 βροντή (brontḗ): thunder. Origin: akin to (to roar); KJV: thunder(-ing)

G1028 βροχή (brochḗ): rain. Origin: from G1026 (βρέχω); KJV: rain

G1029 βρόχος (bróchos): a noose. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: snare

G1030 βρυγμός (brygmós): a grating (of the teeth). Origin: from G1031 (βρύχω); KJV: gnashing

G1031 βρύχω (brýchō): to grate the teeth (in pain or rage). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: gnash

G1032 βρύω (brýō): to swell out, i.e. (by implication) to gush. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: send forth

G1033 βρῶμα (brōma): food (literally or figuratively), especially (ceremonially) articles allowed or forbidden by the Jewish law. Origin: from the base of G977 (βιβρώσκω); KJV: meat, victuals

G1034 βρώσιμος (brṓsimos): eatable. Origin: from G1035 (βρῶσις); KJV: meat

G1035 βρῶσις (brōsis): (abstractly) eating (literally or figuratively); by extension (concretely) food (literally or figuratively). Origin: from the base of G977 (βιβρώσκω); KJV: eating, food, meat

G1036 βυθίζω (bythízō): to sink; by implication, to drown. Origin: from G1037 (βυθός); KJV: begin to sink, drown

G1037 βυθός (bythós): depth, i.e. (by implication) the sea. Origin: a variation of G899 (βάθος); KJV: deep

G1038 βυρσεύς (byrseús): a tanner. Origin: from (a hide); KJV: tanner

G1039 βύσσινος (býssinos): made of linen (neuter a linen cloth). Origin: from G1040 (βύσσος); KJV: fine linen

G1040 βύσσος (býssos): white linen. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H948); KJV: fine linen

G1041 βωμός (bōmós): properly, a stand, i.e. (specially) an altar. Origin: from the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: altar

G1042 γαββαθά (gabbathá): the knoll; gabbatha, a vernacular term for the Roman tribunal in Jerusalem. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H1355); KJV: Gabbatha

G1043 Γαβριήλ (Gabriḗl): Gabriel, an archangel. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1403); KJV: Gabriel

G1044 γάγγραινα (gángraina): an ulcer ("gangrene"). Origin: from (to gnaw); KJV: canker

G1045 Γάδ (Gád): Gad, a tribe of Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1410); KJV: Gad

G1046 Γαδαρηνός (Gadarēnós): a Gadarene or inhabitant of Gadara. Origin: from (a town east of the Jordan); KJV: Gadarene

G1047 γάζα (gáza): a treasure. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: treasure

G1048 Γάζα (Gáza): Gazah (i.e. Azzah), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5804); KJV: Gaza

G1049 γαζοφυλάκιον (gazophylákion): a treasure-house, i.e. a court in the temple for the collection-boxes. Origin: from G1047 (γάζα) and G5438 (φυλακή); KJV: treasury

G1050 Γάϊος (Gáïos): Gaius (i.e. Caius), a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Gaius

G1051 γάλα (gála): milk (figuratively). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: milk

G1052 Γαλάτης (Galátēs): a Galatian or inhabitant of Galatia. Origin: from G1053 (Γαλατία); KJV: Galatian

G1053 Γαλατία (Galatía): Galatia, a region of Asia. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Galatia

G1054 Γαλατικός (Galatikós): Galatic or relating to Galatia. Origin: from G1053 (Γαλατία); KJV: of Galatia

G1055 γαλήνη (galḗnē): tranquillity. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: calm

G1056 Γαλιλαία (Galilaía): Galilæa (i.e. the heathen circle), a region of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1551); KJV: Galilee

G1057 Γαλιλαῖος (Galilaîos): Galilean or belonging to Galilea. Origin: from G1056 (Γαλιλαία); KJV: Galilean, of Galilee

G1058 Γαλλίων (Gallíōn): Gallion (i.e. Gallio), a Roman officer. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Gallio

G1059 Γαμαλιήλ (Gamaliḗl): Gamaliel (i.e. Gamliel), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1583); KJV: Gamaliel

G1060 γαμέω (gaméō): to wed (of either sex). Origin: from G1062 (γάμος); KJV: marry (a wife)

G1061 γαμίσκω (gamískō): to espouse (a daughter to a husband). Origin: from G1062 (γάμος); KJV: give in marriage

G1062 γάμος (gámos): nuptials. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: marriage, wedding

G1063 γάρ (gár): properly, assigning a reason (used in argument, explanation or intensification; often with other particles). Origin: a primary particle; KJV: and, as, because (that), but, even, for, indeed, no doubt, seeing, then, therefore, verily, what, why, yet

G1064 γαστήρ (gastḗr): the stomach; by analogy, the matrix; figuratively, a gourmand. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: belly, + with child, womb

G1065 γέ (gé): Origin: a primary particle of emphasis or qualification (often used with other particles prefixed) KJV: and besides, doubtless, at least, yet

G1066 Γεδεών (Gedeṓn): Gedeon (i.e. Gid(e)on), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1439); KJV: Gedeon (in the King James Version)

G1067 γέεννα (géenna): valley of (the son of) Hinnom; ge-henna (or Ge-Hinnom), a valley of Jerusalem, used (figuratively) as a name for the place (or state) of everlasting punishment. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1516 and H2011); KJV: hell

G1068 Γεθσημανῆ (Gethsēmanē): oil-press; Gethsemane, a garden near Jerusalem. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H1660 and H8081); KJV: Gethsemane

G1069 γείτων (geítōn): a neighbour (as adjoining one's ground); by implication, a friend. Origin: from G1093 (γῆ); KJV: neighbour

G1070 γελάω (geláō): to laugh (as a sign of joy or satisfaction). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: laugh

G1071 γέλως (gélōs): laughter (as a mark of gratification). Origin: from G1070 (γελάω); KJV: laughter

G1072 γεμίζω (gemízō): to fill entirely. Origin: transitive from G1073 (γέμω); KJV: fill (be) full

G1073 γέμω (gémō): to swell out, i.e. be full. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be full

G1074 γενεά (geneá): a generation; by implication, an age (the period or the persons). Origin: from (a presumed derivative of) G1085 (γένος); KJV: age, generation, nation, time

G1075 γενεαλογέω (genealogéō): to reckon by generations, i.e. trace in genealogy. Origin: from G1074 (γενεά) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: count by descent

G1076 γενεαλογία (genealogía): tracing by generations, i.e. "genealogy". Origin: from the same as G1075 (γενεαλογέω); KJV: genealogy

G1077 γενέσια (genésia): birthday ceremonies. Origin: neuter plural of a derivative of G1078 (γένεσις); KJV: birthday

G1078 γένεσις (génesis): nativity; figuratively, nature. Origin: from the same as G1074 (γενεά); KJV: generation, nature(-ral)

G1079 γενετή (genetḗ): birth. Origin: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G1074 (γενεά); KJV: birth

G1080 γεννάω (gennáō): to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother); figuratively, to regenerate. Origin: from a variation of G1085 (γένος); KJV: bear, beget, be born, bring forth, conceive, be delivered of, gender, make, spring

G1081 γέννημα (génnēma): offspring; by analogy, produce (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1080 (γεννάω); KJV: fruit, generation

G1082 Γεννησαρέτ (Gennēsarét): Gennesaret (i.e. Kinnereth), a lake and plain in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H3672); KJV: Gennesaret

G1083 γέννησις (génnēsis): nativity. Origin: from G1080 (γεννάω); KJV: birth

G1084 γεννητός (gennētós): born. Origin: from G1080 (γεννάω); KJV: they that are born

G1085 γένος (génos): "kin" (abstract or concrete, literal or figurative, individual or collective). Origin: from G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: born, country(-man), diversity, generation, kind(-red), nation, offspring, stock

G1086 Γεργεσηνός (Gergesēnós): a Gergesene (i.e. Girgashite) or one of the aborigines of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1622); KJV: Gergesene

G1087 γερουσία (gerousía): the eldership, i.e. (collectively) the Jewish Sanhedrin. Origin: from G1088 (γέρων); KJV: senate

G1088 γέρων (gérōn): aged. Origin: of uncertain affinity (compare G1094 (γῆρας)); KJV: old

G1089 γεύομαι (geúomai): to taste; by implication, to eat; figuratively, to experience (good or ill). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: eat, taste

G1090 γεωργέω (geōrgéō): to till (the soil). Origin: from G1092 (γεωργός); KJV: dress

G1091 γεώργιον (geṓrgion): cultivable, i.e. a farm. Origin: neuter of a (presumed) derivative of G1092 (γεωργός); KJV: husbandry

G1092 γεωργός (geōrgós): a land-worker, i.e. farmer. Origin: from G1093 (γῆ) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: husbandman

G1093 γῆ (gē): soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application). Origin: contracted from a primary word; KJV: country, earth(-ly), ground, land, world

G1094 γῆρας (gēras): senility. Origin: akin to G1088 (γέρων); KJV: old age

G1095 γηράσκω (gēráskō): to be senescent. Origin: from G1094 (γῆρας); KJV: be (wax) old

G1096 γίνομαι (gínomai): to cause to be ("gen"-erate), i.e. (reflexively) to become (come into being), used with great latitude (literal, figurative, intensive, etc.). Origin: a prolongation and middle voice form of a primary verb; KJV: arise, be assembled, be(-come, -fall, -have self), be brought (to pass), (be) come (to pass), continue, be divided, draw, be ended, fall, be finished, follow, be found, be fulfilled, + God forbid, grow, happen, have, be kept, be made, be married, be ordained to be, partake, pass, be performed, be published, require, seem, be showed, X soon as it was, sound, be taken, be turned, use, wax, will, would, be wrought

G1097 γινώσκω (ginṓskō): to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb; KJV: allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand

G1098 γλεῦκος (gleûkos): sweet wine, i.e. (properly) must (fresh juice), but used of the more saccharine (and therefore highly inebriating) fermented wine. Origin: akin to G1099 (γλυκύς); KJV: new wine

G1099 γλυκύς (glykýs): sweet (i.e. not bitter nor salt). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: sweet, fresh

G1100 γλῶσσα (glōssa): the tongue; by implication, a language (specially, one naturally unacquired). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: tongue

G1101 γλωσσόκομον (glōssókomon): properly, a case (to keep mouthpieces of wind-instruments in) i.e. (by extension) a casket or (specially) purse. Origin: from G1100 (γλῶσσα) and the base of G2889 (κόσμος); KJV: bag

G1102 γναφεύς (gnapheús): a cloth-dresser. Origin: by variation for a derivative from (to tease cloth); KJV: fuller

G1103 γνήσιος (gnḗsios): legitimate (of birth), i.e. genuine. Origin: from the same as G1077 (γενέσια); KJV: own, sincerity, true

G1104 γνησίως (gnēsíōs): genuinely, i.e. really. Origin: adverb from G1103 (γνήσιος); KJV: naturally

G1105 γνόφος (gnóphos): gloom (as of a storm). Origin: akin to G3509 (νέφος); KJV: blackness

G1106 γνώμη (gnṓmē): cognition, i.e. (subjectively) opinion, or (objectively) resolve (counsel, consent, etc.). Origin: from G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: advice, + agree, judgment, mind, purpose, will

G1107 γνωρίζω (gnōrízō): to make known; subjectively, to know. Origin: from a derivative of G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: certify, declare, make known, give to understand, do to wit, wot

G1108 γνῶσις (gnōsis): knowing (the act), i.e. (by implication) knowledge. Origin: from G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: knowledge, science

G1109 γνώστης (gnṓstēs): a knower. Origin: from G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: expert

G1110 γνωστός (gnōstós): well-known. Origin: from G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: acquaintance, (which may be) known, notable

G1111 γογγύζω (gongýzō): to grumble. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: murmur

G1112 γογγυσμός (gongysmós): a grumbling. Origin: from G1111 (γογγύζω); KJV: grudging, murmuring

G1113 γογγυστής (gongystḗs): a grumbler. Origin: from G1111 (γογγύζω); KJV: murmurer

G1114 γόης (góēs): properly, a wizard (as muttering spells), i.e. (by implication) an imposter. Origin: from (to wail); KJV: seducer

G1115 Γολγοθᾶ (Golgothâ): the skull; Golgotha, a knoll near Jerusalem. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H1538); KJV: Golgotha

G1116 Γόμοῤῥα (Gómorrha): Gomorrha (i.e. Amorah), a place near the Dead Sea. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6017); KJV: Gomorrha

G1117 γόμος (gómos): a load (as filling), i.e. (specially) a cargo, or (by extension) wares. Origin: from G1073 (γέμω); KJV: burden, merchandise

G1118 γονεύς (goneús): a parent. Origin: from the base of G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: parent

G1119 γόνυ (góny): the "knee". Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: knee(X -l)

G1120 γονυπετέω (gonypetéō): to fall on the knee. Origin: from a compound of G1119 (γόνυ) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: bow the knee, kneel down

G1121 γράμμα (grámma): a writing, i.e. a letter, note, epistle, book, etc.; plural learning. Origin: from G1125 (γράφω); KJV: bill, learning, letter, scripture, writing, written

G1122 γραμματεύς (grammateús): Origin: from G1121 (γράμμα). a writer, i.e. (professionally) scribe or secretary KJV: scribe, town-clerk

G1123 γραπτός (graptós): inscribed (figuratively). Origin: from G1125 (γράφω); KJV: written

G1124 γραφή (graphḗ): a document, i.e. holy Writ (or its contents or a statement in it). Origin: from G1125 (γράφω); KJV: scripture

G1125 γράφω (gráphō): to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: describe, write(-ing, -ten)

G1126 γραώδης (graṓdēs): crone-like, i.e. silly. Origin: from (an old woman) and G1491 (εἶδος); KJV: old wives'

G1127 γρηγορεύω (grēgoreúō): to keep awake, i.e. watch (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1453 (ἐγείρω); KJV: be vigilant, wake, (be) watch(-ful)

G1128 γυμνάζω (gymnázō): to practise naked (in the games), i.e. train (figuratively). Origin: from G1131 (γυμνός); KJV: exercise

G1129 γυμνασία (gymnasía): training, i.e. (figuratively) asceticism. Origin: from G1128 (γυμνάζω); KJV: exercise

G1130 γυμνητεύω (gymnēteúō): to strip, i.e. (reflexively) go poorly clad. Origin: from a derivative of G1131 (γυμνός); KJV: be naked

G1131 γυμνός (gymnós): nude (absolute or relative, literal or figurative). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: naked
