G1132 γυμνότης (gymnótēs): nudity (absolute or comparative). Origin: from G1131 (γυμνός); KJV: nakedness

G1133 γυναικάριον (gynaikárion): a little (i.e. foolish) woman. Origin: a diminutive from G1135 (γυνή); KJV: silly woman

G1134 γυναικεῖος (gynaikeîos): feminine. Origin: from G1135 (γυνή); KJV: wife

G1135 γυνή (gynḗ): a woman; specially, a wife. Origin: probably from the base of G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: wife, woman

G1136 Γώγ (Gṓg): Gog, a symbolic name for some future Antichrist. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1463); KJV: Gog

G1137 γωνία (gōnía): an angle. Origin: probably akin to G1119 (γόνυ); KJV: corner, quarter

G1138 Δαβίδ (Dabíd): Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1732); KJV: David

G1139 δαιμονίζομαι (daimonízomai): to be exercised by a dæmon. Origin: middle voice from G1142 (δαίμων); KJV: have a (be vexed with, be possessed with) devil(-s)

G1140 δαιμόνιον (daimónion): a dæmonic being; by extension a deity. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G1142 (δαίμων); KJV: devil, god

G1141 δαιμονιώδης (daimoniṓdēs): dæmon-like. Origin: from G1140 (δαιμόνιον) and G1142 (δαίμων); KJV: devilish

G1142 δαίμων (daímōn): a dæmon or supernatural spirit (of a bad nature). Origin: from (to distribute fortunes); KJV: devil

G1143 δάκνω (dáknō): to bite, i.e. (figuratively) thwart. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary root; KJV: bite

G1144 δάκρυ (dákry): a tear. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: tear

G1145 δακρύω (dakrýō): to shed tears. Origin: from G1144 (δάκρυ); KJV: weep

G1146 δακτύλιος (daktýlios): a finger-ring. Origin: from G1147 (δάκτυλος); KJV: ring

G1147 δάκτυλος (dáktylos): a finger. Origin: probably from G1176 (δέκα); KJV: finger

G1148 Δαλμανουθά (Dalmanouthá): Dalmanutha, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably of Chaldee origin; KJV: Dalmanutha

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1149 to G1289
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1149 Δαλματία (Dalmatía): Dalmatia, a region of Europe. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Dalmatia

G1150 δαμάζω (damázō): to tame. Origin: a variation of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; KJV: tame

G1151 δάμαλις (dámalis): a heifer (as tame). Origin: probably from the base of G1150 (δαμάζω); KJV: heifer

G1152 Δάμαρις (Dámaris): perhaps gentle; Damaris, an Athenian woman. Origin: probably from the base of G1150 (δαμάζω); KJV: Damaris

G1153 Δαμασκηνός (Damaskēnós): a Damascene or inhabitant of Damascus. Origin: from G1154 (Δαμασκός); KJV: Damascene

G1154 Δαμασκός (Damaskós): Damascus, a city of Syria. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1834); KJV: Damascus

G1155 δανείζω (daneízō): to loan on interest; reflexively, to borrow. Origin: from G1156 (δάνειον); KJV: borrow, lend

G1156 δάνειον (dáneion): probably akin to the base of G1325 (δίδωμι); a loan. Origin: from (a gift); KJV: debt

G1157 δανειστής (daneistḗs): a lender. Origin: from G1155 (δανείζω); KJV: creditor

G1158 Δανιήλ (Daniḗl): Daniel, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1840); KJV: Daniel

G1159 δαπανάω (dapanáō): to expend, i.e. (in a good sense) to incur cost, or (in a bad one) to waste. Origin: from G1160 (δαπάνη); KJV: be at charges, consume, spend

G1160 δαπάνη (dapánē): expense (as consuming). Origin: from (to devour); KJV: cost

G1161 δέ (dé): but, and, etc. Origin: a primary particle (adversative or continuative); KJV: also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English)

G1162 δέησις (déēsis): a petition. Origin: from G1189 (δέομαι); KJV: prayer, request, supplication

G1163 δεῖ (deî): also deon deh-on'; neuter active participle of the same; both used impersonally; it is (was, etc.) necessary (as binding). Origin: 3rd person singular active present of G1210 (δέω); KJV: behoved, be meet, must (needs), (be) need(-ful), ought, should

G1164 δεῖγμα (deîgma): a specimen (as shown). Origin: from the base of G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: example

G1165 δειγματίζω (deigmatízō): to exhibit. Origin: from G1164 (δεῖγμα); KJV: make a shew

G1166 δεικνύω (deiknýō): to show (literally or figuratively). Origin: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary of the same meaning; KJV: shew

G1167 δειλία (deilía): timidity. Origin: from G1169 (δειλός); KJV: fear

G1168 δειλιάω (deiliáō): to be timid. Origin: from G1167 (δειλία); KJV: be afraid

G1169 δειλός (deilós): timid, i.e. (by implication) faithless. Origin: from (dread); KJV: fearful

G1170 δεῖνα (deîna): so and so (when the person is not specified). Origin: probably from the same as G1171 (δεινῶς) (through the idea of forgetting the name as fearful, i.e. strange); KJV: such a man

G1171 δεινῶς (deinōs): terribly, i.e. excessively. Origin: adverb from a derivative of the same as G1169 (δειλός); KJV: grievously, vehemently

G1172 δειπνέω (deipnéō): to dine, i.e. take the principle (or evening) meal. Origin: from G1173 (δεῖπνον); KJV: sup (X -er)

G1173 δεῖπνον (deîpnon): dinner, i.e. the chief meal (usually in the evening). Origin: from the same as G1160 (δαπάνη); KJV: feast, supper

G1174 δεισιδαιμονέστερος (deisidaimonésteros): more religious than others. Origin: the compound of a derivative of the base of G1169 (δειλός) and G1142 (δαίμων); KJV: too superstitious

G1175 δεισιδαιμονία (deisidaimonía): religion. Origin: from the same as G1174 (δεισιδαιμονέστερος); KJV: superstition

G1176 δέκα (déka): ten. Origin: a primary number; KJV: (eight-)een, ten

G1177 δεκαδύο (dekadýo): two and ten, i.e. twelve. Origin: from G1176 (δέκα) and G1417 (δύο); KJV: twelve

G1178 δεκαπέντε (dekapénte): ten and five, i.e. fifteen. Origin: from G1176 (δέκα) and G4002 (πέντε); KJV: fifteen

G1179 Δεκάπολις (Dekápolis): the ten-city region; the Decapolis, a district in Syria. Origin: from G1176 (δέκα) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: Decapolis

G1180 δεκατέσσαρες (dekatéssares): ten and four, i.e. fourteen. Origin: from G1176 (δέκα) and G5064 (τέσσαρες); KJV: fourteen

G1181 δεκάτη (dekátē): a tenth, i.e. as a percentage or (technically) tithe. Origin: feminine of G1182 (δέκατος); KJV: tenth (part), tithe

G1182 δέκατος (dékatos): tenth. Origin: ordinal from G1176 (δέκα); KJV: tenth

G1183 δεκατόω (dekatóō): to tithe, i.e. to give or take a tenth. Origin: from G1181 (δεκάτη); KJV: pay (receive) tithes

G1184 δεκτός (dektós): approved; (figuratively) propitious. Origin: from G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: accepted(-table)

G1185 δελεάζω (deleázō): to entrap, i.e. (figuratively) delude. Origin: from the base of G1388 (δόλος); KJV: allure, beguile, entice

G1186 δένδρον (déndron): a tree. Origin: probably from (an oak); KJV: tree

G1187 δεξιολάβος (dexiolábos): a guardsman (as if taking the right) or light-armed soldier. Origin: from G1188 (δεξιός) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: spearman

G1188 δεξιός (dexiós): the right side or (feminine) hand (as that which usually takes). Origin: from G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: right (hand, side)

G1189 δέομαι (déomai): to beg (as binding oneself), i.e. petition. Origin: middle voice of G1210 (δέω); KJV: beseech, pray (to), make request

G1190 Δερβαῖος (Derbaîos): a Derbæan or inhabitant of Derbe. Origin: from G1191 (Δέρβη); KJV: of Derbe

G1191 Δέρβη (Dérbē): Derbe, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Derbe

G1192 δέρμα (dérma): a hide. Origin: from G1194 (δέρω); KJV: skin

G1193 δερμάτινος (dermátinos): made of hide. Origin: from G1192 (δέρμα); KJV: leathern, of a skin

G1194 δέρω (dérō): properly, to flay, i.e. (by implication) to scourge, or (by analogy) to thrash. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: beat, smite

G1195 δεσμεύω (desmeúō): to be a binder (captor), i.e. to enchain (a prisoner), to tie on (a load). Origin: from a (presumed) derivative of G1196 (δεσμέω); KJV: bind

G1196 δεσμέω (desméō): to tie, i.e. shackle. Origin: from G1199 (δεσμόν); KJV: bind

G1197 δέσμη (désmē): a bundle. Origin: from G1196 (δεσμέω); KJV: bundle

G1198 δέσμιος (désmios): a captive (as bound). Origin: from G1199 (δεσμόν); KJV: in bonds, prisoner

G1199 δεσμόν (desmón): a band, i.e. ligament (of the body) or shackle (of a prisoner); figuratively, an impediment or disability. Origin: neuter and masculine respectively from G1210 (δέω); KJV: band, bond, chain, string

G1200 δεσμοφύλαξ (desmophýlax): a jailer (as guarding the prisoners). Origin: from G1199 (δεσμόν) and G5441 (φύλαξ); KJV: jailor, keeper of the prison

G1201 δεσμωτήριον (desmōtḗrion): a place of bondage, i.e. a dungeon. Origin: from a derivative of G1199 (δεσμόν) (equivalent to G1196 (δεσμέω)); KJV: prison

G1202 δεσμώτης (desmṓtēs): (passively) a captive. Origin: from the same as G1201 (δεσμωτήριον); KJV: prisoner

G1203 δεσπότης (despótēs): an absolute ruler ("despot"). Origin: perhaps from G1210 (δέω) and (a husband); KJV: Lord, master

G1204 δεῦρο (deûro): here; used also imperative hither!; and of time, hitherto. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: come (hither), hither(-to)

G1205 δεῦτε (deûte): come hither!. Origin: from G1204 (δεῦρο) and an imperative form of (to go); KJV: come, X follow

G1206 δευτεραῖος (deuteraîos): secondary, i.e. (specially) on the second day. Origin: from G1208 (δεύτερος); KJV: next day

G1207 δευτερόπρωτος (deuteróprōtos): second-first, i.e. (specially) a designation of the Sabbath immediately after the Paschal week (being the second after Passover day, and the first of the seven Sabbaths intervening before Pentecost). Origin: from G1208 (δεύτερος) and G4413 (πρῶτος); KJV: second … after the first

G1208 δεύτερος (deúteros): (ordinal) second (in time, place, or rank; also adverb). Origin: as the comparative of G1417 (δύο); KJV: afterward, again, second(-arily, time)

G1209 δέχομαι (déchomai): to receive (in various applications, literally or figuratively). Origin: middle voice of a primary verb; KJV: accept, receive, take

G1210 δέω (déō): to bind (in various applications, literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: bind, be in bonds, knit, tie, wind

G1211 δή (dḗ): a particle of emphasis or explicitness; now, then, etc. Origin: probably akin to G1161 (δέ); KJV: also, and, doubtless, now, therefore

G1212 δῆλος (dēlos): clear. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: + bewray, certain, evident, manifest

G1213 δηλόω (dēlóō): to make plain (by words). Origin: from G1212 (δῆλος); KJV: declare, shew, signify

G1214 Δημᾶς (Dēmâs): Demas, a Christian. Origin: probably for G1216 (Δημήτριος); KJV: Demas

G1215 δημηγορέω (dēmēgoréō): to be a people-gatherer, i.e. to address a public assembly. Origin: from a compound of G1218 (δῆμος) and G58 (ἀγορά); KJV: make an oration

G1216 Δημήτριος (Dēmḗtrios): Demetrius, the name of an Ephesian and of a Christian. Origin: from (Ceres); KJV: Demetrius

G1217 δημιουργός (dēmiourgós): a worker for the people, i.e. mechanic (spoken of the Creator). Origin: from G1218 (δῆμος) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: maker

G1218 δῆμος (dēmos): the public (as bound together socially). Origin: from G1210 (δέω); KJV: people

G1219 δημόσιος (dēmósios): public; (feminine singular dative case as adverb) in public. Origin: from G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: common, openly, publickly

G1220 δηνάριον (dēnárion): a denarius (or ten asses). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: pence, penny(-worth)

G1221 δήποτε (dḗpote): a particle of generalization; indeed, at any time. Origin: from G1211 (δή) and G4218 (ποτέ); KJV: (what-)soever

G1222 δήπου (dḗpou): a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless. Origin: from G1211 (δή) and G4225 (πού); KJV: verily

G1223 διά (diá): through (in very wide applications, local, causal, or occasional). Origin: a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; KJV: after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) … fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with (-in)

G1224 διαβαίνω (diabaínō): to cross. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: come over, pass (through)

G1225 διαβάλλω (diabállō): (figuratively) to traduce. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: accuse

G1226 διαβεβαιόομαι (diabebaióomai): to confirm thoroughly (by words), i.e. asseverate. Origin: middle voice of a compound of G1223 (διά) and G950 (βεβαιόω); KJV: affirm constantly

G1227 διαβλέπω (diablépō): to look through, i.e. recover full vision. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: see clearly

G1228 διάβολος (diábolos): a traducer; specially, Satan (compare H07854). Origin: from G1225 (διαβάλλω); KJV: false accuser, devil, slanderer

G1229 διαγγέλλω (diangéllō): to herald thoroughly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: declare, preach, signify

G1230 διαγίνομαι (diagínomai): to elapse meanwhile. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: X after, be past, be spent

G1231 διαγινώσκω (diaginṓskō): to know thoroughly, i.e. ascertain exactly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: (would) enquire, know the uttermost

G1232 διαγνωρίζω (diagnōrízō): to tell abroad. Origin: from G1123 (γραπτός) and G1107 (γνωρίζω); KJV: make known

G1233 διάγνωσις (diágnōsis): (magisterial) examination ("diagnosis"). Origin: from G1231 (διαγινώσκω); KJV: hearing

G1234 διαγογγύζω (diagongýzō): to complain throughout a crowd. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1111 (γογγύζω); KJV: murmur

G1235 διαγρηγορέω (diagrēgoréō): to waken thoroughly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1127 (γρηγορεύω); KJV: be awake

G1236 διάγω (diágō): to pass time or life. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: lead life, living

G1237 διαδέχομαι (diadéchomai): to receive in turn, i.e. (figuratively) succeed to. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: come after

G1238 διάδημα (diádēma): a "diadem" (as bound about the head). Origin: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G1210 (δέω); KJV: crown

G1239 διαδίδωμι (diadídōmi): to give throughout a crowd, i.e. deal out; also to deliver over (as to a successor). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: (make) distribute(-ion), divide, give

G1240 διάδοχος (diádochos): a successor in office. Origin: from G1237 (διαδέχομαι); KJV: room

G1241 διαζώννυμι (diazṓnnymi): to gird tightly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2224 (ζώννυμι); KJV: gird

G1242 διαθήκη (diathḗkē): properly, a disposition, i.e. (specially) a contract (especially a devisory will). Origin: from G1303 (διατίθεμαι); KJV: covenant, testament

G1243 διαίρεσις (diaíresis): a distinction or (concretely) variety. Origin: from G1244 (διαιρέω); KJV: difference, diversity

G1244 διαιρέω (diairéō): to separate, i.e. distribute. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: divide

G1245 διακαθαρίζω (diakatharízō): to cleanse perfectly, i.e. (specially) winnow. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2511 (καθαρίζω); KJV: thoroughly purge

G1246 διακατελέγχομαι (diakatelénchomai): to prove downright, i.e. confute. Origin: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω); KJV: convince

G1247 διακονέω (diakonéō): to be an attendant, i.e. wait upon (menially or as a host, friend, or (figuratively) teacher); technically, to act as a Christian deacon. Origin: from G1249 (διάκονος); KJV: (ad-)minister (unto), serve, use the office of a deacon

G1248 διακονία (diakonía): attendance (as a servant, etc.); figuratively (eleemosynary) aid, (official) service (especially of the Christian teacher, or technically of the diaconate). Origin: from G1249 (διάκονος); KJV: (ad-)minister(-ing, -tration, -try), office, relief, service(-ing)

G1249 διάκονος (diákonos): an attendant, i.e. (genitive case) a waiter (at table or in other menial duties); specially, a Christian teacher and pastor (technically, a deacon or deaconess). Origin: probably from an obsolete (to run on errands; compare G1377 (διώκω)); KJV: deacon, minister, servant

G1250 διακόσιοι (diakósioi): two hundred. Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G1540 (ἑκατόν); KJV: two hundred

G1251 διακούομαι (diakoúomai): to hear throughout, i.e. patiently listen (to a prisoner's plea). Origin: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: hear

G1252 διακρίνω (diakrínō): to separate thoroughly, i.e. (literally and reflexively) to withdraw from, or (by implication) oppose; figuratively, to discriminate (by implication, decide), or (reflexively) hesitate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: contend, make (to) differ(-ence), discern, doubt, judge, be partial, stagger, waver

G1253 διάκρισις (diákrisis): judicial estimation. Origin: from G1252 (διακρίνω); KJV: discern(-ing), disputation

G1254 διακωλύω (diakōlýō): to hinder altogether, i.e. utterly prohibit. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2967 (κωλύω); KJV: forbid

G1255 διαλαλέω (dialaléō): to talk throughout a company, i.e. converse or (genitive case) publish. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: commune, noise abroad

G1256 διαλέγομαι (dialégomai): to say thoroughly, i.e. discuss (in argument or exhortation). Origin: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: dispute, preach (unto), reason (with), speak

G1257 διαλείπω (dialeípō): to leave off in the middle, i.e. intermit. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: cease

G1258 διάλεκτος (diálektos): a (mode of) discourse, i.e. "dialect". Origin: from G1256 (διαλέγομαι); KJV: language, tongue

G1259 διαλλάσσω (diallássō): to change thoroughly, i.e. (mentally) to conciliate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω); KJV: reconcile

G1260 διαλογίζομαι (dialogízomai): to reckon thoroughly, i.e. (genitive case) to deliberate (by reflection or discussion). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3049 (λογίζομαι); KJV: cast in mind, consider, dispute, muse, reason, think

G1261 διαλογισμός (dialogismós): discussion, i.e. (internal) consideration (by implication, purpose), or (external) debate. Origin: from G1260 (διαλογίζομαι); KJV: dispute, doubtful(-ing), imagination, reasoning, thought

G1262 διαλύω (dialýō): to dissolve utterly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: scatter

G1263 διαμαρτύρομαι (diamartýromai): to attest or protest earnestly, or (by implication) hortatively. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3140 (μαρτυρέω); KJV: charge, testify (unto), witness

G1264 διαμάχομαι (diamáchomai): to fight fiercely (in altercation). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: strive

G1265 διαμένω (diaménō): to stay constantly (in being or relation). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: continue, remain

G1266 διαμερίζω (diamerízō): to partition thoroughly (literally in distribution, figuratively in dissension). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3307 (μερίζω); KJV: cloven, divide, part

G1267 διαμερισμός (diamerismós): disunion (of opinion and conduct). Origin: from G1266 (διαμερίζω); KJV: division

G1268 διανέμω (dianémō): to distribute, i.e. (of information) to disseminate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G3551 (νόμος); KJV: spread

G1269 διανεύω (dianeúō): to nod (or express by signs) across an intervening space. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3506 (νεύω); KJV: beckon

G1270 διανόημα (dianóēma): something thought through, i.e. a sentiment. Origin: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: thought

G1271 διάνοια (diánoia): deep thought, properly, the faculty (mind or its disposition), by implication, its exercise. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3563 (νοῦς); KJV: imagination, mind, understanding

G1272 διανοίγω (dianoígō): to open thoroughly, literally (as a first-born) or figuratively (to expound). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G455 (ἀνοίγω); KJV: open

G1273 διανυκτερεύω (dianyktereúō): to sit up the whole night. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G3571 (νύξ); KJV: continue all night

G1274 διανύω (dianýō): to accomplish thoroughly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and (to effect); KJV: finish

G1275 διαπαντός (diapantós): through all time, i.e. (adverbially) constantly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the genitive case of G3956 (πᾶς); KJV: alway(-s), continually

G1276 διαπεράω (diaperáō): to cross entirely. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of the base of G4008 (πέραν); KJV: go over, pass (over), sail over

G1277 διαπλέω (diapléō): to sail through. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4126 (πλέω); KJV: sail over

G1278 διαπονέω (diaponéō): to toil through, i.e. (passively) be worried. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G4192 (πόνος); KJV: be grieved

G1279 διαπορεύομαι (diaporeúomai): to travel through. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: go through, journey in, pass by

G1280 διαπορέω (diaporéō): to be thoroughly nonplussed. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G639 (ἀπορέω); KJV: (be in) doubt, be (much) perplexed

G1281 διαπραγματεύομαι (diapragmateúomai): to thoroughly occupy oneself, i.e. (transitively and by implication) to earn in business. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4231 (πραγματεύομαι); KJV: gain by trading

G1282 διαπρίω (diapríō): to saw asunder, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G4249 (πρίζω); KJV: cut (to the heart)

G1283 διαρπάζω (diarpázō): to seize asunder, i.e. plunder. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: spoil

G1284 διαῤῥήσσω (diarrhḗssō): to tear asunder. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: break, rend

G1285 διασαφέω (diasaphéō): to clear thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) declare. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and (clear); KJV: tell unto

G1286 διασείω (diaseíō): to shake thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to intimidate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4579 (σείω); KJV: do violence to

G1287 διασκορπίζω (diaskorpízō): to dissipate, i.e. (genitive case) to rout or separate; specially, to winnow; figuratively, to squander. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4650 (σκορπίζω); KJV: disperse, scatter (abroad), strew, waste

G1288 διασπάω (diaspáō): to draw apart, i.e. sever or dismember. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4685 (σπάω); KJV: pluck asunder, pull in pieces

G1289 διασπείρω (diaspeírō): to sow throughout, i.e. (figuratively) distribute in foreign lands. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4687 (σπείρω); KJV: scatter abroad

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1290 to G1425
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1290 διασπορά (diasporá): dispersion, i.e. (specially and concretely) the (converted) Israelite resident in Gentile countries. Origin: from G1289 (διασπείρω); KJV: (which are) scattered (abroad)

G1291 διαστέλλομαι (diastéllomai): to set (oneself) apart (figuratively, distinguish), i.e. (by implication) to enjoin. Origin: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: charge, that which was (give) commanded(-ment)

G1292 διάστημα (diástēma): an interval. Origin: from G1339 (διΐστημι); KJV: space

G1293 διαστολή (diastolḗ): a variation. Origin: from G1291 (διαστέλλομαι); KJV: difference, distinction

G1294 διαστρέφω (diastréphō): to distort, i.e. (figuratively) misinterpret, or (morally) corrupt. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: perverse(-rt), turn away

G1295 διασώζω (diasṓzō): to save thoroughly, i.e. (by implication or analogy) to cure, preserve, rescue, etc. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G4982 (σώζω); KJV: bring safe, escape (safe), heal, make perfectly whole, save

G1296 διαταγή (diatagḗ): arrangement, i.e. institution. Origin: from G1299 (διατάσσω); KJV: instrumentality

G1297 διάταγμα (diátagma): an arrangement, i.e. (authoritative) edict. Origin: from G1299 (διατάσσω); KJV: commandment

G1298 διαταράσσω (diatarássō): to disturb wholly, i.e. agitate (with alarm). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5015 (ταράσσω); KJV: trouble

G1299 διατάσσω (diatássō): to arrange thoroughly, i.e. (specially) institute, prescribe, etc. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: appoint, command, give, (set in) order, ordain

G1300 διατελέω (diateléō): to accomplish thoroughly, i.e. (subjectively) to persist. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5055 (τελέω); KJV: continue

G1301 διατηρέω (diatēréō): to watch thoroughly, i.e. (positively and transitively) to observe strictly, or (negatively and reflexively) to avoid wholly. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5083 (τηρέω); KJV: keep

G1302 διατί (diatí): through what cause ?, i.e. why?. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5101 (τίς); KJV: wherefore, why

G1303 διατίθεμαι (diatíthemai): to put apart, i.e. (figuratively) dispose (by assignment, compact, or bequest). Origin: middle voice from G1223 (διά) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: appoint, make, testator

G1304 διατρίβω (diatríbō): to wear through (time), i.e. remain. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος); KJV: abide, be, continue, tarry

G1305 διατροφή (diatrophḗ): nourishment. Origin: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: food

G1306 διαυγάζω (diaugázō): to glimmer through, i.e. break (as day). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G826 (αὐγάζω); KJV: dawn

G1307 διαφανής (diaphanḗs): appearing through, i.e. "diaphanous". Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: transparent

G1308 διαφέρω (diaphérō): to bear through, i.e. (literally) transport; usually to bear apart, i.e. (objectively) to toss about (figuratively, report); subjectively, to "differ", or (by implication) surpass. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: be better, carry, differ from, drive up and down, be (more) excellent, make matter, publish, be of more value

G1309 διαφεύγω (diapheúgō): to flee through, i.e. escape. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5343 (φεύγω); KJV: escape

G1310 διαφημίζω (diaphēmízō): to report thoroughly, i.e. divulgate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G5345 (φήμη); KJV: blaze abroad, commonly report, spread abroad, fame

G1311 διαφθείρω (diaphtheírō): to rot thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to ruin (passively, decay utterly, figuratively, pervert). Origin: from G1225 (διαβάλλω) and G5351 (φθείρω); KJV: corrupt, destroy, perish

G1312 διαφθορά (diaphthorá): decay. Origin: from G1311 (διαφθείρω); KJV: corruption

G1313 διάφορος (diáphoros): varying; also surpassing. Origin: from G1308 (διαφέρω); KJV: differing, divers, more excellent

G1314 διαφυλάσσω (diaphylássō): to guard thoroughly, i.e. protect. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G5442 (φυλάσσω); KJV: keep

G1315 διαχειρίζομαι (diacheirízomai): to handle thoroughly, i.e. lay violent hands upon. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G5495 (χείρ); KJV: kill, slay

G1316 διαχωρίζομαι (diachōrízomai): to remove (oneself) wholly, i.e. retire. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the middle voice of G5563 (χωρίζω); KJV: depart

G1317 διδακτικός (didaktikós): instructive ("didactic"). Origin: from G1318 (διδακτός); KJV: apt to teach

G1318 διδακτός (didaktós): (subjectively) instructed, or (objectively) communicated by teaching. Origin: from G1321 (διδάσκω); KJV: taught, which … teacheth

G1319 διδασκαλία (didaskalía): instruction (the function or the information). Origin: from G1320 (διδάσκαλος); KJV: doctrine, learning, teaching

G1320 διδάσκαλος (didáskalos): an instructor (genitive case or specially). Origin: from G1321 (διδάσκω); KJV: doctor, master, teacher

G1321 διδάσκω (didáskō): to teach (in the same broad application). Origin: a prolonged (causative) form of a primary verb (to learn); KJV: teach

G1322 διδαχή (didachḗ): instruction (the act or the matter). Origin: from G1321 (διδάσκω); KJV: doctrine, hath been taught

G1323 δίδραχμον (dídrachmon): a double drachma (didrachm). Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G1406 (δραχμή); KJV: tribute

G1324 Δίδυμος (Dídymos): double, i.e. twin; Didymus, a Christian. Origin: prolongation from G1364 (δίς); KJV: Didymus

G1325 δίδωμι (dídōmi): to give (used in a very wide application, properly, or by implication, literally or figuratively; greatly modified by the connection). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which is used as an alternative in most of the tenses); KJV: adventure, bestow, bring forth, commit, deliver (up), give, grant, hinder, make, minister, number, offer, have power, put, receive, set, shew, smite (+ with the hand), strike (+ with the palm of the hand), suffer, take, utter, yield

G1326 διεγείρω (diegeírō): to wake fully; i.e. arouse (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1453 (ἐγείρω); KJV: arise, awake, raise, stir up

G1327 διέξοδος (diéxodos): an outlet through, i.e. probably an open square (from which roads diverge). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G1841 (ἔξοδος); KJV: highway

G1328 διερμηνευτής (diermēneutḗs): an explainer. Origin: from G1329 (διερμηνεύω); KJV: interpreter

G1329 διερμηνεύω (diermēneúō): to explain thoroughly, by implication, to translate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2059 (ἑρμηνεύω); KJV: expound, interpret(-ation)

G1330 διέρχομαι (diérchomai): to traverse (literally). Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: come, depart, go (about, abroad, everywhere, over, through, throughout), pass (by, over, through, throughout), pierce through, travel, walk through

G1331 διερωτάω (dierōtáō): to question throughout, i.e. ascertain by interrogation. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2065 (ἐρωτάω); KJV: make enquiry for

G1332 διετής (dietḗs): of two years (in age). Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G2094 (ἔτος); KJV: two years old

G1333 διετία (dietía): a space of two years (biennium). Origin: from G1332 (διετής); KJV: two years

G1334 διηγέομαι (diēgéomai): to relate fully. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: declare, shew, tell

G1335 διήγεσις (diḗgesis): a recital. Origin: from G1334 (διηγέομαι); KJV: declaration

G1336 διηνεκής (diēnekḗs): carried through, i.e. (adverbially with G1519 (εἰς) and G3588 (ὁ) prefixed) perpetually. Origin: neuter of a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of an alternate of G5342 (φέρω); KJV: + continually, for ever

G1337 διθάλασσος (dithálassos): having two seas, i.e. a sound with a double outlet. Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G2281 (θάλασσα); KJV: where two seas meet

G1338 διϊκνέομαι (diïknéomai): to reach through, i.e. penetrate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and the base of G2425 (ἱκανός); KJV: pierce

G1339 διΐστημι (diḯstēmi): to stand apart, i.e. (reflexively) to remove, intervene. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: go further, be parted, after the space of

G1340 διϊσχυρίζομαι (diïschyrízomai): to stout it through, i.e. asservate. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G2478 (ἰσχυρός); KJV: confidently (constantly) affirm

G1341 δικαιοκρισία (dikaiokrisía): a just sentence. Origin: from G1342 (δίκαιος) and G2920 (κρίσις); KJV: righteous judgment

G1342 δίκαιος (díkaios): equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively). Origin: from G1349 (δίκη); KJV: just, meet, right(-eous)

G1343 δικαιοσύνη (dikaiosýnē): equity (of character or act); specially (Christian) justification. Origin: from G1342 (δίκαιος); KJV: righteousness

G1344 δικαιόω (dikaióō): to render (i.e. show or regard as) just or innocent. Origin: from G1342 (δίκαιος); KJV: free, justify(-ier), be righteous

G1345 δικαίωμα (dikaíōma): an equitable deed; by implication, a statute or decision. Origin: from G1344 (δικαιόω); KJV: judgment, justification, ordinance, righteousness

G1346 δικαίως (dikaíōs): equitably. Origin: adverb from G1342 (δίκαιος); KJV: justly, (to) righteously(-ness)

G1347 δικαίωσις (dikaíōsis): aquittal (for Christ's sake). Origin: from G1344 (δικαιόω); KJV: justification

G1348 δικαστής (dikastḗs): a judger. Origin: from a derivative of G1349 (δίκη); KJV: judge

G1349 δίκη (díkē): right (as self-evident), i.e. justice (the principle, a decision, or its execution). Origin: probably from G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: judgment, punish, vengeance

G1350 δίκτυον (díktyon): a seine (for fishing). Origin: probably from a primary verb (to cast); KJV: net

G1351 δίλογος (dílogos): equivocal, i.e. telling a different story. Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: double-tongued

G1352 διό (dió): through which thing, i.e. consequently. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3739 (ὅς); KJV: for which cause, therefore, wherefore

G1353 διοδεύω (diodeúō): to travel through. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3593 (ὁδεύω); KJV: go throughout, pass through

G1354 Διονύσιος (Dionýsios): reveller; Dionysius, an Athenian. Origin: from (Bacchus); KJV: Dionysius

G1355 διόπερ (dióper): on which very account. Origin: from G1352 (διό) and G4007 (περ); KJV: wherefore

G1356 διοπετής (diopetḗs): sky-fallen (i.e. an aerolite). Origin: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: which fell down from Jupiter

G1357 διόρθωσις (diórthōsis): rectification, i.e. (specially) the Messianic restauration. Origin: from a compound of G1223 (διά) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός), meaning to straighten thoroughly; KJV: reformation

G1358 διορύσσω (diorýssō): to penetrate burglariously. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3736 (ὀρύσσω); KJV: break through (up)

G1359 Διόσκουροι (Dióskouroi): sons of Jupiter, i.e. the twins Dioscuri. Origin: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and a form of the base of G2877 (κοράσιον); KJV: Castor and Pollux

G1360 διότι (dióti): on the very account that, or inasmuch as. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and G3754 (ὅτι); KJV: because (that), for, therefore

G1361 Διοτρεφής (Diotrephḗs): Jove-nourished; Diotrephes, an opponent of Christianity. Origin: from the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) and G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: Diotrephes

G1362 διπλοῦς (diploûs): two-fold. Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and (probably) the base of G4119 (πλείων); KJV: double, two-fold more

G1363 διπλόω (diplóō): to render two-fold. Origin: from G1362 (διπλοῦς); KJV: double

G1364 δίς (dís): twice. Origin: adverb from G1417 (δύο); KJV: again, twice

G1365 διστάζω (distázō): properly, to duplicate, i.e. (mentally) to waver (in opinion). Origin: from G1364 (δίς); KJV: doubt

G1366 δίστομος (dístomos): double-edged. Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G4750 (στόμα); KJV: with two edges, two-edged

G1367 δισχίλιοι (dischílioi): two thousand. Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G5507 (χίλιοι); KJV: two thousand

G1368 διϋλίζω (diÿlízō): to strain out. Origin: from G1223 (διά) and (to filter); KJV: strain at (probably by misprint)

G1369 διχάζω (dicházō): to make apart, i.e. sunder (figuratively, alienate). Origin: from a derivative of G1364 (δίς); KJV: set at variance

G1370 διχοστασία (dichostasía): disunion, i.e. (figuratively) dissension. Origin: from a derivative of G1364 (δίς) and G4714 (στάσις); KJV: division, sedition

G1371 διχοτομέω (dichotoméō): to bisect, i.e. (by extension) to flog severely. Origin: from a compound of a derivative of G1364 (δίς) and a derivative of (to cut); KJV: cut asunder (in sunder)

G1372 διψάω (dipsáō): to thirst for (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a variation of G1373 (δίψος); KJV: (be, be a-)thirst(-y)

G1373 δίψος (dípsos): thirst. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: thirst

G1374 δίψυχος (dípsychos): two-spirited, i.e. vacillating (in opinion or purpose). Origin: from G1364 (δίς) and G5590 (ψυχή); KJV: double minded

G1375 διωγμός (diōgmós): persecution. Origin: from G1377 (διώκω); KJV: persecution

G1376 διώκτης (diṓktēs): a persecutor. Origin: from G1377 (διώκω); KJV: persecutor

G1377 διώκω (diṓkō): compare the base of G1169 (δειλός) and G1249 (διάκονος)); to pursue (literally or figuratively); by implication, to persecute. Origin: a prolonged (and causative) form of a primary verb (to flee; KJV: ensue, follow (after), given to, (suffer) persecute(-ion), press forward

G1378 δόγμα (dógma): a law (civil, ceremonial or ecclesiastical). Origin: from the base of G1380 (δοκέω); KJV: decree, ordinance

G1379 δογματίζω (dogmatízō): to prescribe by statute, i.e. (reflexively) to submit to, ceremonially rule. Origin: from G1378 (δόγμα); KJV: be subject to ordinances

G1380 δοκέω (dokéō): compare the base of G1166 (δεικνύω)) of the same meaning; to think; by implication, to seem (truthfully or uncertainly). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb, (used only in an alternate in certain tenses; KJV: be accounted, (of own) please(-ure), be of reputation, seem (good), suppose, think, trow

G1381 δοκιμάζω (dokimázō): to test (literally or figuratively); by implication, to approve. Origin: from G1384 (δόκιμος); KJV: allow, discern, examine, X like, (ap-)prove, try

G1382 δοκιμή (dokimḗ): test (abstractly or concretely); by implication, trustiness. Origin: from the same as G1384 (δόκιμος); KJV: experience(-riment), proof, trial

G1383 δοκίμιον (dokímion): a testing; by implication, trustworthiness. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1382 (δοκιμή); KJV: trial, trying

G1384 δόκιμος (dókimos): properly, acceptable (current after assayal), i.e. approved. Origin: from G1380 (δοκέω); KJV: approved, tried

G1385 δοκός (dokós): a stick of timber. Origin: from G1209 (δέχομαι) (through the idea of holding up); KJV: beam

G1386 δόλιος (dólios): guileful. Origin: from G1388 (δόλος); KJV: deceitful

G1387 δολιόω (dolióō): to be guileful. Origin: from G1386 (δόλιος); KJV: use deceit

G1388 δόλος (dólos): compare G1185 (δελεάζω)); a trick (bait), i.e. (figuratively) wile. Origin: from an obsolete primary verb, (probably meaning to decoy; KJV: craft, deceit, guile, subtilty

G1389 δολόω (dolóō): to ensnare, i.e. (figuratively) adulterate. Origin: from G1388 (δόλος); KJV: handle deceitfully

G1390 δόμα (dóma): a present. Origin: from the base of G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: gift

G1391 δόξα (dóxa): glory (as very apparent), in a wide application (literal or figurative, objective or subjective). Origin: from the base of G1380 (δοκέω); KJV: dignity, glory(-ious), honour, praise, worship

G1392 δοξάζω (doxázō): to render (or esteem) glorious (in a wide application). Origin: from G1391 (δόξα); KJV: (make) glorify(-ious), full of (have) glory, honour, magnify

G1393 Δορκάς (Dorkás): gazelle; Dorcas, a Christian woman. KJV: Dorcas

G1394 δόσις (dósis): a giving; by implication, (concretely) a gift. Origin: from the base of G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: gift, giving

G1395 δότης (dótēs): a giver. Origin: from the base of G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: giver

G1396 δουλαγωγέω (doulagōgéō): to be a slave-driver, i.e. to enslave (figuratively, subdue). Origin: from a presumed compound of G1401 (δοῦλος) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring into subjection

G1397 δουλεία (douleía): slavery (ceremonially or figuratively). Origin: from G1398 (δουλεύω); KJV: bondage

G1398 δουλεύω (douleúō): to be a slave to (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary). Origin: from G1401 (δοῦλος); KJV: be in bondage, (do) serve(-ice)

G1399 δούλη (doúlē): a female slave (involuntarily or voluntarily). Origin: feminine of G1401 (δοῦλος); KJV: handmaid(-en)

G1400 δοῦλον (doûlon): subservient. Origin: neuter of G1401 (δοῦλος); KJV: servant

G1401 δοῦλος (doûlos): a slave (literal or figurative, involuntary or voluntary; frequently, therefore in a qualified sense of subjection or subserviency). Origin: from G1210 (δέω); KJV: bond(-man), servant

G1402 δουλόω (doulóō): to enslave (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1401 (δοῦλος); KJV: bring into (be under) bondage, X given, become (make) servant

G1403 δοχή (dochḗ): a reception, i.e. convivial entertainment. Origin: from G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: feast

G1404 δράκων (drákōn): a fabulous kind of serpent (perhaps as supposed to fascinate). Origin: probably from an alternate form of (to look); KJV: dragon

G1405 δράσσομαι (drássomai): to grasp, i.e. (figuratively) entrap. Origin: perhaps akin to the base of G1404 (δράκων) (through the idea of capturing); KJV: take

G1406 δραχμή (drachmḗ): a drachma or (silver) coin (as handled). Origin: from G1405 (δράσσομαι); KJV: piece (of silver)

G1407 δρέπανον (drépanon): a gathering hook (especially for harvesting). Origin: from (to pluck); KJV: sickle

G1408 δρόμος (drómos): a race, i.e. (figuratively) career. Origin: from the alternate of G5143 (τρέχω); KJV: course

G1409 Δρούσιλλα (Droúsilla): Drusilla, a member of the Herodian family. Origin: a feminine diminutive of Drusus (a Roman name); KJV: Drusilla

G1410 δύναμαι (dýnamai): to be able or possible. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: be able, can (do, + -not), could, may, might, be possible, be of power

G1411 δύναμις (dýnamis): force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself). Origin: from G1410 (δύναμαι); KJV: ability, abundance, meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work

G1412 δυναμόω (dynamóō): to enable. Origin: from G1411 (δύναμις); KJV: strengthen

G1413 δυνάστης (dynástēs): a ruler or officer. Origin: from G1410 (δύναμαι); KJV: of great authority, mighty, potentate

G1414 δυνατέω (dynatéō): to be efficient (figuratively). Origin: from G1415 (δυνατός); KJV: be mighty

G1415 δυνατός (dynatós): powerful or capable (literally or figuratively); neuter possible. Origin: from G1410 (δύναμαι); KJV: able, could, (that is) mighty (man), possible, power, strong

G1416 δύνω (dýnō): to go "down". Origin: prolonged forms of an obsolete primary (to sink); KJV: set

G1417 δύο (dýo): "two". Origin: a primary numeral; KJV: both, twain, two

G1418 δυσ- (dys-): used only in composition as a prefix; hard, i.e. with difficulty. Origin: a primary inseparable particle of uncertain derivation; KJV: + hard, + grievous, etc

G1419 δυσβάστακτος (dysbástaktos): oppressive. Origin: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a derivative of G941 (βαστάζω); KJV: grievous to be borne

G1420 δυσεντερία (dysentería): a "dysentery". Origin: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a comparative of G1787 (ἐντός) (meaning a bowel); KJV: bloody flux

G1421 δυσερμήνευτος (dysermḗneutos): difficult of explanation. Origin: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a presumed derivative of G2059 (ἑρμηνεύω); KJV: hard to be uttered

G1422 δύσκολος (dýskolos): properly, fastidious about eating (peevish), i.e. (genitive case) impracticable. Origin: from G1418 (δυσ-) and (food); KJV: hard

G1423 δυσκόλως (dyskólōs): impracticably. Origin: adverb from G1422 (δύσκολος); KJV: hardly

G1424 δυσμή (dysmḗ): the sun-set, i.e. (by implication) the western region. Origin: from G1416 (δύνω); KJV: west

G1425 δυσνόητος (dysnóētos): difficult of perception. Origin: from G1418 (δυσ-) and a derivative of G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: hard to be understood

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1426 to G1559
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1426 δυσφημία (dysphēmía): defamation. Origin: from a compound of G1418 (δυσ-) and G5345 (φήμη); KJV: evil report

G1427 δώδεκα (dṓdeka): two and ten, i.e. a dozen. Origin: from G1417 (δύο) and G1176 (δέκα); KJV: twelve

G1428 δωδέκατος (dōdékatos): twelfth. Origin: from G1427 (δώδεκα); KJV: twelfth

G1429 δωδεκάφυλον (dōdekáphylon): the commonwealth of Israel. Origin: from G1427 (δώδεκα) and G5443 (φυλή); KJV: twelve tribes

G1430 δῶμα (dōma): properly, an edifice, i.e. (specially) a roof. Origin: from (to build); KJV: housetop

G1431 δωρεά (dōreá): a gratuity. Origin: from G1435 (δῶρον); KJV: gift

G1432 δωρεάν (dōreán): gratuitously (literally or figuratively). Origin: accusative case of G1431 (δωρεά) as adverb; KJV: without a cause, freely, for naught, in vain

G1433 δωρέομαι (dōréomai): to bestow gratuitously. Origin: middle voice from G1435 (δῶρον); KJV: give

G1434 δώρημα (dṓrēma): a bestowment. Origin: from G1433 (δωρέομαι); KJV: gift

G1435 δῶρον (dōron): a present; specially, a sacrifice. KJV: gift, offering

G1436 ἔα (éa): properly, let it be, i.e. (as interjection) aha!. Origin: apparent imperative of G1439 (ἐάω); KJV: let alone

G1437 ἐάν (eán): a conditional particle; in case that, provided, etc.; often used in connection with other particles to denote indefiniteness or uncertainty. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G302 (ἄν); KJV: before, but, except, (and) if, (if) so, (what-, whither-)soever, though, when (-soever), whether (or), to whom, (who-)so(-ever)

G1438 ἑαυτοῦ (heautoû): him- (her-, it-, them-, also (in conjunction with the personal pronoun of the other persons) my-, thy-, our-, your-) self (selves), etc. Origin: from a reflexive pronoun otherwise obsolete and the genitive case (dative case or accusative case) of G846 (αὐτός); KJV: alone, her (own, -self), (he) himself, his (own), itself, one (to) another, our (thine) own(-selves), + that she had, their (own, own selves), (of) them(-selves), they, thyself, you, your (own, own conceits, own selves, -selves)

G1439 ἐάω (eáō): to let be, i.e. permit or leave alone. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: commit, leave, let (alone), suffer

G1440 ἑβδομήκοντα (hebdomḗkonta): seventy. Origin: from G1442 (ἕβδομος) and a modified form of G1176 (δέκα); KJV: seventy, three score and ten

G1441 ἑβδομηκοντάκις (hebdomēkontákis): seventy times. Origin: multiple adverb from G1440 (ἑβδομήκοντα); KJV: seventy times

G1442 ἕβδομος (hébdomos): seventh. Origin: ordinal from G2033 (ἑπτά); KJV: seventh

G1443 Ἐβέρ (Ebér): Eber, a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5677); KJV: Eber

G1444 Ἑβραϊκός (Hebraïkós): Hebraic or the Jewish language. Origin: from G1443 (Ἐβέρ); KJV: Hebrew

G1445 Ἑβραῖος (Hebraîos): a Hebræan (i.e. Hebrew) or Jew. Origin: from G1443 (Ἐβέρ); KJV: Hebrew

G1446 Ἑβραΐς (Hebraḯs): the Hebraistic (Hebrew) or Jewish (Chaldee) language. Origin: from G1443 (Ἐβέρ); KJV: Hebrew

G1447 Ἑβραϊστί (Hebraïstí): Hebraistically or in the Jewish (Chaldee) language. Origin: adverb from G1446 (Ἑβραΐς); KJV: in (the) Hebrew (tongue)

G1448 ἐγγίζω (engízō): to make near, i.e. (reflexively) approach. Origin: from G1451 (ἐγγύς); KJV: approach, be at hand, come (draw) near, be (come, draw) nigh

G1449 ἐγγράφω (engráphō): to "engrave", i.e. inscribe. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1125 (γράφω); KJV: write (in)

G1450 ἔγγυος (éngyos): pledged (as if articulated by a member), i.e. a bondsman. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and (a limb); KJV: surety

G1451 ἐγγύς (engýs): akin to the base of G43 (ἀγκάλη)); near (literally or figuratively, of place or time). Origin: from a primary verb (to squeeze or throttle; KJV: from , at hand, near, nigh (at hand, unto), ready

G1452 ἐγγύτερον (engýteron): nearer. Origin: neuter of the comparative of G1451 (ἐγγύς); KJV: nearer

G1453 ἐγείρω (egeírō): to waken (transitively or intransitively), i.e. rouse (literally, from sleep, from sitting or lying, from disease, from death; or figuratively, from obscurity, inactivity, ruins, nonexistence). Origin: probably akin to the base of G58 (ἀγορά) (through the idea of collecting one's faculties); KJV: awake, lift (up), raise (again, up), rear up, (a-)rise (again, up), stand, take up

G1454 ἔγερσις (égersis): a resurgence (from death). Origin: from G1453 (ἐγείρω); KJV: resurrection

G1455 ἐγκάθετος (enkáthetos): subinduced, i.e. surreptitiously suborned as a lier-in-wait. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G2524 (καθίημι); KJV: spy

G1456 ἐγκαίνια (enkaínia): innovatives, i.e. (specially) renewal (of religious services after the Antiochian interruption). Origin: neuter plural of a presumed compound from G1722 (ἐν) and G2537 (καινός); KJV: dedication

G1457 ἐγκαινίζω (enkainízō): to renew, i.e. inaugurate. Origin: from G1456 (ἐγκαίνια); KJV: consecrate, dedicate

G1458 ἐγκαλέω (enkaléō): to call in (as a debt or demand), i.e. bring to account (charge, criminate, etc.). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: accuse, call in question, implead, lay to the charge

G1459 ἐγκαταλείπω (enkataleípō): to leave behind in some place, i.e. (in a good sense) let remain over, or (in a bad sense) to desert. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2641 (καταλείπω); KJV: forsake, leave

G1460 ἐγκατοικέω (enkatoikéō): to settle down in a place, i.e. reside. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2730 (κατοικέω); KJV: dwell among

G1461 ἐγκεντρίζω (enkentrízō): to prick in, i.e. ingraft. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G2759 (κέντρον); KJV: graff in(-to)

G1462 ἔγκλημα (énklēma): an accusation, i.e. offence alleged. Origin: from G1458 (ἐγκαλέω); KJV: crime laid against, laid to charge

G1463 ἐγκομβόομαι (enkombóomai): to engirdle oneself (for labor), i.e. figuratively (the apron as being a badge of servitude) to wear (in token of mutual deference). Origin: middle voice from G1722 (ἐν) and (to gird); KJV: be clothed with

G1464 ἐγκοπή (enkopḗ): a hindrance. Origin: from G1465 (ἐγκόπτω); KJV: X hinder

G1465 ἐγκόπτω (enkóptō): to cut into, i.e. (figuratively) impede, detain. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: hinder, be tedious unto

G1466 ἐγκράτεια (enkráteia): self-control (especially continence). Origin: from G1468 (ἐγκρατής); KJV: temperance

G1467 ἐγκρατεύομαι (enkrateúomai): to exercise self-restraint (in diet and chastity). Origin: middle voice from G1468 (ἐγκρατής); KJV: can(-not) contain, be temperate

G1468 ἐγκρατής (enkratḗs): strong in a thing (masterful), i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) self-controlled (in appetite, etc.). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2904 (κράτος); KJV: temperate

G1469 ἐγκρίνω (enkrínō): to judge in, i.e. count among. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: make of the number

G1470 ἐγκρύπτω (enkrýptō): to conceal in, i.e. incorporate with. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2928 (κρύπτω); KJV: hid in

G1471 ἔγκυος (énkyos): swelling inside, i.e. pregnant. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G2949 (κῦμα); KJV: great with child

G1472 ἐγχρίω (enchríō): to rub in (oil), i.e. besmear. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5548 (χρίω); KJV: anoint

G1473 ἐγώ (egṓ): Origin: a primary pronoun of the first person I (only expressed when emphatic) KJV: I, me

G1474 ἐδαφίζω (edaphízō): to raze. Origin: from G1475 (ἔδαφος); KJV: lay even with the ground

G1475 ἔδαφος (édaphos): a basis (bottom), i.e. the soil. Origin: from the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: ground

G1476 ἑδραῖος (hedraîos): sedentary, i.e. (by implication) immovable. Origin: from a derivative of (to sit); KJV: settled, stedfast

G1477 ἑδραίωμα (hedraíōma): a support, i.e. (figuratively) basis. Origin: from a derivative of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: ground

G1478 Ἐζεκίας (Ezekías): Ezekias (i.e. Hezekeiah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2396); KJV: Ezekias

G1479 ἐθελοθρησκεία (ethelothrēskeía): voluntary (arbitrary and unwarranted) piety, i.e. sanctimony. Origin: from G2309 (θέλω) and G2356 (θρησκεία); KJV: will worship

G1480 ἐθίζω (ethízō): to accustom, i.e. (neuter passive participle) customary. Origin: from G1485 (ἔθος); KJV: custom

G1481 ἐθνάρχης (ethnárchēs): the governor (not king) of a district. Origin: from G1484 (ἔθνος) and G746 (ἀρχή); KJV: ethnarch

G1482 ἐθνικός (ethnikós): national ("ethnic"), i.e. (specially) a Gentile. Origin: from G1484 (ἔθνος); KJV: heathen (man)

G1483 ἐθνικῶς (ethnikōs): as a Gentile. Origin: adverb from G1482 (ἐθνικός); KJV: after the manner of Gentiles

G1484 ἔθνος (éthnos): a race (as of the same habit), i.e. a tribe; specially, a foreign (non-Jewish) one (usually, by implication, pagan). Origin: probably from G1486 (ἔθω); KJV: Gentile, heathen, nation, people

G1485 ἔθος (éthos): a usage (prescribed by habit or law). Origin: from G1486 (ἔθω); KJV: custom, manner, be wont

G1486 ἔθω (éthō): to be used (by habit or conventionality); neuter perfect participle usage. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be custom (manner, wont)

G1487 εἰ (ei): if, whether, that, etc. Origin: a primary particle of conditionality; KJV: forasmuch as, if, that, (al-)though, whether

G1488 εἶ (eî): thou art. Origin: second person singular present of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: art, be

G1489 εἴγε (eíge): if indeed, seeing that, unless, (with negative) otherwise. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G1065 (γέ); KJV: if (so be that, yet)

G1490 εἰ δὲ μή(γε) (ei dè mḗ(ge)): but if not. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ), G1161 (δέ), and G3361 (μή) (sometimes with G1065 (γέ) added); KJV: (or) else, if (not, otherwise), otherwise

G1491 εἶδος (eîdos): a view, i.e. form (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: appearance, fashion, shape, sight

G1492 εἴδω (eídō): used only in certain past tenses, the others being borrowed from the equivalent G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) and G3708 (ὁράω); properly, to see (literally or figuratively); by implication, (in the perfect tense only) to know. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be aware, behold, X can (+ not tell), consider, (have) know(-ledge), look (on), perceive, see, be sure, tell, understand, wish, wot

G1493 εἰδωλεῖον (eidōleîon): an image-fane. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1497 (εἴδωλον); KJV: idol's temple

G1494 εἰδωλόθυτον (eidōlóthyton): an image-sacrifice, i.e. part of an idolatrous offering. Origin: neuter of a compound of G1497 (εἴδωλον) and a presumed derivative of G2380 (θύω); KJV: (meat, thing that is) offered (in sacrifice, sacrificed) to (unto) idols

G1495 εἰδωλολατρεία (eidōlolatreía): image-worship (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1497 (εἴδωλον) and G2999 (λατρεία); KJV: idolatry

G1496 εἰδωλολάτρης (eidōlolátrēs): an image- (servant or) worshipper (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1497 (εἴδωλον) and the base of G3000 (λατρεύω); KJV: idolater

G1497 εἴδωλον (eídōlon): an image (i.e. for worship); by implication, a heathen god, or (plural) the worship of such. Origin: from G1491 (εἶδος); KJV: idol

G1498 εἴην (eíēn): might (could, would, or should) be. Origin: optative (i.e. English subjunctive) present of G1510 (εἰμί) (including the other person); KJV: mean, + perish, should be, was, were

G1499 εἰ καί (ei kaí): if also (or even). Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G2532 (καί); KJV: if (that), though

G1500 εἰκῆ (eikē): idly, i.e. without reason (or effect). Origin: probably from G1502 (εἴκω) (through the idea of failure); KJV: without a cause, (in) vain(-ly)

G1501 εἴκοσι (eíkosi): a score. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: twenty

G1502 εἴκω (eíkō): properly, to be weak, i.e. yield. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: give place

G1503 εἴκω (eíkō): to resemble. Origin: apparently a primary verb (perhaps akin to G1502 (εἴκω) through the idea of faintness as a copy); KJV: be like

G1504 εἰκών (eikṓn): a likeness, i.e. (literally) statue, profile, or (figuratively) representation, resemblance. Origin: from G1503 (εἴκω); KJV: image

G1505 εἰλικρίνεια (eilikríneia): clearness, i.e. (by implication) purity (figuratively). Origin: from G1506 (εἰλικρινής); KJV: sincerity

G1506 εἰλικρινής (eilikrinḗs): judged by sunlight, i.e. tested as genuine (figuratively). Origin: from (the sun's ray) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: pure, sincere

G1507 εἱλίσσω (heilíssō): to coil or wrap. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary but defective verb (of the same meaning); KJV: roll together

G1508 εἰ μή (ei mḗ): if not. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G3361 (μή); KJV: but, except (that), if not, more than, save (only) that, saving, till

G1509 εἰ μή τι (ei mḗ ti): if not somewhat. Origin: from G1508 (εἰ μή) and the neuter of G5100 (τὶς); KJV: except

G1510 εἰμί (eimí): I exist (used only when emphatic). Origin: the first person singular present indicative; a prolonged form of a primary and defective verb; KJV: am, have been, X it is I, was

G1511 εἶναι (eînai): to exist. Origin: present infinitive from G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: am, was

G1512 εἴ περ (eí per): if perhaps. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G4007 (περ); KJV: if so be (that), seeing, though

G1513 εἴ πως (eí pōs): if somehow. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G4458 (-πώς); KJV: if by any means

G1514 εἰρηνεύω (eirēneúō): to be (act) peaceful. Origin: from G1515 (εἰρήνη); KJV: be at (have, live in) peace, live peaceably

G1515 εἰρήνη (eirḗnē): peace (literally or figuratively); by implication, prosperity. Origin: probably from a primary verb (to join); KJV: one, peace, quietness, rest, + set at one again

G1516 εἰρηνικός (eirēnikós): pacific; by implication, salutary. Origin: from G1515 (εἰρήνη); KJV: peaceable

G1517 εἰρηνοποιέω (eirēnopoiéō): to be a peace-maker, i.e. (figuratively) to harmonize. Origin: from G1518 (εἰρηνοποιός); KJV: make peace

G1518 εἰρηνοποιός (eirēnopoiós): pacificatory, i.e. (subjectively) peaceable. Origin: from G1515 (εἰρήνη) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: peacemaker

G1519 εἰς (eis): to or into (indicating the point reached or entered), of place, time, or (figuratively) purpose (result, etc.); also in adverbial phrases. Origin: a primary preposition; KJV: (abundant-)ly, against, among, as, at, (back-)ward, before, by, concerning, + continual, + far more exceeding, for (intent, purpose), fore, + forth, in (among, at, unto, -so much that, -to), to the intent that, + of one mind, + never, of, (up-)on, + perish, + set at one again, (so) that, therefore(-unto), throughout, til, to (be, the end, -ward), (here-)until(-to), …ward, (where-)fore, with

G1520 εἷς (heîs): one. Origin: a primary numeral; KJV: a(-n, -ny, certain), + abundantly, man, one (another), only, other, some

G1521 εἰσάγω (eiságō): to introduce (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring in(-to), (+ was to) lead into

G1522 εἰσακούω (eisakoúō): to listen to. Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: hear

G1523 εἰσδέχομαι (eisdéchomai): to take into one's favor. Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: receive

G1524 εἴσειμι (eíseimi): to enter. Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and (to go); KJV: enter (go) into

G1525 εἰσέρχομαι (eisérchomai): to enter (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: X arise, come (in, into), enter in(-to), go in (through)

G1526 εἰσί (eisí): they are. Origin: 3rd person plural present indicative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: agree, are, be, dure, X is, were

G1527 εἷς καθ’ εἷς (heîs kath’ heîs): severally. Origin: from G1520 (εἷς) repeated with G2596 (κατά) inserted; KJV: one by one

G1528 εἰσκαλέω (eiskaléō): to invite in. Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: call in

G1529 εἴσοδος (eísodos): an entrance (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G3598 (ὁδός); KJV: coming, enter(-ing) in (to)

G1530 εἰσπηδάω (eispēdáō): to rush in. Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and (to leap); KJV: run (spring) in

G1531 εἰσπορεύομαι (eisporeúomai): to enter (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: come (enter) in, go into

G1532 εἰστρέχω (eistréchō): to hasten inward. Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G5143 (τρέχω); KJV: run in

G1533 εἰσφέρω (eisphérō): to carry inward (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bring (in), lead into

G1534 εἶτα (eîta): a particle of succession (in time or logical enumeration), then, moreover. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: after that(-ward), furthermore, then

G1535 εἴτε (eíte): if too. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: if, or, whether

G1536 εἴ τις (eí tis): if any. Origin: from G1487 (εἰ) and G5100 (τὶς); KJV: he that, if a(-ny) man('s thing, from any, ought), whether any, whosoever

G1537 ἐκ (ek): literal or figurative; direct or remote). Origin: a primary preposition denoting origin (the point whence action or motion proceeds), from, out (of place, time, or cause; KJV: after, among, X are, at, betwixt(-yond), by (the means of), exceedingly, (+ abundantly above), for(- th), from (among, forth, up), + grudgingly, + heartily, X heavenly, X hereby, + very highly, in, …ly, (because, by reason) of, off (from), on, out among (from, of), over, since, X thenceforth, through, X unto, X vehemently, with(-out)

G1538 ἕκαστος (hékastos): each or every. Origin: as if a superlative of (afar); KJV: any, both, each (one), every (man, one, woman), particularly

G1539 ἑκάστοτε (hekástote): at every time. Origin: as if from G1538 (ἕκαστος) and G5119 (τότε); KJV: always

G1540 ἑκατόν (hekatón): a hundred. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: hundred

G1541 ἑκατονταέτης (hekatontaétēs): centenarian. Origin: from G1540 (ἑκατόν) and G2094 (ἔτος); KJV: hundred years old

G1542 ἑκατονταπλασίων (hekatontaplasíōn): a hundred times. Origin: from G1540 (ἑκατόν) and a presumed derivative of G4111 (πλάσσω); KJV: hundredfold

G1543 ἑκατοντάρχης (hekatontárchēs): the captain of one hundred men. Origin: from G1540 (ἑκατόν) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: centurion

G1544 ἐκβάλλω (ekbállō): to eject (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: bring forth, cast (forth, out), drive (out), expel, leave, pluck (pull, take, thrust) out, put forth (out), send away (forth, out)

G1545 ἔκβασις (ékbasis): an exit (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G939 (βάσις) (meaning to go out); KJV: end, way to escape

G1546 ἐκβολή (ekbolḗ): ejection, i.e. (specially) a throwing overboard of the cargo. Origin: from G1544 (ἐκβάλλω); KJV: + lighten the ship

G1547 ἐκγαμίζω (ekgamízō): to marry off a daughter. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a form of G1061 (γαμίσκω) (compare G1548 (ἐκγαμίσκω)); KJV: give in marriage

G1548 ἐκγαμίσκω (ekgamískō): the same as 1547. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1061 (γαμίσκω); KJV: give in marriage

G1549 ἔκγονον (ékgonon): a descendant, i.e. (specially) grandchild. Origin: neuter of a derivative of a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: nephew

G1550 ἐκδαπανάω (ekdapanáō): to expend (wholly), i.e. (figuratively) exhaust. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1159 (δαπανάω); KJV: spend

G1551 ἐκδέχομαι (ekdéchomai): to accept from some source, i.e. (by implication) to await. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: expect, look (tarry) for, wait (for)

G1552 ἔκδηλος (ékdēlos): wholly evident. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1212 (δῆλος); KJV: manifest

G1553 ἐκδημέω (ekdēméō): to emigrate, i.e. (figuratively) vacate or quit. Origin: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: be absent

G1554 ἐκδίδωμι (ekdídōmi): to give forth, i.e. (specially) to lease. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: let forth (out)

G1555 ἐκδιηγέομαι (ekdiēgéomai): to narrate through wholly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a compound of G1223 (διά) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: declare

G1556 ἐκδικέω (ekdikéō): to vindicate, retaliate, punish. Origin: from G1558 (ἔκδικος); KJV: a (re-)venge

G1557 ἐκδίκησις (ekdíkēsis): vindication, retribution. Origin: from G1556 (ἐκδικέω); KJV: (a-, re-)venge(-ance), punishment

G1558 ἔκδικος (ékdikos): carrying justice out, i.e. a punisher. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1349 (δίκη); KJV: a (re-)venger

G1559 ἐκδιώκω (ekdiṓkō): to pursue out, i.e. expel or persecute implacably. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1377 (διώκω); KJV: persecute

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1560 to G1712
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1560 ἔκδοτος (ékdotos): given out or over, i.e. surrendered. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: delivered

G1561 ἐκδοχή (ekdochḗ): expectation. Origin: from G1551 (ἐκδέχομαι); KJV: looking for

G1562 ἐκδύω (ekdýō): to cause to sink out of, i.e. (specially as of clothing) to divest. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G1416 (δύνω); KJV: strip, take off from, unclothe

G1563 ἐκεῖ (ekeî): there; by extension, thither. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: there, thither(-ward), (to) yonder (place)

G1564 ἐκεῖθεν (ekeîthen): thence. Origin: from G1563 (ἐκεῖ); KJV: from that place, (from) thence, there

G1565 ἐκεῖνος (ekeînos): that one (or (neuter) thing); often intensified by the article prefixed. Origin: from G1563 (ἐκεῖ); KJV: he, it, the other (same), selfsame, that (same, very), X their, X them, they, this, those

G1566 ἐκεῖσε (ekeîse): thither. Origin: from G1563 (ἐκεῖ); KJV: there

G1567 ἐκζητέω (ekzētéō): to search out, i.e. (figuratively)investigate, crave, demand, (by Hebraism) worship. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2212 (ζητέω); KJV: en- (re-)quire, seek after (carefully, diligently)

G1568 ἐκθαμβέω (ekthambéō): to astonish utterly. Origin: from G1569 (ἔκθαμβος); KJV: affright, greatly (sore) amaze

G1569 ἔκθαμβος (ékthambos): utterly astounded. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2285 (θάμβος); KJV: greatly wondering

G1570 ἔκθετος (ékthetos): put out, i.e. exposed to perish. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: cast out

G1571 ἐκκαθαίρω (ekkathaírō): to cleanse thoroughly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2508 (καθαίρω); KJV: purge (out)

G1572 ἐκκαίω (ekkaíō): to inflame deeply. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2545 (καίω); KJV: burn

G1573 ἐκκακέω (ekkakéō): to be (bad or) weak, i.e. (by implication) to fail (in heart). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2556 (κακός); KJV: faint, be weary

G1574 ἐκκεντέω (ekkentéō): to transfix. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G2759 (κέντρον); KJV: pierce

G1575 ἐκκλάω (ekkláō): to exscind. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2806 (κλάω); KJV: break off

G1576 ἐκκλείω (ekkleíō): to shut out (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2808 (κλείω); KJV: exclude

G1577 ἐκκλησία (ekklēsía): a calling out, i.e. (concretely) a popular meeting, especially a religious congregation (Jewish synagogue, or Christian community of members on earth or saints in heaven or both). Origin: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G2564 (καλέω); KJV: assembly, church

G1578 ἐκκλίνω (ekklínō): to deviate, i.e. (absolutely) to shun (literally or figuratively), or (relatively) to decline (from piety). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: avoid, eschew, go out of the way

G1579 ἐκκολυμβάω (ekkolymbáō): to escape by swimming. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2860 (κολυμβάω); KJV: swim out

G1580 ἐκκομίζω (ekkomízō): to bear forth (to burial). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2865 (κομίζω); KJV: carry out

G1581 ἐκκόπτω (ekkóptō): to exscind; figuratively, to frustrate. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: cut down (off, out), hew down, hinder

G1582 ἐκκρέμαμαι (ekkrémamai): to hang upon the lips of a speaker, i.e. listen closely. Origin: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2910 (κρεμάννυμι); KJV: be very attentive

G1583 ἐκλαλέω (eklaléō): to divulge. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: tell

G1584 ἐκλάμπω (eklámpō): to be resplendent. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2989 (λάμπω); KJV: shine forth

G1585 ἐκλανθάνομαι (eklanthánomai): to be utterly oblivious of. Origin: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2990 (λανθάνω); KJV: forget

G1586 ἐκλέγομαι (eklégomai): to select. Origin: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its primary sense); KJV: make choice, choose (out), chosen

G1587 ἐκλείπω (ekleípō): to omit, i.e. (by implication) cease (die). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: fail

G1588 ἐκλεκτός (eklektós): select; by implication, favorite. Origin: from G1586 (ἐκλέγομαι); KJV: chosen, elect

G1589 ἐκλογή (eklogḗ): (divine) selection (abstractly or concretely). Origin: from G1586 (ἐκλέγομαι); KJV: chosen, election

G1590 ἐκλύω (eklýō): to relax (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: faint

G1591 ἐκμάσσω (ekmássō): to knead out, i.e. (by analogy) to wipe dry. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι); KJV: wipe

G1592 ἐκμυκτηρίζω (ekmyktērízō): to sneer outright at. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3456 (μυκτηρίζω); KJV: deride

G1593 ἐκνεύω (ekneúō): (by analogy) to slip off, i.e. quietly withdraw. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3506 (νεύω); KJV: convey self away

G1594 ἐκνήφω (eknḗphō): (figuratively) to rouse (oneself) out of stupor. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3525 (νήφω); KJV: awake

G1595 ἑκούσιον (hekoúsion): voluntariness. Origin: neuter of a derivative from G1635 (ἑκών); KJV: willingly

G1596 ἑκουσίως (hekousíōs): voluntarily. Origin: adverb from the same as G1595 (ἑκούσιον); KJV: wilfully, willingly

G1597 ἔκπαλαι (ékpalai): long ago, for a long while. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3819 (πάλαι); KJV: of a long time, of old

G1598 ἐκπειράζω (ekpeirázō): to test thoroughly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3985 (πειράζω); KJV: tempt

G1599 ἐκπέμπω (ekpémpō): to despatch. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3992 (πέμπω); KJV: send away (forth)

G1600 ἐκπετάννυμι (ekpetánnymi): to fly out, i.e. (by analogy) to extend. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a form of G4072 (πέτομαι); KJV: stretch forth

G1601 ἐκπίπτω (ekpíptō): to drop away; specially, be driven out of one's course; figuratively, to lose, become inefficient. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: be cast, fail, fall (away, off), take none effect

G1602 ἐκπλέω (ekpléō): to depart by ship. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4126 (πλέω); KJV: sail (away, thence)

G1603 ἐκπληρόω (ekplēróō): to accomplish entirely. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4137 (πληρόω); KJV: fulfill

G1604 ἐκπλήρωσις (ekplḗrōsis): completion. Origin: from G1603 (ἐκπληρόω); KJV: accomplishment

G1605 ἐκπλήσσω (ekplḗssō): to strike with astonishment. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4141 (πλήσσω); KJV: amaze, astonish

G1606 ἐκπνέω (ekpnéō): to expire. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4154 (πνέω); KJV: give up the ghost

G1607 ἐκπορεύομαι (ekporeúomai): to depart, be discharged, proceed, project. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: come (forth, out of), depart, go (forth, out), issue, proceed (out of)

G1608 ἐκπορνεύω (ekporneúō): to be utterly unchaste. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4203 (πορνεύω); KJV: give self over to fornication

G1609 ἐκπτύω (ekptýō): to spit out, i.e. (figuratively) spurn. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4429 (πτύω); KJV: reject

G1610 ἐκριζόω (ekrizóō): to uproot. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4492 (ῥιζόω); KJV: pluck up by the root, root up

G1611 ἔκστασις (ékstasis): a displacement of the mind, i.e. bewilderment, "ecstasy". Origin: from G1839 (ἐξίστημι); KJV: + be amazed, amazement, astonishment, trance

G1612 ἐκστρέφω (ekstréphō): to pervert (figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: subvert

G1613 ἐκταράσσω (ektarássō): to disturb wholly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5015 (ταράσσω); KJV: exceedingly trouble

G1614 ἐκτείνω (ekteínō): to extend. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and teino (to stretch); KJV: cast, put forth, stretch forth (out)

G1615 ἐκτελέω (ekteléō): to complete fully. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5055 (τελέω); KJV: finish

G1616 ἐκτένεια (ekténeia): intentness. Origin: from G1618 (ἐκτενής); KJV: X instantly

G1617 ἐκτενέστερον (ektenésteron): more intently. Origin: neuter of the comparative of G1618 (ἐκτενής); KJV: more earnestly

G1618 ἐκτενής (ektenḗs): intent. Origin: from G1614 (ἐκτείνω); KJV: without ceasing, fervent

G1619 ἐκτενῶς (ektenōs): intently. Origin: adverb from G1618 (ἐκτενής); KJV: fervently

G1620 ἐκτίθημι (ektíthēmi): to expose; figuratively, to declare. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: cast out, expound

G1621 ἐκτινάσσω (ektinássō): to shake violently. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and tinasso (to swing); KJV: shake (off)

G1622 ἐκτός (ektós): the exterior; figuratively (as a preposition) aside from, besides. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ); KJV: but, except(-ed), other than, out of, outside, unless, without

G1623 ἕκτος (héktos): sixth. Origin: ordinal from G1803 (ἕξ); KJV: sixth

G1624 ἐκτρέπω (ektrépō): to deflect, i.e. turn away (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: avoid, turn (aside, out of the way)

G1625 ἐκτρέφω (ektréphō): to rear up to maturity, i.e. (genitive case) to cherish or train. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: bring up, nourish

G1626 ἔκτρωμα (éktrōma): a miscarriage (abortion), i.e. (by analogy) untimely birth. Origin: from a comparative of G1537 (ἐκ) and (to wound); KJV: born out of due time

G1627 ἐκφέρω (ekphérō): to bear out (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bear, bring forth, carry forth (out)

G1628 ἐκφεύγω (ekpheúgō): to flee out. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5343 (φεύγω); KJV: escape, flee

G1629 ἐκφοβέω (ekphobéō): to frighten utterly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5399 (φοβέω); KJV: terrify

G1630 ἔκφοβος (ékphobos): frightened out of one's wits. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5401 (φόβος); KJV: sore afraid, exceedingly fear

G1631 ἐκφύω (ekphýō): to sprout up. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5453 (φύω); KJV: put forth

G1632 ἐκχέω (ekchéō): to pour forth; figuratively, to bestow. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and (to pour); KJV: gush (pour) out, run greedily (out), shed (abroad, forth), spill

G1633 ἐκχωρέω (ekchōréō): to depart. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5562 (χωρέω); KJV: depart out

G1634 ἐκψύχω (ekpsýchō): to expire. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5594 (ψύχω); KJV: give (yield) up the ghost

G1635 ἑκών (hekṓn): voluntary. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: willingly

G1636 ἐλαία (elaía): an olive (the tree or the fruit). Origin: feminine of a presumed derivative from an obsolete primary; KJV: olive (berry, tree)

G1637 ἔλαιον (élaion): olive oil. Origin: neuter of the same as G1636 (ἐλαία); KJV: oil

G1638 ἐλαιών (elaiṓn): an olive-orchard, i.e. (specially) the Mount of Olives. Origin: from G1636 (ἐλαία); KJV: Olivet

G1639 Ἐλαμίτης (Elamítēs): an Elamite or Persian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5867); KJV: Elamite

G1640 ἐλάσσων (elássōn): smaller (in size, quantity, age or quality). Origin: comparative of the same as G1646 (ἐλάχιστος); KJV: less, under, worse, younger

G1641 ἐλαττονέω (elattonéō): to diminish, i.e. fall short. Origin: from G1640 (ἐλάσσων); KJV: have lack

G1642 ἐλαττόω (elattóō): to lessen (in rank or influence). Origin: from G1640 (ἐλάσσων); KJV: decrease, make lower

G1643 ἐλαύνω (elaúnō): to push (as wind, oars or dæmonical power). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb (obsolete except in certain tenses as an alternative of this) of uncertain affinity; KJV: carry, drive, row

G1644 ἐλαφρία (elaphría): levity (figuratively), i.e. fickleness. Origin: from G1645 (ἐλαφρός); KJV: lightness

G1645 ἐλαφρός (elaphrós): light, i.e. easy. Origin: probably akin to G1643 (ἐλαύνω) and the base of G1640 (ἐλάσσων); KJV: light

G1646 ἐλάχιστος (eláchistos): used as equivalent to G3398 (μικρός); least (in size, amount, dignity, etc.). Origin: superlative of (short); KJV: least, very little (small), smallest

G1647 ἐλαχιστότερος (elachistóteros): far less. Origin: comparative of G1646 (ἐλάχιστος); KJV: less than the least

G1648 Ἐλεάζαρ (Eleázar): Eleazar, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H499); KJV: Eleazar

G1649 ἔλεγξις (élenxis): refutation, i.e. reproof. Origin: from G1651 (ἐλέγχω); KJV: rebuke

G1650 ἔλεγχος (élenchos): proof, conviction. Origin: from G1651 (ἐλέγχω); KJV: evidence, reproof

G1651 ἐλέγχω (elénchō): to confute, admonish. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: convict, convince, tell a fault, rebuke, reprove

G1652 ἐλεεινός (eleeinós): pitiable. Origin: from G1656 (ἔλεος); KJV: miserable

G1653 ἐλεέω (eleéō): to compassionate (by word or deed, specially, by divine grace). Origin: from G1656 (ἔλεος); KJV: have compassion (pity on), have (obtain, receive, shew) mercy (on)

G1654 ἐλεημοσύνη (eleēmosýnē): compassionateness, i.e. (as exercised towards the poor) beneficence, or (concretely) a benefaction. Origin: from G1656 (ἔλεος); KJV: alms(-deeds)

G1655 ἐλεήμων (eleḗmōn): compassionate (actively). Origin: from G1653 (ἐλεέω); KJV: merciful

G1656 ἔλεος (éleos): compassion (human or divine, especially active). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: (+ tender) mercy

G1657 ἐλευθερία (eleuthería): freedom (legitimate or licentious, chiefly moral or ceremonial). Origin: from G1658 (ἐλεύθερος); KJV: liberty

G1658 ἐλεύθερος (eleútheros): unrestrained (to go at pleasure), i.e. (as a citizen) not a slave (whether freeborn or manumitted), or (genitive case) exempt (from obligation or liability). Origin: probably from the alternate of G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: free (man, woman), at liberty

G1659 ἐλευθερόω (eleutheróō): to liberate, i.e. (figuratively) to exempt (from moral, ceremonial or mortal liability). Origin: from G1658 (ἐλεύθερος); KJV: deliver, make free

G1660 ἔλευσις (éleusis): an advent. Origin: from the alternate of G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: coming

G1661 ἐλεφάντινος (elephántinos): elephantine, i.e. (by implication) composed of ivory. Origin: from (an "elephant"); KJV: of ivory

G1662 Ἐλιακείμ (Eliakeím): Eliakim, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H471); KJV: Eliakim

G1663 Ἐλιέζερ (Eliézer): Eliezer, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H461); KJV: Eliezer

G1664 Ἐλιούδ (Elioúd): God of majesty; Eliud, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H410 and H1935); KJV: Eliud

G1665 Ἐλισάβετ (Elisábet): Elisabet, an Israelitess. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H472); KJV: Elisabeth

G1666 Ἐλισσαῖος (Elissaîos): Elissæus, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H477); KJV: Elissæus

G1667 ἑλίσσω (helíssō): to coil or wrap. Origin: a form of G1507 (εἱλίσσω); KJV: fold up

G1668 ἕλκος (hélkos): an ulcer (as if drawn together). Origin: probably from G1670 (ἑλκύω); KJV: sore

G1669 ἑλκόω (helkóō): to cause to ulcerate, i.e. (passively) be ulcerous. Origin: from G1668 (ἕλκος); KJV: full of sores

G1670 ἑλκύω (helkýō): to drag (literally or figuratively). Origin: probably akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: draw

G1671 Ἑλλάς (Hellás): Hellas (or Greece), a country of Europe. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: Greece

G1672 Ἕλλην (Héllēn): a Hellen (Grecian) or inhabitant of Hellas; by extension a Greek-speaking person, especially a non-Jew. Origin: from G1671 (Ἑλλάς); KJV: Gentile, Greek

G1673 Ἑλληνικός (Hellēnikós): Hellenic, i.e. Grecian (in language). Origin: from G1672 (Ἕλλην); KJV: Greek

G1674 Ἑλληνίς (Hellēnís): a Grecian (i.e. non-Jewish) woman. Origin: feminine of G1672 (Ἕλλην); KJV: Greek

G1675 Ἑλληνιστής (Hellēnistḗs): a Hellenist or Greek-speaking Jew. Origin: from a derivative of G1672 (Ἕλλην); KJV: Grecian

G1676 Ἑλληνιστί (Hellēnistí): Hellenistically, i.e. in the Grecian language. Origin: adverb from the same as G1675 (Ἑλληνιστής); KJV: Greek

G1677 ἐλλογέω (ellogéō): to reckon in, i.e. attribute. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3056 (λόγος) (in the sense of account); KJV: impute, put on account

G1678 Ἐλμωδάμ (Elmōdám): Elmodam, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (perhaps for H486); KJV: Elmodam

G1679 ἐλπίζω (elpízō): to expect or confide. Origin: from G1680 (ἐλπίς); KJV: (have, thing) hope(-d) (for), trust

G1680 ἐλπίς (elpís): expectation (abstractly or concretely) or confidence. Origin: from a primary (to anticipate, usually with pleasure); KJV: faith, hope

G1681 Ἐλύμας (Elýmas): Elymas, a wizard. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Elymas

G1682 ἐλοΐ (eloḯ): Origin: of Chaldean origin (H426 with pronominal suffix) my God KJV: Eloi

G1683 ἐμαυτοῦ (emautoû): of myself so likewise the dative case , and accusative case. Origin: genitive case compound of G1700 (ἐμοῦ) and G846 (αὐτός); KJV: me, mine own (self), myself

G1684 ἐμβαίνω (embaínō): to walk on, i.e. embark (aboard a vessel), reach (a pool). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: come (get) into, enter (into), go (up) into, step in, take ship

G1685 ἐμβάλλω (embállō): to throw on, i.e. (figuratively) subject to (eternal punishment). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: cast into

G1686 ἐμβάπτω (embáptō): to whelm on, i.e. wet (a part of the person, etc.) by contact with a fluid. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G911 (βάπτω); KJV: dip

G1687 ἐμβατεύω (embateúō): equivalent to G1684 (ἐμβαίνω); to intrude on (figuratively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and a presumed derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: intrude into

G1688 ἐμβιβάζω (embibázō): causative of G1684 (ἐμβαίνω)); to place on, i.e. transfer (aboard a vessel). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to mount; KJV: put in

G1689 ἐμβλέπω (emblépō): to look on, i.e. (relatively) to observe fixedly, or (absolutely) to discern clearly. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: behold, gaze up, look upon, (could) see
