G1690 ἐμβριμάομαι (embrimáomai): to have indignation on, i.e. (transitively) to blame, (intransitively) to sigh with chagrin, (specially) to sternly enjoin. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to snort with anger); KJV: straitly charge, groan, murmur against

G1691 ἐμέ (emé): me. Origin: a prolonged form of G3165 (μέ); KJV: I, me, my(-self)

G1692 ἐμέω (eméō): to vomit. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: (will) spue

G1693 ἐμμαίνομαι (emmaínomai): to rave on, i.e. rage at. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3105 (μαίνομαι); KJV: be mad against

G1694 Ἐμμανουήλ (Emmanouḗl): God with us; Emmanuel, a name of Christ. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6005); KJV: Emmanuel

G1695 Ἐμμαούς (Emmaoús): Emmaus, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H3222); KJV: Emmaus

G1696 ἐμμένω (emménō): to stay in the same place, i.e. (figuratively) persevere. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: continue

G1697 Ἐμμόρ (Emmór): Emmor (i.e. Chamor), a Canaanite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2544); KJV: Emmor

G1698 ἐμοί (emoí): to me. Origin: a prolonged form of G3427 (μοί); KJV: I, me, mine, my

G1699 ἐμός (emós): my. Origin: from the oblique cases of G1473 (ἐγώ) (G1698 (ἐμοί), G1700 (ἐμοῦ), G1691 (ἐμέ)); KJV: of me, mine (own), my

G1700 ἐμοῦ (emoû): of me. Origin: a prolonged form of G3449 (μόχθος); KJV: me, mine, my

G1701 ἐμπαιγμός (empaigmós): derision. Origin: from G1702 (ἐμπαίζω); KJV: mocking

G1702 ἐμπαίζω (empaízō): to jeer at, i.e. deride. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3815 (παίζω); KJV: mock

G1703 ἐμπαίκτης (empaíktēs): a derider, i.e. (by implication) a false teacher. Origin: from G1702 (ἐμπαίζω); KJV: mocker, scoffer

G1704 ἐμπεριπατέω (emperipatéō): to perambulate on a place, i.e. (figuratively) to be occupied among persons. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4043 (περιπατέω); KJV: walk in

G1705 ἐμπίπλημι (empíplēmi): to fill in (up), i.e. (by implication) to satisfy (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G4118 (πλεῖστος); KJV: fill

G1706 ἐμπίπτω (empíptō): to fall on, i.e. (literally) to be entrapped by, or (figuratively) be overwhelmed with. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall among (into)

G1707 ἐμπλέκω (emplékō): to entwine, i.e. (figuratively) involve with. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4120 (πλέκω); KJV: entangle (in, self with)

G1708 ἐμπλοκή (emplokḗ): elaborate braiding of the hair. Origin: from G1707 (ἐμπλέκω); KJV: plaiting

G1709 ἐμπνέω (empnéō): to inhale, i.e. (figuratively) to be animated by (bent upon). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4154 (πνέω); KJV: breathe

G1710 ἐμπορεύομαι (emporeúomai): to travel in (a country as a pedlar), i.e. (by implication) to trade. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: buy and sell, make merchandise

G1711 ἐμπορία (emporía): traffic. Origin: feminine from G1713 (ἔμπορος); KJV: merchandise

G1712 ἐμπόριον (empórion): a mart ("emporium"). Origin: neuter from G1713 (ἔμπορος); KJV: merchandise

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1713 to G1852
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1713 ἔμπορος (émporos): a (wholesale) tradesman. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: merchant

G1714 ἐμπρήθω (emprḗthō): to enkindle, i.e. set on fire. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to blow a flame); KJV: burn up

G1715 ἔμπροσθεν (émprosthen): in front of (in place (literally or figuratively) or time). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4314 (πρός); KJV: against, at, before, (in presence, sight) of

G1716 ἐμπτύω (emptýō): to spit at or on. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G4429 (πτύω); KJV: spit (upon)

G1717 ἐμφανής (emphanḗs): apparent in self. Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: manifest, openly

G1718 ἐμφανίζω (emphanízō): to exhibit (in person) or disclose (by words). Origin: from G1717 (ἐμφανής); KJV: appear, declare (plainly), inform, (will) manifest, shew, signify

G1719 ἔμφοβος (émphobos): in fear, i.e. alarmed. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5401 (φόβος); KJV: affrighted, afraid, tremble

G1720 ἐμφυσάω (emphysáō): to blow at or on. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to puff) (compare G5453 (φύω)); KJV: breathe on

G1721 ἔμφυτος (émphytos): implanted (figuratively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω); KJV: engrafted

G1722 ἐν (en): "in," at, (up-)on, by, etc. Origin: a primary preposition denoting (fixed) position (in place, time or state), and (by implication) instrumentality (medially or constructively), i.e. a relation of rest (intermediate between G1519 (εἰς) and G1537 (ἐκ)); KJV: about, after, against, + almost, X altogether, among, X as, at, before, between, (here-)by (+ all means), for (… sake of), + give self wholly to, (here-)in(-to, -wardly), X mightily, (because) of, (up-)on, (open-)ly, X outwardly, one, X quickly, X shortly, (speedi-)ly, X that, X there(-in, -on), through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), under, when, where(-with), while, with(-in)

G1723 ἐναγκαλίζομαι (enankalízomai): to take in one's arms, i.e. embrace. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G43 (ἀγκάλη); KJV: take up in arms

G1724 ἐνάλιος (enálios): in the sea, i.e. marine. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G251 (ἅλς); KJV: thing in the sea

G1725 ἔναντι (énanti): in front (i.e. figuratively, presence) of. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G473 (ἀντί); KJV: before

G1726 ἐναντίον (enantíon): (adverbially) in the presence (view) of. Origin: neuter of G1727 (ἐναντίος); KJV: before, in the presence of

G1727 ἐναντίος (enantíos): opposite; figuratively, antagonistic. Origin: from G1725 (ἔναντι); KJV: (over) against, contrary

G1728 ἐνάρχομαι (enárchomai): to commence on. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G756 (ἄρχομαι); KJV: rule (by mistake for G757 (ἄρχω))

G1729 ἐνδεής (endeḗs): deficient in. Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G1210 (δέω) (in the sense of lacking); KJV: lacking

G1730 ἔνδειγμα (éndeigma): an indication (concretely). Origin: from G1731 (ἐνδείκνυμι); KJV: manifest token

G1731 ἐνδείκνυμι (endeíknymi): to indicate (by word or act). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: do, show (forth)

G1732 ἔνδειξις (éndeixis): indication (abstractly). Origin: from G1731 (ἐνδείκνυμι); KJV: declare, evident token, proof

G1733 ἕνδεκα (héndeka): one and ten, i.e. eleven. Origin: from (the neuter of) G1520 (εἷς) and G1176 (δέκα); KJV: eleven

G1734 ἑνδέκατος (hendékatos): eleventh. Origin: ordinal from G1733 (ἕνδεκα); KJV: eleventh

G1735 ἐνδέχεται (endéchetai): (impersonally) it is accepted in, i.e. admitted (possible). Origin: third person singular present of a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: can (+ not) be

G1736 ἐνδημέω (endēméō): to be in one's own country, i.e. home (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: be at home (present)

G1737 ἐνδιδύσκω (endidýskō): to invest (with a garment). Origin: a prolonged form of G1746 (ἐνδύω); KJV: clothe in, wear

G1738 ἔνδικος (éndikos): in the right, i.e. equitable. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1349 (δίκη); KJV: just

G1739 ἐνδόμησις (endómēsis): a housing in (residence), i.e. structure. Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of the base of G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: building

G1740 ἐνδοξάζω (endoxázō): to glorify. Origin: from G1741 (ἔνδοξος); KJV: glorify

G1741 ἔνδοξος (éndoxos): in glory, i.e. splendid, (figuratively) noble. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1391 (δόξα); KJV: glorious, gorgeous(-ly), honourable

G1742 ἔνδυμα (éndyma): apparel (especially the outer robe). Origin: from G1746 (ἐνδύω); KJV: clothing, garment, raiment

G1743 ἐνδυναμόω (endynamóō): to empower. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1412 (δυναμόω); KJV: enable, (increase in) strength(-en), be (make) strong

G1744 ἐνδύνω (endýnō): to sink (by implication, wrap (compare G1746 (ἐνδύω)) on, i.e. (figuratively) sneak. Origin: from G1772 (ἔννομος) and G1416 (δύνω); KJV: creep

G1745 ἔνδυσις (éndysis): investment with clothing. Origin: from G1746 (ἐνδύω); KJV: putting on

G1746 ἐνδύω (endýō): to invest with clothing (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G1416 (δύνω) (in the sense of sinking into a garment); KJV: array, clothe (with), endue, have (put) on

G1747 ἐνέδρα (enédra): an ambuscade, i.e. (figuratively) murderous purpose. Origin: feminine from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: lay wait

G1748 ἐνεδρεύω (enedreúō): to lurk, i.e. (figuratively) plot assassination. Origin: from G1747 (ἐνέδρα); KJV: lay wait for

G1749 ἔνεδρον (énedron): an ambush, i.e. (figuratively) murderous design. Origin: neuter of the same as G1747 (ἐνέδρα); KJV: lying in wait

G1750 ἐνειλέω (eneiléō): to enwrap. Origin: from G1772 (ἔννομος) and the base of G1507 (εἱλίσσω); KJV: wrap in

G1751 ἔνειμι (éneimi): to be within (neuter participle plural). Origin: from G1772 (ἔννομος) and G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: such things as … have

G1752 ἕνεκα (héneka): on account of. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: because, for (cause, sake), (where-)fore, by reason of, that

G1753 ἐνέργεια (enérgeia): efficiency ("energy"). Origin: from G1756 (ἐνεργής); KJV: operation, strong, (effectual) working

G1754 ἐνεργέω (energéō): to be active, efficient. Origin: from G1756 (ἐνεργής); KJV: do, (be) effectual (fervent), be mighty in, shew forth self, work (effectually in)

G1755 ἐνέργημα (enérgēma): an effect. Origin: from G1754 (ἐνεργέω); KJV: operation, working

G1756 ἐνεργής (energḗs): active, operative. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: effectual, powerful

G1757 ἐνευλογέω (eneulogéō): to confer a benefit on. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2127 (εὐλογέω); KJV: bless

G1758 ἐνέχω (enéchō): to hold in or upon, i.e. ensnare; by implication, to keep a grudge. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: entangle with, have a quarrel against, urge

G1759 ἐνθάδε (entháde): properly, within, i.e. (of place) here, hither. Origin: from a prolonged form of G1722 (ἐν); KJV: (t-)here, hither

G1760 ἐνθυμέομαι (enthyméomai): to be inspirited, i.e. ponder. Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: think

G1761 ἐνθύμησις (enthýmēsis): deliberation. Origin: from G1760 (ἐνθυμέομαι); KJV: device, thought

G1762 ἔνι (éni): impersonally, there is in or among. Origin: contraction for the third person singular present indicative of G1751 (ἔνειμι); KJV: be, (there) is

G1763 ἐνιαυτός (eniautós): a year. Origin: prolongation from a primary (a year); KJV: year

G1764 ἐνίστημι (enístēmi): to place on hand, i.e. (reflexively) impend, (participle) be instant. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: come, be at hand, present

G1765 ἐνισχύω (enischýō): to invigorate (transitively or reflexively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G2480 (ἰσχύω); KJV: strengthen

G1766 ἔννατος (énnatos): ninth. Origin: ordinal from G1767 (ἐννέα); KJV: ninth

G1767 ἐννέα (ennéa): nine. Origin: a primary number; KJV: nine

G1768 ἐννενηκονταεννέα (ennenēkontaennéa): ninety-nine. Origin: from a (tenth) multiple of G1767 (ἐννέα) and G1767 (ἐννέα) itself; KJV: ninety and nine

G1769 ἐννεός (enneós): dumb (as making signs), i.e. silent from astonishment. Origin: from G1770 (ἐννεύω); KJV: speechless

G1770 ἐννεύω (enneúō): to nod at, i.e. beckon or communicate by gesture. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3506 (νεύω); KJV: make signs

G1771 ἔννοια (énnoia): thoughtfulness, i.e. moral understanding. Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3563 (νοῦς); KJV: intent, mind

G1772 ἔννομος (énnomos): (subjectively) legal, or (objectively) subject to. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3551 (νόμος); KJV: lawful, under law

G1773 ἔννυχον (énnychon): (adverbially) by night. Origin: neuter of a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3571 (νύξ); KJV: before day

G1774 ἐνοικέω (enoikéō): to inhabit (figuratively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: dwell in

G1775 ἑνότης (henótēs): oneness, i.e. (figuratively) unanimity. Origin: from G1520 (εἷς); KJV: unity

G1776 ἐνοχλέω (enochléō): to crowd in, i.e. (figuratively) to annoy. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G3791 (ὀχλέω); KJV: trouble

G1777 ἔνοχος (énochos): liable to (a condition, penalty or imputation). Origin: from G1758 (ἐνέχω); KJV: in danger of, guilty of, subject to

G1778 ἔνταλμα (éntalma): an injunction, i.e. religious precept. Origin: from G1781 (ἐντέλλομαι); KJV: commandment

G1779 ἐνταφιάζω (entaphiázō): to inswathe with cerements for interment. Origin: from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G5028 (τάφος); KJV: bury

G1780 ἐνταφιασμός (entaphiasmós): preparation for interment. Origin: from G1779 (ἐνταφιάζω); KJV: burying

G1781 ἐντέλλομαι (entéllomai): to enjoin. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G5056 (τέλος); KJV: (give) charge, (give) command(-ments), injoin

G1782 ἐντεῦθεν (enteûthen): hence (literally or figuratively); (repeated) on both sides. Origin: from the same as G1759 (ἐνθάδε); KJV: (from) hence, on either side

G1783 ἔντευξις (énteuxis): an interview, i.e. (specially) supplication. Origin: from G1793 (ἐντυγχάνω); KJV: intercession, prayer

G1784 ἔντιμος (éntimos): valued (figuratively). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: dear, more honourable, precious, in reputation

G1785 ἐντολή (entolḗ): injunction, i.e. an authoritative prescription. Origin: from G1781 (ἐντέλλομαι); KJV: commandment, precept

G1786 ἐντόπιος (entópios): a resident. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5117 (τόπος); KJV: of that place

G1787 ἐντός (entós): inside (adverb or noun). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν); KJV: within

G1788 ἐντρέπω (entrépō): to invert, i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) in a good sense, to respect; or in a bad one, to confound. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: regard, (give) reference, shame

G1789 ἐντρέφω (entréphō): (figuratively) to educate. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: nourish up in

G1790 ἔντρομος (éntromos): terrified. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5156 (τρόμος); KJV: X quake, X trembled

G1791 ἐντροπή (entropḗ): confusion. Origin: from G1788 (ἐντρέπω); KJV: shame

G1792 ἐντρυφάω (entrypháō): to revel in. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5171 (τρυφάω); KJV: sporting selves

G1793 ἐντυγχάνω (entynchánō): to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) confer with; by extension to entreat (in favor or against). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5177 (τυγχάνω); KJV: deal with, make intercession

G1794 ἐντυλίσσω (entylíssō): probably akin to G1507 (εἱλίσσω)); to entwine, i.e. wind up in. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and (to twist; KJV: wrap in (together)

G1795 ἐντυπόω (entypóō): to enstamp, i.e. engrave. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G5179 (τύπος); KJV: engrave

G1796 ἐνυβρίζω (enybrízō): to insult. Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5195 (ὑβρίζω); KJV: do despite unto

G1797 ἐνυπνιάζομαι (enypniázomai): to dream. Origin: middle voice from G1798 (ἐνύπνιον); KJV: dream(-er)

G1798 ἐνύπνιον (enýpnion): something seen in sleep, i.e. a dream (vision in a dream). Origin: from G1722 (ἐν) and G5258 (ὕπνος); KJV: dream

G1799 ἐνώπιον (enṓpion): in the face of (literally or figuratively). Origin: neuter of a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: before, in the presence (sight) of, to

G1800 Ἐνώς (Enṓs): Enos (i.e. Enosh), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H583); KJV: Enos

G1801 ἐνωτίζομαι (enōtízomai): to take in one's ear, i.e. to listen. Origin: middle voice from a compound of G1722 (ἐν) and G3775 (οὖς); KJV: hearken

G1802 Ἐνώχ (Enṓch): Enoch (i.e. Chanok), an antediluvian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2585); KJV: Enoch

G1803 ἕξ (héx): six. Origin: a primary numeral; KJV: six

G1804 ἐξαγγέλλω (exangéllō): to publish, i.e. celebrate. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: shew forth

G1805 ἐξαγοράζω (exagorázō): to buy up, i.e. ransom; figuratively, to rescue from loss (improve opportunity). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G59 (ἀγοράζω); KJV: redeem

G1806 ἐξάγω (exágō): to lead forth. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring forth (out), fetch (lead) out

G1807 ἐξαιρέω (exairéō): actively, to tear out; middle voice, to select; figuratively, to release. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: deliver, pluck out, rescue

G1808 ἐξαίρω (exaírō): to remove. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G142 (αἴρω); KJV: put (take) away

G1809 ἐξαιτέομαι (exaitéomai): to demand (for trial). Origin: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: desire

G1810 ἐξαίφνης (exaíphnēs): of a sudden (unexpectedly). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the base of G160 (αἰφνίδιος); KJV: suddenly

G1811 ἐξακολουθέω (exakolouthéō): to follow out, i.e. (figuratively) to imitate, obey, yield to. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G190 (ἀκολουθέω); KJV: follow

G1812 ἑξακόσιοι (hexakósioi): six hundred. Origin: plural ordinal from G1803 (ἕξ) and G1540 (ἑκατόν); KJV: six hundred

G1813 ἐξαλείφω (exaleíphō): to smear out, i.e. obliterate (erase tears, figuratively, pardon sin). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G218 (ἀλείφω); KJV: blot out, wipe away

G1814 ἐξάλλομαι (exállomai): to spring forth. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G242 (ἅλλομαι); KJV: leap up

G1815 ἐξανάστασις (exanástasis): a rising from death. Origin: from G1817 (ἐξανίστημι); KJV: resurrection

G1816 ἐξανατέλλω (exanatéllō): to start up out of the ground, i.e. germinate. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G393 (ἀνατέλλω); KJV: spring up

G1817 ἐξανίστημι (exanístēmi): objectively, to produce, i.e. (figuratively) beget; subjectively, to arise, i.e. (figuratively) object. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G450 (ἀνίστημι); KJV: raise (rise) up

G1818 ἐξαπατάω (exapatáō): to seduce wholly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G538 (ἀπατάω); KJV: beguile, deceive

G1819 ἐξάπινα (exápina): of a sudden, i.e. unexpectedly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of the same as G160 (αἰφνίδιος); KJV: suddenly

G1820 ἐξαπορέομαι (exaporéomai): to be utterly at a loss, i.e. despond. Origin: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G639 (ἀπορέω); KJV: (in) despair

G1821 ἐξαποστέλλω (exapostéllō): to send away forth, i.e. (on a mission) to despatch, or (peremptorily) to dismiss. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G649 (ἀποστέλλω); KJV: send (away, forth, out)

G1822 ἐξαρτίζω (exartízō): to finish out (time); figuratively, to equip fully (a teacher). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of G739 (ἄρτιος); KJV: accomplish, thoroughly furnish

G1823 ἐξαστράπτω (exastráptō): to lighten forth, i.e. (figuratively) to be radiant (of very white garments). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G797 (ἀστράπτω); KJV: glistening

G1824 ἐξαυτῆς (exautēs): from that hour, i.e. instantly. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and the genitive case singular feminine of G846 (αὐτός) (G5610 (ὥρα) being understood); KJV: by and by, immediately, presently, straightway

G1825 ἐξεγείρω (exegeírō): to rouse fully, i.e. (figuratively) to resuscitate (from death), release (from infliction). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1453 (ἐγείρω); KJV: raise up

G1826 ἔξειμι (éxeimi): to issue, i.e. leave (a place), escape (to the shore). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and (to go); KJV: depart, get (to land), go out

G1827 ἐξελέγχω (exelénchō): to convict fully, i.e. (by implication) to punish. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1651 (ἐλέγχω); KJV: convince

G1828 ἐξέλκω (exélkō): to drag forth, i.e. (figuratively) to entice (to sin). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G1670 (ἑλκύω); KJV: draw away

G1829 ἐξέραμα (exérama): vomit, i.e. food disgorged. Origin: from a comparative of G1537 (ἐκ) and a presumed (to spue); KJV: vomit

G1830 ἐξερευνάω (exereunáō): to explore (figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2045 (ἐρευνάω); KJV: search diligently

G1831 ἐξέρχομαι (exérchomai): to issue (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: come (forth, out), depart (out of), escape, get out, go (abroad, away, forth, out, thence), proceed (forth), spread abroad

G1832 ἔξεστι (éxesti): so also neuter present participle of the same (with or without some form of G1510 (εἰμί) expressed); impersonally, it is right (through the figurative idea of being out in public). Origin: third person singular present indicative of a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: be lawful, let, X may(-est)

G1833 ἐξετάζω (exetázō): to test thoroughly (by questions), i.e. ascertain or interrogate. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and (to examine); KJV: ask, enquire, search

G1834 ἐξηγέομαι (exēgéomai): to consider out (aloud), i.e. rehearse, unfold. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: declare, tell

G1835 ἑξήκοντα (hexḗkonta): sixty. Origin: the tenth multiple of G1803 (ἕξ); KJV: sixty(-fold), threescore

G1836 ἑξῆς (hexēs): successive. Origin: from G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of taking hold of, i.e. adjoining); KJV: after, following, X morrow, next

G1837 ἐξηχέομαι (exēchéomai): to "echo" forth, i.e. resound (be generally reported). Origin: middle voice from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2278 (ἠχέω); KJV: sound forth

G1838 ἕξις (héxis): habit, i.e. (by implication) practice. Origin: from G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: use

G1839 ἐξίστημι (exístēmi): to put (stand) out of wits, i.e. astound, or (reflexively) become astounded, insane. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: amaze, be (make) astonished, be beside self (selves), bewitch, wonder

G1840 ἐξισχύω (exischýō): to have full strength, i.e. be entirely competent. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G2480 (ἰσχύω); KJV: be able

G1841 ἔξοδος (éxodos): an exit, i.e. (figuratively) death. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3598 (ὁδός); KJV: decease, departing

G1842 ἐξολοθρεύω (exolothreúō): to extirpate. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3645 (ὀλοθρεύω); KJV: destroy

G1843 ἐξομολογέω (exomologéō): to acknowledge or (by implication, of assent) agree fully. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3670 (ὁμολογέω); KJV: confess, profess, promise

G1844 ἐξορκίζω (exorkízō): to exact an oath, i.e. conjure. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3726 (ὁρκίζω); KJV: adjure

G1845 ἐξορκιστής (exorkistḗs): one that binds by an oath (or spell), i.e. (by implication) an "exorcist" (conjurer). Origin: from G1844 (ἐξορκίζω); KJV: exorcist

G1846 ἐξορύσσω (exorýssō): to dig out, i.e. (by extension) to extract (an eye), remove (roofing). Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G3736 (ὀρύσσω); KJV: break up, pluck out

G1847 ἐξουδενόω (exoudenóō): to make utterly nothing of, i.e. despise. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and a derivative of the neuter of G3762 (οὐδείς); KJV: set at nought

G1848 ἐξουθενέω (exouthenéō): Origin: a variation of G1847 (ἐξουδενόω) and meaning the same KJV: contemptible, despise, least esteemed, set at nought

G1849 ἐξουσία (exousía): privilege, i.e. (subjectively) force, capacity, competency, freedom, or (objectively) mastery (concretely, magistrate, superhuman, potentate, token of control), delegated influence. Origin: from G1832 (ἔξεστι) (in the sense of ability); KJV: authority, jurisdiction, liberty, power, right, strength

G1850 ἐξουσιάζω (exousiázō): to control. Origin: from G1849 (ἐξουσία); KJV: exercise authority upon, bring under the (have) power of

G1851 ἐξοχή (exochḗ): prominence (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G1537 (ἐκ) and G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to stand out); KJV: principal

G1852 ἐξυπνίζω (exypnízō): to waken. Origin: from G1853 (ἔξυπνος); KJV: awake out of sleep

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1853 to G1983
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1853 ἔξυπνος (éxypnos): awake. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and G5258 (ὕπνος); KJV: X out of sleep

G1854 ἔξω (éxō): out(-side, of doors), literally or figuratively. Origin: adverb from G1537 (ἐκ); KJV: away, forth, (with-)out (of, -ward), strange

G1855 ἔξωθεν (éxōthen): external(-ly). Origin: from G1854 (ἔξω); KJV: out(-side, -ward, - wardly), (from) without

G1856 ἐξωθέω (exōthéō): to expel; by implication, to propel. Origin: from G1537 (ἐκ) and (to push); KJV: drive out, thrust in

G1857 ἐξώτερος (exṓteros): exterior. Origin: comparative of G1854 (ἔξω); KJV: outer

G1858 ἑορτάζω (heortázō): to observe a festival. Origin: from G1859 (ἑορτή); KJV: keep the feast

G1859 ἑορτή (heortḗ): a festival. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: feast, holyday

G1860 ἐπαγγελία (epangelía): an announcement (for information, assent or pledge; especially a divine assurance of good). Origin: from G1861 (ἐπαγγέλλω); KJV: message, promise

G1861 ἐπαγγέλλω (epangéllō): to announce upon (reflexively), i.e. (by implication) to engage to do something, to assert something respecting oneself. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: profess, (make) promise

G1862 ἐπάγγελμα (epángelma): a self-committal (by assurance of conferring some good). Origin: from G1861 (ἐπαγγέλλω); KJV: promise

G1863 ἐπάγω (epágō): to superinduce, i.e. inflict (an evil), charge (a crime). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring upon

G1864 ἐπαγωνίζομαι (epagōnízomai): to struggle for. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G75 (ἀγωνίζομαι); KJV: earnestly contend for

G1865 ἐπαθροίζω (epathroízō): to accumulate. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and (to assemble); KJV: gather thick together

G1866 Ἐπαίνετος (Epaínetos): praised; Epænetus, a Christian. Origin: from G1867 (ἐπαινέω); KJV: Epenetus

G1867 ἐπαινέω (epainéō): to applaud. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G134 (αἰνέω); KJV: commend, laud, praise

G1868 ἔπαινος (épainos): laudation; concretely, a commendable thing. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G134 (αἰνέω); KJV: praise

G1869 ἐπαίρω (epaírō): to raise up (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G142 (αἴρω); KJV: exalt self, poise (lift, take) up

G1870 ἐπαισχύνομαι (epaischýnomai): to feel shame for something. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G153 (αἰσχύνομαι); KJV: be ashamed

G1871 ἐπαιτέω (epaitéō): to ask for. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: beg

G1872 ἐπακολουθέω (epakolouthéō): to accompany. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G190 (ἀκολουθέω); KJV: follow (after)

G1873 ἐπακούω (epakoúō): to hearken (favorably) to. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: hear

G1874 ἐπακροάομαι (epakroáomai): to listen (intently) to. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G202 (ἀκροατής); KJV: hear

G1875 ἐπάν (epán): a particle of indefinite contemporaneousness; whenever, as soon as. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G302 (ἄν); KJV: when

G1876 ἐπάναγκες (epánankes): (adverbially) on necessity, i.e. necessarily. Origin: neuter of a presumed compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G318 (ἀνάγκη); KJV: necessary

G1877 ἐπανάγω (epanágō): to lead up on, i.e. (technical) to put out (to sea); (intransitively) to return. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G321 (ἀνάγω); KJV: launch (thrust) out, return

G1878 ἐπαναμιμνήσκω (epanamimnḗskō): to remind of. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G363 (ἀναμιμνήσκω); KJV: put in mind

G1879 ἐπαναπαύομαι (epanapaúomai): to settle on; literally (remain) or figuratively (rely). Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G373 (ἀναπαύω); KJV: rest in (upon)

G1880 ἐπανέρχομαι (epanérchomai): to come up on, i.e. return. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G424 (ἀνέρχομαι); KJV: come again, return

G1881 ἐπανίσταμαι (epanístamai): to stand up on, i.e. (figuratively) to attack. Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G450 (ἀνίστημι); KJV: rise up against

G1882 ἐπανόρθωσις (epanórthōsis): a straightening up again, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (reformation). Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G461 (ἀνορθόω); KJV: correction

G1883 ἐπάνω (epánō): up above, i.e. over or on (of place, amount, rank, etc.). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G507 (ἄνω); KJV: above, more than, (up-)on, over

G1884 ἐπαρκέω (eparkéō): to avail for, i.e. help. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G714 (ἀρκέω); KJV: relieve

G1885 ἐπαρχία (eparchía): a special region of government, i.e. a Roman præfecture. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G757 (ἄρχω) (meaning a governor of a district, "eparch"); KJV: province

G1886 ἔπαυλις (épaulis): a hut over the head, i.e. a dwelling. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and an equivalent of G833 (αὐλή); KJV: habitation

G1887 ἐπαύριον (epaúrion): occurring on the succeeding day, i.e. (G2250 (ἡμέρα) being implied) to-morrow. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G839 (αὔριον); KJV: day following, morrow, next day (after)

G1888 ἐπαυτοφώρῳ (epautophṓrōi): in theft itself, i.e. (by analogy) in actual crime. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G846 (αὐτός) and (the dative case singular of) a derivative of (a thief); KJV: in the very act

G1889 Ἐπαφρᾶς (Epaphrâs): Epaphras, a Christian. Origin: contracted from G1891 (Ἐπαφρόδιτος); KJV: Epaphras

G1890 ἐπαφρίζω (epaphrízō): to foam upon, i.e. (figuratively) to exhibit (a vile passion). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G875 (ἀφρίζω); KJV: foam out

G1891 Ἐπαφρόδιτος (Epaphróditos): Epaphroditus, a Christian. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) (in the sense of devoted to) and (Venus); KJV: Epaphroditus

G1892 ἐπεγείρω (epegeírō): to rouse upon, i.e. (figuratively) to excite against. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1453 (ἐγείρω); KJV: raise, stir up

G1893 ἐπεί (epeí): thereupon, i.e. since (of time or cause). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1487 (εἰ); KJV: because, else, for that (then, -asmuch as), otherwise, seeing that, since, when

G1894 ἐπειδή (epeidḗ): since now, i.e. (of time) when, or (of cause) whereas. Origin: from G1893 (ἐπεί) and G1211 (δή); KJV: after that, because, for (that, -asmuch as), seeing, since

G1895 ἐπειδήπερ (epeidḗper): since indeed (of cause). Origin: from G1894 (ἐπειδή) and G4007 (περ); KJV: forasmuch

G1896 ἐπεῖδον (epeîdon): to regard (favorably or otherwise). Origin: and other moods and persons of the same tense; from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: behold, look upon

G1897 ἐπείπερ (epeíper): since indeed (of cause). Origin: from G1893 (ἐπεί) and G4007 (περ); KJV: seeing

G1898 ἐπεισαγωγή (epeisagōgḗ): a superintroduction. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G1521 (εἰσάγω); KJV: bringing in

G1899 ἔπειτα (épeita): thereafter. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1534 (εἶτα); KJV: after that(-ward), then

G1900 ἐπέκεινα (epékeina): upon those parts of, i.e. on the further side of. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and (the accusative case plural neuter of) G1565 (ἐκεῖνος); KJV: beyond

G1901 ἐπεκτείνομαι (epekteínomai): to stretch (oneself) forward upon. Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1614 (ἐκτείνω); KJV: reach forth

G1902 ἐπενδύομαι (ependýomai): to invest upon oneself. Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1746 (ἐνδύω); KJV: be clothed upon

G1903 ἐπενδύτης (ependýtēs): a wrapper, i.e. outer garment. Origin: from G1902 (ἐπενδύομαι); KJV: fisher's coat

G1904 ἐπέρχομαι (epérchomai): to supervene, i.e. arrive, occur, impend, attack, (figuratively) influence. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: come (in, upon)

G1905 ἐπερωτάω (eperōtáō): to ask for, i.e. inquire, seek. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2065 (ἐρωτάω); KJV: ask (after, questions), demand, desire, question

G1906 ἐπερώτημα (eperṓtēma): an inquiry. Origin: from G1905 (ἐπερωτάω); KJV: answer

G1907 ἐπέχω (epéchō): to hold upon, i.e. (by implication) to retain; (by extension) to detain; (with implication, of G3563 (νοῦς)) to pay attention to. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: give (take) heed unto, hold forth, mark, stay

G1908 ἐπηρεάζω (epēreázō): to insult, slander. Origin: from a comparative of G1909 (ἐπί) and (probably) (threats); KJV: use despitefully, falsely accuse

G1909 ἐπί (epí): properly, meaning superimposition (of time, place, order, etc.), as a relation of distribution (with the genitive case), i.e. over, upon, etc.; of rest (with the dative case) at, on, etc.; of direction (with the accusative case) towards, upon, etc. Origin: a primary preposition; KJV: about (the times), above, after, against, among, as long as (touching), at, beside, X have charge of, (be-, (where-))fore, in (a place, as much as, the time of, -to), (because) of, (up-)on (behalf of), over, (by, for) the space of, through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), with

G1910 ἐπιβαίνω (epibaínō): to walk upon, i.e. mount, ascend, embark, arrive. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: come (into), enter into, go abroad, sit upon, take ship

G1911 ἐπιβάλλω (epibállō): to throw upon (literal or figurative, transitive or reflexive; usually with more or less force); specially (with G1438 (ἑαυτοῦ) implied) to reflect; impersonally, to belong to. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: beat into, cast (up-)on, fall, lay (on), put (unto), stretch forth, think on

G1912 ἐπιβαρέω (epibaréō): to be heavy upon, i.e. (pecuniarily) to be expensive to; figuratively, to be severe towards. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G916 (βαρέω); KJV: be chargeable to, overcharge

G1913 ἐπιβιβάζω (epibibázō): to cause to mount (an animal). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a reduplicated derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις) (compare G307 (ἀναβιβάζω)); KJV: set on

G1914 ἐπιβλέπω (epiblépō): to gaze at (with favor, pity or partiality). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: look upon, regard, have respect to

G1915 ἐπίβλημα (epíblēma): a patch. Origin: from G1911 (ἐπιβάλλω); KJV: piece

G1916 ἐπιβοάω (epiboáō): to exclaim against. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G994 (βοάω); KJV: cry

G1917 ἐπιβουλή (epiboulḗ): a plan against someone, i.e. a plot. Origin: from a presumed compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G1014 (βούλομαι); KJV: laying (lying) in wait

G1918 ἐπιγαμβρεύω (epigambreúō): to form affinity with, i.e. (specially) in a levirate way. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G1062 (γάμος); KJV: marry

G1919 ἐπίγειος (epígeios): worldly (physically or morally). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1093 (γῆ); KJV: earthly, in earth, terrestrial

G1920 ἐπιγίνομαι (epigínomai): to arrive upon, i.e. spring up (as a wind). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: blow

G1921 ἐπιγινώσκω (epiginṓskō): to know upon some mark, i.e. recognize; by implication, to become fully acquainted with, to acknowledge. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: (ac-, have, take)know(-ledge, well), perceive

G1922 ἐπίγνωσις (epígnōsis): recognition, i.e. (by implication) full discernment, acknowledgement. Origin: from G1921 (ἐπιγινώσκω); KJV: (ac-)knowledge(-ing, - ment)

G1923 ἐπιγραφή (epigraphḗ): an inscription. Origin: from G1924 (ἐπιγράφω); KJV: superscription

G1924 ἐπιγράφω (epigráphō): to inscribe (physically or mentally). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1125 (γράφω); KJV: inscription, write in (over, thereon)

G1925 ἐπιδείκνυμι (epideíknymi): to exhibit (physically or mentally). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: shew

G1926 ἐπιδέχομαι (epidéchomai): to admit (as a guest or (figuratively) teacher). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: receive

G1927 ἐπιδημέω (epidēméō): to make oneself at home, i.e. (by extension) to reside (in a foreign country). Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: (be) dwelling (which were) there, stranger

G1928 ἐπιδιατάσσομαι (epidiatássomai): to appoint besides, i.e. supplement (as a codicil). Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1299 (διατάσσω); KJV: add to

G1929 ἐπιδίδωμι (epidídōmi): to give over (by hand or surrender). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: deliver unto, give, let (+ (her drive)), offer

G1930 ἐπιδιορθόω (epidiorthóō): to straighten further, i.e. (figuratively) arrange additionally. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός); KJV: set in order

G1931 ἐπιδύω (epidýō): to set fully (as the sun). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1416 (δύνω); KJV: go down

G1932 ἐπιείκεια (epieíkeia): suitableness, i.e. (by implication) equity, mildness. Origin: from G1933 (ἐπιεικής); KJV: clemency, gentleness

G1933 ἐπιεικής (epieikḗs): appropriate, i.e. (by implication) mild. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G1503 (εἴκω); KJV: gentle, moderation, patient

G1934 ἐπιζητέω (epizētéō): to search (inquire) for; intensively, to demand, to crave. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2212 (ζητέω); KJV: desire, enquire, seek (after, for)

G1935 ἐπιθανάτιος (epithanátios): doomed to death. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2288 (θάνατος); KJV: appointed to death

G1936 ἐπίθεσις (epíthesis): an imposition (of hands officially). Origin: from G2007 (ἐπιτίθημι); KJV: laying (putting) on

G1937 ἐπιθυμέω (epithyméō): to set the heart upon, i.e. long for (rightfully or otherwise). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: covet, desire, would fain, lust (after)

G1938 ἐπιθυμητής (epithymētḗs): a craver. Origin: from G1937 (ἐπιθυμέω); KJV: + lust after

G1939 ἐπιθυμία (epithymía): a longing (especially for what is forbidden). Origin: from G1937 (ἐπιθυμέω); KJV: concupiscence, desire, lust (after)

G1940 ἐπικαθίζω (epikathízō): to seat upon. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2523 (καθίζω); KJV: set on

G1941 ἐπικαλέομαι (epikaléomai): to entitle; by implication, to invoke (for aid, worship, testimony, decision, etc.). Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: appeal (unto), call (on, upon), surname

G1942 ἐπικάλυμα (epikályma): a covering, i.e. (figuratively) pretext. Origin: from G1943 (ἐπικαλύπτω); KJV: cloke

G1943 ἐπικαλύπτω (epikalýptō): to conceal, i.e. (figuratively) forgive. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: cover

G1944 ἐπικατάρατος (epikatáratos): imprecated, i.e. execrable. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G2672 (καταράομαι); KJV: accursed

G1945 ἐπίκειμαι (epíkeimai): to rest upon (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: impose, be instant, (be) laid (there-, up-)on, (when) lay (on), lie (on), press upon

G1946 Ἐπικούρειος (Epikoúreios): an Epicurean or follower of Epicurus. Origin: from (compare G1947 (ἐπικουρία)) (a noted philosopher); KJV: Epicurean

G1947 ἐπικουρία (epikouría): assistance. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and a (prolonged) form of the base of G2877 (κοράσιον) (in the sense of servant); KJV: help

G1948 ἐπικρίνω (epikrínō): to adjudge. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: give sentence

G1949 ἐπιλαμβάνομαι (epilambánomai): to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively). Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on)

G1950 ἐπιλανθάνομαι (epilanthánomai): to lose out of mind; by implication, to neglect. Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2990 (λανθάνω); KJV: (be) forget(-ful of)

G1951 ἐπιλέγομαι (epilégomai): to surname, select. Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: call, choose

G1952 ἐπιλείπω (epileípō): to leave upon, i.e. (figuratively) to be insufficient for. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: fail

G1953 ἐπιλησμονή (epilēsmonḗ): negligence. Origin: from a derivative of G1950 (ἐπιλανθάνομαι); KJV: X forgetful

G1954 ἐπίλοιπος (epíloipos): left over, i.e. remaining. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3062 (λοιποί); KJV: rest

G1955 ἐπίλυσις (epílysis): explanation, i.e. application. Origin: from G1956 (ἐπιλύω); KJV: interpretation

G1956 ἐπιλύω (epilýō): to solve further, i.e. (figuratively) to explain, decide. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: determine, expound

G1957 ἐπιμαρτυρέω (epimartyréō): to attest further, i.e. corroborate. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3140 (μαρτυρέω); KJV: testify

G1958 ἐπιμέλεια (epiméleia): carefulness, i.e. kind attention (hospitality). Origin: from G1959 (ἐπιμελέομαι); KJV: + refresh self

G1959 ἐπιμελέομαι (epimeléomai): to care for (physically or otherwise). Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and the same as G3199 (μέλω); KJV: take care of

G1960 ἐπιμελῶς (epimelōs): carefully. Origin: adverb from a derivative of G1959 (ἐπιμελέομαι); KJV: diligently

G1961 ἐπιμένω (epiménō): to stay over, i.e. remain (figuratively, persevere). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: abide (in), continue (in), tarry

G1962 ἐπινεύω (epineúō): to nod at, i.e. (by implication) to assent. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3506 (νεύω); KJV: consent

G1963 ἐπίνοια (epínoia): attention of the mind, i.e. (by implication) purpose. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3563 (νοῦς); KJV: thought

G1964 ἐπιορκέω (epiorkéō): to commit perjury. Origin: from G1965 (ἐπίορκος); KJV: forswear self

G1965 ἐπίορκος (epíorkos): on oath, i.e. (falsely) a forswearer. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3727 (ὅρκος); KJV: perjured person

G1966 ἐπιοῦσα (epioûsa): supervening, i.e. (G2250 (ἡμέρα) or G3571 (νύξ) being expressed or implied) the ensuing day or night. Origin: feminine singular participle of a comparative of G1909 (ἐπί) and (to go); KJV: following, next

G1967 ἐπιούσιος (epioúsios): tomorrow's; but more probably from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of the present participle feminine of G1510 (εἰμί); for subsistence, i.e. needful. Origin: perhaps from the same as G1966 (ἐπιοῦσα); KJV: daily

G1968 ἐπιπίπτω (epipíptō): to embrace (with affection) or seize (with more or less violence; literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall into (on, upon) lie on, press upon

G1969 ἐπιπλήσσω (epiplḗssō): to chastise, i.e. (with words) to upbraid. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4141 (πλήσσω); KJV: rebuke

G1970 ἐπιπνίγω (epipnígō): to throttle upon, i.e. (figuratively) overgrow. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4155 (πνίγω); KJV: choke

G1971 ἐπιποθέω (epipothéō): to dote upon, i.e. intensely crave possession (lawfully or wrongfully). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and potheo (to yearn); KJV: (earnestly) desire (greatly), (greatly) long (after), lust

G1972 ἐπιπόθησις (epipóthēsis): a longing for. Origin: from G1971 (ἐπιποθέω); KJV: earnest (vehement) desire

G1973 ἐπιπόθητος (epipóthētos): yearned upon, i.e. greatly loved. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of the latter part of G1971 (ἐπιποθέω); KJV: longed for

G1974 ἐπιποθία (epipothía): intense longing. Origin: from G1971 (ἐπιποθέω); KJV: great desire

G1975 ἐπιπορεύομαι (epiporeúomai): to journey further, i.e. travel on (reach). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: come

G1976 ἐπιῤῥάπτω (epirrháptō): to stitch upon, i.e. fasten with the needle. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G4476 (ῥαφίς); KJV: sew on

G1977 ἐπιῤῥίπτω (epirrhíptō): to throw upon (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4496 (ῥίπτω); KJV: cast upon

G1978 ἐπίσημος (epísēmos): remarkable, i.e. (figuratively) eminent. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and some form of the base of G4591 (σημαίνω); KJV: notable, of note

G1979 ἐπισιτισμός (episitismós): a provisioning, i.e. (concretely) food. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G4621 (σῖτος); KJV: victuals

G1980 ἐπισκέπτομαι (episképtomai): to inspect, i.e. (by implication) to select; by extension, to go to see, relieve. Origin: middle voice from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G4649 (σκοπός); KJV: look out, visit

G1981 ἐπισκηνόω (episkēnóō): to tent upon, i.e. (figuratively) abide with. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4637 (σκηνόω); KJV: rest upon

G1982 ἐπισκιάζω (episkiázō): to cast a shade upon, i.e. (by analogy) to envelop in a haze of brilliancy; figuratively, to invest with preternatural influence. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G4639 (σκιά); KJV: overshadow

G1983 ἐπισκοπέω (episkopéō): to oversee; by implication, to beware. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4648 (σκοπέω); KJV: look diligently, take the oversight

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G1984 to G2120
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G1984 ἐπισκοπή (episkopḗ): inspection (for relief); by implication, superintendence; specially, the Christian "episcopate". Origin: from G1980 (ἐπισκέπτομαι); KJV: the office of a "bishop", bishoprick, visitation

G1985 ἐπίσκοπος (epískopos): a superintendent, i.e. Christian officer in genitive case charge of a (or the) church (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4649 (σκοπός) (in the sense of G1983 (ἐπισκοπέω)); KJV: bishop, overseer

G1986 ἐπισπάομαι (epispáomai): to draw over, i.e. (with G203 (ἀκροβυστία) implied) efface the mark of circumcision (by recovering with the foreskin). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4685 (σπάω); KJV: become uncircumcised

G1987 ἐπίσταμαι (epístamai): to put the mind upon, i.e. comprehend, or be acquainted with. Origin: apparently a middle voice of G2186 (ἐφίστημι) (with G3563 (νοῦς) implied); KJV: know, understand

G1988 ἐπιστάτης (epistátēs): an appointee over, i.e. commander (teacher). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a presumed derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: master

G1989 ἐπιστέλλω (epistéllō): to enjoin (by writing), i.e. (genitive case) to communicate by letter (for any purpose). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: write (a letter, unto)

G1990 ἐπιστήμων (epistḗmōn): intelligent. Origin: from G1987 (ἐπίσταμαι); KJV: endued with knowledge

G1991 ἐπιστηρίζω (epistērízō): to support further, i.e. reestablish. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4741 (στηρίζω); KJV: confirm, strengthen

G1992 ἐπιστολή (epistolḗ): a written message. Origin: from G1989 (ἐπιστέλλω); KJV: "epistle," letter

G1993 ἐπιστομίζω (epistomízō): to put something over the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) to silence. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4750 (στόμα); KJV: stop mouths

G1994 ἐπιστρέφω (epistréphō): to revert (literally, figuratively or morally). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: come (go) again, convert, (re-)turn (about, again)

G1995 ἐπιστροφή (epistrophḗ): reversion, i.e. morally, revolution. Origin: from G1994 (ἐπιστρέφω); KJV: conversion

G1996 ἐπισυνάγω (episynágō): to collect upon the same place. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4863 (συνάγω); KJV: gather (together)

G1997 ἐπισυναγωγή (episynagōgḗ): a complete collection; especially a Christian meeting (for worship). Origin: from G1996 (ἐπισυνάγω); KJV: assembling (gathering) together

G1998 ἐπισυντρέχω (episyntréchō): to hasten together upon one place (or a particular occasion). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4936 (συντρέχω); KJV: come running together

G1999 ἐπισύστασις (episýstasis): a conspiracy, i.e. concourse (riotous or friendly). Origin: from the middle voice of a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G4921 (συνιστάω); KJV: that which cometh upon, + raising up

G2000 ἐπισφαλής (episphalḗs): figuratively, insecure. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and (to trip); KJV: dangerous

G2001 ἐπισχύω (epischýō): to avail further, i.e. (figuratively) insist stoutly. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2480 (ἰσχύω); KJV: be the more fierce

G2002 ἐπισωρεύω (episōreúō): to accumulate further, i.e. (figuratively) seek additionally. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G4987 (σωρεύω); KJV: heap

G2003 ἐπιταγή (epitagḗ): an injunction or decree; by implication, authoritativeness. Origin: from G2004 (ἐπιτάσσω); KJV: authority, commandment

G2004 ἐπιτάσσω (epitássō): to arrange upon, i.e. order. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: charge, command, injoin

G2005 ἐπιτελέω (epiteléō): to fulfill further (or completely), i.e. execute; by implication, to terminate, undergo. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5055 (τελέω); KJV: accomplish, do, finish, (make) (perfect), perform(X -ance)

G2006 ἐπιτήδειος (epitḗdeios): serviceable, i.e. (by implication) requisite. Origin: from (enough); KJV: things which are needful

G2007 ἐπιτίθημι (epitíthēmi): to impose (in a friendly or hostile sense). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: add unto, lade, lay upon, put (up) on, set on (up), + surname, X wound

G2008 ἐπιτιμάω (epitimáō): to tax upon, i.e. censure or admonish; by implication, forbid. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5091 (τιμάω); KJV: (straitly) charge, rebuke

G2009 ἐπιτιμία (epitimía): properly, esteem, i.e. citizenship; used (in the sense of G2008 (ἐπιτιμάω)) of a penalty. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: punishment

G2010 ἐπιτρέπω (epitrépō): to turn over (transfer), i.e. allow. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: give leave (liberty, license), let, permit, suffer

G2011 ἐπιτροπή (epitropḗ): permission, i.e. (by implication) full power. Origin: from G2010 (ἐπιτρέπω); KJV: commission

G2012 ἐπίτροπος (epítropos): a commissioner, i.e. domestic manager, guardian. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5158 (τρόπος) (in the sense of G2011 (ἐπιτροπή)); KJV: steward, tutor

G2013 ἐπιτυγχάνω (epitynchánō): to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) to attain. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5177 (τυγχάνω); KJV: obtain

G2014 ἐπιφαίνω (epiphaínō): to shine upon, i.e. become (literally) visible or (figuratively) known. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: appear, give light

G2015 ἐπιφάνεια (epipháneia): a manifestation, i.e. (specially) the advent of Christ (past or future). Origin: from G2016 (ἐπιφανής); KJV: appearing, brightness

G2016 ἐπιφανής (epiphanḗs): conspicuous, i.e. (figuratively) memorable. Origin: from G2014 (ἐπιφαίνω); KJV: notable

G2017 ἐπιφαύω (epiphaúō): to illuminate (figuratively). Origin: a form of G2014 (ἐπιφαίνω); KJV: give light

G2018 ἐπιφέρω (epiphérō): to bear upon (or further), i.e. adduce (personally or judicially (accuse, inflict)), superinduce. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: add, bring (against), take

G2019 ἐπιφωνέω (epiphōnéō): to call at something, i.e. exclaim. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5455 (φωνέω); KJV: cry (against), give a shout

G2020 ἐπιφώσκω (epiphṓskō): to begin to grow light. Origin: a form of G2017 (ἐπιφαύω); KJV: begin to dawn, X draw on

G2021 ἐπιχειρέω (epicheiréō): to put the hand upon, i.e. undertake. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5495 (χείρ); KJV: go about, take in hand (upon)

G2022 ἐπιχέω (epichéō): Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and (to pour); KJV: --to pour upon:--pour in

G2023 ἐπιχορηγέω (epichorēgéō): to furnish besides, i.e. fully supply, (figuratively) aid or contribute. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5524 (χορηγέω); KJV: add, minister (nourishment, unto)

G2024 ἐπιχορηγία (epichorēgía): contribution. Origin: from G2023 (ἐπιχορηγέω); KJV: supply

G2025 ἐπιχρίω (epichríō): to smear over. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G5548 (χρίω); KJV: anoint

G2026 ἐποικοδομέω (epoikodoméō): to build upon, i.e. (figuratively) to rear up. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3618 (οἰκοδομέω); KJV: build thereon (thereupon, on, upon)

G2027 ἐποκέλλω (epokéllō): to drive upon the shore, i.e. to beach a vessel. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and (to urge); KJV: run aground

G2028 ἐπονομάζω (eponomázō): to name further, i.e. denominate. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3687 (ὀνομάζω); KJV: call

G2029 ἐποπτεύω (epopteúō): to inspect, i.e. watch. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: behold

G2030 ἐπόπτης (epóptēs): a looker-on. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: eye-witness

G2031 ἔπος (épos): a word. Origin: from G2036 (ἔπω); KJV: X say

G2032 ἐπουράνιος (epouránios): above the sky. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G3772 (οὐρανός); KJV: celestial, (in) heaven(-ly), high

G2033 ἑπτά (heptá): seven. Origin: a primary number; KJV: seven

G2034 ἑπτάκις (heptákis): seven times. Origin: adverb from G2033 (ἑπτά); KJV: seven times

G2035 ἑπτακισχίλιοι (heptakischílioi): seven times a thousand. Origin: from G2034 (ἑπτάκις) and G5507 (χίλιοι); KJV: seven thousand

G2036 ἔπω (épō): to speak or say (by word or writing). Origin: a primary verb (used only in the definite past tense, the others being borrowed from G2046 (ἐρέω), G4483 (ῥέω), and G5346 (φημί)); KJV: answer, bid, bring word, call, command, grant, say (on), speak, tell

G2037 Ἔραστος (Érastos): beloved; Erastus, a Christian. Origin: from (to love); KJV: Erastus

G2038 ἐργάζομαι (ergázomai): to toil (as a task, occupation, etc.), (by implication) effect, be engaged in or with, etc. Origin: middle voice from G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: commit, do, labor for, minister about, trade (by), work

G2039 ἐργασία (ergasía): occupation; by implication, profit, pains. Origin: from G2040 (ἐργάτης); KJV: craft, diligence, gain, work

G2040 ἐργάτης (ergátēs): a toiler; figuratively, a teacher. Origin: from G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: labourer, worker(-men)

G2041 ἔργον (érgon): toil (as an effort or occupation); by implication, an act. Origin: from a primary (but obsolete) (to work); KJV: deed, doing, labour, work

G2042 ἐρεθίζω (erethízō): to stimulate (especially to anger). Origin: from a presumed prolonged form of G2054 (ἔρις); KJV: provoke

G2043 ἐρείδω (ereídō): to prop, i.e. (reflexively) get fast. Origin: of obscure affinity; KJV: stick fast

G2044 ἐρεύγομαι (ereúgomai): to belch, i.e. (figuratively) to speak out. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: utter

G2045 ἐρευνάω (ereunáō): to seek, i.e. (figuratively) to investigate. Origin: apparently from G2046 (ἐρέω) (through the idea of inquiry); KJV: search

G2046 ἐρέω (eréō): an alternate for G2036 (ἔπω) in certain tenses; to utter, i.e. speak or say. Origin: probably a fuller form of G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: call, say, speak (of), tell

G2047 ἐρημία (erēmía): solitude (concretely). Origin: from G2048 (ἔρημος); KJV: desert, wilderness

G2048 ἔρημος (érēmos): Origin: of uncertain affinity; lonesome, i.e. (by implication) waste (usually as a noun, G5561 (χώρα) being implied) KJV: desert, desolate, solitary, wilderness

G2049 ἐρημόω (erēmóō): to lay waste (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2048 (ἔρημος); KJV: (bring to, make) desolate(-ion), come to nought

G2050 ἐρήμωσις (erḗmōsis): despoliation. Origin: from G2049 (ἐρημόω); KJV: desolation

G2051 ἐρίζω (erízō): to wrangle. Origin: from G2054 (ἔρις); KJV: strive

G2052 ἐριθεία (eritheía): properly, intrigue, i.e. (by implication) faction. Origin: perhaps as the same as G2042 (ἐρεθίζω); KJV: contention(-ious), strife

G2053 ἔριον (érion): wool. Origin: of obscure affinity; KJV: wool

G2054 ἔρις (éris): a quarrel, i.e. (by implication) wrangling. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: contention, debate, strife, variance

G2055 ἐρίφιον (eríphion): a kidling, i.e. (genitive case) goat (symbolically, wicked person). Origin: from G2056 (ἔριφος); KJV: goat

G2056 ἔριφος (ériphos): a kid or (genitive case) goat. Origin: perhaps from the same as G2053 (ἔριον) (through the idea of hairiness); KJV: goat, kid

G2057 Ἑρμᾶς (Hermâs): Hermas, a Christian. Origin: probably from G2060 (Ἑρμῆς); KJV: Hermas

G2058 ἑρμηνεία (hermēneía): translation. Origin: from the same as G2059 (ἑρμηνεύω); KJV: interpretation

G2059 ἑρμηνεύω (hermēneúō): to translate. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G2060 (Ἑρμῆς) (as the god of language); KJV: interpret

G2060 Ἑρμῆς (Hermēs): Hermes, the name of the messenger of the Greek deities; also of a Christian. Origin: perhaps from G2046 (ἐρέω); KJV: Hermes, Mercury

G2061 Ἑρμογένης (Hermogénēs): born of Hermes; Hermogenes, an apostate Christian. Origin: from G2060 (Ἑρμῆς) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: Hermogenes

G2062 ἑρπετόν (herpetón): a reptile, i.e. (by Hebraism (compare H07431)) a small animal. Origin: neuter of a derivative of (to creep); KJV: creeping thing, serpent

G2063 ἐρυθρός (erythrós): Origin: of uncertain affinity; red, i.e. (with G2281 (θάλασσα)) the Red Sea KJV: red

G2064 ἔρχομαι (érchomai): to come or go (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively). Origin: middle voice of a primary verb (used only in the present and imperfect tenses, the others being supplied by a kindred (middle voice) , or (active) , which do not otherwise occur); KJV: accompany, appear, bring, come, enter, fall out, go, grow, X light, X next, pass, resort, be set

G2065 ἐρωτάω (erōtáō): to interrogate; by implication, to request. Origin: apparently from G2046 (ἐρέω) (compare G2045 (ἐρευνάω)); KJV: ask, beseech, desire, intreat, pray

G2066 ἐσθής (esthḗs): dress. Origin: from (to clothe); KJV: apparel, clothing, raiment, robe

G2067 ἔσθησις (ésthēsis): clothing (concretely). Origin: from a derivative of G2066 (ἐσθής); KJV: government

G2068 ἐσθίω (esthíō): used only in certain tenses, the rest being supplied by G5315 (φάγω); to eat (usually literal). Origin: strengthened for a primary (to eat); KJV: devour, eat, live

G2069 Ἐσλί (Eslí): Esli, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (probably for H454); KJV: Esli

G2070 ἐσμέν (esmén): we are. Origin: first person plural indicative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: are, be, have our being, X have hope, + (the gospel) was (preached unto) us

G2071 ἔσομαι (ésomai): will be. Origin: future of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: shall (should) be (have), (shall) come (to pass), X may have, X fall, what would follow, X live long, X sojourn

G2072 ἔσοπτρον (ésoptron): a mirror (for looking into). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς) and a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: glass

G2073 ἑσπέρα (hespéra): Origin: feminine of an adjective hesperos (evening); the eve (G5610 (ὥρα) being implied) KJV: evening(-tide)

G2074 Ἐσρώμ (Esrṓm): Esrom (i.e. Chetsron), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2696); KJV: Esrom

G2075 ἐστέ (esté): ye are. Origin: second person plural present indicative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: be, have been, belong

G2076 ἐστί (estí): he (she or it) is; also (with neuter plural) they are. Origin: third person singular present indicative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: are, be(-long), call, X can(-not), come, consisteth, X dure for a while, + follow, X have, (that) is (to say), make, meaneth, X must needs, + profit, + remaineth, + wrestle

G2077 ἔστω (éstō): be thou; also , third person of the same; let them be. Origin: second person singular present imperative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: be

G2078 ἔσχατος (éschatos): farthest, final (of place or time). Origin: a superlative probably from G2192 (ἔχω) (in the sense of contiguity); KJV: ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost

G2079 ἐσχάτως (eschátōs): finally, i.e. (with G2192 (ἔχω)) at the extremity of life. Origin: adverb from G2078 (ἔσχατος); KJV: point of death

G2080 ἔσω (ésō): inside (as preposition or adjective). Origin: from G1519 (εἰς); KJV: (with-)in(-ner, -to, -ward)

G2081 ἔσωθεν (ésōthen): from inside; also used as equivalent to G2080 (ἔσω) (inside). Origin: from G2080 (ἔσω); KJV: inward(-ly), (from) within, without

G2082 ἐσώτερος (esṓteros): interior. Origin: comparative of G2080 (ἔσω); KJV: inner, within

G2083 ἑταῖρος (hetaîros): a comrade. Origin: from (a clansman); KJV: fellow, friend

G2084 ἑτερόγλωσσος (heteróglōssos): other- tongued, i.e. a foreigner. Origin: from G2087 (ἕτερος) and G1100 (γλῶσσα); KJV: man of other tongue

G2085 ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω (heterodidaskaléō): to instruct differently. Origin: from G2087 (ἕτερος) and G1320 (διδάσκαλος); KJV: teach other doctrine(-wise)

G2086 ἑτεροζυγέω (heterozygéō): to yoke up differently, i.e. (figuratively) to associate discordantly. Origin: from a compound of G2087 (ἕτερος) and G2218 (ζυγός); KJV: unequally yoke together with

G2087 ἕτερος (héteros): (an-, the) other or different. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: altered, else, next (day), one, (an-)other, some, strange

G2088 ἑτέρως (hetérōs): differently. Origin: adverb from G2087 (ἕτερος); KJV: otherwise

G2089 ἔτι (éti): "yet," still (of time or degree). Origin: perhaps akin to G2094 (ἔτος); KJV: after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet

G2090 ἑτοιμάζω (hetoimázō): to prepare. Origin: from G2092 (ἕτοιμος); KJV: prepare, provide, make ready

G2091 ἑτοιμασία (hetoimasía): preparation. Origin: from G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω); KJV: preparation

G2092 ἕτοιμος (hétoimos): adjusted, i.e. ready. Origin: from an old noun (fitness); KJV: prepared, (made) ready(-iness, to our hand)

G2093 ἑτοίμως (hetoímōs): in readiness. Origin: adverb from G2092 (ἕτοιμος); KJV: ready

G2094 ἔτος (étos): a year. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: year

G2095 εὖ (eû): (adverbially) well. Origin: neuter of a primary (good); KJV: good, well (done)

G2096 Εὖα (Eûa): Eua (or Eva, i.e. Chavvah), the first woman. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2332); KJV: Eve

G2097 εὐαγγελίζω (euangelízō): to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel)

G2098 εὐαγγέλιον (euangélion): a good message, i.e. the gospel. Origin: from the same as G2097 (εὐαγγελίζω); KJV: gospel

G2099 εὐαγγελιστής (euangelistḗs): a preacher of the gospel. Origin: from G2097 (εὐαγγελίζω); KJV: evangelist

G2100 εὐαρεστέω (euarestéō): to gratify entirely. Origin: from G2101 (εὐάρεστος); KJV: please (well)

G2101 εὐάρεστος (euárestos): fully agreeable. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G701 (ἀρεστός); KJV: acceptable(-ted), wellpleasing

G2102 εὐαρέστως (euaréstōs): quite agreeably. Origin: adverb from G2101 (εὐάρεστος); KJV: acceptably, + please well

G2103 Εὔβουλος (Eúboulos): good-willer; Eubulus, a Christian. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G1014 (βούλομαι); KJV: Eubulus

G2104 εὐγενής (eugenḗs): well born, i.e. (literally) high in rank, or (figuratively) generous. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: more noble, nobleman

G2105 εὐδία (eudía): a clear sky, i.e. fine weather. Origin: feminine from G2095 (εὖ) and the alternate of G2203 (Ζεύς) (as the god of the weather); KJV: fair weather

G2106 εὐδοκέω (eudokéō): to think well of, i.e. approve (an act); specially, to approbate (a person or thing). Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G1380 (δοκέω); KJV: think good, (be well) please(-d), be the good (have, take) pleasure, be willing

G2107 εὐδοκία (eudokía): satisfaction, i.e. (subjectively) delight, or (objectively) kindness, wish, purpose. Origin: from a presumed compound of G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G1380 (δοκέω); KJV: desire, good pleasure (will), X seem good

G2108 εὐεργεσία (euergesía): beneficence (genitive case or specially). Origin: from G2110 (εὐεργέτης); KJV: benefit, good deed done

G2109 εὐεργετέω (euergetéō): to be philanthropic. Origin: from G2110 (εὐεργέτης); KJV: do good

G2110 εὐεργέτης (euergétēs): a worker of good, i.e. (specially) a philanthropist. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: benefactor

G2111 εὔθετος (eúthetos): well placed, i.e. (figuratively) appropriate. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: fit, meet

G2112 εὐθέως (euthéōs): directly, i.e. at once or soon. Origin: adverb from G2117 (εὐθύς); KJV: anon, as soon as, forthwith, immediately, shortly, straightway

G2113 εὐθυδρομέω (euthydroméō): to lay a straight course, i.e. sail direct. Origin: from G2117 (εὐθύς) and G1408 (δρόμος); KJV: (come) with a straight course

G2114 εὐθυμέω (euthyméō): to cheer up, i.e. (intransitively) be cheerful; neuter comparative (adverbially) more cheerfully. Origin: from G2115 (εὔθυμος); KJV: be of good cheer (merry)

G2115 εὔθυμος (eúthymos): in fine spirits, i.e. cheerful. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: of good cheer, the more cheerfully

G2116 εὐθύνω (euthýnō): to straighten (level); technically, to steer. Origin: from G2117 (εὐθύς); KJV: governor, make straight

G2117 εὐθύς (euthýs): straight, i.e. (literally) level, or (figuratively) true; adverbially (of time) at once. Origin: perhaps from G2095 (εὖ) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: anon, by and by, forthwith, immediately, straightway

G2118 εὐθύτης (euthýtēs): rectitude. Origin: from G2117 (εὐθύς); KJV: righteousness

G2119 εὐκαιρέω (eukairéō): to have good time, i.e. opportunity or leisure. Origin: from G2121 (εὔκαιρος); KJV: have leisure (convenient time), spend time

G2120 εὐκαιρία (eukairía): a favorable occasion. Origin: from G2121 (εὔκαιρος); KJV: opportunity

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2121 to G2249
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2121 εὔκαιρος (eúkairos): well-timed, i.e. opportune. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G2540 (καιρός); KJV: convenient, in time of need

G2122 εὐκαίρως (eukaírōs): opportunely. Origin: adverb from G2121 (εὔκαιρος); KJV: conveniently, in season

G2123 εὐκοπώτερος (eukopṓteros): better for toil, i.e. more facile. Origin: comparative of a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G2873 (κόπος); KJV: easier

G2124 εὐλάβεια (eulábeia): properly, caution, i.e. (religiously) reverence (piety); by implication, dread (concretely). Origin: from G2126 (εὐλαβής); KJV: fear(-ed)

G2125 εὐλαβέομαι (eulabéomai): to be circumspect, i.e. (by implication) to be apprehensive; religiously, to reverence. Origin: middle voice from G2126 (εὐλαβής); KJV: (moved with) fear

G2126 εὐλαβής (eulabḗs): taking well (carefully), i.e. circumspect (religiously, pious). Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: devout

G2127 εὐλογέω (eulogéō): to speak well of, i.e. (religiously) to bless (thank or invoke a benediction upon, prosper). Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: bless, praise

G2128 εὐλογητός (eulogētós): adorable. Origin: from G2127 (εὐλογέω); KJV: blessed

G2129 εὐλογία (eulogía): fine speaking, i.e. elegance of language; commendation ("eulogy"), i.e. (reverentially) adoration; religiously, benediction; by implication, consecration; by extension, benefit or largess. Origin: from the same as G2127 (εὐλογέω); KJV: blessing (a matter of) bounty (X -tifully), fair speech

G2130 εὐμετάδοτος (eumetádotos): good at imparting, i.e. liberal. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and a presumed derivative of G3330 (μεταδίδωμι); KJV: ready to distribute

G2131 Εὐνίκη (Euníkē): victorious; Eunice, a Jewess. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G3529 (νίκη); KJV: Eunice

G2132 εὐνοέω (eunoéō): to be well- minded, i.e. reconcile. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3563 (νοῦς); KJV: agree

G2133 εὔνοια (eúnoia): kindness; euphemistically, conjugal duty. Origin: from the same as G2132 (εὐνοέω); KJV: benevolence, good will

G2134 εὐνουχίζω (eunouchízō): to castrate (figuratively, live unmarried). Origin: from G2135 (εὐνοῦχος); KJV: make…eunuch

G2135 εὐνοῦχος (eunoûchos): a castrated person (such being employed in Oriental bed-chambers); by extension an impotent or unmarried man; by implication, a chamberlain (state-officer). Origin: from (a bed) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: eunuch

G2136 Εὐοδία (Euodía): fine travelling; Euodia, a Christian woman. Origin: from the same as G2137 (εὐοδόω); KJV: Euodias

G2137 εὐοδόω (euodóō): to help on the road, i.e. (passively) succeed in reaching; figuratively, to succeed in business affairs. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G3598 (ὁδός); KJV: (have a) prosper(-ous journey)

G2138 εὐπειθής (eupeithḗs): good for persuasion, i.e. (intransitively) complaint. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G3982 (πείθω); KJV: easy to be intreated

G2139 εὐπερίστατος (euperístatos): well standing around, i.e. (a competitor) thwarting (a racer) in every direction (figuratively, of sin in genitive case). Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of a presumed compound of G4012 (περί) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: which doth so easily beset

G2140 εὐποιΐα (eupoiḯa): well-doing, i.e. beneficence. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: to do good

G2141 εὐπορέω (euporéō): (intransitively) to be good for passing through, i.e. (figuratively) have pecuniary means. Origin: from a compound of G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω) and the base of G4197 (πορεία); KJV: ability

G2142 εὐπορία (euporía): pecuniary resources. Origin: from the same as G2141 (εὐπορέω); KJV: wealth

G2143 εὐπρέπεια (euprépeia): good suitableness, i.e. gracefulness. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4241 (πρέπω); KJV: grace

G2144 εὐπρόσδεκτος (euprósdektos): well-received, i.e. approved, favorable. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G4327 (προσδέχομαι); KJV: acceptable(-ted)

G2145 εὐπρόσεδρος (euprósedros): sitting well towards, i.e. (figuratively) assiduous (neuter, diligent service). Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and the same as G4332 (προσεδρεύω); KJV: X attend upon

G2146 εὐπροσωπέω (euprosōpéō): to be of good countenance, i.e. (figuratively) to make a display. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G4383 (πρόσωπον); KJV: make a fair show

G2147 εὑρίσκω (heurískō): to find (literally or figuratively). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary , which (together with another cognate form) is used for it in all the tenses except the present and imperfect; KJV: find, get, obtain, perceive, see

G2148 Εὐροκλύδων (Euroklýdōn): a storm from the East (or southeast), i.e. (in modern phrase) a Levanter. Origin: from (the east wind) and G2830 (κλύδων); KJV: Euroklydon

G2149 εὐρύχωρος (eurýchōros): spacious. Origin: from (wide) and G5561 (χώρα); KJV: broad

G2150 εὐσέβεια (eusébeia): piety; specially, the gospel scheme. Origin: from G2152 (εὐσεβής); KJV: godliness, holiness

G2151 εὐσεβέω (eusebéō): to be pious, i.e. (towards God) to worship, or (towards parents) to respect (support). Origin: from G2152 (εὐσεβής); KJV: show piety, worship

G2152 εὐσεβής (eusebḗs): well-reverent, i.e. pious. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G4576 (σέβομαι); KJV: devout, godly

G2153 εὐσεβῶς (eusebōs): piously. Origin: adverb from G2152 (εὐσεβής); KJV: godly

G2154 εὔσημος (eúsēmos): well indicated, i.e. (figuratively) significant. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω); KJV: easy to be understood

G2155 εὔσπλαγχνος (eúsplanchnos): well compassioned, i.e. sympathetic. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G4698 (σπλάγχνον); KJV: pitiful, tender-hearted

G2156 εὐσχημόνως (euschēmónōs): decorously. Origin: adverb from G2158 (εὐσχήμων); KJV: decently, honestly

G2157 εὐσχημοσύνη (euschēmosýnē): decorousness. Origin: from G2158 (εὐσχήμων); KJV: comeliness

G2158 εὐσχήμων (euschḗmōn): well-formed, i.e. (figuratively) decorous, noble (in rank). Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G4976 (σχῆμα); KJV: comely, honourable

G2159 εὐτόνως (eutónōs): in a well-strung manner, i.e. (figuratively) intensely (in a good sense, cogently; in a bad one, fiercely). Origin: adverb from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of (to stretch); KJV: mightily, vehemently

G2160 εὐτραπελία (eutrapelía): witticism, i.e. (in a vulgar sense) ribaldry. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of the base of G5157 (τροπή) (meaning well-turned, i.e. ready at repartee, jocose); KJV: jesting

G2161 Εὔτυχος (Eútychos): well- fated, i.e. fortunate; Eutychus, a young man. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5177 (τυγχάνω); KJV: Eutychus

G2162 εὐφημία (euphēmía): good language ("euphemy"), i.e. praise (repute). Origin: from G2163 (εὔφημος); KJV: good report

G2163 εὔφημος (eúphēmos): well spoken of, i.e. reputable. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G5345 (φήμη); KJV: of good report

G2164 εὐφορέω (euphoréō): to bear well, i.e. be fertile. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G5409 (φορέω); KJV: bring forth abundantly

G2165 εὐφραίνω (euphraínō): to put (middle voice or passively, be) in a good frame of mind, i.e. rejoice. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G5424 (φρήν); KJV: fare, make glad, be (make) merry, rejoice

G2166 Εὐφράτης (Euphrátēs): Euphrates, a river of Asia. Origin: of foreign origin (compare H6578); KJV: Euphrates

G2167 εὐφροσύνη (euphrosýnē): joyfulness. Origin: from the same as G2165 (εὐφραίνω); KJV: gladness, joy

G2168 εὐχαριστέω (eucharistéō): to be grateful, i.e. (actively) to express gratitude (towards); specially, to say grace at a meal. Origin: from G2170 (εὐχάριστος); KJV: (give) thank(-ful, -s)

G2169 εὐχαριστία (eucharistía): gratitude; actively, grateful language (to God, as an act of worship). Origin: from G2170 (εὐχάριστος); KJV: thankfulness, (giving of) thanks(-giving)

G2170 εὐχάριστος (eucháristos): well favored, i.e. (by implication) grateful. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G5483 (χαρίζομαι); KJV: thankful

G2171 εὐχή (euchḗ): properly, a wish, expressed as a petition to God, or in votive obligation. Origin: from G2172 (εὔχομαι); KJV: prayer, vow

G2172 εὔχομαι (eúchomai): to wish; by implication, to pray to God. Origin: middle voice of a primary verb; KJV: pray, will, wish

G2173 εὔχρηστος (eúchrēstos): easily used, i.e. useful. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G5543 (χρηστός); KJV: profitable, meet for use

G2174 εὐψυχέω (eupsychéō): to be in good spirits, i.e. feel encouraged. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and G5590 (ψυχή); KJV: be of good comfort

G2175 εὐωδία (euōdía): good-scentedness, i.e. fragrance. Origin: from a compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G3605 (ὄζω); KJV: sweet savour (smell, -smelling)

G2176 εὐώνυμος (euṓnymos): properly, well-named (good-omened), i.e. the left (which was the lucky side among the pagan Greeks); neuter as adverbial, at the left hand. Origin: from G2095 (εὖ) and G3686 (ὄνομα); KJV: (on the) left

G2177 ἐφάλλομαι (ephállomai): to spring upon. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G242 (ἅλλομαι); KJV: leap on

G2178 ἐφάπαξ (ephápax): upon one occasion (only). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G530 (ἅπαξ); KJV: (at) once (for all)

G2179 Ἐφεσῖνος (Ephesînos): Ephesine, or situated at Ephesus. Origin: from G2181 (Ἔφεσος); KJV: of Ephesus

G2180 Ἐφέσιος (Ephésios): an Ephesian or inhabitant of Ephesus. Origin: from G2181 (Ἔφεσος); KJV: Ephesian, of Ephesus

G2181 Ἔφεσος (Éphesos): Ephesus, a city of Asia Minor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Ephesus

G2182 ἐφευρετής (epheuretḗs): a discoverer, i.e. contriver. Origin: from a compound of G1909 (ἐπί) and G2147 (εὑρίσκω); KJV: inventor

G2183 ἐφημερία (ephēmería): diurnality, i.e. (specially) the quotidian rotation or class of the Jewish priests' service at the Temple, as distributed by families. Origin: from G2184 (ἐφήμερος); KJV: course

G2184 ἐφήμερος (ephḗmeros): for a day ("ephemeral"), i.e. diurnal. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2250 (ἡμέρα); KJV: daily

G2185 ἐφικνέομαι (ephiknéomai): to arrive upon, i.e. extend to. Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and a cognate of G2240 (ἥκω); KJV: reach

G2186 ἐφίστημι (ephístēmi): to stand upon, i.e. be present (in various applications, friendly or otherwise, usually literal). Origin: from G1909 (ἐπί) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: --assault, come (in, to, unto, upon), be at hand (instant), present, stand (before, by, over)

G2187 Ἐφραίμ (Ephraím): Ephraim, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H669 or better H6085); KJV: Ephraim

G2188 ἐφφαθά (ephphathá): be opened!. Origin: of Chaldee origin (H6606); KJV: Ephphatha

G2189 ἔχθρα (échthra): hostility; by implication, a reason for opposition. Origin: feminine of G2190 (ἐχθρός); KJV: enmity, hatred

G2190 ἐχθρός (echthrós): hateful (passively, odious, or actively, hostile); usually as a noun, an adversary (especially Satan). Origin: from a primary (to hate); KJV: enemy, foe

G2191 ἔχιδνα (échidna): an adder or other poisonous snake (literally or figuratively). Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: viper

G2192 ἔχω (échō): to hold (used in very various applications, literally or figuratively, direct or remote; such as possession; ability, contiuity, relation, or condition). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be (able, X hold, possessed with), accompany, + begin to amend, can(+ -not), X conceive, count, diseased, do + eat, + enjoy, + fear, following, have, hold, keep, + lack, + go to law, lie, + must needs, + of necessity, + need, next, + recover, + reign, + rest, + return, X sick, take for, + tremble, + uncircumcised, use

G2193 ἕως (héōs): a conjunction, preposition and adverb of continuance, until (of time and place). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: even (until, unto), (as) far (as), how long, (un-)til(-l), (hither-, un-, up) to, while(-s)

G2194 Ζαβουλών (Zaboulṓn): Zabulon (i.e. Zebulon), a region of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2074); KJV: Zabulon

G2195 Ζακχαῖος (Zakchaîos): Zacchæus, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H2140); KJV: Zacchæus

G2196 Ζαρά (Zará): Zara, (i.e. Zerach), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2226); KJV: Zara

G2197 Ζαχαρίας (Zacharías): Zacharias (i.e. Zechariah), the name of two Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2148); KJV: Zacharias

G2198 ζάω (záō): to live (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: life(-time), (a-)live(-ly), quick

G2199 Ζεβεδαῖος (Zebedaîos): Zebedæus, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H2067); KJV: Zebedee

G2200 ζεστός (zestós): boiled, i.e. (by implication) calid (figuratively, fervent). Origin: from G2204 (ζέω); KJV: hot

G2201 ζεῦγος (zeûgos): a couple, i.e. a team (of oxen yoked together) or brace (of birds tied together). Origin: from the same as G2218 (ζυγός); KJV: yoke, pair

G2202 ζευκτηρία (zeuktēría): a fastening (tiller-rope). Origin: feminine of a derivative (at the second stage) from the same as G2218 (ζυγός); KJV: band

G2203 Ζεύς (Zeús): in the oblique cases there is used instead of it a (probably cognate) name , which is otherwise obsolete; Zeus or Dis (among the Latins, Jupiter or Jove), the supreme deity of the Greeks. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: Jupiter

G2204 ζέω (zéō): to be hot (boil, of liquids; or glow, of solids), i.e. (figuratively) be fervid (earnest). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be fervent

G2205 ζῆλος (zēlos): properly, heat, i.e. (figuratively) "zeal" (in a favorable sense, ardor; in an unfavorable one, jealousy, as of a husband (figuratively, of God), or an enemy, malice). Origin: from G2204 (ζέω); KJV: emulation, envy(-ing), fervent mind, indignation, jealousy, zeal

G2206 ζηλόω (zēlóō): to have warmth of feeling for or against. Origin: from G2205 (ζῆλος); KJV: affect, covet (earnestly), (have) desire, (move with) envy, be jealous over, (be) zealous(-ly affect)

G2207 ζηλωτής (zēlōtḗs): a "zealot". Origin: from G2206 (ζηλόω); KJV: zealous

G2208 Ζηλωτής (Zēlōtḗs): a Zealot, i.e. (specially) partisan for Jewish political independence. Origin: the same as G2207 (ζηλωτής); KJV: Zelotes

G2209 ζημία (zēmía): detriment. Origin: probably akin to the base of G1150 (δαμάζω) (through the idea of violence); KJV: damage, loss

G2210 ζημιόω (zēmióō): to injure, i.e. (reflexively or passively) to experience detriment. Origin: from G2209 (ζημία); KJV: be cast away, receive damage, lose, suffer loss

G2211 Ζηνᾶς (Zēnâs): Jove-given; Zenas, a Christian. Origin: probably contracted from a poetic form of G2203 (Ζεύς) and G1435 (δῶρον); KJV: Zenas

G2212 ζητέω (zētéō): to seek (literally or figuratively); specially, (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against life). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X will) seek (after, for, means)

G2213 ζήτημα (zḗtēma): a search (properly concretely), i.e. (in words) a debate. Origin: from G2212 (ζητέω); KJV: question

G2214 ζήτησις (zḗtēsis): a searching (properly, the act), i.e. a dispute or its theme. Origin: from G2212 (ζητέω); KJV: question

G2215 ζιζάνιον (zizánion): darnel or false grain. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: tares

G2216 Ζοροβάβελ (Zorobábel): Zorobabel (i.e. Zerubbabel), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2216); KJV: Zorobabel

G2217 ζόφος (zóphos): gloom (as shrouding like a cloud). Origin: akin to the base of G3509 (νέφος); KJV: blackness, darkness, mist

G2218 ζυγός (zygós): a coupling, i.e. (figuratively) servitude (a law or obligation); also (literally) the beam of the balance (as connecting the scales). Origin: from the root of (to join, especially by a "yoke"); KJV: pair of balances, yoke

G2219 ζύμη (zýmē): ferment (as if boiling up). Origin: probably from G2204 (ζέω); KJV: leaven

G2220 ζυμόω (zymóō): to cause to ferment. Origin: from G2219 (ζύμη); KJV: leaven

G2221 ζωγρέω (zōgréō): to take alive (make a prisoner of war), i.e. (figuratively) to capture or ensnare. Origin: from the same as G2226 (ζῶον) and G64 (ἀγρεύω); KJV: take captive, catch

G2222 ζωή (zōḗ): life (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2198 (ζάω); KJV: life(-time)

G2223 ζώνη (zṓnē): a belt; by implication, a pocket. Origin: probably akin to the base of G2218 (ζυγός); KJV: girdle, purse
