G2224 ζώννυμι (zṓnnymi): to bind about (especially with a belt). Origin: from G2223 (ζώνη); KJV: gird

G2225 ζωογονέω (zōogonéō): to engender alive, i.e. (by analogy) to rescue (passively, be saved) from death. Origin: from the same as G2226 (ζῶον) and a derivative of G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: live, preserve

G2226 ζῶον (zōon): a live thing, i.e. an animal. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G2198 (ζάω); KJV: beast

G2227 ζωοποιέω (zōopoiéō): to (re-)vitalize (literally or figuratively). Origin: from the same as G2226 (ζῶον) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: make alive, give life, quicken

G2228 ἤ (ḗ): disjunctive, or; comparative, than. Origin: a primary particle of distinction between two connected terms; KJV: and, but (either), (n-)either, except it be, (n-)or (else), rather, save, than, that, what, yea

G2229 ἦ (ē): assuredly. Origin: an adverb of confirmation; perhaps intensive of G2228 (ἤ); used only (in the New Testament) before G3303 (μέν); KJV: surely

G2230 ἡγεμονεύω (hēgemoneúō): to act as ruler. Origin: from G2232 (ἡγεμών); KJV: be governor

G2231 ἡγεμονία (hēgemonía): government, i.e. (in time) official term. Origin: from G2232 (ἡγεμών); KJV: reign

G2232 ἡγεμών (hēgemṓn): a leader, i.e. chief person (or figuratively, place) of a province. Origin: from G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: governor, prince, ruler

G2233 ἡγέομαι (hēgéomai): to lead, i.e. command (with official authority); figuratively, to deem, i.e. consider. Origin: middle voice of a (presumed) strengthened form of G71 (ἄγω); KJV: account, (be) chief, count, esteem, governor, judge, have the rule over, suppose, think

G2234 ἡδέως (hēdéōs): sweetly, i.e. (figuratively) with pleasure. Origin: adverb from a derivative of the base of G2237 (ἡδονή); KJV: gladly

G2235 ἤδη (ḗdē): even now. Origin: apparently from G2228 (ἤ) (or possibly G2229 (ἦ)) and G1211 (δή); KJV: already, (even) now (already), by this time

G2236 ἥδιστα (hḗdista): with great pleasure. Origin: neuter plural of the superlative of the same as G2234 (ἡδέως); KJV: most (very) gladly

G2237 ἡδονή (hēdonḗ): sensual delight; by implication, desire. Origin: from (to please); KJV: lust, pleasure

G2238 ἡδύοσμον (hēdýosmon): a sweet-scented plant, i.e. mint. Origin: neuter of the compound of the same as G2234 (ἡδέως) and G3744 (ὀσμή); KJV: mint

G2239 ἦθος (ēthos): usage, i.e. (plural) moral habits. Origin: a strengthened form of G1485 (ἔθος); KJV: manners

G2240 ἥκω (hḗkō): to arrive, i.e. be present (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: come

G2241 ἠλί (ēlí): my God. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H410 with pronominal suffix); KJV: Eli

G2242 Ἡλί (Hēlí): Heli (i.e. Eli), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5941); KJV: Heli

G2243 Ἡλίας (Hēlías): Helias (i.e. Elijah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H452); KJV: Elias

G2244 ἡλικία (hēlikía): maturity (in years or size). Origin: from the same as G2245 (ἡλίκος); KJV: age, stature

G2245 ἡλίκος (hēlíkos): as big as, i.e. (interjectively) how much. Origin: from (a comrade, i.e. one of the same age); KJV: how (what) great

G2246 ἥλιος (hḗlios): perhaps akin to the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι)); the sun; by implication, light. Origin: from (a ray; KJV: + east, sun

G2247 ἧλος (hēlos): a stud, i.e. spike. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: nail

G2248 ἡμᾶς (hēmâs): us. Origin: accusative case plural of G1473 (ἐγώ); KJV: our, us, we

G2249 ἡμεῖς (hēmeîs): we (only used when emphatic). Origin: nominative plural of G1473 (ἐγώ); KJV: us, we (ourselves)

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2250 to G2396
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2250 ἡμέρα (hēméra): day, i.e. (literally) the time space between dawn and dark, or the whole 24 hours (but several days were usually reckoned by the Jews as inclusive of the parts of both extremes); figuratively, a period (always defined more or less clearly by the context). Origin: feminine (with G5610 (ὥρα) implied) of a derivative of (to sit; akin to the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος)) meaning tame, i.e. gentle; KJV: age, + alway, (mid-)day (by day, (-ly)), + for ever, judgment, (day) time, while, years

G2251 ἡμέτερος (hēméteros): our. Origin: from G2349 (θνητός); KJV: our, your (by a different reading)

G2252 ἤμην (ḗmēn): I was. Origin: a prolonged form of G2258 (ἦν); KJV: be, was

G2253 ἡμιθανής (hēmithanḗs): half dead, i.e. entirely exhausted. Origin: from a presumed compound of the base of G2255 (ἥμισυ) and G2348 (θνήσκω); KJV: half dead

G2254 ἡμῖν (hēmîn): to (or for, with, by) us. Origin: dative case plural of G1473 (ἐγώ); KJV: our, (for) us, we

G2255 ἥμισυ (hḗmisy): (as noun) half. Origin: neuter of a derivative from an inseparable prefix akin to G260 (ἅμα) (through the idea of partition involved in connection) and meaning semi-; KJV: half

G2256 ἡμιώριον (hēmiṓrion): a half-hour. Origin: from the base of G2255 (ἥμισυ) and G5610 (ὥρα); KJV: half an hour

G2257 ἡμῶν (hēmōn): of (or from) us. Origin: genitive case plural of G1473 (ἐγώ); KJV: our (company), us, we

G2258 ἦν (ēn): I (thou, etc.) was (wast or were). Origin: imperfect of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: + agree, be, X have (+ charge of), hold, use, was(-t), were

G2259 ἡνίκα (hēníka): at which time. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: when

G2260 ἤπερ (ḗper): than at all (or than perhaps, than indeed). Origin: from G2228 (ἤ) and G4007 (περ); KJV: than

G2261 ἤπιος (ḗpios): properly, affable, i.e. mild or kind. Origin: probably from G2031 (ἔπος); KJV: gentle

G2262 Ἤρ (Ḗr): Er, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6147); KJV: Er

G2263 ἤρεμος (ḗremos): tranquil. Origin: perhaps by transposition from G2048 (ἔρημος) (through the idea of stillness); KJV: quiet

G2264 Ἡρώδης (Hērṓdēs): heroic; Herod, the name of four Jewish kings. Origin: compound of (a "hero") and G1491 (εἶδος); KJV: Herod

G2265 Ἡρωδιανοί (Hērōdianoí): Herodians, i.e. partisans of Herod. Origin: plural of a derivative of G2264 (Ἡρώδης); KJV: Herodians

G2266 Ἡρωδιάς (Hērōdiás): Herodias, a woman of the Heodian family. Origin: from G2264 (Ἡρώδης); KJV: Herodias

G2267 Ἡρωδίων (Hērōdíōn): Herodion, a Christian. Origin: from G2264 (Ἡρώδης); KJV: Herodion

G2268 Ἡσαΐας (Hēsaḯas): Hesaias (i.e. Jeshajah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3470); KJV: Esaias

G2269 Ἠσαῦ (Ēsaû): Esau, an Edomite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6215); KJV: Esau

G2270 ἡσυχάζω (hēsycházō): to keep still (intransitively), i.e. refrain from labor, meddlesomeness or speech. Origin: from the same as G2272 (ἡσύχιος); KJV: cease, hold peace, be quiet, rest

G2271 ἡσυχία (hēsychía): (as noun) stillness, i.e. desistance from bustle or language. Origin: feminine of G2272 (ἡσύχιος); KJV: quietness, silence

G2272 ἡσύχιος (hēsýchios): properly, keeping one's seat (sedentary), i.e. (by implication) still (undisturbed, undisturbing). Origin: a prolonged form of a compound probably of a derivative of the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος) and perhaps G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: peaceable, quiet

G2273 ἤτοι (ḗtoi): either indeed. Origin: from G2228 (ἤ) and G5104 (τοί); KJV: whether

G2274 ἡττάω (hēttáō): to make worse, i.e. vanquish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to rate lower. Origin: from the same as G2276 (ἥττον); KJV: be inferior, overcome

G2275 ἥττημα (hḗttēma): a deterioration, i.e. (objectively) failure or (subjectively) loss. Origin: from G2274 (ἡττάω); KJV: diminishing, fault

G2276 ἥττον (hḗtton): worse (as noun); by implication, less (as adverb). Origin: neuter of comparative of (slightly) used for that of G2556 (κακός); KJV: less, worse

G2277 ἤτω (ḗtō): let him (or it) be. Origin: third person singular imperative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: let … be

G2278 ἠχέω (ēchéō): to make a loud noise, i.e. reverberate. Origin: from G2279 (ἦχος); KJV: roar, sound

G2279 ἦχος (ēchos): a loud or confused noise ("echo"), i.e. roar; figuratively, a rumor. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: fame, sound

G2280 Θαδδαῖος (Thaddaîos): Thaddæus, one of the Apostles. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Thaddæus

G2281 θάλασσα (thálassa): the sea (genitive case or specially). Origin: probably prolonged from G251 (ἅλς); KJV: sea

G2282 θάλπω (thálpō): to brood, i.e. (figuratively) to foster. Origin: probably akin to (to warm); KJV: cherish

G2283 Θάμαρ (Thámar): Thamar (i.e. Tamar), an Israelitess. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8559); KJV: Thamar

G2284 θαμβέω (thambéō): to stupefy (with surprise), i.e. astound. Origin: from G2285 (θάμβος); KJV: amaze, astonish

G2285 θάμβος (thámbos): stupefaction (by surprise), i.e. astonishment. Origin: akin to an obsolete (to dumbfound); KJV: X amazed, + astonished, wonder

G2286 θανάσιμος (thanásimos): fatal, i.e. poisonous. Origin: from G2288 (θάνατος); KJV: deadly

G2287 θανατήφορος (thanatḗphoros): death-bearing, i.e. fatal. Origin: from (the feminine form of) G2288 (θάνατος) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: deadly

G2288 θάνατος (thánatos): (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2348 (θνήσκω); KJV: X deadly, (be…) death

G2289 θανατόω (thanatóō): Origin: from G2288 (θάνατος) to kill (literally or figuratively) KJV: become dead, (cause to be) put to death, kill, mortify

G2290 θάπτω (tháptō): to celebrate funeral rites, i.e. inter. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: bury

G2291 Θάρα (Thára): Thara (i.e. Terach), the father of Abraham. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8646); KJV: Thara

G2292 θαῤῥέω (tharrhéō): to exercise courage. Origin: another form for G2293 (θαρσέω); KJV: be bold, X boldly, have confidence, be confident

G2293 θαρσέω (tharséō): to have courage. Origin: from G2294 (θάρσος); KJV: be of good cheer (comfort)

G2294 θάρσος (thársos): boldness (subjectively). Origin: akin (by transposition) to (daring); KJV: courage

G2295 θαῦμα (thaûma): wonder (properly concrete; but by implication, abstract). Origin: apparently from a form of G2300 (θεάομαι); KJV: admiration

G2296 θαυμάζω (thaumázō): to wonder; by implication, to admire. Origin: from G2295 (θαῦμα); KJV: admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder

G2297 θαυμάσιος (thaumásios): wondrous, i.e. (neuter as noun) a miracle. Origin: from G2295 (θαῦμα); KJV: wonderful thing

G2298 θαυμαστός (thaumastós): wondered at, i.e. (by implication) wonderful. Origin: from G2296 (θαυμάζω); KJV: marvel(-lous)

G2299 θεά (theá): a female deity. Origin: feminine of G2316 (θεός); KJV: goddess

G2300 θεάομαι (theáomai): to look closely at, i.e. (by implication) perceive (literally or figuratively); by extension to visit. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb; KJV: behold, look (upon), see

G2301 θεατρίζω (theatrízō): to expose as a spectacle. Origin: from G2302 (θέατρον); KJV: make a gazing stock

G2302 θέατρον (théatron): a place for public show ("theatre"), i.e. general audience-room; by implication, a show itself (figuratively). Origin: from G2300 (θεάομαι); KJV: spectacle, theatre

G2303 θεῖον (theîon): sulphur. Origin: probably neuter of G2304 (θεῖος) (in its original sense of flashing); KJV: brimstone

G2304 θεῖος (theîos): godlike (neuter as noun, divinity). Origin: from G2316 (θεός); KJV: divine, godhead

G2305 θειότης (theiótēs): divinity (abstractly). Origin: from G2304 (θεῖος); KJV: godhead

G2306 θειώδης (theiṓdēs): sulphur-like, i.e. sulphurous. Origin: from G2303 (θεῖον) and 1491; KJV: brimstone

G2307 θέλημα (thélēma): a determination (properly, the thing), i.e. (actively) choice (specially, purpose, decree; abstractly, volition) or (passively) inclination. Origin: from the prolonged form of G2309 (θέλω); KJV: desire, pleasure, will

G2308 θέλησις (thélēsis): determination (properly, the act), i.e. option. Origin: from G2309 (θέλω); KJV: will

G2309 θέλω (thélō): to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas G1014 (βούλομαι) properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in. Origin: apparently strengthened from the alternate form of G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly))

G2310 θεμέλιος (themélios): something put down, i.e. a substruction (of a building, etc.), (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: foundation

G2311 θεμελιόω (themelióō): to lay a basis for, i.e. (literally) erect, or (figuratively) consolidate. Origin: from G2310 (θεμέλιος); KJV: (lay the) found(- ation), ground, settle

G2312 θεοδίδακτος (theodídaktos): divinely instructed. Origin: from G2316 (θεός) and G1321 (διδάσκω); KJV: taught of God

G2313 θεομαχέω (theomachéō): to resist deity. Origin: from G2314 (θεομάχος); KJV: fight against God

G2314 θεομάχος (theomáchos): an opponent of deity. Origin: from G2316 (θεός) and G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: to fight against God

G2315 θεόπνευστος (theópneustos): divinely breathed in. Origin: from G2316 (θεός) and a presumed derivative of G4154 (πνέω); KJV: given by inspiration of God

G2316 θεός (theós): figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very. Origin: of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with G3588 (ὁ)) the supreme Divinity; KJV: X exceeding, God, god(-ly, -ward)

G2317 θεοσέβεια (theosébeia): devoutness, i.e. piety. Origin: from G2318 (θεοσεβής); KJV: godliness

G2318 θεοσεβής (theosebḗs): reverent of God, i.e. pious. Origin: from G2316 (θεός) and G4576 (σέβομαι); KJV: worshipper of God

G2319 θεοστυγής (theostygḗs): hateful to God, i.e. impious. Origin: from G2316 (θεός) and the base of G4767 (στυγνητός); KJV: hater of God

G2320 θεότης (theótēs): divinity (abstractly). Origin: from G2316 (θεός); KJV: godhead

G2321 Θεόφιλος (Theóphilos): friend of God; Theophilus, a Christian. Origin: from G2316 (θεός) and G5384 (φίλος); KJV: Theophilus

G2322 θεραπεία (therapeía): attendance (specially, medical, i.e. cure); figuratively and collectively, domestics. Origin: from G2323 (θεραπεύω); KJV: healing, household

G2323 θεραπεύω (therapeúō): to wait upon menially, i.e. (figuratively) to adore (God), or (specially) to relieve (of disease). Origin: from the same as G2324 (θεράπων); KJV: cure, heal, worship

G2324 θεράπων (therápōn): a menial attendant (as if cherishing). Origin: apparently a participle from an otherwise obsolete derivative of the base of G2330 (θέρος); KJV: servant

G2325 θερίζω (therízō): to harvest. Origin: from G2330 (θέρος) (in the sense of the crop); KJV: reap

G2326 θερισμός (therismós): reaping, i.e. the crop. Origin: from G2325 (θερίζω); KJV: harvest

G2327 θεριστής (theristḗs): a harvester. Origin: from G2325 (θερίζω); KJV: reaper

G2328 θερμαίνω (thermaínō): to heat (oneself). Origin: from G2329 (θέρμη); KJV: (be) warm(-ed, self)

G2329 θέρμη (thérmē): warmth. Origin: from the base of G2330 (θέρος); KJV: heat

G2330 θέρος (théros): properly, heat, i.e. summer. Origin: from a primary (to heat); KJV: summer

G2331 Θεσσαλονικεύς (Thessalonikeús): a Thessalonican, i.e. inhabitant of Thessalonice. Origin: from G2332 (Θεσσαλονίκη); KJV: Thessalonian

G2332 Θεσσαλονίκη (Thessaloníkē): Thessalonice, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: from (a Thessalian) and G3529 (νίκη); KJV: Thessalonica

G2333 Θευδᾶς (Theudâs): Theudas, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Theudas

G2334 θεωρέω (theōréō): to be a spectator of, i.e. discern, (literally, figuratively (experience) or intensively (acknowledge)). Origin: from a derivative of G2300 (θεάομαι) (perhaps by addition of G3708 (ὁράω)); KJV: behold, consider, look on, perceive, see

G2335 θεωρία (theōría): spectatorship, i.e. (concretely) a spectacle. Origin: from the same as G2334 (θεωρέω); KJV: sight

G2336 θήκη (thḗkē): a receptacle, i.e. scabbard. Origin: from G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: sheath

G2337 θηλάζω (thēlázō): to suckle, (by implication) to suck. Origin: from (the nipple); KJV: (give) suck(-ling)

G2338 θῆλυς (thēlys): female. Origin: from the same as G2337 (θηλάζω); KJV: female, woman

G2339 θήρα (thḗra): hunting, i.e. (figuratively) destruction. Origin: from (a wild animal, as game); KJV: trap

G2340 θηρεύω (thēreúō): to hunt (an animal), i.e. (figuratively) to carp at. Origin: from G2339 (θήρα); KJV: catch

G2341 θηριομαχέω (thēriomachéō): to be a beast-fighter (in the gladiatorial show), i.e. (figuratively) to encounter (furious men). Origin: from a compound of G2342 (θηρίον) and G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: fight with wild beasts

G2342 θηρίον (thēríon): a dangerous animal. Origin: diminutive from the same as G2339 (θήρα); KJV: (venomous, wild) beast

G2343 θησαυρίζω (thēsaurízō): to amass or reserve (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2344 (θησαυρός); KJV: lay up (treasure), (keep) in store, (heap) treasure (together, up)

G2344 θησαυρός (thēsaurós): a deposit, i.e. wealth (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: treasure

G2345 θιγγάνω (thingánō): to manipulate, i.e. have to do with; by implication, to injure. Origin: a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (to finger); KJV: handle, touch

G2346 θλίβω (thlíbō): to crowd (literally or figuratively). Origin: akin to the base of G5147 (τρίβος); KJV: afflict, narrow, throng, suffer tribulation, trouble

G2347 θλῖψις (thlîpsis): pressure (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2346 (θλίβω); KJV: afflicted(-tion), anguish, burdened, persecution, tribulation, trouble

G2348 θνήσκω (thnḗskō): to die (literally or figuratively). Origin: a strengthened form of a simpler primary (which is used for it only in certain tenses); KJV: be dead, die

G2349 θνητός (thnētós): liable to die. Origin: from G2348 (θνήσκω); KJV: mortal(-ity)

G2350 θορυβέω (thorybéō): to be in tumult, i.e. disturb, clamor. Origin: from G2351 (θόρυβος); KJV: make ado (a noise), trouble self, set on an uproar

G2351 θόρυβος (thórybos): a disturbance. Origin: from the base of G2360 (θροέω); KJV: tumult, uproar

G2352 θραύω (thraúō): to crush. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: bruise

G2353 θρέμμα (thrémma): stock (as raised on a farm). Origin: from G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: cattle

G2354 θρηνέω (thrēnéō): to bewail. Origin: from G2355 (θρῆνος); KJV: lament, mourn

G2355 θρῆνος (thrēnos): wailing. Origin: from the base of G2360 (θροέω); KJV: lamentation

G2356 θρησκεία (thrēskeía): ceremonial observance. Origin: from a derivative of G2357 (θρησκός); KJV: religion, worshipping

G2357 θρησκός (thrēskós): ceremonious in worship (as demonstrative), i.e. pious. Origin: probably from the base of G2360 (θροέω); KJV: religious

G2358 θριαμβεύω (thriambeúō): and a derivative of G680 (ἅπτομαι) (meaning a noisy iambus, sung in honor of Bacchus); to make an acclamatory procession, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer or (by Hebraism) to give victory. Origin: from a prolonged compound of the base of G2360 (θροέω); KJV: (cause) to triumph (over)

G2359 θρίξ (thríx): of uncertain derivation; hair. Origin: genitive case , etc.; KJV: hair

G2360 θροέω (throéō): to clamor, i.e. (by implication) to frighten. Origin: from to wail; KJV: trouble

G2361 θρόμβος (thrómbos): a clot. Origin: perhaps from G5142 (τρέφω) (in the sense of thickening); KJV: great drop

G2362 θρόνος (thrónos): a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate. Origin: from (to sit); KJV: seat, throne

G2363 Θυάτειρα (Thyáteira): Thyatira, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Thyatira

G2364 θυγάτηρ (thygátēr): a female child, or (by Hebraism) descendant (or inhabitant). Origin: apparently a primary word (compare "daughter"); KJV: daughter

G2365 θυγάτριον (thygátrion): a daughterling. Origin: from G2364 (θυγάτηρ); KJV: little (young) daughter

G2366 θύελλα (thýella): Origin: from G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of blowing) a storm KJV: tempest

G2367 θύϊνος (thýïnos): denoting a certain fragrant tree); made of citron-wood. Origin: from a derivative of G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of blowing; KJV: thyine

G2368 θυμίαμα (thymíama): an aroma, i.e. fragrant powder burnt in religious service; by implication, the burning itself. Origin: from G2370 (θυμιάω); KJV: incense, odour

G2369 θυμιαστήριον (thymiastḗrion): a place of fumigation, i.e. the alter of incense (in the Temple). Origin: from a derivative of G2370 (θυμιάω); KJV: censer

G2370 θυμιάω (thymiáō): to fumigate, i.e. offer aromatic fumes. Origin: from a derivative of G2380 (θύω) (in the sense of smoking); KJV: burn incense

G2371 θυμομαχέω (thymomachéō): to be in a furious fight, i.e. (figuratively) to be exasperated. Origin: from a presumed compound of G2372 (θυμός) and G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: be highly displeased

G2372 θυμός (thymós): passion (as if breathing hard). Origin: from G2380 (θύω); KJV: fierceness, indignation, wrath

G2373 θυμόω (thymóō): to put in a passion, i.e. enrage. Origin: from G2372 (θυμός); KJV: be wroth

G2374 θύρα (thýra): a portal or entrance (the opening or the closure, literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary word (compare "door"); KJV: door, gate

G2375 θυρεός (thyreós): a large shield (as door-shaped). Origin: from G2374 (θύρα); KJV: shield

G2376 θυρίς (thyrís): an aperture, i.e. window. Origin: from G2374 (θύρα); KJV: window

G2377 θυρωρός (thyrōrós): a gate- warden. Origin: from G2374 (θύρα) and (a watcher); KJV: that kept the door, porter

G2378 θυσία (thysía): sacrifice (the act or the victim, literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2380 (θύω); KJV: sacrifice

G2379 θυσιαστήριον (thysiastḗrion): a place of sacrifice, i.e. an altar (special or genitive case, literal or figurative). Origin: from a derivative of G2378 (θυσία); KJV: altar

G2380 θύω (thýō): properly, to rush (breathe hard, blow, smoke), i.e. (by implication) to sacrifice (properly, by fire, but genitive case); by extension to immolate (slaughter for any purpose). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: kill, (do) sacrifice, slay

G2381 Θωμᾶς (Thōmâs): the twin; Thomas, a Christian. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H8380); KJV: Thomas

G2382 θώραξ (thṓrax): the chest ("thorax"), i.e. (by implication) a corslet. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: breast-plate

G2383 Ἰάειρος (Iáeiros): Jairus (i.e. Jair), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2971); KJV: Jairus

G2384 Ἰακώβ (Iakṓb): Jacob (i.e. Ja`akob), the progenitor of the Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3290); KJV: also an Israelite:--Jacob

G2385 Ἰάκωβος (Iákōbos): Jacobus, the name of three Israelites. Origin: the same as G2384 (Ἰακώβ) Græcized; KJV: James

G2386 ἴαμα (íama): a cure (the effect). Origin: from G2390 (ἰάομαι); KJV: healing

G2387 Ἰαμβρῆς (Iambrēs): Jambres, an Egyptian. Origin: of Egyptian origin; KJV: Jambres

G2388 Ἰαννά (Ianná): Janna, an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H3238); KJV: Janna

G2389 Ἰαννῆς (Iannēs): Jannes, an Egyptian. Origin: of Egyptian origin; KJV: Jannes

G2390 ἰάομαι (iáomai): to cure (literally or figuratively). Origin: middle voice of apparently a primary verb; KJV: heal, make whole

G2391 Ἰάρεδ (Iáred): Jared (i.e. Jered), an antediluvian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3382); KJV: Jared

G2392 ἴασις (íasis): curing (the act). Origin: from G2390 (ἰάομαι); KJV: cure, heal(-ing)

G2393 ἴασπις (íaspis): "jasper", a gem. Origin: probably of foreign origin (see H3471); KJV: jasper

G2394 Ἰάσων (Iásōn): about to cure; Jason, a Christian. Origin: future active participle masculine of G2390 (ἰάομαι); KJV: Jason

G2395 ἰατρός (iatrós): a physician. Origin: from G2390 (ἰάομαι); KJV: physician

G2396 ἴδε (íde): used as an interjection to denote surprise; lo!. Origin: second person singular imperative active of G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: behold, lo, see

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2397 to G2539
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2397 ἰδέα (idéa): a sight (comparative figuratively "idea"), i.e. aspect. Origin: from G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: countenance

G2398 ἴδιος (ídios): pertaining to self, i.e. one's own; by implication, private or separate. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: X his acquaintance, when they were alone, apart, aside, due, his (own, proper, several), home, (her, our, thine, your) own (business), private(-ly), proper, severally, their (own)

G2399 ἰδιώτης (idiṓtēs): a private person, i.e. (by implication) an ignoramus (compare "idiot"). Origin: from G2398 (ἴδιος); KJV: ignorant, rude, unlearned

G2400 ἰδού (idoú): used as imperative lo!. Origin: second person singular imperative middle voice of G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: --behold, lo, see

G2401 Ἰδουμαία (Idoumaía): Idumæa (i.e. Edom), a region East (and South) of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H123); KJV: Idumæa

G2402 ἱδρώς (hidrṓs): perspiration. Origin: a strengthened form of a primary idos (sweat); KJV: sweat

G2403 Ἰεζαβήλ (Iezabḗl): Jezabel (i.e. Jezebel), a Tyrian woman (used as a synonym of a termagant or false teacher). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H348); KJV: Jezabel

G2404 Ἱεράπολις (Hierápolis): holy city; Hierapolis, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: from G2413 (ἱερός) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: Hierapolis

G2405 ἱερατεία (hierateía): priestliness, i.e. the sacerdotal function. Origin: from G2407 (ἱερατεύω); KJV: office of the priesthood, priest's office

G2406 ἱεράτευμα (hieráteuma): the priestly fraternity, i.e. sacerdotal order (figuratively). Origin: from G2407 (ἱερατεύω); KJV: priesthood

G2407 ἱερατεύω (hierateúō): to be a priest, i.e. perform his functions. Origin: prolongation from G2409 (ἱερεύς); KJV: execute the priest's office

G2408 Ἱερεμίας (Hieremías): Hieremias (i.e. Jermijah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3414); KJV: Jeremiah

G2409 ἱερεύς (hiereús): a priest (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2413 (ἱερός); KJV: (high) priest

G2410 Ἱεριχώ (Hierichṓ): Jericho, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3405); KJV: Jericho

G2411 ἱερόν (hierón): a sacred place, i.e. the entire precincts (whereas G3485 (ναός) denotes the central sanctuary itself) of the Temple (at Jerusalem or elsewhere). Origin: neuter of G2413 (ἱερός); KJV: temple

G2412 ἱεροπρεπής (hieroprepḗs): reverent. Origin: from G2413 (ἱερός) and the same as G4241 (πρέπω); KJV: as becometh holiness

G2413 ἱερός (hierós): sacred. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: holy

G2414 Ἱεροσόλυμα (Hierosólyma): Hierosolyma (i.e. Jerushalaim), the capitol of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3389); KJV: Jerusalem

G2415 Ἱεροσολυμίτης (Hierosolymítēs): a Hierosolymite, i.e. inhabitant of Hierosolyma. Origin: from G2414 (Ἱεροσόλυμα); KJV: of Jerusalem

G2416 ἱεροσυλέω (hierosyléō): to be a temple-robber (figuratively). Origin: from G2417 (ἱερόσυλος); KJV: commit sacrilege

G2417 ἱερόσυλος (hierósylos): a temple-despoiler. Origin: from G2411 (ἱερόν) and G4813 (συλάω); KJV: robber of churches

G2418 ἱερουργέω (hierourgéō): to be a temple-worker, i.e. officiate as a priest (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G2411 (ἱερόν) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: minister

G2419 Ἱερουσαλήμ (Hierousalḗm): Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3389); KJV: Jerusalem

G2420 ἱερωσύνη (hierōsýnē): sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office. Origin: from G2413 (ἱερός); KJV: priesthood

G2421 Ἰεσσαί (Iessaí): Jessæ (i.e. Jishai), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3448); KJV: Jesse

G2422 Ἰεφθάε (Iephtháe): Jephthaë (i.e. Jiphtach), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3316); KJV: Jephthah

G2423 Ἰεχονίας (Iechonías): Jechonias (i.e. Jekonjah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3204); KJV: Jechonias

G2424 Ἰησοῦς (Iēsoûs): Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3091); KJV: Jesus

G2425 ἱκανός (hikanós): competent (as if coming in season), i.e. ample (in amount) or fit (in character). Origin: from ( or , akin to G2240 (ἥκω)) (to arrive); KJV: able, + content, enough, good, great, large, long (while), many, meet, much, security, sore, sufficient, worthy

G2426 ἱκανότης (hikanótēs): ability. Origin: from G2425 (ἱκανός); KJV: sufficiency

G2427 ἱκανόω (hikanóō): to enable, i.e. qualify. Origin: from G2425 (ἱκανός); KJV: make able (meet)

G2428 ἱκετηρία (hiketēría): intreaty. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G2425 (ἱκανός) (through the idea of approaching for a favor); KJV: supplication

G2429 ἱκμάς (hikmás): dampness. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: moisture

G2430 Ἰκόνιον (Ikónion): image-like; Iconium, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: perhaps from G1504 (εἰκών); KJV: Iconium

G2431 ἱλαρός (hilarós): propitious or merry ("hilarious"), i.e. prompt or willing. Origin: from the same as G2436 (ἵλεως); KJV: cheerful

G2432 ἱλαρότης (hilarótēs): alacrity. Origin: from G2431 (ἱλαρός); KJV: cheerfulness

G2433 ἱλάσκομαι (hiláskomai): to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious. Origin: middle voice from the same as G2436 (ἵλεως); KJV: be merciful, make reconciliation for

G2434 ἱλασμός (hilasmós): atonement, i.e. (concretely) an expiator. KJV: propitiation

G2435 ἱλαστήριον (hilastḗrion): an expiatory (place or thing), i.e. (concretely) an atoning victim, or (specially) the lid of the Ark (in the Temple). Origin: neuter of a derivative of G2433 (ἱλάσκομαι); KJV: mercyseat, propitiation

G2436 ἵλεως (híleōs): cheerful (as attractive), i.e. propitious; adverbially (by Hebraism) God be gracious!, i.e. (in averting some calamity) far be it. Origin: perhaps from the alternate form of G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: be it far, merciful

G2437 Ἰλλυρικόν (Illyrikón): (the) Illyrican (shore), i.e. (as a name itself) Illyricum, a region of Europe. Origin: neuter of an adjective from a name of uncertain derivation; KJV: Illyricum

G2438 ἱμάς (himás): a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge). Origin: perhaps from the same as G260 (ἅμα); KJV: latchet, thong

G2439 ἱματίζω (himatízō): to dress. Origin: from G2440 (ἱμάτιον); KJV: clothe

G2440 ἱμάτιον (himátion): a dress (inner or outer). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of ennumi (to put on); KJV: apparel, cloke, clothes, garment, raiment, robe, vesture

G2441 ἱματισμός (himatismós): clothing. Origin: from G2439 (ἱματίζω); KJV: apparel (X -led), array, raiment, vesture

G2442 ἱμείρομαι (himeíromai): of uncertain affinity); to long for. Origin: middle voice from (a yearning; KJV: be affectionately desirous

G2443 ἵνα (hína): compare G3588 (ὁ)); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result). Origin: probably from the same as the former part of G1438 (ἑαυτοῦ) (through the demonstrative idea; KJV: albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to

G2444 ἱνατί (hinatí): for what reason ?, i.e. why?. Origin: from G2443 (ἵνα) and G5101 (τίς); KJV: wherefore, why

G2445 Ἰόππη (Ióppē): Joppe (i.e. Japho), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3305); KJV: Joppa

G2446 Ἰορδάνης (Iordánēs): the Jordanes (i.e. Jarden), a river of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3383); KJV: Jordan

G2447 ἰός (iós): rust (as if emitted by metals); also venom (as emitted by serpents). Origin: perhaps from (to go) or (to send); KJV: poison, rust

G2448 Ἰουδά (Ioudá): Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3063 or perhaps H3194); KJV: Judah

G2449 Ἰουδαία (Ioudaía): the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine. Origin: feminine of G2453 (Ἰουδαῖος) (with G1093 (γῆ) implied); KJV: Judæa

G2450 Ἰουδαΐζω (Ioudaḯzō): to become a Judæan, i.e. "Judaize". Origin: from G2453 (Ἰουδαῖος); KJV: live as the Jews

G2451 Ἰουδαϊκός (Ioudaïkós): Judaïc, i.e. resembling a Judæan. Origin: from G2453 (Ἰουδαῖος); KJV: Jewish

G2452 Ἰουδαϊκῶς (Ioudaïkōs): Judaïcally or in a manner resembling a Judæan. Origin: adverb from G2451 (Ἰουδαϊκός); KJV: as do the Jews

G2453 Ἰουδαῖος (Ioudaîos): Judæan, i.e. belonging to Jehudah. Origin: from G2448 (Ἰουδά) (in the sense of G2455 (Ἰούδας) as a country); KJV: Jew(-ess), of Judæa

G2454 Ἰουδαϊσμός (Ioudaïsmós): "Judaism", i.e. the Jewish faith and usages. Origin: from G2450 (Ἰουδαΐζω); KJV: Jews' religion

G2455 Ἰούδας (Ioúdas): Judas (i.e. Jehudah), the name of ten Israelites; also of the posterity of one of them and its region. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3063); KJV: Juda(-h, -s); Jude

G2456 Ἰουλία (Ioulía): Julia, a Christian woman. Origin: feminine of the same as G2457 (Ἰούλιος); KJV: Julia

G2457 Ἰούλιος (Ioúlios): Julius, a centurion. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Julius

G2458 Ἰουνιᾶς (Iouniâs): Junias, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Junias

G2459 Ἰοῦστος (Ioûstos): Justus, the name of three Christian. Origin: of Latin origin ("just"); KJV: Justus

G2460 ἱππεύς (hippeús): an equestrian, i.e. member of a cavalry corps. Origin: from G2462 (ἵππος); KJV: horseman

G2461 ἱππικόν (hippikón): the cavalry force. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G2462 (ἵππος); KJV: horse(-men)

G2462 ἵππος (híppos): a horse. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: horse

G2463 ἶρις (îris): a rainbow ("iris"). Origin: perhaps from G2046 (ἐρέω) (as a symbol of the female messenger of the pagan deities); KJV: rainbow

G2464 Ἰσαάκ (Isaák): Isaac (i.e. Jitschak), the son of Abraham. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3327); KJV: Isaac

G2465 ἰσάγγελος (isángelos): like an angel, i.e. angelic. Origin: from G2470 (ἴσος) and G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: equal unto the angels

G2466 Ἰσαχάρ (Isachár): Isachar (i.e. Jissaskar), a son of Jacob (figuratively, his descendant). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3485); KJV: Issachar

G2467 ἴσημι (ísēmi): to know. Origin: assumed by some as the base of certain irregular forms of G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: know

G2468 ἴσθι (ísthi): be thou. Origin: second person imperative present of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: + agree, be, X give thyself wholly to

G2469 Ἰσκαριώτης (Iskariṓtēs): inhabitant of Kerioth; Iscariotes (i.e. Keriothite), an epithet of Judas the traitor. Origin: of Hebrew origin (probably H377 and H7149); KJV: Iscariot

G2470 ἴσος (ísos): similar (in amount and kind). Origin: probably from G1492 (εἴδω) (through the idea of seeming); KJV: + agree, as much, equal, like

G2471 ἰσότης (isótēs): likeness (in condition or proportion); by implication, equity. KJV: equal(-ity)

G2472 ἰσότιμος (isótimos): of equal value or honor. Origin: from G2470 (ἴσος) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: like precious

G2473 ἰσόψυχος (isópsychos): of similar spirit. Origin: from G2470 (ἴσος) and G5590 (ψυχή); KJV: likeminded

G2474 Ἰσραήλ (Israḗl): Israel (i.e. Jisrael), the adopted name of Jacob, including his descendants (literally or figuratively). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3478); KJV: Israel

G2475 Ἰσραηλίτης (Israēlítēs): an "Israelite", i.e. descendant of Israel (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2474 (Ἰσραήλ); KJV: Israelite

G2476 ἵστημι (hístēmi): to stand (transitively or intransitively), used in various applications (literally or figuratively). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary (of the same meaning, and used for it in certain tenses); KJV: abide, appoint, bring, continue, covenant, establish, hold up, lay, present, set (up), stanch, stand (by, forth, still, up)

G2477 ἱστορέω (historéō): to be knowing (learned), i.e. (by implication) to visit for information (interview). Origin: from a derivative of G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: see

G2478 ἰσχυρός (ischyrós): forcible (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2479 (ἰσχύς); KJV: boisterous, mighty(-ier), powerful, strong(-er, man), valiant

G2479 ἰσχύς (ischýs): compare , a form of G2192 (ἔχω)); forcefulness (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a derivative of (force; KJV: ability, might(-ily), power, strength

G2480 ἰσχύω (ischýō): to have (or exercise) force (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2479 (ἰσχύς); KJV: be able, avail, can do(-not), could, be good, might, prevail, be of strength, be whole, + much work

G2481 ἴσως (ísōs): likely, i.e. perhaps. Origin: adverb from G2470 (ἴσος); KJV: it may be

G2482 Ἰταλία (Italía): Italia, a region of Europe. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Italy

G2483 Ἰταλικός (Italikós): Italic, i.e. belonging to Italia. Origin: from G2482 (Ἰταλία); KJV: Italian

G2484 Ἰτουραΐα (Itouraḯa): Ituræa (i.e. Jetur), a region of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3195); KJV: Ituræa

G2485 ἰχθύδιον (ichthýdion): a petty fish. Origin: diminutive from G2486 (ἰχθύς); KJV: little (small) fish

G2486 ἰχθύς (ichthýs): a fish. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: fish

G2487 ἴχνος (íchnos): compare G2240 (ἥκω)); a track (figuratively). Origin: from (to arrive; KJV: step

G2488 Ἰωάθαμ (Iōátham): Joatham (i.e. Jotham), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3147); KJV: Joatham

G2489 Ἰωάννα (Iōánna): Joanna, a Christian. Origin: feminine of the same as G2491 (Ἰωάννης); KJV: Joanna

G2490 Ἰωαννᾶς (Iōannâs): Joannas, an Israelite. Origin: a form of G2491 (Ἰωάννης); KJV: Joannas

G2491 Ἰωάννης (Iōánnēs): Joannes (i.e. Jochanan), the name of four Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3110); KJV: John

G2492 Ἰώβ (Iṓb): Job (i.e. Ijob), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H347); KJV: Job

G2493 Ἰωήλ (Iōḗl): Joel, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3100); KJV: Joel

G2494 Ἰωνάν (Iōnán): Jonan, an Israelite. Origin: probably for G2491 (Ἰωάννης) or G2495 (Ἰωνᾶς); KJV: Jonan

G2495 Ἰωνᾶς (Iōnâs): Jonas (i.e. Jonah), the name of two Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3124); KJV: Jonas

G2496 Ἰωράμ (Iōrám): Joram, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3141); KJV: Joram

G2497 Ἰωρείμ (Iōreím): Jorim, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps for G2496 (Ἰωράμ); KJV: Jorim

G2498 Ἰωσαφάτ (Iōsaphát): Josaphat (i.e. Jehoshaphat), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3092); KJV: Josaphat

G2499 Ἰωσή (Iōsḗ): Jose, an Israelite. Origin: genitive case of G2500 (Ἰωσῆς); KJV: Jose

G2500 Ἰωσῆς (Iōsēs): Joses, the name of two Israelites. Origin: perhaps for G2501 (Ἰωσήφ); KJV: Joses

G2501 Ἰωσήφ (Iōsḗph): Joseph, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3130); KJV: Joseph

G2502 Ἰωσίας (Iōsías): Josias (i.e. Joshiah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2977); KJV: Josias

G2503 ἰῶτα (iōta): "iota", the name of the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet, put (figuratively) for a very small part of anything. Origin: of Hebrew origin (the tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet); KJV: jot

G2504 κἀγώ (kagṓ): so also the dative case , and accusative case and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me. Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G1473 (ἐγώ); KJV: (and, even, even so, so) I (also, in like wise), both me, me also

G2505 καθά (kathá): according to which things, i.e. just as. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the neuter plural of G3739 (ὅς); KJV: as

G2506 καθαίρεσις (kathaíresis): demolition; figuratively, extinction. Origin: from G2507 (καθαιρέω); KJV: destruction, pulling down

G2507 καθαιρέω (kathairéō): to lower (or with violence) demolish (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G138 (αἱρέομαι) (including its alternate); KJV: cast (pull, put, take) down, destroy

G2508 καθαίρω (kathaírō): to cleanse, i.e. (specially) to prune; figuratively, to expiate. Origin: from G2513 (καθαρός); KJV: purge

G2509 καθάπερ (katháper): exactly as. Origin: from G2505 (καθά) and G4007 (περ); KJV: (even, as well) as

G2510 καθάπτω (katháptō): to seize upon. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G680 (ἅπτομαι); KJV: fasten on

G2511 καθαρίζω (katharízō): to cleanse (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2513 (καθαρός); KJV: (make) clean(-se), purge, purify

G2512 καθαρισμός (katharismós): a washing off, i.e. (ceremonially) ablution, (morally) expiation. Origin: from G2511 (καθαρίζω); KJV: cleansing, + purge, purification(-fying)

G2513 καθαρός (katharós): clean (literally or figuratively). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: clean, clear, pure

G2514 καθαρότης (katharótēs): cleanness (ceremonially). Origin: from G2513 (καθαρός); KJV: purification

G2515 καθέδρα (kathédra): a bench (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the same as G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: seat

G2516 καθέζομαι (kathézomai): to sit down. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: sit

G2517 καθεξῆς (kathexēs): thereafter, i.e. consecutively; as a noun (by ellipsis of noun) a subsequent person or time. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1836 (ἑξῆς); KJV: after(-ward), by (in) order

G2518 καθεύδω (katheúdō): to lie down to rest, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and (to sleep); KJV: (be a-)sleep

G2519 καθηγητής (kathēgētḗs): a guide, i.e. (figuratively) a teacher. Origin: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: master

G2520 καθήκω (kathḗkō): to reach to, i.e. (neuter of present active participle, figuratively as adjective) becoming. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2240 (ἥκω); KJV: convenient, fit

G2521 κάθημαι (káthēmai): and (to sit; akin to the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος)); to sit down; figuratively, to remain, reside. Origin: from G2596 (κατά); KJV: dwell, sit (by, down)

G2522 καθημερινός (kathēmerinós): quotidian. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2250 (ἡμέρα); KJV: daily

G2523 καθίζω (kathízō): to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively, appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle (hover, dwell). Origin: another (active) form for G2516 (καθέζομαι); KJV: continue, set, sit (down), tarry

G2524 καθίημι (kathíēmi): and (to send); to lower. Origin: from G2596 (κατά); KJV: let down

G2525 καθίστημι (kathístēmi): to place down (permanently), i.e. (figuratively) to designate, constitute, convoy. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: appoint, be, conduct, make, ordain, set

G2526 καθό (kathó): according to which thing, i.e. precisely as, in proportion as. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3739 (ὅς); KJV: according to that, (inasmuch) as

G2527 καθόλου (kathólou): on the whole, i.e. entirely. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3650 (ὅλος); KJV: at all

G2528 καθοπλίζω (kathoplízō): and G3695 (ὁπλίζω); to equip fully with armor. Origin: from G2596 (κατά); KJV: arm

G2529 καθοράω (kathoráō): to behold fully, i.e. (figuratively) distinctly apprehend. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: clearly see

G2530 καθότι (kathóti): and G3739 (ὅς) and G5100 (τὶς); according to which certain thing, i.e. as far (or inasmuch) as. Origin: from G2596 (κατά); KJV: (according, forasmuch) as, because (that)

G2531 καθώς (kathṓs): just (or inasmuch) as, that. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5613 (ὡς); KJV: according to, (according, even) as, how, when

G2532 καί (kaí): and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words. Origin: apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also a cumulative force; KJV: and, also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when, yet

G2533 Καϊάφας (Kaïáphas): the dell; Caiaphas (i.e. Cajepha), an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin; KJV: Caiaphas

G2534 καίγε (kaíge): and at least (or even, indeed). Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G1065 (γέ); KJV: and, at least

G2535 Κάϊν (Káïn): Cain, (i.e. Cajin), the son of Adam. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7014); KJV: Cain

G2536 Καϊνάν (Kaïnán): Cainan (i.e. Kenan), the name of two patriarchs. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7018); KJV: Cainan

G2537 καινός (kainós): Origin: of uncertain affinity; new (especially in freshness; while G3501 (νέος) is properly so with respect to age KJV: new

G2538 καινότης (kainótēs): renewal (figuratively). Origin: from G2537 (καινός); KJV: newness

G2539 καίπερ (kaíper): and indeed, i.e. nevertheless or notwithstanding. Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G4007 (περ); KJV: and yet, although

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2540 to G2671
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2540 καιρός (kairós): an occasion, i.e. set or proper time. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: X always, opportunity, (convenient, due) season, (due, short, while) time, a while

G2541 Καῖσαρ (Kaîsar): Cæsar, a title of the Roman emperor. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Cæsar

G2542 Καισάρεια (Kaisáreia): Cæsaria, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from G2541 (Καῖσαρ); KJV: Cæsarea

G2543 καίτοι (kaítoi): and yet, i.e. nevertheless. Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G5104 (τοί); KJV: although

G2544 καίτοιγε (kaítoige): and yet indeed, i.e. although really. Origin: from G2543 (καίτοι) and G1065 (γέ); KJV: nevertheless, though

G2545 καίω (kaíō): to set on fire, i.e. kindle or (by implication) consume. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: burn, light

G2546 κἀκεῖ (kakeî): likewise in that place. Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G1563 (ἐκεῖ); KJV: and there, there (thither) also

G2547 κἀκεῖθεν (kakeîthen): likewise from that place (or time). Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G1564 (ἐκεῖθεν); KJV: and afterward (from) (thence), thence also

G2548 κἀκεῖνος (kakeînos): likewise that (or those). Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G1565 (ἐκεῖνος); KJV: and him (other, them), even he, him also, them (also), (and) they

G2549 κακία (kakía): badness, i.e. (subjectively) depravity, or (actively) malignity, or (passively) trouble. Origin: from G2556 (κακός); KJV: evil, malice(-iousness), naughtiness, wickedness

G2550 κακοήθεια (kakoḗtheia): bad character, i.e. (specially) mischievousness. Origin: from a compound of G2556 (κακός) and G2239 (ἦθος); KJV: malignity

G2551 κακολογέω (kakologéō): to revile. Origin: from a compound of G2556 (κακός) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: curse, speak evil of

G2552 κακοπάθεια (kakopátheia): hardship. Origin: from a compound of G2256 (ἡμιώριον) and G3806 (πάθος); KJV: suffering affliction

G2553 κακοπαθέω (kakopathéō): to undergo hardship. Origin: from the same as G2552 (κακοπάθεια); KJV: be afflicted, endure afflictions (hardness), suffer trouble

G2554 κακοποιέω (kakopoiéō): to be a bad-doer, i.e. (objectively) to injure, or (genitive) to sin. Origin: from G2555 (κακοποιός); KJV: do(ing) evil

G2555 κακοποιός (kakopoiós): a bad-doer; (specially), a criminal. Origin: from G2556 (κακός) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: evil-doer, malefactor

G2556 κακός (kakós): worthless (intrinsically, such; whereas G4190 (πονηρός) properly refers to effects), i.e. (subjectively) depraved, or (objectively) injurious. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: bad, evil, harm, ill, noisome, wicked

G2557 κακοῦργος (kakoûrgos): a wrong-doer, i.e. criminal. Origin: from G2556 (κακός) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: evil-doer, malefactor

G2558 κακουχέω (kakouchéō): to maltreat. Origin: from a presumed compound of G2556 (κακός) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: which suffer adversity, torment

G2559 κακόω (kakóō): to injure; figuratively, to exasperate. Origin: from G2556 (κακός); KJV: make evil affected, entreat evil, harm, hurt, vex

G2560 κακῶς (kakōs): badly (physically or morally). Origin: from G2556 (κακός); KJV: amiss, diseased, evil, grievously, miserably, sick, sore

G2561 κάκωσις (kákōsis): maltreatment. Origin: from G2559 (κακόω); KJV: affliction

G2562 καλάμη (kalámē): a stalk of grain, i.e. (collectively) stubble. Origin: feminine of G2563 (κάλαμος); KJV: stubble

G2563 κάλαμος (kálamos): a reed (the plant or its stem, or that of a similar plant); by implication, a pen. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: pen, reed

G2564 καλέω (kaléō): to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a variety of applications, directly or otherwise). Origin: akin to the base of G2753 (κελεύω); KJV: bid, call (forth), (whose, whose sur-)name (was (called))

G2565 καλλιέλαιος (kalliélaios): a cultivated olive tree, i.e. a domesticated or improved one. Origin: from the base of G2566 (καλλίον) and G1636 (ἐλαία); KJV: good olive tree

G2566 καλλίον (kallíon): (adverbially) better than many. Origin: neuter of the (irregular) comparative of G2570 (καλός); KJV: very well

G2567 καλοδιδάσκαλος (kalodidáskalos): a teacher of the right. Origin: from G2570 (καλός) and G1320 (διδάσκαλος); KJV: teacher of good things

G2568 Καλοὶ Λιμένες (Kaloì Liménes): Good Harbors, i.e. Fairhaven, a bay of Crete. Origin: plural of G2570 (καλός) and G3040 (λιμήν); KJV: fair havens

G2569 καλοποιέω (kalopoiéō): to do well, i.e. live virtuously. Origin: from G2570 (καλός) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: well doing

G2570 καλός (kalós): Origin: of uncertain affinity; properly, beautiful, but chiefly (figuratively) good (literally or morally), i.e. valuable or virtuous (for appearance or use, and thus distinguished from G18 (ἀγαθός), which is properly intrinsic) KJV: X better, fair, good(-ly), honest, meet, well, worthy

G2571 κάλυμα (kályma): a cover, i.e. veil. Origin: from G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: vail

G2572 καλύπτω (kalýptō): to cover up (literally or figuratively). Origin: akin to G2813 (κλέπτω) and G2928 (κρύπτω); KJV: cover, hide

G2573 καλῶς (kalōs): well (usually morally). Origin: adverb from G2570 (καλός); KJV: (in a) good (place), honestly, + recover, (full) well

G2574 κάμηλος (kámēlos): a "camel". Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1581); KJV: camel

G2575 κάμινος (káminos): a furnace. Origin: probably from G2545 (καίω); KJV: furnace

G2576 καμμύω (kammýō): to shut down, i.e. close the eyes. Origin: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and the base of G3466 (μυστήριον); KJV: close

G2577 κάμνω (kámnō): properly, to toil, i.e. (by implication) to tire (figuratively, faint, sicken). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: faint, sick, be wearied

G2578 κάμπτω (kámptō): to bend. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: bow

G2579 κἄν (kán): and (or even) if. Origin: from G2532 (καί) and G1437 (ἐάν); KJV: and (also) if (so much as), if but, at the least, though, yet

G2580 Κανᾶ (Kanâ): Cana, a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H7071); KJV: Cana

G2581 Κανανίτης (Kananítēs): zealous; Cananites, an epithet. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H7067); KJV: Canaanite (by mistake for a derivative from G5477 (Χαναάν))

G2582 Κανδάκη (Kandákē): Candacè, an Egyptian queen. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Candace

G2583 κανών (kanṓn): a rule ("canon"), i.e. (figuratively) a standard (of faith and practice); by implication, a boundary, i.e. (figuratively) a sphere (of activity). Origin: from (a straight reed, i.e. rod); KJV: line, rule

G2584 Καπερναούμ (Kapernaoúm): Capernaum (i.e. Caphanachum), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (probably H3723 and H5151); KJV: Capernaum

G2585 καπηλεύω (kapēleúō): to retail, i.e. (by implication) to adulterate (figuratively). Origin: from (a huckster); KJV: corrupt

G2586 καπνός (kapnós): smoke. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: smoke

G2587 Καππαδοκία (Kappadokía): Cappadocia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Cappadocia

G2588 καρδία (kardía): the heart, i.e. (figuratively) the thoughts or feelings (mind); also (by analogy) the middle. Origin: prolonged from a primary (Latin cor, "heart"); KJV: (+ broken-)heart(-ed)

G2589 καρδιογνώστης (kardiognṓstēs): a heart-knower. Origin: from G2588 (καρδία) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: which knowest the hearts

G2590 καρπός (karpós): fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively. Origin: probably from the base of G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: fruit

G2591 Κάρπος (Kárpos): Carpus, probably a Christian. Origin: perhaps for G2590 (καρπός); KJV: Carpus

G2592 καρποφορέω (karpophoréō): to be fertile (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2593 (καρποφόρος); KJV: be (bear, bring forth) fruit(-ful)

G2593 καρποφόρος (karpophóros): fruitbearing (figuratively). Origin: from G2590 (καρπός) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: fruitful

G2594 καρτερέω (karteréō): to be strong, i.e. (figuratively) steadfast (patient). Origin: from a derivative of G2904 (κράτος) (transposed); KJV: endure

G2595 κάρφος (kárphos): a dry twig or straw. Origin: from (to wither); KJV: mote

G2596 κατά (katá): (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined). Origin: a primary particle; KJV: about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), … by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with

G2597 καταβαίνω (katabaínō): to descend (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: come (get, go, step) down, fall (down)

G2598 καταβάλλω (katabállō): to throw down. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: cast down, lay

G2599 καταβαρέω (katabaréō): to impose upon. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G916 (βαρέω); KJV: burden

G2600 κατάβασις (katábasis): a declivity. Origin: from G2597 (καταβαίνω); KJV: descent

G2601 καταβιβάζω (katabibázō): to cause to go down, i.e. precipitate. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: bring (thrust) down

G2602 καταβολή (katabolḗ): a deposition, i.e. founding; figuratively, conception. Origin: from G2598 (καταβάλλω); KJV: conceive, foundation

G2603 καταβραβεύω (katabrabeúō): to award the price against, i.e. (figuratively) to defraud (of salvation). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1018 (βραβεύω) (in its original sense); KJV: beguile of reward

G2604 καταγγελεύς (katangeleús): a proclaimer. Origin: from G2605 (καταγγέλλω); KJV: setter forth

G2605 καταγγέλλω (katangéllō): to proclaim, promulgate. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: declare, preach, shew, speak of, teach

G2606 καταγελάω (katageláō): to laugh down, i.e. deride. KJV: laugh to scorn

G2607 καταγινώσκω (kataginṓskō): to note against, i.e. find fault with. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: blame, condemn

G2608 κατάγνυμι (katágnymi): to rend in pieces, i.e. crack apart. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: break

G2609 κατάγω (katágō): to lead down; specially, to moor a vessel. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring (down, forth), (bring to) land, touch

G2610 καταγωνίζομαι (katagōnízomai): to struggle against, i.e. (by implication) to overcome. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G75 (ἀγωνίζομαι); KJV: subdue

G2611 καταδέω (katadéō): to tie down, i.e. bandage (a wound). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1210 (δέω); KJV: bind up

G2612 κατάδηλος (katádēlos): manifest. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) intensive and G1212 (δῆλος); KJV: far more evident

G2613 καταδικάζω (katadikázō): to adjudge against, i.e. pronounce guilty. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G1349 (δίκη); KJV: condemn

G2614 καταδιώκω (katadiṓkō): to hunt down, i.e. search for. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1377 (διώκω); KJV: follow after

G2615 καταδουλόω (katadoulóō): to enslave utterly. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1402 (δουλόω); KJV: bring into bondage

G2616 καταδυναστεύω (katadynasteúō): to exercise dominion against, i.e. oppress. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G1413 (δυνάστης); KJV: oppress

G2617 καταισχύνω (kataischýnō): to shame down, i.e. disgrace or (by implication) put to the blush. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G153 (αἰσχύνομαι); KJV: confound, dishonour, (be a-, make a-)shame(-d)

G2618 κατακαίω (katakaíō): to burn down (to the ground), i.e. consume wholly. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2545 (καίω); KJV: burn (up, utterly)

G2619 κατακαλύπτω (katakalýptō): to cover wholly, i.e. veil. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: cover, hide

G2620 κατακαυχάομαι (katakaucháomai): to exult against (i.e. over). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2744 (καυχάομαι); KJV: boast (against), glory, rejoice against

G2621 κατάκειμαι (katákeimai): to lie down, i.e. (by implication) be sick; specially, to recline at a meal. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: keep, lie, sit at meat (down)

G2622 κατακλάω (katakláō): to break down, i.e. divide. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2806 (κλάω); KJV: break

G2623 κατακλείω (katakleíō): to shut down (in a dungeon), i.e. incarcerate. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2808 (κλείω); KJV: shut up

G2624 κατακληροδοτέω (kataklērodotéō): to be a giver of lots to each, i.e. (by implication) to apportion an estate. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of a compound of G2819 (κλῆρος) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: divide by lot

G2625 κατακλίνω (kataklínō): to recline down, i.e. (specially) to take a place at table. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: (make) sit down (at meat)

G2626 κατακλύζω (kataklýzō): to dash (wash) down, i.e. (by implication) to deluge. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G2830 (κλύδων); KJV: overflow

G2627 κατακλυσμός (kataklysmós): an inundation. Origin: from G2626 (κατακλύζω); KJV: flood

G2628 κατακολουθέω (katakolouthéō): to accompany closely. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G190 (ἀκολουθέω); KJV: follow (after)

G2629 κατακόπτω (katakóptō): to chop down, i.e. mangle. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: cut

G2630 κατακρημνίζω (katakrēmnízō): to precipitate down. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G2911 (κρημνός); KJV: cast down headlong

G2631 κατάκριμα (katákrima): an adverse sentence (the verdict). Origin: from G2632 (κατακρίνω); KJV: condemnation

G2632 κατακρίνω (katakrínō): to judge against, i.e. sentence. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: condemn, damn

G2633 κατάκρισις (katákrisis): sentencing adversely (the act). Origin: from G2632 (κατακρίνω); KJV: condemn(-ation)

G2634 κατακυριεύω (katakyrieúō): to lord against, i.e. control, subjugate. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2961 (κυριεύω); KJV: exercise dominion over (lordship), be lord over, overcome

G2635 καταλαλέω (katalaléō): to be a traducer, i.e. to slander. Origin: from G2637 (κατάλαλος); KJV: speak against (evil of)

G2636 καταλαλία (katalalía): defamation. Origin: from G2637 (κατάλαλος); KJV: backbiting, evil speaking

G2637 κατάλαλος (katálalos): talkative against, i.e. a slanderer. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and the base of G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: backbiter

G2638 καταλαμβάνω (katalambánō): to take eagerly, i.e. seize, possess, etc. (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: apprehend, attain, come upon, comprehend, find, obtain, perceive, (over-)take

G2639 καταλέγω (katalégō): to lay down, i.e. (figuratively) to enrol. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original meaning); KJV: take into the number

G2640 κατάλειμμα (katáleimma): a remainder, i.e. (by implication) a few. Origin: from G2641 (καταλείπω); KJV: remnant

G2641 καταλείπω (kataleípō): to leave down, i.e. behind; by implication, to abandon, have remaining. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: forsake, leave, reserve

G2642 καταλιθάζω (katalitházō): to stone down, i.e. to death. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3034 (λιθάζω); KJV: stone

G2643 καταλλαγή (katallagḗ): exchange (figuratively, adjustment), i.e. restoration to (the divine) favor. Origin: from G2644 (καταλλάσσω); KJV: atonement, reconciliation(-ing)

G2644 καταλλάσσω (katallássō): to change mutually, i.e. (figuratively) to compound a difference. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω); KJV: reconcile

G2645 κατάλοιπος (katáloipos): left down (behind), i.e remaining (plural the rest). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3062 (λοιποί); KJV: residue

G2646 κατάλυμα (katályma): properly, a dissolution (breaking up of a journey), i.e. (by implication) a lodging-place. Origin: from G2647 (καταλύω); KJV: guestchamber, inn

G2647 καταλύω (katalýō): to loosen down (disintegrate), i.e. (by implication) to demolish (literally or figuratively); specially (compare G2646 (κατάλυμα)) to halt for the night. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: destroy, dissolve, be guest, lodge, come to nought, overthrow, throw down

G2648 καταμανθάνω (katamanthánō): to learn thoroughly, i.e. (by implication) to note carefully. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3129 (μανθάνω); KJV: consider

G2649 καταμαρτυρέω (katamartyréō): to testify against. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3140 (μαρτυρέω); KJV: witness against

G2650 καταμένω (kataménō): to stay fully, i.e. reside. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: abide

G2651 καταμόνας (katamónas): according to sole places, i.e. (adverbially) separately. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and accusative case plural feminine of G3441 (μόνος) (with G5561 (χώρα) implied); KJV: alone

G2652 κατανάθεμα (katanáthema): an imprecation. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) (intensive) and G331 (ἀνάθεμα); KJV: curse

G2653 καταναθεματίζω (katanathematízō): to imprecate. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) (intensive) and G332 (ἀναθεματίζω); KJV: curse

G2654 καταναλίσκω (katanalískō): to consume utterly. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G355 (ἀναλίσκω); KJV: consume

G2655 καταναρκάω (katanarkáō): to grow utterly torpid, i.e. (by implication) slothful (figuratively, expensive). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and (to be numb); KJV: be burdensome (chargeable)

G2656 κατανεύω (kataneúō): to nod down (towards), i.e. (by analogy) to make signs to. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3506 (νεύω); KJV: beckon

G2657 κατανοέω (katanoéō): to observe fully. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: behold, consider, discover, perceive

G2658 καταντάω (katantáō): to meet against, i.e. arrive at (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί); KJV: attain, come

G2659 κατάνυξις (katányxis): a prickling (sensation, as of the limbs asleep), i.e. (by implication, (perhaps by some confusion with G3506 (νεύω) or even with G3571 (νύξ))) stupor (lethargy). Origin: from G2660 (κατανύσσω); KJV: slumber

G2660 κατανύσσω (katanýssō): to pierce thoroughly, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate violently ("sting to the quick"). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3572 (νύσσω); KJV: prick

G2661 καταξιόω (kataxióō): to deem entirely deserving. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G515 (ἀξιόω); KJV: (ac-)count worthy

G2662 καταπατέω (katapatéō): to trample down; figuratively, to reject with disdain. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3961 (πατέω); KJV: trample, tread (down, underfoot)

G2663 κατάπαυσις (katápausis): reposing down, i.e. (by Hebraism) abode. Origin: from G2664 (καταπαύω); KJV: rest

G2664 καταπαύω (katapaúō): to settle down, i.e. (literally) to colonize, or (figuratively) to (cause to) desist. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3973 (παύω); KJV: cease, (give) rest(-rain)

G2665 καταπέτασμα (katapétasma): something spread thoroughly, i.e. (specially) the door screen (to the Most Holy Place) in the Jewish Temple. Origin: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and a congener of G4072 (πέτομαι); KJV: vail

G2666 καταπίνω (katapínō): to drink down, i.e. gulp entire (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4095 (πίνω); KJV: devour, drown, swallow (up)

G2667 καταπίπτω (katapíptō): to fall down. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall (down)

G2668 καταπλέω (katapléō): to sail down upon a place, i.e. to land at. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4126 (πλέω); KJV: arrive

G2669 καταπονέω (kataponéō): to labor down, i.e. wear with toil (figuratively, harass). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G4192 (πόνος); KJV: oppress, vex

G2670 καταποντίζω (katapontízō): to plunge down, i.e. submerge. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of the same as G4195 (Πόντος); KJV: drown, sink

G2671 κατάρα (katára): imprecation, execration. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) (intensive) and G685 (ἀρά); KJV: curse(-d, ing)

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2672 to G2818
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2672 καταράομαι (kataráomai): to execrate; by analogy, to doom. Origin: middle voice from G2671 (κατάρα); KJV: curse

G2673 καταργέω (katargéō): to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G691 (ἀργέω); KJV: abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void

G2674 καταριθμέω (katarithméō): to reckon among. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G705 (ἀριθμέω); KJV: number with

G2675 καταρτίζω (katartízō): to complete thoroughly, i.e. repair (literally or figuratively) or adjust. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G739 (ἄρτιος); KJV: fit, frame, mend, (make) perfect(-ly join together), prepare, restore

G2676 κατάρτισις (katártisis): thorough equipment (subjectively). Origin: from G2675 (καταρτίζω); KJV: perfection

G2677 καταρτισμός (katartismós): complete furnishing (objectively). Origin: from G2675 (καταρτίζω); KJV: perfecting

G2678 κατασείω (kataseíō): to sway downward, i.e. make a signal. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4579 (σείω); KJV: beckon

G2679 κατασκάπτω (kataskáptō): to undermine, i.e. (by implication) destroy. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4626 (σκάπτω); KJV: dig down, ruin

G2680 κατασκευάζω (kataskeuázō): to prepare thoroughly (properly, by external equipment; whereas G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω) refers rather to internal fitness); by implication, to construct, create. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος); KJV: build, make, ordain, prepare

G2681 κατασκηνόω (kataskēnóō): to camp down, i.e. haunt; figuratively, to remain. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4637 (σκηνόω); KJV: lodge, rest

G2682 κατασκήνωσις (kataskḗnōsis): an encamping, i.e. (figuratively) a perch. Origin: from G2681 (κατασκηνόω); KJV: nest

G2683 κατασκιάζω (kataskiázō): to overshade, i.e. cover. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G4639 (σκιά); KJV: shadow

G2684 κατασκοπέω (kataskopéō): to be a sentinel, i.e. to inspect insidiously. Origin: from G2685 (κατάσκοπος); KJV: spy out

G2685 κατάσκοπος (katáskopos): a reconnoiterer. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) (intensive) and G4649 (σκοπός) (in the sense of a watcher); KJV: spy

G2686 κατασοφίζομαι (katasophízomai): to be crafty against, i.e. circumvent. Origin: middle voice from G2596 (κατά) and G4679 (σοφίζω); KJV: deal subtilly with

G2687 καταστέλλω (katastéllō): to put down, i.e. quell. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: appease, quiet

G2688 κατάστημα (katástēma): properly, a position or condition, i.e. (subjectively) demeanor. Origin: from G2525 (καθίστημι); KJV: behaviour

G2689 καταστολή (katastolḗ): a deposit, i.e. (specially) costume. Origin: from G2687 (καταστέλλω); KJV: apparel

G2690 καταστρέφω (katastréphō): to turn upside down, i.e. upset. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: overthrow

G2691 καταστρηνιάω (katastrēniáō): to become voluptuous against. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4763 (στρηνιάω); KJV: begin to wax wanton against

G2692 καταστροφή (katastrophḗ): an overturn ("catastrophe"), i.e. demolition; figuratively, apostasy. Origin: from G2690 (καταστρέφω); KJV: overthrow, subverting

G2693 καταστρώννυμι (katastrṓnnymi): to strew down, i.e. (by implication) to prostrate (slay). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4766 (στρώννυμι); KJV: overthrow

G2694 κατασύρω (katasýrō): to drag down, i.e. arrest judicially. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4951 (σύρω); KJV: hale

G2695 κατασφάττω (kataspháttō): to kill down, i.e. slaughter. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4969 (σφάζω); KJV: slay

G2696 κατασφραγίζω (katasphragízō): to seal closely. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G4972 (σφραγίζω); KJV: seal

G2697 κατάσχεσις (katáschesis): a holding down, i.e. occupancy. Origin: from G2722 (κατέχω); KJV: possession

G2698 κατατίθημι (katatíthēmi): to place down, i.e. deposit (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: do, lay, shew

G2699 κατατομή (katatomḗ): a cutting down (off), i.e. mutilation (ironically). Origin: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and (to cut); KJV: concision

G2700 κατατοξεύω (katatoxeúō): to shoot down with an arrow or other missile. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G5115 (τόξον); KJV: thrust through

G2701 κατατρέχω (katatréchō): to run down, i.e. hasten from a tower. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5143 (τρέχω); KJV: run down

G2702 καταφέρω (kataphérō): to bear down, i.e. (figuratively) overcome (with drowsiness); specially, to cast a vote. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate); KJV: fall, give, sink down

G2703 καταφεύγω (katapheúgō): to flee down (away). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5343 (φεύγω); KJV: flee

G2704 καταφθείρω (kataphtheírō): to spoil entirely, i.e. (literally) to destroy; or (figuratively) to deprave. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5351 (φθείρω); KJV: --corrupt, utterly perish

G2705 καταφιλέω (kataphiléō): to kiss earnestly. Origin: from 2596 and 5368; KJV: kiss

G2706 καταφρονέω (kataphronéō): to think against, i.e. disesteem. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5426 (φρονέω); KJV: despise

G2707 καταφροντής (kataphrontḗs): a contemner. Origin: from G2706 (καταφρονέω); KJV: despiser

G2708 καταχέω (katachéō): to pour down (out). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and cheo (to pour); KJV: pour

G2709 καταχθόνιος (katachthónios): subterranean, i.e. infernal (belonging to the world of departed spirits). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and (the ground); KJV: under the earth

G2710 καταχράομαι (katachráomai): to overuse, i.e. misuse. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5530 (χράομαι); KJV: abuse

G2711 καταψύχω (katapsýchō): to cool down (off), i.e. refresh. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G5594 (ψύχω); KJV: cool

G2712 κατείδωλος (kateídōlos): utterly idolatrous. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) (intensively) and G1497 (εἴδωλον); KJV: wholly given to idolatry

G2713 κατέναντι (katénanti): directly opposite. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1725 (ἔναντι); KJV: before, over against

G2714 κατενώπιον (katenṓpion): directly in front of. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1799 (ἐνώπιον); KJV: before (the presence of), in the sight of

G2715 κατεξουσιάζω (katexousiázō): to have (wield) full privilege over. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G1850 (ἐξουσιάζω); KJV: exercise authority

G2716 κατεργάζομαι (katergázomai): to work fully, i.e. accomplish; by implication, to finish, fashion. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2038 (ἐργάζομαι); KJV: cause, to (deed), perform, work (out)

G2718 κατέρχομαι (katérchomai): to come (or go) down (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate); KJV: come (down), depart, descend, go down, land

G2719 κατεσθίω (katesthíō): to eat down, i.e. devour (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2068 (ἐσθίω) (including its alternate); KJV: devour

G2720 κατευθύνω (kateuthýnō): to straighten fully, i.e. (figuratively) direct. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2116 (εὐθύνω); KJV: guide, direct

G2721 κατεφίστημι (katephístēmi): to stand over against, i.e. rush upon (assault). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2186 (ἐφίστημι); KJV: make insurrection against

G2722 κατέχω (katéchō): to hold down (fast), in various applications (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: have, hold (fast), keep (in memory), let, X make toward, possess, retain, seize on, stay, take, withhold

G2723 κατηγορέω (katēgoréō): to be a plaintiff, i.e. to charge with some offence. Origin: from G2725 (κατήγορος); KJV: accuse, object

G2724 κατηγορία (katēgoría): a complaint ("category"), i.e. criminal charge. Origin: from G2725 (κατήγορος); KJV: accusation (X -ed)

G2725 κατήγορος (katḗgoros): against one in the assembly, i.e. a complainant at law; specially, Satan. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G58 (ἀγορά); KJV: accuser

G2726 κατήφεια (katḗpheia): demureness, i.e. (by implication) sadness. Origin: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and perhaps a derivative of the base of G5316 (φαίνω) (meaning downcast in look); KJV: heaviness

G2727 κατηχέω (katēchéō): to sound down into the ears, i.e. (by implication) to indoctrinate ("catechize") or (genitive case) to apprise of. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2279 (ἦχος); KJV: inform, instruct, teach

G2728 κατιόω (katióō): to rust down, i.e. corrode. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G2447 (ἰός); KJV: canker

G2729 κατισχύω (katischýō): to overpower. Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G2480 (ἰσχύω); KJV: prevail (against)

G2730 κατοικέω (katoikéō): to house permanently, i.e. reside (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2596 (κατά) and G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: dwell(-er), inhabitant(-ter)

G2731 κατοίκησις (katoíkēsis): residence (properly, the act; but by implication, concretely, the mansion). Origin: from G2730 (κατοικέω); KJV: dwelling

G2732 κατοικητήριον (katoikētḗrion): a dwelling-place. Origin: from a derivative of G2730 (κατοικέω); KJV: habitation

G2733 κατοικία (katoikía): residence (properly, the condition; but by implication, the abode itself). KJV: habitation

G2734 κατοπτρίζομαι (katoptrízomai): to mirror oneself, i.e. to see reflected (figuratively). Origin: middle voice from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) (compare G2072 (ἔσοπτρον)); KJV: behold as in a glass

G2735 κατόρθωμα (katórthōma): something made fully upright, i.e. (figuratively) rectification (specially, good public administration). Origin: from a compound of G2596 (κατά) and a derivative of G3717 (ὀρθός) (compare G1357 (διόρθωσις)); KJV: very worthy deed

G2736 κάτω (kátō): downwards. Origin: (compare G2737 (κατώτερος)); adverb from G2596 (κατά); KJV: beneath, bottom, down, under

G2737 κατώτερος (katṓteros): inferior (locally, of Hades). Origin: comparative from G2736 (κάτω); KJV: lower

G2738 καῦμα (kaûma): properly, a burn (concretely), but used (abstractly) of a glow. Origin: from G2545 (καίω); KJV: heat

G2739 καυματίζω (kaumatízō): to burn. Origin: from G2738 (καῦμα); KJV: scorch

G2740 καῦσις (kaûsis): burning (the act). Origin: from G2545 (καίω); KJV: be burned

G2741 καυσόω (kausóō): to set on fire. Origin: from G2740 (καῦσις); KJV: fervent heat

G2742 καύσων (kaúsōn): a glare. Origin: from G2741 (καυσόω); KJV: (burning) heat

G2743 καυτηριάζω (kautēriázō): to brand ("cauterize"), i.e. (by implication) to render unsensitive (figuratively). Origin: from a derivative of G2545 (καίω); KJV: sear with a hot iron

G2744 καυχάομαι (kaucháomai): to vaunt (in a good or a bad sense). Origin: from some (obsolete) base akin to that of (to boast) and G2172 (εὔχομαι); KJV: (make) boast, glory, joy, rejoice

G2745 καύχημα (kaúchēma): a boast (properly, the object; by implication, the act) in a good or a bad sense. Origin: from G2744 (καυχάομαι); KJV: boasting, (whereof) to glory (of), glorying, rejoice(-ing)

G2746 καύχησις (kaúchēsis): boasting (properly, the act; by implication, the object), in a good or a bad sense. Origin: from G2744 (καυχάομαι); KJV: boasting, whereof I may glory, glorying, rejoicing

G2747 Κεγχρεαί (Kenchreaí): Cenchreæ, a port of Corinth. Origin: probably from kegchros (millet); KJV: Cencrea

G2748 Κεδρών (Kedrṓn): Cedron (i.e. Kidron), a brook near Jerusalem. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6939); KJV: Cedron

G2749 κεῖμαι (keîmai): to lie outstretched (literally or figuratively). Origin: middle voice of a primary verb; KJV: be (appointed, laid up, made, set), lay, lie

G2750 κειρία (keiría): a swathe, i.e. winding-sheet. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: graveclothes

G2751 κείρω (keírō): to shear. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: shear(-er)

G2752 κέλευμα (kéleuma): a cry of incitement. Origin: from G2753 (κελεύω); KJV: shout

G2753 κελεύω (keleúō): "hail"; to incite by word, i.e. order. Origin: from a primary (to urge on); KJV: bid, (at, give) command(-ment)

G2754 κενοδοξία (kenodoxía): empty glorying, i.e. self-conceit. Origin: from G2755 (κενόδοξος); KJV: vain-glory

G2755 κενόδοξος (kenódoxos): vainly glorifying, i.e. self-conceited. Origin: from G2756 (κενός) and G1391 (δόξα); KJV: desirous of vain-glory

G2756 κενός (kenós): empty (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: empty, (in) vain

G2757 κενοφωνία (kenophōnía): empty sounding, i.e. fruitless discussion. Origin: from a presumed compound of G2756 (κενός) and G5456 (φωνή); KJV: vain

G2758 κενόω (kenóō): to make empty, i.e. (figuratively) to abase, neutralize, falsify. Origin: from G2756 (κενός); KJV: make (of none effect, of no reputation, void), be in vain

G2759 κέντρον (kéntron): a point ("centre"), i.e. a sting (figuratively, poison) or goad (figuratively, divine impulse). Origin: from (to prick); KJV: prick, sting

G2760 κεντυρίων (kentyríōn): a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred soldiers. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: centurion

G2761 κενῶς (kenōs): vainly, i.e. to no purpose. Origin: adverb from G2756 (κενός); KJV: in vain

G2762 κεραία (keraía): something horn-like, i.e. (specially) the apex of a Hebrew letter (figuratively, the least particle). Origin: feminine of a presumed derivative of the base of G2768 (κέρας); KJV: tittle

G2763 κεραμεύς (kerameús): a potter. Origin: from G2766 (κέραμος); KJV: potter

G2764 κεραμικός (keramikós): made of clay, i.e. earthen. Origin: from G2766 (κέραμος); KJV: of a potter

G2765 κεράμιον (kerámion): an earthenware vessel, i.e. jar. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2766 (κέραμος); KJV: pitcher

G2766 κέραμος (kéramos): earthenware, i.e. a tile (by analogy, a thin roof or awning). Origin: probably from the base of G2767 (κεράννυμι) (through the idea of mixing clay and water); KJV: tiling

G2767 κεράννυμι (keránnymi): to mingle, i.e. (by implication) to pour out (for drinking). Origin: prolonged form of a more primary (which is used in certain tenses); KJV: fill, pour out

G2768 κέρας (kéras): a horn (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a primary (the hair of the head); KJV: horn

G2769 κεράτιον (kerátion): something horned, i.e. (specially) the pod of the carob-tree. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2768 (κέρας); KJV: husk

G2770 κερδαίνω (kerdaínō): to gain (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2771 (κέρδος); KJV: (get) gain, win

G2771 κέρδος (kérdos): gain (pecuniary or genitive case). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: gain, lucre

G2772 κέρμα (kérma): a clipping (bit), i.e. (specially) a coin. Origin: from G2751 (κείρω); KJV: money

G2773 κερματιστής (kermatistḗs): a handler of coins, i.e. money-broker. Origin: from a derivative of G2772 (κέρμα); KJV: changer of money

G2774 κεφάλαιον (kephálaion): a principal thing, i.e. main point; specially, an amount (of money). Origin: neuter of a derivative of G2776 (κεφαλή); KJV: sum

G2775 κεφαλαιόω (kephalaióō): (specially) to strike on the head. Origin: from the same as G2774 (κεφάλαιον); KJV: wound in the head

G2776 κεφαλή (kephalḗ): the head (as the part most readily taken hold of), literally or figuratively. Origin: from the primary (in the sense of seizing); KJV: head

G2777 κεφαλίς (kephalís): properly, a knob, i.e. (by implication) a roll (by extension from the end of a stick on which the manuscript was rolled). Origin: from G2776 (κεφαλή); KJV: volume

G2778 κῆνσος (kēnsos): properly, an enrollment ("census"), i.e. (by implication) a tax. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: tribute

G2779 κῆπος (kēpos): a garden. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: garden

G2780 κηπουρός (kēpourós): a garden-keeper, i.e. gardener. Origin: from G2779 (κῆπος) and (a warden); KJV: gardener

G2781 κηρίον (kēríon): a cell for honey, i.e. (collectively) the comb. Origin: diminutive from (wax); KJV: (honey-)comb
