G2782 κήρυγμα (kḗrygma): a proclamation (especially of the gospel; by implication, the gospel itself). Origin: from G2784 (κηρύσσω); KJV: preaching

G2783 κῆρυξ (kēryx): a herald, i.e. of divine truth (especially of the gospel). Origin: from G2784 (κηρύσσω); KJV: preacher

G2784 κηρύσσω (kērýssō): to herald (as a public crier), especially divine truth (the gospel). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: preacher(-er), proclaim, publish

G2785 κῆτος (kētos): a huge fish (as gaping for prey). Origin: probably from the base of G5490 (χάσμα); KJV: whale

G2786 Κηφᾶς (Kēphâs): the Rock; Cephas (i.e. Kepha), a surname of Peter. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H3710); KJV: Cephas

G2787 κιβωτός (kibōtós): a box, i.e. the sacred ark and that of Noah. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: ark

G2788 κιθάρα (kithára): a lyre. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: harp

G2789 κιθαρίζω (kitharízō): to play on a lyre. Origin: from G2788 (κιθάρα); KJV: harp

G2790 κιθαρῳδός (kitharōidós): a lyre-singer(-player), i.e. harpist. Origin: from G2788 (κιθάρα) and a derivative of the same as G5603 (ᾠδή); KJV: harper

G2791 Κιλικία (Kilikía): Cilicia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Cilicia

G2792 κινάμωμον (kinámōmon): cinnamon. Origin: of foreign origin (compare H7076); KJV: cinnamon

G2793 κινδυνεύω (kindyneúō): to undergo peril. Origin: from G2794 (κίνδυνος); KJV: be in danger, be (stand) in jeopardy

G2794 κίνδυνος (kíndynos): danger. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: peril

G2795 κινέω (kinéō): to stir (transitively), literally or figuratively. Origin: from (poetic for , to go); KJV: (re-)move(-r), way

G2796 κίνησις (kínēsis): a stirring. Origin: from G2795 (κινέω); KJV: moving

G2797 Κίς (Kís): Cis (i.e. Kish), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7027); KJV: Cis

G2798 κλάδος (kládos): a twig or bough (as if broken off). Origin: from G2806 (κλάω); KJV: branch

G2799 κλαίω (klaíō): to sob, i.e. wail aloud (whereas 1145 is rather to cry silently). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: bewail, weep

G2800 κλάσις (klásis): fracture (the act). Origin: from G2806 (κλάω); KJV: breaking

G2801 κλάσμα (klásma): a piece (bit). Origin: from G2806 (κλάω); KJV: broken, fragment

G2802 Κλαύδη (Klaúdē): Claude, an island near Crete. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Clauda

G2803 Κλαυδία (Klaudía): Claudia, a Christian woman. Origin: feminine of G2804 (Κλαύδιος); KJV: Claudia

G2804 Κλαύδιος (Klaúdios): Claudius, the name of two Romans. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Claudius

G2805 κλαυθμός (klauthmós): lamentation. Origin: from G2799 (κλαίω); KJV: wailing, weeping, X wept

G2806 κλάω (kláō): to break (specially, of bread). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: break

G2807 κλείς (kleís): a key (as shutting a lock), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G2808 (κλείω); KJV: key

G2808 κλείω (kleíō): to close (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: shut (up)

G2809 κλέμμα (klémma): stealing (properly, the thing stolen, but used of the act). Origin: from G2813 (κλέπτω); KJV: theft

G2810 Κλεόπας (Kleópas): Cleopas, a Christian. Origin: probably contracted from (compound of G2811 (κλέος) and G3962 (πατήρ)); KJV: Cleopas

G2811 κλέος (kléos): renown (as if being called). Origin: from a shorter form of G2564 (καλέω); KJV: glory

G2812 κλέπτης (kléptēs): a stealer (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2813 (κλέπτω); KJV: thief

G2813 κλέπτω (kléptō): to filch. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: steal

G2814 κλῆμα (klēma): a limb or shoot (as if broken off). Origin: from G2806 (κλάω); KJV: branch

G2815 Κλήμης (Klḗmēs): merciful; Clemes (i.e. Clemens), a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Clement

G2816 κληρονομέω (klēronoméō): to be an heir to (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2818 (κληρονόμος); KJV: be heir, (obtain by) inherit(-ance)

G2817 κληρονομία (klēronomía): heirship, i.e. (concretely) a patrimony or (genitive case) a possession. Origin: from G2818 (κληρονόμος); KJV: inheritance

G2818 κληρονόμος (klēronómos): a sharer by lot, i.e. inheritor (literally or figuratively); by implication, a possessor. Origin: from G2819 (κλῆρος) and the base of G3551 (νόμος) (in its original sense of partitioning, i.e. (reflexively) getting by apportionment); KJV: heir

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2819 to G2970
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2819 κλῆρος (klēros): a die (for drawing chances); by implication, a portion (as if so secured); by extension, an acquisition (especially a patrimony, figuratively). Origin: probably from G2806 (κλάω) (through the idea of using bits of wood, etc., for the purpose; KJV: heritage, inheritance, lot, part

G2820 κληρόω (klēróō): to allot, i.e. (figuratively) to assign (a privilege). Origin: from G2819 (κλῆρος); KJV: obtain an inheritance

G2821 κλῆσις (klēsis): an invitation (figuratively). Origin: from a shorter form of G2564 (καλέω); KJV: calling

G2822 κλητός (klētós): invited, i.e. appointed, or (specially), a saint. Origin: from the same as G2821 (κλῆσις); KJV: called

G2823 κλίβανος (klíbanos): an earthen pot used for baking in. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: oven

G2824 κλίμα (klíma): a slope, i.e. (specially) a "clime" or tract of country. Origin: from G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: part, region

G2825 κλίνη (klínē): a couch (for sleep, sickness, sitting or eating). Origin: from G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: bed, table

G2826 κλινίδιον (klinídion): a pallet or little couch. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2825 (κλίνη); KJV: bed

G2827 κλίνω (klínō): to slant or slope, i.e. incline or recline (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: bow (down), be far spent, lay, turn to flight, wear away

G2828 κλισία (klisía): properly, reclination, i.e. (concretely and specially), a party at a meal. Origin: from a derivative of G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: company

G2829 κλοπή (klopḗ): stealing. Origin: from G2813 (κλέπτω); KJV: theft

G2830 κλύδων (klýdōn): a surge of the sea (literally or figuratively). Origin: from (to billow or dash over); KJV: raging, wave

G2831 κλυδωνίζομαι (klydōnízomai): to surge, i.e. (figuratively) to fluctuate. Origin: middle voice from G2830 (κλύδων); KJV: toss to and fro

G2832 Κλωπᾶς (Klōpâs): Clopas, an Israelite. Origin: of Chaldee origin (corresponding to H256); KJV: Cleophas

G2833 κνήθω (knḗthō): to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to tickle. Origin: from a primary (to scrape); KJV: X itching

G2834 Κνίδος (Knídos): Cnidus, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Cnidus

G2835 κοδράντης (kodrántēs): a quadrans, i.e. the fourth part of an as. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: farthing

G2836 κοιλία (koilía): a cavity, i.e. (especially) the abdomen; by implication, the matrix; figuratively, the heart. Origin: from ("hollow"); KJV: belly, womb

G2837 κοιμάω (koimáō): to put to sleep, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to slumber; figuratively, to decease. Origin: from G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: (be a-, fall a-, fall on) sleep, be dead

G2838 κοίμησις (koímēsis): sleeping, i.e. (by implication) repose. Origin: from G2837 (κοιμάω); KJV: taking of rest

G2839 κοινός (koinós): common, i.e. (literally) shared by all or several, or (ceremonially) profane. Origin: probably from G4862 (σύν); KJV: common, defiled, unclean, unholy

G2840 κοινόω (koinóō): to make (or consider) profane (ceremonially). Origin: from G2839 (κοινός); KJV: call common, defile, pollute, unclean

G2841 κοινωνέω (koinōnéō): to share with others (objectively or subjectively). Origin: from G2844 (κοινωνός); KJV: communicate, distribute, be partaker

G2842 κοινωνία (koinōnía): partnership, i.e. (literally) participation, or (social) intercourse, or (pecuniary) benefaction. Origin: from G2844 (κοινωνός); KJV: (to) communicate(-ation), communion, (contri-)distribution, fellowship

G2843 κοινωνικός (koinōnikós): communicative, i.e. (pecuniarily) liberal. Origin: from G2844 (κοινωνός); KJV: willing to communicate

G2844 κοινωνός (koinōnós): a sharer, i.e. associate. Origin: from G2839 (κοινός); KJV: companion, X fellowship, partaker, partner

G2845 κοίτη (koítē): a couch; by extension, cohabitation; by implication, the male sperm. Origin: from G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: bed, chambering, X conceive

G2846 κοιτών (koitṓn): a bedroom. Origin: from G2845 (κοίτη); KJV: + chamberlain

G2847 κόκκινος (kókkinos): crimson-colored. Origin: from G2848 (κόκκος) (from the kernel-shape of the insect); KJV: scarlet (colour, coloured)

G2848 κόκκος (kókkos): a kernel of seed. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: corn, grain

G2849 κολάζω (kolázō): properly, to curtail, i.e. (figuratively) to chastise (or reserve for infliction). Origin: from (dwarf); KJV: punish

G2850 κολακεία (kolakeía): flattery. Origin: from a derivative of (a fawner); KJV: X flattering

G2851 κόλασις (kólasis): penal infliction. Origin: from G2849 (κολάζω); KJV: punishment, torment

G2852 κολαφίζω (kolaphízō): to rap with the fist. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G2849 (κολάζω); KJV: buffet

G2853 κολλάω (kolláō): to glue, i.e. (passively or reflexively) to stick (figuratively). Origin: from ("glue"); KJV: cleave, join (self), keep company

G2854 κολλούριον (kolloúrion): prob akin to the base of G2853 (κολλάω)); properly, a poultice (as made of or in the form of crackers), i.e. (by analogy) a plaster. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a cake; KJV: eyesalve

G2855 κολλυβιστής (kollybistḗs): probably akin to G2854 (κολλούριον)); a coin-dealer. Origin: from a presumed derivative of (a small coin; KJV: (money-)changer

G2856 κολοβόω (kolobóō): to dock, i.e. (figuratively) abridge. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G2849 (κολάζω); KJV: shorten

G2857 Κολοσσαί (Kolossaí): Colossæ, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: apparently feminine plural of kolossos ("colossal"); KJV: Colosse

G2858 Κολοσσαεύς (Kolossaeús): a Colossæan, (i.e. inhabitant of Colossæ. Origin: from G2857 (Κολοσσαί); KJV: Colossian

G2859 κόλπος (kólpos): the bosom; by analogy, a bay. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: bosom, creek

G2860 κολυμβάω (kolymbáō): to plunge into water. Origin: from (a diver); KJV: swim

G2861 κολυμβήθρα (kolymbḗthra): a diving-place, i.e. pond for bathing (or swimming). Origin: from G2860 (κολυμβάω); KJV: pool

G2862 κολωνία (kolōnía): a Roman "colony" for veterans. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: colony

G2863 κομάω (komáō): to wear tresses of hair. Origin: from G2864 (κόμη); KJV: have long hair

G2864 κόμη (kómē): the hair of the head (locks, as ornamental, and thus differing from G2359 (θρίξ); which properly denotes merely the scalp). Origin: apparently from the same as G2865 (κομίζω); KJV: hair

G2865 κομίζω (komízō): properly, to provide for, i.e. (by implication) to carry off (as if from harm; genitive case obtain). Origin: from a primary (to tend, i.e. take care of); KJV: bring, receive

G2866 κομψότερον (kompsóteron): figuratively, convalescent. Origin: neuter comparative of a derivative of the base of 2865 (meaning, properly, well dressed, i.e. nice); KJV: + began to amend

G2867 κονιάω (koniáō): by analogy, lime); to whitewash. Origin: from (dust; KJV: whiten

G2868 κονιορτός (koniortós): pulverulence (as blown about). Origin: from the base of G2867 (κονιάω) and ornumi (to "rouse"); KJV: dust

G2869 κοπάζω (kopázō): to tire, i.e. (figuratively) to relax. Origin: from G2873 (κόπος); KJV: cease

G2870 κοπετός (kopetós): mourning (properly, by beating the breast). Origin: from G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: lamentation

G2871 κοπή (kopḗ): cutting, i.e. carnage. Origin: from G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: slaughter

G2872 κοπιάω (kopiáō): to feel fatigue; by implication, to work hard. Origin: from a derivative of G2873 (κόπος); KJV: (bestow) labour, toil, be wearied

G2873 κόπος (kópos): a cut, i.e. (by analogy) toil (as reducing the strength), literally or figuratively; by implication, pains. Origin: from G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: labour, + trouble, weariness

G2874 κοπρία (kopría): perhaps akin to G2875 (κόπτω)); manure. Origin: from (ordure; KJV: dung(-hill)

G2875 κόπτω (kóptō): to "chop"; specially, to beat the breast in grief. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: cut down, lament, mourn, (be-)wail

G2876 κόραξ (kórax): a crow (from its voracity). Origin: perhaps from G2880 (κορέννυμι); KJV: raven

G2877 κοράσιον (korásion): a (little) girl. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a maiden); KJV: damsel, maid

G2878 κορβᾶν (korbân): a votive offering and the offering; a consecrated present (to the Temple fund); by extension (the latter term) the Treasury itself, i.e. the room where the contribution boxes stood. Origin: of Hebrew and Chaldee origin respectively (H7133); KJV: Corban, treasury

G2879 Κορέ (Koré): Core (i.e. Korach), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7141); KJV: Core

G2880 κορέννυμι (korénnymi): to cram, i.e. glut or sate. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: eat enough, full

G2881 Κορίνθιος (Korínthios): a Corinthian, i.e. inhabitant of Corinth. Origin: from G2882 (Κόρινθος); KJV: Corinthian

G2882 Κόρινθος (Kórinthos): Corinthus, a city of Greece. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Corinth

G2883 Κορνήλιος (Kornḗlios): Cornelius, a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Cornelius

G2884 κόρος (kóros): a cor, i.e. a specific measure. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3734); KJV: measure

G2885 κοσμέω (kosméō): to put in proper order, i.e. decorate (literally or figuratively); specially, to snuff (a wick). Origin: from G2889 (κόσμος); KJV: adorn, garnish, trim

G2886 κοσμικός (kosmikós): terrene ("cosmic"), literally (mundane) or figuratively (corrupt). Origin: from G2889 (κόσμος) (in its secondary sense); KJV: worldly

G2887 κόσμιος (kósmios): orderly, i.e. decorous. Origin: from G2889 (κόσμος) (in its primary sense); KJV: of good behaviour, modest

G2888 κοσμοκράτωρ (kosmokrátōr): a world-ruler, an epithet of Satan. Origin: from G2889 (κόσμος) and G2902 (κρατέω); KJV: ruler

G2889 κόσμος (kósmos): orderly arrangement, i.e. decoration; by implication, the world (in a wide or narrow sense, including its inhabitants, literally or figuratively (morally)). Origin: probably from the base of G2865 (κομίζω); KJV: adorning, world

G2890 Κούαρτος (Koúartos): Quartus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin (fourth); KJV: Quartus

G2891 κοῦμι (koûmi): cumi (i.e. rise!). Origin: of Chaldee origin (H6966); KJV: cumi

G2892 κουστωδία (koustōdía): "custody", i.e. a Roman sentry. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: watch

G2893 κουφίζω (kouphízō): to unload. Origin: from (light in weight); KJV: lighten

G2894 κόφινος (kóphinos): a (small) basket. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: basket

G2895 κράββατος (krábbatos): a mattress. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: bed

G2896 κράζω (krázō): properly, to "croak" (as a raven) or scream, i.e. (genitive case) to call aloud (shriek, exclaim, intreat). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: cry (out)

G2897 κραιπάλη (kraipálē): properly, a headache (as a seizure of pain) from drunkenness, i.e. (by implication) a debauch (by analogy, a glut). Origin: probably from the same as G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: surfeiting

G2898 κρανίον (kraníon): a skull ("cranium"). Origin: diminutive of a derivative of the base of G2768 (κέρας); KJV: Calvary, skull

G2899 κράσπεδον (kráspedon): a margin, i.e. (specially), a fringe or tassel. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: border, hem

G2900 κραταιός (krataiós): powerful. Origin: from G2904 (κράτος); KJV: mighty

G2901 κραταιόω (krataióō): to empower, i.e. (passively) increase in vigor. Origin: from G2900 (κραταιός); KJV: be strengthened, be (wax) strong

G2902 κρατέω (kratéō): to use strength, i.e. seize or retain (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2904 (κράτος); KJV: hold (by, fast), keep, lay hand (hold) on, obtain, retain, take (by)

G2903 κράτιστος (krátistos): strongest, i.e. (in dignity) very honorable. Origin: superlative of a derivative of G2904 (κράτος); KJV: most excellent (noble)

G2904 κράτος (krátos): vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively). Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: dominion, might(-ily), power, strength

G2905 κραυγάζω (kraugázō): to clamor. Origin: from G2906 (κραυγή); KJV: cry out

G2906 κραυγή (kraugḗ): an outcry (in notification, tumult or grief). Origin: from G2896 (κράζω); KJV: clamour, cry(-ing)

G2907 κρέας (kréas): (butcher's) meat. Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: flesh

G2908 κρεῖσσον (kreîsson): (as noun) better, i.e. greater advantage. Origin: neuter of an alternate form of G2909 (κρείττων); KJV: better

G2909 κρείττων (kreíttōn): stronger, i.e. (figuratively) better, i.e. nobler. Origin: comparative of a derivative of G2904 (κράτος); KJV: best, better

G2910 κρεμάννυμι (kremánnymi): to hang. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb; KJV: hang

G2911 κρημνός (krēmnós): overhanging, i.e. a precipice. Origin: from G2910 (κρεμάννυμι); KJV: steep place

G2912 Κρής (Krḗs): a Cretan, i.e. inhabitant of Crete. Origin: from G2914 (Κρήτη); KJV: Crete, Cretian

G2913 Κρήσκης (Krḗskēs): growing; Cresces (i.e. Crescens), a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Crescens

G2914 Κρήτη (Krḗtē): Crete, an island in the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Crete

G2915 κριθή (krithḗ): barley. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: barley

G2916 κρίθινος (kríthinos): consisting of barley. Origin: from G2915 (κριθή); KJV: barley

G2917 κρίμα (kríma): a decision (the function or the effect, for or against ("crime")). Origin: from G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: avenge, condemned, condemnation, damnation, + go to law, judgment

G2918 κρίνον (krínon): a lily. Origin: perhaps a prim word; KJV: lily

G2919 κρίνω (krínō): by implication, to try, condemn, punish. Origin: properly, to distinguish, i.e. decide (mentally or judicially); KJV: avenge, conclude, condemn, damn, decree, determine, esteem, judge, go to (sue at the) law, ordain, call in question, sentence to, think

G2920 κρίσις (krísis): decision (subjectively or objectively, for or against); by extension, a tribunal; by implication, justice (especially, divine law). KJV: accusation, condemnation, damnation, judgment

G2921 Κρίσπος (Kríspos): "crisp"; Crispus, a Corinthian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Crispus

G2922 κριτήριον (kritḗrion): a rule of judging ("criterion"), i.e. (by implication) a tribunal. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2923 (κριτής); KJV: to judge, judgment (seat)

G2923 κριτής (kritḗs): a judge (genitive case or specially). Origin: from G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: judge

G2924 κριτικός (kritikós): decisive ("critical"), i.e. discriminative. Origin: from G2923 (κριτής); KJV: discerner

G2925 κρούω (kroúō): to rap. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: knock

G2926 κρύπτη (krýptē): a hidden place, i.e. cellar ("crypt"). Origin: feminine of G2927 (κρυπτός); KJV: secret

G2927 κρυπτός (kryptós): concealed, i.e. private. Origin: from G2928 (κρύπτω); KJV: hid(-den), inward(-ly), secret

G2928 κρύπτω (krýptō): to conceal (properly, by covering). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: hide (self), keep secret, secret(-ly)

G2929 κρυσταλλίζω (krystallízō): to make (i.e. intransitively, resemble) ice ("crystallize"). Origin: from G2930 (κρύσταλλος); KJV: be clear as crystal

G2930 κρύσταλλος (krýstallos): ice, i.e. (by analogy) rock "crystal". Origin: from a derivative of (frost); KJV: crystal

G2931 κρυφῆ (kryphē): privately. Origin: adverb from G2928 (κρύπτω); KJV: in secret

G2932 κτάομαι (ktáomai): to get, i.e. acquire (by any means; own). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: obtain, possess, provide, purchase

G2933 κτῆμα (ktēma): an acquirement, i.e. estate. Origin: from G2932 (κτάομαι); KJV: possession

G2934 κτῆνος (ktēnos): property, i.e. (specially) a domestic animal. Origin: from G2932 (κτάομαι); KJV: beast

G2935 κτήτωρ (ktḗtōr): an owner. Origin: from G2932 (κτάομαι); KJV: possessor

G2936 κτίζω (ktízō): to fabricate, i.e. found (form originally). Origin: probably akin to G2932 (κτάομαι) (through the idea of proprietorship of the manufacturer); KJV: create, Creator, make

G2937 κτίσις (ktísis): original formation (properly, the act; by implication, the thing, literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2936 (κτίζω); KJV: building, creation, creature, ordinance

G2938 κτίσμα (ktísma): an original formation (concretely), i.e. product (created thing). Origin: from G2936 (κτίζω); KJV: creature

G2939 κτίστης (ktístēs): a founder, i.e. God (as author of all things). Origin: from G2936 (κτίζω); KJV: Creator

G2940 κυβεία (kybeía): gambling, i.e. (figuratively) artifice or fraud. Origin: from (a "cube", i.e. die for playing); KJV: sleight

G2941 κυβέρνησις (kybérnēsis): pilotage, i.e. (figuratively) directorship (in the church). Origin: from (of Latin origin, to steer); KJV: government

G2942 κυβερνήτης (kybernḗtēs): helmsman, i.e. (by implication) captain. Origin: from the same as G2941 (κυβέρνησις); KJV: (ship) master

G2943 κυκλόθεν (kyklóthen): from the circle, i.e. all around. Origin: adverb from the same as G2945 (κύκλῳ); KJV: (round) about

G2944 κυκλόω (kyklóō): to encircle, i.e. surround. Origin: from the same as G2945 (κύκλῳ); KJV: compass (about), come (stand) round about

G2945 κύκλῳ (kýklōi): akin to G2947 (κυλιόω)); i.e. in a circle (by implication, of G1722 (ἐν)), i.e. (adverbially) all around. Origin: as if dative case of (a ring, "cycle"; KJV: round about

G2946 κύλισμα (kýlisma): a wallow (the effect of rolling), i.e. filth. Origin: from G2947 (κυλιόω); KJV: wallowing

G2947 κυλιόω (kylióō): compare G2945 (κύκλῳ), G1507 (εἱλίσσω)); to roll about. Origin: from the base of G2949 (κῦμα) (through the idea of circularity; KJV: wallow

G2948 κυλλός (kyllós): rocking about, i.e. crippled (maimed, in feet or hands). Origin: from the same as G2947 (κυλιόω); KJV: maimed

G2949 κῦμα (kŷma): a billow (as bursting or toppling). Origin: from (to swell (with young), i.e. bend, curve); KJV: wave

G2950 κύμβαλον (kýmbalon): a "cymbal" (as hollow). Origin: from a derivative of the base of G2949 (κῦμα); KJV: cymbal

G2951 κύμινον (kýminon): dill or fennel ("cummin"). Origin: of foreign origin (compare H3646); KJV: cummin

G2952 κυνάριον (kynárion): a puppy. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G2965 (κύων); KJV: dog

G2953 Κύπριος (Kýprios): a Cyprian (Cypriot), i.e. inhabitant of Cyprus. Origin: from G2954 (Κύπρος); KJV: of Cyprus

G2954 Κύπρος (Kýpros): Cyprus, an island in the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Cyprus

G2955 κύπτω (kýptō): to bend forward. Origin: probably from the base of G2949 (κῦμα); KJV: stoop (down)

G2956 Κυρηναῖος (Kyrēnaîos): i.e. Cyrenæan, i.e. inhabitant of Cyrene. Origin: from G2957 (Κυρήνη); KJV: of Cyrene, Cyrenian

G2957 Κυρήνη (Kyrḗnē): Cyrene, a region of Africa. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Cyrene

G2958 Κυρήνιος (Kyrḗnios): Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Cyrenius

G2959 Κυρία (Kyría): Cyria, a Christian woman. Origin: feminine of G2962 (κύριος); KJV: lady

G2960 κυριακός (kyriakós): belonging to the Lord (Jehovah or Jesus). Origin: from G2962 (κύριος); KJV: Lord's

G2961 κυριεύω (kyrieúō): to rule. Origin: from G2962 (κύριος); KJV: have dominion over, lord, be lord of, exercise lordship over

G2962 κύριος (kýrios): supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title). Origin: from (supremacy); KJV: God, Lord, master, Sir

G2963 κυριότης (kyriótēs): mastery, i.e. (concretely and collectively) rulers. Origin: from G2962 (κύριος); KJV: dominion, government

G2964 κυρόω (kyróō): to make authoritative, i.e. ratify. Origin: from the same as G2962 (κύριος); KJV: confirm

G2965 κύων (kýōn): a dog ("hound") (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary word; KJV: dog

G2966 κῶλον (kōlon): a limb of the body (as if lopped). Origin: from the base of G2849 (κολάζω); KJV: carcase

G2967 κωλύω (kōlýō): to estop, i.e. prevent (by word or act). Origin: from the base of G2849 (κολάζω); KJV: forbid, hinder, keep from, let, not suffer, withstand

G2968 κώμη (kṓmē): a hamlet (as if laid down). Origin: from G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: town, village

G2969 κωμόπολις (kōmópolis): an unwalled city. Origin: from G2968 (κώμη) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: town

G2970 κῶμος (kōmos): a carousal (as if letting loose). Origin: from G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: revelling, rioting

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G2971 to G3119
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G2971 κώνωψ (kṓnōps): a mosquito (from its stinging proboscis). Origin: apparently a derivative of the base of G2759 (κέντρον) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: gnat

G2972 Κώς (Kṓs): Cos, an island in the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Cos

G2973 Κωσάμ (Kōsám): Cosam (i.e. Kosam) an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H7081); KJV: Cosam

G2974 κωφός (kōphós): blunted, i.e. (figuratively) of hearing (deaf) or speech (dumb). Origin: from G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: deaf, dumb, speechless

G2975 λαγχάνω (lanchánō): to lot, i.e. determine (by implication, receive) especially by lot. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses; KJV: his lot be, cast lots, obtain

G2976 Λάζαρος (Lázaros): Lazarus (i.e. Elazar), the name of two Israelites (one imaginary). Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (H499); KJV: Lazarus

G2977 λάθρα (láthra): privately. Origin: adverb from G2990 (λανθάνω); KJV: privily, secretly

G2978 λαῖλαψ (laîlaps): a whirlwind (squall). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: storm, tempest

G2979 λακτίζω (laktízō): to recalcitrate. Origin: from adverb (heelwise); KJV: kick

G2980 λαλέω (laléō): to talk, i.e. utter words. Origin: a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; KJV: preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter

G2981 λαλιά (laliá): talk. Origin: from G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: saying, speech

G2982 λαμά (lamá): lama (i.e. why). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4100 with prepositional prefix); KJV: lama

G2983 λαμβάνω (lambánō): while G138 (αἱρέομαι) is more violent, to seize or remove)). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas G1209 (δέχομαι) is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; KJV: accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up)

G2984 Λάμεχ (Lámech): Lamech (i.e. Lemek), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3929); KJV: Lamech

G2985 λαμπάς (lampás): a "lamp" or flambeau. Origin: from G2989 (λάμπω); KJV: lamp, light, torch

G2986 λαμπρός (lamprós): radiant; by analogy, limpid; figuratively, magnificent or sumptuous (in appearance). Origin: from the same as G2985 (λαμπάς); KJV: bright, clear, gay, goodly, gorgeous, white

G2987 λαμπρότης (lamprótēs): brilliancy. Origin: from G2986 (λαμπρός); KJV: brightness

G2988 λαμπρῶς (lamprōs): brilliantly, i.e. figuratively, luxuriously. Origin: adverb from G2986 (λαμπρός); KJV: sumptuously

G2989 λάμπω (lámpō): to beam, i.e. radiate brilliancy (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: give light, shine

G2990 λανθάνω (lanthánō): to lie hid (literally or figuratively); often used adverbially, unwittingly. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is used only as an alternate in certain tenses; KJV: be hid, be ignorant of, unawares

G2991 λαξευτός (laxeutós): rock-quarried. Origin: from a compound of (a stone) and the base of G3584 (ξηρός) (in its original sense of scraping); KJV: hewn in stone

G2992 λαός (laós): a people (in general; thus differing from G1218 (δῆμος), which denotes one's own populace). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: people

G2993 Λαοδίκεια (Laodíkeia): Laodicia, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: from a compound of G2992 (λαός) and G1349 (δίκη); KJV: Laodicea

G2994 Λαοδικεύς (Laodikeús): a Laodicean, i.e. inhabitant of Laodicia. Origin: from G2993 (Λαοδίκεια); KJV: Laodicean

G2995 λάρυγξ (lárynx): the throat ("larynx"). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: throat

G2996 Λασαία (Lasaía): Lasæa, a place in Crete. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Lasea

G2997 λάσχω (láschō): to crack open (from a fall). Origin: a strengthened form of a primary verb, which only occurs in this and another prolonged form as alternate in certain tenses; KJV: burst asunder

G2998 λατομέω (latoméō): to quarry. Origin: from the same as the first part of G2991 (λαξευτός) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος); KJV: hew

G2999 λατρεία (latreía): ministration of God, i.e. worship. Origin: from G3000 (λατρεύω); KJV: (divine) service

G3000 λατρεύω (latreúō): to minister (to God), i.e. render religious homage. Origin: from (a hired menial); KJV: serve, do the service, worship(-per)

G3001 λάχανον (láchanon): a vegetable. Origin: from (to dig); KJV: herb

G3002 Λεββαῖος (Lebbaîos): Lebbæus, a Christian. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Lebbæus

G3003 λεγεών (legeṓn): a "legion", i.e. Roman regiment (figuratively). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: legion

G3004 λέγω (légō): properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas G2036 (ἔπω) and G5346 (φημί) generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while G4483 (ῥέω) is properly to break silence merely, and G2980 (λαλέω) means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter

G3005 λεῖμμα (leîmma): a remainder. Origin: from G3007 (λείπω); KJV: remnant

G3006 λεῖος (leîos): smooth, i.e. "level". Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: smooth

G3007 λείπω (leípō): to leave, i.e. (intransitively or passively) to fail or be absent. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: be destitute (wanting), lack

G3008 λειτουργέω (leitourgéō): to be a public servant, i.e. (by analogy) to perform religious or charitable functions (worship, obey, relieve). Origin: from G3011 (λειτουργός); KJV: minister

G3009 λειτουργία (leitourgía): public function (as priest ("liturgy") or almsgiver). Origin: from G3008 (λειτουργέω); KJV: ministration(-try), service

G3010 λειτουργικός (leitourgikós): functional publicly ("liturgic"); i.e. beneficient. Origin: from the same as G3008 (λειτουργέω); KJV: ministering

G3011 λειτουργός (leitourgós): a public servant, i.e. a functionary in the Temple or Gospel, or (genitive case) a worshipper (of God) or benefactor (of man). Origin: from a derivative of G2992 (λαός) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: minister(-ed)

G3012 λέντιον (léntion): a "linen" cloth, i.e. apron. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: towel

G3013 λεπίς (lepís): a flake. Origin: from (to peel); KJV: scale

G3014 λέπρα (lépra): scaliness, i.e. "leprosy". Origin: from the same as G3013 (λεπίς); KJV: leprosy

G3015 λεπρός (leprós): scaly, i.e. leprous (a leper). Origin: from the same as G3014 (λέπρα); KJV: leper

G3016 λεπτόν (leptón): something scaled (light), i.e. a small coin. Origin: neuter of a derivative of the same as G3013 (λεπίς); KJV: mite

G3017 Λευΐ (Leuḯ): Levi, the name of three Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3878); KJV: Levi

G3018 Λευΐς (Leuḯs): Lewis (i.e. Levi), a Christian. Origin: a form of G3017 (Λευΐ); KJV: Levi

G3019 Λευΐτης (Leuḯtēs): a Levite, i.e. descendant of Levi. Origin: from G3017 (Λευΐ); KJV: Levite

G3020 Λευϊτικός (Leuïtikós): Levitic, i.e. relating to the Levites. Origin: from G3019 (Λευΐτης); KJV: Levitical

G3021 λευκαίνω (leukaínō): to whiten. Origin: from G3022 (λευκός); KJV: make white, whiten

G3022 λευκός (leukós): white. Origin: from ("light"); KJV: white

G3023 λέων (léōn): a "lion". Origin: a primary word; KJV: lion

G3024 λήθη (lḗthē): forgetfulness. Origin: from G2990 (λανθάνω); KJV: + forget

G3025 ληνός (lēnós): a trough, i.e. wine-vat. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: winepress

G3026 λῆρος (lēros): twaddle, i.e. an incredible story. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: idle tale

G3027 λῃστής (lēistḗs): a brigand. Origin: from (to plunder); KJV: robber, thief

G3028 λῆμψις (lēmpsis): receipt (the act). Origin: from G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: receiving

G3029 λίαν (lían): much (adverbially). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: exceeding, great(-ly), sore, very (+ chiefest)

G3030 λίβανος (líbanos): the incense-tree, i.e. (by implication) incense itself. Origin: of foreign origin (H3828); KJV: frankincense

G3031 λιβανωτός (libanōtós): frankincense, i.e. (by extension) a censer for burning it. Origin: from G3030 (λίβανος); KJV: censer

G3032 Λιβερτῖνος (Libertînos): a Roman freedman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Libertine

G3033 Λιβύη (Libýē): Libye, a region of Africa. Origin: probably from G3047 (λίψ); KJV: Libya

G3034 λιθάζω (litházō): to lapidate. Origin: from G3037 (λίθος); KJV: stone

G3035 λίθινος (líthinos): stony, i.e. made of stone. Origin: from G3037 (λίθος); KJV: of stone

G3036 λιθοβολέω (lithoboléō): to throw stones, i.e. lapidate. Origin: from a compound of G3037 (λίθος) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: stone, cast stones

G3037 λίθος (líthos): a stone (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: (mill-, stumbling-)stone

G3038 λιθόστρωτος (lithóstrōtos): stone-strewed, i.e. a tessellated mosaic on which the Roman tribunal was placed. Origin: from G3037 (λίθος) and a derivative of G4766 (στρώννυμι); KJV: Pavement

G3039 λικμάω (likmáō): to winnow, i.e. (by analogy), to triturate. Origin: from , the equivalent of (a winnowing fan or basket); KJV: grind to powder

G3040 λιμήν (limḗn): a harbor. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: haven

G3041 λίμνη (límnē): a pond (large or small). Origin: probably from G3040 (λιμήν) (through the idea of nearness of shore); KJV: lake

G3042 λιμός (limós): a scarcity of food. Origin: probably from G3007 (λείπω) (through the idea of destitution); KJV: dearth, famine, hunger

G3043 λίνον (línon): flax, i.e. (by implication) "linen". Origin: probably a primary word; KJV: linen

G3044 Λίνος (Línos): Linus, a Christian. Origin: perhaps from G3043 (λίνον); KJV: Linus

G3045 λιπαρός (liparós): fat, i.e. (figuratively) sumptuous. Origin: from (grease); KJV: dainty

G3046 λίτρα (lítra): a pound in weight. Origin: of Latin origin (libra); KJV: pound

G3047 λίψ (líps): the south(- west) wind (as bringing rain, i.e. (by extension) the south quarter). Origin: probably from (to pour a "libation"); KJV: southwest

G3048 λογία (logía): a contribution. Origin: from G3056 (λόγος) (in the commercial sense); KJV: collection, gathering

G3049 λογίζομαι (logízomai): to take an inventory, i.e. estimate (literally or figuratively). Origin: middle voice from G3056 (λόγος); KJV: conclude, (ac-)count (of), + despise, esteem, impute, lay, number, reason, reckon, suppose, think (on)

G3050 λογικός (logikós): rational ("logical"). Origin: from G3056 (λόγος); KJV: reasonable, of the word

G3051 λόγιον (lógion): an utterance (of God). Origin: neuter of G3052 (λόγιος); KJV: oracle

G3052 λόγιος (lógios): fluent, i.e. an orator. Origin: from G3056 (λόγος); KJV: eloquent

G3053 λογισμός (logismós): computation, i.e. (figuratively) reasoning (conscience, conceit). Origin: from G3049 (λογίζομαι); KJV: imagination, thought

G3054 λογομαχέω (logomachéō): to be disputatious (on trifles). Origin: from a compound of G3056 (λόγος) and G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: strive about words

G3055 λογομαχία (logomachía): disputation about trifles ("logomachy"). Origin: from the same as G3054 (λογομαχέω); KJV: strife of words

G3056 λόγος (lógos): something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ). Origin: from G3004 (λέγω); KJV: account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work

G3057 λόγχη (lónchē): a "lance". Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: spear

G3058 λοιδορέω (loidoréō): to reproach, i.e. vilify. Origin: from G3060 (λοίδορος); KJV: revile

G3059 λοιδορία (loidoría): slander or vituperation. Origin: from G3060 (λοίδορος); KJV: railing, reproach(-fully)

G3060 λοίδορος (loídoros): abusive, i.e. a blackguard. Origin: from (mischief); KJV: railer, reviler

G3061 λοιμός (loimós): a plague (literally, the disease, or figuratively, a pest). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: pestilence(-t)

G3062 λοιποί (loipoí): remaining ones. Origin: masculine plural of a derivative of G3007 (λείπω); KJV: other, which remain, remnant, residue, rest

G3063 λοιπόν (loipón): something remaining (adverbially). Origin: neuter singular of the same as G3062 (λοιποί); KJV: besides, finally, furthermore, (from) henceforth, moreover, now, + it remaineth, then

G3064 λοιποῦ (loipoû): remaining time. Origin: genitive case singular of the same as G3062 (λοιποί); KJV: from henceforth

G3065 Λουκᾶς (Loukâs): Lucas, a Christian. Origin: contracted from Latin Lucanus; KJV: Lucas, Luke

G3066 Λούκιος (Loúkios): illuminative; Lucius, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Lucius

G3067 λουτρόν (loutrón): a bath, i.e. (figuratively), baptism. Origin: from G3068 (λούω); KJV: washing

G3068 λούω (loúō): to bathe (the whole person; whereas G3538 (νίπτω) means to wet a part only, and G4150 (πλύνω) to wash, cleanse garments exclusively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: wash

G3069 Λύδδα (Lýdda): Lydda (i.e. Lod), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3850); KJV: Lydda

G3070 Λυδία (Lydía): Lydia, a Christian woman. Origin: properly, feminine of Ludios (of foreign origin) (a Lydian, in Asia Minor); KJV: Lydia

G3071 Λυκαονία (Lykaonía): Lycaonia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: perhaps remotely from G3074 (λύκος); KJV: Lycaonia

G3072 Λυκαονιστί (Lykaonistí): Lycaonistically, i.e. in the language of the Lycaonians. Origin: adverb from a derivative of G3071 (Λυκαονία); KJV: in the speech of Lycaonia

G3073 Λυκία (Lykía): Lycia, a province of Asia Minor. Origin: probably remotely from G3074 (λύκος); KJV: Lycia

G3074 λύκος (lýkos): a wolf. Origin: perhaps akin to the base of G3022 (λευκός) (from the whitish hair); KJV: wolf

G3075 λυμαίνομαι (lymaínomai): properly, to soil, i.e. (figuratively) insult (maltreat). Origin: middle voice from a probably derivative of G3089 (λύω) (meaning filth); KJV: make havock of

G3076 λυπέω (lypéō): to distress; reflexively or passively, to be sad. Origin: from G3077 (λύπη); KJV: cause grief, grieve, be in heaviness, (be) sorrow(-ful), be (make) sorry

G3077 λύπη (lýpē): sadness. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: grief, grievous, + grudgingly, heaviness, sorrow

G3078 Λυσανίας (Lysanías): grief-dispelling; Lysanias, a governor of Abilene. Origin: from G3080 (λύσις) and (trouble); KJV: Lysanias

G3079 Λυσίας (Lysías): Lysias, a Roman. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: Lysias

G3080 λύσις (lýsis): a loosening, i.e. (specially), divorce. Origin: from G3089 (λύω); KJV: to be loosed

G3081 λυσιτελεῖ (lysiteleî): impersonally, it answers the purpose, i.e. is advantageous. Origin: third person singular present indicative active of a derivative of a compound of G3080 (λύσις) and G5056 (τέλος); KJV: it is better

G3082 Λύστρα (Lýstra): Lystra, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Lystra

G3083 λύτρον (lýtron): something to loosen with, i.e. a redemption price (figuratively, atonement). Origin: from G3089 (λύω); KJV: ransom

G3084 λυτρόω (lytróō): to ransom (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3083 (λύτρον); KJV: redeem

G3085 λύτρωσις (lýtrōsis): a ransoming (figuratively). Origin: from G3084 (λυτρόω); KJV: + redeemed, redemption

G3086 λυτρωτής (lytrōtḗs): a redeemer (figuratively). Origin: from G3084 (λυτρόω); KJV: deliverer

G3087 λυχνία (lychnía): a lamp-stand (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3088 (λύχνος); KJV: candlestick

G3088 λύχνος (lýchnos): a portable lamp or other illuminator (literally or figuratively). Origin: from the base of G3022 (λευκός); KJV: candle, light

G3089 λύω (lýō): to "loosen" (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: break (up), destroy, dissolve, (un-)loose, melt, put off

G3090 Λωΐς (Lōḯs): Lois, a Christian woman. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Lois

G3091 Λώτ (Lṓt): Lot, a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3876); KJV: Lot

G3092 Μαάθ (Maáth): Maath, an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin; KJV: Maath

G3093 Μαγδαλά (Magdalá): the tower; Magdala (i.e. Migdala), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H4026); KJV: Magdala

G3094 Μαγδαληνή (Magdalēnḗ): a female Magdalene, i.e. inhabitant of Magdala. Origin: feminine of a derivative of G3093 (Μαγδαλά); KJV: Magdalene

G3095 μαγεία (mageía): "magic". Origin: from G3096 (μαγεύω); KJV: sorcery

G3096 μαγεύω (mageúō): to practice magic. Origin: from G3097 (μάγος); KJV: use sorcery

G3097 μάγος (mágos): a Magian, i.e. Oriental scientist; by implication, a magician. Origin: of foreign origin (H7248); KJV: sorcerer, wise man

G3098 Μαγώγ (Magṓg): Magog, a foreign nation, i.e. (figuratively) an Antichristian party. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4031); KJV: Magog

G3099 Μαδιάν (Madián): Madian (i.e. Midian), a region of Arabia. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4080); KJV: Madian

G3100 μαθητεύω (mathēteúō): intransitively, to become a pupil; transitively, to disciple, i.e. enrol as scholar. Origin: from G3101 (μαθητής); KJV: be disciple, instruct, teach

G3101 μαθητής (mathētḗs): a learner, i.e. pupil. Origin: from G3129 (μανθάνω); KJV: disciple

G3102 μαθήτρια (mathḗtria): a female pupil. Origin: feminine from G3101 (μαθητής); KJV: disciple

G3103 Μαθουσάλα (Mathousála): Mathusala (i.e. Methushelach), an antediluvian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4968); KJV: Mathusala

G3104 Μαϊνάν (Maïnán): Mainan, an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin; KJV: Mainan

G3105 μαίνομαι (maínomai): through the idea of insensate craving); to rave as a "maniac". Origin: middle voice from a primary (to long for; KJV: be beside self (mad)

G3106 μακαρίζω (makarízō): to beatify, i.e. pronounce (or esteem) fortunate. Origin: from G3107 (μακάριος); KJV: call blessed, count happy

G3107 μακάριος (makários): supremely blest; by extension, fortunate, well off. Origin: a prolonged form of the poetical (meaning the same); KJV: blessed, happy(X -ier)

G3108 μακαρισμός (makarismós): beatification, i.e. attribution of good fortune. Origin: from G3106 (μακαρίζω); KJV: blessedness

G3109 Μακεδονία (Makedonía): Macedonia, a region of Greece. Origin: from G3110 (Μακεδών); KJV: Macedonia

G3110 Μακεδών (Makedṓn): a Macedon (Macedonian), i.e. inhabitant of Macedonia. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: of Macedonia, Macedonian

G3111 μάκελλον (mákellon): a butcher's stall, meat market or provision-shop. Origin: of Latin origin (macellum); KJV: shambles

G3112 μακράν (makrán): at a distance (literally or figuratively). Origin: feminine accusative case singular of G3117 (μακρός) (G3598 (ὁδός) being implied); KJV: (a-)far (off), good (great) way off

G3113 μακρόθεν (makróthen): from a distance or afar. Origin: adverb from G3117 (μακρός); KJV: afar off, from far

G3114 μακροθυμέω (makrothyméō): to be long-spirited, i.e. (objectively) forbearing or (subjectively) patient. Origin: from the same as G3116 (μακροθυμώς); KJV: bear (suffer) long, be longsuffering, have (long) patience, be patient, patiently endure

G3115 μακροθυμία (makrothymía): longanimity, i.e. (objectively) forbearance or (subjectively) fortitude. Origin: from the same as G3116 (μακροθυμώς); KJV: longsuffering, patience

G3116 μακροθυμώς (makrothymṓs): with long (enduring) temper, i.e. leniently. Origin: adverb of a compound of G3117 (μακρός) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: patiently

G3117 μακρός (makrós): long (in place (distant) or time (neuter plural)). Origin: from G3372 (μῆκος); KJV: far, long

G3118 μακροχρόνιος (makrochrónios): long-timed, i.e. long-lived. Origin: from G3117 (μακρός) and G5550 (χρόνος); KJV: live long

G3119 μαλακία (malakía): softness, i.e. enervation (debility). Origin: from G3120 (μαλακός); KJV: disease

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G3120 to G3349
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G3120 μαλακός (malakós): soft, i.e. fine (clothing); figuratively, a catamite. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: effeminate, soft

G3121 Μαλελεήλ (Maleleḗl): Maleleel (i.e. Mahalalel), an antediluvian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4111); KJV: Maleleel

G3122 μάλιστα (málista): (adverbially) most (in the greatest degree) or particularly. Origin: neuter plural of the superlative of an apparently primary adverb (very); KJV: chiefly, most of all, (e-)specially

G3123 μᾶλλον (mâllon): (adverbially) more (in a greater degree)) or rather. Origin: neuter of the comparative of the same as G3122 (μάλιστα); KJV: + better, X far, (the) more (and more), (so) much (the more), rather

G3124 Μάλχος (Málchos): Malchus, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4429); KJV: Malchus

G3125 μάμμη (mámmē): a grandmother. Origin: of natural origin ("mammy"); KJV: grandmother

G3126 μαμμωνᾶς (mammōnâs): mammonas, i.e. avarice (deified). Origin: of Chaldee origin (confidence, i.e. wealth, personified); KJV: mammon

G3127 Μαναήν (Manaḗn): Manaën, a Christian. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Manaen

G3128 Μανασσῆς (Manassēs): Mannasses (i.e. Menashsheh), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4519); KJV: Manasses

G3129 μανθάνω (manthánō): to learn (in any way). Origin: prolongation from a primary verb, another form of which, , is used as an alternate in certain tenses; KJV: learn, understand

G3130 μανία (manía): craziness. Origin: from G3105 (μαίνομαι); KJV: (+ make) X mad

G3131 μάννα (mánna): manna (i.e. man), an edible gum. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4478); KJV: manna

G3132 μαντεύομαι (manteúomai): to divine, i.e. utter spells (under pretense of foretelling. Origin: from a derivative of G3105 (μαίνομαι) (meaning a prophet, as supposed to rave through inspiration); KJV: by soothsaying

G3133 μαραίνω (maraínō): to extinguish (as fire), i.e. (figuratively and passively) to pass away. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: fade away

G3134 μαρὰν ἀθά (maràn athá): maranatha, i.e. an exclamation of the approaching divine judgment. Origin: of Chaldee origin (meaning our Lord has come); KJV: Maran-atha

G3135 μαργαρίτης (margarítēs): a pearl. Origin: from (a pearl-oyster); KJV: pearl

G3136 Μάρθα (Mártha): Martha, a Christian woman. Origin: probably of Chaldee origin (meaning mistress); KJV: Martha

G3137 Μαρία (María): Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4813); KJV: Mary

G3138 Μάρκος (Márkos): Marcus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Marcus, Mark

G3139 μάρμαρος (mármaros): marble (as sparkling white). Origin: from (to glisten); KJV: marble

G3140 μαρτυρέω (martyréō): to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3144 (μάρτυς); KJV: charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness

G3141 μαρτυρία (martyría): evidence given (judicially or genitive case). Origin: from G3144 (μάρτυς); KJV: record, report, testimony, witness

G3142 μαρτύριον (martýrion): something evidential, i.e. (genitive case) evidence given or (specially), the Decalogue (in the sacred Tabernacle). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3144 (μάρτυς); KJV: to be testified, testimony, witness

G3143 μαρτύρομαι (martýromai): to be adduced as a witness, i.e. (figuratively) to obtest (in affirmation or exhortation). Origin: middle voice from G3144 (μάρτυς); KJV: take to record, testify

G3144 μάρτυς (mártys): a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr". Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: martyr, record, witness

G3145 μασσάομαι (massáomai): to chew. Origin: from a primary (to handle or squeeze); KJV: gnaw

G3146 μαστιγόω (mastigóō): to flog (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3148 (μάστιξ); KJV: scourge

G3147 μαστίζω (mastízō): to whip (literally). Origin: from G3149 (μαστός); KJV: scourge

G3148 μάστιξ (mástix): a whip (literally, the Roman flagellum for criminals; figuratively, a disease). Origin: probably from the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι) (through the idea of contact); KJV: plague, scourging

G3149 μαστός (mastós): a (properly, female) breast (as if kneaded up). Origin: from the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι); KJV: pap

G3150 ματαιολογία (mataiología): random talk, i.e. babble. Origin: from G3151 (ματαιολόγος); KJV: vain jangling

G3151 ματαιολόγος (mataiológos): an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler. Origin: from G3152 (μάταιος) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: vain talker

G3152 μάταιος (mátaios): empty, i.e. (literally) profitless, or (specially), an idol. Origin: from the base of G3155 (μάτην); KJV: vain, vanity

G3153 ματαιότης (mataiótēs): inutility; figuratively, transientness; morally, depravity. Origin: from G3152 (μάταιος); KJV: vanity

G3154 ματαιόω (mataióō): to render (passively, become) foolish, i.e. (morally) wicked or (specially), idolatrous. Origin: from G3152 (μάταιος); KJV: become vain

G3155 μάτην (mátēn): folly, i.e. (adverbially) to no purpose. Origin: accusative case of a derivative of the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι) (through the idea of tentative manipulation, i.e. unsuccessful search, or else of punishment); KJV: in vain

G3156 Ματθαῖος (Matthaîos): Matthæus (i.e. Matthitjah), an Israelite and a Christian. Origin: a shorter form of G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: Matthew

G3157 Ματθάν (Matthán): Matthan (i.e. Mattan), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4977); KJV: Matthan

G3158 Ματθάτ (Matthát): Matthat (i.e. Mattithjah), the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably a shortened form of G3161 (Ματταθίας); KJV: Mathat

G3159 Ματθίας (Matthías): Matthias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite. Origin: apparently a shortened form of G3161 (Ματταθίας); KJV: Matthias

G3160 Ματταθά (Mattathá): Mattatha (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite. Origin: probably a shortened form of G3161 (Ματταθίας) (compare G4992 (σωτήριον)); KJV: Mattatha

G3161 Ματταθίας (Mattathías): Mattathias (i.e. Mattithjah), an Israelite and a Christian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4993); KJV: Mattathias

G3162 μάχαιρα (máchaira): a knife, i.e. dirk; figuratively, war, judicial punishment. Origin: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of G3163 (μάχη); KJV: sword

G3163 μάχη (máchē): a battle, i.e. (figuratively) controversy. Origin: from G3164 (μάχομαι); KJV: fighting, strive, striving

G3164 μάχομαι (máchomai): to war, i.e. (figuratively) to quarrel, dispute. Origin: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; KJV: fight, strive

G3165 μέ (mé): me. Origin: a shorter (and probably original) form of G1691 (ἐμέ); KJV: I, me, my

G3166 μεγαλαυχέω (megalauchéō): akin to G837 (αὐξάνω) and G2744 (καυχάομαι)); to talk big, i.e. be grandiloquent (arrogant, egotistic). Origin: from a compound of G3173 (μέγας) and (to boast; KJV: boast great things

G3167 μεγαλεῖος (megaleîos): magnificent, i.e. (neuter, plural as noun) a conspicuous favor, or (subjectively) perfection. Origin: from G3173 (μέγας); KJV: great things, wonderful works

G3168 μεγαλειότης (megaleiótēs): superbness, i.e. glory or splendor. Origin: from G3167 (μεγαλεῖος); KJV: magnificence, majesty, mighty power

G3169 μεγαλοπρεπής (megaloprepḗs): befitting greatness or magnificence (majestic). Origin: from G3173 (μέγας) and G4241 (πρέπω); KJV: excellent

G3170 μεγαλύνω (megalýnō): to make (or declare) great, i.e. increase or (figuratively) extol. Origin: from G3173 (μέγας); KJV: enlarge, magnify, shew great

G3171 μεγάλως (megálōs): much. Origin: adverb from G3173 (μέγας); KJV: greatly

G3172 μεγαλωσύνη (megalōsýnē): greatness, i.e. (figuratively) divinity (often God himself). Origin: from G3173 (μέγας); KJV: majesty

G3173 μέγας (mégas): big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application). Origin: (including the prolonged forms, feminine , plural , etc.; compare also G3176 (μέγιστος), G3187 (μείζων)); KJV: (+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years

G3174 μέγεθος (mégethos): magnitude (figuratively). Origin: from G3173 (μέγας); KJV: greatness

G3175 μεγιστᾶνες (megistânes): grandees. Origin: plural from G3176 (μέγιστος); KJV: great men, lords

G3176 μέγιστος (mégistos): greatest or very great. Origin: superlative of G3173 (μέγας); KJV: exceeding great

G3177 μεθερμηνεύω (methermēneúō): to explain over, i.e. translate. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G2059 (ἑρμηνεύω); KJV: (by) interpret(-ation)

G3178 μέθη (méthē): an intoxicant, i.e. (by implication) intoxication. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: drunkenness

G3179 μεθίστημι (methístēmi): to transfer, i.e. carry away, depose or (figuratively) exchange, seduce. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: put out, remove, translate, turn away

G3180 μεθοδεία (methodeía): travelling over, i.e. travesty (trickery). Origin: from a compound of G3326 (μετά) and G3593 (ὁδεύω) (compare "method"); KJV: wile, lie in wait

G3181 μεθόριος (methórios): bounded alongside, i.e. contiguous (neuter plural as noun, frontier). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G3725 (ὅριον); KJV: border

G3182 μεθύσκω (methýskō): to intoxicate. Origin: a prolonged (transitive) form of G3184 (μεθύω); KJV: be drunk(-en)

G3183 μέθυσος (méthysos): tipsy, i.e. (as noun) a sot. Origin: from G3184 (μεθύω); KJV: drunkard

G3184 μεθύω (methýō): to drink to intoxication, i.e. get drunk. Origin: from another form of G3178 (μέθη); KJV: drink well, make (be) drunk(-en)

G3185 μεῖζον (meîzon): (adverbially) in greater degree. Origin: neuter of G3187 (μείζων); KJV: the more

G3186 μειζότερος (meizóteros): still larger (figuratively). Origin: continued comparative of G3187 (μείζων); KJV: greater

G3187 μείζων (meízōn): larger (literally or figuratively, specially, in age). Origin: irregular comparative of G3173 (μέγας); KJV: elder, greater(-est), more

G3188 μέλαν (mélan): ink. Origin: neuter of G3189 (μέλας) as noun; KJV: ink

G3189 μέλας (mélas): black. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: black

G3190 Μελεᾶς (Meleâs): Meleas, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Meleas

G3191 μελετάω (meletáō): to take care of, i.e. (by implication) revolve in the mind. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G3199 (μέλω); KJV: imagine, (pre-)meditate

G3192 μέλι (méli): honey. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: honey

G3193 μελίσσιος (melíssios): relating to honey, i.e. bee (comb). Origin: from G3192 (μέλι); KJV: honeycomb

G3194 Μελίτη (Melítē): Melita, an island in the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Melita

G3195 μέλλω (méllō): to intend, i.e. be about to be, do, or suffer something (of persons or things, especially events; in the sense of purpose, duty, necessity, probability, possibility, or hesitation). Origin: a strengthened form of G3199 (μέλω) (through the idea of expectation); KJV: about, after that, be (almost), (that which is, things, + which was for) to come, intend, was to (be), mean, mind, be at the point, (be) ready, + return, shall (begin), (which, that) should (after, afterwards, hereafter) tarry, which was for, will, would, be yet

G3196 μέλος (mélos): a limb or part of the body. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: member

G3197 Μελχί (Melchí): Melchi (i.e. Malki), the name of two Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4428 with pronominal suffix, my king); KJV: Melchi

G3198 Μελχισεδέκ (Melchisedék): Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4442); KJV: Melchisedec

G3199 μέλω (mélō): to be of interest to, i.e. to concern (only third person singular present indicative used impersonally, it matters). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: (take) care

G3200 μεμβράνα (membrána): a (written) sheep-skin. Origin: of Latin origin ("membrane"); KJV: parchment

G3201 μέμφομαι (mémphomai): to blame. Origin: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; KJV: find fault

G3202 μεμψίμοιρος (mempsímoiros): akin to the base of G3313 (μέρος)); blaming fate, i.e. querulous (discontented). Origin: from a presumed derivative of G3201 (μέμφομαι) and (fate; KJV: complainer

G3303 μέν (mén): properly, indicative of affirmation or concession (in fact); usually followed by a contrasted clause with G1161 (δέ) (this one, the former, etc.). Origin: a primary particle; KJV: even, indeed, so, some, truly, verily

G3304 μενοῦνγε (menoûnge): so then at least. Origin: from G3203 and G3767 (οὖν) and G1065 (γέ); KJV: nay but, yea doubtless (rather, verily)

G3305 μέντοι (méntoi): indeed though, i.e. however. Origin: from G3203 and G5104 (τοί); KJV: also, but, howbeit, nevertheless, yet

G3306 μένω (ménō): to stay (in a given place, state, relation or expectancy). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: abide, continue, dwell, endure, be present, remain, stand, tarry (for), X thine own

G3307 μερίζω (merízō): to part, i.e. (literally) to apportion, bestow, share, or (figuratively) to disunite, differ. Origin: from G3313 (μέρος); KJV: deal, be difference between, distribute, divide, give participle

G3308 μέριμνα (mérimna): solicitude. Origin: from G3307 (μερίζω) (through the idea of distraction); KJV: care

G3309 μεριμνάω (merimnáō): to be anxious about. Origin: from G3308 (μέριμνα); KJV: (be, have) care(-ful), take thought

G3310 μερίς (merís): a portion, i.e. province, share or (abstractly) participation. Origin: feminine of G3313 (μέρος); KJV: part (X -akers)

G3311 μερισμός (merismós): a separation or distribution. Origin: from G3307 (μερίζω); KJV: dividing asunder, gift

G3312 μεριστής (meristḗs): an apportioner (administrator). Origin: from G3307 (μερίζω); KJV: divider

G3313 μέρος (méros): a division or share (literally or figuratively, in a wide application). Origin: from an obsolete but more primary form of (to get as a section or allotment); KJV: behalf, course, coast, craft, particular (+ -ly), part (+ -ly), piece, portion, respect, side, some sort(-what)

G3314 μεσημβρία (mesēmbría): midday; by implication, the south. Origin: from G3319 (μέσος) and G2250 (ἡμέρα); KJV: noon, south

G3315 μεσιτεύω (mesiteúō): to interpose (as arbiter), i.e (by implication) to ratify (as surety). Origin: from G3316 (μεσίτης); KJV: confirm

G3316 μεσίτης (mesítēs): a go-between, i.e. (simply) an internunciator, or (by implication) a reconciler (intercessor). Origin: from G3319 (μέσος); KJV: mediator

G3317 μεσονύκτιον (mesonýktion): midnight (especially as a watch). Origin: neuter of compound of G3319 (μέσος) and G3571 (νύξ); KJV: midnight

G3318 Μεσοποταμία (Mesopotamía): Mesopotamia (as lying between the Euphrates and the Tigris; compare 0763), a region of Asia. Origin: from G3319 (μέσος) and G4215 (ποταμός); KJV: Mesopotamia

G3319 μέσος (mésos): middle (as an adjective or (neuter) noun). Origin: from G3326 (μετά); KJV: among, X before them, between, + forth, mid(-day, -night), midst, way

G3320 μεσότοιχον (mesótoichon): a partition (figuratively). Origin: from G3319 (μέσος) and G5109 (τοῖχος); KJV: middle wall

G3321 μεσουράνημα (mesouránēma): mid-sky. Origin: from a presumed compound of G3319 (μέσος) and G3772 (οὐρανός); KJV: midst of heaven

G3322 μεσόω (mesóō): to form the middle, i.e. (in point of time), to be half-way over. Origin: from G3319 (μέσος); KJV: be about the midst

G3323 Μεσσίας (Messías): the Messias (i.e. Mashiach), or Christ. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4899); KJV: Messias

G3324 μεστός (mestós): replete (literally or figuratively). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: full

G3325 μεστόω (mestóō): to replenish, i.e. (by implication) to intoxicate. Origin: from G3324 (μεστός); KJV: fill

G3326 μετά (metá): properly, denoting accompaniment; "amid" (local or causal); modified variously according to the case (genitive association, or accusative succession) with which it is joined; occupying an intermediate position between G575 (ἀπό) or G1537 (ἐκ) and G1519 (εἰς) or G4314 (πρός); less intimate than G1722 (ἐν) and less close than G4862 (σύν)). Origin: a primary preposition (often used adverbially); KJV: after(-ward), X that he again, against, among, X and, + follow, hence, hereafter, in, of, (up-)on, + our, X and setting, since, (un-)to, + together, when, with (+ -out)

G3327 μεταβαίνω (metabaínō): to change place. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: depart, go, pass, remove

G3328 μεταβάλλω (metabállō): to throw over, i.e. (middle voice figuratively) to turn about in opinion. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: change mind

G3329 μετάγω (metágō): to lead over, i.e. transfer (direct). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G718 (ἁρμόζω); KJV: turn about

G3330 μεταδίδωμι (metadídōmi): to give over, i.e. share. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: give, impart

G3331 μετάθεσις (metáthesis): transposition, i.e. transferral (to heaven), disestablishment (of a law). Origin: from G3346 (μετατίθημι); KJV: change, removing, translation

G3332 μεταίρω (metaírō): to betake oneself, i.e. remove (locally). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G142 (αἴρω); KJV: depart

G3333 μετακαλέω (metakaléō): to call elsewhere, i.e. summon. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: call (for, hither)

G3334 μετακινέω (metakinéō): to stir to a place elsewhere, i.e. remove (figuratively). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G2795 (κινέω); KJV: move away

G3335 μεταλαμβάνω (metalambánō): to participate; genitive case, to accept (and use). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: eat, have, be partaker, receive, take

G3336 μετάλημψις (metálēmpsis): participation. Origin: from G3335 (μεταλαμβάνω); KJV: taking

G3337 μεταλλάσσω (metallássō): to exchange. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω); KJV: change

G3338 μεταμέλλομαι (metaméllomai): to care afterwards, i.e. regret. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and the middle voice of G3199 (μέλω); KJV: repent (self)

G3339 μεταμορφόω (metamorphóō): to transform (literally or figuratively, "metamorphose"). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G3445 (μορφόω); KJV: change, transfigure, transform

G3340 μετανοέω (metanoéō): to think differently or afterwards, i.e. reconsider (morally, feel compunction). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: repent

G3341 μετάνοια (metánoia): (subjectively) compunction (for guilt, including reformation); by implication, reversal (of (another's) decision). Origin: from G3340 (μετανοέω); KJV: repentance

G3342 μεταξύ (metaxý): betwixt (of place or person); (of time) as adjective, intervening, or (by implication) adjoining. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and a form of G4862 (σύν); KJV: between, mean while, next

G3343 μεταπέμπω (metapémpō): to send from elsewhere, i.e. (middle voice) to summon or invite. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G3992 (πέμπω); KJV: call (send) for

G3344 μεταστρέφω (metastréphō): to turn across, i.e. transmute or (figuratively) corrupt. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: pervert, turn

G3345 μετασχηματίζω (metaschēmatízō): to transfigure or disguise; figuratively, to apply (by accommodation). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and a derivative of G4976 (σχῆμα); KJV: transfer, transform (self)

G3346 μετατίθημι (metatíthēmi): to transfer, i.e. (literally) transport, (by implication) exchange, (reflexively) change sides, or (figuratively) pervert. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: carry over, change, remove, translate, turn

G3347 μετέπειτα (metépeita): thereafter. Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G1899 (ἔπειτα); KJV: afterward

G3348 μετέχω (metéchō): to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: be partaker, pertain, take part, use

G3349 μετεωρίζω (meteōrízō): to raise in mid-air, i.e. (figuratively) suspend (passively, fluctuate or be anxious). Origin: from a compound of G3326 (μετά) and a collateral form of G142 (αἴρω) or perhaps rather G109 (ἀήρ) (compare "meteor"); KJV: be of doubtful mind

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G3350 to G3502
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G3350 μετοικεσία (metoikesía): a change of abode, i.e. (specially), expatriation. Origin: from a derivative of a compound of G3326 (μετά) and G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: X brought, carried(-ying) away (in-)to

G3351 μετοικίζω (metoikízō): to transfer as a settler or captive, i.e colonize or exile. Origin: from the same as G3350 (μετοικεσία); KJV: carry away, remove into

G3352 μετοχή (metochḗ): participation, i.e. intercourse. Origin: from G3348 (μετέχω); KJV: fellowship

G3353 μέτοχος (métochos): participant, i.e. (as noun) a sharer; by implication, an associate. Origin: from G3348 (μετέχω); KJV: fellow, partaker, partner

G3354 μετρέω (metréō): to measure (i.e. ascertain in size by a fixed standard); by implication, to admeasure (i.e. allot by rule). Origin: from G3358 (μέτρον); KJV: figuratively, to estimate:--measure, mete

G3355 μετρητής (metrētḗs): a measurer, i.e. (specially), a certain standard measure of capacity for liquids. Origin: from G3354 (μετρέω); KJV: firkin

G3356 μετριοπαθέω (metriopathéō): to be moderate in passion, i.e. gentle (to treat indulgently). Origin: from a compound of the base of G3357 (μετρίως) and G3806 (πάθος); KJV: have compassion

G3357 μετρίως (metríōs): moderately, i.e. slightly. Origin: adverb from a derivative of G3358 (μέτρον); KJV: a little

G3358 μέτρον (métron): a measure ("metre"), literally or figuratively; by implication, a limited portion (degree). Origin: an apparently primary word; KJV: measure

G3359 μέτωπον (métōpon): the forehead (as opposite the countenance). Origin: from G3326 (μετά) and ops (the face); KJV: forehead

G3360 μέχρι (méchri): as far as, i.e. up to a certain point (as a preposition, of extent (denoting the terminus, whereas G891 (ἄχρι) refers especially to the space of time or place intervening) or conjunction). Origin: from G3372 (μῆκος); KJV: till, (un-)to, until

G3361 μή (mḗ): (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas G3756 (οὐ) expects an affirmative one)) whether. Origin: a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas G3756 (οὐ) expresses an absolute denial); KJV: any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without

G3362 ἐὰν μή (eàn mḗ): if not, i.e. unless. Origin: i.e. G1437 (ἐάν) and G3361 (μή); KJV: X before, but, except, if, no, (if, + whosoever) not

G3363 ἵνα μή (hína mḗ): in order (or so) that not. Origin: i.e. G2443 (ἵνα) and G3361 (μή); KJV: albeit not, lest, that, no(-t, (-thing))

G3364 οὐ μή (ou mḗ): a double negative strengthening the denial; not at all. Origin: i.e. G3756 (οὐ) and G3361 (μή); KJV: any more, at all, by any (no) means, neither, never, no (at all), in no case (wise), nor ever, not (at all, in any wise)

G3365 μηδαμῶς (mēdamōs): by no means. Origin: adverb from a compound of G3361 (μή) and (somebody); KJV: not so

G3366 μηδέ (mēdé): but not, not even; in a continued negation, nor. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G1161 (δέ); KJV: neither, nor (yet), (no) not (once, so much as)

G3367 μηδείς (mēdeís): not even one (man, woman, thing). Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G1520 (εἷς); KJV: any (man, thing), no (man), none, not (at all, any man, a whit), nothing, + without delay

G3368 μηδέποτε (mēdépote): not even ever. Origin: from G3366 (μηδέ) and G4218 (ποτέ); KJV: never

G3369 μηδέπω (mēdépō): not even yet. Origin: from G3366 (μηδέ) and G4452 (-πω); KJV: not yet

G3370 Μῆδος (Mēdos): a Median, or inhabitant of Media. Origin: of foreign origin (compare H4074); KJV: Mede

G3371 μηκέτι (mēkéti): no further. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G2089 (ἔτι); KJV: any longer, (not) henceforth, hereafter, no henceforward (longer, more, soon), not any more

G3372 μῆκος (mēkos): length (literally or figuratively) length. Origin: probably akin to G3173 (μέγας);

G3373 μηκύνω (mēkýnō): to lengthen, i.e. (middle voice) to enlarge. Origin: from G3372 (μῆκος); KJV: grow up

G3374 μηλωτή (mēlōtḗ): a sheep-skin. Origin: from (a sheep); KJV: sheepskin

G3375 μήν (mḗn): a particle of affirmation (only with G2229 (ἦ)); assuredly. Origin: a stronger form of G3303 (μέν); KJV: + surely

G3376 μήν (mḗn): a month. Origin: a primary word; KJV: month

G3377 μηνύω (mēnýō): to disclose (through the idea of mental effort and thus calling to mind), i.e. report, declare, intimate. Origin: probably from the same base as G3145 (μασσάομαι) and G3415 (μνάομαι) (i.e. , to strive); KJV: shew, tell

G3378 μὴ οὐκ (mḕ ouk): as interrogative and negative, is it not that?. Origin: i.e. G3361 (μή) and G3756 (οὐ); KJV: neither (followed by no), + never, not

G3379 μήποτε (mḗpote): not ever; also if (or lest) ever (or perhaps). Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G4218 (ποτέ); KJV: if peradventure, lest (at any time, haply), not at all, whether or not

G3380 μήπω (mḗpō): not yet. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G4452 (-πω); KJV: not yet

G3381 μήπως (mḗpōs): lest somehow. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G4458 (-πώς); KJV: lest (by any means, by some means, haply, perhaps)

G3382 μηρός (mērós): a thigh. Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: thigh

G3383 μήτε (mḗte): not too, i.e. (in continued negation) neither or nor; also, not even. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: neither, (n-)or, so as much

G3384 μήτηρ (mḗtēr): a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: mother

G3385 μήτι (mḗti): whether at all. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and the neuter of G5100 (τὶς); KJV: not (the particle usually not expressed, except by the form of the question)

G3386 μήτιγε (mḗtige): not at all then, i.e. not to say (the rather still). Origin: from G3385 (μήτι) and G1065 (γέ); KJV: how much more

G3387 μήτις (mḗtis): whether any. Origin: from G3361 (μή) and G5100 (τὶς); KJV: any (sometimes unexpressed except by the simple interrogative form of the sentence)

G3388 μήτρα (mḗtra): the matrix. Origin: from G3384 (μήτηρ); KJV: womb

G3389 μητραλῴας (mētralṓias): a mother-thresher, i.e. matricide. Origin: from G3384 (μήτηρ) and the base of G257 (ἅλων); KJV: murderer of mothers

G3390 μητρόπολις (mētrópolis): a mother city, i.e. "metropolis". Origin: from G3384 (μήτηρ) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: chiefest city

G3391 μία (mía): one or first. Origin: irregular feminine of G1520 (εἷς); KJV: a (certain), + agree, first, one, X other

G3392 μιαίνω (miaínō): to sully or taint, i.e. contaminate (ceremonially or morally). Origin: perhaps a primary verb; KJV: defile

G3393 μίασμα (míasma): (morally) foulness (properly, the effect). Origin: from G3392 (μιαίνω) ("miasma"); KJV: pollution

G3394 μιασμός (miasmós): (morally) contamination (properly, the act). Origin: from G3392 (μιαίνω); KJV: uncleanness

G3395 μίγμα (mígma): a compound. Origin: from G3396 (μίγνυμι); KJV: mixture

G3396 μίγνυμι (mígnymi): to mix. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: mingle

G3397 μικρόν (mikrón): a small space of time or degree. Origin: masculine or neuter singular of G3398 (μικρός) (as noun); KJV: a (little) (while)

G3398 μικρός (mikrós): small (in size, quantity, number or (figuratively) dignity). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: least, less, little, small

G3399 Μίλητος (Mílētos): Miletus, a city of Asia Minor. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Miletus

G3400 μίλιον (mílion): a thousand paces, i.e. a "mile". Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: mile

G3401 μιμέομαι (miméomai): to imitate. Origin: middle voice from (a "mimic"); KJV: follow

G3402 μιμητής (mimētḗs): an imitator. Origin: from G3401 (μιμέομαι); KJV: follower

G3403 μιμνήσκω (mimnḗskō): to remind, i.e. (middle voice) to recall to mind. Origin: a prolonged form of G3415 (μνάομαι) (from which some of the tenses are borrowed); KJV: be mindful, remember

G3404 μισέω (miséō): to detest (especially to persecute); by extension, to love less. Origin: from a primary (hatred); KJV: hate(-ful)

G3405 μισθαποδοσία (misthapodosía): requital (good or bad). Origin: from G3406 (μισθαποδότης); KJV: recompence of reward

G3406 μισθαποδότης (misthapodótēs): a renumerator. Origin: from G3409 (μισθόω) and G591 (ἀποδίδωμι); KJV: rewarder

G3407 μίσθιος (místhios): a wage-earner. Origin: from G3408 (μισθός); KJV: hired servant

G3408 μισθός (misthós): pay for service (literally or figuratively), good or bad. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: hire, reward, wages

G3409 μισθόω (misthóō): to let out for wages, i.e. (middle voice) to hire. Origin: from G3408 (μισθός); KJV: hire

G3410 μίσθωμα (místhōma): a rented building. Origin: from G3409 (μισθόω); KJV: hired house

G3411 μισθωτός (misthōtós): a wage-worker (good or bad). Origin: from G3409 (μισθόω); KJV: hired servant, hireling

G3412 Μιτυλήνη (Mitylḗnē): Mitylene (or Mytilene), a town on the island of Lesbos. Origin: for (abounding in shellfish); KJV: Mitylene

G3413 Μιχαήλ (Michaḗl): Michael, an archangel. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4317); KJV: Michael

G3414 μνᾶ (mnâ): a mna (i.e. mina), a certain weight. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: pound

G3415 μνάομαι (mnáomai): to bear in mind, i.e. recollect; by implication, to reward or punish. Origin: middle voice of a derivative of G3306 (μένω) or perhaps of the base of G3145 (μασσάομαι) (through the idea of fixture in the mind or of mental grasp); KJV: be mindful, remember, come (have) in remembrance

G3416 Μνάσων (Mnásōn): Mnason, a Christian. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Mnason

G3417 μνεία (mneía): recollection; by implication, recital. Origin: from G3415 (μνάομαι) or G3403 (μιμνήσκω); KJV: mention, remembrance

G3418 μνῆμα (mnēma): a memorial, i.e. sepulchral monument (burial-place). Origin: from G3415 (μνάομαι); KJV: grave, sepulchre, tomb

G3419 μνημεῖον (mnēmeîon): a remembrance, i.e. cenotaph (place of interment). Origin: from G3420 (μνήμη); KJV: grave, sepulchre, tomb

G3420 μνήμη (mnḗmē): memory. Origin: from G3403 (μιμνήσκω); KJV: remembrance

G3421 μνημονεύω (mnēmoneúō): to exercise memory, i.e. recollect; by implication, to punish; also to rehearse. Origin: from a derivative of G3420 (μνήμη); KJV: make mention; be mindful, remember

G3422 μνημόσυνον (mnēmósynon): a reminder (memorandum), i.e. record. Origin: from G3421 (μνημονεύω); KJV: memorial

G3423 μνηστεύω (mnēsteúō): to give a souvenir (engagement present), i.e. betroth. Origin: from a derivative of G3415 (μνάομαι); KJV: espouse

G3424 μογιλάλος (mogilálos): hardly talking, i.e. dumb (tongue-tied). Origin: from G3425 (μόγις) and G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: having an impediment in his speech

G3425 μόγις (mógis): with difficulty. Origin: adverb from a primary (toil); KJV: hardly

G3426 μόδιος (módios): a modius, i.e. certain measure for things dry (the quantity or the utensil). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: bushel

G3427 μοί (moí): to me. Origin: the simpler form of G1698 (ἐμοί); KJV: I, me, mine, my

G3428 μοιχαλίς (moichalís): an adulteress (literally or figuratively). Origin: a prolonged form of the feminine of G3432 (μοιχός); KJV: adulteress(-ous, -y)

G3429 μοιχάω (moicháō): (middle voice) to commit adultery. Origin: from G3432 (μοιχός); KJV: commit adultery

G3430 μοιχεία (moicheía): adultery. Origin: from G3431 (μοιχεύω); KJV: adultery

G3431 μοιχεύω (moicheúō): to commit adultery. Origin: from G3432 (μοιχός); KJV: commit adultery

G3432 μοιχός (moichós): a (male) paramour; figuratively, apostate. Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: adulterer

G3433 μόλις (mólis): with difficulty. Origin: probably by variation for G3425 (μόγις); KJV: hardly, scarce(-ly), + with much work

G3434 Μολόχ (Molóch): Moloch (i.e. Molek), an idol. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H4432); KJV: Moloch

G3435 μολύνω (molýnō): to soil (figuratively). Origin: probably from G3189 (μέλας); KJV: defile

G3436 μολυσμός (molysmós): a stain; i.e. (figuratively) immorality. Origin: from G3435 (μολύνω); KJV: filthiness

G3437 μομφή (momphḗ): blame, i.e. (by implication), a fault. Origin: from G3201 (μέμφομαι); KJV: quarrel

G3438 μονή (monḗ): a staying, i.e. residence (the act or the place). Origin: from G3306 (μένω); KJV: abode, mansion

G3439 μονογενής (monogenḗs): only-born, i.e. sole. Origin: from G3441 (μόνος) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: only (begotten, child)

G3440 μόνον (mónon): merely. Origin: neuter of G3441 (μόνος) as adverb; KJV: alone, but, only

G3441 μόνος (mónos): remaining, i.e. sole or single; by implication, mere. Origin: probably from G3306 (μένω); KJV: alone, only, by themselves

G3442 μονόφθαλμος (monóphthalmos): one-eyed. Origin: from G3441 (μόνος) and G3788 (ὀφθαλμός); KJV: with one eye

G3443 μονόω (monóō): to isolate, i.e. bereave. Origin: from G3441 (μόνος); KJV: be desolate

G3444 μορφή (morphḗ): shape; figuratively, nature. Origin: perhaps from the base of G3313 (μέρος) (through the idea of adjustment of parts); KJV: form

G3445 μορφόω (morphóō): to fashion (figuratively). Origin: from the same as G3444 (μορφή); KJV: form

G3446 μόρφωσις (mórphōsis): formation, i.e. (by implication), appearance (semblance or (concretely) formula). Origin: from G3445 (μορφόω); KJV: form

G3447 μοσχοποιέω (moschopoiéō): to fabricate the image of a bullock. Origin: from G3448 (μόσχος) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: make a calf

G3448 μόσχος (móschos): a young bullock. Origin: probably strengthened for (a shoot); KJV: calf

G3449 μόχθος (móchthos): toil, i.e. (by implication) sadness. Origin: from the base of G3425 (μόγις); KJV: painfulness, travail

G3450 μοῦ (moû): of me. Origin: the simpler form of G1700 (ἐμοῦ); KJV: I, me, mine (own), my

G3451 μουσικός (mousikós): "musical", i.e. (as noun) a minstrel. Origin: from (a Muse); KJV: musician

G3452 μυελός (myelós): the marrow. Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: marrow

G3453 μυέω (myéō): to initiate, i.e. (by implication) to teach. Origin: from the base of G3466 (μυστήριον); KJV: instruct

G3454 μῦθος (mŷthos): a tale, i.e. fiction ("myth"). Origin: perhaps from the same as G3453 (μυέω) (through the idea of tuition); KJV: fable

G3455 μυκάομαι (mykáomai): to bellow (roar). Origin: from a presumed derivative of ( to "moo"); KJV: roar

G3456 μυκτηρίζω (myktērízō): to make mouths at, i.e. ridicule. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G3455 (μυκάομαι) (meaning snout, as that whence lowing proceeds); KJV: mock

G3457 μυλικός (mylikós): belonging to a mill. Origin: from G3458 (μύλος); KJV: mill(-stone)

G3458 μύλος (mýlos): a "mill", i.e. (by implication), a grinder (millstone). Origin: probably ultimately from the base of G3433 (μόλις) (through the idea of hardship); KJV: millstone

G3459 μύλων (mýlōn): a mill-house. Origin: from G3458 (μύλος); KJV: mill

G3460 Μύρα (Mýra): Myra, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Myra

G3461 μυριάς (myriás): a ten-thousand; by extension, a "myriad" or indefinite number. Origin: from G3463 (μύριοι); KJV: ten thousand

G3462 μυρίζω (myrízō): to apply (perfumed) unguent to. Origin: from G3464 (μύρον); KJV: anoint

G3463 μύριοι (mýrioi): ten thousand; by extension, innumerably many. Origin: plural of an apparently primary word (properly, meaning very many); KJV: ten thousand
