G3464 μύρον (mýron): "myrrh", i.e. (by implication) perfumed oil. Origin: probably of foreign origin (compare H4753, G4666 (σμύρνα)); KJV: ointment

G3465 Μυσία (Mysía): Mysia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Mysia

G3466 μυστήριον (mystḗrion): a secret or "mystery" (through the idea of silence imposed by initiation into religious rites). Origin: from a derivative of (to shut the mouth); KJV: mystery

G3467 μυωπάζω (myōpázō): from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); to shut the eyes, i.e. blink (see indistinctly). Origin: from a compound of the base of G3466 (μυστήριον) and (the face; KJV: cannot see far off

G3468 μώλωψ (mṓlōps): probably akin to the base of G3433 (μόλις)) and probably (the face; from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); a mole ("black eye") or blow-mark. Origin: from ("moil"; KJV: stripe

G3469 μωμάομαι (mōmáomai): to carp at, i.e. censure (discredit). Origin: from G3470 (μῶμος); KJV: blame

G3470 μῶμος (mōmos): a flaw or blot, i.e. (figuratively) disgraceful person. Origin: perhaps from G3201 (μέμφομαι); KJV: blemish

G3471 μωραίνω (mōraínō): to become insipid; figuratively, to make (passively, act) as a simpleton. Origin: from G3474 (μωρός); KJV: become fool, make foolish, lose savour

G3472 μωρία (mōría): silliness, i.e. absurdity. Origin: from G3474 (μωρός); KJV: foolishness

G3473 μωρολογία (mōrología): silly talk, i.e. buffoonery. Origin: from a compound of G3474 (μωρός) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: foolish talking

G3474 μωρός (mōrós): dull or stupid (as if shut up), i.e. heedless, (morally) blockhead, (apparently) absurd. Origin: probably from the base of G3466 (μυστήριον); KJV: fool(-ish, X -ishness)

G3475 Μωσεύς (Mōseús): Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver. Origin: of Hebrew origin; (H4872); KJV: Moses

G3476 Ναασσών (Naassṓn): Naasson (i.e. Nachshon), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5177); KJV: Naasson

G3477 Ναγγαί (Nangaí): Nangæ (i.e. perhaps Nogach), an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H5052); KJV: Nagge

G3478 Ναζαρέθ (Nazaréth): Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Nazareth

G3479 Ναζαρηνός (Nazarēnós): a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth. Origin: from G3478 (Ναζαρέθ); KJV: of Nazareth

G3480 Ναζωραῖος (Nazōraîos): a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian. Origin: from G3478 (Ναζαρέθ); KJV: Nazarene, of Nazareth

G3481 Ναθάν (Nathán): Nathan, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5416); KJV: Nathan

G3482 Ναθαναήλ (Nathanaḗl): Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5417); KJV: Nathanael

G3483 ναί (naí): yes. Origin: a primary particle of strong affirmation; KJV: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes

G3484 Ναΐν (Naḯn): Nain, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (compare H4999); KJV: Nain

G3485 ναός (naós): a fane, shrine, temple. Origin: from a primary (to dwell); KJV: shrine, temple

G3486 Ναούμ (Naoúm): Naum (i.e. Nachum), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5151); KJV: Naum

G3487 νάρδος (nárdos): "nard". Origin: of foreign origin (compare H5373); KJV: (spike-)nard

G3488 Νάρκισσος (Nárkissos): Narcissus, a Roman. Origin: a flower of the same name, from (stupefaction, as a "narcotic"); KJV: Narcissus

G3489 ναυαγέω (nauagéō): to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively. Origin: from a compound of G3491 (ναῦς) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: make (suffer) shipwreck

G3490 ναύκληρος (naúklēros): a captain. Origin: from G3491 (ναῦς) and G2819 (κλῆρος) ("clerk"); KJV: owner of a ship

G3491 ναῦς (naûs): a boat (of any size). Origin: from or (to float); KJV: ship

G3492 ναύτης (naútēs): a boatman, i.e. seaman. Origin: from G3491 (ναῦς); KJV: sailor, shipman

G3493 Ναχώρ (Nachṓr): Nachor, the grandfather of Abraham. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5152); KJV: Nachor

G3494 νεανίας (neanías): a youth (up to about forty years). Origin: from a derivative of G3501 (νέος); KJV: young man

G3495 νεανίσκος (neanískos): a youth (under forty). Origin: from the same as G3494 (νεανίας); KJV: young man

G3496 Νεάπολις (Neápolis): new town; Neapolis, a place in Macedonia. Origin: from G3501 (νέος) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: Neapolis

G3497 Νεεμάν (Neemán): Neeman (i.e. Naaman), a Syrian. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5283); KJV: Naaman

G3498 νεκρός (nekrós): dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun). Origin: from an apparently primary (a corpse); KJV: dead

G3499 νεκρόω (nekróō): to deaden, i.e. (figuratively) to subdue. Origin: from G3498 (νεκρός); KJV: be dead, mortify

G3500 νέκρωσις (nékrōsis): decease; figuratively, impotency. Origin: from G3499 (νεκρόω); KJV: deadness, dying

G3501 νέος (néos): "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate. Origin: including the comparative ; a primary word; KJV: new, young

G3502 νεοσσός (neossós): a youngling (nestling). Origin: from G3501 (νέος); KJV: young

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G3503 to G3642
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G3503 νεότης (neótēs): newness, i.e. youthfulness. Origin: from G3501 (νέος); KJV: youth

G3504 νεόφυτος (neóphytos): newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte"). Origin: from G3501 (νέος) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω); KJV: novice

G3505 Νέρων (Nérōn): Neron (i.e. Nero), a Roman emperor. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Nero

G3506 νεύω (neúō): to "nod", i.e. (by analogy), signal. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: beckon

G3507 νεφέλη (nephélē): properly, cloudiness, i.e. (concretely) a cloud. Origin: from G3509 (νέφος); KJV: cloud

G3508 Νεφθαλείμ (Nephthaleím): Nephthaleim (i.e. Naphthali), a tribe in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5321); KJV: Nephthalim

G3509 νέφος (néphos): a cloud. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: cloud

G3510 νεφρός (nephrós): a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: reins

G3511 νεωκόρος (neōkóros): a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary. Origin: from a form of G3485 (ναός) and (to sweep); KJV: worshipper

G3512 νεωτερικός (neōterikós): appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile. Origin: from the comparative of G3501 (νέος); KJV: youthful

G3513 νή (nḗ): a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as. Origin: probably an intensive form of G3483 (ναί); KJV: I protest by

G3514 νήθω (nḗthō): to spin. Origin: from (of like meaning); KJV: spin

G3515 νηπιάζω (nēpiázō): to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently. Origin: from G3516 (νήπιος); KJV: be a child

G3516 νήπιος (nḗpios): not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian. Origin: from an obsolete particle (implying negation) and G2031 (ἔπος); KJV: babe, child (+ -ish)

G3517 Νηρεύς (Nēreús): Nereus, a Christian. Origin: apparently from a derivative of the base of G3491 (ναῦς) (meaning wet); KJV: Nereus

G3518 Νηρί (Nērí): Neri (i.e. Nerijah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5374); KJV: Neri

G3519 νησίον (nēsíon): an islet. Origin: diminutive of G3520 (νῆσος); KJV: island

G3520 νῆσος (nēsos): an island. Origin: probably from the base of G3491 (ναῦς); KJV: island, isle

G3521 νηστεία (nēsteía): abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement. Origin: from G3522 (νηστεύω); KJV: fast(-ing)

G3522 νηστεύω (nēsteúō): to abstain from food (religiously). Origin: from G3523 (νῆστις); KJV: fast

G3523 νῆστις (nēstis): not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously). Origin: from the inseparable negative particle (not) and G2068 (ἐσθίω); KJV: fasting

G3524 νηφάλεος (nēpháleos): sober, i.e. (figuratively) circumspect. Origin: from G3525 (νήφω); KJV: sober

G3525 νήφω (nḗphō): to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: be sober, watch

G3526 Νίγερ (Níger): black; Niger, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Niger

G3527 Νικάνωρ (Nikánōr): victorious; Nicanor, a Christian. Origin: probably from G3528 (νικάω); KJV: Nicanor

G3528 νικάω (nikáō): to subdue (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3529 (νίκη); KJV: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory

G3529 νίκη (níkē): conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: victory

G3530 Νικόδημος (Nikódēmos): victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite. Origin: from G3534 (νῖκος) and G1218 (δῆμος); KJV: Nicodemus

G3531 Νικολαΐτης (Nikolaḯtēs): a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus. Origin: from G3532 (Νικόλαος); KJV: Nicolaitane

G3532 Νικόλαος (Nikólaos): victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic. Origin: from G3534 (νῖκος) and G2994 (Λαοδικεύς); KJV: Nicolaus

G3533 Νικόπολις (Nikópolis): victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia. Origin: from G3534 (νῖκος) and G4172 (πόλις); KJV: Nicopolis

G3534 νῖκος (nîkos): a conquest (concretely), i.e. (by implication) triumph. Origin: from G3529 (νίκη); KJV: victory

G3535 Νινευΐ (Nineuḯ): Ninevi (i.e. Nineveh), the capital of Assyria. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5210); KJV: Nineve

G3536 Νινευΐτης (Nineuḯtēs): a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh. Origin: from G3535 (Νινευΐ); KJV: of Nineve, Ninevite

G3537 νιπτήρ (niptḗr): a ewer. Origin: from G3538 (νίπτω); KJV: bason

G3538 νίπτω (níptō): to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution. KJV: wash

G3539 νοιέω (noiéō): to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed. Origin: from G3563 (νοῦς); KJV: consider, perceive, think, understand

G3540 νόημα (nóēma): a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself. Origin: from G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: device, mind, thought

G3541 νόθος (nóthos): a spurious or illegitimate son. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: bastard

G3542 νομή (nomḗ): pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage. Origin: feminine from the same as G3551 (νόμος); KJV: X eat, pasture

G3543 νομίζω (nomízō): properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard. Origin: from G3551 (νόμος); KJV: suppose, thing, be wont

G3544 νομικός (nomikós): according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law. Origin: from G3551 (νόμος); KJV: about the law, lawyer

G3545 νομίμως (nomímōs): legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists). Origin: adverb from a derivative of G3551 (νόμος); KJV: lawfully

G3546 νόμισμα (nómisma): what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin. Origin: from G3543 (νομίζω); KJV: money

G3547 νομοδιδάσκαλος (nomodidáskalos): an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi. Origin: from G3551 (νόμος) and G1320 (διδάσκαλος); KJV: doctor (teacher) of the law

G3548 νομοθεσία (nomothesía): legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code). Origin: from G3550 (νομοθέτης); KJV: giving of the law

G3549 νομοθετέω (nomothetéō): to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them). Origin: from G3550 (νομοθέτης); KJV: establish, receive the law

G3550 νομοθέτης (nomothétēs): a legislator. Origin: from G3551 (νόμος) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: lawgiver

G3551 νόμος (nómos): law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle). Origin: from a primary (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); KJV: law

G3552 νοσέω (noséō): to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon). Origin: from G3554 (νόσος); KJV: dote

G3553 νόσημα (nósēma): an ailment. Origin: from G3552 (νοσέω); KJV: disease

G3554 νόσος (nósos): a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: disease, infirmity, sickness

G3555 νοσσιά (nossiá): a brood (of chickens). Origin: from G3502 (νεοσσός); KJV: brood

G3556 νοσσίον (nossíon): a birdling. Origin: diminutive of G3502 (νεοσσός); KJV: chicken

G3557 νοσφίζομαι (nosphízomai): to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle. Origin: middle voice from (apart or clandestinely); KJV: keep back, purloin

G3558 νότος (nótos): the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: south (wind)

G3559 νουθεσία (nouthesía): calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning. Origin: from G3563 (νοῦς) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: admonition

G3560 νουθετέω (nouthetéō): to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently. Origin: from the same as G3559 (νουθεσία); KJV: admonish, warn

G3561 νουμηνία (noumēnía): the festival of new moon. Origin: feminine of a compound of G3501 (νέος) and G3376 (μήν) (as noun by implication, of G2250 (ἡμέρα)); KJV: new moon

G3562 νουνεχῶς (nounechōs): in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently. Origin: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of G3563 (νοῦς) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: discreetly

G3563 νοῦς (noûs): the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning. Origin: probably from the base of G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: mind, understanding

G3564 Νυμφᾶς (Nymphâs): nymph-given (i.e. -born); Nymphas, a Christian. Origin: probably contracted for a compound of G3565 (νύμφη) and G1435 (δῶρον); KJV: Nymphas

G3565 νύμφη (nýmphē): compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife. Origin: from a primary but obsolete verb (to veil as a bride; KJV: bride, daughter in law

G3566 νυμφίος (nymphíos): a bride-groom (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3565 (νύμφη); KJV: bridegroom

G3567 νυμφών (nymphṓn): the bridal room. Origin: from G3565 (νύμφη); KJV: bridechamber

G3568 νῦν (nŷn): "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate. Origin: a primary particle of present time; KJV: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time)

G3569 τανῦν (tanŷn): the things now, i.e. (adverbially) at present. Origin: from neuter plural of G3588 (ὁ) and G3568 (νῦν); KJV: (but) now

G3570 νυνί (nyní): just now. Origin: a prolonged form of G3568 (νῦν) for emphasis; KJV: now

G3571 νύξ (nýx): "night" (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary word; KJV: (mid-)night

G3572 νύσσω (nýssō): to prick ("nudge"). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: pierce

G3573 νυστάζω (nystázō): to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G3506 (νεύω); KJV: slumber

G3574 νυχθήμερον (nychthḗmeron): a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours. Origin: from G3571 (νύξ) and G2250 (ἡμέρα); KJV: night and day

G3575 Νῶε (Nōe): Noë, (i.e. Noäch), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5146); KJV: Noe

G3576 νωθρός (nōthrós): sluggish, i.e. (literally) lazy, or (figuratively) stupid. Origin: from a derivative of G3541 (νόθος); KJV: dull, slothful

G3577 νῶτος (nōtos): the back. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: back

G3578 ξενία (xenía): hospitality, i.e. (by implication) a place of entertainment. Origin: from G3581 (ξένος); KJV: lodging

G3579 ξενίζω (xenízō): to be a host (passively, a guest); by implication, be (make, appear) strange. Origin: from G3581 (ξένος); KJV: entertain, lodge, (think it) strange

G3580 ξενοδοχέω (xenodochéō): to be hospitable. Origin: from a compound of G3581 (ξένος) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: lodge strangers

G3581 ξένος (xénos): foreign (literally, alien, or figuratively, novel); by implication, a guest or (vice-versa) entertainer. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: host, strange(-r)

G3582 ξέστης (xéstēs): by implication, (of friction) to boil or heat); a vessel (as fashioned or for cooking) (or perhaps by corruption from the Latin sextarius, the sixth of a modius, i.e. about a pint), i.e. (specially), a measure for liquids or solids, (by analogy, a pitcher). Origin: as if from (properly, to smooth; KJV: pot

G3583 ξηραίνω (xēraínō): to desiccate; by implication, to shrivel, to mature. Origin: from G3584 (ξηρός); KJV: dry up, pine away, be ripe, wither (away)

G3584 ξηρός (xērós): arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water). Origin: from the base of G3582 (ξέστης) (through the idea of scorching); KJV: dry land, withered

G3585 ξύλινος (xýlinos): wooden. Origin: from G3586 (ξύλον); KJV: of wood

G3586 ξύλον (xýlon): timber (as fuel or material); by implication, a stick, club or tree or other wooden article or substance. Origin: from another form of the base of G3582 (ξέστης); KJV: staff, stocks, tree, wood

G3587 ξυράω (xyráō): to shave or "shear" the hair. Origin: from a derivative of the same as G3586 (ξύλον) (meaning a razor); KJV: shave

G3588 ὁ (ho): the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom). Origin: the definite article; KJV: the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc

G3589 ὀγδοήκοντα (ogdoḗkonta): ten times eight. Origin: from G3590 (ὄγδοος); KJV: fourscore

G3590 ὄγδοος (ógdoos): the eighth. Origin: from G3638 (ὀκτώ); KJV: eighth

G3591 ὄγκος (ónkos): a mass (as bending or bulging by its load), i.e. burden (hindrance). Origin: probably from the same as G43 (ἀγκάλη); KJV: weight

G3592 ὅδε (hóde): the same, i.e. this or that one (plural these or those); often used as a personal pronoun. Origin: from G3588 (ὁ) and G1161 (δέ); KJV: he, she, such, these, thus

G3593 ὁδεύω (hodeúō): to travel. Origin: from G3598 (ὁδός); KJV: journey

G3594 ὁδηγέω (hodēgéō): to show the way (literally or figuratively (teach)). Origin: from G3595 (ὁδηγός); KJV: guide, lead

G3595 ὁδηγός (hodēgós): a conductor (literally or figuratively (teacher)). Origin: from G3598 (ὁδός) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: guide, leader

G3596 ὁδοιπορέω (hodoiporéō): to be a wayfarer, i.e. travel. Origin: from a compound of G3598 (ὁδός) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: go on a journey

G3597 ὁδοιπορία (hodoiporía): travel. Origin: from the same as G3596 (ὁδοιπορέω); KJV: journey(-ing)

G3598 ὁδός (hodós): a road; by implication, a progress (the route, act or distance); figuratively, a mode or means. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: journey, (high-)way

G3599 ὀδούς (odoús): a "tooth". Origin: perhaps from the base of G2068 (ἐσθίω); KJV: tooth

G3600 ὀδυνάω (odynáō): to grieve. Origin: from G3601 (ὀδύνη); KJV: sorrow, torment

G3601 ὀδύνη (odýnē): grief (as dejecting). Origin: from G1416 (δύνω); KJV: sorrow

G3602 ὀδυρμός (odyrmós): moaning, i.e. lamentation. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G1416 (δύνω); KJV: mourning

G3603 ὅ ἐστι (hó esti): which is. Origin: from the neuter of G3739 (ὅς) and the third person singular present indicative of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: called, which is (make), that is (to say)

G3604 Ὀζίας (Ozías): Ozias (i.e. Uzzijah), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5818); KJV: Ozias

G3605 ὄζω (ózō): to scent (usually an ill "odor"). Origin: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); KJV: stink

G3606 ὅθεν (hóthen): from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction). Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) with the directive enclitic of source; KJV: from thence, (from) whence, where(-by, -fore, -upon)

G3607 ὀθόνη (othónē): a linen cloth, i.e. (especially) a sail. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: sheet

G3608 ὀθόνιον (othónion): a linen bandage. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3607 (ὀθόνη); KJV: linen clothes

G3609 οἰκεῖος (oikeîos): domestic, i.e. (as noun), a relative, adherent. Origin: from G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: (those) of the (his own) house(-hold)

G3610 οἰκέτης (oikétēs): a fellow resident, i.e. menial domestic. Origin: from G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: (household) servant

G3611 οἰκέω (oikéō): to occupy a house, i.e. reside (figuratively, inhabit, remain, inhere); by implication, to cohabit. Origin: from G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: dwell

G3612 οἴκημα (oíkēma): a tenement, i.e. (specially), a jail. Origin: from G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: prison

G3613 οἰκητήριον (oikētḗrion): a residence (literally or figuratively). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3611 (οἰκέω) (equivalent to G3612 (οἴκημα)); KJV: habitation, house

G3614 οἰκία (oikía): properly, residence (abstractly), but usually (concretely) an abode (literally or figuratively); by implication, a family (especially domestics). Origin: from G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: home, house(-hold)

G3615 οἰκιακός (oikiakós): familiar, i.e. (as noun) relatives. Origin: from G3614 (οἰκία); KJV: they (them) of (his own) household

G3616 οἰκοδεσποτέω (oikodespotéō): to be the head of (i.e. rule) a family. Origin: from G3617 (οἰκοδεσπότης); KJV: guide the house

G3617 οἰκοδεσπότης (oikodespótēs): the head of a family. Origin: from G3624 (οἶκος) and G1203 (δεσπότης); KJV: goodman (of the house), householder, master of the house

G3618 οἰκοδομέω (oikodoméō): to be a house-builder, i.e. construct or (figuratively) confirm. Origin: from the same as G3619 (οἰκοδομή); KJV: (be in) build(-er, -ing, up), edify, embolden

G3619 οἰκοδομή (oikodomḗ): architecture, i.e. (concretely) a structure; figuratively, confirmation. Origin: feminine (abstract) of a compound of G3624 (οἶκος) and the base of G1430 (δῶμα); KJV: building, edify(-ication, -ing)

G3620 οἰκοδομία (oikodomía): confirmation. Origin: from the same as G3619 (οἰκοδομή); KJV: edifying

G3621 οἰκονομέω (oikonoméō): to manage (a house, i.e. an estate). Origin: from G3623 (οἰκονόμος); KJV: be steward

G3622 οἰκονομία (oikonomía): administration (of a household or estate); specially, a (religious) "economy". Origin: from G3623 (οἰκονόμος); KJV: dispensation, stewardship

G3623 οἰκονόμος (oikonómos): a house-distributor (i.e. manager), or overseer, i.e. an employee in that capacity; by extension, a fiscal agent (treasurer); figuratively, a preacher (of the Gospel). Origin: from G3624 (οἶκος) and the base of G3551 (νόμος); KJV: chamberlain, governor, steward

G3624 οἶκος (oîkos): a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: home, house(-hold), temple

G3625 οἰκουμένη (oikouménē): land, i.e. the (terrene part of the) globe; specially, the Roman empire. Origin: feminine participle present passive of G3611 (οἰκέω) (as noun, by implication, of G1093 (γῆ)); KJV: earth, world

G3626 οἰκουρός (oikourós): be "ware"); a stayer at home, i.e. domestically inclined (a "good housekeeper"). Origin: from G3624 (οἶκος) and (a guard; KJV: keeper at home

G3627 οἰκτείρω (oikteírō): to exercise pity. Origin: from (pity); KJV: have compassion on

G3628 οἰκτιρμός (oiktirmós): pity. Origin: from G3627 (οἰκτείρω); KJV: mercy

G3629 οἰκτίρμων (oiktírmōn): compassionate. Origin: from G3627 (οἰκτείρω); KJV: merciful, of tender mercy

G3630 οἰνοπότης (oinopótēs): a tippler. Origin: from G3631 (οἶνος) and a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: winebibber

G3631 οἶνος (oînos): "wine" (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary word (or perhaps of Hebrew origin (H3196)); KJV: wine

G3632 οἰνοφλυγία (oinophlygía): an overflow (or surplus) of wine, i.e. vinolency (drunkenness). Origin: from G3631 (οἶνος) and a form of the base of G5397 (φλύαρος); KJV: excess of wine

G3633 οἴομαι (oíomai): to make like (oneself), i.e. imagine (be of the opinion). Origin: middle voice apparently from G3634 (οἷος); KJV: suppose, think

G3634 οἷος (hoîos): such or what sort of (as a correlation or exclamation); especially the neuter (adverbially) with negative, not so. Origin: probably akin to G3588 (ὁ), G3739 (ὅς), and G3745 (ὅσος); KJV: so (as), such as, what (manner of), which

G3635 ὀκνέω (oknéō): to be slow (figuratively, loath). Origin: from (hesitation); KJV: delay

G3636 ὀκνηρός (oknērós): tardy, i.e. indolent; (figuratively) irksome. Origin: from G3635 (ὀκνέω); KJV: grievous, slothful

G3637 ὀκταήμερος (oktaḗmeros): an eight-day old person or act. Origin: from G3638 (ὀκτώ) and G2250 (ἡμέρα); KJV: the eighth day

G3638 ὀκτώ (oktṓ): "eight". Origin: a primary numeral; KJV: eight

G3639 ὄλεθρος (ólethros): a prolonged form); ruin, i.e. death, punishment. Origin: from a primary (to destroy; KJV: destruction

G3640 ὀλιγόπιστος (oligópistos): incredulous, i.e. lacking confidence (in Christ). Origin: from G3641 (ὀλίγος) and G4102 (πίστις); KJV: of little faith

G3641 ὀλίγος (olígos): puny (in extent, degree, number, duration or value); especially neuter (adverbially) somewhat. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: + almost, brief(-ly), few, (a) little, + long, a season, short, small, a while

G3642 ὀλιγόψυχος (oligópsychos): little-spirited, i.e. faint-hearted. Origin: from G3641 (ὀλίγος) and G6590; KJV: feebleminded

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G3643 to G3771
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G3643 ὀλιγωρέω (oligōréō): to have little regard for, i.e. to disesteem. Origin: from a compound of G3641 (ὀλίγος) and ("care"); KJV: despise

G3644 ὀλοθρευτής (olothreutḗs): a ruiner, i.e. (specially), a venomous serpent. Origin: from G3645 (ὀλοθρεύω); KJV: destroyer

G3645 ὀλοθρεύω (olothreúō): to spoil, i.e. slay. Origin: from G3639 (ὄλεθρος); KJV: destroy

G3646 ὁλοκαύτωμα (holokaútōma): a wholly-consumed sacrifice ("holocaust"). Origin: from a derivative of a compound of G3650 (ὅλος) and a derivative of G2545 (καίω); KJV: (whole) burnt offering

G3647 ὁλοκληρία (holoklēría): integrity, i.e. physical wholeness. Origin: from G3648 (ὁλόκληρος); KJV: perfect soundness

G3648 ὁλόκληρος (holóklēros): complete in every part, i.e. perfectly sound (in body). Origin: from G3650 (ὅλος) and G2819 (κλῆρος); KJV: entire, whole

G3649 ὀλολύζω (ololýzō): to "howl" or "halloo", i.e. shriek. Origin: a reduplicated primary verb; KJV: howl

G3650 ὅλος (hólos): "whole" or "all", i.e. complete (in extent, amount, time or degree), especially (neuter) as noun or adverb. Origin: a primary word; KJV: all, altogether, every whit, + throughout, whole

G3651 ὁλοτελής (holotelḗs): complete to the end, i.e. absolutely perfect. Origin: from G3650 (ὅλος) and G5056 (τέλος); KJV: wholly

G3652 Ὀλυμπᾶς (Olympâs): Olympas, a Christian. Origin: probably a contraction from (Olympian-bestowed, i.e. heaven-descended); KJV: Olympas

G3653 ὄλυνθος (ólynthos): an unripe (because out of season) fig. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: untimely fig

G3654 ὅλως (hólōs): completely, i.e. altogether; (by analogy), everywhere; (negatively) not by any means. Origin: adverb from G3650 (ὅλος); KJV: at all, commonly, utterly

G3655 ὄμβρος (ómbros): a thunder storm. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: shower

G3656 ὁμιλέω (homiléō): to be in company with, i.e. (by implication) to converse. Origin: from G3658 (ὅμιλος); KJV: commune, talk

G3657 ὁμιλία (homilía): companionship ("homily"), i.e. (by implication) intercourse. Origin: from G3658 (ὅμιλος); KJV: communication

G3658 ὅμιλος (hómilos): association together, i.e. a multitude. Origin: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and a derivative of the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι) (meaning a crowd); KJV: company

G3659 ὄμμα (ómma): a sight, i.e. (by implication) the eye. Origin: from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: eye

G3660 ὀμνύω (omnýō): to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath. Origin: a prolonged form of a primary, but obsolete , for which another prolonged form is used in certain tenses; KJV: swear

G3661 ὁμοθυμαδόν (homothymadón): unanimously. Origin: adverb from a compound of the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: with one accord (mind)

G3662 ὁμοιάζω (homoiázō): to resemble. Origin: from G3664 (ὅμοιος); KJV: agree

G3663 ὁμοιοπαθής (homoiopathḗs): similarly affected. Origin: from G3664 (ὅμοιος) and the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω); KJV: of (subject to) like passions

G3664 ὅμοιος (hómoios): similar (in appearance or character). Origin: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ); KJV: like, + manner

G3665 ὁμοιότης (homoiótēs): resemblance. Origin: from G3664 (ὅμοιος); KJV: like as, similitude

G3666 ὁμοιόω (homoióō): to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar. Origin: from G3664 (ὅμοιος); KJV: be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble

G3667 ὁμοίωμα (homoíōma): a form; abstractly, resemblance. Origin: from G3666 (ὁμοιόω); KJV: made like to, likeness, shape, similitude

G3668 ὁμοίως (homoíōs): similarly. Origin: adverb from G3664 (ὅμοιος); KJV: likewise, so

G3669 ὁμοίωσις (homoíōsis): assimilation, i.e. resemblance. Origin: from G3666 (ὁμοιόω); KJV: similitude

G3670 ὁμολογέω (homologéō): to assent, i.e. covenant, acknowledge. Origin: from a compound of the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: con- (pro-)fess, confession is made, give thanks, promise

G3671 ὁμολογία (homología): acknowledgment. Origin: from the same as G3670 (ὁμολογέω); KJV: con- (pro-)fession, professed

G3672 ὁμολογουμένως (homologouménōs): confessedly. Origin: adverb of present passive participle of G3670 (ὁμολογέω); KJV: without controversy

G3673 ὁμότεχνος (homótechnos): a fellow-artificer. Origin: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5078 (τέχνη); KJV: of the same craft

G3674 ὁμοῦ (homoû): akin to G260 (ἅμα)) as adverb; at the same place or time. Origin: genitive case of (the same; KJV: together

G3675 ὁμόφρων (homóphrōn): like-minded, i.e. harmonious. Origin: from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ) and G5424 (φρήν); KJV: of one mind

G3676 ὅμως (hómōs): at the same time, i.e. (conjunctionally) notwithstanding, yet still. Origin: adverb from the base of G3674 (ὁμοῦ); KJV: and even, nevertheless, though but

G3677 ὄναρ (ónar): a dream. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: dream

G3678 ὀνάριον (onárion): a little ass. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3688 (ὄνος); KJV: young ass

G3679 ὀνειδίζω (oneidízō): to defame, i.e. rail at, chide, taunt. Origin: from G3681 (ὄνειδος); KJV: cast in teeth, (suffer) reproach, revile, upbraid

G3680 ὀνειδισμός (oneidismós): contumely. Origin: from G3679 (ὀνειδίζω); KJV: reproach

G3681 ὄνειδος (óneidos): notoriety, i.e. a taunt (disgrace). Origin: probably akin to the base of G3686 (ὄνομα); KJV: reproach

G3682 Ὀνήσιμος (Onḗsimos): profitable; Onesimus, a Christian. Origin: from G3685 (ὀνίνημι); KJV: Onesimus

G3683 Ὀνησίφορος (Onēsíphoros): profit-bearer; Onesiphorus, a Christian. Origin: from a derivative of G3685 (ὀνίνημι) and G5411 (φόρος); KJV: Onespiphorus

G3684 ὀνικός (onikós): belonging to a ass, i.e. large (so as to be turned by a ass). Origin: from G3688 (ὄνος); KJV: millstone

G3685 ὀνίνημι (onínēmi): for which another prolonged form () is used as an alternate in some tenses (unless indeed it be identical with the base of G3686 (ὄνομα) through the idea of notoriety); to gratify, i.e. (middle voice) to derive pleasure or advantage from. Origin: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb (, to slur); KJV: have joy

G3686 ὄνομα (ónoma): a "name" (literally or figuratively) (authority, character). Origin: from a presumed derivative of the base of G1097 (γινώσκω) (compare G3685 (ὀνίνημι)); KJV: called, (+ sur-)name(-d)

G3687 ὀνομάζω (onomázō): to name, i.e. assign an appellation; by extension, to utter, mention, profess. Origin: from G3686 (ὄνομα); KJV: call, name

G3688 ὄνος (ónos): a donkey. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: an ass

G3689 ὄντως (óntōs): really. Origin: adverb of the oblique cases of G5607 (ὤν); KJV: certainly, clean, indeed, of a truth, verily

G3690 ὄξος (óxos): vinegar, i.e. sour wine. Origin: from G3691 (ὀξύς); KJV: vinegar

G3691 ὀξύς (oxýs): keen; by analogy, rapid. Origin: probably akin to the base of G188 (ἀκμήν) ("acid"); KJV: sharp, swift

G3692 ὀπή (opḗ): a hole (as if for light), i.e. cavern; by analogy, a spring (of water). Origin: probably from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: cave, place

G3693 ὄπισθεν (ópisthen): from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)) with enclitic of source; from the rear (as a secure aspect), i.e. at the back (adverb and preposition of place or time). Origin: from (regard; KJV: after, backside, behind

G3694 ὀπίσω (opísō): to the back, i.e. aback (as adverb or preposition of time or place; or as noun). Origin: from the same as G3693 (ὄπισθεν) with enclitic of direction; KJV: after, back(-ward), (+ get) behind, + follow

G3695 ὁπλίζω (hoplízō): to equip (with weapons (middle voice and figuratively)). Origin: from G3696 (ὅπλον); KJV: arm self

G3696 ὅπλον (hóplon): an implement or utensil or tool (literally or figuratively, especially, offensive for war). Origin: probably from a primary (to be busy about); KJV: armour, instrument, weapon

G3697 ὁποῖος (hopoîos): of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent G5108 (τοιοῦτος) of quality). Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G4169 (ποῖος); KJV: what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever

G3698 ὁπότε (hopóte): what(-ever) then, i.e. (of time) as soon as. Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G4218 (ποτέ); KJV: when

G3699 ὅπου (hópou): what(-ever) where, i.e. at whichever spot. Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G4225 (πού); KJV: in what place, where(-as, -soever), whither (+ soever)

G3700 ὀπτάνομαι (optánomai): to gaze (i.e. with wide-open eyes, as at something remarkable; and thus differing from G991 (βλέπω), which denotes simply voluntary observation; and from G1492 (εἴδω), which expresses merely mechanical, passive or casual vision; while G2300 (θεάομαι), and still more emphatically its intensive G2334 (θεωρέω), signifies an earnest but more continued inspection; and G4648 (σκοπέω) a watching from a distance). Origin: a (middle voice) prolonged form of the primary (middle voice) ; which is used for it in certain tenses; and both as alternate of G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: appear, look, see, shew self

G3701 ὀπτασία (optasía): visuality, i.e. (concretely) an apparition. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: vision

G3702 ὀπτός (optós): cooked, i.e. roasted. Origin: from an obsolete verb akin to (to "steep"); KJV: broiled

G3703 ὀπώρα (opṓra): properly, even-tide of the (summer) season (dog-days), i.e. (by implication) ripe fruit. Origin: apparently from the base of G3796 (ὀψέ) and G5610 (ὥρα); KJV: fruit

G3704 ὅπως (hópōs): what(-ever) how, i.e. in the manner that (as adverb or conjunction of coincidence, intentional or actual). Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G4459 (πῶς); KJV: because, how, (so) that, to, when

G3705 ὅραμα (hórama): something gazed at, i.e. a spectacle (especially supernatural). Origin: from G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: sight, vision

G3706 ὅρασις (hórasis): the act of gazing, i.e. (externally) an aspect or (internally) an inspired appearance. Origin: from G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: sight, vision

G3707 ὁρατός (horatós): gazed at, i.e. (by implication) capable of being seen. Origin: from G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: visible

G3708 ὁράω (horáō): by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear. Origin: properly, to stare at (compare G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); KJV: behold, perceive, see, take heed

G3709 ὀργή (orgḗ): properly, desire (as a reaching forth or excitement of the mind), i.e. (by analogy), violent passion (ire, or (justifiable) abhorrence); by implication punishment. Origin: from G3713 (ὀρέγομαι); KJV: anger, indignation, vengeance, wrath

G3710 ὀργίζω (orgízō): to provoke or enrage, i.e. (passively) become exasperated. Origin: from G3709 (ὀργή); KJV: be angry (wroth)

G3711 ὀργίλος (orgílos): irascible. Origin: from G3709 (ὀργή); KJV: soon angry

G3712 ὀργυιά (orguiá): a stretch of the arms, i.e. a fathom. Origin: from G3713 (ὀρέγομαι); KJV: fathom

G3713 ὀρέγομαι (orégomai): to stretch oneself, i.e. reach out after (long for). Origin: middle voice of apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary (compare G3735 (ὄρος)); KJV: covet after, desire

G3714 ὀρεινός (oreinós): mountainous, i.e. (feminine by implication, of G5561 (χώρα)) the Highlands (of Judæa). Origin: from G3735 (ὄρος); KJV: hill country

G3715 ὄρεξις (órexis): excitement of the mind, i.e. longing after. Origin: from G3713 (ὀρέγομαι); KJV: lust

G3716 ὀρθοποδέω (orthopodéō): to be straight-footed, i.e. (figuratively) to go directly forward. Origin: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and G4228 (πούς); KJV: walk uprightly

G3717 ὀρθός (orthós): right (as rising), i.e. (perpendicularly) erect (figuratively, honest), or (horizontally) level or direct. Origin: probably from the base of G3735 (ὄρος); KJV: straight, upright

G3718 ὀρθοτομέω (orthotoméō): Origin: from a compound of G3717 (ὀρθός) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος), to make a straight cut, i.e. (figuratively) to dissect (expound) correctly (the divine message) KJV: rightly divide

G3719 ὀρθρίζω (orthrízō): to use the dawn, i.e. (by implication) to repair betimes. Origin: from G3722 (ὄρθρος); KJV: come early in the morning

G3720 ὀρθρινός (orthrinós): relating to the dawn, i.e. matutinal (as an epithet of Venus, especially brilliant in the early day). Origin: from G3722 (ὄρθρος); KJV: morning

G3721 ὄρθριος (órthrios): in the dawn, i.e. up at day-break. Origin: from G3722 (ὄρθρος); KJV: early

G3722 ὄρθρος (órthros): dawn (as sun-rise, rising of light); by extension, morn. Origin: from the same as G3735 (ὄρος); KJV: early in the morning

G3723 ὀρθῶς (orthōs): in a straight manner, i.e. (figuratively) correctly (also morally). Origin: adverb from G3717 (ὀρθός); KJV: plain, right(-ly)

G3724 ὁρίζω (horízō): to mark out or bound ("horizon"), i.e. (figuratively) to appoint, decree, specify. Origin: from G3725 (ὅριον); KJV: declare, determine, limit, ordain

G3725 ὅριον (hórion): a boundary-line, i.e. (by implication) a frontier (region). Origin: neuter of a derivative of an apparently primary (a bound or limit); KJV: border, coast

G3726 ὁρκίζω (horkízō): to put on oath, i.e. make swear; by analogy, to solemnly enjoin. Origin: from G3727 (ὅρκος); KJV: adjure, charge

G3727 ὅρκος (hórkos): perhaps akin to G3725 (ὅριον)); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath). Origin: from (a fence; KJV: oath

G3728 ὁρκωμοσία (horkōmosía): asseveration on oath. Origin: from a compound of G3727 (ὅρκος) and a derivative of G3660 (ὀμνύω); KJV: oath

G3729 ὁρμάω (hormáō): to start, spur or urge on, i.e. (reflexively) to dash or plunge. Origin: from G3730 (ὁρμή); KJV: run (violently), rush

G3730 ὁρμή (hormḗ): a violent impulse, i.e. onset. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: assault

G3731 ὅρμημα (hórmēma): an attack, i.e. (abstractly) precipitancy. Origin: from G3730 (ὁρμή); KJV: violence

G3732 ὄρνεον (órneon): a birdling. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3733 (ὄρνις); KJV: bird, fowl

G3733 ὄρνις (órnis): a bird (as rising in the air), i.e. (specially), a hen (or female domestic fowl). Origin: probably from a prolonged form of the base of G3735 (ὄρος); KJV: hen

G3734 ὁροθεσία (horothesía): a limit-placing, i.e. (concretely) boundary-line. Origin: from a compound of the base of G3725 (ὅριον) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: bound

G3735 ὄρος (óros): perhaps akin to G142 (αἴρω); compare G3733 (ὄρνις)); a mountain (as lifting itself above the plain). Origin: probably from an obsolete (to rise or "rear"; KJV: hill, mount(-ain)

G3736 ὀρύσσω (orýssō): to "burrow" in the ground, i.e. dig. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: dig

G3737 ὀρφανός (orphanós): bereaved ("orphan"), i.e. parentless. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: comfortless, fatherless

G3738 ὀρχέομαι (orchéomai): to dance (from the ranklike or regular motion). Origin: middle voice from (a row or ring); KJV: dance

G3739 ὅς (hós): the relatively (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that. Origin: probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article G3588 (ὁ)); KJV: one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who(-m, -se), etc

G3740 ὁσάκις (hosákis): how (i.e. with G302 (ἄν), so) many times as. Origin: multiple adverb from G3739 (ὅς); KJV: as oft(-en) as

G3741 ὅσιος (hósios): and from G40 (ἅγιος), which relates to purity from defilement), i.e. hallowed (pious, sacred, sure). Origin: of uncertain affinity; properly, right (by intrinsic or divine character; thus distinguished from 1342, which refers rather to human statutes and relations; from G2413 (ἱερός), which denotes formal consecration; KJV: holy, mercy, shalt be

G3742 ὁσιότης (hosiótēs): piety. Origin: from G3741 (ὅσιος); KJV: holiness

G3743 ὁσίως (hosíōs): piously. Origin: adverb from G3741 (ὅσιος); KJV: holily

G3744 ὀσμή (osmḗ): fragrance (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G3605 (ὄζω); KJV: odour, savour

G3745 ὅσος (hósos): as (much, great, long, etc.) as. Origin: by reduplication from G3739 (ὅς); KJV: all (that), as (long, many, much) (as), how great (many, much), (in-)asmuch as, so many as, that (ever), the more, those things, what (great, -soever), wheresoever, wherewithsoever, which, X while, who(-soever)

G3746 ὅσπερ (hósper): who especially. Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G4007 (περ); KJV: whomsoever

G3747 ὀστέον (ostéon): a bone. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: bone

G3748 ὅστις (hóstis): which some, i.e. any that; also (definite) which same. Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G5100 (τὶς); KJV: X and (they), (such) as, (they) that, in that they, what(-soever), whereas ye, (they) which, who(-soever)

G3749 ὀστράκινος (ostrákinos): earthen-ware, i.e. clayey; by implication, frail. Origin: from ("oyster") (a tile, i.e. terra cotta); KJV: of earth, earthen

G3750 ὄσφρησις (ósphrēsis): smell (the sense). Origin: from a derivative of G3605 (ὄζω); KJV: smelling

G3751 ὀσφῦς (osphŷs): the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: loin

G3752 ὅταν (hótan): whenever (implying hypothesis or more or less uncertainty); also causatively (conjunctionally) inasmuch as. Origin: from G3753 (ὅτε) and G302 (ἄν); KJV: as long (soon) as, that, + till, when(-soever), while

G3753 ὅτε (hóte): at which (thing) too, i.e. when. Origin: from G3739 (ὅς) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: after (that), as soon as, that, when, while

G3754 ὅτι (hóti): demonstrative, that (sometimes redundant); causative, because. Origin: neuter of G3748 (ὅστις) as conjunction; KJV: as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why

G3755 ὅτου (hótou): during which same time, i.e. whilst. Origin: for the genitive case of G3748 (ὅστις) (as adverb); KJV: whiles

G3756 οὐ (ou): the absolute negative (compare G3361 (μή)) adverb; no or not. Origin: a primary word; KJV: + long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but

G3757 οὗ (hoû): at which place, i.e. where. Origin: genitive case of G3739 (ὅς) as adverb; KJV: where(-in), whither(-soever)

G3758 οὐά (ouá): "ah". Origin: a primary exclamation of surprise; KJV: ah

G3759 οὐαί (ouaí): "woe". Origin: a primary exclamation of grief; KJV: alas, woe

G3760 οὐδαμῶς (oudamōs): by no means. Origin: adverb from (the feminine) of G3762 (οὐδείς); KJV: not

G3761 οὐδέ (oudé): not however, i.e. neither, nor, not even. Origin: from G3756 (οὐ) and G1161 (δέ); KJV: neither (indeed), never, no (more, nor, not), nor (yet), (also, even, then) not (even, so much as), + nothing, so much as

G3762 οὐδείς (oudeís): not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing. Origin: from G3761 (οὐδέ) and G1520 (εἷς); KJV: any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought

G3763 οὐδέποτε (oudépote): not even at any time, i.e. never at all. Origin: from G3761 (οὐδέ) and G4218 (ποτέ); KJV: neither at any time, never, nothing at any time

G3764 οὐδέπω (oudépō): not even yet. Origin: from G3761 (οὐδέ) and G4452 (-πω); KJV: as yet not, never before (yet), (not) yet

G3765 οὐκέτι (oukéti): not yet, no longer. Origin: from G3756 (οὐ) and G2089 (ἔτι); KJV: after that (not), (not) any more, henceforth (hereafter) not, no longer (more), not as yet (now), now no more (not), yet (not)

G3766 οὐκοῦν (oukoûn): is it not therefore that, i.e. (affirmatively) hence or so. Origin: from G3756 (οὐ) and G3767 (οὖν); KJV: then

G3767 οὖν (oûn): (adverbially) certainly, or (conjunctionally) accordingly. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: and (so, truly), but, now (then), so (likewise then), then, therefore, verily, wherefore

G3768 οὔπω (oúpō): not yet. Origin: from G3756 (οὐ) and G4452 (-πω); KJV: hitherto not, (no…) as yet, not yet

G3769 οὐρά (ourá): a tail. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: tail

G3770 οὐράνιος (ouránios): celestial, i.e. belonging to or coming from the sky. Origin: from G3772 (οὐρανός); KJV: heavenly

G3771 οὐρανόθεν (ouranóthen): from the sky. Origin: from G3772 (οὐρανός) and the enclitic of source; KJV: from heaven

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G3772 to G3888
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G3772 οὐρανός (ouranós): the sky; by extension, heaven (as the abode of God); by implication, happiness, power, eternity; specially, the Gospel (Christianity). Origin: perhaps from the same as G3735 (ὄρος) (through the idea of elevation); KJV: air, heaven(-ly), sky

G3773 Οὐρβανός (Ourbanós): Urbanus (of the city, "urbane"), a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Urbanus

G3774 Οὐρίας (Ourías): Urias (i.e. Urijah), a Hittite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H223); KJV: Urias

G3775 οὖς (oûs): the ear (physically or mentally). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: ear

G3776 οὐσία (ousía): substance, i.e. property (possessions). Origin: from the feminine of G5607 (ὤν); KJV: goods, substance

G3777 οὔτε (oúte): not too, i.e. neither or nor; by analogy, not even. Origin: from G3756 (οὐ) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: neither, none, nor (yet), (no, yet) not, nothing

G3778 οὗτος (hoûtos): the he (she or it), i.e. this or that (often with article repeated). Origin: from the article G3588 (ὁ) and G846 (αὐτός); KJV: he (it was that), hereof, it, she, such as, the same, these, they, this (man, same, woman), which, who

G3779 οὕτω (hoútō): in this way (referring to what precedes or follows). Origin: adverb from G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: after that, after (in) this manner, as, even (so), for all that, like(-wise), no more, on this fashion(-wise), so (in like manner), thus, what

G3780 οὐχί (ouchí): not indeed. Origin: intensive of G3756 (οὐ); KJV: nay, not

G3781 ὀφειλέτης (opheilétēs): an ower, i.e. person indebted; figuratively, a delinquent; morally, a transgressor (against God). Origin: from G3784 (ὀφείλω); KJV: debtor, which owed, sinner

G3782 ὀφειλή (opheilḗ): indebtedness, i.e. (concretely) a sum owed; figuratively, obligation, i.e. (conjugal) duty. Origin: from G3784 (ὀφείλω); KJV: debt, due

G3783 ὀφείλημα (opheílēma): something owed, i.e. (figuratively) a due; morally, a fault. Origin: from (the alternate of) G3784 (ὀφείλω); KJV: debt

G3784 ὀφείλω (opheílō): to owe (pecuniarily); figuratively, to be under obligation (ought, must, should); morally, to fail in duty. Origin: probably from the base of G3786 (ὄφελος) (through the idea of accruing); KJV: behove, be bound, (be) debt(-or), (be) due(-ty), be guilty (indebted), (must) need(-s), ought, owe, should

G3785 ὄφελον (óphelon): I ought (wish), i.e. (interjection) oh that!. Origin: first person singular of a past tense of G3784 (ὀφείλω); KJV: would (to God)

G3786 ὄφελος (óphelos): gain. Origin: from (to heap up, i.e. accumulate or benefit); KJV: advantageth, profit

G3787 ὀφθαλμοδουλεία (ophthalmodouleía): sight-labor, i.e. that needs watching (remissness). Origin: from G3788 (ὀφθαλμός) and G1397 (δουλεία); KJV: eye-service

G3788 ὀφθαλμός (ophthalmós): the eye (literally or figuratively); by implication, vision; figuratively, envy (from the jealous side-glance). Origin: from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: eye, sight

G3789 ὄφις (óphis): a snake, figuratively, (as a type of sly cunning) an artful malicious person, especially Satan. Origin: probably from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) (through the idea of sharpness of vision); KJV: serpent

G3790 ὀφρῦς (ophrŷs): the eye-"brow" or forehead, i.e. (figuratively) the brink of a precipice. Origin: perhaps from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) (through the idea of the shading or proximity to the organ of vision); KJV: brow

G3791 ὀχλέω (ochléō): to mob, i.e. (by implication) to harass. Origin: from G3793 (ὄχλος); KJV: vex

G3792 ὀχλοποιέω (ochlopoiéō): to make a crowd, i.e. raise a public disturbance. Origin: from G3793 (ὄχλος) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: gather a company

G3793 ὄχλος (óchlos): a throng (as borne along); by implication, the rabble; by extension, a class of people; figuratively, a riot. Origin: from a derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning a vehicle); KJV: company, multitude, number (of people), people, press

G3794 ὀχύρωμα (ochýrōma): a castle (figuratively, argument). Origin: from a remote derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to fortify, through the idea of holding safely); KJV: stronghold

G3795 ὀψάριον (opsárion): a relish to other food (as if cooked sauce), i.e. (specially), fish (presumably salted and dried as a condiment). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G3702 (ὀπτός); KJV: fish

G3796 ὀψέ (opsé): (adverbially) late in the day; by extension, after the close of the day. Origin: from the same as G3694 (ὀπίσω) (through the idea of backwardness); KJV: (at) even, in the end

G3797 ὄψιμος (ópsimos): later, i.e. vernal (showering). Origin: from G3796 (ὀψέ); KJV: latter

G3798 ὄψιος (ópsios): late; feminine (as noun) afternoon (early eve) or nightfall (later eve). Origin: from G3796 (ὀψέ); KJV: even(-ing, (-tide))

G3799 ὄψις (ópsis): properly, sight (the act), i.e. (by implication) the visage, an external show. Origin: from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: appearance, countenance, face

G3800 ὀψώνιον (opsṓnion): rations for a soldier, i.e. (by extension) his stipend or pay. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of the same as G3795 (ὀψάριον); KJV: wages

G3801 ὁ ὢν καί ὁ ἦν καί ὁ ἐρχόμενος (ho ṑn kaí ho ēn kaí ho erchómenos): the one being and the one that was and the one coming, i.e. the Eternal, as a divine epithet of Christ. Origin: a phrase combining G3588 (ὁ) with the present participle and imperfect of G1510 (εἰμί) and the present participle of G2064 (ἔρχομαι) by means of G2532 (καί); KJV: which art (is, was), and (which) wast (is, was), and art (is) to come (shalt be)

G3802 παγιδεύω (pagideúō): to ensnare (figuratively). Origin: from G3803 (παγίς); KJV: entangle

G3803 παγίς (pagís): a trap (as fastened by a noose or notch); figuratively, a trick or statagem (temptation). Origin: from G4078 (πήγνυμι); KJV: snare

G3804 πάθημα (páthēma): something undergone, i.e. hardship or pain; subjectively, an emotion or influence. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G3806 (πάθος); KJV: affection, affliction, motion, suffering

G3805 παθητός (pathētós): liable (i.e. doomed) to experience pain. Origin: from the same as G3804 (πάθημα); KJV: suffer

G3806 πάθος (páthos): properly, suffering ("pathos"), i.e. (subjectively) a passion (especially concupiscence). Origin: from the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω); KJV: (inordinate) affection, lust

G3807 παιδαγωγός (paidagōgós): a boy-leader, i.e. a servant whose office it was to take the children to school; (by implication, (figuratively) a tutor ("pædagogue")). Origin: from G3816 (παῖς) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω); KJV: instructor, schoolmaster

G3808 παιδάριον (paidárion): a little boy. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G3816 (παῖς); KJV: child, lad

G3809 παιδεία (paideía): tutorage, i.e. education or training; by implication, disciplinary correction. Origin: from G3811 (παιδεύω); KJV: chastening, chastisement, instruction, nurture

G3810 παιδευτής (paideutḗs): a trainer, i.e. teacher or (by implication) discipliner. Origin: from G3811 (παιδεύω); KJV: which corrected, instructor

G3811 παιδεύω (paideúō): to train up a child, i.e. educate, or (by implication), discipline (by punishment). Origin: from G3816 (παῖς); KJV: chasten(-ise), instruct, learn, teach

G3812 παιδιόθεν (paidióthen): from infancy. Origin: adverb (of source) from G3813 (παιδίον); KJV: of a child

G3813 παιδίον (paidíon): a childling (of either sex), i.e. (properly), an infant, or (by extension) a half-grown boy or girl; figuratively, an immature Christian. Origin: neuter diminutive of G3816 (παῖς); KJV: (little, young) child, damsel

G3814 παιδίσκη (paidískē): a girl, i.e. (specially), a female slave or servant. Origin: feminine diminutive of G3816 (παῖς); KJV: bondmaid(-woman), damsel, maid(-en)

G3815 παίζω (paízō): to sport (as a boy). Origin: from G3816 (παῖς); KJV: play

G3816 παῖς (paîs): a boy (as often beaten with impunity), or (by analogy), a girl, and (genitive case) a child; specially, a slave or servant (especially a minister to a king; and by eminence to God). Origin: perhaps from G3817 (παίω); KJV: child, maid(-en), (man) servant, son, young man

G3817 παίω (paíō): to hit (as if by a single blow and less violently than G5180 (τύπτω)); specially, to sting (as a scorpion). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: smite, strike

G3818 Πακατιανή (Pakatianḗ): Pacatianian, a section of Phrygia. Origin: feminine of an adjective of uncertain derivation; KJV: Pacatiana

G3819 πάλαι (pálai): (adverbially) formerly, or (by relatively) sometime since; (elliptically as adjective) ancient. Origin: probably another form for G3825 (πάλιν) (through the idea of retrocession); KJV: any while, a great while ago, (of) old, in time past

G3820 παλαιός (palaiós): antique, i.e. not recent, worn out. Origin: from G3819 (πάλαι); KJV: old

G3821 παλαιότης (palaiótēs): antiquatedness. Origin: from G3820 (παλαιός); KJV: oldness

G3822 παλαιόω (palaióō): to make (passively, become) worn out, or declare obsolete. Origin: from G3820 (παλαιός); KJV: decay, make (wax) old

G3823 πάλη (pálē): another form for G906 (βάλλω)); wrestling. Origin: from (to vibrate; KJV: + wrestle

G3824 παλιγγενεσία (palingenesía): (spiritual) rebirth (the state or the act), i.e. (figuratively) spiritual renovation; specially, Messianic restoration. Origin: from G3825 (πάλιν) and G1078 (γένεσις); KJV: regeneration

G3825 πάλιν (pálin): (adverbially) anew, i.e. (of place) back, (of time) once more, or (conjunctionally) furthermore or on the other hand. Origin: probably from the same as G3823 (πάλη) (through the idea of oscillatory repetition); KJV: again

G3826 παμπληθεί (pamplētheí): in full multitude, i.e. concertedly or simultaneously. Origin: dative case (adverb) of a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G4128 (πλῆθος); KJV: all at once

G3827 πάμπολυς (pámpolys): full many, i.e. immense. Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and G4183 (πολύς); KJV: very great

G3828 Παμφυλία (Pamphylía): every-tribal, i.e. heterogeneous (G5561 (χώρα) being implied); Pamphylia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: from a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G4443 (πυρά); KJV: Pamphylia

G3829 πανδοχεῖον (pandocheîon): all-receptive, i.e. a public lodging-place (caravanserai or khan). Origin: neuter of a presumed compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: inn

G3830 πανδοχεύς (pandocheús): an innkeeper (warden of a caravanserai). Origin: from the same as G3829 (πανδοχεῖον); KJV: host

G3831 πανήγυρις (panḗgyris): a mass-meeting, i.e. (figuratively) universal companionship. Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά); KJV: general assembly

G3832 πανοικί (panoikí): with the whole family. Origin: adverb from G3956 (πᾶς) and G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: with all his house

G3833 πανοπλία (panoplía): full armor ("panoply"). Origin: from a compound of G3956 (πᾶς) and G3696 (ὅπλον); KJV: all (whole) armour

G3834 πανουργία (panourgía): adroitness, i.e. (in a bad sense) trickery or sophistry. Origin: from G3835 (πανοῦργος); KJV: (cunning) craftiness, subtilty

G3835 πανοῦργος (panoûrgos): all-working, i.e. adroit (shrewd). Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: crafty

G3836 πανταχόθεν (pantachóthen): from all directions. Origin: adverb (of source) from G3837 (πανταχοῦ); KJV: from every quarter

G3837 πανταχοῦ (pantachoû): universally. Origin: genitive case (as adverb of place) of a presumed derivative of G3956 (πᾶς); KJV: in all places, everywhere

G3838 παντελής (pantelḗs): full-ended, i.e. entire (neuter as noun, completion). Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and G5056 (τέλος); KJV: + in (no) wise, uttermost

G3839 πάντη (pántē): wholly. Origin: adverb (of manner) from G3956 (πᾶς); KJV: always

G3840 πάντοθεν (pántothen): from (i.e. on) all sides. Origin: adverb (of source) from G3956 (πᾶς); KJV: on every side, round about

G3841 παντοκράτωρ (pantokrátōr): the all-ruling, i.e. God (as absolute and universal sovereign). Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and G2904 (κράτος); KJV: Almighty, Omnipotent

G3842 πάντοτε (pántote): every when, i.e. at all times. Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and G3753 (ὅτε); KJV: alway(-s), ever(-more)

G3843 πάντως (pántōs): entirely; specially, at all events, (with negative, following) in no event. Origin: adverb from G3956 (πᾶς); KJV: by all means, altogether, at all, needs, no doubt, in (no) wise, surely

G3844 παρά (pará): properly, near; i.e. (with genitive case) from beside (literally or figuratively), (with dative case) at (or in) the vicinity of (objectively or subjectively), (with accusative case) to the proximity with (local (especially beyond or opposed to) or causal (on account of). Origin: a primary preposition; KJV: above, against, among, at, before, by, contrary to, X friend, from, + give (such things as they), + that (she) had, X his, in, more than, nigh unto, (out) of, past, save, side…by, in the sight of, than, (there-)fore, with

G3845 παραβαίνω (parabaínō): to go contrary to, i.e. violate a command. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: (by) transgress(-ion)

G3846 παραβάλλω (parabállō): to throw alongside, i.e. (reflexively) to reach a place, or (figuratively) to liken. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: arrive, compare

G3847 παράβασις (parábasis): violation. Origin: from G3845 (παραβαίνω); KJV: breaking, transgression

G3848 παραβάτης (parabátēs): a violator. Origin: from G3845 (παραβαίνω); KJV: breaker, transgress(-or)

G3849 παραβιάζομαι (parabiázomai): to force contrary to (nature), i.e. compel (by entreaty). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G971 (βιάζω); KJV: constrain

G3850 παραβολή (parabolḗ): a similitude ("parable"), i.e. (symbolic) fictitious narrative (of common life conveying a moral), apothegm or adage. Origin: from G3846 (παραβάλλω); KJV: comparison, figure, parable, proverb

G3851 παραβουλεύομαι (parabouleúomai): to misconsult, i.e. disregard. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G1011 (βουλεύω); KJV: not (to) regard(-ing)

G3852 παραγγελία (parangelía): a mandate. Origin: from G3853 (παραγγέλλω); KJV: charge, command

G3853 παραγγέλλω (parangéllō): to transmit a message, i.e. (by implication) to enjoin. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G32 (ἄγγελος); KJV: (give in) charge, (give) command(-ment), declare

G3854 παραγίνομαι (paragínomai): to become near, i.e. approach (have arrived); by implication, to appear publicly. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: come, go, be present

G3855 παράγω (parágō): to lead near, i.e. (reflexively or intransitively) to go along or away. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: depart, pass (away, by, forth)

G3856 παραδειγματίζω (paradeigmatízō): to show alongside (the public), i.e. expose to infamy. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1165 (δειγματίζω); KJV: make a public example, put to an open shame

G3857 παράδεισος (parádeisos): a park, i.e. (specially), an Eden (place of future happiness, "paradise"). Origin: of Oriental origin (compare H6508); KJV: paradise

G3858 παραδέχομαι (paradéchomai): to accept near, i.e. admit or (by implication) delight in. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: receive

G3859 παραδιατριβή (paradiatribḗ): misemployment, i.e. meddlesomeness. Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G1304 (διατρίβω); KJV: perverse disputing

G3860 παραδίδωμι (paradídōmi): to surrender, i.e yield up, intrust, transmit. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: betray, bring forth, cast, commit, deliver (up), give (over, up), hazard, put in prison, recommend

G3861 παράδοξος (parádoxos): contrary to expectation, i.e. extraordinary ("paradox"). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1391 (δόξα) (in the sense of seeming); KJV: strange

G3862 παράδοσις (parádosis): transmission, i.e. (concretely) a precept; specially, the Jewish traditionary law. Origin: from G3860 (παραδίδωμι); KJV: ordinance, tradition

G3863 παραζηλόω (parazēlóō): to stimulate alongside, i.e. excite to rivalry. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2206 (ζηλόω); KJV: provoke to emulation (jealousy)

G3864 παραθαλάσσιος (parathalássios): along the sea, i.e. maritime (lacustrine). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2281 (θάλασσα); KJV: upon the sea coast

G3865 παραθεωρέω (paratheōréō): to overlook or disregard. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2334 (θεωρέω); KJV: neglect

G3866 παραθήκη (parathḗkē): a deposit, i.e. (figuratively) trust. Origin: from G3908 (παρατίθημι); KJV: committed unto

G3867 παραινέω (parainéō): to mispraise, i.e. recommend or advise (a different course). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G134 (αἰνέω); KJV: admonish, exhort

G3868 παραιτέομαι (paraitéomai): to beg off, i.e. deprecate, decline, shun. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: avoid, (make) excuse, intreat, refuse, reject

G3869 παρακαθίζω (parakathízō): to sit down near. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2523 (καθίζω); KJV: sit

G3870 παρακαλέω (parakaléō): to call near, i.e. invite, invoke (by imploration, hortation or consolation). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: beseech, call for, (be of good) comfort, desire, (give) exhort(-ation), intreat, pray

G3871 παρακαλύπτω (parakalýptō): to cover alongside, i.e. veil (figuratively). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: hide

G3872 παρακαταθήκη (parakatathḗkē): something put down alongside, i.e. a deposit (sacred trust). Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G2698 (κατατίθημι); KJV: that (thing) which is committed (un-)to (trust)

G3873 παράκειμαι (parákeimai): to lie near, i.e. be at hand (figuratively, be prompt or easy). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: be present

G3874 παράκλησις (paráklēsis): imploration, hortation, solace. Origin: from G3870 (παρακαλέω); KJV: comfort, consolation, exhortation, intreaty

G3875 παράκλητος (paráklētos): an intercessor, consoler. KJV: advocate, comforter

G3876 παρακοή (parakoḗ): inattention, i.e. (by implication) disobedience. Origin: from G3878 (παρακούω); KJV: disobedience

G3877 παρακολουθέω (parakolouthéō): to follow near, i.e. (figuratively) attend (as a result), trace out, conform to. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G190 (ἀκολουθέω); KJV: attain, follow, fully know, have understanding

G3878 παρακούω (parakoúō): to mishear, i.e. (by implication) to disobey. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: neglect to hear

G3879 παρακύπτω (parakýptō): to bend beside, i.e. lean over (so as to peer within). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2955 (κύπτω); KJV: look (into), stoop down

G3880 παραλαμβάνω (paralambánō): to receive near, i.e. associate with oneself (in any familiar or intimate act or relation); by analogy, to assume an office; figuratively, to learn. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: receive, take (unto, with)

G3881 παραλέγομαι (paralégomai): (specially), to lay one's course near, i.e. sail past. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense); KJV: pass, sail by

G3882 παράλιος (parálios): beside the salt (sea), i.e. maritime. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G251 (ἅλς); KJV: sea coast

G3883 παραλλαγή (parallagḗ): transmutation (of phase or orbit), i.e. (figuratively) fickleness. Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G236 (ἀλλάσσω); KJV: variableness

G3884 παραλογίζομαι (paralogízomai): to misreckon, i.e. delude. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3049 (λογίζομαι); KJV: beguile, deceive

G3885 παραλυτικός (paralytikós): as if dissolved, i.e. "paralytic". Origin: from a derivative of G3886 (παραλύω); KJV: that had (sick of) the palsy

G3886 παραλύω (paralýō): to loosen beside, i.e. relax (perfect passive participle, paralyzed or enfeebled). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3089 (λύω); KJV: feeble, sick of the (taken with) palsy

G3887 παραμένω (paraménō): to stay near, i.e. remain (literally, tarry; or figuratively, be permanent, persevere). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: abide, continue

G3888 παραμυθέομαι (paramythéomai): to relate near, i.e. (by implication) encourage, console. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the middle voice of a derivative of G3454 (μῦθος); KJV: comfort

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G3889 to G4017
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G3889 παραμυθία (paramythía): consolation (properly, abstract). Origin: from G3888 (παραμυθέομαι); KJV: comfort

G3890 παραμύθιον (paramýthion): consolation (properly, concretely). Origin: neuter of G3889 (παραμυθία); KJV: comfort

G3891 παρανομέω (paranoméō): to be opposed to law, i.e. to transgress. Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G3551 (νόμος); KJV: contrary to law

G3892 παρανομία (paranomía): transgression. Origin: from the same as G3891 (παρανομέω); KJV: iniquity

G3893 παραπικραίνω (parapikraínō): to embitter alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G4087 (πικραίνω); KJV: provoke

G3894 παραπικρασμός (parapikrasmós): irritation. Origin: from G3893 (παραπικραίνω); KJV: provocation

G3895 παραπίπτω (parapíptō): to fall aside, i.e. (figuratively) to apostatize. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall away

G3896 παραπλέω (parapléō): to sail near. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G4126 (πλέω); KJV: sail by

G3897 παραπλήσιον (paraplḗsion): close by, i.e. (figuratively) almost. Origin: neuter of a compound of G3844 (παρά) and the base of G4139 (πλησίον) (as adverb); KJV: nigh unto

G3898 παραπλησίως (paraplēsíōs): in a manner near by, i.e. (figuratively) similarly. Origin: adverb from the same as G3897 (παραπλήσιον); KJV: likewise

G3899 παραπορεύομαι (paraporeúomai): to travel near. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: go, pass (by)

G3900 παράπτωμα (paráptōma): a side-slip (lapse or deviation), i.e. (unintentional) error or (wilful) transgression. Origin: from G3895 (παραπίπτω); KJV: fall, fault, offence, sin, trespass

G3901 παραῤῥυέω (pararrhyéō): to flow by, i.e. (figuratively) carelessly pass (miss). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the alternate of G4482 (ῥέω); KJV: let slip

G3902 παράσημος (parásēmos): side-marked, i.e. labelled (with a badge (figure-head) of a ship). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω); KJV: sign

G3903 παρασκευάζω (paraskeuázō): to furnish aside, i.e. get ready. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G4632 (σκεῦος); KJV: prepare self, be (make) ready

G3904 παρασκευή (paraskeuḗ): readiness. Origin: as if from G3903 (παρασκευάζω); KJV: preparation

G3905 παρατείνω (parateínō): to extend along, i.e. prolong (in point of time). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and teino (to stretch); KJV: continue

G3906 παρατηρέω (paratēréō): to inspect alongside, i.e. note insidiously or scrupulously. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5083 (τηρέω); KJV: observe, watch

G3907 παρατήρησις (paratḗrēsis): inspection, i.e. ocular evidence. Origin: from G3906 (παρατηρέω); KJV: obervation

G3908 παρατίθημι (paratíthēmi): to place alongside, i.e. present (food, truth); by implication, to deposit (as a trust or for protection). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: allege, commend, commit (the keeping of), put forth, set before

G3909 παρατυγχάνω (paratynchánō): to chance near, i.e. fall in with. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5177 (τυγχάνω); KJV: meet with

G3910 παραυτίκα (parautíka): at the very instant, i.e. momentary. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G846 (αὐτός); KJV: but for a moment

G3911 παραφέρω (paraphérō): to bear along or aside, i.e. carry off (literally or figuratively); by implication, to avert. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate forms); KJV: remove, take away

G3912 παραφρονέω (paraphronéō): to misthink, i.e. be insane (silly). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5426 (φρονέω); KJV: as a fool

G3913 παραφρονία (paraphronía): insanity, i.e. foolhardiness. Origin: from G3912 (παραφρονέω); KJV: madness

G3914 παραχειμάζω (paracheimázō): to winter near, i.e. stay with over the rainy season. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5492 (χειμάζω); KJV: winter

G3915 παραχειμασία (paracheimasía): a wintering over. Origin: from G3914 (παραχειμάζω); KJV: winter in

G3916 παραχρῆμα (parachrēma): at the thing itself, i.e. instantly. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G5536 (χρῆμα) (in its original sense); KJV: forthwith, immediately, presently, straightway, soon

G3917 πάρδαλις (párdalis): a leopard. Origin: feminine of (a panther); KJV: leopard

G3918 πάρειμι (páreimi): to be near, i.e. at hand; neuter present participle (singular) time being, or (plural) property. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1510 (εἰμί) (including its various forms); KJV: come, X have, be here, + lack, (be here) present

G3919 παρεισάγω (pareiságō): to lead in aside, i.e. introduce surreptitiously. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1521 (εἰσάγω); KJV: privily bring in

G3920 παρείσακτος (pareísaktos): smuggled in. Origin: from G3919 (παρεισάγω); KJV: unawares brought in

G3921 παρεισδύνω (pareisdýnō): to settle in alongside, i.e. lodge stealthily. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and a compound of G1519 (εἰς) and G1416 (δύνω); KJV: creep in unawares

G3922 παρεισέρχομαι (pareisérchomai): to come in alongside, i.e. supervene additionally or steathily. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1525 (εἰσέρχομαι); KJV: come in privily, enter

G3923 παρεισφέρω (pareisphérō): to bear in alongside, i.e. introduce simultaneously. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1533 (εἰσφέρω); KJV: give

G3924 παρεκτός (parektós): near outside, i.e. besides. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1622 (ἐκτός); KJV: except, saving, without

G3925 παρεμβολή (parembolḗ): a throwing in beside (juxtaposition), i.e. (specially), battle-array, encampment or barracks (tower Antonia). Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G1685 (ἐμβάλλω); KJV: army, camp, castle

G3926 παρενοχλέω (parenochléō): to harass further, i.e. annoy. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G1776 (ἐνοχλέω); KJV: trouble

G3927 παρεπίδημος (parepídēmos): an alien alongside, i.e. a resident foreigner. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G1927 (ἐπιδημέω); KJV: pilgrim, stranger

G3928 παρέρχομαι (parérchomai): to come near or aside, i.e. to approach (arrive), go by (or away), (figuratively) perish or neglect, (causative) avert. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: come (forth), go, pass (away, by, over), past, transgress

G3929 πάρεσις (páresis): praetermission, i.e. toleration. Origin: from G2935 (κτήτωρ); KJV: remission

G3930 παρέχω (paréchō): to hold near, i.e. present, afford, exhibit, furnish occasion. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: bring, do, give, keep, minister, offer, shew, + trouble

G3931 παρηγορία (parēgoría): an address alongside, i.e. (specially), consolation. Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά) (meaning to harangue an assembly); KJV: comfort

G3932 παρθενία (parthenía): maidenhood. Origin: from G3933 (παρθένος); KJV: virginity

G3933 παρθένος (parthénos): a maiden; by implication, an unmarried daughter. Origin: of unknown origin; KJV: virgin

G3934 Πάρθος (Párthos): a Parthian, i.e. inhabitant of Parthia. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Parthian

G3935 παρίημι (paríēmi): to let by, i.e. relax. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and hiemi (to send); KJV: hang down

G3936 παρίστημι (parístēmi): to stand beside, i.e. (transitively) to exhibit, proffer, (specially), recommend, (figuratively) substantiate; or (intransitively) to be at hand (or ready), aid. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: assist, bring before, command, commend, give presently, present, prove, provide, shew, stand (before, by, here, up, with), yield

G3937 Παρμενᾶς (Parmenâs): constant; Parmenas, a Christian. Origin: probably by contraction for (a derivative of a compound of G3844 (παρά) and G3306 (μένω)); KJV: Parmenas

G3938 πάροδος (párodos): a by-road, i.e. (actively) a route. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3598 (ὁδός); KJV: way

G3939 παροικέω (paroikéō): to dwell near, i.e. reside as a foreigner. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: sojourn in, be a stranger

G3940 παροικία (paroikía): foreign residence. Origin: from G3941 (πάροικος); KJV: sojourning, X as strangers

G3941 πάροικος (pároikos): having a home near, i.e. (as noun) a by-dweller (alien resident). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: foreigner, sojourn, stranger

G3942 παροιμία (paroimía): apparently a state alongside of supposition, i.e. (concretely) an adage; specially, an enigmatical or fictitious illustration. Origin: from a compound of G3844 (παρά) and perhaps a derivative of G3633 (οἴομαι); KJV: parable, proverb

G3943 πάροινος (pároinos): staying near wine, i.e. tippling (a toper). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3631 (οἶνος); KJV: given to wine

G3944 παροίχομαι (paroíchomai): to escape along, i.e. be gone. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and (to depart); KJV: past

G3945 παρομοιάζω (paromoiázō): to resemble. Origin: from G3946 (παρόμοιος); KJV: be like unto

G3946 παρόμοιος (parómoios): alike nearly, i.e. similar. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3664 (ὅμοιος); KJV: like

G3947 παροξύνω (paroxýnō): to sharpen alongside, i.e. (figuratively) to exasperate. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and a derivative of G3691 (ὀξύς); KJV: easily provoke, stir

G3948 παροξυσμός (paroxysmós): incitement (to good), or dispute (in anger). Origin: from G3947 (παροξύνω) ("paroxysm"); KJV: contention, provoke unto

G3949 παροργίζω (parorgízō): to anger alongside, i.e. enrage. Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and G3710 (ὀργίζω); KJV: anger, provoke to wrath

G3950 παροργισμός (parorgismós): rage. Origin: from G3949 (παροργίζω); KJV: wrath

G3951 παροτρύνω (parotrýnō): to urge along, i.e. stimulate (to hostility). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and (to spur); KJV: stir up

G3952 παρουσία (parousía): a being near, i.e. advent (often, return; specially, of Christ to punish Jerusalem, or finally the wicked); (by implication) physically, aspect. Origin: from the present participle of G3918 (πάρειμι); KJV: coming, presence

G3953 παροψίς (paropsís): a side-dish (the receptacle). Origin: from G3844 (παρά) and the base of G3795 (ὀψάριον); KJV: platter

G3954 παῤῥησία (parrhēsía): all out-spokenness, i.e. frankness, bluntness, publicity; by implication, assurance. Origin: from G3956 (πᾶς) and a derivative of G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: bold (X -ly, -ness, -ness of speech), confidence, X freely, X openly, X plainly(-ness)

G3955 παῤῥησιάζομαι (parrhēsiázomai): to be frank in utterance, or confident in spirit and demeanor. Origin: middle voice from G3954 (παῤῥησία); KJV: be (wax) bold, (preach, speak) boldly

G3956 πᾶς (pâs): all, any, every, the whole. Origin: including all the forms of declension; apparently a primary word; KJV: all (manner of, means), alway(-s), any (one), X daily, + ever, every (one, way), as many as, + no(-thing), X thoroughly, whatsoever, whole, whosoever

G3957 πάσχα (páscha): the Passover (the meal, the day, the festival or the special sacrifices connected with it). Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H6453); KJV: Easter, Passover

G3958 πάσχω (páschō): to experience a sensation or impression (usually painful). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: feel, passion, suffer, vex

G3959 Πάταρα (Pátara): Patara, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Patara

G3960 πατάσσω (patássō): to knock (gently or with a weapon or fatally). Origin: probably prolongation from G3817 (παίω); KJV: smite, strike

G3961 πατέω (patéō): to trample (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a derivative probably of G3817 (παίω) (meaning a "path"); KJV: tread (down, under foot)

G3962 πατήρ (patḗr): a "father" (literally or figuratively, near or more remote). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: father, parent

G3963 Πάτμος (Pátmos): Patmus, an islet in the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Patmos

G3964 πατραλῴας (patralṓias): a parricide. Origin: from G3962 (πατήρ) and the same as the latter part of G3389 (μητραλῴας); KJV: murderer of fathers

G3965 πατριά (patriá): paternal descent, i.e. (concretely) a group of families or a whole race (nation). Origin: as if feminine of a derivative of G3962 (πατήρ); KJV: family, kindred, lineage

G3966 πατριάρχης (patriárchēs): a progenitor ("patriarch"). Origin: from G3965 (πατριά) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: patriarch

G3967 πατρικός (patrikós): paternal, i.e. ancestral. Origin: from G3962 (πατήρ); KJV: of fathers

G3968 πατρίς (patrís): a father-land, i.e. native town; (figuratively) heavenly home. Origin: from G3902 (παράσημος); KJV: (own) country

G3969 Πατροβᾶς (Patrobâs): father's life; Patrobas, a Christian. Origin: perhaps a contraction for (a compound of G3962 (πατήρ) and G979 (βίος)); KJV: Patrobas

G3970 πατροπαράδοτος (patroparádotos): traditionary. Origin: from G3962 (πατήρ) and a derivative of G3860 (παραδίδωμι) (in the sense of handing over or down); KJV: received by tradition from fathers

G3971 πατρῷος (patrōios): paternal, i.e. hereditary. Origin: from G3962 (πατήρ); KJV: of fathers

G3972 Παῦλος (Paûlos): (little; but remotely from a derivative of G3973 (παύω), meaning the same); Paulus, the name of a Roman and of an apostle. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Paul, Paulus

G3973 παύω (paúō): to stop (transitively or intransitively), i.e. restrain, quit, desist, come to an end. Origin: a primary verb ("pause"); KJV: cease, leave, refrain

G3974 Πάφος (Páphos): Paphus, a place in Cyprus. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Paphos

G3975 παχύνω (pachýnō): to thicken, i.e. (by implication) to fatten (figuratively, stupefy or render callous). Origin: from a derivative of G4078 (πήγνυμι) (meaning thick); KJV: wax gross

G3976 πέδη (pédē): a shackle for the feet. Origin: ultimately from G4228 (πούς); KJV: fetter

G3977 πεδινός (pedinós): level (as easy for the feet). Origin: from a derivative of G4228 (πούς) (meaning the ground); KJV: plain

G3978 πεζεύω (pezeúō): to foot a journey, i.e. travel by land. Origin: from the same as G3979 (πεζῇ); KJV: go afoot

G3979 πεζῇ (pezēi): foot-wise, i.e. by walking. Origin: dative case feminine of a derivative of G4228 (πούς) (as adverb); KJV: a- (on) foot

G3980 πειθαρχέω (peitharchéō): to be persuaded by a ruler, i.e. (genitive case) to submit to authority; by analogy, to conform to advice. Origin: from a compound of G3982 (πείθω) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: hearken, obey (magistrates)

G3981 πειθός (peithós): persuasive. Origin: from G3982 (πείθω); KJV: enticing
