G3982 πείθω (peíthō): to convince (by argument, true or false); by analogy, to pacify or conciliate (by other fair means); reflexively or passively, to assent (to evidence or authority), to rely (by inward certainty). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: agree, assure, believe, have confidence, be (wax) conflent, make friend, obey, persuade, trust, yield

G3983 πεινάω (peináō): "pine"); to famish (absolutely or comparatively); figuratively, to crave. Origin: from the same as G3993 (πένης) (through the idea of pinching toil; KJV: be an hungered

G3984 πεῖρα (peîra): a test, i.e. attempt, experience. Origin: from the base of G4008 (πέραν) (through the idea of piercing); KJV: assaying, trial

G3985 πειράζω (peirázō): to test (objectively), i.e. endeavor, scrutinize, entice, discipline. Origin: from G3984 (πεῖρα); KJV: assay, examine, go about, prove, tempt(-er), try

G3986 πειρασμός (peirasmós): a putting to proof (by experiment (of good), experience (of evil), solicitation, discipline or provocation); by implication, adversity. Origin: from G3985 (πειράζω); KJV: temptation, X try

G3987 πειράω (peiráō): to test (subjectively), i.e. (reflexively) to attempt. Origin: from G3984 (πεῖρα); KJV: assay

G3988 πεισμονή (peismonḗ): persuadableness, i.e. credulity. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G3982 (πείθω); KJV: persuasion

G3989 πέλαγος (pélagos): deep or open sea, i.e. the main. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: depth, sea

G3990 πελεκίζω (pelekízō): to chop off (the head), i.e. truncate. Origin: from a derivative of G4141 (πλήσσω) (meaning an axe); KJV: behead

G3991 πέμπτος (pémptos): fifth. Origin: from G4002 (πέντε); KJV: fifth

G3992 πέμπω (pémpō): to dispatch (from the subjective view or point of departure, whereas (as a stronger form of ) refers rather to the objective point or terminus ad quem, and G4724 (στέλλω) denotes properly, the orderly motion involved), especially on a temporary errand; also to transmit, bestow, or wield. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: send, thrust in

G3993 πένης (pénēs): starving, i.e. indigent. Origin: from a primary (to toil for daily subsistence); KJV: poor

G3994 πενθερά (pentherá): a wife's mother. Origin: feminine of G3995 (πενθερός); KJV: mother in law, wife's mother

G3995 πενθερός (pentherós): a wife's father. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: father in law

G3996 πενθέω (penthéō): to grieve (the feeling or the act). Origin: from G3997 (πένθος); KJV: mourn, (be-)wail

G3997 πένθος (pénthos): grief. Origin: strengthened from the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω); KJV: mourning, sorrow

G3998 πενιχρός (penichrós): necessitous. Origin: prolongation from the base of G3993 (πένης); KJV: poor

G3999 πεντάκις (pentákis): five times. Origin: multiplicative adverb from G4002 (πέντε); KJV: five times

G4000 πεντακισχίλιοι (pentakischílioi): five times a thousand. Origin: from G3999 (πεντάκις) and G5507 (χίλιοι); KJV: five thousand

G4001 πεντακόσιοι (pentakósioi): five hundred. Origin: from G4002 (πέντε) and G1540 (ἑκατόν); KJV: five hundred

G4002 πέντε (pénte): "five". Origin: a primary number; KJV: five

G4003 πεντεκαιδέκατος (pentekaidékatos): five and tenth. Origin: from G4002 (πέντε) and G2532 (καί) and G1182 (δέκατος); KJV: fifteenth

G4004 πεντήκοντα (pentḗkonta): fifty. Origin: multiplicative of G4002 (πέντε); KJV: fifty

G4005 πεντηκοστή (pentēkostḗ): fiftieth (G2250 (ἡμέρα) being implied) from Passover, i.e. the festival of "Pentecost". Origin: feminine of the ordinal of G4004 (πεντήκοντα); KJV: Pentecost

G4006 πεποίθησις (pepoíthēsis): reliance. Origin: from the perfect of the alternate of G3958 (πάσχω); KJV: confidence, trust

G4007 περ (per): an enclitic particle significant of abundance (thoroughness), i.e. emphasis; much, very or ever. Origin: from the base of G4008 (πέραν); KJV: (whom-)soever

G4008 πέραν (péran): through (as adverb or preposition), i.e. across. Origin: apparently accusative case of an obsolete derivative of (to "pierce"); KJV: beyond, farther (other) side, over

G4009 πέρας (péras): an extremity. Origin: from the same as G4008 (πέραν); KJV: end, ut-(ter-)most participle

G4010 Πέργαμος (Pérgamos): fortified; Pergamus, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: from G4444 (πύργος); KJV: Pergamos

G4011 Πέργη (Pérgē): a tower; Perga, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: probably from the same as G4010 (Πέργαμος); KJV: Perga

G4012 περί (perí): properly, through (all over), i.e. around; figuratively with respect to; used in various applications, of place, cause or time (with the genitive case denoting the subject or occasion or superlative point; with the accusative case the locality, circuit, matter, circumstance or general period). Origin: from the base of G4008 (πέραν); KJV: (there-)about, above, against, at, on behalf of, X and his company, which concern, (as) concerning, for, X how it will go with, ((there-, where-)) of, on, over, pertaining (to), for sake, X (e-)state, (as) touching, (where-)by (in), with

G4013 περιάγω (periágō): to take around (as a companion); reflexively, to walk around. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: compass, go (round) about, lead about

G4014 περιαιρέω (periairéō): to remove all around, i.e. unveil, cast off (anchor); figuratively, to expiate. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G138 (αἱρέομαι) (including its alternate); KJV: take away (up)

G4015 περιαστράπτω (periastráptō): to flash all around, i.e. envelop in light. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G797 (ἀστράπτω); KJV: shine round (about)

G4016 περιβάλλω (peribállō): to throw all around, i.e. invest (with a palisade or with clothing). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: array, cast about, clothe(-d me), put on

G4017 περιβλέπω (periblépō): to look all around. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: look (round) about (on)

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4018 to G4142
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4018 περιβόλαιον (peribólaion): something thrown around one, i.e. a mantle, veil. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4016 (περιβάλλω); KJV: covering, vesture

G4019 περιδέω (peridéō): to bind around one, i.e. enwrap. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G1210 (δέω); KJV: bind about

G4020 περιεργάζομαι (periergázomai): to work all around, i.e. bustle about (meddle). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2038 (ἐργάζομαι); KJV: be a busybody

G4021 περίεργος (períergos): working all around, i.e. officious (meddlesome, neuter plural magic). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: busybody, curious arts

G4022 περιέρχομαι (periérchomai): to come all around, i.e. stroll, vacillate, veer. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate); KJV: fetch a compass, vagabond, wandering about

G4023 περιέχω (periéchō): to hold all around, i.e. include, clasp (figuratively). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: + astonished, contain, after (this manner)

G4024 περιζώννυμι (perizṓnnymi): to gird all around, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to fasten on one's belt (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2224 (ζώννυμι); KJV: gird (about, self)

G4025 περίθεσις (períthesis): a putting all around, i.e. decorating oneself with. Origin: from G4060 (περιτίθημι); KJV: wearing

G4026 περιΐστημι (periḯstēmi): to stand all around, i.e. (near) to be a bystander, or (aloof) to keep away from. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: avoid, shun, stand by (round about)

G4027 περικάθαρμα (perikátharma): something cleaned off all around, i.e. refuse (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2508 (καθαίρω); KJV: filth

G4028 περικαλύπτω (perikalýptō): to cover all around, i.e. entirely (the face, a surface). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: blindfold, cover, overlay

G4029 περίκειμαι (períkeimai): to lie all around, i.e. inclose, encircle, hamper (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: be bound (compassed) with, hang about

G4030 περικεφαλαία (perikephalaía): encirclement of the head, i.e. a helmet. Origin: feminine of a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2776 (κεφαλή); KJV: helmet

G4031 περικρατής (perikratḗs): strong all around, i.e. a master (manager). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2904 (κράτος); KJV: + come by

G4032 περικρύπτω (perikrýptō): to conceal all around, i.e. entirely. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2928 (κρύπτω); KJV: hide

G4033 περικυκλόω (perikyklóō): to encircle all around, i.e. blockade completely. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2944 (κυκλόω); KJV: compass round

G4034 περιλάμπω (perilámpō): to illuminate all around, i.e. invest with a halo. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G2989 (λάμπω); KJV: shine round about

G4035 περιλείπω (perileípō): to leave all around, i.e. (passively) survive. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: remain

G4036 περίλυπος (perílypos): grieved all around, i.e. intensely sad. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G3077 (λύπη); KJV: exceeding (very) sorry(-owful)

G4037 περιμένω (periménō): to stay around, i.e. await. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: wait for

G4038 πέριξ (périx): all around, i.e. (as an adjective) circumjacent. Origin: adverb from G4012 (περί); KJV: round about

G4039 περιοικέω (perioikéō): to reside around, i.e. be a neighbor. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: dwell round about

G4040 περίοικος (períoikos): housed around, i.e. neighboring (used elliptically as a noun). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G3624 (οἶκος); KJV: neighbour

G4041 περιούσιος (perioúsios): being beyond usual, i.e. special (one's own). Origin: from the present participle feminine of a compound of 4012 and G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: peculiar

G4042 περιοχή (periochḗ): a being held around, i.e. (concretely) a passage (of Scripture, as circumscribed). Origin: from G4023 (περιέχω); KJV: place

G4043 περιπατέω (peripatéō): to tread all around, i.e. walk at large (especially as proof of ability); figuratively, to live, deport oneself, follow (as a companion or votary). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G3961 (πατέω); KJV: go, be occupied with, walk (about)

G4044 περιπείρω (peripeírō): to penetrate entirely, i.e. transfix (figuratively). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and the base of G4008 (πέραν); KJV: pierce through

G4045 περιπίπτω (peripíptō): to fall into something that is all around, i.e. light among or upon, be surrounded with. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall among (into)

G4046 περιποιέομαι (peripoiéomai): to make around oneself, i.e. acquire (buy). Origin: middle voice from G4012 (περί) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: purchase

G4047 περιποίησις (peripoíēsis): acquisition (the act or the thing); by extension, preservation. Origin: from G4046 (περιποιέομαι); KJV: obtain(-ing), peculiar, purchased, possession, saving

G4048 περιῤῥήγνυμι (perirrhḗgnymi): to tear all around, i.e. completely away. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: rend off

G4049 περισπάω (perispáō): to drag all around, i.e. (figuratively) to distract (with care). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G4685 (σπάω); KJV: cumber

G4050 περισσεία (perisseía): surplusage, i.e. superabundance. Origin: from G4052 (περισσεύω); KJV: abundance(-ant, (-ly)), superfluity

G4051 περίσσευμα (perísseuma): a surplus, or superabundance. Origin: from G4052 (περισσεύω); KJV: abundance, that was left, over and above

G4052 περισσεύω (perisseúō): to superabound (in quantity or quality), be in excess, be superfluous; also (transitively) to cause to superabound or excel. Origin: from G4053 (περισσός); KJV: (make, more) abound, (have, have more) abundance (be more) abundant, be the better, enough and to spare, exceed, excel, increase, be left, redound, remain (over and above)

G4053 περισσός (perissós): superabundant (in quantity) or superior (in quality); by implication, excessive; adverbially (with G1537 (ἐκ)) violently; neuter (as noun) preeminence. Origin: from G4012 (περί) (in the sense of beyond); KJV: exceeding abundantly above, more abundantly, advantage, exceedingly, very highly, beyond measure, more, superfluous, vehement(-ly)

G4054 περισσότερον (perissóteron): in a more superabundant way. Origin: neuter of G4055 (περισσότερος) (as adverb); KJV: more abundantly, a great deal, far more

G4055 περισσότερος (perissóteros): more superabundant (in number, degree or character). Origin: comparative of G4053 (περισσός); KJV: more abundant, greater (much) more, overmuch

G4056 περισσοτέρως (perissotérōs): more superabundantly. Origin: adverb from G4055 (περισσότερος); KJV: more abundant(-ly), X the more earnest, (more) exceedingly, more frequent, much more, the rather

G4057 περισσῶς (perissōs): superabundantly. Origin: adverb from G4053 (περισσός); KJV: exceedingly, out of measure, the more

G4058 περιστερά (peristerá): a pigeon. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: dove, pigeon

G4059 περιτέμνω (peritémnō): to cut around, i.e. (specially) to circumcise. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος); KJV: circumcise

G4060 περιτίθημι (peritíthēmi): to place around; by implication, to present. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: bestow upon, hedge round about, put about (on, upon), set about

G4061 περιτομή (peritomḗ): circumcision (the rite, the condition or the people, literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4059 (περιτέμνω); KJV: X circumcised, circumcision

G4062 περιτρέπω (peritrépō): to turn around, i.e. (mentally) to craze. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: + make mad

G4063 περιτρέχω (peritréchō): to run around, i.e. traverse. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate); KJV: run through

G4064 περιφέρω (periphérō): to convey around, i.e. transport hither and thither. Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bear (carry) about

G4065 περιφρονέω (periphronéō): to think beyond, i.e. depreciate (contemn). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G5426 (φρονέω); KJV: despise

G4066 περίχωρος (períchōros): around the region, i.e. circumjacent (as noun, with G1093 (γῆ) implied vicinity). Origin: from G4012 (περί) and G5561 (χώρα); KJV: country (round) about, region (that lieth) round about

G4067 περίψωμα (perípsōma): something brushed all around, i.e. off-scrapings (figuratively, scum). Origin: from a comparative of G4012 (περί) and (to rub); KJV: offscouring

G4068 περπερεύομαι (perpereúomai): perhaps by reduplication of the base of G4008 (πέραν)); to boast. Origin: middle voice from (braggart; KJV: vaunt itself

G4069 Περσίς (Persís): a Persian woman; Persis, a Christian female. KJV: Persis

G4070 πέρυσι (pérysi): the by-gone, i.e. (as noun) last year. Origin: adverb from G4009 (πέρας); KJV: + a year ago

G4071 πετεινόν (peteinón): a flying animal, i.e. bird. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G4072 (πέτομαι); KJV: bird, fowl

G4072 πέτομαι (pétomai): to fly. Origin: middle voice of a primary verb; KJV: fly(-ing)

G4073 πέτρα (pétra): a (mass of) rock (literally or figuratively). Origin: feminine of the same as G4074 (Πέτρος); KJV: rock

G4074 Πέτρος (Pétros): a (piece of) rock (larger than G3037 (λίθος)); as a name, Petrus, an apostle. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: Peter, rock

G4075 πετρώδης (petrṓdēs): rock-like, i.e. rocky. Origin: from G4073 (πέτρα) and G1491 (εἶδος); KJV: stony

G4076 πήγανον (pḗganon): rue (from its thick or fleshy leaves). Origin: from G4078 (πήγνυμι); KJV: rue

G4077 πηγή (pēgḗ): a fount (literally or figuratively), i.e. source or supply (of water, blood, enjoyment) (not necessarily the original spring). Origin: probably from G4078 (πήγνυμι) (through the idea of gushing plumply); KJV: fountain, well

G4078 πήγνυμι (pḗgnymi): to fix ("peg"), i.e. (specially) to set up (a tent). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which in its simpler form occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); KJV: pitch

G4079 πηδάλιον (pēdálion): from the same as G3976 (πέδη)); a "pedal", i.e. helm. Origin: neuter of a (presumed) derivative of (the blade of an oar; KJV: rudder

G4080 πηλίκος (pēlíkos): how much (as an indefinite), i.e. in size or (figuratively) dignity. Origin: a quantitative form (the feminine) of the base of G4225 (πού); KJV: how great (large)

G4081 πηλός (pēlós): clay. Origin: perhaps a primary word; KJV: clay

G4082 πήρα (pḗra): a wallet or leather pouch for food. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: scrip

G4083 πῆχυς (pēchys): the fore-arm, i.e. (as a measure) a cubit. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: cubit

G4084 πιάζω (piázō): to squeeze, i.e. seize (gently by the hand (press), or officially (arrest), or in hunting (capture)). Origin: probably another form of G971 (βιάζω); KJV: apprehend, catch, lay hand on, take

G4085 πιέζω (piézō): to pack. Origin: another form for G4084 (πιάζω); KJV: press down

G4086 πιθανολογία (pithanología): persuasive language. Origin: from a compound of a derivative of G3982 (πείθω) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: enticing words

G4087 πικραίνω (pikraínō): to embitter (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4089 (πικρός); KJV: be (make) bitter

G4088 πικρία (pikría): acridity (especially poison), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G4089 (πικρός); KJV: bitterness

G4089 πικρός (pikrós): sharp (pungent), i.e. acrid (literally or figuratively). Origin: perhaps from G4078 (πήγνυμι) (through the idea of piercing); KJV: bitter

G4090 πικρῶς (pikrōs): bitterly, i.e. (figuratively) violently. Origin: adverb from G4089 (πικρός); KJV: bitterly

G4091 Πιλᾶτος (Pilâtos): close-pressed, i.e. firm; Pilatus, a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Pilate

G4092 πίμπρημι (pímprēmi): to fire, i.e. burn (figuratively and passively, become inflamed with fever). Origin: a reduplicated and prolonged form of a primary ; which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); KJV: be (X should have) swollen

G4093 πινακίδιον (pinakídion): a tablet (for writing on). Origin: diminutive of G4094 (πίναξ); KJV: writing table

G4094 πίναξ (pínax): a plate. Origin: apparently a form of G4109 (πλάξ); KJV: charger, platter

G4095 πίνω (pínō): to imbibe (literally or figuratively). Origin: a prolonged form of ; which (together with another form) ; occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses; KJV: drink

G4096 πιότης (piótēs): perhaps akin to the alternate of G4095 (πίνω) through the idea of repletion); plumpness, i.e. (by implication) richness (oiliness). Origin: from (fat; KJV: fatness

G4097 πιπράσκω (pipráskō): from the base of G4008 (πέραν)); to traffic (by travelling), i.e. dispose of as merchandise or into slavery (literally or figuratively). Origin: contracted from (to traverse; KJV: sell

G4098 πίπτω (píptō): to fall (literally or figuratively). Origin: probably akin to G4072 (πέτομαι) through the idea of alighting; KJV: fail, fall (down), light on

G4099 Πισιδία (Pisidía): Pisidia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Pisidia

G4100 πιστεύω (pisteúō): to have faith (in, upon, or with respect to, a person or thing), i.e. credit; by implication, to entrust (especially one's spiritual well-being to Christ). Origin: from G4102 (πίστις); KJV: believe(-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with

G4101 πιστικός (pistikós): trustworthy, i.e. genuine (unadulterated). Origin: from G4102 (πίστις); KJV: spike-(nard)

G4102 πίστις (pístis): persuasion, i.e. credence; moral conviction (of religious truth, or the truthfulness of God or a religious teacher), especially reliance upon Christ for salvation; abstractly, constancy in such profession; by extension, the system of religious (Gospel) truth itself. Origin: from G3982 (πείθω); KJV: assurance, belief, believe, faith, fidelity

G4103 πιστός (pistós): objectively, trustworthy; subjectively, trustful. Origin: from G3982 (πείθω); KJV: believe(-ing, -r), faithful(-ly), sure, true

G4104 πιστόω (pistóō): to assure. Origin: from G4103 (πιστός); KJV: assure of

G4105 πλανάω (planáō): to (properly, cause to) roam (from safety, truth, or virtue). Origin: from G4106 (πλάνη); KJV: go astray, deceive, err, seduce, wander, be out of the way

G4106 πλάνη (plánē): objectively, fraudulence; subjectively, a straying from orthodoxy or piety. Origin: feminine of G4108 (πλάνος) (as abstractly); KJV: deceit, to deceive, delusion, error

G4107 πλανήτης (planḗtēs): a rover ("planet"), i.e. (figuratively) an erratic teacher. Origin: from G4108 (πλάνος); KJV: wandering

G4108 πλάνος (plános): roving (as a tramp), i.e. (by implication) an impostor or misleader. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: --deceiver, seducing

G4109 πλάξ (pláx): a moulding-board, i.e. flat surface ("plate", or tablet, literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4111 (πλάσσω); KJV: table

G4110 πλάσμα (plásma): something moulded. Origin: from G4111 (πλάσσω); KJV: thing formed

G4111 πλάσσω (plássō): to mould, i.e. shape or fabricate. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: form

G4112 πλαστός (plastós): moulded, i.e. (by implication) artificial or (figuratively) fictitious (false). Origin: from G4111 (πλάσσω); KJV: feigned

G4113 πλατεῖα (plateîa): a wide "plat" or "place", i.e. open square. Origin: feminine of G4116 (πλατύς); KJV: street

G4114 πλάτος (plátos): width. Origin: from G4116 (πλατύς); KJV: breadth

G4115 πλατύνω (platýnō): to widen (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4116 (πλατύς); KJV: make broad, enlarge

G4116 πλατύς (platýs): spread out "flat" ("plot"), i.e. broad. Origin: from G4111 (πλάσσω); KJV: wide

G4117 πλέγμα (plégma): a plait (of hair). Origin: from G4120 (πλέκω); KJV: broidered hair

G4118 πλεῖστος (pleîstos): the largest number or very large. Origin: irregular superlative of G4183 (πολύς); KJV: very great, most

G4119 πλείων (pleíōn): more in quantity, number, or quality; also (in plural) the major portion. Origin: comparative of G4183 (πολύς); KJV: X above, + exceed, more excellent, further, (very) great(-er), long(-er), (very) many, greater (more) part, + yet but

G4120 πλέκω (plékō): to twine or braid. Origin: a primary word; KJV: plait

G4121 πλεονάζω (pleonázō): to do, make or be more, i.e. increase (transitively or intransitively); by extension, to superabound. Origin: from G4119 (πλείων); KJV: abound, abundant, make to increase, have over

G4122 πλεονεκτέω (pleonektéō): to be covetous, i.e. (by implication) to over-reach. Origin: from G4123 (πλεονέκτης); KJV: get an advantage, defraud, make a gain

G4123 πλεονέκτης (pleonéktēs): holding (desiring) more, i.e. eager for gain (avaricious, hence a defrauder). Origin: from G4119 (πλείων) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: covetous

G4124 πλεονεξία (pleonexía): avarice, i.e. (by implication) fraudulency, extortion. Origin: from G4123 (πλεονέκτης); KJV: covetous(-ness) practices, greediness

G4125 πλευρά (pleurá): a rib, i.e. (by extension) side. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: side

G4126 πλέω (pléō): to pass in a vessel. Origin: probably a form of G4150 (πλύνω) (through the idea of plunging through the water); KJV: sail

G4127 πληγή (plēgḗ): a stroke; by implication, a wound; figuratively, a calamity. Origin: from G4141 (πλήσσω); KJV: plague, stripe, wound(-ed)

G4128 πλῆθος (plēthos): a fulness, i.e. a large number, throng, populace. Origin: from G4130 (πλήθω); KJV: bundle, company, multitude

G4129 πληθύνω (plēthýnō): to increase (transitively or intransitively). Origin: from another form of G4128 (πλῆθος); KJV: abound, multiply

G4130 πλήθω (plḗthō): to "fill" (literally or figuratively (imbue, influence, supply)); specially, to fulfil (time). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary (which appears only as an alternate in certain tenses and in the reduplicated form pimplemi); KJV: accomplish, full (…come), furnish

G4131 πλήκτης (plḗktēs): a smiter, i.e. pugnacious (quarrelsome). Origin: from G4141 (πλήσσω); KJV: striker

G4132 πλήμμυρα (plḗmmyra): flood-tide, i.e. (by analogy) a freshet. Origin: prolonged from G4130 (πλήθω); KJV: flood

G4133 πλήν (plḗn): moreover (besides), i.e. albeit, save that, rather, yet. Origin: from G4119 (πλείων); KJV: but (rather), except, nevertheless, notwithstanding, save, than

G4134 πλήρης (plḗrēs): replete, or covered over; by analogy, complete. Origin: from G4130 (πλήθω); KJV: full

G4135 πληροφορέω (plērophoréō): to carry out fully (in evidence), i.e. completely assure (or convince), entirely accomplish. Origin: from G4134 (πλήρης) and G5409 (φορέω); KJV: most surely believe, fully know (persuade), make full proof of

G4136 πληροφορία (plērophoría): entire confidence. Origin: from G4135 (πληροφορέω); KJV: (full) assurance

G4137 πληρόω (plēróō): to make replete, i.e. (literally) to cram (a net), level up (a hollow), or (figuratively) to furnish (or imbue, diffuse, influence), satisfy, execute (an office), finish (a period or task), verify (or coincide with a prediction), etc. Origin: from G4134 (πλήρης); KJV: accomplish, X after, (be) complete, end, expire, fill (up), fulfil, (be, make) full (come), fully preach, perfect, supply

G4138 πλήρωμα (plḗrōma): repletion or completion, i.e. (subjectively) what fills (as contents, supplement, copiousness, multitude), or (objectively) what is filled (as container, performance, period). Origin: from G4137 (πληρόω); KJV: which is put in to fill up, piece that filled up, fulfilling, full, fulness

G4139 πλησίον (plēsíon): (adverbially) close by; as noun, a neighbor, i.e. fellow (as man, countryman, Christian or friend). Origin: neuter of a derivative of (near); KJV: near, neighbour

G4140 πλησμονή (plēsmonḗ): a filling up, i.e. (figuratively) gratification. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G4130 (πλήθω); KJV: satisfying

G4141 πλήσσω (plḗssō): to pound, i.e. (figuratively) to inflict with (calamity). Origin: apparently another form of G4111 (πλάσσω) (through the idea of flattening out); KJV: smite

G4142 πλοιάριον (ploiárion): a boat. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4143 (πλοῖον); KJV: boat, little (small) ship

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4143 to G4268
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4143 πλοῖον (ploîon): a sailer, i.e. vessel. Origin: from G4126 (πλέω); KJV: ship(-ing)

G4144 πλόος (plóos): a sail, i.e. navigation. Origin: from G4126 (πλέω); KJV: course, sailing, voyage

G4145 πλούσιος (ploúsios): wealthy; figuratively, abounding with. Origin: from G4149 (πλοῦτος); KJV: rich

G4146 πλουσίως (plousíōs): copiously. Origin: adverb from G4145 (πλούσιος); KJV: abundantly, richly

G4147 πλουτέω (ploutéō): to be (or become) wealthy (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4148 (πλουτίζω); KJV: be increased with goods, (be made, wax) rich

G4148 πλουτίζω (ploutízō): to make wealthy (figuratively). Origin: from G4149 (πλοῦτος); KJV: en- (make) rich

G4149 πλοῦτος (ploûtos): wealth (as fulness), i.e. (literally) money, possessions, or (figuratively) abundance, richness, (specially), valuable bestowment. Origin: from the base of G4130 (πλήθω); KJV: riches

G4150 πλύνω (plýnō): to "plunge", i.e. launder clothing. Origin: a prolonged form of an obsolete (to "flow"); KJV: wash

G4151 πνεῦμα (pneûma): a current of air, i.e. breath (blast) or a breeze; by analogy or figuratively, a spirit, i.e. (human) the rational soul, (by implication) vital principle, mental disposition, etc., or (superhuman) an angel, demon, or (divine) God, Christ's spirit, the Holy Spirit. Origin: from G4154 (πνέω); KJV: ghost, life, spirit(-ual, -ually), mind

G4152 πνευματικός (pneumatikós): non-carnal, i.e. (humanly) ethereal (as opposed to gross), or (dæmoniacally) a spirit (concretely), or (divinely) supernatural, regenerate, religious. Origin: from G4151 (πνεῦμα); KJV: spiritual

G4153 πνευματικῶς (pneumatikōs): non-physically, i.e. divinely, figuratively. Origin: adverb from G4152 (πνευματικός); KJV: spiritually

G4154 πνέω (pnéō): to breathe hard, i.e. breeze. Origin: a primary word; KJV: blow

G4155 πνίγω (pnígō): to wheeze, i.e. (causative, by implication) to throttle or strangle (drown). Origin: strengthened from G4154 (πνέω); KJV: choke, take by the throat

G4156 πνικτός (pniktós): throttled, i.e. (neuter concretely) an animal choked to death (not bled). Origin: from G4155 (πνίγω); KJV: strangled

G4157 πνοή (pnoḗ): respiration, a breeze. Origin: from G4154 (πνέω); KJV: breath, wind

G4158 ποδήρης (podḗrēs): a dress (G2066 (ἐσθής) implied) reaching the ankles. Origin: from G4228 (πούς) and another element of uncertain affinity; KJV: garment down to the foot

G4159 πόθεν (póthen): from which (as interrogative) or what (as relative) place, state, source or cause. Origin: from the base of G4213 (πόσις) with enclitic adverb of origin; KJV: whence

G4160 ποιέω (poiéō): to make or do (in a very wide application, more or less direct). Origin: apparently a prolonged form of an obsolete primary; KJV: abide, + agree, appoint, X avenge, + band together, be, bear, + bewray, bring (forth), cast out, cause, commit, + content, continue, deal, + without any delay, (would) do(-ing), execute, exercise, fulfil, gain, give, have, hold, X journeying, keep, + lay wait, + lighten the ship, make, X mean, + none of these things move me, observe, ordain, perform, provide, + have purged, purpose, put, + raising up, X secure, shew, X shoot out, spend, take, tarry, + transgress the law, work, yield

G4161 ποίημα (poíēma): a product, i.e. fabric (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: thing that is made, workmanship

G4162 ποίησις (poíēsis): action, i.e. performance (of the law). Origin: from G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: deed

G4163 ποιητής (poiētḗs): a performer; specially, a "poet". Origin: from G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: --doer, poet

G4164 ποικίλος (poikílos): motley, i.e. various in character. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: divers, manifold

G4165 ποιμαίνω (poimaínō): to tend as a shepherd of (figuratively, superviser). Origin: from G4166 (ποιμήν); KJV: feed (cattle), rule

G4166 ποιμήν (poimḗn): a shepherd (literally or figuratively). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: shepherd, pastor

G4167 ποίμνη (poímnē): a flock (literally or figuratively). Origin: contraction from G4165 (ποιμαίνω); KJV: flock, fold

G4168 ποίμνιον (poímnion): a flock, i.e. (figuratively) group (of believers). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4167 (ποίμνη); KJV: flock

G4169 ποῖος (poîos): individualizing interrogative (of character) what sort of, or (of number) which one. Origin: from the base of G4226 (ποῦ) and G3634 (οἷος); KJV: what (manner of), which

G4170 πολεμέω (poleméō): to be (engaged) in warfare, i.e. to battle (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4171 (πόλεμος); KJV: fight, (make) war

G4171 πόλεμος (pólemos): warfare (literally or figuratively; a single encounter or a series). Origin: from (to bustle); KJV: battle, fight, war

G4172 πόλις (pólis): a town (properly, with walls, of greater or less size). Origin: probably from the same as G4171 (πόλεμος), or perhaps from G4183 (πολύς); KJV: city

G4173 πολιτάρχης (politárchēs): a town-officer, i.e. magistrate. Origin: from G4172 (πόλις) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: ruler of the city

G4174 πολιτεία (politeía): citizenship; concretely, a community. Origin: from G4177 (πολίτης) ("polity"); KJV: commonwealth, freedom

G4175 πολίτευμα (políteuma): a community, i.e. (abstractly) citizenship (figuratively). Origin: from G4176 (πολιτεύομαι); KJV: conversation

G4176 πολιτεύομαι (politeúomai): to behave as a citizen (figuratively). Origin: middle voice of a derivative of G4177 (πολίτης); KJV: let conversation be, live

G4177 πολίτης (polítēs): a townsman. Origin: from G4172 (πόλις); KJV: citizen

G4178 πολλάκις (pollákis): many times, i.e. frequently. Origin: multiplicative adverb from G4183 (πολύς); KJV: oft(-en, -entimes, -times)

G4179 πολλαπλασίων (pollaplasíōn): manifold, i.e. (neuter as noun) very much more. Origin: from G4183 (πολύς) and probably a derivative of G4120 (πλέκω); KJV: manifold more

G4180 πολυλογία (polylogía): loquacity, i.e. prolixity. Origin: from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: much speaking

G4181 πολυμερῶς (polymerōs): in many portions, i.e. variously as to time and agency (piecemeal). Origin: adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G3313 (μέρος); KJV: at sundry times

G4182 πολυποίκιλος (polypoíkilos): much variegated, i.e. multifarious. Origin: from G4183 (πολύς) and G4164 (ποικίλος); KJV: manifold

G4183 πολύς (polýs): (singular) much (in any respect) or (plural) many; neuter (singular) as adverbial, largely; neuter (plural) as adverb or noun often, mostly, largely. Origin: including the forms from the alternate ; KJV: abundant, + altogether, common, + far (passed, spent), (+ be of a) great (age, deal, -ly, while), long, many, much, oft(-en (-times)), plenteous, sore, straitly

G4184 πολύσπλαγχνος (polýsplanchnos): extremely compassionate. Origin: from G4183 (πολύς) and G4698 (σπλάγχνον) (figuratively); KJV: very pitiful

G4185 πολυτελής (polytelḗs): extremely expensive. Origin: from G4183 (πολύς) and G5056 (τέλος); KJV: costly, very precious, of great price

G4186 πολύτιμος (polýtimos): extremely valuable. Origin: from G4183 (πολύς) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: very costly, of great price

G4187 πολυτρόπως (polytrópōs): in many ways, i.e. variously as to method or form. Origin: adverb from a compound of G4183 (πολύς) and G5158 (τρόπος); KJV: in divers manners

G4188 πόμα (póma): a beverage. Origin: from the alternate of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: drink

G4189 πονηρία (ponēría): depravity, i.e. (specially), malice; plural (concretely) plots, sins. Origin: from G4190 (πονηρός); KJV: iniquity, wickedness

G4190 πονηρός (ponērós): hurtful, i.e. evil (properly, in effect or influence, and thus differing from G2556 (κακός), which refers rather to essential character, as well as from G4550 (σαπρός), which indicates degeneracy from original virtue); figuratively, calamitous; also (passively) ill, i.e. diseased; but especially (morally) culpable, i.e. derelict, vicious, facinorous; neuter (singular) mischief, malice, or (plural) guilt; masculine (singular) the devil, or (plural) sinners. Origin: from a derivative of G4192 (πόνος); KJV: bad, evil, grievous, harm, lewd, malicious, wicked(-ness)

G4191 πονηρότερος (ponēróteros): more evil. Origin: comparative of G4190 (πονηρός); KJV: more wicked

G4192 πόνος (pónos): toil, i.e. (by implication) anguish. Origin: from the base of G3993 (πένης); KJV: pain

G4193 Ποντικός (Pontikós): a Pontican, i.e. native of Pontus. Origin: from G4195 (Πόντος); KJV: born in Pontus

G4194 Πόντιος (Póntios): apparently bridged; Pontius, a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Pontius

G4195 Πόντος (Póntos): a sea; Pontus, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Pontus

G4196 Πόπλιος (Póplios): apparently "popular"; Poplius (i.e. Publius), a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Publius

G4197 πορεία (poreía): travel (by land); figuratively (plural) proceedings, i.e. career. Origin: from G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: journey(-ing), ways

G4198 πορεύομαι (poreúomai): to traverse, i.e. travel (literally or figuratively; especially to remove (figuratively, die), live, etc.). Origin: middle voice from a derivative of the same as G3984 (πεῖρα); KJV: --depart, go (away, forth, one's way, up), (make a, take a) journey, walk

G4199 πορθέω (porthéō): to ravage (figuratively). Origin: prolongation from (to sack); KJV: destroy, waste

G4200 πορισμός (porismós): furnishing (procuring), i.e. (by implication) money-getting (acquisition). Origin: from a derivative of (a way, i.e. means); KJV: gain

G4201 Πόρκιος (Pórkios): apparently swinish; Porcius, a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Porcius

G4202 πορνεία (porneía): harlotry (including adultery and incest); figuratively, idolatry. Origin: from G4203 (πορνεύω); KJV: fornication

G4203 πορνεύω (porneúō): to act the harlot, i.e. (literally) indulge unlawful lust (of either sex), or (figuratively) practise idolatry. Origin: from G4204 (πόρνη); KJV: commit (fornication)

G4204 πόρνη (pórnē): a strumpet; figuratively, an idolater. Origin: feminine of G4205 (πόρνος); KJV: harlot, whore

G4205 πόρνος (pórnos): akin to the base of G4097 (πιπράσκω)); a (male) prostitute (as venal), i.e. (by analogy) a debauchee (libertine). Origin: from (to sell; KJV: fornicator, whoremonger

G4206 πόῤῥω (pórrhō): forwards, i.e. at a distance. Origin: adverb from G4253 (πρό); KJV: far, a great way off

G4207 πόῤῥωθεν (pórrhōthen): from far, or (by implication) at a distance, i.e. distantly. Origin: from G4206 (πόῤῥω) with adverbial enclitic of source; KJV: afar off

G4208 ποῤῥωτέρω (porrhōtérō): further, i.e. a greater distance. Origin: adverb comparative of G4206 (πόῤῥω); KJV: farther

G4209 πορφύρα (porphýra): the "purple" mussel, i.e. (by implication) the red-blue color itself, and finally a garment dyed with it. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: purple

G4210 πορφυροῦς (porphyroûs): purpureal, i.e. bluish red. Origin: from G4209 (πορφύρα); KJV: purple

G4211 πορφυρόπωλις (porphyrópōlis): a female trader in purple cloth. Origin: feminine of a compound of G4209 (πορφύρα) and G4453 (πωλέω); KJV: seller of purple

G4212 ποσάκις (posákis): how many times. Origin: multiplicative from G4214 (πόσος); KJV: how oft(-en)

G4213 πόσις (pósis): a drinking (the act), i.e. (concretely) a draught. Origin: from the alternate of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: drink

G4214 πόσος (pósos): interrogative pronoun (of amount) how much (large, long or (plural) many). Origin: from an absolute (who, what) and G3739 (ὅς); KJV: how great (long, many), what

G4215 ποταμός (potamós): a current, brook or freshet (as drinkable), i.e. running water. Origin: probably from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω) (compare G4224 (πότος)); KJV: flood, river, stream, water

G4216 ποταμοφόρητος (potamophórētos): river-borne, i.e. overwhelmed by a stream. Origin: from G4215 (ποταμός) and a derivative of G5409 (φορέω); KJV: carried away of the flood

G4217 ποταπός (potapós): interrogatively, whatever, i.e. of what possible sort. Origin: apparently from G4219 (πότε) and the base of G4226 (ποῦ); KJV: what (manner of)

G4218 ποτέ (poté): indefinite adverb, at some time, ever. Origin: from the base of G4225 (πού) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: afore-(any, some-)time(-s), at length (the last), (+ n- )ever, in the old time, in time past, once, when

G4219 πότε (póte): interrogative adverb, at what time. Origin: from the base of G4226 (ποῦ) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: + how long, when

G4220 πότερον (póteron): interrogative as adverb, which (of two), i.e. is it this or that. Origin: neuter of a comparative of the base of G4226 (ποῦ); KJV: whether

G4221 ποτήριον (potḗrion): a drinking-vessel; by extension, the contents thereof, i.e. a cupful (draught); figuratively, a lot or fate. Origin: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: cup

G4222 ποτίζω (potízō): to furnish drink, irrigate. Origin: from a derivative of the alternate of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: give (make) to drink, feed, water

G4223 Ποτίολοι (Potíoloi): little wells, i.e. mineral springs; Potioli (i.e. Puteoli), a place in Italy. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Puteoli

G4224 πότος (pótos): a drinking-bout or carousal. Origin: from the alternate of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: banqueting

G4225 πού (poú): as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly. Origin: genitive case of an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare G4214 (πόσος)); KJV: about, a certain place

G4226 ποῦ (poû): as adverb of place; at (by implication, to) what locality. Origin: genitive case of an interrogative pronoun (what) otherwise obsolete (perhaps the same as G4225 (πού) used with the rising slide of inquiry); KJV: where, whither

G4227 Πούδης (Poúdēs): modest; Pudes (i.e. Pudens), a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Pudens

G4228 πούς (poús): a "foot" (figuratively or literally). Origin: a primary word; KJV: foot(-stool)

G4229 πρᾶγμα (prâgma): a deed; by implication, an affair; by extension, an object (material). Origin: from G4238 (πράσσω); KJV: business, matter, thing, work

G4230 πραγματεία (pragmateía): a transaction, i.e. negotiation. Origin: from G4231 (πραγματεύομαι); KJV: affair

G4231 πραγματεύομαι (pragmateúomai): to busy oneself with, i.e. to trade. Origin: from G4229 (πρᾶγμα); KJV: occupy

G4232 πραιτώριον (praitṓrion): the prætorium or governor's courtroom (sometimes including the whole edifice and camp). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: (common, judgment) hall (of judgment), palace, prætorium

G4233 πράκτωρ (práktōr): a practiser, i.e. (specially), an official collector. Origin: from a derivative of G4238 (πράσσω); KJV: officer

G4234 πρᾶξις (prâxis): practice, i.e. (concretely) an act; by extension, a function. Origin: from G4238 (πράσσω); KJV: deed, office, work

G4235 πρᾷος (prâios): gentle, i.e. humble. Origin: a form of G4239 (πραΰς), used in certain parts; KJV: meek

G4236 πρᾳότης (praiótēs): gentleness, by implication, humility. Origin: from G4235 (πρᾷος); KJV: meekness

G4237 πρασιά (prasiá): a garden plot, i.e. (by implication, of regular beds) a row (repeated in plural by Hebraism, to indicate an arrangement). Origin: perhaps from (a leek, and so an onion-patch); KJV: in ranks

G4238 πράσσω (prássō): to "practise", i.e. perform repeatedly or habitually (thus differing from G4160 (ποιέω), which properly refers to a single act); by implication, to execute, accomplish, etc.; specially, to collect (dues), fare (personally). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: commit, deeds, do, exact, keep, require, use arts

G4239 πραΰς (praÿs): mild, i.e. (by implication) humble. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: meek

G4240 πραΰτης (praÿtēs): mildness, i.e. (by implication) humility. Origin: from G4239 (πραΰς); KJV: meekness

G4241 πρέπω (prépō): to tower up (be conspicuous), i.e. (by implication) to be suitable or proper (third person singular present indicative, often used impersonally, it is fit or right). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: become, comely

G4242 πρεσβεία (presbeía): seniority (eldership), i.e. (by implication) an embassy (concretely, ambassadors). Origin: from G4243 (πρεσβεύω); KJV: ambassage, message

G4243 πρεσβεύω (presbeúō): to be a senior, i.e. (by implication) act as a representative (figuratively, preacher). Origin: from the base of G4245 (πρεσβύτερος); KJV: be an ambassador

G4244 πρεσβυτέριον (presbytérion): the order of elders, i.e. (specially), Israelite Sanhedrin or Christian "presbytery". Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4245 (πρεσβύτερος); KJV: (estate of) elder(-s), presbytery

G4245 πρεσβύτερος (presbýteros): older; as noun, a senior; specially, an Israelite Sanhedrist (also figuratively, member of the celestial council) or Christian "presbyter". Origin: comparative of (elderly); KJV: elder(-est), old

G4246 πρεσβύτης (presbýtēs): an old man. Origin: from the same as G4245 (πρεσβύτερος); KJV: aged (man), old man

G4247 πρεσβῦτις (presbŷtis): an old woman. Origin: feminine of G4246 (πρεσβύτης); KJV: aged woman

G4248 πρηνής (prēnḗs): leaning (falling) forward ("prone"), i.e. head foremost. Origin: from G4253 (πρό); KJV: headlong

G4249 πρίζω (prízō): to saw in two. Origin: a strengthened form of a primary prio (to saw); KJV: saw asunder

G4250 πρίν (prín): prior, sooner. Origin: adverb from G4253 (πρό); KJV: before (that), ere

G4251 Πρίσκα (Príska): feminine of Priscus, ancient; Priska, a Christian woman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Prisca

G4252 Πρίσκιλλα (Prískilla): Priscilla (i.e. little Prisca), a Christian woman. Origin: diminutive of G4251 (Πρίσκα); KJV: Priscilla

G4253 πρό (pró): "fore", i.e. in front of, prior (figuratively, superior) to. Origin: a primary preposition; KJV: above, ago, before, or ever

G4254 προάγω (proágō): to lead forward (magisterially); intransitively, to precede (in place or time (participle, previous)). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring (forth, out), go before

G4255 προαιρέομαι (proairéomai): to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: purpose

G4256 προαιτιάομαι (proaitiáomai): to accuse already, i.e. previously charge. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G156 (αἰτία); KJV: prove before

G4257 προακούω (proakoúō): to hear already,i.e. anticipate. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: hear before

G4258 προαμαρτάνω (proamartánō): to sin previously (to conversion). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G264 (ἁμαρτάνω); KJV: sin already, heretofore sin

G4259 προαύλιον (proaúlion): a forecourt, i.e. vestibule (alley-way). Origin: neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 (πρό) and G833 (αὐλή); KJV: porch

G4260 προβαίνω (probaínō): to walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: + be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken

G4261 προβάλλω (probállō): to throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: put forward, shoot forth

G4262 προβατικός (probatikós): relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem. Origin: from G4263 (πρόβατον); KJV: sheep (market)

G4263 πρόβατον (próbaton): something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively). Origin: probably neuter of a presumed derivative of G4260 (προβαίνω); KJV: sheep(-fold)

G4264 προβιβάζω (probibázō): to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and a reduplicated form of G971 (βιάζω); KJV: draw, before instruct

G4265 προβλέπω (problépō): to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G991 (βλέπω); KJV: provide

G4266 προγίνομαι (progínomai): to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: be past

G4267 προγινώσκω (proginṓskō): to know beforehand, i.e. foresee. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: foreknow (ordain), know (before)

G4268 πρόγνωσις (prógnōsis): forethought. Origin: from G4267 (προγινώσκω); KJV: foreknowledge

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4269 to G4386
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4269 πρόγονος (prógonos): an ancestor, (grand-)parent. Origin: from G4266 (προγίνομαι); KJV: forefather, parent

G4270 προγράφω (prográphō): to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1125 (γράφω); KJV: before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime)

G4271 πρόδηλος (pródēlos): plain before all men, i.e. obvious. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1212 (δῆλος); KJV: evident, manifest (open) beforehand

G4272 προδίδωμι (prodídōmi): to give before the other party has given. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1325 (δίδωμι); KJV: first give

G4273 προδότης (prodótēs): a surrender. Origin: from G4272 (προδίδωμι) (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands); KJV: betrayer, traitor

G4274 πρόδρομος (pródromos): a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor). Origin: from the alternate of G4390 (προτρέχω); KJV: forerunner

G4275 προείδω (proeídō): foresee. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: foresee, saw before

G4276 προελπίζω (proelpízō): to hope in advance of other confirmation. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1679 (ἐλπίζω); KJV: first trust

G4277 προέπω (proépō): to say already, to predict. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2036 (ἔπω); KJV: forewarn, say (speak, tell) before

G4278 προενάρχομαι (proenárchomai): to commence already. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G1728 (ἐνάρχομαι); KJV: begin (before)

G4279 προεπαγγέλλομαι (proepangéllomai): to promise of old. Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G1861 (ἐπαγγέλλω); KJV: promise before

G4280 προερέω (proeréō): used as alternate of G4277 (προέπω); to say already, predict. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2046 (ἐρέω); KJV: foretell, say (speak, tell) before

G4281 προέρχομαι (proérchomai): to go onward, precede (in place or time). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate); KJV: go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on

G4282 προετοιμάζω (proetoimázō): to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2090 (ἑτοιμάζω); KJV: ordain before, prepare afore

G4283 προευαγγελίζομαι (proeuangelízomai): to announce glad news in advance. Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2097 (εὐαγγελίζω); KJV: preach before the gospel

G4284 προέχομαι (proéchomai): to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel. Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: be better

G4285 προηγέομαι (proēgéomai): to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: prefer

G4286 πρόθεσις (próthesis): a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God. Origin: from G4388 (προτίθεμαι); KJV: purpose, shew(-bread)

G4287 προθέσμιος (prothésmios): fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with G2250 (ἡμέρα) implied) a designated day. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: time appointed

G4288 προθυμία (prothymía): predisposition, i.e. alacrity. Origin: from G4289 (πρόθυμος); KJV: forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind

G4289 πρόθυμος (próthymos): forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2372 (θυμός); KJV: ready, willing

G4290 προθύμως (prothýmōs): with alacrity. Origin: adverb from G4289 (πρόθυμος); KJV: willingly

G4291 προΐστημι (proḯstēmi): to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: maintain, be over, rule

G4292 προκαλέομαι (prokaléomai): to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate. Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: provoke

G4293 προκαταγγέλλω (prokatangéllō): to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2605 (καταγγέλλω); KJV: foretell, have notice, (shew) before

G4294 προκαταρτίζω (prokatartízō): to prepare in advance. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2675 (καταρτίζω); KJV: make up beforehand

G4295 πρόκειμαι (prókeimai): to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2749 (κεῖμαι); KJV: be first, set before (forth)

G4296 προκηρύσσω (prokērýssō): to herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2784 (κηρύσσω); KJV: before (first) preach

G4297 προκοπή (prokopḗ): progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or objectively). Origin: from G4298 (προκόπτω); KJV: furtherance, profit

G4298 προκόπτω (prokóptō): to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax

G4299 πρόκριμα (prókrima): a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. prepossession. Origin: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: prefer one before another

G4300 προκυρόω (prokyróō): to ratify previously. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2964 (κυρόω); KJV: confirm before

G4301 προλαμβάνω (prolambánō): to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: come aforehand, overtake, take before

G4302 προλέγω (prolégō): to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: foretell, tell before

G4303 προμαρτύρομαι (promartýromai): to be a witness in advance i.e. predict. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3143 (μαρτύρομαι); KJV: testify beforehand

G4304 προμελετάω (promeletáō): to premeditate. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3191 (μελετάω); KJV: meditate before

G4305 προμεριμνάω (promerimnáō): to care (anxiously) in advance. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3309 (μεριμνάω); KJV: take thought beforehand

G4306 προνοέω (pronoéō): to consider in advance, i.e. look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: provide (for)

G4307 πρόνοια (prónoia): forethought, i.e. provident care or supply. Origin: from G4306 (προνοέω); KJV: providence, provision

G4308 προοράω (prooráō): to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: foresee, see before

G4309 προορίζω (proorízō): to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3724 (ὁρίζω); KJV: determine before, ordain, predestinate

G4310 προπάσχω (propáschō): to undergo hardship previously. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3958 (πάσχω); KJV: suffer before

G4311 προπέμπω (propémpō): to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in travel. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G3992 (πέμπω); KJV: accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth

G4312 προπετής (propetḗs): falling forward, i.e. headlong (figuratively, precipitate). Origin: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: heady, rash(-ly)

G4313 προπορεύομαι (proporeúomai): to precede (as guide or herald). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: go before

G4314 πρός (prós): a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is predicated). Origin: a strengthened form of G4253 (πρό); KJV: about, according to , against, among, at, because of, before, between, (where-)by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), X together, to (you) -ward, unto, with(-in)

G4315 προσάββατον (prosábbaton): a fore-sabbath, i.e. the Sabbath-eve. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G4521 (σάββατον); KJV: day before the sabbath

G4316 προσαγορεύω (prosagoreúō): to address, i.e. salute by name. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of G58 (ἀγορά) (mean to harangue); KJV: call

G4317 προσάγω (proságō): to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bring, draw near

G4318 προσαγωγή (prosagōgḗ): admission. Origin: from G4317 (προσάγω) (compare G72 (ἀγωγή)); KJV: access

G4319 προσαιτέω (prosaitéō): to ask repeatedly (importune), i.e. solicit. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G154 (αἰτέω); KJV: beg

G4320 προσαναβαίνω (prosanabaínō): to ascend farther, i.e. be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G305 (ἀναβαίνω); KJV: go up

G4321 προσαναλίσκω (prosanalískō): to expend further. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G355 (ἀναλίσκω); KJV: spend

G4322 προσαναπληρόω (prosanaplēróō): to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G378 (ἀναπληρόω); KJV: supply

G4323 προσανατίθημι (prosanatíthēmi): to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G394 (ἀνατίθεμαι); KJV: in conference add, confer

G4324 προσαπειλέω (prosapeiléō): to menace additionally. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G546 (ἀπειλέω); KJV: i

G4325 προσδαπανάω (prosdapanáō): to expend additionally. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G1159 (δαπανάω); KJV: spend more

G4326 προσδέομαι (prosdéomai): to require additionally, i.e. want further. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G1189 (δέομαι); KJV: need

G4327 προσδέχομαι (prosdéchomai): to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence, or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with confidence or patience). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: accept, allow, look (wait) for, take

G4328 προσδοκάω (prosdokáō): to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and dokeuo (to watch); KJV: (be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for

G4329 προσδοκία (prosdokía): apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated. Origin: from G4328 (προσδοκάω); KJV: expectation, looking after

G4330 προσεάω (proseáō): to permit further progress. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G1439 (ἐάω); KJV: suffer

G4331 προσεγγίζω (prosengízō): to approach near. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G1448 (ἐγγίζω); KJV: come nigh

G4332 προσεδρεύω (prosedreúō): to sit near, i.e. attend as a servant. Origin: from a compound of G4314 (πρός) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: wait at

G4333 προσεργάζομαι (prosergázomai): to work additionally, i.e. (by implication) acquire besides. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2038 (ἐργάζομαι); KJV: gain

G4334 προσέρχομαι (prosérchomai): to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι) (including its alternate); KJV: (as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto)

G4335 προσευχή (proseuchḗ): prayer (worship); by implication, an oratory (chapel). Origin: from G4336 (προσεύχομαι); KJV: X pray earnestly, prayer

G4336 προσεύχομαι (proseúchomai): to pray to God, i.e. supplicate, worship. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2172 (εὔχομαι); KJV: pray (X earnestly, for), make prayer

G4337 προσέχω (proséchō): (figuratively) to hold the mind (3563 implied) towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: (give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard

G4338 προσηλόω (prosēlóō): to peg to, i.e. spike fast. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of G2247 (ἧλος); KJV: nail to

G4339 προσήλυτος (prosḗlytos): an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte"). Origin: from the alternate of G4334 (προσέρχομαι); KJV: proselyte

G4340 πρόσκαιρος (próskairos): for the occasion only, i.e. temporary. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2540 (καιρός); KJV: dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal

G4341 προσκαλέομαι (proskaléomai): to call toward oneself, i.e. summon, invite. Origin: middle voice from G4314 (πρός) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: call (for, to, unto)

G4342 προσκαρτερέω (proskarteréō): to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2594 (καρτερέω); KJV: attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually)

G4343 προσκαρτέρησις (proskartérēsis): persistancy. Origin: from G4342 (προσκαρτερέω); KJV: perseverance

G4344 προσκεφάλαιον (proskephálaion): something for the head, i.e. a cushion. Origin: neuter of a presumed compound of G4314 (πρός) and G2776 (κεφαλή); KJV: pillow

G4345 προσκληρόω (prosklēróō): to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2820 (κληρόω); KJV: consort with

G4346 πρόσκλισις (prósklisis): a leaning towards, i.e. (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism). Origin: from a compound of G4314 (πρός) and G2827 (κλίνω); KJV: partiality

G4347 προσκολλάω (proskolláō): to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2853 (κολλάω); KJV: cleave, join (self)

G4348 πρόσκομμα (próskomma): a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy. Origin: from G4350 (προσκόπτω); KJV: offence, stumbling(-block, (-stone))

G4349 προσκοπή (proskopḗ): a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin. Origin: from G4350 (προσκόπτω); KJV: offence

G4350 προσκόπτω (proskóptō): to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2875 (κόπτω); KJV: beat upon, dash, stumble (at)

G4351 προσκυλίω (proskylíō): to roll towards, i.e. block against. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2947 (κυλιόω); KJV: roll (to)

G4352 προσκυνέω (proskynéō): to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and a probable derivative of G2965 (κύων) (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); KJV: worship

G4353 προσκυνητής (proskynētḗs): an adorer. Origin: from G4352 (προσκυνέω); KJV: worshipper

G4354 προσλαλέω (proslaléō): to talk to, i.e. converse with. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: speak to (with)

G4355 προσλαμβάνω (proslambánō): to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: receive, take (unto)

G4356 πρόσληψις (próslēpsis): admission. Origin: from G4355 (προσλαμβάνω); KJV: receiving

G4357 προσμένω (prosménō): to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with)

G4358 προσορμίζω (prosormízō): to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and a derivative of the same as G3730 (ὁρμή) (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); KJV: draw to the shore

G4359 προσοφείλω (prosopheílō): to be indebted additionally. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G3784 (ὀφείλω); KJV: over besides

G4360 προσοχθίζω (prosochthízō): to feel indignant at. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and a form of (to be vexed with something irksome); KJV: be grieved at

G4361 πρόσπεινος (próspeinos): hungering further, i.e. intensely hungry. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and the same as G3983 (πεινάω); KJV: very hungry

G4362 προσπήγνυμι (prospḗgnymi): to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G4078 (πήγνυμι); KJV: crucify

G4363 προσπίπτω (prospíptō): to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: beat upon, fall (down) at (before)

G4364 προσποιέομαι (prospoiéomai): to do forward for oneself, i.e. pretend (as if about to do a thing). Origin: middle voice from G4314 (πρός) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: make as though

G4365 προσπορεύομαι (prosporeúomai): to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as G4313 (προπορεύομαι)). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: go before

G4366 προσρήγνυμι (prosrḗgnymi): to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: beat vehemently against (upon)

G4367 προστάσσω (prostássō): to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: bid, command

G4368 προστάτις (prostátis): a patroness, i.e. assistant. Origin: feminine of a derivative of G4291 (προΐστημι); KJV: succourer

G4369 προστίθημι (prostíthēmi): to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex, repeat. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more

G4370 προστρέχω (prostréchō): to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate); KJV: run (thither to, to)

G4371 προσφάγιον (prosphágion): something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare G3795 (ὀψάριον)). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4314 (πρός) and G5315 (φάγω); KJV: meat

G4372 πρόσφατος (prósphatos): previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G4969 (σφάζω); KJV: new

G4373 προσφάτως (prosphátōs): recently. Origin: adverb from G4372 (πρόσφατος); KJV: lately

G4374 προσφέρω (prosphérō): to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate); KJV: bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to

G4375 προσφιλής (prosphilḗs): friendly towards, i.e. acceptable. Origin: from a presumed compound of G4314 (πρός) and G5368 (φιλέω); KJV: lovely

G4376 προσφορά (prosphorá): presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice. Origin: from G4374 (προσφέρω); KJV: offering (up)

G4377 προσφωνέω (prosphōnéō): to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim, summon. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and G5455 (φωνέω); KJV: call unto, speak (un-)to

G4378 πρόσχυσις (próschysis): a shedding forth, i.e. affusion. Origin: from a comparative of G4314 (πρός) and (to pour); KJV: sprinkling

G4379 προσψαύω (prospsaúō): to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in order to relieve). Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and (to touch); KJV: touch

G4380 προσωποληπτέω (prosōpolēptéō): to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality. Origin: from G4381 (προσωπολήπτης); KJV: have respect to persons

G4381 προσωπολήπτης (prosōpolḗptēs): an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality. Origin: from G4383 (πρόσωπον) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: respecter of persons

G4382 προσωποληψία (prosōpolēpsía): partiality, i.e. favoritism. Origin: from G4381 (προσωπολήπτης); KJV: respect of persons

G4383 πρόσωπον (prósōpon): the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person. Origin: from G4314 (πρός) and (the visage, from G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι)); KJV: (outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence

G4384 προτάσσω (protássō): to pre-arrange, i.e. prescribe. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: before appoint

G4385 προτείνω (proteínō): to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging). Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and (to stretch); KJV: bind

G4386 πρότερον (próteron): previously. Origin: neuter of G4387 (πρότερος) as adverb (with or without the article); KJV: before, (at the) first, former

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4387 to G4520
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4387 πρότερος (próteros): prior or previous. Origin: comparative of G4253 (πρό); KJV: former

G4388 προτίθεμαι (protíthemai): to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine). Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: purpose, set forth

G4389 προτρέπομαι (protrépomai): to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage. Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: exhort

G4390 προτρέχω (protréchō): to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate); KJV: outrun, run before

G4391 προϋπάρχω (proÿpárchō): to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5225 (ὑπάρχω); KJV: + be before(-time)

G4392 πρόφασις (próphasis): an outward showing, i.e. pretext. Origin: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: cloke, colour, pretence, show

G4393 προφέρω (prophérō): to bear forward, i.e. produce. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bring forth

G4394 προφητεία (prophēteía): prediction (scriptural or other). Origin: from G4396 (προφήτης) ("prophecy"); KJV: prophecy, prophesying

G4395 προφητεύω (prophēteúō): to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office. Origin: from G4396 (προφήτης); KJV: prophesy

G4396 προφήτης (prophḗtēs): a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet. Origin: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G5346 (φημί); KJV: prophet

G4397 προφητικός (prophētikós): pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic"). Origin: from G4396 (προφήτης); KJV: of prophecy, of the prophets

G4398 προφῆτις (prophētis): a female foreteller or an inspired woman. Origin: feminine of G4396 (προφήτης); KJV: prophetess

G4399 προφθάνω (prophthánō): to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5348 (φθάνω); KJV: prevent

G4400 προχειρίζομαι (procheirízomai): to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose. Origin: middle voice from G4253 (πρό) and a derivative of G5495 (χείρ); KJV: choose, make

G4401 προχειροτονέω (procheirotonéō): to elect in advance. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5500 (χειροτονέω); KJV: choose before

G4402 Πρόχορος (Próchoros): before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian. Origin: from G4253 (πρό) and G5525 (χορός); KJV: Prochorus

G4403 πρύμνα (prýmna): the stern of a ship. Origin: feminine of (hindmost); KJV: hinder part, stern

G4404 πρωΐ (prōḯ): at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch. Origin: adverb from G4253 (πρό); KJV: early (in the morning), (in the) morning

G4405 πρωΐα (prōḯa): day-dawn. Origin: feminine of a derivative of G4404 (πρωΐ) as noun; KJV: early, morning

G4406 πρώϊμος (prṓïmos): dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season). Origin: from G4404 (πρωΐ); KJV: early

G4407 πρωϊνός (prōïnós): pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal. Origin: from G4404 (πρωΐ); KJV: morning

G4408 πρῶρα (prōra): the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel. Origin: feminine of a presumed derivative of G4253 (πρό) as noun; KJV: forepart(-ship)

G4409 πρωτεύω (prōteúō): to be first (in rank or influence). Origin: from G4413 (πρῶτος); KJV: have the preeminence

G4410 πρωτοκαθεδρία (prōtokathedría): a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council. Origin: from G4413 (πρῶτος) and G2515 (καθέδρα); KJV: chief (highest, uppermost) seat

G4411 πρωτοκλισία (prōtoklisía): a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals. Origin: from G4413 (πρῶτος) and G2828 (κλισία); KJV: chief (highest, uppermost) room

G4412 πρῶτον (prōton): firstly (in time, place, order, or importance). Origin: neuter of G4413 (πρῶτος) as adverb (with or without G3588 (ὁ)); KJV: before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all)

G4413 πρῶτος (prōtos): foremost (in time, place, order or importance). Origin: contracted superlative of G4253 (πρό); KJV: before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former

G4414 πρωτοστάτης (prōtostátēs): one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion). Origin: from G4413 (πρῶτος) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: ringleader

G4415 πρωτοτόκια (prōtotókia): primogeniture (as a privilege). Origin: from G4416 (πρωτότοκος); KJV: birthright

G4416 πρωτότοκος (prōtótokos): first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4413 (πρῶτος) and the alternate of G5088 (τίκτω); KJV: firstbegotten(-born)

G4417 πταίω (ptaíō): to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation). Origin: a form of G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall, offend, stumble

G4418 πτέρνα (ptérna): the heel (figuratively). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: heel

G4419 πτερύγιον (pterýgion): a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4420 (πτέρυξ); KJV: pinnacle

G4420 πτέρυξ (ptéryx): a wing. Origin: from a derivative of G4072 (πέτομαι) (meaning a feather); KJV: wing

G4421 πτηνόν (ptēnón): a bird. Origin: contraction for G4071 (πετεινόν); KJV: bird

G4422 πτοέω (ptoéō): to scare. Origin: probably akin to the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω) (through the idea of causing to fall) or to G4072 (πέτομαι) (through that of causing to fly away); KJV: frighten

G4423 πτόησις (ptóēsis): alarm. Origin: from G4422 (πτοέω); KJV: amazement

G4424 Πτολεμαΐς (Ptolemaḯs): Ptolemais, a place in Palestine. Origin: from (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); KJV: Ptolemais

G4425 πτύον (ptýon): a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle). Origin: from G4429 (πτύω); KJV: fan

G4426 πτύρω (ptýrō): to frighten. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G4429 (πτύω) (and thus akin to G4422 (πτοέω)); KJV: terrify

G4427 πτύσμα (ptýsma): saliva. Origin: from G4429 (πτύω); KJV: spittle

G4428 πτύσσω (ptýssō): and thus apparently allied to G4072 (πέτομαι) through the idea of expansion, and to 4429 through that of flattening; compare G3961 (πατέω)); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll. Origin: probably akin to (to spread; KJV: close

G4429 πτύω (ptýō): to spit. Origin: a primary verb (compare G4428 (πτύσσω)); KJV: spit

G4430 πτῶμα (ptōma): a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion). Origin: from the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: dead body, carcase, corpse

G4431 πτῶσις (ptōsis): a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or figuratively). Origin: from the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω); KJV: fall

G4432 πτωχεία (ptōcheía): beggary, i.e. indigence (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4433 (πτωχεύω); KJV: poverty

G4433 πτωχεύω (ptōcheúō): to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively). Origin: from G4434 (πτωχός); KJV: become poor

G4434 πτωχός (ptōchós): akin to G4422 (πτοέω) and the alternate of G4098 (πίπτω)); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas G3993 (πένης) properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed). Origin: from (to crouch); KJV: beggar(-ly), poor

G4435 πυγμή (pygmḗ): the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing). Origin: from a primary (the fist as a weapon); KJV: oft

G4436 Πύθων (Pýthōn): a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying). Origin: from (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); KJV: divination

G4437 πυκνός (pyknós): clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently. Origin: from the same as G4635 (σκηνοποιός); KJV: often(-er)

G4438 πυκτέω (pyktéō): to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively). Origin: from a derivative of the same as G4435 (πυγμή); KJV: fight

G4439 πύλη (pýlē): a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: gate

G4440 πυλών (pylṓn): a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule. Origin: from G4439 (πύλη); KJV: gate, porch

G4441 πυνθάνομαι (pynthánomai): to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from G2065 (ἐρωτάω), which properly means a request as a favor; and from G154 (αἰτέω), which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from G2212 (ζητέω), which implies a search for something hidden; and from G1189 (δέομαι), which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence). Origin: middle voice prolonged from a primary (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); KJV: ask, demand, enquire, understand

G4442 πῦρ (pŷr): "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning). Origin: a primary word; KJV: fiery, fire

G4443 πυρά (pyrá): a fire (concretely). Origin: from G4442 (πῦρ); KJV: fire

G4444 πύργος (pýrgos): a tower or castle. Origin: apparently a primary word ("burgh"); KJV: tower

G4445 πυρέσσω (pyréssō): to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever. Origin: from G4443 (πυρά); KJV: be sick of a fever

G4446 πυρετός (pyretós): inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever). Origin: from G4445 (πυρέσσω); KJV: fever

G4447 πύρινος (pýrinos): fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming. Origin: from G4443 (πυρά); KJV: of fire

G4448 πυρόω (pyróō): to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust). Origin: from G4442 (πῦρ); KJV: burn, fiery, be on fire, try

G4449 πυῤῥάζω (pyrrházō): to redden (intransitively). Origin: from G4450 (πυῤῥός); KJV: be red

G4450 πυῤῥός (pyrrhós): fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored. Origin: from G4442 (πῦρ); KJV: red

G4451 πύρωσις (pýrōsis): ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test). Origin: from G4448 (πυρόω); KJV: burning, trial

G4452 -πω (-pō): an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the comparative. See G3369 (μηδέπω), G3380 (μήπω), G3764 (οὐδέπω), G3768 (οὔπω), G4455 (πώποτε). Origin: another form of the base of G4458 (-πώς);

G4453 πωλέω (pōléō): to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell. Origin: probably ultimately from (to be busy, to trade); KJV: sell, whatever is sold

G4454 πῶλος (pōlos): a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: colt

G4455 πώποτε (pṓpote): at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time. Origin: from G4452 (-πω) and G4218 (ποτέ); KJV: at any time, + never (…to any man), + yet, never man

G4456 πωρόω (pōróō): to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous). Origin: apparently from (a kind of stone); KJV: blind, harden

G4457 πώρωσις (pṓrōsis): stupidity or callousness. Origin: from G4456 (πωρόω); KJV: blindness, hardness

G4458 -πώς (-pṓs): an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition. Origin: adverb from the base of G4225 (πού); KJV: haply, by any (some) means, perhaps

G4459 πῶς (pōs): an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!. Origin: adverb from the base of G4226 (ποῦ); KJV: how, after (by) what manner (means), that

G4460 Ῥαάβ (Rhaáb): Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess. Origin: of Hebrew origin (G7343); KJV: Rahab

G4461 ῥαββί (rhabbí): my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7227 with pronominal suffix); KJV: Master, Rabbi

G4462 ῥαββονί (rhabboní): corresponding to G4461 (ῥαββί). Origin: of Chaldee origin; KJV: Lord, Rabboni

G4463 ῥαβδίζω (rhabdízō): to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado. Origin: from G4464 (ῥάβδος); KJV: beat (with rods)

G4464 ῥάβδος (rhábdos): a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty). Origin: from the base of G4474 (ῥαπίζω); KJV: rod, sceptre, staff

G4465 ῥαβδοῦχος (rhabdoûchos): a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner). Origin: from G4464 (ῥάβδος) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: serjeant

G4466 Ῥαγαῦ (Rhagaû): Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7466); KJV: Ragau

G4467 ῥᾳδιούργημα (rhaidioúrgēma): easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime. Origin: from a comparative of (easy, i.e. reckless) and G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: lewdness

G4468 ῥᾳδιουργία (rhaidiourgía): recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity. Origin: from the same as G4467 (ῥᾳδιούργημα); KJV: mischief

G4469 ῥακά (rhaká): O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification). Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H7386); KJV: Raca

G4470 ῥάκος (rhákos): a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth. Origin: from G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: cloth

G4471 Ῥαμᾶ (Rhamâ): Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7414); KJV: Rama

G4472 ῥαντίζω (rhantízō): to render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively). Origin: from a derivative of (to sprinkle); KJV: sprinkle

G4473 ῥαντισμός (rhantismós): aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively). Origin: from G4472 (ῥαντίζω); KJV: sprinkling
