G4474 ῥαπίζω (rhapízō): to slap. Origin: from a derivative of a primary (to let fall, "rap"); KJV: smite (with the palm of the hand)

G4475 ῥάπισμα (rhápisma): a slap. Origin: from G4474 (ῥαπίζω); KJV: (+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand

G4476 ῥαφίς (rhaphís): perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474 (ῥαπίζω) through the idea of puncturing); a needle. Origin: from a primary (to sew; KJV: needle

G4477 Ῥαχάβ (Rhacháb): Rachab, a Canaanitess. Origin: from the same as G4460 (Ῥαάβ); KJV: Rachab

G4478 Ῥαχήλ (Rhachḗl): Rachel, the wife of Jacob. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7354); KJV: Rachel

G4479 Ῥεβέκκα (Rhebékka): Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7259); KJV: Rebecca

G4480 ῥέδα (rhéda): a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: chariot

G4481 Ῥεμφάν (Rhemphán): Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol. Origin: by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (H3594); KJV: Remphan

G4482 ῥέω (rhéō): for some tenses of which a prolonged form is used to flow ("run"; as water). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: flow

G4483 ῥέω (rhéō): to utter, i.e. speak or say. Origin: perhaps akin (or identical) with G4482 (ῥέω) (through the idea of pouring forth); KJV: command, make, say, speak (of)

G4484 Ῥήγιον (Rhḗgion): Rhegium, a place in Italy. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Rhegium

G4485 ῥῆγμα (rhēgma): something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall). Origin: from G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: ruin

G4486 ῥήγνυμι (rhḗgnymi): G2608 (κατάγνυμι) being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and G2352 (θραύω) a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like G3089 (λύω)) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions. Origin: both prolonged forms of (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of (see in G2608 (κατάγνυμι))) to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; KJV: break (forth), burst, rend, tear

G4487 ῥῆμα (rhēma): an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever. Origin: from G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: + evil, + nothing, saying, word

G4488 Ῥησά (Rhēsá): Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for H7509); KJV: Rhesa

G4489 ῥήτωρ (rhḗtōr): a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate. Origin: from G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: orator

G4490 ῥητῶς (rhētōs): out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly. Origin: adverb from a derivative of G4483 (ῥέω); KJV: expressly

G4491 ῥίζα (rhíza): a "root" (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: root

G4492 ῥιζόω (rhizóō): to root (figuratively, become stable). Origin: from G4491 (ῥίζα); KJV: root

G4493 ῥιπή (rhipḗ): a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant). Origin: from G4496 (ῥίπτω); KJV: twinkling

G4494 ῥιπίζω (rhipízō): to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves). Origin: from a derivative of G4496 (ῥίπτω) (meaning a fan or bellows); KJV: toss

G4495 ῥιπτέω (rhiptéō): to toss up. Origin: from a derivative of G4496 (ῥίπτω); KJV: cast off

G4496 ῥίπτω (rhíptō): to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from G906 (βάλλω), which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from (see in G1614 (ἐκτείνω)), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse. Origin: a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474 (ῥαπίζω), through the idea of sudden motion); KJV: cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw

G4497 Ῥοβοάμ (Rhoboám): Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7346); KJV: Roboam

G4498 Ῥόδη (Rhódē): Rode, a servant girl. Origin: probably for rhode (a rose); KJV: Rhoda

G4499 Ῥόδος (Rhódos): Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean. Origin: probably from (a rose); KJV: Rhodes

G4500 ῥοιζηδόν (rhoizēdón): whizzingly, i.e. with a crash. Origin: adverb from a derivative of (a whir); KJV: with a great noise

G4501 ῥομφαία (rhomphaía): a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively). Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: sword

G4502 Ῥουβήν (Rhoubḗn): Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7205); KJV: Reuben

G4503 Ῥούθ (Rhoúth): Ruth, a Moabitess. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7327); KJV: Ruth

G4504 Ῥοῦφος (Rhoûphos): red; Rufus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Rufus

G4505 ῥύμη (rhýmē): an alley or avenue (as crowded). Origin: prolongation from G4506 (ῥύομαι) in its original sense; KJV: lane, street

G4506 ῥύομαι (rhýomai): compare G4511 (ῥύσις)); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue. Origin: middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to G4482 (ῥέω) (through the idea of a current; KJV: deliver(-er)

G4507 ῥυπαρία (rhyparía): dirtiness (morally). Origin: from G4508 (ῥυπαρός); KJV: turpitude

G4508 ῥυπαρός (rhyparós): dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked. Origin: from G4509 (ῥύπος); KJV: vile

G4509 ῥύπος (rhýpos): dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: filth

G4510 ῥυπόω (rhypóō): to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally). Origin: from G4509 (ῥύπος); KJV: be filthy

G4511 ῥύσις (rhýsis): a flux (of blood). Origin: from G4506 (ῥύομαι) in the sense of its congener G4482 (ῥέω); KJV: issue

G4512 ῥυτίς (rhytís): a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face). Origin: from G4506 (ῥύομαι); KJV: wrinkle

G4513 Ῥωμαϊκός (Rhōmaïkós): Romaic, i.e. Latin. Origin: from G4514 (Ῥωμαῖος); KJV: Latin

G4514 Ῥωμαῖος (Rhōmaîos): Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun). Origin: from G4516 (Ῥώμη); KJV: Roman, of Rome

G4515 Ῥωμαϊστί (Rhōmaïstí): Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language. Origin: adverb from a presumed derivative of G4516 (Ῥώμη); KJV: Latin

G4516 Ῥώμη (Rhṓmē): strength; Roma, the capital of Italy. Origin: from the base of G4517 (ῥώννυμι); KJV: Rome

G4517 ῥώννυμι (rhṓnnymi): probably akin to G4506 (ῥύομαι)); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye). Origin: prolongation from (to dart; KJV: farewell

G4518 σαβαχθάνι (sabachtháni): thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress. Origin: of Chaldee or (H7662 with pronominal suffix); KJV: sabachthani

G4519 σαβαώθ (sabaṓth): armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6635 in feminine plural); KJV: sabaoth

G4520 σαββατισμός (sabbatismós): a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven). Origin: from a derivative of G4521 (σάββατον); KJV: rest

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4521 to G4661
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4521 σάββατον (sábbaton): the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7676); KJV: sabbath (day), week

G4522 σαγήνη (sagḗnē): a "seine" for fishing. Origin: from a derivative of (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); KJV: net

G4523 Σαδδουκαῖος (Saddoukaîos): a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite. Origin: probably from G4524 (Σαδώκ); KJV: Sadducee

G4524 Σαδώκ (Sadṓk): Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6659); KJV: Sadoc

G4525 σαίνω (saínō): to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb). Origin: akin to G4579 (σείω); KJV: move

G4526 σάκκος (sákkos): "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8242); KJV: sackcloth

G4527 Σαλά (Salá): Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7974); KJV: Sala

G4528 Σαλαθιήλ (Salathiḗl): Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7597); KJV: Salathiel

G4529 Σαλαμίς (Salamís): Salamis, a place in Cyprus. Origin: probably from G4535 (σάλος) (from the surge on the shore); KJV: Salamis

G4530 Σαλείμ (Saleím): Salim, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from the same as G4531 (σαλεύω); KJV: Salim

G4531 σαλεύω (saleúō): to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite. Origin: from G4535 (σάλος); KJV: move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up

G4532 Σαλήμ (Salḗm): Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8004); KJV: Salem

G4533 Σαλμών (Salmṓn): Salmon, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8012); KJV: Salmon

G4534 Σαλμώνη (Salmṓnē): Salmone, a place in Crete. Origin: perhaps of similar origin to G4529 (Σαλαμίς); KJV: Salmone

G4535 σάλος (sálos): a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow. Origin: probably from the base of G4525 (σαίνω); KJV: wave

G4536 σάλπιγξ (sálpinx): a trumpet. Origin: perhaps from G4535 (σάλος) (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); KJV: trump(-et)

G4537 σαλπίζω (salpízō): to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4536 (σάλπιγξ); KJV: (which are yet to) sound (a trumpet)

G4538 σαλπιστής (salpistḗs): a trumpeter. Origin: from G4537 (σαλπίζω); KJV: trumpeter

G4539 Σαλώμη (Salṓmē): Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from H7965); KJV: Salome

G4540 Σαμάρεια (Samáreia): Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8111); KJV: Samaria

G4541 Σαμαρείτης (Samareítēs): a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria. Origin: from G4540 (Σαμάρεια); KJV: Samaritan

G4542 Σαμαρεῖτις (Samareîtis): a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria. Origin: feminine of G4541 (Σαμαρείτης); KJV: of Samaria

G4543 Σαμοθρᾴκη (Samothráikē): Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean. Origin: from G4544 (Σάμος) and (Thrace); KJV: Samothracia

G4544 Σάμος (Sámos): Samus, an island of the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: Samos

G4545 Σαμουήλ (Samouḗl): Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8050); KJV: Samuel

G4546 Σαμψών (Sampsṓn): Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8123); KJV: Samson

G4547 σανδάλιον (sandálion): of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad. Origin: neuter of a derivative of (a "sandal"; KJV: sandal

G4548 σανίς (sanís): a plank. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: board

G4549 Σαούλ (Saoúl): Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7586); KJV: Saul

G4550 σαπρός (saprós): rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally). Origin: from G4595 (σήπω); KJV: bad, corrupt

G4551 Σαπφείρη (Sappheírē): Sapphire, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine of G4552 (σάπφειρος); KJV: Sapphira

G4552 σάπφειρος (sáppheiros): a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5601); KJV: sapphire

G4553 σαργάνη (sargánē): a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work. Origin: apparently of Hebrew origin (H8276); KJV: basket

G4554 Σάρδεις (Sárdeis): Sardis, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: plural of uncertain derivation; KJV: Sardis

G4555 σάρδινος (sárdinos): sardine (G3037 (λίθος) being implied), i.e. a gem, so called. Origin: from the same as G4556 (σάρδιος); KJV: sardine

G4556 σάρδιος (sárdios): sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called. Origin: properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; KJV: sardius

G4557 σαρδόνυξ (sardónyx): hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called. Origin: from the base of G4556 (σάρδιος) and (the nail of a finger; KJV: sardonyx

G4558 Σάρεπτα (Sárepta): Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6886); KJV: Sarepta

G4559 σαρκικός (sarkikós): pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate. Origin: from G4561 (σάρξ); KJV: carnal, fleshly

G4560 σάρκινος (sárkinos): similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft. Origin: from G4561 (σάρξ); KJV: fleshly

G4561 σάρξ (sárx): flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such). Origin: probably from the base of G4563 (σαρόω); KJV: carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly)

G4562 Σαρούχ (Saroúch): Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8286); KJV: Saruch

G4563 σαρόω (saróō): akin to G4951 (σύρω)); meaning a broom; to sweep. Origin: from a derivative of (to brush off; KJV: sweep

G4564 Σάῤῥα (Sárrha): Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8283); KJV: Sara, Sarah

G4565 Σάρων (Sárōn): Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8289); KJV: Saron

G4566 Σατᾶν (Satân): Satan, i.e. the devil. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7854); KJV: Satan

G4567 Σατανᾶς (Satanâs): the accuser, i.e. the devil. Origin: of Chaldee origin corresponding to H4566 (with the definite affix); KJV: Satan

G4568 σάτον (sáton): a certain measure for things dry. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5429); KJV: measure

G4569 Σαῦλος (Saûlos): Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul. Origin: of Hebrew origin, the same as G4549 (Σαούλ); KJV: Saul

G4570 σβέννυμι (sbénnymi): to extinguish (literally or figuratively). Origin: a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; KJV: go out, quench

G4571 σέ (sé): thee. Origin: accusative case singular of G4771 (σύ); KJV: thee, thou, X thy house

G4572 σεαυτοῦ (seautoû): of (with, to) thyself. Origin: genitive case from G4571 (σέ) and G846 (αὐτός), also dative case of the same, , and accusative case , likewise contracted , , and , respectively; KJV: thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self)

G4573 σεβάζομαι (sebázomai): to venerate, i.e. adore. Origin: middle voice from a derivative of G4576 (σέβομαι); KJV: worship

G4574 σέβασμα (sébasma): something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc). Origin: from G4573 (σεβάζομαι); KJV: devotion, that is worshipped

G4575 σεβαστός (sebastós): venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial. Origin: from G4573 (σεβάζομαι); KJV: Augustus(-')

G4576 σέβομαι (sébomai): to revere, i.e. adore. Origin: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; KJV: devout, religious, worship

G4577 σειρά (seirá): akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι)); a chain (as binding or drawing). Origin: probably from G4951 (σύρω) through its congener (to fasten; KJV: chain

G4578 σεισμός (seismós): a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake. Origin: from G4579 (σείω); KJV: earthquake, tempest

G4579 σείω (seíō): to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: move, quake, shake

G4580 Σεκοῦνδος (Sekoûndos): "second"; Secundus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Secundus

G4581 Σελεύκεια (Seleúkeia): Seleuceia, a place in Syria. Origin: from (Seleucus, a Syrian king); KJV: Seleucia

G4582 σελήνη (selḗnē): probably akin to the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι), through the idea of attractiveness); the moon. Origin: from (brilliancy; KJV: moon

G4583 σεληνιάζομαι (selēniázomai): to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy. Origin: middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of G4582 (σελήνη); KJV: be a lunatic

G4584 Σεμεΐ (Semeḯ): Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8096); KJV: Semei

G4585 σεμίδαλις (semídalis): fine wheaten flour. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: fine flour

G4586 σεμνός (semnós): venerable, i.e. honorable. Origin: from G4576 (σέβομαι); KJV: grave, honest

G4587 σεμνότης (semnótēs): venerableness, i.e. probity. Origin: from G4586 (σεμνός); KJV: gravity, honesty

G4588 Σέργιος (Sérgios): Sergius, a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Sergius

G4589 Σήθ (Sḗth): Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8352); KJV: Seth

G4590 Σήμ (Sḗm): Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8035); KJV: Sem

G4591 σημαίνω (sēmaínō): of uncertain derivation); to indicate. Origin: from (a mark; KJV: signify

G4592 σημεῖον (sēmeîon): an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4591 (σημαίνω); KJV: miracle, sign, token, wonder

G4593 σημειόω (sēmeióō): to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance). Origin: from G4592 (σημεῖον); KJV: note

G4594 σήμερον (sḗmeron): on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto). Origin: neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article G3588 (ὁ) (t changed to s) and G2250 (ἡμέρα); KJV: this (to-)day

G4595 σήπω (sḗpō): to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: be corrupted

G4596 σηρικός (sērikós): hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric). Origin: from (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; KJV: silk

G4597 σής (sḗs): a moth. Origin: apparently of Hebrew origin (H5580); KJV: moth

G4598 σητόβρωτος (sētóbrōtos): moth-eaten. Origin: from G4597 (σής) and a derivative of G977 (βιβρώσκω); KJV: motheaten

G4599 σθενόω (sthenóō): probably akin to the base of G2476 (ἵστημι)); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power). Origin: from (bodily vigor; KJV: strengthen

G4600 σιαγών (siagṓn): the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: cheek

G4601 σιγάω (sigáō): to keep silent (transitively or intransitively). Origin: from G4602 (σιγή); KJV: keep close (secret, silence), hold peace

G4602 σιγή (sigḗ): silence. Origin: apparently from (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); KJV: silence

G4603 σιδήρεος (sidḗreos): made of iron. Origin: from G4604 (σίδηρος); KJV: (of) iron

G4604 σίδηρος (sídēros): iron. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: iron

G4605 Σιδών (Sidṓn): Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6721); KJV: Sidon

G4606 Σιδώνιος (Sidṓnios): a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon. Origin: from G4605 (Σιδών); KJV: of Sidon

G4607 σικάριος (sikários): a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: murderer

G4608 σίκερα (síkera): an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7941); KJV: strong drink

G4609 Σίλας (Sílas): Silas, a Christian. Origin: contraction for G4610 (Σιλουανός); KJV: Silas

G4610 Σιλουανός (Silouanós): "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Silvanus

G4611 Σιλωάμ (Silōám): Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7975); KJV: Siloam

G4612 σιμικίνθιον (simikínthion): a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: apron

G4613 Σίμων (Símōn): Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8095); KJV: Simon

G4614 Σινᾶ (Sinâ): Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5514); KJV: Sina

G4615 σίναπι (sínapi): mustard (the plant). Origin: perhaps from (to hurt, i.e. sting); KJV: mustard

G4616 σινδών (sindṓn): byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it). Origin: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; KJV: (fine) linen (cloth)

G4617 σινιάζω (siniázō): to riddle (figuratively). Origin: from (a sieve); KJV: sift

G4618 σιτευτός (siteutós): grain-fed, i.e. fattened. Origin: from a derivative of G4621 (σῖτος); KJV: fatted

G4619 σιτιστός (sitistós): grained, i.e. fatted. Origin: from a derivative of G4621 (σῖτος); KJV: fatling

G4620 σιτόμετρον (sitómetron): a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food). Origin: from G4621 (σῖτος) and G3358 (μέτρον); KJV: portion of meat

G4621 σῖτος (sîtos): grain, especially wheat. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: corn, wheat

G4622 Σιών (Siṓn): Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant). Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6726); KJV: Sion

G4623 σιωπάω (siōpáō): properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602 (σιγή), which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water). Origin: from (silence, i.e. a hush; KJV: dumb, (hold) peace

G4624 σκανδαλίζω (skandalízō): to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure). Origin: from G4625 (σκάνδαλον); KJV: (make to) offend

G4625 σκάνδαλον (skándalon): a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin). Origin: ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of G2578 (κάμπτω); KJV: occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock

G4626 σκάπτω (skáptō): to dig. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: dig

G4627 σκάφη (skáphē): a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing). KJV: boat

G4628 σκέλος (skélos): through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank). Origin: apparently from (to parch; KJV: leg

G4629 σκέπασμα (sképasma): perhaps akin to the base of G4649 (σκοπός) through the idea of noticeableness); clothing. Origin: from a derivative of (a covering; KJV: raiment

G4630 Σκευᾶς (Skeuâs): left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite. Origin: apparently of Latin origin; KJV: Sceva

G4631 σκευή (skeuḗ): furniture, i.e. spare tackle. Origin: from G4632 (σκεῦος); KJV: tackling

G4632 σκεῦος (skeûos): a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: goods, sail, stuff, vessel

G4633 σκηνή (skēnḗ): a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently akin to G4632 (σκεῦος) and G4639 (σκιά); KJV: habitation, tabernacle

G4634 σκηνοπηγία (skēnopēgía): the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes). Origin: from G4636 (σκῆνος) and G4078 (πήγνυμι); KJV: tabernacles

G4635 σκηνοποιός (skēnopoiós): a manufacturer of tents. Origin: from G4633 (σκηνή) and G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: tent-maker

G4636 σκῆνος (skēnos): a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit). Origin: from G4633 (σκηνή); KJV: tabernacle

G4637 σκηνόω (skēnóō): to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion). Origin: from G4636 (σκῆνος); KJV: dwell

G4638 σκήνωμα (skḗnōma): an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul). Origin: from G4637 (σκηνόω); KJV: tabernacle

G4639 σκιά (skiá): "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: shadow

G4640 σκιρτάω (skirtáō): to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus). Origin: akin to (to skip); KJV: leap (for joy)

G4641 σκληροκαρδία (sklērokardía): hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception. Origin: feminine of a compound of G4642 (σκληρός) and G2588 (καρδία); KJV: hardness of heart

G4642 σκληρός (sklērós): dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe). Origin: from the base of G4628 (σκέλος); KJV: fierce, hard

G4643 σκληρότης (sklērótēs): callousness, i.e. (figuratively) stubbornness. Origin: from G4642 (σκληρός); KJV: hardness

G4644 σκληροτράχηλος (sklērotráchēlos): hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate. Origin: from G4642 (σκληρός) and G5137 (τράχηλος); KJV: stiffnecked

G4645 σκληρύνω (sklērýnō): to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn. Origin: from G4642 (σκληρός); KJV: harden

G4646 σκολιός (skoliós): warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse. Origin: from the base of G4628 (σκέλος); KJV: crooked, froward, untoward

G4647 σκόλοψ (skólops): withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability). Origin: perhaps from the base of G4628 (σκέλος) and G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: thorn

G4648 σκοπέω (skopéō): to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard. Origin: from G4649 (σκοπός); KJV: consider, take heed, look at (on), mark

G4649 σκοπός (skopós): perhaps akin to G4626 (σκάπτω) through the idea of concealment; compare G4629 (σκέπασμα)); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal. Origin: from (to peer about ("skeptic"); KJV: mark

G4650 σκορπίζω (skorpízō): to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal. Origin: apparently from the same as G4651 (σκορπίος) (through the idea of penetrating); KJV: disperse abroad, scatter (abroad)

G4651 σκορπίος (skorpíos): a "scorpion" (from its sting). Origin: probably from an obsolete (perhaps strengthened from the base of G4649 (σκοπός) and meaning to pierce); KJV: scorpion

G4652 σκοτεινός (skoteinós): opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted. Origin: from G4655 (σκότος); KJV: dark, full of darkness

G4653 σκοτία (skotía): dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4655 (σκότος); KJV: dark(-ness)

G4654 σκοτίζω (skotízō): to obscure (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4655 (σκότος); KJV: darken

G4655 σκότος (skótos): shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively). Origin: from the base of G4639 (σκιά); KJV: darkness

G4656 σκοτόω (skotóō): to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4655 (σκότος); KJV: be full of darkness

G4657 σκύβαλον (skýbalon): what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G1519 (εἰς) and G2965 (κύων) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: dung

G4658 Σκύθης (Skýthēs): a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Scythian

G4659 σκυθρωπός (skythrōpós): angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance. Origin: from (sullen) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: of a sad countenance

G4660 σκύλλω (skýllō): to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: trouble(self)

G4661 σκῦλον (skŷlon): something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty. Origin: neuter from G4660 (σκύλλω); KJV: spoil

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4662 to G4789
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4662 σκωληκόβρωτος (skōlēkóbrōtos): worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots. Origin: from G4663 (σκώληξ) and a derivative of G977 (βιβρώσκω); KJV: eaten of worms

G4663 σκώληξ (skṓlēx): a grub, maggot or earth-worm. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: worm

G4664 σμαράγδινος (smarágdinos): consisting of emerald. Origin: from G4665 (σμάραγδος); KJV: emerald

G4665 σμάραγδος (smáragdos): the emerald or green gem so called. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: emerald

G4666 σμύρνα (smýrna): myrrh. Origin: apparently strengthened for G3464 (μύρον); KJV: myrrh

G4667 Σμύρνα (Smýrna): Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: the same as G4666 (σμύρνα); KJV: Smyrna

G4668 Σμυρναῖος (Smyrnaîos): a Smyrnæan. Origin: from G4667 (Σμύρνα); KJV: in Smyrna

G4669 σμυρνίζω (smyrnízō): to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic). Origin: from G4667 (Σμύρνα); KJV: mingle with myrrh

G4670 Σόδομα (Sódoma): Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of Hebrew origin (H5467); KJV: Sodom

G4671 σοί (soí): to thee. Origin: dative case of G4771 (σύ); KJV: thee, thine own, thou, thy

G4672 Σολομών (Solomṓn): Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8010); KJV: Solomon

G4673 σορός (sorós): a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier. Origin: probably akin to the base of G4987 (σωρεύω); KJV: bier

G4674 σός (sós): thine. Origin: from G4771 (σύ); KJV: thine (own), thy (friend)

G4675 σοῦ (soû): of thee, thy. Origin: genitive case of G4771 (σύ); KJV: X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy

G4676 σουδάριον (soudárion): a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: handkerchief, napkin

G4677 Σουσάννα (Sousánna): lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7799 feminine); KJV: Susanna

G4678 σοφία (sophía): wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual). Origin: from G4680 (σοφός); KJV: wisdom

G4679 σοφίζω (sophízō): to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error. Origin: from G4680 (σοφός); KJV: cunningly devised, make wise

G4680 σοφός (sophós): wise (in a most general application). Origin: akin to (clear); KJV: wise

G4681 Σπανία (Spanía): Spania, a region of Europe. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Spain

G4682 σπαράσσω (sparássō): apparently strengthened from G4685 (σπάω) through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy. Origin: prolongation from (to grasp; KJV: rend, tear

G4683 σπαργανόω (sparganóō): from a derivative of the base of G4682 (σπαράσσω) meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom). Origin: from (a strip; KJV: wrap in swaddling clothes

G4684 σπαταλάω (spataláō): to be voluptuous. Origin: from (luxury); KJV: live in pleasure, be wanton

G4685 σπάω (spáō): to draw. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: draw (out)

G4686 σπεῖρα (speîra): a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors). Origin: of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of G138 (αἱρέομαι) in the sense of its cognate G1507 (εἱλίσσω); KJV: band

G4687 σπείρω (speírō): to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively). Origin: probably strengthened from G4685 (σπάω) (through the idea of extending); KJV: sow(- er), receive seed

G4688 σπεκουλάτωρ (spekoulátōr): a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: executioner

G4689 σπένδω (spéndō): to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: (be ready to) be offered

G4690 σπέρμα (spérma): something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting). Origin: from G4687 (σπείρω); KJV: issue, seed

G4691 σπερμολόγος (spermológos): a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk). Origin: from G4690 (σπέρμα) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: babbler

G4692 σπεύδω (speúdō): to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly. Origin: probably strengthened from G4228 (πούς); KJV: (make, with) haste unto

G4693 σπήλαιον (spḗlaion): a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a grotto); KJV: cave, den

G4694 σπιλάς (spilás): a ledge or reef of rock in the sea. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: spot (by confusion with G4696 (σπίλος))

G4695 σπιλόω (spilóō): to stain or soil (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4696 (σπίλος); KJV: defile, spot

G4696 σπίλος (spílos): a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: spot

G4697 σπλαγχνίζομαι (splanchnízomai): to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity. Origin: middle voice from G4698 (σπλάγχνον); KJV: have (be moved with) compassion

G4698 σπλάγχνον (splánchnon): an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy. Origin: probably strengthened from (the "spleen"); KJV: bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy

G4699 σπόγγος (spóngos): a "sponge". Origin: perhaps of foreign origin; KJV: spunge

G4700 σποδός (spodós): ashes. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: ashes

G4701 σπορά (sporá): a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage. Origin: from G4687 (σπείρω); KJV: seed

G4702 σπόριμος (spórimos): sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field. Origin: from G4703 (σπόρος); KJV: corn(-field)

G4703 σπόρος (spóros): a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown). Origin: from G4687 (σπείρω); KJV: seed (X sown)

G4704 σπουδάζω (spoudázō): to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest. Origin: from G4710 (σπουδή); KJV: do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study

G4705 σπουδαῖος (spoudaîos): prompt, energetic, earnest. Origin: from G4710 (σπουδή); KJV: diligent

G4706 σπουδαιότερον (spoudaióteron): more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly. Origin: neuter of G4707 (σπουδαιότερος) as adverb; KJV: very diligently

G4707 σπουδαιότερος (spoudaióteros): more prompt, more earnest. Origin: comparative of G4705 (σπουδαῖος); KJV: more diligent (forward)

G4708 σπουδαιοτέρως (spoudaiotérōs): more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise. Origin: adverb from G4707 (σπουδαιότερος); KJV: more carefully

G4709 σπουδαίως (spoudaíōs): earnestly, promptly. Origin: adverb from G4705 (σπουδαῖος); KJV: diligently, instantly

G4710 σπουδή (spoudḗ): "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness. Origin: from G4692 (σπεύδω); KJV: business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste

G4711 σπυρίς (spyrís): a hamper or lunch-receptacle. Origin: from G4687 (σπείρω) (as woven); KJV: basket

G4712 στάδιον (stádion): a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course. Origin: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as fixed); KJV: furlong, race

G4713 στάμνος (stámnos): a jar or earthen tank. Origin: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι) (as stationary); KJV: pot

G4714 στάσις (stásis): a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy. Origin: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar

G4715 στατήρ (statḗr): a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin. Origin: from the base of G2746 (καύχησις); KJV: piece of money

G4716 σταυρός (staurós): a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ. Origin: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: cross

G4717 σταυρόω (stauróō): to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness. Origin: from G4716 (σταυρός); KJV: crucify

G4718 σταφυλή (staphylḗ): a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined). Origin: probably from the base of G4735 (στέφανος); KJV: grapes

G4719 στάχυς (stáchys): a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk). Origin: from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: ear (of corn)

G4720 Στάχυς (Stáchys): Stachys, a Christian. Origin: the same as G4719 (στάχυς); KJV: Stachys

G4721 στέγη (stégē): a roof. Origin: strengthened from a primary (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); KJV: roof

G4722 στέγω (stégō): to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently). Origin: from G4721 (στέγη); KJV: (for-)bear, suffer

G4723 στείρος (steíros): "sterile". Origin: a contraction from G4731 (στερεός) (as stiff and unnatural); KJV: barren

G4724 στέλλω (stéllō): properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with). Origin: probably strengthened from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: avoid, withdraw self

G4725 στέμμα (stémma): a wreath for show. Origin: from the base of G4735 (στέφανος); KJV: garland

G4726 στεναγμός (stenagmós): a sigh. Origin: from G4727 (στενάζω); KJV: groaning

G4727 στενάζω (stenázō): to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly. Origin: from G4728 (στενός); KJV: with grief, groan, grudge, sigh

G4728 στενός (stenós): narrow (from obstacles standing close about). Origin: probably from the base of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: strait

G4729 στενοχωρέω (stenochōréō): to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp. Origin: from the same as G4730 (στενοχωρία); KJV: distress, straiten

G4730 στενοχωρία (stenochōría): narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity. Origin: from a compound of G4728 (στενός) and G5561 (χώρα); KJV: anguish, distress

G4731 στερεός (stereós): stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: stedfast, strong, sure

G4732 στερεόω (stereóō): to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4731 (στερεός); KJV: establish, receive strength, make strong

G4733 στερέωμα (steréōma): something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability). Origin: from G4732 (στερεόω); KJV: stedfastness

G4734 Στεφανᾶς (Stephanâs): from G4737 (στεφανόω)); Stephanas, a Christian. Origin: probably contraction for (crowned; KJV: Stephanas

G4735 στέφανος (stéphanos): a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, G1238 (διάδημα)), literally or figuratively. Origin: from an apparently primary (to twine or wreathe); KJV: crown

G4736 Στέφανος (Stéphanos): Stephanus, a Christian. Origin: the same as G4735 (στέφανος); KJV: Stephen

G4737 στεφανόω (stephanóō): to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4735 (στέφανος); KJV: crown

G4738 στῆθος (stēthos): the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest. Origin: from G2476 (ἵστημι) (as standing prominently); KJV: breast

G4739 στήκω (stḗkō): to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere. Origin: from the perfect tense of G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: stand (fast)

G4740 στηριγμός (stērigmós): stability (figuratively). Origin: from G4741 (στηρίζω); KJV: stedfastness

G4741 στηρίζω (stērízō): to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G2476 (ἵστημι) (like G4731 (στερεός)); KJV: fix, (e-)stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen

G4742 στίγμα (stígma): a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service. Origin: from a primary (to "stick", i.e. prick); KJV: mark

G4743 στιγμή (stigmḗ): a point of time, i.e. an instant. Origin: feminine of G4742 (στίγμα); KJV: moment

G4744 στίλβω (stílbō): to gleam, i.e. flash intensely. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: shining

G4745 στοά (stoá): a colonnade or interior piazza. Origin: probably from G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: porch

G4746 στοιβάς (stoibás): a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed. Origin: from a primary (to "step" or "stamp"); KJV: branch

G4747 στοιχεῖον (stoicheîon): something orderly in arrangement, i.e. (by implication) a serial (basal, fundamental, initial) constituent (literally), proposition (figuratively). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4748 (στοιχέω); KJV: element, principle, rudiment

G4748 στοιχέω (stoichéō): to march in (military) rank (keep step), i.e. (figuratively) to conform to virtue and piety. Origin: from a derivative of (to range in regular line); KJV: walk (orderly)

G4749 στολή (stolḗ): equipment, i.e. (specially), a "stole" or long-fitting gown (as a mark of dignity). Origin: from G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: long clothing (garment), (long) robe

G4750 στόμα (stóma): the mouth (as if a gash in the face); by implication, language (and its relations); figuratively, an opening (in the earth); specially, the front or edge (of a weapon). Origin: probably strengthened from a presumed derivative of the base of G5114 (τομώτερος); KJV: edge, face, mouth

G4751 στόμαχος (stómachos): an orifice (the gullet), i.e. (specially), the "stomach". Origin: from G4750 (στόμα); KJV: stomach

G4752 στρατεία (strateía): military service, i.e. (figuratively) the apostolic career (as one of hardship and danger). Origin: from G4754 (στρατεύομαι); KJV: warfare

G4753 στράτευμα (stráteuma): an armament, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops (more or less extensive or systematic). Origin: from G4754 (στρατεύομαι); KJV: army, soldier, man of war

G4754 στρατεύομαι (strateúomai): to serve in a military campaign; figuratively, to execute the apostolate (with its arduous duties and functions), to contend with carnal inclinations. Origin: middle voice from the base of G4756 (στρατιά); KJV: soldier, (go to) war(-fare)

G4755 στρατηγός (stratēgós): a general, i.e. (by implication or analogy) a (military) governor (prætor), the chief (præfect) of the (Levitical) temple-wardens. Origin: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G71 (ἄγω) or G2233 (ἡγέομαι); KJV: captain, magistrate

G4756 στρατιά (stratiá): from the base of G4766 (στρώννυμι), as encamped); camp-likeness, i.e. an army, i.e. (figuratively) the angels, the celestial luminaries. Origin: feminine of a derivative of (an army; KJV: host

G4757 στρατιώτης (stratiṓtēs): a camper-out, i.e. a (common) warrior (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a presumed derivative of the same as G4756 (στρατιά); KJV: soldier

G4758 στρατολογέω (stratologéō): to gather (or select) as a warrior, i.e. enlist in the army. Origin: from a compound of the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense); KJV: choose to be a soldier

G4759 στρατοπεδάρχης (stratopedárchēs): a ruler of an army, i.e. (specially), a Prætorian præfect. Origin: from G4760 (στρατόπεδον) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: captain of the guard

G4760 στρατόπεδον (stratópedon): a camping-ground, i.e. (by implication) a body of troops. Origin: from the base of G4756 (στρατιά) and the same as G3977 (πεδινός); KJV: army

G4761 στρεβλόω (streblóō): to wrench, i.e. (specially), to torture (by the rack), but only figuratively, to pervert. Origin: from a derivative of G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: wrest

G4762 στρέφω (stréphō): to twist, i.e. turn quite around or reverse (literally or figuratively). Origin: strengthened from the base of G5157 (τροπή); KJV: convert, turn (again, back again, self, self about)

G4763 στρηνιάω (strēniáō): to be luxurious. Origin: from a presumed derivative of G4764 (στρῆνος); KJV: live deliciously

G4764 στρῆνος (strēnos): a "straining", "strenuousness" or "strength", i.e. (figuratively) luxury (voluptuousness). Origin: akin to G4731 (στερεός); KJV: delicacy

G4765 στρουθίον (strouthíon): a little sparrow. Origin: diminutive of (a sparrow); KJV: sparrow

G4766 στρώννυμι (strṓnnymi): to "strew," i.e. spread (as a carpet or couch). Origin: prolongation from a still simpler , (used only as an alternate in certain tenses) (probably akin to G4731 (στερεός) through the idea of positing); KJV: make bed, furnish, spread, strew

G4767 στυγνητός (stygnētós): hated, i.e. odious. Origin: from a derivative of an obsolete apparently primary (to hate); KJV: hateful

G4768 στυγνάζω (stygnázō): to render gloomy, i.e. (by implication) glower (be overcast with clouds, or sombreness of speech). Origin: from the same as G4767 (στυγνητός); KJV: lower, be sad

G4769 στῦλος (stŷlos): properly akin to the base of G2476 (ἵστημι)); a post ("style"), i.e. (figuratively) support. Origin: from (to stiffen; KJV: pillar

G4770 Στωϊκός (Stōïkós): a "Stoic" (as occupying a particular porch in Athens), i.e. adherent of a certin philosophy. Origin: from G4745 (στοά); KJV: Stoick

G4771 σύ (sý): thou. Origin: the personal pronoun of the second person singular; KJV: thou

G4772 συγγένεια (syngéneia): relationship, i.e. (concretely) relatives. Origin: from G4773 (συγγενής); KJV: kindred

G4773 συγγενής (syngenḗs): a relative (by blood); by extension, a fellow countryman. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1085 (γένος); KJV: cousin, kin(-sfolk, -sman)

G4774 συγγνώμη (syngnṓmē): fellow knowledge, i.e. concession. Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G1097 (γινώσκω); KJV: permission

G4775 συγκάθημαι (synkáthēmai): to seat oneself in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2521 (κάθημαι); KJV: sit with

G4776 συγκαθίζω (synkathízō): to give (or take) a seat in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2523 (καθίζω); KJV: (make) sit (down) together

G4777 συγκακοπαθέω (synkakopathéō): to suffer hardship in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2553 (κακοπαθέω); KJV: be partaker of afflictions

G4778 συγκακουχέω (synkakouchéō): to maltreat in company with, i.e. (passively) endure persecution together. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2558 (κακουχέω); KJV: suffer affliction with

G4779 συγκαλέω (synkaléō): to convoke. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2564 (καλέω); KJV: call together

G4780 συγκαλύπτω (synkalýptō): to conceal altogether. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2572 (καλύπτω); KJV: cover

G4781 συγκάμπτω (synkámptō): to bend together, i.e. (figuratively) to afflict. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2578 (κάμπτω); KJV: bow down

G4782 συγκαταβαίνω (synkatabaínō): to descend in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2597 (καταβαίνω); KJV: go down with

G4783 συγκατάθεσις (synkatáthesis): a deposition (of sentiment) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) accord with. Origin: from G4784 (συγκατατίθεμαι); KJV: agreement

G4784 συγκατατίθεμαι (synkatatíthemai): to deposit (one's vote or opinion) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to accord with. Origin: middle from G4862 (σύν) and G2698 (κατατίθημι); KJV: consent

G4785 συγκαταψηφίζω (synkatapsēphízō): to count down in company with, i.e. enroll among. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G2596 (κατά) and G5585 (ψηφίζω); KJV: number with

G4786 συγκεράννυμι (synkeránnymi): to commingle, i.e. (figuratively) to combine or assimilate. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2767 (κεράννυμι); KJV: mix with, temper together

G4787 συγκινέω (synkinéō): to move together, i.e. (specially), to excite as a mass (to sedition). Origin: from G4682 (σπαράσσω) and G2795 (κινέω); KJV: stir up

G4788 συγκλείω (synkleíō): to shut together, i.e. include or (figuratively) embrace in a common subjection to. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2808 (κλείω); KJV: conclude, inclose, shut up

G4789 συγκληρονόμος (synklēronómos): a co-heir, i.e. (by analogy) participant in common. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2818 (κληρονόμος); KJV: fellow (joint)-heir, heir together, heir with

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4790 to G4909
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4790 συγκοινωνέω (synkoinōnéō): to share in company with, i.e. co-participate in. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2841 (κοινωνέω); KJV: communicate (have fellowship) with, be partaker of

G4791 συγκοινωνός (synkoinōnós): a co-participant. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2844 (κοινωνός); KJV: companion, partake(-r, -r with)

G4792 συγκομίζω (synkomízō): to convey together, i.e. collect or bear away in company with others. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2865 (κομίζω); KJV: carry

G4793 συγκρίνω (synkrínō): to judge of one thing in connection with another, i.e. combine (spiritual ideas with appropriate expressions) or collate (one person with another by way of contrast or resemblance). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: compare among (with)

G4794 συγκύπτω (synkýptō): to stoop altogether, i.e. be completely overcome by. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2955 (κύπτω); KJV: bow together

G4795 συγκυρία (synkyría): from the base of G2962 (κύριος)); concurrence, i.e. accident. Origin: from a comparative of G4862 (σύν) and (to light or happen; KJV: chance

G4796 συγχαίρω (synchaírō): to sympathize in gladness, congratulate. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5463 (χαίρω); KJV: rejoice in (with)

G4797 συγχέω (synchéō): to commingle promiscuously, i.e. (figuratively) to throw (an assembly) into disorder, to perplex (the mind). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to pour) or its alternate; KJV: confound, confuse, stir up, be in an uproar

G4798 συγχράομαι (synchráomai): to use jointly, i.e. (by implication) to hold intercourse in common. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5530 (χράομαι); KJV: have dealings with

G4799 σύγχυσις (sýnchysis): commixture, i.e. (figuratively) riotous disturbance. Origin: from G4797 (συγχέω); KJV: confusion

G4800 συζάω (syzáō): to continue to live in common with, i.e. co-survive (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2198 (ζάω); KJV: live with

G4801 συζεύγνυμι (syzeúgnymi): to yoke together, i.e. (figuratively) conjoin (in marriage). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2201 (ζεῦγος); KJV: join together

G4802 συζητέω (syzētéō): to investigate jointly, i.e. discuss, controvert, cavil. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2212 (ζητέω); KJV: dispute (with), enquire, question (with), reason (together)

G4803 συζήτησις (syzḗtēsis): mutual questioning, i.e. discussion. Origin: from G4802 (συζητέω); KJV: disputation(-ting), reasoning

G4804 συζητητής (syzētētḗs): a disputant, i.e. sophist. Origin: from G4802 (συζητέω); KJV: disputer

G4805 σύζυγος (sýzygos): co-yoked, i.e. (figuratively) as noun, a colleague; probably rather as a proper name; Syzygus, a Christian. Origin: from G4801 (συζεύγνυμι); KJV: yokefellow

G4806 συζωοποιέω (syzōopoiéō): to reanimate conjointly with (figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2227 (ζωοποιέω); KJV: quicken together with

G4807 συκάμινος (sykáminos): a sycamore-fig tree. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H8256) in imitation of G4809 (συκομωραία); KJV: sycamine tree

G4808 συκῆ (sykē): a fig-tree. Origin: from G4810 (σῦκον); KJV: fig tree

G4809 συκομωραία (sykomōraía): the "sycamore"-fig tree. Origin: from G4810 (σῦκον) and (the mulberry); KJV: sycamore tree

G4810 σῦκον (sŷkon): a fig. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: fig

G4811 συκοφαντέω (sykophantéō): to be a fig-informer (reporter of the law forbidding the exportation of figs from Greece), "sycophant", i.e. (genitive and by extension) to defraud (exact unlawfully, extort). Origin: from a compound of G4810 (σῦκον) and a derivative of G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: accuse falsely, take by false accusation

G4812 συλαγωγέω (sylagōgéō): to lead away as booty, i.e. (figuratively) seduce. Origin: from the base of G4813 (συλάω) and (the reduplicated form of) G71 (ἄγω); KJV: spoil

G4813 συλάω (syláō): probably akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι); compare G4661 (σκῦλον)); to despoil. Origin: from a derivative of (to strip; KJV: rob

G4814 συλλαλέω (syllaléō): to talk together, i.e. converse. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2980 (λαλέω); KJV: commune (confer, talk) with, speak among

G4815 συλλαμβάνω (syllambánō): to clasp, i.e. seize (arrest, capture); specially, to conceive (literally or figuratively); by implication, to aid. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: catch, conceive, help, take

G4816 συλλέγω (syllégō): to collect. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3004 (λέγω) in its original sense; KJV: gather (together, up)

G4817 συλλογίζομαι (syllogízomai): to reckon together (with oneself), i.e. deliberate. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3049 (λογίζομαι); KJV: reason with

G4818 συλλυπέω (syllypéō): to afflict jointly, i.e. (passive) sorrow at (on account of) someone. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3076 (λυπέω); KJV: be grieved

G4819 συμβαίνω (symbaínō): to walk (figuratively, transpire) together, i.e. concur (take place). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: be(-fall), happen (unto)

G4820 συμβάλλω (symbállō): to combine, i.e. (in speaking) to converse, consult, dispute, (mentally) to consider, (by implication) to aid, (personally) to join, attack. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: confer, encounter, help, make, meet with, ponder

G4821 συμβασιλεύω (symbasileúō): to be co-regent (figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G936 (βασιλεύω); KJV: reign with

G4822 συμβιβάζω (symbibázō): causative (by reduplication) of the base of G939 (βάσις)); to drive together, i.e. unite (in association or affection), (mentally) to infer, show, teach. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to force; KJV: compact, assuredly gather, intrust, knit together, prove

G4823 συμβουλεύω (symbouleúō): to give (or take) advice jointly, i.e. recommend, deliberate or determine. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1011 (βουλεύω); KJV: consult, (give, take) counsel (together)

G4824 συμβούλιον (symboúlion): advisement; specially, a deliberative body, i.e. the provincial assessors or lay-court. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G4825 (σύμβουλος); KJV: consultation, counsel, council

G4825 σύμβουλος (sýmboulos): a consultor, i.e. adviser. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1012 (βουλή); KJV: counsellor

G4826 Συμεών (Symeṓn): Symeon (i.e. Shimon), the name of five Israelites. Origin: from the same as G4613 (Σίμων); KJV: Simeon, Simon

G4827 συμμαθητής (symmathētḗs): a co-learner (of Christianity). Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3129 (μανθάνω); KJV: fellow disciple

G4828 συμμαρτυρέω (symmartyréō): to testify jointly, i.e. corroborate by (concurrent) evidence. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3140 (μαρτυρέω); KJV: testify unto, (also) bear witness (with)

G4829 συμμερίζομαι (symmerízomai): to share jointly, i.e. participate in. Origin: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and G3307 (μερίζω); KJV: be partaker with

G4830 συμμέτοχος (symmétochos): a co-participant. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3353 (μέτοχος); KJV: partaker

G4831 συμμιμητής (symmimētḗs): a co-imitator, i.e. fellow votary. Origin: from a presumed compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3401 (μιμέομαι); KJV: follower together

G4832 σύμμορφος (sýmmorphos): jointly formed, i.e. (figuratively) similar. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3444 (μορφή); KJV: conformed to, fashioned like unto

G4833 συμμορφόω (symmorphóō): to render like, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate. Origin: from G4832 (σύμμορφος); KJV: make conformable unto

G4834 συμπαθέω (sympathéō): to feel "sympathy" with, i.e. (by implication) to commiserate. Origin: from G4835 (συμπαθής); KJV: have compassion, be touched with a feeling of

G4835 συμπαθής (sympathḗs): having a fellow-feeling ("sympathetic"), i.e. (by implication) mutually commiserative. Origin: from G4841 (συμπάσχω); KJV: having compassion one of another

G4836 συμπαραγίνομαι (symparagínomai): to be present together, i.e. to convene; by implication, to appear in aid. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3854 (παραγίνομαι); KJV: come together, stand with

G4837 συμπαρακαλέω (symparakaléō): to console jointly. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3870 (παρακαλέω); KJV: comfort together

G4838 συμπαραλαμβάνω (symparalambánō): to take along in company. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3880 (παραλαμβάνω); KJV: take with

G4839 συμπαραμένω (symparaménō): to remain in company, i.e. still live. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3887 (παραμένω); KJV: continue with

G4840 συμπάρειμι (sympáreimi): to be at hand together, i.e. now present. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3918 (πάρειμι); KJV: be here present with

G4841 συμπάσχω (sympáschō): to experience pain jointly or of the same kind (specially, persecution; to "sympathize"). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3958 (πάσχω) (including its alternate); KJV: suffer with

G4842 συμπέμπω (sympémpō): to despatch in company. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3992 (πέμπω); KJV: send with

G4843 συμπεριλαμβάνω (symperilambánō): to take by enclosing altogether, i.e. earnestly throw the arms about one. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G4012 (περί) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: embrace

G4844 συμπίνω (sympínō): to partake a beverage in company. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4095 (πίνω); KJV: drink with

G4845 συμπληρόω (symplēróō): to implenish completely, i.e. (of space) to swamp (a boat), or (of time) to accomplish (passive, be complete). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4137 (πληρόω); KJV: (fully) come, fill up

G4846 συμπνίγω (sympnígō): to strangle completely, i.e. (literally) to drown, or (figuratively) to crowd. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4155 (πνίγω); KJV: choke, throng

G4847 συμπολίτης (sympolítēs): a native of the same town, i.e. (figuratively) co-religionist (fellow-Christian). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4177 (πολίτης); KJV: fellow- citizen

G4848 συμπορεύομαι (symporeúomai): to journey together; by implication, to assemble. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4198 (πορεύομαι); KJV: go with, resort

G4849 συμπόσιον (sympósion): a drinking-party ("symposium"), i.e. (by extension) a room of guests. Origin: neuter of a derivative of the alternate of G4844 (συμπίνω); KJV: company

G4850 συμπρεσβύτερος (sympresbýteros): a co-presbyter. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4245 (πρεσβύτερος); KJV: presbyter, also an elder

G4851 συμφέρω (symphérō): to bear together (contribute), i.e. (literally) to collect, or (figuratively) to conduce; especially (neuter participle as a noun) advantage. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5342 (φέρω) (including its alternate); KJV: be better for, bring together, be expedient (for), be good, (be) profit(-able for)

G4852 σύμφημι (sýmphēmi): to say jointly, i.e. assent to. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5346 (φημί); KJV: consent unto

G4853 συμφυλέτης (symphylétēs): a co-tribesman, i.e. native of the same country. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G5443 (φυλή); KJV: countryman

G4854 σύμφυτος (sýmphytos): grown along with (connate), i.e. (figuratively) closely united to. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω); KJV: planted together

G4855 συμφύω (symphýō): passive, to grow jointly. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5453 (φύω); KJV: spring up with

G4856 συμφωνέω (symphōnéō): to be harmonious, i.e. (figuratively) to accord (be suitable, concur) or stipulate (by compact). Origin: from G4859 (σύμφωνος); KJV: agree (together, with)

G4857 συμφώνησις (symphṓnēsis): accordance. Origin: from G4856 (συμφωνέω); KJV: concord

G4858 συμφωνία (symphōnía): unison of sound ("symphony"), i.e. a concert of instruments (harmonious note). Origin: from G4859 (σύμφωνος); KJV: music

G4859 σύμφωνος (sýmphōnos): sounding together (alike), i.e. (figuratively) accordant (neuter as noun, agreement). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5456 (φωνή); KJV: consent

G4860 συμψηφίζω (sympsēphízō): to compute jointly. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5585 (ψηφίζω); KJV: reckon

G4861 σύμψυχος (sýmpsychos): co-spirited, i.e. similar in sentiment. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5590 (ψυχή); KJV: like-minded

G4862 σύν (sýn): with or together (but much closer than G3326 (μετά) or G3844 (παρά)), i.e. by association, companionship, process, resemblance, possession, instrumentality, addition, etc. Origin: a primary preposition denoting union; KJV: beside, with

G4863 συνάγω (synágō): to lead together, i.e. collect or convene; specially, to entertain (hospitably). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: + accompany, assemble (selves, together), bestow, come together, gather (selves together, up, together), lead into, resort, take in

G4864 συναγωγή (synagōgḗ): an assemblage of persons; specially, a Jewish "synagogue" (the meeting or the place); by analogy, a Christian church. Origin: from (the reduplicated form of) G4863 (συνάγω); KJV: assembly, congregation, synagogue

G4865 συναγωνίζομαι (synagōnízomai): to struggle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to be a partner (assistant). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G75 (ἀγωνίζομαι); KJV: strive together with

G4866 συναθλέω (synathléō): to wrestle in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to seek jointly. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G118 (ἀθλέω); KJV: labour with, strive together for

G4867 συναθροίζω (synathroízō): to convene. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to hoard); KJV: call (gather) together

G4868 συναίρω (synaírō): to make up together, i.e. (figuratively) to compute (an account). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G142 (αἴρω); KJV: reckon, take

G4869 συναιχμάλωτος (synaichmálōtos): a co-captive. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G164 (αἰχμάλωτος); KJV: fellowprisoner

G4870 συνακολουθέω (synakolouthéō): to accompany. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G190 (ἀκολουθέω); KJV: follow

G4871 συναλίζω (synalízō): to accumulate, i.e. convene. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to throng); KJV: assemble together

G4872 συναναβαίνω (synanabaínō): to ascend in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G305 (ἀναβαίνω); KJV: come up with

G4873 συνανάκειμαι (synanákeimai): to recline in company with (at a meal). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G345 (ἀνακεῖμαι); KJV: sit (down, at the table, together) with (at meat)

G4874 συναναμίγνυμι (synanamígnymi): to mix up together, i.e. (figurative) associate with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a compound of G303 (ἀνά) and G3396 (μίγνυμι); KJV: (have, keep) company (with)

G4875 συναναπαύομαι (synanapaúomai): to recruit oneself in company with. Origin: middle from G4862 (σύν) and G373 (ἀναπαύω); KJV: refresh with

G4876 συναντάω (synantáō): to meet with; figuratively, to occur. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί); KJV: befall, meet

G4877 συνάντησις (synántēsis): a meeting with. Origin: from G4876 (συναντάω); KJV: meet

G4878 συναντιλαμβάνομαι (synantilambánomai): to take hold of opposite together, i.e. co-operate (assist). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G482 (ἀντιλαμβάνομαι); KJV: help

G4879 συναπάγω (synapágō): to take off together, i.e. transport with (seduce, passively, yield). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G520 (ἀπάγω); KJV: carry (lead) away with, condescend

G4880 συναποθνήσκω (synapothnḗskō): to decease (literally) in company with, or (figuratively), similarly to. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G599 (ἀποθνήσκω); KJV: be dead (die) with

G4881 συναπόλλυμι (synapóllymi): to destroy (middle voice or passively, be slain) in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G622 (ἀπόλλυμι); KJV: perish with

G4882 συναποστέλλω (synapostéllō): to despatch (on an errand) in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G649 (ἀποστέλλω); KJV: send with

G4883 συναρμολογέω (synarmologéō): to render close-jointed together, i.e. organize compactly. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of G719 (ἁρμός) and G3004 (λέγω) (in its original sense of laying); KJV: be fitly framed (joined) together

G4884 συναρπάζω (synarpázō): to snatch together, i.e. seize. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G726 (ἁρπάζω); KJV: catch

G4885 συναυξάνω (synauxánō): to increase (grow up) together. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G837 (αὐξάνω); KJV: grow together

G4886 σύνδεσμος (sýndesmos): a joint tie, i.e. ligament, (figuratively) uniting principle, control. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1199 (δεσμόν); KJV: band, bond

G4887 συνδέω (syndéō): to bind with, i.e. (passively) be a fellow-prisoner (figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1210 (δέω); KJV: be bound with

G4888 συνδοξάζω (syndoxázō): to exalt to dignity in company (i.e. similarly) with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1392 (δοξάζω); KJV: glorify together

G4889 σύνδουλος (sýndoulos): a co-slave, i.e. servitor or ministrant of the same master (human or divine). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1401 (δοῦλος); KJV: fellowservant

G4890 συνδρομή (syndromḗ): a running together, i.e. (riotous) concourse. Origin: from (the alternate of) G4936 (συντρέχω); KJV: run together

G4891 συνεγείρω (synegeírō): to rouse (from death) in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to revivify (spirtually) in resemblance to. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1453 (ἐγείρω); KJV: raise up together, rise with

G4892 συνέδριον (synédrion): a joint session, i.e. (specially), the Jewish Sanhedrin; by analogy, a subordinate tribunal. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G1476 (ἑδραῖος); KJV: council

G4893 συνείδησις (syneídēsis): co-perception, i.e. moral consciousness. Origin: from a prolonged form of G4894 (συνείδω); KJV: conscience

G4894 συνείδω (syneídō): to see completely; used (like its primary) only in two past tenses, respectively meaning to understand or become aware, and to be conscious or (clandestinely) informed of. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: consider, know, be privy, be ware of

G4895 σύνειμι (sýneimi): to be in company with, i.e. present at the time. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1510 (εἰμί) (including its various inflections); KJV: be with

G4896 σύνειμι (sýneimi): to assemble. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to go); KJV: gather together

G4897 συνεισέρχομαι (syneisérchomai): to enter in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1525 (εἰσέρχομαι); KJV: go in with, go with into

G4898 συνέκδημος (synékdēmos): a co-absentee from home, i.e. fellow-traveller. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G1553 (ἐκδημέω); KJV: companion in travel, travel with

G4899 συνεκλεκτός (syneklektós): chosen in company with, i.e. co-elect (fellow Christian). Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G1586 (ἐκλέγομαι); KJV: elected together with

G4900 συνελαύνω (synelaúnō): to drive together, i.e. (figuratively) exhort (to reconciliation). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1643 (ἐλαύνω); KJV: + set at one again

G4901 συνεπιμαρτυρέω (synepimartyréō): to testify further jointly, i.e. unite in adding evidence. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G1957 (ἐπιμαρτυρέω); KJV: also bear witness

G4902 συνέπομαι (synépomai): to attend (travel) in company with. Origin: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and a primary (to follow); KJV: accompany

G4903 συνεργέω (synergéō): to be a fellow-worker, i.e. co-operate. Origin: from G4904 (συνεργός); KJV: help (work) with, work(-er) together

G4904 συνεργός (synergós): a co-laborer, i.e. coadjutor. Origin: from a presumed compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: companion in labour, (fellow-)helper(-labourer, -worker), labourer together with, workfellow

G4905 συνέρχομαι (synérchomai): to convene, depart in company with, associate with, or (specially), cohabit (conjugally). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2064 (ἔρχομαι); KJV: accompany, assemble (with), come (together), come (company, go) with, resort

G4906 συνεσθίω (synesthíō): to take food in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2068 (ἐσθίω) (including its alternate); KJV: eat with

G4907 σύνεσις (sýnesis): a mental putting together, i.e. intelligence or (concretely) the intellect. Origin: from G4920 (συνίημι); KJV: knowledge, understanding

G4908 συνετός (synetós): mentally put (or putting) together, i.e. sagacious. Origin: from G4920 (συνίημι); KJV: prudent

G4909 συνευδοκέω (syneudokéō): to think well of in common, i.e. assent to, feel gratified with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2106 (εὐδοκέω); KJV: allow, assent, be pleased, have pleasure

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G4910 to G5033
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G4910 συνευωχέω (syneuōchéō): to entertain sumptuously in company with, i.e. (middle voice or passive) to revel together. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a presumed compound of G2095 (εὖ) and a derivative of G2192 (ἔχω) (meaning to be in good condition, i.e. (by implication) to fare well, or feast); KJV: feast with

G4911 συνεφίστημι (synephístēmi): to stand up together, i.e. to resist (or assault) jointly. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2186 (ἐφίστημι); KJV: rise up together

G4912 συνέχω (synéchō): to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng

G4913 συνήδομαι (synḗdomai): to rejoice in with oneself, i.e. feel satisfaction concerning. Origin: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G2237 (ἡδονή); KJV: delight

G4914 συνήθεια (synḗtheia): mutual habituation, i.e. usage. Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G2239 (ἦθος); KJV: custom

G4915 συνηλικιώτης (synēlikiṓtēs): a co-aged person, i.e. alike in years. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G2244 (ἡλικία); KJV: equal

G4916 συνθάπτω (syntháptō): to inter in company with, i.e. (figuratively) to assimilate spiritually (to Christ by a sepulture as to sin). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2290 (θάπτω); KJV: bury with

G4917 συνθλάω (synthláō): to dash together, i.e. shatter. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and thlao (to crush); KJV: break

G4918 συνθλίβω (synthlíbō): to compress, i.e. crowd on all sides. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2346 (θλίβω); KJV: throng

G4919 συνθρύπτω (synthrýptō): to crush together, i.e. (figuratively) to dispirit. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to crumble); KJV: break

G4920 συνίημι (syníēmi): to put together, i.e. (mentally) to comprehend; by implication, to act piously. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and (to send); KJV: consider, understand, be wise

G4921 συνιστάω (synistáō): to set together, i.e. (by implication) to introduce (favorably), or (figuratively) to exhibit; intransitively, to stand near, or (figuratively) to constitute. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G2476 (ἵστημι) (including its collateral forms); KJV: approve, commend, consist, make, stand (with)

G4922 συνοδεύω (synodeúō): to travel in company with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3593 (ὁδεύω); KJV: journey with

G4923 συνοδία (synodía): companionship on a journey, i.e. (by implication), a caravan. Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3598 (ὁδός) ("synod"); KJV: company

G4924 συνοικέω (synoikéō): to reside together (as a family). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3611 (οἰκέω); KJV: dwell together

G4925 συνοικοδομέω (synoikodoméō): to construct, i.e. (passively) to compose (in company with other Christians, figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3618 (οἰκοδομέω); KJV: build together

G4926 συνομιλέω (synomiléō): to converse mutually. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G3656 (ὁμιλέω); KJV: talk with

G4927 συνομορέω (synomoréō): to border together, i.e. adjoin. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of the base of 3674 and the base of G3725 (ὅριον); KJV: join hard

G4928 συνοχή (synochḗ): restraint, i.e. (figuratively) anxiety. Origin: from G4912 (συνέχω); KJV: anguish, distress

G4929 συντάσσω (syntássō): to arrange jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to direct. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: appoint

G4930 συντέλεια (syntéleia): entire completion, i.e. consummation (of a dispensation). Origin: from G4931 (συντελέω); KJV: end

G4931 συντελέω (synteléō): to complete entirely; generally, to execute (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5055 (τελέω); KJV: end, finish, fulfil, make

G4932 συντέμνω (syntémnō): to contract by cutting, i.e. (figuratively) do concisely (speedily). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G5114 (τομώτερος); KJV: (cut) short

G4933 συντηρέω (syntēréō): to keep closely together, i.e. (by implication) to conserve (from ruin); mentally, to remember (and obey). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5083 (τηρέω); KJV: keep, observe, preserve

G4934 συντίθεμαι (syntíthemai): to place jointly, i.e. (figuratively) to consent (bargain, stipulate), concur. Origin: middle voice from G4862 (σύν) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: agree, assent, covenant

G4935 συντόμως (syntómōs): concisely (briefly). Origin: adverb from a derivative of G4932 (συντέμνω); KJV: a few words

G4936 συντρέχω (syntréchō): to rush together (hastily assemble) or headlong (figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate); KJV: run (together, with)

G4937 συντρίβω (syntríbō): to crush completely, i.e. to shatter (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος); KJV: break (in pieces), broken to shivers (+ -hearted), bruise

G4938 σύντριμμα (sýntrimma): concussion or utter fracture (properly, concretely), i.e. complete ruin. Origin: from G4937 (συντρίβω); KJV: destruction

G4939 σύντροφος (sýntrophos): a fellow-nursling, i.e. comrade. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5162 (τροφός) (in a passive sense); KJV: brought up with

G4940 συντυγχάνω (syntynchánō): to chance together, i.e. meet with (reach). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5177 (τυγχάνω); KJV: come at

G4941 Συντύχη (Syntýchē): an accident; Syntyche, a Christian female. Origin: from G4940 (συντυγχάνω); KJV: Syntyche

G4942 συνυποκρίνομαι (synypokrínomai): to act hypocritically in concert with. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5271 (ὑποκρίνομαι); KJV: dissemble with

G4943 συνυπουργέω (synypourgéō): to be a co-auxiliary, i.e. assist. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and the base of G2041 (ἔργον); KJV: help together

G4944 συνωδίνω (synōdínō): to have (parturition) pangs in company (concert, simultaneously) with, i.e. (figuratively) to sympathize (in expectation of relief from suffering). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G5605 (ὠδίνω); KJV: travail in pain together

G4945 συνωμοσία (synōmosía): a swearing together, i.e. (by implication) a plot. Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and G3660 (ὀμνύω); KJV: comspiracy

G4946 Συράκουσαι (Syrákousai): Syracuse, the capital of Sicily. Origin: plural of uncertain derivation; KJV: Syracuse

G4947 Συρία (Syría): Syria (i.e. Tsyria or Tyre), a region of Asia. Origin: probably of Hebrew origin (H6865); KJV: Syria

G4948 Σύρος (Sýros): a Syran (i.e. probably Tyrian), a native of Syria. Origin: from the same as G4947 (Συρία); KJV: Syrian

G4949 Συροφοίνισσα (Syrophoínissa): a Syro-phœnician woman, i.e. a female native of Phœnicia in Syria. Origin: feminine of a compound of G4948 (Σύρος) and the same as G5403 (Φοινίκη); KJV: Syrophenician

G4950 σύρτις (sýrtis): a shoal (from the sand drawn thither by the waves), i.e. the Syrtis Major or great bay on the north coast of Africa. Origin: from G4951 (σύρω); KJV: quicksands

G4951 σύρω (sýrō): to trail. Origin: probably akin to G138 (αἱρέομαι); KJV: drag, draw, hale

G4952 συσπαράσσω (sysparássō): to rend completely, i.e. (by analogy) to convulse violently. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4682 (σπαράσσω); KJV: throw down

G4953 σύσσημον (sýssēmon): a sign in common, i.e. preconcerted signal. Origin: neuter of a compound of G4862 (σύν) and the base of G4591 (σημαίνω); KJV: token

G4954 σύσσωμος (sýssōmos): of a joint body, i.e. (figuratively) a fellow-member of the Christian community. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4983 (σῶμα); KJV: of the same body

G4955 συστασιαστής (systasiastḗs): a fellow-insurgent. Origin: from a compound of G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4714 (στάσις); KJV: make insurrection with

G4956 συστατικός (systatikós): introductory, i.e. recommendatory. Origin: from a derivative of G4921 (συνιστάω); KJV: of commendation

G4957 συσταυρόω (systauróō): to impale in company with (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4717 (σταυρόω); KJV: crucify with

G4958 συστέλλω (systéllō): to send (draw) together, i.e. enwrap (enshroud a corpse for burial), contract (an interval). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: short, wind up

G4959 συστενάζω (systenázō): to moan jointly, i.e. (figuratively) experience a common calamity. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4727 (στενάζω); KJV: groan together

G4960 συστοιχέω (systoichéō): to file together (as soldiers in ranks), i.e. (figuratively) to correspond to. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4748 (στοιχέω); KJV: answer to

G4961 συστρατιώτης (systratiṓtēs): a co-campaigner, i.e. (figuratively) an associate in Christian toil. Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4757 (στρατιώτης); KJV: fellowsoldier

G4962 συστρέφω (systréphō): to twist together, i.e. collect (a bundle, a crowd). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: gather

G4963 συστροφή (systrophḗ): a twisting together, i.e. (figuratively) a secret coalition, riotous crowd. Origin: from G4962 (συστρέφω); KJV: + band together, concourse

G4964 συσχηματίζω (syschēmatízō): to fashion alike, i.e. conform to the same pattern (figuratively). Origin: from G4862 (σύν) and a derivative of G4976 (σχῆμα); KJV: conform to, fashion self according to

G4965 Συχάρ (Sychár): Sychar (i.e. Shekar), a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7941); KJV: Sychar

G4966 Συχέμ (Sychém): Sychem (i.e. Shekem), the name of a Canaanite and of a place in Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H7927); KJV: Sychem

G4967 σφαγή (sphagḗ): butchery (of animals for food or sacrifice, or (figuratively) of men (destruction)). Origin: from G4969 (σφάζω); KJV: slaughter

G4968 σφάγιον (sphágion): a victim (in sacrifice). Origin: neuter of a derivative of G4967 (σφαγή); KJV: slain beast

G4969 σφάζω (spházō): to butcher (especially an animal for food or in sacrifice) or (generally) to slaughter, or (specially), to maim (violently). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: kill, slay, wound

G4970 σφόδρα (sphódra): of uncertain derivation) as adverb; vehemently, i.e. in a high degree, much. Origin: neuter plural of (violent; KJV: exceeding(-ly), greatly, sore, very

G4971 σφοδρῶς (sphodrōs): very much. Origin: adverb from the same as G4970 (σφόδρα); KJV: exceedingly

G4972 σφραγίζω (sphragízō): to stamp (with a signet or private mark) for security or preservation (literally or figuratively); by implication, to keep secret, to attest. Origin: from G4973 (σφραγίς); KJV: (set a, set to) seal up, stop

G4973 σφραγίς (sphragís): a signet (as fencing in or protecting from misappropriation); by implication, the stamp impressed (as a mark of privacy, or genuineness), literally or figuratively. Origin: probably strengthened from G5420 (φράσσω); KJV: seal

G4974 σφυρόν (sphyrón): compare the feminine , a hammer); the ankle (as globular). Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative probably of the same as (a ball, "sphere"; KJV: ancle bone

G4975 σχεδόν (schedón): nigh, i.e. nearly. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω) as adverb; KJV: almost

G4976 σχῆμα (schēma): a figure (as a mode or circumstance), i.e. (by implication) external condition. Origin: from the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: fashion

G4977 σχίζω (schízō): to split or sever (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: break, divide, open, rend, make a rent

G4978 σχίσμα (schísma): a split or gap ("schism"), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G4977 (σχίζω); KJV: division, rent, schism

G4979 σχοινίον (schoiníon): of uncertain derivation); a rushlet, i.e. grass-withe or tie (generally). Origin: diminutive of (a rush or flag-plant; KJV: small cord, rope

G4980 σχολάζω (scholázō): to take a holiday, i.e. be at leisure for (by implication, devote oneself wholly to); figuratively, to be vacant (of a house). Origin: from G4981 (σχολή); KJV: empty, give self

G4981 σχολή (scholḗ): properly, loitering (as a withholding of oneself from work) or leisure, i.e. (by implication) a "school" (as vacation from physical employment). Origin: probably feminine of a presumed derivative of the alternate of G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: school

G4982 σώζω (sṓzō): to save, i.e. deliver or protect (literally or figuratively). Origin: from a primary (contraction for obsolete , "safe"); KJV: heal, preserve, save (self), do well, be (make) whole
