G4983 σῶμα (sōma): the body (as a sound whole), used in a very wide application, literally or figuratively. Origin: from G4982 (σώζω); KJV: bodily, body, slave

G4984 σωματικός (sōmatikós): corporeal or physical. Origin: from G4983 (σῶμα); KJV: bodily

G4985 σωματικῶς (sōmatikōs): corporeally or physically. Origin: adverb from G4984 (σωματικός); KJV: bodily

G4986 Σώπατρος (Sṓpatros): of a safe father; Sopatrus, a Christian. Origin: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and G3962 (πατήρ); KJV: Sopater

G4987 σωρεύω (sōreúō): to pile up (literally or figuratively). Origin: from another form of G4673 (σορός); KJV: heap, load

G4988 Σωσθένης (Sōsthénēs): of safe strength; Sosthenes, a Christian. Origin: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and that of G4599 (σθενόω); KJV: Sosthenes

G4989 Σωσίπατρος (Sōsípatros): Sosipatrus, a Christian. Origin: prolongation for G4986 (Σώπατρος); KJV: Sosipater

G4990 σωτήρ (sōtḗr): a deliverer, i.e. God or Christ. Origin: from G4982 (σώζω); KJV: saviour

G4991 σωτηρία (sōtēría): rescue or safety (physically or morally). Origin: feminine of a derivative of G4990 (σωτήρ) as (properly, abstract) noun; KJV: deliver, health, salvation, save, saving

G4992 σωτήριον (sōtḗrion): defender or (by implication) defence. Origin: neuter of the same as G4991 (σωτηρία) as (properly, concretely) noun; KJV: salvation

G4993 σωφρονέω (sōphronéō): to be of sound mind, i.e. sane, (figuratively) moderate. Origin: from G4998 (σώφρων); KJV: be in right mind, be sober (minded), soberly

G4994 σωφρονίζω (sōphronízō): to make of sound mind, i.e. (figuratively) to discipline or correct. Origin: from G4998 (σώφρων); KJV: teach to be sober

G4995 σωφρονισμός (sōphronismós): discipline, i.e. self-control. Origin: from G4994 (σωφρονίζω); KJV: sound mind

G4996 σωφρόνως (sōphrónōs): with sound mind, i.e. moderately. Origin: adverb from G4998 (σώφρων); KJV: soberly

G4997 σωφροσύνη (sōphrosýnē): soundness of mind, i.e. (literally) sanity or (figuratively) self-control. Origin: from G4998 (σώφρων); KJV: soberness, sobriety

G4998 σώφρων (sṓphrōn): safe (sound) in mind, i.e. self-controlled (moderate as to opinion or passion). Origin: from the base of G4982 (σώζω) and that of G5424 (φρήν); KJV: discreet, sober, temperate

G4999 Ταβέρναι (Tabérnai): huts or wooden-walled buildings; Tabernæ. Origin: plural of Latin origin; KJV: taverns

G5000 Ταβιθά (Tabithá): the gazelle; Tabitha (i.e. Tabjetha), a Christian female. Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H6646); KJV: Tabitha

G5001 τάγμα (tágma): something orderly in arrangement (a troop), i.e. (figuratively) a series or succession. Origin: from G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: order

G5002 τακτός (taktós): arranged, i.e. appointed or stated. Origin: from G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: set

G5003 ταλαιπωρέω (talaipōréō): to be wretched, i.e. realize one's own misery. Origin: from G5005 (ταλαίπωρος); KJV: be afflicted

G5004 ταλαιπωρία (talaipōría): wretchedness, i.e. calamity. Origin: from G5005 (ταλαίπωρος); KJV: misery

G5005 ταλαίπωρος (talaípōros): enduring trial, i.e. miserable. Origin: from the base of G5007 (τάλαντον) and a derivative of the base of G3984 (πεῖρα); KJV: wretched

G5006 ταλαντιαῖος (talantiaîos): talent-like in weight. Origin: from G5007 (τάλαντον); KJV: weight of a talent

G5007 τάλαντον (tálanton): equivalent to G5342 (φέρω)); a balance (as supporting weights), i.e. (by implication) a certain weight (and thence a coin or rather sum of money) or "talent". Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of the original form of (to bear; KJV: talent

G5008 ταλιθά (talithá): the fresh, i.e. young girl; talitha (O maiden). Origin: of Chaldee origin (compare H2924); KJV: talitha

G5009 ταμεῖον (tameîon): akin to , to cut); a dispensary or magazine, i.e. a chamber on the ground-floor or interior of an Oriental house (generally used for storage or privacy, a spot for retirement). Origin: neuter contraction of a presumed derivative of (a dispenser or distributor; KJV: secret chamber, closet, storehouse

G5010 τάξις (táxis): regular arrangement, i.e. (in time) fixed succession (of rank or character), official dignity. Origin: from G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: order

G5011 ταπεινός (tapeinós): depressed, i.e. (figuratively) humiliated (in circumstances or disposition). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: base, cast down, humble, of low degree (estate), lowly

G5012 ταπεινοφροσύνη (tapeinophrosýnē): humiliation of mind, i.e. modesty. Origin: from a compound of G5011 (ταπεινός) and the base of G5424 (φρήν); KJV: humbleness of mind, humility (of mind, loneliness (of mind)

G5013 ταπεινόω (tapeinóō): to depress; figuratively, to humiliate (in condition or heart). Origin: from G5011 (ταπεινός); KJV: abase, bring low, humble (self)

G5014 ταπείνωσις (tapeínōsis): depression (in rank or feeling). Origin: from G5013 (ταπεινόω); KJV: humiliation, be made low, low estate, vile

G5015 ταράσσω (tarássō): to stir or agitate (roil water). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: trouble

G5016 ταραχή (tarachḗ): disturbance, i.e. (of water) roiling, or (of a mob) sedition. Origin: feminine from G5015 (ταράσσω); KJV: trouble(-ing)

G5017 τάραχος (tárachos): a disturbance, i.e. (popular) tumult. Origin: masculine from G5015 (ταράσσω); KJV: stir

G5018 Ταρσεύς (Tarseús): a Tarsean, i.e. native of Tarsus. Origin: from G5019 (Ταρσός); KJV: of Tarsus

G5019 Ταρσός (Tarsós): Tarsus, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: perhaps the same as (a flat basket); KJV: Tarsus

G5020 ταρταρόω (tartaróō): to incarcerate in eternal torment. Origin: from (the deepest abyss of Hades); KJV: cast down to hell

G5021 τάσσω (tássō): to arrange in an orderly manner, i.e. assign or dispose (to a certain position or lot). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary verb (which latter appears only in certain tenses); KJV: addict, appoint, determine, ordain, set

G5022 ταῦρος (taûros): a bullock. Origin: apparently a primary word (compare H8450, "steer"); KJV: bull, ox

G5023 ταῦτα (taûta): these things. Origin: nominative or accusative case neuter plural of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: + afterward, follow, + hereafter, X him, the same, so, such, that, then, these, they, this, those, thus

G5024 ταὐτά (tautá): in the same way. Origin: neuter plural of G3588 (ὁ) and G846 (αὐτός) as adverb; KJV: even thus, (manner) like, so

G5025 ταύταις (taútais): (to or with or by, etc.) these. Origin: dative case and accusative case feminine plural respectively of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: hence, that, then, these, those

G5026 ταύτῃ (taútēi): (towards or of) this. Origin: dative case, accusative case and genitive case respectively of the feminine singular of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: her, + hereof, it, that, + thereby, the (same), this (same)

G5027 ταφή (taphḗ): burial (the act). Origin: feminine from G2290 (θάπτω); KJV: X bury

G5028 τάφος (táphos): a grave (the place of interment). Origin: masculine from G2290 (θάπτω); KJV: sepulchre, tomb

G5029 τάχα (tácha): shortly, i.e. (figuratively) possibly. Origin: as if neuter plural of G5036 (ταχύς) (adverbially); KJV: peradventure(-haps)

G5030 ταχέως (tachéōs): briefly, i.e. (in time) speedily, or (in manner) rapidly. Origin: adverb from G5036 (ταχύς); KJV: hastily, quickly, shortly, soon, suddenly

G5031 ταχινός (tachinós): curt, i.e. impending. Origin: from G5034 (τάχος); KJV: shortly, swift

G5032 τάχιον (táchion): more swiftly, i.e. (in manner) more rapidly, or (in time) more speedily. Origin: neuter singular of the comparative of G5036 (ταχύς) (as adverb); KJV: out (run), quickly, shortly, sooner

G5033 τάχιστα (táchista): most quickly, i.e. (with G5613 (ὡς) prefixed) as soon as possible. Origin: neuter plural of the superlative of G5036 (ταχύς) (as adverb); KJV: + with all speed

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G5034 to G5155
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G5034 τάχος (táchos): a brief space (of time), i.e. (with G1722 (ἐν) prefixed) in haste. Origin: from the same as G5036 (ταχύς); KJV: + quickly, + shortly, + speedily

G5035 ταχύ (tachý): shortly, i.e. without delay, soon, or (by surprise) suddenly, or (by implication, of ease) readily. Origin: neuter singular of G5036 (ταχύς) (as adverb); KJV: lightly, quickly

G5036 ταχύς (tachýs): fleet, i.e. (figuratively) prompt or ready. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: swift

G5037 τέ (té): both or also (properly, as correlation of G2532 (καί)). Origin: a primary particle (enclitic) of connection or addition; KJV: also, and, both, even, then, whether

G5038 τεῖχος (teîchos): a wall (as formative of a house). Origin: akin to the base of G5088 (τίκτω); KJV: wall

G5039 τεκμήριον (tekmḗrion): a token (as defining a fact), i.e. criterion of certainty. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a goal or fixed limit); KJV: infallible proof

G5040 τεκνίον (tekníon): an infant, i.e. (plural figuratively) darlings (Christian converts). Origin: diminutive of G5043 (τέκνον); KJV: little children

G5041 τεκνογονέω (teknogonéō): to be a child-bearer, i.e. parent (mother). Origin: from a compound of G5043 (τέκνον) and the base of G1096 (γίνομαι); KJV: bear children

G5042 τεκνογονία (teknogonía): childbirth (parentage), i.e. (by implication) maternity (the performance of maternal duties). Origin: from the same as G5041 (τεκνογονέω); KJV: childbearing

G5043 τέκνον (téknon): a child (as produced). Origin: from the base of G5098 (τιμωρία); KJV: child, daughter, son

G5044 τεκνοτροφέω (teknotrophéō): to be a childrearer, i.e. fulfil the duties of a female parent. Origin: from a compound of G5043 (τέκνον) and G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: bring up children

G5045 τέκτων (téktōn): an artificer (as producer of fabrics), i.e. (specially), a craftsman in wood. Origin: from the base of G5098 (τιμωρία); KJV: carpenter

G5046 τέλειος (téleios): complete (in various applications of labor, growth, mental and moral character, etc.); neuter (as noun, with G3588 (ὁ)) completeness. Origin: from G5056 (τέλος); KJV: of full age, man, perfect

G5047 τελειότης (teleiótēs): (the state) completeness (mentally or morally). Origin: from G5046 (τέλειος); KJV: perfection(-ness)

G5048 τελειόω (teleióō): to complete, i.e. (literally) accomplish, or (figuratively) consummate (in character). Origin: from G5046 (τέλειος); KJV: consecrate, finish, fulfil, make) perfect

G5049 τελείως (teleíōs): completely, i.e. (of hope) without wavering. Origin: adverb from G5046 (τέλειος); KJV: to the end

G5050 τελείωσις (teleíōsis): (the act) completion, i.e. (of prophecy) verification, or (of expiation) absolution. Origin: from G5448 (φυσιόω); KJV: perfection, performance

G5051 τελειωτής (teleiōtḗs): a completer, i.e. consummater. Origin: from G5048 (τελειόω); KJV: finisher

G5052 τελεσφορέω (telesphoréō): to be a bearer to completion (maturity), i.e. to ripen fruit (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G5056 (τέλος) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bring fruit to perfection

G5053 τελευτάω (teleutáō): to finish life (by implication, of G979 (βίος)), i.e. expire (demise). Origin: from a presumed derivative of G5055 (τελέω); KJV: be dead, decease, die

G5054 τελευτή (teleutḗ): decease. Origin: from G5053 (τελευτάω); KJV: death

G5055 τελέω (teléō): to end, i.e. complete, execute, conclude, discharge (a debt). Origin: from G5056 (τέλος); KJV: accomplish, make an end, expire, fill up, finish, go over, pay, perform

G5056 τέλος (télos): properly, the point aimed at as a limit, i.e. (by implication) the conclusion of an act or state (termination (literally, figuratively or indefinitely), result (immediate, ultimate or prophetic), purpose); specially, an impost or levy (as paid). Origin: from a primary (to set out for a definite point or goal); KJV: + continual, custom, end(-ing), finally, uttermost

G5057 τελώνης (telṓnēs): a tax-farmer, i.e. collector of public revenue. Origin: from G5056 (τέλος) and G5608 (ὠνέομαι); KJV: publican

G5058 τελώνιον (telṓnion): a tax-gatherer's place of business. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of G5057 (τελώνης); KJV: receipt of custom

G5059 τέρας (téras): a prodigy or omen. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: wonder

G5060 Τέρτιος (Tértios): third; Tertius, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Tertius

G5061 Τέρτυλλος (Tértyllos): Tertullus, a Roman. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Tertullus

G5062 τεσσαράκοντα (tessarákonta): forty. Origin: the decade of G5064 (τέσσαρες); KJV: forty

G5063 τεσσαρακονταετής (tessarakontaetḗs): of forty years of age. Origin: from G5062 (τεσσαράκοντα) and G2094 (ἔτος); KJV: (+ full, of) forty years (old)

G5064 τέσσαρες (téssares): four. Origin: a plural number; KJV: four

G5065 τεσσαρεσκαιδέκατος (tessareskaidékatos): fourteenth. Origin: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G2532 (καί) and G1182 (δέκατος); KJV: fourteenth

G5066 τεταρταῖος (tetartaîos): pertaining to the fourth day. Origin: from G5064 (τέσσαρες); KJV: four days

G5067 τέταρτος (tétartos): fourth. Origin: ordinal from G5064 (τέσσαρες); KJV: four(-th)

G5068 τετράγωνος (tetrágōnos): four-cornered, i.e. square. Origin: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G1137 (γωνία); KJV: foursquare

G5069 τετράδιον (tetrádion): from G5064 (τέσσαρες)); a quaternion or squad (picket) of four Roman soldiers. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of (a tetrad; KJV: quaternion

G5070 τετρακισχίλιοι (tetrakischílioi): four times a thousand. Origin: from the multiplicative adverb of G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G5507 (χίλιοι); KJV: four thousand

G5071 τετρακόσιοι (tetrakósioi): four hundred. Origin: plural from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G1540 (ἑκατόν); KJV: four hundred

G5072 τετράμηνον (tetrámēnon): a four months' space. Origin: neuter of a compound of G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G3376 (μήν); KJV: four months

G5073 τετραπλόος (tetraplóos): quadruple. Origin: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and a derivative of the base of G4118 (πλεῖστος); KJV: fourfold

G5074 τετράπους (tetrápous): a quadruped. Origin: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G4228 (πούς); KJV: fourfooted beast

G5075 τετραρχέω (tetrarchéō): to be a tetrarch. Origin: from G5076 (τετράρχης); KJV: (be) tetrarch

G5076 τετράρχης (tetrárchēs): the ruler of a fourth part of a country ("tetrarch"). Origin: from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: tetrarch

G5077 τεφρόω (tephróō): to incinerate, i.e. consume. Origin: from (ashes); KJV: turn to ashes

G5078 τέχνη (téchnē): art (as productive), i.e. (specially), a trade, or (generally) skill. Origin: from the base of G5088 (τίκτω); KJV: art, craft, occupation

G5079 τεχνίτης (technítēs): an artisan; figuratively, a founder (Creator). Origin: from G5078 (τέχνη); KJV: builder, craftsman

G5080 τήκω (tḗkō): to liquefy. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: melt

G5081 τηλαυγῶς (tēlaugōs): in a far-shining manner, i.e. plainly. Origin: adverb from a compound of a derivative of G5056 (τέλος) and G827 (αὐγή); KJV: clearly

G5082 τηλικοῦτος (tēlikoûtos): such as this, i.e. (in (figurative) magnitude) so vast. Origin: from a compound of G3588 (ὁ) with G2245 (ἡλίκος) and G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: so great, so mighty

G5083 τηρέω (tēréō): perhaps akin to G2334 (θεωρέω)); to guard (from loss or injury, properly, by keeping the eye upon; and thus differing from G5442 (φυλάσσω), which is properly to prevent escaping; and from G2892 (κουστωδία), which implies a fortress or full military lines of apparatus), i.e. to note (a prophecy; figuratively, to fulfil a command); by implication, to detain (in custody; figuratively, to maintain); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried); by extension, to withhold (for personal ends; figuratively, to keep unmarried). Origin: from (a watch; KJV: hold fast, keep(- er), (pre-, re-)serve, watch

G5084 τήρησις (tḗrēsis): a watching, i.e. (figuratively) observance, or (concretely) a prison. Origin: from G5083 (τηρέω); KJV: hold

G5085 Τιβεριάς (Tiberiás): Tiberias, the name of a town and a lake in Palestine. Origin: from G5086 (Τιβέριος); KJV: Tiberias

G5086 Τιβέριος (Tibérios): probably pertaining to the river Tiberis or Tiber; Tiberius, a Roman emperor. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Tiberius

G5087 τίθημι (títhēmi): to place (in the widest application, literally and figuratively; properly, in a passive or horizontal posture, and thus different from G2476 (ἵστημι), which properly denotes an upright and active position, while G2749 (κεῖμαι) is properly reflexive and utterly prostrate). Origin: a prolonged form of a primary (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); KJV: + advise, appoint, bow, commit, conceive, give, X kneel down, lay (aside, down, up), make, ordain, purpose, put, set (forth), settle, sink down

G5088 τίκτω (tíktō): to produce (from seed, as a mother, a plant, the earth, etc.), literally or figuratively. Origin: a strengthened form of a primary (which is used only as alternate in certain tenses); KJV: bear, be born, bring forth, be delivered, be in travail

G5089 τίλλω (tíllō): to pull off. Origin: perhaps akin to the alternate of G138 (αἱρέομαι), and thus to G4951 (σύρω); KJV: pluck

G5090 Τιμαῖος (Timaîos): Timæus (i.e. Timay), an Israelite. Origin: probably of Chaldee origin (compare H2931); KJV: Timæus

G5091 τιμάω (timáō): to prize, i.e. fix a valuation upon; by implication, to revere. Origin: from G5093 (τίμιος); KJV: honour, value

G5092 τιμή (timḗ): a value, i.e. money paid, or (concretely and collectively) valuables; by analogy, esteem (especially of the highest degree), or the dignity itself. Origin: from G5099 (τίνω); KJV: honour, precious, price, some

G5093 τίμιος (tímios): valuable, i.e. (objectively) costly, or (subjectively) honored, esteemed, or (figuratively) beloved. Origin: from G5092 (τιμή); KJV: dear, honourable, (more, most) precious, had in reputation

G5094 τιμιότης (timiótēs): expensiveness, i.e. (by implication) magnificence. Origin: from G5093 (τίμιος); KJV: costliness

G5095 Τιμόθεος (Timótheos): dear to God; Timotheus, a Christian. Origin: from G5092 (τιμή) and G2316 (θεός); KJV: Timotheus, Timothy

G5096 Τίμων (Tímōn): valuable; Timon, a Christian. Origin: from G5092 (τιμή); KJV: Timon

G5097 τιμωρέω (timōréō): properly, to protect one's honor, i.e. to avenge (inflict a penalty). Origin: from a comparative of G5092 (τιμή) and ouros (a guard); KJV: punish

G5098 τιμωρία (timōría): vindication, i.e. (by implication) a penalty. Origin: from G5097 (τιμωρέω); KJV: punishment

G5099 τίνω (tínō): to pay a price, i.e. as a penalty. Origin: strengthened for a primary (which is only used as an alternate in certain tenses); KJV: be punished with

G5100 τὶς (tìs): some or any person or object. Origin: an enclitic indefinite pronoun; KJV: a (kind of), any (man, thing, thing at all), certain (thing), divers, he (every) man, one (X thing), ought, + partly, some (man, -body, - thing, -what), (+ that no-)thing, what(-soever), X wherewith, whom(-soever), whose(-soever)

G5101 τίς (tís): an interrogative pronoun, who, which or what (in direct or indirect questions). Origin: probably emphatic of G5100 (τὶς); KJV: every man, how (much), + no(-ne, thing), what (manner, thing), where (-by, -fore, -of, -unto, - with, -withal), whether, which, who(-m, -se), why

G5102 τίτλος (títlos): a titulus or "title" (placard). Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: title

G5103 Τίτος (Títos): Titus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin but uncertain significance; KJV: Titus

G5104 τοί (toí): an enclitic particle of asseveration by way of contrast; in sooth. Origin: probably for the dative case of G3588 (ὁ); KJV: (used only with other particles in the comparative, as G2544 (καίτοιγε), G3305 (μέντοι), G5105 (τοιγαροῦν), G5106 (τοίνυν), etc

G5105 τοιγαροῦν (toigaroûn): truly for then, i.e. consequently. Origin: from G5104 (τοί) and G1063 (γάρ) and G3767 (οὖν); KJV: there-(where-)fore

G5106 τοίνυν (toínyn): truly now, i.e. accordingly. Origin: from G5104 (τοί) and G3568 (νῦν); KJV: then, therefore

G5107 τοιόσδε (toiósde): such-like then, i.e. so great. Origin: (including the other inflections); from a derivative of 5104 and G1161 (δέ); KJV: such

G5108 τοιοῦτος (toioûtos): truly this, i.e. of this sort (to denote character or individuality). Origin: (including the other inflections); from G5104 (τοί) and G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: like, such (an one)

G5109 τοῖχος (toîchos): a wall. Origin: another form of G5038 (τεῖχος); KJV: wall

G5110 τόκος (tókos): interest on money loaned (as a produce). Origin: from the base of G5088 (τίκτω); KJV: usury

G5111 τολμάω (tolmáō): probably itself from the base of G5056 (τέλος) through the idea of extreme conduct); to venture (objectively or in act; while G2292 (θαῤῥέω) is rather subjective or in feeling); by implication, to be courageous. Origin: from (boldness; KJV: be bold, boldly, dare, durst

G5112 τολμηρότερον (tolmēróteron): more daringly, i.e. with greater confidence than otherwise. Origin: neuter of the compound of a derivative of the base of 5111 (as adverb); KJV: the more boldly

G5113 τολμητής (tolmētḗs): a daring (audacious) man. Origin: from G5111 (τολμάω); KJV: presumptuous

G5114 τομώτερος (tomṓteros): more comprehensive or decisive than G2875 (κόπτω), as if by a single stroke; whereas that implies repeated blows, like hacking); more keen. Origin: comparative of a derivative of the primary (to cut; KJV: sharper

G5115 τόξον (tóxon): a bow (apparently as the simplest fabric). Origin: from the base of G5088 (τίκτω); KJV: bow

G5116 τοπάζιον (topázion): of uncertain origin); a gem, probably the chrysolite. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative (alternately) of (a "topaz"; KJV: topaz

G5117 τόπος (tópos): a spot (general in space, but limited by occupancy; whereas G5561 (χώρα) is a large but participle locality), i.e. location (as a position, home, tract, etc.); figuratively, condition, opportunity; specially, a scabbard. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: coast, licence, place, X plain, quarter, + rock, room, where

G5118 τοσοῦτος (tosoûtos): apparently from G3588 (ὁ) and G3739 (ὅς)) and G3778 (οὗτος) (including its variations); so vast as this, i.e. such (in quantity, amount, number of space). Origin: from (so much; KJV: as large, so great (long, many, much), these many

G5119 τότε (tóte): the when, i.e. at the time that (of the past or future, also in consecution). Origin: from (the neuter of) G3588 (ὁ) and G3753 (ὅτε); KJV: that time, then

G5120 τοῦ (toû): sometimes used for G5127 (τούτου); of this person. Origin: properly, the genitive case of G3588 (ὁ); KJV: his

G5121 τοὐναντίον (tounantíon): on the contrary. Origin: contraction for the neuter of G3588 (ὁ) and G1726 (ἐναντίον); KJV: contrariwise

G5122 τοὔνομα (toúnoma): the name (is). Origin: contraction for the neuter of G3588 (ὁ) and G3686 (ὄνομα); KJV: named

G5123 τουτέστι (toutésti): that is. Origin: contraction for G5124 (τοῦτο) and G2076 (ἐστί); KJV: that is (to say)

G5124 τοῦτο (toûto): that thing. Origin: neuter singular nominative or accusative case of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: here (-unto), it, partly, self(-same), so, that (intent), the same, there(-fore, -unto), this, thus, where(-fore)

G5125 τούτοις (toútois): to (for, in, with or by) these (persons or things). Origin: dative case plural masculine or neuter of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: such, them, there(-in, -with), these, this, those

G5126 τοῦτον (toûton): this (person, as objective of verb or preposition). Origin: accusative case singular masculine of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: him, the same, that, this

G5127 τούτου (toútou): of (from or concerning) this (person or thing). Origin: genitive case singular masculine or neuter of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: here(-by), him, it, + such manner of, that, thence(-forth), thereabout, this, thus

G5128 τούτους (toútous): these (persons, as objective of verb or preposition). Origin: accusative case plural masculine of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: such, them, these, this

G5129 τούτῳ (toútōi): to (in, with or by) this (person or thing). Origin: dative case singular masculine or neuter of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: here(-by, -in), him, one, the same, there(-in), this

G5130 τούτων (toútōn): of (from or concerning) these (persons or things). Origin: genitive case plural masculine or neuter of G3778 (οὗτος); KJV: such, their, these (things), they, this sort, those

G5131 τράγος (trágos): a he-goat (as a gnawer). Origin: from the base of G5176 (τρώγω); KJV: goat

G5132 τράπεζα (trápeza): a table or stool (as being four-legged), usually for food (figuratively, a meal); also a counter for money (figuratively, a broker's office for loans at interest). Origin: probably contracted from G5064 (τέσσαρες) and G3979 (πεζῇ); KJV: bank, meat, table

G5133 τραπεζίτης (trapezítēs): a money-broker or banker. Origin: from G5132 (τράπεζα); KJV: exchanger

G5134 τραῦμα (traûma): akin to the base of G2352 (θραύω), G5147 (τρίβος), G5149 (τρίζω), etc.); a wound. Origin: from the base of (to wound; KJV: wound

G5135 τραυματίζω (traumatízō): to inflict a wound. Origin: from G5134 (τραῦμα); KJV: wound

G5136 τραχηλίζω (trachēlízō): to seize by the throat or neck, i.e. to expose the gullet of a victim for killing (generally, to lay bare). Origin: from G5137 (τράχηλος); KJV: opened

G5137 τράχηλος (tráchēlos): the throat (neck), i.e. (figuratively) life. Origin: probably from G5143 (τρέχω) (through the idea of mobility); KJV: neck

G5138 τραχύς (trachýs): uneven, rocky (reefy). Origin: perhaps strengthened from the base of G4486 (ῥήγνυμι) (as if jagged by rents); KJV: rock, rough

G5139 Τραχωνῖτις (Trachōnîtis): rough district; Trachonitis, a region of Syria. Origin: from a derivative of G5138 (τραχύς); KJV: Trachonitis

G5140 τρεῖς (treîs): "three". Origin: a primary (plural) number; KJV: three

G5141 τρέμω (trémō): to "tremble" or fear. Origin: strengthened from a primary (to "dread", "terrify"); KJV: be afraid, trembling

G5142 τρέφω (tréphō): but perhaps strengthened from the base of G5157 (τροπή) through the idea of convolution); properly, to stiffen, i.e. fatten (by implication, to cherish (with food, etc.), pamper, rear). Origin: a primary verb (properly, ; KJV: bring up, feed, nourish

G5143 τρέχω (tréchō): compare G2359 (θρίξ)); which uses (the base of G1408 (δρόμος)) as alternate in certain tenses; to run or walk hastily (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary verb (properly, ; KJV: have course, run

G5144 τριάκοντα (triákonta): thirty. Origin: the decade of G5140 (τρεῖς); KJV: thirty

G5145 τριακόσιοι (triakósioi): three hundred. Origin: plural from G5140 (τρεῖς) and G1540 (ἑκατόν); KJV: three hundred

G5146 τρίβολος (tríbolos): properly, a crow-foot (three-pronged obstruction in war), i.e. (by analogy) a thorny plant (caltrop). Origin: from G5140 (τρεῖς) and G956 (βέλος); KJV: brier, thistle

G5147 τρίβος (tríbos): akin to , , and the base of G5131 (τράγος), G5134 (τραῦμα)); a rut or worn track. Origin: from (to "rub"; KJV: path

G5148 τριετία (trietía): a three years' period (triennium). Origin: from a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G2094 (ἔτος); KJV: space of three years

G5149 τρίζω (trízō): to creak (squeak), i.e. (by analogy) to grate the teeth (in frenzy). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: gnash

G5150 τρίμηνον (trímēnon): a three months' space. Origin: neuter of a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G3376 (μήν) as noun; KJV: three months

G5151 τρίς (trís): three times. Origin: adverb from G5140 (τρεῖς); KJV: three times, thrice

G5152 τρίστεγον (trístegon): a third roof (story). Origin: neuter of a compound of G5140 (τρεῖς) and G4721 (στέγη) as noun; KJV: third loft

G5153 τρισχίλιοι (trischílioi): three times a thousand. Origin: from G5151 (τρίς) and G5507 (χίλιοι); KJV: three thousand

G5154 τρίτος (trítos): third; neuter (as noun) a third part, or (as adverb) a (or the) third time, thirdly. Origin: ordinal from G5140 (τρεῖς); KJV: third(-ly)

G5155 τρίχινος (tríchinos): hairy, i.e. made of hair (mohair). Origin: from G2359 (θρίξ); KJV: of hair

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G5156 to G5275
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G5156 τρόμος (trómos): a "trembling", i.e. quaking with fear. Origin: from G5141 (τρέμω); KJV: + tremble(-ing)

G5157 τροπή (tropḗ): a turn ("trope"), i.e. revolution (figuratively, variation). Origin: from an apparently primary to turn; KJV: turning

G5158 τρόπος (trópos): a turn, i.e. (by implication) mode or style (especially with preposition or relative prefix as adverb, like); figuratively, deportment or character. Origin: from the same as G5157 (τροπή); KJV: (even) as, conversation, (+ like) manner, (+ by any) means, way

G5159 τροποφορέω (tropophoréō): to endure one's habits. Origin: from G5158 (τρόπος) and G5409 (φορέω); KJV: suffer the manners

G5160 τροφή (trophḗ): nourishment (literally or figuratively); by implication, rations (wages). Origin: from G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: food, meat

G5161 Τρόφιμος (Tróphimos): nutritive; Trophimus, a Christian. Origin: from G5160 (τροφή); KJV: Trophimus

G5162 τροφός (trophós): a nourisher, i.e. nurse. Origin: from G5142 (τρέφω); KJV: nurse

G5163 τροχιά (trochiá): a track (as a wheel-rut), i.e. (figuratively) a course of conduct. Origin: from G5164 (τροχός); KJV: path

G5164 τροχός (trochós): a wheel (as a runner), i.e. (figuratively) a circuit of physical effects. Origin: from G5143 (τρέχω); KJV: course

G5165 τρύβλιον (trýblion): a bowl. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of uncertain affinity; KJV: dish

G5166 τρυγάω (trygáō): to collect the vintage. Origin: from a derivative of (to dry) meaning ripe fruit (as if dry); KJV: gather

G5167 τρυγών (trygṓn): akin to G5149 (τρίζω), but denoting a duller sound); a turtle-dove (as cooing). Origin: from (to murmur; KJV: turtle-dove

G5168 τρυμαλιά (trymaliá): akin to the base of G5134 (τραῦμα), G5147 (τρίβος) and G5176 (τρώγω)); an orifice, i.e. needle's eye. Origin: from a derivative of (to wear away; KJV: eye

G5169 τρύπημα (trýpēma): an aperture, i.e. a needle's eye. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G5168 (τρυμαλιά); KJV: eye

G5170 Τρύφαινα (Trýphaina): luxurious; Tryphæna, a Christian woman. Origin: from G5172 (τρυφή); KJV: Tryphena

G5171 τρυφάω (trypháō): to indulge in luxury. Origin: from G5172 (τρυφή); KJV: live in pleasure

G5172 τρυφή (tryphḗ): effeminacy, i.e. luxury or debauchery. Origin: from (to break up or (figuratively) enfeeble, especially the mind and body by indulgence); KJV: delicately, riot

G5173 Τρυφῶσα (Tryphōsa): luxuriating; Tryphosa, a Christian female. Origin: from G5172 (τρυφή); KJV: Tryphosa

G5174 Τρωάς (Trōás): the Troad (or plain of Troy), i.e. Troas, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: from (a Trojan); KJV: Troas

G5175 Τρωγύλλιον (Trōgýllion): Trogyllium, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Trogyllium

G5176 τρώγω (trṓgō): or perhaps rather of a base of G5167 (τρυγών) and G5149 (τρίζω) through the idea of a craunching sound; to gnaw or chew, i.e. (generally) to eat. Origin: probably strengthened from a collateral form of the base of G5134 (τραῦμα) and G5147 (τρίβος) through the idea of corrosion or wear; KJV: eat

G5177 τυγχάνω (tynchánō): akin to the base of G5088 (τίκτω) through the idea of effecting; properly, to affect; or (specially), to hit or light upon (as a mark to be reached), i.e. (transitively) to attain or secure an object or end, or (intransitively) to happen (as if meeting with); but in the latter application only impersonal (with G1487 (εἰ)), i.e. perchance; or (present participle) as adjective, usual (as if commonly met with, with G3756 (οὐ), extraordinary), neuter (as adverb) perhaps; or (with another verb) as adverb, by accident (as it were). Origin: probably for an obsolete (for which the middle voice of another alternate (to make ready or bring to pass) is used in certain tenses; KJV: be, chance, enjoy, little, obtain, X refresh…self, + special

G5178 τυμπανίζω (tympanízō): to stretch on an instrument of torture resembling a drum, and thus beat to death. Origin: from a derivative of G5180 (τύπτω) (meaning a drum, "tympanum"); KJV: torture

G5179 τύπος (týpos): a die (as struck), i.e. (by implication) a stamp or scar; by analogy, a shape, i.e. a statue, (figuratively) style or resemblance; specially, a sampler ("type"), i.e. a model (for imitation) or instance (for warning). Origin: from G5180 (τύπτω); KJV: en-(ex-)ample, fashion, figure, form, manner, pattern, print

G5180 τύπτω (týptō): to "thump", i.e. cudgel or pummel (properly, with a stick or bastinado), but in any case by repeated blows; thus differing from G3817 (παίω) and G3960 (πατάσσω), which denote a (usually single) blow with the hand or any instrument, or G4141 (πλήσσω) with the fist (or a hammer), or G4474 (ῥαπίζω) with the palm; as well as from G5177 (τυγχάνω), an accidental collision); by implication, to punish; figuratively, to offend (the conscience). Origin: a primary verb (in a strengthened form); KJV: beat, smite, strike, wound

G5181 Τύραννος (Týrannos): a "tyrant"; Tyrannus, an Ephesian. Origin: a provincial form of the derivative of the base of G2962 (κύριος); KJV: Tyrannus

G5182 τυρβάζω (tyrbázō): akin to G2351 (θόρυβος)); to make "turbid", i.e. disturb. Origin: from (Latin turba, a crowd; KJV: trouble

G5183 Τύριος (Týrios): a Tyrian, i.e. inhabitant of Tyrus. Origin: from G5184 (Τύρος); KJV: of Tyre

G5184 Τύρος (Týros): Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6865): Tyrus (i.e. Tsor), a place in Palestine KJV: Tyre

G5185 τυφλός (typhlós): opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally). Origin: from, G5187 (τυφόω); KJV: blind

G5186 τυφλόω (typhlóō): to make blind, i.e. (figuratively) to obscure. Origin: from G5185 (τυφλός); KJV: blind

G5187 τυφόω (typhóō): to envelop with smoke, i.e. (figuratively) to inflate with self-conceit. Origin: from a derivative of G5188 (τύφω); KJV: high-minded, be lifted up with pride, be proud

G5188 τύφω (týphō): to make a smoke, i.e. slowly consume without flame. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: smoke

G5189 τυφωνικός (typhōnikós): stormy (as if smoky). Origin: from a derivative of G5188 (τύφω); KJV: tempestuous

G5190 Τυχικός (Tychikós): fortuitous, i.e. fortunate; Tychicus, a Christian. Origin: from a derivative of G5177 (τυγχάνω); KJV: Tychicus

G5191 ὑακίνθινος (hyakínthinos): "hyacinthine" or "jacinthine", i.e. deep blue. Origin: from G5192 (ὑάκινθος); KJV: jacinth

G5192 ὑάκινθος (hyákinthos): the "hyacinth" or "jacinth", i.e. some gem of a deep blue color, probably the zirkon. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: jacinth

G5193 ὑάλινος (hyálinos): glassy, i.e. transparent. Origin: from G5194 (ὕαλος); KJV: of glass

G5194 ὕαλος (hýalos): glass. Origin: perhaps from the same as G5205 (ὑετός) (as being transparent like rain); KJV: glass

G5195 ὑβρίζω (hybrízō): to exercise violence, i.e. abuse. Origin: from G5196 (ὕβρις); KJV: use despitefully, reproach, entreat shamefully (spitefully)

G5196 ὕβρις (hýbris): insolence (as over-bearing), i.e. insult, injury. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ); KJV: harm, hurt, reproach

G5197 ὑβριστής (hybristḗs): an insulter, i.e. maltreater. Origin: from G5195 (ὑβρίζω); KJV: despiteful, injurious

G5198 ὑγιαίνω (hygiaínō): to have sound health, i.e. be well (in body); figuratively, to be uncorrupt (true in doctrine). Origin: from G5199 (ὑγιής); KJV: be in health, (be safe and) sound, (be) whole(-some)

G5199 ὑγιής (hygiḗs): healthy, i.e. well (in body); figuratively, true (in doctrine). Origin: from the base of G837 (αὐξάνω); KJV: sound, whole

G5200 ὑγρός (hygrós): wet (as if with rain), i.e. (by implication) sappy (fresh). Origin: from the base of G5205 (ὑετός); KJV: green

G5201 ὑδρία (hydría): a water-jar, i.e. receptacle for family supply. Origin: from G5204 (ὕδωρ); KJV: water-pot

G5202 ὑδροποτέω (hydropotéō): to be a water-drinker, i.e. to abstain from vinous beverages. Origin: from a compound of G5204 (ὕδωρ) and a derivative of G4095 (πίνω); KJV: drink water

G5203 ὑδρωπικός (hydrōpikós): to be "dropsical". Origin: from a compound of G5204 (ὕδωρ) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι) (as if looking watery); KJV: have the dropsy

G5204 ὕδωρ (hýdōr): water (as if rainy) literally or figuratively. Origin: from the base of G5205 (ὑετός); KJV: water

G5205 ὑετός (hyetós): rain, especially a shower. Origin: from a primary (to rain); KJV: rain

G5206 υἱοθεσία (huiothesía): the placing as a son, i.e. adoption (figuratively, Christian sonship in respect to God). Origin: from a presumed compound of G5207 (υἱός) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: adoption (of children, of sons)

G5207 υἱός (huiós): a "son" (sometimes of animals), used very widely of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: child, foal, son

G5208 ὕλη (hýlē): a forest, i.e. (by implication) fuel. Origin: perhaps akin to G3586 (ξύλον); KJV: matter

G5209 ὑμᾶς (hymâs): you (as the objective of a verb or preposition). Origin: accusative case of G5210 (ὑμεῖς); KJV: ye, you (+ -ward), your (+ own)

G5210 ὑμεῖς (hymeîs): you (as subjective of verb). Origin: irregular plural of G4771 (σύ); KJV: ye (yourselves), you

G5211 Ὑμεναῖος (Hymenaîos): "hymenæal"; Hymenæus, an opponent of Christianity. Origin: from (the god of weddings); KJV: Hymenæus

G5212 ὑμέτερος (hyméteros): yours, i.e. pertaining to you. Origin: from G5210 (ὑμεῖς); KJV: your (own)

G5213 ὑμῖν (hymîn): to (with or by) you. Origin: irregular dative case of G5210 (ὑμεῖς); KJV: ye, you, your(-selves)

G5214 ὑμνέω (hymnéō): to hymn, i.e. sing a religious ode; by implication, to celebrate (God) in song. Origin: from G5215 (ὕμνος); KJV: sing a hymn (praise unto)

G5215 ὕμνος (hýmnos): probably akin to G103 (ᾄδω); compare H05667); a "hymn" or religious ode (one of the Psalms). Origin: apparently from a simpler (obsolete) form of (to celebrate; KJV: hymn

G5216 ὑμῶν (hymōn): of (from or concerning) you. Origin: genitive case of G5210 (ὑμεῖς); KJV: ye, you, your (own, -selves)

G5217 ὑπάγω (hypágō): to lead (oneself) under, i.e. withdraw or retire (as if sinking out of sight), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: depart, get hence, go (a-)way

G5218 ὑπακοή (hypakoḗ): attentive hearkening, i.e. (by implication) compliance or submission. Origin: from G5219 (ὑπακούω); KJV: obedience, (make) obedient, obey(-ing)

G5219 ὑπακούω (hypakoúō): to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G191 (ἀκούω); KJV: hearken, be obedient to, obey

G5220 ὕπανδρος (hýpandros): in subjection under a man, i.e. a married woman. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G435 (ἀνήρ); KJV: which hath an husband

G5221 ὑπαντάω (hypantáō): to go opposite (meet) under (quietly), i.e. to encounter, fall in with. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G473 (ἀντί); KJV: (go to) meet

G5222 ὑπάντησις (hypántēsis): an encounter or concurrence (with G1519 (εἰς) for infinitive, in order to fall in with). Origin: from G5221 (ὑπαντάω); KJV: meeting

G5223 ὕπαρξις (hýparxis): existency or proprietorship, i.e. (concretely) property, wealth. Origin: from G5225 (ὑπάρχω); KJV: goods, substance

G5224 ὑπάρχοντα (hypárchonta): things extant or in hand, i.e. property or possessions. Origin: neuter plural of present participle active of G5225 (ὑπάρχω) as noun; KJV: goods, that which one has, things which (one) possesseth, substance, that hast

G5225 ὑπάρχω (hypárchō): to begin under (quietly), i.e. come into existence (be present or at hand); expletively, to exist (as copula or subordinate to an adjective, participle, adverb or preposition, or as an auxiliary to a principal (verb). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G756 (ἄρχομαι); KJV: after, behave, live

G5226 ὑπείκω (hypeíkō): to surrender. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and (to yield, be "weak"); KJV: submit self

G5227 ὑπεναντίος (hypenantíos): under (covertly) contrary to, i.e. opposed or (as noun) an opponent. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G1727 (ἐναντίος); KJV: adversary, against

G5228 ὑπέρ (hypér): "over", i.e. (with the genitive case) of place, above, beyond, across, or causal, for the sake of, instead, regarding; with the accusative case superior to, more than. Origin: a primary preposition; KJV: (+ exceeding, abundantly) above, in (on) behalf of, beyond, by, + very chiefest, concerning, exceeding (above, -ly), for, + very highly, more (than), of, over, on the part of, for sake of, in stead, than, to(-ward), very

G5229 ὑπεραίρομαι (hyperaíromai): to raise oneself over, i.e. (figuratively) to become haughty. Origin: middle voice from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G142 (αἴρω); KJV: exalt self, be exalted above measure

G5230 ὑπέρακμος (hypérakmos): beyond the "acme", i.e. figuratively (of a daughter) past the bloom (prime) of youth. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the base of G188 (ἀκμήν); KJV: + pass the flower of (her) age

G5231 ὑπεράνω (hyperánō): above upward, i.e. greatly higher (in place or rank). Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G507 (ἄνω); KJV: far above, over

G5232 ὑπεραυξάνω (hyperauxánō): to increase above ordinary degree. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G837 (αὐξάνω); KJV: grow exceedingly

G5233 ὑπερβαίνω (hyperbaínō): to transcend, i.e. (figuratively) to overreach. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the base of G939 (βάσις); KJV: go beyond

G5234 ὑπερβαλλόντως (hyperballóntōs): excessively. Origin: adverb from present participle active of G5235 (ὑπερβάλλω); KJV: beyond measure

G5235 ὑπερβάλλω (hyperbállō): to throw beyod the usual mark, i.e. (figuratively) to surpass (only active participle supereminent). Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: exceeding, excel, pass

G5236 ὑπερβολή (hyperbolḗ): a throwing beyond others, i.e. (figuratively) supereminence; adverbially (with G1519 (εἰς) or G2596 (κατά)) pre- eminently. Origin: from G5235 (ὑπερβάλλω); KJV: abundance, (far more) exceeding, excellency, more excellent, beyond (out of) measure

G5237 ὑπερείδω (hypereídō): to overlook, i.e. not punish. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G1492 (εἴδω); KJV: wink at

G5238 ὑπερέκεινα (hyperékeina): above those parts, i.e. still farther. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the neuter plural of G1565 (ἐκεῖνος); KJV: beyond

G5239 ὑπερεκτείνω (hyperekteínō): to extend inordinately. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G1614 (ἐκτείνω); KJV: stretch beyond

G5240 ὑπερεκχύνω (hyperekchýnō): to pour out over, i.e. (passively) to overflow. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and the alternate form of G1632 (ἐκχέω); KJV: run over

G5241 ὑπερεντυγχάνω (hyperentynchánō): to intercede in behalf of. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G1793 (ἐντυγχάνω); KJV: make intercession for

G5242 ὑπερέχω (hyperéchō): to hold oneself above, i.e. (figuratively) to excel; participle (as adjective, or neuter as noun) superior, superiority. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: better, excellency, higher, pass, supreme

G5243 ὑπερηφανία (hyperēphanía): haughtiness. Origin: from G5244 (ὑπερήφανος); KJV: pride

G5244 ὑπερήφανος (hyperḗphanos): appearing above others (conspicuous), i.e. (figuratively) haughty. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: proud

G5245 ὑπερνικάω (hypernikáō): to vanquish beyond, i.e. gain a decisive victory. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G3528 (νικάω); KJV: more than conquer

G5246 ὑπέρογκος (hypéronkos): bulging over, i.e. (figuratively) insolent. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G3591 (ὄγκος); KJV: great swelling

G5247 ὑπεροχή (hyperochḗ): prominence, i.e. (figuratively) superiority (in rank or character). Origin: from G5242 (ὑπερέχω); KJV: authority, excellency

G5248 ὑπερπερισσεύω (hyperperisseúō): to super-abound. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G4052 (περισσεύω); KJV: abound much more, exceeding

G5249 ὑπερπερισσῶς (hyperperissōs): superabundantly, i.e. exceedingly. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G4057 (περισσῶς); KJV: beyond measure

G5250 ὑπερπλεονάζω (hyperpleonázō): to superabound. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G4121 (πλεονάζω); KJV: be exceeding abundant

G5251 ὑπερυψόω (hyperypsóō): to elevate above others, i.e. raise to the highest position. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G5312 (ὑψόω); KJV: highly exalt

G5252 ὑπερφρονέω (hyperphronéō): to esteem oneself overmuch, i.e. be vain or arrogant. Origin: from G5228 (ὑπέρ) and G5426 (φρονέω); KJV: think more highly

G5253 ὑπερῷον (hyperōion): a higher part of the house, i.e. apartment in the third story. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G5228 (ὑπέρ); KJV: upper chamber (room)

G5254 ὑπέχω (hypéchō): to hold oneself under, i.e. endure with patience. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G2192 (ἔχω); KJV: suffer

G5255 ὑπήκοος (hypḗkoos): attentively listening, i.e. (by implication) submissive. Origin: from G5219 (ὑπακούω); KJV: obedient

G5256 ὑπηρετέω (hypēretéō): to be a subordinate, i.e. (by implication) subserve. Origin: from G5257 (ὑπηρέτης); KJV: minister (unto), serve

G5257 ὑπηρέτης (hypērétēs): an under-oarsman, i.e. (generally) subordinate (assistant, sexton, constable). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of (to row); KJV: minister, officer, servant

G5258 ὕπνος (hýpnos): sleep, i.e. (figuratively) spiritual torpor. Origin: from an obsolete primary (perhaps akin to G5259 (ὑπό) through the idea of subsilience); KJV: sleep

G5259 ὑπό (hypó): under, i.e. (with the genitive case) of place (beneath), or with verbs (the agency or means, through); (with the accusative case) of place (whither (underneath) or where (below) or time (when (at)). Origin: a primary preposition; KJV: among, by, from, in, of, under, with

G5260 ὑποβάλλω (hypobállō): to throw in stealthily, i.e. introduce by collusion. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G906 (βάλλω); KJV: suborn

G5261 ὑπογραμμός (hypogrammós): an underwriting, i.e. copy for imitation (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G1125 (γράφω); KJV: example

G5262 ὑπόδειγμα (hypódeigma): an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration). Origin: from G5263 (ὑποδείκνυμι); KJV: en-(ex-)ample, pattern

G5263 ὑποδείκνυμι (hypodeíknymi): to exhibit under the eyes, i.e. (figuratively) to exemplify (instruct, admonish). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G1166 (δεικνύω); KJV: show, (fore-)warn

G5264 ὑποδέχομαι (hypodéchomai): to admit under one's roof, i.e. entertain hospitably. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G1209 (δέχομαι); KJV: receive

G5265 ὑποδέω (hypodéō): to bind under one's feet, i.e. put on shoes or sandals. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G1210 (δέω); KJV: bind on, (be) shod

G5266 ὑπόδημα (hypódēma): something bound under the feet, i.e. a shoe or sandal. Origin: from G5265 (ὑποδέω); KJV: shoe

G5267 ὑπόδικος (hypódikos): under sentence, i.e. (by implication) condemned. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G1349 (δίκη); KJV: guilty

G5268 ὑποζύγιον (hypozýgion): an animal under the yoke (draught-beast), i.e. (specially), a donkey. Origin: neuter of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G2218 (ζυγός); KJV: ass

G5269 ὑποζώννυμι (hypozṓnnymi): to gird under, i.e. frap (a vessel with cables across the keel, sides and deck). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G2224 (ζώννυμι); KJV: undergirt

G5270 ὑποκάτω (hypokátō): down under, i.e. beneath. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G2736 (κάτω); KJV: under

G5271 ὑποκρίνομαι (hypokrínomai): to decide (speak or act) under a false part, i.e. (figuratively) dissemble (pretend). Origin: middle voice from G5259 (ὑπό) and G2919 (κρίνω); KJV: feign

G5272 ὑπόκρισις (hypókrisis): acting under a feigned part, i.e. (figuratively) deceit ("hypocrisy"). Origin: from G5271 (ὑποκρίνομαι); KJV: condemnation, dissimulation, hypocrisy

G5273 ὑποκριτής (hypokritḗs): an actor under an assumed character (stage-player), i.e. (figuratively) a dissembler ("hypocrite". Origin: from G5271 (ὑποκρίνομαι); KJV: hypocrite

G5274 ὑπολαμβάνω (hypolambánō): to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G2983 (λαμβάνω); KJV: answer, receive, suppose

G5275 ὑπολείπω (hypoleípō): to leave under (behind), i.e. (passively) to remain (survive). Origin: from G5295 (ὑποτρέχω) and G3007 (λείπω); KJV: be left

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G5276 to G5409
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G5276 ὑπολήνιον (hypolḗnion): vessel or receptacle under the press, i.e. lower wine-vat. Origin: neuter of a presumed compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G3025 (ληνός); KJV: winefat

G5277 ὑπολιμπάνω (hypolimpánō): to leave behind, i.e. bequeath. Origin: a prolonged form for G5275 (ὑπολείπω); KJV: leave

G5278 ὑπομένω (hypoménō): to stay under (behind), i.e. remain; figuratively, to undergo, i.e. bear (trials), have fortitude, persevere. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G3306 (μένω); KJV: abide, endure, (take) patient(-ly), suffer, tarry behind

G5279 ὑπομιμνήσκω (hypomimnḗskō): to remind quietly, i.e. suggest to the (middle voice, one's own) memory. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G3403 (μιμνήσκω); KJV: put in mind, remember, bring to (put in) remembrance

G5280 ὑπόμνησις (hypómnēsis): a reminding or (reflexively) recollection. Origin: from G5279 (ὑπομιμνήσκω); KJV: remembrance

G5281 ὑπομονή (hypomonḗ): cheerful (or hopeful) endurance, constancy. Origin: from G5278 (ὑπομένω); KJV: enduring, patience, patient continuance (waiting)

G5282 ὑπονοέω (hyponoéō): to think under (privately), i.e. to surmise or conjecture. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G3539 (νοιέω); KJV: think, suppose, deem

G5283 ὑπόνοια (hypónoia): suspicion. Origin: from G5282 (ὑπονοέω); KJV: surmising

G5284 ὑποπλέω (hypopléō): to sail under the lee of. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G4126 (πλέω); KJV: sail under

G5285 ὑποπνέω (hypopnéō): to breathe gently, i.e. breeze. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G4154 (πνέω); KJV: blow softly

G5286 ὑποπόδιον (hypopódion): something under the feet, i.e. a foot-rest (figuratively). Origin: neuter of a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G4228 (πούς); KJV: footstool

G5287 ὑπόστασις (hypóstasis): a setting under (support), i.e. (figuratively) concretely, essence, or abstractly, assurance (objectively or subjectively). Origin: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and G2476 (ἵστημι); KJV: confidence, confident, person, substance

G5288 ὑποστέλλω (hypostéllō): to withhold under (out of sight), i.e. (reflexively) to cower or shrink, (figuratively) to conceal (reserve). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G4724 (στέλλω); KJV: draw (keep) back, shun, withdraw

G5289 ὑποστολή (hypostolḗ): shrinkage (timidity), i.e. (by implication) apostasy. Origin: from G5288 (ὑποστέλλω); KJV: draw back

G5290 ὑποστρέφω (hypostréphō): to turn under (behind), i.e. to return (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G4762 (στρέφω); KJV: come again, return (again, back again), turn back (again)

G5291 ὑποστρώννυμι (hypostrṓnnymi): to strew underneath (the feet as a carpet). Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G4766 (στρώννυμι); KJV: spread

G5292 ὑποταγή (hypotagḗ): subordination. Origin: from G5293 (ὑποτάσσω); KJV: subjection

G5293 ὑποτάσσω (hypotássō): to subordinate; reflexively, to obey. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5021 (τάσσω); KJV: be under obedience (obedient), put under, subdue unto, (be, make) subject (to, unto), be (put) in subjection (to, under), submit self unto

G5294 ὑποτίθημι (hypotíthēmi): to place underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to hazard, (reflexively) to suggest. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5087 (τίθημι); KJV: lay down, put in remembrance

G5295 ὑποτρέχω (hypotréchō): to run under, i.e. (specially), to sail past. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5143 (τρέχω) (including its alternate); KJV: run under

G5296 ὑποτύπωσις (hypotýpōsis): typification under (after), i.e. (concretely) a sketch (figuratively) for imitation. Origin: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G5179 (τύπος); KJV: form, pattern

G5297 ὑποφέρω (hypophérō): to bear from underneath, i.e. (figuratively) to undergo hardship. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: bear, endure

G5298 ὑποχωρέω (hypochōréō): to vacate down, i.e. retire quietly. Origin: from G5259 (ὑπό) and G5562 (χωρέω); KJV: go aside, withdraw self

G5299 ὑπωπιάζω (hypōpiázō): to hit under the eye (buffet or disable an antagonist as a pugilist), i.e. (figuratively) to tease or annoy (into compliance), subdue (one's passions). Origin: from a compound of G5259 (ὑπό) and a derivative of G3700 (ὀπτάνομαι); KJV: keep under, weary

G5300 ὗς (hŷs): a hog ("swine"). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: sow

G5301 ὕσσωπος (hýssōpos): "hyssop". Origin: of foreign origin (H231); KJV: hyssop

G5302 ὑστερέω (hysteréō): to be later, i.e. (by implication) to be inferior; generally, to fall short (be deficient). Origin: from G5306 (ὕστερος); KJV: come behind (short), be destitute, fail, lack, suffer need, (be in) want, be the worse

G5303 ὑστέρημα (hystérēma): a deficit; specially, poverty. Origin: from G5302 (ὑστερέω); KJV: that which is behind, (that which was) lack(-ing), penury, want

G5304 ὑστέρησις (hystérēsis): a falling short, i.e. (specially), penury. Origin: from G5302 (ὑστερέω); KJV: want

G5305 ὕστερον (hýsteron): more lately, i.e. eventually. Origin: neuter of G5306 (ὕστερος) as adverb; KJV: afterward, (at the) last (of all)

G5306 ὕστερος (hýsteros): later. Origin: comparative from G5259 (ὑπό) (in the sense of behind); KJV: latter

G5307 ὑφαντός (hyphantós): woven, i.e. (perhaps) knitted. Origin: from to weave; KJV: woven

G5308 ὑψηλός (hypsēlós): lofty (in place or character). Origin: from G5311 (ὕψος); KJV: high(-er, -ly) (esteemed)

G5309 ὑψηλοφρονέω (hypsēlophronéō): to be lofty in mind, i.e. arrogant. Origin: from a compound of G5308 (ὑψηλός) and G5424 (φρήν); KJV: be highminded

G5310 ὕψιστος (hýpsistos): highest, i.e. (masculine singular) the Supreme (God), or (neuter plural) the heavens. Origin: superlative from the base of G5311 (ὕψος); KJV: most high, highest

G5311 ὕψος (hýpsos): elevation, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, (specially), the sky, or (figuratively) dignity. Origin: from a derivative of G5228 (ὑπέρ); KJV: be exalted, height, (on) high

G5312 ὑψόω (hypsóō): to elevate (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5311 (ὕψος); KJV: exalt, lift up

G5313 ὕψωμα (hýpsōma): an elevated place or thing, i.e. (abstractly) altitude, or (by implication) a barrier (figuratively). Origin: from G5312 (ὑψόω); KJV: height, high thing

G5314 φάγος (phágos): a glutton. Origin: from G5315 (φάγω); KJV: gluttonous

G5315 φάγω (phágō): to eat (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primary verb (used as an alternate of G2068 (ἐσθίω) in certain tenses); KJV: eat, meat

G5316 φαίνω (phaínō): to lighten (shine), i.e. show (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative). Origin: prolongation for the base of G5457 (φῶς); KJV: appear, seem, be seen, shine, X think

G5317 Φάλεκ (Phálek): Phalek (i.e. Peleg), a patriarch. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6389); KJV: Phalec

G5318 φανερός (phanerós): shining, i.e. apparent (literally or figuratively); neuter (as adverb) publicly, externally. Origin: from G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: abroad, + appear, known, manifest, open (+ -ly), outward (+ -ly)

G5319 φανερόω (phaneróō): to render apparent (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5318 (φανερός); KJV: appear, manifestly declare, (make) manifest (forth), shew (self)

G5320 φανερῶς (phanerōs): plainly, i.e. clearly or publicly. Origin: adverb from G5318 (φανερός); KJV: evidently, openly

G5321 φανέρωσις (phanérōsis): exhibition, i.e. (figuratively) expression, (by extension) a bestowment. Origin: from G5319 (φανερόω); KJV: manifestation

G5322 φανός (phanós): a lightener, i.e. light; lantern. Origin: from G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: lantern

G5323 Φανουήλ (Phanouḗl): Phanuel (i.e. Penuel), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6439); KJV: Phanuel

G5324 φαντάζω (phantázō): to make apparent, i.e. (passively) to appear (neuter participle as noun, a spectacle). Origin: from a derivative of G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: sight

G5325 φαντασία (phantasía): (properly abstract) a (vain) show ("fantasy"). Origin: from a derivative of G5324 (φαντάζω); KJV: pomp

G5326 φάντασμα (phántasma): (properly concrete) a (mere) show ("phantasm"), i.e. spectre. Origin: from G5324 (φαντάζω); KJV: spirit

G5327 φάραγξ (pháranx): a gap or chasm, i.e. ravine (winter-torrent). Origin: properly, strengthened from the base of G4008 (πέραν) or rather of G4486 (ῥήγνυμι); KJV: valley

G5328 Φαραώ (Pharaṓ): Pharao (i.e. Pharoh), an Egyptian king. Origin: of foreign origin (H6547); KJV: Pharaoh

G5329 Φάρες (Pháres): Phares (i.e. Perets), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H6557); KJV: Phares

G5330 Φαρισαῖος (Pharisaîos): a separatist, i.e. exclusively religious; a Pharisean, i.e. Jewish sectary. Origin: of Hebrew origin (compare H6567); KJV: Pharisee

G5331 φαρμακεία (pharmakeía): medication ("pharmacy"), i.e. (by extension) magic (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5332 (φαρμακεύς); KJV: sorcery, witchcraft

G5332 φαρμακεύς (pharmakeús): a druggist ("pharmacist") or poisoner, i.e. (by extension) a magician. Origin: from (a drug, i.e. spell-giving potion); KJV: sorcerer

G5333 φάρμακος (phármakos): Origin: the same as 5332 KJV: sorcerer

G5334 φάσις (phásis): a saying, i.e. report. Origin: from G5346 (φημί) (not the same as "phase", which is from G5316 (φαίνω)); KJV: tidings

G5335 φάσκω (pháskō): to assert. Origin: prolongation from the same as G5346 (φημί); KJV: affirm, profess, say

G5336 φάτνη (phátnē): a crib (for fodder). Origin: from (to eat); KJV: manager, stall

G5337 φαῦλος (phaûlos): "foul" or "flawy", i.e. (figuratively) wicked. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: evil

G5338 φέγγος (phéngos): brilliancy. Origin: probably akin to the base of G5457 (φῶς) (compare G5350 (φθέγγομαι)); KJV: light

G5339 φείδομαι (pheídomai): to be chary of, i.e. (subjectively) to abstain or (objectively) to treat leniently. Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: forbear, spare

G5340 φειδομένως (pheidoménōs): abstemiously, i.e. stingily. Origin: adverb from participle of G5339 (φείδομαι); KJV: sparingly

G5341 φελόνης (phelónēs): a mantle (surtout). Origin: by transposition for a derivative probably of G5316 (φαίνω) (as showing outside the other garments); KJV: cloke

G5342 φέρω (phérō): to "bear" or carry (in a very wide application, literally and figuratively, as follows). Origin: a primary verb (for which other, and apparently not cognate ones are used in certain tenses only; namely, ; and ; KJV: be, bear, bring (forth), carry, come, + let her drive, be driven, endure, go on, lay, lead, move, reach, rushing, uphold

G5343 φεύγω (pheúgō): to run away (literally or figuratively); by implication, to shun; by analogy, to vanish. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: escape, flee (away)

G5344 Φῆλιξ (Phēlix): happy; Phelix (i.e. Felix), a Roman. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Felix

G5345 φήμη (phḗmē): a saying, i.e. rumor ("fame"). Origin: from G5346 (φημί); KJV: fame

G5346 φημί (phēmí): to show or make known one's thoughts, i.e. speak or say. Origin: properly, the same as the base of G5457 (φῶς) and G5316 (φαίνω); KJV: affirm, say

G5347 Φῆστος (Phēstos): festal; Phestus (i.e. Festus), a Roman. Origin: of Latin derivation; KJV: Festus

G5348 φθάνω (phthánō): to be beforehand, i.e. anticipate or precede; by extension, to have arrived at. Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: (already) attain, come, prevent

G5349 φθαρτός (phthartós): decayed, i.e. (by implication) perishable. Origin: from G5351 (φθείρω); KJV: corruptible

G5350 φθέγγομαι (phthéngomai): to utter a clear sound, i.e. (generally) to proclaim. Origin: probably akin to G5338 (φέγγος) and thus to G5346 (φημί); KJV: speak

G5351 φθείρω (phtheírō): properly, to shrivel or wither, i.e. to spoil (by any process) or (generally) to ruin (especially figuratively, by moral influences, to deprave). Origin: probably strengthened from (to pine or waste); KJV: corrupt (self), defile, destroy

G5352 φθινοπωρινός (phthinopōrinós): akin to the base of G5351 (φθείρω)) and G3703 (ὀπώρα) (meaning late autumn); autumnal (as stripped of leaves). Origin: from derivative of (to wane; KJV: whose fruit withereth

G5353 φθόγγος (phthóngos): utterance, i.e. a musical note (vocal or instrumental). Origin: from G5350 (φθέγγομαι); KJV: sound

G5354 φθονέω (phthonéō): to be jealous of. Origin: from G5355 (φθόνος); KJV: envy

G5355 φθόνος (phthónos): ill-will (as detraction), i.e. jealousy (spite). Origin: probably akin to the base of G5351 (φθείρω); KJV: envy

G5356 φθορά (phthorá): decay, i.e. ruin (spontaneous or inflicted, literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5351 (φθείρω); KJV: corruption, destroy, perish

G5357 φιάλη (phiálē): a broad shallow cup ("phial"). Origin: of uncertain affinity; KJV: vial

G5358 φιλάγαθος (philágathos): fond to good, i.e. a promoter of virtue. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G18 (ἀγαθός); KJV: love of good men

G5359 Φιλαδέλφεια (Philadélpheia): Philadelphia, a place in Asia Minor. Origin: from (the same as G5361 (φιλάδελφος)), a king of Pergamos; KJV: Philadelphia

G5360 φιλαδελφία (philadelphía): fraternal affection. Origin: from G5361 (φιλάδελφος); KJV: brotherly love (kindness), love of the brethren

G5361 φιλάδελφος (philádelphos): fond of brethren, i.e. fraternal. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G80 (ἀδελφός); KJV: love as brethren

G5362 φίλανδρος (phílandros): fond of man, i.e. affectionate as a wife. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G435 (ἀνήρ); KJV: love their husbands

G5363 φιλανθρωπία (philanthrōpía): fondness of mankind, i.e. benevolence ("philanthropy"). Origin: from the same as G5364 (φιλανθρώπως); KJV: kindness, love towards man

G5364 φιλανθρώπως (philanthrṓpōs): fondly to man ("philanthropically"), i.e. humanely. Origin: adverb from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G444 (ἄνθρωπος); KJV: courteously

G5365 φιλαργυρία (philargyría): avarice. Origin: from G5366 (φιλάργυρος); KJV: love of money

G5366 φιλάργυρος (philárgyros): fond of silver (money), i.e. avaricious. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G696 (ἄργυρος); KJV: covetous

G5367 φίλαυτος (phílautos): fond of self, i.e. selfish. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G846 (αὐτός); KJV: lover of own self

G5368 φιλέω (philéō): to be a friend to (fond of (an individual or an object)), i.e. have affection for (denoting personal attachment, as a matter of sentiment or feeling; while G25 (ἀγαπάω) is wider, embracing especially the judgment and the deliberate assent of the will as a matter of principle, duty and propriety: the two thus stand related very much as G2309 (θέλω) and G1014 (βούλομαι), or as G2372 (θυμός) and G3563 (νοῦς) respectively; the former being chiefly of the heart and the latter of the head); specially, to kiss (as a mark of tenderness). Origin: from G5384 (φίλος); KJV: kiss, love

G5369 φιλήδονος (philḗdonos): fond of pleasure, i.e. voluptuous. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G2237 (ἡδονή); KJV: lover of pleasure

G5370 φίλημα (phílēma): a kiss. Origin: from G5368 (φιλέω); KJV: kiss

G5371 Φιλήμων (Philḗmōn): friendly; Philemon, a Christian. Origin: from G5368 (φιλέω); KJV: Philemon

G5372 Φίλητος (Phílētos): amiable; Philetus, an opposer of Christianity. Origin: from G5368 (φιλέω); KJV: Philetus

G5373 φιλία (philía): fondness. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος); KJV: friendship

G5374 Φιλιππήσιος (Philippḗsios): a Philippesian (Philippian), i.e. native of Philippi. Origin: from G5375 (Φίλιπποι); KJV: Philippian

G5375 Φίλιπποι (Phílippoi): Philippi, a place in Macedonia. Origin: plural of G5376 (Φίλιππος); KJV: Philippi

G5376 Φίλιππος (Phílippos): fond of horses; Philippus, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G2462 (ἵππος); KJV: Philip

G5377 φιλόθεος (philótheos): fond of God, i.e. pious. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G2316 (θεός); KJV: lover of God

G5378 Φιλόλογος (Philólogos): fond of words, i.e. talkative (argumentative, learned, "philological"); Philologus, a Christian. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G3056 (λόγος); KJV: Philologus

G5379 φιλονεικία (philoneikía): quarrelsomeness, i.e. a dispute. Origin: from G5380 (φιλόνεικος); KJV: strife

G5380 φιλόνεικος (philóneikos): probably akin to G3534 (νῖκος)); fond of strife, i.e. disputatious. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and (a quarrel; KJV: contentious

G5381 φιλονεξία (philonexía): hospitableness. Origin: from G5382 (φιλόξενος); KJV: entertain stranger, hospitality

G5382 φιλόξενος (philóxenos): fond of guests, i.e. hospitable. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G3581 (ξένος); KJV: given to (lover of, use) hospitality

G5383 φιλοπρωτεύω (philoprōteúō): to be fond of being first, i.e. ambitious of distinction. Origin: from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G4413 (πρῶτος); KJV: love to have the preeminence

G5384 φίλος (phílos): actively, fond, i.e. friendly (still as a noun, an associate, neighbor, etc.). Origin: properly, dear, i.e. a friend; KJV: friend

G5385 φιλοσοφία (philosophía): "philosophy", i.e. (specially), Jewish sophistry. Origin: from G5386 (φιλόσοφος); KJV: philosophy

G5386 φιλόσοφος (philósophos): fond of wise things, i.e. a "philosopher". Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G4680 (σοφός); KJV: philosopher

G5387 φιλόστοργος (philóstorgos): fond of natural relatives, i.e. fraternal towards fellow Christian. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and (cherishing one's kindred, especially parents or children); KJV: kindly affectioned

G5388 φιλότεκνος (philóteknos): fond of one's children, i.e. maternal. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G5043 (τέκνον); KJV: love their children

G5389 φιλοτιμέομαι (philotiméomai): to be fond of honor, i.e. emulous (eager or earnest to do something). Origin: middle voice from a compound of G5384 (φίλος) and G5092 (τιμή); KJV: labour, strive, study

G5390 φιλοφρόνως (philophrónōs): with friendliness of mind, i.e. kindly. Origin: adverb from G5391 (φιλόφρων); KJV: courteously

G5391 φιλόφρων (philóphrōn): friendly of mind, i.e. kind. Origin: from G5384 (φίλος) and G5424 (φρήν); KJV: courteous

G5392 φιμόω (phimóō): to muzzle. Origin: from (a muzzle); KJV: muzzle

G5393 Φλέγων (Phlégōn): blazing; Phlegon, a Christian. Origin: active participle of the base of G5395 (φλόξ); KJV: Phlegon

G5394 φλογίζω (phlogízō): to cause a blaze, i.e. ignite (figuratively, to inflame with passion). Origin: from G5395 (φλόξ); KJV: set on fire

G5395 φλόξ (phlóx): a blaze. Origin: from a primary (to "flash" or "flame"); KJV: flame(-ing)

G5396 φλυαρέω (phlyaréō): to be a babbler or trifler, i.e. (by implication) to berate idly or mischievously. Origin: from G5397 (φλύαρος); KJV: prate against

G5397 φλύαρος (phlýaros): a garrulous person, i.e. prater. Origin: from (to bubble); KJV: tattler

G5398 φοβερός (phoberós): frightful, i.e. (objectively) formidable. Origin: from G5401 (φόβος); KJV: fearful, terrible

G5399 φοβέω (phobéō): to frighten, i.e. (passively) to be alarmed; by analogy, to be in awe of, i.e. revere. Origin: from G5401 (φόβος); KJV: be (+ sore) afraid, fear (exceedingly), reverence

G5400 φόβητρον (phóbētron): a frightening thing, i.e. terrific portent. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G5399 (φοβέω); KJV: fearful sight

G5401 φόβος (phóbos): alarm or fright. Origin: from a primary (to be put in fear); KJV: be afraid, + exceedingly, fear, terror

G5402 Φοίβη (Phoíbē): probably akin to the base of G5457 (φῶς)); Phœbe, a Christian woman. Origin: feminine of (bright; KJV: Phebe

G5403 Φοινίκη (Phoiníkē): palm-country; Phœnice (or Phœnicia), a region of Palestine. Origin: from G5404 (φοῖνιξ); KJV: Phenice, Phenicia

G5404 φοῖνιξ (phoînix): a palm-tree. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: palm (tree)

G5405 Φοῖνιξ (Phoînix): Phœnix, a place in Crete. Origin: probably the same as G5404 (φοῖνιξ); KJV: Phenice

G5406 φονεύς (phoneús): a murderer (always of criminal (or at least intentional) homicide; which G443 (ἀνθρωποκτόνος) does not necessarily imply; while G4607 (σικάριος) is a special term for a public bandit). Origin: from G5408 (φόνος); KJV: murderer

G5407 φονεύω (phoneúō): to be a murderer (of). Origin: from G5406 (φονεύς); KJV: kill, do murder, slay

G5408 φόνος (phónos): murder. Origin: from an obsolete primary (to slay); KJV: murder, + be slain with, slaughter

G5409 φορέω (phoréō): to have a burden, i.e. (by analogy) to wear as clothing or a constant accompaniment. Origin: from G5411 (φόρος); KJV: bear, wear

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G5410 to G5532
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G5410 Φόρον (Phóron): a forum or market-place; only in comparative with G675 (Ἄππιος); a station on the Appian road. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: forum

G5411 φόρος (phóros): a load (as borne), i.e. (figuratively) a tax (properly, an individual assessment on persons or property; whereas G5056 (τέλος) is usually a general toll on goods or travel). Origin: from G5342 (φέρω); KJV: tribute

G5412 φορτίζω (phortízō): to load up (properly, as a vessel or animal), i.e. (figuratively) to overburden with ceremony (or spiritual anxiety). Origin: from G5414 (φόρτος); KJV: lade, by heavy laden

G5413 φορτίον (phortíon): an invoice (as part of freight), i.e. (figuratively) a task or service. Origin: diminutive of G5414 (φόρτος); KJV: burden

G5414 φόρτος (phórtos): something carried, i.e. the cargo of a ship. Origin: from G5342 (φέρω); KJV: lading

G5415 Φορτουνᾶτος (Phortounâtos): "fortunate"; Fortunatus, a Christian. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: Fortunatus

G5416 φραγέλλιον (phragéllion): a whip, i.e. Roman lash as a public punishment. Origin: neuter of a derivative from the base of G5417 (φραγελλόω); KJV: scourge

G5417 φραγελλόω (phragellóō): to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment. Origin: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; KJV: scourge

G5418 φραγμός (phragmós): a fence, or inclosing barrier (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5420 (φράσσω); KJV: hedge (+ round about), partition

G5419 φράζω (phrázō): to indicate (by word or act), i.e. (specially), to expound. Origin: probably akin to G5420 (φράσσω) through the idea of defining; KJV: declare

G5420 φράσσω (phrássō): to fence or inclose, i.e. (specially), to block up (figuratively, to silence). Origin: apparently a strengthening form of the base of G5424 (φρήν); KJV: stop

G5421 φρέαρ (phréar): a hole in the ground (dug for obtaining or holding water or other purposes), i.e. a cistern or well; figuratively, an abyss (as a prison). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: well, pit

G5422 φρεναπατάω (phrenapatáō): to be a mind-misleader, i.e. delude. Origin: from G5423 (φρεναπάτης); KJV: deceive

G5423 φρεναπάτης (phrenapátēs): a mind-misleader, i.e. seducer. Origin: from G5424 (φρήν) and G539 (ἀπάτη); KJV: deceiver

G5424 φρήν (phrḗn): the midrif (as a partition of the body), i.e. (figuratively and by implication, of sympathy) the feelings (or sensitive nature; by extension (also in the plural) the mind or cognitive faculties). Origin: probably from an obsolete (to rein in or curb; compare G5420 (φράσσω)); KJV: understanding

G5425 φρίσσω (phríssō): to "bristle" or chill, i.e. shudder (fear). Origin: apparently a primary verb; KJV: tremble

G5426 φρονέω (phronéō): to exercise the mind, i.e. entertain or have a sentiment or opinion; by implication, to be (mentally) disposed (more or less earnestly in a certain direction); intensively, to interest oneself in (with concern or obedience). Origin: from G5424 (φρήν); KJV: set the affection on, (be) care(-ful), (be like-, + be of one, + be of the same, + let this) mind(-ed), regard, savour, think

G5427 φρόνημα (phrónēma): (mental) inclination or purpose. Origin: from G5426 (φρονέω); KJV: (be, + be carnally, + be spiritually) mind(-ed)

G5428 φρόνησις (phrónēsis): mental action or activity, i.e. intellectual or moral insight. Origin: from G5426 (φρονέω); KJV: prudence, wisdom

G5429 φρόνιμος (phrónimos): thoughtful, i.e. sagacious or discreet (implying a cautious character; while G4680 (σοφός) denotes practical skill or acumen; and G4908 (συνετός) indicates rather intelligence or mental acquirement); in a bad sense conceited (also in the comparative). Origin: from G5424 (φρήν); KJV: wise(-r)

G5430 φρονίμως (phronímōs): prudently. Origin: adverb from G5429 (φρόνιμος); KJV: wisely

G5431 φροντίζω (phrontízō): to exercise thought, i.e. be anxious. Origin: from a derivative of G5424 (φρήν); KJV: be careful

G5432 φρουρέω (phrouréō): to be a watcher in advance, i.e. to mount guard as a sentinel (post spies at gates); figuratively, to hem in, protect. Origin: from a compound of G4253 (πρό) and G3708 (ὁράω); KJV: keep (with a garrison)

G5433 φρυάσσω (phryássō): to snort (as a spirited horse), i.e. (figuratively) to make a tumult. Origin: akin to G1032 (βρύω), G1031 (βρύχω); KJV: rage

G5434 φρύγανον (phrýganon): akin to the base of G5395 (φλόξ)); something desiccated, i.e. a dry twig. Origin: neuter of a presumed derivative of (to roast or parch; KJV: stick

G5435 Φρυγία (Phrygía): Phrygia, a region of Asia Minor. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Phrygia

G5436 Φύγελλος (Phýgellos): fugitive; Phygellus, an apostate Christian. Origin: probably from G5343 (φεύγω); KJV: Phygellus

G5437 φυγή (phygḗ): a fleeing, i.e. escape. Origin: from G5343 (φεύγω); KJV: flight

G5438 φυλακή (phylakḗ): a guarding or (concretely, guard), the act, the person; figuratively, the place, the condition, or (specially), the time (as a division of day or night), literally or figuratively. Origin: from G5442 (φυλάσσω); KJV: cage, hold, (im-)prison(-ment), ward, watch

G5439 φυλακίζω (phylakízō): to incarcerate. Origin: from G5441 (φύλαξ); KJV: imprison

G5440 φυλακτήριον (phylaktḗrion): a guard-case, i.e. "phylactery" for wearing slips of Scripture texts. Origin: neuter of a derivative of G5442 (φυλάσσω); KJV: phylactery

G5441 φύλαξ (phýlax): a watcher or sentry. Origin: from G5442 (φυλάσσω); KJV: keeper

G5442 φυλάσσω (phylássō): to watch, i.e. be on guard (literally of figuratively); by implication, to preserve, obey, avoid. Origin: probably from G5443 (φυλή) through the idea of isolation; KJV: beward, keep (self), observe, save

G5443 φυλή (phylḗ): an offshoot, i.e. race or clan. Origin: from G5453 (φύω) (compare G5444 (φύλλον)); KJV: kindred, tribe

G5444 φύλλον (phýllon): a sprout, i.e. leaf. Origin: from the same as G5443 (φυλή); KJV: leaf

G5445 φύραμα (phýrama): perhaps akin to G5453 (φύω) through the idea of swelling in bulk), mean to knead; a mass of dough. Origin: from a prolonged form of (to mix a liquid with a solid; KJV: lump

G5446 φυσικός (physikós): "physical", i.e. (by implication) instinctive. Origin: from G5449 (φύσις); KJV: natural

G5447 φυσικῶς (physikōs): "physically", i.e. (by implication) instinctively. Origin: adverb from G5446 (φυσικός); KJV: naturally

G5448 φυσιόω (physióō): to inflate, i.e. (figuratively) make proud (haughty). Origin: from G5449 (φύσις) in the primary sense of blowing; KJV: puff up

G5449 φύσις (phýsis): growth (by germination or expansion), i.e. (by implication) natural production (lineal descent); by extension, a genus or sort; figuratively, native disposition, constitution or usage. Origin: from G5453 (φύω); KJV: (man-)kind, nature(-al)

G5450 φυσίωσις (physíōsis): inflation, i.e. (figuratively) haughtiness. Origin: from G5448 (φυσιόω); KJV: swelling

G5451 φυτεία (phyteía): trans-planting, i.e. (concretely) a shrub or vegetable. Origin: from G5452 (φυτεύω); KJV: plant

G5452 φυτεύω (phyteúō): to set out in the earth, i.e. implant; figuratively, to instil doctrine. Origin: from a derivative of G5453 (φύω); KJV: plant

G5453 φύω (phýō): probably originally, to "puff" or blow, i.e. to swell up; but only used in the implied sense, to germinate or grow (sprout, produce), literally or figuratively. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: spring (up)

G5454 φωλεός (phōleós): a burrow or lurking-place. Origin: of uncertain derivative; KJV: hole

G5455 φωνέω (phōnéō): to emit a sound (animal, human or instrumental); by implication, to address in words or by name, also in imitation. Origin: from G5456 (φωνή); KJV: call (for), crow, cry

G5456 φωνή (phōnḗ): a tone (articulate, bestial or artificial); by implication, an address (for any purpose), saying or language. Origin: probably akin to G5316 (φαίνω) through the idea of disclosure; KJV: noise, sound, voice

G5457 φῶς (phōs): compare G5316 (φαίνω), G5346 (φημί)); luminousness (in the widest application, natural or artificial, abstract or concrete, literal or figurative). Origin: from an obsolete (to shine or make manifest, especially by rays; KJV: fire, light

G5458 φωστήρ (phōstḗr): an illuminator, i.e. (concretely) a luminary, or (abstractly) brilliancy. Origin: from G5457 (φῶς); KJV: light

G5459 φωσφόρος (phōsphóros): light-bearing ("phosphorus"), i.e. (specially), the morning-star (figuratively). Origin: from G5457 (φῶς) and G5342 (φέρω); KJV: day star

G5460 φωτεινός (phōteinós): lustrous, i.e. transparent or well-illuminated (figuratively). Origin: from G5457 (φῶς); KJV: bright, full of light

G5461 φωτίζω (phōtízō): to shed rays, i.e. to shine or (transitively) to brighten up (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5457 (φῶς); KJV: enlighten, illuminate, (bring to, give) light, make to see

G5462 φωτισμός (phōtismós): illumination (figuratively). Origin: from G5461 (φωτίζω); KJV: light

G5463 χαίρω (chaírō): to be "cheer"ful, i.e. calmly happy or well-off; impersonally, especially as salutation (on meeting or parting), be well. Origin: a primary verb; KJV: farewell, be glad, God speed, greeting, hall, joy(- fully), rejoice

G5464 χάλαζα (chálaza): hail. Origin: probably from G5465 (χαλάω); KJV: hail

G5465 χαλάω (chaláō): to lower (as into a void). Origin: from the base of G5490 (χάσμα); KJV: let down, strike

G5466 Χαλδαῖος (Chaldaîos): a Chaldæan (i.e. Kasdi), or native or the region of the lower Euphrates. Origin: probably of Hebrew or (H3778); KJV: Chaldæan

G5467 χαλεπός (chalepós): difficult, i.e. dangerous, or (by implication) furious. Origin: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of reducing the strength; KJV: fierce, perilous

G5468 χαλιναγωγέω (chalinagōgéō): to be a bit-leader, i.e. to curb (figuratively). Origin: from a compound of G5469 (χαλινός) and the reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω); KJV: bridle

G5469 χαλινός (chalinós): a curb or head-stall (as curbing the spirit). Origin: from G5465 (χαλάω); KJV: bit, bridle

G5470 χάλκεος (chálkeos): coppery. Origin: from G5475 (χαλκός); KJV: brass

G5471 χαλκεύς (chalkeús): a copper-worker or brazier. Origin: from G5475 (χαλκός); KJV: coppersmith

G5472 χαλκηδών (chalkēdṓn): copper-like, i.e. "chalcedony". Origin: from G5475 (χαλκός) and perhaps G1491 (εἶδος); KJV: chalcedony

G5473 χαλκίον (chalkíon): a copper dish. Origin: diminutive from G5475 (χαλκός); KJV: brazen vessel

G5474 χαλκολίβανον (chalkolíbanon): burnished copper, an alloy of copper (or gold) and silver having a brilliant lustre. Origin: neuter of a compound of G5475 (χαλκός) and G3030 (λίβανος) (in the implied mean of whiteness or brilliancy); KJV: fine brass

G5475 χαλκός (chalkós): copper (the substance, or some implement or coin made of it). Origin: perhaps from G5465 (χαλάω) through the idea of hollowing out as a vessel (this metal being chiefly used for that purpose); KJV: brass, money

G5476 χαμαί (chamaí): earthward, i.e. prostrate. Origin: adverb perhaps from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of a fissure in the soil; KJV: on (to) the ground

G5477 Χαναάν (Chanaán): Chanaan (i.e. Kenaan), the early name of Palestine. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3667); KJV: Chanaan

G5478 Χανααναῖος (Chanaanaîos): a Chanaanæan (i.e. Kenaanite), or native of gentile Palestine. Origin: from G5477 (Χαναάν); KJV: of Canaan
