G5479 χαρά (chará): cheerfulness, i.e. calm delight. Origin: from G5463 (χαίρω); KJV: gladness, X greatly, (X be exceeding) joy(-ful, -fully, -fulness, -ous)

G5480 χάραγμα (cháragma): a scratch or etching, i.e. stamp (as a badge of servitude), or scupltured figure (statue). Origin: from the same as G5482 (χάραξ); KJV: graven, mark

G5481 χαρακτήρ (charaktḗr): a graver (the tool or the person), i.e. (by implication) engraving (("character"), the figure stamped, i.e. an exact copy or (figuratively) representation). Origin: from the same as G5482 (χάραξ); KJV: express image

G5482 χάραξ (chárax): akin to G1125 (γράφω) through the idea of scratching); a stake, i.e. (by implication) a palisade or rampart (military mound for circumvallation in a siege). Origin: from (to sharpen to a point; KJV: trench

G5483 χαρίζομαι (charízomai): to grant as a favor, i.e. gratuitously, in kindness, pardon or rescue. Origin: middle voice from G5485 (χάρις); KJV: deliver, (frankly) forgive, (freely) give, grant

G5484 χάριν (chárin): through favor of, i.e. on account of. Origin: accusative case of G5485 (χάρις) as preposition; KJV: be-(for) cause of, for sake of, +…fore, X reproachfully

G5485 χάρις (cháris): graciousness (as gratifying), of manner or act (abstract or concrete; literal, figurative or spiritual; especially the divine influence upon the heart, and its reflection in the life; including gratitude). Origin: from G5463 (χαίρω); KJV: acceptable, benefit, favour, gift, grace(- ious), joy, liberality, pleasure, thank(-s, -worthy)

G5486 χάρισμα (chárisma): a (divine) gratuity, i.e. deliverance (from danger or passion); (specially), a (spiritual) endowment, i.e. (subjectively) religious qualification, or (objectively) miraculous faculty. Origin: from G5483 (χαρίζομαι); KJV: (free) gift

G5487 χαριτόω (charitóō): to grace, i.e. indue with special honor. Origin: from G5485 (χάρις); KJV: make accepted, be highly favoured

G5488 Χαῤῥάν (Charrhán): Charrhan (i.e. Charan), a place in Mesopotamia. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H2771); KJV: Charran

G5489 χάρτης (chártēs): a sheet ("chart") of writing-material (as to be scribbled over). Origin: from the same as G5482 (χάραξ); KJV: paper

G5490 χάσμα (chásma): a "chasm" or vacancy (impassable interval). Origin: from a form of an obsolete primary (to "gape" or "yawn"); KJV: gulf

G5491 χεῖλος (cheîlos): a lip (as a pouring place); figuratively, a margin (of water). Origin: from a form of the same as G5490 (χάσμα); KJV: lip, shore

G5492 χειμάζω (cheimázō): to storm, i.e. (passively) to labor under a gale. Origin: from the same as G5494 (χειμών); KJV: be tossed with tempest

G5493 χείμαῤῥος (cheímarrhos): a storm-runlet, i.e. winter-torrent. Origin: from the base of G5494 (χειμών) and G4482 (ῥέω); KJV: brook

G5494 χειμών (cheimṓn): akin to the base of 5490 through the idea of a channel), meaning a storm (as pouring rain); by implication, the rainy season, i.e. winter. Origin: from a derivative of (to pour; KJV: tempest, foul weather, winter

G5495 χείρ (cheír): the hand (literally or figuratively (power); especially (by Hebraism) a means or instrument). Origin: perhaps from the base of G5494 (χειμών) in the sense of its congener the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (through the idea of hollowness for grasping); KJV: hand

G5496 χειραγωγέω (cheiragōgéō): to be a hand-leader, i.e. to guide (a blind person). Origin: from G5497 (χειραγωγός); KJV: lead by the hand

G5497 χειραγωγός (cheiragōgós): a hand-leader, i.e. personal conductor (of a blind person). Origin: from G5495 (χείρ) and a reduplicated form of G71 (ἄγω); KJV: some to lead by the hand

G5498 χειρόγραφον (cheirógraphon): something hand-written ("chirograph"), i.e. a manuscript (specially, a legal document or bond (figuratively)). Origin: neuter of a compound of G5495 (χείρ) and G1125 (γράφω); KJV: handwriting

G5499 χειροποίητος (cheiropoíētos): manufactured, i.e. of human construction. Origin: from G5495 (χείρ) and a derivative of G4160 (ποιέω); KJV: made by (make with) hands

G5500 χειροτονέω (cheirotonéō): to be a hand-reacher or voter (by raising the hand), i.e. (generally) to select or appoint. Origin: from a comparative of G5495 (χείρ) and (to stretch); KJV: choose, ordain

G5501 χείρων (cheírōn): from an obsolete equivalent (of uncertain derivation); more evil or aggravated (physically, mentally or morally). Origin: irregular comparative of G2556 (κακός); KJV: sorer, worse

G5502 χερουβίμ (cheroubím): "cherubim" (i.e. cherubs or kerubim). Origin: plural of Hebrew origin (H3742); KJV: cherubims

G5503 χήρα (chḗra): a widow (as lacking a husband), literally or figuratively. Origin: feminine of a presumed derivative apparently from the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of deficiency; KJV: widow

G5504 χθές (chthés): "yesterday"; by extension, in time past or hitherto. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: yesterday

G5505 χιλιάς (chiliás): one thousand ("chiliad"). Origin: from G5507 (χίλιοι); KJV: thousand

G5506 χιλίαρχος (chilíarchos): the commander of a thousand soldiers ("chiliarch"; i.e. colonel. Origin: from G5507 (χίλιοι) and G757 (ἄρχω); KJV: (chief, high) captain

G5507 χίλιοι (chílioi): a thousand. Origin: plural of uncertain affinity; KJV: thousand

G5508 Χίος (Chíos): Chios, an island in the Mediterranean. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Chios

G5509 χιτών (chitṓn): a tunic or shirt. Origin: of foreign origin (H3801); KJV: clothes, coat, garment

G5510 χιών (chiṓn): snow. Origin: perhaps akin to the base of G5490 (χάσμα) (G5465 (χαλάω)) or G5494 (χειμών) (as descending or empty); KJV: snow

G5511 χλαμύς (chlamýs): a military cloak. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: robe

G5512 χλευάζω (chleuázō): to throw out the lip, i.e. jeer at. Origin: from a derivative probably of G5491 (χεῖλος); KJV: mock

G5513 χλιαρός (chliarós): tepid. Origin: from (to warm); KJV: lukewarm

G5514 Χλόη (Chlóē): "green"; Chloë, a Christian female. Origin: feminine of apparently a primary word; KJV: Chloe

G5515 χλωρός (chlōrós): greenish, i.e. verdant, dun-colored. Origin: from the same as G5514 (Χλόη); KJV: green, pale

G5516 χξϛ (chx stigma): 666 as a numeral. Origin: the 22nd, 14th and an obsolete letter (G4742 (στίγμα) as a cross) of the Greek alphabet (intermediate between the 5th and 6th), used as numbers; denoting respectively 600, 60 and 6; KJV: six hundred threescore and six

G5517 χοϊκός (choïkós): dusty or dirty (soil-like), i.e. (by implication) terrene. Origin: from G5522 (χόος); KJV: earthy

G5518 χοῖνιξ (choînix): a chœnix or certain dry measure. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: measure

G5519 χοῖρος (choîros): a hog. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: swine

G5520 χολάω (choláō): to be bilious, i.e. (by implication) irritable (enraged, "choleric"). Origin: from G5521 (χολή); KJV: be angry

G5521 χολή (cholḗ): "gall" or bile, i.e. (by analogy) poison or an anodyne (wormwood, poppy, etc.). Origin: feminine of an equivalent perhaps akin to the same as 5514 (from the greenish hue); KJV: gall

G5522 χόος (chóos): a heap (as poured out), i.e. rubbish; loose dirt. Origin: from the base of G5494 (χειμών); KJV: dust

G5523 Χοραζίν (Chorazín): Chorazin, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Chorazin

G5524 χορηγέω (chorēgéō): to be a dance-leader, i.e. (generally) to furnish. Origin: from a compound of G5525 (χορός) and G71 (ἄγω); KJV: give, minister

G5525 χορός (chorós): a ring, i.e. round dance ("choir". Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: dancing

G5526 χορτάζω (chortázō): to fodder, i.e. (generally) to gorge (supply food in abundance). Origin: from G5528 (χόρτος); KJV: feed, fill, satisfy

G5527 χόρτασμα (chórtasma): forage, i.e. food. Origin: from G5526 (χορτάζω); KJV: sustenance

G5528 χόρτος (chórtos): a "court" or "garden", i.e. (by implication, of pasture) herbage or vegetation. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: blade, grass, hay

G5529 Χουζᾶς (Chouzâs): Chuzas, an officer of Herod. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Chuza

G5530 χράομαι (chráomai): to furnish what is needed; (give an oracle, "graze" (touch slightly), light upon, etc.), i.e. (by implication) to employ or (by extension) to act towards one in a given manner. Origin: middle voice of a primary verb (perhaps rather from G5495 (χείρ), to handle); KJV: entreat, use

G5531 χράω (chráō): to loan. Origin: probably the same as the base of G5530 (χράομαι); KJV: lend

G5532 χρεία (chreía): employment, i.e. an affair; also (by implication) occasion, demand, requirement or destitution. Origin: from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) or G5534 (χρή); KJV: business, lack, necessary(-ity), need(-ful), use, want

title: Strong's Greek Dictionary, G5533 to G5624
source: James Strong, Dictionary of the Greek Testament words (1890), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Greek word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
G5533 χρεωφειλέτης (chreōpheilétēs): a loan-ower, i.e. indebted person. Origin: from a derivative of G5531 (χράω) and G3781 (ὀφειλέτης); KJV: debtor

G5534 χρή (chrḗ): it needs (must or should) be. Origin: third person singular of the same as G5530 (χράομαι) or G5531 (χράω) used impersonally; KJV: ought

G5535 χρῄζω (chrḗizō): to make (i.e. have) necessity, i.e. be in want of. Origin: from G5532 (χρεία); KJV: (have) need

G5536 χρῆμα (chrēma): something useful or needed, i.e. wealth, price. KJV: money, riches

G5537 χρηματίζω (chrēmatízō): to utter an oracle (compare the original sense of G5530 (χράομαι)), i.e. divinely intimate; by implication, (compare the secular sense of G5532 (χρεία)) to constitute a firm for business, i.e. (generally) bear as a title. Origin: from G5536 (χρῆμα); KJV: be called, be admonished (warned) of God, reveal, speak

G5538 χρηματισμός (chrēmatismós): a divine response or revelation. Origin: from G5537 (χρηματίζω); KJV: answer of God

G5539 χρήσιμος (chrḗsimos): serviceable. Origin: from G5540 (χρῆσις); KJV: profit

G5540 χρῆσις (chrēsis): employment, i.e. (specially), sexual intercourse (as an occupation of the body). Origin: from G5530 (χράομαι); KJV: use

G5541 χρηστεύομαι (chrēsteúomai): to show oneself useful, i.e. act benevolently. Origin: middle voice from G5543 (χρηστός); KJV: be kind

G5542 χρηστολογία (chrēstología): fair speech, i.e. plausibility. Origin: from a compound of G5543 (χρηστός) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: good words

G5543 χρηστός (chrēstós): employed, i.e. (by implication) useful (in manner or morals). Origin: from G5530 (χράομαι); KJV: better, easy, good(-ness), gracious, kind

G5544 χρηστότης (chrēstótēs): usefulness, i.e. morally, excellence (in character or demeanor). Origin: from G5543 (χρηστός); KJV: gentleness, good(-ness), kindness

G5545 χρῖσμα (chrîsma): an unguent or smearing, i.e. (figuratively) the special endowment ("chrism") of the Holy Spirit. Origin: from G5548 (χρίω); KJV: anointing, unction

G5546 Χριστιανός (Christianós): a Christian, i.e. follower of Christ. Origin: from G5547 (Χριστός); KJV: Christian

G5547 Χριστός (Christós): anointed, i.e. the Messiah, an epithet of Jesus. Origin: from G5548 (χρίω); KJV: Christ

G5548 χρίω (chríō): to smear or rub with oil, i.e. (by implication) to consecrate to an office or religious service. Origin: probably akin to G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of contact; KJV: anoint

G5549 χρονίζω (chronízō): to take time, i.e. linger. Origin: from G5550 (χρόνος); KJV: delay, tarry

G5550 χρόνος (chrónos): a space of time (in general, and thus properly distinguished from G2540 (καιρός), which designates a fixed or special occasion; and from G165 (αἰών), which denotes a particular period) or interval; by extension, an individual opportunity; by implication, delay. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: + years old, season, space, (X often-)time(-s), (a) while

G5551 χρονοτριβέω (chronotribéō): to be a time-wearer, i.e. to procrastinate (linger). Origin: from a presumed compound of G5550 (χρόνος) and the base of G5147 (τρίβος); KJV: spend time

G5552 χρύσεος (chrýseos): made of gold. Origin: from G5557 (χρυσός); KJV: of gold, golden

G5553 χρυσίον (chrysíon): a golden article, i.e. gold plating, ornament, or coin. Origin: diminutive of G5557 (χρυσός); KJV: gold

G5554 χρυσοδακτύλιος (chrysodaktýlios): gold-ringed, i.e. wearing a golden finger-ring or similar jewelry. Origin: from G5557 (χρυσός) and G1146 (δακτύλιος); KJV: with a gold ring

G5555 χρυσόλιθος (chrysólithos): gold-stone, i.e. a yellow gem ("chrysolite"). Origin: from G5557 (χρυσός) and G3037 (λίθος); KJV: chrysolite

G5556 χρυσόπρασος (chrysóprasos): a greenish-yellow gem ("chrysoprase"). Origin: from G5557 (χρυσός) and (a leek); KJV: chrysoprase

G5557 χρυσός (chrysós): gold; by extension, a golden article, as an ornament or coin. Origin: perhaps from the base of G5530 (χράομαι) (through the idea of the utility of the metal); KJV: gold

G5558 χρυσόω (chrysóō): to gild, i.e. bespangle with golden ornaments. Origin: from G5557 (χρυσός); KJV: deck

G5559 χρώς (chrṓs): the body (properly, its surface or skin). Origin: probably akin to the base of G5530 (χράομαι) through the idea of handling; KJV: body

G5560 χωλός (chōlós): "halt", i.e. limping. Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: cripple, halt, lame

G5561 χώρα (chṓra): room, i.e. a space of territory (more or less extensive; often including its inhabitants). Origin: feminine of a derivative of the base of G5490 (χάσμα) through the idea of empty expanse; KJV: coast, county, fields, ground, land, region

G5562 χωρέω (chōréō): to be in (give) space, i.e. (intransitively) to pass, enter, or (transitively) to hold, admit (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5561 (χώρα); KJV: come, contain, go, have place, (can, be room to) receive

G5563 χωρίζω (chōrízō): to place room between, i.e. part; reflexively, to go away. Origin: from G5561 (χώρα); KJV: depart, put asunder, separate

G5564 χωρίον (chōríon): a spot or plot of ground. Origin: diminutive of G5561 (χώρα); KJV: field, land, parcel of ground, place, possession

G5565 χωρίς (chōrís): at a space, i.e. separately or apart from (often as preposition). Origin: adverb from G5561 (χώρα); KJV: beside, by itself, without

G5566 χῶρος (chōros): the north-west wind. Origin: of Latin origin; KJV: north west

G5567 ψάλλω (psállō): compare G5597 (ψώχω)); to twitch or twang, i.e. to play on a stringed instrument (celebrate the divine worship with music and accompanying odes). Origin: probably strengthened from (to rub or touch the surface; KJV: make melody, sing (psalms)

G5568 ψαλμός (psalmós): a set piece of music, i.e. a sacred ode (accompanied with the voice, harp or other instrument; a "psalm"); collectively, the book of the Psalms. Origin: from G5567 (ψάλλω); KJV: psalm

G5569 ψευδάδελφος (pseudádelphos): a spurious brother, i.e. pretended associate. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G80 (ἀδελφός); KJV: false brethren

G5570 ψευδαπόστολος (pseudapóstolos): a spurious apostle, i.e. pretended pracher. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G652 (ἀπόστολος); KJV: false teacher

G5571 ψευδής (pseudḗs): untrue, i.e. erroneous, deceitful, wicked. Origin: from G5574 (ψεύδομαι); KJV: false, liar

G5572 ψευδοδιδάσκαλος (pseudodidáskalos): a spurious teacher, i.e. propagator of erroneous Christian doctrine. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G1320 (διδάσκαλος); KJV: false teacher

G5573 ψευδολόγος (pseudológos): mendacious, i.e. promulgating erroneous Christian doctrine. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G3004 (λέγω); KJV: speaking lies

G5574 ψεύδομαι (pseúdomai): to utter an untruth or attempt to deceive by falsehood. Origin: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; KJV: falsely, lie

G5575 ψευδομάρτυρ (pseudomártyr): a spurious witness, i.e. bearer of untrue testimony. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and a kindred form of G3144 (μάρτυς); KJV: false witness

G5576 ψευδομαρτυρέω (pseudomartyréō): to be an untrue testifier, i.e. offer falsehood in evidence. Origin: from G5575 (ψευδομάρτυρ); KJV: be a false witness

G5577 ψευδομαρτυρία (pseudomartyría): untrue testimony. Origin: from G5575 (ψευδομάρτυρ); KJV: false witness

G5578 ψευδοπροφήτης (pseudoprophḗtēs): a spurious prophet, i.e. pretended foreteller or religious impostor. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G4396 (προφήτης); KJV: false prophet

G5579 ψεῦδος (pseûdos): a falsehood. Origin: from G5574 (ψεύδομαι); KJV: lie, lying

G5580 ψευδόχριστος (pseudóchristos): a spurious Messiah. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G5547 (Χριστός); KJV: false Christ

G5581 ψευδώνυμος (pseudṓnymos): untruly named. Origin: from G5571 (ψευδής) and G3686 (ὄνομα); KJV: falsely so called

G5582 ψεῦσμα (pseûsma): a fabrication, i.e. falsehood. Origin: from G5574 (ψεύδομαι); KJV: lie

G5583 ψεύστης (pseústēs): a falsifier. Origin: from G5574 (ψεύδομαι); KJV: liar

G5584 ψηλαφάω (psēlapháō): to manipulate, i.e. verify by contact; figuratively, to search for. Origin: from the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (compare G5586 (ψῆφος)); KJV: feel after, handle, touch

G5585 ψηφίζω (psēphízō): to use pebbles in enumeration, i.e. (generally) to compute. Origin: from G5586 (ψῆφος); KJV: count

G5586 ψῆφος (psēphos): a pebble (as worn smooth by handling), i.e. (by implication, of use as a counter or ballot) a verdict (of acquittal) or ticket (of admission); a vote. Origin: from the same as G5584 (ψηλαφάω); KJV: stone, voice

G5587 ψιθυρισμός (psithyrismós): by implication, a slander; probably akin to G5574 (ψεύδομαι)); whispering, i.e. secret detraction. Origin: from a derivative of (a whisper; KJV: whispering

G5588 ψιθυριστής (psithyristḗs): a secret calumniator. Origin: from the same as G5587 (ψιθυρισμός); KJV: whisperer

G5589 ψιχίον (psichíon): a little bit or morsel. Origin: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5567 (ψάλλω) (meaning a crumb); KJV: crumb

G5590 ψυχή (psychḗ): breath, i.e. (by implication) spirit, abstractly or concretely (the animal sentient principle only; thus distinguished on the one hand from G4151 (πνεῦμα), which is the rational and immortal soul; and on the other from G2222 (ζωή), which is mere vitality, even of plants: these terms thus exactly correspond respectively to the Hebrew H05315, H07307 and H02416). Origin: from G5594 (ψύχω); KJV: heart (+ -ily), life, mind, soul, + us, + you

G5591 ψυχικός (psychikós): sensitive, i.e. animate (in distinction on the one hand from G4152 (πνευματικός), which is the higher or renovated nature; and on the other from G5446 (φυσικός), which is the lower or bestial nature). Origin: from G5590 (ψυχή); KJV: natural, sensual

G5592 ψύχος (psýchos): coolness. Origin: from G5594 (ψύχω); KJV: cold

G5593 ψυχρός (psychrós): chilly (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5592 (ψύχος); KJV: cold

G5594 ψύχω (psýchō): to breathe (voluntarily but gently, thus differing on the one hand from G4154 (πνέω), which denotes properly a forcible respiration; and on the other from the base of G109 (ἀήρ), which refers properly to an inanimate breeze), i.e. (by implication, of reduction of temperature by evaporation) to chill (figuratively). Origin: a primary verb; KJV: wax cold

G5595 ψωμίζω (psōmízō): to supply with bits, i.e. (generally) to nourish. Origin: from the base of G5596 (ψωμίον); KJV: (bestow to) feed

G5596 ψωμίον (psōmíon): a crumb or morsel (as if rubbed off), i.e. a mouthful. Origin: diminutive from a derivative of the base of G5597 (ψώχω); KJV: sop

G5597 ψώχω (psṓchō): to triturate, i.e. (by analogy) to rub out (kernels from husks with the fingers or hand). Origin: prolongation from the same base as G5567 (ψάλλω); KJV: rub

G5598 Ω (Ō): the last letter of the Greek alphabet, i.e. (figuratively) the finality. KJV: Omega

G5599 ὦ (ō): as a sign of the vocative case, O; as a note of exclamation, oh. Origin: a primary interjection; KJV: O

G5600 ὦ (ō): (may, might, can, could, would, should, must, etc.; also with G1487 (εἰ) and its comparative, as well as with other particles) be. Origin: the subjunctive of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: + appear, are, (may, might, should) be, X have, is, + pass the flower of her age, should stand, were

G5601 Ὠβήδ (Ōbḗd): Obed, an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H5744); KJV: Obed

G5602 ὧδε (hōde): in this same spot, i.e. here or hither. Origin: from an adverb form of G3592 (ὅδε); KJV: here, hither, (in) this place, there

G5603 ᾠδή (ōidḗ): a chant or "ode" (the general term for any words sung; while G5215 (ὕμνος) denotes especially a religious metrical composition, and G5568 (ψαλμός) still more specially, a Hebrew cantillation). Origin: from G103 (ᾄδω); KJV: song

G5604 ὠδίν (ōdín): a pang or throe, especially of childbirth. Origin: akin to G3601 (ὀδύνη); KJV: pain, sorrow, travail

G5605 ὠδίνω (ōdínō): to experience the pains of parturition (literally or figuratively). Origin: from G5604 (ὠδίν); KJV: travail in (birth)

G5606 ὦμος (ōmos): the shoulder (as that on which burdens are borne). Origin: perhaps from the alternate of G5342 (φέρω); KJV: shoulder

G5607 ὤν (ṓn): being. Origin: present participle of G1510 (εἰμί); KJV: be, come, have

G5608 ὠνέομαι (ōnéomai): to purchase (synonymous with the earlier G4092 (πίμπρημι)). Origin: middle voice from an apparently primary (a sum or price); KJV: buy

G5609 ὠόν (ōón): an "egg". Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: egg

G5610 ὥρα (hṓra): an "hour" (literally or figuratively). Origin: apparently a primary word; KJV: day, hour, instant, season, X short, (even-)tide, (high) time

G5611 ὡραῖος (hōraîos): belonging to the right hour or season (timely), i.e. (by implication) flourishing (beauteous (figuratively)). Origin: from G5610 (ὥρα); KJV: beautiful

G5612 ὠρύομαι (ōrýomai): to "roar". Origin: middle voice of an apparently primary verb; KJV: roar

G5613 ὡς (hōs): which how, i.e. in that manner (very variously used, as follows). Origin: probably adverb of comparative from G3739 (ὅς); KJV: about, after (that), (according) as (it had been, it were), as soon (as), even as (like), for, how (greatly), like (as, unto), since, so (that), that, to wit, unto, when(-soever), while, X with all speed

G5614 ὡσαννά (hōsanná): oh save!; hosanna (i.e. hoshia-na), an exclamation of adoration. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H3467 and H4994); KJV: hosanna

G5615 ὡσαύτως (hōsaútōs): as thus, i.e. in the same way. Origin: from G5613 (ὡς) and an adverb from G846 (αὐτός); KJV: even so, likewise, after the same (in like) manner

G5616 ὡσεί (hōseí): as if. Origin: from G5613 (ὡς) and G1487 (εἰ); KJV: about, as (it had been, it were), like (as)

G5617 Ὡσηέ (Hōsēé): Hosee (i.e. Hoshea), an Israelite. Origin: of Hebrew origin (H1954); KJV: Osee

G5618 ὥσπερ (hṓsper): just as, i.e. exactly like. Origin: from G5613 (ὡς) and G4007 (περ); KJV: (even, like) as

G5619 ὡσπερεί (hōspereí): just as if, i.e. as it were. Origin: from G5618 (ὥσπερ) and G1487 (εἰ); KJV: as

G5620 ὥστε (hṓste): so too, i.e. thus therefore (in various relations of consecution, as follow). Origin: from G5613 (ὡς) and G5037 (τέ); KJV: (insomuch) as, so that (then), (insomuch) that, therefore, to, wherefore

G5621 ὠτίον (ōtíon): an earlet, i.e. one of the ears, or perhaps the lobe of the ear. Origin: diminutive of G3775 (οὖς); KJV: ear

G5622 ὠφέλεια (ōphéleia): usefulness, i.e. benefit. Origin: from a derivative of the base of G5624 (ὠφέλιμος); KJV: advantage, profit

G5623 ὠφελέω (ōpheléō): to be useful, i.e. to benefit. Origin: from the same as G5622 (ὠφέλεια); KJV: advantage, better, prevail, profit

G5624 ὠφέλιμος (ōphélimos): helpful or serviceable, i.e. advantageous. Origin: from a form of G3786 (ὄφελος); KJV: profit(-able)

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1 to H133
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1 אָב (ʼâb, awb): father, in a literal and immediate, or figurative and remote application. Origin: a primitive word; KJV: chief, (fore-) father(-less), [idiom] patrimony, principal. Compare names in 'Abi-'.

H2 אַב (ʼab, ab): {father}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1 (אָב) KJV: father.

H3 אֵב (ʼêb, abe): a green plant. Origin: from the same as H24 (אָבִיב); KJV: greenness, fruit.

H4 אֵב (ʼêb, abe): {a green plant}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3 (אֵב) KJV: fruit.

H5 אֲבַגְתָא (ʼĂbagthâʼ, ab-ag-thaw'): Abagtha, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Abagtha.

H6 אָבַד (ʼâbad, aw-bad'): properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break, destroy(-uction), [phrase] not escape, fail, lose, (cause to, make) perish, spend, [idiom] and surely, take, be undone, [idiom] utterly, be void of, have no way to flee.

H7 אֲבַד (ʼăbad, ab-ad'): {properly, to wander away, i.e. lose oneself; by implication to perish (causative, destroy)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6 (אָבַד) KJV: destroy, perish.

H8 אֹבֵד (ʼôbêd, o-bade'): (concrete) wretched or (abstract) destruction. Origin: active of participle of H6 (אָבַד); KJV: perish.

H9 אֲבֵדָה (ʼăbêdâh, ab-ay-daw'): concrete, something lost; abstract, destruction, i.e. Hades. Origin: from H6 (אָבַד); Compare H10 (אֲבַדֹּה). KJV: lost.

H10 אֲבַדֹּה (ʼăbaddôh, ab-ad-do'): a perishing. Origin: the same as H9 (אֲבֵדָה), miswritten for H11 (אֲבַדּוֹן); KJV: destruction.

H11 אֲבַדּוֹן (ʼăbaddôwn, ab-ad-done'): abstract, a perishing; concrete, Hades. Origin: intensive from H6 (אָבַד); KJV: destruction.

H12 אַבְדָן (ʼabdân, ab-dawn'): a perishing. Origin: from H6 (אָבַד); KJV: destruction.

H13 אׇבְדַן (ʼobdan, ob-dawn'): a perishing. Origin: from H6 (אָבַד); KJV: destruction.

H14 אָבָה (ʼâbâh, aw-baw'): to breathe after, i.e. (figuratively) to be acquiescent. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consent, rest content will, be willing.

H15 אָבֶה (ʼâbeh, aw-beh'): longing. Origin: from H14 (אָבָה); KJV: desire.

H16 אֵבֶה (ʼêbeh, ay-beh'): the papyrus. Origin: from H14 (אָבָה) (in the sense of bending toward); KJV: swift.

H17 אֲבוֹי (ʼăbôwy, ab-o'ee): want. Origin: from H14 (אָבָה) (in the sense of desiring); KJV: sorrow.

H18 אֵבוּס (ʼêbûwç, ay-booce'): a manger or stall. Origin: from H75 (אָבַס); KJV: crib.

H19 אִבְחָה (ʼibchâh, ib-khaw'): brandishing of a sword. Origin: from an unused root (apparently meaning to turn); KJV: point.

H20 אֲבַטִּיחַ (ʼăbaṭṭîyach, ab-at-tee'-akh): a melon (only plural). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: melon.

H21 אֲבִי (ʼĂbîy, ab-ee'): Abi, Hezekiah's mother. Origin: from H1 (אָב); fatherly; KJV: Abi.

H22 אֲבִיאֵל (ʼĂbîyʼêl, ab-ee-ale'): Abiel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H410 (אֵל); father (i.e. possessor) of God; KJV: Abiel.

H23 אֲבִיאָסָף (ʼĂbîyʼâçâph, ab-ee-aw-sawf'): Abiasaph, an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H622 (אָסַף); father of gathering (i.e. gatherer); KJV: Abiasaph.

H24 אָבִיב (ʼâbîyb, aw-beeb'): green, i.e. a young ear of grain; hence, the name of the month Abib or Nisan. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be tender); KJV: Abib, ear, green ears of corn (not maize).

H25 אֲבִי גִבְעוֹן (ʼĂbîy Gibʻôwn, ab-ee' ghib-one'): Abi-Gibon, perhaps an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H1391 (גִּבְעוֹן); father (i.e. founder) of Gibon; KJV: father of Gibeon.

H26 אֲבִיגַיִל (ʼĂbîygayil, ab-ee-gah'-yil): Abigail or Abigal, the name of two Israelitesses. Origin: or shorter אֲבִיגַל; from H1 (אָב) and H1524 (גִּיל); father (i.e. source) of joy; KJV: Abigal.

H27 אֲבִידָן (ʼĂbîydân, ab-ee-dawn'): Abidan, an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H1777 (דִּין); father of judgment (i.e. judge); KJV: Abidan.

H28 אֲבִידָע (ʼĂbîydâʻ, ab-ee-daw'): Abida, a son of Abraham by Keturah. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H3045 (יָדַע); father of knowledge (i.e. knowing); KJV: Abida, Abidah.

H29 אֲבִיָּה (ʼĂbîyâh, ab-ee-yaw'): Abijah, the name of several Israelite men and two Israelitesses. Origin: or prolonged אֲבִיָּהוּ ; from H1 (אָב) and H3050 (יָהּ); father (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; KJV: Abiah, Abijah.

H30 אֲבִיהוּא (ʼĂbîyhûwʼ, ab-ee-hoo'): Abihu, a son of Aaron. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H1931 (הוּא); father (i.e. worshipper) of Him (i.e. God); KJV: Abihu.

H31 אֲבִיהוּד (ʼĂbîyhûwd, ab-ee-hood'): Abihud, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H1935 (הוֹד); father (i.e. possessor) of renown; KJV: Abihud.

H32 אֲבִיהַיִל (ʼĂbîyhayil, ab-ee-hah'-yil): Abihail or Abichail, the name of three Israelites and two Israelitesses. Origin: or (more correctly) אֲבִיחַיִל ; from H1 (אָב) and H2428 (חַיִל); father (i.e. possessor) of might; KJV: Abihail.

H33 אֲבִי הָעֶזְרִי (ʼĂbîy hâ-ʻEzrîy, ab-ee'-haw-ez-ree'): an Abiezrite or descendant of Abiezer. Origin: from H44 (אֲבִיעֶזֶר) with the article inserted; father of the Ezrite; KJV: Abiezrite.

H34 אֶבְיוֹן (ʼebyôwn, eb-yone'): destitute. Origin: from H14 (אָבָה), in the sense of want (especially in feeling); KJV: beggar, needy, poor (man).

H35 אֲבִיּוֹנָה (ʼăbîyôwnâh, ab-ee-yo-naw'): provocative of desire; the caper berry (from its stimulative taste). Origin: from H14 (אָבָה); KJV: desire.

H36 אֲבִיטוּב (ʼĂbîyṭûwb, ab-ee-toob'): Abitub, an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H2898 (טוּב); father of goodness (i.e. good); KJV: Abitub.

H37 אֲבִיטָל (ʼĂbîyṭâl, ab-ee-tal'): Abital, a wife of King David. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H2919 (טַל); father of dew (i.e. fresh); KJV: Abital.

H38 אֲבִיָּם (ʼĂbîyâm, ab-ee-yawm'): Abijam (or Abijah), a king of Judah. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H3220 (יָם); father of (the) sea (i.e. seaman); KJV: Abijam.

H39 אֲבִימָאֵל (ʼĂbîymâʼêl, ab-ee-maw-ale'): Abimael, a son of Joktan. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and an elsewhere unused (probably foreign) word; father of Mael (apparently some Arab tribe); KJV: Abimael.

H40 אֲבִימֶלֶךְ (ʼĂbîymelek, ab-ee-mel'-ek): Abimelek, the name of two Philistine kings and of two Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); father of (the) king; KJV: Abimelech.

H41 אֲבִינָדָב (ʼĂbîynâdâb, ab-ee-naw-dawb'): Abinadab, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H5068 (נָדַב); father of generosity (i.e. liberal); KJV: Abinadab.

H42 אֲבִינֹעַם (ʼĂbîynôʻam, ab-ee-no'-am): Abinoam, an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H5278 (נֹעַם); father of pleasantness (i.e. gracious); KJV: Abinoam.

H43 אֶבְיָסָף (ʼEbyâçâph, eb-yaw-sawf'): Ebjasaph, an Israelite. Origin: contracted from H23 (אֲבִיאָסָף); KJV: Ebiasaph.

H44 אֲבִיעֶזֶר (ʼĂbîyʻezer, ab-ee-ay'-zer): Abiezer, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H5829 (עֵזֶר); father of help (i.e. helpful); KJV: Abiezer.

H45 אֲבִי־עַלְבוֹן (ʼĂbîy-ʻalbôwn, ab-ee-al-bone'): Abialbon, an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and an unused root of uncertain derivation; probably, father of strength (i.e. valiant); KJV: Abialbon.

H46 אָבִיר (ʼâbîyr, aw-beer'): mighty (spoken of God). Origin: from H82 (אָבַר); KJV: mighty (one).

H47 אַבִּיר (ʼabbîyr, ab-beer'): {mighty (spoken of God)}. Origin: for H46 (אָבִיר) KJV: angel, bull, chiefest, mighty (one), stout(-hearted), strong (one), valiant.

H48 אֲבִירָם (ʼĂbîyrâm, ab-ee-rawm'): Abiram, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H7311 (רוּם); father of height (i.e. lofty); KJV: Abiram.

H49 אֲבִישַׁג (ʼĂbîyshag, ab-ee-shag'): Abishag, a concubine of David. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H7686 (שָׁגָה); father of error (i.e. blundering); KJV: Abishag.

H50 אֲבִישׁוּעַ (ʼĂbîyshûwaʻ, ab-ee-shoo'-ah): Abishua, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H7771 (שׁוֹעַ); father of plenty (i.e. prosperous); KJV: Abishua.

H51 אֲבִישׁוּר (ʼĂbîyshûwr, ab-ee-shoor'): Abishur, an Israelite. Origin: from H1 (אָב) and H7791 (שׁוּר); father of (the) wall (i.e. perhaps mason); KJV: Abishur.

H52 אֲבִישַׁי (ʼĂbîyshay, ab-ee-shah'ee): Abishai, an Israelite. Origin: or (shorter) אַבְשַׁי ; from H1 (אָב) and H7862 (שַׁי); father of a gift (i.e. probably generous); KJV: Abishai.

H53 אֲבִישָׁלוֹם (ʼĂbîyshâlôwm, ab-ee-shaw-lome'): Abshalom, a son of David; also (the fuller form) a later Israelite. Origin: or (shortened) אַבְשָׁלוֹם ; from H1 (אָב) and H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); father of peace (i.e. friendly); KJV: Abishalom, Absalom.

H54 אֶבְיָתָר (ʼEbyâthâr, ab-yaw-thawr'): Ebjathar, an Israelite. Origin: contracted from H1 (אָב) and H3498 (יָתַר); father of abundance (i.e. liberal); KJV: Abiathar.

H55 אָבַךְ (ʼâbak, aw-bak'): probably to coil upward. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mount up.

H56 אָבַל (ʼâbal, aw-bal'): to bewail. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lament, mourn.

H57 אָבֵל (ʼâbêl, aw-bale'): lamenting. Origin: from H56 (אָבַל); KJV: mourn(-er, -ing).

H58 אָבֵל (ʼâbêl, aw-bale'): a meadow. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be grassy); KJV: plain. Compare also the proper names beginning with Abel-.

H59 אָבֵל (ʼÂbêl, aw-bale'): Abel, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל); a meadow; KJV: Abel.

H60 אֵבֶל (ʼêbel, ay'-bel): lamentation. Origin: from H56 (אָבַל); KJV: mourning.

H61 אֲבָל (ʼăbâl, ab-awl'): nay, i.e. truly or yet. Origin: apparently from H56 (אָבַל) through the idea of negation; KJV: but, indeed, nevertheless, verily.

H62 אָבֵל בֵּית־מֲעַכָה (ʼÂbêl Bêyth-Măʻakâh, aw-bale' bayth ma-akaw'): Abel of Beth-maakah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H1004 (בַּיִת) and H4601 (מַעֲכָה); meadow of Beth-Maakah; KJV: Abel-beth-maachah, Abel of Beth-maachah,

H63 אָבֵל הַשִּׁטִּים (ʼÂbêl hash-Shiṭṭîym, aw-bale' hash-shit-teem'): Abel hash-Shittim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל) and the plural of H7848 (שִׁטָּה), with the article inserted; meadow of the acacias; KJV: Abelshittim.

H64 אָבֵל כְּרָמִים (ʼÂbêl Kᵉrâmîym, aw-bale' ker-aw-meem'): Abel-Keramim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל) and the plural of H3754 (כֶּרֶם); meadow of vineyards; KJV: plain of the vineyards.

H65 אָבֵל מְחוֹלָה (ʼÂbêl Mᵉchôwlâh, aw-bale' mekh-o-law'): Abel-Mecholah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4246 (מְחֹלָה)xlit mᵉchôwlâh corrected to mᵉchôlâh; meadow of dancing; KJV: Abel-meholah.

H66 אַבֵל מַיִם (ʼAbêl Mayim, aw-bale' mah'-yim): Abel-Majim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4325 (מַיִם); meadow of water; KJV: Abel-maim.

H67 אָבֵל מִצְרַיִם (ʼÂbêl Mitsrayim, aw-bale' mits-rah'-yim): Abel-Mitsrajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H58 (אָבֵל) and H4714 (מִצְרַיִם); meadow of Egypt; KJV: Abel-mizraim.

H68 אֶבֶן (ʼeben, eh'-ben): a stone. Origin: from the root of H1129 (בָּנָה) through the meaning to build; KJV: [phrase] carbuncle, [phrase] mason, [phrase] plummet, (chalk-, hail-, head-, sling-) stone(-ny), (divers) weight(-s).

H69 אֶבֶן (ʼeben, eh'-ben): {a stone}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H68 (אֶבֶן) KJV: stone.

H70 אֹבֶן (ʼôben, o' ben): a pair of stones (only dual); a potter's wheel or a midwife's stool (consisting alike of two horizontal disks with a support between). Origin: from the same as H68 (אֶבֶן); KJV: wheel, stool.

H71 אֲבָנָה (ʼĂbânâh, ab-aw-naw'): Abanah, a river near Damascus. Origin: perhaps feminine of H68 (אֶבֶן); stony; Compare H549 (אֲמָנָה). KJV: Abana.

H72 אֶבֶן הָעֵזֶר (ʼEben hâ-ʻÊzer, eh'-ben haw-e'-zer): Eben-ha-Ezer, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H68 (אֶבֶן) and H5828 (עֵזֶר) with the article inserted; stone of the help; KJV: Ebenezer.

H73 אַבְנֵט (ʼabnêṭ, ab-nate'): a belt. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: girdle.

H74 אַבְנֵר (ʼAbnêr, ab-nare'): Abner, an Israelite. Origin: or (fully) אֲבִינֵר ; from H1 (אָב) and H5216 (נִיר); father of light (i.e. enlightening); KJV: Abner.

H75 אָבַס (ʼâbaç, aw-bas'): to fodder. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fatted, stalled.

H76 אֲבַעְבֻּעָה (ʼăbaʻbuʻâh, ab-ah-boo-aw'): an inflammatory pustule (as eruption). Origin: (by reduplication) from an unused root (meaning to belch forth); KJV: blains.

H77 אֶבֶץ (ʼEbets, eh'-bets): Ebets, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to gleam; conspicuous; KJV: Abez.

H78 אִבְצָן (ʼIbtsân, ib-tsawn'): Ibtsan, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H76 (אֲבַעְבֻּעָה); splendid; KJV: Ibzan.

H79 אָבַק (ʼâbaq, aw-bak'): to bedust, i.e. grapple. Origin: a primitive root, probably to float away (as vapor), but used only as denominative from H80 (אָבָק); KJV: wrestle.

H80 אָבָק (ʼâbâq, aw-bawk'): light particles (as volatile). Origin: from root of H79 (אָבַק); KJV: (small) dust, powder.

H81 אֲבָקָה (ʼăbâqâh, ab-aw-kaw'): {light particles (as volatile)}. Origin: feminine of H80 (אָבָק) KJV: powder.

H82 אָבַר (ʼâbar, aw-bar'): to soar. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fly.

H83 אֵבֶר (ʼêber, ay-ber'): a pinion. Origin: from H82 (אָבַר); KJV: (long-) wing(-ed).

H84 אֶבְרָה (ʼebrâh, eb-raw'): {a pinion}. Origin: feminine of H83 (אֵבֶר) KJV: feather, wing.

H85 אַבְרָהָם (ʼAbrâhâm, ab-raw-hawm'): Abraham, the later name of Abram. Origin: contracted from H1 (אָב) and an unused root (probably meaning to be populous); father of a multitude; KJV: Abraham.

H86 אַבְרֵךְ (ʼabrêk, ab-rake'): kneel. Origin: probably an Egyptian word meaning KJV: bow the knee.

H87 אַבְרָם (ʼAbrâm, ab-rawm'): Abram, the original name of Abraham. Origin: contracted from H48 (אֲבִירָם); high father; KJV: Abram.

H88 אֹבֹת (ʼôbôth, o-both'): Oboth, a place in the Desert. Origin: plural of H178 (אוֹב); water-skins; KJV: Oboth.

H89 אָגֵא (ʼÂgêʼ, aw-gay'): Age, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation (compare H90 (אֲגַג)); KJV: Agee.

H90 אֲגַג (ʼĂgag, ag-ag'): Agag, a title of Amalekitish kings. Origin: or אֲגָג; of uncertain derivation (compare H89 (אָגֵא)); flame; KJV: Agag.

H91 אֲגָגִי (ʼĂgâgîy, ag-aw-ghee'): an Agagite or descendent (subject) of Agag. Origin: patrial or patronymic from H90 (אֲגַג); KJV: Agagite.

H92 אֲגֻדָּה (ʼăguddâh, ag-ood-daw'): a band, bundle, knot, or arch. Origin: feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to bind); KJV: bunch, burden, troop.

H93 אֱגוֹז (ʼĕgôwz, eg-oze'): a nut. Origin: prob of Persian origin; KJV: nut.

H94 אָגוּר (ʼÂgûwr, aw-goor'): Agur, a fanciful name for Solomon. Origin: passive participle of H103 (אָגַר); gathered (i.e. received among the sages); KJV: Agur.

H95 אֲגוֹרָה (ʼăgôwrâh, ag-o-raw'): properly, something gathered, i.e. perhaps a grain or berry; used only of a small (silver) coin. Origin: from the same as H94 (אָגוּר); KJV: piece (of) silver.

H96 אֶגֶל (ʼegel, eh'-ghel): a reservoir. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to flow down or together as drops); KJV: drop.

H97 אֶגְלַיִם (ʼEglayim, eg-lah'-yim): Eglajim, a place in Moab. Origin: dual of H96 (אֶגֶל).; a double pond; KJV: Eglaim.

H98 אֲגַם (ʼăgam, ag-am'): a marsh; hence a rush (as growing in swamps); hence a stockade of reeds. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to collect as water); KJV: pond, pool, standing (water).

H99 אָגֵם (ʼâgêm, aw-game'): figuratively, sad. Origin: probably from the same as H98 (אֲגַם) (in the sense of stagnant water); KJV: pond.

H100 אַגְמוֹן (ʼagmôwn, ag-mone'): a bulrush (as growing there); collectively a rope of bulrushes. Origin: from the same as H98 (אֲגַם); a marshy pool (others from a different root, a kettle); by implication KJV: bulrush, caldron, hook, rush.

H101 אַגָּן (ʼaggân, ag-gawn'): a bowl (as pounded out hollow). Origin: probably from H5059 (נָגַן); KJV: basin, cup, goblet.

H102 אַגָּף (ʼaggâph, ag-gawf'): (only plural) wings of an army, or crowds of troops. Origin: probably from H5062 (נָגַף) (through the idea of impending); a cover or heap; i.e. KJV: bands.

H103 אָגַר (ʼâgar, aw-gar'): to harvest. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather.

H104 אִגְּרָא (ʼiggᵉrâʼ, ig-er-aw'): an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman). Origin: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; KJV: letter.

H105 אֲגַרְטָל (ʼăgarṭâl, ag-ar-tawl'): a basin. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: charger.

H106 אֶגְרֹף (ʼegrôph, eg-rofe'): the clenched hand. Origin: from H1640 (גָּרַף) (in the sense of grasping); KJV: fist.

H107 אִגֶּרֶת (ʼiggereth, ig-eh'-reth): an epistle. Origin: feminine of H104 (אִגְּרָא); KJV: letter.

H108 אֵד (ʼêd, ade): a fog. Origin: from the same as H181 (אוּד) (in the sense of enveloping); KJV: mist, vapor.

H109 אָדַב (ʼâdab, aw-dab'): to languish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: grieve.

H110 אַדְבְּאֵל (ʼAdbᵉʼêl, ad-beh-ale'): Adbeel, a son of Ishmael. Origin: probably from H109 (אָדַב) (in the sense of chastisement) and H410 (אֵל); disciplined of God; KJV: Adbeel.

H111 אֲדַד (ʼĂdad, ad-ad'): Adad (or Hadad), an Edomite. Origin: probably an orthographical variation for H2301 (חֲדַד); KJV: Hadad.

H112 אִדּוֹ (ʼIddôw, id-do): Iddo, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Iddo.

H113 אָדוֹן (ʼâdôwn, aw-done'): sovereign, i.e. controller (human or divine). Origin: or (shortened) אָדֹן; from an unused root (meaning to rule); KJV: lord, master, owner. Compare also names beginning with 'Adoni-'.

H114 אַדּוֹן (ʼAddôwn, ad-done'): Addon, apparently an Israelite. Origin: probably intensive for H113 (אָדוֹן); powerful; KJV: Addon.

H115 אֲדוֹרַיִם (ʼĂdôwrayim, ad-o-rah'-yim): Adorajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual from H142 (אָדַר) (in the sense of eminence); double mound; KJV: Adoraim.

H116 אֱדַיִן (ʼĕdayin, ed-ah'-yin): then (of time). Origin: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; KJV: now, that time, then.

H117 אַדִּיר (ʼaddîyr, ad-deer'): wide or (generally) large; figuratively, powerful. Origin: from H142 (אָדַר); KJV: excellent, famous, gallant, glorious, goodly, lordly, mighty(-ier one), noble, principal, worthy.

H118 אֲדַלְיָא (ʼĂdalyâʼ, ad-al-yaw'): Adalja, a son of Haman. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Adalia.

H119 אָדַם (ʼâdam, aw-dam'): flush or turn rosy. Origin: to show blood (in the face), i.e. KJV: be (dyed, made) red (ruddy).

H120 אָדָם (ʼâdâm, aw-dawm'): ruddy i.e. a human being (an individual or the species, mankind, etc.). Origin: from H119 (אָדַם); KJV: [idiom] another, [phrase] hypocrite, [phrase] common sort, [idiom] low, man (mean, of low degree), person.

H121 אָדָם (ʼÂdâm, aw-dawm'): Adam the name of the first man, also of a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H120 (אָדָם); KJV: Adam.

H122 אָדֹם (ʼâdôm, aw-dome'): rosy. Origin: from H119 (אָדַם); KJV: red, ruddy.

H123 אֱדֹם (ʼĔdôm, ed-ome'): Edom, the elder twin-brother of Jacob; hence the region (Idumaea) occupied by him. Origin: or (fully) אֱדוֹם ; from H122 (אָדֹם); red (see Genesis 25:25); KJV: Edom, Edomites, Idumea.

H124 אֹדֶם (ʼôdem, o'-dem): redness, i.e. the ruby, garnet, or some other red gem. Origin: from H119 (אָדַם); KJV: sardius.

H125 אֲדַמְדָּם (ʼădamdâm, ad-am-dawm'): reddish. Origin: reduplicated from H119 (אָדַם); KJV: (somewhat) reddish.

H126 אַדְמָה (ʼAdmâh, ad-maw'): Admah, a place near the Dead Sea. Origin: contracted for H127 (אֲדָמָה); earthy; KJV: Admah.

H127 אֲדָמָה (ʼădâmâh, ad-aw-maw'): soil (from its general redness). Origin: from H119 (אָדַם); KJV: country, earth, ground, husband(-man) (-ry), land.

H128 אֲדָמָה (ʼĂdâmâh, ad-aw-maw'): Adamah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H127 (אֲדָמָה); KJV: Adamah.

H129 אֲדָמִי (ʼĂdâmîy, ad-aw-mee'): Adami, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H127 (אֲדָמָה); earthy; KJV: Adami.

H130 אֱדֹמִי (ʼĔdômîy, ed-o-mee'): an Edomite, or descendants from (or inhabitants of) Edom. Origin: or (fully) אֱדוֹמִי ; patronymic from H123 (אֱדֹם); See H726 (אֲרוֹמִי). KJV: Edomite.

H131 אֲדֻמִּים (ʼĂdummîym, ad-oom-meem'): Adummim, a pass in Palestine. Origin: plural of H121 (אָדָם); red spots; KJV: Adummim.

H132 אַדְמֹנִי (ʼadmônîy, ad-mo-nee'): reddish (of the hair or the complexion). Origin: or (fully) אַדְמוֹנִי ; from H119 (אָדַם); KJV: red, ruddy.

H133 אַדְמָתָא (ʼAdmâthâʼ, ad-maw-thaw'): Admatha, a Persian nobleman. Origin: probably of Persian derivation; KJV: Admatha.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H134 to H264
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H134 אֶדֶן (ʼeden, eh'-den): a basis (of a building, a column, etc.). Origin: from the same as H113 (אָדוֹן) (in the sense of strength); KJV: foundation, socket.

H135 אַדָּן (ʼAddân, ad-dawn'): Addan, an Israelite. Origin: intensive from the same as H134 (אֶדֶן); firm; KJV: Addan.

H136 אֲדֹנָי (ʼĂdônây, ad-o-noy'): the Lord (used as a proper name of God only). Origin: an emphatic form of H113 (אָדוֹן); KJV: (my) Lord.

H137 אֲדֹנִי־בֶזֶק (ʼĂdônîy-Bezeq, ad-o''-nee-beh'-zek): Adoni-Bezek; a Canaanitish king. Origin: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H966 (בֶּזֶק); lord of Bezek; KJV: Adonibezek.

H138 אֲדֹנִיָּה (ʼĂdônîyâh, ad-o-nee-yaw'): Adonijah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: original (prolonged) אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ ; from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H3050 (יָהּ); lord (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; KJV: Adonijah.

H139 אֲדֹנִי־צֶדֶק (ʼĂdônîy-Tsedeq, ad-o''-nee-tseh'-dek): Adoni-Tsedek, a Canaanitish king. Origin: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H6664 (צֶדֶק); lord of justice; KJV: Adonizedec.

H140 אֲדֹנִיקָם (ʼĂdônîyqâm, ad-o-nee-kawm'): Adonikam, the name of one or two Israelites. Origin: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H6965 (קוּם); lord of rising (i.e. high); KJV: Adonikam.

H141 אֲדֹנִירָם (ʼĂdônîyrâm, ad-o-nee-rawm'): Adoniram, an Israelite. Origin: from H113 (אָדוֹן) and H7311 (רוּם); lord of height; KJV: Adoniram.

H142 אָדַר (ʼâdar, aw-dar'): to expand, i.e. be great or (figuratively) magnificent. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (become) glorious, honourable.

H143 אֲדָר (ʼĂdâr, ad-awr'): Adar, the 12th Hebrew month. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; perhaps meaning fire; KJV: Adar.

H144 אֲדָר (ʼĂdâr, ad-awr'): {Adar, the 12th Hebrew month}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H143 (אֲדָר) KJV: Adar.

H145 אֶדֶר (ʼeder, eh'-der): amplitude, i.e. (concrete) a mantle; also (figuratively) splendor. Origin: from H142 (אָדַר); KJV: goodly, robe.

H146 אַדָּר (ʼAddâr, ad-dawr'): Addar, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite. Origin: intensive from H142 (אָדַר); ample; KJV: Addar.

H147 אִדַּר (ʼiddar, id-dar'): ample, i.e. a threshing-floor. Origin: (Aramaic) intensive, from a root corresponding to H142 (אָדַר); KJV: threshingfloor.

H148 אֲדַרְגָּזֵר (ʼădargâzêr, ad-ar''-gaw-zare'): a chief diviner, or astrologer. Origin: (Aramaic) from the same as H147 (אִדַּר), and H1505 (גְּזַר); KJV: judge.

H149 אַדְרַזְדָּא (ʼadrazdâʼ, ad-raz-daw'): quickly or carefully. Origin: (Aramaic) probably of Persian origin; KJV: diligently.

H150 אֲדַרְכֹּן (ʼădarkôn, ad-ar-kone'): a daric or Persian coin. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: dram.

H151 אֲדֹרָם (ʼĂdôrâm, ad-o-rawm'): Adoram (or Adoniram), an Israelite. Origin: contracted for H141 (אֲדֹנִירָם); KJV: Adoram.

H152 אֲדְרַמֶּלֶךְ (ʼĂdrammelek, ad-ram-meh'-lek): Adrammelek, the name of an Assyrian idol, also of a son of Sennacherib. Origin: from H142 (אָדַר) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); splendor of (the) king; KJV: Adrammelech.

H153 אֶדְרָע (ʼedrâʻ, ed-raw'): an arm, i.e. (figuratively) power. Origin: (Aramaic) an orthographical variation for H1872 (דְּרַע); KJV: force.

H154 אֶדְרֶעִי (ʼedreʻîy, ed-reh'-ee): Edrei, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from the equivalent of H153 (אֶדְרָע); mighty; KJV: Edrei.

H155 אַדֶּרֶת (ʼaddereth, ad-deh'-reth): something ample (as a large vine, a wide dress). Origin: feminine of H117 (אַדִּיר); ; also the same as H145 (אֶדֶר) KJV: garment, glory, goodly, mantle, robe.

H156 אָדַשׁ (ʼâdash, aw-dash'): to tread out (grain). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: thresh.

H157 אָהַב (ʼâhab, aw-hab'): to have affection for (sexually or otherwise). Origin: or אָהֵב ; a primitive root; KJV: (be-) love(-d, -ly, -r), like, friend.

H158 אַהַב (ʼahab, ah'-hab): affection (in a good or a bad sense). Origin: from H157 (אָהַב); KJV: love(-r).

H159 אֹהַב (ʼôhab, o'-hab): {affection (in a good or a bad sense)}. Origin: from H156 (אָדַשׁ); meaning the same as H158 (אַהַב) KJV: love.

H160 אַהֲבָה (ʼahăbâh, a-hab-aw): {affection (in a good or a bad sense)}. Origin: feminine of H158 (אַהַב) and meaning the same KJV: love.

H161 אֹהַד (ʼÔhad, o'-had): Ohad, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be united; unity; KJV: Ohad.

H162 אֲהָהּ (ʼăhâhh, a-haw'): Oh!. Origin: apparently a primitive word expressing pain exclamatorily; KJV: ah, alas.

H163 אַהֲוָא (ʼAhăvâʼ, a-hav-aw'): Ahava, a river of Babylonia. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Ahava.

H164 אֵהוּד (ʼÊhûwd, ay-hood'): Ehud, the name of two or three Israelites. Origin: from the same as H161 (אֹהַד); united; KJV: Ehud.

H165 אֱהִי (ʼĕhîy, e-hee'): where. Origin: apparently an orthographical variation for H346 (אַיֵּה); KJV: I will be (Hosea 13:10,14) (which is often the rendering of the same Hebrew form from H1961 (הָיָה)).

H166 אָהַל (ʼâhal, aw-hal'): to be clear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shine.

H167 אָהַל (ʼâhal, aw-hal'): to tent. Origin: a denominative from H168 (אֹהֶל); KJV: pitch (remove) a tent.

H168 אֹהֶל (ʼôhel, o'-hel): a tent (as clearly conspicuous from a distance). Origin: from H166 (אָהַל); KJV: covering, (dwelling) (place), home, tabernacle, tent.

H169 אֹהֶל (ʼÔhel, o'-hel): Ohel, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H168 (אֹהֶל); KJV: Ohel.

H170 אׇהֳלָה (ʼOhŏlâh, o-hol-aw'): Oholah, a symbolic name for Samaria. Origin: in form a feminine of H168 (אֹהֶל), but in fact for אׇהֳלָהּ; from H168 (אֹהֶל); her tent (i.e. idolatrous sanctuary); KJV: Aholah.

H171 אׇהֳלִיאָב (ʼOhŏlîyʼâb, o''-hol-e-awb'): Oholiab, an Israelite. Origin: from H168 (אֹהֶל) and H1 (אָב); tent of (his) father; KJV: Aholiab.

H172 אׇהֳלִיבָה (ʼOhŏlîybâh, o''-hol-ee-baw'): Oholibah, a symbolic name for Judah. Origin: (similarly with H170 (אׇהֳלָה)) for אׇהֳלִיבָהּ ; from H168 (אֹהֶל); my tent (is) in her; KJV: Aholibah.

H173 אׇהֳלִיבָמָה (ʼOhŏlîybâmâh, o''-hol-ee-baw-maw'): Oholibamah, a wife of Esau. Origin: from H168 (אֹהֶל) and H1116 (בָּמָה); tent of (the) height; KJV: Aholibamah.

H174 אֲהָלִים (ʼăhâlîym, a-haw-leem'): aloe wood (i.e. sticks). Origin: or (feminine) אֲהָלוֹת (only used thus in the plural); of foreign origin; KJV: (tree of lign-) aloes.

H175 אַהֲרוֹן (ʼAhărôwn, a-har-one'): Aharon, the brother of Moses. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Aaron.

H176 אוֹ (ʼôw, o): desire (and so probably in Proverbs 31:4); hence (by way of alternative) or, also if. Origin: presumed to be the 'constructive' or genitival form of אַו ; short for H185 (אַוָּה); KJV: also, and, either, if, at the least, [idiom] nor, or, otherwise, then, whether.

H177 אוּאֵל (ʼÛwʼêl, oo-ale'): Uel, and Israelite. Origin: from H176 (אוֹ) and H410 (אֵל); wish of God; KJV: Uel.

H178 אוֹב (ʼôwb, obe): properly, a mumble, i.e. a water skin (from its hollow sound); hence a necromancer (ventriloquist, as from a jar). Origin: from the same as H1 (אָב) (apparently through the idea of prattling a father's name); KJV: bottle, familiar spirit.

H179 אוֹבִיל (ʼôwbîyl, o-beel'): Obil, an Ishmaelite. Origin: probably from H56 (אָבַל); mournful; KJV: Obil.

H180 אוּבָל (ʼûwbâl, oo-bawl'): a stream. Origin: or (shortened) אֻבָל ; from H2986 (יָבַל) (in the sense of H2988 (יָבָל)); KJV: river.

H181 אוּד (ʼûwd, ood): a poker (for turning or gathering embers). Origin: from an unused root meaning to rake together; KJV: (fire-) brand.

H182 אוֹדוֹת (ʼôwdôwth, o-doth'): turnings (i.e. occasions); (adverb) on account of. Origin: or (shortened) אֹדוֹת (only thus in the plural); from the same as H181 (אוּד); KJV: (be-) cause, concerning, sake.

H183 אָוָה (ʼâvâh, aw-vaw'): to wish for. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: covet, (greatly) desire, be desirous, long, lust (after).

H184 אָוָה (ʼâvâh, aw-vaw'): to extend or mark out. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: point out.

H185 אַוָּה (ʼavvâh, av-vaw'): longing. Origin: from H183 (אָוָה); KJV: desire, lust after, pleasure.

H186 אוּזַי (ʼÛwzay, oo-zah'-ee): Uzai, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps by permutation for H5813 (עֻזִּי), strong; KJV: Uzai.

H187 אוּזָל (ʼÛwzâl, oo-zawl'): Uzal, a son of Joktan. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Uzal.

H188 אוֹי (ʼôwy, o'-ee): lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!. Origin: probably from H183 (אָוָה) (in the sense of crying out after); KJV: alas, woe.

H189 אֱוִי (ʼĔvîy, ev-ee'): Evi, a Midianitish chief. Origin: probably from H183 (אָוָה); desirous; KJV: Evi.

H190 אוֹיָה (ʼôwyâh, o-yaw'): {lamentation; also interjectionally Oh!}. Origin: feminine of H188 (אוֹי) KJV: woe.

H191 אֱוִיל (ʼĕvîyl, ev-eel'): (figuratively) silly. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be perverse); KJV: fool(-ish) (man).

H192 אֱוִיל מְרֹדַךְ (ʼĔvîyl Mᵉrôdak, ev-eel' mer-o-dak'): Evil-Merodak, a Babylonian king. Origin: of Aramaic derivation and probably meaning soldier of Merodak; KJV: Evil-merodach.

H193 אוּל (ʼûwl, ool): the body (as being rolled together); also powerful. Origin: from an unused root meaning to twist, i.e. (by implication) be strong; KJV: mighty, strength.

H194 אוּלַי (ʼûwlay, oo-lah'ee): if not; hence perhaps. Origin: or (shortened) אֻלַי; from H176 (אוֹ); KJV: if so be, may be, peradventure, unless.

H195 אוּלַי (ʼÛwlay, oo-lah'ee): the Ulai (or Eulaeus), a river of Persia. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Ulai.

H196 אֱוִלִי (ʼĕvilîy, ev-ee-lee'): silly, foolish; hence (morally) impious. Origin: from H191 (אֱוִיל); KJV: foolish.

H197 אוּלָם (ʼûwlâm, oo-lawm'): a vestibule (as bound to the building). Origin: or (shortened), אֻלָם ; from H481 (אָלַם) (in the sense of tying); KJV: porch.

H198 אוּלָם (ʼÛwlâm, oo-lawm'): Ulam, the name of two Israelites. Origin: appar, from H481 (אָלַם) (in the sense of dumbness); solitary; KJV: Ulam.

H199 אוּלָם (ʼûwlâm, oo-lawm'): however or on the contrary. Origin: apparently a variation of H194 (אוּלַי); KJV: as for, but, howbeit, in very deed, surely, truly, wherefore.

H200 אִוֶּלֶת (ʼivveleth, iv-veh'-leth): silliness. Origin: from the same as H191 (אֱוִיל); KJV: folly, foolishly(-ness).

H201 אוֹמָר (ʼÔwmâr, o-mawr'): Omar, a grandson of Esau. Origin: from H559 (אָמַר); talkative; KJV: Omar.

H202 אוֹן (ʼôwn, one): ability, power, (figuratively) wealth. Origin: probably from the same as H205 (אָוֶן) (in the sense of effort, but successful); KJV: force, goods, might, strength, substance.

H203 אוֹן (ʼÔwn, one): On, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H202 (אוֹן); KJV: On.

H204 אוֹן (ʼÔwn, one): On, a city of Egypt. Origin: or (shortened); אֹן; of Egyptian derivation; KJV: On.

H205 אָוֶן (ʼâven, aw-ven'): strictly nothingness; also trouble. vanity, wickedness; specifically an idol. Origin: from an unused root perhaps meaning properly, to pant (hence, to exert oneself, usually in vain; to come to naught); KJV: affliction, evil, false, idol, iniquity, mischief, mourners(-ing), naught, sorrow, unjust, unrighteous, vain, vanity, wicked(-ness). Compare H369 (אַיִן).

H206 אָוֶן (ʼÂven, aw'-ven): Aven, the contemptuous synonym of three places, one in Coele-Syria, one in Egypt (On), and one in Palestine (Bethel). Origin: the same as H205 (אָוֶן); idolatry; KJV: Aven. See also H204 (אוֹן), H1007 (בֵּית אָוֶן).

H207 אוֹנוֹ (ʼÔwnôw, o-no'): Ono, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (shortened) אֹנוֹ; prolonged from H202 (אוֹן); strong; KJV: Ono.

H208 אוֹנָם (ʼÔwnâm, o-nawm'): Onam, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite. Origin: a variation of H209 (אוֹנָן); strong; KJV: Onam.

H209 אוֹנָן (ʼÔwnân, o-nawn'): Onan, a son of Judah. Origin: a variation of H207 (אוֹנוֹ); strong; KJV: Onan.

H210 אוּפָז (ʼÛwphâz, oo-fawz'): Uphaz, a famous gold region. Origin: perhaps a corruption of H211 (אוֹפִיר); KJV: Uphaz.

H211 אוֹפִיר (ʼÔwphîyr, o-feer'): Ophir, the name of a son of Joktan, and of a gold region in the East. Origin: or (shortened) אֹפִיר; and אוֹפִר; of uncertain derivation; KJV: Ophir.

H212 אוֹפָן (ʼôwphân, o-fawn'): a wheel. Origin: or (shortened) אֹפָן; from an unused root meaning to revolve; KJV: wheel.

H213 אוּץ (ʼûwts, oots): to press; (by implication) to be close, hurry, withdraw. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) haste(-n, -y), labor, be narrow.

H214 אוֹצָר (ʼôwtsâr, o-tsaw'): a depository. Origin: from H686 (אָצַר); KJV: armory, cellar, garner, store(-house), treasure(-house) (-y).

H215 אוֹר (ʼôwr, ore): to be (causative, make) luminous (literally and metaphorically). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] break of day, glorious, kindle, (be, en-, give, show) light (-en, -ened), set on fire, shine.

H216 אוֹר (ʼôwr, ore): illumination or (concrete) luminary (in every sense, including lightning, happiness, etc.). Origin: from H215 (אוֹר); KJV: bright, clear, [phrase] day, light (-ning), morning, sun.

H217 אוּר (ʼûwr, ore): flame; hence (in the plural) the East (as being the region of light). Origin: from H215 (אוֹר); KJV: fire, light. See also H224 (אוּרִים).

H218 אוּר (ʼÛwr, oor): Ur, a place in Chaldaea; also an Israelite. Origin: the same as H217 (אוּר); KJV: Ur.

H219 אוֹרָה (ʼôwrâh, o-raw'): luminousness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity; also a plant (as being bright). Origin: feminine of H216 (אוֹר); KJV: herb, light.

H220 אֲוֵרָה (ʼăvêrâh, av-ay-raw'): a stall. Origin: by transposition for H723 (אֻרְוָה); KJV: cote.

H221 אוּרִי (ʼÛwrîy, oo-ree'): Uri, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H217 (אוּר); fiery; KJV: Uri.

H222 אוּרִיאֵל (ʼÛwrîyʼêl, oo-ree-ale'): Uriel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H217 (אוּר) and H410 (אֵל); flame of God; KJV: Uriel.

H223 אוּרִיָּה (ʼÛwrîyâh, oo-ree-yaw'): Urijah, the name of one Hittite and five Israelites. Origin: or (prolonged) אוּרִיָּהוּ ; from H217 (אוּר) and H3050 (יָהּ); flame of Jah; KJV: Uriah, Urijah.

H224 אוּרִים (ʼÛwrîym, oo-reem'): Urim, the oracular brilliancy of the figures in the high-priest's breastplate. Origin: plural of H217 (אוּר); lights; KJV: Urim.

H225 אוּת (ʼûwth, ooth): properly, to come, i.e. (implied) to assent. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consent.

H226 אוֹת (ʼôwth, oth): a signal (literally or figuratively), as aflag, beacon, monument, omen, prodigy, evidence, etc. Origin: probably from H225 (אוּת) (in the sense of appearing); KJV: mark, miracle, (en-) sign, token.

H227 אָז (ʼâz, awz): at that time or place; also as a conjunction, therefore. Origin: a demonstrative adverb; KJV: beginning, for, from, hitherto, now, of old, once, since, then, at which time, yet.

H228 אֲזָא (ʼăzâʼ, az-zaw'): to kindle; (by implication) to heat. Origin: (Aramaic) or אֲזָה (Aramaic); KJV: heat, hot.

H229 אֶזְבַּי (ʼEzbay, ez-bah'ee): Ezbai, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H231 (אֵזוֹב); hyssop-like; KJV: Ezbai.

H230 אֲזָד (ʼăzâd, az-zawd'): firm. Origin: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; KJV: be gone.

H231 אֵזוֹב (ʼêzôwb, ay-zobe'): hyssop. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: hyssop.

H232 אֵזוֹר (ʼêzôwr, ay-zore'): something girt; a belt, also a band. Origin: from H246 (אֲזִקִּים); KJV: girdle.

H233 אֲזַי (ʼăzay, az-ah'ee): at that time. Origin: probably from H227 (אָז); KJV: then.

H234 אַזְכָּרָה (ʼazkârâh, az-kaw-raw'): a reminder; specifically remembrance-offering. Origin: from H2142 (זָכַר); KJV: memorial.

H235 אָזַל (ʼâzal, aw-zal'): to go away, hence, to disappear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fail, gad about, go to and fro (but in Ezekiel 27:19 the word is rendered by many 'from Uzal,' by others 'yarn'), be gone (spent).

H236 אֲזַל (ʼăzal, az-al'): to depart. Origin: (Aramaic) the same as H235 (אָזַל); KJV: go (up).

H237 אֶזֶל (ʼezel, eh'-zel): Ezel, a memorial stone in Palestine. Origin: from H235 (אָזַל); departure; KJV: Ezel.

H238 אָזַן (ʼâzan, aw-zan'): to broaden out the ear (with the hand), i.e. (by implication) to listen. Origin: a primitive root; probably to expand; but used only as a denominative from H241 (אֹזֶן); KJV: give (perceive by the) ear, hear(-ken). See H239 (אָזַן).

H239 אָזַן (ʼâzan, aw-zan'): to weigh, i.e. (figuratively) ponder. Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H238 (אָזַן) through the idea of scales as if two ears); KJV: give good heed.

H240 אָזֵן (ʼâzên, aw-zane'): a spade or paddle (as having a broad end). Origin: from H238 (אָזַן); KJV: weapon.

H241 אֹזֶן (ʼôzen, o'-zen): broadness. i.e. (concrete) the ear (from its form in man). Origin: from H238 (אָזַן); KJV: [phrase] advertise, audience, [phrase] displease, ear, hearing, [phrase] show.

H242 אֻזֵּן שֶׁאֱרָה (ʼUzzên Sheʼĕrâh, ooz-zane' sheh-er-aw'): Uzzen-Sheerah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H238 (אָזַן) and H7609 (שֶׁאֱרָה); plot of Sheerah (i.e. settled by him); KJV: Uzzen-sherah.

H243 אַזְנוֹת תָּבוֹר (ʼAznôwth Tâbôwr, az-noth' taw-bore'): Aznoth-Tabor, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H238 (אָזַן) and H8396 (תָּבוֹר); flats (i.e. tops) of Tabor (i.e. situated on it); KJV: Aznoth-tabor.

H244 אׇזְנִי (ʼOznîy, oz-nee'): Ozni, an Israelite; also an Oznite (collectively), his descendant. Origin: from H241 (אֹזֶן); having (quick) ears; KJV: Ozni, Oznites.

H245 אֲזַנְיָה (ʼĂzanyâh, az-an-yaw'): Azanjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H238 (אָזַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); heard by Jah; KJV: Azaniah.

H246 אֲזִקִּים (ʼăziqqîym, az-ik-keem'): manacles. Origin: a variation for H2131 (זִיקָה); KJV: chains.

H247 אָזַר (ʼâzar, aw-zar'): to belt. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind (compass) about, gird (up, with).

H248 אֶזְרוֹעַ (ʼezrôwaʻ, ez-ro'-a): the arm. Origin: a variation for H2220 (זְרוֹעַ); KJV: arm.

H249 אֶזְרָח (ʼezrâch, ez-rawkh'): a spontaneous growth, i.e. native (tree or persons). Origin: from H2224 (זָרַח) (in the sense of springing up); KJV: bay tree, (home-) born (in the land), of the (one's own) country (nation).

H250 אֶזְרָחִי (ʼEzrâchîy, ez-raw-khee'): an Ezrachite or descendant of Zerach. Origin: patronymic from H2246 (חֹבָב); KJV: Ezrahite.

H251 אָח (ʼâch, awkh): a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance (like father)). Origin: a primitive word; KJV: another, brother(-ly); kindred, like, other. Compare also the proper names beginning with 'Ah-' or 'Ahi-'.

H252 אַח (ʼach, akh): {a brother (used in the widest sense of literal relationship and metaphorical affinity or resemblance)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H251 (אָח) KJV: brother.

H253 אָח (ʼâch, awkh): Oh! (expressive of grief or surprise). Origin: a variation for H162 (אֲהָהּ); KJV: ah, alas.

H254 אָח (ʼâch, awkh): a fire-pot or chafing dish. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: hearth.

H255 אֹחַ (ʼôach, o'-akh): a howler or lonesome wild animal. Origin: probably from H253 (אָח); KJV: doleful creature.

H256 אַחְאָב (ʼAchʼâb, akh-awb'): Achab, the name of a king of Israel and of a prophet at Babylon. Origin: once (by contraction) אֶחָב (Jeremiah 29:22); from H251 (אָח) and H1 (אָב); brother (i.e. friend) of (his) father; KJV: Ahab.

H257 אַחְבָן (ʼAchbân, akh-bawn'): Achban, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H995 (בִּין); brother (i.e. possessor) of understanding; KJV: Ahban.

H258 אָחַד (ʼâchad, aw-khad'): to unify, i.e. (figuratively) collect (one's thoughts). Origin: perhaps a primitive root; KJV: go one way or other.

H259 אֶחָד (ʼechâd, ekh-awd'): properly, united, i.e. one; or (as an ordinal) first. Origin: a numeral from H258 (אָחַד); KJV: a, alike, alone, altogether, and, any(-thing), apiece, a certain, (dai-) ly, each (one), [phrase] eleven, every, few, first, [phrase] highway, a man, once, one, only, other, some, together,

H260 אָחוּ (ʼâchûw, aw'-khoo): a bulrush or any marshy grass (particularly that along the Nile). Origin: of uncertain (perhaps Egyptian) derivation; KJV: flag, meadow.

H261 אֵחוּד (ʼÊchûwd, ay-khood'): Echud, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H258 (אָחַד); united; KJV: Ehud.

H262 אַחְוָה (ʼachvâh, akh-vaw'): an utterance. Origin: from H2331 (חָוָה) (in the sense of H2324 (חֲוָא)); KJV: declaration.

H263 אַחֲוָה (ʼachăvâh, akh-av-aw'): solution (of riddles). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H262 (אַחְוָה); KJV: showing.

H264 אַחֲוָה (ʼachăvâh, akh-av-aw'): fraternity. Origin: from H251 (אָח); KJV: brotherhood.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H265 to H386
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H265 אֲחוֹחַ (ʼĂchôwach, akh-o'-akh): Achoach, an Israelite. Origin: by reduplication from H251 (אָח); brotherly; KJV: Ahoah.

H266 אֲחוֹחִי (ʼĂchôwchîy, akh-o-khee'): an Achochite or descendant of Achoach. Origin: patronymic from H264 (אַחֲוָה); KJV: Ahohite.

H267 אֲחוּמַי (ʼĂchûwmay, akh-oo-mah'-ee): Achumai, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H251 (אָח) and H4325 (מַיִם); brother (i.e. neighbour) of water; KJV: Ahumai.

H268 אָחוֹר (ʼâchôwr, aw-khore'): the hinder part; hence (adverb) behind, backward; also (as facing north) the West. Origin: or (shortened) אָחֹר ; from H299 (אֲחִירַע); KJV: after(-ward), back (part, -side, -ward), hereafter, (be-) hind(-er part), time to come, without.

H269 אָחוֹת (ʼâchôwth, aw-khoth'): a sister (used very widely (like brother), literally and figuratively). Origin: irregular feminine of H251 (אָח); KJV: (an-) other, sister, together.

H270 אָחַז (ʼâchaz, aw-khaz'): to seize (often with the accessory idea of holding in possession). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [phrase] be affrighted, bar, (catch, lay, take) hold (back), come upon, fasten, handle, portion, (get, have or take) possess(-ion).

H271 אָחָז (ʼÂchâz, aw-khawz'): Achaz, the name of a Jewish king and of an Israelite. Origin: from H270 (אָחַז); possessor; KJV: Ahaz.

H272 אֲחֻזָּה (ʼăchuzzâh, akh-ooz-zaw'): something seized, i.e. a possession (especially of land). Origin: feminine passive participle from H270 (אָחַז); KJV: possession.

H273 אַחְזַי (ʼAchzay, akh-zah'ee): Achzai, an Israelite. Origin: from H270 (אָחַז); seizer; KJV: Ahasai.

H274 אֲחַזְיָה (ʼĂchazyâh, akh-az-yaw'): Achazjah, the name of a Jewish and an Israelite king. Origin: or (prolonged) אֲחַזְיָהוּ ; from H270 (אָחַז) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has seized; KJV: Ahaziah.

H275 אֲחֻזָּם (ʼĂchuzzâm, akh-ooz-zawm'): Achuzzam, an Israelite. Origin: from H270 (אָחַז); seizure; KJV: Ahuzam.

H276 אֲחֻזַּת (ʼĂchuzzath, akh-ooz-zath'): Achuzzath, a Philistine. Origin: a variation of H272 (אֲחֻזָּה); possession; KJV: Ahuzzath.

H277 אֲחִי (ʼĂchîy, akh-ee'): Achi, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H251 (אָח); brotherly; KJV: Ahi.

H278 אֵחִי (ʼÊchîy, ay-khee'): Echi, an Israelite. Origin: probably the same as H277 (אֲחִי); KJV: Ehi.

H279 אֲחִיאָם (ʼĂchîyʼâm, akh-ee-awm'): Achiam, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H517 (אֵם); brother of the mother (i.e. uncle); KJV: Ahiam.

H280 אֲחִידָה (ʼăchîydâh, akh-ee-daw'): an enigma. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2420 (חִידָה), KJV: hard sentence.

H281 אֲחִיָּה (ʼĂchîyâh, akh-ee-yaw): Achijah, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: or (prolonged) אֲחִיָּהוּ ; from H251 (אָח) and H3050 (יָהּ); brother (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; KJV: Ahiah, Ahijah.

H282 אֲחִיהוּד (ʼĂchîyhûwd, akh-ee-hood'): Achihud, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H1935 (הוֹד); brother (i.e. possessor) of renown; KJV: Ahihud.

H283 אַחְיוֹ (ʼAchyôw, akh-yo'): Achio, the name of three Israelites. Origin: prolonged from H251 (אָח); brotherly; KJV: Ahio.

H284 אֲחִיחֻד (ʼĂchîychud, akh-ee-khood'): Achichud, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H2330 (חוּד); brother of a riddle (i.e. mysterious); KJV: Ahihud.

H285 אֲחִיטוּב (ʼĂchîyṭûwb, akh-ee-toob'): Achitub, the name of several priests. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H2898 (טוּב); brother of goodness; KJV: Ahitub.

H286 אֲחִילוּד (ʼĂchîylûwd, akh-ee-lood'): Achilud, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H3205 (יָלַד); brother of one born; KJV: Ahilud.

H287 אֲחִימוֹת (ʼĂchîymôwth, akh-ee-moth'): Achimoth, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H4191 (מוּת); brother of death; KJV: Ahimoth.

H288 אֲחִימֶלֶךְ (ʼĂchîymelek, akh-ee-meh'-lek): Achimelek, the name of an Israelite and of a Hittite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); brother of (the) king; KJV: Ahimelech.

H289 אֲחִימַן (ʼĂchîyman, akh-ee-man'): Achiman, the name of an Anakite and of an Israelite. Origin: or אֲחִימָן ; from H251 (אָח) and H4480 (מִן); brother of a portion (i.e. gift); KJV: Ahiman.

H290 אֲחִימַעַץ (ʼĂchîymaʻats, akh-ee-mah'-ats): Achimaats, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and the equivalent of H4619 (מַעַץ); brother of anger; KJV: Ahimaaz.

H291 אַחְיָן (ʼAchyân, akh-yawn'): Achjan, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח); brotherly; KJV: Ahian.

H292 אֲחִינָדָב (ʼĂchîynâdâb, akh-ee-naw-dawb'): Achinadab, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H5068 (נָדַב); brother of liberality; KJV: Ahinadab.

H293 אֲחִינֹעַם (ʼĂchîynôʻam, akh-ee-no'-am): Achinoam, the name of two Israelitesses. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H5278 (נֹעַם); brother of pleasantness; KJV: Ahinoam.

H294 אֲחִיסָמָךְ (ʼĂchîyçâmâk, akh-ee-saw-mawk'): Achisamak, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H5564 (סָמַךְ); brother of support; KJV: Ahisamach.

H295 אֲחִיעֶזֶר (ʼĂchîyʻezer, akh-ee-eh'-zer): Achiezer, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); brother of help; KJV: Ahiezer.

H296 אֲחִיקָם (ʼĂchîyqâm, akh-ee-kawm'): Achikam, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H6965 (קוּם); brother of rising (i.e. high); KJV: Ahikam.

H297 אֲחִירָם (ʼĂchîyrâm, akh-ee-rawm'): Achiram, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H7311 (רוּם); brother of height (i.e. high); KJV: Ahiram.

H298 אֲחִירָמִי (ʼĂchîyrâmîy, akh-ee-raw-mee'): an Achiramite or descendant (collectively) of Achiram. Origin: patronymic from H297 (אֲחִירָם); KJV: Ahiramites.

H299 אֲחִירַע (ʼĂchîyraʻ, akh-ee-rah'): Achira, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H7451 (רַע); brother of wrong; KJV: Ahira.

H300 אֲחִישַׁחַר (ʼĂchîyshachar, akh-ee-shakh'-ar): Achishachar, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H7837 (שַׁחַר); brother of (the) dawn; KJV: Ahishar.

H301 אֲחִישָׁר (ʼĂchîyshâr, akh-ee-shawr'): Achishar, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H7891 (שִׁיר); brother of (the) singer; KJV: Ahishar.

H302 אֲחִיתֹפֶל (ʼĂchîythôphel, akh-ee-tho'-fel): Achithophel, an Israelite. Origin: from H251 (אָח) and H8602 (תָּפֵל); brother of folly; KJV: Ahithophel.

H303 אַחְלָב (ʼAchlâb, akh-lawb'): Achlab, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same root as H2459 (חֶלֶב); fatness (i.e. fertile); KJV: Ahlab.

H304 אַחְלַי (ʼAchlay, akh-lah'ee): Achlai, the name of an Israelitess and of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H305 (אַחֲלַי); wishful; KJV: Ahlai.

H305 אַחֲלַי (ʼachălay, akh-al-ah'ee): would that!. Origin: or אַחֲלֵי; prob from H253 (אָח) and a variation of H3863 (לוּא); KJV: O that, would God.

H306 אַחְלָמָה (ʼachlâmâh, akh-law'-maw): a gem, probably the amethyst. Origin: perhaps from H2492 (חָלַם) (and thus dream-stone); KJV: amethyst.

H307 אַחְמְתָא (ʼAchmᵉthâʼ, akh-me-thaw'): Achmetha (i.e. Ecbatana), the summer capital of Persia. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Achmetha.

H308 אֲחַסְבַּי (ʼĂchaçbay, akh-as-bah'ee): Achasbai, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Ahasbai.

H309 אָחַר (ʼâchar, aw-khar'): to loiter (i.e. be behind); by implication to procrastinate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: continue, defer, delay, hinder, be late (slack), stay (there), tarry (longer).

H310 אַחַר (ʼachar, akh-ar'): properly, the hind part; generally used as an adverb or conjunction, after (in various senses). Origin: from H309 (אָחַר); KJV: after (that, -ward), again, at, away from, back (from, -side), behind, beside, by, follow (after, -ing), forasmuch, from, hereafter, hinder end, [phrase] out (over) live, [phrase] persecute, posterity, pursuing, remnant, seeing, since, thence(-forth), when, with.

H311 אַחַר (ʼachar, akh-ar'): after. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H310 (אַחַר); KJV: (here-) after.

H312 אַחֵר (ʼachêr, akh-air'): properly, hinder; generally, next, other, etc. Origin: from H309 (אָחַר); KJV: (an-) other man, following, next, strange.

H313 אַחֵר (ʼAchêr, akh-air'): Acher, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H312 (אַחֵר); KJV: Aher.

H314 אַחֲרוֹן (ʼachărôwn, akh-ar-one'): hinder; generally, late or last; specifically (as facing the east) western. Origin: or (shortened) אַחֲרֹן; from H309 (אָחַר); KJV: after (-ward), to come, following, hind(-er, -ermost, -most), last, latter, rereward, ut(ter) most.

H315 אַחְרַח (ʼAchrach, akh-rakh'): Achrach, an Israelite. Origin: from H310 (אַחַר) and H251 (אָח); after (his) brother; KJV: Aharah.

H316 אֲחַרְחֵל (ʼĂcharchêl, akh-ar-kale'): Acharchel, an Israelite. Origin: from H310 (אַחַר) and H2426 (חֵיל); behind (the) intrenchment (i.e. safe); KJV: Aharhel,

H317 אׇחֳרִי (ʼochŏrîy, okh-or-ee'): other. Origin: (Aramaic) from H311 (אַחַר); KJV: (an-) other.

H318 אׇחֳרֵין (ʼochŏrêyn, okh-or-ane'): last. Origin: (Aramaic) or (shortened) אׇחֳרֵן; (Aramaic) from H317 (אׇחֳרִי); KJV: at last.

H319 אַחֲרִית (ʼachărîyth, akh-ar-eeth'): the last or end, hence, the future; also posterity. Origin: from H310 (אַחַר); KJV: (last, latter) end (time), hinder (utter) -most, length, posterity, remnant, residue, reward.

H320 אַחֲרִית (ʼachărîyth, akh-ar-eeth'): later. Origin: (Aramaic) from H311 (אַחַר); the same as H319 (אַחֲרִית); KJV: latter.

H321 אׇחֳרָן (ʼochŏrân, okh-or-awn'): other. Origin: (Aramaic) from H311 (אַחַר); the same as H317 (אׇחֳרִי); KJV: (an-) other.

H322 אֲחֹרַנִּית (ʼăchôrannîyth, akh-o-ran-neeth'): backwards. Origin: prolonged from H268 (אָחוֹר); KJV: back (-ward, again).

H323 אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפַּן (ʼăchashdarpan, akh-ash-dar-pan'): a satrap or governorof amain province (of Persia). Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: lieutenant.

H324 אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפַּן (ʼăchashdarpan, akh-ash-dar-pan'): {a satrap or governorof amain province (of Persia)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H323 (אֲחַשְׁדַּרְפַּן) KJV: prince.

H325 אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ (ʼĂchashvêrôwsh, akh-ash-vay-rosh'): Achashverosh (i.e. Ahasuerus or Artaxerxes, but in this case Xerxes), the title (rather than name) of a Persian king. Origin: or (shortened) אַחַשְׁרֹשׁ (Esther 10:1); of Persian origin; KJV: Ahasuerus.

H326 אֲחַשְׁתָּרִי (ʼăchashtârîy, akh-ash-taw-ree'): an achastarite (i.e. courier); the designation (rather than name) of an Israelite. Origin: probably of Persian derivation; KJV: Haakashtari (includ. the article).

H327 אֲחַשְׁתָּרָן (ʼăchashtârân, akh-ash-taw-rawn'): a mule. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: camel.

H328 אַט (ʼaṭ, at): (as a noun) a necromancer (from their soft incantations), (as an adverb) gently. Origin: from an unused root perhaps meaning to move softly; KJV: charmer, gently, secret, softly.

H329 אָטָד (ʼâṭâd, aw-tawd'): a thorn-tree (especially the buckthorn). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to pierce or make fast; KJV: Atad, bramble, thorn.

H330 אֵטוּן (ʼêṭûwn, ay-toon'): properly, twisted (yarn), i.e. tapestry. Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to bind); KJV: fine linen.

H331 אָטַם (ʼâṭam, aw-tam'): to close (the lips or ears); by analology to contract (a window by bevelled jambs). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: narrow, shut, stop.

H332 אָטַר (ʼâṭar, aw-tar'): to close up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shut.

H333 אָטֵר (ʼÂṭêr, aw-tare'): Ater, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H332 (אָטַר); maimed; KJV: Ater.

H334 אִטֵּר (ʼiṭṭêr, it-tare'): shut up, i.e. impeded (as to the use of the right hand). Origin: from H332 (אָטַר); KJV: [phrase] left-handed.

H335 אַי (ʼay, ah'ee): where? hence how?. Origin: perhaps from H370 (אַיִן); KJV: how, what, whence, where, whether, which (way).

H336 אִי (ʼîy, ee): not. Origin: probably identical with H335 (אַי) (through the idea of a query); KJV: island (Job 22:30).

H337 אִי (ʼîy, ee): alas!. Origin: short from H188 (אוֹי); KJV: woe.

H338 אִי (ʼîy, ee): a howler (used only in the plural), i.e. any solitary wild creature. Origin: probably identical with H337 (אִי) (through the idea of a doleful sound); KJV: wild beast of the islands.

H339 אִי (ʼîy, ee): properly, a habitable spot (as desirable); dry land, a coast, an island. Origin: from H183 (אָוָה); KJV: country, isle, island.

H340 אָיַב (ʼâyab, aw-yab'): to hate (as one of an opposite tribe or party); hence to be hostile. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be an enemy.

H341 אֹיֵב (ʼôyêb, o-yabe'): hating; an adversary. Origin: or (fully) אוֹיֵב; active participle of H340 (אָיַב); KJV: enemy, foe.

H342 אֵיבָה (ʼêybâh, ay-baw'): hostility. Origin: from H340 (אָיַב); KJV: emnity, hatred.

H343 אֵיד (ʼêyd, ade): oppression; by implication misfortune, ruin. Origin: from the same as H181 (אוּד) (in the sense of bending down); KJV: calamity, destruction.

H344 אַיָּה (ʼayâh, ah-yaw'): the screamer, i.e. a hawk. Origin: perhaps from H337 (אִי); KJV: kite, vulture.

H345 אַיָּה (ʼAyâh, ah-yaw'): Ajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H344 (אַיָּה); KJV: Aiah, Ajah.

H346 אַיֵּה (ʼayêh, ah-yay'): where?. Origin: prolonged from H335 (אַי); KJV: where.

H347 אִיּוֹב (ʼÎyôwb, ee-yobe'): Ijob, the patriarch famous for his patience. Origin: from H340 (אָיַב); hated (i.e. persecuted); KJV: Job.

H348 אִיזֶבֶל (ʼÎyzebel, ee-zeh'-bel): Izebel, the wife of king Ahab. Origin: from H336 (אִי)lemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי and H2083 (זְבֻל); KJV: Jezebel.

H349 אֵיךְ (ʼêyk, ake): how? or how!; also where. Origin: also אֵיכָה ; and אֵיכָכָה ; prolonged from H335 (אַי); KJV: how, what.

H350 אִי־כָבוֹד (ʼÎy-kâbôwd, ee-kaw-bode'): Ikabod, a son of Phineas. Origin: from H336 (אִי)lemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי and H3519 (כָּבוֹד); (there is) no glory, i.e. inglorious; KJV: I-chabod.

H351 אֵיכֹה (ʼêykôh, ay-ko): where. Origin: probably a variation for H349 (אֵיךְ), but not as an interogative; KJV: where.

H352 אַיִל (ʼayil, ah'-yil): properly, strength; hence, anything strong; specifically a chief (politically); also a ram (from his strength); a pilaster (as a strong support); an oak or other strong tree. Origin: from the same as H193 (אוּל); KJV: mighty (man), lintel, oak, post, ram, tree.

H353 אֱיָל (ʼĕyâl, eh-yawl'): strength. Origin: a variation of H352 (אַיִל); KJV: strength.

H354 אַיָּל (ʼayâl, ah-yawl'): a stag or male deer. Origin: an intensive form of H352 (אַיִל) (in the sense of ram); KJV: hart.

H355 אַיָּלָה (ʼayâlâh, ah-yaw-law'): a doe or female deer. Origin: feminine of H354 (אַיָּל); KJV: hind.

H356 אֵילוֹן (ʼÊylôwn, ay-lone'): Elon, the name of a place in Palestine, and also of one Hittite, two Israelites. Origin: or (shortened) אֵלוֹן ; or אֵילֹן ; from H352 (אַיִל); oak-grove; KJV: Elon.

H357 אַיָּלוֹן (ʼAyâlôwn, ah-yaw-lone'): Ajalon, the name of five places in Palestine. Origin: from H354 (אַיָּל); deer-field; KJV: Aijalon, Ajalon.

H358 אֵילוֹן בֵּית חָנָן (ʼÊylôwn Bêyth Chânân, ay-lone' bayth-chawnawn'): Elon of Beth-chanan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H356 (אֵילוֹן), H1004 (בַּיִת), and H2603 (חָנַן); oak-grove of (the) house of favor; KJV: Elon-bethhanan.

H359 אֵילוֹת (ʼÊylôwth, ay-loth'): Eloth or Elath, a place on the Red Sea. Origin: or אֵילַת ; from H352 (אַיִל); trees or a grove (i.e. palms); KJV: Elath, Eloth.

H360 אֱיָלוּת (ʼĕyâlûwth, eh-yaw-looth'): power; by implication, protection. Origin: feminine of H353 (אֱיָל); KJV: strength.

H361 אֵילָם (ʼêylâm, ay-lawm'): a pillar-space (or colonnade), i.e. a pale (or portico). Origin: or (shortened) אֵלָם ; or (feminine) אֵלַמָּה ; probably from H352 (אַיִל); KJV: arch.

H362 אֵילִם (ʼÊylim, ay-leem'): Elim, a place in the Desert. Origin: plural of H352 (אַיִל); palm-trees; KJV: Elim.

H363 אִילָן (ʼîylân, ee-lawn'): a tree. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H356 (אֵילוֹן); KJV: tree.

H364 אֵיל פָּארָן (ʼÊyl Pâʼrân, ale paw-rawn'): El-Paran, a portion of the district of Paran. Origin: from H352 (אַיִל) and H6290 (פָּארָן); oak of Paran; KJV: El-paran.

H365 אַיֶּלֶת (ʼayeleth, ah-yeh'-leth): a doe. Origin: the same as H355 (אַיָּלָה); KJV: hind, Aijeleth.

H366 אָיֹם (ʼâyôm, aw-yome'): frightful. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to frighten); KJV: terrible.
