H367 אֵימָה (ʼêymâh, ay-maw'): fright; concrete, an idol (as a bugbear). Origin: or (shortened) אֵמָה; from the same as H366 (אָיֹם); KJV: dread, fear, horror, idol, terrible, terror.

H368 אֵימִים (ʼÊymîym, ay-meem'): Emim, an early Canaanitish (or Maobitish) tribe. Origin: plural of H367 (אֵימָה); terrors; KJV: Emims.

H369 אַיִן (ʼayin, ah'-yin): a non-entity; generally used as a negative particle. Origin: as if from a primitive root meaning to be nothing or not exist; KJV: else, except, fail, (father-) less, be gone, in(-curable), neither, never, no (where), none, nor, (any, thing), not, nothing, to nought, past, un(-searchable), well-nigh, without. Compare H370 (אַיִן).

H370 אַיִן (ʼayin, ah-yin'): where? (only in connection with prepositional prefix, whence). Origin: probably identical with H369 (אַיִן) in the sense of query (compare H336 (אִי)lemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי) KJV: whence, where.

H371 אִין (ʼîyn, een): is it not?. Origin: apparently a shortened form of H369 (אַיִן); but (like H370 (אַיִן)) an interrogative; KJV: not.

H372 אִיעֶזֵר (ʼÎyʻezêr, ee-eh'-zer): Iezer, an Israelite. Origin: from H336 (אִי)lemma אי missing vowel, corrected to אִי and H5828 (עֵזֶר); helpless; KJV: Jeezer.

H373 אִיעֶזְרִי (ʼÎyʻezrîy, ee-ez-ree'): an Iezrite or descendant of Iezer. Origin: patronymic from H372 (אִיעֶזֵר); KJV: Jezerite.

H374 אֵיפָה (ʼêyphâh, ay-faw'): an ephah or measure for grain; hence, a measure in general. Origin: or (shortened) אֵפָה ; of Egyptian derivation; KJV: ephah, (divers) measure(-s).

H375 אֵיפֹה (ʼêyphôh, ay-fo'): what place?; also (of time) when?; or (of means) how?. Origin: from H335 (אַי) and H6311 (פֹּה); KJV: what manner, where.

H376 אִישׁ (ʼîysh, eesh): a man as an individual or a male person; often used as an adjunct to a more definite term (and in such cases frequently not expressed in translation). Origin: contracted for H582 (אֱנוֹשׁ) (or perhaps rather from an unused root meaning to be extant); KJV: also, another, any (man), a certain, [phrase] champion, consent, each, every (one), fellow, (foot-, husband-) man, (good-, great, mighty) man, he, high (degree), him (that is), husband, man(-kind), [phrase] none, one, people, person, [phrase] steward, what (man) soever, whoso(-ever), worthy. Compare H802 (אִשָּׁה).

H377 אִישׁ (ʼîysh, eesh): to be a man, i.e. act in amanly way. Origin: denominative from H376 (אִישׁ); KJV: show (one) self a man.

H378 אִישׁ־בֹּשֶׁת (ʼÎysh-Bôsheth, eesh-bo'-sheth): Ish-Bosheth, a son of King Saul. Origin: from H376 (אִישׁ) and H1322 (בֹּשֶׁת); man of shame; KJV: Ish-bosheth.

H379 אִישְׁהוֹד (ʼÎyshᵉhôwd, eesh-hode'): Ishod, an Israelite. Origin: from H376 (אִישׁ) and H1935 (הוֹד); man of renown; KJV: Ishod.

H380 אִישׁוֹן (ʼîyshôwn, ee-shone'): the little man of the eye; the pupil or ball; hence, the middle (of night). Origin: diminutive from H376 (אִישׁ); KJV: apple (of the eye), black, obscure.

H381 אִישׁ־חַיִל (ʼÎysh-Chayil, eesh-khah'-yil): Ishchail (or Ish-chai), an Israelite. Origin: from H376 (אִישׁ) and H2428 (חַיִל); man of might; by defective transcription (2 Samuel 23:20) אִישׁ־חַיxlit ʼÎsh-Chay corrected to ʼÎysh-Chay; as if from H376 (אִישׁ) and H2416 (חַי); living man; KJV: a valiant man.

H382 אִישׁ־טוֹב (ʼÎysh-Ṭôwb, eesh-tobe'): Ish-Tob, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H376 (אִישׁ) and H2897 (טוֹב); man of Tob; KJV: Ish-tob.

H383 אִיתַי (ʼîythay, ee-thah'ee): properly, entity; used only as aparticle of affirmation, there is. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3426 (יֵשׁ); KJV: art thou, can, do ye, have, it be, there is (are), [idiom] we will not.

H384 אִיתִיאֵל (ʼÎythîyʼêl, eeth-ee-ale'): Ithiel, the name of an Israelite, also of a symbolical person. Origin: perhaps from H837 (אֹשֶׁר) and H410 (אֵל); God has arrived; KJV: Ithiel.

H385 אִיתָמָר (ʼÎythâmâr, eeth-aw-mawr'): Ithamar, a son of Aaron. Origin: from H339 (אִי) and H8558 (תָּמָר); coast of the palm-tree; KJV: Ithamar.

H386 אֵיתָן (ʼêythân, ay-thawn'): permanence; hence (concrete) permanent; specifically a chieftain. Origin: or (shortened) אֵתָן ; from an unused root (meaning to continue); KJV: hard, mighty, rough, strength, strong.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H387 to H512
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H387 אֵיתָן (ʼÊythân, ay-thawn'): Ethan, the name of four Israelites. Origin: the same as H386 (אֵיתָן); permanent; KJV: Ethan.

H388 אֵיתָנִים (ʼÊythânîym, ay-thaw-neem'): Ethanim, the name of a month. Origin: plural of H386 (אֵיתָן); always with the article; the permanent brooks; KJV: Ethanim.

H389 אַךְ (ʼak, ak): a particle of affirmation, surely; hence (by limitation) only. Origin: akin to H403 (אָכֵן); KJV: also, in any wise, at least, but, certainly, even, howbeit, nevertheless, notwithstanding, only, save, surely, of a surety, truly, verily, [phrase] wherefore, yet (but).

H390 אַכַּד (ʼAkkad, ak-kad'): Accad, a place in Babylon. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to strengthen; a fortress; KJV: Accad.

H391 אַכְזָב (ʼakzâb, ak-zawb'): falsehood; by implication treachery. Origin: from H3576 (כָּזַב); KJV: liar, lie.

H392 אַכְזִיב (ʼAkzîyb, ak-zeeb'): Akzib, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H391 (אַכְזָב); deceitful (in the sense of a winter-torrent which fails in summer); KJV: Achzib.

H393 אַכְזָר (ʼakzâr, ak-zawr'): violent; by implication deadly; also (in a good sense) brave. Origin: from an unused root (apparently meaning to act harshly); KJV: cruel, fierce.

H394 אַכְזָרִי (ʼakzârîy, ak-zawr-ree'): terrible. Origin: from H393 (אַכְזָר); KJV: cruel (one).

H395 אַכְזְרִיּוּת (ʼakzᵉrîyûwth, ak-ze-ree-ooth'): fierceness. Origin: from H394 (אַכְזָרִי); KJV: cruel.

H396 אֲכִילָה (ʼăkîylâh, ak-ee-law'): something eatable, i.e. food. Origin: feminine from H398 (אָכַל); KJV: meat.

H397 אֲכִישׁ (ʼĂkîysh, aw-keesh'): Akish, a Philistine king. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Achish.

H398 אָכַל (ʼâkal, aw-kal'): to eat (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, burn up, consume, devour(-er, up), dine, eat(-er, up), feed (with), food, [idiom] freely, [idiom] in...wise(-deed, plenty), (lay) meat, [idiom] quite.

H399 אֲכַל (ʼăkal, ak-al'): {to eat (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H398 (אָכַל) KJV: [phrase] accuse, devour, eat.

H400 אֹכֶל (ʼôkel, o'-kel): food. Origin: from H398 (אָכַל); KJV: eating, food, meal(-time), meat, prey, victuals.

H401 אֻכָל (ʼUkâl, oo-kawl'): Ucal, a fancy name. Origin: or אֻכָּל; apparently from H398 (אָכַל); devoured; KJV: Ucal.

H402 אׇכְלָה (ʼoklâh, ok-law'): food. Origin: feminine of H401 (אֻכָל); KJV: consume, devour, eat, food, meat.

H403 אָכֵן (ʼâkên, aw-kane'): firmly; figuratively, surely; also (advers.) but. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן) (compare H3651 (כֵּן)); KJV: but, certainly, nevertheless, surely, truly, verily.

H404 אָכַף (ʼâkaph, aw-kaf'): to urge. Origin: a primitive root; apparently meaning to curve (as with a burden); KJV: crave.

H405 אֶכֶף (ʼekeph, eh'-kef): a load; by implication, a stroke (others dignity). Origin: from H404 (אָכַף); KJV: hand.

H406 אִכָּר (ʼikkâr, ik-kawr'): a farmer. Origin: from an unused root meaning to dig; KJV: husbandman, ploughman.

H407 אַכְשָׁף (ʼAkshâph, ak-shawf'): Acshaph, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3784 (כָּשַׁף); fascination; KJV: Achshaph.

H408 אַל (ʼal, al): not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing. Origin: a negative particle (akin to H3808 (לֹא)); KJV: nay, neither, [phrase] never, no, nor, not, nothing (worth), rather than.

H409 אַל (ʼal, al): {not (the qualified negation, used as a deprecative); once (Job 24:25) as a noun, nothing}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H408 (אַל) KJV: not.

H410 אֵל (ʼêl, ale): strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity). Origin: shortened from H352 (אַיִל); KJV: God (god), [idiom] goodly, [idiom] great, idol, might(-y one), power, strong. Compare names in '-el.'

H411 אֵל (ʼêl, ale): these or those. Origin: a demonstrative particle (but only in a plural sense) KJV: these, those. Compare H428 (אֵלֶּה).

H412 אֵל (ʼêl, ale): {these or those}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H411 (אֵל) KJV: these.

H413 אֵל (ʼêl, ale): near, with or among; often in general, to. Origin: (but only used in the shortened constructive form אֶל ); a primitive particle; properly, denoting motion towards, but occasionally used of a quiescent position, i.e. KJV: about, according to, after, against, among, as for, at, because(-fore, -side), both...and, by, concerning, for, from, [idiom] hath, in(-to), near, (out) of, over, through, to(-ward), under, unto, upon, whether, with(-in).

H414 אֵלָא (ʼÊlâʼ, ay-law'): Ela, an Israelite. Origin: a variation of H424 (אֵלָה)lemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; oak; KJV: Elah.

H415 אֵל אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (ʼÊl ʼĕlôhêy Yisrâʼêl, ale el-o-hay' yis-rawale'): El-Elohi-Jisrael, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H430 (אֱלֹהִים) and H3478 (יִשְׂרָאֵל); the mighty god if Jisrael; KJV: Elelohe-israel.

H416 אֵל בֵּית־אֵל (ʼÊl Bêyth-ʼÊl, ale bayth-ale'): El-Bethel, the title given to a consecrated spot by Jacob. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H1008 (בֵּית־אֵל); the God of Bethel; KJV: El-beth-el.

H417 אֶלְגָּבִישׁ (ʼelgâbîysh, el-gaw-beesh'): hail (as if a great pearl). Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H1378 (גָּבִישׁ); KJV: great hail(-stones).

H418 אַלְגּוּמִּים (ʼalgûwmmîym, al-goom-meem'): sticks of algum wood. Origin: by transposition for H484 (אַלְמֻגִּים); KJV: algum (trees).

H419 אֶלְדָּד (ʼEldâd, el-dad'): Eldad, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H1730 (דּוֹד); God has loved; KJV: Eldad.

H420 אֶלְדָּעָה (ʼEldâʻâh, el-daw-aw'): Eldaah, a son of Midian. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H3045 (יָדַע); God of knowledge; KJV: Eldaah.

H421 אָלָה (ʼâlâh, aw-law'): to bewail. Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H422 (אָלָה) through the idea of invocation); KJV: lament.

H422 אָלָה (ʼâlâh, aw-law'): properly, to adjure, i.e. (usually in a bad sense) imprecate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: adjure, curse, swear.

H423 אָלָה (ʼâlâh, aw-law'): an imprecation. Origin: from H422 (אָלָה); KJV: curse, cursing, execration, oath, swearing.

H424 אֵלָה (ʼêlâh, ay-law'): an oak or other strong tree. Origin: feminine of H352 (אַיִל); KJV: elm, oak, teil-tree.

H425 אֵלָה (ʼÊlâh, ay-law'): Elah, the name of an Edomite, of four Israelites, and also of a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H424 (אֵלָה)lemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה; KJV: Elah.

H426 אֱלָהּ (ʼĕlâhh, el-aw'): God. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H433 (אֱלוֹהַּ); KJV: God, god.

H427 אַלָּה (ʼallâh, al-law'): {an oak or other strong tree}. Origin: A variation of H424 (אֵלָה)lemma אִלָה first vowel, corrected to אֵלָה KJV: oak.

H428 אֵלֶּה (ʼêl-leh, ale'-leh): these or those. Origin: prolonged from H411 (אֵל); KJV: an-(the) other; one sort, so, some, such, them, these (same), they, this, those, thus, which, who(-m).

H429 אֵלֶּה (ʼêlleh, ale'-leh): {these or those}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H428 (אֵלֶּה) KJV: these.

H430 אֱלֹהִים (ʼĕlôhîym, el-o-heem'): gods in the ordinary sense; but specifically used (in the plural thus, especially with the article) of the supreme God; occasionally applied by way of deference to magistrates; and sometimes as a superlative. Origin: plural of H433 (אֱלוֹהַּ); KJV: angels, [idiom] exceeding, God (gods) (-dess, -ly), [idiom] (very) great, judges, [idiom] mighty.

H431 אֲלוּ (ʼălûw, al-oo'): lo!. Origin: (Aramaic) probably prolonged from H412 (אֵל); KJV: behold.

H432 אִלּוּ (ʼillûw, il-loo'): nay, i.e. (softened) if. Origin: probably from H408 (אַל); KJV: but if, yea though.

H433 אֱלוֹהַּ (ʼĕlôwahh, el-o'-ah): a deity or the Deity. Origin: rarely (shortened) אֱלֹהַּ; probably prolonged (emphatic) from H410 (אֵל); KJV: God, god. See H430 (אֱלֹהִים).

H434 אֱלוּל (ʼĕlûwl, el-ool'): good for nothing. Origin: for H457 (אֱלִיל); KJV: thing of nought.

H435 אֱלוּל (ʼĔlûwl, el-ool'): Elul, the sixth Jewish month. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Elul.

H436 אֵלוֹן (ʼêlôwn, ay-lone'): an oak or other strong tree. Origin: prolonged from H352 (אַיִל); KJV: plain. See also H356 (אֵילוֹן).

H437 אַלּוֹן (ʼallôwn, al-lone'): {an oak or other strong tree}. Origin: a variation of H436 (אֵלוֹן) KJV: oak.

H438 אַלּוֹן (ʼAllôwn, al-lone'): Allon, an Israelite, also a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H437 (אַלּוֹן); KJV: Allon.

H439 אַלּוֹן בָּכוּת (ʼAllôwn Bâkûwth, al-lone' baw-kooth'): Allon-Bakuth, a monumental tree. Origin: from H437 (אַלּוֹן) and a variation of H1068 (בְּכִית); oak of weeping; KJV: Allon-bachuth.

H440 אֵלוֹנִי (ʼÊlôwnîy, ay-lo-nee'): an Elonite or descendant (collectively) of Elon. Origin: or rather (shortened) אֵלֹנִי; patron from H438 (אַלּוֹן); KJV: Elonites.

H441 אַלּוּף (ʼallûwph, al-loof'): familiar; a friend, also gentle; hence, a bullock (as being tame; applied, although masculine, to a cow); and so, a chieftain (as notable, like neat cattle). Origin: or (shortened) אַלֻּף; from H502 (אָלַף); KJV: captain, duke, (chief) friend, governor, guide, ox.

H442 אָלוּשׁ (ʼÂlûwsh, aw-loosh'): Alush, a place in the Desert. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Alush.

H443 אֶלְזָבָד (ʼElzâbâd, el-zaw-bawd'): Elzabad, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H2064 (זָבַד); God has bestowed; KJV: Elzabad.

H444 אָלַח (ʼâlach, aw-lakh'): to muddle, i.e. (figuratively and intransitive) to turn (morally) corrupt. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: become filthy.

H445 אֶלְחָנָן (ʼElchânân, el-khaw-nawn'): Elchanan, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H2603 (חָנַן); God (is) gracious; KJV: Elkanan.

H446 אֱלִיאָב (ʼĔlîyʼâb, el-ee-awb'): Eliab, the name of six Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H1 (אָב); God of (his) father; KJV: Eliab.

H447 אֱלִיאֵל (ʼĔlîyʼêl, el-ee-ale'): Eliel, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) repeated; God of (his) God; KJV: Eliel.

H448 אֱלִיאָתָה (ʼĔlîyʼâthâh, el-ee-aw-thaw'): Eliathah, an Israelite. Origin: or (contraction) אֱלִיָּתָה; from H410 (אֵל) and H225 (אוּת); God of (his) consent; KJV: Eliathah.

H449 אֱלִידָד (ʼĔlîydâd, el-ee-dawd'): Elidad, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H419 (אֶלְדָּד); God of (his) love; KJV: Elidad.

H450 אֶלְיָדָע (ʼElyâdâʻ, el-yaw-daw'): Eljada, the name of two Israelites and of an Aramaean leader. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H3045 (יָדַע); God (is) knowing; KJV: Eliada.

H451 אַלְיָה (ʼalyâh, al-yaw'): the stout part, i.e. the fat tail of the Oriental sheep. Origin: from H422 (אָלָה) (in the original sense of strength); KJV: rump.

H452 אֵלִיָּה (ʼÊlîyâh, ay-lee-yaw'): Elijah, the name of the famous prophet and of two other Israelites. Origin: or prolonged אֵלִיָּהוּ; from H410 (אֵל) and H3050 (יָהּ); God of Jehovah; KJV: Elijah, Eliah.

H453 אֱלִיהוּ (ʼĔlîyhûw, el-ee-hoo'): Elihu, the name of one of Job's friends, and of three Israelites. Origin: or (fully) אֱלִיהוּא; from H410 (אֵל) and H1931 (הוּא); God of him; KJV: Elihu.

H454 אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי (ʼElyᵉhôwʻêynay, el-ye-ho-ay-nah'ee): Eljehoenai or Eljoenai, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: or (shortened) אֶלְיוֹעֵינַי; from H413 (אֵל) and H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5869 (עַיִן); towards Jehovah (are) my eyes; KJV: Elihoenai, Elionai.

H455 אֶלְיַחְבָּא (ʼElyachbâʼ, el-yakh-baw'): Eljachba, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H2244 (חָבָא); God will hide; KJV: Eliahbah.

H456 אֱלִיחֹרֶף (ʼĔlîychôreph, el-ee-kho'-ref): Elichoreph, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H2779 (חֹרֶף); God of autumn; KJV: Elihoreph.

H457 אֱלִיל (ʼĕlîyl, el-eel'): good for nothing, by anal. vain or vanity; specifically an idol. Origin: apparently from H408 (אַל); KJV: idol, no value, thing of nought.

H458 אֱלִימֶלֶךְ (ʼĔlîymelek, el-ee-meh'-lek): Elimelek, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); God of (the) king; KJV: Elimelech.

H459 אִלֵּין (ʼillêyn, il-lane'): these. Origin: (Aramaic) or shorter אִלֵּן; prolonged from H412 (אֵל); KJV: the, these.

H460 אֶלְיָסָף (ʼElyâçâph, el-yaw-sawf'): Eljasaph, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H3254 (יָסַף); God (is) gatherer; KJV: Eliasaph.

H461 אֱלִיעֶזֶר (ʼĔlîyʻezer, el-ee-eh'-zer): Eliezer, the name of a Damascene and of ten Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); God of help; KJV: Eliezer.

H462 אֱלִיעֵינַי (ʼĔlîyʻêynay, el-ee-ay-nah'ee): Elienai, an Israelite. Origin: probably contracted for H454 (אֶלְיְהוֹעֵינַי); KJV: Elienai.

H463 אֱלִיעָם (ʼĔlîyʻâm, el-ee-awm'): Eliam, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5971 (עַם); God of (the) people; KJV: Eliam.

H464 אֱלִיפַז (ʼĔlîyphaz, el-ee-faz'): Eliphaz, the name of one of Job's friends, and of a son of Esau. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6337 (פָּז); God of gold; KJV: Eliphaz.

H465 אֱלִיפָל (ʼĔlîyphâl, el-ee-fawl'): Eliphal, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6419 (פָּלַל); God of judgment; KJV: Eliphal.

H466 אֱלִיפְלֵהוּ (ʼĔlîyphᵉlêhûw, el-ee-fe-lay'-hoo): Eliphelehu, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6395 (פָּלָה); God of his distinction; KJV: Elipheleh.

H467 אֱלִיפֶלֶט (ʼĔlîypheleṭ, el-ee-feh'-let): Eliphelet or Elpelet, the name of six Israelites. Origin: or (shortened) אֱלְפֶּלֶט; from H410 (אֵל) and H6405 (פַּלֵּט); God of deliverance; KJV: Eliphalet, Eliphelet, Elpalet.

H468 אֱלִיצוּר (ʼĔlîytsûwr, el-ee-tsoor'): Elitsur, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6697 (צוּר); God of (the) rock; KJV: Elizur.

H469 אֱלִיצָפָן (ʼĔlîytsâphân, el-ee-tsaw-fawn'): Elitsaphan or Eltsaphan, an Israelite. Origin: or (shortened) אֶלְצָפָן; from H410 (אֵל) and H6845 (צָפַן); God of treasure; KJV: Elizaphan, Elzaphan.

H470 אֱלִיקָא (ʼĔlîyqâʼ, el-ee-kaw'): Elika, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6958 (קוֹא); God of rejection; KJV: Elika.

H471 אֶלְיָקִים (ʼElyâqîym, el-yaw-keem'): Eljakim, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6965 (קוּם); God of raising; KJV: Eliakim.

H472 אֱלִישֶׁבַע (ʼĔlîyshebaʻ, el-ee-sheh'-bah): Elisheba, the wife of Aaron. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H7651 (שֶׁבַע) (in the sense of H7650 (שָׁבַע)); God of (the) oath; KJV: Elisheba.

H473 אֱלִישָׁה (ʼĔlîyshâh, el-ee-shaw'): Elishah, a son of Javan. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Elishah.

H474 אֱלִישׁוּעַ (ʼĔlîyshûwaʻ, el-ee-shoo'-ah): Elishua, the son of King David. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H7769 (שׁוּעַ); God of supplication (or of riches); KJV: Elishua.

H475 אֶלְיָשִׁיב (ʼElyâshîyb, el-yaw-sheeb'): Eljashib, the name of six Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H7725 (שׁוּב); God will restore; KJV: Eliashib.

H476 אֱלִישָׁמָע (ʼĔlîyshâmâʻ, el-ee-shaw-maw'): Elishama, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H8085 (שָׁמַע); God of hearing; KJV: Elishama.

H477 אֱלִישָׁע (ʼĔlîyshâʻ, el-ee-shaw'): Elisha, the famous prophet. Origin: contracted for H474 (אֱלִישׁוּעַ).; KJV: Elisha.

H478 אֱלִישָׁפָט (ʼĔlîyshâphâṭ, el-ee-shaw-fawt'): Elishaphat, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H8199 (שָׁפַט); God of judgment; KJV: Elishaphat.

H479 אִלֵּךְ (ʼillêk, il-lake'): these. Origin: (Aramaic) prolonged from H412 (אֵל); KJV: these, those.

H480 אַלְלַי (ʼalᵉlay, al-le-lah'ee): alas!. Origin: by reduplication from H421 (אָלָה); KJV: woe.

H481 אָלַם (ʼâlam, aw-lam'): to tie fast; hence (of the mouth) to be tongue-tied. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind, be dumb, put to silence.

H482 אֵלֶם (ʼêlem, ay'-lem): silence (i.e. mute justice). Origin: from H481 (אָלַם); KJV: congregation. Compare H3128 (יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחֹקִים).

H483 אִלֵּם (ʼillêm, il-lame'): speechless. Origin: from H481 (אָלַם); KJV: dumb (man).

H484 אַלְמֻגִּים (ʼalmuggîym, al-moog-gheem'): almug (i.e. probably sandle-wood) sticks. Origin: probably of foreign derivation (used thus only in the plural); KJV: almug trees. Compare H418 (אַלְגּוּמִּים).

H485 אֲלֻמָּה (ʼălummâh, al-oom-maw'): something bound; a sheaf. Origin: or (masculine) אָלֻם; passive participle of H481 (אָלַם); KJV: sheaf.

H486 אַלְמוֹדָד (ʼAlmôwdâd, al-mo-dawd'): Almodad, a son of Joktan. Origin: probably of foreign derivation KJV: Almodad.

H487 אַלַּמֶּלֶךְ (ʼAllammelek, al-lam-meh'-lek): Allammelek, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H427 (אַלָּה) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); oak of (the) king; KJV: Alammelech.

H488 אַלְמָן (ʼalmân, al-mawn'): discarded (as a divorced person). Origin: prolonged from H481 (אָלַם) in the sense of bereavement; KJV: forsaken.

H489 אַלְמֹן (ʼalmôn, al-mone'): bereavement. Origin: from H481 (אָלַם) as in H488 (אַלְמָן); KJV: widowhood.

H490 אַלְמָנָה (ʼalmânâh, al-maw-naw'): a widow; also a desolate place. Origin: feminine of H488 (אַלְמָן); KJV: desolate house (palace), widow.

H491 אַלְמָנוּת (ʼalmânûwth, al-maw-nooth'): concrete, a widow; abstract, widowhood. Origin: feminine of H488 (אַלְמָן); KJV: widow, widowhood.

H492 אַלְמֹנִי (ʼalmônîy, al-mo-nee'): some one (i.e. so and so, without giving the name of the person or place). Origin: from H489 (אַלְמֹן) in the sense of concealment; KJV: one, and such.

H493 אֶלְנַעַם (ʼElnaʻam, el-nah'-am): Elnaam, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5276 (נָעֵם); God (is his) delight; KJV: Elnaam.

H494 אֶלְנָתָן (ʼElnâthân, el-naw-thawn'): Elnathan, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5414 (נָתַן); God (is the) giver; KJV: Elnathan.

H495 אֶלָּסָר (ʼEllâçâr, el-law-sawr'): Ellasar, an early country of Asia. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Ellasar.

H496 אֶלְעָד (ʼElʻâd, el-awd'): Elad, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5749 (עוּד); God has testified; KJV: Elead.

H497 אֶלְעָדָה (ʼElʻâdâh, el-aw-daw'): Eladah, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5710 (עָדָה); God has decked; KJV: Eladah.

H498 אֶלְעוּזַי (ʼElʻûwzay, el-oo-zah'ee): Eluzai, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5756 (עוּז) (in the sense of H5797 (עֹז)); God (is) defensive; KJV: Eluzai.

H499 אֶלְעָזָר (ʼElʻâzâr, el-aw-zawr'): Elazar, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H5826 (עָזַר); God (is) helper; KJV: Eleazar.

H500 אֶלְעָלֵא (ʼElʻâlêʼ, el-aw-lay'): Elale or Elaleh, a place east of the Jordan. Origin: or (more properly) אֶלְעָלֵה; from H410 (אֵל) and H5927 (עָלָה); God (is) going up; KJV: Elealeh.

H501 אֶלְעָשָׂה (ʼElʻâsâh, el-aw-saw'): Elasah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6213 (עָשָׂה); God has made; KJV: Elasah, Eleasah.

H502 אָלַף (ʼâlaph, aw-lof'): hence, to learn (and causatively to teach). Origin: a primitive root, to associate with; KJV: learn, teach, utter.

H503 אָלַף (ʼâlaph, aw-laf'): causative, to make athousandfold. Origin: denominative from H505 (אֶלֶף); KJV: bring forth thousands.

H504 אֶלֶף (ʼeleph, eh'-lef): a family; also (from the sense of yoking or taming) an ox or cow. Origin: from H502 (אָלַף); KJV: family, kine, oxen.

H505 אֶלֶף (ʼeleph, eh'-lef): hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand. Origin: prop, the same as H504 (אֶלֶף); KJV: thousand.

H506 אֲלַף (ʼălaph, al-af'): {hence (the ox's head being the first letter of the alphabet, and this eventually used as a numeral) a thousand}. Origin: (Aramaic) or אֶלֶף; (Aramaic), corresponding to H505 (אֶלֶף) KJV: thousand.

H507 אֶלֶף (ʼEleph, eh'-lef): Eleph, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H505 (אֶלֶף); KJV: Eleph.

H508 אֶלְפַּעַל (ʼElpaʻal, el-pah'-al): Elpaal, an Israelite. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H6466 (פָּעַל); God (is) act; KJV: Elpaal.

H509 אָלַץ (ʼâlats, aw-lats'): to press. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: urge.

H510 אַלְקוּם (ʼalqûwm, al-koom'): a non-rising (i.e. resistlessness). Origin: probably from H408 (אַל) and H6965 (קוּם); KJV: no rising up.

H511 אֶלְקָנָה (ʼElqânâh, el-kaw-naw'): Elkanah, the name of several Israelites. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H7069 (קָנָה); God has obtained; KJV: Elkanah.

H512 אֶלְקֹשִׁי (ʼElqôshîy, el-ko-shee'): an Elkoshite or native of Elkosh. Origin: patrial from a name of uncertain derivation; KJV: Elkoshite.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H513 to H639
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H513 אֶלְתּוֹלַד (ʼEltôwlad, el-to-lad'): Eltolad, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H410 (אֵל) and a masculine form of H8435 (תּוֹלְדָה) (compare H8434 (תּוֹלָד)); God (is) generator; KJV: Eltolad.

H514 אֶלְתְּקֵא (ʼEltᵉqêʼ, el-te-kay'): Eltekeh or Elteke, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (more properly) אֶלְתְּקֵה; of uncertain derivation; KJV: Eltekeh.

H515 אֶלְתְּקֹן (ʼEltᵉqôn, el-te-kone'): Eltekon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H410 (אֵל) and H8626 (תָּקַן); God (is) straight; KJV: Eltekon.

H516 אַל תַּשְׁחֵת (ʼAl tashchêth, al tash-kayth'): 'Thou must not destroy'; probably the opening words to a popular song. Origin: from H408 (אַל) and H7843 (שָׁחַת); KJV: Al-taschith.

H517 אֵם (ʼêm, ame): a mother (as the bond of the family); in a wide sense (both literally and figuratively (like father)). Origin: a primitive word; KJV: dam, mother, [idiom] parting.

H518 אִם (ʼim, eem): used very widely as demonstrative, lo!; interrogative, whether?; or conditional, if, although; also Oh that!, when; hence, as a negative, not. Origin: a primitive particle; KJV: (and, can-, doubtless, if, that) (not), [phrase] but, either, [phrase] except, [phrase] more(-over if, than), neither, nevertheless, nor, oh that, or, [phrase] save (only, -ing), seeing, since, sith, [phrase] surely (no more, none, not), though, [phrase] of a truth, [phrase] unless, [phrase] verily, when, whereas, whether, while, [phrase] yet.

H519 אָמָה (ʼâmâh, aw-maw'): a maidservant or female slave. Origin: apparently a primitive word; KJV: (hand-) bondmaid(-woman), maid(-servant).

H520 אַמָּה (ʼammâh, am-maw'): properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance). Origin: prolonged from H517 (אֵם); KJV: cubit, [phrase] hundred (by exchange for H3967 (מֵאָה)), measure, post.

H521 אַמָּה (ʼammâh, am-maw'): {properly, a mother (i.e. unit of measure, or the fore-arm (below the elbow), i.e. a cubit; also a door-base (as a bond of the entrance)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H520 (אַמָּה) KJV: cubit.

H522 אַמָּה (ʼAmmâh, am-maw'): Ammah, a hill in Palestine. Origin: the same as H520 (אַמָּה); KJV: Ammah.

H523 אֻמַּה (ʼummah, oom-maw'): a collection, i.e. community of persons. Origin: from the same as H517 (אֵם); KJV: nation, people.

H524 אֻמָּה (ʼummâh, oom-maw'): {a collection, i.e. community of persons}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H523 (אֻמַּה) KJV: nation.

H525 אָמוֹן (ʼâmôwn, aw-mone'): skilled, i.e. an architect. Origin: from H539 (אָמַן), probably in the sense of training; like H542 (אָמָן) KJV: one brought up.

H526 אָמוֹן (ʼÂmôwn, aw-mone'): Amon, the name of three Israelites. Origin: the same as H525 (אָמוֹן); KJV: Amon.

H527 אָמוֹן (ʼâmôwn, aw-mone'): a throng of people. Origin: a variation for H1995 (הָמוֹן); KJV: multitude.

H528 אָמוֹן (ʼÂmôwn, aw-mone'): Amon (i.e. Ammon or Amn), a deity of Egypt. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; used only as an adjunct of H4996 (נֹא) KJV: multitude, populous.

H529 אֵמוּן (ʼêmûwn, ay-moon'): established, i.e. (figuratively) trusty; also (abstractly) trustworthiness. Origin: from H539 (אָמַן); KJV: faith(-ful), truth.

H530 אֱמוּנָה (ʼĕmûwnâh, em-oo-naw'): literally firmness; figuratively security; morally fidelity. Origin: or (shortened) אֱמֻנָה; feminine of H529 (אֵמוּן); KJV: faith(-ful, -ly, -ness, (man)), set office, stability, steady, truly, truth, verily.

H531 אָמוֹץ (ʼÂmôwts, aw-mohts'): Amots, an Israelite. Origin: from H553 (אָמַץ); strong; KJV: Amoz.

H532 אָמִי (ʼÂmîy, aw-mee'): Ami, an Israelite. Origin: an abbreviated form for H526 (אָמוֹן); KJV: Ami.

H533 אַמִּיץ (ʼammîyts, am-meets'): strong or (abstractly) strength. Origin: or (shortened) אַמִּץ; from H553 (אָמַץ); KJV: courageous, mighty, strong (one).

H534 אָמִיר (ʼâmîyr, aw-meer'): a summit (of a tree or mountain. Origin: apparently from H559 (אָמַר) (in the sense of self-exaltation); KJV: bough, branch.

H535 אָמַל (ʼâmal, aw-mal'): to droop; by implication to be sick, to mourn. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: languish, be weak, wax feeble.

H536 אֻמְלַל (ʼumlal, oom-lal'): sick. Origin: from H535 (אָמַל); KJV: weak.

H537 אֲמֵלָל (ʼămêlâl, am-ay-lawl'): languid. Origin: from H535 (אָמַל); KJV: feeble.

H538 אֲמָם (ʼĂmâm, am-awm'): Amam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H517 (אֵם); gathering-spot; KJV: Amam.

H539 אָמַן (ʼâman, aw-man'): properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain. Origin: a primitive root; (Isaiah 30:21; interchangeable with H541 (אָמַן), to go to the right hand) KJV: hence, assurance, believe, bring up, establish, [phrase] fail, be faithful (of long continuance, stedfast, sure, surely, trusty, verified), nurse, (-ing father), (put), trust, turn to the right.

H540 אֲמַן (ʼăman, am-an'): {properly, to build up or support; to foster as a parent or nurse; figuratively to render (or be) firm or faithful, to trust or believe, to be permanent or quiet; morally to be true or certain}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H539 (אָמַן) KJV: believe, faithful, sure.

H541 אָמַן (ʼâman, aw-man'): to take the right hand road. Origin: denominative from H3225 (יָמִין); KJV: turn to the right. See H539 (אָמַן).

H542 אָמָן (ʼâmân, aw-mawn'): an expert. Origin: from H539 (אָמַן) (in the sense of training); KJV: cunning workman.

H543 אָמֵן (ʼâmên, aw-mane'): sure; abstract, faithfulness; adverb, truly. Origin: from H539 (אָמַן); KJV: Amen, so be it, truth.

H544 אֹמֶן (ʼômen, oh-men'): verity. Origin: from H539 (אָמַן); KJV: truth.

H545 אׇמְנָה (ʼomnâh, om-naw'): tutelage. Origin: feminine of H544 (אֹמֶן) (in the specific sense of training); KJV: brought up.

H546 אׇמְנָה (ʼomnâh, om-naw'): adverb, surely. Origin: feminine form of H544 (אֹמֶן) (in its usual sense); KJV: indeed.

H547 אֹמְנָה (ʼômᵉnâh, om-me-naw'): a column. Origin: feminine active participle of H544 (אֹמֶן) (in the original sense of supporting); KJV: pillar.

H548 אֲמָנָה (ʼămânâh, am-aw-naw'): something fixed, i.e. a covenant. an allowance. Origin: feminine of H543 (אָמֵן); KJV: certain portion, sure.

H549 אֲמָנָה (ʼĂmânâh, am-aw-naw'): Amanah, a mountain near Damascus. Origin: the same as H548 (אֲמָנָה); KJV: Amana.

H550 אַמְנוֹן (ʼAmnôwn, am-nohn'): Amnon (or Aminon), a son of David. Origin: or אֲמִינוֹן; from H539 (אָמַן); faithful; KJV: Amnon.

H551 אׇמְנָם (ʼomnâm, om-nawm'): verily. Origin: adverb from H544 (אֹמֶן); KJV: indeed, no doubt, surely, (it is, of a) true(-ly, -th).

H552 אֻמְנָם (ʼumnâm, oom-nawm'): {verily}. Origin: an orthographical variation of H551 (אׇמְנָם) KJV: in (very) deed; of a surety.

H553 אָמַץ (ʼâmats, aw-mats'): to be alert, physically (on foot) or mentally (in courage). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: confirm, be courageous (of good courage, stedfastly minded, strong, stronger), establish, fortify, harden, increase, prevail, strengthen (self), make strong (obstinate, speed).

H554 אָמֹץ (ʼâmôts, aw-mohts'): of a strong color, i.e. red (others fleet). Origin: probably from H553 (אָמַץ); KJV: bay.

H555 אֹמֶץ (ʼômets, o'-mets): strength. Origin: from H553 (אָמַץ); KJV: stronger.

H556 אַמְצָה (ʼamtsâh, am-tsaw'): force. Origin: from H553 (אָמַץ); KJV: strength.

H557 אַמְצִי (ʼAmtsîy, am-tsee'): Amtsi, an Israelite. Origin: from H553 (אָמַץ); strong; KJV: Amzi.

H558 אֲמַצְיָה (ʼĂmatsyâh, am-ats-yaw'): Amatsjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or אֲמַצְיָהוּ; from H553 (אָמַץ) and H3050 (יָהּ); strength of Jah; KJV: Amaziah.

H559 אָמַר (ʼâmar, aw-mar'): to say (used with great latitude). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: answer, appoint, avouch, bid, boast self, call, certify, challenge, charge, [phrase] (at the, give) command(-ment), commune, consider, declare, demand, [idiom] desire, determine, [idiom] expressly, [idiom] indeed, [idiom] intend, name, [idiom] plainly, promise, publish, report, require, say, speak (against, of), [idiom] still, [idiom] suppose, talk, tell, term, [idiom] that is, [idiom] think, use (speech), utter, [idiom] verily, [idiom] yet.

H560 אֲמַר (ʼămar, am-ar'): {to say (used with great latitude)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H559 (אָמַר) KJV: command, declare, say, speak, tell.

H561 אֵמֶר (ʼêmer, ay'-mer): something said. Origin: from H559 (אָמַר); KJV: answer, [idiom] appointed unto him, saying, speech, word.

H562 אֹמֶר (ʼômer, o'-mer): {something said}. Origin: the same as H561 (אֵמֶר) KJV: promise, speech, thing, word.

H563 אִמַּר (ʼimmar, im-mar'): a lamb. Origin: (Aramaic) perhaps from H560 (אֲמַר) (in the sense of bringing forth); KJV: lamb.

H564 אִמֵּר (ʼImmêr, im-mare'): Immer, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H559 (אָמַר); talkative; KJV: Immer.

H565 אִמְרָה (ʼimrâh, im-raw'): {something said}. Origin: or אֶמְרָה; feminine of H561 (אֵמֶר), and meaning the same KJV: commandment, speech, word.

H566 אִמְרִי (ʼImrîy, im-ree'): Imri, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H564 (אִמֵּר); KJV: Imri.

H567 אֱמֹרִי (ʼĔmôrîy, em-o-ree'): an Emorite, one of the Canaanitish tribes. Origin: probably a patronymic from an unused name derived from H559 (אָמַר) in the sense of publicity, i.e. prominence; thus, a mountaineer; KJV: Amorite.

H568 אֲמַרְיָה (ʼĂmaryâh, am-ar-yaw'): Amarjah, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: or prolonged אֲמַרְיָהוּ; from H559 (אָמַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has said (i.e. promised); KJV: Amariah.

H569 אַמְרָפֶל (ʼAmrâphel, am-raw-fel'): Amraphel, a king of Shinar. Origin: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; KJV: Amraphel.

H570 אֶמֶשׁ (ʼemesh, eh'-mesh): yesterday or last night. Origin: time past, i.e. KJV: former time, yesterday(-night)

H571 אֶמֶת (ʼemeth, eh'-meth): stability; (figuratively) certainty, truth, trustworthiness. Origin: contracted from H539 (אָמַן); KJV: assured(-ly), establishment, faithful, right, sure, true (-ly, -th), verity.

H572 אַמְתַּחַת (ʼamtachath, am-takh'-ath): properly, something expansive, i.e. a bag. Origin: from H4969 (מָתַח); KJV: sack.

H573 אֲמִתַּי (ʼĂmittay, am-it-tah'ee): Amittai, an Israelite. Origin: from H571 (אֶמֶת); veracious; KJV: Amittai.

H574 אֵמְתָּנִי (ʼêmᵉtânîy, em-taw-nee'): well-loined (i.e. burly) or mighty. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of H4975 (מֹתֶן); KJV: terrible.

H575 אָן (ʼân, awn): where?; hence, whither?, when?; also hither and thither. Origin: or אָנָה; contracted from H370 (אַיִן); KJV: [phrase] any (no) whither, now, where, whither(-soever).

H576 אֲנָא (ʼănâʼ, an-aw'): I. Origin: (Aramaic) or אֲנָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H589 (אֲנִי)lemma אֲנַי second vowel, corrected to אֲנִי; KJV: I, as for me.

H577 אָנָּא (ʼânnâʼ, awn-naw'): oh now!. Origin: or אָנָּה; apparent contracted from H160 (אַהֲבָה) and H4994 (נָא); KJV: I (me) beseech (pray) thee, O.

H578 אָנָה (ʼânâh, aw-naw'): to groan. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lament, mourn.

H579 אָנָה (ʼânâh, aw-naw'): to approach; hence, to meet in various senses. Origin: a primitive root (perhaps rather identical with H578 (אָנָה) through the idea of contraction in anguish); KJV: befall, deliver, happen, seek a quarrel.

H580 אֲנוּ (ʼănûw, an-oo'): we. Origin: contracted for H587 (אֲנַחְנוּ); KJV: we.

H581 אִנּוּן (ʼinnûwn, in-noon'): they. Origin: (Aramaic) or (feminine) אִנִּיןlemma אֵנִּין first vowel, corrected to אִנִּין; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1992 (הֵם); KJV: [idiom] are, them, these.

H582 אֱנוֹשׁ (ʼĕnôwsh, en-oshe'): a man in general (singly or collectively). Origin: from H605 (אָנַשׁ); properly, a mortal (and thus differing from the more dignified H120 (אָדָם)); hence, KJV: another, [idiom] (blood-) thirsty, certain, chap(-man); divers, fellow, [idiom] in the flower of their age, husband, (certain, mortal) man, people, person, servant, some ([idiom] of them), [phrase] stranger, those, [phrase] their trade. It is often unexpressed in the English versions, especially when used in apposition with another word. Compare H376 (אִישׁ).

H583 אֱנוֹשׁ (ʼĔnôwsh, en-ohsh'): Enosh, a son of Seth. Origin: the same as H582 (אֱנוֹשׁ); KJV: Enos.

H584 אָנַח (ʼânach, aw-nakh'): to sigh. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: groan, mourn, sigh.

H585 אֲנָחָה (ʼănâchâh, an-aw-khaw'): sighing. Origin: from H585 (אֲנָחָה); KJV: groaning, mourn, sigh.

H586 אֲנַחְנָא (ʼănachnâʼ, an-akh'-naw): we. Origin: (Aramaic) or אֲנַחְנָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H587 (אֲנַחְנוּ); KJV: we.

H587 אֲנַחְנוּ (ʼănachnûw, an-akh'-noo): we. Origin: apparently from H595 (אָנֹכִי); KJV: ourselves, us, we.

H588 אֲנָחֲרָת (ʼĂnâchărâth, an-aw-kha-rawth'): Anacharath, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from the same root as H5170 (נַחַר); a gorge or narrow pass; KJV: Anaharath.

H589 אֲנִי (ʼănîy, an-ee'): I. Origin: contracted from H595 (אָנֹכִי); KJV: I, (as for) me, mine, myself, we, [idiom] which, [idiom] who.

H590 אֳנִי (ʼŏnîy, on-ee'): -a ship or (collectively) a fleet. Origin: probably from H579 (אָנָה) (in the sense of conveyance); KJV: galley, navy (of ships).

H591 אֳנִיָּה (ʼŏnîyâh, on-ee-yaw'): a ship. Origin: feminine of H590 (אֳנִי); KJV: ship(-men).

H592 אֲנִיָּה (ʼănîyâh, an-ee-yaw'): groaning. Origin: from H578 (אָנָה); KJV: lamentation, sorrow.

H593 אֲנִיעָם (ʼĂnîyʻâm, an-ee-awm'): Aniam, an Israelite. Origin: from H578 (אָנָה) and H5971 (עַם); groaning of (the) people; KJV: Aniam.

H594 אֲנָךְ (ʼănâk, an-awk'): according to most a plumb-line, and to others a hook. Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to be narrow; KJV: plumb-line

H595 אָנֹכִי (ʼânôkîy, aw-no-kee'): I. Origin: sometimes, ; a primitive pronoun; KJV: I, me, [idiom] which.

H596 אָנַן (ʼânan, aw-nan'): to mourn, i.e. complain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: complain.

H597 אָנַס (ʼânaç, aw-nas'): to insist. KJV: compel.

H598 אֲנַס (ʼănaç, an-as'): figuratively, to distress. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H597 (אָנַס); KJV: trouble.

H599 אָנַף (ʼânaph, aw-naf'): to breathe hard, i.e. be enraged. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be angry (displeased).

H600 אֲנַף (ʼănaph, an-af'): the face. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H639 (אַף) (only in the plural as a singular); KJV: face, visage.

H601 אֲנָפָה (ʼănâphâh, an-aw-faw'): an unclean bird, perhaps the parrot (from its irascibility). Origin: from H599 (אָנַף); KJV: heron.

H602 אָנַק (ʼânaq, aw-nak'): to shriek. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cry, groan.

H603 אֲנָקָה (ʼănâqâh, an-aw-kaw'): shrieking. Origin: from H602 (אָנַק); KJV: crying out, groaning, sighing.

H604 אֲנָקָה (ʼănâqâh, an-aw-kaw'): some kind of lizard, probably the gecko (from its wail). Origin: the same as H603 (אֲנָקָה); KJV: ferret.

H605 אָנַשׁ (ʼânash, aw-nash'): to be frail, feeble, or (figuratively) melancholy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: desperate(-ly wicked), incurable, sick, woeful.

H606 אֱנָשׁ (ʼĕnâsh, en-awsh'): a man. Origin: (Aramaic) or אֱנַשׁ; (Aramaic), corresponding to H582 (אֱנוֹשׁ); KJV: man, [phrase] whosoever.

H607 אַנְתָּה (ʼantâh, an-taw'): thou. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H859 (אַתָּה); KJV: as for thee, thou.

H608 אַנְתּוּן (ʼantûwn, an-toon'): ye. Origin: (Aramaic) plural of H607 (אַנְתָּה); KJV: ye.

H609 אָסָא (ʼÂçâʼ, aw-saw'): Asa, the name of a king and of a Levite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Asa.

H610 אָסוּךְ (ʼâçûwk, aw-sook'): anointed, i.e. an oil-flask. Origin: from H5480 (סוּךְ); KJV: pot.

H611 אָסוֹן (ʼâçôwn, aws-sone'): hurt. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: mischief.

H612 אֵסוּר (ʼêçûwr, ay-soor'): a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner). Origin: from H631 (אָסַר); KJV: band, [phrase] prison.

H613 אֱסוּר (ʼĕçûwr, es-oor'): {a bond (especially manacles of a prisoner)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H612 (אֵסוּר) KJV: band, imprisonment.

H614 אָסִיף (ʼâçîyph, aw-seef'): gathered, i.e. (abstractly) a gathering in of crops. Origin: or אָסִף; from H622 (אָסַף); KJV: ingathering.

H615 אָסִיר (ʼâçîyr, aw-sere'): bound, i.e. a captive. Origin: from H631 (אָסַר); KJV: (those which are) bound, prisoner.

H616 אַסִּיר (ʼaççîyr, as-sere'): {bound, i.e. a captive}. Origin: for H615 (אָסִיר) KJV: prisoner.

H617 אַסִּיר (ʼAççîyr, as-sere'): Assir, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H616 (אַסִּיר); prisoner; KJV: Assir.

H618 אָסָם (ʼâçâm, aw-sawm'): a storehouse (only in the plural). Origin: from an unused root meaning to heap together; KJV: barn, storehouse.

H619 אַסְנָה (ʼAçnâh, as-naw'): Asnah, one of the Nethinim. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Asnah.

H620 אׇסְנַפַּר (ʼOçnappar, os-nap-par'): Osnappar, an Assyrian king. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Asnapper.

H621 אָסְנַת (ʼÂçᵉnath, aw-se-nath'): Asenath, the wife of Joseph. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Asenath.

H622 אָסַף (ʼâçaph, aw-saf'): to gather for any purpose; hence, to receive, take away, i.e. remove (destroy, leave behind, put up, restore, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: assemble, bring, consume, destroy, felch, gather (in, together, up again), [idiom] generally, get (him), lose, put all together, receive, recover (another from leprosy), (be) rereward, [idiom] surely, take (away, into, up), [idiom] utterly, withdraw.

H623 אָסָף (ʼÂçâph, aw-sawf'): Asaph, the name of three Israelites, and of the family of the first. Origin: from H622 (אָסַף); collector; KJV: Asaph.

H624 אָסֻף (ʼâçuph, aw-soof'): collected (only in the plural), i.e. a collection of offerings). Origin: passive participle of H622 (אָסַף); KJV: threshold, Asuppim.

H625 אֹסֶף (ʼôçeph, o'-sef): a collection (of fruits). Origin: from H622 (אָסַף); KJV: gathering.

H626 אֲסֵפָה (ʼăçêphâh, as-ay-faw'): a collection of people (only adverbial). Origin: from H622 (אָסַף); KJV: [idiom] together.

H627 אֲסֻפָּה (ʼăçuppâh, as-up-paw'): a collection of (learned) men (only in the plural). Origin: feminine of H624 (אָסֻף); KJV: assembly.

H628 אֲסְפְּסֻף (ʼăçpᵉçuph, as-pes-oof'): gathered up together, i.e. a promiscuous assemblage (of people). Origin: by reduplication from H624 (אָסֻף); KJV: mixt multitude.

H629 אׇסְפַּרְנָא (ʼoçparnâʼ, os-par-naw'): diligently. Origin: (Aramaic) of Persian derivation; KJV: fast, forthwith, speed(-ily).

H630 אַסְפָּתָא (ʼAçpâthâʼ, as-paw-thaw'): Aspatha, a son of Haman. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Aspatha.

H631 אָסַר (ʼâçar, aw-sar'): to yoke or hitch; by analogy, to fasten in any sense, to join battle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind, fast, gird, harness, hold, keep, make ready, order, prepare, prison(-er), put in bonds, set in array, tie.

H632 אֱסָר (ʼĕçâr, es-sawr'): an obligation or vow (of abstinence). Origin: or אִסָּר; from H631 (אָסַר); KJV: binding, bond.

H633 אֱסָר (ʼĕçâr, es-sawr'): an interdict. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H632 (אֱסָר) in a legal sense; KJV: decree.

H634 אֵסַר־חַדּוֹן (ʼÊçar-Chaddôwn, ay-sar' Chad-dohn'): Esar-chaddon, an Assyrian king. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Esar-haddon.

H635 אֶסְתֵּר (ʼEçtêr, es-tare'): Ester, the Jewish heroine. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Esther.

H636 אָע (ʼâʻ, aw): a tree or wood. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6086 (עֵץ); KJV: timber, wood.

H637 אַף (ʼaph, af): meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though. Origin: a primitive particle; KJV: also, [phrase] although, and (furthermore, yet), but, even, [phrase] how much less (more, rather than), moreover, with, yea.

H638 אַף (ʼaph, af): {meaning accession (used as an adverb or conjunction); also or yea; adversatively though}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H637 (אַף) KJV: also.

H639 אַף (ʼaph, af): properly, the nose or nostril; hence, the face, and occasionally a person; also (from the rapid breathing in passion) ire. Origin: from H599 (אָנַף); KJV: anger(-gry), [phrase] before, countenance, face, [phrase] forebearing, forehead, [phrase] (long-) suffering, nose, nostril, snout, [idiom] worthy, wrath.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H640 to H780
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H640 אָפַד (ʼâphad, aw-fad'): to gird on (the ephod). Origin: a primitive root (rather a denominative from H646 (אֵפוֹד)); KJV: bind, gird.

H641 אֵפֹד (ʼÊphôd, ay-fode'): Ephod, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H646 (אֵפוֹד) shortened; KJV: Ephod.

H642 אֵפֻדָּה (ʼêphuddâh, ay-food-daw'): a girding on (of the ephod); hence, generally, a plating (of metal). Origin: feminine of H646 (אֵפוֹד); KJV: ephod, ornament.

H643 אַפֶּדֶן (ʼappeden, ap-peh'-den): a pavilion or palace-tent. Origin: apparently of foreign derivation; KJV: palace.

H644 אָפָה (ʼâphâh, aw-faw'): to cook, especially to bake. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bake(-r, (-meats)).

H645 אֵפוֹ (ʼêphôw, ay-fo'): strictly a demonstrative particle, here; but used of time, now or then. Origin: or אֵפוֹא; from H6311 (פֹּה); KJV: here, now, where?

H646 אֵפוֹד (ʼêphôwd, ay-fode'): a girdle; specifically the ephod or highpriest's shoulder-piece; also generally, an image. Origin: rarely אֵפֹד; probably of foreign derivation KJV: ephod.

H647 אֲפִיחַ (ʼĂphîyach, af-ee'-akh): Aphiach, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H6315 (פּוּחַ); breeze; KJV: Aphiah.

H648 אָפִיל (ʼâphîyl, aw-feel'): unripe. Origin: from the same as H651 (אָפֵל) (in the sense of weakness); KJV: not grown up.

H649 אַפַּיִם (ʼAppayim, ap-pah'-yim): Appajim, an Israelite. Origin: dual of H639 (אַף); two nostrils; KJV: Appaim.

H650 אָפִיק (ʼâphîyq, aw-feek'): properly, containing, i.e. a tube; also a bed or valley of astream; also a strong thing or a hero. Origin: from H622 (אָסַף); KJV: brook, channel, mighty, river, [phrase] scale, stream, strong piece.

H651 אָפֵל (ʼâphêl, aw-fale'): dusky. Origin: from an unused root meaning to set as the sun; KJV: very dark.

H652 אֹפֶל (ʼôphel, o'fel): dusk. Origin: from the same as H651 (אָפֵל); KJV: darkness, obscurity, privily.

H653 אֲפֵלָה (ʼăphêlâh, af-ay-law'): duskiness, figuratively, misfortune; concrete, concealment. Origin: feminine of H651 (אָפֵל); KJV: dark, darkness, gloominess, [idiom] thick.

H654 אֶפְלָל (ʼEphlâl, ef-lawl'): Ephlal, an Israelite. Origin: from H6419 (פָּלַל); judge; KJV: Ephlal.

H655 אֹפֶן (ʼôphen, o'-fen): a turn, i.e. a season. Origin: from an unused root meaning to revolve; KJV: [phrase] fitly.

H656 אָפֵס (ʼâphêç, aw-face'): to disappear, i.e. cease. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be clean gone (at an end, brought to nought), fail.

H657 אֶפֶס (ʼepheç, eh'-fes): cessation, i.e. an end (especially of the earth); often used adverb, no further; also the ankle (in the dual), as being the extremity of the leg or foot. Origin: from H656 (אָפֵס); (sometimes like H6466 (פָּעַל)) KJV: ankle, but (only), end, howbeit, less than nothing, nevertheless (where), no, none (beside), not (any, -withstanding), thing of nought, save(-ing), there, uttermost part, want, without (cause).

H658 אֶפֶס דַּמִּים (ʼEpheç Dammîym, eh'-fes dam-meem'): Ephes-Dammim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H657 (אֶפֶס) and the plural of H1818 (דָּם); boundary of blood-drops; KJV: Ephes-dammim.

H659 אֵפַע (ʼêphaʻ, eh'-fah): properly, a breath, i.e. nothing. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to breathe; KJV: of nought.

H660 אֶפְעֶה (ʼephʻeh, ef-eh'): an asp or other venomous serpent. Origin: from H659 (אֵפַע) (in the sense of hissing); KJV: viper.

H661 אָפַף (ʼâphaph, aw-faf'): to surround. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: compass.

H662 אָפַק (ʼâphaq, aw-fak'): to contain, i.e. (reflex.) abstain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: force (oneself), restrain.

H663 אֲפֵק (ʼĂphêq, af-ake'): Aphek (or Aphik), the name of three places in Palestine. Origin: or אֲפִיק; from H662 (אָפַק) (in the sense of strength); fortress; KJV: Aphek, Aphik.

H664 אֲפֵקָה (ʼĂphêqâh, af-ay-kaw'): Aphekah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H663 (אֲפֵק); fortress; KJV: Aphekah.

H665 אֵפֶר (ʼêpher, ay'-fer): ashes. Origin: from an unused root meaning to bestrew; KJV: ashes.

H666 אֲפֵר (ʼăphêr, af-ayr'): a turban. Origin: from the same as H665 (אֵפֶר) (in the sense of covering); KJV: ashes.

H667 אֶפְרֹחַ (ʼephrôach, ef-ro'-akh): the brood of a bird. Origin: from H6524 (פָּרַח) (in the sense of bursting the shell); KJV: young (one).

H668 אַפִּרְיוֹן (ʼappiryôwn, ap-pir-yone'): a palanquin. Origin: probably of Egyptian derivation; KJV: chariot.

H669 אֶפְרַיִם (ʼEphrayim, ef-rah'-yim): Ephrajim, a son of Joseph; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory. Origin: dual of masculine form of H672 (אֶפְרָת); double fruit; KJV: Ephraim, Ephraimites.

H670 אֲפָרְסַי (ʼĂphârᵉçay, af-aw-re-sah'ee): an Apherasite or inhabitant of an unknown region of Assyria. Origin: (Aramaic) of foreign origin (only in the plural); KJV: Apharsite.

H671 אֲפַרְסְכַי (ʼĂpharçᵉkay, af-ar-sek-ah'ee): an Apharsekite or Apharsathkite, an unknown Assyrian tribe. Origin: (Aramaic) or אֲפַרְסַתְכַי; (Aramaic), of foreign origin (only in the plural); KJV: Apharsachites, Apharasthchites.

H672 אֶפְרָת (ʼEphrâth, ef-rawth'): Ephrath, another name for Bethlehem. Origin: or אֶפְרָתָה; from H6509 (פָּרָה); fruitfulness; KJV: once (Psalm 132:6) perhaps for Ephraim; also of an Israelitish woman; Ephrath, Ephratah.

H673 אֶפְרָתִי (ʼEphrâthîy, ef-rawth-ee'): an Ephrathite or an Ephraimite. Origin: patrial from H672 (אֶפְרָת); KJV: Ephraimite, Ephrathite.

H674 אַפְּתֹם (ʼappᵉthôm, ap-pe-thome'): revenue; others at the last. Origin: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; KJV: revenue.

H675 אֶצְבּוֹן (ʼEtsbôwn, ets-bone'): Etsbon, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or אֶצְבֹּן; of uncertain derivation; KJV: Ezbon.

H676 אֶצְבַּע (ʼetsbaʻ, ets-bah'): something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe. Origin: from the same as H6648 (צֶבַע) (in the sense of grasping); KJV: finger, toe.

H677 אֶצְבַּע (ʼetsbaʻ, ets-bah'): {something to sieze with, i.e. a finger; by analogy, a toe}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H676 (אֶצְבַּע) KJV: finger, toe.

H678 אָצִיל (ʼâtsîyl, aw-tseel'): an extremity (Isaiah 41:9), also a noble. Origin: from H680 (אָצַל) (in its secondary sense of separation); KJV: chief man, noble.

H679 אַצִּיל (ʼatstsîyl, ats-tseel'): a joint of the hand (i.e. knuckle); also (according to some) a party-wall (Ezekiel 41:8). Origin: from H680 (אָצַל) (in its primary sense of uniting); KJV: (arm) hole, great.

H680 אָצַל (ʼâtsal, aw-tsal'): to separate; hence, to select, refuse, contract. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to join; used only as a denominative from H681 (אֵצֶל); KJV: keep, reserve, straiten, take.

H681 אֵצֶל (ʼêtsel, ay'-tsel): a side; (as a preposition) near. Origin: from H680 (אָצַל) (in the sense of joining); KJV: at, (hard) by, (from) (beside), near (unto), toward, with. See also H1018 (בֵּית הָאֵצֶל).

H682 אָצֵל (ʼÂtsêl, aw-tsale'): Atsel, the name of an Israelite, and of a place in Palestine. Origin: from H680 (אָצַל); noble; KJV: Azal, Azel.

H683 אֲצַלְיָהוּ (ʼĂtsalyâhûw, ats-al-yaw'-hoo): Atsaljah, an Israelite. Origin: from H680 (אָצַל) and H3050 (יָהּ) prolonged; Jah has reserved; KJV: Azaliah.

H684 אֹצֶם (ʼÔtsem, o'-tsem): Otsem, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to be strong; strength (i.e. strong); KJV: Ozem.

H685 אֶצְעָדָה (ʼetsʻâdâh, ets-aw-daw'): properly, a step-chain; by analogy, a bracelet. Origin: a variation from H6807 (צְעָדָה); KJV: bracelet, chain.

H686 אָצַר (ʼâtsar, aw-tsar'): to store up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (lay up in) store, [phrase] (make) treasure(-r).

H687 אֶצֶר (ʼEtser, ay'-tser): Etser, an Idumaean. Origin: from H686 (אָצַר); treasure; KJV: Ezer.

H688 אֶקְדָּח (ʼeqdâch, ek-dawkh'): burning, i.e. a carbuncle or other fiery gem. Origin: from H6916 (קִדָּה); KJV: carbuncle.

H689 אַקּוֹ (ʼaqqôw, ak-ko'): slender, i.e. the ibex. Origin: probably from H602 (אָנַק); KJV: wild goat.

H690 אֲרָא (ʼărâʼ, ar-aw'): Ara, an Israelite. Origin: probably for H738 (אֲרִי); lion; KJV: Ara.

H691 אֶרְאֵל (ʼerʼêl, er-ale'): a hero (collectively). Origin: probably for H739 (אֲרִיאֵל); KJV: valiant one.

H692 אַרְאֵלִי (ʼArʼêlîy, ar-ay-lee'): Areli (or an Arelite, collectively), an Israelite and his descendants. Origin: from H691 (אֶרְאֵל); heroic; KJV: Areli, Arelites.

H693 אָרַב (ʼârab, aw-rab'): to lurk. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (lie in) ambush(-ment), lay (lie in) wait.

H694 אֲרָב (ʼĂrâb, ar-awb'): Arab, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H693 (אָרַב); ambush; KJV: Arab.

H695 אֶרֶב (ʼereb, eh'-reb): ambuscade. Origin: from H693 (אָרַב); KJV: den, lie in wait.

H696 אֹרֶב (ʼôreb, o'-reb): {ambuscade}. Origin: the same as H695 (אֶרֶב) KJV: wait.

H697 אַרְבֶּה (ʼarbeh, ar-beh'): a locust (from its rapid increase). Origin: from H7235 (רָבָה); KJV: grasshopper, locust.

H698 אׇרֳבָה (ʼorŏbâh, or-ob-aw'): ambuscades. Origin: feminine of H696 (אֹרֶב) (only in the plural); KJV: spoils.

H699 אֲרֻבָּה (ʼărubbâh, ar-oob-baw'): a lattice; (by implication) a window, dovecot (because of the pigeon-holes), chimney (with its apertures for smoke), sluice (with openings for water). Origin: feminine participle passive of H693 (אָרַב) (as if for lurking); KJV: chimney, window.

H700 אֲרֻבּוֹת (ʼĂrubbôwth, ar-oob-both): Arubboth, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H699 (אֲרֻבָּה); KJV: Aruboth.

H701 אַרְבִּי (ʼArbîy, ar-bee'): an Arbite or native of Arab. Origin: patrial from H694 (אֲרָב); KJV: Arbite.

H702 אַרְבַּע (ʼarbaʻ, ar-bah'): four. Origin: masculine אַרְבָּעָה; from H7251 (רָבַע); KJV: four.

H703 אַרְבַּע (ʼarbaʻ, ar-bah'): {four}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H702 (אַרְבַּע) KJV: four.

H704 אַרְבַּע (ʼArbaʻ, ar-bah'): Arba, one of the Anakim. Origin: the same as H702 (אַרְבַּע); KJV: Arba.

H705 אַרְבָּעִים (ʼarbâʻîym, ar-baw-eem'): forty. Origin: multiple of H702 (אַרְבַּע); KJV: -forty.

H706 אַרְבַּעְתַּיִם (ʼarbaʻtayim, ar-bah-tah'-yim): fourfold. Origin: dual of H702 (אַרְבַּע); KJV: fourfold.

H707 אָרַג (ʼârag, aw-rag'): to plait or weave. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: weaver(-r).

H708 אֶרֶג (ʼereg, eh'-reg): a weaving; a braid; also a shuttle. Origin: from H707 (אָרַג); KJV: beam, weaver's shuttle.

H709 אַרְגֹּב (ʼArgôb, ar-gobe'): Argob, a district of Palestine. Origin: from the same as H7263 (רֶגֶב); stony; KJV: Argob.

H710 אַרְגְּוָן (ʼargᵉvân, arg-ev-awn'): purple. Origin: a variation for H713 (אַרְגָּמָן); KJV: purple.

H711 אַרְגְּוָן (ʼargᵉvân, arg-ev-awn'): {purple}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H710 (אַרְגְּוָן) KJV: purple.

H712 אַרְגָּז (ʼargâz, ar-gawz'): a box (as a pannier). Origin: perhaps from H7264 (רָגַז) (in the sense of being suspended), KJV: coffer.

H713 אַרְגָּמָן (ʼargâmân, ar-gaw-mawn'): purple (the color or the dyed stuff). Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: purple.

H714 אַרְדְּ (ʼArd, ard): Ard, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to wander; fugitive; KJV: Ard.

H715 אַרְדּוֹן (ʼArdôwn, ar-dohn'): Ardon, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H714 (אַרְדְּ); roaming; KJV: Ardon.

H716 אַרְדִּי (ʼArdîy, ar-dee): an Ardite (collectively) or descendant of Ard. Origin: patronymic from H714 (אַרְדְּ); KJV: Ardites.

H717 אָרָה (ʼârâh, aw-raw'): to pluck. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather, pluck.

H718 אֲרוּ (ʼărûw, ar-oo'): lo!. Origin: (Aramaic) probably akin to H431 (אֲלוּ); KJV: behold, lo.

H719 אַרְוַד (ʼArvad, ar-vad'): Arvad, an island-city of Palestine. Origin: probably from H7300 (רוּד); a refuge for the roving; KJV: Arvad.

H720 אֲרוֹד (ʼĂrôwd, ar-ode'): Arod, an Israelite. Origin: an orthographical variation of H719 (אַרְוַד); fugitive; KJV: Arod.

H721 אַרְוָדִי (ʼArvâdîy, ar-vaw-dee'): an Arvadite or citizen of Arvad. Origin: patrial from H719 (אַרְוַד); KJV: Arvadite.

H722 אֲרוֹדִי (ʼĂrôwdîy, ar-o-dee'): an Arodite or descendant of Arod. Origin: patronymic from H721 (אַרְוָדִי); KJV: Arodi, Arodites.

H723 אֻרְוָה (ʼurvâh, oor-vaw'): a herding-place for an animal. Origin: or אֲרָיָה; from H717 (אָרָה) (in the sense of feeding); KJV: stall.

H724 אֲרוּכָה (ʼărûwkâh, ar-oo-kaw'): wholeness (literally or figuratively). Origin: or אֲרֻכָה; feminine passive participle of H748 (אָרַךְ) (in the sense of restoring to soundness); KJV: health, made up, perfected.

H725 אֲרוּמָה (ʼĂrûwmâh, ar-oo-maw'): Arumah, a place in Palestine. Origin: a variation of H7316 (רוּמָה); height; KJV: Arumah.

H726 אֲרוֹמִי (ʼĂrôwmîy, ar-o-mee'): an Edomite (as in the margin). Origin: a clerical error for H130 (אֱדֹמִי); KJV: Syrian.

H727 אָרוֹן (ʼârôwn, aw-rone'): a box. Origin: or אָרֹן; from H717 (אָרָה) (in the sense of gathering); KJV: ark, chest, coffin.

H728 אֲרַוְנָה (ʼĂravnâh, ar-av-naw'): Aravnah (or Arnijah or Ornah), a Jebusite. Origin: or (by transposition) אוֹרְנָה; or אַרְנִיָּהlemma אַנִיָּה missing resh, corrected to אַרְנִיָּה; all by orthographical variation for H771 (אׇרְנָן); KJV: Araunah.

H729 אָרַז (ʼâraz, aw-raz'): of cedar. Origin: a primitive root; to be firm; used only in the passive participle as a denominative from H730 (אֶרֶז); KJV: made of cedar.

H730 אֶרֶז (ʼerez, eh-rez'): a cedar tree (from the tenacity of its roots). Origin: from H729 (אָרַז); KJV: cedar (tree).

H731 אַרְזָה (ʼarzâh, ar-zaw'): cedar wainscoating. Origin: feminine of H730 (אֶרֶז); KJV: cedar work.

H732 אָרַח (ʼârach, aw-rakh'): to travel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: go, wayfaring (man).

H733 אָרַח (ʼÂrach, aw-rakh'): Arach, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H732 (אָרַח); way faring; KJV: Arah.

H734 אֹרַח (ʼôrach, o'-rakh): a well-trodden road (literally or figuratively); also a caravan. Origin: from H732 (אָרַח); KJV: manner, path, race, rank, traveller, troop, (by-, high-) way.

H735 אֹרַח (ʼôrach, o'-rakh): a road. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H734 (אֹרַח); KJV: way.

H736 אֹרְחָה (ʼôrᵉchâh, o-rekh-aw'): a caravan. Origin: feminine active participle of H732 (אָרַח); KJV: (travelling) company.

H737 אֲרֻחָה (ʼăruchâh, ar-oo-khaw'): a ration of food. Origin: feminine passive participle of H732 (אָרַח) (in the sense of appointing); KJV: allowance, diet, dinner, victuals.

H738 אֲרִי (ʼărîy, ar-ee'): a lion. Origin: or (prolonged) []; from H717 (אָרָה) (in the sense of violence); KJV: (young) lion, [phrase] pierce (from the margin).

H739 אֲרִיאֵל (ʼărîyʼêl, ar-ee-ale'): lion of God; i.e. heroic. Origin: or אֲרִאֵל; from H738 (אֲרִי) and H410 (אֵל); KJV: lionlike men.

H740 אֲרִיאֵל (ʼĂrîyʼêl, ar-ee-ale'): Ariel, a symbolical name for Jerusalem, also the name of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H739 (אֲרִיאֵל); KJV: Ariel.

H741 אֲרִאֵיל (ʼăriʼêyl, ar-ee-ale'): the altar of the temple. Origin: either by transposition for H739 (אֲרִיאֵל) or, more probably, an orthographical variation for H2025 (הַרְאֵל); KJV: altar.

H742 אֲרִידַי (ʼĂrîyday, ar-ee-dah'-ee): Aridai, a son of Haman. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Aridai.

H743 אֲרִידָתָא (ʼĂrîydâthâʼ, ar-ee-daw-thaw'): Aridatha, a son of Haman. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Aridatha.

H744 אַרְיֵה (ʼaryêh, ar-yay'): {a lion}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H738 (אֲרִי) KJV: lion.

H745 אַרְיֵה (ʼAryêh, ar-yay'): Arjeh, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H738 (אֲרִי); lion; KJV: Arieh.

H746 אֲרְיוֹךְ (ʼĂryôwk, ar-yoke'): Arjok, the name of two Babylonians. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Arioch.

H747 אֲרִיסַי (ʼĂrîyçay, ar-ee-sah'-ee): Arisai, a son of Haman. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Arisai.

H748 אָרַךְ (ʼârak, aw-rak'): to be (causative, make) long (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: defer, draw out, lengthen, (be, become, make, pro-) long, [phrase] (out-, over-) live, tarry (long).

H749 אֲרַךְ (ʼărak, ar-ak'): to suit. Origin: (Aramaic) properly, corresponding to H748 (אָרַךְ), but used only in the sense of reaching to a given point; KJV: be meet.

H750 אָרֵךְ (ʼârêk, aw-rake'): long. Origin: from H748 (אָרַךְ); KJV: long(-suffering, -winged), patient, slow (to anger).

H751 אֶרֶךְ (ʼErek, eh'-rek): Erek, a place in Babylon. Origin: from H748 (אָרַךְ); length; KJV: Erech.

H752 אָרֹךְ (ʼârôk, aw-roke'): long. Origin: from H748 (אָרַךְ); KJV: long.

H753 אֹרֶךְ (ʼôrek, o'rek'): length. Origin: from H748 (אָרַךְ); KJV: [phrase] forever, length, long.

H754 אַרְכָּא (ʼarkâʼ, ar-kaw'): length. Origin: (Aramaic) or אַרְכָּה; (Aramaic), from H749 (אֲרַךְ); KJV: lengthening, prolonged.

H755 אַרְכֻבָה (ʼarkubâh, ar-koo-baw'): the knee. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root corresponding to H7392 (רָכַב) (in the sense of bending the knee); KJV: knee.

H756 אַרְכְּוַי (ʼArkᵉvay, ar-kev-ah'ee): an Arkevite (collectively) or native of Erek. Origin: (Aramaic) patrial from H751 (אֶרֶךְ); KJV: Archevite.

H757 אַרְכִּי (ʼArkîy, ar-kee'): an Arkite or native of Erek. Origin: patrial from another place (in Palestine) of similar name with H751 (אֶרֶךְ); KJV: Archi, Archite.

H758 אֲרָם (ʼĂrâm, arawm'): Aram or Syria, and its inhabitants; also the name of the son of Shem, a grandson of Nahor, and of an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H759 (אַרְמוֹן); the highland; KJV: Aram, Mesopotamia, Syria, Syrians.

H759 אַרְמוֹן (ʼarmôwn, ar-mone'): a citadel (from its height). Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be elevated); KJV: castle, palace. Compare H2038 (הַרְמוֹן).

H760 אֲרַם צוֹבָה (ʼĂram Tsôwbâh, ar-am' tso-baw'): Aram of Tsoba (or Coele-Syria). Origin: from H758 (אֲרָם) and H6678 (צוֹבָא); KJV: Aram-zobah.

H761 אֲרַמִּי (ʼĂrammîy, ar-am-mee'): an Aramite or Aramaean. Origin: patrial from H758 (אֲרָם); KJV: Syrian, Aramitess.

H762 אֲרָמִית (ʼĂrâmîyth, ar-aw-meeth'): (only adverbial) in Aramean. Origin: feminine of H761 (אֲרַמִּי); KJV: in the Syrian language (tongue), in Syriac.

H763 אֲרַם נַהֲרַיִם (ʼĂram Nahărayim, ar-am' nah-har-ah'-yim): Aram of (the) two rivers (Euphrates and Tigris) or Mesopotamia. Origin: from H758 (אֲרָם) and the dual of H5104 (נָהָר); KJV: Aham-naharaim, Mesopotamia.

H764 אַרְמֹנִי (ʼArmônîy, ar-mo-nee'): Armoni, an Israelite. Origin: from H759 (אַרְמוֹן); palatial; KJV: Armoni.

H765 אֲרָן (ʼĂrân, ar-awn'): Aran, an Edomite. Origin: from H7442 (רָנַן); stridulous; KJV: Aran.

H766 אֹרֶן (ʼôren, o'-ren): the ash tree (from its toughness). Origin: from the same as H765 (אֲרָן) (in the sense of strength); KJV: ash.

H767 אֹרֶן (ʼÔren, o'-ren): Oren, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H766 (אֹרֶן); KJV: Oren.

H768 אַרְנֶבֶת (ʼarnebeth, ar-neh'-beth): the hare. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: hare.

H769 אַרְנוֹן (ʼArnôwn, ar-nohn'): the Arnon, a river east of the Jordan, also its territory. Origin: or אַרְנֹןlemma אַרְנן missing vowel, corrected to אַרְנֹן; from H7442 (רָנַן); a brawling stream; KJV: Arnon.

H770 אַרְנָן (ʼArnân, ar-nawn'): Arnan, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the same as H769 (אַרְנוֹן); noisy; KJV: Arnan.

H771 אׇרְנָן (ʼOrnân, or-nawn'): Ornan, a Jebusite. Origin: probably from H766 (אֹרֶן); strong; KJV: Ornan. See H728 (אֲרַוְנָה).

H772 אֲרַע (ʼăraʻ, ar-ah'): the earth; by implication (figuratively) low. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H776 (אֶרֶץ); KJV: earth, interior.

H773 אַרְעִית (ʼarʻîyth, arh-eeth'): the bottom. Origin: (Aramaic) feminine of H772 (אֲרַע); KJV: bottom.

H774 אַרְפָּד (ʼArpâd, ar-pawd'): Arpad, a place in Syria. Origin: from H7502 (רָפַד); spread out; KJV: Arpad, Arphad.

H775 אַרְפַּכְשַׁד (ʼArpakshad, ar-pak-shad'): Arpakshad, a son of Noah; also the region settled by him. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Arphaxad.

H776 אֶרֶץ (ʼerets, eh'-rets): the earth (at large, or partitively a land). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to be firm; KJV: [idiom] common, country, earth, field, ground, land, [idiom] natins, way, [phrase] wilderness, world.

H777 אַרְצָא (ʼartsâʼ, ar-tsaw'): Artsa, an Israelite. Origin: from H776 (אֶרֶץ); earthiness; KJV: Arza.

H778 אֲרַק (ʼăraq, ar-ak'): the earth. Origin: (Aramaic) by transmutation for H772 (אֲרַע); KJV: earth.

H779 אָרַר (ʼârar, aw-rar'): to execrate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] bitterly curse.

H780 אֲרָרַט (ʼĂrâraṭ, ar-aw-rat'): Ararat (or rather Armenia). Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Ararat, Armenia.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H781 to H903
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H781 אָרַשׂ (ʼâras, aw-ras'): to engage for matrimony. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: betroth, espouse.

H782 אֲרֶשֶׁת (ʼăresheth, ar-eh'-sheth): a longing for. Origin: from H781 (אָרַשׂ) (in the sense of desiring to possess); KJV: request.

H783 אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׁתָּא (ʼArtachshashtâʼ, ar-takh-shash-taw'): Artachshasta (or Artaxerxes), a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings. Origin: or אַרְתַּחְשַׁשְׁתְּא; or by permutation אַרְתַּחְשַׁסְתְּא; of foreign origin; KJV: Artaxerxes.

H784 אֵשׁ (ʼêsh, aysh): fire (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive word; KJV: burning, fiery, fire, flaming, hot.

H785 אֵשׁ (ʼêsh, aysh): {fire (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H784 (אֵשׁ) KJV: flame.

H786 אִשׁ (ʼish, eesh): entity, used only adverbially, there is or are. Origin: identical (in origin and formation) with H784 (אֵשׁ); KJV: are there, none can. Compare H3426 (יֵשׁ).

H787 אֹשׁ (ʼôsh, ohsh): a foundation. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding (by transposition and abbreviation) to H803 (אֲשׁוּיָה); KJV: foundation.

H788 אַשְׁבֵּל (ʼAshbêl, ash-bale'): Ashbel, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the same as H7640 (שֹׁבֶל); flowing; KJV: Ashbel.

H789 אַשְׁבֵּלִי (ʼAshbêlîy, ash-bay-lee'): an Ashbelite (collectively) or descendant of Ashbel. Origin: patronymic from H788 (אַשְׁבֵּל); KJV: Ashbelites.

H790 אֶשְׁבָּן (ʼEshbân, esh-bawn'): Eshban, an Idumaean. Origin: probably from the same as H7644 (שֶׁבְנָא); vigorous; KJV: Eshban.

H791 אַשְׁבֵּעַ (ʼAshbêaʻ, ash-bay'-ah): Asbea, an Israelite. Origin: from H7650 (שָׁבַע); adjurer; KJV: Ashbea.

H792 אֶשְׁבַּעַל (ʼEshbaʻal, esh-bah'-al): Eshbaal (or Ishbosheth), a son of Saul. Origin: from H376 (אִישׁ) and H1168 (בַּעַל); man of Baal; KJV: Eshbaal.

H793 אֶשֶׁד (ʼeshed, eh'-shed): an outpouring. Origin: from an unused root meaning to pour; KJV: stream.

H794 אֲשֵׁדָה (ʼăshêdâh, ash-ay-daw'): a ravine. Origin: feminine of H793 (אֶשֶׁד); KJV: springs.

H795 אַשְׁדּוֹד (ʼAshdôwd, ash-dode'): Ashdod, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7703 (שָׁדַד); ravager; KJV: Ahdod.

H796 אַשְׁדּוֹדִי (ʼAshdôwdîy, ash-do-dee'): an Ashdodite (often collectively) or inhabitant of Asdod. Origin: patrial from H795 (אַשְׁדּוֹד); KJV: Ashdodites, of Ashdod.

H797 אַשְׁדּוֹדִית (ʼAshdôwdîyth, ash-do-deeth'): (only adverb) in the language of Ashdod. Origin: feminine of H796 (אַשְׁדּוֹדִי); KJV: in the speech of Ashdod.

H798 אַשְׁדּוֹת הַפִּסְגָּה (ʼAshdôwth hap-Piçgâh, ash-doth' hap-pisgaw'): Ashdoth-Pisgah, a place east of the Jordan. Origin: from the plural of H794 (אֲשֵׁדָה) and H6449 (פִּסְגָּה) with the article interposed; ravines of the Pisgah; KJV: Ashdoth-pisgah.

H799 אֶשְׁדָּת (ʼeshdâth, esh-dawth'): a fire-law. Origin: from H784 (אֵשׁ) and H1881 (דָּת); KJV: fiery law.

H800 אֶשָּׁה (ʼeshshâh, esh-shaw'): fire. Origin: feminine of H784 (אֵשׁ); KJV: fire.

H801 אִשָּׁה (ʼishshâh, ish-shaw'): properly, a burnt-offering; but occasionally of any sacrifice. Origin: the same as H800 (אֶשָּׁה), but used in a liturgical sense; KJV: (offering, sacrifice), (made) by fire.

H802 אִשָּׁה (ʼishshâh, ish-shaw'): a woman. Origin: feminine of H376 (אִישׁ) or H582 (אֱנוֹשׁ); irregular plural, נָשִׁים;(used in the same wide sense as H582 (אֱנוֹשׁ)) KJV: (adulter) ess, each, every, female, [idiom] many, [phrase] none, one, [phrase] together, wife, woman. Often unexpressed in English.

H803 אֲשׁוּיָה (ʼăshûwyâh, ash-oo-yah'): foundation. Origin: feminine passive participle from an unused root meaning to found; KJV: foundation.

H804 אַשּׁוּר (ʼAshshûwr, ash-shoor'): Ashshur, the second son of Shem; also his descendants and the country occupied by them (i.e. Assyria), its region and its empire. Origin: or אַשֻּׁר; apparently from H833 (אָשַׁר) (in the sense of successful); KJV: Asshur, Assur, Assyria, Assyrians. See H838 (אָשֻׁר).

H805 אֲשׁוּרִי (ʼĂshûwrîy, ash-oo-ree'): an Ashurite (collectively) or inhabitant of Ashur, a district in Palestine. Origin: or אַשּׁוּרִי; from a patrial word of the same form as H804 (אַשּׁוּר); KJV: Asshurim, Ashurites.

H806 אַשְׁחוּר (ʼAshchûwr, ash-khoor'): Ashchur, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H7835 (שָׁחַר); black; KJV: Ashur.

H807 אַשִׁימָא (ʼAshîymâʼ, ash-ee-maw'): Ashima, a deity of Hamath. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Ashima.

H808 אָשִׁישׁ (ʼâshîysh, aw-sheesh'): a (ruined) foundation. Origin: from the same as H784 (אֵשׁ) (in the sense of pressing down firmly; compare H803 (אֲשׁוּיָה)); KJV: foundation.

H809 אֲשִׁישָׁה (ʼăshîyshâh, ash-ee-shaw'): something closely pressed together, i.e. a cake of raisins or other comfits. Origin: feminine of H808 (אָשִׁישׁ); KJV: flagon.

H810 אֶשֶׁךְ (ʼeshek, eh'-shek): a testicle (as a lump). Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to bunch together); KJV: stone.

H811 אֶשְׁכּוֹל (ʼeshkôwl, esh-kole'): a bunch of grapes or other fruit. Origin: or אֶשְׁכֹּל; probably prolonged from H810 (אֶשֶׁךְ); KJV: cluster (of grapes).

H812 אֶשְׁכֹּל (ʼEshkôl, esh-kole'): Eshcol, the name of an Amorite, also of a valley in Palestine. Origin: the same as H811 (אֶשְׁכּוֹל); KJV: Eshcol.

H813 אַשְׁכְּנַז (ʼAshkᵉnaz, ash-ken-az'): Ashkenaz, a Japhethite, also his descendants. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Ashkenaz.

H814 אֶשְׁכָּר (ʼeshkâr, esh-cawr'): a gratuity. Origin: for H7939 (שָׂכָר); KJV: gift, present.

H815 אֵשֶׁל (ʼêshel, ay'-shel): a tamarisk tree; by extension, a grove of any kind. Origin: from a root of uncertain signification; KJV: grove, tree.

H816 אָשַׁם (ʼâsham, aw-sham'): to be guilty; by implication to be punished or perish. Origin: or אָשֵׁם; a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] certainly, be(-come, made) desolate, destroy, [idiom] greatly, be(-come, found, hold) guilty, offend (acknowledge offence), trespass.

H817 אָשָׁם (ʼâshâm, aw-shawm'): guilt; by implication, a fault; also a sin-offering. Origin: from H816 (אָשַׁם); KJV: guiltiness, (offering for) sin, trespass (offering).

H818 אָשֵׁם (ʼâshêm, aw-shame'): guilty; hence, presenting asin-offering. Origin: from H816 (אָשַׁם); KJV: one which is faulty, guilty.

H819 אַשְׁמָה (ʼashmâh, ash-maw'): guiltiness, a fault, the presentation of asin-offering. Origin: feminine of H817 (אָשָׁם); KJV: offend, sin, (cause of) trespass(-ing, offering).

H820 אַשְׁמָן (ʼashmân, ash-mawn'): a fat-field. Origin: probably from H8081 (שֶׁמֶן); KJV: desolate place.

H821 אַשְׁמֻרָה (ʼashmurâh, ash-moo-raw'): a night watch. Origin: or אַשׁמוּרָה; or אַשׁמֹרֶת; (feminine) from H8104 (שָׁמַר); KJV: watch.

H822 אֶשְׁנָב (ʼeshnâb, esh-nawb'): a latticed window. Origin: apparently from an unused root (probably meaning to leave interstices); KJV: casement, lattice.

H823 אַשְׁנָה (ʼAshnâh, ash-naw'): Ashnah, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: probably a variation for H3466 (יְשָׁנָה); KJV: Ashnah.

H824 אֶשְׁעָן (ʼEshʻân, esh-awn'): Eshan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H8172 (שָׁעַן); support; KJV: Eshean.

H825 אַשָּׁף (ʼashshâph, ash-shawf'): a conjurer. Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to lisp, i.e. practice enchantment); KJV: astrologer.

H826 אַשָּׁף (ʼashshâph, ash-shawf'): {a conjurer}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H825 (אַשָּׁף) KJV: astrologer.

H827 אַשְׁפָּה (ʼashpâh, ash-paw'): a quiver or arrow-case. Origin: perhaps (feminine) from the same as H825 (אַשָּׁף) (in the sense of covering); KJV: quiver.

H828 אַשְׁפְּנַז (ʼAshpᵉnaz, ash-pen-az'): Ashpenaz, a Babylonian eunuch. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Ashpenaz.

H829 אֶשְׁפָּר (ʼeshpâr, esh-pawr'): a measured portion. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: good piece (of flesh).

H830 אַשְׁפֹּת (ʼashpôth, ash-pohth'): a heap of rubbish or filth. Origin: or אַשְׁפּוֹת; or שְׁפֹת; (contraction) plural of a noun of the same form as H827 (אַשְׁפָּה), from H8192 (שָׁפָה) (in the sense of scraping); KJV: dung (hill).

H831 אַשְׁקְלוֹן (ʼAshqᵉlôwn, ash-kel-one'): Ashkelon, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H8254 (שָׁקַל) in the sense of weighing-place (i.e. mart); KJV: Ashkelon, Askalon.

H832 אֶשְׁקְלוֹנִי (ʼEshqᵉlôwnîy, esh-kel-o-nee'): Ashkelonite (collectively) or inhabitant of Ashkelon. Origin: patrial from H831 (אַשְׁקְלוֹן); KJV: Eshkalonites.

H833 אָשַׁר (ʼâshar, aw-shar'): to be straight (used in the widest sense, especially to be level, right, happy); figuratively, to go forward, be honest, proper. Origin: or אָשֵׁר; a primitive root; KJV: (call, be) bless(-ed, happy), go, guide, lead, relieve.

H834 אֲשֶׁר (ʼăsher, ash-er'): who, which, what, that; also (as an adverb and a conjunction) when, where, how, because, in order that, etc. Origin: a primitive relative pronoun (of every gender and number); KJV: [idiom] after, [idiom] alike, as (soon as), because, [idiom] every, for, [phrase] forasmuch, [phrase] from whence, [phrase] how(-soever), [idiom] if, (so) that ((thing) which, wherein), [idiom] though, [phrase] until, [phrase] whatsoever, when, where ([phrase] -as, -in, -of, -on, -soever, -with), which, whilst, [phrase] whither(-soever), who(-m, -soever, -se). As it is indeclinable, it is often accompanied by the personal pronoun expletively, used to show the connection.

H835 אֶשֶׁר (ʼesher, eh'-sher): happiness; only in masculine plural construction as interjection, how happy!. Origin: from H833 (אָשַׁר); KJV: blessed, happy.

H836 אָשֵׁר (ʼÂshêr, aw-share'): happy; Asher, a son of Jacob, and the tribe descended from him, with its territory; also a place in Palestine. Origin: from H833 (אָשַׁר), KJV: Asher

H837 אֹשֶׁר (ʼôsher, o'-sher): happiness. Origin: from H833 (אָשַׁר); KJV: happy.

H838 אָשֻׁר (ʼâshur, aw-shoor'): a step. Origin: or אַשֻּׁר; from H833 (אָשַׁר) in the sense of going; KJV: going, step.

H839 אֲשֻׁר (ʼăshur, ash-oor'): the cedar tree or some other light elastic wood. Origin: contracted for H8391 (תְּאַשּׁוּר); KJV: Ashurite.

H840 אֲשַׂרְאֵל (ʼĂsarʼêl, as-ar-ale'): Asarel, an Israelite. Origin: by orthographical variation from H833 (אָשַׁר) and H410 (אֵל); right of God; KJV: Asareel.

H841 אֲשַׂרְאֵלָה (ʼĂsarʼêlâh, as-ar-ale'-aw): Asarelah, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H840 (אֲשַׂרְאֵל); right toward God; KJV: Asarelah. Compare H3480 (יְשַׂרְאֵלָה).

H842 אֲשֵׁרָה (ʼăshêrâh, ash-ay-raw'): Asherah (or Astarte) a Phoenician goddess; also an image of the same. Origin: or אֲשֵׁירָה; from H833 (אָשַׁר); happy; KJV: grove. Compare H6253 (עַשְׁתֹּרֶת).

H843 אָשֵׁרִי (ʼÂshêrîy, aw-shay-ree'): an Asherite (collectively) or descendant of Asher. Origin: patronymic from H836 (אָשֵׁר); KJV: Asherites.

H844 אַשְׂרִיאֵל (ʼAsrîyʼêl, as-ree-ale'): Asriel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: an orthographical variation for H840 (אֲשַׂרְאֵל); KJV: Ashriel, Asriel.

H845 אַשְׂרִאֵלִי (ʼAsriʼêlîy, as-ree-ale-ee'): an Asrielite (collectively) or descendant of Asriel. Origin: patronymic from H844 (אַשְׂרִיאֵל); KJV: Asrielites.

H846 אֻשַּׁרְנָא (ʼushsharnâʼ, oosh-ar-naw'): a wall (from its uprightness). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H833 (אָשַׁר); KJV: wall.

H847 אֶשְׁתָּאֹל (ʼEshtâʼôl, esh-taw-ole'): Eshtaol, a place in Palestine. Origin: or אֶשְׁתָּאוֹל; probably from H7592 (שָׁאַל); intreaty; KJV: Eshtaol.

H848 אֶשְׁתָּאֻלִי (ʼEshtâʼulîy, esh-taw-oo-lee'): an Eshtaolite (collectively) or inhabitant of Eshtaol. Origin: patrial from H847 (אֶשְׁתָּאֹל); KJV: Eshtaulites.

H849 אֶשְׁתַּדּוּר (ʼeshtaddûwr, esh-tad-dure'): rebellion. Origin: (Aramaic) from H7712 (שְׁדַר) (in a bad sense); KJV: sedition.

H850 אֶשְׁתּוֹן (ʼEshtôwn, esh-tone'): Eshton, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the same as H7764 (שׁוּנִי); restful; KJV: Eshton.

H851 אֶשְׁתְּמֹעַ (ʼEshtᵉmôaʻ, esh-tem-o'-ah): Eshtemoa or Eshtemoh, a place in Palestine. Origin: or אֶשְׁתְּמוֹעַ; or אֶשְׁתְּמֹה; from H8085 (שָׁמַע) (in the sense of obedience); KJV: Eshtemoa, Eshtemoh.

H852 אָת (ʼâth, awth): a portent. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H226 (אוֹת); KJV: sign.

H853 אֵת (ʼêth, ayth): properly, self (but generally used to point out more definitely the object of a verb or preposition, even or namely). Origin: apparent contracted from H226 (אוֹת) in the demonstrative sense of entity; KJV: (as such unrepresented in English).

H854 אֵת (ʼêth, ayth): properly, nearness (used only as a preposition or an adverb), near; hence, generally, with, by, at, among, etc. Origin: probably from H579 (אָנָה); KJV: against, among, before, by, for, from, in(-to), (out) of, with. Often with another prepositional prefix.

H855 אֵת (ʼêth, ayth): a hoe or other digging implement. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: coulter, plowshare.

H856 אֶתְבַּעַל (ʼEthbaʻal, eth-bah'-al): Ethbaal, a Phoenician king. Origin: from H854 (אֵת) and H1168 (בַּעַל); with Baal; KJV: Ethbaal.

H857 אָתָה (ʼâthâh, aw-thaw'): to arrive. Origin: or אָתָא; a primitive root (collateral to H225 (אוּת) contraction); KJV: (be-, things to) come (upon), bring.

H858 אָתָה (ʼâthâh, aw-thaw'): {to arrive}. Origin: (Aramaic) or אָתָא; (Aramaic), corresponding to H857 (אָתָה) KJV: (be-) come, bring.

H859 אַתָּה (ʼattâh, at-taw'): thou and thee, or (plural) ye and you. Origin: or (shortened); אַתָּ; or אַת; feminine (irregular) sometimes אַתִּי; plural masculine אַתֶּם; feminine אַתֶּן; or אַתֵּנָהlemma אתֵּנָה missing vowel, corrected to אַתֵּנָה; or אַתֵּנָּה; a primitive pronoun of the second person; KJV: thee, thou, ye, you.

H860 אָתוֹן (ʼâthôwn, aw-thone'): a female donkey (from its docility). Origin: probably from the same as H386 (אֵיתָן) (in the sense of patience); KJV: (she) ass.

H861 אַתּוּן (ʼattûwn, at-toon'): probably a fire-place, i.e. furnace. Origin: (Aramaic) probably from the corresponding to H784 (אֵשׁ); KJV: furnace.

H862 אַתּוּק (ʼattûwq, at-tooke'): a ledge or offset in abuilding. Origin: or אַתִּיק; from H5423 (נָתַק) in the sense of decreasing; KJV: gallery.

H863 אִתַּי (ʼIttay, it-tah'ee): Ittai or Ithai, the name of a Gittite and of an Israelite. Origin: or אִיתַי; from H854 (אֵת); near; KJV: Ithai, Ittai.

H864 אֵתָם (ʼÊthâm, ay-thawm'): Etham, a place in the Desert. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Etham.

H865 אֶתְמוֹל (ʼethmôwl, eth-mole'): heretofore; definitely yesterday. Origin: or אִתְמוֹל; or אֶתְמוּל; probably from H853 (אֵת) or H854 (אֵת) and H4136 (מוּל); KJV: [phrase] before (that) time, [phrase] heretofore, of late (old), [phrase] times past, yester(day).

H866 אֶתְנָה (ʼethnâh, eth-naw'): a present (as the price of harlotry). Origin: from H8566 (תָּנָה); KJV: reward.

H867 אֶתְנִי (ʼEthnîy, eth-nee'): Ethni, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H866 (אֶתְנָה); munificence; KJV: Ethni.

H868 אֶתְנַן (ʼethnan, eth-nan'): a gift (as the price of harlotry or idolatry). Origin: the same as H866 (אֶתְנָה); KJV: hire, reward.

H869 אֶתְנַן (ʼEthnan, eth-nan'): Ethnan, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H868 (אֶתְנַן) in the sense of H867 (אֶתְנִי); KJV: Ethnan.

H870 אֲתַר (ʼăthar, ath-ar'): a place; (adverb) after. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of H871 (אֲתָרִים); KJV: after, place.
