H871 אֲתָרִים (ʼĂthârîym, ath-aw-reem'): Atharim, a place near Palestine. Origin: plural from an unused root (probably meaning to step); places; KJV: spies. b

H872 בְּאָה (bᵉʼâh, be-aw'): an entrance to a building. Origin: from H935 (בּוֹא); KJV: entry.

H873 בִּאוּשׁ (biʼûwsh, be-oosh'): wicked. Origin: (Aramaic) from H888 (בְּאֵשׁ); KJV: bad.

H874 בָּאַר (bâʼar, baw-ar'): to dig; by analogy, to engrave; figuratively, to explain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: declare, (make) plain(-ly).

H875 בְּאֵר (bᵉʼêr, be-ayr'): a pit; especially a well. Origin: from H874 (בָּאַר); KJV: pit, well.

H876 בְּאֵר (Bᵉʼêr, be-ayr'): Beer, a place in the Desert, also one in Palestine. Origin: the same as H875 (בְּאֵר); KJV: Beer.

H877 בֹּאר (bôʼr, bore): a cistern. Origin: from H874 (בָּאַר); KJV: cistern.

H878 בְּאֵרָא (Bᵉʼêrâʼ, be-ay-raw'): Beera, an Israelite. Origin: from H875 (בְּאֵר); a well; KJV: Beera.

H879 בְּאֵר אֵלִים (Bᵉʼêr ʼÊlîym, be-ayr' ay-leem'): Beer-Elim, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H875 (בְּאֵר) and the plural of H410 (אֵל); well of heroes; KJV: Beer-elim.

H880 בְּאֵרָה (Bᵉʼêrâh, be-ay-raw'): Beerah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H878 (בְּאֵרָא); KJV: Beerah.

H881 בְּאֵרוֹת (Bᵉʼêrôwth, be-ay-rohth'): Beeroth, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine plural of H875 (בְּאֵר); wells; KJV: Beeroth.

H882 בְּאֵרִי (Bᵉʼêrîy, be-ay-ree'): Beeri, the name of a Hittite and of an Israelite. Origin: from H875 (בְּאֵר); fountained; KJV: Beeri.

H883 בְּאֵר לַחַי רֹאִי (Bᵉʼêr la-Chay Rôʼîy, be-ayr' lakh-ah'ee ro-ee'): Beer-Lachai-Roi, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H875 (בְּאֵר) and H2416 (חַי) (with prefix) and H7203 (רֹאֶה); well of a living (One) my Seer; KJV: Beer-lahai-roi.

H884 בְּאֵר שֶׁבַע (Bᵉʼêr Shebaʻ, be-ayr' sheh'-bah): Beer-Sheba, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H875 (בְּאֵר) and H7651 (שֶׁבַע) (in the sense of H7650 (שָׁבַע)); well of an oath; KJV: Beer-shebah.

H885 בְּאֵרֹת בְּנֵי־יַעֲקַן (Bᵉʼêrôth Bᵉnêy-Yaʻăqan, be-ay-roth' be-nay' yah-a-can'): Beeroth-Bene-Jaakan, a place in the Desert. Origin: from the feminine plural of H875 (בְּאֵר), and the plural contraction of H1121 (בֵּן), and H3292 (יַעֲקָן); wells of (the) sons of Jaakan; KJV: Beeroth of the children of Jaakan.

H886 בְּאֵרֹתִי (Bᵉʼêrôthîy, be-ay-ro-thee'): a Beerothite or inhabitant of Beeroth. Origin: patrial from H881 (בְּאֵרוֹת); KJV: Beerothite.

H887 בָּאַשׁ (bâʼash, baw-ash'): to smell bad; figuratively, to be offensive morally. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make to) be abhorred (had in abomination, loathsome, odious), (cause a, make to) stink(-ing savour), [idiom] utterly.

H888 בְּאֵשׁ (bᵉʼêsh, be-aysh'): {to smell bad; figuratively, to be offensive morally}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H887 (בָּאַשׁ) KJV: displease.

H889 בְּאֹשׁ (bᵉʼôsh, be-oshe'): a stench. Origin: from H877 (בֹּאר); KJV: stink.

H890 בׇּאְשָׁה (boʼshâh, bosh-aw'): stink-weed or any other noxious or useless plant. Origin: feminine of H889 (בְּאֹשׁ); KJV: cockle.

H891 בְּאֻשִׁים (bᵉʼushîym, be-oo-sheem'): poison-berries. Origin: plural of H889 (בְּאֹשׁ); KJV: wild grapes.

H892 בָּבָה (bâbâh, baw-baw'): something hollowed (as a gate), i.e. pupil of the eye. Origin: feminine active participle of an unused root meaning to hollow out; KJV: apple (of the eye).

H893 בֵּבַי (Bêbay, bay-bah'ee): Bebai, an Israelite. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Bebai.

H894 בָּבֶל (Bâbel, baw-bel'): Babel (i.e. Babylon), including Babylonia and the Babylonian empire. Origin: from H1101 (בָּלַל); confusion; KJV: Babel, Babylon.

H895 בַּבֶל (Babel, baw-bel'): {Babel (i.e. Babylon), including Babylonia and the Babylonian empire}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H894 (בָּבֶל) KJV: Babylon.

H896 בַּבְלִי (Bablîy, bab-lee'): a Babylonian. Origin: (Aramaic) patrial from H895 (בַּבֶל); KJV: Babylonia.

H897 בַּג (bag, bag): food. Origin: a Persian word; KJV: spoil (from the margin for H957 (בַּז).)

H898 בָּגַד (bâgad, baw-gad'): to cover (with a garment); figuratively, to act covertly; by implication, to pillage. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deal deceitfully (treacherously, unfaithfully), offend, transgress(-or), (depart), treacherous (dealer, -ly, man), unfaithful(-ly, man), [idiom] very.

H899 בֶּגֶד (beged, behg'-ed): a covering, i.e. clothing; also treachery or pillage. Origin: from H898 (בָּגַד); KJV: apparel, cloth(-es, ing), garment, lap, rag, raiment, robe, [idiom] very (treacherously), vesture, wardrobe.

H900 בֹּגְדוֹת (bôgᵉdôwth, bohg-ed-ohth): treacheries. Origin: feminine plural active participle of H898 (בָּגַד); KJV: treacherous.

H901 בָּגוֹד (bâgôwd, baw-gode'): treacherous. Origin: from H898 (בָּגַד); KJV: treacherous.

H902 בִּגְוַי (Bigvay, big-vah'ee): Bigvai, an Israelite. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Bigvai.

H903 בִּגְתָא (Bigthâʼ, big-thaw'): Bigtha, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Bigtha.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H904 to H1024
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H904 בִּגְתָן (Bigthân, big-thawn'): Bigthan or Bigthana, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: or בִּגְתָנָא; of similar derivation to H903 (בִּגְתָא); KJV: Bigthan, Bigthana.

H905 בַּד (bad, bad): properly, separation; by implication, a part of the body, branch of atree, bar forcarrying; figuratively, chief of a city; especially (with prepositional prefix) as an adverb, apart, only, besides. Origin: from H909 (בָּדַד); KJV: alone, apart, bar, besides, branch, by self, of each alike, except, only, part, staff, strength.

H906 בַּד (bad, bad): flaxen thread or yarn; hence, a linen garment. Origin: perhaps from H909 (בָּדַד) (in the sense of divided fibres); KJV: linen.

H907 בַּד (bad, bad): a brag or lie; also a liar. Origin: from H908 (בָּדָא); KJV: liar, lie.

H908 בָּדָא (bâdâʼ, baw-daw'): (figuratively) to invent. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: devise, feign.

H909 בָּדַד (bâdad, baw-dad'): to divide, i.e. (reflex.) be solitary. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: alone.

H910 בָּדָד (bâdâd, baw-dawd'): separate; adverb, separately. Origin: from H909 (בָּדַד); KJV: alone, desolate, only, solitary.

H911 בְּדַד (Bᵉdad, bed-ad'): Bedad, an Edomite. Origin: from H909 (בָּדַד); separation; KJV: Bedad.

H912 בֵּדְיָה (Bêdᵉyâh, bay-de-yaw'): Bedejah, an Israelite. Origin: probably a shortened form H5662 (עֹבַדְיָה); servant of Jehovah; KJV: Bedeiah.

H913 בְּדִיל (bᵉdîyl, bed-eel'): alloy (because removed by smelting); by analogy, tin. Origin: from H914 (בָּדַל); KJV: [phrase] plummet, tin.

H914 בָּדַל (bâdal, baw-dal'): to divide (in variation senses literally or figuratively, separate, distinguish, differ, select, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make, put) difference, divide (asunder), (make) separate (self, -ation), sever (out), [idiom] utterly.

H915 בָּדָל (bâdâl, baw-dawl'): a part. Origin: from H914 (בָּדַל); KJV: piece.

H916 בְּדֹלַח (bᵉdôlach, bed-o'-lakh): something in pieces, i.e. bdellium, a (fragrant) gum (perhaps amber); others a pearl. Origin: probably from H914 (בָּדַל); KJV: bdellium.

H917 בְּדָן (Bᵉdân, bed-awn'): Bedan, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably shortened for H5658 (עַבְדוֹן); servile; KJV: Bedan.

H918 בָּדַק (bâdaq, baw-dak'): to mend a breach. Origin: a primitive root; to gap open; used only as a denominative from H919 (בֶּדֶק); KJV: repair.

H919 בֶּדֶק (bedeq, beh'-dek): a gap or leak (in a building or a ship). Origin: from H918 (בָּדַק); KJV: breach, [phrase] calker.

H920 בִּדְקַר (Bidqar, bid-car'): Bidkar, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H1856 (דָּקַר) with a prepositional prefix; by stabbing, i.e. assassin; KJV: Bidkar.

H921 בְּדַר (bᵉdar, bed-ar'): to scatter. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding (by transposition) to H6504 (פָּרַד); KJV: scatter.

H922 בֹּהוּ (bôhûw, bo'-hoo): a vacuity, i.e. (superficially) an undistinguishable ruin. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be empty); KJV: emptiness, void.

H923 בַּהַט (bahaṭ, bah'-hat): white marble or perhaps alabaster. Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to glisten); KJV: red (marble).

H924 בְּהִילוּ (bᵉhîylûw, be-hee-loo'): a hurry; only adverb, hastily. Origin: (Aramaic) from H927 (בְּהַל); KJV: in haste.

H925 בָּהִיר (bâhîyr, baw-here'): shining. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be bright); KJV: bright.

H926 בָּהַל (bâhal, baw-hal'): to tremble inwardly (or palpitate), i.e. (figuratively) be (causative, make) (suddenly) alarmed or agitated; by implication to hasten anxiously. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (make) affrighted (afraid, amazed, dismayed, rash), (be, get, make) haste(-n, -y, -ily), (give) speedy(-ily), thrust out, trouble, vex.

H927 בְּהַל (bᵉhal, be-hal'): to terrify, hasten. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H926 (בָּהַל); KJV: in haste, trouble.

H928 בֶּהָלָה (behâlâh, beh-haw-law'): panic, destruction. Origin: from H926 (בָּהַל); KJV: terror, trouble.

H929 בְּהֵמָה (bᵉhêmâh, be-hay-maw'): properly, a dumb beast; especially any large quadruped or animal (often collective). Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to be mute); KJV: beast, cattle.

H930 בְּהֵמוֹת (bᵉhêmôwth, be-hay-mohth'): a water-ox, i.e. the hippopotamus or Nile-horse. Origin: in form a plural or H929 (בְּהֵמָה), but really a singular of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Behemoth.

H931 בֹּהֶן (bôhen, bo'-hen): the thumb of the hand or great toe of the foot. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to be thick; KJV: thumb, great toe.

H932 בֹּהַן (Bôhan, bo'han): thumb, Bohan, an Israelite. Origin: an orthographical variation of H931 (בֹּהֶן); KJV: Bohan.

H933 בֹּהַק (bôhaq, bo'-hak): white scurf. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be pale; KJV: freckled spot.

H934 בֹּהֶרֶת (bôhereth, bo-heh'-reth): a whitish spot on the skin. Origin: feminine active participle of the same as H925 (בָּהִיר); KJV: bright spot.

H935 בּוֹא (bôwʼ, bo): to go or come (in a wide variety of applications). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abide, apply, attain, [idiom] be, befall, [phrase] besiege, bring (forth, in, into, to pass), call, carry, [idiom] certainly, (cause, let, thing for) to come (against, in, out, upon, to pass), depart, [idiom] doubtless again, [phrase] eat, [phrase] employ, (cause to) enter (in, into, -tering, -trance, -try), be fallen, fetch, [phrase] follow, get, give, go (down, in, to war), grant, [phrase] have, [idiom] indeed, (in-) vade, lead, lift (up), mention, pull in, put, resort, run (down), send, set, [idiom] (well) stricken (in age), [idiom] surely, take (in), way.

H936 בּוּז (bûwz, booz): to disrespect. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: contemn, despise, [idiom] utterly.

H937 בּוּז (bûwz, booz): disrespect. Origin: from H936 (בּוּז); KJV: contempt(-uously), despised, shamed.

H938 בּוּז (Bûwz, booz): Buz, the name of a son of Nahor, and of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H937 (בּוּז); KJV: Buz.

H939 בּוּזָה (bûwzâh, boo-zaw'): something scorned; an object of contempt. Origin: feminine passive participle of H936 (בּוּז); KJV: despised.

H940 בּוּזִי (Bûwzîy, boo-zee'): a Buzite or descendant of Buz. Origin: patronymic from H938 (בּוּז); KJV: Buzite.

H941 בּוּזִי (Bûwzîy, boo-zee'): Buzi, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H940 (בּוּזִי); KJV: Buzi.

H942 בַּוַּי (Bavvay, bav-vah'ee): Bavvai, an Israelite. Origin: probably of Persian origin; KJV: Bavai.

H943 בּוּךְ (bûwk, book): to involve (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be entangled, (perplexed).

H944 בּוּל (bûwl, bool): produce (of the earth, etc.). Origin: for H2981 (יְבוּל); KJV: food, stock.

H945 בּוּל (Bûwl, bool): Bul, the eighth Hebrew month. Origin: the same as H944 (בּוּל) (in the sense of rain); KJV: Bul.

H946 בּוּנָה (Bûwnâh, boo-naw'): Bunah, an Israelite. Origin: from H995 (בִּין); discretion; KJV: Bunah.

H947 בּוּס (bûwç, boos): to trample (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: loath, tread (down, under (foot)), be polluted.

H948 בּוּץ (bûwts, boots): probably cotton (of some sort). Origin: from an unused root (of the same form) meaning to bleach, i.e. (intransitive) be white; KJV: fine (white) linen.

H949 בּוֹצֵץ (Bôwtsêts, bo-tsates'): Botsets, a rock near Michmash. Origin: from the same as H948 (בּוּץ); shining; KJV: Bozez.

H950 בּוּקָה (bûwqâh, boo-kaw'): emptiness (as adjective). Origin: feminine passive participle of an unused root (meaning to be hollow); KJV: empty.

H951 בּוֹקֵר (bôwqêr, bo-kare'): a cattle-tender. Origin: properly, active participle from H1239 (בָּקַר) as denominative from H1241 (בָּקָר); KJV: herdman.

H952 בּוּר (bûwr, boor): to bore, i.e. (figuratively) examine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: declare.

H953 בּוֹר (bôwr, bore): a pit hole (especially one used as a cistern or a prison). Origin: from H952 (בּוּר) (in the sense of H877 (בֹּאר)); KJV: cistern, dungeon, fountain, pit, well.

H954 בּוּשׁ (bûwsh, boosh): properly, to pale, i.e. by implication to be ashamed; also (by implication) to be disappointed or delayed. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be, make, bring to, cause, put to, with, a-) shamed(-d), be (put to) confounded(-fusion), become dry, delay, be long.

H955 בּוּשָׁה (bûwshâh, boo-shaw'): shame. Origin: feminine participle passive of H954 (בּוּשׁ); KJV: shame.

H956 בּוּת (bûwth, booth): to lodge over night. Origin: (Aramaic) apparent denominative from H1005 (בַּיִת); KJV: pass the night.

H957 בַּז (baz, baz): plunder. Origin: from H962 (בָּזַז); KJV: booty, prey, spoil(-ed).

H958 בָּזָא (bâzâʼ, baw-zaw'): probably to cleave. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: spoil.

H959 בָּזָה (bâzâh, baw-zaw'): to disesteem. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: despise, disdain, contemn(-ptible), [phrase] think to scorn, vile person.

H960 בָּזֹה (bâzôh, baw-zo'): scorned. Origin: from H959 (בָּזָה); KJV: despise.

H961 בִּזָּה (bizzâh, biz-zaw'): booty. Origin: feminine of H957 (בַּז); KJV: prey, spoil.

H962 בָּזַז (bâzaz, baw-zaz'): to plunder. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch, gather, (take) for a prey, rob(-ber), spoil, take (away, spoil), [idiom] utterly.

H963 בִּזָּיוֹן (bizzâyôwn, biz-zaw-yone'): disesteem. Origin: from H959 (בָּזָה) KJV: contempt.

H964 בִּזְיוֹתְיָה (bizyôwthᵉyâh, biz-yo-the-yaw'): Bizjothjah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H959 (בָּזָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); contempts of Jah; KJV: Bizjothjah.

H965 בָּזָק (bâzâq, baw-zawk'): a flash of lightning. Origin: from an unused root meaning to lighten; KJV: flash of lightning.

H966 בֶּזֶק (Bezeq, beh'-zak): Bezek, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H965 (בָּזָק); lightning; KJV: Bezek.

H967 בָּזַר (bâzar, baw-zar'): to disperse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: scatter.

H968 בִּזְתָא (Bizthâʼ, biz-thaw'): Biztha, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Biztha.

H969 בָּחוֹן (bâchôwn, baw-khone'): an assayer or metals. Origin: from H974 (בָּחַן); KJV: tower.

H970 בָּחוּר (bâchûwr, baw-khoor'): properly, selected, i.e. a youth (often collective). Origin: or בָּחֻר; participle passive of H977 (בָּחַר); KJV: (choice) young (man), chosen, [idiom] hole.

H971 בַּחִין (bachîyn, bakh-een'): a watch-tower of besiegers. Origin: another form of H975 (בַּחַן); KJV: tower.

H972 בָּחִיר (bâchîyr, baw-kheer'): select. Origin: from H977 (בָּחַר); KJV: choose, chosen one, elect.

H973 בָּחַל (bâchal, baw-khal'): to loath. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor, get hastily (from the margin for H926 (בָּהַל)).

H974 בָּחַן (bâchan, baw-khan'): to test (especially metals); generally and figuratively, to investigate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: examine, prove, tempt, try (trial).

H975 בַּחַן (bachan, bakh'-an): a watch-tower. Origin: from H974 (בָּחַן) (in the sense of keeping a look-out); KJV: tower.

H976 בֹּחַן (bôchan, bo'-khan): trial. Origin: from H974 (בָּחַן); KJV: tried.

H977 בָּחַר (bâchar, baw-khar'): properly, to try, i.e. (by implication) select. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: acceptable, appoint, choose (choice), excellent, join, be rather, require.

H978 בַּחֲרוּמִי (Bachărûwmîy, bakh-ar-oo-mee'): a Bacharumite or inhabitant of Bachurim. Origin: patrial from H980 (בַּחֻרִים) (by transposition); KJV: Baharumite.

H979 בְּחֻרוֹת (bᵉchurôwth, bekh-oo-rothe'): youth (collectively and abstractly). Origin: or בְּחוּרוֹת; feminine plural of H970 (בָּחוּר); also (masculine plural) בְּחֻרִים; KJV: young men, youth.

H980 בַּחֻרִים (Bachurîym, bakh-oo-reem'): Bachurim, a place in Palestine. Origin: or בַּחוּרִים; masculine plural of H970 (בָּחוּר); young men; KJV: Bahurim.

H981 בָּטָא (bâṭâʼ, baw-taw'): to babble; hence, to vociferate angrily. Origin: or בָּטָה; a primitive root; KJV: pronounce, speak (unadvisedly).

H982 בָּטַח (bâṭach, baw-takh'): figuratively, to trust, be confident or sure. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to hide for refuge (but not so precipitately as H2620 (חָסָה)); KJV: be bold (confident, secure, sure), careless (one, woman), put confidence, (make to) hope, (put, make to) trust.

H983 בֶּטַח (beṭach, beh'takh): properly, a place of refuge; abstract, safety, both the fact (security) and the feeling (trust); often (adverb with or without preposition) safely. Origin: from H982 (בָּטַח); KJV: assurance, boldly, (without) care(-less), confidence, hope, safe(-ly, -ty), secure, surely.

H984 בֶּטַח (Beṭach, beh'takh): Betach, a place in Syria. Origin: the same as H983 (בֶּטַח); KJV: Betah.

H985 בִּטְחָה (biṭchâh, bit-khaw'): trust. Origin: feminine of H984 (בֶּטַח); KJV: confidence.

H986 בִּטָּחוֹן (biṭṭâchôwn, bit-taw-khone'): trust. Origin: from H982 (בָּטַח); KJV: confidence, hope.

H987 בַּטֻּחוֹת (baṭṭuchôwth, bat-too-khoth'): security. Origin: feminine plural from H982 (בָּטַח); KJV: secure.

H988 בָּטֵל (bâṭêl, baw-tale'): to desist from labor. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease.

H989 בְּטֵל (bᵉṭêl, bet-ale'): to stop. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H988 (בָּטֵל); KJV: (cause, make to), cease, hinder.

H990 בֶּטֶן (beṭen, beh'-ten): the belly, especially the womb; also the bosom or body of anything. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to be hollow; KJV: belly, body, [phrase] as they be born, [phrase] within, womb.

H991 בֶּטֶן (Beṭen, beh'-ten): Beten. a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H990 (בֶּטֶן); KJV: Beten.

H992 בֹּטֶן (bôṭen, bo'-ten): (only in plural) a pistachio-nut (from its form). Origin: from H990 (בֶּטֶן); KJV: nut.

H993 בְּטֹנִים (Bᵉṭônîym, bet-o-neem'): Betonim, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably plural from H992 (בֹּטֶן); hollows; KJV: Betonim.

H994 בִּי (bîy, bee): oh that!; with leave, or if it please. Origin: perhaps from H1158 (בָּעָה) (in the sense of asking); properly, a request; used only adverbially (always with 'my Lord'); KJV: alas, O, oh.

H995 בִּין (bîyn, bene): to separate mentally (or distinguish), i.e.(generally) understand. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: attend, consider, be cunning, diligently, direct, discern, eloquent, feel, inform, instruct, have intelligence, know, look well to, mark, perceive, be prudent, regard, (can) skill(-full), teach, think, (cause, make to, get, give, have) understand(-ing), view, (deal) wise(-ly, man).

H996 בֵּין (bêyn, bane): between (repeated before each noun, often with other particles); also as a conjunction, either...or. Origin: (sometimes in the plural masculine or feminine); properly, the constructive form of an otherwise unused noun from H995 (בִּין); a distinction; but used only as a preposition, KJV: among, asunder, at, between (-twixt...and), [phrase] from (the widest), [idiom] in, out of, whether (it be...or), within.

H997 בֵּין (bêyn, bane): {between (repeated before each noun, often with other particles); also as a conjunction, either...or}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H996 (בֵּין) KJV: among, between.

H998 בִּינָה (bîynâh, bee-naw'): understanding. Origin: from H995 (בִּין); KJV: knowledge, meaning, [idiom] perfectly, understanding, wisdom.

H999 בִּינָה (bîynâh, bee-naw'): {understanding}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H998 (בִּינָה) KJV: knowledge.

H1000 בֵּיצָה (bêytsâh, bay-tsaw'): an egg (from its whiteness). Origin: from the same as H948 (בּוּץ); KJV: egg.

H1001 בִּירָא (bîyrâʼ, bee-raw'): a palace. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1002 (בִּירָה); KJV: palace.

H1002 בִּירָה (bîyrâh, bee-raw'): a castle or palace. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: palace.

H1003 בִּירָנִית (bîyrânîyth, bee-raw-neeth'): a fortress. Origin: from H1002 (בִּירָה); KJV: castle.

H1004 בַּיִת (bayith, bah'-yith): a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family, etc.). Origin: probably from H1129 (בָּנָה) abbreviated; KJV: court, daughter, door, [phrase] dungeon, family, [phrase] forth of, [idiom] great as would contain, hangings, home(born), (winter) house(-hold), inside(-ward), palace, place, [phrase] prison, [phrase] steward, [phrase] tablet, temple, web, [phrase] within(-out).

H1005 בַּיִת (bayith, bah-yith): {a house (in the greatest variation of applications, especially family, etc.)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1004 (בַּיִת) KJV: house.

H1006 בַּיִת (Bayith, bah'-yith): Bajith, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1004 (בַּיִת); KJV: Bajith.

H1007 בֵּית אָוֶן (Bêyth ʼÂven, bayth aw'-ven): Beth-Aven, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H205 (אָוֶן); house of vanity; KJV: Beth-aven.

H1008 בֵּית־אֵל (Bêyth-ʼÊl, bayth-ale'): Beth-El, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H410 (אֵל); house of God; KJV: Beth-el.

H1009 בֵּית אַרְבֵּאל (Bêyth ʼArbêʼl, bayth ar-bale'): Beth-Arbel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H695 (אֶרֶב) and H410 (אֵל); house of God's ambush; KJV: Beth-Arbel.

H1010 בֵּית בַּעַל מְעוֹן (Bêyth Baʻal Mᵉʻôwn, bayth bah'-al me-own'): Beth-Baal-Meon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H1168 (בַּעַל) and H4583 (מָעוֹן); house of Baal of (the) habitation of (apparently by transposition); or (shorter) בֵּית מְעוֹןlemma בֵּית מעוֹן missing vowel, corrected to בֵּית מְעוֹן; house of habitation of (Baal); KJV: Beth-baal-meon. Compare H1186 (בַּעַל מְעוֹן) and H1194 (בְּעֹן).

H1011 בֵּית בִּרְאִי (Bêyth Birʼîy, bayth bir-ee'): Beth-Biri, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H1254 (בָּרָא); house of a creative one; KJV: Bethbirei.

H1012 בֵּית בָּרָה (Bêyth Bârâh, bayth baw-raw'): Beth-Barah, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H5679 (עֲבָרָה); house of (the) ford; KJV: Beth-barah.

H1013 בֵּית־גָּדֵר (Bêyth-Gâdêr, bayth-gaw-dare'): Beth-Gader, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H1447 (גָּדֵר); house of (the) wall; KJV: Beth-gader.

H1014 בֵּית גָּמוּל (Bêyth Gâmûwl, bayth gaw-mool'): Beth-Gamul, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the passive participle of H1576 (גְּמוּל); house of (the) weaned; KJV: Beth-gamul.

H1015 בֵּית דִּבְלָתַיִם (Bêyth Diblâthayim, bayth dib-law-thah'-yim): Beth-Diblathajim, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the dual of H1690 (דְּבֵלָה); house of (the) two figcakes; KJV: Beth-diblathaim.

H1016 בֵּית־דָּגוֹן (Bêyth-Dâgôwn, bayth-daw-gohn'): Beth-Dagon, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H1712 (דָּגוֹן); house of Dagon; KJV: Beth-dagon.

H1017 בֵּית הָאֱלִי (Bêyth hâ-ʼĔlîy, bayth haw-el-ee'): a Beth-elite, or inhabitant of Bethel. Origin: patrial from H1008 (בֵּית־אֵל) with the article interposed; KJV: Bethelite.

H1018 בֵּית הָאֵצֶל (Bêyth hâʼêtsel, bayth haw-ay'-tsel): Beth-ha-Etsel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H681 (אֵצֶל) with the article interposed; house of the side; KJV: Beth-ezel.

H1019 בֵּית הַגִּלְגָּל (Bêyth hag-Gilgâl, bayth hag-gil gawl'): Beth-hag-Gilgal, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H1537 (גִּלְגָּל) with the article interposed; house of Gilgal (or rolling); KJV: Beth-gilgal.

H1020 בֵּית הַיְשִׁימוֹת (Bêyth ha-Yshîy-môwth, bayth hah-yesh-eemoth'): Beth-ha-Jeshimoth, a town East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the plural of H3451 (יְשִׁימַה) with the article interposed; house of the deserts; KJV: Beth-jeshimoth.

H1021 בֵּית הַכֶּרֶם (Bêyth hak-Kerem, bayth hak-keh'-rem): Beth-hak-Kerem, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H3754 (כֶּרֶם) with the article interposed; house of the vineyard; KJV: Beth-haccerem.

H1022 בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי (Bêyth hal-Lachmîy, bayth hal-lakh-mee'): a Beth-lechemite, or native of Bethlechem. Origin: patrial from H1035 (בֵּית לֶחֶם) with the article inserted; KJV: Bethlehemite.

H1023 בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָק (Bêyth ham-Merchâq, bayth ham-mer-khawk'): Beth-ham-Merchak, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H4801 (מֶרְחָק) with the article interposed; house of the breadth; KJV: place that was far off.

H1024 בֵּית הַמַּרְכָּבוֹת (Bêyth ham-Markâbôwth, bayth ham-markaw-both'): Beth-ham-Markaboth or Beth-Markaboth, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (shortened) בֵּית מַרְכָּבוֹת; from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the plural of H4818 (מֶרְכָּבָה) (with or without the article interposed); place of (the) chariots; KJV: Bethmarcaboth.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1025 to H1140
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1025 בֵּית הָעֵמֶק (Bêyth hâ-ʻÊmeq, bayth haw-Ay'-mek): Beth-ha-Emek, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H6010 (עֵמֶק) with the article interposed; house of the valley; KJV: Beth-emek.

H1026 בֵּית הָעֲרָבָה (Bêyth hâ-ʻĂrâbâh, bayth haw-ar-aw-baw): Beth-ha-Arabah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H6160 (עֲרָבָה) with the article interposed; house of the Desert; KJV: Beth-arabah.

H1027 בֵּית הָרָם (Bêyth hâ-Râm, bayth haw-rawm'): Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H7311 (רוּם) with the article interposed; house of the height; KJV: Beth-aram.

H1028 בֵּית הָרָן (Bêyth hâ-Rân, bayth haw-rawn'): Beth-ha-Ram, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: probably for H1027 (בֵּית הָרָם); KJV: Beth-haran.

H1029 בֵּית הַשִּׁטָּה (Bêyth hash-Shiṭṭâh, bayth hash-shit-taw'): Beth-hash-Shittah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H7848 (שִׁטָּה) with the article interposed; house of the acacia; KJV: Beth-shittah.

H1030 בֵּית הַשִּׁמְשִׁי (Bêyth hash-Shimshîy, bayth hash-shim-shee'): a Beth-shimshite, or inhabitant of Bethshemesh. Origin: patrial from H1053 (בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ) with the article inserted; KJV: Bethshemite.

H1031 בֵּית חׇגְלָה (Bêyth Choglâh, bayth chog-law'): Beth-Choglah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the same as H2295 (חׇגְלָה); house of a partridge; KJV: Beth-hoglah.

H1032 בֵּית חוֹרוֹן (Bêyth Chôwrôwn, bayth kho-rone'): Beth-Choron, the name of two adjoining places in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H2356 (חוֹר); house of hollowness; KJV: Beth-horon.

H1033 בֵּית כַּר (Bêyth Kar, bayth kar): Beth-Car, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H3733 (כַּר); house of pasture; KJV: Beth-car.

H1034 בֵּית לְבָאוֹת (Bêyth Lᵉbâʼôwth, bayth leb-aw-oth'): Beth-Lebaoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the plural of H3833 (לָבִיא); house of lionesses; KJV: Beth-lebaoth. Compare H3822 (לְבָאוֹת).

H1035 בֵּית לֶחֶם (Bêyth Lechem, bayth leh'-khem): Beth-Lechem, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H3899 (לֶחֶם); house of bread; KJV: Bethlehem.

H1036 בֵּית לְעַפְרָה (Bêyth lᵉ-ʻAphrâh, bayth le-af-raw'): Beth-le-Aphrah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the feminine of H6083 (עָפָר) (with preposition interposed); house to (i.e. of) dust; KJV: house of Aphrah.

H1037 בֵּית מִלּוֹא (Bêyth Millôwʼ, bayth mil-lo'): Beth-Millo, the name of two citadels. Origin: or בֵּית מִלֹּא; from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H4407 (מִלּוֹא); house of (the) rampart; KJV: house of Millo.

H1038 בֵּית מַעֲכָה (Bêyth Maʻăkâh, bayth mah-ak-aw'): Beth-Maakah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H4601 (מַעֲכָה); house of Maakah; KJV: Beth-maachah.

H1039 בֵּית נִמְרָה (Bêyth Nimrâh, bayth nim-raw'): Beth-Nimrah, a place east of the Jordan. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and the feminine of H5246 (נָמֵר); house of (the) leopard; KJV: Beth-Nimrah. Compare H5247 (נִמְרָה).

H1040 בֵּית עֵדֶן (Bêyth ʻÊden, bayth ay'-den): Beth-Eden, a place in Syria. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H5730 (עֵדֶן); house of pleasure; KJV: Beth-eden.

H1041 בֵּית עַזְמָוֶת (Bêyth ʻAzmâveth, bayth az-maw'-veth): house of Azmaveth, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H5820 (עַזְמָוֶת); KJV: Bethaz-maveth. Compare H5820 (עַזְמָוֶת).

H1042 בֵּית עֲנוֹת (Bêyth ʻĂnôwth, bayth an-oth'): Beth-Anoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and a plural from H6030 (עָנָה); house of replies; KJV: Beth-anoth.

H1043 בֵּית עֲנָת (Bêyth ʻĂnâth, bayth an-awth'): Beth-Anath, a place in Palestine. Origin: an orthographical variation for H1042 (בֵּית עֲנוֹת); KJV: Beth-anath.

H1044 בֵּית עֵקֶד (Bêyth ʻÊqed, bayth ay'-ked): Beth-Eked, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and a derivative of H6123 (עָקַד); house of (the) binding (for sheep-shearing); KJV: shearing house.

H1045 בֵּית עַשְׁתָּרוֹת (Bêyth ʻAshtârôwth, bayth ash-taw-roth'): Beth-Ashtaroth, a place in Palestine. Origin: ; from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H6252 (עַשְׁתָּרוֹת); house of Ashtoreths; KJV: house of Ashtaroth. Compare H1203 (בְּעֶשְׁתְּרָה), H6252 (עַשְׁתָּרוֹת).

H1046 בֵּית פֶּלֶט (Bêyth Peleṭ, bayth peh'-let): Beth-Palet, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H6412 (פָּלִיט); house of escape; KJV: Beth-palet.

H1047 בֵּית פְּעוֹר (Bêyth Pᵉʻôwr, bayth pe-ore'): Beth-Peor, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H6465 (פְּעוֹר); house of Peor; KJV: Bethpeor.

H1048 בֵּית פַּצֵּץ (Bêyth Patstsêts, bayth pats-tsates'): Beth-Patstsets, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and a derivative from H6327 (פּוּץ); house of dispersion; KJV: Beth-pazzez.

H1049 בֵּית צוּר (Bêyth Tsûwr, bayth tsoor'): Beth-Tsur, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H6697 (צוּר); house of (the) rock; KJV: Beth-zur.

H1050 בֵּית רְחוֹב (Bêyth Rᵉchôwb, bayth re-khobe'): Beth-Rechob, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H7339 (רְחֹב); house of (the) street; KJV: Beth-rehob.

H1051 בֵּית רָפָא (Bêyth Râphâʼ, bayth raw-faw'): Beth-Rapha, an Israelite. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H7497 (רָפָא); house of (the) giant; KJV: Beth-rapha.

H1052 בֵּית שְׁאָן (Bêyth Shᵉʼân, bayth she-awn'): Beth-Shean or Beth-Shan, a place in Palestine. Origin: or בֵּית שָׁן; from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H7599 (שָׁאַן); house of ease; KJV: Beth-shean, Beth-Shan.

H1053 בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ (Bêyth Shemesh, bayth sheh'-mesh): Beth-Shemesh, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); house of (the) sun; KJV: Beth-shemesh.

H1054 בֵּית תַּפּוּחַ (Bêyth Tappûwach, bayth tap-poo'-akh): Beth-Tappuach, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1004 (בַּיִת) and H8598 (תַּפּוּחַ); house of (the) apple; KJV: Beth-tappuah.

H1055 בִּיתָן (bîythân, bee-thawn'): a palace (i.e. large house). Origin: probably from H1004 (בַּיִת); KJV: palace.

H1056 בָּכָא (Bâkâʼ, baw-kaw'): Baca, a valley in Palestine. Origin: from H1058 (בָּכָה), weeping; KJV: Baca.

H1057 בָּכָא (bâkâʼ, baw-kaw'): the weeping tree (some gum-distilling tree, perhaps the balsam). Origin: the same as H1056 (בָּכָא); KJV: mulberry tree.

H1058 בָּכָה (bâkâh, baw-kaw'): to weep; generally to bemoan. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, bewail, complain, make lamentation, [idiom] more, mourn, [idiom] sore, [idiom] with tears, weep.

H1059 בֶּכֶה (bekeh, beh'-keh): a weeping. Origin: from H1058 (בָּכָה); KJV: [idiom] sore.

H1060 בְּכוֹר (bᵉkôwr, bek-ore'): firstborn; hence, chief. Origin: from H1069 (בָּכַר); KJV: eldest (son), firstborn(-ling).

H1061 בִּכּוּר (bikkûwr, bik-koor'): the first-fruits of the crop. Origin: from H1069 (בָּכַר); KJV: first fruit (-ripe (figuratively)), hasty fruit.

H1062 בְּכוֹרָה (bᵉkôwrâh, bek-o-raw'): the firstling of man or beast; abstractly primogeniture. Origin: or (short) בְּכֹרָה; feminine of H1060 (בְּכוֹר); KJV: birthright, firstborn(-ling).

H1063 בִּכּוּרָה (bikkûwrâh, bik-koo-raw'): the early fig. Origin: feminine of H1061 (בִּכּוּר); KJV: firstripe (fruit).

H1064 בְּכוֹרַת (Bᵉkôwrath, bek-o-rath'): Bekorath, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H1062 (בְּכוֹרָה); primogeniture; KJV: Bechorath.

H1065 בְּכִי (Bᵉkîy, bek-ee'): a weeping; by analogy, a dripping. Origin: from H1058 (בָּכָה); KJV: overflowing, [idiom] sore, (continual) weeping, wept.

H1066 בֹּכִים (Bôkîym, bo-keem'): Bo-kim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural active participle of H1058 (בָּכָה); (with the article) the weepers; KJV: Bochim.

H1067 בְּכִירָה (bᵉkîyrâh, bek-ee-raw'): the eldest daughter. Origin: feminine from H1069 (בָּכַר); KJV: firstborn.

H1068 בְּכִית (bᵉkîyth, bek-eeth'): a weeping. Origin: from H1058 (בָּכָה); KJV: mourning.

H1069 בָּכַר (bâkar, baw-kar'): to give the birthright. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to burst the womb, i.e. (causatively) bear or make early fruit (of woman or tree); also (as denominative from H1061 (בִּכּוּר)) KJV: make firstborn, be firstling, bring forth first child (new fruit).

H1070 בֶּכֶר (beker, beh'-ker): a young camel. Origin: from H1069 (בָּכַר) (in the sense of youth); KJV: dromedary.

H1071 בֶכֶר (Beker, beh'-ker): Beker, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H1070 (בֶּכֶר); KJV: Becher.

H1072 בִּכְרָה (bikrâh, bik-raw'): a young she-camel. Origin: feminine of H1070 (בֶּכֶר); KJV: dromedary.

H1073 בַּכֻּרָה (bakkurâh, bak-koo-raw'): a first-ripe fig. Origin: by orthographical variation for H1063 (בִּכּוּרָה); KJV: firstripe.

H1074 בֹּכְרוּ (Bôkᵉrûw, bo-ker-oo'): Bokeru, an Israelite. Origin: from H1069 (בָּכַר); first-born; KJV: Bocheru.

H1075 בִּכְרִי (Bikrîy, bik-ree'): Bikri, an Israelite. Origin: from H1069 (בָּכַר); youth-ful; KJV: Bichri.

H1076 בַּכְרִי (Bakrîy, bak-ree'): a Bakrite (collectively) or descendants of Beker. Origin: patronymically from H1071 (בֶכֶר); KJV: Bachrites.

H1077 בַּל (bal, bal): properly, a failure; by implication nothing; usually (adverb) not at all; also lest. Origin: from H1086 (בָּלָה); KJV: lest, neither, no, none (that...), not (any), nothing.

H1078 בֵּל (Bêl, bale): Bel, the Baal of the Babylonians. Origin: by contraction for H1168 (בַּעַל); KJV: Bel.

H1079 בָּל (bâl, bawl): properly, anxiety, i.e. (by implication) the heart (as its seat). Origin: (Aramaic) from H1080 (בְּלָא); KJV: heart.

H1080 בְּלָא (bᵉlâʼ, bel-aw'): to afflict. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1086 (בָּלָה) (but used only in a mental sense); KJV: wear out.

H1081 בַּלְאֲדָן (Balʼădân, bal-ad-awn'): Baladan, the name of a Babylonian prince. Origin: from H1078 (בֵּל) and H113 (אָדוֹן) (contracted); Bel (is his) lord; KJV: Baladan.

H1082 בָּלַג (bâlag, baw-lag'): to break off or loose (in a favorable or unfavorable sense), i.e. desist (from grief) or invade (with destruction). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: comfort, (recover) strength(-en).

H1083 בִּלְגַה (Bilgah, bil-gaw'): Bilgah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1082 (בָּלַג); desistance; KJV: Bilgah.

H1084 בִּלְגַּי (Bilgay, bil-gah'ee): Bilgai, an Israelite. Origin: from H1082 (בָּלַג); desistant; KJV: Bilgai.

H1085 בִּלְדַּד (Bildad, bil-dad'): Bildad, one of Job's friends. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Bildad.

H1086 בָּלָה (bâlâh, baw-law'): to fail; by implication to wear out, decay (causatively, consume, spend). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consume, enjoy long, become (make, wax) old, spend, waste.

H1087 בָּלֶה (bâleh, baw-leh'): worn out. Origin: from H1086 (בָּלָה); KJV: old.

H1088 בָּלָה (Bâlâh, baw-law'): Balah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H1087 (בָּלֶה); failure; KJV: Balah.

H1089 בָּלַהּ (bâlahh, baw-lah'): to palpitate; hence, (causatively) to terrify. Origin: a primitive root (rather by transposition for H926 (בָּהַל)); KJV: trouble.

H1090 בִּלְהָה (Bilhâh, bil-haw'): Bilhah, the name of one of Jacob's concubines; also of a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1089 (בָּלַהּ); timid; KJV: Bilhah.

H1091 בַּלָּהָה (ballâhâh, bal-law-haw'): alarm; hence, destruction. Origin: from H1089 (בָּלַהּ); KJV: terror, trouble.

H1092 בִּלְהָן (Bilhân, bil-hawn'): Bilhan, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite. Origin: from H1089 (בָּלַהּ); timid; KJV: Bilhan.

H1093 בְּלוֹ (bᵉlôw, bel-o'): excise (on articles consumed). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H1086 (בָּלָה); KJV: tribute.

H1094 בְּלוֹא (bᵉlôwʼ, bel-o'): (only in plural construction) rags. Origin: or (fully) בְּלוֹי; from H1086 (בָּלָה); KJV: old.

H1095 בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר (Bêlṭᵉshaʼtstsar, bale-tesh-ats-tsar'): Belteshatstsar, the Babylonian name of Daniel. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Belteshazzar.

H1096 בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר (Bêlṭᵉshaʼtstsar, bale-tesh-ats-tsar'): {Belteshatstsar, the Babylonian name of Daniel}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1095 (בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר) KJV: Belteshazzar.

H1097 בְּלִי (bᵉlîy, bel-ee'): properly, failure, i.e. nothing or destruction; usually (with preposition) without, not yet, because not, as long as, etc. Origin: from H1086 (בָּלָה); KJV: corruption, ig(norantly), for lack of, where no...is, so that no, none, not, un(awares), without.

H1098 בְּלִיל (bᵉlîyl, bel-eel'): mixed, i.e. (specifically) feed (for cattle). Origin: from H1101 (בָּלַל); KJV: corn, fodder, provender.

H1099 בְּלִימָה (bᵉlîymâh, bel-ee-mah'): (as indefinitely) nothing whatever. Origin: from H1097 (בְּלִי) and H4100 (מָה); KJV: nothing.

H1100 בְּלִיַּעַל (bᵉlîyaʻal, bel-e-yah'-al): without profit, worthlessness; by extension, destruction, wickedness. Origin: from H1097 (בְּלִי) and H3276 (יַעַל);(often in connection with H376 (אִישׁ), H802 (אִשָּׁה), H1121 (בֵּן), etc.) KJV: Belial, evil, naughty, ungodly (men), wicked.

H1101 בָּלַל (bâlal, baw-lal'): to overflow (specifically with oil.); by implication, to mix; to fodder. Origin: a primitive root; (also denominatively from H1098 (בְּלִיל)) to fodder KJV: anoint, confound, [idiom] fade, mingle, mix (self), give provender, temper.

H1102 בָּלַם (bâlam, baw-lam'): to muzzle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be held in.

H1103 בָּלַס (bâlaç, baw-las'): to pinch sycamore figs (a process necessary to ripen them). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gatherer.

H1104 בָּלַע (bâlaʻ, baw-lah'): to make away with (specifically by swallowing); generally, to destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover, destroy, devour, eat up, be at end, spend up, swallow down (up).

H1105 בֶּלַע (belaʻ, beh'-lah): a gulp; figuratively, destruction. Origin: from H1104 (בָּלַע); KJV: devouring, that which he hath swallowed up.

H1106 בֶּלַע (Belaʻ, beh'-lah): Bela, the name of a place, also of an Edomite and of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H1105 (בֶּלַע); KJV: Bela.

H1107 בִּלְעֲדֵי (bilʻădêy, bil-ad-ay'): except, without, besides. Origin: or בַּלְעֲדֵי; constructive plural from H1077 (בַּל) and H5703 (עַד), not till, i.e. (as preposition or adverb) KJV: beside, not (in), save, without.

H1108 בַּלְעִי (Balʻîy, bel-ee'): a Belaite (collectively) or descendants of Bela. Origin: patronymically from H1106 (בֶּלַע); KJV: Belaites.

H1109 בִּלְעָם (Bilʻâm, bil-awm'): Bilam, a Mesopotamian prophet; also a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H1077 (בַּל) and H5971 (עַם); not (of the) people, i.e. foreigner; KJV: Balaam, Bileam.

H1110 בָּלַק (bâlaq, baw-lak'): to annihilate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) waste.

H1111 בָּלָק (Bâlâq, baw-lawk'): Balak, a Moabitish king. Origin: from H1110 (בָּלַק); waster; KJV: Balak.

H1112 בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר (Bêlshaʼtstsar, bale-shats-tsar'): Belshatstsar, a Babylonian king. Origin: or בֵּלְאשַׁצַּרlemma בֵּלְאשַׁצּר missing vowel, corrected to בֵּלְאשַׁצַּר; of foreign origin (compare H1095 (בֵּלְטְשַׁאצַּר)); KJV: Belshazzar.

H1113 בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר (Bêlshaʼtstsar, bale-shats-tsar'): {Belshatstsar, a Babylonian king}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1112 (בֵּלְשַׁאצַּר) KJV: Belshazzar.

H1114 בִּלְשָׁן (Bilshân, bil-shawn'): Bilshan, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Bilshan.

H1115 בִּלְתִּי (biltîy, bil-tee'): properly, a failure of, i.e. (used only as a negative particle, usually with a prepositional prefix) not, except, without, unless, besides, because not, until, etc. Origin: constructive feminine of H1086 (בָּלָה) (equivalent to H1097 (בְּלִי)); KJV: because un(satiable), beside, but, [phrase] continual, except, from, lest, neither, no more, none, not, nothing, save, that no, without.

H1116 בָּמָה (bâmâh, bam-maw'): an elevation. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be high); KJV: height, high place, wave.

H1117 בָּמָה (Bâmâh, baw-maw'): Bamah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1116 (בָּמָה); KJV: Bamah. See also H1120 (בָּמוֹת).

H1118 בִּמְהָל (Bimhâl, bim-hawl'): Bimhal, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H4107 (מָהַל) with prepositional prefix; with pruning; KJV: Bimhal.

H1119 בְּמוֹ (bᵉmôw, bem-o'): in, with, by, etc. Origin: prolongation for prepositional prefix; KJV: for, in into, through.

H1120 בָּמוֹת (Bâmôwth, baw-moth'): Bamoth or Bamoth-Baal, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: plural of H1116 (בָּמָה); heights; or (fully) בָּמוֹת בַּעַל; from the same and H1168 (בַּעַל); heights of Baal; KJV: Bamoth, Bamoth-baal.

H1121 בֵּן (bên, bane): a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense (of literal and figurative relationship, including grandson, subject, nation, quality or condition, etc., (like father or brother), etc.). Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: [phrase] afflicted, age, (Ahoh-) (Ammon-) (Hachmon-) (Lev-) ite, (anoint-) ed one, appointed to, ([phrase]) arrow, (Assyr-) (Babylon-) (Egypt-) (Grec-) ian, one born, bough, branch, breed, [phrase] (young) bullock, [phrase] (young) calf, [idiom] came up in, child, colt, [idiom] common, [idiom] corn, daughter, [idiom] of first, [phrase] firstborn, foal, [phrase] very fruitful, [phrase] postage, [idiom] in, [phrase] kid, [phrase] lamb, ([phrase]) man, meet, [phrase] mighty, [phrase] nephew, old, ([phrase]) people, [phrase] rebel, [phrase] robber, [idiom] servant born, [idiom] soldier, son, [phrase] spark, [phrase] steward, [phrase] stranger, [idiom] surely, them of, [phrase] tumultuous one, [phrase] valiant(-est), whelp, worthy, young (one), youth.

H1122 בֵּן (Bên, bane): Ben, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H1121 (בֵּן); KJV: Ben.

H1123 בֵּן (bên, bane): {a son (as a builder of the family name), in the widest sense}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1121 (בֵּן) KJV: child, son, young.

H1124 בְּנָא (bᵉnâʼ, ben-aw'): to build. Origin: (Aramaic) or בְּנָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: build, make.

H1125 בֶּן־אֲבִינָדָב (Ben-ʼĂbîynâdâb, ben-ab-ee''-naw-dawb'): Ben-Abinadab, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H40 (אֲבִימֶלֶךְ); (the) son of Abinadab; KJV: the son of Abinadab.

H1126 בֶּן־אוֹנִי (Ben-ʼÔwnîy, ben-o-nee'): Ben-Oni, the original name of Benjamin. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H205 (אָוֶן); son of my sorrow; KJV: Ben-oni.

H1127 בֶּן־גֶּבֶר (Ben-Geber, ben-gheh'-ber): Ben-Geber, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H1397 (גֶּבֶר); son of (the) hero; KJV: the son of Geber.

H1128 בֶּן־דֶּקֶר (Ben-Deqer, ben-deh'-ker): Ben-Deker, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and a derivative of H1856 (דָּקַר); son of piercing (or of a lance); KJV: the son of Dekar.

H1129 בָּנָה (bânâh, baw-naw'): to build (literally and figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (begin to) build(-er), obtain children, make, repair, set (up), [idiom] surely.

H1130 בֶּן־הֲדַד (Ben-Hădad, ben-had-ad'): Ben-Hadad, the name of several Syrian kings. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H1908 (הֲדַד); son of Hadad; KJV: Benhadad.

H1131 בִּנּוּי (Binnûwy, bin-noo'-ee): Binnui, an Israelite. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); built up; KJV: Binnui.

H1132 בֶּן־זוֹחֵת (Ben-Zôwchêth, ben-zo-khayth'): Ben-Zocheth, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H2105 (זוֹחֵת); son of Zocheth; KJV: Ben-zoketh.

H1133 בֶּן־חוּר (Ben-Chûwr, ben-khoor'): Ben-Chur, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H2354 (חוּר); son of Chur; KJV: the son of Hur.

H1134 בֶּן־חַיִל (Ben-Chayil, ben-khah'-yil): Ben-Chail, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H2428 (חַיִל); son of might; KJV: Ben-hail.

H1135 בֶּן־חָנָן (Ben-Chânân, ben-khaw-nawn'): Ben-Chanan, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H2605 (חָנָן); son of Chanan; KJV: Ben-hanan.

H1136 בֶּן־חֶסֶד (Ben-Cheçed, ben-kheh'-sed): Ben-Chesed, an Israelite. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H2617 (חֵסֵד); son of kindness; KJV: the son of Hesed.

H1137 בָּנִי (Bânîy, baw-nee'): Bani, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); built; KJV: Bani.

H1138 בֻּנִּי (Bunnîy, boon-nee'): Bunni or Buni, an Israelite. Origin: or (fuller) בּוּנִי; from H1129 (בָּנָה); built; KJV: Bunni.

H1139 בְּנֵי־בְּרַק (Bᵉnêy-Bᵉraq, ben-ay'-ber-ak'): sons of lightning, Bene-berak, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the plural construction of H1121 (בֵּן) and H1300 (בָּרָק); KJV: Bene-barak.

H1140 בִּנְיָה (binyâh, bin-yaw'): a structure. Origin: feminine from H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: building.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1141 to H1261
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1141 בְּנָיָה (Bᵉnâyâh, ben-aw-yaw'): Benajah, the name of twelve Israelites. Origin: or בּנָיָהוּ; (prolonged) from H1129 (בָּנָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has built; KJV: Benaiah.

H1142 בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן (Bᵉnêy Yaʻăqân, ben-ay' yah-ak-awn'): Bene-Jaakan, a place in the Desert. Origin: from the plural of H1121 (בֵּן) and H3292 (יַעֲקָן); sons of Yaakan; KJV: Bene-jaakan.

H1143 בֵּנַיִם (bênayim, bay-nah'-yim): a double interval, i.e. the space between two armies. Origin: dual of H996 (בֵּין); KJV: [phrase] champion.

H1144 בִּנְיָמִין (Binyâmîyn, bin-yaw-mene'): Binjamin, youngest son of Jacob; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H3225 (יָמִין); son of (the) right hand; KJV: Benjamin.

H1145 בֶּן־יְמִינִי (Ben-yᵉmîynîy, ben-yem-ee-nee'): a Benjaminite, or descendent of Benjamin. Origin: sometimes (with the article inserted) בֵּן־הַיּמִינִי; with H376 (אִישׁ) inserted (1 Samuel 9:1) בֶּן־אִישׁ ימִינִי; son of a man of Jemini; or shortened אִישׁ יְמִינִי; (1 Samuel 9:4; Esther 2:5) a man of Jemini, or (1 Samuel 20:1) simply יְמִינִיxlit Yᵉmînîy corrected to Yᵉmîynîy; a Jeminite; (plural) בְּנֵי יְמִינִיxlit Bᵉnîy corrected to Bᵉnêy; patron from H1144 (בִּנְיָמִין); KJV: Benjamite, of Benjamin.

H1146 בִּנְיָן (binyân, bin-yawn'): an edifice. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: building.

H1147 בִּנְיָן (binyân, bin-yawn'): {an edifice}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1146 (בִּנְיָן) KJV: building.

H1148 בְּנִינוּ (Bᵉnîynûw, ben-ee-noo'): Beninu, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H1121 (בֵּן) with pron. suff.; our son; KJV: Beninu.

H1149 בְּנַס (bᵉnaç, ben-as'): to be enraged. Origin: (Aramaic) of uncertain affinity; KJV: be angry.

H1150 בִּנְעָא (Binʻâʼ, bin-aw'): Bina or Binah, an Israelite. Origin: or בִּנְעָה; of uncertain derivation; KJV: Binea, Bineah.

H1151 בֶּן־עַמִּי (Ben-ʻAmmîy, ben-am-mee'): Ben-Ammi, a son of Lot. Origin: from H1121 (בֵּן) and H5971 (עַם) with pronomial suffix; son of my people; KJV: Ben-ammi.

H1152 בְּסוֹדְיָה (Bᵉçôwdᵉyâh, bes-o-deh-yaw'): Besodejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H5475 (סוֹד) and H3050 (יָהּ) with prepositional prefix; in (the) counsel of Jehovah; KJV: Besodeiah.

H1153 בְּסַי (Bᵉçay, bes-ah'-ee): Besai, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from H947 (בּוּס); domineering; KJV: Besai.

H1154 בֶּסֶר (beçer, beh'-ser): an immature grape. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be sour; KJV: unripe grape.

H1155 בֹּסֶר (bôçer, bo'ser): {an immature grape}. Origin: from the same as H1154 (בֶּסֶר) KJV: sour grape.

H1156 בְּעָא (bᵉʻâʼ, beh-aw'): to seek or ask. Origin: (Aramaic) or בְּעָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1158 (בָּעָה); KJV: ask, desire, make (petition), pray, request, seek.

H1157 בְּעַד (bᵉʻad, beh-ad'): in up to or over against; generally at, beside, among, behind, for, etc. Origin: from H5704 (עַד) with prepositional prefix; KJV: about, at by (means of), for, over, through, up (-on), within.

H1158 בָּעָה (bâʻâh, baw-aw'): to gush over, i.e. to swell; (figuratively) to desire earnestly; by implication to ask. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cause, inquire, seek up, swell out.

H1159 בָּעוּ (bâʻûw, baw-oo'): a request. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1156 (בְּעָא); KJV: petition.

H1160 בְּעוֹר (Bᵉʻôwr, beh-ore'): Beor, the name of the father of an Edomitish king; also of that of Balaam. Origin: from H1197 (בָּעַר) (in the sense of burning); a lamp; KJV: Beor.

H1161 בִּעוּתִים (biʻûwthîym, be-oo-theme'): alarms. Origin: masculine plural from H1204 (בָּעַת); KJV: terrors.

H1162 בֹּעַז (Bôʻaz, bo'-az): Boaz, the ancestor of David; also the name of a pillar in front of the temple. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: Boaz.

H1163 בָּעַט (bâʻaṭ, baw-at'): to trample down, i.e. (figuratively) despise. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: kick.

H1164 בְּעִי (bᵉʻîy, beh-ee'): a prayer. Origin: from H1158 (בָּעָה); KJV: grave.

H1165 בְּעִיר (bᵉʻîyr, beh-ere'): cattle. Origin: from H1197 (בָּעַר) (in the sense of eating); KJV: beast, cattle.

H1166 בָּעַל (bâʻal, baw-al'): to be master; hence, to marry. Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative from H1167 (בַּעַל) KJV: have dominion (over), be husband, marry(-ried, [idiom] wife).

H1167 בַּעַל (baʻal, bah'-al): a master; hence, a husband, or (figuratively) owner (often used with another noun in modifications of this latter sense). Origin: from H1166 (בָּעַל); KJV: [phrase] archer, [phrase] babbler, [phrase] bird, captain, chief man, [phrase] confederate, [phrase] have to do, [phrase] dreamer, those to whom it is due, [phrase] furious, those that are given to it, great, [phrase] hairy, he that hath it, have, [phrase] horseman, husband, lord, man, [phrase] married, master, person, [phrase] sworn, they of.

H1168 בַּעַל (Baʻal, bah'-al): Baal, a Phoenician deity. Origin: the same as H1167 (בַּעַל); KJV: Baal, (plural) Baalim.

H1169 בְּעֵל (bᵉʻêl, beh-ale'): {a master; hence, a husband,}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1167 (בַּעַל) KJV: [phrase] chancellor.

H1170 בַּעַל בְּרִית (Baʻal Bᵉrîyth, bah'-al ber-eeth'): Baal-Berith, a special deity of the Shechemites. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H1285 (בְּרִית); Baal of (the) covenant; KJV: Baal-berith.

H1171 בַּעַל גָּד (Baʻal Gâd, bah'-al gawd): Baal-Gad, a place in Syria. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H1409 (גָּד); Baal of Fortune; KJV: Baal-gad.

H1172 בַּעֲלָה (baʻălâh, bah-al-aw'): a mistress. Origin: feminine of H1167 (בַּעַל); KJV: that hath, mistress.

H1173 בַּעֲלָה (Baʻălâh, bah-al-aw'): Baalah, the name of three places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1172 (בַּעֲלָה); KJV: Baalah.

H1174 בַּעַל הָמוֹן (Baʻal Hâmôwn, bah'-al haw-mone'): Baal-Hamon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and H1995 (הָמוֹן); possessor of a multitude; KJV: Baal-hamon.

H1175 בְּעָלוֹת (Bᵉʻâlôwth, beh-aw-loth'): Bealoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H1172 (בַּעֲלָה); mistresses; KJV: Bealoth, in Aloth (by mistake for a plural from H5927 (עָלָה) with prepositional prefix).

H1176 בַּעַל זְבוּב (Baʻal Zᵉbûwb, bah'-al zeb-oob'): Baal-Zebub, a special deity of the Ekronites. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H2070 (זְבוּב); Baal of (the) Fly; KJV: Baal-zebub.

H1177 בַּעַל חָנָן (Baʻal Chânân, bah'-al khaw-nawn'): Baal-Chanan, the name of an Edomite, also of an Israelite. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and H2603 (חָנַן); possessor of grace; KJV: Baal-hanan.

H1178 בַּעַל חָצוֹר (Baʻal Châtsôwr, bah'-al khaw-tsore'): Baal-Chatsor, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and a modification of H2691 (חָצֵר); possessor of a village; KJV: Baal-hazor.

H1179 בַּעַל חֶרְמוֹן (Baʻal Chermôwn, bah'-al kher-mone'): Baal-Chermon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and H2768 (חֶרְמוֹן); possessor of Hermon; KJV: Baal-hermon.

H1180 בַּעֲלִי (Baʻălîy, bah-al-ee'): Baali, a symbolical name for Jehovah. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) with pron. suff.; my master; KJV: Baali.

H1181 בַּעֲלֵי בָּמוֹת (Baʻălêy Bâmôwth, bah-al-ay' baw-moth'): Baale-Bamoth, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from the plural of H1168 (בַּעַל) and the plural of H1116 (בָּמָה); Baals of (the) heights; KJV: lords of the high places.

H1182 בְּעֶלְיָדָע (Bᵉʻelyâdâʻ, beh-el-yaw-daw'): Beeljada, an Israelite. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H3045 (יָדַע); Baal has known; KJV: Beeliada.

H1183 בְּעַלְיָה (Bᵉʻalyâh, beh-al-yaw'): Bealjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah (is) master; KJV: Bealiah.

H1184 בַּעֲלֵי יְהוּדָה (Baʻălêy Yᵉhûwdâh, bah-al-ay' yeh-hoo-daw'): Baale-Jehudah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the plural of H1167 (בַּעַל) and H3063 (יְהוּדָה); masters of Judah; KJV: Baale of Judah.

H1185 בַּעֲלִיס (Baʻălîyç, bah-al-ece'): Baalis, an Ammonitish king. Origin: probably from a derivative of H5965 (עָלַס) with prepositional prefix; in exultation; KJV: Baalis.

H1186 בַּעַל מְעוֹן (Baʻal Mᵉʻôwn, bah-al meh-one'): Baal-Meon, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H4583 (מָעוֹן); Baal of (the) habitation (of) (compare H1010 (בֵּית בַּעַל מְעוֹן)); KJV: Baal-meon.

H1187 בַּעַל פְּעוֹר (Baʻal Pᵉʻôwr, bah'-al peh-ore'): Baal-Peor, a Moabitish deity. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H6465 (פְּעוֹר); Baal of Peor; KJV: Baal-peor.

H1188 בַּעַל פְּרָצִים (Baʻal Pᵉrâtsîym, bah'-al per-aw-tseem'): Baal-Peratsim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and the plural of H6556 (פֶּרֶץ); possessor of breaches; KJV: Baal-perazim.

H1189 בַּעַל צְפוֹן (Baʻal Tsᵉphôwn, bah'-al tsef-one'): Baal-Tsephon, a place in Eqypt. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H6828 (צָפוֹן) (in the sense of cold) (according to others an Egyptian form of Typhon, the destroyer); Baal of winter; KJV: Baal-zephon.

H1190 בַּעַל שָׁלִשָׁה (Baʻal Shâlishâh, bah'-al shaw-lee-shaw'): Baal of Shalishah, Baal-Shalishah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1168 (בַּעַל) and H8031 (שָׁלִשָׁה); KJV: Baal-shalisha.

H1191 בַּעֲלָת (Baʻălâth, bah-al-awth'): Baalath, a place in Palestine. Origin: a modification of H1172 (בַּעֲלָה); mistressship; KJV: Baalath.

H1192 בַּעֲלַת בְּאֵר (Baʻălath Bᵉʼêr, bah-al-ath' beh-ayr'): Baalath-Beer, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1172 (בַּעֲלָה) and H875 (בְּאֵר); mistress of a well; KJV: Baalath-beer.

H1193 בַּעַל תָּמָר (Baʻal Tâmâr, bah'-al taw-mawr'): Baal-Tamar, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1167 (בַּעַל) and H8558 (תָּמָר); possessor of (the) palm-tree; KJV: Baal-tamar.

H1194 בְּעֹן (Bᵉʻôn, beh-ohn'): Beon, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: probably a contraction of H1010 (בֵּית בַּעַל מְעוֹן); KJV: Beon.

H1195 בַּעֲנָא (Baʻănâʼ, bah-an-aw'): Banana, the name of four Israelite. Origin: the same as H1196 (בַּעֲנָה); KJV: Baana, Baanah.

H1196 בַּעֲנָה (Baʻănâh, bah-an-aw'): Baanah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from a derivative of H6031 (עָנָה) with prepositional prefix; in affliction KJV: Baanah.

H1197 בָּעַר (bâʻar, baw-ar'): to kindle, i.e. consume (by fire or by eating); to be(-come) brutish. Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative from H1198 (בַּעַר) KJV: be brutish, bring (put, take) away, burn, (cause to) eat (up), feed, heat, kindle, set (on fire), waste.

H1198 בַּעַר (baʻar, bah'-ar): properly, foot (as consumed); i.e. (by exten.) of cattle brutishness; (concretely) stupid. Origin: from H1197 (בָּעַר); KJV: brutish (person), foolish.

H1199 בָּעֲרָא (Bâʻărâʼ, bah-ar-aw'): Baara, an Israelitish woman. Origin: from H1198 (בַּעַר); brutish; KJV: Baara.

H1200 בְּעֵרָה (bᵉʻêrâh, be-ay-raw'): a burning. Origin: from H1197 (בָּעַר); KJV: fire.

H1201 בַּעְשָׁא (Baʻshâʼ, bah-shaw'): Basha, a king of Israel. Origin: from an unused root meaning to stink; offensiveness; KJV: Baasha.

H1202 בַּעֲשֵׂיָה (Baʻăsêyâh, bah-as-ay-yaw'): Baasejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה) and H3050 (יָהּ) with a prepositional prefix; in (the) work of Jah; KJV: Baaseiah.

H1203 בְּעֶשְׁתְּרָה (Bᵉʻeshtᵉrâh, beh-esh-ter-aw'): Beeshterah, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H6251 (עַשְׁתְּרָה) (as singular of H6252 (עַשְׁתָּרוֹת)) with a prepositional prefix; with Ashtoreth; KJV: Beeshterah.

H1204 בָּעַת (bâʻath, baw-ath'): to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: affright, be (make) afraid, terrify, trouble.

H1205 בְּעָתָה (bᵉʻâthâh, beh-aw-thaw'): fear. Origin: from H1204 (בָּעַת); KJV: trouble.

H1206 בֹץ (bôts, botse): mud (as whitish clay). Origin: probably the same as H948 (בּוּץ); KJV: mire.

H1207 בִּצָּה (bitstsâh, bits-tsaw'): a swamp. Origin: intensive from H1206 (בֹץ); KJV: fen, mire(-ry place).

H1208 בָּצוֹר (bâtsôwr, baw-tsore'): inaccessible, i.e. lofty. Origin: from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: vintage (by confusion with H1210 (בָּצִיר)).

H1209 בֵּצַי (Bêtsay, bay-tsah'-ee): Betsai, the name of two Israelites. Origin: perhaps the same as H1153 (בְּסַי); KJV: Bezai.

H1210 בָּצִיר (bâtsîyr, baw-tseer'): clipped, i.e. the grape crop. Origin: from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: vintage.

H1211 בֶּצֶל (betsel, beh'-tsel): an onion. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to peel; KJV: onion.

H1212 בְּצַלְאֵל (Bᵉtsalʼêl, bets-al-ale'): Betsalel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably from H6738 (צֵל) and H410 (אֵל) with a prepositional prefix; in (the) shadow (i.e. protection) of God; KJV: Bezaleel.

H1213 בַּצְלוּת (Batslûwth, bats-looth'): Batsluth or Batslith, an Israelite. Origin: or בַּצְלִית; from the same as H1211 (בֶּצֶל)xlit bᵉtsel corrected to betsel; a peeling; KJV: Bazlith, Bazluth.

H1214 בָּצַע (bâtsaʻ, baw-tsah'): figuratively, to finish, or (intransitively) stop. Origin: a primitive root to break off, i.e. (usually) plunder; KJV: (be) covet(-ous), cut (off), finish, fulfill, gain (greedily), get, be given to (covetousness), greedy, perform, be wounded.

H1215 בֶּצַע (betsaʻ, beh'-tsah): plunder; by extension, gain (usually unjust). Origin: from H1214 (בָּצַע); KJV: covetousness, (dishonest) gain, lucre, profit.

H1216 בָּצֵק (bâtsêq, baw-tsake'): perhaps to swell up, i.e. blister. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: swell.

H1217 בָּצֵק (bâtsêq, baw-tsake'): dough (as swelling by fermentation). Origin: from H1216 (בָּצֵק); KJV: dough, flour.

H1218 בׇּצְקַת (Botsqath, bots-cath'): Botscath, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1216 (בָּצֵק); a swell of ground; KJV: Bozcath, Boskath.

H1219 בָּצַר (bâtsar, baw-tsar'): to gather grapes; also to be isolated (i.e. inaccessible by height or fortification). Origin: a primitive root; to clip off; specifically (as denominative from H1210 (בָּצִיר)) KJV: cut off, (de-) fenced, fortify, (grape) gather(-er), mighty things, restrain, strong, wall (up), withhold.

H1220 בֶּצֶר (betser, beh'-tser): strictly a clipping, i.e. gold (as dug out). Origin: from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: gold defence.

H1221 בֶּצֶר (Betser, beh'-tser): Betser, a place in Palestine; also an Israelite. Origin: the same as H1220 (בֶּצֶר), an inaccessible spot; KJV: Bezer.

H1222 בְּצַר (bᵉtsar, bets-ar'): gold. Origin: another form for H1220 (בֶּצֶר); KJV: gold.

H1223 בׇּצְרָה (botsrâh, bots-raw'): an enclosure, i.e. sheep fold. Origin: feminine from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: Bozrah.

H1224 בׇּצְרָה (Botsrâh, bots-raw'): Botsrah, a place in Edom. Origin: the same as H1223 (בׇּצְרָה); KJV: Bozrah.

H1225 בִּצָּרוֹן (bitstsârôwn, bits-tsaw-rone'): a fortress. Origin: masculine intensive from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: stronghold.

H1226 בַּצֹּרֶת (batstsôreth, bats-tso'-reth): restraint (of rain), i.e. drought. Origin: feminine intensive from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: dearth, drought.

H1227 בַּקְבּוּק (Baqbûwq, bak-book'): Bakbuk, one of the Nethinim. Origin: the same as H1228 (בַּקְבֻּק)xlit baqbûk corrected to baqbuq; KJV: Bakbuk.

H1228 בַּקְבֻּק (baqbuq, bak-book'): a bottle (from the gurgling in emptying). Origin: from H1238 (בָּקַק); KJV: bottle, cruse.

H1229 בַּקְבֻּקְיָה (Baqbuqyâh, bak-book-yaw'): Bakbukjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1228 (בַּקְבֻּק)xlit baqbûk corrected to baqbuq and H3050 (יָהּ); emptying (i.e. wasting) of Jah; KJV: Bakbukiah.

H1230 בַּקְבַּקַּר (Baqbaqqar, bak-bak-kar'): Bakbakkar, an Israelite. Origin: reduplicated from H1239 (בָּקַר); searcher; KJV: Bakbakkar.

H1231 בֻּקִּי (Buqqîy, book-kee'): Bukki, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1238 (בָּקַק); wasteful; KJV: Bukki.

H1232 בֻּקִּיָּה (Buqqîyâh, book-kee-yaw'): Bukkijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1238 (בָּקַק) and H3050 (יָהּ); wasting of Jah; KJV: Bukkiah.

H1233 בְּקִיעַ (bᵉqîyaʻ, bek-ee'-ah): a fissure. Origin: from H1234 (בָּקַע); KJV: breach, cleft.

H1234 בָּקַע (bâqaʻ, baw-kah'): to cleave; generally, to rend, break, rip or open. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make a breach, break forth (into, out, in pieces, through, up), be ready to burst, cleave (asunder), cut out, divide, hatch, rend (asunder), rip up, tear, win.

H1235 בֶּקַע (beqaʻ, beh'-kah): a section (half) of ashekel, i.e. a beka (a weight and a coin). Origin: from H1234 (בָּקַע); KJV: bekah, half a shekel.

H1236 בִּקְעָא (biqʻâʼ, bik-aw'): {properly, a split, i.e. a wide level valley between mountains}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1237 (בִּקְעָה) KJV: plain.

H1237 בִּקְעָה (biqʻâh, bik-aw'): properly, a split, i.e. a wide level valley between mountains. Origin: from H1234 (בָּקַע); KJV: plain, valley.

H1238 בָּקַק (bâqaq, baw-kah'): to pour out, i.e. to empty, figuratively, to depopulate; by analogy, to spread out (as a fruitful vine). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) empty (out), fail, [idiom] utterly, make void.

H1239 בָּקַר (bâqar, baw-kar): properly, to plough, or (generally) break forth, i.e. (figuratively) to inspect, admire, care for, consider. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) inquire (-ry), (make) search, seek out.

H1240 בְּקַר (bᵉqar, bek-ar'): {properly, to plough, or (generally) break forth, i.e. (figuratively) to inspect, admire, care for, consider}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1239 (בָּקַר) KJV: inquire, make search.

H1241 בָּקָר (bâqâr, baw-kawr'): beef cattle or an animal of the ox family of either gender (as used for plowing); collectively, a herd. Origin: from H1239 (בָּקַר); KJV: beeve, bull ([phrase] -ock), [phrase] calf, [phrase] cow, great (cattle), [phrase] heifer, herd, kine, ox.

H1242 בֹּקֶר (bôqer, bo'-ker): properly, dawn (as the break of day); generally, morning. Origin: from H1239 (בָּקַר); KJV: ([phrase]) day, early, morning, morrow.

H1243 בַּקָּרָה (baqqârâh, bak-kaw-raw'): a looking after. Origin: intensive from H1239 (בָּקַר); KJV: seek out.

H1244 בִּקֹּרֶת (biqqôreth, bik-ko-reth): properly, examination, i.e. (by implication) punishment. Origin: from H1239 (בָּקַר); KJV: scourged.

H1245 בָּקַשׁ (bâqash, baw-kash'): to search out (by any method, specifically in worship or prayer); by implication, to strive after. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: ask, beg, beseech, desire, enquire, get, make inquisition, procure, (make) request, require, seek (for).

H1246 בַּקָּשָׁה (baqqâshâh, bak-kaw-shaw'): a petition. Origin: from H1245 (בָּקַשׁ); KJV: request.

H1247 בַּר (bar, bar): a son, grandson, etc. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1121 (בֵּן); KJV: [idiom] old, son.

H1248 בַּר (bar, bar): the heir (apparent to the throne). Origin: borrowed (as a title) from H1247 (בַּר); KJV: son.

H1249 בַּר (bar, bar): beloved; also pure, empty. Origin: from H1305 (בָּרַר) (in its various senses); KJV: choice, clean, clear, pure.

H1250 בָּר (bâr, bawr): grain of any kind (even while standing in the field); by extension the open country. Origin: or בַּר; from H1305 (בָּרַר) (in the sense of winnowing); KJV: corn, wheat.

H1251 בַּר (bar, bar): a field. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1250 (בָּר); KJV: field.

H1252 בֹּר (bôr, bore): purify. Origin: from H1305 (בָּרַר); KJV: cleanness, pureness.

H1253 בֹּר (bôr, bore): vegetable lye (from its cleansing); used as a soap forwashing, or a flux formetals. Origin: the same as H1252 (בֹּר); KJV: [idiom] never so, purely.

H1254 בָּרָא (bârâʼ, baw-raw'): (absolutely) to create; (qualified) to cut down (a wood), select, feed (as formative processes). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: choose, create (creator), cut down, dispatch, do, make (fat).

H1255 בְּרֹאדַךְ בַּלְאֲדָן (Bᵉrôʼdak Balʼădân, ber-o-dak' bal-ad-awn'): Berodak-Baladan, a Babylonian king. Origin: a variation of H4757 (מְרֹאדַךְ בַּלְאָדָן); KJV: Berodach-baladan.Birliy.

H1256 בְּרָאיָה (Bᵉrâʼyâh, ber-aw-yaw'): Berajah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1254 (בָּרָא) and H8050 (שְׁמוּאֵל); Jah has created; KJV: Beraiah.

H1257 בַּרְבֻּר (barbur, bar-boor'): a fowl (as fattened on grain). Origin: by reduplication from H1250 (בָּר); KJV: fowl.

H1258 בָּרַד (bârad, baw-rad'): to hail. Origin: a primitive root, KJV: hail.

H1259 בָּרָד (bârâd, baw-rawd'): hail. Origin: from H1258 (בָּרַד); KJV: hail(stones).

H1260 בֶּרֶד (Bered, beh'red): Bered, the name of a place south of Palestine, also of an Israelite. Origin: from H1258 (בָּרַד); hail; KJV: Bered.

H1261 בָּרֹד (bârôd, baw-rode'): spotted (as if with hail). Origin: from H1258 (בָּרַד); KJV: grisled.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1262 to H1385
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1262 בָּרָה (bârâh, baw-raw'): to select; to feed; to render clear. Origin: a primitive root; to select; also (as denominative from H1250 (בָּר)) to feed; also (as equivalent to H1305 (בָּרַר)) to render clear (Ecclesiastes 3:18) KJV: choose, (cause to) eat, manifest, (give) meat.

H1263 בָּרוּךְ (Bârûwk, baw-rook'): Baruk, the name of three Israelites. Origin: passive participle from H1288 (בָרַךְ); blessed; KJV: Baruch.

H1264 בְּרוֹם (bᵉrôwm, ber-ome'): damask (stuff of variegated thread). Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: rich apparel.

H1265 בְּרוֹשׁ (bᵉrôwsh, ber-osh'): a cypress (?) tree; hence, a lance or a musical instrument (as made of that wood). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: fir (tree).

H1266 בְּרוֹת (bᵉrôwth, ber-oth'): the cypress (or some elastic tree). Origin: a variation of H1265 (בְּרוֹשׁ); KJV: fir.

H1267 בָּרוּת (bârûwth, baw-rooth): food. Origin: from H1262 (בָּרָה); KJV: meat.

H1268 בֵּרוֹתָה (Bêrôwthâh, bay-ro-thaw'): Berothah or Berothai, a place north of Palestine. Origin: or בֵּרֹתַי; probably from H1266 (בְּרוֹת)lemma בֻּרוֹת first vowel, corrected to בְּרוֹת; cypress or cypresslike; KJV: Berothah, Berothai.

H1269 בִּרְזוֹת (Birzôwth, beer-zoth'): Birzoth, an Israelite. Origin: probably feminine plural from an unused root (apparently mean to pierce); holes; KJV: Birzavith (from the marg.).

H1270 בַּרְזֶל (barzel, bar-zel'): iron (as cutting); by extension, an iron implement. Origin: perhaps from the root of H1269 (בִּרְזוֹת); KJV: (ax) head, iron.

H1271 בַּרְזִלַּי (Barzillay, bar-zil-lah'-ee): Barzillai, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H1270 (בַּרְזֶל); iron-hearted; KJV: Barzillai.

H1272 בָּרַח (bârach, baw-rakh'): to bolt, i.e. figuratively, to flee suddenly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: chase (away); drive away, fain, flee (away), put to flight, make haste, reach, run away, shoot.

H1273 בַּרְחֻמִי (Barchumîy, bar-khoo-mee'): a Barchumite, or native of Bachurim. Origin: by transposition for H978 (בַּחֲרוּמִי); KJV: Barhumite.

H1274 בְּרִי (bᵉrîy, ber-ee'): fat. Origin: from H1262 (בָּרָה); KJV: fat.

H1275 בֵּרִי (Bêrîy, bay-ree'): Beri, an Israelite. Origin: probably by contraction from H882 (בְּאֵרִי); KJV: Beri.

H1276 בֵּרִי (Bêrîy, bay-ree'): (only in the plural and with the article) the Berites, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Berites.

H1277 בָּרִיא (bârîyʼ, baw-ree'): fatted or plump. Origin: from H1254 (בָּרָא) (in the sense of H1262 (בָּרָה)); KJV: fat ((fleshed), -ter), fed, firm, plenteous, rank.

H1278 בְּרִיאָה (bᵉrîyʼâh, ber-ee-aw'): a creation, i.e. a novelty. Origin: feminine from H1254 (בָּרָא); KJV: new thing.

H1279 בִּרְיָה (biryâh, beer-yaw'): food. Origin: feminine from H1262 (בָּרָה); KJV: meat.

H1280 בְּרִיחַ (bᵉrîyach, ber-ee'-akh): a bolt. Origin: from H1272 (בָּרַח); KJV: bar, fugitive.

H1281 בָּרִיחַ (bârîyach, baw-ree'-akh): a fugitive, i.e. the serpent (as fleeing), and the constellation by that name. Origin: or בָּרִחַ; (shortened) from H1272 (בָּרַח); KJV: crooked, noble, piercing.

H1282 בָּרִיחַ (Bârîyach, baw-ree'-akh): Bariach, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H1281 (בָּרִיחַ); KJV: Bariah.

H1283 בְּרִיעָה (Bᵉrîyʻâh, ber-ee'-aw): Beriah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: apparently from the feminine of H7451 (רַע) with a prepositional prefix; in trouble; KJV: Beriah.

H1284 בְּרִיעִי (Bᵉrîyʻîy, ber-ee-ee'): a Beriite (collectively) or descendants of Beriah. Origin: patronymically from H1283 (בְּרִיעָה); KJV: Beerites.

H1285 בְּרִית (bᵉrîyth, ber-eeth'): a compact (because made by passing between pieces of flesh). Origin: from H1262 (בָּרָה) (in the sense of cutting (like H1254 (בָּרָא))); KJV: confederacy, (con-) feder(-ate), covenant, league.

H1286 בְּרִית (Bᵉrîyth, ber-eeth'): Berith, a Shechemitish deity. Origin: the same as H1285 (בְּרִית); KJV: Berith.

H1287 בֹּרִית (bôrîyth, bo-reeth'): vegetable alkali. Origin: feminine of H1253 (בֹּר); KJV: sope.

H1288 בָרַךְ (bârak, baw-rak'): to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit); also (by euphemism) to curse (God or the king, as treason). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] abundantly, [idiom] altogether, [idiom] at all, blaspheme, bless, congratulate, curse, [idiom] greatly, [idiom] indeed, kneel (down), praise, salute, [idiom] still, thank.

H1289 בְּרַךְ (bᵉrak, ber-ak'): {to kneel; by implication to bless God (as an act of adoration), and (vice-versa) man (as a benefit); also (by euphemism) to curse (God or the king, as treason)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1288 (בָרַךְ) KJV: bless, kneel.

H1290 בֶּרֶךְ (berek, beh'-rek): a knee. Origin: from H1288 (בָרַךְ); KJV: knee.

H1291 בֶּרֶךְ (berek, beh'-rek): {a knee}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1290 (בֶּרֶךְ) KJV: knee.

H1292 בָּרַכְאֵל (Bârakʼêl, baw-rak-ale'): Barakel, the father of one of Job's friends. Origin: from H1288 (בָרַךְ) and H410 (אֵל), God has blessed; KJV: Barachel.

H1293 בְּרָכָה (Bᵉrâkâh, ber-aw-kaw'): benediction; by implication prosperity. Origin: from H1288 (בָרַךְ); KJV: blessing, liberal, pool, present.

H1294 בְּרָכָה (Bᵉrâkâh, ber-aw-kaw'): Berakah, the name of an Israelite, and also of a valley in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1293 (בְּרָכָה); KJV: Berachah.

H1295 בְּרֵכָה (bᵉrêkâh, ber-ay-kaw'): a reservoir (at which camels kneel as a resting-place). Origin: from H1288 (בָרַךְ); KJV: (fish-) pool.

H1296 בֶּרֶכְיָה (Berekyâh, beh-rek-yaw'): Berekjah, the name of six Israelites. Origin: or בֶּרֶכְיָהוּ; from H1290 (בֶּרֶךְ) and H3050 (יָהּ); knee (i.e. blessing) of Jah; KJV: Berachiah, Berechiah.

H1297 בְּרַם (bᵉram, ber-am'): properly, highly, i.e. surely; but used adversatively, however. Origin: (Aramaic) perhaps from H7313 (רוּם) with a prepositional prefix; KJV: but, nevertheless, yet.

H1298 בֶּרַע (Beraʻ, beh'-rah): Bera, a Sodomitish king. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Bera.

H1299 בָּרַק (bâraq, baw-rak'): to lighten (lightning). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast forth.

H1300 בָּרָק (bârâq, baw-rawk'): lightning; by analogy, a gleam; concretely, a flashing sword. Origin: from H1299 (בָּרַק); KJV: bright, glitter(-ing sword), lightning.

H1301 בָּרָק (Bârâq, baw-rawk'): Barak, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H1300 (בָּרָק); KJV: Barak.

H1302 בַּרְקוֹס (Barqôwç, bar-kose'): Barkos, one of the Nethimim. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Barkos.

H1303 בַּרְקָן (barqân, bar-kwan'): a thorn (perhaps as burning brightly). Origin: from H1300 (בָּרָק); KJV: brier.

H1304 בָּרֶקֶת (bâreqeth, baw-reh'-keth): a gem (as flashing), perhaps the emerald. Origin: or בָּרְקַתxlit bârᵉkath corrected to bârᵉqath; from H1300 (בָּרָק); KJV: carbuncle.

H1305 בָּרַר (bârar, baw-rar'): to clarify (i.e. brighten), examine, select. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make bright, choice, chosen, cleanse (be clean), clearly, polished, (shew self) pure(-ify), purge (out).

H1306 בִּרְשַׁע (Birshaʻ, beer-shah'): Birsha, a king of Gomorrah. Origin: probably from H7562 (רֶשַׁע) with a prepositional prefix; with wickedness; KJV: Birsha.

H1307 בֵּרֹתִי (Bêrôthîy, bay-ro-thee'): a Berothite, or inhabitant of Berothai. Origin: patrial from H1268 (בֵּרוֹתָה); KJV: Berothite.

H1308 בְּשׂוֹר (Bᵉsôwr, bes-ore'): Besor, a stream of Palestine. Origin: from H1319 (בָּשַׂר); cheerful; KJV: Besor.

H1309 בְּשׂוֹרָה (bᵉsôwrâh, bes-o-raw'): glad tidings; by implication, reward forgood news. Origin: or (shortened) בְּשֹׂרָה; feminine from H1319 (בָּשַׂר); KJV: reward for tidings.

H1310 בָּשַׁל (bâshal, baw-shal'): properly, to boil up; hence, to be done in cooking; figuratively to ripen. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bake, boil, bring forth, roast, seethe, sod (be sodden).

H1311 בָּשֵׁל (bâshêl, baw-shale'): boiled. Origin: from H1310 (בָּשַׁל); KJV: [idiom] at all, sodden.

H1312 בִּשְׁלָם (Bishlâm, bish-lawm'): Bishlam, a Persian. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Bishlam.

H1313 בָּשָׂם (bâsâm, baw-sawm'): the balsam plant. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be fragrant; (compare H5561 (סַם)) KJV: spice.

H1314 בֶּשֶׂם (besem, beh'-sem): fragrance; by implication, spicery; also the balsam plant. Origin: or בֹּשֶׂם; from the same as H1313 (בָּשָׂם); KJV: smell, spice, sweet (odour).

H1315 בׇּשְׂמַת (Bosmath, bos-math'): Bosmath, the name of a wife of Esau, and of a daughter of Solomon. Origin: feminine of H1314 (בֶּשֶׂם) (the second form); fragrance; KJV: Bashemath, Basmath.

H1316 בָּשָׁן (Bâshân, baw-shawn'): Bashan (often with the article), a region East of the Jordan. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Bashan.

H1317 בׇּשְׁנָה (boshnâh, bosh-naw'): shamefulness. Origin: feminine from H954 (בּוּשׁ); KJV: shame.

H1318 בָּשַׁס (bâshaç, baw-shas'): to trample down. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tread.

H1319 בָּשַׂר (bâsar, baw-sar'): properly, to be fresh, i.e. full (rosy, (figuratively) cheerful); to announce (glad news). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: messenger, preach, publish, shew forth, (bear, bring, carry, preach, good, tell good) tidings.

H1320 בָּשָׂר (bâsâr, baw-sawr'): flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphemistically) the pudenda of aman. Origin: from H1319 (בָּשַׂר); KJV: body, (fat, lean) flesh(-ed), kin, (man-) kind, [phrase] nakedness, self, skin.

H1321 בְּשַׁר (bᵉshar, bes-ar'): {flesh (from its freshness); by extension, body, person; also (by euphemistically) the pudenda of aman}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1320 (בָּשָׂר) KJV: flesh.

H1322 בֹּשֶׁת (bôsheth, bo'-sheth): shame (the feeling and the condition, as well as its cause); by implication (specifically) an idol. Origin: from H954 (בּוּשׁ); KJV: ashamed, confusion, [phrase] greatly, (put to) shame(-ful thing).

H1323 בַּת (bath, bath): a daughter (used in the same wide sense as other terms of relationship, literally and figuratively). Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה) (as feminine of H1121 (בֵּן)); KJV: apple (of the eye), branch, company, daughter, [idiom] first, [idiom] old, [phrase] owl, town, village.

H1324 בַּת (bath, bath): a bath or Hebrew measure (as a means of division) of liquids. Origin: probably from the same as H1327 (בַּתָּה); KJV: bath.

H1325 בַּת (bath, bath): {a bath or Hebrew measure (as a means of division) of liquids}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1324 (בַּת) KJV: bath.

H1326 בָּתָה (bâthâh, baw-thaw'): desolation. Origin: probably an orthographical variation for H1327 (בַּתָּה); KJV: waste.

H1327 בַּתָּה (battâh, bat-taw'): desolation. Origin: feminine from an unused root (meaning to break in pieces); KJV: desolate.

H1328 בְּתוּאֵל (Bᵉthûwʼêl, beth-oo-ale'): Bethuel, the name of a nephew of Abraham, and of a place in Palestine. Origin: apparently from the same as H1326 (בָּתָה) and H410 (אֵל); destroyed of God; KJV: Bethuel. Compare H1329 (בְּתוּל).

H1329 בְּתוּל (Bᵉthûwl, beth-ool'): Bethul (i.e. Bethuel), a place in Palestine. Origin: for H1328 (בְּתוּאֵל); KJV: Bethuel.

H1330 בְּתוּלָה (bᵉthûwlâh, beth-oo-law'): a virgin (from her privacy); sometimes (by continuation) a bride; also (figuratively) a city or state. Origin: feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to separate; KJV: maid, virgin.

H1331 בְּתוּלִים (bᵉthûwlîym, beth-oo-leem'): (collectively and abstractly) virginity; by implication and concretely, the tokens of it. Origin: masculine plural of the same as H1330 (בְּתוּלָה); KJV: [idiom] maid, virginity.

H1332 בִּתְיָה (Bithyâh, bith-yaw'): Bithjah, an Egyptian woman. Origin: from H1323 (בַּת) and H3050 (יָהּ); daughter (i.e. worshipper) of Jah; KJV: Bithiah.

H1333 בָּתַק (bâthaq, baw-thak'): to cut in pieces. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: thrust through.

H1334 בָּתַר (bâthar, baw-thar'): to chop up. Origin: a primitive root, KJV: divide.

H1335 בֶּתֶר (bether, beh'-ther): a section. Origin: from H1334 (בָּתַר); KJV: part, piece.

H1336 בֶּתֶר (Bether, beh'-ther): Bether, a (craggy) place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1335 (בֶּתֶר); KJV: Bether.

H1337 בַּת רַבִּים (Bath Rabbîym, bath rab-beem'): the daughter (i.e. city) of Rabbah. Origin: from H1323 (בַּת) and a masculine plural from H7227 (רַב); KJV: Bath-rabbim.

H1338 בִּתְרוֹן (Bithrôwn, bith-rone'): Bithron, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1334 (בָּתַר); (with the article) the craggy spot; KJV: Bithron.

H1339 בַּת־שֶׁבַע (Bath-Shebaʻ, bath-sheh'-bah): Bath-Sheba, the mother of Solomon. Origin: from H1323 (בַּת) and H7651 (שֶׁבַע) (in the sense of H7650 (שָׁבַע)); daughter of an oath; KJV: Bath-sheba.

H1340 בַּת־שׁוּעַ (Bath-Shûwaʻ, bath-shoo'-ah): Bath-shua. Origin: from H1323 (בַּת) and H7771 (שׁוֹעַ); daughter of wealth; the same as H1339 (בַּת־שֶׁבַע) KJV: Bath-shua.

H1341 גֵּא (gêʼ, gay'): haughty. Origin: for H1343 (גֵּאֶה); KJV: proud.

H1342 גָּאָה (gâʼâh, gaw-aw'): to mount up; hence, in general, to rise, (figuratively) be majestic. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gloriously, grow up, increase, be risen, triumph.

H1343 גֵּאֶה (gêʼeh, gay-eh'): lofty; figuratively, arrogant. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה); KJV: proud.

H1344 גֵּאָה (gêʼâh, gay-aw'): arrogance. Origin: feminine from H1342 (גָּאָה); KJV: pride.

H1345 גְּאוּאֵל (Gᵉʼûwʼêl, gheh-oo-ale'): Geuel, an Israelite. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה) and H410 (אֵל); majesty of God; KJV: Geuel.

H1346 גַּאֲוָה (gaʼăvâh, gah-av-aw'): arrogance or majesty; by implication, (concretely) ornament. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה); KJV: excellency, haughtiness, highness, pride, proudly, swelling.

H1347 גָּאוֹן (gâʼôwn, gaw-ohn'): {arrogance or majesty; by implication, (concretely) ornament}. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה); the same as H1346 (גַּאֲוָה)xlit gaʻăvâh corrected to gaʼăvâh KJV: arrogancy, excellency(-lent), majesty, pomp, pride, proud, swelling.
