H1348 גֵּאוּת (gêʼûwth, gay-ooth'): {arrogance or majesty; by implication, (concretely) ornament}. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה); the same as H1346 (גַּאֲוָה)xlit gaʻăvâh corrected to gaʼăvâh KJV: excellent things, lifting up, majesty, pride, proudly, raging.

H1349 גַּאֲיוֹן (gaʼăyôwn, gah-ah-yone'): haughty. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה); KJV: proud.

H1350 גָּאַל (gâʼal, gaw-al'): to be the next of kin (and as such to buy back a relative's property, marry his widow, etc.). Origin: a primitive root, to redeem (according to the Oriental law of kinship), i.e. KJV: [idiom] in any wise, [idiom] at all, avenger, deliver, (do, perform the part of near, next) kinsfolk(-man), purchase, ransom, redeem(-er), revenger.

H1351 גָּאַל (gâʼal, gaw-al'): to soil or (figuratively) desecrate. Origin: a primitive root, (rather identified with H1350 (גָּאַל), through the idea of freeing, i.e. repudiating); KJV: defile, pollute, stain.

H1352 גֹּאֶל (gôʼel, go'-el): profanation. Origin: from H1351 (גָּאַל); KJV: defile.

H1353 גְּאֻלָּה (gᵉʼullâh, gheh-ool-law'): redemption (including the right and the object); by implication, relationship. Origin: feminine passive participle of H1350 (גָּאַל); KJV: kindred, redeem, redemption, right.

H1354 גַב (gab, gab): the back (as rounded); by analogy, the top or rim, a boss, a vault, arch of eye, bulwarks, etc. Origin: from an unused root meaning to hollow or curve; (compare H1460 (גֵּו) and H1479 (גּוּף)) KJV: back, body, boss, eminent (higher) place, (eye) brows, nave, ring.

H1355 גַּב (gab, gab): {the back (as rounded); by analogy, the top or rim, a boss, a vault, arch of eye, bulwarks, etc.}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1354 (גַב) KJV: back.

H1356 גֵּב (gêb, gabe): a log (as cut out); also well or cistern (as dug). Origin: from H1461 (גּוּב); KJV: beam, ditch, pit.

H1357 גֵּב (gêb, gabe): a locust (from its cutting). Origin: probably from H1461 (גּוּב) (compare H1462 (גּוֹב)); KJV: locust.

H1358 גֹּב (gôb, gobe): a pit (for wild animals) (as cut out). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H1461 (גּוּב); KJV: den.

H1359 גֹּב (Gôb, gobe): Gob, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (fully) גּוֹב; from H1461 (גּוּב); pit; KJV: Gob.

H1360 גֶּבֶא (gebeʼ, geh'-beh): a reservoir; by analogy, a marsh. Origin: from an unused root meaning probably to collect; KJV: marish, pit.

H1361 גָּבַהּ (gâbahh, gaw-bah'): to soar, i.e. be lofty; figuratively, to be haughty. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: exalt, be haughty, be (make) high(-er), lift up, mount up, be proud, raise up great height, upward.

H1362 גָּבָהּ (gâbâhh, gaw-bawh'): lofty (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H1361 (גָּבַהּ); KJV: high, proud.

H1363 גֹּבַהּ (gôbahh, go'-bah): elation, grandeur, arrogance. Origin: from H1361 (גָּבַהּ); KJV: excellency, haughty, height, high, loftiness, pride.

H1364 גָּבֹהַּ (gâbôahh, gaw-bo'-ah): elevated (or elated), powerful, arrogant. Origin: or גָּבוֹהַּ; (fully) from H1361 (גָּבַהּ); KJV: haughty, height, high(-er), lofty, proud, [idiom] exceeding proudly.

H1365 גַּבְהוּת (gabhûwth, gab-hooth'): pride. Origin: from H1361 (גָּבַהּ); KJV: loftiness, lofty.

H1366 גְּבוּל (gᵉbûwl, gheb-ool'): properly, a cord (as twisted), i.e. (by implication) a boundary; by extension the territory inclosed. Origin: or גְּבֻל; (shortened) from H1379 (גָּבַל); KJV: border, bound, coast, [idiom] great, landmark, limit, quarter, space.

H1367 גְּבוּלָה (gᵉbûwlâh, gheb-oo-law'): a boundary, region. Origin: or גְּבֻלָה; (shortened) feminine of H1366 (גְּבוּל); KJV: border, bound, coast, landmark. place.

H1368 גִּבּוֹר (gibbôwr, ghib-bore'): powerful; by implication, warrior, tyrant. Origin: or גִּבֹּר; (shortened) intensive from the same as H1397 (גֶּבֶר); KJV: champion, chief, [idiom] excel, giant, man, mighty (man, one), strong (man), valiant man.

H1369 גְּבוּרָה (gᵉbûwrâh, gheb-oo-raw'): force (literally or figuratively); by implication, valor, victory. Origin: feminine passive participle from the same as H1368 (גִּבּוֹר); KJV: force, mastery, might, mighty (act, power), power, strength.

H1370 גְּבוּרָה (gᵉbûwrâh, gheb-oo-raw'): power. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1369 (גְּבוּרָה); KJV: might.

H1371 גִּבֵּחַ (gibbêach, ghib-bay'-akh): bald in the forehead. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be high (in the forehead); KJV: forehead bald.

H1372 גַּבַּחַת (gabbachath, gab-bakh'-ath): baldness in the forehead; by analogy, a bare spot on the right side of cloth. Origin: from the same as H1371 (גִּבֵּחַ); KJV: bald forehead, [idiom] without.

H1373 גַּבַּי (Gabbay, gab-bah'ee): Gabbai, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H1354 (גַב); collective KJV: Gabbai.

H1374 גֵּבִים (Gêbîym, gay-beem'): Gebim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H1356 (גֵּב); cisterns; KJV: Gebim.

H1375 גְּבִיעַ (gᵉbîyaʻ, gheb-ee'-ah): a goblet; by analogy, the calyx of aflower. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be convex); KJV: house, cup, pot.

H1376 גְּבִיר (gᵉbîyr, gheb-eer'): a master. Origin: from H1396 (גָּבַר); KJV: lord.

H1377 גְּבִירָה (gᵉbîyrâh, gheb-ee-raw'): a mistress. Origin: feminine of H1376 (גְּבִיר); KJV: queen.

H1378 גָּבִישׁ (gâbîysh, gaw-beesh'): crystal (from its resemblance to ice). Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to freeze); KJV: pearl.

H1379 גָּבַל (gâbal, gaw-bal'): properly, to twist as arope; to bound (as by a line). Origin: a primitive root; also as a denominative from H1366 (גְּבוּל) KJV: be border, set (bounds about).

H1380 גְּבַל (Gᵉbal, gheb-al'): Gebal, a place in Phoenicia. Origin: from H1379 (גָּבַל) (in the sense of a chain of hills); a mountain; KJV: Gebal.

H1381 גְּבָל (Gᵉbâl, gheb-awl'): Gebal, a region in Idumaea. Origin: the same as H1380 (גְּבַל); KJV: Gebal.

H1382 גִּבְלִי (Giblîy, ghib-lee'): a Gebalite, or inhabitant of Gebal. Origin: ; patrial from H1380 (גְּבַל); KJV: Giblites, stone-squarer.

H1383 גַּבְלֻת (gabluth, gab-looth'): a twisted chain or lace. Origin: from H1379 (גָּבַל); KJV: end.

H1384 גִּבֵּן (gibbên, gib-bane'): hunch-backed. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be arched or contracted; KJV: crookbackt.

H1385 גְּבִנָה (gᵉbinâh, gheb-ee-naw'): curdled milk. Origin: feminine from the same as H1384 (גִּבֵּן); KJV: cheese.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1386 to H1519
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1386 גַּבְנֹן (gabnôn, gab-nohn'): a hump or peak of hills. Origin: from the same as H1384 (גִּבֵּן); KJV: high.

H1387 גֶּבַע (Gebaʻ, gheh'-bah): Geba, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H1375 (גְּבִיעַ), a hillock; KJV: Gaba, Geba, Gibeah.

H1388 גִּבְעָא (Gibʻâʼ, ghib-aw'): Giba, a place in Palestine. Origin: by permutation for H1389 (גִּבְעָה); a hill; KJV: Gibeah.

H1389 גִּבְעָה (gibʻâh, ghib-aw'): a hillock. Origin: feminine from the same as H1387 (גֶּבַע); KJV: hill, little hill.

H1390 גִּבְעָה (Gibʻâh, ghib-aw'): Gibah; the name of three places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1389 (גִּבְעָה); KJV: Gibeah, the hill.

H1391 גִּבְעוֹן (Gibʻôwn, ghib-ohn'): Gibon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H1387 (גֶּבַע); hilly; KJV: Gibeon.

H1392 גִּבְעֹל (gibʻôl, ghib-ole'): the calyx of a flower. Origin: prolonged from H1375 (גְּבִיעַ); KJV: bolled.

H1393 גִּבְעֹנִי (Gibʻônîy, ghib-o-nee'): a Gibonite, or inhabitant of Gibon. Origin: patrial from H1391 (גִּבְעוֹן); KJV: Gibeonite.

H1394 גִּבְעַת (Gibʻath, ghib-ath'): Gibath. Origin: from the same as H1375 (גְּבִיעַ); hilliness; KJV: Gibeath.

H1395 גִּבְעָתִי (Gibʻâthîy, ghib-aw-thee'): a Gibathite, or inhabitant of Gibath. Origin: patrial from H1390 (גִּבְעָה); KJV: Gibeathite.

H1396 גָּבַר (gâbar, gaw-bar'): to be strong; by implication, to prevail, act insolently. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: exceed, confirm, be great, be mighty, prevail, put to more (strength), strengthen, be stronger, be valiant.

H1397 גֶּבֶר (geber, gheh'-ber): properly, a valiant man or warrior; generally, a person simply. Origin: from H1396 (גָּבַר); KJV: every one, man, [idiom] mighty.

H1398 גֶּבֶר (Geber, gheh'-ber): Geber, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H1397 (גֶּבֶר); KJV: Geber.

H1399 גְּבַר (gᵉbar, gheb-ar'): a person. Origin: from H1396 (גָּבַר); the same as H1397 (גֶּבֶר); KJV: man.

H1400 גְּבַר (gᵉbar, gheb-ar'): {a person}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1399 (גְּבַר) KJV: certain, man.

H1401 גִּבָּר (gibbâr, ghib-bawr'): valiant, or warrior. Origin: (Aramaic) intensive of H1400 (גְּבַר); KJV: mighty.

H1402 גִּבָּר (Gibbâr, ghib-bawr'): Gibbar, an Israelite. Origin: intensive of H1399 (גְּבַר); KJV: Gibbar.

H1403 גַּבְרִיאֵל (Gabrîyʼêl, gab-ree-ale'): Gabriel, an archangel. Origin: from H1397 (גֶּבֶר) and H410 (אֵל); man of God; KJV: Garbriel.

H1404 גְּבֶרֶת (gᵉbereth, gheb-eh'-reth): mistress. Origin: feminine of H1376 (גְּבִיר); KJV: lady, mistress.

H1405 גִּבְּתוֹן (Gibbᵉthôwn, ghib-beth-one'): Gibbethon, a place in Palestine. Origin: intensive from H1389 (גִּבְעָה); a hilly spot; KJV: Gibbethon.

H1406 גָּג (gâg, gawg): a roof; by analogy, the top of an altar. Origin: probably by reduplication from H1342 (גָּאָה); KJV: roof (of the house), (house) top (of the house).

H1407 גַּד (gad, gad): coriander seed (from its furrows). Origin: from H1413 (גָּדַד) (in the sense of cutting); KJV: coriander.

H1408 גַּד (Gad, gad): Fortune, a Babylonian deity. Origin: a variation of H1409 (גָּד); KJV: that troop.

H1409 גָּד (gâd, gawd): fortune. Origin: from H1464 (גּוּד) (in the sense of distributing); KJV: troop.

H1410 גָּד (Gâd, gawd): Gad, a son of Jacob, including his tribe and its territory; also a prophet. Origin: from H1464 (גּוּד); KJV: Gad.

H1411 גְּדָבָר (gᵉdâbâr, ghed-aw-bawr'): a treasurer. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1489 (גִּזְבָּר); KJV: treasurer.

H1412 גֻּדְגֹּדָה (Gudgôdâh, gud-go'-daw): Gudgodah, a place in the Desert. Origin: by reduplication from H1413 (גָּדַד) (in the sense of cutting) cleft; KJV: Gudgodah.

H1413 גָּדַד (gâdad, gaw-dad'): to crowd; also to gash (as if by pressing into). Origin: a primitive root (compare H1464 (גּוּד)); KJV: assemble (selves by troops), gather (selves together, self in troops), cut selves.

H1414 גְּדַד (gᵉdad, ghed-ad'): to cut down. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1413 (גָּדַד); KJV: hew down.

H1415 גָּדָה (gâdâh, gaw-daw'): a border of a river (as cut into by the stream). Origin: from an unused root (meaning to cut off); KJV: bank.

H1416 גְּדוּד (gᵉdûwd, ghed-ood'): a crowd (especially of soldiers). Origin: from H1413 (גָּדַד); KJV: army, band (of men), company, troop (of robbers).

H1417 גְּדוּד (gᵉdûwd, ghed-ood'): a furrow (as cut). Origin: or גְּדֻדָה; (feminine) from H1413 (גָּדַד); KJV: furrow.

H1418 גְּדוּדָה (gᵉdûwdâh, ghed-oo-daw'): an incision. Origin: feminine participle passive of H1413 (גָּדַד); KJV: cutting.

H1419 גָּדוֹל (gâdôwl, gaw-dole'): great (in any sense); hence, older; also insolent. Origin: or גָּדֹל; (shortened) from H1431 (גָּדַל); KJV: [phrase] aloud, elder(-est), [phrase] exceeding(-ly), [phrase] far, (man of) great (man, matter, thing,-er,-ness), high, long, loud, mighty, more, much, noble, proud thing, [idiom] sore, ([idiom]) very.

H1420 גְּדוּלָה (gᵉdûwlâh, ghed-oo-law'): greatness; (concretely) mighty acts. Origin: or גְּדֻלָּה; (shortened) or (less accurately) גְּדוּלָּה; feminine of H1419 (גָּדוֹל); KJV: dignity, great things(-ness), majesty.

H1421 גִּדּוּף (giddûwph, ghid-doof'): vilification. Origin: or (shortened) גִּדֻּף; and (feminine) גִּדּוּפָהxlit giddûphâh corrected to giddûwphâh; or גִּדֻּפָה; from H1422 (גְּדוּפָה); KJV: reproach, reviling.

H1422 גְּדוּפָה (gᵉdûwphâh, ghed-oo-faw'): a revilement. Origin: feminine passive participle of H1442 (גָּדַף); KJV: taunt.

H1423 גְּדִי (gᵉdîy, ghed-ee'): a young goat (from browsing). Origin: from the same as H1415 (גָּדָה); KJV: kid.

H1424 גָּדִי (Gâdîy, gaw-dee'): Gadi, an Israelite. Origin: from H1409 (גָּד); fortunate; KJV: Gadi.

H1425 גָּדִי (Gâdîy, gaw-dee'): a Gadite (collectively) or descendants of Gad. Origin: patronymically from H1410 (גָּד); KJV: Gadites, children of Gad.

H1426 גַּדִּי (Gaddîy, gad-dee'): Gaddi, an Israelite. Origin: intensive for H1424 (גָּדִי); KJV: Gaddi.

H1427 גַּדִּיאֵל (Gaddîyʼêl, gad-dee-ale'): Gaddiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H1409 (גָּד) and H410 (אֵל); fortune of God; KJV: Gaddiel.

H1428 גִּדְיָה (gidyâh, ghid-yaw'): a river brink. Origin: or גַּדיָה; the same as H1415 (גָּדָה); KJV: bank.

H1429 גְּדִיָּה (gᵉdîyâh, ghed-ee-yaw'): a young female goat. Origin: feminine of H1423 (גְּדִי); KJV: kid.

H1430 גָּדִישׁ (gâdîysh, gaw-deesh'): a stack of sheaves; by analogy, a tomb. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to heap up); KJV: shock (stack) (of corn), tomb.

H1431 גָּדַל (gâdal, gaw-dal'): to be (causatively make) large (in various senses, as in body, mind, estate or honor, also in pride). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to twist (compare H1434 (גְּדִל)), i.e. KJV: advance, boast, bring up, exceed, excellent, be(-come, do, give, make, wax), great(-er, come to... estate, [phrase] things), grow(up), increase, lift up, magnify(-ifical), be much set by, nourish (up), pass, promote, proudly (spoken), tower.

H1432 גָּדֵל (gâdêl, gaw-dale'): large (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H1431 (גָּדַל); KJV: great, grew.

H1433 גֹּדֶל (gôdel, go'-del): magnitude (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H1431 (גָּדַל); KJV: greatness, stout(-ness).

H1434 גְּדִל (gᵉdil, ghed-eel'): thread, i.e. a tassel or festoon. Origin: from H1431 (גָּדַל) (in the sense of twisting); KJV: fringe, wreath.

H1435 גִּדֵּל (Giddêl, ghid-dale'): Giddel, the name of one of the Nethinim, also of one of 'Solomon's servants'. Origin: from H1431 (גָּדַל); stout; KJV: Giddel.

H1436 גְּדַּלְיָה (Gᵉdalyâh, ghed-al-yaw'): Gedaljah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or (prolonged) גְּדַלְיָהוּ; from H1431 (גָּדַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has become great; KJV: Gedaliah.

H1437 גִּדַּלְתִּי (Giddaltîy, ghid-dal'-tee): Giddalti, an Israelite. Origin: from H1431 (גָּדַל); I have made great; KJV: Giddalti.

H1438 גָּדַע (gâdaʻ, gaw-dah'): to fell a tree; generally, to destroy anything. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut (asunder, in sunder, down, off), hew down.

H1439 גִּדְעוֹן (Gidʻôwn, ghid-ohn'): Gidon, an Israelite. Origin: from H1438 (גָּדַע); feller (i.e. warrior); KJV: Gideon.

H1440 גִּדְעֹם (Gidʻôm, ghid-ohm'): Gidom, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1438 (גָּדַע); a cutting (i.e. desolation); KJV: Gidom.

H1441 גִּדְעֹנִי (Gidʻônîy, ghid-o-nee'): Gidoni, an Israelite. Origin: from H1438 (גָּדַע); warlike (compare H1439 (גִּדְעוֹן)); KJV: Gideoni.

H1442 גָּדַף (gâdaph, gaw-daf'): to hack (with words), i.e. revile. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: blaspheme, reproach.

H1443 גָּדַר (gâdar, gaw-dar'): to wall in or around. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: close up, fence up, hedge, inclose, make up (a wall), mason, repairer.

H1444 גֶּדֶר (geder, gheh'-der): a circumvallation. Origin: from H1443 (גָּדַר); KJV: wall.

H1445 גֶּדֶר (Geder, gheh'-der): Geder, a place in Palestine. Origin: ; the same as H1444 (גֶּדֶר); KJV: Geder.

H1446 גְדֹר (Gᵉdôr, ghed-ore'): Gedor, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites. Origin: or (fully) גְּדוֹר; from H1443 (גָּדַר); inclosure; KJV: Gedor.

H1447 גָּדֵר (gâdêr, gaw-dare'): a circumvallation; by implication, an inclosure. Origin: from H1443 (גָּדַר); KJV: fence, hedge, wall.

H1448 גְּדֵרָה (gᵉdêrâh, ghed-ay-raw'): enclosure (especially for flocks). Origin: feminine of H1447 (גָּדֵר); KJV: (sheep-) cote (fold) hedge, wall.

H1449 גְּדֵרָה (Gᵉdêrâh, ghed-ay-raw'): (with the article) Gederah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1448 (גְּדֵרָה); KJV: Gederah, hedges.

H1450 גְּדֵרוֹת (Gᵉdêrôwth, ghed-ay-rohth'): Gederoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H1448 (גְּדֵרָה); walls; KJV: Gederoth.

H1451 גְּדֵרִי (Gᵉdêrîy, ghed-ay-ree'): a Gederite, or inhabitant of Geder. Origin: patrial from H1445 (גֶּדֶר); KJV: Gederite.

H1452 גְּדֵרָתִי (Gᵉdêrâthîy, ghed-ay-raw-thee'): a Gederathite, or inhabitant of Gederah. Origin: patrial from H1449 (גְּדֵרָה); KJV: Gederathite.

H1453 גְּדֵרֹתַיִם (Gᵉdêrôthayim, ghed-ay-ro-thah'-yim): Gederothajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of H1448 (גְּדֵרָה); double wall; KJV: Gederothaim.

H1454 גֵּה (gêh, gay): this. Origin: probably a clerical error for H2088 (זֶה); KJV: this.

H1455 גָּהָה (gâhâh, gaw-haw'): to remove (a bandage from a wound, i.e. heal it). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cure.

H1456 גֵּהָה (gêhâh, gay-haw'): a cure. Origin: from H1455 (גָּהָה); KJV: medicine.

H1457 גָּהַר (gâhar, gaw-har'): to prostrate oneself. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast self down, stretch self.

H1458 גַּו (gav, gav): the back. Origin: another form for H1460 (גֵּו); KJV: back.

H1459 גַּו (gav, gav): the middle. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1460 (גֵּו); KJV: midst, same, there-(where-) in.

H1460 גֵּו (gêv, gave): the back; by analogy, the middle. Origin: from H1342 (גָּאָה) (corresponding to H1354 (גַב)); KJV: [phrase] among, back, body.

H1461 גּוּב (gûwb, goob): to dig. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: husbandman.

H1462 גּוֹב (gôwb, gobe): the locust (from its grubbing as a larvae). Origin: from H1461 (גּוּב); KJV: grasshopper, [idiom] great.

H1463 גּוֹג (Gôwg, gohg): Gog, the name of an Israelite, also of some nothern nation. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Gog.

H1464 גּוּד (gûwd, goode): to crowd upon, i.e. attack. Origin: a primitive root (akin to H1413 (גָּדַד)); KJV: invade, overcome.

H1465 גֵּוָה (gêvâh, gay-vaw'): the back, i.e. (by extensive) the person. Origin: feminine of H1460 (גֵּו); KJV: body.

H1466 גֵּוָה (gêvâh, gay-vaw'): exaltation; (figuratively) arrogance. Origin: the same as H1465 (גֵּוָה); KJV: lifting up, pride.

H1467 גֵּוָה (gêvâh, gay-vaw'): {exaltation; (figuratively) arrogance}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1466 (גֵּוָה) KJV: pride.

H1468 גּוּז (gûwz, gooz): properly, to shear off; but used only in the (figuratively) sense of passing rapidly. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1494 (גַּזָז)); KJV: bring, cut off.

H1469 גּוֹזָל (gôwzâl, go-zawl'): a nestling (as being comparatively nude of feathers). Origin: or (shortened) גֹזָלlemma גזָל missing vowel, corrected to גֹזָל; from H1497 (גָּזַל); KJV: young (pigeon).

H1470 גּוֹזָן (Gôwzân, go-zawn'): Gozan, a province of Assyria. Origin: probably from H1468 (גּוּז); a quarry (as a place of cutting stones); KJV: Gozan.

H1471 גּוֹי (gôwy, go'-ee): a foreign nation; hence, a Gentile; also (figuratively) a troop of animals, or a flight of locusts. Origin: rarely (shortened) גֹּי; apparently from the same root as H1465 (גֵּוָה) (in the sense of massing); KJV: Gentile, heathen, nation, people.

H1472 גְּוִיָּה (gᵉvîyâh, ghev-ee-yaw'): a body, whether alive or dead. Origin: prolonged for H1465 (גֵּוָה); KJV: (dead) body, carcase, corpse.

H1473 גּוֹלָה (gôwlâh, go-law'): exile; concretely and collectively exiles. Origin: or (shortened) גֹּלָה; active participle feminine of H1540 (גָּלָה); KJV: (carried away), captive(-ity), removing.

H1474 גּוֹלָן (Gôwlân, go-lawn'): Golan, a place east of the Jordan. Origin: from H1473 (גּוֹלָה); captive; KJV: Golan.

H1475 גּוּמָּץ (gûwmmâts, goom-mawts'): a pit. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: pit.

H1476 גּוּנִי (Gûwnîy, goo-nee'): Guni, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably from H1598 (גָּנַן); protected; KJV: Guni.

H1477 גּוּנִי (Gûwnîy, goo-nee'): a Gunite (collectively with article prefix) or descendants of Guni. Origin: patronymically from H1476 (גּוּנִי); KJV: Gunites.

H1478 גָּוַע (gâvaʻ, gaw-vah'): to breathe out, i.e. (by implication) expire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: die, be dead, give up the ghost, perish.

H1479 גּוּף (gûwph, goof): properly, to hollow or arch, i.e. (figuratively) close; to shut. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shut.

H1480 גּוּפָה (gûwphâh, goo-faw'): a corpse (as closed to sense). Origin: from H1479 (גּוּף); KJV: body.

H1481 גּוּר (gûwr, goor): properly, to turn aside from the road (for a lodging or any other purpose), i.e. sojourn (as a guest); also to shrink, fear (as in a strange place); also to gather forhostility (as afraid). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abide, assemble, be afraid, dwell, fear, gather (together), inhabitant, remain, sojourn, stand in awe, (be) stranger, [idiom] surely.

H1482 גּוּר (gûwr, goor): a cub (as still abiding in the lair), especially of the lion. Origin: or (shortened) גֻּר; perhaps from H1481 (גּוּר); KJV: whelp, young one.

H1483 גּוּר (Gûwr, goor): Gur, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1482 (גּוּר); KJV: Gur.

H1484 גּוֹר (gôwr, gore): {a cub (as still abiding in the lair), especially of the lion}. Origin: or (feminine) גֹּרָה; a variation of H1482 (גּוּר) KJV: whelp.

H1485 גּוּר־בַּעַל (Gûwr-Baʻal, goor-bah'-al): Gur-Baal, a place in Arabia. Origin: from H1481 (גּוּר) and H1168 (בַּעַל); dwelling of Baal; KJV: Gur-baal.

H1486 גּוֹרָל (gôwrâl, go-rawl'): properly, a pebble, i.e. a lot (small stones being used for that purpose); figuratively, a portion or destiny (as if determined by lot). Origin: or (shortened) גֹּרָל; from an unused root meaning to be rough (as stone); KJV: lot.

H1487 גּוּשׁ (gûwsh, goosh): a mass of earth. Origin: or rather (by permutation) גִּישׁ; of uncertain derivation; KJV: clod.

H1488 גֵּז (gêz, gaze): a fleece (as shorn); also mown grass. Origin: from H1494 (גַּזָז); KJV: fleece, mowing, mown grass.

H1489 גִּזְבָּר (gizbâr, ghiz-bawr'): treasurer. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: treasurer.

H1490 גִּזְבָּר (gizbâr, ghiz-bawr'): {treasurer}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1489 (גִּזְבָּר) KJV: treasurer.

H1491 גָּזָה (gâzâh, gaw-zaw'): to cut off, i.e. portion out. Origin: a primitive root (akin to H1468 (גּוּז)); KJV: take.

H1492 גָּזַּה (gâzzah, gaz-zaw'): a fleece. Origin: feminine from H1494 (גַּזָז); KJV: fleece.

H1493 גִּזוֹנִי (Gizôwnîy, ghee-zo-nee'): a Gizonite or inhabitant of Gizoh. Origin: patrial from the unused name of a place apparently in Palestine; KJV: Gizonite.

H1494 גַּזָז (gazâz, gaw-zaz'): to cut off; specifically to shear aflock or shave the hair; figuratively to destroy an enemy. Origin: a primitive root (akin to H1468 (גּוּז)); KJV: cut off (down), poll, shave, (sheep-) shear(-er).

H1495 גָּזֵז (Gâzêz, gaw-zaze'): Gazez, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1494 (גַּזָז); shearer; KJV: Gazez.

H1496 גָּזִית (gâzîyth, gaw-zeeth'): something cut, i.e. dressed stone. Origin: from H1491 (גָּזָה); KJV: hewed, hewn stone, wrought.

H1497 גָּזַל (gâzal, gaw-zal'): to pluck off; specifically to flay, strip or rob. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch, consume, exercise (robbery), pluck (off), rob, spoil, take away (by force, violence), tear.

H1498 גָּזֵל (gâzêl, gaw-zale'): robbery, or (concretely) plunder. Origin: from H1497 (גָּזַל); KJV: robbery, thing taken away by violence.

H1499 גֵּזֶל (gêzel, ghe'-zel): plunder, i.e. violence. Origin: from H1497 (גָּזַל); KJV: violence, violent perverting.. gozal. See H1469 (גּוֹזָל).

H1500 גְּזֵלָה (gᵉzêlâh, ghez-ay-law'): {robbery, or (concretely) plunder}. Origin: feminine of H1498 (גָּזֵל) and mean the same KJV: that (he had robbed) (which he took violently away), spoil, violence.

H1501 גָּזָם (gâzâm, gaw-zawm'): a kind of locust. Origin: from an unused root meaning to devour; KJV: palmer-worm.

H1502 גַּזָּם (Gazzâm, gaz-zawm'): Gazzam, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from the same as H1501 (גָּזָם); devourer KJV: Gazzam.

H1503 גֶּזַע (gezaʻ, geh'-zah): the trunk or stump of atree (as felled or as planted). Origin: from an unused root meaning to cut down (trees); KJV: stem, stock.

H1504 גָּזַר (gâzar, gaw-zar'): to cut down or off; (figuratively) to destroy, divide, exclude, or decide. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut down (off), decree, divide, snatch.

H1505 גְּזַר (gᵉzar, ghez-ar'): to quarry; determine. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1504 (גָּזַר); KJV: cut out, soothsayer.

H1506 גֶּזֶר (gezer, gheh'-zer): something cut off; a portion. Origin: from H1504 (גָּזַר); KJV: part, piece.

H1507 גֶּזֶר (Gezer, gheh'-zer): Gezer, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1506 (גֶּזֶר); KJV: Gazer, Gezer.

H1508 גִּזְרָה (gizrâh, ghiz-raw'): the figure or person (as if cut out); also an inclosure (as separated). Origin: feminine of H1506 (גֶּזֶר); KJV: polishing, separate place.

H1509 גְּזֵרָה (gᵉzêrâh, ghez-ay-raw'): a desert (as separated). Origin: from H1504 (גָּזַר); KJV: not inhabited.

H1510 גְּזֵרָה (gᵉzêrâh, ghez-ay-raw'): a decree. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1505 (גְּזַר) (as H1504 (גָּזַר)); KJV: decree.

H1511 גִּזְרִי (Gizrîy, ghiz-ree'): a Grizite (collectively) or member of a native tribe in Palestine. Origin: (in the m patrial from H1507 (גֶּזֶר); a Gezerite (collectively) or inhabitants of Gezer; but better (as in the text) bytransposition גִּזְרִיxlit Girzîy corrected to Gizrîy; patrial of H1630 (גְּרִזִים); KJV: Gezrites.

H1512 גָּחוֹן (gâchôwn, gaw-khone'): the external abdomen, belly (as the source of the faetus ). Origin: probably from H1518 (גִּיחַ)lemma גּיחַ missing vowel, corrected to גִּיחַ; (compare H1521 (גִּיחוֹן)) KJV: belly.

H1513 גֶּחֶל (gechel, geh'-khel): an ember. Origin: or (feminine) גַּחֶלֶת; from an unused root meaning to glow or kindle; KJV: (burning) coal.

H1514 גַּחַם (Gacham, gah'-kham): Gacham, a son of Nahor. Origin: from an unused root meaning to burn; flame; KJV: Gaham.

H1515 גַּחַר (Gachar, gah'-khar): Gachar, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from an unused root meaning to hide; lurker; KJV: Gahar.

H1516 גַּיְא (gayʼ, gah'-ee): a gorge (from its lofty sides; hence, narrow, but not a gully or winter-torrent). Origin: or (shortened) גַּי; probably (by transmutation) from the same root as H1466 (גֵּוָה) (abbreviated); KJV: valley.

H1517 גִּיד (gîyd, gheed): a thong (as compressing); by analogy, a tendon. Origin: probably from H1464 (גּוּד); KJV: sinew.

H1518 גִּיחַ (gîyach, ghee'-akh): to gush forth (as water), generally to issue. Origin: or (shortened) גֹּחַ; a primitive root; KJV: break forth, labor to bring forth, come forth, draw up, take out.

H1519 גִּיחַ (gîyach, ghee'-akh): to rush forth. Origin: (Aramaic) or (shortened) גּוּחַ; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1518 (גִּיחַ)lemma גּיחַ missing vowel, corrected to גִּיחַ; KJV: strive.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1520 to H1654
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1520 גִּיחַ (Gîyach, ghee'-akh): Giach, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1518 (גִּיחַ)lemma גּיחַ missing vowel, corrected to גִּיחַ; a fountain; KJV: Giah.

H1521 גִּיחוֹן (Gîychôwn, ghee-khone'): Gichon, a river of Paradise; also a valley (or pool) near Jerusalem. Origin: or (shortened) גִּחוֹן; from H1518 (גִּיחַ)lemma גּיחַ missing vowel, corrected to גִּיחַ; stream; KJV: Gihon.

H1522 גֵּיחֲזִי (Gêychăzîy, gay-khah-zee'): Gechazi, the servant of Elisha. Origin: or גֵּחֲזִי; apparently from H1516 (גַּיְא) and H2372 (חָזָה); valley of a visionary; KJV: Gehazi.

H1523 גִּיל (gîyl, gheel): properly, to spin round (under the influence of any violent emotion), i.e. usually rejoice, or (as cringing) fear. Origin: or (by permutation) גּוּל; a primitive root; KJV: be glad, joy, be joyful, rejoice.

H1524 גִּיל (gîyl, gheel): a revolution (of time, i.e. an age); also joy. Origin: from H1523 (גִּיל); KJV: [idiom] exceedingly, gladness, [idiom] greatly, joy, rejoice(-ing), sort.

H1525 גִּילָה (gîylâh, ghee-law'): joy. Origin: or גִּילַת; feminine of H1524 (גִּיל); KJV: joy, rejoicing.

H1526 גִּילֹנִי (Gîylônîy, ghee-lo-nee'): a Gilonite or inhabitant of Giloh. Origin: patrial from H1542 (גִּלֹה); KJV: Gilonite.

H1527 גִּינַת (Gîynath, ghee-nath'): Ginath, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Ginath.

H1528 גִּיר (gîyr, gheer): lime. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1615 (גִּר); KJV: plaster.

H1529 גֵּישָׁן (Gêyshân, gay-shawn'): Geshan, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H1487 (גּוּשׁ); lumpish; KJV: Geshan.

H1530 גַּל (gal, gal): something rolled, i.e. a heap of stone or dung (plural ruins), by analogy, a spring of water (plural waves). Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: billow, heap, spring, wave.

H1531 גֹּל (gôl, gole): a cup for oil (as round). Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: bowl.

H1532 גַּלָּב (gallâb, gal-lawb'): a barber. Origin: from an unused root meaning to shave; KJV: barber.

H1533 גִּלְבֹּעַ (Gilbôaʻ, ghil-bo'-ah): Gilboa, a mountain of Palestine. Origin: from H1530 (גַּל) and H1158 (בָּעָה); fountain of ebullition; KJV: Gilboa.

H1534 גַּלְגַּל (galgal, gal-gal'): a wheel; by analogy, a whirlwind; also dust (as whirled). Origin: by reduplication from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: heaven, rolling thing, wheel.

H1535 גַּלְגַּל (galgal, gal-gal'): a wheel. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1534 (גַּלְגַּל); KJV: wheel.

H1536 גִּלְגָּל (gilgâl, ghil-gawl'): {a wheel; by analogy, a whirlwind; also dust (as whirled)}. Origin: a variation of H1534 (גַּלְגַּל) KJV: wheel.

H1537 גִּלְגָּל (Gilgâl, ghil-gawl'): Gilgal, the name of three places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1536 (גִּלְגָּל) (with the article as a properly, noun); KJV: Gilgal. See also H1019 (בֵּית הַגִּלְגָּל).

H1538 גֻּלְגֹּלֶת (gulgôleth, gul-go'-leth): a skull (as round); by implication, a head (in enumeration of persons). Origin: by reduplication from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: head, every man, poll, skull.

H1539 גֶּלֶד (geled, ghe'-led): the (human) skin (as smooth). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to polish; KJV: skin.

H1540 גָּלָה (gâlâh, gaw-law'): to denude (especially in a disgraceful sense); by implication, to exile (captives being usually stripped); figuratively, to reveal. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [phrase] advertise, appear, bewray, bring, (carry, lead, go) captive (into captivity), depart, disclose, discover, exile, be gone, open, [idiom] plainly, publish, remove, reveal, [idiom] shamelessly, shew, [idiom] surely, tell, uncover.

H1541 גְּלָה (gᵉlâh, ghel-aw'): {to denude (especially in a disgraceful sense); by implication, to exile (captives being usually stripped); figuratively, to reveal}. Origin: (Aramaic) or גְּלָא; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1540 (גָּלָה) KJV: bring over, carry away, reveal.

H1542 גִּלֹה (Gilôh, ghee-lo'): Giloh, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (fully) גִּילֹה; from H1540 (גָּלָה); open; KJV: Giloh.

H1543 גֻּלָּה (gullâh, gool-law'): a fountain, bowl or globe (all as round). Origin: feminine from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: bowl, pommel, spring.

H1544 גִּלּוּל (gillûwl, ghil-lool'): properly, a log (as round); by implication, an idol. Origin: or (shortened) גִּלֻּל; from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: idol.

H1545 גְּלוֹם (gᵉlôwm, ghel-ome'): clothing (as wrapped). Origin: from H1563 (גָּלַם); KJV: clothes.

H1546 גָּלוּת (gâlûwth, gaw-looth'): captivity; concretely, exiles (collectively). Origin: feminine from H1540 (גָּלָה); KJV: (they that are carried away) captives(-ity).

H1547 גָּלוּת (gâlûwth, gaw-looth'): {captivity; concretely, exiles (collectively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1546 (גָּלוּת) KJV: captivity.

H1548 גָּלַח (gâlach, gaw-lakh'): properly, to be bald, i.e. (causatively) to shave; figuratively to lay waste. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: poll, shave (off).

H1549 גִּלָּיוֹן (gillâyôwn, ghil-law-yone'): a tablet for writing (as bare); by analogy, a mirror (as a plate). Origin: or גִּלְיוֹן; from H1540 (גָּלָה); KJV: glass, roll.

H1550 גָּלִיל (gâlîyl, gaw-leel'): a valve of a folding door (as turning); also a ring (as round). Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: folding, ring.

H1551 גָּלִיל (Gâlîyl, gaw-leel'): Galil (as a special circuit) in the North of Palestine. Origin: or (prolonged) גָּלִילָה; the same as H1550 (גָּלִיל); a circle (with the article); KJV: Galilee.

H1552 גְלִילָה (gᵉlîylâh, ghel-ee-law'): a circuit or region. Origin: feminine of H1550 (גָּלִיל); KJV: border, coast, country.

H1553 גְּלִילוֹת (Gᵉlîylôwth, ghel-ee-lowth'): Geliloth, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H1552 (גְלִילָה); circles; KJV: Geliloth.

H1554 גַּלִּים (Gallîym, gal-leem'): Gallim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H1530 (גַּל); springs; KJV: Gallim.

H1555 גׇּלְיַת (Golyath, gol-yath'): Goljath, a Philistine. Origin: perhaps from H1540 (גָּלָה); exile; KJV: Goliath.

H1556 גָּלַל (gâlal, gaw-lal'): to roll (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: commit, remove, roll (away, down, together), run down, seek occasion, trust, wallow.

H1557 גָּלָל (gâlâl, gaw-lawl'): dung (as in balls). Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: dung.

H1558 גָּלָל (gâlâl, gaw-lawl'): a circumstance (as rolled around); only used adverbially, on account of. Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: because of, for (sake).

H1559 גָּלָל (Gâlâl, gaw-lawl'): Galal, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל), in the sense of H1560 (גְּלָל); great; KJV: Galal.

H1560 גְּלָל (gᵉlâl, ghel-awl'): weight or size (as if rolled). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: great.

H1561 גֵּלֶל (gêlel, gay'-lel): dung (plural balls of dung). Origin: a variation of H1557 (גָּלָל); KJV: dung.

H1562 גִּלֲלַי (Gilălay, ghe-lal-ah'-ee): Gilalai, an Israelite. Origin: from H1561 (גֵּלֶל); dungy; KJV: Gilalai.

H1563 גָּלַם (gâlam, gaw-lam'): to fold. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wrap together.

H1564 גֹּלֶם (gôlem, go'-lem): a wrapped (and unformed mass, i.e. as the embryo). Origin: from H1563 (גָּלַם); KJV: substance yet being unperfect.

H1565 גַּלְמוּד (galmûwd, gal-mood'): sterile (as wrapped up too hard); figuratively, desolate. Origin: probably by prolonged from H1563 (גָּלַם); KJV: desolate, solitary.

H1566 גָּלַע (gâlaʻ, gaw-lah'): to be obstinate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (inter-) meddle (with).

H1567 גַּלְעֵד (Galʻêd, gal-ade'): Galed, a memorial cairn East of the Jordan. Origin: from H1530 (גַּל) and H5707 (עֵד); heap of testimony; KJV: Galeed.

H1568 גִּלְעָד (Gilʻâd, ghil-awd'): Gilad, a region East of the Jordan; also the name of three Israelites. Origin: probably from H1567 (גַּלְעֵד); KJV: Gilead, Gileadite.

H1569 גִּלְעָדִי (Gilʻâdîy, ghil-aw-dee'): a Giladite or descendant of Gilad. Origin: patronymically from H1568 (גִּלְעָד); KJV: Gileadite.

H1570 גָּלַשׁ (gâlash, gaw-lash'): probably to caper (as a goat). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appear.

H1571 גַּם (gam, gam): properly, assemblage; used only adverbially also, even, yea, though; often repeated as correl. both...and. Origin: by contraction from an unused root meaning to gather; KJV: again, alike, also, (so much) as (soon), both (so)...and, but, either...or, even, for all, (in) likewise (manner), moreover, nay...neither, one, then(-refore), though, what, with, yea.

H1572 גָּמָא (gâmâʼ, gaw-maw'): to absorb. Origin: a primitive root (literally or figuratively) to absorb KJV: swallow, drink.

H1573 גֹּמֶא (gômeʼ, go'-meh): properly, an absorbent, i.e. the bulrush (from its porosity); specifically the papyrus. Origin: from H1572 (גָּמָא); KJV: (bul-) rush.

H1574 גֹּמֶד (gômed, go'-med): properly, a span. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to grasp; KJV: cubit.

H1575 גַּמָּד (gammâd, gam-mawd'): a warrior (as grasping weapons). Origin: from the same as H1574 (גֹּמֶד); KJV: Gammadims.

H1576 גְּמוּל (gᵉmûwl, ghem-ool'): treatment, i.e. an act (of good or ill); by implication, service or requital. Origin: from H1580 (גָּמַל); KJV: [phrase] as hast served, benefit, desert, deserving, that which he hath given, recompense, reward.

H1577 גָּמוּל (gâmûwl, gaw-mool'): Gamul, an Israelite. Origin: passive participle of H1580 (גָּמַל); rewarded; KJV: Gamul. See also H1014 (בֵּית גָּמוּל).

H1578 גְּמוּלָה (gᵉmûwlâh, ghem-oo-law'): meaning the same. Origin: feminine of H1576 (גְּמוּל); KJV: deed, recompense, such a reward.

H1579 גִּמְזוֹ (Gimzôw, ghim-zo'): Gimzo, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Gimzo.

H1580 גָּמַל (gâmal, gaw-mal'): to treat a person (well or ill), i.e. benefit or requite; by implication (of toil), to ripen, i.e. (specifically) to wean. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bestow on, deal bountifully, do (good), recompense, requite, reward, ripen, [phrase] serve, mean, yield.

H1581 גָּמָל (gâmâl, gaw-mawl'): a camel. Origin: apparently from H1580 (גָּמַל) (in the sense of labor or burden-bearing); KJV: camel.

H1582 גְּמַלִּי (Gᵉmallîy, ghem-al-lee'): Gemalli, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H1581 (גָּמָל); cameldriver; KJV: Gemalli.

H1583 גַּמְלִיאֵל (Gamlîyʼêl, gam-lee-ale'): Gamliel, an Israelite. Origin: from H1580 (גָּמַל) and H410 (אֵל); reward of God; KJV: Gamaliel.

H1584 גָּמַר (gâmar, gaw-mar'): to end (in the sense of completion or failure). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease, come to an end, fail, perfect, perform.

H1585 גְּמַר (gᵉmar, ghem-ar'): {to end (in the sense of completion or failure)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1584 (גָּמַר) KJV: perfect.

H1586 גֹּמֶר (Gômer, go'-mer): Gomer, the name of a son of Japheth and of his descendants; also of a Hebrewess. Origin: from H1584 (גָּמַר); completion; KJV: Gomer.

H1587 גְּמַרְיָה (Gᵉmaryâh, ghem-ar-yaw'): Gemarjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or גְּמַרְיָהוּ; from H1584 (גָּמַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has perfected; KJV: Gemariah.

H1588 גַּן (gan, gan): a garden (as fenced). Origin: from H1598 (גָּנַן); KJV: garden.

H1589 גָּנַב (gânab, gaw-nab'): to thieve (literally or figuratively); by implication, to deceive. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: carry away, [idiom] indeed, secretly bring, steal (away), get by stealth.

H1590 גַּנָּב (gannâb, gaw-nab'): a stealer. Origin: from H1589 (גָּנַב); KJV: thief.

H1591 גְּנֵבָה (gᵉnêbâh, ghen-ay-baw'): stealing, i.e. (concretely) something stolen. Origin: from H1589 (גָּנַב); KJV: theft.

H1592 גְּנֻבַת (Gᵉnubath, ghen-oo-bath'): Genubath, an Edomitish prince. Origin: from H1589 (גָּנַב); theft; KJV: Genubath.

H1593 גַּנָּה (gannâh, gan-naw'): a garden. Origin: feminine of H1588 (גַּן); KJV: garden.

H1594 גִּנָּה (ginnâh, ghin-naw'): {a garden}. Origin: another form for H1593 (גַּנָּה) KJV: garden.

H1595 גֶּנֶז (genez, gheh'-nez): treasure; by implication, a coffer. Origin: from an unused root meaning to store; KJV: chest, treasury.

H1596 גְּנַז (gᵉnaz, ghen-az'): treasure. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1595 (גֶּנֶז); KJV: treasure.

H1597 גִּנְזַךְ (ginzak, ghin-zak'): a treasury. Origin: prolonged from H1595 (גֶּנֶז); KJV: treasury.

H1598 גָּנַן (gânan, gaw-nan'): to hedge about, i.e. (generally) protect. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: defend.

H1599 גִּנְּתוֹן (Ginnᵉthôwn, ghin-neth-one): Ginnethon or Ginnetho, an Israelite. Origin: or גִּנְּתוֹ; from H1598 (גָּנַן); gardener; KJV: Ginnetho, Ginnethon.

H1600 גָּעָה (gâʻâh, gaw-aw'): to bellow (as cattle). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: low.

H1601 גֹּעָה (Gôʻâh, go-aw'): Goah, a place near Jerusalem. Origin: feminine active participle of H1600 (גָּעָה); lowing; KJV: Goath.

H1602 גָּעַל (gâʻal, gaw-al'): to detest; by implication, to reject. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor, fail, lothe, vilely cast away.

H1603 גַּעַל (Gaʻal, gah'-al): Gaal, an Israelite. Origin: from H1602 (גָּעַל); loathing; KJV: Gaal.

H1604 גֹּעַל (gôʻal, go'-al): abhorrence. Origin: from H1602 (גָּעַל); KJV: loathing.

H1605 גָּעַר (gâʻar, gaw-ar'): to chide. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: corrupt, rebuke, reprove.

H1606 גְּעָרָה (gᵉʻârâh, gheh-aw-raw'): a chiding. Origin: from H1605 (גָּעַר); KJV: rebuke(-ing), reproof.

H1607 גָּעַשׁ (gâʻash, gaw-ash'): to agitate violently. Origin: a primitive root KJV: move, shake, toss, trouble.

H1608 גַּעַשׁ (Gaʻash, ga'-ash): Gaash, a hill in Palestine. Origin: from H1607 (גָּעַשׁ); a quaking; KJV: Gaash.

H1609 גַּעְתָּם (Gaʻtâm, gah-tawm'): Gatam, an Edomite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Gatam.

H1610 גַּף (gaph, gaf): the back; by extension the body or self. Origin: from an unused root meaning to arch; KJV: [phrase] highest places, himself.

H1611 גַּף (gaph, gaf): a wing. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1610 (גַּף); KJV: wing.

H1612 גֶּפֶן (gephen, gheh'-fen): a vine (as twining), especially the grape. Origin: from an unused root meaning to bend; KJV: vine, tree.

H1613 גֹּפֶר (gôpher, go'-fer): a kind of tree or wood (as used for building), apparently the cypress. Origin: from an unused root, probably meaning to house in; KJV: gopher.

H1614 גׇּפְרִית (gophrîyth, gof-reeth'): properly, cypress-resin; by analogy, sulphur (as equally inflammable). Origin: probably feminine of H1613 (גֹּפֶר); KJV: brimstone.

H1615 גִּר (gir, gheer): lime (from being burned in a kiln). Origin: perhaps from H3564 (כּוּר); KJV: chalk(-stone).

H1616 גֵּר (gêr, gare): properly, a guest; by implication, a foreigner. Origin: or (fully) geyr (gare); from H1481 (גּוּר); KJV: alien, sojourner, stranger.

H1617 גֵּרָא (Gêrâʼ, gay-raw'): Gera, the name of six Israelites. Origin: perhaps from H1626 (גֵּרָה); a grain; KJV: Gera.

H1618 גָּרָב (gârâb, gaw-rawb'): scurf (from itching). Origin: from an unused root meaning to scratch; KJV: scab, scurvy.

H1619 גָּרֵב (Gârêb, gaw-rabe'): Gareb, the name of an Israelite, also of a hill near Jerusalem. Origin: from the same as H1618 (גָּרָב); scabby; KJV: Gareb.

H1620 גַּרְגַּר (gargar, gar-gar'): a berry (as if a pellet of rumination). Origin: by reduplication from H1641 (גָּרַר); KJV: berry.

H1621 גַּרְגְּרוֹת (gargᵉrôwth, gar-gher-owth'): the throat (as used in rumination). Origin: feminine plural from H1641 (גָּרַר); KJV: neck.

H1622 גִּרְגָּשִׁי (Girgâshîy, ghir-gaw-shee'): a Girgashite, one of the native tribes of Canaan. Origin: patrial from an unused name (of uncertain derivation); KJV: Girgashite, Girgasite.

H1623 גָּרַד (gârad, gaw-rad'): to abrade. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: scrape.

H1624 גָּרָה (gârâh, gaw-raw'): properly, to grate, i.e. (figuratively) to anger. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: contend, meddle, stir up, strive.

H1625 גֵּרָה (gêrâh, gay-raw'): the cud (as scraping the throat). Origin: from H1641 (גָּרַר); KJV: cud.

H1626 גֵּרָה (gêrâh, gay-raw'): a gerah or small weight (and coin). Origin: from H1641 (גָּרַר) (as in H1625 (גֵּרָה)); properly, (like H1620 (גַּרְגַּר)) a kernel (round as if scraped), i.e. KJV: gerah.

H1627 גָּרוֹן (gârôwn, gaw-rone'): the throat (as roughened by swallowing). Origin: or (shortened) גָּרֹן; from H1641 (גָּרַר); (compare H1621 (גַּרְגְּרוֹת)) KJV: [idiom] aloud, mouth, neck, throat.

H1628 גֵּרוּת (gêrûwth, gay-rooth'): a (temporary) residence. Origin: from H1481 (גּוּר); KJV: habitation.

H1629 גָּרַז (gâraz, gaw-raz'): to cut off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut off.

H1630 גְּרִזִים (Gᵉrizîym, gher-ee-zeem'): Gerizim, a mountain of Palestine. Origin: plural of an unused noun from H1629 (גָּרַז) (compare H1511 (גִּזְרִי)), cut up (i.e. rocky); KJV: Gerizim.

H1631 גַּרְזֶן (garzen, gar-zen'): an axe. Origin: from H1629 (גָּרַז); KJV: ax.

H1632 גָּרֹל (gârôl, gaw-role'): harsh. Origin: from the same as H1486 (גּוֹרָל); KJV: man of great (as in the margin which reads H1419 (גָּדוֹל)).

H1633 גָּרַם (gâram, gaw-ram'): (causative) to bone, i.e. denude (by extensive, craunch) the bones. Origin: a primitive root; to be spare or skeleton-like; used only as a denominative from H1634 (גֶּרֶם); KJV: gnaw the bones, break.

H1634 גֶּרֶם (gerem, gheh'-rem): a bone (as the skeleton of the body); hence, self, i.e. (figuratively) very. Origin: from H1633 (גָּרַם); KJV: bone, strong, top.

H1635 גֶּרֶם (gerem, gheh'-rem): a bone. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1634 (גֶּרֶם); KJV: bone.

H1636 גַּרְמִי (Garmîy, gar-mee'): bony, i.e. strong. Origin: from H1634 (גֶּרֶם); KJV: Garmite.

H1637 גֹּרֶן (gôren, go'-ren): a threshing-floor (as made even); by analogy, any open area. Origin: from an unused root meaning to smooth; KJV: (barn, corn, threshing-) floor, (threshing-, void) place.

H1638 גָּרַס (gâraç, gaw-ras'): to crush; also (intransitively and figuratively) to dissolve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break.

H1639 גָּרַע (gâraʻ, gaw-rah'): to scrape off; by implication, to shave, remove, lessen, withhold. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abate, clip, (di-) minish, do (take) away, keep back, restrain, make small, withdraw.

H1640 גָּרַף (gâraph, gaw-raf'): to bear off violently. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sweep away.

H1641 גָּרַר (gârar, gaw-rar'): to drag off roughly; by implication, to bring up the cud (i.e. ruminate); by analogy, to saw. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch, chew, [idiom] continuing, destroy, saw.

H1642 גְּרָר (Gᵉrâr, gher-awr'): Gerar, a Philistine city. Origin: probably from H1641 (גָּרַר); a rolling country; KJV: Gerar.

H1643 גֶּרֶשׂ (geres, gheh'-res): a kernel (collectively), i.e. grain. Origin: from an unused root meaning to husk; KJV: beaten corn.

H1644 גָּרַשׁ (gârash, gaw-rash'): to drive out from a possession; especially to expatriate or divorce. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast up (out), divorced (woman), drive away (forth, out), expel, [idiom] surely put away, trouble, thrust out.

H1645 גֶּרֶשׁ (geresh, gheh'-resh): produce (as if expelled). Origin: from H1644 (גָּרַשׁ); KJV: put forth.

H1646 גְרֻשָׁה (gᵉrushâh, gher-oo-shaw'): (abstractly) dispossession. Origin: feminine passive participle of H1644 (גָּרַשׁ); KJV: exaction.

H1647 גֵּרְשֹׁם (Gêrᵉshôm, gay-resh-ome'): Gereshom, the name of four Israelites. Origin: for H1648 (גֵּרְשׁוֹן); KJV: Gershom.

H1648 גֵּרְשׁוֹן (Gêrᵉshôwn, gay-resh-one'): Gereshon or Gereshom, an Israelite. Origin: or גֵּרְשׁוֹם; from H1644 (גָּרַשׁ); a refugee; KJV: Gershon, Gershom.

H1649 גֵּרְשֻׁנִּי (Gêrᵉshunnîy, gay-resh-oon-nee'): a Gereshonite or descendant of Gereshon. Origin: patronymically from H1648 (גֵּרְשׁוֹן); KJV: Gershonite, sons of Gershon.

H1650 גְּשׁוּר (Gᵉshûwr, ghesh-oor'): Geshur, a district of Syria. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to join); bridge; KJV: Geshur, Geshurite.

H1651 גְּשׁוּרִי (Gᵉshûwrîy, ghe-shoo-ree'): a Geshurite (also collectively) or inhabitants of Geshur. Origin: patrial from H1650 (גְּשׁוּר); KJV: Geshuri, Geshurites.

H1652 גָּשַׁם (gâsham, gaw-sham'): to shower violently. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) rain.

H1653 גֶּשֶׁם (geshem, gheh'-shem): a shower. Origin: from H1652 (גָּשַׁם); KJV: rain, shower.

H1654 גֶּשֶׁם (Geshem, gheh'-shem): Geshem or Gashmu, an Arabian. Origin: or (prolonged) גַּשְׁמוּ; the same as H1653 (גֶּשֶׁם); KJV: Geshem, Gashmu.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1655 to H1786
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1655 גֶּשֶׁם (geshem, gheh'-shem): used in a peculiar sense, the body (probably for the (figuratively) idea of a hard rain). Origin: (Aramaic) apparently the same as H1653 (גֶּשֶׁם); KJV: body.

H1656 גֹּשֶׁם (gôshem, go'-shem): {a shower}. Origin: from H1652 (גָּשַׁם); equivalent to H1653 (גֶּשֶׁם) KJV: rained upon.

H1657 גֹּשֶׁן (Gôshen, go'-shen): Goshen, the residence of the Israelites in Egypt; also a place in Palestine. Origin: probably of Egyptian origin; KJV: Goshen.

H1658 גִּשְׁפָּא (Gishpâʼ, ghish-paw'): Gishpa, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Gispa.

H1659 גָּשַׁשׁ (gâshash, gaw-shash'): to feel about. Origin: a primitive root; apparently KJV: grope.

H1660 גַּת (gath, gath): a wine-press (or vat for holding the grapes in pressing them). Origin: probably from H5059 (נָגַן) (in the sense of treading out grapes); KJV: (wine-) press (fat).

H1661 גַּת (Gath, gath): Gath, a Philistine city. Origin: the same as H1660 (גַּת); KJV: Gath.

H1662 גַּת־הַחֵפֶר (Gath-ha-Chêpher, gath-hah-khay'-fer): Gath-Chepher, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (abridged) גִּתָּה־חֵפֶר; from H1660 (גַּת) and H2658 (חָפַר) with the article inserted; wine-press of (the) well; KJV: Gath-kephr, Gittah-kephr.

H1663 גִּתִּי (Gittîy, ghit-tee'): a Gittite or inhabitant of Gath. Origin: patrial from H1661 (גַּת); KJV: Gittite.

H1664 גִּתַּיִם (Gittayim, ghit-tah'-yim): Gittajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of H1660 (גַּת); double winepress; KJV: Gittaim.

H1665 גִּתִּית (Gittîyth, ghit-teeth'): a Gittite harp. Origin: feminine of H1663 (גִּתִּי); KJV: Gittith.

H1666 גֶּתֶר (Gether, gheh'-ther): Gether, a son of Aram, and the region settled by him. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Gether.

H1667 גַּת־רִמּוֹן (Gath-Rimmôwn, gath-rim-mone'): Gath-Rimmon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1660 (גַּת) and H7416 (רִמּוֹן); wine-press of (the) pomegranate; KJV: Gath-rimmon. d

H1668 דָּא (dâʼ, daw): this. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2088 (זֶה); KJV: one..another, this.

H1669 דָּאַב (dâʼab, daw-ab'): to pine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mourn, sorrow(-ful).

H1670 דְּאָבָה (dᵉʼâbâh, deh-aw-baw'): properly, pining; by analogy, fear. Origin: from H1669 (דָּאַב); KJV: sorrow.

H1671 דְּאָבוֹן (dᵉʼâbôwn, deh-aw-bone'): pining. Origin: from H1669 (דָּאַב); KJV: sorrow.

H1672 דָּאַג (dâʼag, daw-ag'): be anxious. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be afraid (careful, sorry), sorrow, take thought.

H1673 דֹּאֵג (Dôʼêg, do-ayg'): Doeg, an Edomite. Origin: or (fully) דּוֹאֵג; active participle of H1672 (דָּאַג); anxious; KJV: Doeg.

H1674 דְּאָגָה (dᵉʼâgâh, deh-aw-gaw'): anxiety. Origin: from H1672 (דָּאַג); KJV: care(-fulness), fear, heaviness, sorrow.

H1675 דָּאָה (dâʼâh, daw-aw'): to dart, i.e. fly rapidly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fly.

H1676 דָּאָה (dâʼâh, daw-aw'): the kite (from its rapid flight). Origin: from H1675 (דָּאָה); KJV: vulture. See H7201 (רָאָה).

H1677 דֹּב (dôb, dobe): the bear (as slow). Origin: or (fully) דּוֹב; from H1680 (דָּבַב); KJV: bear.

H1678 דֹּב (dôb, dobe): {the bear (as slow)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1677 (דֹּב) KJV: bear.

H1679 דֹּבֶא (dôbeʼ, do'-beh): quiet. Origin: from an unused root (compare H1680 (דָּבַב)) (probably meaning to be sluggish, i.e. restful); KJV: strength.

H1680 דָּבַב (dâbab, daw-bab'): to move slowly, i.e. glide. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1679 (דֹּבֶא)); KJV: cause to speak.

H1681 דִּבָּה (dibbâh, dib-baw'): slander. Origin: from H1680 (דָּבַב) (in the sense of furtive motion); KJV: defaming, evil report, infamy, slander.

H1682 דְּבוֹרָה (dᵉbôwrâh, deb-o-raw'): the bee (from its systematic instincts). Origin: or (shortened) דְּבֹרָה; from H1696 (דָבַר) (in the sense of orderly motion); KJV: bee.

H1683 דְּבּוֹרָה (Dᵉbôwrâh, deb-o-raw'): Deborah, the name of two Hebrewesses. Origin: or (shortened) דְּבֹרָה; the same as H1682 (דְּבוֹרָה); KJV: Deborah.

H1684 דְּבַח (dᵉbach, deb-akh'): to sacrifice (an animal). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2076 (זָבַח); KJV: offer (sacrifice).

H1685 דְּבַח (dᵉbach, deb-akh'): a sacrifice. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1684 (דְּבַח); KJV: sacrifice.

H1686 דִּבְיוֹן (dibyôwn, dib-yone'): probably some cheap vegetable, perhaps a bulbous root. Origin: in the margin for the textual reading, חֶרְיוֹן; both, (in the plural only and) of uncertain derivation, KJV: dove's dung.

H1687 דְּבִיר (dᵉbîyr, deb-eer'): the shrine or innermost part of the sanctuary. Origin: or (shortened) דְּבִר; from H1696 (דָבַר) (apparently in the sense of oracle); KJV: oracle.

H1688 דְּבִיר (Dᵉbîyr, deb-eer'): Debir, the name of an Amoritish king and of two places in Palestine. Origin: or (shortened) דְּבִר; (Joshua 13:26 (but see H3810 (לֹא דְבַר))), the same as H1687 (דְּבִיר); KJV: Debir.

H1689 דִּבְלָה (Diblâh, dib-law'): Diblah, a place in Syria. Origin: probably an orthographical error for H7247 (רִבְלָה); KJV: Diblath.

H1690 דְּבֵלָה (dᵉbêlâh, deb-ay-law'): a cake of pressed figs. Origin: from an unused root (akin to H2082 (זָבַל)) probably meaning to press together; KJV: cake (lump) of figs.

H1691 דִּבְלַיִם (Diblayim, dib-lah'-yim): Diblajim, a symbolic name. Origin: dual from the masculine of H1690 (דְּבֵלָה); two cakes; KJV: Diblaim.

H1692 דָּבַק (dâbaq, daw-bak'): properly, to impinge, i.e. cling or adhere; figuratively, to catch by pursuit. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abide fast, cleave (fast together), follow close (hard after), be joined (together), keep (fast), overtake, pursue hard, stick, take.

H1693 דְּבַק (dᵉbaq, deb-ak'): to stick to. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1692 (דָּבַק); KJV: cleave.

H1694 דֶּבֶק (debeq, deh'-bek): a joint; by implication, solder. Origin: from H1692 (דָּבַק); KJV: joint, solder.

H1695 דָּבֵק (dâbêq, daw-bake'): adhering. Origin: from H1692 (דָּבַק); KJV: cleave, joining, stick closer.

H1696 דָבַר (dâbar, daw-bar'): perhaps properly, to arrange; but used figuratively (of words), to speak; rarely (in a destructive sense) to subdue. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: answer, appoint, bid, command, commune, declare, destroy, give, name, promise, pronounce, rehearse, say, speak, be spokesman, subdue, talk, teach, tell, think, use (entreaties), utter, [idiom] well, [idiom] work.

H1697 דָּבָר (dâbâr, daw-baw'): a word; by implication, a matter (as spoken of) or thing; adverbially, a cause. Origin: from H1696 (דָבַר); KJV: act, advice, affair, answer, [idiom] any such (thing), because of, book, business, care, case, cause, certain rate, [phrase] chronicles, commandment, [idiom] commune(-ication), [phrase] concern(-ing), [phrase] confer, counsel, [phrase] dearth, decree, deed, [idiom] disease, due, duty, effect, [phrase] eloquent, errand, (evil favoured-) ness, [phrase] glory, [phrase] harm, hurt, [phrase] iniquity, [phrase] judgment, language, [phrase] lying, manner, matter, message, (no) thing, oracle, [idiom] ought, [idiom] parts, [phrase] pertaining, [phrase] please, portion, [phrase] power, promise, provision, purpose, question, rate, reason, report, request, [idiom] (as hast) said, sake, saying, sentence, [phrase] sign, [phrase] so, some (uncleanness), somewhat to say, [phrase] song, speech, [idiom] spoken, talk, task, [phrase] that, [idiom] there done, thing (concerning), thought, [phrase] thus, tidings, what(-soever), [phrase] wherewith, which, word, work.

H1698 דֶּבֶר (deber, deh'-ber): a pestilence. Origin: from H1696 (דָבַר) (in the sense of destroying); KJV: murrain, pestilence, plague.

H1699 דֹּבֶר (dôber, do'-ber): a pasture (from its arrangement of the flock). Origin: from H1696 (דָבַר) (in its original sense); KJV: fold, manner.

H1700 דִּבְרָה (dibrâh, dib-raw'): a reason, suit or style. Origin: feminine of H1697 (דָּבָר); KJV: cause, end, estate, order, regard.

H1701 דִּבְרָה (dibrâh, dib-raw'): {a reason, suit or style}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1700 (דִּבְרָה) KJV: intent, sake.

H1702 דֹּבְרָה (dôbᵉrâh, do-ber-aw'): a raft. Origin: feminine active participle of H1696 (דָבַר) in the sense of driving (compare H1699 (דֹּבֶר)); KJV: float.

H1703 דַּבָּרָה (dabbârâh, dab-baw-raw'): a word. Origin: intensive from H1696 (דָבַר); KJV: word.

H1704 דִּבְרִי (Dibrîy, dib-ree'): Dibri, an Israelite. Origin: from H1697 (דָּבָר); wordy; KJV: Dibri.

H1705 דֲּבְרַת (Dăbrath, daw-ber-ath'): Daberath, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1697 (דָּבָר) (perhaps in the sense of H1699 (דֹּבֶר)); KJV: Dabareh, Daberath.

H1706 דְּבַשׁ (dᵉbash, deb-ash'): honey (from its stickiness); by analogy, syrup. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be gummy; KJV: honey(-comb).

H1707 דַּבֶּשֶׁת (dabbesheth, dab-beh'-sheth): a sticky mass, i.e. the hump of acamel. Origin: intensive from the same as H1706 (דְּבַשׁ); KJV: hunch (of a camel).

H1708 דַּבֶּשֶׁת (Dabbesheth, dab-beh'-sheth): Dabbesheth, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H1707 (דַּבֶּשֶׁת); KJV: Dabbesheth.

H1709 דָּג (dâg, dawg): a fish (often used collectively). Origin: or (fully) דָּאג; (Nehemiah 13:16), from H1711 (דָּגָה); a fish (as prolific); or perhaps rather from H1672 (דָּאַג) (as timid); but still better from H1672 (דָּאַג) (in the sense of squirming, i.e. moving by the vibratory action of the tail); KJV: fish.

H1710 דָּגָה (dâgâh, daw-gaw'): {a fish (often used collectively)}. Origin: feminine of H1709 (דָּג), and meaning the same KJV: fish.

H1711 דָּגָה (dâgâh, daw-gaw'): to spawn, i.e. become numerous. Origin: a primitive root; to move rapidly; used only as a denominative from H1709 (דָּג); KJV: grow.

H1712 דָּגוֹן (Dâgôwn, daw-gohn'): Dagon, a Philistine deity. Origin: from H1709 (דָּג); the fish-god; KJV: Dagon.

H1713 דָּגַל (dâgal, daw-gal'): to flaunt, i.e. raise a flag; figuratively, to be conspicuous. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (set up, with) banners, chiefest.

H1714 דֶּגֶל (degel, deh'-gel): a flag. Origin: from H1713 (דָּגַל); KJV: banner, standard.

H1715 דָּגָן (dâgân, daw-gawn'): properly, increase, i.e. grain. Origin: from H1711 (דָּגָה); KJV: corn (floor), wheat.

H1716 דָּגַר (dâgar, daw-gar'): to brood over eggs or young. Origin: a primitive root, KJV: gather, sit.

H1717 דַּד (dad, dad): the breast (as the seat of love, or from its shape). Origin: apparently from the same as H1730 (דּוֹד); KJV: breast, teat.

H1718 דָּדָה (dâdâh, daw-daw'): to walk gently. Origin: a doubtful root; KJV: go (softly, with).

H1719 דְּדָן (Dᵉdân, ded-awn'): Dedan, the name of two Cushites and of their territory. Origin: or (prolonged) דְּדָנֶה; (Ezekiel 25:13), of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dedan.

H1720 דְּדָנִים (Dᵉdânîym, ded-aw-neem'): Dedanites, the descendants or inhabitants of Dedan. Origin: plural of H1719 (דְּדָן) (as patrial); KJV: Dedanim.

H1721 דֹּדָנִים (Dôdânîym, do-daw-neem'): Dodanites, or descendants of a son of Javan. Origin: or (by orthographical error) רֹדָנִים (1 Chronicles 1:7); a plural of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dodanim.

H1722 דְּהַב (dᵉhab, deh-hab'): gold. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2091 (זָהָב); KJV: gold(-en).

H1723 דַּהֲוָא (Dahăvâʼ, dah-hav-aw'): Dahava, a people colonized in Samaria. Origin: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dehavites.

H1724 דָּהַם (dâham, daw-ham'): to be dumb, i.e. (figuratively) dumbfounded. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1740 (דּוּחַ)); KJV: astonished.

H1725 דָּהַר (dâhar, daw-har'): to curvet or move irregularly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pause.

H1726 דַּהֲהַר (dahăhar, dah-hah-har'): a gallop. Origin: by reduplication from H1725 (דָּהַר); KJV: pransing.

H1727 דּוּב (dûwb, doob): to mope, i.e. (figuratively) pine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sorrow.

H1728 דַּוָּג (davvâg, dav-vawg'): a fisherman. Origin: an orthographical variation of H1709 (דָּג) as a denominative (H1771 (דַּיָּג)); KJV: fisher.

H1729 דּוּגָה (dûwgâh, doo-gaw'): properly, fishery, i.e. a hook forfishing. Origin: feminine from the same as H1728 (דַּוָּג); KJV: fish (hook).

H1730 דּוֹד (dôwd, dode): (figuratively) to love; by implication, a love-token, lover, friend; specifically an uncle. Origin: or (shortened) דֹּד; from an unused root meaning properly, to boil, i.e. KJV: (well-) beloved, father's brother, love, uncle.

H1731 דּוּד (dûwd, dood): a pot (for boiling); also (by resemblance of shape) a basket. Origin: from the same as H1730 (דּוֹד); KJV: basket, caldron, kettle, (seething) pot.

H1732 דָּוִד (Dâvid, daw-veed'): David, the youngest son of Jesse. Origin: rarely (fully); דָּוִיד; from the same as H1730 (דּוֹד); loving; KJV: David.

H1733 דּוֹדָה (dôwdâh, do-daw'): an aunt. Origin: feminine of H1730 (דּוֹד); KJV: aunt, father's sister, uncle's wife.

H1734 דּוֹדוֹ (Dôwdôw, do-do'): Dodo, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H1730 (דּוֹד); loving; KJV: Dodo.

H1735 דּוֹדָוָהוּ (Dôwdâvâhûw, do-daw-vaw'-hoo): Dodavah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1730 (דּוֹד) and H3050 (יָהּ); love of Jah; KJV: Dodavah.

H1736 דּוּדַי (dûwday, doo-dah'-ee): a boiler or basket; also the mandrake (as an aphrodisiac). Origin: from H1731 (דּוּד); KJV: basket, mandrake.

H1737 דּוֹדַי (Dôwday, do-dah'ee): Dodai, an Israelite. Origin: formed like H1736 (דּוּדַי); amatory; KJV: Dodai.

H1738 דָּוָה (dâvâh, daw-vaw'): to be sick (as if in menstruation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: infirmity.

H1739 דָּוֶה (dâveh, daw-veh'): sick (especially in menstruation). Origin: from H1738 (דָּוָה); KJV: faint, menstruous cloth, she that is sick, having sickness.

H1740 דּוּחַ (dûwach, doo'-akh): to thrust away; figuratively, to cleanse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast out, purge, wash.

H1741 דְּוַי (dᵉvay, dev-ah'ee): sickness; figuratively, loathing. Origin: from H1739 (דָּוֶה); KJV: languishing, sorrowful.

H1742 דַּוָּי (davvây, dav-voy'): sick; figuratively, troubled. Origin: from H1739 (דָּוֶה); KJV: faint.

H1743 דּוּךְ (dûwk, dook): to bruise in a mortar. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat.

H1744 דּוּכִיפַת (dûwkîyphath, doo-kee-fath'): the hoopoe or else the grouse. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: lapwing.

H1745 דּוּמָה (dûwmâh, doo-maw'): silence; figuratively, death. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be dumb (compare H1820 (דָּמָה)); KJV: silence.

H1746 דּוּמָה (Dûwmâh, doo-maw'): Dumah, a tribe and region of Arabia. Origin: the same as H1745 (דּוּמָה); KJV: Dumah.

H1747 דּוּמִיָּה (dûwmîyâh, doo-me-yaw'): stillness; adverbially, silently; abstractly quiet, trust. Origin: from H1820 (דָּמָה); KJV: silence, silent, waiteth.

H1748 דּוּמָם (dûwmâm, doo-mawm'): still; adverbially, silently. Origin: from H1826 (דָּמַם); KJV: dumb, silent, quietly wait.

H1749 דּוֹנַג (dôwnag, do-nag'): wax. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: wax.

H1750 דּוּץ (dûwts, doots): to leap. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be turned.

H1751 דּוּק (dûwq, dook): to crumble. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1854 (דָּקַק); KJV: be broken to pieces.

H1752 דּוּר (dûwr, dure): properly, to gyrate (or move in a circle), i.e. to remain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dwell.

H1753 דּוּר (dûwr, dure): to reside. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1752 (דּוּר); KJV: dwell.

H1754 דּוּר (dûwr, dure): a circle, ball or pile. Origin: from H1752 (דּוּר); KJV: ball, turn, round about.

H1755 דּוֹר (dôwr, dore): properly, a revolution of time, i.e. an age or generation; also a dwelling. Origin: or (shortened) דֹּר; from H1752 (דּוּר); KJV: age, [idiom] evermore, generation, (n-) ever, posterity.

H1756 דּוֹר (Dôwr, dore): Dor, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (by permutation) דֹּאר; (Joshua 17:11; 1 Kings 4:11), from H1755 (דּוֹר); dwelling; KJV: Dor.

H1757 דּוּרָא (Dûwrâʼ, doo-raw'): Dura, a place in Babylonia. Origin: (Aramaic) probably from H1753 (דּוּר); circle or dwelling; KJV: Dura.

H1758 דּוּשׁ (dûwsh, doosh): to trample or thresh. Origin: or דּוֹשׁ; or דִּישׁ; a primitive root; KJV: break, tear, thresh, tread out (down), at grass (Jeremiah 50:11, by mistake for H1877 (דֶּשֶׁא)).

H1759 דּוּשׁ (dûwsh, doosh): to trample. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1758 (דּוּשׁ); KJV: tread down.

H1760 דָּחָה (dâchâh, daw-khaw'): to push down. Origin: or דָּחַח; (Jeremiah 23:12), a primitive root; KJV: chase, drive away (on), overthrow, outcast, [idiom] sore, thrust, totter.

H1761 דַּחֲוָה (dachăvâh, dakh-av-aw'): probably a musical instrument (as being struck). Origin: (Aramaic) from the equivalent of H1760 (דָּחָה); KJV: instrument of music.

H1762 דְּחִי (dᵉchîy, deh-khee'): a push, i.e. (by implication) a fall. Origin: from H1760 (דָּחָה); KJV: falling.

H1763 דְּחַל (dᵉchal, deh-khal'): to slink, i.e. (by implication) to fear, or (causatively) be formidable. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2119 (זָחַל); KJV: make afraid, dreadful, fear, terrible.

H1764 דֹּחַן (dôchan, do'-khan): millet. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: millet.

H1765 דָּחַף (dâchaph, daw-khaf'): to urge, i.e. hasten. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) haste(-ned), pressed on.

H1766 דָּחַק (dâchaq, daw-khak'): to press, i.e. oppress. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: thrust, vex.

H1767 דַּי (day, dahee): enough (as noun or adverb), used chiefly with preposition in phrases. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: able, according to, after (ability), among, as (oft as), (more than) enough, from, in, since, (much as is) sufficient(-ly), too much, very, when.

H1768 דִּי (dîy, dee): that, used as relative conjunction, and especially (with a preposition) in adverbial phrases; also as preposition of. Origin: (Aramaic) apparently for H1668 (דָּא); KJV: [idiom] as, but, for(-asmuch [phrase]), [phrase] now, of, seeing, than, that, therefore, until, [phrase] what (-soever), when, which, whom, whose.

H1769 דִּיבוֹן (Dîybôwn, dee-bome'): Dibon, the name of three places in Palestine. Origin: or (shortened) דִּיבֹן; from H1727 (דּוּב); pining KJV: Dibon. (Also, with H1410 (גָּד) added, Dibon-gad.)

H1770 דִּיג (dîyg, deeg): to fish. Origin: denominative from H1709 (דָּג); KJV: fish.

H1771 דַּיָּג (dayâg, dah-yawg'): a fisherman. Origin: from H1770 (דִּיג); KJV: fisher.

H1772 דַּיָּה (dayâh, dah-yaw'): a falcon (from its rapid flight). Origin: intensive from H1675 (דָּאָה); KJV: vulture.

H1773 דְּיוֹ (dᵉyôw, deh-yo'): ink. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: ink.

H1774 דִּי זָהָב (Dîy zâhâb, dee zaw-hawb'): Dizahab, a place in the Desert. Origin: as if from H1768 (דִּי) and H2091 (זָהָב); of gold; KJV: Dizahab.

H1775 דִּימוֹן (Dîymôwn, dee-mone'): Dimon, a place in Palestine. Origin: perhaps for H1769 (דִּיבוֹן); KJV: Dimon.

H1776 דִּימוֹנָה (Dîymôwnâh, dee-mo-naw'): Dimonah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H1775 (דִּימוֹן); KJV: Dimonah.

H1777 דִּין (dîyn, deen): a straight course, i.e. sail direct. Origin: or (Genesis 6:3) דּוּן; a primitive root; KJV: (come) with a straight course.

H1778 דִּין (dîyn, deen): to judge. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1777 (דִּין); KJV: judge.

H1779 דִּין (dîyn, deen): judgement (the suit, justice, sentence or tribunal); by implication also strife. Origin: or (Job 19:29) דּוּן; from H1777 (דִּין); KJV: cause, judgement, plea, strife.

H1780 דִּין (dîyn, deen): {judgement (the suit, justice, sentence or tribunal); by implication also strife}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1779 (דִּין) KJV: judgement.

H1781 דַּיָּן (dayân, dah-yawn'): a judge or advocate. Origin: from H1777 (דִּין); KJV: judge.

H1782 דַּיָּן (dayân, dah-yawn'): {a judge or advocate}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1781 (דַּיָּן) KJV: judge.

H1783 דִּינָה (Dîynâh, dee-naw'): Dinah, the daughter of Jacob. Origin: feminine of H1779 (דִּין); justice; KJV: Dinah.

H1784 דִּינַי (Dîynay, dee-nah'-ee): a Dinaite or inhabitant of some unknown Assyria province. Origin: (Aramaic) partial from uncertain primitive; KJV: Dinaite.

H1785 דָּיֵק (dâyêq, daw-yake'): a battering-tower. Origin: from a root corresp. to H1751 (דּוּק); KJV: fort.

H1786 דַּיִשׁ (dayish, dah-yish'): threshing-time. Origin: from H1758 (דּוּשׁ); KJV: threshing.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1787 to H1922
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1787 דִּישׁוֹן (Dîyshôwn, dee-shone'): Dishon, the name of two Edomites. Origin: (Diyshon, the same as H1788 (דִּישֹׁן); KJV: Dishon.

H1788 דִּישֹׁן (dîyshôn, dee-shone'): the leaper, i.e. an antelope. Origin: from H1758 (דּוּשׁ); KJV: pygarg.

H1789 דִּישָׁן (Dîyshân, dee-shawn'): Dishan, an Edomite. Origin: another form of H1787 (דִּישׁוֹן) KJV: Dishan, Dishon.

H1790 דַּךְ (dak, dak): crushed, i.e. (figuratively) injured. Origin: from an unused root (compare H1794 (דָּכָה)); KJV: afflicted, oppressed.

H1791 דֵּךְ (dêk, dake): this. Origin: (Aramaic) or דָּךְ; (Aramaic), prolonged from H1668 (דָּא); KJV: the same, this.

H1792 דָּכָא (dâkâʼ, daw-kaw'): to crumble; transitively, to bruise (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root (compare H1794 (דָּכָה)); KJV: beat to pieces, break (in pieces), bruise, contrite, crush, destroy, humble, oppress, smite.

H1793 דַּכָּא (dakkâʼ, dak-kaw'): crushed (literally powder, or figuratively, contrite). Origin: from H1792 (דָּכָא); KJV: contrite, destruction.

H1794 דָּכָה (dâkâh, daw-kaw'): to collapse (phys. or mentally). Origin: a primitive root (compare H1790 (דַּךְ), H1792 (דָּכָא)); KJV: break (sore), contrite, crouch.

H1795 דַּכָּה (dakkâh, dak-kaw'): mutilated. Origin: from H1794 (דָּכָה) like H1793 (דַּכָּא); KJV: [phrase] wounded.

H1796 דֳּכִי (dŏkîy, dok-ee'): a dashing of surf. Origin: from H1794 (דָּכָה); KJV: wave.

H1797 דִּכֵּן (dikkên, dik-kane'): this. Origin: (Aramaic) prolonged from H1791 (דֵּךְ); KJV: same, that, this.

H1798 דְּכַר (dᵉkar, dek-ar'): properly, a male, i.e. of sheep. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2145 (זָכָר); KJV: ram.

H1799 דִּכְרוֹן (dikrôwn, dik-rone'): a register. Origin: (Aramaic) or דׇּכְרָן (Aramaic); corresponding to H2146 (זִכְרוֹן); KJV: record.

H1800 דַּל (dal, dal): properly, dangling, i.e. (by implication) weak or thin. Origin: from H1809 (דָּלַל); KJV: lean, needy, poor (man), weaker.

H1801 דָּלַג (dâlag, daw-lag'): to spring. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: leap.

H1802 דָּלָה (dâlâh, daw-law'): properly, to dangle, i.e. to let down abucket (for drawing out water); figuratively, to deliver. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1809 (דָּלַל)); KJV: draw (out), [idiom] enough, lift up.

H1803 דַּלָּה (dallâh, dal-law'): properly, something dangling, i.e. a loose thread or hair; figuratively, indigent. Origin: from H1802 (דָּלָה); KJV: hair, pining sickness, poor(-est sort).

H1804 דָּלַח (dâlach, daw-lakh'): to roil water. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: trouble.

H1805 דְּלִי (dᵉlîy, del-ee'): a pail or jar (for drawing water). Origin: or דֳּלִי; from H1802 (דָּלָה); KJV: bucket.

H1806 דְּלָיָה (Dᵉlâyâh, del-aw-yaw'): Delajah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or (prolonged) דְּלָיָהוּxlit Dᵉlâyâhhûw corrected to Dᵉlâyâhûw; from H1802 (דָּלָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has delivered; KJV: Dalaiah, Delaiah.

H1807 דְּלִילָה (Dᵉlîylâh, del-ee-law'): Delilah, a Philistine woman. Origin: from H1809 (דָּלַל); languishing KJV: Delilah.

H1808 דָּלִיָּה (dâlîyâh, daw-lee-yaw'): something dangling, i.e. a bough. Origin: from H1802 (דָּלָה); KJV: branch.

H1809 דָּלַל (dâlal, daw-lal'): to slacken or be feeble; figuratively, to be oppressed. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1802 (דָּלָה)); KJV: bring low, dry up, be emptied, be not equal, fail, be impoverished, be made thin.

H1810 דִּלְעָן (Dilʻân, dil-awn'): Dilan, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dilean.

H1811 דָּלַף (dâlaph, daw-laf'): to drip; by implication, to weep. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drop through, melt, pour out.

H1812 דֶּלֶף (deleph, deh'-lef): a dripping. Origin: from H1811 (דָּלַף); KJV: dropping.

H1813 דַּלְפוֹן (Dalphôwn, dal-fone'): Dalphon, a son of Haman. Origin: from H1811 (דָּלַף); dripping; KJV: Dalphon.

H1814 דָּלַק (dâlaq, daw-lak'): to flame (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burning, chase, inflame, kindle, persecute(-or), pursue hotly.

H1815 דְּלַק (dᵉlaq, del-ak'): {to flame (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1814 (דָּלַק) KJV: burn.

H1816 דַּלֶּקֶת (dalleqeth, dal-lek'-keth): a burning fever. Origin: ; from H1814 (דָּלַק); KJV: inflammation.

H1817 דֶּלֶת (deleth, deh'-leth): something swinging, i.e. the valve of adoor. Origin: from H1802 (דָּלָה); KJV: door (two-leaved), gate, leaf, lid. (Psalm 141:3).

H1818 דָּם (dâm, dawm): blood (as that which when shed causes death) of man or an animal; by analogy, the juice of the grape; figuratively (especially in the plural) bloodshed (i.e. drops of blood). Origin: from H1826 (דָּמַם) (compare H119 (אָדַם)); KJV: blood(-y, -guiltiness, (-thirsty), [phrase] innocent.

H1819 דָּמָה (dâmâh, daw-maw'): to compare; by implication, to resemble, liken, consider. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: compare, devise, (be) like(-n), mean, think, use similitudes.

H1820 דָּמָה (dâmâh, daw-mam'): to be dumb or silent; hence, to fail or perish; trans. to destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease, be cut down (off), destroy, be brought to silence, be undone, [idiom] utterly.

H1821 דְּמָה (dᵉmâh, dem-aw'): to resemble. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1819 (דָּמָה); KJV: be like.

H1822 דֻּמָּה (dummâh, doom-maw'): desolation; concretely, desolate. Origin: from H1820 (דָּמָה); KJV: destroy.

H1823 דְּמוּת (dᵉmûwth, dem-ooth'): resemblance; concretely, model, shape; adverbially, like. Origin: from H1819 (דָּמָה); KJV: fashion, like (-ness, as), manner, similitude.

H1824 דְּמִי (dᵉmîy, dem-ee'): quiet. Origin: or דֳּמִי; from H1820 (דָּמָה); KJV: cutting off, rest, silence.

H1825 דִּמְיוֹן (dimyôwn, dim-yone'): resemblance. Origin: from H1819 (דָּמָה); KJV: [idiom] like.

H1826 דָּמַם (dâmam, daw-man'): to be dumb; by implication, to be astonished, to stop; also to perish. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1724 (דָּהַם), H1820 (דָּמָה)); KJV: cease, be cut down (off), forbear, hold peace, quiet self, rest, be silent, keep (put to) silence, be (stand) still, tarry, wait.

H1827 דְּמָמָה (dᵉmâmâh, dem-aw-maw'): quiet. Origin: feminine from H1826 (דָּמַם); KJV: calm, silence, still.

H1828 דֹּמֶן (dômen, do'-men): manure. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: dung.

H1829 דִּמְנָה (Dimnâh, dim-naw'): Dimnah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine from the same as H1828 (דֹּמֶן); a dung-heap; KJV: Dimnah.

H1830 דָּמַע (dâmaʻ, daw-mah'): to weep. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] sore, weep.

H1831 דֶּמַע (demaʻ, dah'-mah): a tear; figuratively, juice. Origin: from H1830 (דָּמַע); KJV: liquor.

H1832 דִּמְעָה (dimʻâh, dim-aw'): weeping. Origin: feminine of H1831 (דֶּמַע); KJV: tears.

H1833 דְּמֶשֶׁק (dᵉmesheq, dem-eh'-shek): damask (as a fabric of Damascus). Origin: by orthographical variation from H1834 (דַּמֶּשֶׂק); KJV: in Damascus.

H1834 דַּמֶּשֶׂק (Dammeseq, dam-meh'-sek): Damascus, a city of Syria. Origin: or דּוּמֶשֶׂק; or דַּרְמֶשֶׂק; of foreign origin; KJV: Damascus.

H1835 דָּן (Dân, dawn): Dan, one of the sons of Jacob; also the tribe descended from him, and its territory; likewise a place in Palestine colonized by them. Origin: from H1777 (דִּין); judge; KJV: Daniel

H1836 דֵּן (dên, dane): this. Origin: (Aramaic) an orthographical variation of H1791 (דֵּךְ); KJV: (afore-) time, [phrase] after this manner, here (-after), one...another, such, there(-fore), these, this (matter), [phrase] thus, where(-fore), which.

H1837 דַּנָּה (Dannâh, dan-naw'): Dannah, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dannah.

H1838 דִּנְהָבָה (Dinhâbâh, din-haw-baw'): Dinhabah, an Edomitish town. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dinhaban.

H1839 דָּנִי (Dânîy, daw-nee'): a Danite (often collectively) or descendants (or inhabitants) of Dan. Origin: patronymically from H1835 (דָּן); KJV: Danites, of Daniel

H1840 דָנִיֵּאל (Dânîyêʼl, daw-nee-yale'): Daniel or Danijel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: in Ezekiel it is; דָּנִאֵל; from H1835 (דָּן) and H410 (אֵל); judge of God; KJV: Daniel.

H1841 דָּנִיֵּאל (Dânîyêʼl, daw-nee-yale'): Danijel, the Hebrew prophet. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1840 (דָנִיֵּאל); KJV: Daniel.

H1842 דָּן יַעַן (Dân Yaʻan, dawn yah'-an): Dan-Jaan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1835 (דָּן) and (apparently) H3282 (יַעַן); judge of purpose; KJV: Dan-jaan.

H1843 דֵּעַ (dêaʻ, day'-ah): knowledge. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: knowledge, opinion.

H1844 דֵּעָה (dêʻâh, day-aw'): knowledge. Origin: feminine of H1843 (דֵּעַ); KJV: knowledge.

H1845 דְּעוּאֵל (Dᵉʻûwʼêl, deh-oo-ale'): Deuel, an Israelite. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע) and H410 (אֵל); known of God; KJV: Deuel.

H1846 דָּעַךְ (dâʻak, daw-ak'): to be extinguished; figuratively, to expire or be dried up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be extinct, consumed, put out, quenched.

H1847 דַּעַת (daʻath, dah'-ath): knowledge. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: cunning, (ig-) norantly, know(-ledge), (un-) awares (wittingly).

H1848 דׇּפִי (dophîy, dof'-ee): a stumbling-block. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to push over); KJV: slanderest.

H1849 דָּפַק (dâphaq, daw-fak'): to knock; by analogy, to press severely. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat, knock, overdrive.

H1850 דׇּפְקָה (Dophqâh, dof-kaw'): Dophkah, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H1849 (דָּפַק); a knock; KJV: Dophkah.

H1851 דַּק (daq, dak): crushed, i.e. (by implication) small or thin. Origin: from H1854 (דָּקַק); KJV: dwarf, lean(-fleshed), very little thing, small, thin.

H1852 דֹּק (dôq, doke): something crumbling, i.e. fine (as a thin cloth). Origin: from H1854 (דָּקַק); KJV: curtain.

H1853 דִּקְלָה (Diqlâh, dik-law'): Diklah, a region of Arabia. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Diklah.

H1854 דָּקַק (dâqaq, daw-kak'): to crush (or intransitively) crumble. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1915 (הָדַךְ)lemma הָדךְ missing vowel, corrected to הָדַךְ); KJV: beat in pieces (small), bruise, make dust, (into) [idiom] powder, (be, very) small, stamp (small).

H1855 דְּקַק (dᵉqaq, dek-ak'): to crumble or (trans.) crush. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1854 (דָּקַק); KJV: break to pieces.

H1856 דָּקַר (dâqar, daw-kar'): to stab; by analogy, to starve; figuratively, to revile. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pierce, strike (thrust) through, wound.

H1857 דֶּקֶר (Deqer, deh'-ker): Deker, an Israelite. Origin: from H1856 (דָּקַר); a stab; KJV: Dekar.

H1858 דַּר (dar, dar): properly, a pearl (from its sheen as rapidly turned); by analogy, pearl-stone, i.e. mother-of-pearl or alabaster. Origin: apparently from the same as H1865 (דְּרוֹר); KJV: [idiom] white.

H1859 דָּר (dâr, dawr): an age. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1755 (דּוֹר); KJV: generation.

H1860 דְּרָאוֹן (dᵉrâʼôwn, der-aw-one'): an object of aversion. Origin: or דֵּרָאוֹן; from an unused root (meaning to repulse); KJV: abhorring, contempt.

H1861 דׇּרְבוֹן (dorbôwn, dor-bone'): a goad. Origin: (also dor-bawn'); of uncertain derivation; KJV: goad.

H1862 דַּרְדַּע (Dardaʻ, dar-dah'): Darda, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H1858 (דַּר) and H1843 (דֵּעַ); pearl of knowledge; KJV: Darda.

H1863 דַּרְדַּר (dardar, dar-dar'): a thorn. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: thistle.

H1864 דָּרוֹם (dârôwm, daw-rome'): the south; poet. the south wind. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: south.

H1865 דְּרוֹר (dᵉrôwr, der-ore'): freedom; hence, spontaneity of outflow, and so clear. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to move rapidly); KJV: liberty, pure.

H1866 דְּרוֹר (dᵉrôwr, der-ore'): the swift, a kind of swallow. Origin: the same as H1865 (דְּרוֹר), applied to a bird; KJV: swallow.

H1867 דָּֽרְיָוֵשׁ (Dârᵉyâvêsh, daw-reh-yaw-vaysh'): Darejavesh, a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Darius.

H1868 דָּֽרְיָוֵשׁ (Dârᵉyâvêsh, daw-reh-yaw-vaysh'): {Darejavesh, a title (rather than name) of several Persian kings}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1867 (דָּֽרְיָוֵשׁ) KJV: Darius.

H1869 דָּרַךְ (dârak, daw-rak'): to tread; by implication, to walk; also to string abow (by treading on it in bending). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: archer, bend, come, draw, go (over), guide, lead (forth), thresh, tread (down), walk.

H1870 דֶּרֶךְ (derek, deh'-rek): a road (as trodden); figuratively, a course of life or mode of action, often adverb. Origin: from H1869 (דָּרַךְ); KJV: along, away, because of, [phrase] by, conversation, custom, (east-) ward, journey, manner, passenger, through, toward, (high-) (path-) way(-side), whither(-soever).

H1871 דַּרְכְּמוֹן (darkᵉmôwn, dar-kem-one'): a 'drachma', or coin. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: dram.

H1872 דְּרַע (dᵉraʻ, der-aw'): an arm. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2220 (זְרוֹעַ); KJV: arm.
