H1873 דָּרַע (Dâraʻ, daw-rah'): Dara, an Israelite. Origin: probably a contraction from H1862 (דַּרְדַּע); KJV: Dara.

H1874 דַּרְקוֹן (Darqôwn, dar-kone'): Darkon, one of 'Solomon's servants'. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Darkon.

H1875 דָּרַשׁ (dârash, daw-rash'): properly, to tread or frequent; usually to follow (for pursuit or search); by implication, to seek or ask; specifically to worship. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: ask, [idiom] at all, care for, [idiom] diligently, inquire, make inquisition, (necro-) mancer, question, require, search, seek (for, out), [idiom] surely.

H1876 דָּשָׁא (dâshâʼ, daw-shaw'): to sprout. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring forth, spring.

H1877 דֶּשֶׁא (desheʼ, deh'-sheh): a sprout; by analogy, grass. Origin: from H1876 (דָּשָׁא); KJV: (tender) grass, green, (tender) herb.

H1878 דָּשֵׁן (dâshên, daw-shane'): to be fat; transitively, to fatten (or regard as fat); specifically to anoint; figuratively, to satisfy; to remove (fat) ashes (of sacrifices). Origin: a primitive root; also denominatively (from H1880 (דֶּשֶׁן)) KJV: accept, anoint, take away the (receive) ashes (from), make (wax) fat.

H1879 דָּשֵׁן (dâshên, daw-shane'): fat; figuratively, rich, fertile. Origin: from H1878 (דָּשֵׁן); KJV: fat.

H1880 דֶּשֶׁן (deshen, deh'-shen): the fat; abstractly fatness, i.e. (figuratively) abundance; specifically the (fatty) ashes of sacrifices. Origin: from H1878 (דָּשֵׁן); KJV: ashes, fatness.

H1881 דָּת (dâth, dawth): a royal edict or statute. Origin: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; KJV: commandment, commission, decree, law, manner.

H1882 דָּת (dâth, dawth): {a royal edict or statute}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1881 (דָּת); KJV: decree, law.

H1883 דֶּתֶא (detheʼ, deh'-thay): {a sprout; by analogy, grass}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1877 (דֶּשֶׁא) KJV: tender grass.

H1884 דְּתָבָר (dᵉthâbâr, deth-aw-bawr'): meaning one skilled in law; a judge. Origin: (Aramaic) of Persian origin; KJV: counsellor.

H1885 דָּתָן (Dâthân, daw-thawn'): Dathan, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dathan.

H1886 דֹּתָן (Dôthân, do'-thawn): Dothan, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (Aramaic dual) דֹּתַיִן; (Genesis 37:17), of uncertain derivation; KJV: Dothan. h

H1887 הֵא (hêʼ, hay): lo!. Origin: a primitive particle; KJV: behold, lo.

H1888 הֵא (hêʼ, hay): {lo!}. Origin: (Aramaic) or הָא; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1887 (הֵא) KJV: even, lo.

H1889 הֶאָח (heʼâch, heh-awkh'): aha!. Origin: from H1887 (הֵא) and H253 (אָח); KJV: ah, aha, ha.

H1890 הַבְהָב (habhâb, hab-hawb'): gift (in sacrifice), i.e. holocaust. Origin: by reduplication from H3051 (יָהַב); KJV: offering.

H1891 הָבַל (hâbal, haw-bal'): to be vain in act, word, or expectation; specifically to lead astray. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (become, make) vain.

H1892 הֶבֶל (hebel, heh'bel): emptiness or vanity; figuratively, something transitory and unsatisfactory; often used as an adverb. Origin: or (rarely in the abs.) הֲבֵל; from H1891 (הָבַל); KJV: [idiom] altogether, vain, vanity.

H1893 הֶבֶל (Hebel, heh'-bel): Hebel, the son of Adam. Origin: the same as H1892 (הֶבֶל); KJV: Abel.

H1894 הֹבֶן (hôben, ho'-ben): ebony. Origin: only in plural, from an unused root meaning to be hard; KJV: ebony.

H1895 הָבַר (hâbar, haw-bar'): to be a horoscopist. Origin: a primitive root of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; KJV: [phrase] (astro-) loger.

H1896 הֵגֵא (Hêgêʼ, hay-gay'): Hege or Hegai, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: or (by permutation) הֵגַי; probably of Persian origin; KJV: Hegai, Hege.

H1897 הָגָה (hâgâh, daw-gaw'): to murmur (in pleasure or anger); by implication, to ponder. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1901 (הָגִיג)); KJV: imagine, meditate, mourn, mutter, roar, [idiom] sore, speak, study, talk, utter.

H1898 הָגָה (hâgâh, haw-gaw'): to remove. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: stay, stay away.

H1899 הֶגֶה (hegeh, heh'-geh): a muttering (in sighing, thought, or as thunder). Origin: from H1897 (הָגָה); KJV: mourning, sound, tale.

H1900 הָגוּת (hâgûwth, haw-gooth'): musing. Origin: from H1897 (הָגָה); KJV: meditation.

H1901 הָגִיג (hâgîyg, haw-gheeg'): properly, a murmur, i.e. complaint. Origin: from an unused root akin to H1897 (הָגָה); KJV: meditation, musing.

H1902 הִגָּיוֹן (higgâyôwn, hig-gaw-yone'): a murmuring sound, i.e. a musical notation (probably similar to the modern affettuoso to indicate solemnity of movement); by implication, a machination. Origin: intensive from H1897 (הָגָה); KJV: device, Higgaion, meditation, solemn sound.

H1903 הָגִין (hâgîyn, haw-gheen'): perhaps suitable or turning. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: directly.

H1904 הָגָר (Hâgâr, haw-gawr'): Hagar, the mother of Ishmael. Origin: of uncertain (perhaps foreign) derivation; KJV: Hagar.

H1905 הַגְרִי (Hagrîy, hag-ree'): a Hagrite or member of a certain Arabian clan. Origin: or (prolonged) הַגְרִיאxlit Hagrîʼ corrected to Hagrîyʼ; perhaps patronymically from H1904 (הָגָר); KJV: Hagarene, Hagarite, Haggeri.

H1906 הֵד (hêd, hade): a shout. Origin: for H1959 (הֵידָד); KJV: sounding again.

H1907 הַדָּבָר (haddâbâr, had-daw-bawr'): a vizier. Origin: (Aramaic) probably of foreign origin; KJV: counsellor.

H1908 הֲדַד (Hădad, had-ad'): Hadad, the name of an idol, and of several kings of Edom. Origin: probably of foreign origin (compare H111 (אֲדַד)); KJV: Hadad.

H1909 הֲדַדְעֶזֶר (Hădadʻezer, had-ad-eh'-zer): Hadadezer, a Syrian king. Origin: from H1908 (הֲדַד) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); Hadad (is his) help; KJV: Hadadezer. Compare H1928 (הֲדַרְעֶזֶר).

H1910 הֲדַדְרִמּוֹן (Hădadrimmôwn, had-ad-rim-mone'): Hadad-Rimmon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1908 (הֲדַד) and H7417 (רִמּוֹן); KJV: Hadad-rimmon.

H1911 הָדָה (hâdâh, haw-daw'): to stretch forth the hand. Origin: a primitive root (compare H3034 (יָדָה)); KJV: put.

H1912 הֹדוּ (Hôdûw, ho'-doo): Hodu (i.e. Hindustan). Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: India.

H1913 הֲדוֹרָם (Hădôwrâm, had-o-rawm'): Hadoram, a son of Joktan, and the tribe descended from him. Origin: or הֲדֹרָם; probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Hadoram.

H1914 הִדַּי (Hidday, hid-dah'ee): Hiddai, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Hiddai.

H1915 הָדַךְ (hâdak, haw-dak'): to crush with the foot. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1854 (דָּקַק)); KJV: tread down.

H1916 הֲדֹם (hădôm, had-ome'): a foot stool. Origin: from an unused root meaning to stamp upon; KJV: (foot-) stool.

H1917 הַדָּם (haddâm, had-dawm'): something stamped to pieces, i.e. a bit. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of H1916 (הֲדֹם); KJV: piece.

H1918 הֲדַס (hădaç, had-as'): the myrtle. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: myrtle (tree).

H1919 הֲדַסָּה (Hădaççâh, had-as-saw'): Hadassah (or Esther). Origin: feminine of H1918 (הֲדַס); KJV: Hadassah.

H1920 הָדַף (Hâdaph, haw-daf'): to push away or down. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast away (out), drive, expel, thrust (away).

H1921 הָדַר (hâdar, haw-dar'): to swell up (literally or figuratively, active or passive); by implication, to favor or honour, be high or proud. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: countenance, crooked place, glorious, honour, put forth.

H1922 הֲדַר (hădar, had-ar'): to magnify (figuratively). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1921 (הָדַר); KJV: glorify, honour.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H1923 to H2047
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H1923 הֲדַר (hădar, had-ar'): magnificence. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1922 (הֲדַר)lemma הֲדַּר extra dagesh, corrected to הֲדַר; KJV: honour, majesty.

H1924 הֲדַר (Hădar, had-ar'): Hadar, an Edomite. Origin: the same as H1926 (הָדָר); KJV: Hadar.

H1925 הֶדֶר (heder, heh'-der): honour; used (figuratively) for the capital city (Jerusalem). Origin: from H1921 (הָדַר); KJV: glory.

H1926 הָדָר (hâdâr, haw-dawr'): magnificence, i.e. ornament or splendor. Origin: from H1921 (הָדַר); KJV: beauty, comeliness, excellency, glorious, glory, goodly, honour, majesty.

H1927 הֲדָרָה (hădârâh, had-aw-raw'): decoration. Origin: feminine of H1926 (הָדָר); KJV: beauty, honour.

H1928 הֲדַרְעֶזֶר (Hădarʻezer, had-ar-eh'-zer): Hadarezer, a Syrian king. Origin: from H1924 (הֲדַר) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); Hadar (i.e. Hadad, H1908 (הֲדַד)) is his help; (i.e. Hadadezer, H1909 (הֲדַדְעֶזֶר)) KJV: Hadarezer.

H1929 הָהּ (hâhh, haw): ah! expressing grief. Origin: a shortened form of H162 (אֲהָהּ); KJV: woe worth.

H1930 הוֹ (hôw, ho): oh!. Origin: by permutation from H1929 (הָהּ); KJV: alas.

H1931 הוּא (hûwʼ, hoo): he (she or it); only expressed when emphatic or without a verb; also (intensively) self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are. Origin: of which the feminine (beyond the Pentateuch) is הִיא; a primitive word, the third person pronoun singular; KJV: he, as for her, him(-self), it, the same, she (herself), such, that (...it), these, they, this, those, which (is), who.

H1932 הוּא (hûwʼ, hoo): {he (she or it); self, or (especially with the article) the same; sometimes (as demonstrative) this or that; occasionally (instead of copula) as or are}. Origin: (Aramaic) or (feminine) הִיא; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1931 (הוּא) KJV: [idiom] are, it, this.

H1933 הָוָא (hâvâʼ, haw-vaw'): to be (in the sense of existence). Origin: or הָוָה; a primitive root (compare H183 (אָוָה), H1961 (הָיָה)) supposed to mean properly, to breathe; KJV: be, [idiom] have.

H1934 הָוָא (hâvâʼ, hav-aw'): to exist; used in a great variety of applications (especially in connection with other words). Origin: (Aramaic) or הָוָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1933 (הָוָא); KJV: be, become, [phrase] behold, [phrase] came (to pass), [phrase] cease, [phrase] cleave, [phrase] consider, [phrase] do, [phrase] give, [phrase] have, [phrase] judge, [phrase] keep, [phrase] labour, [phrase] mingle (self), [phrase] put, [phrase] see, [phrase] seek, [phrase] set, [phrase] slay, [phrase] take heed, tremble, [phrase] walk, [phrase] would.

H1935 הוֹד (hôwd, hode): grandeur (i.e. an imposing form and appearance). Origin: from an unused root; KJV: beauty, comeliness, excellency, glorious, glory, goodly, honour, majesty.

H1936 הוֹד (Hôwd, hode): Hod, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H1935 (הוֹד); KJV: Hod.

H1937 הוֹדְוָה (Hôwdᵉvâh, ho-dev-aw'): Hodevah (or Hodevjah), an Israelite. Origin: a form of H1938 (הוֹדַוְיָה); KJV: Hodevah.

H1938 הוֹדַוְיָה (Hôwdavyâh, ho-dav-yaw'): Hodavjah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H1935 (הוֹד) and H3050 (יָהּ); majesty of Jah; KJV: Hodaviah.

H1939 הוֹדַיְוָהוּ (Hôwdayvâhûw, ho-dah-yeh-vaw'-hoo): Hodajvah, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H1938 (הוֹדַוְיָה); KJV: Hodaiah.

H1940 הוֹדִיָּה (Hôwdîyâh, ho-dee-yaw'): a Jewess. Origin: a form for the feminine of H3064 (יְהוּדִי); KJV: Hodiah.

H1941 הוֹדִיָּה (Hôwdîyâh, ho-dee-yaw'): Hodijah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: a form of H1938 (הוֹדַוְיָה); KJV: Hodijah.

H1942 הַוָּה (havvâh, hav-vaw'): by implication, of falling); desire; also ruin. Origin: from H1933 (הָוָא) (in the sense of eagerly coveting and rushing upon; KJV: calamity, iniquity, mischief, mischievous (thing), naughtiness, naughty, noisome, perverse thing, substance, very wickedness.

H1943 הֹוָה (hôvâh, ho-vaw'): ruin. Origin: another form for H1942 (הַוָּה); KJV: mischief.

H1944 הוֹהָם (Hôwhâm, ho-hawm'): Hoham, a Canaanitish king. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Hoham.

H1945 הוֹי (hôwy, hoh'ee): oh!. Origin: a prolonged form of H1930 (הוֹ) (akin to H188 (אוֹי)); KJV: ah, alas, ho, O, woe.

H1946 הוּךְ (hûwk, hook): to go; causatively, to bring. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1981 (הֲלַךְ); KJV: bring again, come, go (up).

H1947 הוֹלֵלָה (hôwlêlâh, ho-lay-law'): folly. Origin: feminine active participle of H1984 (הָלַל); KJV: madness.

H1948 הוֹלֵלוּת (hôwlêlûwth, ho-lay-looth'): folly. Origin: from active participle of H1984 (הָלַל); KJV: madness.

H1949 הוּם (hûwm, hoom): to make an uproar, or agitate greatly. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2000 (הָמַם)); KJV: destroy, move, make a noise, put, ring again.

H1950 הוֹמָם (Hôwmâm, ho-mawm'): Homam, an Edomitish chieftain. Origin: from H2000 (הָמַם); raging; KJV: Homam. Compare H1967 (הֵימָם).

H1951 הוּן (hûwn, hoon): properly, to be naught, i.e. (figuratively) to be (causatively, act) light. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be ready.

H1952 הוֹן (hôwn, hone): wealth; by implication, enough. Origin: from the same as H1951 (הוּן) in the sense of H202 (אוֹן); KJV: enough, [phrase] for nought, riches, substance, wealth.

H1953 הוֹשָׁמָע (Hôwshâmâʻ, ho-shaw-maw'): Hoshama, an Israelite. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H8085 (שָׁמַע); Jehovah has heard; KJV: Hoshama.

H1954 הוֹשֵׁעַ (Hôwshêaʻ, ho-shay'-ah): Hoshea, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H3467 (יָשַׁע); deliverer; KJV: Hosea, Hoshea, Oshea.

H1955 הוֹשַׁעְיָה (Hôwshaʻyâh, ho-shah-yaw'): Hoshajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3467 (יָשַׁע) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has saved; KJV: Hoshaiah.

H1956 הוֹתִיר (Hôwthîyr, ho-theer'): Hothir, an Israelite. Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); he has caused to remain; KJV: Hothir.

H1957 הָזָה (hâzâh, haw-zaw'): to dream. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2372 (חָזָה)); KJV: sleep.

H1958 הִי (hîy, he): lamentation. Origin: for H5092 (נְהִי); KJV: woe. (For hiyr. See H1931 (הוּא), H1932 (הוּא).)

H1959 הֵידָד (hêydâd, hay-dawd'): acclamation. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to shout); KJV: shout(-ing).

H1960 הֻיְּדָה (huyᵉdâh, hoo-yed-aw'): properly, an acclaim, i.e. a choir of singers. Origin: from the same as H1959 (הֵידָד); KJV: thanksgiving.

H1961 הָיָה (hâyâh, haw-yaw): to exist, i.e. be or become, come to pass (always emphatic, and not a mere copula or auxiliary). Origin: a primitive root (compare H1933 (הָוָא)); KJV: beacon, [idiom] altogether, be(-come), accomplished, committed, like), break, cause, come (to pass), do, faint, fall, [phrase] follow, happen, [idiom] have, last, pertain, quit (one-) self, require, [idiom] use.

H1962 הַיָּה (hayâh, hah-yaw'): ruin. Origin: another form for H1943 (הֹוָה); KJV: calamity.

H1963 הֵיךְ (hêyk, hake): how?. Origin: another form for H349 (אֵיךְ); KJV: how.

H1964 הֵיכָל (hêykâl, hay-kawl'): a large public building, such as a palace or temple. Origin: probably from H3201 (יָכֹל) (in the sense of capacity); KJV: palace, temple.

H1965 הֵיכַל (hêykal, hay-kal'): {a large public building, such as a palace or temple}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1964 (הֵיכָל) KJV: palace, temple.

H1966 הֵילֵל (hêylêl, hay-lale'): the morning-star. Origin: from H1984 (הָלַל) (in the sense of brightness); KJV: lucifer.

H1967 הֵימָם (Hêymâm, hay-mawm'): Hemam, an Idumaean. Origin: another form for H1950 (הוֹמָם); KJV: Hemam.

H1968 הֵימָן (Hêymân, hay-mawn'): Heman, the name of at least two Israelites. Origin: probably from H539 (אָמַן); faithful; KJV: Heman.

H1969 הִין (hîyn, heen): a hin or liquid measure. Origin: probably of Egyptian origin; KJV: hin.

H1970 הָכַר (hâkar, haw-kar'): to injure. Origin: a primitive root; apparently KJV: make self strange.

H1971 הַכָּרָה (hakkârâh, hak-kaw-raw'): respect, i.e. partiality. Origin: from H5234 (נָכַר); KJV: shew.

H1972 הָלָא (hâlâʼ, haw-law'): to remove or be remote. Origin: probably denominatively from H1973 (הָלְאָה)xlit hâlᵉâh corrected to hâlᵉʼâh; KJV: cast far off.

H1973 הָלְאָה (hâlᵉʼâh, haw-leh-aw'): to the distance, i.e. far away; also (of time) thus far. Origin: from the primitive form of the article (hal); KJV: back, beyond, (hence,-) forward, hitherto, thence, forth, yonder.

H1974 הִלּוּל (hillûwl, hil-lool'): a celebration of thanksgiving for harvest. Origin: from H1984 (הָלַל) (in the sense of rejoicing); KJV: merry, praise.

H1975 הַלָּז (hallâz, hal-lawz'): this or that. Origin: from H1976 (הַלָּזֶה); KJV: side, that, this.

H1976 הַלָּזֶה (hallâzeh, hal-law-zeh'): this very. Origin: from the article (see H1973 (הָלְאָה)xlit hâlᵉâh corrected to hâlᵉʼâh) and H2088 (זֶה); KJV: this.

H1977 הַלֵּזוּ (hallêzûw, hal-lay-zoo'): that. Origin: another form of H1976 (הַלָּזֶה); KJV: this.

H1978 הָלִיךְ (hâlîyk, haw-leek'): a walk, i.e. (by implication) a step. Origin: from H1980 (הָלַךְ); KJV: step.

H1979 הֲלִיכָה (hălîykâh, hal-ee-kaw'): a walking; by implication, a procession or march, a caravan. Origin: feminine of H1978 (הָלִיךְ); KJV: company, going, walk, way.

H1980 הָלַךְ (hâlak, haw-lak'): to walk (in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively). Origin: akin to H3212 (יָלַךְ); a primitive root; KJV: (all) along, apace, behave (self), come, (on) continually, be conversant, depart, [phrase] be eased, enter, exercise (self), [phrase] follow, forth, forward, get, go (about, abroad, along, away, forward, on, out, up and down), [phrase] greater, grow, be wont to haunt, lead, march, [idiom] more and more, move (self), needs, on, pass (away), be at the point, quite, run (along), [phrase] send, speedily, spread, still, surely, [phrase] tale-bearer, [phrase] travel(-ler), walk (abroad, on, to and fro, up and down, to places), wander, wax, (way-) faring man, [idiom] be weak, whirl.

H1981 הֲלַךְ (hălak, hal-ak'): to walk. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1980 (הָלַךְ) (compare H1946 (הוּךְ)); KJV: walk.

H1982 הֵלֶךְ (hêlek, hay'-lek): properly, a journey, i.e. (by implication) a wayfarer; also a flowing. Origin: from H1980 (הָלַךְ); KJV: [idiom] dropped, traveller.

H1983 הֲלָךְ (hălâk, hal-awk'): properly, a journey, i.e. (by implication) toll on goods at aroad. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1981 (הֲלַךְ); KJV: custom.

H1984 הָלַל (hâlal, haw-lal'): to be clear (orig. of sound, but usually of color); to shine; hence, to make ashow, to boast; and thus to be (clamorously) foolish; to rave; causatively, to celebrate; also to stultify. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) boast (self), celebrate, commend, (deal, make), fool(-ish, -ly), glory, give (light), be (make, feign self) mad (against), give in marriage, (sing, be worthy of) praise, rage, renowned, shine.

H1985 הִלֵּל (Hillêl, hil-layl'): Hillel, an Israelite. Origin: from H1984 (הָלַל); praising (namely God); KJV: Hillel.

H1986 הָלַם (hâlam, haw-lam'): to strike down; by implication, to hammer, stamp, conquer, disband. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat (down), break (down), overcome, smite (with the hammer).

H1987 הֶלֶם (Helem, hay'-lem): Helem, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1986 (הָלַם); smiter; KJV: Helem.

H1988 הֲלֹם (hălôm, hal-ome'): hither. Origin: from the article (see H1973 (הָלְאָה)xlit hâlᵉâh corrected to hâlᵉʼâh); KJV: here, hither(-(to)), thither.

H1989 הַלְמוּת (halmûwth, hal-mooth'): a hammer (or mallet). Origin: from H1986 (הָלַם); KJV: hammer.

H1990 הָם (Hâm, hawm): Ham, a region of Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Ham.

H1991 הֵם (hêm, haym): abundance, i.e. wealth. Origin: from H1993 (הָמָה); KJV: any of theirs.

H1992 הֵם (hêm, haym): they (only used when emphatic). Origin: or (prolonged) הֵמָּה; masculine plural from H1981 (הֲלַךְ); KJV: it, like, [idiom] (how, so) many (soever, more as) they (be), (the) same, [idiom] so, [idiom] such, their, them, these, they, those, which, who, whom, withal, ye.

H1993 הָמָה (hâmâh, haw-maw'): to make a loud sound (like English 'hum'); by implication, to be in great commotion or tumult, to rage, war, moan, clamor. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1949 (הוּם)); KJV: clamorous, concourse, cry aloud, be disquieted, loud, mourn, be moved, make a noise, rage, roar, sound, be troubled, make in tumult, tumultuous, be in an uproar.

H1994 הִמּוֹ (himmôw, him-mo'): they. Origin: (Aramaic) or (prolonged) הִמּוֹן; (Aramaic), corresponding to H1992 (הֵם); KJV: [idiom] are, them, those.

H1995 הָמוֹן (hâmôwn, haw-mone'): a noise, tumult, crowd; also disquietude, wealth. Origin: or הָמֹן; (Ezekiel 5:7), from H1993 (הָמָה); KJV: abundance, company, many, multitude, multiply, noise, riches, rumbling, sounding, store, tumult.

H1996 הֲמוֹן גּוֹג (Hămôwn Gôwg, ham-one' gohg): the multitude of Gog; the fanciful name of an emblematic place in Palestine. Origin: from H1995 (הָמוֹן) and H1463 (גּוֹג); KJV: Hamogog.

H1997 הֲמוֹנָה (Hămôwnâh, ham-o-naw'): Hamonah. Origin: feminine of H1995 (הָמוֹן); multitude; , the same as H1996 (הֲמוֹן גּוֹג) KJV: Hamonah.

H1998 הֶמְיָה (hemyâh, hem-yaw'): sound. Origin: from H1993 (הָמָה); KJV: noise.

H1999 הֲמֻלָּה (hămullâh, ham-ool-law'): a sound. Origin: or (too fully) הֲמוּלָּה; (Jeremiah 11:16), feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to rush (as rain with a windy roar); KJV: speech, tumult.

H2000 הָמַם (hâmam, haw-mam'): properly, to put in commotion; by implication, to disturb, drive, destroy. Origin: a primitive root (compare H1949 (הוּם), H1993 (הָמָה)); KJV: break, consume, crush, destroy, discomfit, trouble, vex.

H2001 הָמָן (Hâmân, haw-mawn'): Haman, a Persian vizier. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Haman.

H2002 הַמְנִיךְ (hamnîyk, ham-neek'): a necklace. Origin: (Aramaic) but the text is הֲמוּנֵךְ; of foreign origin; KJV: chain.

H2003 הָמָס (hâmâç, haw-mawce'): a dry twig or brushwood. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to crackle; KJV: melting.

H2004 הֵן (hên, hane): they (only used when emphatic). Origin: feminine plural from H1931 (הוּא); KJV: [idiom] in, such like, (with) them, thereby, therein, (more than) they, wherein, in which, whom, withal.

H2005 הֵן (hên, hane): lo!; also (as expressing surprise) if. Origin: a primitive particle; KJV: behold, if, lo, though.

H2006 הֵן (hên, hane): lo! also there(-fore), (un-) less, whether, but, if. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2005 (הֵן); KJV: (that) if, or, whether.

H2007 הֵנָּה (hênnâh, hane'-naw): themselves (often used emphatic for the copula, also in indirect relation). Origin: prolongation for H2004 (הֵן); KJV: [idiom] in, [idiom] such (and such things), their, (into) them, thence, therein, these, they (had), on this side, whose, wherein.

H2008 הֵנָּה (hênnâh, hane'-naw): hither or thither (but used both of place and time). Origin: from H2004 (הֵן); KJV: here, hither(-to), now, on this (that) side, [phrase] since, this (that) way, thitherward, [phrase] thus far, to...fro, [phrase] yet.

H2009 הִנֵּה (hinnêh, hin-nay'): lo!. Origin: prolongation for H2005 (הֵן); KJV: behold, lo, see.

H2010 הֲנָחָה (hănâchâh, han-aw-khaw'): permission of rest, i.e. quiet. Origin: from H5117 (נוּחַ); KJV: release.

H2011 הִנֹּם (Hinnôm, hin-nome'): Hinnom, apparently a Jebusite. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Hinnom.

H2012 הֵנַע (Hênaʻ, hay-nah'): Hena, a place apparently in Mesopotamia. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Hena.

H2013 הָסָה (hâçâh, haw-saw'): to hush. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hold peace (tongue), (keep) silence, be silent, still.

H2014 הֲפֻגָה (hăphugâh, haf-oo-gaw'): relaxation. Origin: from H6313 (פּוּג); KJV: intermission.

H2015 הָפַךְ (hâphak, haw-fak'): to turn about or over; by implication, to change, overturn, return, pervert. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] become, change, come, be converted, give, make (a bed), overthrow (-turn), perverse, retire, tumble, turn (again, aside, back, to the contrary, every way).

H2016 הֶפֶךְ (hephek, heh'-fek): a turn, i.e. the reverse. Origin: ; or הֵפֶךְ; from H2015 (הָפַךְ); KJV: contrary.

H2017 הֹפֶךְ (hôphek, ho'-fek): an upset, i.e. (abstract) perversity. Origin: from H2015 (הָפַךְ); KJV: turning of things upside down.

H2018 הֲפֵכָה (hăphêkâh, haf-ay-kaw'): destruction. Origin: feminine of H2016 (הֶפֶךְ); KJV: overthrow.

H2019 הֲפַכְפַּךְ (hăphakpak, haf-ak-pak'): very perverse. Origin: by reduplication from H2015 (הָפַךְ); KJV: froward.

H2020 הַצָּלָה (hatstsâlâh, hats-tsaw-law'): rescue. Origin: from H5337 (נָצַל); KJV: deliverance.

H2021 הֹצֶן (hôtsen, ho'-tsen): a weapon of war. Origin: from an unused root meaning apparently to be sharp or strong; KJV: chariot.

H2022 הַר (har, har): a mountain or range of hills (sometimes used figuratively). Origin: a shortened form of H2042 (הָרָר); KJV: hill (country), mount(-ain), [idiom] promotion.

H2023 הֹר (Hôr, hore): Hor, the name of a peak in Idumaea and of one in Syria. Origin: another form of H2022 (הַר); mountain; KJV: Hor.

H2024 הָרָא (Hârâʼ, haw-raw'): Hara, a region of Media. Origin: perhaps from H2022 (הַר); mountainousness; KJV: Hara.

H2025 הַרְאֵל (harʼêl, har-ale'): mount of God; figuratively, the altar of burnt-offering. Origin: from H2022 (הַר) and H410 (אֵל); KJV: altar. Compare H739 (אֲרִיאֵל).

H2026 הָרַג (hârag, haw-rag'): to smite with deadly intent. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destroy, out of hand, kill, murder(-er), put to (death), make (slaughter), slay(-er), [idiom] surely.

H2027 הֶרֶג (hereg, heh'-reg): slaughter. Origin: from H2026 (הָרַג); KJV: be slain, slaughter.

H2028 הֲרֵגָה (hărêgâh, har-ay-gaw'): slaughter. Origin: feminine of H2027 (הֶרֶג); KJV: slaughter.

H2029 הָרָה (hârâh, haw-raw'): to be (or become) pregnant, conceive (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: been, be with child, conceive, progenitor.

H2030 הָרֶה (hâreh, haw-reh'): pregnant. Origin: or הָרִי; (Hosea 14:1), from H2029 (הָרָה); KJV: (be, woman) with child, conceive, [idiom] great.

H2031 הַרְהֹר (harhôr, har-hor'): a mental conception. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2029 (הָרָה); KJV: thought.

H2032 הֵרוֹן (hêrôwn, hay-rone'): pregnancy. Origin: or הֵרָיוֹן; from H2029 (הָרָה); KJV: conception.

H2033 הֲרוֹרִי (Hărôwrîy, har-o-ree'): a Harorite or mountaineer. Origin: another form for H2043 (הֲרָרִי); KJV: Harorite.

H2034 הֲרִיסָה (hărîyçâh, har-ee-saw'): something demolished. Origin: from H2040 (הָרַס); KJV: ruin.

H2035 הֲרִיסוּת (hărîyçûwth, har-ee-sooth'): demolition. Origin: from H2040 (הָרַס); KJV: destruction.

H2036 הֹרָם (Hôrâm, ho-rawm'): Horam, a Canaanitish king. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to tower up); high; KJV: Horam.

H2037 הָרֻם (Hârum, haw-room'): Harum, an Israelite. Origin: passive participle of the same as H2036 (הֹרָם); high; KJV: Harum.

H2038 הַרְמוֹן (harmôwn, har-mone'): a castle (from its height). Origin: from the same as H2036 (הֹרָם); KJV: palace.

H2039 הָרָן (Hârân, haw-rawn'): Haran, the name of two men. Origin: perhaps from H2022 (הַר); mountaineer; KJV: Haran.

H2040 הָרַס (hâraç, haw-ras'): to pull down or in pieces, break, destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat down, break (down, through), destroy, overthrow, pluck down, pull down, ruin, throw down, [idiom] utterly.

H2041 הֶרֶס (hereç, heh'-res): demolition. Origin: from H2040 (הָרַס); KJV: destruction.

H2042 הָרָר (hârâr, haw-rawr'): a mountain. Origin: from an unused root meaning to loom up; KJV: hill, mount(-ain).

H2043 הֲרָרִי (Hărârîy, hah-raw-ree'): {Hararite}. Origin: or הָרָרִי; (2 Samuel 23:11), or הָארָרִי; (2 Samuel 23:34, last clause [), apparently from H2042 (הָרָר); a mountaineer KJV: Hararite.

H2044 הָשֵׁם (Hâshêm, haw-shame'): Hashem, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from the same as H2828 (חָשֻׁם); wealthy; KJV: Hashem.

H2045 הַשְׁמָעוּת (hashmâʻûwth, hashmaw-ooth'): announcement. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע); KJV: to cause to hear.

H2046 הִתּוּךְ (hittûwk, hit-took'): a melting. Origin: from H5413 (נָתַךְ); KJV: is melted.

H2047 הֲתָךְ (Hăthâk, hath-awk'): Hathak, a Persian eunuch. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Hatach.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2048 to H2184
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2048 הָתַל (hâthal, haw-thal'): to deride; by implication, to cheat. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deal deceitfully, deceive, mock.

H2049 הָתֹל (hâthôl, haw-thole'): a derision. Origin: from H2048 (הָתַל) (only in plural collectively); KJV: mocker.

H2050 הָתַת (hâthath, haw-thath'): properly, to break in upon, i.e. to assail. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: imagine mischief. w

H2051 וְדָן (Vᵉdân, ved-awn'): Vedan (or Aden), a place in Arabia. Origin: perhaps for H5730 (עֵדֶן); KJV: Dan also.

H2052 וָהֵב (Vâhêb, vaw-habe'): Vaheb, a place in Moab. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: what he did.

H2053 וָו (vâv, vaw): a hook (the name of the sixth Hebrew letter). Origin: probably KJV: hook.

H2054 וָזָר (vâzâr, vaw-zawr'): crime. Origin: presumed to be from an unused root meaning to bear guilt; KJV: [idiom] strange.

H2055 וַיְזָתָא (Vayzâthâʼ, vah-yez-aw'-thaw): Vajezatha, a son of Haman. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Vajezatha.

H2056 וָלָד (vâlâd, vaw-lawd'): a boy. Origin: for H3206 (יֶלֶד); KJV: child.

H2057 וַנְיָה (Vanyâh, van-yaw'): Vanjah, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps for H6043 (עֲנָיָה); KJV: Vaniah.

H2058 וׇפְסִי (Vophçîy, vof-see'): Vophsi, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H3254 (יָסַף); additional; KJV: Vophsi.

H2059 וַשְׁנִי (Vashnîy, vash-nee'): Vashni, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H3461 (יִשְׁמְרַי); weak; KJV: Vashni.

H2060 וַשְׁתִּי (Vashtîy, vash-tee'): Vashti, the queen of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Vashti. z

H2061 זְאֵב (zᵉʼêb, zeh-abe'): a wolf. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be yellow; KJV: wolf.

H2062 זְאֵב (Zᵉʼêb, zeh-abe'): Zeeb, a Midianitish prince. Origin: the same as H2061 (זְאֵב); KJV: Zeeb.

H2063 זֹאת (zôʼth, zothe'): this (often used adverb). Origin: irregular feminine of H2089 (זֶה); KJV: hereby (-in, -with), it, likewise, the one (other, same), she, so (much), such (deed), that, therefore, these, this (thing), thus.

H2064 זָבַד (zâbad, zaw-bad'): to confer. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: endure.

H2065 זֶבֶד (zebed, zeh'-bed): a gift. Origin: from H2064 (זָבַד); KJV: dowry.

H2066 זָבָד (Zâbâd, zaw-bawd'): Zabad, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: from H2064 (זָבַד); giver; KJV: Zabad.

H2067 זַבְדִּי (Zabdîy, zab-dee'): Zabdi, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H2065 (זֶבֶד); giving; KJV: Zabdi.

H2068 זַבְדִּיאֵל (Zabdîyʼêl, zab-dee-ale'): gift of God; zabdiel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2065 (זֶבֶד) and H410 (אֵל); KJV: Zabdiel.

H2069 זְבַדְיָה (Zᵉbadyâh, zeb-ad-yaw'): Zebadjah, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: or זְבַדְיָהוּ; from H2064 (זָבַד) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has given; KJV: Zebadiah.

H2070 זְבוּב (zᵉbûwb, zeb-oob'): a fly (especially one of a stinging nature). Origin: from an unused root (meaning to flit); KJV: fly.

H2071 זָבוּד (Zâbûwd, zaw-bood'): given, Zabud, an Israelite. Origin: from H2064 (זָבַד); KJV: Zabud.

H2072 זַבּוּד (Zabbûwd, zab-bood'): Zabbud, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H2071 (זָבוּד); given; KJV: Zabbud.

H2073 זְבוּל (zᵉbûwl, ze-bool'): a residence. Origin: or זְבֻל; from H2082 (זָבַל); KJV: dwell in, dwelling, habitation.

H2074 זְבוּלוּן (Zᵉbûwlûwn, zeb-oo-loon'): Zebulon, a son of Jacob; also his territory and tribe. Origin: or זְבֻלוּן; or זְבוּלֻן; from H2082 (זָבַל); habitation; KJV: Zebulun.

H2075 זְבוּלֹנִי (Zᵉbûwlônîy, zeb-oo-lo-nee'): a Zebulonite or descendant of Zebulun. Origin: patronymically from H2074 (זְבוּלוּן); KJV: Zebulonite.

H2076 זָבַח (zâbach, zaw-bakh'): to slaughter an animal (usually in sacrifice). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: kill, offer, (do) sacrifice, slay.

H2077 זֶבַח (zebach, zeh'-bakh): properly, a slaughter, i.e. the flesh of an animal; by implication, a sacrifice (the victim or the act). Origin: from H2076 (זָבַח); KJV: offer(-ing), sacrifice.

H2078 זֶבַח (Zebach, zeh'-bakh): Zebach, a Midianitish prince. Origin: the same as H2077 (זֶבַח); sacrifice; KJV: Zebah.

H2079 זַבַּי (Zabbay, zab-bah'-ee): Zabbai (or Zaccai), an Israelite. Origin: probably by orthographical error for H2140 (זַכַּי); KJV: Zabbai.

H2080 זְבִידָה (Zᵉbîydâh, zeb-ee-daw'): Zebidah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine from H2064 (זָבַד); giving; KJV: Zebudah.

H2081 זְבִינָא (Zᵉbîynâʼ, zeb-ee-naw'): Zebina, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to purchase); gainfulness; KJV: Zebina.

H2082 זָבַל (zâbal, zaw-bal'): to reside. Origin: a primitive root; apparently properly, to inclose, i.e. KJV: dwell with.

H2083 זְבֻל (Zᵉbul, zeb-ool'): Zebul, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2073 (זְבוּל); dwelling; KJV: Zebul. Compare H2073 (זְבוּל).

H2084 זְבַן (zᵉban, zeb-an'): to acquire by purchase. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of H2081 (זְבִינָא); KJV: gain.

H2085 זָג (zâg, zawg): the skin of a grape. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to inclose; KJV: husk.

H2086 זֵד (zêd, zade'): arrogant. Origin: from H2102 (זוּד); KJV: presumptuous, proud.

H2087 זָדוֹן (zâdôwn, zaw-done'): arrogance. Origin: from H2102 (זוּד); KJV: presumptuously, pride, proud (man).

H2088 זֶה (zeh, zeh): the masculine demonstrative pronoun, this or that. Origin: a primitive word; KJV: he, [idiom] hence, [idiom] here, it(-self), [idiom] now, [idiom] of him, the one...the other, [idiom] than the other, ([idiom] out of) the (self) same, such (a one) that, these, this (hath, man), on this side...on that side, [idiom] thus, very, which. Compare H2063 (זֹאת), H2090 (זֹה), H2097 (זוֹ), H2098 (זוּ).

H2089 זֶה (zeh, zeh): a sheep. Origin: (1 Samuel by permutation for H7716 (שֶׂה); KJV: lamb.

H2090 זֹה (zôh, zo): this or that. Origin: for H2088 (זֶה); KJV: as well as another, it, this, that, thus and thus.

H2091 זָהָב (zâhâb, zaw-hawb'): gold, figuratively, something gold-colored (i.e. yellow), as oil, a clear sky. Origin: from an unused root meaning to shimmer; KJV: gold(-en), fair weather.

H2092 זָהַם (zâham, zaw-ham'): to be rancid, i.e. (transitively) to loathe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor.

H2093 זַהַם (Zaham, zah'-ham): Zaham, an Israelite. Origin: from H2092 (זָהַם); loathing; KJV: Zaham.

H2094 זָהַר (zâhar, zaw-har'): to gleam; figuratively, to enlighten (by caution). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: admonish, shine, teach, (give) warn(-ing).

H2095 זְהַר (zᵉhar, zeh-har'): (passively) be admonished. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2094 (זָהַר); KJV: take heed.

H2096 זֹהַר (zôhar, zo'-har): brilliancy. Origin: from H2094 (זָהַר); KJV: brightness.

H2097 זוֹ (zôw, zo): this or that. Origin: for H2088 (זֶה); KJV: that, this.

H2098 זוּ (zûw, zoo): this or that. Origin: for H2088 (זֶה); KJV: that, this, [idiom] wherein, which, whom.

H2099 זִו (Ziv, zeev'): Ziv (corresponding to Ijar or May). Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to be prominent; properly, brightness (compare H2122 (זִיו)), i.e. (figuratively) the month of flowers; KJV: Zif.

H2100 זוּב (zûwb, zoob): to flow freely (as water), i.e. (specifically) to have a (sexual) flux; figuratively, to waste away; also to overflow. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: flow, gush out, have a (running) issue, pine away, run.

H2101 זוֹב (zôwb, zobe): a seminal or menstrual flux. Origin: from H2100 (זוּב); KJV: issue.

H2102 זוּד (zûwd, zood): to seethe; figuratively, to be insolent. Origin: or (by permutation) זִיד; a primitive root; KJV: be proud, deal proudly, presume, (come) presumptuously, sod.

H2103 זוּד (zûwd, zood): to be proud. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2102 (זוּד); KJV: in pride.

H2104 זוּזִים (Zûwzîym, zoo-zeem'): Zuzites, an aboriginal tribe of Palestine. Origin: plural probably from the same as H2123 (זִיז); prominent; KJV: Zuzims.

H2105 זוֹחֵת (Zôwchêth, zo-khayth'): Zocheth, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain origin; KJV: Zoheth.

H2106 זָוִית (zâvîyth, zaw-veeth'): an angle (as projecting), i.e. (by implication) a corner-column (or anta). Origin: apparently from the same root as H2099 (זִו) (in the sense of prominence); KJV: corner(stone).

H2107 זוּל (zûwl, zool): probably to shake out, i.e. (by implication) to scatter profusely; figuratively, to treat lightly. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2151 (זָלַל)); KJV: lavish, despise.

H2108 זוּלָה (zûwlâh, zoo-law'): probably scattering, i.e. removal; used adverbially, except. Origin: from H2107 (זוּל); KJV: beside, but, only, save.

H2109 זוּן (zûwn, zoon): perhaps properly, to be plump, i.e. (transitively) to nourish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: feed.

H2110 זוּן (zûwn, zoon): {perhaps properly, to be plump, i.e. (transitively) to nourish}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2109 (זוּן) KJV: feed.

H2111 זוּעַ (zûwaʻ, zoo'-ah): properly, to shake off, i.e. (figuratively) to agitate (as with fear). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: move, tremble, vex.

H2112 זוּעַ (zûwaʻ, zoo'-ah): to shake (with fear). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2111 (זוּעַ); KJV: tremble.

H2113 זְוָעָה (zᵉvâʻâh, zev-aw-aw'): agitation, fear. Origin: from H2111 (זוּעַ); KJV: be removed, trouble, vexation. Compare H2189 (זַעֲוָה).

H2114 זוּר (zûwr, zoor): to turn aside (especially for lodging); hence to be aforeigner, strange, profane; specifically (active participle) to commit adultery. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (come from) another (man, place), fanner, go away, (e-) strange(-r, thing, woman).

H2115 זוּר (zûwr, zoor): to press together, tighten. Origin: a primitive root (compare H6695 (צוֹק)); KJV: close, rush, thrust together.

H2116 זוּרֶה (zûwreh, zoo-reh'): trodden on. Origin: from H2115 (זוּר); KJV: that which is crushed.

H2117 זָזָא (zâzâʼ, zaw-zaw'): Zaza, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the root of H2123 (זִיז); prominent; KJV: Zaza.

H2118 זָחַח (zâchach, zaw-khakh'): to shove or displace. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: loose.

H2119 זָחַל (zâchal, zaw-khal'): to crawl; by implication, to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be afraid, serpent, worm.

H2120 זֹחֶלֶת (Zôcheleth, zo-kheh'-leth): Zocheleth, a boundary stone in. Palestine. Origin: feminine active participle of H2119 (זָחַל); crawling (i.e. serpent); KJV: Zoheleth.

H2121 זֵידוֹן (zêydôwn, zay-dohn'): boiling of water, i.e. wave. Origin: from H2102 (זוּד); KJV: proud.

H2122 זִיו (zîyv, zeev): (figuratively) cheerfulness. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2099 (זִו); KJV: brightness, countenance.

H2123 זִיז (zîyz, zeez): fulness of the breast; also a moving creature. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to be conspicuous; KJV: abundance, wild beast.

H2124 זִיזָא (Zîyzâʼ, zee-zaw'): Ziza, the name of two Israelites. Origin: apparently from the same as H2123 (זִיז); prominence; KJV: Ziza.

H2125 זִיזָה (Zîyzâh, zee-zaw'): Zizah, an Israelite. Origin: another form for H2124 (זִיזָא); KJV: Zizah.

H2126 זִינָא (Zîynâʼ, zee-naw'): Zina, an Israelite. Origin: from H2109 (זוּן); well-fed; or perhaps an orthographical error for H2124 (זִיזָא); KJV: Zina.

H2127 זִיעַ (Zîyaʻ, zee'-ah): Zia, an Israelite. Origin: from H2111 (זוּעַ); agitation; KJV: Zia.

H2128 זִיף (Zîyph, zeef): Ziph, the name of a place in Palestine; also of an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H2203 (זֶפֶת); flowing; KJV: Ziph.

H2129 זִיפָה (Zîyphâh, zee-faw'): Ziphah, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H2128 (זִיף); a flowing; KJV: Ziphah.

H2130 זִיפִי (Zîyphîy, zee-fee'): a Ziphite or inhabitant of Ziph. Origin: patrial from H2128 (זִיף); KJV: Ziphim, Ziphite.

H2131 זִיקָה (zîyqâh, zee-kaw'): properly, what leaps forth, i.e. flash of fire, or a burning arrow; also (from the original sense of the root) a bond. Origin: (Isaiah 50: (feminine); and זִק; or זֵק; from H2187 (זָנַק); KJV: chain, fetter, firebrand, spark.

H2132 זַיִת (zayith, zay'-yith): an olive (as yielding illuminating oil), the tree, the branch or the berry. Origin: probably from an unused root (akin to H2099 (זִו)); KJV: olive (tree, -yard), Olivet.

H2133 זֵיתָן (Zêythân, zay-thawn'): Zethan, an Israelite. Origin: from H2132 (זַיִת); olive grove; KJV: Zethan.

H2134 זַךְ (zak, zak): clear. Origin: from H2141 (זָכַךְ); KJV: clean, pure.

H2135 זָכָה (zâkâh, zaw-kaw'): to be translucent; figuratively, to be innocent. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2141 (זָכַךְ)); KJV: be (make) clean, cleanse, be clear, count pure.

H2136 זָכוּ (zâkûw, zaw-koo'): purity. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2135 (זָכָה); KJV: innocency.

H2137 זְכוּכִית (zᵉkûwkîyth, zek-oo-keeth): properly, transparency, i.e. glass. Origin: from H2135 (זָכָה); KJV: crystal.

H2138 זָכוּר (zâkûwr, zaw-koor'): a male (of man or animals). Origin: properly, passive participle of H2142 (זָכַר), but used for H2145 (זָכָר); KJV: males, men-children.

H2139 זַכּוּר (Zakkûwr, zaw-koor'): Zakkur, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: from H2142 (זָכַר); mindful; KJV: Zaccur, Zacchur.

H2140 זַכַּי (Zakkay, zak-kah'-ee): Zakkai, an Israelite. Origin: from H2141 (זָכַךְ); pure; KJV: Zaccai.

H2141 זָכַךְ (zâkak, zaw-kak'): to be transparent or clean (phys. or morally). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2135 (זָכָה)); KJV: be (make) clean, be pure(-r).

H2142 זָכַר (zâkar, zaw-kar'): properly, to mark (so as to be recognized), i.e. to remember; by implication, to mention; to be male. Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative from H2145 (זָכָר) KJV: [idiom] burn (incense), [idiom] earnestly, be male, (make) mention (of), be mindful, recount, record(-er), remember, make to be remembered, bring (call, come, keep, put) to (in) remembrance, [idiom] still, think on, [idiom] well.

H2143 זֵכֶר (zêker, zay'-ker): a memento, abstractly recollection (rarely if ever); by implication, commemoration. Origin: or זֶכֶר; from H2142 (זָכַר); KJV: memorial, memory, remembrance, scent.

H2144 זֶכֶר (Zeker, zeh'-ker): Zeker, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2143 (זֵכֶר); KJV: Zeker.

H2145 זָכָר (zâkâr, zaw-kawr'): properly, remembered, i.e. a male (of man or animals, as being the most noteworthy sex). Origin: from H2142 (זָכַר); KJV: [idiom] him, male, man(child, -kind).

H2146 זִכְרוֹן (zikrôwn, zik-rone'): a memento (or memorable thing, day or writing). Origin: from H2142 (זָכַר); KJV: memorial, record.

H2147 זִכְרִי (Zikrîy, zik-ree'): Zicri, the name of twelve Israelites. Origin: from H2142 (זָכַר); memorable; KJV: Zichri.

H2148 זְכַרְיָה (Zᵉkaryâh, zek-ar-yaw'): Zecarjah, the name of twenty-nine Israelites. Origin: or זְכַרְיָהוּ; from H2142 (זָכַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has remembered; KJV: Zachariah, Zechariah.

H2149 זֻלּוּת (zullûwth, zool-looth'): properly, a shaking, i.e. perhaps a tempest. Origin: from H2151 (זָלַל); KJV: vilest.

H2150 זַלְזַל (zalzal, zal-zal'): tremulous, i.e. a twig. Origin: by reduplication from H2151 (זָלַל); KJV: sprig.

H2151 זָלַל (zâlal, zaw-lal'): to shake (as in the wind), i.e. to quake; figuratively, to be loose morally, worthless or prodigal. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2107 (זוּל)); KJV: blow down, glutton, riotous (eater), vile.

H2152 זַלְעָפָה (zalʻâphâh, zal-aw-faw'): a glow (of wind or anger); also a famine (as consuming). Origin: or זִלְעָפָהxlit zilʻâphâph corrected to zilʻâphâh; from H2196 (זָעַף); KJV: horrible, horror, terrible.

H2153 זִלְפָּה (Zilpâh, zil-paw): Zilpah, Leah's maid. Origin: ; from an unused root apparently meaning to trickle, as myrrh; fragrant dropping; KJV: Zilpah.

H2154 זִמָּה (zimmâh, zim-maw'): a plan, especially a bad one. Origin: or זַמָּה; from H2161 (זָמַם); KJV: heinous crime, lewd(-ly, -ness), mischief, purpose, thought, wicked (device, mind, -ness).

H2155 זִמָּה (Zimmâh, zim-maw'): Zimmah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H2154 (זִמָּה); KJV: Zimmah.

H2156 זְמוֹרָה (zᵉmôwrâh, zem-o-raw'): a twig (as pruned). Origin: or זְמֹרָה (feminine); and זְמֹר (masculine); from H2168 (זָמַר); KJV: vine, branch, slip.

H2157 זַמְזֹם (Zamzôm, zam-zome'): a Zamzumite, or native tribe of Palestine. Origin: from H2161 (זָמַם); intriguing; KJV: Zamzummim.

H2158 זָמִיר (zâmîyr, zaw-meer'): a song to be accompanied with instrumental music. Origin: or זָמִר; and (feminine) זְמִרָה; from H2167 (זָמַר); KJV: psalm(-ist), singing, song.

H2159 זָמִיר (zâmîyr, zaw-meer'): a twig (as pruned). Origin: from H2168 (זָמַר); KJV: branch.

H2160 זְמִירָה (Zᵉmîyrâh, zem-ee-raw'): Zemirah, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H2158 (זָמִיר); song; KJV: Zemira.

H2161 זָמַם (zâmam, zaw-mam'): to plan, usually in a bad sense. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consider, devise, imagine, plot, purpose, think (evil).

H2162 זָמָם (zâmâm, zaw-mawm'): a plot. Origin: from H2161 (זָמַם); KJV: wicked device.

H2163 זָמַן (zâman, zaw-man'): to fix (a time). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint.

H2164 זְמַן (zᵉman, zem-an'): to agree (on a time and place). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2163 (זָמַן); KJV: prepare.

H2165 זְמָן (zᵉmân, zem-awn'): an appointed occasion. Origin: from H2163 (זָמַן); KJV: season, time.

H2166 זְמָן (zᵉmân, zem-awn'): {an appointed occasion}. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2165 (זְמָן); the same as H2165 (זְמָן) KJV: season, time.

H2167 זָמַר (zâmar, zaw-mar'): play upon it; to make music, accompanied by the voice; hence to celebrate in song and music. Origin: a primitive root (perhaps identical with H2168 (זָמַר) through the idea of striking with the fingers); properly, to touch the strings or parts of a musical instrument, i.e. KJV: give praise, sing forth praises, psalms.

H2168 זָמַר (zâmar, zaw-mar'): to trim (a vine). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2167 (זָמַר), H5568 (סָמַר), H6785 (צֶמֶר)); KJV: prune.

H2169 זֶמֶר (zemer, zeh'-mer): a gazelle (from its lightly touching the ground). Origin: apparently from H2167 (זָמַר) or H2168 (זָמַר); KJV: chamois.

H2170 זְמָר (zᵉmâr, zem-awr'): instrumental music. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2167 (זָמַר); KJV: musick.

H2171 זַמָּר (zammâr, zam-mawr'): an instrumental musician. Origin: (Aramaic) from the same as H2170 (זְמָר); KJV: singer.

H2172 זִמְרָה (zimrâh, zim-raw'): a musical piece or song to be accompanied by an instrument. Origin: from H2167 (זָמַר); KJV: melody, psalm.

H2173 זִמְרָה (zimrâh, zim-raw'): pruned (i.e. choice) fruit. Origin: from H2168 (זָמַר); KJV: best fruit.

H2174 זִמְרִי (Zimrîy, zim-ree'): Zimri, the name of five Israelites, and of an Arabian tribe. Origin: from H2167 (זָמַר); musical; KJV: Zimri.

H2175 זִמְרָן (Zimrân, zim-rawn'): Zimran, a son of Abraham by Keturah. Origin: from H2167 (זָמַר); musical; KJV: Zimran.

H2176 זִמְרָת (zimrâth, zim-rawth'): instrumental music; by implication, praise. Origin: from H2167 (זָמַר); KJV: song.

H2177 זַן (zan, zan): properly, nourished (or fully developed), i.e. a form or sort. Origin: from H2109 (זוּן); KJV: divers kinds, [idiom] all manner of store.

H2178 זַן (zan, zan): sort. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2177 (זַן); KJV: kind.

H2179 זָנַב (zânab, zaw-nab'): to curtail, i.e. cut off the rear. Origin: a primitive root meaning to wag; used only as a denominative from H2180 (זָנָב); KJV: smite the hindmost.

H2180 זָנָב (zânâb, zaw-nawb'): the tail (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H2179 (זָנַב) (in the original sense of flapping); KJV: tail.

H2181 זָנָה (zânâh, zaw-naw'): to commit adultery (usually of the female, and less often of simple fornication, rarely of involuntary ravishment); figuratively, to commit idolatry (the Jewish people being regarded as the spouse of Jehovah). Origin: a primitive root (highly-fed and therefore wanton); KJV: (cause to) commit fornication, [idiom] continually, [idiom] great, (be an, play the) harlot, (cause to be, play the) whore, (commit, fall to) whoredom, (cause to) go a-whoring, whorish.

H2182 זָנוֹחַ (Zânôwach, zaw-no'-akh): Zanoach, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H2186 (זָנַח); rejected; KJV: Zanoah.

H2183 זָנוּן (zânûwn, zaw-noon'): adultery; figuratively, idolatry. Origin: from H2181 (זָנָה); KJV: whoredom.

H2184 זְנוּת (zᵉnûwth, zen-ooth'): adultery, i.e. (figuratively) infidelity, idolatry. Origin: from H2181 (זָנָה); KJV: whoredom.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2185 to H2324
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2185 זֹנוֹת (zônôwth, zo-noth'): harlots. Origin: regarded by some as if from H2109 (זוּן) or an unused root, and applied to military equipments; but evidently the feminine plural active participle of H2181 (זָנָה); KJV: armour.

H2186 זָנַח (zânach, zaw-nakh'): reject, forsake, fail. Origin: a primitive root meaning to push aside, i.e. KJV: cast away (off), remove far away (off).

H2187 זָנַק (zânaq, zaw-nak'): properly, to draw together the feet (as an animal about to dart upon its prey), i.e. to spring forward. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: leap.

H2188 זֵעָה (zêʻâh, zay-aw'): perspiration. Origin: from H2111 (זוּעַ) (in the sense of H3154 (יֶזַע)); KJV: sweat.

H2189 זַעֲוָה (zaʻăvâh, zah-av-aw'): agitation, maltreatment. Origin: by transposition for H2113 (זְוָעָה); KJV: [idiom] removed, trouble.

H2190 זַעֲוָן (Zaʻăvân, zah-av-awn'): Zaavan, an Idumaean. Origin: from H2111 (זוּעַ); disquiet; KJV: Zaavan.

H2191 זְעֵיר (zᵉʻêyr, zeh-ayr'): small. Origin: from an unused root (akin (by permutation) to H6819 (צָעַר)), meaning to dwindle; KJV: little.

H2192 זְעֵיר (zᵉʻêyr, zeh-ayr'): {small}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2191 (זְעֵיר)xlit zeʻêyr corrected to zᵉʻêyr KJV: little.

H2193 זָעַךְ (zâʻak, zaw-ak'): to extinguish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be extinct.

H2194 זָעַם (zâʻam, zaw-am'): properly, to foam at the mouth, i.e. to be enraged. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor, abominable, (be) angry, defy, (have) indignation.

H2195 זַעַם (zaʻam, zah'-am): strictly froth at the mouth, i.e. (figuratively) fury (especially of God's displeasure with sin). Origin: from H2194 (זָעַם); KJV: angry, indignation, rage.

H2196 זָעַף (zâʻaph, zaw-af'): properly, to boil up, i.e. (figuratively) to be peevish or angry. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fret, sad, worse liking, be wroth.

H2197 זַעַף (zaʻaph, zah'-af): anger. Origin: from H2196 (זָעַף); KJV: indignation, rage(-ing), wrath.

H2198 זָעֵף (zâʻêph, zaw-afe'): angry. Origin: from H2196 (זָעַף); KJV: displeased.

H2199 זָעַק (zâʻaq, zaw-ak'): to shriek (from anguish or danger); by analogy, (as a herald) to announce or convene publicly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: assemble, call (together), (make a) cry (out), come with such a company, gather (together), cause to be proclaimed.

H2200 זְעִק (zᵉʻiq, zek'-eek): to make an outcry. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2199 (זָעַק); KJV: cry.

H2201 זַעַק (zaʻaq, zah'-ak): a shriek or outcry. Origin: and (feminine) זְעָקָהxlit zᵉâqâh corrected to zᵉʻâqâh; from H2199 (זָעַק); KJV: cry(-ing).

H2202 זִפְרֹן (Ziphrôn, zi-frone'): Ziphron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to be fragrant); KJV: Ziphron.

H2203 זֶפֶת (zepheth, zeh'-feth): asphalt (from its tendency to soften in the sun). Origin: from an unused root (meaning to liquify); KJV: pitch.

H2204 זָקֵן (zâqên, zaw-kane'): to be old. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: aged man, be (wax) old (man).

H2205 זָקֵן (zâqên, zaw-kane'): old. Origin: from H2204 (זָקֵן); KJV: aged, ancient (man), elder(-est), old (man, men and...women), senator.

H2206 זָקָן (zâqân, zaw-kawn'): the beard (as indicating age). Origin: from H2204 (זָקֵן); KJV: beard.

H2207 זֹקֶן (zôqen, zo'-ken): old age. Origin: from H2204 (זָקֵן); KJV: age.

H2208 זָקֻן (zâqun, zaw-koon'): old age. Origin: properly, passive participle of H2204 (זָקֵן) (used only in the plural as a noun); KJV: old age.

H2209 זִקְנָה (ziqnâh, zik-naw'): old age. Origin: feminine of H2205 (זָקֵן); KJV: old (age).

H2210 זָקַף (zâqaph, zaw-kaf'): to life, i.e. (figuratively) comfort. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: raise (up).

H2211 זְקַף (zᵉqaph, zek-af'): to hang, i.e. impale. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2210 (זָקַף); KJV: set up.

H2212 זָקַק (zâqaq, zaw-kak'): to strain, (figuratively) extract, clarify. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fine, pour down, purge, purify, refine.

H2213 זֵר (zêr, zare): a chaplet (as spread around the top), i.e. (specifically) a border moulding. Origin: from H2237 (זָרַר) (in the sense of scattering); KJV: crown.

H2214 זָרָא (zârâʼ, zaw-raw'): disgust. Origin: from H2114 (זוּר) (in the sense of estrangement) (compare H2219 (זָרָה)); KJV: loathsome.

H2215 זָרַב (zârab, zaw-rab'): to flow away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wax warm.

H2216 זְרֻבָּבֶל (Zᵉrubbâbel, zer-oob-baw-bel'): Zerubbabel, an Israelite. Origin: from H2215 (זָרַב) and H894 (בָּבֶל); descended of (i.e. from) Babylon, i.e. born there; KJV: Zerubbabel.

H2217 זְרֻבָּבֶל (Zᵉrubbâbel, zer-oob-baw-bel'): {Zerubbabel, an Israelite}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2216 (זְרֻבָּבֶל) KJV: Zerubbabel.

H2218 זֶרֶד (Zered, zeh'-red): Zered, a brook East of the Dead Sea. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be exuberant in growth; lined with shrubbery; KJV: Zared, Zered.

H2219 זָרָה (zârâh, zaw-raw'): to toss about; by implication, to diffuse, winnow. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2114 (זוּר)); KJV: cast away, compass, disperse, fan, scatter (away), spread, strew, winnow.

H2220 זְרוֹעַ (zᵉrôwaʻ, zer-o'-ah): the arm (as stretched out), or (of animals) the foreleg; figuratively, force. Origin: or (shortened) זְרֹעַ; and (feminine) זְרוֹעָה; or זְרֹעָה; from H2232 (זָרַע); KJV: arm, [phrase] help, mighty, power, shoulder, strength.

H2221 זֵרוּעַ (zêrûwaʻ, zay-roo'-ah): something sown, i.e. a plant. Origin: from H2232 (זָרַע); KJV: sowing, thing that is sown.

H2222 זַרְזִיף (zarzîyph, zar-zeef'): a pouring rain. Origin: by reduplication from an unused root meaning to flow; KJV: water.

H2223 זַרְזִיר (zarzîyr, zar-zeer'): properly, tightly girt, i.e. probably a racer, or some fleet animal (as being slender in the waist). Origin: by reduplication from H2115 (זוּר); KJV: [phrase] greyhound.

H2224 זָרַח (zârach, zaw-rakh'): properly, to irradiate (or shoot forth beams), i.e. to rise (as the sun); specifically, to appear (as a symptom of leprosy). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: arise, rise (up), as soon as it is up.

H2225 זֶרַח (zerach, zeh'-rakh): a rising of light. Origin: from H2224 (זָרַח); KJV: rising.

H2226 זֶרַח (Zerach, zeh'-rakh): Zerach, the name of three Israelites, also of an Idumaean and an Ethiopian prince. Origin: the same as H2225 (זֶרַח); KJV: Zarah, Zerah.

H2227 זַרְחִי (Zarchîy, zar-khee'): a Zarchite or descendant of Zerach. Origin: patronymically from H2226 (זֶרַח); KJV: Zarchite.

H2228 זְרַחְיָה (Zᵉrachyâh, zer-akh-yaw'): Zerachjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2225 (זֶרַח) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has risen; KJV: Zerahiah.

H2229 זָרַם (zâram, zaw-ram'): to gush (as water). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: carry away as with a flood, pour out.

H2230 זֶרֶם (zerem, zeh'-rem): a gush of water. Origin: from H2229 (זָרַם); KJV: flood, overflowing, shower, storm, tempest.

H2231 זִרְמָה (zirmâh, zir-maw'): a gushing of fluid (semen). Origin: feminine of H2230 (זֶרֶם); KJV: issue.

H2232 זָרַע (zâraʻ, zaw-rah'): to sow; figuratively, to disseminate, plant, fructify. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear, conceive seed, set with sow(-er), yield.

H2233 זֶרַע (zeraʻ, zeh'-rah): seed; figuratively, fruit, plant, sowing-time, posterity. Origin: from H2232 (זָרַע); KJV: [idiom] carnally, child, fruitful, seed(-time), sowing-time.

H2234 זְרַע (zᵉraʻ, zer-ah'): posterity. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2233 (זֶרַע); KJV: seed.

H2235 זֵרֹעַ (zêrôaʻ, zay-ro'-ah): something sown (only in the plural), i.e. a vegetable (as food). Origin: or זֵרָעֹן; from H2232 (זָרַע); KJV: pulse.

H2236 זָרַק (zâraq, zaw-rak'): to sprinkle (fluid or solid particles). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be here and there, scatter, sprinkle, strew.

H2237 זָרַר (zârar, zaw-rar'): perhaps to diffuse, i.e. (specifically) to sneeze. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2114 (זוּר)); KJV: sneeze.

H2238 זֶרֶשׁ (Zeresh, zeh'-resh): Zeresh, Haman's wife. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Zeresh.

H2239 זֶרֶת (zereth, zeh'-reth): the spread of the fingers, i.e. a span. Origin: from H2219 (זָרָה); KJV: span.

H2240 זַתּוּא (Zattûwʼ, zat-too'): Zattu, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Zattu.

H2241 זֵתָם (Zêthâm, zay-thawm'): Zetham, an Israelite. Origin: apparently a variation for H2133 (זֵיתָן); KJV: Zetham.

H2242 זֵתַר (Zêthar, zay-thar'): Zethar, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Zethar. j

H2243 חֹב (chôb, khobe): properly, a cherisher, i.e. the bosom. Origin: by contraction from H2245 (חָבַב); KJV: bosom.

H2244 חָבָא (châbâʼ, khaw-baw'): to secrete. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2245 (חָבַב)); KJV: [idiom] held, hide (self), do secretly.

H2245 חָבַב (châbab, khaw-bab'): properly, to hide (as in the bosom), i.e. to cherish (with affection). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2244 (חָבָא), H2247 (חָבָה)); KJV: love.

H2246 חֹבָב (Chôbâb, kho-bawb'): Chobab, father-in-law of Moses. Origin: from H2245 (חָבַב); cherished; KJV: Hobab.

H2247 חָבָה (châbâh, khaw-bah'): to secrete. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2245 (חָבַב)); KJV: hide (self).

H2248 חֲבוּלָה (chăbûwlâh, khab-oo-law'): properly, overthrown, i.e. (morally) crime. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2255 (חֲבַל); KJV: hurt.

H2249 חָבוֹר (Châbôwr, khaw-bore'): Chabor, a river of Assyria. Origin: from H2266 (חָבַר); united; KJV: Habor.

H2250 חַבּוּרָה (chabbûwrâh, khab-boo-raw'): properly, bound (with stripes), i.e. a weal (or black-and-blue mark itself). Origin: or חַבֻּרָה; or חֲבֻרָה; from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: blueness, bruise, hurt, stripe, wound.

H2251 חָבַט (châbaṭ, khaw-bat'): to knock out or off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat (off, out), thresh.

H2252 חֲבַיָּה (Chăbayâh, khab-ah-yaw'): Chabajah, an Israelite. Origin: or חֲבָיָהlemma חֲבָיה missing vowel, corrected to חֲבָיָה; from H2247 (חָבָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has hidden; KJV: Habaiah.

H2253 חֶבְיוֹן (chebyôwn, kheb-yone'): a concealment. Origin: from H2247 (חָבָה); KJV: hiding.

H2254 חָבַל (châbal, khaw-bal'): to wind tightly (as a rope), i.e. to bind; specifically, by a pledge; figuratively, to pervert, destroy; also to writhe in pain (especially of parturition). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, band, bring forth, (deal) corrupt(-ly), destroy, offend, lay to (take a) pledge, spoil, travail, [idiom] very, withhold.

H2255 חֲבַל (chăbal, khab-al'): to ruin. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2254 (חָבַל); KJV: destroy, hurt.

H2256 חֶבֶל (chebel, kheh'-bel): a rope (as twisted), especially a measuring line; by implication, a district or inheritance (as measured); or a noose (as of cords); figuratively, a company (as if tied together); also a throe (especially of parturition); also ruin. Origin: or חֵבֶל; from H2254 (חָבַל); KJV: band, coast, company, cord, country, destruction, line, lot, pain, pang, portion, region, rope, snare, sorrow, tackling.

H2257 חֲבַל (chăbal, khab-al'): harm (personal or pecuniary). Origin: (Aramaic) from H2255 (חֲבַל); KJV: damage, hurt.

H2258 חֲבֹל (chăbôl, khab-ole'): a pawn (as security for debt). Origin: or (feminine) חֲבֹלָה; from H2254 (חָבַל); KJV: pledge.

H2259 חֹבֵל (chôbêl, kho-bale'): a sailor. Origin: active participle from H2254 (חָבַל) (in the sense of handling ropes); KJV: pilot, shipmaster.

H2260 חִבֵּל (chibbêl, khib-bale'): a mast. Origin: from H2254 (חָבַל) (in the sense of furnished with ropes); KJV: mast.

H2261 חֲבַצֶּלֶת (chăbatstseleth, khab-ats-tseh'-leth): probably meadow-saffron. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: rose.

H2262 חֲבַצַּנְיָה (Chăbatstsanyâh, khab-ats-tsan-yaw'): Chabatstsanjah, a Rechabite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Habazaniah.

H2263 חָבַק (châbaq, khaw-bak'): to clasp (the hands or in embrace). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: embrace, fold.

H2264 חִבֻּק (chibbuq, khib-book'): a clasping of the hands (in idleness). Origin: from H2263 (חָבַק); KJV: fold.

H2265 חֲבַקּוּק (Chăbaqqûwq, khab-ak-kook'): Chabakkuk, the prophet. Origin: by reduplication from H2263 (חָבַק); embrace; KJV: Habakkuk.

H2266 חָבַר (châbar, khaw-bar'): to join (literally or figuratively); specifically (by means of spells) to fascinate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: charm(-er), be compact, couple (together), have fellowship with, heap up, join (self, together), league.

H2267 חֶבֶר (cheber, kheh'-ber): a society; also a spell. Origin: from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: [phrase] charmer(-ing), company, enchantment, [idiom] wide.

H2268 חֶבֶר (Cheber, kheh'-ber): Cheber, the name of a Kenite and of three Israelites. Origin: the same as H2267 (חֶבֶר); community; KJV: Heber.

H2269 חֲבַר (chăbar, khab-ar'): an associate. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: companion, fellow.

H2270 חָבֵר (châbêr, khaw-bare'): an associate. Origin: from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: companion, fellow, knit together.

H2271 חַבָּר (chabbâr, khab-bawr'): a partner. Origin: from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: companion.

H2272 חֲבַרְבֻּרָה (chăbarburâh, khab-ar-boo-raw'): a streak (like a line), as on the tiger. Origin: by reduplication from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: spot.

H2273 חַבְרָה (chabrâh, khab-raw'): an associate. Origin: (Aramaic) feminine of H2269 (חֲבַר); KJV: other.

H2274 חֶבְרָה (chebrâh, kheb-raw'): association. Origin: feminine of H2267 (חֶבֶר); KJV: company.

H2275 חֶבְרוֹן (Chebrôwn, kheb-rone'): Chebron, a place in Palestine, also the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2267 (חֶבֶר); seat of association; KJV: Hebron.

H2276 חֶבְרוֹנִי (Chebrôwnîy, kheb-ro-nee'): Chebronite (collectively), an inhabitant of Chebron. Origin: or חֶבְרֹנִי; patronymically from H2275 (חֶבְרוֹן); KJV: Hebronites.

H2277 חֶבְרִי (Chebrîy, kheb-ree'): a Chebrite (collectively) or descendants of Cheber. Origin: patronymically from H2268 (חֶבֶר); KJV: Heberites.

H2278 חֲבֶרֶת (chăbereth, khab-eh'-reth): a consort. Origin: feminine of H2270 (חָבֵר); KJV: companion.

H2279 חֹבֶרֶת (chôbereth, kho-beh'-reth): a joint. Origin: feminine active participle of H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: which coupleth, coupling.

H2280 חָבַשׁ (châbash, khaw-bash'): to wrap firmly (especially a turban, compress, or saddle); figuratively, to stop, to rule. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind (up), gird about, govern, healer, put, saddle, wrap about.

H2281 חָבֵת (châbêth, khaw-bayth'): something fried, probably a griddle-cake. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to cook (compare H4227 (מַחֲבַת)); KJV: pan.

H2282 חַג (chag, khag): a festival, or a victim therefor. Origin: or חָג; from H2287 (חָגַג); KJV: (solemn) feast (day), sacrifice, solemnity.

H2283 חָגָא (châgâʼ, khaw-gaw'): properly, vertigo, i.e. (figuratively) fear. Origin: from an unused root meaning to revolve (compare H2287 (חָגַג)); KJV: terror.

H2284 חָגָב (châgâb, khaw-gawb'): a locust. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: locust.

H2285 חָגָב (Châgâb, khaw-gawb'): Chagab, one of the Nethinim. Origin: the same as H2284 (חָגָב); locust; KJV: Hagab.

H2286 חֲגָבָא (Chăgâbâʼ, khag-aw-baw'): Chagaba or Chagabah, one of the Nethinim. Origin: or חֲגָבָה; feminine of H2285 (חָגָב); locust; KJV: Hagaba, Hagabah.

H2287 חָגַג (châgag, khaw-gag'): properly, to move in acircle, i.e. (specifically) to march in asacred procession, to observe afestival; by implication, to be giddy. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2283 (חָגָא), H2328 (חוּג)); KJV: celebrate, dance, (keep, hold) a (solemn) feast (holiday), reel to and fro.

H2288 חֲגָו (chăgâv, khag-awv'): a rift in rocks. Origin: from an unused root meaning to take refuge; KJV: cleft.

H2289 חָגוֹר (châgôwr, khaw-gore'): belted. Origin: from H2296 (חָגַר); KJV: girded with.

H2290 חֲגוֹר (chăgôwr, khag-ore'): a belt (for the waist). Origin: or חֲגֹר; and (feminine) חֲגוֹרָה; or חֲגֹרָה; from H2296 (חָגַר); KJV: apron, armour, gird(-le).

H2291 חַגִּי (Chaggîy, khag-ghee'): Chaggi, an Israelite; also (patronymically) a Chaggite, or descendant of the same. Origin: from H2287 (חָגַג); festive KJV: Haggi, Haggites.

H2292 חַגַּי (Chaggay, khag-gah'-ee): Chaggai, a Hebrew prophet. Origin: from H2282 (חַג); festive; KJV: Haggai.

H2293 חַגִּיָּה (Chaggîyâh, khag-ghee-yaw'): Chaggijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2282 (חַג) and H3050 (יָהּ); festival of Jah; KJV: Haggiah.

H2294 חַגִּית (Chaggîyth, khag-gheeth'): Chaggith, a wife of David. Origin: feminine of H2291 (חַגִּי); festive; KJV: Haggith.

H2295 חׇגְלָה (Choglâh, khog-law'): Choglah, an Israelitess. Origin: of uncertain derivation; probably a partridge; KJV: Hoglah. See also H1031 (בֵּית חׇגְלָה).

H2296 חָגַר (châgar, khaw-gar'): to gird on (as a belt, armor, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be able to put on, be afraid, appointed, gird, restrain, [idiom] on every side.

H2297 חַד (chad, khad): one. Origin: abridged from H259 (אֶחָד); KJV: one.

H2298 חַד (chad, khad): as card. one; as article single; as an ordinal, first; adverbially, at once. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2297 (חַד); KJV: a, first, one, together.

H2299 חַד (chad, khad): sharp. Origin: from H2300 (חָדַד); KJV: sharp.

H2300 חָדַד (châdad, khaw-dad'): to be (causatively, make) sharp or (figuratively) severe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be fierce, sharpen.

H2301 חֲדַד (Chădad, khad-ad'): Chadad, an Ishmaelite. Origin: from H2300 (חָדַד); fierce; KJV: Hadad.

H2302 חָדָה (châdâh, khaw-daw'): to rejoice. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make glad, be joined, rejoice.

H2303 חַדּוּד (chaddûwd, khad-dood'): a point. Origin: from H2300 (חָדַד); KJV: sharp.

H2304 חֶדְוָה (chedvâh, khed-vaw'): rejoicing. Origin: from H2302 (חָדָה); KJV: gladness, joy.

H2305 חֶדְוָה (chedvâh, khed-vaw'): {rejoicing}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2304 (חֶדְוָה) KJV: joy.

H2306 חֲדִי (chădîy, khad-ee'): a breast. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2373 (חָזֶה); KJV: breast.

H2307 חָדִיד (Châdîyd, khaw-deed'): Chadid, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2300 (חָדַד); a peak; KJV: Hadid.

H2308 חָדַל (châdal, khaw-dal'): properly, to be flabby, i.e. (by implication) desist; (figuratively) be lacking or idle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease, end, fall, forbear, forsake, leave (off), let alone, rest, be unoccupied, want.

H2309 חֶדֶל (chedel, kheh'-del): rest, i.e. the state of the dead. Origin: from H2308 (חָדַל); KJV: world.

H2310 חָדֵל (châdêl, khaw-dale'): vacant, i.e. ceasing or destitute. Origin: from H2308 (חָדַל); KJV: he that forbeareth, frail, rejected.

H2311 חַדְלַי (Chadlay, khad-lah'-ee): Chadlai, an Israelite. Origin: from H2309 (חֶדֶל); idle; KJV: Hadlai.

H2312 חֵדֶק (chêdeq, khay'-dek): a prickly plant. Origin: from an unused root meaning to sting; KJV: brier, thorn.

H2313 חִדֶּקֶל (Chiddeqel, khid-deh'-kel): the Chiddekel (or Tigris) river. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Hiddekel.

H2314 חָדַר (châdar, khaw-dar'): properly, to inclose (as a room), i.e. (by analogy,) to beset (as in a siege). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: enter a privy chamber.

H2315 חֶדֶר (cheder, kheh'-der): an apartment (usually literal). Origin: from H2314 (חָדַר); KJV: ((bed) inner) chamber, innermost(-ward) part, parlour, [phrase] south, [idiom] within.

H2316 חֲדַר (Chădar, khad-ar'): Chadar, an Ishmaelite. Origin: another form for H2315 (חֶדֶר); chamber; KJV: Hadar.

H2317 חַדְרָךְ (Chadrâk, khad-rawk'): Chadrak, a Syrian deity. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Hadrach.

H2318 חָדַשׁ (châdash, khaw-dash'): to be new; causatively, to rebuild. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: renew, repair.

H2319 חָדָשׁ (châdâsh, khaw-dawsh'): new. Origin: from H2318 (חָדַשׁ); KJV: fresh, new thing.

H2320 חֹדֶשׁ (chôdesh, kho'-desh): the new moon; by implication, a month. Origin: from H2318 (חָדַשׁ); KJV: month(-ly), new moon.

H2321 חֹדֶשׁ (Chôdesh, kho'-desh): Chodesh, an Israelitess. Origin: the same as H2320 (חֹדֶשׁ); KJV: Hodesh.

H2322 חֲדָשָׁה (Chădâshâh, khad-aw-shaw'): Chadashah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H2319 (חָדָשׁ); new; KJV: Hadashah.

H2323 חֲדָת (chădâth, khad-ath'): new. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2319 (חָדָשׁ); KJV: new.

H2324 חֲוָא (chăvâʼ, khav-aw'): to show. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2331 (חָוָה); KJV: shew.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2325 to H2449
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2325 חוּב (chûwb, khoob): properly, perhaps to tie, i.e. (figuratively and reflexively) to owe, or (by implication) to forfeit. Origin: also חָיַב; a primitive root; KJV: make endanger.

H2326 חוֹב (chôwb, khobe): debt. Origin: from H2325 (חוּב); KJV: debtor.

H2327 חוֹבָה (chôwbâh, kho-baw'): Chobah, a place in Syria. Origin: feminine active participle of H2247 (חָבָה); hiding place; KJV: Hobah.

H2328 חוּג (chûwg, khoog): to describe a circle. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2287 (חָגַג)); KJV: compass.

H2329 חוּג (chûwg, khoog): a circle. Origin: from H2328 (חוּג); KJV: circle, circuit, compass.

H2330 חוּד (chûwd, khood): properly, to tie a knot, i.e. (figuratively) to propound a riddle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: put forth.

H2331 חָוָה (châvâh, khaw-vah'): properly, to live; by implication (intensively) to declare or show. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H2324 (חֲוָא), H2421 (חָיָה)); KJV: show.

H2332 חַוָּה (Chavvâh, khav-vaw'): Chavvah (or Eve), the first woman. Origin: causatively from H2331 (חָוָה); life-giver; KJV: Eve.

H2333 חַוָּה (chavvâh, khav-vaw'): by implication, an encampment or village. Origin: properly, the same as H2332 (חַוָּה) (lifegiving, i.e. living-place); KJV: (small) town.

H2334 חַוּוֹת יָעִיר (Chavvôwth Yâʻîyr, khav-vothe' yaw-eer'): hamlets of Jair, a region of Palestine. Origin: from the plural of H2333 (חַוָּה) and a modification of H3265 (יָעוּר); KJV: (Bashan-) Havoth-jair.

H2335 חוֹזַי (Chôwzay, kho-zah'-ee): Chozai, an Israelite. Origin: from H2374 (חֹזֶה); visionary; KJV: the seers.

H2336 חוֹחַ (chôwach, kho'-akh): a thorn; by analogy, a ring forthe nose. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to pierce; KJV: bramble, thistle, thorn.

H2337 חָוָח (châvâch, khaw-vawkh'): a dell or crevice (as if pierced in the earth). Origin: perhaps the same as H2336 (חוֹחַ); KJV: thicket.

H2338 חוּט (chûwṭ, khoot): to string together, i.e. (figuratively) to repair. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of H2339 (חוּט), perhaps as a denominative; KJV: join.

H2339 חוּט (chûwṭ, khoot): a string; by implication, a measuring tape. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to sew; KJV: cord, fillet, line, thread.

H2340 חִוִּי (Chivvîy, khiv-vee'): a Chivvite, one of the aboriginal tribes of Palestine. Origin: perhaps from H2333 (חַוָּה); a villager; KJV: Hivite.

H2341 חֲוִילָה (Chăvîylâh, khav-ee-law'): Chavilah, the name of two or three eastern regions; also perhaps of two men. Origin: probably from H2342 (חוּל); circular; KJV: Havilah.

H2342 חוּל (chûwl, khool): properly, to twist or whirl (in a circular or spiral manner), i.e. (specifically) to dance, to writhe in pain (especially of parturition) or fear; figuratively, to wait, to pervert. Origin: or חִיל; a primitive root; KJV: bear, (make to) bring forth, (make to) calve, dance, drive away, fall grievously (with pain), fear, form, great, grieve, (be) grievous, hope, look, make, be in pain, be much (sore) pained, rest, shake, shapen, (be) sorrow(-ful), stay, tarry, travail (with pain), tremble, trust, wait carefully (patiently), be wounded.

H2343 חוּל (Chûwl, khool): Chul, a son of Aram; also the region settled by him. Origin: from H2342 (חוּל); a circle; KJV: Hul.

H2344 חוֹל (chôwl, khole): sand (as round or whirling particles). Origin: from H2342 (חוּל); KJV: sand.

H2345 חוּם (chûwm, khoom): sunburnt or swarthy (blackish). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be warm, i.e. (by implication) KJV: brown.

H2346 חוֹמָה (chôwmâh, kho-maw'): a wall of protection. Origin: feminine active participle of an unused root apparently meaning to join; KJV: wall, walled.

H2347 חוּס (chûwç, khoos): properly, to cover, i.e. (figuratively) to compassionate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pity, regard, spare.

H2348 חוֹף (chôwph, khofe): a cove (as a sheltered bay). Origin: from an unused root meaning to cover; KJV: coast (of the sea), haven, shore, (sea-) side.

H2349 חוּפָם (Chûwphâm, khoo-fawm'): Chupham, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H2348 (חוֹף); protection; KJV: Hupham.

H2350 חוּפָמִי (Chûwphâmîy, khoo-faw-mee'): a Chuphamite or descendant of Chupham. Origin: patronymically from H2349 (חוּפָם); KJV: Huphamites.

H2351 חוּץ (chûwts, khoots): properly, separate by awall, i.e. outside, outdoors. Origin: or (shortened) חֻץ; (both forms feminine in the plural) from an unused root meaning to sever; KJV: abroad, field, forth, highway, more, out(-side, -ward), street, without.

H2352 חוּר (chûwr, khoor): the crevice of a serpent; the cell of aprison. Origin: or (shortened) חֻר; from an unused root probably meaning to bore; KJV: hole.

H2353 חוּר (chûwr, khoor): white linen. Origin: from H2357 (חָוַר); KJV: white.

H2354 חוּר (Chûwr, khoor): Chur, the name of four Israelites and one Midianite. Origin: the same as H2353 (חוּר) or H2352 (חוּר); KJV: Hur.

H2355 חוֹר (chôwr, khore): white linen. Origin: the same as H2353 (חוּר); KJV: network. Compare H2715 (חֹר).

H2356 חוֹר (chôwr, khore): a cavity, socket, den. Origin: or (shortened) חֹר; the same as H2352 (חוּר); KJV: cave, hole.

H2357 חָוַר (châvar, khaw-var'): to blanch (as with shame). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wax pale.

H2358 חִוָּר (chivvâr, khiv-vawr'): white. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2357 (חָוַר); KJV: white.

H2359 חוּרִי (Chûwrîy, khoo-ree'): Churi, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H2353 (חוּר); linen-worker; KJV: Huri.

H2360 חוּרַי (Chûwray, khoo-rah'ee): Churai, an Israelite. Origin: probably an orthographical variation for H2359 (חוּרִי); KJV: Hurai.

H2361 חוּרָם (Chûwrâm, khoo-rawm'): Churam, the name of an Israelite and two Syrians. Origin: probably from H2353 (חוּר); whiteness, i.e. noble; KJV: Huram. Compare H2438 (חִירָם).

H2362 חַוְרָן (Chavrân, khav-rawn'): Chavran, a region East of the Jordan. Origin: apparently from H2357 (חָוַר) (in the sense of H2352 (חוּר)); cavernous; KJV: Hauran.

H2363 חוּשׁ (chûwsh, koosh): to hurry; figuratively, to be eager with excitement or enjoyment. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) haste(-n), ready.

H2364 חוּשָׁה (Chûwshâh, khoo-shaw'): Chushah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2363 (חוּשׁ); haste; KJV: Hushah.

H2365 חוּשַׁי (Chûwshay, khoo-shah'-ee): Chushai, an Israelite. Origin: from H2363 (חוּשׁ); hasty; KJV: Hushai.

H2366 חוּשִׁים (Chûwshîym, khoo-sheem'): Chushim, the name of three Israelites. Origin: or חֻשִׁים; or חֻשִׁם; plural from H2363 (חוּשׁ); hasters; KJV: Hushim.

H2367 חוּשָׁם (Chûwshâm, khoo-shawm'): Chusham, an Idumaean. Origin: or חֻשָׁם; from H2363 (חוּשׁ); hastily; KJV: Husham.

H2368 חוֹתָם (chôwthâm, kho-thawm'): a signature-ring. Origin: or חֹתָם; from H2856 (חָתַם); KJV: seal, signet.

H2369 חוֹתָם (Chôwthâm, kho-thawm'): Chotham, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H2368 (חוֹתָם); seal; KJV: Hotham, Hothan.

H2370 חֲזָא (chăzâʼ, khaz-aw'): to gaze upon; mentally to dream, be usual (i.e. seem). Origin: (Aramaic) or חֲזָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: behold, have (a dream), see, be wont.

H2371 חֲזָאֵל (Chăzâʼêl, khaz-aw-ale'): Chazael, a king of Syria. Origin: or חֲזָהאֵל; from H2372 (חָזָה) and H410 (אֵל); God has seen; KJV: Hazael.

H2372 חָזָה (châzâh, khaw-zaw'): to gaze at; mentally to perceive, contemplate (with pleasure); specifically, to have avision of. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: behold, look, prophesy, provide, see.

H2373 חָזֶה (châzeh, khaw-zeh'): the breast (as most seen in front). Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: breast.

H2374 חֹזֶה (chôzeh, kho-zeh'): a beholder in vision; also a compact (as looked upon with approval). Origin: active participle of H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: agreement, prophet, see that, seer, (star-) gazer.

H2375 חֲזוֹ (Chăzôw, khaz-o'): Chazo, a nephew of Abraham. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); seer; KJV: Hazo.

H2376 חֵזֵו (chêzêv, khay'-zev): a sight. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2370 (חֲזָא); KJV: look, vision.

H2377 חָזוֹן (châzôwn, khaw-zone'): a sight (mentally), i.e. a dream, revelation, or oracle. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: vision.

H2378 חָזוֹת (châzôwth, khaw-zooth'): a revelation. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: vision.

H2379 חֲזוֹת (chăzôwth, khaz-oth'): a view. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2370 (חֲזָא); KJV: sight.

H2380 חָזוּת (châzûwth, khaw-zooth'): a look; hence (figuratively) striking appearance, revelation, or (by implication) compact. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: agreement, notable (one), vision.

H2381 חֲזִיאֵל (Chăzîyʼêl, khaz-ee-ale'): Chaziel, a Levite. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה) and H410 (אֵל); seen of God; KJV: Haziel.

H2382 חֲזָיָה (Chăzâyâh, khaz-aw-yaw'): Chazajah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has seen; KJV: Hazaiah.

H2383 חֶזְיוֹן (Chezyôwn, khez-yone'): Chezjon, a Syrian. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); vision; KJV: Hezion.

H2384 חִזָּיוֹן (chizzâyôwn, khiz-zaw-yone'): a revelation, expectation by dream. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: vision.

H2385 חֲזִיז (chăzîyz, khaw-zeez'): a flash of lightning. Origin: from an unused root meaning to glare; KJV: bright cloud, lightning.

H2386 חֲזִיר (chăzîyr, khaz-eer'): a hog (perhaps as penned). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to enclose; KJV: boar, swine.

H2387 חֵזִיר (Chêzîyr, khay-zeer'): Chezir, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from the same as H2386 (חֲזִיר); perhaps protected; KJV: Hezir.

H2388 חָזַק (châzaq, khaw-zak'): to fasten upon; hence, to seize, be strong (figuratively, courageous, causatively strengthen, cure, help, repair, fortify), obstinate; to bind, restrain, conquer. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: aid, amend, [idiom] calker, catch, cleave, confirm, be constant, constrain, continue, be of good (take) courage(-ous, -ly), encourage (self), be established, fasten, force, fortify, make hard, harden, help, (lay) hold (fast), lean, maintain, play the man, mend, become (wax) mighty, prevail, be recovered, repair, retain, seize, be (wax) sore, strengthen (self), be stout, be (make, shew, wax) strong(-er), be sure, take (hold), be urgent, behave self valiantly, withstand.

H2389 חָזָק (châzâq, khaw-zawk'): strong (usu. in a bad sense, hard, bold, violent). Origin: from H2388 (חָזַק); KJV: harder, hottest, [phrase] impudent, loud, mighty, sore, stiff(-hearted), strong(-er).

H2390 חָזֵק (châzêq, khaw-zake'): powerful. Origin: from H2388 (חָזַק); KJV: [idiom] wax louder, stronger.

H2391 חֵזֶק (chêzeq, khay'-zek): help. Origin: from H2388 (חָזַק); KJV: strength.

H2392 חֹזֶק (chôzeq, kho'-zek): power. Origin: from H2388 (חָזַק); KJV: strength.

H2393 חֶזְקָה (chezqâh, khez-kaw'): prevailing power. Origin: feminine of H2391 (חֵזֶק); KJV: strength(-en self), (was) strong.

H2394 חׇזְקָה (chozqâh, khoz-kaw'): vehemence (usually in a bad sense). Origin: feminine of H2392 (חֹזֶק); KJV: force, mightily, repair, sharply.

H2395 חִזְקִי (Chizqîy, khiz-kee'): Chizki, an Israelite. Origin: from H2388 (חָזַק); strong; KJV: Hezeki.

H2396 חִזְקִיָּה (Chizqîyâh, khiz-kee-yaw'): Chizkijah, a king of Judah, also the name of two other Israelites. Origin: or חִזְקִיָּהוּ; also יְחִזְקִיָּה; or יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ; from H2388 (חָזַק) and H3050 (יָהּ); strengthened of Jah; KJV: Hezekiah, Hizkiah, Hizkijah. Compare H3169 (יְחִזְקִיָּה).

H2397 חָח (châch, khawkh): a ring for the nose (or lips). Origin: once (Ezekiel 29:4) חָחִי; from the same as H2336 (חוֹחַ); KJV: bracelet, chain, hook.

H2398 חָטָא (châṭâʼ, khaw-taw'): properly, to miss; hence (figuratively and generally) to sin; by inference, to forfeit, lack, expiate, repent, (causatively) lead astray, condemn.
