Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear the blame, cleanse, commit (sin), by fault, harm he hath done, loss, miss, (make) offend(-er), offer for sin, purge, purify (self), make reconciliation, (cause, make) sin(-ful, -ness), trespass.

H2399 חֵטְא (chêṭᵉʼ, khate): a crime or its penalty. Origin: from H2398 (חָטָא); KJV: fault, [idiom] grievously, offence, (punishment of) sin.

H2400 חַטָּא (chaṭṭâʼ, khat-taw'): a criminal, or one accounted guilty. Origin: intensively from H2398 (חָטָא); KJV: offender, sinful, sinner.

H2401 חֲטָאָה (chăṭâʼâh, khat-aw-aw'): an offence, or a sacrifice forit. Origin: feminine of H2399 (חֵטְא); KJV: sin (offering).

H2402 חַטָּאָה (chaṭṭâʼâh, khat-taw-aw'): an offence, and the penalty or sacrifice forit. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2401 (חֲטָאָה); KJV: sin (offering).

H2403 חַטָּאָה (chaṭṭâʼâh, khat-taw-aw'): an offence (sometimes habitual sinfulness), and its penalty, occasion, sacrifice, or expiation; also (concretely) an offender. Origin: or חַטָּאת; from H2398 (חָטָא); KJV: punishment (of sin), purifying(-fication for sin), sin(-ner, offering).

H2404 חָטַב (châṭab, khaw-tab'): to chop or carve wood. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut down, hew(-er), polish.

H2405 חֲטֻבָה (chăṭubâh, khat-oo-baw'): properly, a carving; hence, a tapestry (as figured). Origin: feminine passive participle of H2404 (חָטַב); KJV: carved.

H2406 חִטָּה (chiṭṭâh, khit-taw'): wheat, whether the grain or the plant. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: wheat(-en).

H2407 חַטּוּשׁ (Chaṭṭûwsh, khat-toosh'): Chattush, the name of four or five Israelites. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain signification; KJV: Hattush.

H2408 חֲטִי (chăṭîy, khat-ee'): an offence. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2398 (חָטָא); KJV: sin.

H2409 חֲטָּיָא (chăṭṭâyâʼ, khat-taw-yaw'): an expiation. Origin: (Aramaic) from the same as H2408 (חֲטִי); KJV: sin offering.

H2410 חֲטִיטָא (Chăṭîyṭâʼ, khat-ee-taw'): Chatita, a temple porter. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to dig out; explorer; KJV: Hatita.

H2411 חַטִּיל (Chaṭṭîyl, khat-teel'): Chattil, one of 'Solomon's servants'. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to wave; fluctuating; KJV: Hattil.

H2412 חֲטִיפָא (Chăṭîyphâʼ, khat-ee-faw'): Chatipha, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from H2414 (חָטַף); robber; KJV: Hatipha.

H2413 חָטַם (châṭam, khaw-tam'): to stop. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: refrain.

H2414 חָטַף (châṭaph, khaw-taf'): to clutch; hence, to seize as aprisoner. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch.

H2415 חֹטֵר (chôṭêr, kho'-ter): a twig. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain signification; KJV: rod.

H2416 חַי (chay, khah'-ee): alive; hence, raw (flesh); fresh (plant, water, year), strong; also (as noun, especially in the feminine singular and masculine plural) life (or living thing), whether literally or figuratively. Origin: from H2421 (חָיָה); KJV: [phrase] age, alive, appetite, (wild) beast, company, congregation, life(-time), live(-ly), living (creature, thing), maintenance, [phrase] merry, multitude, [phrase] (be) old, quick, raw, running, springing, troop.

H2417 חַי (chay, khah'-ee): alive; also (as noun in plural) life. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2418 (חֲיָא); KJV: life, that liveth, living.

H2418 חֲיָא (chăyâʼ, khah-yaw'): to live. Origin: (Aramaic) or חֲיָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H2421 (חָיָה); KJV: live, keep alive.

H2419 חִיאֵל (Chîyʼêl, khee-ale'): Chiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H2416 (חַי) and H410 (אֵל); living of God; KJV: Hiel.

H2420 חִידָה (chîydâh, khee-daw'): a puzzle, hence, a trick, conundrum, sententious maxim. Origin: from H2330 (חוּד); KJV: dark saying (sentence, speech), hard question, proverb, riddle.

H2421 חָיָה (châyâh, khaw-yaw'): to live, whether literally or figuratively; causatively, to revive. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2331 (חָוָה), H2421 (חָיָה)); KJV: keep (leave, make) alive, [idiom] certainly, give (promise) life, (let, suffer to) live, nourish up, preserve (alive), quicken, recover, repair, restore (to life), revive, ([idiom] God) save (alive, life, lives), [idiom] surely, be whole.

H2422 חָיֶה (châyeh, khaw-yeh'): vigorous. Origin: from H2421 (חָיָה); KJV: lively.

H2423 חֵיוָא (chêyvâʼ, khay-vaw'): an animal. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2418 (חֲיָא); KJV: beast.

H2424 חַיּוּת (chayûwth, khah-yooth'): life. Origin: from H2421 (חָיָה); KJV: [idiom] living.

H2425 חָיַי (châyay, khaw-yah'-ee): to live; causatively to revive. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2421 (חָיָה)); KJV: live, save life.

H2426 חֵיל (chêyl, khale): an army; also (by analogy,) an intrenchment. Origin: or (shortened) חֵל; a collateral form of H2428 (חַיִל); KJV: army, bulwark, host, [phrase] poor, rampart, trench, wall.

H2427 חִיל (chîyl, kheel): a throe (expectant of childbirth). Origin: and (feminine) חִילָה; from H2342 (חוּל); KJV: pain, pang, sorrow.

H2428 חַיִל (chayil, khah'-yil): probably a force, whether of men, means or other resources; an army, wealth, virtue, valor, strength. Origin: from H2342 (חוּל); KJV: able, activity, ([phrase]) army, band of men (soldiers), company, (great) forces, goods, host, might, power, riches, strength, strong, substance, train, ([phrase]) valiant(-ly), valour, virtuous(-ly), war, worthy(-ily).

H2429 חַיִל (chayil, khah'-yil): an army, or strength. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2428 (חַיִל); KJV: aloud, army, [idiom] most (mighty), power.

H2430 חֵילָה (chêylâh, khay-law'): an intrenchment. Origin: feminine of H2428 (חַיִל); KJV: bulwark.

H2431 חֵילָם (Chêylâm, khay-lawm'): Chelam, a place East of Palestine. Origin: or חֵלָאםxlit Chêlʼâm corrected to Chêlâʼm; from H2428 (חַיִל); fortress; KJV: Helam.

H2432 חִילֵן (Chîylên, khee-lane'): Chilen, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2428 (חַיִל); fortress; KJV: Hilen.

H2433 חִין (chîyn, kheen): beauty. Origin: another form for H2580 (חֵן); KJV: comely.

H2434 חַיִץ (chayits, khah'-yits): a wall. Origin: another form for H2351 (חוּץ); KJV: wall.

H2435 חִיצוֹן (chîytsôwn, khee-tsone'): properly, the (outer) wall side; hence, exterior; figuratively, secular (as opposed to sacred). Origin: from H2434 (חַיִץ); KJV: outer, outward, utter, without.

H2436 חֵיק (chêyq, khake): the bosom (literally or figuratively). Origin: or חֵק; and חוֹק; from an unused root, apparently meaning to inclose; KJV: bosom, bottom, lap, midst, within.

H2437 חִירָה (Chîyrâh, khee-raw'): Chirah, an Adullamite. Origin: from H2357 (חָוַר) in the sense of splendor; KJV: Hirah.

H2438 חִירָם (Chîyrâm, khee-rawm'): Chiram or Chirom, the name of two Tyrians. Origin: or חִירוֹםlemma חִירֹם missing vav, corrected to חִירוֹם; another form of H2361 (חוּרָם); KJV: Hiram, Huram.

H2439 חִישׁ (chîysh, kheesh): to hurry. Origin: another form of H2363 (חוּשׁ); KJV: make haste.

H2440 חִישׁ (chîysh, kheesh): properly, a hurry; hence (adverb) quickly. Origin: from H2439 (חִישׁ); KJV: soon.

H2441 חֵךְ (chêk, khake): properly, the palate or inside of the mouth; hence, the mouth itself (as the organ of speech, taste and kissing). Origin: probably from H2596 (חָנַךְ) in the sense of tasting; KJV: (roof of the) mouth, taste.

H2442 חָכָה (châkâh, khaw-kaw'): properly, to adhere to; hence, to await. Origin: a primitive root (apparently akin to H2707 (חָקָה) through the idea of piercing); KJV: long, tarry, wait.

H2443 חַכָּה (chakkâh, khak-kaw'): a hook (as adhering). Origin: probably from H2442 (חָכָה); KJV: angle, hook.

H2444 חֲכִילָה (Chăkîylâh, khak-ee-law'): Chakilah, a hill in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H2447 (חַכְלִיל); dark; KJV: Hachilah.

H2445 חַכִּים (chakkîym, khak-keem'): wise, i.e. a Magian. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2449 (חָכַם); KJV: wise.

H2446 חֲכַלְיָה (Chăkalyâh, khak-al-yaw'): Chakaljah, an Israelite. Origin: from the base of H2447 (חַכְלִיל) and H3050 (יָהּ); darkness of Jah; KJV: Hachaliah.

H2447 חַכְלִיל (chaklîyl, khak-leel'): darkly flashing (only of the eyes); in a good sense, brilliant (as stimulated by wine). Origin: by reduplication from an unused root apparently meaning to be dark; KJV: red.

H2448 חַכְלִלוּת (chaklilûwth, khak-lee-looth'): flash (of the eyes); in a bad sense, blearedness. Origin: from H2447 (חַכְלִיל); KJV: redness.

H2449 חָכַם (châkam, khaw-kam'): to be wise (in mind, word or act). Origin: a primitive root, KJV: [idiom] exceeding, teach wisdom, be (make self, shew self) wise, deal (never so) wisely, make wiser.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2450 to H2582
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2450 חָכָם (châkâm, khaw-kawm'): wise, (i.e. intelligent, skilful or artful). Origin: from H2449 (חָכַם); KJV: cunning (man), subtil, (un-), wise((hearted), man).

H2451 חׇכְמָה (chokmâh, khok-maw'): wisdom (in a good sense). Origin: from H2449 (חָכַם); KJV: skilful, wisdom, wisely, wit.

H2452 חׇכְמָה (chokmâh, khok-maw'): wisdom. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2451 (חׇכְמָה); KJV: wisdom.

H2453 חַכְמוֹנִי (Chakmôwnîy, khak-mo-nee'): Chakmoni, an Israelite. Origin: from H2449 (חָכַם); skilful; KJV: Hachmoni, Hachmonite.

H2454 חׇכְמוֹת (chokmôwth, khok-moth'): wisdom. Origin: or חַכְמוֹת; collateral forms of H2451 (חׇכְמָה); KJV: wisdom, every wise (woman).

H2455 חֹל (chôl, khole): properly, exposed; hence, profane. Origin: from H2490 (חָלַל); KJV: common, profane (place), unholy.

H2456 חָלָא (châlâʼ, khaw-law'): to be sick. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2470 (חָלָה)); KJV: be diseased.

H2457 חֶלְאָה (chelʼâh, khel-aw'): properly, disease; hence, rust. Origin: from H2456 (חָלָא); KJV: scum.

H2458 חֶלְאָה (Chelʼâh, khel-aw'): Chelah, an Israelitess. Origin: the same as H2457 (חֶלְאָה); KJV: Helah.

H2459 חֶלֶב (cheleb, kheh'-leb): fat, whether literally or figuratively; hence, the richest or choice part. Origin: or חֵלֶב; from an unused root meaning to be fat; KJV: [idiom] best, fat(-ness), [idiom] finest, grease, marrow.

H2460 חֵלֶב (Chêleb, khay'-leb): Cheleb, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2459 (חֶלֶב); fatness; KJV: Heleb.

H2461 חָלָב (châlâb, khaw-lawb'): milk (as the richness of kine). Origin: from the same as H2459 (חֶלֶב); KJV: [phrase] cheese, milk, sucking.

H2462 חֶלְבָּה (Chelbâh, khel-baw'): Chelbah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H2459 (חֶלֶב); fertility; KJV: Helbah.

H2463 חֶלְבּוֹן (Chelbôwn, khel-bone'): Chelbon, a place in Syria. Origin: from H2459 (חֶלֶב); fruitful; KJV: Helbah.

H2464 חֶלְבְּנָה (chelbᵉnâh, khel-ben-aw'): galbanam, an odorous gum (as if fatty). Origin: from H2459 (חֶלֶב); KJV: galbanum.

H2465 חֶלֶד (cheled, kheh'-led): life (as a fleeting portion of time); hence, the world (as transient). Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to glide swiftly; KJV: age, short time, world.

H2466 חֵלֶד (chêled, khay'-led): Cheled, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2465 (חֶלֶד); KJV: Heled.

H2467 חֹלֶד (chôled, kho'-led): a weasel (from its gliding motion). Origin: from the same as H2465 (חֶלֶד); KJV: weasel.

H2468 חֻלְדָּה (Chuldâh, khool-daw'): Chuldah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine of H2467 (חֹלֶד); KJV: Huldah.

H2469 חֶלְדַּי (Chelday, khel-dah'-ee): Cheldai, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2466 (חֵלֶד); worldliness; KJV: Heldai.

H2470 חָלָה (châlâh, khaw-law'): properly, to be rubbed or worn; hence (figuratively) to be weak, sick, afflicted; or (causatively) to grieve, make sick; also to stroke (in flattering), entreat. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2342 (חוּל), H2470 (חָלָה), H2490 (חָלַל)); KJV: beseech, (be) diseased, (put to) grief, be grieved, (be) grievous, infirmity, intreat, lay to, put to pain, [idiom] pray, make prayer, be (fall, make) sick, sore, be sorry, make suit ([idiom] supplication), woman in travail, be (become) weak, be wounded.

H2471 חַלָּה (challâh, khal-law'): a cake (as usually punctured). Origin: from H2490 (חָלַל); KJV: cake.

H2472 חֲלוֹם (chălôwm, khal-ome'): a dream. Origin: or (shortened) חֲלֹם; from H2492 (חָלַם); KJV: dream(-er).

H2473 חֹלוֹן (Chôlôwn, kho-lone'): Cholon, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: or (shortened) חֹלֹן; probably from H2344 (חוֹל); sandy; KJV: Holon.

H2474 חַלּוֹן (challôwn, khal-lone'): a window (as perforated). KJV: window.

H2475 חֲלוֹף (chălôwph, khal-ofe'): properly, surviving; by implication (collectively) orphans. Origin: from H2498 (חָלַף); KJV: [idiom] destruction.

H2476 חֲלוּשָׁה (chălûwshâh, khal-oo-shaw'): defeat. Origin: feminine passive participle of H2522 (חָלַשׁ); KJV: being overcome.

H2477 חֲלַח (Chălach, khal-akh'): Chalach, a region of Assyria. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Halah.

H2478 חַלְחוּל (Chalchûwl, khal-khool'): Chalchul, a place in Palestine. Origin: by reduplication from H2342 (חוּל); contorted; KJV: Halhul.

H2479 חַלְחָלָה (chalchâlâh, khal-khaw-law'): writhing (in childbirth); by implication, terror. Origin: feminine from the same as H2478 (חַלְחוּל); KJV: (great, much) pain.

H2480 חָלַט (châlaṭ, khaw-lat'): to snatch at. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch.

H2481 חֲלִי (chălîy, khal-ee'): a trinket (as polished). Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); KJV: jewel, ornament.

H2482 חֲלִי (Chălîy, khal-ee'): Chali, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H2481 (חֲלִי); KJV: Hali.

H2483 חֳלִי (chŏlîy, khol-ee'): malady, anxiety, calamity. Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); KJV: disease, grief, (is) sick(-ness).

H2484 חֶלְיָה (chelyâh, khel-yaw'): a trinket. Origin: feminine of H2481 (חֲלִי); KJV: jewel.

H2485 חָלִיל (châlîyl, khaw-leel'): a flute (as perforated). Origin: from H2490 (חָלַל); KJV: pipe.

H2486 חָלִילָה (châlîylâh, khaw-lee'-law): literal fora profaned thing; used (interj.) far be it!. Origin: or חָלִלָה; a directive from H2490 (חָלַל); KJV: be far, ([idiom] God) forbid.

H2487 חֲלִיפָה (chălîyphâh, khal-ee-faw'): alternation. Origin: from H2498 (חָלַף); KJV: change, course.

H2488 חֲלִיצָה (chălîytsâh, khal-ee-tsaw'): spoil. Origin: from H2503 (חֶלֶץ); KJV: armour.

H2489 חֵלְכָא (chêlᵉkâʼ, khay-lek-aw'): a wretch, i.e. unfortunate. Origin: or חֵלְכָה; apparently from an unused root probably meaning to be dark or (figuratively) unhappy; KJV: poor.

H2490 חָלַל (châlal, khaw-lal'): properly, to bore, i.e. (by implication) to wound, to dissolve; figuratively, to profane (a person, place or thing), to break (one's word), to begin (as if by an 'opening wedge'); to play (the flute). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2470 (חָלָה)); also denominative (from H2485 (חָלִיל)) KJV: begin ([idiom] men began), defile, [idiom] break, defile, [idiom] eat (as common things), [idiom] first, [idiom] gather the grape thereof, [idiom] take inheritance, pipe, player on instruments, pollute, (cast as) profane (self), prostitute, slay (slain), sorrow, stain, wound.

H2491 חָלָל (châlâl, khaw-lawl'): pierced (especially to death); figuratively, polluted. Origin: from H2490 (חָלַל); KJV: kill, profane, slain (man), [idiom] slew, (deadly) wounded.

H2492 חָלַם (châlam, khaw-lam'): properly, to bind firmly, i.e. (by implication) to be (causatively to make) plump; also (through the figurative sense of dumbness) to dream. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) dream(-er), be in good liking, recover.

H2493 חֵלֶם (chêlem, khay'-lem): a dream. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2492 (חָלַם); KJV: dream.

H2494 חֵלֶם (Chêlem, khay'lem): Chelem, an Israelite. Origin: from H2492 (חָלַם); a dream; KJV: Helem. Compare H2469 (חֶלְדַּי).

H2495 חַלָּמוּת (challâmûwth, khal-law-mooth'): probably purslain. Origin: from H2492 (חָלַם) (in the sense of insipidity); KJV: egg.

H2496 חַלָּמִישׁ (challâmîysh, klal-law-meesh'): flint. Origin: probably from H2492 (חָלַם) (in the sense of hardness); KJV: flint(-y), rock.

H2497 חֵלֹן (Chêlôn, khay-lone'): Chelon, an Israelite. Origin: from H2428 (חַיִל); strong; KJV: Helon.

H2498 חָלַף (châlaph, khaw-laf'): properly, to slide by, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, pass on, spring up, pierce or change. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abolish, alter, change, cut off, go on forward, grow up, be over, pass (away, on, through), renew, sprout, strike through.

H2499 חֲלַף (chălaph, khal-af'): to pass on (of time). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2498 (חָלַף); KJV: pass.

H2500 חֵלֶף (chêleph, klay'-lef): properly, exchange; hence (as preposition) instead of. Origin: from H2498 (חָלַף); KJV: [idiom] for.

H2501 חֶלֶף (Cheleph, kheh'lef): Cheleph, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H2500 (חֵלֶף); change; KJV: Heleph.

H2502 חָלַץ (châlats, khaw-lats'): to pull off; hence (intensively) to strip, (reflex.) to depart; by implication, to deliver, equip (for fight); present, strengthen. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: arm (self), (go, ready) armed ([idiom] man, soldier), deliver, draw out, make fat, loose, (ready) prepared, put off, take away, withdraw self.

H2503 חֶלֶץ (Chelets, kheh'-lets): Chelets, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or חֵלֶץ; from H2502 (חָלַץ); perhaps, strength; KJV: Helez.

H2504 חָלָץ (châlâts, khaw-lawts'): the loins (as the seat of vigor). Origin: from H2502 (חָלַץ) (in the sense of strength); only in the dual; KJV: loins, reins.

H2505 חָלַק (châlaq, khaw-lak'): to be smooth (figuratively); by implication (as smooth stones were used for lots) to apportion or separate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deal, distribute, divide, flatter, give, (have, im-) part(-ner), take away a portion, receive, separate self, (be) smooth(-er).

H2506 חֵלֶק (chêleq, khay'lek): properly, smoothness (of the tongue); also an allotment. Origin: from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: flattery, inheritance, part, [idiom] partake, portion.

H2507 חֵלֶק (Chêleq, khay'-lek): Chelek, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2506 (חֵלֶק); portion; KJV: Helek.

H2508 חֲלָק (chălâq, khal-awk'): a part. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: portion.

H2509 חָלָק (châlâq, khaw-lawk'): smooth (especially of tongue). Origin: from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: flattering, smooth.

H2510 חָלָק (Châlâq, khaw-lawk'): Chalak, a mountain of Idumaea. Origin: the same as H2509 (חָלָק); bare; KJV: Halak.

H2511 חַלָּק (challâq, khal-lawk'): smooth. Origin: from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: smooth.

H2512 חַלֻּק (challuq, khal-look'): smooth. Origin: from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: smooth.

H2513 חֶלְקָה (chelqâh, khel-kaw'): properly, smoothness; figuratively, flattery; also an allotment. Origin: feminine of H2506 (חֵלֶק); KJV: field, flattering(-ry), ground, parcel, part, piece of land (ground), plat, portion, slippery place, smooth (thing).

H2514 חֲלַקָּה (chălaqqâh, khal-ak-kaw'): flattery. Origin: feminine from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: flattery.

H2515 חֲלֻקָּה (chăluqqâh, khal-ook-kaw'): a distribution. Origin: feminine of H2512 (חַלֻּק); KJV: division.

H2516 חֶלְקִי (Chelqîy, khel-kee'): a Chelkite or descendant of Chelek. Origin: patronymically from H2507 (חֵלֶק); KJV: Helkites.

H2517 חֶלְקַי (Chelqay, khel-kah'ee): Chelkai, an Israelite. Origin: from H2505 (חָלַק); apportioned; KJV: Helkai.

H2518 חִלְקִיָּה (Chilqîyâh, khil-kee-yaw'): Chilhijah, the name of eight Israelites. Origin: or חִלְקִיָּהוּ; from H2506 (חֵלֶק) and H3050 (יָהּ); portion of Jah; KJV: Hillkiah.

H2519 חֲלַקְלַקָּה (chălaqlaqqâh, khal-ak-lak-kaw'): properly, something very smooth; i.e. a treacherous spot; figuratively, blandishment. Origin: by reduplication from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: flattery, slippery.

H2520 חֶלְקַת (Chelqath, khel-kath'): Chelkath, a place in Palestine. Origin: a form of H2513 (חֶלְקָה); smoothness; KJV: Helkath.

H2521 חֶלְקַת הַצֻּרִים (Chelqath hats-Tsurîym, khel-kath' hatstsoo-reem'): Chelkath Hats-tsurim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2520 (חֶלְקַת) and the plural of H6697 (צוּר), with the article inserted; smoothness of the rocks; KJV: Helkath-hazzurim.

H2522 חָלַשׁ (châlash, khaw-lash'): to prostrate; by implication, to overthrow, decay. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: discomfit, waste away, weaken.

H2523 חַלָּשׁ (challâsh, khal-lawsh'): frail. Origin: from H2522 (חָלַשׁ); KJV: weak.

H2524 חָם (châm, khawm): a father-in-law (as in affinity). Origin: from the same as H2346 (חוֹמָה); KJV: father in law.

H2525 חָם (châm, khawm): hot. Origin: from H2552 (חָמַם); KJV: hot, warm.

H2526 חָם (Châm, khawm): Cham, a son of Noah; also (as a patronymic) his descendants or their country. Origin: the same as H2525 (חָם); hot (from the tropical habitat); KJV: Ham.

H2527 חֹם (chôm, khome): heat. Origin: from H2552 (חָמַם); KJV: heat, to be hot (warm).

H2528 חֱמָא (chĕmâʼ, khem-aw'): anger. Origin: (Aramaic) or חֲמָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H2534 (חֵמָה); KJV: fury.

H2529 חֶמְאָה (chemʼâh, khem-aw'): curdled milk or cheese. Origin: or (shortened) חֵמָה; from the same root as H2346 (חוֹמָה); KJV: butter.

H2530 חָמַד (châmad, khaw-mad'): to delight in. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beauty, greatly beloved, covet, delectable thing, ([idiom] great) delight, desire, goodly, lust, (be) pleasant (thing), precious (thing).

H2531 חֶמֶד (chemed, kheh'-med): delight. Origin: from H2530 (חָמַד); KJV: desirable, pleasant.

H2532 חֶמְדָּה (chemdâh, khem-daw'): delight. Origin: feminine of H2531 (חֶמֶד); KJV: desire, goodly, pleasant, precious.

H2533 חֶמְדָּן (Chemdân, khem-dawn'): Chemdan, an Idumaean. Origin: from H2531 (חֶמֶד); pleasant; KJV: Hemdan.

H2534 חֵמָה (chêmâh, khay-maw'): heat; figuratively, anger, poison (from its fever). Origin: or (Daniel 11:44) חֵמָא; from H3179 (יָחַם); KJV: anger, bottles, hot displeasure, furious(-ly, -ry), heat, indignation, poison, rage, wrath(-ful). See H2529 (חֶמְאָה).

H2535 חַמָּה (chammâh, kham-maw'): heat; by implication, the sun. Origin: from H2525 (חָם); KJV: heat, sun.

H2536 חַמּוּאֵל (Chammûwʼêl, kham-moo-ale'): Chammuel, an Israelite. Origin: from H2535 (חַמָּה) and H410 (אֵל); anger of God; KJV: Hamuel.

H2537 חֲמוּטַל (Chămûwṭal, kham-oo-tal'): Chamutal or Chamital, an Israelitess. Origin: or חֲמִיטַל; from H2524 (חָם) and H2919 (טַל); father-in-law of dew; KJV: Hamutal.

H2538 חָמוּל (Châmûwl, khaw-mool'): Chamul, an Israelite. Origin: from H2550 (חָמַל); pitied; KJV: Hamul.

H2539 חָמוּלִי (Châmûwlîy, khaw-moo-lee'): a Chamulite (collectively) or descendants of Chamul. Origin: patronymically from H2538 (חָמוּל); KJV: Hamulites.

H2540 חַמּוֹן (Chammôwn, kham-mone'): Chammon, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H2552 (חָמַם); warm spring; KJV: Hammon.

H2541 חָמוֹץ (châmôwts, khaw-motse'): properly, violent; by implication, a robber. Origin: from H2556 (חָמֵץ); KJV: oppressed.

H2542 חַמּוּק (chammûwq, kham-mook'): a wrapping, i.e. drawers. Origin: from H2559 (חָמַק); KJV: joints.

H2543 חֲמוֹר (chămôwr, kham-ore'): a male ass (from its dun red). Origin: or (shortened) חֲמֹר; from H2560 (חָמַר); KJV: (he) ass.

H2544 חֲמוֹר (Chămôwr, kham-ore'): Chamor, a Canaanite. Origin: the same as H2543 (חֲמוֹר); donkey; KJV: Hamor.

H2545 חֲמוֹת (chămôwth, kham-oth'): a mother-in-law. Origin: or (shortened) חֲמֹת; feminine of H2524 (חָם); KJV: mother in law.

H2546 חֹמֶט (chômeṭ, kho'met): a lizard (as creeping). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning, to lie low; KJV: snail.

H2547 חֻמְטָה (Chumṭâh, khoom-taw'): Chumtah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H2546 (חֹמֶט); low; KJV: Humtah.

H2548 חָמִיץ (châmîyts, khaw-meets'): seasoned, i.e. salt provender. Origin: from H2556 (חָמֵץ); KJV: clean.

H2549 חֲמִישִׁי (chămîyshîy, kham-ee-shee'): fifth; also a fifth. Origin: or חֲמִשִּׁי; ordinal from H2568 (חָמֵשׁ); KJV: fifth (part).

H2550 חָמַל (châmal, khaw-mal'): to commiserate; by implication, to spare. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have compassion, (have) pity, spare.

H2551 חֶמְלָה (chemlâh, khem-law'): commiseration. Origin: from H2550 (חָמַל); KJV: merciful, pity.

H2552 חָמַם (châmam, khaw-mam'): to be hot (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: enflame self, get (have) heat, be (wax) hot, (be, wax) warm (self, at).

H2553 חַמָּן (chammân, kham-mawn'): a sun-pillar. Origin: from H2535 (חַמָּה); KJV: idol, image.

H2554 חָמַס (châmaç, khaw-mas'): to be violent; by implication, to maltreat. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make bare, shake off, violate, do violence, take away violently, wrong, imagine wrongfully.

H2555 חָמָס (châmâç, khaw-mawce'): violence; by implication, wrong; by meton. unjust gain. Origin: from H2554 (חָמַס); KJV: cruel(-ty), damage, false, injustice, [idiom] oppressor, unrighteous, violence (against, done), violent (dealing), wrong.

H2556 חָמֵץ (châmêts, khaw-mates'): to be pungent; i.e. in taste (sour, i.e. literally fermented, or figuratively, harsh), in color (dazzling). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cruel (man), dyed, be grieved, leavened.

H2557 חָמֵץ (châmêts, khaw-mates'): ferment, (figuratively) extortion. Origin: from H2556 (חָמֵץ); KJV: leaven, leavened (bread).

H2558 חֹמֶץ (chômets, kho'-mets): vinegar. Origin: from H2556 (חָמֵץ); KJV: vinegar.

H2559 חָמַק (châmaq, khaw-mak'): properly, to wrap; hence, to depart (i.e. turn about). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: go about, withdraw self.

H2560 חָמַר (châmar, khaw-mar'): properly, to boil up; hence, to ferment (with scum); to glow (with redness); to smear with pitch. Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative (from H2564 (חֵמָר)) KJV: daub, befoul, be red, trouble.

H2561 חֶמֶר (chemer, kheh'-mer): wine (as fermenting). Origin: from H2560 (חָמַר); KJV: [idiom] pure, red wine.

H2562 חֲמַר (chămar, kham-ar'): wine. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2561 (חֶמֶר); KJV: wine.

H2563 חֹמֶר (chômer, kho'mer): properly, a bubbling up, i.e. of water, a wave; of earth, mire or clay (cement); also a heap; hence, a chomer or dry measure. Origin: from H2560 (חָמַר); KJV: clay, heap, homer, mire, motion.

H2564 חֵמָר (chêmâr, khay-mawr'): bitumen (as rising to the surface). Origin: from H2560 (חָמַר); KJV: slime(-pit).

H2565 חֲמֹרָה (chămôrâh, kham-o-raw'): a heap. Origin: from H2560 (חָמַר) (compare H2563 (חֹמֶר)); KJV: heap.

H2566 חַמְרָן (Chamrân, kham-rawn'): Chamran, an Idumaean. Origin: from H2560 (חָמַר); red; KJV: Amran.

H2567 חָמַשׁ (châmash, khaw-mash'): to tax a fifth. Origin: a denominative from H2568 (חָמֵשׁ); KJV: take up the fifth participle

H2568 חָמֵשׁ (châmêsh, khaw-maysh'): five. Origin: masculine חֲמִשָּׁה; a primitive numeral; KJV: fif(-teen), fifth, five ([idiom] apiece).

H2569 חֹמֶשׁ (chômesh, kho'-mesh): a fifth tax. Origin: from H2567 (חָמַשׁ); KJV: fifth participle

H2570 חֹמֶשׁ (chômesh, kho'-mesh): the abdomen (as obese). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning, to be stout; KJV: fifth (rib).

H2571 חָמֻשׁ (châmush, khaw-moosh'): staunch, i.e. able-bodied soldiers. Origin: passive participle of the same as H2570 (חֹמֶשׁ); KJV: armed (men), harnessed.

H2572 חֲמִשִּׁים (chămishshîym, kham-ish-sheem'): fifty. Origin: multiple of H2568 (חָמֵשׁ); KJV: fifty.

H2573 חֵמֶת (chêmeth, klay'-meth): a skin bottle (as tied up). Origin: from the same as H2346 (חוֹמָה); KJV: bottle.

H2574 חֲמָת (Chămâth, kham-awth'): Chamath, a place in Syria. Origin: from the same as H2346 (חוֹמָה); walled; KJV: Hamath, Hemath.

H2575 חַמַּת (Chammath, klam-math'): Chammath, a place in Palestine. Origin: a variation for the first part of H2576 (חַמֹּת דֹּאר); hot springs; KJV: Hammath.

H2576 חַמֹּת דֹּאר (Chammôth Dôʼr, kham-moth' dore): Chammath-Dor, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the plural of H2535 (חַמָּה) and H1756 (דּוֹר); hot springs of Dor; KJV: Hamath-Dor.

H2577 חֲמָתִי (Chămâthîy, kham-aw-thee'): a Chamathite or native of Chamath. Origin: patrial from H2574 (חֲמָת); KJV: Hamathite.

H2578 חֲמַת צוֹבָה (Chămath Tsôwbâh, kham-ath' tso-baw'): Chamath-Tsobah. Origin: from H2574 (חֲמָת) and H6678 (צוֹבָא); Chamath of Tsobah; probably the same as H2574 (חֲמָת) KJV: Hamath-Zobah.

H2579 חֲמַת רַבָּה (Chămath Rabbâh, kham-ath' rab-baw'): Chamath-Rabbah. Origin: from H2574 (חֲמָת) and H7237 (רַבָּה); Chamath of Rabbah; probably the same as H2574 (חֲמָת).

H2580 חֵן (chên, khane): graciousness, i.e. subjective (kindness, favor) or objective (beauty). Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); KJV: favour, grace(-ious), pleasant, precious, (well-) favoured.

H2581 חֵן (Chên, khane): Chen, a figurative name for an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2580 (חֵן); grace; KJV: Hen.

H2582 חֵנָדָד (Chênâdâd, khay-naw-dawd'): Chenadad, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H2580 (חֵן) and H1908 (הֲדַד); favor of Hadad; KJV: Henadad.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2583 to H2704
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2583 חָנָה (chânâh, khaw-naw'): properly, to incline; by implication, to decline (of the slanting rays of evening); specifically, to pitch atent; gen. to encamp (for abode or siege). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2603 (חָנַן)); KJV: abide (in tents), camp, dwell, encamp, grow to an end, lie, pitch (tent), rest in tent.

H2584 חַנָּה (Channâh, khan-naw'): Channah, an Israelitess. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); favored; KJV: Hannah.

H2585 חֲנוֹךְ (Chănôwk, khan-oke'): Chanok, an antediluvian patriach. Origin: from H2596 (חָנַךְ); initiated; KJV: Enoch.

H2586 חָנוּן (Chânûwn, khaw-noon'): Chanun, the name of an Ammonite and of two Israelites. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); favored; KJV: Hanun.

H2587 חַנּוּן (channûwn, khan-noon'): gracious. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); KJV: gracious.

H2588 חָנוּת (chânûwth, khaw-nooth'): properly, a vault or cell (with an arch); by implication, a prison. Origin: from H2583 (חָנָה); KJV: cabin.

H2589 חַנּוֹת (channôwth, klan-noth'): supplication. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן) (in the sense of prayer); KJV: be gracious, intreated.

H2590 חָנַט (chânaṭ, khaw-nat'): to spice; by implication, to embalm; also to ripen. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: embalm, put forth.

H2591 חִנְטָא (chinṭâʼ, khint-taw'): wheat. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2406 (חִטָּה); KJV: wheat.

H2592 חַנִּיאֵל (Channîyʼêl, khan-nee-ale'): Channiel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן) and H410 (אֵל); favor of God; KJV: Hanniel.

H2593 חָנִיךְ (chânîyk, kaw-neek'): initiated; i.e. practiced. Origin: from H2596 (חָנַךְ); KJV: trained.

H2594 חֲנִינָה (chănîynâh, khan-ee-naw'): graciousness. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); KJV: favour.

H2595 חֲנִית (chănîyth, khan-eeth'): a lance (for thrusting, like pitching a tent). Origin: from H2583 (חָנָה); KJV: javelin, spear.

H2596 חָנַךְ (chânak, khaw-nak'): properly, to narrow; figuratively, to initiate or discipline. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H2614 (חָנַק)) KJV: dedicate, train up.

H2597 חֲנֻכָּא (chănukkâʼ, chan-ook-kaw'): consecration. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2598 (חֲנֻכָּה); KJV: dedication.

H2598 חֲנֻכָּה (chănukkâh, khan-ook-kaw'): initiation, i.e. consecration. Origin: from H2596 (חָנַךְ); KJV: dedicating(-tion).

H2599 חֲנֹכִי (Chănôkîy, khan-o-kee'): a Chanokite (collectively) or descendants of Chanok. Origin: patronymically from H2585 (חֲנוֹךְ); KJV: Hanochites.

H2600 חִנָּם (chinnâm, khin-nawm'): gratis, i.e. devoid of cost, reason or advantage. Origin: from H2580 (חֵן); KJV: without a cause (cost, wages), causeless, to cost nothing, free(-ly), innocent, for nothing (nought, in vain.

H2601 חֲנַמְאֵל (Chănamʼêl, khan-am-ale'): Chanamel, an Israelite. Origin: probably by orthographical variation for H2606 (חֲנַנְאֵל); KJV: Hanameel.

H2602 חֲנָמָל (chănâmâl, khan-aw-mawl'): perhaps the aphis or plantlouse. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: frost.

H2603 חָנַן (chânan, khaw-nan'): properly, to bend or stoop in kindness to an inferior; to favor, bestow; causatively to implore (i.e. move to favor by petition). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2583 (חָנָה)); KJV: beseech, [idiom] fair, (be, find, shew) favour(-able), be (deal, give, grant (gracious(-ly), intreat, (be) merciful, have (shew) mercy (on, upon), have pity upon, pray, make supplication, [idiom] very.

H2604 חֲנַן (chănan, khan-an'): to favor or (causatively) to entreat. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2603 (חָנַן); KJV: shew mercy, make supplication.

H2605 חָנָן (Chânân, khaw-nawn'): Chanan, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); favor; KJV: Canan.

H2606 חֲנַנְאֵל (Chănanʼêl, khan-an-ale'): Chananel, probably an Israelite, from whom a tower of Jerusalem was named. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן) and H410 (אֵל); God has favored; KJV: Hananeel.

H2607 חֲנָנִי (Chănânîy, khan-aw-nee'): Chanani, the name of six Israelites. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); gracious; KJV: Hanani.

H2608 חֲנַנְיָה (Chănanyâh, khan-an-yaw'): Chananjah, the name of thirteen Israelites. Origin: or חֲנַנְיָהוּ; from H2603 (חָנַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has favored; KJV: Hananiah.

H2609 חָנֵס (Chânêç, khaw-nace'): Chanes, a place in Egypt. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Hanes.

H2610 חָנֵף (chânêph, khaw-nafe'): to soil, especially in a moral sense. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: corrupt, defile, [idiom] greatly, pollute, profane.

H2611 חָנֵף (chânêph, khaw-nafe'): soiled (i.e. with sin), impious. Origin: from H2610 (חָנֵף); KJV: hypocrite(-ical).

H2612 חֹנֶף (chôneph, kho'-nef): moral filth, i.e. wickedness. Origin: from H2610 (חָנֵף); KJV: hypocrisy.

H2613 חֲנֻפָה (chănuphâh, khan-oo-faw'): impiety. Origin: feminine from H2610 (חָנֵף); KJV: profaneness.

H2614 חָנַק (chânaq, khaw-nak'): to be narrow; by implication, to throttle, or (reflex.) to choke oneself to death (by a rope). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2596 (חָנַךְ)); KJV: hang self, strangle.

H2615 חַנָּתֹן (Channâthôn, khan-naw-thone'): Channathon, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H2603 (חָנַן); favored; KJV: Hannathon.

H2616 חָסַד (châçad, khaw-sad'): properly, perhaps to bow (the neck only in courtesy to an equal), i.e. to be kind; also (by euphemistically, but rarely) to reprove. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H2603 (חָנַן)); (compare H1288 (בָרַךְ)) KJV: shew self merciful, put to shame.

H2617 חֵסֵד (chêçêd, kheh'-sed): kindness; by implication (towards God) piety; rarely (by opposition) reproof, or (subject.) beauty. Origin: from H2616 (חָסַד); KJV: favour, good deed(-liness, -ness), kindly, (loving-) kindness, merciful (kindness), mercy, pity, reproach, wicked thing.

H2618 חֶסֶד (Cheçed, kheh'-sed): Chesed, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2617 (חֵסֵד); favor; KJV: Hesed.

H2619 חֲסַדְיָה (Chăçadyâh, khas-ad-yaw'): Chasadjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2617 (חֵסֵד) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has favored; KJV: Hasadiah.

H2620 חָסָה (châçâh, khaw-saw'): to flee for protection; figuratively, to confide in. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H982 (בָּטַח)) KJV: have hope, make refuge, (put) trust.

H2621 חֹסָה (Chôçâh, kho-saw'): Chosah, an Israelite; also a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2620 (חָסָה); hopeful; KJV: Hosah.

H2622 חָסוּת (châçûwth, khaw-sooth'): confidence. Origin: from H2620 (חָסָה); KJV: trust.

H2623 חָסִיד (châçîyd, khaw-seed'): properly, kind, i.e. (religiously) pious (a saint). Origin: from H2616 (חָסַד); KJV: godly (man), good, holy (one), merciful, saint, (un-) godly.

H2624 חֲסִידָה (chăçîydâh, khas-ee-daw'): the kind (maternal) bird, i.e. a stork. Origin: feminine of H2623 (חָסִיד); KJV: [idiom] feather, stork.

H2625 חָסִיל (châçîyl, khaw-seel'): the ravager, i.e. a locust. Origin: from H2628 (חָסַל); KJV: caterpillar.

H2626 חֲסִין (chăçîyn, khas-een'): properly, firm, i.e. (by implication) mighty. Origin: from H2630 (חָסַן); KJV: strong.

H2627 חַסִּיר (chaççîyr, khas-seer'): deficient. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2637 (חָסֵר); KJV: wanting.

H2628 חָסַל (châçal, khaw-sal'): to eat off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consume.

H2629 חָסַם (châçam, khaw-sam'): to muzzle; by analogy, to stop the nose. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: muzzle, stop.

H2630 חָסַן (châçan, khaw-san'): properly, to (be) compact; by implication, to hoard. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lay up.

H2631 חֲסַן (chăçan, khas-an'): to hold in occupancy. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2630 (חָסַן); KJV: possess.

H2632 חֵסֶן (chêçen, khay'-sen): strength. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2631 (חֲסַן); KJV: power.

H2633 חֹסֶן (chôçen, kho'-sen): wealth. Origin: from H2630 (חָסַן); KJV: riches, strength, treasure.

H2634 חָסֹן (châçôn, khaw-sone'): powerful. Origin: from H2630 (חָסַן); KJV: strong.

H2635 חֲסַף (chăçaph, khas-af'): a clod. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of H2636 (חַסְפַּס); KJV: clay.

H2636 חַסְפַּס (chaçpaç, khas-pas'): a shred or scale. Origin: reduplicated from an unused root meaning apparently to peel; KJV: round thing.

H2637 חָסֵר (châçêr, khaw-sare'): to lack; by implication, to fail, want, lessen. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be abated, bereave, decrease, (cause to) fail, (have) lack, make lower, want.

H2638 חָסֵר (châçêr, khaw-sare'): lacking; hence, without. Origin: from H2637 (חָסֵר); KJV: destitute, fail, lack, have need, void, want.

H2639 חֶסֶר (cheçer, kheh'-ler): lack; hence, destitution. Origin: from H2637 (חָסֵר); KJV: poverty, want.

H2640 חֹסֶר (chôçer, kho'-ser): poverty. Origin: from H2637 (חָסֵר); KJV: in want of.

H2641 חַסְרָה (Chaçrâh, khas-raw'): Chasrah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2637 (חָסֵר); want KJV: Hasrah.

H2642 חֶסְרוֹן (cheçrôwn, khes-rone'): deficiency. Origin: from H2637 (חָסֵר); KJV: wanting.

H2643 חַף (chaph, khaf): pure. Origin: from H2653 (חׇפַף) (in the moral sense of covered from soil); KJV: innocent.

H2644 חָפָא (châphâʼ, khaw-faw'): properly, to cover, i.e. (in a sinister sense) to act covertly. Origin: an orthographical variation of H2645 (חָפָה); KJV: do secretly.

H2645 חָפָה (châphâh, khaw-faw'): to cover; by implication, to veil, to encase, protect. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2644 (חָפָא), H2653 (חׇפַף)); KJV: ceil, cover, overlay.

H2646 חֻפָּה (chuppâh, khoop-paw'): a canopy. Origin: from H2645 (חָפָה); KJV: chamber, closet, defence.

H2647 חֻפָּה (Chuppâh, khoop-paw'): Chuppah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2646 (חֻפָּה); KJV: Huppah.

H2648 חָפַז (châphaz, khaw-faz'): properly, to start up suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to hasten away, to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) haste (away), tremble.

H2649 חִפָּזוֹן (chippâzôwn, khip-paw-zone'): hasty flight. Origin: from H2468 (חֻלְדָּה); KJV: haste.

H2650 חֻפִּים (Chuppîym, khoop-peem'): Chuppim, an Israelite. Origin: plural of H2646 (חֻפָּה) (compare H2349 (חוּפָם)); KJV: Huppim.

H2651 חֹפֶן (chôphen, kho'-fen): a fist (only in the dual). Origin: from an unused root of uncertain signification; KJV: fists, (both) hands, hand(-ful).

H2652 חׇפְנִי (Chophnîy, khof-nee'): Chophni, an Israelite. Origin: from H2651 (חֹפֶן); perhaps pugilist; KJV: Hophni.

H2653 חׇפַף (chophaph, khaw-faf'): to cover (in protection). Origin: a primitive root (compare H2645 (חָפָה), H3182 (יָחֵף)); KJV: cover.

H2654 חָפֵץ (châphêts, khaw-fates'): properly, to incline to; by implication (literally but rarely) to bend; figuratively, to be pleased with, desire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] any at all, (have, take) delight, desire, favour, like, move, be (well) pleased, have pleasure, will, would.

H2655 חָפֵץ (châphêts, khaw-fates'): pleased with. Origin: from H2654 (חָפֵץ); KJV: delight in, desire, favour, please, have pleasure, whosoever would, willing, wish.

H2656 חֵפֶץ (chêphets, khay'-fets): pleasure; hence (abstractly) desire; concretely, a valuable thing; hence (by extension) a matter (as something in mind). Origin: from H2654 (חָפֵץ); KJV: acceptable, delight(-some), desire, things desired, matter, pleasant(-ure), purpose, willingly.

H2657 חֶפְצִי בָּהּ (Chephtsîy bâhh, khef-tsee'baw): Cheptsi-bah, a fanciful name for Palestine. Origin: from H2656 (חֵפֶץ) with suffixes; my delight (is) in her; KJV: Hephzi-bah.

H2658 חָפַר (châphar, khaw-far'): properly, to pry into; by implication, to delve, to explore. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dig, paw, search out, seek.

H2659 חָפֵר (châphêr, khaw-fare'): to blush; figuratively, to be ashamed, disappointed; causatively, to shame, reproach. Origin: a primitive root (perhaps rather the same as H2658 (חָפַר) through the idea of detection); KJV: be ashamed, be confounded, be brought to confusion (unto shame), come (be put to) shame, bring reproach.

H2660 חֵפֶר (Chêpher, khay'-fer): Chepher, a place in Palestine; also the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H2658 (חָפַר) or H2659 (חָפֵר); a pit of shame; KJV: Hepher.

H2661 חֲפֹר (chăphôr, khaf-ore'): a burrower, i.e. probably a rat. Origin: from H2658 (חָפַר); a hole; only in connection with H6512 (פֵּרָה), which ought rather to be joined as one word, thus חַפַרְפֵּרָה; by reduplication from H2658 (חָפַר); KJV: [phrase] mole.

H2662 חֶפְרִי (Chephrîy, khef-ree'): a Chephrite (collectively) or descendants of Chepher. Origin: patronymically from H2660 (חֵפֶר); KJV: Hepherites.

H2663 חֲפָרַיִם (Chăphârayim, khaf-aw-rah'-yim): Chapharajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of H2660 (חֵפֶר); double pit; KJV: Haphraim.

H2664 חָפַשׂ (châphas, khaw-fas'): to seek; causatively, to conceal oneself (i.e. let be sought), or mask. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: change, (make) diligent (search), disquise self, hide, search (for, out).

H2665 חֵפֶשׂ (chêphes, khay'-fes): something covert, i.e. a trick. Origin: from H2664 (חָפַשׂ); KJV: search.

H2666 חָפַשׁ (châphash, khaw-fash'): to spread loose; figuratively, to manumit. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be free.

H2667 חֹפֶשׁ (Chôphesh, kho'-fesh): something spread loosely, i.e. a carpet. Origin: from H2666 (חָפַשׁ); KJV: precious.

H2668 חֻפְשָׁה (chuphshâh, khoof-shaw'): liberty (from slavery). Origin: from H2666 (חָפַשׁ); KJV: freedom.

H2669 חׇפְשׁוּת (chophshûwth, khof-shooth'): prostration by sickness. Origin: and חׇפְשִׁית; from H2666 (חָפַשׁ); (with H1004 (בַּיִת), a hospital) KJV: several.

H2670 חׇפְשִׁי (chophshîy, khof-shee'): exempt (from bondage, tax or care). Origin: from H2666 (חָפַשׁ); KJV: free, liberty.

H2671 חֵץ (chêts, khayts): properly, a piercer, i.e. an arrow; by implication, a wound; figuratively, (of God) thunderbolt; the shaft of aspear. Origin: from H2686 (חָצַץ); also by interchange for H6086 (עֵץ) KJV: [phrase] archer, arrow, dart, shaft, staff, wound.

H2672 חָצַב (châtsab, khaw-tsab'): to cut or carve (wood, stone or other material); by implication, to hew, split, square, quarry, engrave. Origin: or חָצֵב; a primitive root; KJV: cut, dig, divide, grave, hew (out, -er), made, mason.

H2673 חָצָה (châtsâh, khaw-tsaw'): to cut or split in two; to halve. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2086 (זֵד))); KJV: divide, [idiom] live out half, reach to the midst, participle

H2674 חָצוֹר (Châtsôwr, khaw-tsore'): Chatsor, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine and of one in Arabia. Origin: a collective form of H2691 (חָצֵר); village; KJV: Hazor.

H2675 חָצוֹר חֲדַתָּה (Châtsôwr Chădattâh, khaw-tsore' khad-attaw'): new Chatsor, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2674 (חָצוֹר) and a Aramaizing form of the feminine of H2319 (חָדָשׁ) (compare H2323 (חֲדָת)); KJV: Hazor, Hadattah (as if two places).

H2676 חָצוֹת (châtsôwth, khaw-tsoth'): the middle (of the night). Origin: from H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; KJV: mid(-night).

H2677 חֵצִי (chêtsîy, khay-tsee'): the half or middle. Origin: from H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; KJV: half, middle, mid(-night), midst, part, two parts.

H2678 חִצִּי (chitstsîy, khits-tsee'): an arrow. Origin: or חֵצִי; prolongation from H2671 (חֵץ); KJV: arrow.

H2679 חֲצִי הַמְּנֻחוֹת (Chătsîy ham-Mᵉnuchôwth, chat-tsee' hammen-oo-khoth'): Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth, an Israelite. Origin: from H2677 (חֵצִי) and the plural of H4496 (מְנוּחָה), with the article interposed; midst of the resting-places; KJV: half of the Manahethites.

H2680 חֲצִי הַמְּנַחְתִּי (Chătsîy ham-Mᵉnachtîy, khat-see' ham-menakh-tee'): a Chatsi-ham-Menachtite or descendant of Chatsi-ham-Menuchoth. Origin: patronymically from H2679 (חֲצִי הַמְּנֻחוֹת); KJV: half of the Manahethites.

H2681 חָצִיר (châtsîyr, khaw-tseer'): a court or abode. Origin: a collateral form of H2691 (חָצֵר); KJV: court.

H2682 חָצִיר (châtsîyr, khaw-tseer'): grass; also a leek (collectively). Origin: perhaps originally the same as H2681 (חָצִיר), from the greenness of a courtyard; KJV: grass, hay, herb, leek.

H2683 חֵצֶן (chêtsen, khay'-tsen): the bosom (as comprised between the arms). Origin: from an unused root meaning to hold firmly; KJV: bosom.

H2684 חֹצֶן (chôtsen, kho'tsen): {the bosom (as comprised between the arms)}. Origin: a collateral form of H2683 (חֵצֶן), and meaning the same KJV: arm, lap.

H2685 חֲצַף (chătsaph, khats-af'): properly, to shear or cut close; figuratively, to be severe. Origin: (Aramaic) a primitive root; KJV: hasty, be urgent.

H2686 חָצַץ (châtsats, khaw-tsats'): properly, to chop into, pierce or sever; hence, to curtail, to distribute (into ranks); to shoot an arrow. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה); also as denominative from H2671 (חֵץ) KJV: archer, [idiom] bands, cut off in the midst.

H2687 חָצָץ (châtsâts, khaw-tsawts'): properly, something cutting; hence, gravel (as grit); an arrow. Origin: from H2687 (חָצָץ); also like H2671 (חֵץ) KJV: arrow, gravel (stone).

H2688 חַצְצוֹן תָּמָר (Chatsᵉtsôwn Tâmâr, khats-ets-one' taw-mawr'): Chatsetson-tamar, a place in Palestine. Origin: or חַצֲצֹן תָּמָר; from H2686 (חָצַץ) and H8558 (תָּמָר); division (i.e. perhaps row) of (the) palm-tree; KJV: Hazezon-tamar.

H2689 חֲצֹצְרָה (chătsôtsᵉrâh, khats-o-tser-aw'): a trumpet (from its sundered or quavering note). Origin: by reduplication from H2690 (חָצַר); KJV: trumpet(-er).

H2690 חָצַר (châtsar, khaw-tsar'): to trumpet, i.e. blow on that instrument. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to surround with a stockade, and thus separate from the open country; but used only in the reduplicated form חֲצֹצֵר; or (2 Chronicles 5:12) חֲצֹרֵר; as dem. from H2689 (חֲצֹצְרָה); KJV: blow, sound, trumpeter.

H2691 חָצֵר (châtsêr, khaw-tsare'): a yard (as inclosed by a fence); also a hamlet (as similarly surrounded with walls). Origin: (masculine and feminine); from H2690 (חָצַר) in its original sense; KJV: court, tower, village.

H2692 חֲצַר אַדָּר (Chătsar ʼAddâr, khats-ar' addawr'): Chatsar-Addar, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and H146 (אַדָּר); (the) village of Addar; KJV: Hazar-addar.

H2693 חֲצַר גַּדָּה (Chătsar Gaddâh, khats-ar' gad-daw'): Chatsar-Gaddah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and a feminine of H1408 (גַּד); (the) village of (female) Fortune; KJV: Hazar-gaddah.

H2694 חֲצַר הַתִּיכוֹן (Chătsar hat-Tîykôwn, khats-ar' hat-tee-kone'): Chatsar-hat-Tikon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and H8484 (תִּיכוֹן) with the article interposed; village of the middle; KJV: Hazar-hatticon.

H2695 חֶצְרוֹ (Chetsrôw, khets-ro'): Chetsro, an Israelite. Origin: by an orthographical variation for H2696 (חֶצְרוֹן); enclosure; KJV: Hezro, Hezrai.

H2696 חֶצְרוֹן (Chetsrôwn, khets-rone'): Chetsron, the name of a place in Palestine; also of two Israelites. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר); court-yard; KJV: Hezron.

H2697 חֶצְרוֹנִי (Chetsrôwnîy, khets-ro-nee'): a Chetsronite or (collectively) descendants of Chetsron. Origin: patronymically from H2696 (חֶצְרוֹן); KJV: Hezronites.

H2698 חֲצֵרוֹת (Chătsêrôwth, khats-ay-roth'): Chatseroth, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine plural of H2691 (חָצֵר); yards; KJV: Hazeroth.

H2699 חֲצֵרִים (Chătsêrîym, khats-ay-reem'): Chatserim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural masculine of H2691 (חָצֵר); yards; KJV: Hazerim.

H2700 חֲצַרְמָוֶת (Chătsarmâveth, khats-ar-maw'-veth): Chatsarmaveth, a place in Arabia. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and H4194 (מָוֶת); village of death; KJV: Hazarmaveth.

H2701 חֲצַר סוּסָה (Chătsar Çûwçâh, khats-ar'soo-saw'): Chatsar-Susah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and H5484 (סוּסָה); village of cavalry; KJV: Hazar-susah.

H2702 חֲצַר סוּסִים (Chătsar Çûwçîym, khats-ar' soo-seem'): Chatsar-Susim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and the plural of H5483 (סוּס); village of horses; KJV: Hazar-susim.

H2703 חֲצַר עֵינוֹן (Chătsar ʻÊynôwn, khats-ar' ay-none'): Chatsar-Enon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and a derivative of H5869 (עַיִן); village of springs; KJV: Hazar-enon.

H2704 חֲצַר עֵינָן (Chătsar ʻÊynân, khats-ar' ay-nawn'): Chatsar-Enan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and the same as H5881 (עֵינָן); village of springs; KJV: Hazar-enan.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2705 to H2821
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2705 חֲצַר שׁוּעָל (Chătsar Shûwʻâl, khats-ar' shoo-awl'): Chatsar-Shual, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2691 (חָצֵר) and H7776 (שׁוּעָל); village of (the) fox; KJV: Hazar-shual.

H2706 חֹק (chôq, khoke): an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage). Origin: from H2710 (חָקַק); KJV: appointed, bound, commandment, convenient, custom, decree(-d), due, law, measure, [idiom] necessary, ordinance(-nary), portion, set time, statute, task.

H2707 חָקָה (châqâh, khaw-kaw'): to carve; by implication, to delineate; also to entrench. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: carved work, portrayed, set a print.

H2708 חֻקָּה (chuqqâh, khook-kaw'): {an enactment; hence, an appointment (of time, space, quantity, labor or usage)}. Origin: feminine of H2706 (חֹק), and meaning substantially the same KJV: appointed, custom, manner, ordinance, site, statute.

H2709 חֲקוּפָא (Chăqûwphâʼ, khah-oo-faw'): Chakupha, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to bend; crooked; KJV: Hakupha.

H2710 חָקַק (châqaq, khaw-kak'): properly, to hack, i.e. engrave (Judges 5:14, to be a scribe simply); by implication, to enact (laws being cut in stone or metal tablets in primitive times) or (gen.) prescribe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, decree, governor, grave, lawgiver, note, pourtray, print, set.

H2711 חֵקֶק (chêqeq, khay'-kek): an enactment, a resolution. Origin: from H2710 (חָקַק); KJV: decree, thought.

H2712 חֻקֹּק (Chuqqôq, Khook-koke'): Chukkok or Chukok, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (fully) חוּקֹק; from H2710 (חָקַק); appointed; KJV: Hukkok, Hukok.

H2713 חָקַר (châqar, khaw-kar'): properly, to penetrate; hence, to examine intimately. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: find out, (make) search (out), seek (out), sound, try.

H2714 חֵקֶר (chêqer, khay'-ker): examination, enumeration, deliberation. Origin: from H2713 (חָקַר); KJV: finding out, number, (un-) search(-able, -ed, out, -ing).

H2715 חֹר (chôr, khore): properly, white or pure (from the cleansing or shining power of fire; hence (figuratively) noble (in rank). Origin: or (fully) חוֹר; from H2787 (חָרַר); (compare H2751 (חֹרִי)) KJV: noble.

H2716 חֶרֶא (chereʼ, kheh'-reh): excrement. Origin: from an unused (and vulgar) root probably meaning to evacuate the bowels; KJV: dung. Also חֲרִי.

H2717 חָרַב (chârab, khaw-rab'): to parch (through drought) i.e. (by analogy,) to desolate, destroy, kill. Origin: or חֲרֵב; a primitive root; KJV: decay, (be) desolate, destroy(-er), (be) dry (up), slay, [idiom] surely, (lay, lie, make) waste.

H2718 חֲרַב (chărab, khar-ab'): to demolish. Origin: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to H2717 (חָרַב); KJV: destroy.

H2719 חֶרֶב (chereb, kheh'-reb): drought; also a cutting instrument (from its destructive effect), as a knife, sword, or other sharp implement. Origin: from H2717 (חָרַב); KJV: axe, dagger, knife, mattock, sword, tool.

H2720 חָרֵב (chârêb, khaw-rabe'): parched or ruined. Origin: from H2717 (חָרַב); KJV: desolate, dry, waste.

H2721 חֹרֶב (chôreb, kho'-reb): drought or desolation. Origin: a collaterally form of H2719 (חֶרֶב); KJV: desolation, drought, dry, heat, [idiom] utterly, waste.

H2722 חֹרֵב (Chôrêb, kho-rabe'): Choreb, a (generic) name for the Sinaitic mountains. Origin: from H2717 (חָרַב); desolate; KJV: Horeb.

H2723 חׇרְבָּה (chorbâh, khor-baw'): properly, drought, i.e. (by implication) a desolation. Origin: feminine of H2721 (חֹרֶב); KJV: decayed place, desolate (place, -tion), destruction, (laid) waste (place).

H2724 חָרָבָה (chârâbâh, khaw-raw-baw'): a desert. Origin: feminine of H2720 (חָרֵב); KJV: dry (ground, land).

H2725 חֲרָבוֹן (chărâbôwn, khar-aw-bone'): parching heat. Origin: from H2717 (חָרַב); KJV: drought.

H2726 חַרְבוֹנָא (Charbôwnâʼ, khar-bo-naw'): Charbona or Charbonah, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: or חַרְבוֹנָה; of Persian origin; KJV: Harbona, Harbonah.

H2727 חָרַג (chârag, khaw-rag'): properly, to leap suddenly, i.e. (by implication) to be dismayed. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be afraid.

H2728 חָרְגֹּל (chârᵉgôl, khar-gole'): the leaping insect, i.e. a locust. Origin: from H2727 (חָרַג); KJV: beetle.

H2729 חָרַד (chârad, khaw-rad'): to shudder with terror; hence, to fear; also to hasten (with anxiety). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (make) afraid, be careful, discomfit, fray (away), quake, tremble.

H2730 חָרֵד (chârêd, khaw-rade'): fearful; also reverential. Origin: from H2729 (חָרַד); KJV: afraid, trembling.

H2731 חֲרָדָה (chărâdâh, khar-aw-daw'): fear, anxiety. Origin: feminine of H2730 (חָרֵד); KJV: care, [idiom] exceedingly, fear, quaking, trembling.

H2732 חֲרָדָה (Chărâdâh, khar-aw-daw'): Charadah, a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H2731 (חֲרָדָה); KJV: Haradah.

H2733 חֲרֹדִי (Chărôdîy, khar-o-dee'): a Charodite, or inhabitant of Charod. Origin: patrial from a derivative of H2729 (חָרַד) (compare H5878 (עֵין חֲרֹד)); KJV: Harodite.

H2734 חָרָה (chârâh, khaw-raw'): to glow or grow warm; figuratively (usually) to blaze up, of anger, zeal, jealousy. Origin: a primitive root (compare H2787 (חָרַר)); KJV: be angry, burn, be displeased, [idiom] earnestly, fret self, grieve, be (wax) hot, be incensed, kindle, [idiom] very, be wroth. See H8474 (תַּחָרָה).

H2735 חֹר הַגִּדְגָּד (Chôr hag-Gidgâd, khore hag-ghid-gawd'): Chor-hag-Gidgad, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H2356 (חוֹר) and a collateral (masculine) form of H1412 (גֻּדְגֹּדָה), with the article interposed; hole of the cleft; KJV: Hor-hagidgad.

H2736 חַרְהֲיָה (Charhăyâh, khar-hah-yaw'): Charhajah, an Israelite. Origin: ; from H2734 (חָרָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); fearing Jah; KJV: Harhaiah.

H2737 חָרוּז (chârûwz, khaw-rooz'): properly, pierced, i.e. a bead of pearl, gems or jewels (as strung). Origin: from an unused root meaning to perforate; KJV: chain.

H2738 חָרוּל (chârûwl, khaw-rool'): properly, pointed, i.e. a bramble or other thorny weed. Origin: or (shortened) חָרֻל; apparently, a passive participle of an unused root probably meaning to be prickly; KJV: nettle.

H2739 חֲרוּמַף (chărûwmaph, khar-oo-maf'): Charumaph, an Israelite. Origin: from passive participle of H2763 (חָרַם) and H639 (אַף); snub-nosed; KJV: Harumaph.

H2740 חָרוֹן (chârôwn, khaw-rone'): a burning of anger. Origin: or (shortened) חָרֹן; from H2734 (חָרָה); KJV: sore displeasure, fierce(-ness), fury, (fierce) wrath(-ful).

H2741 חֲרוּפִי (Chărûwphîy, khar-oo-fee'): a Charuphite or inhabitant of Charuph (or Chariph). Origin: a patrial from (probably) a collateral form of H2756 (חָרִיף); KJV: Haruphite.

H2742 חֲרוּץ (chărûwts, khaw-roots'): properly, incised or (active) incisive; hence (as noun masculine or feminine) a trench (as dug), gold (as mined), a threshing-sledge (having sharp teeth); (figuratively) determination; also eager. Origin: or חָרֻץ; passive participle of H2782 (חָרַץ); KJV: decision, diligent, (fine) gold, pointed things, sharp, threshing instrument, wall.

H2743 חָרוּץ (Chârûwts, khaw-roots'): Charuts, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2742 (חֲרוּץ); earnest; KJV: Haruz.

H2744 חַרְחוּר (Charchûwr, khar-khoor'): Charchur, one of the Nethinim. Origin: a fuller form of H2746 (חַרְחֻר); inflammation; KJV: Harhur.

H2745 חַרְחַס (Charchaç, khar-khas'): Charchas, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H2775 (חֶרֶס); perhaps shining; KJV: Harhas.

H2746 חַרְחֻר (charchur, khar-khoor'): fever (as hot). Origin: from H2787 (חָרַר); KJV: extreme burning.

H2747 חֶרֶט (chereṭ, kheh'-ret): a chisel or graver; also a style forwriting. Origin: from a primitive root meaning to engrave; KJV: graving tool, pen.

H2748 חַרְטֹם (charṭôm, khar-tome'): a horoscopist (as drawing magical lines or circles). Origin: from the same as H2747 (חֶרֶט); KJV: magician.

H2749 חַרְטֹם (charṭôm, khar-tome'): {a horoscopist (as drawing magical lines or circles)}. Origin: (Aramaic) the same as H2748 (חַרְטֹם) KJV: magician.

H2750 חֳרִי (chŏrîy, khor-ee'): a burning (i.e. intense) anger. Origin: from H2734 (חָרָה); KJV: fierce, [idiom] great, heat.

H2751 חֹרִי (chôrîy, kho-ree'): white bread. Origin: from the same as H2353 (חוּר); KJV: white.

H2752 חֹרִי (Chôrîy, kho-ree'): a Chorite or aboriginal Idumaean. Origin: from H2356 (חוֹר); cave-dweller or troglodyte; KJV: Horims, Horites.

H2753 חֹרִי (Chôrîy, kho-ree'): Chori, the name of two men. Origin: or חוֹרִי; the same as H2752 (חֹרִי); KJV: Hori.

H2754 חָרִיט (chârîyṭ, khaw-reet'): properly, cut out (or hollow), i.e. (by implication) a pocket. Origin: or חָרִט; from the same as H2747 (חֶרֶט); KJV: bag, crisping pin.

H2755 חֲרֵי־יוֹנִים (chărêy-yôwnîym, khar-ay'-yo-neem'): excrements of doves {or a vegetable}. Origin: from the plural of H2716 (חֶרֶא) and the plural of H3123 (יוֹנָה); or perhaps rather the plural of a single word חֲרָאיוֹן, probably a kind of vegetable KJV: doves' dung.

H2756 חָרִיף (Chârîyph, khaw-reef'): Chariph, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2778 (חָרַף); autumnal; KJV: Hariph.

H2757 חָרִיץ (chârîyts, khaw-reets'): properly, incisure or (passively) incised; hence, a threshing-sledge (with sharp teeth); also a slice (as cut). Origin: or חֲרִץ; from H2782 (חָרַץ); (compare H2742 (חֲרוּץ)) KJV: [phrase] cheese, harrow.

H2758 חָרִישׁ (chârîysh, khaw-reesh'): ploughing or its season. Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: earing (time), ground.

H2759 חֲרִישִׁי (chărîyshîy, khar-ee-shee'): quiet, i.e. sultry (as feminine noun, the sirocco or hot east wind). Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ) in the sense of silence; KJV: vehement.

H2760 חָרַךְ (chârak, khaw-rak'): to braid (i.e. to entangle or snare) or catch (game) in anet. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: roast.

H2761 חֲרַךְ (chărak, khar-ak'): to scorch. Origin: (Aramaic) a root probably allied to the equivalent of H2787 (חָרַר); KJV: singe.

H2762 חֶרֶךְ (cherek, kheh'-rek): properly, a net, i.e. (by analogy) lattice. Origin: from H2760 (חָרַךְ); KJV: lattice.

H2763 חָרַם (châram, khaw-ram'): to seclude; specifically (by a ban) to devote to religious uses (especially destruction); physical and reflexive, to be blunt as to the nose. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make accursed, consecrate, (utterly) destroy, devote, forfeit, have a flat nose, utterly (slay, make away).

H2764 חֵרֶם (chêrem, khay'-rem): physical (as shutting in) a net (either literally or figuratively); usually a doomed object; abstractly extermination. Origin: or (Zechariah 14:11) חֶרֶם; from H2763 (חָרַם); KJV: (ac-) curse(-d, -d thing), dedicated thing, things which should have been utterly destroyed, (appointed to) utter destruction, devoted (thing), net.

H2765 חֳרֵם (Chŏrêm, khor-ame'): Chorem, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2763 (חָרַם); devoted; KJV: Horem.

H2766 חָרִם (Chârim, khaw-reem'): Charim, an Israelite. Origin: from H2763 (חָרַם); snub-nosed; KJV: Harim.

H2767 חׇרְמָה (Chormâh, khor-maw'): Chormah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2763 (חָרַם); devoted; KJV: Hormah.

H2768 חֶרְמוֹן (Chermôwn, kher-mone'): Chermon, a mount of Palestine. Origin: from H2763 (חָרַם); abrupt; KJV: Hermon.

H2769 חֶרְמוֹנִים (Chermôwnîym, kher-mo-neem'): Hermons, i.e. its peaks. Origin: plural of H2768 (חֶרְמוֹן); KJV: the Hermonites.

H2770 חֶרְמֵשׁ (chermêsh, kher-mashe'): a sickle (as cutting). Origin: from H2763 (חָרַם); KJV: sickle.

H2771 חָרָן (Chârân, kaw-rawn'): Charan, the name of a man and also of a place. Origin: from H2787 (חָרַר); parched; KJV: Haran.

H2772 חֹרֹנִי (Chôrônîy, kho-ro-nee'): a Choronite or inhabitant of Choronaim. Origin: patrial from H2773 (חֹרֹנַיִם); KJV: Horonite.

H2773 חֹרֹנַיִם (Chôrônayim, kho-ro-nah'-yim): Choronajim, a place in Moab. Origin: dual of a derivative from H2356 (חוֹר); double cave-town; KJV: Horonaim.

H2774 חַרְנֶפֶר (Charnepher, khar-neh'fer): Charnepher, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Harnepher.

H2775 חֶרֶס (chereç, kheh'-res): the itch; the sun. Origin: or (with a directive enclitic) חַרְסָה; from an unused root meaning to scrape; also perhaps from the mediating idea of H2777 (חַרְסוּת) KJV: itch, sun.

H2776 חֶרֶס (Chereç, kheh'-res): Cheres, a mountain in Palestine. Origin: the same as H2775 (חֶרֶס); shining; KJV: Heres.

H2777 חַרְסוּת (charçûwth, khar-sooth'): a potsherd, i.e. (by implication) a pottery; the name of a gate at Jerusalem. Origin: from H2775 (חֶרֶס) (apparently in the sense of a red tile used for scraping); KJV: east.

H2778 חָרַף (châraph, khaw-raf'): to pull off, i.e. (by implication) to expose (as by stripping); specifically, to betroth (as if a surrender); figuratively, to carp at, i.e. defame; to spend the winter. Origin: a primitive root; also denominative (from H2779 (חֹרֶף)) KJV: betroth, blaspheme, defy, jeopard, rail, reproach, upbraid.

H2779 חֹרֶף (chôreph, kho'-ref): properly, the crop gathered, i.e. (by implication) the autumn (and winter) season; figuratively, ripeness of age. Origin: from H2778 (חָרַף); KJV: cold, winter (-house), youth.

H2780 חָרֵף (Chârêph, khaw-rafe'): Chareph, an Israelite. Origin: from H2778 (חָרַף); reproachful; KJV: Hareph.

H2781 חֶרְפָּה (cherpâh, kher-paw'): contumely, disgrace, the pudenda. Origin: from H2778 (חָרַף); KJV: rebuke, reproach(-fully), shame.

H2782 חָרַץ (chârats, khaw-rats'): properly, to point sharply, i.e. (literally) to wound; figuratively, to be alert, to decide. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bestir self, decide, decree, determine, maim, move.

H2783 חֲרַץ (chărats, khar-ats'): the loin (as the seat of strength). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2782 (חָרַץ) in the sense of vigor; KJV: loin.

H2784 חַרְצֻבָּה (chartsubbâh, khar-tsoob-baw'): a fetter; figuratively, a pain. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: band.

H2785 חַרְצַן (chartsan, kchar-tsan'): a sour grape (as sharp in taste). Origin: from H2782 (חָרַץ); KJV: kernel.

H2786 חָרַק (châraq, khaw-rak'): to grate the teeth. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gnash.

H2787 חָרַר (chârar, khaw-rar'): to glow, i.e. literally (to melt, burn, dry up) or figuratively (to show or incite passion). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be angry, burn, dry, kindle.

H2788 חָרֵר (chârêr, khaw-rare'): arid. Origin: from H2787 (חָרַר); KJV: parched place.

H2789 חֶרֶשׂ (cheres, kheh'-res): a piece of pottery. Origin: a collateral form mediating between H2775 (חֶרֶס) and H2791 (חֶרֶשׁ); KJV: earth(-en), (pot-) sherd, [phrase] stone.

H2790 חָרַשׁ (chârash, khaw-rash'): to scratch, i.e. (by implication) to engrave, plough; hence (from the use of tools) to fabricate (of any material); figuratively, to devise (in a bad sense); hence (from the idea of secrecy) to be silent, to let alone; hence (by implication) to be deaf (as an accompaniment of dumbness). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] altogether, cease, conceal, be deaf, devise, ear, graven, imagine, leave off speaking, hold peace, plow(-er, man), be quiet, rest, practise secretly, keep silence, be silent, speak not a word, be still, hold tongue, worker.

H2791 חֶרֶשׁ (cheresh, kheh'-resh): magical craft; also silence. Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: cunning, secretly.

H2792 חֶרֶשׁ (Cheresh, kheh'-resh): Cheresh, a Levite. Origin: the same as H2791 (חֶרֶשׁ) KJV: Heresh.

H2793 חֹרֶשׁ (chôresh, kho'-resh): a forest (perhaps as furnishing the material for fabric). Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: bough, forest, shroud, wood.

H2794 חֹרֵשׁ (chôrêsh, kho-rashe'): a fabricator or mechanic. Origin: active participle of H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: artificer.

H2795 חֵרֵשׁ (chêrêsh, khay-rashe'): deaf (whether literally or spiritual). Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: deaf.

H2796 חָרָשׁ (chârâsh, khaw-rawsh'): a fabricator or any material. Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: artificer, ([phrase]) carpenter, craftsman, engraver, maker, [phrase] mason, skilful, ([phrase]) smith, worker, workman, such as wrought.

H2797 חַרְשָׁא (Charshâʼ, khar-shaw'): Charsha, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from H2792 (חֶרֶשׁ); magician; KJV: Harsha.

H2798 חֲרָשִׁים (Chărâshîym, khar-aw-sheem'): mechanics, the name of a valley in Jerusalem. Origin: plural of H2796 (חָרָשׁ); KJV: Charashim, craftsmen.

H2799 חֲרֹשֶׁת (chărôsheth, khar-o'-sheth): mechanical work. Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: carving, cutting.

H2800 חֲרֹשֶׁת (Chărôsheth, khar-o'-sheth): Charosheth, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H2799 (חֲרֹשֶׁת); KJV: Harosheth.

H2801 חָרַת (chârath, khaw-rath'): to engrave. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: graven.

H2802 חֶרֶת (Chereth, kheh'-reth): Chereth, a thicket in Palestine. Origin: from H2801 (חָרַת) (but equivalent to H2793 (חֹרֶשׁ)); forest; KJV: Hereth.

H2803 חָשַׁב (châshab, khaw-shab'): properly, to plait or interpenetrate, i.e. (literally) to weave or (generally) to fabricate; figuratively, to plot or contrive (usually in a malicious sense); hence (from the mental effort) to think, regard, value, compute. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) account (of), conceive, consider, count, cunning (man, work, workman), devise, esteem, find out, forecast, hold, imagine, impute, invent, be like, mean, purpose, reckon(-ing be made), regard, think.

H2804 חֲשַׁב (chăshab, khash-ab'): to regard. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2803 (חָשַׁב); KJV: repute.

H2805 חֵשֶׁב (chêsheb, khay'-sheb): a belt or strap (as being interlaced). Origin: from H2803 (חָשַׁב); KJV: curious girdle.

H2806 חַשְׁבַּדָּנָה (Chashbaddânâh, khash-bad-daw'-naw): Chasbaddanah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2803 (חָשַׁב) and H1777 (דִּין); considerate judge; KJV: Hasbadana.

H2807 חֲשֻׁבָה (Chăshubâh, khash-oo-baw'): Cashubah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2803 (חָשַׁב); estimation; KJV: Hashubah.

H2808 חֶשְׁבּוֹן (cheshbôwn, khesh-bone'): properly, contrivance; by implication, intelligence. Origin: from H2803 (חָשַׁב); KJV: account, device, reason.

H2809 חֶשְׁבּוֹן (Cheshbôwn, khesh-bone'): Cheshbon, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: the same as H2808 (חֶשְׁבּוֹן); KJV: Heshbon.

H2810 חִשָּׁבוֹן (chishshâbôwn, khish-shaw-bone'): a contrivance, i.e. actual (a warlike machine) or mental (a machination). Origin: from H2803 (חָשַׁב); KJV: engine, invention.

H2811 חֲשַׁבְיָה (Chăshabyâh, khash-ab-yaw'): Chashabjah, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: or חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ; from H2803 (חָשַׁב) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has regarded; KJV: Hashabiah.

H2812 חֲשַׁבְנָה (Chăshabnâh, khash-ab-naw'): Chashnah, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H2808 (חֶשְׁבּוֹן); inventiveness; KJV: Hashabnah.

H2813 חֲשַׁבְנְיָה (Chăshabnᵉyâh, khash-ab-neh-yaw'): Chashabnejah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2808 (חֶשְׁבּוֹן) and H3050 (יָהּ); thought of Jah; KJV: Hashabniah.

H2814 חָשָׁה (châshâh, khaw-shaw'): to hush or keep quiet. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hold peace, keep silence, be silent, (be) still.

H2815 חַשּׁוּב (Chashshûwb, khash-shoob'): Chashshub, the name of two or three Israelites. Origin: from H2803 (חָשַׁב); intelligent; KJV: Hashub, Hasshub.

H2816 חֲשׁוֹךְ (chăshôwk, khash-oke'): the dark. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2821 (חָשַׁךְ); KJV: darkness.

H2817 חֲשׂוּפָא (Chăsûwphâʼ, khas-oo-faw'): Chasupha, one of the Nethinim. Origin: or חֲשֻׂפָא; from H2834 (חָשַׂף); nakedness; KJV: Hashupha, Hasupha.

H2818 חֲשַׁח (chăshach, khash-akh'): to be necessary (from the idea of convenience) or (transitively) to need. Origin: (Aramaic) a collateral root to one corresponding to H2363 (חוּשׁ) in the sense of readiness; KJV: careful, have need of.

H2819 חַשְׁחוּת (chashchûwth, khash-khooth'): necessity. Origin: from a root corresponding to H2818 (חֲשַׁח); KJV: be needful.

H2820 חָשַׂךְ (châsak, khaw-sak'): to restrain or (reflex.) refrain; by implication, to refuse, spare, preserve; to observe. Origin: a primitive root; also interchangeable with H2821 (חָשַׁךְ) KJV: assuage, [idiom] darken, forbear, hinder, hold back, keep (back), punish, refrain, reserve, spare, withhold.

H2821 חָשַׁךְ (châshak, khaw-shak'): to be dark (as withholding light); transitively, to darken. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be black, be (make) dark, darken, cause darkness, be dim, hide.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2822 to H2952
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2822 חֹשֶׁךְ (chôshek, kho-shek'): the dark; hence (literally) darkness; figuratively, misery, destruction, death, ignorance, sorrow, wickedness. Origin: from H2821 (חָשַׁךְ); KJV: dark(-ness), night, obscurity.

H2823 חָשֹׁךְ (châshôk, khaw-shoke'): dark (figuratively, i.e. obscure). Origin: from H2821 (חָשַׁךְ); KJV: meaning

H2824 חֶשְׁכָה (cheshkâh, khesh-kaw'): darkness. Origin: from H2821 (חָשַׁךְ); KJV: dark.

H2825 חֲשֵׁכָה (chăshêkâh, khash-ay-kaw'): darkness; figuratively, misery. Origin: or חֲשֵׁיכָהxlit chăshêkâh corrected to chăshêykâh; from H2821 (חָשַׁךְ); KJV: darkness.

H2826 חָשַׁל (châshal, khaw-shal'): to make (intrans. be) unsteady, i.e. weak. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: feeble.

H2827 חֲשַׁל (chăshal, khash-al'): to weaken, i.e. crush. Origin: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to H2826 (חָשַׁל); KJV: subdue.

H2828 חָשֻׁם (Châshum, khaw-shoom'): Chashum, the name of two or three Israelites. Origin: from the same as H2831 (חַשְׁמַן); enriched; KJV: Hashum.

H2829 חֶשְׁמוֹן (Cheshmôwn, klesh-mone'): Cheshmon, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H2831 (חַשְׁמַן); opulent; KJV: Heshmon.

H2830 חַשְׁמַל (chashmal, khash-mal'): probably bronze or polished spectrum metal. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: amber.

H2831 חַשְׁמַן (chashman, khash-man'): wealthy. Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning firm or capacious in resources); apparently KJV: princes.

H2832 חַשְׁמֹנָה (Chashmônâh, khash-mo-naw'): Chasmonah, a place in the Desert. Origin: feminine of H2831 (חַשְׁמַן); fertile; KJV: Hashmonah.

H2833 חֹשֶׁן (chôshen, kho'-shen): perhaps a pocket (as holding the Urim and Thummim), or rich (as containing gems), used only of the gorget of the highpriest. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to contain or sparkle; KJV: breastplate.

H2834 חָשַׂף (châsaph, khaw-saf'): to strip off, i.e. generally to make naked (for exertion or in disgrace), to drain away or bail up (a liquid). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make bare, clean, discover, draw out, take, uncover.

H2835 חָשִׂף (châsiph, khaw-seef'): properly, drawn off, i.e. separated; hence, a small company (as divided from the rest). Origin: from H2834 (חָשַׂף); KJV: little flock.

H2836 חָשַׁק (châshaq, khaw-shak'): to cling, i.e. join, (figuratively) to love, delight in; elliptically; to deliver. Origin: a primitive root; also interchangeable for H2820 (חָשַׂךְ) KJV: have a delight, (have a) desire, fillet, long, set (in) love.

H2837 חֵשֶׁק (chêsheq, khay'-shek): delight. Origin: from H2836 (חָשַׁק); KJV: desire, pleasure.

H2838 חָשֻׁק (châshuq, khaw-shook'): attached, i.e. a fence-rail or rod connecting the posts or pillars. Origin: or חָשׁוּק; past participle of H2836 (חָשַׁק); KJV: fillet.

H2839 חִשֻּׁק (chishshuq, khish-shook'): conjoined, i.e. a wheel-spoke or rod connecting the hub with the rim. Origin: from H2836 (חָשַׁק); KJV: felloe.

H2840 חִשֻּׁר (chishshur, khish-shoor'): combined, i.e. the nave or hub of awheel (as holding the spokes together). Origin: from an unused root meaning to bind together; KJV: spoke.

H2841 חַשְׁרָה (chashrâh, khash-raw'): properly, a combination or gathering, i.e. of watery clouds. Origin: from the same as H2840 (חִשֻּׁר); KJV: dark.

H2842 חָשַׁשׁ (châshash, khaw-shash'): dry grass. Origin: by variation for H7179 (קַשׁ); KJV: chaff.

H2843 חֻשָׁתִי (Chushâthîy, khoo-shaw-thee'): a Chushathite or descendant of Chushah. Origin: patronymically from H2364 (חוּשָׁה); KJV: Hushathite.

H2844 חַת (chath, khath): concretely, crushed; also afraid; abstractly, terror. Origin: from H2865 (חָתַת); KJV: broken, dismayed, dread, fear.

H2845 חֵת (Chêth, khayth): Cheth, an aboriginal Canaanite. Origin: from H2865 (חָתַת); terror; KJV: Heth.

H2846 חָתָה (châthâh, khaw-thaw'): to lay hold of; especially to pick up fire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: heap, take (away).

H2847 חִתָּה (chittâh, khit-taw'): fear. Origin: from H2865 (חָתַת); KJV: terror.

H2848 חִתּוּל (chittûwl, khit-tool'): swathed, i.e. a bandage. Origin: from H2853 (חָתַל); KJV: roller.

H2849 חַתְחַת (chathchath, khath-khath'): terror. Origin: from H2844 (חַת); KJV: fear.

H2850 חִתִּי (Chittîy, khit-tee'): a Chittite, or descendant of Cheth. Origin: patronymically from H2845 (חֵת); KJV: Hittite, Hittities.

H2851 חִתִּית (chittîyth, khit-teeth'): fear. Origin: from H2865 (חָתַת); KJV: terror.

H2852 חָתַךְ (châthak, khaw-thak'): properly, to cut off, i.e. (figuratively) to decree. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: determine.

H2853 חָתַל (châthal, khaw-thal'): to swathe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, swaddle.

H2854 חֲתֻלָּה (chăthullâh, khath-ool-law'): a swathing cloth (figuratively). Origin: from H2853 (חָתַל); KJV: swaddling band.

H2855 חֶתְלֹן (Chethlôn, kheth-lone'): Chethlon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H2853 (חָתַל); enswathed; KJV: Hethlon.

H2856 חָתַם (châtham, khaw-tham'): to close up; especially to seal. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make an end, mark, seal (up), stop.

H2857 חֲתַם (chătham, khath-am'): to seal. Origin: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to H2856 (חָתַם); KJV: seal.

H2858 חֹתֶמֶת (chôthemeth, kho-the-meth): a seal. Origin: feminine active participle of H2856 (חָתַם); KJV: signet.

H2859 חָתַן (châthan, khaw-than'): to give (a daughter) away in marriage; hence (generally) to contract affinity by marriage. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: join in affinity, father in law, make marriages, mother in law, son in law.

H2860 חָתָן (châthân, khaw-thawn'): a relative by marriage (especially through the bride); figuratively, a circumcised child (as a species of religious espousal). Origin: from H2859 (חָתַן); KJV: bridegroom, husband, son in law.

H2861 חֲתֻנָּה (chăthunnâh, khath-oon-naw'): a wedding. Origin: from H2859 (חָתַן); KJV: espousal.

H2862 חָתַף (châthaph, khaw-thaf'): to clutch. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: take away.

H2863 חֶתֶף (chetheph, kheh'-thef): properly, rapine; figuratively, robbery. Origin: from H2862 (חָתַף); KJV: prey.

H2864 חָתַר (châthar, khaw-thar'): to force a passage, as by burglary; figuratively, with oars. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dig (through), row.

H2865 חָתַת (châthath, khaw-thath'): properly, to prostrate; hence, to break down, either (literally) by violence, or (figuratively) by confusion and fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abolish, affright, be (make) afraid, amaze, beat down, discourage, (cause to) dismay, go down, scare, terrify.

H2866 חֲתַת (chăthath, khath-ath'): dismay. Origin: from H2865 (חָתַת); KJV: casting down.

H2867 חֲתַת (Chăthath, khath-ath'): Chathath, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2866 (חֲתַת); KJV: cathath. f

H2868 טְאֵב (ṭᵉʼêb, teh-abe'): to rejoice. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be glad

H2869 טָב (ṭâb, teh-abe'): good. Origin: the same as H2896 (טוֹב); KJV: fine, good.

H2870 טָבְאֵל (ṭâbᵉʼêl, taw-beh-ale'): Tabeel, the name of a Syrian and of a Persian. Origin: from H2895 (טוֹב) and H410 (אֵל); pleasing (to) God; KJV: Tabeal, Tabeel.

H2871 טָבוּל (ṭâbûwl, taw-bool'): properly, dyed, i.e. a turban (probably as of colored stuff). Origin: passive participle of H2881 (טָבַל); KJV: dyed attire.

H2872 טַבּוּר (ṭabbûwr, tab-boor'): properly, accumulated; i.e. (by implication) a summit. Origin: from an unused root meaning to pile up; KJV: middle, midst.

H2873 טָבַח (ṭâbach, taw-bakh'): to slaughter (animals or men). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: kill, (make) slaughter, slay.

H2874 טֶבַח (ṭebach, teh'-bakh): properly, something slaughtered; hence, a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstractly butchery (or concretely, a place of slaughter). Origin: from H2873 (טָבַח); KJV: [idiom] beast, slaughter, [idiom] slay, [idiom] sore.

H2875 טֶבַח (Ṭebach, teh'-bakh): Tebach, the name of a Mesopotamian and of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H2874 (טֶבַח); massacre; KJV: Tebah.

H2876 טַבָּח (ṭabbâch, tab-bawkh'): properly, a butcher; hence, a lifeguardsman (because he was acting as an executioner); also a cook (usually slaughtering the animal for food). Origin: from H2873 (טָבַח); KJV: cook, guard.

H2877 טַבָּח (ṭabbâch, tab-bawkh'): a lifeguardsman. Origin: (Aramaic) the same as H2876 (טַבָּח); KJV: guard.

H2878 טִבְחָה (ṭibchâh, tib-khaw'): {properly, something slaughtered; hence, a beast (or meat, as butchered); abstractly butchery (or concretely, a place of slaughter)}. Origin: feminine of H2874 (טֶבַח) and meaning the same KJV: flesh, slaughter.

H2879 טַבָּחָה (ṭabbâchâh, tab-baw-khaw'): a female cook. Origin: feminine of H2876 (טַבָּח); KJV: cook.

H2880 טִבְחַת (Ṭibchath, tib-khath'): Tibchath, a place in Syria. Origin: from H2878 (טִבְחָה); slaughter; KJV: Tibhath.

H2881 טָבַל (ṭâbal, taw-bal'): to dip, to immerse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dip, plunge.

H2882 טְבַלְיָהוּ (Ṭᵉbalyâhûw, teb-al-yaw'-hoo): Tebaljah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2881 (טָבַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has dipped; KJV: Tebaliah.

H2883 טָבַע (ṭâbaʻ, taw-bah'): to sink. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drown, fasten, settle, sink.

H2884 טַבָּעוֹת (Ṭabbâʻôwth, tab-baw-othe'): Tabbaoth, one of the Nethinim. Origin: plural of H2885 (טַבַּעַת); rings; KJV: Tabaoth.

H2885 טַבַּעַת (ṭabbaʻath, tab-bah'-ath): properly, a seal (as sunk into the wax), i.e. signet (for sealing); hence (generally) a ring of any kind. Origin: from H2883 (טָבַע); KJV: ring.

H2886 טַבְרִמּוֹן (Ṭabrimmôwn, tab-rim-mone'): Tabrimmon, a Syrian. Origin: from H2895 (טוֹב) and H7417 (רִמּוֹן); pleasing (to) Rimmon; KJV: Tabrimmon.

H2887 טֵבֶת (Ṭêbeth, tay'-beth): Tebeth, the tenth Hebrew month. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Tebeth.

H2888 טַבַּת (Ṭabbath, tab-bath'): Tabbath, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Tabbath.

H2889 טָהוֹר (ṭâhôwr, taw-hore'): pure (in a physical, chemical, ceremonial or moral sense). Origin: or טָהֹר; from H2891 (טָהֵר); KJV: clean, fair, pure(-ness).

H2890 טְהוֹר (ṭᵉhôwr, teh-hore'): purity. Origin: from H2891 (טָהֵר); KJV: pureness.

H2891 טָהֵר (ṭâhêr, taw-hare'): to be pure (physical sound, clear, unadulterated; Levitically, uncontaminated; morally, innocent or holy). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to be bright; i.e. (by implication) KJV: be (make, make self, pronounce) clean, cleanse (self), purge, purify(-ier, self).

H2892 טֹהַר (ṭôhar, to'-har): literally brightness; ceremonially purification. Origin: from H2891 (טָהֵר); KJV: clearness, glory, purifying.

H2893 טׇהֳרָה (ṭohŏrâh, toh-or-aw'): ceremonial purification; moral purity. Origin: feminine of H2892 (טֹהַר); KJV: [idiom] is cleansed, cleansing, purification(-fying).

H2894 טוּא (ṭûwʼ, too): to sweep away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sweep.
