H2895 טוֹב (ṭôwb, tobe): to be (transitively, do or make) good (or well) in the widest sense. Origin: a primitive root, KJV: be (do) better, cheer, be (do, seem) good, (make) goodly, [idiom] please, (be, do, go, play) well.

H2896 טוֹב (ṭôwb, tobe): good (as an adjective) in the widest sense; used likewise as a noun, both in the masculine and the feminine, the singular and the plural (good, a good or good thing, a good man or woman; the good, goods or good things, good men or women), also as an adverb (well). Origin: from H2895 (טוֹב); KJV: beautiful, best, better, bountiful, cheerful, at ease, [idiom] fair (word), (be in) favour, fine, glad, good (deed, -lier, -liest, -ly, -ness, -s), graciously, joyful, kindly, kindness, liketh (best), loving, merry, [idiom] most, pleasant, [phrase] pleaseth, pleasure, precious, prosperity, ready, sweet, wealth, welfare, (be) well(-favoured).

H2897 טוֹב (Ṭôwb, tobe): Tob, a region apparently East of the Jordan. Origin: the same as H2896 (טוֹב); good; KJV: Tob.

H2898 טוּב (ṭûwb, toob): good (as a noun), in the widest sense, especially goodness (superlative concretely, the best), beauty, gladness, welfare. Origin: from H2895 (טוֹב); KJV: fair, gladness, good(-ness, thing, -s), joy, go well with.

H2899 טוֹב אֲדֹנִיָּהוּ (Ṭôwb ʼĂdônîyâhûw, tobe ado-nee-yah'-hoo): Tob-Adonijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2896 (טוֹב) and H138 (אֲדֹנִיָּה); pleasing (to) Adonijah; KJV: Tob-adonijah.

H2900 טוֹבִיָּה (Ṭôwbîyâh, to-bee-yaw'): Tobijah, the name of three Israelites and of one Samaritan. Origin: or טוֹבִיָּהוּ; from H2896 (טוֹב) and H3050 (יָהּ); goodness of Jehovah; KJV: Tobiah, Tobijah.

H2901 טָוָה (ṭâvâh, taw-vaw'): to spin. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: spin.

H2902 טוּחַ (ṭûwach, too'-akh): to smear, especially with lime. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: daub, overlay, plaister, smut.

H2903 טוֹפָפָה (ṭôwphâphâh, to-faw-faw'): a fillet for the forehead. Origin: from an unused root meaning to go around or bind; KJV: frontlet.

H2904 טוּל (ṭûwl, tool): to pitch over or reel; hence (transitively) to cast down or out. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: carry away, (utterly) cast (down, forth, out), send out.

H2905 טוּר (ṭûwr, toor): a row; hence, a wall. Origin: from an unused root meaning to range in a regular manner; KJV: row.

H2906 טוּר (ṭûwr, toor): a rock or hill. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6697 (צוּר); KJV: mountain.

H2907 טוּשׂ (ṭûws, toos): to pounce as a bird of prey. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: haste.

H2908 טְוָת (ṭᵉvâth, tev-awth'): hunger (as twisting). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H2901 (טָוָה); KJV: fasting.

H2909 טָחָה (ṭâchâh, taw-khaw'): to stretch a bow, as an archer. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (bow-) shot.

H2910 טֻחָה (ṭuchâh, too-khaw'): (in the plural only) the kidneys (as being covered); hence (figuratively) the inmost thought. Origin: from H2909 (טָחָה) (or H2902 (טוּחַ)) in the sense of overlaying; KJV: inward parts.

H2911 טְחוֹן (ṭᵉchôwn, tekh-one'): a hand mill; hence, a millstone. Origin: from H2912 (טָחַן); KJV: to grind.

H2912 טָחַן (ṭâchan, taw-khan'): to grind meal; hence, to be aconcubine (that being their employment). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: grind(-er).

H2913 טַחֲנָה (ṭachănâh, takh-an-aw'): a hand mill; hence (figuratively) chewing. Origin: from H2912 (טָחַן); KJV: grinding.

H2914 טְחֹר (ṭᵉchôr, tekh-ore'): a boil or ulcer (from the inflammation), especially a tumorin the anus or pudenda (the piles). Origin: from an unused root meaning to burn; KJV: emerod.

H2915 טִיחַ (ṭîyach, tee'akh): mortar or plaster. Origin: from (the equiv. of) H2902 (טוּחַ); KJV: daubing.

H2916 טִיט (ṭîyṭ, teet): mud or clay; figuratively, calamity. Origin: from an unused root meaning apparently to be sticky (rather perb. a demonstrative); from H2894 (טוּא), through the idea of dirt to be swept away); KJV: clay, dirt, mire.

H2917 טִין (ṭîyn, teen): clay. Origin: (Aramaic) perhaps, by interchange, for a word corresponding to H2916 (טִיט); KJV: miry.

H2918 טִירָה (ṭîyrâh, tee-raw'): a wall; hence, a fortress or a hamlet. Origin: feminine of (an equivalent to) H2905 (טוּר); KJV: (goodly) castle, habitation, palace, row.

H2919 טַל (ṭal, tal): dew (as covering vegetation). Origin: from H2926 (טָלַל); KJV: dew.

H2920 טַל (ṭal, tal): {dew (as covering vegetation)}. Origin: (Aramaic) the same as H2919 (טַל) KJV: dew.

H2921 טָלָא (ṭâlâʼ, taw-law'): properly, to cover with pieces; i.e. (by implication) to spot or variegate (as tapestry). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: clouted, with divers colours, spotted.

H2922 טְלָא (ṭᵉlâʼ, tel-aw'): a lamb. Origin: apparently from H2921 (טָלָא) in the (orig.) sense of covering (for protection); (compare H2924 (טָלֶה)) KJV: lamb.

H2923 טְלָאִים (Ṭᵉlâʼîym, tel-aw-eem'): Telaim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the plural of H2922 (טְלָא); lambs; KJV: Telaim.

H2924 טָלֶה (ṭâleh, taw-leh'): a lamb. Origin: by variation for H2922 (טְלָא); KJV: lamb.

H2925 טַלְטֵלָה (ṭalṭêlâh, tal-tay-law'): overthrow or rejection. Origin: from H2904 (טוּל); KJV: captivity.

H2926 טָלַל (ṭâlal, taw-lal'): properly, to strew over, i.e. (by implication) to cover in or plate (with beams). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover.

H2927 טְלַל (ṭᵉlal, tel-al'): to cover with shade. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2926 (טָלַל); KJV: have a shadow.

H2928 טֶלֶם (Ṭelem, teh'-lem): Telem, the name of a place in Idumaea, also of a temple doorkeeper. Origin: from an unused root meaning to break up or treat violently; oppression; KJV: Telem.

H2929 טַלְמוֹן (Ṭalmôwn, tal-mone'): Talmon, a temple doorkeeper. Origin: from the same as H2728 (חָרְגֹּל); oppressive; KJV: Talmon.

H2930 טָמֵא (ṭâmêʼ, taw-may'): to be foul, especially in a ceremial or moral sense (contaminated). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: defile (self), pollute (self), be (make, make self, pronounce) unclean, [idiom] utterly.

H2931 טָמֵא (ṭâmêʼ, taw-may'): foul in a religious sense. Origin: from H2930 (טָמֵא); KJV: defiled, [phrase] infamous, polluted(-tion), unclean.

H2932 טֻמְאָה (ṭumʼâh, toom-aw'): religious impurity. Origin: from H2930 (טָמֵא); KJV: filthiness, unclean(-ness).

H2933 טָמָה (ṭâmâh, taw-maw'): to be impure in a religious sense. Origin: a collateral form of H2930 (טָמֵא); KJV: be defiled, be reputed vile.

H2934 טָמַן (ṭâman, taw-man'): to hide (by covering over). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hide, lay privily, in secret.

H2935 טֶנֶא (ṭeneʼ, teh'-neh): a basket (of interlaced osiers). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to weave; KJV: basket.

H2936 טָנַף (ṭânaph, taw-naf'): to soil. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: defile.

H2937 טָעָה (ṭâʻâh, taw-aw'): to wander; causatively to lead astray. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: seduce.

H2938 טָעַם (ṭâʻam, taw-am'): to taste; figuratively, to perceive. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] but, perceive, taste.

H2939 טְעַם (ṭᵉʻam, teh-am'): to taste; causatively to feed. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2938 (טָעַם); KJV: make to eat, feed.

H2940 טַעַם (ṭaʻam, tah'-am): properly, a taste, i.e. (figuratively) perception; by implication, intelligence; transitively, a mandate. Origin: from H2938 (טָעַם); KJV: advice, behaviour, decree, discretion, judgment, reason, taste, understanding.

H2941 טַעַם (ṭaʻam, tah'-am): properly, a taste, i.e. ajudicial sentence. Origin: (Aramaic) from H2939 (טְעַם); compare H2940 (טַעַם)) KJV: account, [idiom] to be commanded, commandment, matter.

H2942 טְעֵם (ṭᵉʻêm, teh-ame'): properly, flavor; figuratively, judgment (both subjective and objective); hence, account (both subjectively and objectively). Origin: (Aramaic) from H2939 (טְעַם), and equivalent to H2941 (טַעַם); KJV: [phrase] chancellor, [phrase] command, commandment, decree, [phrase] regard, taste, wisdom.

H2943 טָעַן (ṭâʻan, taw-an'): to load a beast. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lade.

H2944 טָעַן (ṭâʻan, taw-an'): to stab. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: thrust through.

H2945 טַף (ṭaph, taf): a family (mostly used collectively in the singular). Origin: from H2952 (טָפַף) (perhaps referring to the tripping gait of children); KJV: (little) children (ones), families.

H2946 טָפַח (ṭâphach, taw-fakh'): to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively, to nurse achild (as promotive of growth). Origin: a primitive root; or perhaps a denominative from H2947 (טֵפַח), from dandling on the palms KJV: span, swaddle.

H2947 טֵפַח (ṭêphach, tay'-fakh): a spread of the hand, i.e. a palm-breadth (not 'span' of the fingers); architecturally, a corbel (as a supporting palm). Origin: from H2946 (טָפַח); KJV: coping, hand-breadth.

H2948 טֹפַח (ṭôphach, to'-fakh): {a spread of the hand, i.e. a palm-breadth (not 'span' of the fingers); architecturally, a corbel (as a supporting palm)}. Origin: from H2946 (טָפַח) (the same as H2947 (טֵפַח)) KJV: hand-breadth (broad).

H2949 טִפֻּח (ṭippuch, tip-pookh'): nursing. Origin: from H2946 (טָפַח); KJV: span long.

H2950 טָפַל (ṭâphal, taw-fal'): properly, to stick on as apatch; figuratively, to impute falsely. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: forge(-r), sew up.

H2951 טִפְסַר (ṭiphçar, tif-sar'): a military governor. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: captain.

H2952 טָפַף (ṭâphaph, taw-faf'): to trip (with short steps) coquettishly. Origin: a primitive root; apparently KJV: mince.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H2953 to H3070
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H2953 טְפַר (ṭᵉphar, tef-ar'): a finger-nail; also a hoof or claw. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H6852 (צָפַר), and meaning the same as H6856 (צִפֹּרֶן); KJV: nail.

H2954 טָפַשׁ (ṭâphash, taw-fash'): properly, apparently to be thick; figuratively, to be stupid. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be fat.

H2955 טָפַת (Ṭâphath, taw-fath'): Taphath, an Israelitess. Origin: probably from H5197 (נָטַף); a dropping (of ointment); KJV: Taphath.

H2956 טָרַד (ṭârad, taw-rad'): to drive on; figuratively, to follow close. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: continual.

H2957 טְרַד (ṭᵉrad, ter-ad'): to expel. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2956 (טָרַד); KJV: drive.

H2958 טְרוֹם (ṭᵉrôwm, ter-ome'): not yet. Origin: a variation of H2962 (טֶרֶם); KJV: before.

H2959 טָרַח (ṭârach, taw-rakh'): to overburden. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: weary.

H2960 טֹרַח (ṭôrach, to'-rakh): a burden. Origin: from H2959 (טָרַח); KJV: cumbrance, trouble.

H2961 טָרִי (ṭârîy, taw-ree'): properly, dripping; hence, fresh (i.e. recently made such). Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to be moist; KJV: new, putrefying.

H2962 טֶרֶם (ṭerem, teh'-rem): properly, non-occurrence; used adverbially, not yet or before. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to interrupt or suspend; KJV: before, ere, not yet.

H2963 טָרַף (ṭâraph, taw-raf'): to pluck off or pull to pieces; causatively to supply with food (as in morsels). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch, [idiom] without doubt, feed, ravin, rend in pieces, [idiom] surely, tear (in pieces).

H2964 טֶרֶף (ṭereph, teh'-ref): something torn, i.e. a fragment, e.g. a fresh leaf, prey, food. Origin: from H2963 (טָרַף); KJV: leaf, meat, prey, spoil.

H2965 טָרָף (ṭârâph, taw-rawf'): recently torn off, i.e. fresh. Origin: from H2963 (טָרַף); KJV: pluckt off.

H2966 טְרֵפָה (ṭᵉrêphâh, ter-ay-faw'): prey, i.e. flocks devoured by animals. Origin: feminine (collectively) of H2964 (טֶרֶף); KJV: ravin, (that which was) torn (of beasts, in pieces).

H2967 טַרְפְּלַי (Ṭarpᵉlay, tar-pel-ah'-ee): a Tarpelite (collectively) or inhabitants of Tarpel, a place in Assyria. Origin: (Aramaic) from a name of foreign derivation; KJV: Tarpelites. y

H2968 יָאַב (yâʼab, yaw-ab'): to desire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: long.

H2969 יָאָה (yâʼâh, yaw-aw'): to be suitable. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appertain.

H2970 יַאֲזַנְיָה (Yaʼăzanyâh, yah-az-an-yaw'): Jaazanjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or יַאֲזַנְיָהוּ; from H238 (אָזַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); heard of Jah; KJV: Jaazaniah. Compare H3153 (יְזַנְיָה).

H2971 יָאִיר (Yâʼîyr, yaw-ere'): Jair, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H215 (אוֹר); enlightener; KJV: Jair.

H2972 יָאִרִי (Yâʼirîy, yaw-ee-ree'): a Jairite or descendant of Jair. Origin: patronymically from H2971 (יָאִיר); KJV: Jairite.

H2973 יָאַל (yâʼal, yaw-al'): properly, to be slack, i.e. (figuratively) to be foolish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dote, be (become, do) foolish(-ly).

H2974 יָאַל (yâʼal, yaw-al'): properly, to yield, especially assent; hence (pos.) to undertake as an act of volition. Origin: a primitive root (probably rather the same as H2973 (יָאַל) through the idea of mental weakness); KJV: assay, begin, be content, please, take upon, [idiom] willingly, would.

H2975 יְאֹר (yᵉʼôr, yeh-ore'): a channel, e.g. a fosse, canal, shaft; specifically the Nile, as the one river of Egypt, including its collateral trenches; also the Tigris, as the main river of Assyria. Origin: of Egyptian origin; KJV: brook, flood, river, stream.

H2976 יָאַשׁ (yâʼash, yaw-ash'): to desist, i.e. (figuratively) to despond. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) despair, one that is desperate, be no hope.

H2977 יֹאשִׁיָּה (Yôʼshîyâh, yo-shee-yaw'): Joshijah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or יֹאשִׁיָּהוּ; from the same root as H803 (אֲשׁוּיָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); founded of Jah; KJV: Josiah.

H2978 יְאִתוֹן (yᵉʼithôwn, yeh-ee-thone'): an entry. Origin: from H857 (אָתָה); KJV: entrance.

H2979 יְאָתְרַי (yᵉʼâthᵉray, yeh-aw-ther-ah'ee): Jeatherai, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H871 (אֲתָרִים); stepping; KJV: Jeaterai.

H2980 יָבַב (yâbab, yaw-bab): to bawl. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cry out.

H2981 יְבוּל (yᵉbûwl, yeb-ool'): produce, i.e. a crop or (figuratively) wealth. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: fruit, increase.

H2982 יְבוּס (Yᵉbûwç, yeb-oos'): Jebus, the original name of Jerusalem. Origin: from H947 (בּוּס); trodden, i.e. threshing-place; KJV: Jebus.

H2983 יְבוּסִי (Yᵉbûwçîy, yeb-oo-see'): a Jebusite or inhabitant of Jebus. Origin: patrial from H2982 (יְבוּס); KJV: Jebusite(-s).

H2984 יִבְחַר (Yibchar, yib-khar'): Jibchar, an Israelite. Origin: from H977 (בָּחַר); choice; KJV: Ibhar.

H2985 יָבִין (Yâbîyn, yaw-bene'): Jabin, the name of two Canaanitish kings. Origin: from H995 (בִּין); intelligent; KJV: Jabin.

H2986 יָבַל (yâbal, yaw-bal'): properly, to flow; causatively, to bring (especially with pomp). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring (forth), carry, lead (forth).

H2987 יְבַל (yᵉbal, yeb-al'): to bring. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: bring, carry.

H2988 יָבָל (yâbâl, yaw-bawl'): a stream. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: (water-) course, stream.

H2989 יָבָל (Yâbâl, yaw-bawl'): Jabal, an antediluvian. Origin: the same as H2988 (יָבָל); KJV: Jabal.

H2990 יַבֵּל (yabbêl, yab-bale'): having running sores. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: wen.

H2991 יִבְלְעָם (Yiblᵉʻâm, yib-leh-awm'): Jibleam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1104 (בָּלַע) and H5971 (עַם); devouring people; KJV: Ibleam.

H2992 יָבַם (yâbam, yaw-bam'): to marry a (deceased) brother's widow. Origin: a primitive root of doubtful meaning; used only as a denominative from H2993 (יָבָם); KJV: perform the duty of a husband's brother, marry.

H2993 יָבָם (yâbâm, yaw-bawm'): a brotherin-law. Origin: from (the orig. of) H2992 (יָבַם); KJV: husband's brother.

H2994 יְבֵמֶת (Yᵉbêmeth, yeb-ay'-meth): a sister-in-law. Origin: feminine participle of H2992 (יָבַם); KJV: brother's wife, sister in law.

H2995 יַבְנְאֵל (Yabnᵉʼêl, yab-neh-ale'): Jabneel, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה) and H410 (אֵל); built of God; KJV: Jabneel.

H2996 יַבְנֶה (Yabneh, yab-neh'): Jabneh, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); a building; KJV: Jabneh.

H2997 יִבְנְיָה (Yibnᵉyâh, yib-neh-yaw'): Jibnejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); built of Jah; KJV: Ibneiah.

H2998 יִבְנִיָּה (Yibnîyâh, yib-nee-yaw'): Jibnijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); building of Jah; KJV: Ibnijah.

H2999 יַבֹּק (Yabbôq, yab-boke'): Jabbok, a river east of the Jordan. Origin: probably from H1238 (בָּקַק); pouring forth; KJV: Jabbok.

H3000 יְבֶרֶכְיָהוּ (Yᵉberekyâhûw, yeb-eh-rek-yaw'-hoo): Jeberekjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1288 (בָרַךְ) and H3050 (יָהּ); blessed of Jah; KJV: Jeberechiah.

H3001 יָבֵשׁ (yâbêsh, yaw-bashe'): to be ashamed, confused or disappointed; also (as failing) to dry up (as water) or wither (as herbage). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be ashamed, clean, be confounded, (make) dry (up), (do) shame(-fully), [idiom] utterly, wither (away).

H3002 יָבֵשׁ (yâbêsh, yaw-bashe'): dry. Origin: from H3001 (יָבֵשׁ); KJV: dried (away), dry.

H3003 יָבֵשׁ (Yâbêsh, yaw-bashe'): Jobesh, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3002 (יָבֵשׁ) (also יָבֵישׁ; often with the addition of H1568 (גִּלְעָד), i.e. Jabesh of Gilad); KJV: Jobesh (-Gilead).

H3004 יַבָּשָׁה (yabbâshâh, yab-baw-shaw'): dry ground. Origin: from H3001 (יָבֵשׁ); KJV: dry (ground, land).

H3005 יִבְשָׂם (Yibsâm, yib-sawm'): Jibsam, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H1314 (בֶּשֶׂם); fragrant; KJV: Jibsam.

H3006 יַבֶּשֶׁת (yabbesheth, yab-beh'-sheth): dry ground. Origin: a variation of H3004 (יַבָּשָׁה); KJV: dry land.

H3007 יַבֶּשֶׁת (yabbesheth, yab-beh'-sheth): dry land. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3006 (יַבֶּשֶׁת); KJV: earth.

H3008 יִגְאָל (Yigʼâl, yig-awl'): Jigal, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H1350 (גָּאַל); avenger; KJV: Igal, Igeal.

H3009 יָגַב (yâgab, yaw-gab'): to dig or plow. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: husbandman.

H3010 יָגֵב (yâgêb, yaw-gabe'): a plowed field. Origin: from H3009 (יָגַב); KJV: field.

H3011 יׇגְבְּהָה (Yogbᵉhâh, yog-beh-haw'): Jogbehah, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: feminine from H1361 (גָּבַהּ); hillock; KJV: Jogbehah.

H3012 יִגְדַּלְיָהוּ (Yigdalyâhûw, yig-dal-yaw'-hoo): Jigdaljah, an Israelite. Origin: from H1431 (גָּדַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); magnified of Jah; KJV: Igdaliah.

H3013 יָגָה (yâgâh, yaw-gaw'): to grieve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: afflict, cause grief, grieve, sorrowful, vex.

H3014 יָגָה (yâgâh, yaw-gaw'): to push away. Origin: a primitive root (probably rather the same as H3013 (יָגָה) through the common idea of dissatisfaction); KJV: be removed.

H3015 יָגוֹן (yâgôwn, yaw-gohn'): affliction. Origin: from H3013 (יָגָה); KJV: grief, sorrow.

H3016 יָגוֹר (yâgôwr, yaw-gore'): fearful. Origin: from H3025 (יָגֹר); KJV: afraid, fearest.

H3017 יָגוּר (Yâgûwr, yaw-goor'): Jagur, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H1481 (גּוּר); a lodging; KJV: Jagur.

H3018 יְגִיעַ (yᵉgîyaʻ, yeg-ee'-ah): toil; hence, a work, produce, property (as the result of labor). Origin: from H3021 (יָגַע); KJV: labour, work.

H3019 יָגִיעַ (yâgîyaʻ, yaw-ghee'-ah): tired. Origin: from H3021 (יָגַע); KJV: weary.

H3020 יׇגְלִי (Yoglîy, yog-lee'): Jogli, an Israelite. Origin: from H1540 (גָּלָה); exiled; KJV: Jogli.

H3021 יָגַע (yâgaʻ, yaw-gah'): properly, to gasp; hence, to be exhausted, to tire, to toil. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: faint, (make to) labour, (be) weary.

H3022 יָגָע (yâgâʻ, yaw-gaw'): earnings (as the product of toil). Origin: from H3021 (יָגַע); KJV: that which he laboured for.

H3023 יָגֵעַ (yâgêaʻ, yaw-gay'-ah): tired; hence (transitive) tiresome. Origin: from H3021 (יָגַע); KJV: full of labour, weary.

H3024 יְגִעָה (yᵉgiʻâh, yeg-ee-aw'): fatigue. Origin: feminine of H3019 (יָגִיעַ); KJV: weariness.

H3025 יָגֹר (yâgôr, yaw-gore'): to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be afraid, fear.

H3026 יְגַר שַׂהֲדוּתָא (Yᵉgar Sahădûwthâʼ, yegar' sah-had-oo-thaw'): Jegar-Sahadutha, a cairn East of the Jordan. Origin: (Aramaic) from a word derived from an unused root (meaning to gather) and a derivation of a root corresponding to H7717 (שָׂהֵד); heap of the testimony; KJV: Jegar-Sahadutha.

H3027 יָד (yâd, yawd): a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.). Origin: a primitive word; in distinction from H3709 (כַּף), the closed one); used (as noun, adverb, etc.) in a great variety of applications, both literally and figuratively, both proximate and remote (as follows) KJV: ([phrase] be) able, [idiom] about, [phrase] armholes, at, axletree, because of, beside, border, [idiom] bounty, [phrase] broad, (broken-) handed, [idiom] by, charge, coast, [phrase] consecrate, [phrase] creditor, custody, debt, dominion, [idiom] enough, [phrase] fellowship, force, [idiom] from, hand(-staves, -y work), [idiom] he, himself, [idiom] in, labour, [phrase] large, ledge, (left-) handed, means, [idiom] mine, ministry, near, [idiom] of, [idiom] order, ordinance, [idiom] our, parts, pain, power, [idiom] presumptuously, service, side, sore, state, stay, draw with strength, stroke, [phrase] swear, terror, [idiom] thee, [idiom] by them, [idiom] themselves, [idiom] thine own, [idiom] thou, through, [idiom] throwing, [phrase] thumb, times, [idiom] to, [idiom] under, [idiom] us, [idiom] wait on, (way-) side, where, [phrase] wide, [idiom] with (him, me, you), work, [phrase] yield, [idiom] yourselves.

H3028 יַד (yad, yad): {a hand (the open one (indicating power, means, direction, etc.)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3027 (יָד) KJV: hand, power.

H3029 יְדָא (yᵉdâʼ, yed-aw'): to praise. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3034 (יָדָה); KJV: (give) thank(-s).

H3030 יִדְאֲלָה (Yidʼălâh, yid-al-aw'): Jidalah, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Idalah.

H3031 יִדְבָּשׁ (Yidbâsh, yid-bawsh'): Jidbash, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H1706 (דְּבַשׁ); perhaps honeyed; KJV: Idbash.

H3032 יָדַד (yâdad, yaw-dad'): properly, to handle, i.e. to throw, e.g. lots. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H3034 (יָדָה)) KJV: cast.

H3033 יְדִדוּת (yᵉdidûwth, yed-ee-dooth'): properly, affection; concretely, a darling object. Origin: from H3039 (יְדִיד); KJV: dearly beloved.

H3034 יָדָה (yâdâh, yaw-daw'): physically, to throw (a stone, an arrow) at or away; especially to revere or worship (with extended hands); intensively, to bemoan (by wringing the hands). Origin: a primitive root; used only as denominative from H3027 (יָד); literally, to use (i.e. hold out) the hand; KJV: cast (out), (make) confess(-ion), praise, shoot, (give) thank(-ful, -s, -sgiving).

H3035 יִדּוֹ (Yiddôw, yid-do'): Jiddo, an Israelite. Origin: from H3034 (יָדָה); praised; KJV: Iddo.

H3036 יָדוֹן (Yâdôwn, yaw-done'): Jadon, an Israelite. Origin: from H3034 (יָדָה); thankful; KJV: Jadon.

H3037 יַדּוּעַ (Yaddûwaʻ, yad-doo'-ah): Jaddua, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע); knowing; KJV: Jaddua.

H3038 יְדוּתוּן (Yᵉdûwthûwn, yed-oo-thoon'): Jeduthun, an Israelite. Origin: or יְדֻתוּן; or יְדִיתוּן; probably from H3034 (יָדָה); laudatory; KJV: Jeduthun.

H3039 יְדִיד (yᵉdîyd, yed-eed'): loved. Origin: from the same as H1730 (דּוֹד); KJV: amiable, (well-) beloved, loves.

H3040 יְדִידָה (Yᵉdîydâh, yed-ee-daw'): Jedidah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine of H3039 (יְדִיד); beloved; KJV: Jedidah.

H3041 יְדִידְיָה (Yᵉdîydᵉyâh, yed-ee-deh-yaw'): Jedidejah, a name of Solomon. Origin: from H3039 (יְדִיד) and H3050 (יָהּ); beloved of Jah; KJV: Jedidiah.

H3042 יְדָיָה (Yᵉdâyâh, yed-aw-yaw'): Jedajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3034 (יָדָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); praised of Jah; KJV: Jedaiah.

H3043 יְדִיעֲאֵל (Yᵉdîyʻăʼêl, yed-ee-ah-ale'): Jediael, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע) and H410 (אֵל); knowing God; KJV: Jediael.

H3044 יִדְלָף (Yidlâph, yid-lawf'): Jidlaph, a Mesopotamian. Origin: from H1811 (דָּלַף); tearful; KJV: Jidlaph.

H3045 יָדַע (yâdaʻ, yaw-dah'): to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: acknowledge, acquaintance(-ted with), advise, answer, appoint, assuredly, be aware, (un-) awares, can(-not), certainly, comprehend, consider, [idiom] could they, cunning, declare, be diligent, (can, cause to) discern, discover, endued with, familiar friend, famous, feel, can have, be (ig-) norant, instruct, kinsfolk, kinsman, (cause to let, make) know, (come to give, have, take) knowledge, have (knowledge), (be, make, make to be, make self) known, [phrase] be learned, [phrase] lie by man, mark, perceive, privy to, [idiom] prognosticator, regard, have respect, skilful, shew, can (man of) skill, be sure, of a surety, teach, (can) tell, understand, have (understanding), [idiom] will be, wist, wit, wot.

H3046 יְדַע (yᵉdaʻ, yed-ah'): {to know (properly, to ascertain by seeing); used in a great variety of senses, figuratively, literally, euphemistically and inferentially (including observation, care, recognition; and causatively, instruction, designation, punishment, etc.)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3045 (יָדַע) KJV: certify, know, make known, teach.

H3047 יָדָע (Yâdâʻ, yaw-daw'): Jada, an Israelite. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע); knowing; KJV: Jada.

H3048 יְדַעְיָה (Yᵉdaʻyâh, yed-ah-yaw'): Jedajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has known; KJV: Jedaiah.

H3049 יִדְּעֹנִי (yiddᵉʻônîy, yid-deh-o-nee'): properly, a knowing one; specifically, a conjurer; (by impl) a ghost. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: wizard.

H3050 יָהּ (Yâhh, yaw): Jah, the sacred name. Origin: contraction for H3068 (יְהֹוָה), and meaning the same; KJV: Jah, the Lord, most vehement. Compare names in '-iah,' '-jah.'

H3051 יָהַב (yâhab, yaw-hab'): to give (whether literal or figurative); generally, to put; imperatively (reflexive) come. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: ascribe, bring, come on, give, go, set, take.

H3052 יְהַב (yᵉhab, yeh-hab'): {to give (whether literal or figurative); generally, to put; imperatively (reflexive) come}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3051 (יָהַב) KJV: deliver, give, lay, [phrase] prolong, pay, yield.

H3053 יְהָב (yᵉhâb, ye-hawb'): properly, what is given (by Providence), i.e. a lot. Origin: from H3051 (יָהַב); KJV: burden.

H3054 יָהַד (yâhad, yaw-had'): to Judaize, i.e. become Jewish. Origin: denominative from a form corresponding to H3061 (יְהוּד)lemma יְהיּד yod, corrected to יְהוּד; KJV: become Jews.

H3055 יְהֻד (Yᵉhud, yeh-hood'): Jehud, a place in Palestine. Origin: a briefer form of one corresponding to H3061 (יְהוּד)lemma יְהיּד yod, corrected to יְהוּד; KJV: Jehud.

H3056 יֶהְדַי (Yehday, yeh-dah'-ee): Jehdai, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from a form corresponding to H3061 (יְהוּד)lemma יְהיּד yod, corrected to יְהוּד; Judaistic; KJV: Jehdai.

H3057 יְהֻדִיָּה (Yᵉhudîyâh, yeh-hoo-dee-yaw'): Jehudijah, a Jewess. Origin: feminine of H3064 (יְהוּדִי); KJV: Jehudijah.

H3058 יֵהוּא (Yêhûwʼ, yay-hoo'): Jehu, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H1931 (הוּא); Jehovah (is) He; KJV: Jehu.

H3059 יְהוֹאָחָז (Yᵉhôwʼâchâz, yeh-ho-aw-khawz'): Jehoachaz, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H270 (אָחַז); Jehovah-seized; KJV: Jehoahaz. Compare H3099 (יוֹאָחָז).

H3060 יְהוֹאָשׁ (Yᵉhôwʼâsh, yeh-ho-awsh'): Jehoash, the name of two Israelite kings. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and (perhaps) H784 (אֵשׁ); Jehovah-fired; KJV: Jehoash. Compare H3101 (יוֹאָשׁ).

H3061 יְהוּד (Yᵉhûwd, yeh-hood'): properly, Judah, hence, Judaea. Origin: (Aramaic) contracted from a form corresponding to H3063 (יְהוּדָה); KJV: Jewry, Judah, Judea.

H3062 יְהוּדָאִי (Yᵉhûwdâʼîy, yeh-hoo-daw-ee'): a Jehudaite (or Judaite), i.e. Jew. Origin: (Aramaic) patrial from H3061 (יְהוּד)lemma יְהיּד yod, corrected to יְהוּד; KJV: Jew.

H3063 יְהוּדָה (Yᵉhûwdâh, yeh-hoo-daw'): Jehudah (or Judah), the name of five Israelites; also of the tribe descended from the first, and of its territory. Origin: from H3034 (יָדָה); celebrated; KJV: Judah.

H3064 יְהוּדִי (Yᵉhûwdîy, yeh-hoo-dee'): a Jehudite (i.e. Judaite or Jew), or descendant of Jehudah (i.e. Judah). Origin: patronymically from H3063 (יְהוּדָה); KJV: Jew.

H3065 יְהוּדִי (Yᵉhûwdîy, yeh-hoo-dee'): Jehudi, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H3064 (יְהוּדִי); KJV: Jehudi.

H3066 יְהוּדִית (Yᵉhûwdîyth, yeh-hoo-deeth'): the Jewish (used adverbially) language. Origin: feminine of H3064 (יְהוּדִי); KJV: in the Jews' language.

H3067 יְהוּדִית (Yᵉhûwdîyth, yeh-ho-deeth'): Jehudith, a Canaanitess. Origin: the same as H3066 (יְהוּדִית); Jewess; KJV: Judith.

H3068 יְהֹוָה (Yᵉhôvâh, yeh-ho-vaw'): Jehovah, Jewish national name of God. Origin: from H1961 (הָיָה); (the) self-Existent or Eternal; KJV: Jehovah, the Lord. Compare H3050 (יָהּ), H3069 (יְהֹוִה).

H3069 יְהֹוִה (Yᵉhôvih, yeh-ho-vee'): {YHWH}. Origin: a variation of H3068 (יְהֹוָה) (used after H136 (אֲדֹנָי), and pronounced by Jews as H430 (אֱלֹהִים), in order to prevent the repetition of the same sound, since they elsewhere pronounce H3068 (יְהֹוָה) as H136 (אֲדֹנָי)) KJV: God.

H3070 יְהֹוָה יִרְאֶה (Yᵉhôvâh yirʼeh, yeh-ho-vaw' yir-eh'): Jehovah-Jireh, a symbolical name for Mount Moriah. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H7200 (רָאָה); Jehovah will see (to it); KJV: Jehovah-jireh.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3071 to H3188
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3071 יְהֹוָה נִסִּי (Yᵉhôvâh niççîy, yeh-ho-vaw' nis-see'): Jehovah-Nissi, a symbolical name of an altar in the Desert. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5251 (נֵס) with the prononimal suffix; Jehovah (is) my banner; KJV: Jehovah-nissi.

H3072 יְהֹוָה צִדְקֵנוּ (Yᵉhôvâh tsidqênûw, ye-ho-vaw' tsid-kay'-noo): Jehovah-Tsidkenu, a symbolical epithet of the Messiah and of Jerusalem. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H6664 (צֶדֶק) with pronominal suffix; Jehovah (is) our right; KJV: the Lord our righteousness.

H3073 יְהֹוָה שָׁלוֹם (Yᵉhôvâh shâlôwm, yeh-ho-vaw' shaw-lome'): Jehovah-Shalom, a symbolical name of an altar in Palestine. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); Jehovah (is) peace; KJV: Jehovah-shalom.

H3074 יְהֹוָה שָׁמָּה (Yᵉhôvâh shâmmâh, yeh-ho-vaw' shawm'-maw): Jehovah-Shammah, a symbolic title of Jerusalem. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H8033 (שָׁם) with directive enclitic; Jehovah (is) thither; KJV: Jehovahshammah.

H3075 יְהוֹזָבָד (Yᵉhôwzâbâd, yeh-ho-zaw-bawd'): Jehozabad, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H2064 (זָבַד); Jehovah-endowed; KJV: Jehozabad. Compare H3107 (יוֹזָבָד).

H3076 יְהוֹחָנָן (Yᵉhôwchânân, yeh-ho-khaw-nawn'): Jehochanan, the name of eight Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H2603 (חָנַן); Jehovah-favored; KJV: Jehohanan, Johanan. Compare H3110 (יוֹחָנָן).

H3077 יְהוֹיָדָע (Yᵉhôwyâdâʻ, yeh-ho-yaw-daw'): Jehojada, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H3045 (יָדַע); Jehovah-known; KJV: Jehoiada. Compare H3111 (יוֹיָדָע).

H3078 יְהוֹיָכִין (Yᵉhôwyâkîyn, yeh-ho-yaw-keen'): Jehojakin, a Jewish king. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H3559 (כּוּן); Jehovah will establish; KJV: Jehoiachin. Compare H3112 (יוֹיָכִין).

H3079 יְהוֹיָקִים (Yᵉhôwyâqîym, yeh-ho-yaw-keem'): Jehojakim, a Jewish king. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) abbreviated and H6965 (קוּם); Jehovah will raise; KJV: Jehoiakim. Compare H3113 (יוֹיָקִים).

H3080 יְהוֹיָרִיב (Yᵉhôwyârîyb, yeh-ho-yaw-reeb'): Jehojarib, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H7378 (רִיב); Jehovah will contend; KJV: Jehoiarib. Compare H3114 (יוֹיָרִיב).

H3081 יְהוּכַל (Yᵉhûwkal, yeh-hoo-kal'): Jehukal, an Israelite. Origin: from H3201 (יָכֹל); potent; KJV: Jehucal. Compare H3116 (יוּכַל).

H3082 יְהוֹנָדָב (Yᵉhôwnâdâb, yeh-ho-naw-dawb'): Jehonadab, the name of an Israelite and of an Arab. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5068 (נָדַב); Jehovah-largessed; KJV: Jehonadab, Jonadab. Compare H3122 (יוֹנָדָב).

H3083 יְהוֹנָתָן (Yᵉhôwnâthân, yeh-ho-naw-thawn'): Jehonathan, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5414 (נָתַן); Jehovah-given; KJV: Jonathan. Compare H3129 (יוֹנָתָן).

H3084 יְהוֹסֵף (Yᵉhôwçêph, yeh-ho-safe'): Jehoseph (i.e. Joseph), a son of Jacob. Origin: a fuller form of H3130 (יוֹסֵף); KJV: Joseph.

H3085 יְהוֹעַדָּה (Yᵉhôwʻaddâh, yeh-ho-ad-daw'): Jehoaddah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5710 (עָדָה); Jehovah-adorned; KJV: Jehoada.

H3086 יְהוֹעַדִּין (Yᵉhôwʻaddîyn, yeh-ho-ad-deen'): Jehoaddin or Jehoaddan, an Israelitess. Origin: or יְהוֹעַדָּן; from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5727 (עָדַן); Jehovahpleased; KJV: Jehoaddan.

H3087 יְהוֹצָדָק (Yᵉhôwtsâdâq, yeh-ho-tsaw-dawk'): Jehotsadak, an Israelite. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H6663 (צָדַק); Jehovah-righted; KJV: Jehozadek, Josedech. Compare H3136 (יוֹצָדָק).

H3088 יְהוֹרָם (Yᵉhôwrâm, yeh-ho-rawm'): Jehoram, the name of a Syrian and of three Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H7311 (רוּם); Jehovah-raised; KJV: Jehoram, Joram. Compare H3141 (יוֹרָם).

H3089 יְהוֹשֶׁבַע (Yᵉhôwshebaʻ, yeh-ho-sheh'-bah): Jehosheba, an Israelitess. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H7650 (שָׁבַע); Jehovah-sworn; KJV: Jehosheba. Compare H3090 (יְהוֹשַׁבְעַת).

H3090 יְהוֹשַׁבְעַת (Yᵉhôwshabʻath, yeh-ho-shab-ath'): Jehoshabath, an Israelitess. Origin: a form of H3089 (יְהוֹשֶׁבַע); KJV: Jehoshabeath.

H3091 יְהוֹשׁוּעַ (Yᵉhôwshûwaʻ, yeh-ho-shoo'-ah): Jehoshua (i.e. Joshua), the Jewish leader. Origin: or יְהוֹשֻׁעַ; from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H3467 (יָשַׁע); Jehovah-saved; KJV: Jehoshua, Jehoshuah, Joshua. Compare H1954 (הוֹשֵׁעַ), H3442 (יֵשׁוּעַ).

H3092 יְהוֹשָׁפָט (Yᵉhôwshâphâṭ, yeh-ho-shaw-fawt'): Jehoshaphat, the name of six Israelites; also of a valley near Jerusalem. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H8199 (שָׁפַט); Jehovah-judged; KJV: Jehoshaphat. Compare H3146 (יוֹשָׁפָט).

H3093 יָהִיר (yâhîyr, yaw-here'): elated; hence, arrogant. Origin: probably from the same as H2022 (הַר); KJV: haughty, proud.

H3094 יְהַלֶּלְאֵל (Yᵉhallelʼêl, yeh-hal-lel-ale'): Jehallelel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H1984 (הָלַל) and H410 (אֵל); praising God; KJV: Jehalellel, Jehalelel.

H3095 יַהֲלֹם (yahălôm, yah-hal-ome'): a precious stone, probably onyx. Origin: from H1986 (הָלַם) (in the sense of hardness); KJV: diamond.

H3096 יַהַץ (Yahats, yah'-hats): Jahats or Jahtsah, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: or יַהְצָה; or (feminine) יַהְצָה; from an unused root meaning to stamp; perhaps threshing-floor; KJV: Jahaz, Jahazah, Jahzah.

H3097 יוֹאָב (Yôwʼâb, yo-awb'): Joab, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H1 (אָב); Jehovah-fathered; KJV: Joab.

H3098 יוֹאָח (Yôwʼâch, yo-awkh'): Joach, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H251 (אָח); Jehovahbrothered; KJV: Joah.

H3099 יוֹאָחָז (Yôwʼâchâz, yo-aw-khawz'): Joachaz, the name of two Israelites. Origin: a form of H3059 (יְהוֹאָחָז); KJV: Jehoahaz, Joahaz.

H3100 יוֹאֵל (Yôwʼêl, yo-ale'): Joel, the name of twelve Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H410 (אֵל); Jehovah (is his) God; KJV: Joel.

H3101 יוֹאָשׁ (Yôwʼâsh, yo-awsh'): Joash, the name of six Israelites. Origin: or יֹאָשׁ; (2 Chronicles 24:1), a form of H3060 (יְהוֹאָשׁ); KJV: Joash.

H3102 יוֹב (Yôwb, yobe): Job, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps a form of H3103 (יוֹבָב), but more probably by erroneous transcription for H3437 (יָשׁוּב); KJV: Job.

H3103 יוֹבָב (Yôwbâb, yo-bawb'): Jobab, the name of two Israelites and of three foreigners. Origin: from H2980 (יָבַב); howler; KJV: Jobab.

H3104 יוֹבֵל (yôwbêl, yo-bale'): the blast of a horn (from its continuous sound); specifically, the signal of the silver trumpets; hence, the instrument itself and the festival thus introduced. Origin: or יֹבֵל; apparently from H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: jubile, ram's horn, trumpet.

H3105 יוּבַל (yûwbal, yoo-bal'): a stream. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: river.

H3106 יוּבַל (Yûwbal, yoo-bawl'): Jubal, an antediluvian. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל); stream; KJV: Jubal.

H3107 יוֹזָבָד (Yôwzâbâd, yo-zaw-bawd'): Jozabad, the name of ten Israelites. Origin: a form of H3075 (יְהוֹזָבָד); KJV: Josabad, Jozabad.

H3108 יוֹזָכָר (Yôwzâkâr, yo-zaw-kawr'): Jozacar, an Israelite. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H2142 (זָכַר); Jehovah-remembered; KJV: Jozachar.

H3109 יוֹחָא (Yôwchâʼ, yo-khaw'): Jocha, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and a variation of H2421 (חָיָה); Jehovah-revived; KJV: Joha.

H3110 יוֹחָנָן (Yôwchânân, yo-khaw-nawn'): Jochanan, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: a form of H3076 (יְהוֹחָנָן); KJV: Johanan.

H3111 יוֹיָדָע (Yôwyâdâʻ, yo-yaw-daw'): Jojada, the name of two Israelites. Origin: a form of H3077 (יְהוֹיָדָע); KJV: Jehoiada, Joiada.

H3112 יוֹיָכִין (Yôwyâkîyn, yo-yaw-keen'): Jojakin, an Israelite king. Origin: a form of H3078 (יְהוֹיָכִין); KJV: Jehoiachin.

H3113 יוֹיָקִים (Yôwyâqîym, yo-yaw-keem'): Jojakim, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3079 (יְהוֹיָקִים); KJV: Joiakim. Compare H3137 (יוֹקִים).

H3114 יוֹיָרִיב (Yôwyârîyb, yo-yaw-reeb'): Jojarib, the name of four Israelites. Origin: a form of H3080 (יְהוֹיָרִיב); KJV: Joiarib.

H3115 יוֹכֶבֶד (Yôwkebed, yo-keh'-bed): Jokebed, the mother of Moses. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) contracted and H3513 (כָּבַד); Jehovah-gloried; KJV: Jochebed.

H3116 יוּכַל (Yûwkal, yoo-kal'): Jukal, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3081 (יְהוּכַל); KJV: Jucal.

H3117 יוֹם (yôwm, yome): a day (as the warm hours), whether literal (from sunrise to sunset, or from one sunset to the next), or figurative (a space of time defined by an associated term), (often used adverb). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be hot; KJV: age, [phrase] always, [phrase] chronicals, continually(-ance), daily, ((birth-), each, to) day, (now a, two) days (agone), [phrase] elder, [idiom] end, [phrase] evening, [phrase] (for) ever(-lasting, -more), [idiom] full, life, as (so) long as (... live), (even) now, [phrase] old, [phrase] outlived, [phrase] perpetually, presently, [phrase] remaineth, [idiom] required, season, [idiom] since, space, then, (process of) time, [phrase] as at other times, [phrase] in trouble, weather, (as) when, (a, the, within a) while (that), [idiom] whole ([phrase] age), (full) year(-ly), [phrase] younger.

H3118 יוֹם (yôwm, yome): a day. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3117 (יוֹם); KJV: day (by day), time.

H3119 יוֹמָם (yôwmâm, yo-mawm'): daily. Origin: from H3117 (יוֹם); KJV: daily, (by, in the) day(-time).

H3120 יָוָן (Yâvân, yaw-vawn'): Javan, the name of a son of Joktan, and of the race (Ionians, i.e. Greeks) descended from him, with their territory; also of a place in Arabia. Origin: probably from the same as H3196 (יַיִן); effervescing (i.e. hot and active); KJV: Javan.

H3121 יָוֵן (yâvên, yaw-ven'): properly, dregs (as effervescing); hence, mud. Origin: from the same as H3196 (יַיִן); KJV: mire, miry.

H3122 יוֹנָדָב (Yôwnâdâb, yo-naw-dawb'): Jonadab, the name of an Israelite and of a Rechabite. Origin: a form of H3082 (יְהוֹנָדָב); KJV: Jonadab.

H3123 יוֹנָה (yôwnâh, yo-naw'): a dove (apparently from the warmth of their mating). Origin: probably from the same as H3196 (יַיִן); KJV: dove, pigeon.

H3124 יוֹנָה (Yôwnâh, yo-naw'): Jonah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H3123 (יוֹנָה); KJV: Jonah.

H3125 יְוָנִי (Yᵉvânîy, yev-aw-nee'): a Jevanite, or descendant of Javan. Origin: patronymically from H3121 (יָוֵן); KJV: Grecian.

H3126 יוֹנֵק (yôwnêq, yo-nake'): a sucker; hence, a twig (of a tree felled and sprouting). Origin: active participle of H3243 (יָנַק); KJV: tender plant.

H3127 יוֹנֶקֶת (yôwneqeth, yo-neh'-keth): a sprout. Origin: feminine of H3126 (יוֹנֵק); KJV: (tender) branch, young twig.

H3128 יוֹנַת אֵלֶם רְחֹקִים (yôwnath ʼêlem rᵉchôqîym, yo-nath' ay'-lem rekh-o-keem'): dove of (the) silence (i.e. dumb Israel) of (i.e. among) distances (i.e. strangers); the title of a ditty (used for a name of its melody). Origin: from H3123 (יוֹנָה) and H482 (אֵלֶם) and the plural of H7350 (רָחוֹק); KJV: Jonath-elem-rechokim.

H3129 יוֹנָתָן (Yôwnâthân, yo-naw-thawn'): Jonathan, the name of ten Israelites. Origin: a form of H3083 (יְהוֹנָתָן); KJV: Jonathan.

H3130 יוֹסֵף (Yôwçêph, yo-safe'): Joseph, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: future of H3254 (יָסַף); let him add (or perhaps simply active participle adding); KJV: Joseph. Compare H3084 (יְהוֹסֵף).

H3131 יוֹסִפְיָה (Yôwçiphyâh, yo-sif-yaw'): Josiphjah, an Israelite. Origin: from active participle of H3254 (יָסַף) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah (is) adding; KJV: Josiphiah.

H3132 יוֹעֵאלָה (Yôwʻêʼlâh, yo-ay-law'): Joelah, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps feminine active participle of H3276 (יַעַל); furthermore; KJV: Joelah.

H3133 יוֹעֵד (Yôwʻêd, yo-ade'): Joed, an Israelite. Origin: apparently the active participle of H3259 (יָעַד); appointer; KJV: Joed.

H3134 יוֹעֶזֶר (Yôwʻezer, yo-eh'-zer): Joezer, an Israelite. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); Jehovah (is his) help; KJV: Joezer.

H3135 יוֹעָשׁ (Yôwʻâsh, yo-awsh'): Joash, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H5789 (עוּשׁ); Jehovahhastened; KJV: Joash.

H3136 יוֹצָדָק (Yôwtsâdâq, yo-tsaw-dawk'): Jotsadak, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3087 (יְהוֹצָדָק); KJV: Jozadak.

H3137 יוֹקִים (Yôwqîym, yo-keem'): Jokim, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3113 (יוֹיָקִים); KJV: Jokim.

H3138 יוֹרֶה (yôwreh, yo-reh'): sprinkling; hence, a sprinkling (or autumnal showers). Origin: active participle of H3384 (יָרָה); KJV: first rain, former (rain).

H3139 יוֹרָה (Yôwrâh, yo-raw'): Jorah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3384 (יָרָה); rainy; KJV: Jorah.

H3140 יוֹרַי (Yôwray, yo-rah'-ee): Jorai, an Israelite. Origin: from H3384 (יָרָה); rainy; KJV: Jorai.

H3141 יוֹרָם (Yôwrâm, yo-rawm'): Joram, the name of three Israelites and one Syrian. Origin: a form of H3088 (יְהוֹרָם); KJV: Joram.

H3142 יוּשַׁב חֶסֶד (Yûwshab Cheçed, yoo-shab' kheh'-sed): Jushab-Chesed, an Israelite. Origin: from H7725 (שׁוּב) and H2617 (חֵסֵד); kindness will be returned; KJV: Jushab-hesed.

H3143 יוֹשִׁבְיָה (Yôwshibyâh, yo-shi-yaw'): Josibjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3427 (יָשַׁב) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jehovah will cause to dwell; KJV: Josibiah.

H3144 יוֹשָׁה (Yôwshâh, yo-shaw'): Joshah, an Israelite. Origin: probably a form of H3145 (יוֹשַׁוְיָה); KJV: Joshah.

H3145 יוֹשַׁוְיָה (Yôwshavyâh, yo-shav-yaw'): Joshavjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H7737 (שָׁוָה); Jehovah-set; KJV: Joshaviah. Compare H3144 (יוֹשָׁה).

H3146 יוֹשָׁפָט (Yôwshâphâṭ, yo-shaw-fawt'): Joshaphat, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3092 (יְהוֹשָׁפָט); KJV: Joshaphat.

H3147 יוֹתָם (Yôwthâm, yo-thawm'): Jotham, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3068 (יְהֹוָה) and H8535 (תָּם); Jehovah (is) perfect; KJV: Jotham.

H3148 יוֹתֵר (yôwthêr, yo-thare'): properly, redundant; hence, over and above, as adjective, noun, adverb or conjunction. Origin: active participle of H3498 (יָתַר); KJV: better, more(-over), over, profit.

H3149 יְזַוְאֵל (Yᵉzavʼêl, yez-av-ale'): Jezavel, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root (meaning to sprinkle) and H410 (אֵל); sprinkled of God; KJV: Jeziel (from the margin).

H3150 יִזִּיָּה (Yizzîyâh, yiz-zee-yaw'): Jizzijah, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as the first part of H3149 (יְזַוְאֵל) and H3050 (יָהּ); sprinkled of Jah; KJV: Jeziah.

H3151 יָזִיז (Yâzîyz, yaw-zeez'): Jaziz, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H2123 (זִיז); he will make prominent; KJV: Jaziz.

H3152 יִזְלִיאָה (Yizlîyʼâh, yiz-lee-aw'): Jizliah, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from an unused root (meaning to draw up); he will draw out; KJV: Jezliah.

H3153 יְזַנְיָה (Yᵉzanyâh, yez-an-yaw'): Jezanjah, an Israelite. Origin: or יְזַנְיָהוּ; probably for H2970 (יַאֲזַנְיָה); KJV: Jezaniah.

H3154 יֶזַע (yezaʻ, yeh'-zah): sweat, i.e. (by implication) a sweating dress. Origin: from an unused root mean to ooze; KJV: any thing that causeth sweat.

H3155 יִזְרָח (Yizrâch, yiz-rawkh'): a Jizrach (i.e. Ezrachite or Zarchite) or descendant of Zerach. Origin: a variation for H250 (אֶזְרָחִי); KJV: Izrahite.

H3156 יִזְרַחְיָה (Yizrachyâh, yiz-rakh-yaw'): Jizrachjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2224 (זָרַח) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will shine; KJV: Izrahiah, Jezrahiah.

H3157 יִזְרְעֵאל (Yizrᵉʻêʼl, yiz-reh-ale'): Jizreel, the name of two places in Palestine and of two Israelites. Origin: from H2232 (זָרַע) and H410 (אֵל); God will sow; KJV: Jezreel.

H3158 יִזְרְעֵאלִי (Yizrᵉʻêʼlîy, yiz-reh-ay-lee'): a Jizreelite or native of Jizreel. Origin: patronymically from H3157 (יִזְרְעֵאל); KJV: Jezreelite.

H3159 יִזְרְעֵאלִית (Yizrᵉʻêʼlîyth, yiz-reh-ay-leeth'): a Jezreelitess. Origin: feminine of H3158 (יִזְרְעֵאלִי); KJV: Jezreelitess.

H3160 יְחֻבָּה (Yᵉchubbâh, yekh-oob-baw'): Jechubbah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2247 (חָבָה); hidden; KJV: Jehubbah.

H3161 יָחַד (yâchad, yaw-khad'): to be (or become) one. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: join, unite.

H3162 יַחַד (yachad, yakh'-ad): properly, a unit, i.e. (adverb) unitedly. Origin: from H3161 (יָחַד); KJV: alike, at all (once), both, likewise, only, (al-) together, withal.

H3163 יַחְדוֹ (Yachdôw, yakh-doe'): Jachdo, an Israelite. Origin: from H3162 (יַחַד) with pronominal suffix; his unity, i.e. (adverb) together; KJV: Jahdo.

H3164 יַחְדִּיאֵל (Yachdîyʼêl, yakh-dee-ale'): Jachdiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H3162 (יַחַד) and H410 (אֵל); unity of God; KJV: Jahdiel.

H3165 יֶחְדִּיָּהוּ (Yechdîyâhûw, yekh-dee-yaw'-hoo): Jechdijah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3162 (יַחַד) and H3050 (יָהּ); unity of Jah; KJV: Jehdeiah.

H3166 יַחֲזִיאֵל (Yachăzîyʼêl, yakh-az-ee-ale'): Jachaziel, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה) and H410 (אֵל); beheld of God; KJV: Jahaziel, Jahziel.

H3167 יַחְזְיָה (Yachzᵉyâh, yakh-zeh-yaw'): Jachzejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will behold; KJV: Jahaziah.

H3168 יְחֶזְקֵאל (Yᵉchezqêʼl, yekh-ez-kale'): Jechezkel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2388 (חָזַק) and H410 (אֵל); God will strengthen; KJV: Ezekiel, Jehezekel.

H3169 יְחִזְקִיָּה (Yᵉchizqîyâh, yekh-iz-kee-yaw'): Jechizkijah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or יְחִזְקִיָּהוּ; from H3388 (יְרוּשָׁא) and H3050 (יָהּ); strengthened of Jah; KJV: Hezekiah, Jehizkiah. Compare H2396 (חִזְקִיָּה).

H3170 יַחְזֵרָה (Yachzêrâh, yakh-zay-raw'): Jachzerah, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H2386 (חֲזִיר); perhaps protection; KJV: Jahzerah.

H3171 יְחִיאֵל (Yᵉchîyʼêl, yekh-ee-ale'): Jechiel (or Jechavel), the name of eight Israelites. Origin: or (2 Chronicles 29:14) יְחַוְאֵל; from H2421 (חָיָה) and H410 (אֵל); God will live; KJV: Jehiel.

H3172 יְחִיאֵלִי (Yᵉchîyʼêlîy, yekh-ee-ay-lee'): a Jechielite or descendant of Jechiel. Origin: patronymically from H3171 (יְחִיאֵל); KJV: Jehieli.

H3173 יָחִיד (yâchîyd, yaw-kheed'): properly, united, i.e. sole; by implication, beloved; also lonely; (feminine) the life (as not to be replaced). Origin: from H3161 (יָחַד); KJV: darling, desolate, only (child, son), solitary.

H3174 יְחִיָּה (Yᵉchîyâh, yekh-ee-yaw'): Jechijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H2421 (חָיָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will live; KJV: Jehiah.

H3175 יָחִיל (yâchîyl, yaw-kheel'): expectant. Origin: from H3176 (יָחַל); KJV: should hope.

H3176 יָחַל (yâchal, yaw-chal'): to wait; by implication, to be patient, hope. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to, have, make to) hope, be pained, stay, tarry, trust, wait.

H3177 יַחְלְאֵל (Yachlᵉʼêl, yakh-leh-ale'): Jachleel, an Israelite. Origin: from H3176 (יָחַל) and H410 (אֵל); expectant of God; KJV: Jahleel.

H3178 יַחְלְאֵלִי (Yachlᵉʼêlîy, yakh-leh-ay-lee'): a Jachleelite or descendant of Jachleel. Origin: patronymically from H3177 (יַחְלְאֵל); KJV: Jahleelites.

H3179 יָחַם (yâcham, yaw-kham'): probably to be hot; figuratively, to conceive. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: get heat, be hot, conceive, be warm.

H3180 יַחְמוּר (yachmûwr, yakh-moor'): a kind of deer. Origin: from H2560 (חָמַר); KJV: fallow deer.

H3181 יַחְמַי (Yachmay, yakh-mah'-ee): Jachmai, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H3179 (יָחַם); hot; KJV: Jahmai.

H3182 יָחֵף (yâchêph, yaw-khafe'): unsandalled. Origin: from an unused root meaning to take off the shoes; KJV: barefoot, being unshod.

H3183 יַחְצְאֵל (Yachtsᵉʼêl, yakh-tseh-ale'): Jachtseel, an Israelite. Origin: from H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה and H410 (אֵל); God will allot; KJV: Jahzeel. Compare H3185 (יַחְצִיאֵל).

H3184 יַחְצְאֵלִי (Yachtsᵉʼêlîy, yakh-tseh-ay-lee'): a Jachtseelite (collectively) or descendants of Jachtseel. Origin: patronymically from H3183 (יַחְצְאֵל); KJV: Jahzeelites.

H3185 יַחְצִיאֵל (Yachtsîyʼêl, yakh-tsee-ale'): Jachtsiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה and H410 (אֵל); allotted of God; KJV: Jahziel. Compare H3183 (יַחְצְאֵל).

H3186 יָחַר (yâchar, yaw-khar'): to delay. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tarry longer.

H3187 יָחַשׂ (yâchas, yaw-khas'): to enroll by pedigree. Origin: a primitive root; to sprout; used only as denominative from H3188 (יַחַשׂ); KJV: (number after, number throughout the) genealogy (to be reckoned), be reckoned by genealogies.

H3188 יַחַשׂ (yachas, yakh'-as): a pedigree or family list (as growing spontaneously). Origin: from H3187 (יָחַשׂ); KJV: genealogy.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3189 to H3304
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3189 יַחַת (Yachath, yakh'-ath): Jachath, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H3161 (יָחַד); unity; KJV: Jahath.

H3190 יָטַב (yâṭab, yaw-tab'): to be (causative) make well, literally (sound, beautiful) or figuratively (happy, successful, right). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be accepted, amend, use aright, benefit, be (make) better, seem best, make cheerful, be comely, [phrase] be content, diligent(-ly), dress, earnestly, find favour, give, be glad, do (be, make) good(-ness), be (make) merry, please ([phrase] well), shew more (kindness), skilfully, [idiom] very small, surely, make sweet, thoroughly, tire, trim, very, be (can, deal, entreat, go, have) well (said, seen).

H3191 יְטַב (yᵉṭab, yet-ab'): {to be (causative) make well, literally (sound, beautiful) or figuratively (happy, successful, right)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3190 (יָטַב) KJV: seem good.

H3192 יׇטְבָה (Yoṭbâh, yot-baw'): Jotbah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3190 (יָטַב); pleasantness; KJV: Jotbah.

H3193 יׇטְבָתָה (Yoṭbâthâh, yot-baw'-thaw): Jotbathah, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H3192 (יׇטְבָה); KJV: Jotbath, Jotbathah.

H3194 יֻטָּה (Yuṭṭâh, yoo-taw'): Juttah (or Jutah), a place in Palestine. Origin: or יוּטָה; from H5186 (נָטָה); extended; KJV: Juttah.

H3195 יְטוּר (Yᵉṭûwr, yet-oor'): Jetur, a son of Ishmael. Origin: probably from the same as H2905 (טוּר); encircled (i.e. inclosed); KJV: Jetur.

H3196 יַיִן (yayin, yah'-yin): wine (as fermented); by implication, intoxication. Origin: from an unused root meaning to effervesce; KJV: banqueting, wine, wine(-bibber).

H3197 יַךְ (yak, yak): a hand or side. Origin: by erroneous transcription for H3027 (יָד); KJV: (way-) side.

H3198 יָכַח (yâkach, yaw-kahh'): to be right (i.e. correct); reciprocal, to argue; causatively, to decide, justify or convict. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, argue, chasten, convince, correct(-ion), daysman, dispute, judge, maintain, plead, reason (together), rebuke, reprove(-r), surely, in any wise.

H3199 יָכִין (Yâkîyn, yaw-keen'): Jakin, the name of three Israelites and of a temple pillar. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); he (or it) will establish; KJV: Jachin.

H3200 יָכִינִי (Yâkîynîy, yaw-kee-nee'): a Jakinite (collectively) or descendants of Jakin. Origin: patronymically from H3199 (יָכִין)lemma יִכִין first vowel, corrected to יָכִין; KJV: Jachinites.

H3201 יָכֹל (yâkôl, yaw-kole'): to be able, literally (can, could) or morally (may, might). Origin: or (fuller) יָכוֹל; a primitive root; KJV: be able, any at all (ways), attain, can (away with, (-not)), could, endure, might, overcome, have power, prevail, still, suffer.

H3202 יְכֵל (yᵉkêl, yek-ale'): {to be able, literally (can, could) or morally (may, might)}. Origin: (Aramaic) or יְכִיל; (Aramaic), to H3201 (יָכֹל) KJV: be able, can, couldest, prevail.

H3203 יְכׇלְיָה (Yᵉkolyâh, yek-ol-yaw'): Jekoljah or Jekiljah, an Israelitess. Origin: and יְכׇלְיָהוּ; or (2 Chronicles 26:3) יְכִילְיָה; from H3201 (יָכֹל) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will enable; KJV: Jecholiah, Jecoliah.

H3204 יְכׇנְיָה (Yᵉkonyâh, yek-on-yaw'): Jekonjah, a Jewish king. Origin: and יְכׇנְיָהוּ; or (Jeremiah 27:20) יְכוֹנְיָה; from H3559 (כּוּן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will establish; KJV: Jeconiah. Compare H3659 (כׇּנְיָהוּ).

H3205 יָלַד (yâlad, yaw-lad'): to bear young; causatively, to beget; medically, to act as midwife; specifically, to show lineage. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear, beget, birth(-day), born, (make to) bring forth (children, young), bring up, calve, child, come, be delivered (of a child), time of delivery, gender, hatch, labour, (do the office of a) midwife, declare pedigrees, be the son of, (woman in, woman that) travail(-eth, -ing woman).

H3206 יֶלֶד (yeled, yeh'-led): something born, i.e. a lad or offspring. Origin: from H3205 (יָלַד); KJV: boy, child, fruit, son, young man (one).

H3207 יַלְדָּה (yaldâh, yal-daw'): a lass. Origin: feminine of H3206 (יֶלֶד); KJV: damsel, girl.

H3208 יַלְדוּת (yaldûwth, yal-dooth'): boyhood (or girlhood). Origin: abstractly from H3206 (יֶלֶד); KJV: childhood, youth.

H3209 יִלּוֹד (yillôwd, yil-lode'): born. Origin: passive from H3205 (יָלַד); KJV: born.

H3210 יָלוֹן (Yâlôwn, yaw-lone'): Jalon, an Israelite. Origin: from H3885 (לוּן); lodging; KJV: Jalon.

H3211 יָלִיד (yâlîyd, yaw-leed'): born. Origin: from H3205 (יָלַד); KJV: (home-) born, child, son.

H3212 יָלַךְ (yâlak, yaw-lak'): to walk (literally or figuratively); causatively, to carry (in various senses). H3213 יָלַל (yâlal, yaw-lal'): to howl (with a wailing tone) or yell (with a boisterous one). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make to) howl, be howling.

H3214 יְלֵל (yᵉlêl, yel-ale'): a howl. Origin: from H3213 (יָלַל); KJV: howling.

H3215 יְלָלָה (yᵉlâlâh, yel-aw-law'): {a howl}. Origin: feminine of H3214 (יְלֵל) KJV: a howling.

H3216 יָלַע (yâlaʻ, yaw-lah'): to blurt or utter inconsiderately. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: devour.

H3217 יַלֶּפֶת (yallepheth, yal-leh'-feth): scurf or tetter. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to stick or scrape; KJV: scabbed.

H3218 יֶלֶק (yeleq, yeh'-lek): a devourer; specifically, the young locust. Origin: from an unused root meaning to lick up; KJV: cankerworm, caterpillar.

H3219 יַלְקוּט (yalqûwṭ, yal-koot'): a travelling pouch (as if for gleanings). Origin: from H3950 (לָקַט); KJV: scrip.

H3220 יָם (yâm, yawm): a sea (as breaking in noisy surf) or large body of water; specifically (with the article), the Mediterranean Sea; sometimes a large river, or an artifical basin; locally, the west, or (rarely) the south. Origin: from an unused root meaning to roar; KJV: sea ([idiom] -faring man, (-shore)), south, west (-ern, side, -ward).

H3221 יָם (yâm, yawm): {a sea (as breaking in noisy surf) or large body of water; specifically (with the article), the Mediterranean Sea; sometimes a large river, or an artifical basin; locally, the west, or (rarely) the south}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3220 (יָם) KJV: sea.

H3222 יֵם (yêm, yame): a warm spring. Origin: from the same as H3117 (יוֹם); KJV: mule.

H3223 יְמוּאֵל (Yᵉmûwʼêl, yem-oo-ale'): Jemuel, an Israelite. Origin: from H3117 (יוֹם) and H410 (אֵל); day of God; KJV: Jemuel.

H3224 יְמִימָה (Yᵉmîymâh, yem-ee-maw'): Jemimah, one of Job's daughters. Origin: perhaps from the same as H3117 (יוֹם); properly, warm, i.e. affectionate; hence, dove (compare H3123 (יוֹנָה)); KJV: Jemimah.

H3225 יָמִין (yâmîyn, yaw-meen'): the right hand or side (leg, eye) of a person or other object (as the stronger and more dexterous); locally, the south. Origin: from H3231 (יָמַן); KJV: [phrase] left-handed, right (hand, side), south.

H3226 יָמִין (Yâmîyn, yaw-meen'): Jamin, the name of three Israelites. Origin: the same as H3225 (יָמִין); KJV: Jamin. See also H1144 (בִּנְיָמִין).

H3227 יְמִינִי (yᵉmîynîy, yem-ee-nee'): right. Origin: for H3225 (יָמִין); KJV: (on the) right (hand).

H3228 יְמִינִי (Yᵉmîynîy, yem-ee-nee'): a Jeminite (collectively) or descendants of Jamin. Origin: patronymically from H3226 (יָמִין); KJV: Jaminites. See also H1145 (בֶּן־יְמִינִי).

H3229 יִמְלָא (Yimlâʼ, yeem-law'): Jimla or Jimlah, an Israelite. Origin: or יִמְלָה; from H4390 (מָלֵא); full; KJV: Imla, Imlah.

H3230 יַמְלֵךְ (Yamlêk, yam-lake'): Jamlek, an Israelite. Origin: from H4427 (מָלַךְ); he will make king; KJV: Jamlech.

H3231 יָמַן (yâman, yaw-man'): to be right-handed or take the right-hand side. Origin: a primitive root; to be (physically) right (i.e. firm); but used only as denominative from H3225 (יָמִין) and transitive, KJV: go (turn) to (on, use) the right hand.

H3232 יִמְנָה (Yimnâh, yim-naw'): Jimnah, the name of two Israelites; also (with the article) of the posterity of one of them. Origin: from H3231 (יָמַן); prosperity (as betokened by the right hand); KJV: Imna, Imnah, Jimnah, Jimnites.

H3233 יְמָנִי (yᵉmânîy, yem-aw-nee'): right (i.e. at the right hand). Origin: from H3231 (יָמַן); KJV: (on the) right (hand).

H3234 יִמְנָע (Yimnâʻ, yim-naw'): Jimna, an Israelite. Origin: from H4513 (מָנַע); he will restrain; KJV: Imna.

H3235 יָמַר (yâmar, yaw-mar'): to exchange; by implication, to change places. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: boast selves, change.

H3236 יִמְרָה (Yimrâh, yim-raw'): Jimrah, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H3235 (יָמַר); interchange; KJV: Imrah.

H3237 יָמַשׁ (yâmash, yaw-mash'): to touch. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: feel.

H3238 יָנָה (yânâh, yaw-naw'): to rage or be violent; by implication, to suppress, to maltreat. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destroy, (thrust out by) oppress(-ing, -ion, -or), proud, vex, do violence.

H3239 יָנוֹחַ (Yânôwach, yaw-no'-akh or (with enclitic) Yanowchah yaw-no'-khaw): Janoach or Janochah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3240 (יָנַח); quiet; KJV: Janoah, Janohah.

H3240 יָנַח (yânach, yaw-nakh'): to deposit; by implication, to allow to stay. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bestow, cast down, lay (down, up), leave (off), let alone (remain), pacify, place, put, set (down), suffer, withdraw, withhold. (The Hiphil forms with the dagesh are here referred to, in accordance with the older grammarians; but if any distinction of the kind is to be made, these should rather be referred to H5117 (נוּחַ), and the others here.)

H3241 יָנִים (Yânîym, yaw-neem'): Janim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5123 (נוּם); asleep; KJV: Janum (from the margin).

H3242 יְנִיקָה (yᵉnîyqâh, yen-ee-kaw'): a sucker or sapling. Origin: from H3243 (יָנַק); KJV: young twig.

H3243 יָנַק (yânaq, yaw-nak'): to suck; causatively, to give milk. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: milch, nurse(-ing mother), (give, make to) suck(-ing child, -ling).

H3244 יַנְשׁוּף (yanshûwph, yan-shoof'): an unclean (acquatic) bird; probably the heron (perhaps from its blowing cry, or because the nightheron is meant )). Origin: or יַנְשׁוֹף; apparently from H5398 (נָשַׁף); (compare H5399 (נֶשֶׁף)) KJV: (great) owl.s

H3245 יָסַד (yâçad, yaw-sad'): to set (literally or figuratively); intensively, to found; reflexively, to sit down together, i.e. settle, consult. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, take counsel, establish, (lay the, lay for a) found(-ation), instruct, lay, ordain, set, [idiom] sure.

H3246 יְסֻד (yᵉçud, yes-ood'): a foundation (figuratively, i.e. beginning). Origin: from H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: [idiom] began.

H3247 יְסוֹד (yᵉçôwd, yes-ode'): a foundation (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: bottom, foundation, repairing

H3248 יְסוּדָה (yᵉçûwdâh, yes-oo-daw'): a foundation. Origin: feminine of H3246 (יְסֻד); KJV: foundation.

H3249 יָסוּר (yâçûwr, yaw-soor'): departing. Origin: from H5493 (סוּר); KJV: they that depart

H3250 יִסּוֹר (yiççôwr, yis-sore'): a reprover. Origin: from H3256 (יָסַר); KJV: instruct.

H3251 יָסַךְ (yâçak, yaw-sak'): to pour (intransitive). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be poured.

H3252 יִסְכָּה (Yiçkâh, yis-kaw'): Jiskah, sister of Lot. Origin: from an unused root meaning to watch; observant; KJV: Iscah.

H3253 יִסְמַכְיָהוּ (Yiçmakyâhûw, yis-mak-yaw-hoo'): Jismakjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H5564 (סָמַךְ) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will sustain; KJV: Ismachiah.

H3254 יָסַף (yâçaph, yaw-saf'): to add or augment (often adverbial, to continue to do a thing). H3255 יְסַף (yᵉçaph, yes-af'): {to add or augment (often adverbial, to continue to do a thing)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3254 (יָסַף) KJV: add.

H3256 יָסַר (yâçar, yaw-sar'): to chastise, literally (with blows) or figuratively (with words); hence, to instruct. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind, chasten, chastise, correct, instruct, punish, reform, reprove, sore, teach.

H3257 יָע (yâʻ, yaw): a shovel. Origin: from H3261 (יָעָה); KJV: shovel.

H3258 יַעְבֵּץ (Yaʻbêts, yah-bates'): Jabets, the name of an Israelite, and also of a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to grieve; sorrowful; KJV: Jabez.

H3259 יָעַד (yâʻad, yaw-ad'): to fix upon (by agreement or appointment); by implication, to meet (at a stated time), to summon (to trial), to direct (in a certain quarter or position), to engage (for marriage). H3260 יֶעְדִּי (Yeʻdîy, yed-ee'): Jedi, an Israelite. Origin: from H3259 (יָעַד); appointed; KJV: Iddo (from the margin) See H3035 (יִדּוֹ).

H3261 יָעָה (yâʻâh, yaw-aw'): to brush aside. Origin: a primitive root; apparently KJV: sweep away.

H3262 יְעוּאֵל (Yᵉʻûwʼêl, yeh-oo-ale'): Jeuel, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H3261 (יָעָה) and H410 (אֵל); carried away of God; KJV: Jehiel, Jeiel, Jeuel. Compare H3273 (יְעִיאֵל).

H3263 יְעוּץ (Yᵉʻûwts, yeh-oots'): Jeuts, an Israelite. Origin: from H5779 (עוּץ); counsellor; KJV: Jeuz

H3264 יָעוֹר (yâʻôwr, yaw-ore'): a forest. Origin: a variation of H3298 (יַעֲרֶשְׁיָה); KJV: wood.

H3265 יָעוּר (Yâʻûwr, yaw-oor'): Jaur, an Israelite. Origin: apparently the passive participle of the same as H3293 (יַעַר); wooded; KJV: Jair(from the margin).

H3266 יְעוּשׁ (Yᵉʻûwsh, yeh-oosh'): Jeush, the name of an Edomite and of four Israelites. Origin: from H5789 (עוּשׁ); hasty; KJV: Jehush, Jeush. Compare H3274 (יְעִישׁ).

H3267 יָעַז (yâʻaz, yaw-az'): to be bold or obstinate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fierce.

H3268 יַעֲזִיאֵל (Yaʻăzîyʼêl, yah-az-ee-ale'): Jaaziel, an Israelite. Origin: from H3267 (יָעַז) and H410 (אֵל); emboldened of God; KJV: Jaaziel.

H3269 יַעֲזִיָּהוּ (Yaʻăzîyâhûw, yah-az-ee-yaw'-hoo): Jaazijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3267 (יָעַז) and H3050 (יָהּ); emboldened of Jah; KJV: Jaaziah.

H3270 יַעֲזֵיר (Yaʻăzêyr, yah-az-ayr'): Jaazer or Jazer, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: or יַעְזֵר; from H5826 (עָזַר); helpful; KJV: Jaazer, Jazer.

H3271 יָעַט (yâʻaṭ, yaw-at'): to clothe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover.

H3272 יְעַט (yᵉʻaṭ, yeh-at'): to counsel; reflexively, to consult. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3289 (יָעַץ); KJV: counsellor, consult together.

H3273 יְעִיאֵל (Yᵉʻîyʼêl, yeh-ee-ale'): Jeiel, the name of six Israelites. Origin: from H3261 (יָעָה) and H410 (אֵל); carried away of God; KJV: Jeiel, Jehiel. Compare H3262 (יְעוּאֵל).

H3274 יְעִישׁ (Yᵉʻîysh, yeh-eesh'): Jeish, the name of an Edomite and of a an Israelite. Origin: from H5789 (עוּשׁ); hasty; KJV: Jeush (from the margin). Compare H3266 (יְעוּשׁ).

H3275 יַעְכָּן (Yaʻkân, yah-kawn'): Jakan, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H5912 (עָכָן); troublesome; KJV: Jachan.

H3276 יַעַל (yaʻal, yaw-al'): properly, to ascend; figuratively, to be valuable (objectively; useful, subjectively; benefited). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, set forward, can do good, (be, have) profit, (able).

H3277 יָעֵל (yâʻêl, yaw-ale'): an ibex (as climbing). Origin: from H3276 (יַעַל); KJV: wild goat.

H3278 יָעֵל (Yâʻêl, yaw-ale'): Jael, a Canaanite. Origin: the same as H3277 (יָעֵל); KJV: Jael.

H3279 יַעֲלָא (Yaʻălâʼ, yah-al-aw'): Jaala or Jaalah, one of the Nethinim. Origin: or יַעֲלָה; the same as H3280 (יַעֲלָה) or direct from H3276 (יַעַל); KJV: Jaala, Jaalah.

H3280 יַעֲלָה (yaʻălâh, yah-al-aw'): {an ibex (as climbing)}. Origin: feminine of H3277 (יָעֵל) KJV: roe.

H3281 יַעְלָם (Yaʻlâm, yah-lawm'): Jalam, an Edomite. Origin: from H5956 (עָלַם); occult; KJV: Jalam.

H3282 יַעַן (yaʻan, yah'-an): properly, heed; by implication, purpose (sake or account); used adverbially to indicate the reason or cause. Origin: from an unused root meaning to pay attention; KJV: because (that), forasmuch ([phrase] as), seeing then, [phrase] that, [phrase] wheras, [phrase] why.

H3283 יָעֵן (yâʻên, yaw-ane'): the ostrich (probably from its answering cry. Origin: from the same as H3282 (יַעַן); KJV: ostrich.

H3284 יַעֲנָה (yaʻănâh, yah-an-aw'): {the ostrich (probably from its answering cry}. Origin: feminine of H3283 (יָעֵן), and meaning the same KJV: [phrase] owl.

H3285 יַעֲנַי (Yaʻănay, yah-an-ah'ee): Jaanai, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H3283 (יָעֵן); responsive; KJV: Jaanai.

H3286 יָעַף (yâʻaph, yaw-af'): to tire (as if from wearisome flight). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: faint, cause to fly, (be) weary (self).

H3287 יָעֵף (yâʻêph, yaw-afe'): fatigued; figuratively, exhausted. Origin: from H3286 (יָעַף); KJV: faint, weary.

H3288 יְעָף (yᵉʻâph, yeh-awf'): fatigue (adverb, utterly exhausted). Origin: from H3286 (יָעַף); KJV: swiftly.e

H3289 יָעַץ (yâʻats, yaw-ats'): to advise; reflexively, to deliberate or resolve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: advertise, take advise, advise (well), consult, (give, take) counsel(-lor), determine, devise, guide, purpose.

H3290 יַעֲקֹב (Yaʻăqôb, yah-ak-obe'): Jaakob, the Israelitish patriarch. Origin: from H6117 (עָקַב); heel-catcher (i.e. supplanter); KJV: Jacob.

H3291 יַעֲקֹבָה (Yaʻăqôbâh, yah-ak-o'-baw): Jaakobah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3290 (יַעֲקֹב); KJV: Jaakobah.

H3292 יַעֲקָן (Yaʻăqân, yah-ak-awn'): Jaakan, an Idumaean. Origin: from the same as H6130 (עָקָן); KJV: Jaakan. Compare H1142 (בְּנֵי יַעֲקָן).

H3293 יַעַר (yaʻar, yah'-ar): a copse of bushes; hence, a forest; hence, honey in the comb (as hived in trees). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to thicken with verdure; KJV: (honey-) comb, forest, wood.

H3295 יַעֲרָה (yaʻărâh, yah-ar-aw'): {a copse of bushes; hence, a forest; hence, honey in the comb (as hived in trees)}. Origin: feminine of H3293 (יַעַר), and meaning the same KJV: (honey-) comb, forest.

H3296 יַעֲרֵי אֹרְגִים (Yaʻărêy ʼÔrᵉgîym, yah-ar-ay' o-reg-eem'): Jaare-Oregim, an Israelite. Origin: from the plural of H3293 (יַעַר) and the masculine plural active participle of H707 (אָרַג); woods of weavers; KJV: Jaare-oregim.

H3297 יְעָרִים (Yᵉʻârîym, yeh-aw-reem'): Jearim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H3293 (יַעַר); forests; KJV: Jearim. Compare H7157 (קִרְיַת יְעָרִים).

H3298 יַעֲרֶשְׁיָה (Yaʻăreshyâh, yah-ar-esh-yaw'): Jaareshjah, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain signification and H3050 (יָהּ); KJV: Jaresiah.

H3299 יַעֲשׂוּ (Yaʻăsûw, yah-as-oo'): Jaasu, an Israelite. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה); they will do; KJV: Jaasau.

H3300 יַעֲשִׂיאֵל (Yaʻăsîyʼêl, yah-as-ee-ale'): Jaasiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה) and H410 (אֵל); made of God; KJV: Jaasiel, Jasiel.

H3301 יִפְדְּיָה (Yiphdᵉyâh, yif-deh-yaw'): Jiphdejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H6299 (פָּדָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will liberate; KJV: Iphedeiah.

H3302 יָפָה (yâphâh, yaw-faw'): properly, to be bright, i.e. (by implication) beautiful. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be beautiful, be (make self) fair(-r), deck.

H3303 יָפֶה (yâpheh, yaw-feh'): beautiful (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H3302 (יָפָה); KJV: [phrase] beautiful, beauty, comely, fair(-est, one), [phrase] goodly, pleasant, well.

H3304 יְפֵה־פִיָּה (yᵉphêh-phîyâh, yef-eh' fee-yaw'): very beautiful. Origin: from H3302 (יָפָה) by reduplication; KJV: very fair.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3305 to H3421
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3305 יָפוֹ (Yâphôw, yaw-fo'): Japho, a place in Palestine. Origin: or יָפוֹא; (Ezra 3:7), from H3302 (יָפָה); beautiful; KJV: Japha, Joppa.

H3306 יָפַח (yâphach, yaw-fakh'): properly, to breathe hard, i.e. (by implication) to sigh. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bewail self.

H3307 יָפֵחַ (yâphêach, yaw-fay'-akh): properly, puffing, i.e. (figuratively) meditating. Origin: from H3306 (יָפַח); KJV: such as breathe out.

H3308 יֳפִי (yŏphîy, yof-ee'): beauty. Origin: from H3302 (יָפָה); KJV: beauty.

H3309 יָפִיעַ (Yâphîyaʻ, yaw-fee'-ah): Japhia, the name of a Canaanite, an Israelite, and a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3313 (יָפַע); bright; KJV: Japhia.

H3310 יַפְלֵט (Yaphlêṭ, yaf-late'): Japhlet, an Israelite. Origin: from H6403 (פָּלַט); he will deliver; KJV: Japhlet.

H3311 יַפְלֵטִי (Yaphlêṭîy, yaf-lay-tee'): a Japhletite or descendant of Japhlet. Origin: patronymically from H3310 (יַפְלֵט); KJV: Japhleti.

H3312 יְפֻנֶּה (Yᵉphunneh, yef-oon-neh'): Jephunneh, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6437 (פָּנָה); he will be prepared; KJV: Jephunneh.

H3313 יָפַע (yâphaʻ, yaw-fah'): to shine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be light, shew self, (cause to) shine (forth).

H3314 יִפְעָה (yiphʻâh, yif-aw'): splendor or (figuratively) beauty. Origin: from H3313 (יָפַע); KJV: brightness.

H3315 יֶפֶת (Yepheth, yeh'-feth): Jepheth, a son of Noah; also his posterity. Origin: from H6601 (פָּתָה); expansion; KJV: Japheth.

H3316 יִפְתָּח (Yiphtâch, yif-tawkh'): Jiphtach, an Israelite; also a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6605 (פָּתַח); he will open; KJV: Jephthah, Jiphtah.

H3317 יִפְתַּח־אֵל (Yiphtach-ʼêl, yif-tach-ale'): Jiphtach-el, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6605 (פָּתַח) and H410 (אֵל); God will open; KJV: Jiphthah-el.

H3318 יָצָא (yâtsâʼ, yaw-tsaw'): to go (causatively, bring) out, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, direct and proxim. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] after, appear, [idiom] assuredly, bear out, [idiom] begotten, break out, bring forth (out, up), carry out, come (abroad, out, thereat, without), [phrase] be condemned, depart(-ing, -ure), draw forth, in the end, escape, exact, fail, fall (out), fetch forth (out), get away (forth, hence, out), (able to, cause to, let) go abroad (forth, on, out), going out, grow, have forth (out), issue out, lay (lie) out, lead out, pluck out, proceed, pull out, put away, be risen, [idiom] scarce, send with commandment, shoot forth, spread, spring out, stand out, [idiom] still, [idiom] surely, take forth (out), at any time, [idiom] to (and fro), utter.

H3319 יְצָא (yᵉtsâʼ, yets-aw'): {to go (causatively, bring) out, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively, direct and proxim.}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3318 (יָצָא) KJV: finish.

H3320 יָצַב (yâtsab, yaw-tsab'): to place (any thing so as to stay); reflexively, to station, offer, continue. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: present selves, remaining, resort, set (selves), (be able to, can, with-) stand (fast, forth, -ing, still, up).

H3321 יְצַב (yᵉtsab, yets-abe'): to be firm; hence, to speak surely. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3320 (יָצַב); KJV: truth.

H3322 יָצַג (yâtsag, yaw-tsag'): to place permanently. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: establish, leave, make, present, put, set, stay.

H3323 יִצְהָר (yitshâr, yits-hawr'): oil (as producing light); figuratively, anointing. Origin: from H6671 (צָהַר); KJV: [phrase] anointed oil.

H3324 יִצְהָר (Yitshâr, yits-hawr'): Jitshar, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H3323 (יִצְהָר); KJV: Izhar.

H3325 יִצְהָרִי (Yitshârîy, yits-haw-ree'): a Jitsharite or descendant of Jitshar. Origin: patronymically from H3324 (יִצְהָר); KJV: Izeharites, Izharites.

H3326 יָצוּעַ (yâtsûwaʻ, yaw-tsoo'-ah): spread, i.e. a bed; (architecture) an extension, i.e. wing or lean-to (a single story or collectively). Origin: passive participle of H3331 (יַצַע); KJV: bed, chamber, couch.

H3327 יִצְחָק (Yitschâq, yits-khawk'): Jitschak (or Isaac), son of Abraham. Origin: from H6711 (צָחַק); laughter (i.e. mochery); KJV: Isaac. Compare H3446 (יִשְׂחָק).

H3328 יִצְחַר (Yitschar, yits-khar'): Jitschar, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H6713 (צַחַר); he will shine; KJV: and Zehoar (from the margin).

H3329 יָצִיא (yâtsîyʼ, yaw-tsee'): issue, i.e. offspring. Origin: from H3318 (יָצָא); KJV: those that came forth.

H3330 יַצִּיב (yatstsîyb, yats-tseeb'): fixed, sure; concretely, certainty. Origin: (Aramaic) from H3321 (יְצַב)lemma יְצב missing vowel, corrected to יְצַבxlit yᵉtsêb corrected to yᵉtsab; KJV: certain(-ty), true, truth.

H3331 יַצַע (yatsaʻ, yaw-tsah'): to strew as a surface. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make (one's) bed, [idiom] lie, spread.

H3332 יָצַק (yâtsaq, yaw-tsak'): properly, to pour out (transitive or intransitive); by implication, to melt or cast as metal; by extension, to place firmly, to stiffen or grow hard. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast, cleave fast, be (as) firm, grow, be hard, lay out, molten, overflow, pour (out), run out, set down, stedfast.

H3333 יְצֻקָה (yᵉtsuqâh, yets-oo-kaw'): poured out, i.e. run into amould. Origin: passive participle feminine of H3332 (יָצַק); KJV: when it was cast.

H3334 יָצַר (yâtsar, yaw-tsar'): to press (intransitive), i.e. be narrow; figuratively, be in distress. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be distressed, be narrow, be straitened (in straits), be vexed.

H3335 יָצַר (yâtsar, yaw-tsar'): to mould into a form; especially as apotter; figuratively, to determine (i.e. form a resolution). Origin: probably identical with H3334 (יָצַר) (through the squeezing into shape); (compare H3331 (יַצַע)); KJV: [idiom] earthen, fashion, form, frame, make(-r), potter, purpose.

H3336 יֵצֶר (yêtser, yay'-tser): a form; figuratively, conception (i.e. purpose). Origin: from H3335 (יָצַר); KJV: frame, thing framed, imagination, mind, work.

H3337 יֵצֶר (Yêtser, yay-tser): Jetser, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H3336 (יֵצֶר); KJV: Jezer.

H3338 יָצֻר (yâtsur, yaw-tsoor'): structure, i.e. limb or part. Origin: passive participle of H3335 (יָצַר); KJV: member.ql

H3339 יִצְרִי (Yitsrîy, yits-ree'): Jitsri, an Israelite. Origin: from H3335 (יָצַר); formative; KJV: Isri.

H3340 יִצְרִי (Yitsrîy, yits-ree'): a Jitsrite (collectively) or descendants of Jetser. Origin: ; patronymically from H3337 (יֵצֶר); KJV: Jezerites.

H3341 יָצַת (yâtsath, yaw-tsath'): to burn or set on fire; figuratively, to desolate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn (up), be desolate, set (on) fire (fire), kindle.

H3342 יֶקֶב (yeqeb, yeh'-keb): a trough (as dug out); specifically, a wine-vat (whether the lower one, into which the juice drains; or the upper, in which the grapes are crushed). Origin: from an unused root meaning to excavate; KJV: fats, presses, press-fat, wine(-press).

H3343 יְקַבְצְאֵל (Yᵉqabtsᵉʼêl, yek-ab-tseh-ale'): Jekabtseel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6908 (קָבַץ) and H410 (אֵל); God will gather; KJV: Jekabzeel. Compare H6909 (קַבְצְאֵל).

H3344 יָקַד (yâqad, yaw-kad'): to burn. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) burn(-ing), [idiom] from the hearth, kindle.

H3345 יְקַד (yᵉqad, yek-ad'): {to burn}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3344 (יָקַד) KJV: burning.

H3346 יְקֵדָא (yᵉqêdâʼ, yek-ay-daw'): a conflagration. Origin: (Aramaic) from H3345 (יְקַד); KJV: burning.

H3347 יׇקְדְעָם (Yoqdᵉʻâm, yok-deh-awm'): Jokdeam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3344 (יָקַד) and H5971 (עַם); burning of (the) people; KJV: Jokdeam.

H3348 יָקֶה (Yâqeh, yaw-keh'): Jakeh, a symbolical name (for Solomon). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to obey; obedient; KJV: Jakeh.

H3349 יִקָּהָה (yiqqâhâh, yik-kaw-haw'): obedience. Origin: from the same as H3348 (יָקֶה); KJV: gathering, to obey.

H3350 יְקוֹד (yᵉqôwd, yek-ode'): a burning. Origin: from H3344 (יָקַד); KJV: burning.

H3351 יְקוּם (yᵉqûwm, yek-oom'): properly, standing (extant), i.e. by implication, a living thing. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); KJV: (living) substance.

H3352 יָקוֹשׁ (yâqôwsh, yaw-koshe'): properly, entangling; hence, a snarer. Origin: from H3369 (יָקֹשׁ); KJV: fowler.

H3353 יָקוּשׁ (yâqûwsh, yaw-koosh'): properly, entangled, i.e. by implication (intransitively) a snare, or (transitive) a snarer. Origin: passive participle of H3369 (יָקֹשׁ); KJV: fowler, snare.

H3354 יְקוּתִיאֵל (Yᵉqûwthîyʼêl, yek-ooth-ee'-ale): Jekuthiel, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H3348 (יָקֶה) and H410 (אֵל); obedience of God; KJV: Jekuthiel.

H3355 יׇקְטָן (Yoqṭân, yok-tawn'): Joktan, an Arabian patriarch. Origin: from H6994 (קָטֹן); he will be made little; KJV: Joktan.

H3356 יָקִים (Yâqîym, yaw-keem'): Jakim, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); he will raise; KJV: Jakim. Compare H3079 (יְהוֹיָקִים).

H3357 יַקִּיר (yaqqîyr, yak-keer'): precious. Origin: from H3365 (יָקַר); KJV: dear.

H3358 יַקִּיר (yaqqîyr, yak-keer'): {precious}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3357 (יַקִּיר) KJV: noble, rare.

H3359 יְקַמְיָה (Yᵉqamyâh, yek-am-yaw'): Jekamjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will rise; KJV: Jekamiah. Compare H3079 (יְהוֹיָקִים).

H3360 יְקַמְעָם (Yᵉqamʻâm, yek-am'-awm): Jekamam, an Israelite. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם) and H5971 (עַם); (the) people will rise; KJV: Jekameam. Compare H3079 (יְהוֹיָקִים), H3361 (יׇקְמְעָם).

H3361 יׇקְמְעָם (Yoqmᵉʻâm, yok-meh-awm'): Jokmeam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם) and H5971 (עַם); (the) people will be raised; KJV: Jokmeam. Compare H3360 (יְקַמְעָם), H3362 (יׇקְנְעָם).

H3362 יׇקְנְעָם (Yoqnᵉʻâm, yok-neh-awm'): Jokneam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6969 (קוּן) and H5971 (עַם); (the) people will be lamented; KJV: Jokneam.

H3363 יָקַע (yâqaʻ, yaw-kah'): properly, to sever oneself, i.e. (by implication) to be dislocated; figuratively, to abandon; causatively, to impale (and thus allow to drop to pieces by rotting). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be alienated, depart, hang (up), be out of joint.

H3364 יָקַץ (yâqats, yaw-kats'): to awake (intransitive). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) awake(-d).

H3365 יָקַר (yâqar, yaw-kar'): properly, apparently, to be heavy, i.e. (figuratively) valuable; causatively, to make rare (figuratively, to inhibit). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (make) precious, be prized, be set by, withdraw.

H3366 יְקָר (yᵉqâr, yek-awr'): value, i.e. (concretely) wealth; abstractly, costliness, dignity. Origin: from H3365 (יָקַר); KJV: honour, precious (things), price.

H3367 יְקָר (yᵉqâr, yek-awr'): {value, i.e. (concretely) wealth; abstractly, costliness, dignity}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3366 (יְקָר) KJV: glory, honour.

H3368 יָקָר (yâqâr, yaw-kawr'): valuable (objectively or subjectively). Origin: from H3365 (יָקַר); KJV: brightness, clear, costly, excellent, fat, honourable women, precious, reputation.

H3369 יָקֹשׁ (yâqôsh, yaw-koshe'): to ensnare (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fowler (lay a) snare.
