H3370 יׇקְשָׁן (Yoqshân, yok-shawn'): Jokshan, an Arabian patriarch. Origin: from H3369 (יָקֹשׁ); insidious; KJV: Jokshan.

H3371 יׇקְתְאֵל (Yoqthᵉʼêl, yok-theh-ale'): Joktheel, the name of a place in Palestine, and of one in Idumaea. Origin: probably from the same as H3348 (יָקֶה) and H410 (אֵל); veneration of God (compare H3354 (יְקוּתִיאֵל)); KJV: Joktheel.

H3372 יָרֵא (yârêʼ, yaw-ray'): to fear; morally, to revere; caus. to frighten. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: affright, be (make) afraid, dread(-ful), (put in) fear(-ful, -fully, -ing), (be had in) reverence(-end), [idiom] see, terrible (act, -ness, thing).

H3373 יָרֵא (yârêʼ, yaw-ray'): fearing; morally, reverent. Origin: from H3372 (יָרֵא); KJV: afraid, fear (-ful).

H3374 יִרְאָה (yirʼâh, yir-aw'): fear (also used as infinitive); morally, reverence. Origin: feminine of H3373 (יָרֵא); KJV: [idiom] dreadful, [idiom] exceedingly, fear(-fulness).

H3375 יִרְאוֹן (Yirʼôwn, yir-ohn'): Jiron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3372 (יָרֵא); fearfulness; KJV: Iron.

H3376 יִרְאִיָּיה (Yirʼîyâyh, yir-ee-yaw'): Jirijah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3373 (יָרֵא) and H3050 (יָהּ); fearful of Jah; KJV: Irijah.

H3377 יָרֵב (Yârêb, yaw-rabe'): Jareb, a symbolical name for Assyria. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב); he will contend; KJV: Jareb. Compare H3402 (יָרִיב).

H3378 יְרֻבַּעַל (Yᵉrubbaʻal, yer-oob-bah'-al): Jerubbaal, a symbolic name of Gideon. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב) and H1168 (בַּעַל); Baal will contend; KJV: Jerubbaal.

H3379 יָרׇבְעָם (Yârobʻâm, yaw-rob-awm'): Jarobam, the name of two Israelite kings. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב) and H5971 (עַם); (the) people will contend; KJV: Jeroboam.

H3380 יְרֻבֶּשֶׁת (Yᵉrubbesheth, yer-oob-beh'-sheth): Jerubbesheth, a symbolic name for Gideon. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב) and H1322 (בֹּשֶׁת); shame (i.e. the idol) will contend; KJV: Jerubbesheth.

H3381 יָרַד (yârad, yaw-rad'): to descend (literally, to go downwards; or conventionally to a lower region, as the shore, a boundary, the enemy, etc.; or figuratively, to fall); causatively, to bring down (in all the above applications). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] abundantly, bring down, carry down, cast down, (cause to) come(-ing) down, fall (down), get down, go(-ing) down(-ward), hang down, [idiom] indeed, let down, light (down), put down (off), (cause to, let) run down, sink, subdue, take down.

H3382 יֶרֶד (Yered, yeh'-red): Jered, the name of an antediluvian, and of an Israelite. Origin: from H3381 (יָרַד); a descent; KJV: Jared.

H3383 יַרְדֵּן (Yardên, yar-dane'): Jarden, the principal river of Palestine. Origin: from H3381 (יָרַד); a descender; KJV: Jordan.

H3384 יָרָה (yârâh, yaw-raw'): properly, to flow as water (i.e. to rain); transitively, to lay or throw (especially an arrow, i.e. to shoot); figuratively, to point out (as if by aiming the finger), to teach. Origin: or (2 Chronicles 26:15) יָרָא; a primitive root; KJV: ([phrase]) archer, cast, direct, inform, instruct, lay, shew, shoot, teach(-er,-ing), through.

H3385 יְרוּאֵל (Yᵉrûwʼêl, yer-oo-ale'): Jeruel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3384 (יָרָה) and H410 (אֵל); founded of God; KJV: Jeruel.

H3386 יָרוֹחַ (Yârôwach, yaw-ro'-akh): Jaroach, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps denominative from H3394 (יָרֵחַ); (born at the) new moon; KJV: Jaroah.

H3387 יָרוֹק (yârôwq, yaw-roke'): green, i.e. an herb. Origin: from H3417 (יָרָק); KJV: green thing.

H3388 יְרוּשָׁא (Yᵉrûwshâʼ, yer-oo-shaw'): Jerusha or Jerushah, as Israelitess. Origin: or יְרוּשָׁה feminine passive participle of H3423 (יָרַשׁ); possessed; KJV: Jerusha, Jerushah.

H3389 יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם (Yᵉrûwshâlaim, yer-oo-shaw-lah'-im): Jerushalaim or Jerushalem, the capital city of Palestine. Origin: rarely יְרוּשָׁלַיִם; a dual (in allusion to its two main hills (the true pointing, at least of the former reading, seems to be that of H3390 (יְרוּשָׁלֵם))); probably from (the passive participle of) H3384 (יָרָה) and H7999 (שָׁלַם); founded peaceful; KJV: Jerusalem.

H3390 יְרוּשָׁלֵם (Yᵉrûwshâlêm, yer-oo-shaw-lame'): {Jerusalem}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3389 (יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם) KJV: {Jerusalem}

H3391 יֶרַח (yerach, yeh'-rakh): a lunation, i.e. month. Origin: from a unused root of uncertain signification; KJV: month, moon.

H3392 יֶרַח (Yerach, yeh'-rakh): Jerach, an Arabian patriarch. Origin: the same as H3391 (יֶרַח); KJV: Jerah.

H3393 יְרַח (yᵉrach, yeh-rakh'): a month. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3391 (יֶרַח); KJV: month.

H3394 יָרֵחַ (yârêach, yaw-ray'-akh): the moon. Origin: from the same as H3391 (יֶרַח); KJV: moon. Yrechow. See H3405 (יְרִיחוֹ).

H3395 יְרֹחָם (Yᵉrôchâm, yer-o-khawm'): Jerocham, the name of seven or eight Israelites. Origin: from H7355 (רָחַם); compassionate; KJV: Jeroham.

H3396 יְרַחְמְאֵל (Yᵉrachmᵉʼêl, yer-akh-meh-ale'): Jerachmeel, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H7355 (רָחַם) and H410 (אֵל); God will compassionate; KJV: Jerahmeel.

H3397 יְרַחְמְאֵלִי (Yᵉrachmᵉʼêlîy, yer-akh-meh-ay-lee'): a Jerachmeelite or descendant of Jerachmeel. Origin: patronymically from H3396 (יְרַחְמְאֵל); KJV: Jerahmeelites.

H3398 יַרְחָע (Yarchâʻ, yar-khaw'): Jarcha, an Egyptian. Origin: probably of Egyptian origin; KJV: Jarha.

H3399 יָרַט (yâraṭ, yaw-rat'): to precipitate or hurl (rush) headlong; (intransitively) to be rash. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be perverse, turn over.

H3400 יְרִיאֵל (Yᵉrîyʼêl, yer-ee-ale'): Jeriel, an Israelite. Origin: from H3384 (יָרָה) and H410 (אֵל); thrown of God; KJV: Jeriel. Compare H3385 (יְרוּאֵל).

H3401 יָרִיב (yârîyb, yaw-rebe'): literally he will contend; properly, adjective, contentious; used as noun, an adversary. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב); KJV: that content(-eth), that strive.

H3402 יָרִיב (Yârîyb, yaw-rebe'): Jarib, the name of three Israelites. Origin: the same as H3401 (יָרִיב); KJV: Jarib.

H3403 יְרִיבַי (Yᵉrîybay, yer-eeb-ah'ee): Jeribai, an Israelite. Origin: from H3401 (יָרִיב); contentious; KJV: Jeribai.

H3404 יְרִיָּה (Yᵉrîyâh, yer-ee-yaw'): Jerijah, an Israelite. Origin: or יְרִיָּהוּ; from H3384 (יָרָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will throw; KJV: Jeriah, Jerijah.

H3405 יְרִיחוֹ (Yᵉrîychôw, yer-ee-kho'): Jericho or Jerecho, a place in Palestine. Origin: or יְרֵחוֹ; or variation (1 Kings 16:34) יְרִיחֹה; perhaps from H3394 (יָרֵחַ); its month; or else from H7306 (רוּחַ); fragrant; KJV: Jericho.

H3406 יְרִימוֹת (Yᵉrîymôwth, yer-ee-mohth'): Jerimoth or Jeremoth, the name of twelve Israelites. Origin: or יְרֵימוֹת; or יְרֵמוֹת; feminine plural from H7311 (רוּם); elevations; KJV: Jermoth, Jerimoth, and Ramoth (from the margin).

H3407 יְרִיעָה (yᵉrîyʻâh, yer-ee-aw'): a hanging (as tremulous). Origin: from H3415 (יָרַע); KJV: curtain.

H3408 יְרִיעוֹת (Yᵉrîyʻôwth, yer-ee-ohth'): Jerioth, an Israelitess. Origin: plural of H3407 (יְרִיעָה); curtains; KJV: Jerioth.

H3409 יָרֵךְ (yârêk, yaw-rake'): the thigh (from its fleshy softness); by euphemistically the generative parts; figuratively, a shank, flank, side. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be soft; KJV: [idiom] body, loins, shaft, side, thigh.

H3410 יַרְכָא (yarkâʼ, yar-kaw'): a thigh. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3411 (יְרֵכָה); KJV: thigh.

H3411 יְרֵכָה (yᵉrêkâh, yer-ay-kaw'): properly, the flank; but used only figuratively, the rear or recess. Origin: feminine of H3409 (יָרֵךְ); KJV: border, coast, part, quarter, side.

H3412 יַרְמוּת (Yarmûwth, yar-mooth'): Jarmuth, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from H7311 (רוּם); elevation; KJV: Jarmuth.

H3413 יְרֵמַי (Yᵉrêmay, yer-ay-mah'-ee): Jeremai, an Israelite. Origin: from H7311 (רוּם); elevated; KJV: Jeremai.

H3414 יִרְמְיָה (Yirmᵉyâh, yir-meh-yaw'): Jirmejah, the name of eight or nine Israelites. Origin: or יִרְמְיָהוּ; from H7311 (רוּם) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will rise; KJV: Jeremiah.

H3415 יָרַע (yâraʻ, yaw-rah'): properly, to be broken up (with any violent action) i.e. (figuratively) to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be grevious (only Isaiah 15:4; the rest belong to H7489 (רָעַע)).

H3416 יִרְפְּאֵל (Yirpᵉʼêl, yir-peh-ale'): Jirpeel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7495 (רָפָא) and H410 (אֵל); God will heal; KJV: Irpeel.

H3417 יָרָק (yârâq, yaw-rak'): to spit. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] but, spit.

H3418 יֶרֶק (yereq, yeh'-rek): properly, pallor, i.e. hence, the yellowish green of young and sickly vegetation; concretely, verdure, i.e. grass or vegetation. Origin: from H3417 (יָרָק) (in the sense of vacuity of color); KJV: grass, green (thing).

H3419 יָרָק (yârâq, yaw-rawk'): properly, green; concretely, a vegetable. Origin: from the same as H3418 (יֶרֶק); KJV: green, herbs.

H3420 יֵרָקוֹן (yêrâqôwn, yay-raw-kone'): paleness, whether of persons (from fright), or of plants (from drought). Origin: from H3418 (יֶרֶק); KJV: greenish, yellow.

H3421 יׇרְקְעָם (Yorqᵉʻâm, yor-keh-awm'): Jorkeam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7324 (רוּק) and H5971 (עַם); people will be poured forth; KJV: Jorkeam.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3422 to H3536
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3422 יְרַקְרַק (yᵉraqraq, yer-ak-rak'): yellowishness. Origin: from the same as H3418 (יֶרֶק); KJV: greenish, yellow.

H3423 יָרַשׁ (yârash, yaw-rash'): to occupy (by driving out previous tenants, and possessing in their place); by implication, to seize, to rob, to inherit; also to expel, to impoverish, to ruin. Origin: or יָרֵשׁ; a primitive root; KJV: cast out, consume, destroy, disinherit, dispossess, drive(-ing) out, enjoy, expel, [idiom] without fail, (give to, leave for) inherit(-ance, -or) [phrase] magistrate, be (make) poor, come to poverty, (give to, make to) possess, get (have) in (take) possession, seize upon, succeed, [idiom] utterly.

H3424 יְרֵשָׁה (yᵉrêshâh, yer-ay-shaw'): occupancy. Origin: from H3423 (יָרַשׁ); KJV: possession.

H3425 יְרֻשָּׁה (yᵉrushshâh, yer-oosh-shaw'): something occupied; a conquest; also a patrimony. Origin: from H3423 (יָרַשׁ); KJV: heritage, inheritance, possession.

H3426 יֵשׁ (yêsh, yaysh): there is or are (or any other form of the verb to be, as may suit the connection). Origin: perhaps from an unused root meaning to stand out, or exist; entity; used adverbially or as a copula for the substantive verb (H1961 (הָיָה)); KJV: (there) are, (he, it, shall, there, there may, there shall, there should) be, thou do, had, hast, (which) hath, (I, shalt, that) have, (he, it, there) is, substance, it (there) was, (there) were, ye will, thou wilt, wouldest.

H3427 יָשַׁב (yâshab, yaw-shab'): properly, to sit down (specifically as judge. in ambush, in quiet); by implication, to dwell, to remain; causatively, to settle, to marry. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make to) abide(-ing), continue, (cause to, make to) dwell(-ing), ease self, endure, establish, [idiom] fail, habitation, haunt, (make to) inhabit(-ant), make to keep (house), lurking, [idiom] marry(-ing), (bring again to) place, remain, return, seat, set(-tle), (down-) sit(-down, still, -ting down, -ting (place) -uate), take, tarry.

H3428 יֶשֶׁבְאָב (Yeshebʼâb, yeh-sheb-awb'): Jeshebab, an Israelite. Origin: from H3427 (יָשַׁב) and H1 (אָב); seat of (his) father; KJV: Jeshebeab.

H3429 יֹשֵׁב בַּשֶּׁבֶת (Yôshêb bash-Shebeth, yo-shabe' bash-sheh'-beth): Joshebbash-Shebeth, an Israelite. Origin: from the active participle of H3427 (יָשַׁב) and H7674 (שֶׁבֶת), with a preposition and the article interposed; sitting in the seat; KJV: that sat in the seat.

H3430 יִשְׁבּוֹ בְּנֹב (Yishbôw bᵉ-Nôb, yish-bo'beh-nobe): Jishbo-be-Nob, a Philistine. Origin: from H3427 (יָשַׁב) and H5011 (נֹב), with a pronominal suffix and a preposition interposed; his dwelling (is) in Nob; KJV: Ishbi-benob (from the margin).

H3431 יִשְׁבַּח (Yishbach, yish-bakh'): Jishbach, an Israelite. Origin: from H7623 (שָׁבַח); he will praise; KJV: Ishbah.

H3432 יָשֻׁבִי (Yâshubîy, yaw-shoo-bee'): a Jashubite, or descendant of Jashub. Origin: patronymically from H3437 (יָשׁוּב); KJV: Jashubites.

H3433 יָשֻׁבִי לֶחֶם (Yâshubîy Lechem, yaw-shoo-bee' leh'-khem): Jashubi-Lechem, an Israelite. Origin: from H7725 (שׁוּב) and H3899 (לֶחֶם); returner of bread; KJV: Jashubi-lehem. (Prob. the text should be pointed יֹשְׁבֵי לֶחֶם and rendered '(they were) inhabitants of Lechem,' i.e. of Bethlehem (by contraction). Compare H3902 (לַחְמִי)).

H3434 יָשׇׁבְעָם (Yâshobʻâm, yaw-shob-awm'): Jashobam, the name of two or three Israelites. Origin: from H7725 (שׁוּב) and H5971 (עַם); people will return; KJV: Jashobeam.

H3435 יִשְׁבָּק (Yishbâq, yish-bawk'): Jishbak, a son of Abraham. Origin: from an unused root corresponding to H7662 (שְׁבַק); he will leave; KJV: Ishbak.

H3436 יׇשְׁבְּקָשָׁה (Yoshbᵉqâshâh, yosh-bek-aw-shaw'): Joshbekashah, an Israelite. Origin: from H3427 (יָשַׁב) and H7186 (קָשֶׁה); a hard seat; KJV: Joshbekashah.

H3437 יָשׁוּב (Yâshûwb, yaw-shoob'): Jashub, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or יָשִׁיב; from H7725 (שׁוּב); he will return; KJV: Jashub.

H3438 יִשְׁוָה (Yishvâh, yish-vaw'): Jishvah, an Israelite. Origin: from H7737 (שָׁוָה); he will level; KJV: Ishvah, Isvah.

H3439 יְשׁוֹחָיָה (Yᵉshôwchâyâh, yesh-o-khaw-yaw'): Jeshochajah, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H3445 (יֶשַׁח) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will empty; KJV: Jeshoaiah.

H3440 יִשְׁוִי (Yishvîy, yish-vee'): Jishvi, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H7737 (שָׁוָה); level; KJV: Ishuai, Ishvi, Isui, Jesui.

H3441 יִשְׁוִי (Yishvîy, yish-vee'): a Jishvite (collectively) or descendants of Jishvi. Origin: patronymically from H3440 (יִשְׁוִי); KJV: Jesuites.

H3442 יֵשׁוּעַ (Yêshûwaʻ, yay-shoo'-ah): Jeshua, the name of ten Israelites, also of a place in Palestine. Origin: for H3091 (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ); he will save; KJV: Jeshua.

H3443 יֵשׁוּעַ (Yêshûwaʻ, yay-shoo'-ah): {Jeshua, the name of ten Israelites, also of a place in Palestine}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3442 (יֵשׁוּעַ) KJV: Jeshua.

H3444 יְשׁוּעָה (yᵉshûwʻâh, yesh-oo'-aw): something saved, i.e. (abstractly) deliverance; hence, aid, victory, prosperity. Origin: feminine passive participle of H3467 (יָשַׁע); KJV: deliverance, health, help(-ing), salvation, save, saving (health), welfare.

H3445 יֶשַׁח (yeshach, yeh'-shakh): hunger. Origin: from an unused root meaning to gape (as the empty stomach); KJV: casting down.

H3446 יִשְׂחָק (Yischâq, yis-khawk'): Jischak, the heir of Abraham. Origin: from H7831 (שַׁחֲצוֹם); he will laugh; KJV: Isaac. Compare H3327 (יִצְחָק).

H3447 יָשַׁט (yâshaṭ, yaw-shat'): to extend. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hold out.

H3448 יִשַׁי (Yishay, yee-shah'-ee): Jishai, David's father. Origin: by Aramaic אִישַׁי; from the same as H3426 (יֵשׁ); extant; KJV: Jesse.

H3449 יִשִּׁיָּה (Yishshîyâh, yish-shee-yaw'): Jishshijah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or יִשִּׁיָּהוּ; from H5383 (נָשָׁה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will lend; KJV: Ishiah, Isshiah, Ishijah, Jesiah.

H3450 יְשִׁימָאֵל (Yᵉshîymâʼêl, yes-eem-aw-ale'): Jesimael, an Israelite. Origin: from H7760 (שׂוּם) and H410 (אֵל); God will place; KJV: Jesimael.

H3451 יְשִׁימַה (yᵉshîymah, yesh-ee-maw'): desolation. Origin: from H3456 (יָשַׁם); KJV: let death seize (from the margin).

H3452 יְשִׁימוֹן (yᵉshîymôwn, yesh-ee-mone'): a desolation. Origin: from H3456 (יָשַׁם); KJV: desert, Jeshimon, solitary, wilderness.

H3453 יָשִׁישׁ (yâshîysh, yaw-sheesh'): an old man. Origin: from H3486 (יָשֵׁשׁ); KJV: (very) aged (man), ancient, very old.

H3454 יְשִׁישָׁי (Yᵉshîyshây, yesh-ee-shah'-ee): Jeshishai, an Israelite. Origin: from H3453 (יָשִׁישׁ); aged; KJV: Jeshishai.

H3455 יָשַׂם (yâsam, yaw-sam'): to place; intransitively, to be placed. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be put (set).

H3456 יָשַׁם (yâsham, yaw-sham'): to lie waste. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be desolate.

H3457 יִשְׁמָא (Yishmâʼ, yish-maw'): Jishma, an Israelite. Origin: from H3456 (יָשַׁם); desolate; KJV: Ishma.

H3458 יִשְׁמָעֵאל (Yishmâʻêʼl, yish-maw-ale'): Jishmael, the name of Abraham's oldest son, and of five Israelites. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע) and H410 (אֵל); God will hear; KJV: Ishmael.

H3459 יִשְׁמָעֵאלִי (Yishmâʻêʼlîy, yish-maw-ay-lee'): a Jishmaelite or descendant of Jishmael. Origin: patronymically from H3458 (יִשְׁמָעֵאל); KJV: Ishmaelite.

H3460 יִשְׁמַעְיָה (Yishmaʻyâh, yish-mah-yaw'): Jishmajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or יִשְׁמַעְיָהוּlemma יְשְׁמַעְיָהוּ first vowel, corrected to יִשְׁמַעְיָהוּ; from H8085 (שָׁמַע) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah will hear; KJV: Ishmaiah.

H3461 יִשְׁמְרַי (Yishmᵉray, yish-mer-ah'-ee): Jishmerai, an Israelite. Origin: from H8104 (שָׁמַר); preservative; KJV: Ishmerai.

H3462 יָשֵׁן (yâshên, yaw-shane'): properly, to be slack or languid, i.e. (by implication) sleep (figuratively, to die); also to grow old, stale or inveterate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: old (store), remain long, (make to) sleep.

H3463 יָשֵׁן (yâshên, yaw-shane'): sleepy. Origin: from H3462 (יָשֵׁן); KJV: asleep, (one out of) sleep(-eth, -ing), slept.

H3464 יָשֵׁן (Yâshên, yaw-shane'): Jashen, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H3463 (יָשֵׁן); KJV: Jashen.

H3465 יָשָׁן (yâshân, yaw-shawn'): old. Origin: from H3462 (יָשֵׁן); KJV: old.

H3466 יְשָׁנָה (Yᵉshânâh, yesh-aw-naw'): Jeshanah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H3465 (יָשָׁן); KJV: Jeshanah.

H3467 יָשַׁע (yâshaʻ, yaw-shah'): properly, to be open, wide or free, i.e. (by implication) to be safe; causatively, to free or succor. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, avenging, defend, deliver(-er), help, preserve, rescue, be safe, bring (having) salvation, save(-iour), get victory.

H3468 יֶשַׁע (yeshaʻ, yeh'-shah): liberty, deliverance, prosperity. Origin: or יֵשַׁע; from H3467 (יָשַׁע); KJV: safety, salvation, saving.

H3469 יִשְׁעִי (Yishʻîy, yish-ee'): Jishi, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H3467 (יָשַׁע); saving; KJV: Ishi.

H3470 יְשַׁעְיָה (Yᵉshaʻyâh, yesh-ah-yaw'): Jeshajah, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: or יְשַׁעְיָהוּ; from H3467 (יָשַׁע) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has saved; KJV: Isaiah, Jesaiah, Jeshaiah.

H3471 יָשְׁפֵה (yâshᵉphêh, yaw-shef-ay'): a gem supposed to be jasper (from the resemblance in name). Origin: from an unused root meaning to polish; KJV: jasper.

H3472 יִשְׁפָּה (Yishpâh, yish-paw'): Jishpah, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H8192 (שָׁפָה); he will scratch; KJV: Ispah.

H3473 יִשְׁפָּן (Yishpân, yish-pawn'): Jishpan, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the same as H8227 (שָׁפָן); he will hide; KJV: Ishpan.

H3474 יָשַׁר (yâshar, yaw-shar'): to be straight or even; figuratively, to be (causatively, to make) right, pleasant, prosperous. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: direct, fit, seem good (meet), [phrase] please (will), be (esteem, go) right (on), bring (look, make, take the) straight (way), be upright(-ly).

H3475 יֵשֶׁר (Yêsher, yay'-sher): Jesher, an Israelite. Origin: from H3474 (יָשַׁר); the right; KJV: Jesher.

H3476 יֹשֶׁר (yôsher, yo'-sher): the right. Origin: from H3474 (יָשַׁר); KJV: equity, meet, right, upright(-ness).

H3477 יָשָׁר (yâshâr, yaw-shawr'): straight (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H3474 (יָשַׁר); KJV: convenient, equity, Jasher, just, meet(-est), [phrase] pleased well right(-eous), straight, (most) upright(-ly, -ness).

H3478 יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yisrâʼêl, yis-raw-ale'): Jisrael, a symbolical name of Jacob; also (typically) of his posterity. Origin: from H8280 (שָׂרָה) and H410 (אֵל); he will rule as God; KJV: Israel.

H3479 יִשְׂרָאֵל (Yisrâʼêl, yis-raw-ale'): {Jisrael, a symbolical name of Jacob; also (typically) of his posterity}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3478 (יִשְׂרָאֵל) KJV: Israel.

H3480 יְשַׂרְאֵלָה (Yᵉsarʼêlâh, yes-ar-ale'-aw): Jesarelah, an Israelite. Origin: by variation from H3477 (יָשָׁר) and H410 (אֵל) with directive enclitic; right towards God; KJV: Jesharelah.

H3481 יִשְׂרְאֵלִי (Yisrᵉʼêlîy, yis-reh-ay-lee'): a Jisreelite or descendant of Jisrael. Origin: patronymically from H3478 (יִשְׂרָאֵל); KJV: of Israel, Israelite.

H3482 יִשְׂרְאֵלִית (Yisrᵉʼêlîyth, yis-reh-ay-leeth'): a Jisreelitess or female descendant of Jisrael. Origin: feminine of H3481 (יִשְׂרְאֵלִי); KJV: Israelitish.

H3483 יִשְׁרָה (yishrâh, yish-raw'): rectitude. Origin: feminine of H3477 (יָשָׁר); KJV: uprightness.

H3484 יְשֻׁרוּן (Yᵉshurûwn, yesh-oo-roon'): Jeshurun, a symbolic name for Israel. Origin: from H3474 (יָשַׁר); upright; KJV: Jeshurun.

H3485 יִשָּׂשכָר (Yissâˢkâr, yis-saw-kawr'): Jissaskar, a son of Jacob. Origin: (strictly yis-saws-kawr'); from H5375 (נָשָׂא) and H7939 (שָׂכָר); he will bring a reward; KJV: Issachar.

H3486 יָשֵׁשׁ (yâshêsh, yaw-shaysh'): gray-haired, i.e. an aged man. Origin: from an unused root meaning to blanch; KJV: stoop for age.

H3487 יַת (yath, yath): a sign of the object of a verb. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H853 (אֵת); KJV: [phrase] whom.

H3488 יְתִב (yᵉthib, yeth-eeb'): to sit or dwell. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3427 (יָשַׁב); KJV: dwell, (be) set, sit.

H3489 יָתֵד (yâthêd, yaw-thade'): a peg. Origin: from an unused root meaning to pin through or fast; KJV: nail, paddle, pin, stake.

H3490 יָתוֹם (yâthôwm, yaw-thome'): a bereaved person. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be lonely; KJV: fatherless (child), orphan.

H3491 יָתוּר (yâthûwr, yaw-thoor'): properly, what is left, i.e. (by implication) a gleaning. Origin: passive participle of H3498 (יָתַר); KJV: range.

H3492 יַתִּיר (Yattîyr, yat-teer'): Jattir, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); redundant; KJV: Jattir.

H3493 יַתִּיר (yattîyr, yat-teer'): preeminent; as an adverb, very. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3492 (יַתִּיר); KJV: exceeding(-ly), excellent.

H3494 יִתְלָה (Yithlâh, yith-law'): Jithlah, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H8518 (תָּלָה); it will hang, i.e. be high; KJV: Jethlah.

H3495 יִתְמָה (Yithmâh, yith-maw'): Jithmah, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H3490 (יָתוֹם); orphanage; KJV: Ithmah.

H3496 יַתְנִיאֵל (Yathnîyʼêl, yath-nee-ale'): Jathniel, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to endure, and H410 (אֵל); continued of God; KJV: Jathniel.

H3497 יִתְנָן (Yithnân, yith-nawn'): Jithnan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H8577 (תַּנִּין); extensive; KJV: Ithnan.

H3498 יָתַר (yâthar, yaw-thar'): to jut over or exceed; by implication, to excel; (intransitively) to remain or be left; causatively, to leave, cause to abound, preserve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: excel, leave (a remnant), left behind, too much, make plenteous, preserve, (be, let) remain(-der, -ing, -nant), reserve, residue, rest.

H3499 יֶתֶר (yether, yeh'-ther): properly, an overhanging, i.e. (by implication) an excess, superiority, remainder; also a small rope (as hanging free). Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); KJV: [phrase] abundant, cord, exceeding, excellancy(-ent), what they leave, that hath left, plentifully, remnant, residue, rest, string, with.

H3500 יֶתֶר (Yether, yeh'-ther): Jether, the name of five or six Israelites and of one Midianite. Origin: the same as H3499 (יֶתֶר); KJV: Jether, Jethro. Compare H3503 (יִתְרוֹ).

H3501 יִתְרָא (Yithrâʼ, yith-raw'): Jithra, an Israelite (or Ishmaelite). Origin: by variation for H3502 (יִתְרָה); KJV: Ithra.

H3502 יִתְרָה (yithrâh, yith-raw'): properly, excellence, i.e. (by implication) wealth. Origin: feminine of H3499 (יֶתֶר); KJV: abundance, riches.

H3503 יִתְרוֹ (Yithrôw, yith-ro'): Jethro, Moses' father-in-law. Origin: from H3499 (יֶתֶר) with pron. suffix; his excellence; KJV: Jethro. Compare H3500 (יֶתֶר).

H3504 יִתְרוֹן (yithrôwn, yith-rone'): preeminence, gain. Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); KJV: better, excellency(-leth), profit(-able).

H3505 יִתְרִי (Yithrîy, yith-ree'): a Jithrite or descendant of Jether. Origin: patronymically from H3500 (יֶתֶר); KJV: Ithrite.

H3506 יִתְרָן (Yithrân, yith-rawn'): Jithran, the name of an Edomite and of an Israelite. Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); excellent; KJV: Ithran.

H3507 יִתְרְעָם (Yithrᵉʻâm, yith-reh-awm'): Jithream, a son of David. Origin: from H3499 (יֶתֶר) and H5971 (עַם); excellence of people; KJV: Ithream.

H3508 יֹתֶרֶת (yôthereth, yo-theh'-reth): the lobe or flap of the liver (as if redundant or outhanging). Origin: feminine active participle of H3498 (יָתַר); KJV: caul.

H3509 יְתֵת (Yᵉthêth, yeh-thayth'): Jetheth, an Edomite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Jetheth. k

H3510 כָּאַב (kâʼab, kaw-ab'): properly, to feel pain; by implication, to grieve; figuratively, to spoil. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: grieving, mar, have pain, make sad (sore), (be) sorrowful.

H3511 כְּאֵב (kᵉʼêb, keh-abe'): suffering (physical or mental), adversity. Origin: from H3510 (כָּאַב); KJV: grief, pain, sorrow.

H3512 כָּאָה (kâʼâh, kaw-aw'): to despond; causatively, to deject. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: broken, be grieved, make sad.

H3513 כָּבַד (kâbad, kaw-bad'): to be heavy, i.e. in a bad sense (burdensome, severe, dull) or in a good sense (numerous, rich, honorable; causatively, to make weighty (in the same two senses). Origin: or כָּבֵד; a primitive root; KJV: abounding with, more grievously afflict, boast, be chargeable, [idiom] be dim, glorify, be (make) glorious (things), glory, (very) great, be grievous, harden, be (make) heavy, be heavier, lay heavily, (bring to, come to, do, get, be had in) honour (self), (be) honourable (man), lade, [idiom] more be laid, make self many, nobles, prevail, promote (to honour), be rich, be (go) sore, stop.

H3514 כֹּבֶד (kôbed, ko'-bed): weight, multitude, vehemence. Origin: from H3513 (כָּבַד); KJV: grievousness, heavy, great number.

H3515 כָּבֵד (kâbêd, kaw-bade'): heavy; figuratively in a good sense (numerous) or in a bad sense (severe, difficult, stupid). Origin: from H3513 (כָּבַד); KJV: (so) great, grievous, hard(-ened), (too) heavy(-ier), laden, much, slow, sore, thick.

H3516 כָּבֵד (kâbêd, kaw-bade'): the liver (as the heaviest of the viscera). Origin: the same as H3515 (כָּבֵד); KJV: liver.

H3517 כְּבֵדֻת (kᵉbêduth, keb-ay-dooth'): difficulty. Origin: feminine of H3515 (כָּבֵד); KJV: [idiom] heavily.

H3518 כָּבָה (kâbâh, kaw-baw'): to expire or (causatively) to extinguish (fire, light, anger). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: go (put) out, quench.

H3519 כָּבוֹד (kâbôwd, kaw-bode'): properly, weight, but only figuratively in a good sense, splendor or copiousness. Origin: rarely כָּבֹד; from H3513 (כָּבַד); KJV: glorious(-ly), glory, honour(-able).

H3520 כְּבוּדָּה (kᵉbûwddâh, keb-ood-daw'): weightiness, i.e. magnificence, wealth. Origin: irregular feminine passive participle of H3513 (כָּבַד); KJV: carriage, all glorious, stately.

H3521 כָּבוּל (Kâbûwl, kaw-bool'): Cabul, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H3525 (כֶּבֶל) in the sense of limitation; sterile; KJV: Cabul.

H3522 כַּבּוֹן (Kabbôwn, kab-bone'): Cabon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root meaning to heap up; hilly; KJV: Cabbon.

H3523 כְּבִיר (kᵉbîyr, keb-eer): a matrass (of intertwined materials). Origin: from H3527 (כָּבַר) in the original sense of plaiting; KJV: pillow.

H3524 כַּבִּיר (kabbîyr, kab-beer'): vast, whether in extent (figuratively, of power, mighty; of time, aged), or in number, many. Origin: from H3527 (כָּבַר); KJV: [phrase] feeble, mighty, most, much, strong, valiant.

H3525 כֶּבֶל (kebel, keh'-bel): a fetter. Origin: from an unused root meaning to twine or braid together; KJV: fetter.

H3526 כָּבַס (kâbaç, kaw-bas'): to trample; hence, to wash (properly, by stamping with the feet), whether literal (including the fulling process) or figurative. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fuller, wash(-ing).

H3527 כָּבַר (kâbar, kaw-bar'): properly, to plait together, i.e. (figuratively) to augment (especially in number or quantity, to accumulate). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: in abundance, multiply.

H3528 כְּבָר (kᵉbâr, keb-awr'): properly, extent of time, i.e. a great while; hence, long ago, formerly, hitherto. Origin: from H3527 (כָּבַר); KJV: already, (seeing that which), now.

H3529 כְּבָר (Kᵉbâr, keb-awr'): Kebar, a river of Mesopotamia. Origin: the same as H3528 (כְּבָר); length; KJV: Chebar. Compare H2249 (חָבוֹר).

H3530 כִּבְרָה (kibrâh, kib-raw'): properly, length, i.e. a measure (of uncertain dimension). Origin: feminine of H3528 (כְּבָר); KJV: [idiom] little.

H3531 כְּבָרָה (kᵉbârâh, keb-aw-raw'): a sieve (as netted). Origin: from H3527 (כָּבַר) in its original sense; KJV: sieve.

H3532 כֶּבֶשׂ (kebes, keh-bes'): a ram (just old enough to butt). Origin: from an unused root meaning to dominate; KJV: lamb, sheep.

H3533 כָּבַשׁ (kâbash, kaw-bash'): to tread down; hence, negatively, to disregard; positively, to conquer, subjugate, violate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring into bondage, force, keep under, subdue, bring into subjection.

H3534 כֶּבֶשׁ (kebesh, keh'-besh): a footstool (as trodden upon). Origin: from H3533 (כָּבַשׁ); KJV: footstool.

H3535 כִּבְשָׂה (kibsâh, kib-saw'): a ewe. Origin: or כַּבְשָׂה; feminine of H3532 (כֶּבֶשׂ); KJV: (ewe) lamb.

H3536 כִּבְשָׁן (kibshân, kib-shawn'): a smelting furnace (as reducing metals). Origin: from H3533 (כָּבַשׁ); KJV: furnace.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3537 to H3647
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3537 כַּד (kad, kad): properly, a pail; but generally of earthenware; a jar for domestic purposes. Origin: from an unused root meaning to deepen; KJV: barrel, pitcher.

H3538 כְּדַב (kᵉdab, ked-ab'): false. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H3576 (כָּזַב); KJV: lying.

H3539 כַּדְכֹּד (kadkôd, kad-kode'): a sparkling gem, probably the ruby. Origin: from the same as H3537 (כַּד) in the sense of striking fire from a metal forged; KJV: agate.

H3540 כְּדׇרְלָעֹמֶר (Kᵉdorlâʻômer, ked-or-law-o'-mer): Kedorlaomer, an early Persian king. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Chedorlaomer.

H3541 כֹּה (kôh, ko): properly, like this, i.e. by implication, (of manner) thus (or so); also (of place) here (or hither); or (of time) now. Origin: from the prefix k and H1931 (הוּא); KJV: also, here, + hitherto, like, on the other side, so (and much), such, on that manner, (on) this (manner, side, way, way and that way), + mean while, yonder.

H3542 כָּה (kâh, kaw): {properly, like this, i.e. by implication, (of manner) thus (or so); also (of place) here (or hither); or (of time) now}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3541 (כֹּה) KJV: hitherto.

H3543 כָּהָה (kâhâh, kaw-haw'): to be weak, i.e. (figuratively) to despond (causatively, rebuke), or (of light, the eye) to grow dull. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: darken, be dim, fail, faint, restrain, [idiom] utterly.

H3544 כֵּהֶה (kêheh, kay-heh'): feeble, obscure. Origin: from H3543 (כָּהָה); KJV: somewhat dark, darkish, wax dim, heaviness, smoking.

H3545 כֵּהָה (kêhâh, kay-haw'): properly, a weakening; figuratively, alleviation, i.e. cure. Origin: feminine of H3544 (כֵּהֶה); KJV: healing.

H3546 כְּהַל (kᵉhal, keh-hal'): to be able. Origin: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to and H3557 (כּוּל); KJV: be able, could.

H3547 כָּהַן (kâhan, kaw-han'): to officiate as a priest; figuratively, to put on regalia. Origin: a primitive root, apparently meaning to mediate in religious services; but used only as denominative from H3548 (כֹּהֵן); KJV: deck, be (do the office of a, execute the, minister in the) priest('s office).

H3548 כֹּהֵן (kôhên, ko-hane'): literally one officiating, a priest; also (by courtesy) an acting priest (although a layman). Origin: active participle of H3547 (כָּהַן); KJV: chief ruler, [idiom] own, priest, prince, principal officer.

H3549 כָּהֵן (kâhên, kaw-hane'): {one officiating, a priest; also (by courtesy) an acting priest (although a layman)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3548 (כֹּהֵן) KJV: priest.

H3550 כְּהֻנָּה (kᵉhunnâh, keh-hoon-naw'): priesthood. Origin: from H3547 (כָּהַן); KJV: priesthood, priest's office.

H3551 כַּו (kav, kav): a window (as a perforation). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H3854 (לַהַג) in the sense of piercing; KJV: window.

H3552 כּוּב (Kûwb, koob): Kub, a country near Egypt. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Chub.

H3553 כּוֹבַע (kôwbaʻ, ko'-bah): a helmet (as arched). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be high or rounded; KJV: helmet. Compare H6959 (קוֹבַע).

H3554 כָּוָה (kâvâh, kaw-vaw'): properly, to prick or penetrate; hence, to blister (as smarting or eating into). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn.

H3555 כְּוִיָּה (kᵉvîyâh, kev-ee-yaw'): a branding. Origin: from H3554 (כָּוָה); KJV: burning.

H3556 כּוֹכָב (kôwkâb, ko-kawb'): a star (as round or as shining); figuratively, a prince. Origin: probably from the same as H3522 (כַּבּוֹן) (in the sense of rolling) or H3554 (כָּוָה) (in the sense of blazing); KJV: star(-gazer).

H3557 כּוּל (kûwl, kool): properly, to keep in; hence, to measure; figuratively, to maintain (in various senses). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be able to, can) abide, bear, comprehend, contain, feed, forbearing, guide, hold(-ing in), nourish(-er), be present, make provision, receive, sustain, provide sustenance (victuals).

H3558 כּוּמָז (kûwmâz, koo-mawz'): a jewel (probably gold beads). Origin: from an unused root meaning to store away; KJV: tablet.

H3559 כּוּן (kûwn, koon): properly, to be erect (i.e. stand perpendicular); hence (causatively) to set up, in a great variety of applications, whether literal (establish, fix, prepare, apply), or figurative (appoint, render sure, proper or prosperous). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: certain(-ty), confirm, direct, faithfulness, fashion, fasten, firm, be fitted, be fixed, frame, be meet, ordain, order, perfect, (make) preparation, prepare (self), provide, make provision, (be, make) ready, right, set (aright, fast, forth), be stable, (e-) stablish, stand, tarry, [idiom] very deed.

H3560 כּוּן (Kûwn, koon): Kun, a place in Syria. Origin: probably from H3559 (כּוּן); established; KJV: Chun.

H3561 כַּוָּן (kavvân, kav-vawn'): something prepared, i.e. a sacrificial wafer. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); KJV: cake.

H3562 כּוֹנַנְיָהוּ (Kôwnanyâhûw, ko-nan-yaw'-hoo): Conanjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has sustained; KJV: Conaniah, Cononiah. Compare H3663 (כְּנַנְיָה).

H3563 כּוֹס (kôwç, koce): a cup (as a container), often figuratively, a lot (as if a potion); also some unclean bird, probably an owl (perhaps from the cup-like cavity of its eye). Origin: from an unused root meaning to hold together; KJV: cup, (small) owl. Compare H3599 (כִּיס).

H3564 כּוּר (kûwr, koor): a pot or furnace (as if excavated). Origin: from an unused root meaning properly, to dig through; KJV: furnace. Compare H3600 (כִּיר).

H3565 כּוֹר עָשָׁן (Kôwr ʻÂshân, kore aw-shawn'): Cor-Ashan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3564 (כּוּר) and H6227 (עָשָׁן); furnace of smoke; KJV: Chorashan.

H3566 כּוֹרֶשׁ (Kôwresh, ko'-resh): Koresh (or Cyrus), the Persian king. Origin: or (Ezra 1:1 (last time),2) כֹּרֶשׁ; from the Persians; KJV: Cyrus.

H3567 כּוֹרֶשׁ (Kôwresh, ko'-resh): {Koresh (or Cyrus), the Persian king}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3566 (כּוֹרֶשׁ) KJV: Cyrus.

H3568 כּוּשׁ (Kûwsh, koosh): Cush (or Ethiopia), the name of a son of Ham, and of his territory; also of an Israelite. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Chush, Cush, Ethiopia.

H3569 כּוּשִׁי (Kûwshîy, koo-shee'): a Cushite, or descendant of Cush. Origin: patronymically from H3568 (כּוּשׁ); KJV: Cushi, Cushite, Ethiopian(-s).

H3570 כּוּשִׁי (Kûwshîy, koo-shee'): Cushi, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H3569 (כּוּשִׁי); KJV: Cushi.

H3571 כּוּשִׁית (Kûwshîyth, koo-sheeth'): a Cushite woman. Origin: feminine of H3569 (כּוּשִׁי); KJV: Ethiopian.

H3572 כּוּשָׁן (Kûwshân, koo-shawn'): Cushan, a region of Arabia. Origin: perhaps from H3568 (כּוּשׁ); KJV: Cushan.

H3573 כּוּשַׁן רִשְׁעָתַיִם (Kûwshan Rishʻâthayim, koo-shan' rish-awthah'-yim): Cushan-Rishathajim, a Mesopotamian king. Origin: apparently from H3572 (כּוּשָׁן) and the dual of H7564 (רִשְׁעָה); Cushan of double wickedness; KJV: Chushan-rishathayim.

H3574 כּוֹשָׁרָה (kôwshârâh, ko-shaw-raw'): prosperity; in plural freedom. Origin: from H3787 (כָּשֵׁר); KJV: [idiom] chain.

H3575 כּוּת (Kûwth, kooth): Cuth or Cuthah, a province of Assyria. Origin: or (feminine) כּוּתָה; of foreign origin; KJV: Cuth.

H3576 כָּזַב (kâzab, kaw-zab'): to lie (i.e. deceive), literally or figuratively. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fail, (be found a, make a) liar, lie, lying, be in vain.

H3577 כָּזָב (kâzâb, kaw-zawb'): falsehood; literally (untruth) or figuratively (idol). Origin: from H3576 (כָּזַב); KJV: deceitful, false, leasing, + liar, lie, lying.

H3578 כֹּזְבָא (Kôzᵉbâʼ, ko-zeb-aw'): Cozeba, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3576 (כָּזַב); fallacious; KJV: Choseba.

H3579 כֹּזְבִי (Kôzᵉbîy, koz-bee'): Cozbi, a Midianitess. Origin: from H3576 (כָּזַב); false; KJV: Cozbi.

H3580 כְּזִיב (Kᵉzîyb, kez-eeb'): Kezib, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3576 (כָּזַב); falsified; KJV: Chezib.

H3581 כֹּחַ (kôach, ko'-akh): vigor, literally (force, in a good or a bad sense) or figuratively (capacity, means, produce); also (from its hardiness) a large lizard. Origin: or (Daniel 11:6) כּוֹחַ; from an unused root meaning to be firm; KJV: ability, able, chameleon, force, fruits, might, power(-ful), strength, substance, wealth.

H3582 כָּחַד (kâchad, kaw-khad'): to secrete, by act or word; hence (intensively) to destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: conceal, cut down (off), desolate, hide.

H3583 כָּחַל (kâchal, kaw-khal'): to paint (with stibium). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: paint.

H3584 כָּחַשׁ (kâchash, kaw-khash'): to be untrue, in word (to lie, feign, disown) or deed (to disappoint, fail, cringe). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deceive, deny, dissemble, fail, deal falsely, be found liars, (be-) lie, lying, submit selves.

H3585 כַּחַשׁ (kachash, kakh'-ash): literally a failure of flesh, i.e. emaciation; figuratively, hypocrisy. Origin: from H3584 (כָּחַשׁ); KJV: leanness, lies, lying.

H3586 כֶּחָשׁ (kechâsh, kekh-awsh'): faithless. Origin: from H3584 (כָּחַשׁ); KJV: lying.

H3587 כִּי (kîy, kee): a brand or scar. Origin: from H3554 (כָּוָה); KJV: burning.

H3588 כִּי (kîy, kee): (by implication) very widely used as a relative conjunction or adverb (as below); often largely modified by other particles annexed. Origin: a primitive particle (the full form of the prepositional prefix) indicating causal relations of all kinds, antecedent or consequent; KJV: and, + (forasmuch, inasmuch, where-) as, assured(-ly), + but, certainly, doubtless, + else, even, + except, for, how, (because, in, so, than) that, + nevertheless, now, rightly, seeing, since, surely, then, therefore, + (al-) though, + till, truly, + until, when, whether, while, whom, yea, yet.

H3589 כִּיד (kîyd, keed): a crushing; figuratively, calamity. Origin: from a primitive root meaning to strike; KJV: destruction.

H3590 כִידוֹד (kîydôwd, kee-dode'): properly, something struck off, i.e. a spark (as struck). Origin: from the same as H3589 (כִּיד) (compare H3539 (כַּדְכֹּד)); KJV: spark.

H3591 כִּידוֹן (kîydôwn, kee-dohn'): properly, something to strike with, i.e. a dart. Origin: from the same as H3589 (כִּיד); (perhaps smaller than H2595 (חֲנִית)lemma חֲניִת second vowel, corrected to חֲנִית) KJV: lance, shield, spear, target.

H3592 כִּידוֹן (Kîydôwn, kee-dohn'): Kidon, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3591 (כִּידוֹן); KJV: Chidon.

H3593 כִּידוֹר (kîydôwr, kee-dore'): perhaps tumult. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: battle.

H3594 כִּיּוּן (Kîyûwn, kee-yoon'): properly, a statue, i.e. idol; but used (by euphemism) forsome heathen deity (perhaps corresponding to Priapus or Baal-peor). Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); KJV: Chiun.

H3595 כִּיּוֹר (kîyôwr, kee-yore'): properly, something round (as excavated or bored), i.e. a chafing-dish forcoals or a caldron forcooking; hence (from similarity of form) a washbowl; also (for the same reason) a pulpit or platform. Origin: or כִּיֹּר; from the same as H3564 (כּוּר); KJV: hearth, laver, pan, scaffold.

H3596 כִּילַי (kîylay, kee-lah'-ee): niggardly. Origin: or כֵּלַי; from H3557 (כּוּל) in the sense of withholding; KJV: churl.

H3597 כֵּילַף (kêylaph, kay-laf'): a club or sledge-hammer. Origin: from an unused root meaning to clap or strike with noise; KJV: hammer.

H3598 כִּימָה (Kîymâh, kee-maw'): a cluster of stars, i.e. the Pleiades. Origin: from the same as H3558 (כּוּמָז); KJV: Pleiades, seven stars.

H3599 כִּיס (kîyç, keece): a cup; also a bag formoney or weights. Origin: a form for H3563 (כּוֹס); KJV: bag, cup, purse.

H3600 כִּיר (kîyr, keer): a cooking range (consisting of two parallel stones, across which the boiler is set). Origin: a form for H3564 (כּוּר) (only in the dual); KJV: ranges for pots.

H3601 כִּישׁוֹר (kîyshôwr, kee-shore'): literally a director, i.e. the spindle or shank of adistaff, by which it is twirled. Origin: from H3787 (כָּשֵׁר); compare H6418 (פֶּלֶךְ) KJV: spindle.

H3602 כָּכָה (kâkâh, kaw'-kaw): just so, referring to the previous or following context. Origin: from H3541 (כֹּה); KJV: after that (this) manner, this matter, (even) so, in such a case, thus.

H3603 כִּכָּר (kikkâr, kik-kawr'): a circle, i.e. (by implication) a circumjacent tract or region, especially the Ghor or valley of the Jordan; also a (round) loaf; also a talent (or large [round] coin). Origin: from H3769 (כָּרַר); KJV: loaf, morsel, piece, plain, talent.

H3604 כִּכֵּר (kikkêr, kik-kare'): a talent. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3603 (כִּכָּר); KJV: talent.

H3605 כֹּל (kôl, kole): properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense). Origin: or (Jeremiah 33:8) כּוֹל; from H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: (in) all (manner, (ye)), altogether, any (manner), enough, every (one, place, thing), howsoever, as many as, (no-) thing, ought, whatsoever, (the) whole, whoso(-ever).

H3606 כֹּל (kôl, kole): {properly, the whole; hence, all, any or every (in the singular only, but often in a plural sense)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3605 (כֹּל) KJV: all, any, + (forasmuch) as, + be-(for this) cause, every, + no (manner, -ne), + there (where) -fore, + though, what (where, who) -soever, (the) whole.

H3607 כָּלָא (kâlâʼ, kaw-law'): to restrict, by act (hold back or in) or word (prohibit). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: finish, forbid, keep (back), refrain, restrain, retain, shut up, be stayed, withhold.

H3608 כֶּלֶא (keleʼ, keh'-leh): a prison. Origin: from H3607 (כָּלָא); KJV: prison. Compare H3610 (כִּלְאַיִם), H3628 (כְּלִיא).

H3609 כִּלְאָב (Kilʼâb, kil-awb'): Kilab, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H3607 (כָּלָא) and H1 (אָב); restraint of (his) father; KJV: Chileab.

H3610 כִּלְאַיִם (kilʼayim, kil-ah'-yim): two heterogeneities. Origin: dual of H3608 (כֶּלֶא) in the original sense of separation; KJV: divers seeds (-e kinds), mingled (seed).

H3611 כֶּלֶב (keleb, keh'-leb): a dog; hence (by euphemism) a male prostitute. Origin: from an unused root means. to yelp, or else to attack; KJV: dog.

H3612 כָּלֵב (Kâlêb, kaw-labe'): Caleb, the name of three Israelites. Origin: perhaps a form of H3611 (כֶּלֶב), or else from the same root in the sense of forcible; KJV: Caleb.

H3613 כָּלֵב אֶפְרָתָה (Kâlêb ʼEphrâthâh, kaw-labe' ef-raw'-thaw): Caleb-Ephrathah, a place in Egypt (if the text is correct). Origin: from H3612 (כָּלֵב) and H672 (אֶפְרָת); KJV: Caleb-ephrathah.

H3614 כָּלִבּוֹ (Kâlibbôw, kaw-lib-bo'): a Calebite or descendant of Caleb. Origin: probably by erroneous transcription for כָּלֵבִי; patronymically from H3612 (כָּלֵב); KJV: of the house of Caleb.

H3615 כָּלָה (kâlâh, kaw-law'): to end, whether intransitive (to cease, be finished, perish) or transitived (to complete, prepare, consume). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: accomplish, cease, consume (away), determine, destroy (utterly), be (when... were) done, (be an) end (of), expire, (cause to) fail, faint, finish, fulfil, [idiom] fully, [idiom] have, leave (off), long, bring to pass, wholly reap, make clean riddance, spend, quite take away, waste.

H3616 כָּלֶה (kâleh, kaw-leh'): pining. Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: fail.

H3617 כָּלָה (kâlâh, kaw-law'): a completion; adverb, completely; also destruction. Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: altogether, (be, utterly) consume(-d), consummation(-ption), was determined, (full, utter) end, riddance.

H3618 כַּלָּה (kallâh, kal-law'): a bride (as if perfect); hence, a son's wife. Origin: from H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: bride, daughter-in-law, spouse.

H3619 כְּלוּב (kᵉlûwb, kel-oob'): a bird-trap (as furnished with a clap-stick or treadle to spring it); hence, a basket (as resembling a wicker cage). Origin: from the same as H3611 (כֶּלֶב); KJV: basket, cage.

H3620 כְּלוּב (Kᵉlûwb, kel-oob'): Kelub, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H3619 (כְּלוּב)xlit kᵉlûb corrected to kᵉlûwb; KJV: Chelub.

H3621 כְּלוּבַי (Kᵉlûwbay, kel-oo-bay'-ee): Kelubai, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3612 (כָּלֵב); KJV: Chelubai.

H3622 כְּלוּהַי (Kᵉlûwhay, kel-oo-hah'-ee): Keluhai, an Israelite. Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); completed; KJV: Chelluh.

H3623 כְּלוּלָה (kᵉlûwlâh, kel-oo-law'): bridehood (only in the plural). Origin: denominative passive participle from H3618 (כַּלָּה)lemma כַּלָה missing dagesh, corrected to כַּלָּה; KJV: espousal.

H3624 כֶּלַח (kelach, keh'-lakh): maturity. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be complete; KJV: full (old) age.

H3625 כֶּלַח (Kelach, keh'-lakh): Kelach, a place in Assyria. Origin: the same as H3624 (כֶּלַח); KJV: Calah.

H3626 כׇּל־חֹזֶה (Kol-Chôzeh, kol-kho-zeh'): Col-Chozeh, an Israelite. Origin: from H3605 (כֹּל) and H2374 (חֹזֶה); every seer; KJV: Col-hozeh.

H3627 כְּלִי (kᵉlîy, kel-ee'): something prepared, i.e. any apparatus (as an implement, utensil, dress, vessel or weapon). Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: armour(-bearer), artillery, bag, carriage, [phrase] furnish, furniture, instrument, jewel, that is made of, [idiom] one from another, that which pertaineth, pot, [phrase] psaltery, sack, stuff, thing, tool, vessel, ware, weapon, [phrase] whatsoever.

H3628 כְּלִיא (kᵉlîyʼ, kel-ee'): a prison. Origin: or כְּלוּא; from H3627 (כְּלִי) (compare H3608 (כֶּלֶא)); KJV: prison.

H3629 כִּלְיָה (kilyâh, kil-yaw'): a kidney (as an essential organ); figuratively, the mind (as the interior self). Origin: feminine of H3627 (כְּלִי) (only in the plural); KJV: kidneys, reins.

H3630 כִּלְיוֹן (Kilyôwn, kil-yone'): Kiljon, an Israelite. Origin: a form of H3631 (כִּלָּיוֹן); KJV: Chilion.

H3631 כִּלָּיוֹן (killâyôwn, kil-law-yone'): pining, destruction. Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: consumption, failing.

H3632 כָּלִיל (kâlîyl, kaw-leel'): complete; as noun, the whole (specifically, a sacrifice entirely consumed); as adverb, fully. Origin: from H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: all, every whit, flame, perfect(-ion), utterly, whole burnt offering (sacrifice), wholly.

H3633 כַּלְכֹּל (Kalkôl, kal-kole'): Calcol, an Israelite. Origin: from H3557 (כּוּל); sustenance; KJV: Calcol, Chalcol.

H3634 כָּלַל (kâlal, kaw-lal'): to complete. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make) perfect.

H3635 כְּלַל (kᵉlal, kel-al'): to complete. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: finish, make (set) up.

H3636 כְּלָל (Kᵉlâl, kel-awl'): Kelal, an Israelite. Origin: from H3634 (כָּלַל); complete; KJV: Chelal.

H3637 כָּלַם (kâlam, kaw-lawm'): properly, to wound; but only figuratively, to taunt or insult. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (make) ashamed, blush, be confounded, be put to confusion, hurt, reproach, (do, put to) shame.

H3638 כִּלְמָד (Kilmâd, kil-mawd'): Kilmad, a place apparently in the Assyrian empire. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Chilmad.

H3639 כְּלִמָּה (kᵉlimmâh, kel-im-maw'): disgrace. Origin: from H3637 (כָּלַם); KJV: confusion, dishonour, reproach, shame.

H3640 כְּלִמּוּת (kᵉlimmûwth, kel-im-mooth'): disgrace. Origin: from H3639 (כְּלִמָּה); KJV: shame.

H3641 כַּלְנֶה (Kalneh, kal-neh'): Calneh or Calno, a place in the Assyrian empire. Origin: or כַּלְנֵה; also כַּלְנוֹ; of foreign derivation; KJV: Calneh, Calno. Compare H3656 (כַּנֶּה).

H3642 כָּמַהּ (kâmahh, kaw-mah): to pine after. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: long.

H3643 כִּמְהָם (Kimhâm, kim-hawm'): Kimham, an Israelite. Origin: from H3642 (כָּמַהּ); pining; KJV: Chimham.

H3644 כְּמוֹ (kᵉmôw, kem-o'): a form of the prefix 'k-', but used separately as, thus, so. Origin: or כָּמוֹ; (compare H3651 (כֵּן)); KJV: according to, (such) as (it were, well as), in comparison of, like (as, to, unto), thus, when, worth.

H3645 כְּמוֹשׁ (Kᵉmôwsh, kem-oshe'): Kemosh, the god of the Moabites. Origin: or (Jeremiah 48:7) כְּמִישׁ; from an unused root meaning to subdue; the powerful; KJV: Chemosh.

H3646 כַּמֹּן (kammôn, kam-mone'): 'cummin' (from its use as a condiment). Origin: from an unused root meaning to store up or preserve; KJV: cummin.

H3647 כָּמַס (kâmaç, kaw-mas'): to store away, i.e. (figuratively) in the memory. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lay up in store.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3648 to H3771
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3648 כָּמַר (kâmar, kaw-mar'): properly, to intertwine or contract, i.e. (by implication) to shrivel (as with heat); figuratively, to be deeply affected with passion (love or pity). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be black, be kindled, yearn.

H3649 כָּמָר (kâmâr, kaw-mawr'): properly, an ascetic (as if shrunk with self-maceration), i.e. an idolatrous priest (only in plural). Origin: from H3648 (כָּמַר); KJV: Chemarims (idolatrous) priests.

H3650 כִּמְרִיר (kimrîyr, kim-reer'): obscuration (as if from shrinkage of light, i.e. an eclipse (only in plural). Origin: redupl. from H3648 (כָּמַר); KJV: blackness.

H3651 כֵּן (kên, kane): properly, set upright; hence (figuratively as adjective) just; but usually (as adverb or conjunction) rightly or so (in various applications to manner, time and relation; often with other particles). Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); KJV: [phrase] after that (this, -ward, -wards), as... as, [phrase] (for-) asmuch as yet, [phrase] be (for which) cause, [phrase] following, howbeit, in (the) like (manner, -wise), [idiom] the more, right, (even) so, state, straightway, such (thing), surely, [phrase] there (where) -fore, this, thus, true, well, [idiom] you.

H3652 כֵּן (kên, kane): so. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3651 (כֵּן); KJV: thus.

H3653 כֵּן (kên, kane): a stand, i.e. pedestal or station. Origin: the same as H3651 (כֵּן), used as a noun; KJV: base, estate, foot, office, place, well.

H3654 כֵּן (kên, kane): a gnat. Origin: from H3661 (כָּנַן) in the sense of fastening; (from infixing its sting; used only in plural (and irregular in Exodus 8:17,18; Hebrews 13:14)) KJV: lice, [idiom] manner.

H3655 כָּנָה (kânâh, kaw-naw'): to address by an additional name; hence, to eulogize. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: give flattering titles, surname (himself).

H3656 כַּנֶּה (Kanneh, kan-neh'): Canneh, a place in Assyria. Origin: for H3641 (כַּלְנֶה); KJV: Canneh.

H3657 כַּנָּה (kannâh, kaw-naw'): a plant (as set). Origin: from H3661 (כָּנַן); KJV: [idiom] vineyard.

H3658 כִּנּוֹר (kinnôwr, kin-nore'): a harp. Origin: from a unused root meaning to twang; KJV: harp.

H3659 כׇּנְיָהוּ (Konyâhûw, kon-yaw'-hoo): Conjah, an Israelite king. Origin: for H3204 (יְכׇנְיָה); KJV: Coniah.

H3660 כְּנֵמָא (kᵉnêmâʼ, ken-ay-maw'): so or thus. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3644 (כְּמוֹ); KJV: so, (in) this manner (sort), thus.

H3661 כָּנַן (kânan, kaw-nan'): to set out, i.e. plant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] vineyard.

H3662 כְּנָנִי (Kᵉnânîy, ken-aw-nee'): Kenani, an Israelite. Origin: from H3661 (כָּנַן); planted; KJV: Chenani.

H3663 כְּנַנְיָה (Kᵉnanyâh, ken-an-yaw'): Kenanjah, an Israelite. Origin: or כְּנַנְיָהוּ; from H3661 (כָּנַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has planted; KJV: Chenaniah.

H3664 כָּנַס (kânaç, kaw-nas'): to collect; hence, to enfold. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather (together), heap up, wrap self.

H3665 כָּנַע (kânaʻ, kaw-nah'): properly, to bend the knee; hence, to humiliate, vanquish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring down (low), into subjection, under, humble (self), subdue.

H3666 כִּנְעָה (kinʻâh, kin-aw'): a package. Origin: from H3665 (כָּנַע) in the sense of folding (compare H3664 (כָּנַס)); KJV: wares.

H3667 כְּנַעַן (Kᵉnaʻan, ken-ah'-an): Kenaan, a son a Ham; also the country inhabited by him. Origin: from H3665 (כָּנַע); humiliated; KJV: Canaan, merchant, traffick.

H3668 כְּנַעֲנָה (Kᵉnaʻănâh, ken-ah-an-aw'): Kenaanah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: feminine of H3667 (כְּנַעַן); KJV: Chenaanah.

H3669 כְּנַעַנִי (Kᵉnaʻanîy, ken-ah-an-ee'): a Kenaanite or inhabitant of Kenaan; by implication, a pedlar (the Canaanites standing for their neighbors the Ishmaelites, who conducted mercantile caravans). Origin: patrial from H3667 (כְּנַעַן); KJV: Canaanite, merchant, trafficker.

H3670 כָּנַף (kânaph, kaw-naf'): properly, to project laterally, i.e. probably (reflexive) to withdraw. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be removed.

H3671 כָּנָף (kânâph, kaw-nawf'): an edge or extremity; specifically (of a bird or army) a wing, (of a garment or bedclothing) a flap, (of the earth) a quarter, (of a building) a pinnacle. Origin: from H3670 (כָּנַף); KJV: [phrase] bird, border, corner, end, feather(-ed), [idiom] flying, [phrase] (one an-) other, overspreading, [idiom] quarters, skirt, [idiom] sort, uttermost part, wing(-ed).

H3672 כִּנְּרוֹת (Kinnᵉrôwth, kin-ner-oth'): Kinneroth or Kinnereth, a place in Palestine. Origin: or כִּנֶּרֶתlemma כִּנֶרֶת missing dagesh, corrected to כִּנֶּרֶת; respectively plural and singular feminine from the same as H3658 (כִּנּוֹר); perhaps harp-shaped; KJV: Chinnereth, Chinneroth, Cinneroth.

H3673 כָּנַשׁ (kânash, kaw-nash'): to assemble. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3664 (כָּנַס); KJV: gather together.

H3674 כְּנָת (kᵉnâth, ken-awth'): a colleague (as having the same title). Origin: from H3655 (כָּנָה); KJV: companion.

H3675 כְּנָת (kᵉnâth, ken-awth'): {a colleague (as having the same title)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3674 (כְּנָת) KJV: companion.

H3676 כֵּס (kêç, kace): {a flag; also a sail; by implication, a flagstaff; generally a signal; figuratively, a token}. Origin: apparently a contraction for H3678 (כִּסֵּא), but probably by erroneous transcription for H5251 (נֵס) KJV: sworn.

H3677 כֶּסֶא (keçeʼ, keh'-seh): properly, fulness or the full moon, i.e. its festival. Origin: or כֶּסֶה; apparently from H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: (time) appointed.

H3678 כִּסֵּא (kiççêʼ, kis-say'): properly, covered, i.e. a throne (as canopied). Origin: or כִּסֵּה; from H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: seat, stool, throne.

H3679 כַּסְדַּי (Kaçday, kas-dah'-ee): {a Kasdite, or descendant of Kesed; by implication, a Chaldaean (as if so descended); also an astrologer (as if proverbial of that people}. Origin: for H3778 (כַּשְׂדִּי) KJV: Chaldean.

H3680 כָּסָה (kâçâh, kaw-saw'): properly, to plump, i.e. fill up hollows; by implication, to cover (for clothing or secrecy). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: clad self, close, clothe, conceal, cover (self), (flee to) hide, overwhelm. Compare H3780 (כָּשָׂה).

H3681 כָּסוּי (kâçûwy, kaw-soo'-ee): properly, covered, i.e. (as noun) a covering. Origin: passive participle of H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: covering.

H3682 כְּסוּת (kᵉçûwth, kes-ooth'): a cover (garment); figuratively, a veiling. Origin: from H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: covering, raiment, vesture.

H3683 כָּסַח (kâçach, kaw-sakh'): to cut off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut down (up).

H3684 כְּסִיל (kᵉçîyl, kes-eel'): properly, fat, i.e. (figuratively) stupid or silly. Origin: from H3688 (כָּסַל); KJV: fool(-ish).

H3685 כְּסִיל (Kᵉçîyl, kes-eel'): any notable constellation; specifically Orion (as if a burly one). Origin: the same as H3684 (כְּסִיל); KJV: constellation, Orion.

H3686 כְּסִיל (Kᵉçîyl, kes-eel'): Kesil, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3684 (כְּסִיל); KJV: Chesil.

H3687 כְּסִילוּת (kᵉçîylûwth, kes-eel-ooth'): silliness. Origin: from H3684 (כְּסִיל); KJV: foolish.

H3688 כָּסַל (kâçal, kaw-sal'): properly, to be fat, i.e. (figuratively) silly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be foolish.

H3689 כֶּסֶל (keçel, keh'-sel): properly, fatness, i.e. by implication (literally) the loin (as the seat of the leaf fat) or (generally) the viscera; also (figuratively) silliness or (in a good sense) trust. Origin: from H3688 (כָּסַל); KJV: confidence, flank, folly, hope, loin.

H3690 כִּסְלָה (kiçlâh, kis-law'): in a good sense, trust; in a bad one, silliness. Origin: feminine of H3689 (כֶּסֶל); KJV: confidence, folly.

H3691 כִּסְלֵו (Kiçlêv, kis-lave'): Kisleu, the 9th Hebrew month. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Chisleu.

H3692 כִּסְלוֹן (Kiçlôwn, kis-lone'): Kislon, an Israelite. Origin: from H3688 (כָּסַל); hopeful; KJV: Chislon.

H3693 כְּסָלוֹן (Kᵉçâlôwn, kes-aw-lone'): Kesalon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3688 (כָּסַל); fertile; KJV: Chesalon.

H3694 כְּסֻלּוֹת (Kᵉçullôwth, kes-ool-loth'): Kesulloth, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine plural of passive participle of H3688 (כָּסַל); fattened; KJV: Chesulloth.

H3695 כַּסְלֻחִים (Kaçluchîym, kas-loo'-kheem): Casluchim, a people cognate to the Egyptians. Origin: a plural probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Casluhim.

H3696 כִּסְלֹת תָּבֹר (Kiçlôth Tâbôr, kis-loth' taw-bore'): Kisloth-Tabor, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the feminine plural of H3689 (כֶּסֶל) and H8396 (תָּבוֹר); flanks of Tabor; KJV: Chisloth-tabor.

H3697 כָּסַם (kâçam, kaw-sam'): to shear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] only, poll. Compare H3765 (כִּרְסֵם).

H3698 כֻּסֶּמֶת (kuççemeth, koos-seh'-meth): spelt (from its bristliness as if just shorn). Origin: from H3697 (כָּסַם); KJV: fitches, rie.

H3699 כָּסַס (kâçaç, kaw-sas'): to estimate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make count.

H3700 כָּסַף (kâçaph, kaw-saf'): properly, to become pale, i.e. (by implication) to pine after; also to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (have) desire, be greedy, long, sore.

H3701 כֶּסֶף (keçeph, keh'-sef): silver (from its pale color); by implication, money. Origin: from H3700 (כָּסַף); KJV: money, price, silver(-ling).

H3702 כְּסַף (kᵉçaph, kes-af'): {silver (from its pale color); by implication, money}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3701 (כֶּסֶף) KJV: money, silver.

H3703 כָּסִפְיָא (Kâçiphyâʼ, kaw-sif-yaw'): Casiphja, a place in Babylon. Origin: perhaps from H3701 (כֶּסֶף); silvery; KJV: Casiphia.

H3704 כֶּסֶת (keçeth, keh'-seth): a cushion or pillow (as covering a seat or bed). Origin: from H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: pillow.

H3705 כְּעַן (kᵉʻan, keh-an'): now. Origin: (Aramaic) probably from H3652 (כֵּן); KJV: now.

H3706 כְּעֶנֶת (kᵉʻeneth, keh-eh'-neth): thus (only in the formula 'and so forth'). Origin: (Aramaic) or כְּעֶת; (Aramaic), feminine of H3705 (כְּעַן); KJV: at such a time.

H3707 כַּעַס (kaʻaç, kaw-as'): to trouble; by implication, to grieve, rage, be indignant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be angry, be grieved, take indignation, provoke (to anger, unto wrath), have sorrow, vex, be wroth.

H3708 כַּעַס (kaʻaç, kah'-as): vexation. Origin: or (in Job) כַּעַשׂ; from H3707 (כַּעַס); KJV: anger, angry, grief, indignation, provocation, provoking, [idiom] sore, sorrow, spite, wrath.

H3709 כַּף (kaph, kaf): the hollow hand or palm (so of the paw of an animal, of the sole, and even of the bowl of a dish or sling, the handle of a bolt, the leaves of a palm-tree); figuratively, power. Origin: from H3721 (כָּפַף); KJV: branch, [phrase] foot, hand((-ful), -dle, (-led)), hollow, middle, palm, paw, power, sole, spoon.

H3710 כֵּף (kêph, kafe): a hollow rock. Origin: from H3721 (כָּפַף); KJV: rock.

H3711 כָּפָה (kâphâh, kaw-faw'): properly, to bend, i.e. (figuratively) to tame or subdue. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pacify.

H3712 כִּפָּה (kippâh, kip-paw'): a leaf of a palmtree. Origin: feminine of H3709 (כַּף); KJV: branch.

H3713 כְּפוֹר (kᵉphôwr, kef-ore'): properly, a cover, i.e. (by implication) a tankard (or covered goblet); also white frost (as covering the ground). Origin: from H3722 (כָּפַר); KJV: bason, hoar(-y) frost.

H3714 כָּפִיס (kâphîyç, kaw-fece'): a girder. Origin: from an unused root meaning to connect; KJV: beam.

H3715 כְּפִיר (kᵉphîyr, kef-eer'): a village (as covered in by walls); also a young lion (perhaps as covered with a mane). Origin: from H3722 (כָּפַר); KJV: (young) lion, village. Compare H3723 (כָּפָר).

H3716 כְּפִירָה (Kᵉphîyrâh, kef-ee-raw'): Kephirah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H3715 (כְּפִיר); the village (always with the art.); KJV: Chephirah.

H3717 כָּפַל (kâphal, kaw-fal'): to fold together; figuratively, to repeat. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: double.

H3718 כֶּפֶל (kephel, keh'-fel): a duplicate. Origin: from H3717 (כָּפַל); KJV: double.

H3719 כָּפַן (kâphan, kaw-fan'): to bend. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bend.

H3720 כָּפָן (kâphân, kaw-fawn'): hunger (as making to stoop with emptiness and pain). Origin: from H3719 (כָּפַן); KJV: famine.

H3721 כָּפַף (kâphaph, kaw-faf'): to curve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bow down (self).

H3722 כָּפַר (kâphar, kaw-far'): to cover (specifically with bitumen); figuratively, to expiate or condone, to placate or cancel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appease, make (an atonement, cleanse, disannul, forgive, be merciful, pacify, pardon, purge (away), put off, (make) reconcile(-liation).

H3723 כָּפָר (kâphâr, kaw-fawr'): a village (as protected by walls). Origin: from H3722 (כָּפַר); KJV: village. Compare H3715 (כְּפִיר).

H3724 כֹּפֶר (kôpher, ko'-fer): properly, a cover, i.e. (literally) a village (as covered in); (specifically) bitumen (as used for coating), and the henna plant (as used for dyeing); figuratively, a redemption-price. Origin: from H3722 (כָּפַר); KJV: bribe, camphire, pitch, ransom, satisfaction, sum of money, village.

H3725 כִּפֻּר (kippur, kip-poor'): expiation (only in plural). Origin: from H3722 (כָּפַר); KJV: atonement.

H3726 כְּפַר הָעַמּוֹנִי (Kᵉphar hâ-ʻAmmôwnîy, kef-ar' haw-am-monee'): Kefar-ha-Ammoni, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3723 (כָּפָר) and H5984 (עַמּוֹנִי), with the article interposed; village of the Ammonite; KJV: Chefarhaamonai.

H3727 כַּפֹּרֶת (kappôreth, kap-po'-reth): a lid (used only of the cover of the sacred Ark). Origin: from H3722 (כָּפַר); KJV: mercy seat.

H3728 כָּפַשׁ (kâphash, kaw-fash'): to tread down; figuratively, to humiliate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover.

H3729 כְּפַת (kᵉphath, kef-ath'): to fetter. Origin: (Aramaic) a root of uncertain correspondence; KJV: bind.

H3730 כַּפְתֹּר (kaphtôr, kaf-tore'): a chaplet; but used only in an architectonic sense, i.e. the capital of acolumn, or a wreath-like button or disk on the candelabrum. Origin: or (Amos 9:1) כַּפְתּוֹר; probably from an unused root meaning to encircle; KJV: knop, (upper) lintel.

H3731 כַּפְתֹּר (Kaphtôr, kaf-tore'): Caphtor (i.e. a wreath-shaped island), the original seat of the Philistines. Origin: or (Amos 9:7) כַּפְתּוֹר; apparently the same as H3730 (כַּפְתֹּר); KJV: Caphtor.

H3732 כַּפְתֹּרִי (Kaphtôrîy, kaf-to-ree'): a Caphtorite (collectively) or native of Caphtor. Origin: patrial from H3731 (כַּפְתֹּר); KJV: Caphthorim, Caphtorim(-s).

H3733 כַּר (kar, kar): a ram (as full-grown and fat), including a battering-ram (as butting); hence, a meadow (as for sheep); also a pad or camel's saddle (as puffed out). Origin: from H3769 (כָּרַר) in the sense of plumpness; KJV: captain, furniture, lamb, (large) pasture, ram. See also H1033 (בֵּית כַּר), H3746 (כָּרִי).

H3734 כֹּר (kôr, kore): properly, a deep round vessel, i.e. (specifically) a cor or measure for things dry. Origin: from the same as H3564 (כּוּר); KJV: cor, measure. Aramaic the same.

H3735 כָּרָא (Kârâʼ, kaw-raw'): to grieve. Origin: (Aramaic) probably corresponding to H3738 (כָּרָה) in the sense of piercing(figuratively); KJV: be grieved.

H3736 כַּרְבֵּל (karbêl, kar-bale'): to gird or clothe. Origin: from the same as H3525 (כֶּבֶל); KJV: clothed.

H3737 כַּרְבְּלָא (karbᵉlâʼ, kar-bel-aw'): a mantle. Origin: (Aramaic) from a verb corresponding to that of H3736 (כַּרְבֵּל); KJV: hat.

H3738 כָּרָה (kârâh, kaw-raw'): properly, to dig; figuratively, to plot; generally, to bore or open. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dig, [idiom] make (a banquet), open.

H3739 כָּרָה (kârâh, kaw-raw'): to purchase. Origin: usually assigned as a primitive root, but probably only a special application of H3738 (כָּרָה) (through the common idea of planning implied in a bargain); KJV: buy, prepare.

H3740 כֵּרָה (kêrâh, kay-raw'): a purchase. Origin: from H3739 (כָּרָה); KJV: provision.

H3741 כָּרָה (kârâh, kaw-raw'): a meadow. Origin: feminine of H3733 (כַּר); KJV: cottage.

H3742 כְּרוּב (kᵉrûwb, ker-oob'): a cherub or imaginary figure. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: cherub, (plural) cherubims.

H3743 כְּרוּב (Kᵉrûwb, ker-oob'): Kerub, a place in Babylon. Origin: the same as H3742 (כְּרוּב); KJV: Cherub.

H3744 כָּרוֹז (kârôwz, kaw-roze'): a herald. Origin: (Aramaic) from H3745 (כְּרַז); KJV: herald.

H3745 כְּרַז (kᵉraz, ker-az'): to proclaim. Origin: (Aramaic) probably of Greek origin; KJV: make a proclamation.

H3746 כָּרִי (kârîy, kaw-ree'): a life-guardsman. Origin: perhaps an abridged plural of H3733 (כַּר) in the sense of leader (of the flock); KJV: captains, Cherethites (from the margin).

H3747 כְּרִית (Kᵉrîyth, ker-eeth'): Kerith, a brook of Palestine. Origin: from H3772 (כָּרַת); a cut; KJV: Cherith.

H3748 כְּרִיתוּת (kᵉrîythûwth, ker-ee-thooth'): a cutting (of the matrimonial bond), i.e. divorce. Origin: from H3772 (כָּרַת); KJV: divorce(-ment).

H3749 כַּרְכֹּב (karkôb, kar-kobe'): a rim or top margin. Origin: expanded from the same as H3522 (כַּבּוֹן); KJV: compass.

H3750 כַּרְכֹּם (karkôm, kar-kome'): the crocus. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: saffron.

H3751 כַּרְכְּמִישׁ (Karkᵉmîysh, kar-kem-eesh'): Karkemish, a place in Syria. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Carchemish.

H3752 כַּרְכַּס (Karkaç, kar-kas'): Karkas, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Carcas.

H3753 כַּרְכָּרָה (karkârâh, kar-kaw-raw'): a dromedary (from its rapid motion as if dancing). Origin: from H3769 (כָּרַר); KJV: swift beast.

H3754 כֶּרֶם (kerem, keh'-rem): a garden or vineyard. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: vines, (increase of the) vineyard(-s), vintage. See also H1021 (בֵּית הַכֶּרֶם).

H3755 כֹּרֵם (kôrêm, ko-rame'): a vinedresser. Origin: active participle of an imaginary denominative from H3754 (כֶּרֶם); KJV: vine dresser (as one or two words).

H3756 כַּרְמִי (Karmîy, kar-mee'): Karmi, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H3754 (כֶּרֶם); gardener; KJV: Carmi.

H3757 כַּרְמִי (Karmîy, kar-mee'): a Karmite or descendant of Karmi. Origin: patronymically from H3756 (כַּרְמִי); KJV: Carmites.

H3758 כַּרְמִיל (karmîyl, kar-mele'): carmine, a deep red. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: crimson.

H3759 כַּרְמֶל (karmel, kar-mel'): a planted field (garden, orchard, vineyard or park); by implication, garden produce. Origin: from H3754 (כֶּרֶם); KJV: full (green) ears (of corn), fruitful field (place), plentiful (field).

H3760 כַּרְמֶל (Karmel, kar-mel'): Karmel, the name of a hill and of a town in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3759 (כַּרְמֶל); KJV: Carmel, fruitful (plentiful) field, (place).

H3761 כַּרְמְלִי (Karmᵉlîy, kar-mel-ee'): a Karmelite or inhabitant of Karmel (the town). Origin: patron from H3760 (כַּרְמֶל); KJV: Carmelite.

H3762 כַּרְמְלִית (Karmᵉlîyth, kar-mel-eeth'): a Karmelitess or female inhabitant of Karmel. Origin: feminine of H3761 (כַּרְמְלִי); KJV: Carmelitess.

H3763 כְּרָן (Kᵉrân, ker-awn'): Keran, an aboriginal Idumaean. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Cheran.

H3764 כׇּרְסֵא (korçêʼ, kor-say'): a throne. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3678 (כִּסֵּא); KJV: throne.

H3765 כִּרְסֵם (kirçêm, kir-same'): to lay waste. Origin: from H3697 (כָּסַם); KJV: waste.

H3766 כָּרַע (kâraʻ, kaw-rah'): to bend the knee; by implication, to sink, to prostrate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bow (down, self), bring down (low), cast down, couch, fall, feeble, kneeling, sink, smite (stoop) down, subdue, [idiom] very.

H3767 כָּרָע (kârâʻ, kaw-raw'): the leg (from the knee to the ankle) of men or locusts (only in the dual). Origin: from H3766 (כָּרַע); KJV: leg.

H3768 כַּרְפַּס (karpaç, kar-pas'): byssus or fine vegetable wool. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: green.

H3769 כָּרַר (kârar, kaw-rar'): to dance (i.e. whirl). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dance(-ing).

H3770 כְּרֵשׂ (kᵉrês, ker-ace'): the paunch or belly (as swelling out). Origin: by variation from H7164 (קָרַס); KJV: belly.

H3771 כַּרְשְׁנָא (Karshᵉnâʼ, kar-shen-aw'): Karshena, a courtier of Xerxes. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Carshena.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3772 to H3885
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3772 כָּרַת (kârath, kaw-rath'): to cut (off, down or asunder); by implication, to destroy or consume; specifically, to covenant (i.e. make an alliance or bargain, originally by cutting flesh and passing between the pieces). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be chewed, be con-(feder-) ate, covenant, cut (down, off), destroy, fail, feller, be freed, hew (down), make a league (covenant), [idiom] lose, perish, [idiom] utterly, [idiom] want.

H3773 כָּרֻתָה (kâruthâh, kaw-rooth-aw'): something cut, i.e. a hewn timber. Origin: passive participle feminine of H3772 (כָּרַת); KJV: beam.

H3774 כְּרֵתִי (Kᵉrêthîy, ker-ay-thee'): a Kerethite or life-guardsman. Origin: probably from H3772 (כָּרַת) in the sense of executioner; (compare H2876 (טַבָּח)) (only collectively in the singular as plural) KJV: Cherethims, Cherethites.

H3775 כֶּשֶׂב (keseb, keh'-seb): a young sheep. Origin: apparently by transposition for H3532 (כֶּבֶשׂ); KJV: lamb.

H3776 כִּשְׂבָּה (kisbâh, kis-baw'): a young ewe. Origin: feminine of H3775 (כֶּשֶׂב); KJV: lamb.

H3777 כֶּשֶׂד (Kesed, keh'-sed): Kesed, a relative of Abraham. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: Chesed.

H3778 כַּשְׂדִּי (Kasdîy, kas-dee'): a Kasdite, or descendant of Kesed; by implication, a Chaldaean (as if so descended); also an astrologer (as if proverbial of that people. Origin: (occasionally with enclitic) כַּשְׂדִּימָה; towards the Kasdites into Chaldea), patronymically from H3777 (כֶּשֶׂד) (only in the plural); KJV: Chaldeans, Chaldees, inhabitants of Chaldea.

H3779 כַּשְׂדַּי (Kasday, kas-dah'-ee): a Chaldaean or inhabitant of Chaldaea; by implication, a Magian or professional astrologer. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3778 (כַּשְׂדִּי); KJV: Chaldean.

H3780 כָּשָׂה (kâsâh, kaw-saw'): to grow fat (i.e. be covered with flesh). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be covered. Compare H3680 (כָּסָה).

H3781 כַּשִּׁיל (kashshîyl, kash-sheel'): properly, a feller, i.e. an axe. Origin: from H3782 (כָּשַׁל); KJV: ax.

H3782 כָּשַׁל (kâshal, kaw-shal'): to totter or waver (through weakness of the legs, especially the ankle); by implication, to falter, stumble, faint or fall. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bereave (from the margin), cast down, be decayed, (cause to) fail, (cause, make to) fall (down, -ing), feeble, be (the) ruin(-ed, of), (be) overthrown, (cause to) stumble, [idiom] utterly, be weak.

H3783 כִּשָּׁלוֹן (kishshâlôwn, kish-shaw-lone'): properly, a tottering, i.e. ruin. Origin: from H3782 (כָּשַׁל); KJV: fall.

H3784 כָּשַׁף (kâshaph, kaw-shaf'): properly, to whisper aspell, i.e. to inchant or practise magic. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sorcerer, (use) witch(-craft).

H3785 כֶּשֶׁף (kesheph, keh'-shef): magic. Origin: from H3784 (כָּשַׁף); KJV: sorcery, witchcraft.

H3786 כַּשָּׁף (kashshâph, kash-shawf'): a magician. Origin: from H3784 (כָּשַׁף); KJV: sorcerer.

H3787 כָּשֵׁר (kâshêr, kaw-share'): by implication, to be acceptable; also to succeed or prosper. Origin: a primitive root properly, to be straight or right; KJV: direct, be right, prosper.

H3788 כִּשְׁרוֹן (kishrôwn, kish-rone'): success, advantage. Origin: from H3787 (כָּשֵׁר); KJV: equity, good, right.

H3789 כָּתַב (kâthab, kaw-thab'): to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: describe, record, prescribe, subscribe, write(-ing, -ten).

H3790 כְּתַב (kᵉthab, keth-ab'): {to grave, by implication, to write (describe, inscribe, prescribe, subscribe)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3789 (כָּתַב) KJV: write(-ten).

H3791 כָּתָב (kâthâb, kaw-thawb'): something written, i.e. a writing, record or book. Origin: from H3789 (כָּתַב); KJV: register, scripture, writing.

H3792 כְּתָב (kᵉthâb, keth-awb'): {something written, i.e. a writing, record or book}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3791 (כָּתָב) KJV: prescribing, writing(-ten).

H3793 כְּתֹבֶת (kᵉthôbeth, keth-o'-beth): a letter or other mark branded on the skin. Origin: from H3789 (כָּתַב); KJV: [idiom] any (mark).

H3794 כִּתִּי (Kittîy, kit-tee'): a Kittite or Cypriote; hence, an islander in general, i.e. the Greeks or Romans on the shores opposite Palestine. Origin: or כִּתִּיִּי; patrial from an unused name denoting Cyprus (only in the plural); KJV: Chittim, Kittim.

H3795 כָּתִית (kâthîyth, kaw-theeth'): beaten, i.e. pure (oil). Origin: from H3807 (כָּתַת); KJV: beaten.

H3796 כֹּתֶל (kôthel, ko'-thel): a wall (as gathering inmates). Origin: from an unused root meaning to compact; KJV: wall.

H3797 כְּתַל (kᵉthal, keth-al'): {a wall (as gathering inmates)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3796 (כֹּתֶל) KJV: wall.

H3798 כִּתְלִישׁ (Kithlîysh, kith-leesh'): Kithlish, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3796 (כֹּתֶל) and H376 (אִישׁ); wall of a man; KJV: Kithlish.

H3799 כָּתַם (kâtham, kaw-tham'): properly, to carve or engrave, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe indelibly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mark.

H3800 כֶּתֶם (kethem, keh'-them): properly, something carved out, i.e. ore; hence, gold (pure as originally mined). Origin: from H3799 (כָּתַם); KJV: ((most) fine, pure) gold(-en wedge).

H3801 כְּתֹנֶת (kᵉthôneth, keth-o'-neth): a shirt. Origin: or כֻּתֹּנֶת; from an unused root meaning to cover (compare H3802 (כָּתֵף)); KJV: coat, garment, robe.

H3802 כָּתֵף (kâthêph, kaw-thafe'): the shoulder (proper, i.e. upper end of the arm; as being the spot where the garments hang); figuratively, side-piece or lateral projection of anything. Origin: from an unused root meaning to clothe; KJV: arm, corner, shoulder(-piece), side, undersetter.

H3803 כָּתַר (kâthar, kaw-thar'): to enclose; hence (in a friendly sense) to crown, (in a hostile one) to besiege; also to wait (as restraining oneself). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beset round, compass about, be crowned inclose round, suffer.

H3804 כֶּתֶר (kether, keh'-ther): properly, a circlet, i.e. a diadem. Origin: from H3803 (כָּתַר); KJV: crown.

H3805 כֹתֶרֶת (kôthereth, ko-theh'-reth): the capital of a column. Origin: feminine active participle of H3803 (כָּתַר); KJV: chapiter.

H3806 כָּתַשׁ (kâthash, kaw-thash'): to butt or pound. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bray.

H3807 כָּתַת (kâthath, kaw-thath'): to bruise or violently strike. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat (down, to pieces), break in pieces, crushed, destroy, discomfit, smite, stamp. l

H3808 לֹא (lôʼ, lo): not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no; often used with other particles. Origin: or לוֹא; or לֹה; (Deuteronomy 3:11), a primitive particle; KJV: [idiom] before, [phrase] or else, ere, [phrase] except, ig(-norant), much, less, nay, neither, never, no((-ne), -r, (-thing)), ([idiom] as though...,(can-), for) not (out of), of nought, otherwise, out of, [phrase] surely, [phrase] as truly as, [phrase] of a truth, [phrase] verily, for want, [phrase] whether, without.

H3809 לָא (lâʼ, law): {not (the simple or abs. negation); by implication, no;}. Origin: (Aramaic) or לָה; (Aramaic) (Daniel 4:32), corresponding to H3808 (לֹא) KJV: or even, neither, no(-ne, -r), (can-) not, as nothing, without.

H3810 לֹא דְבַר (Lôʼ Dᵉbar, lo deb-ar'): Lo-Debar, a place in Palestine. Origin: or לוֹ דבַר; (Samuel 9:4,5), or לִדְבִר; (Joshua 13:26), (probably rather לֹדְבַר ); from H3808 (לֹא) and H1699 (דֹּבֶר); pastureless; KJV: Debir, Lodebar.

H3811 לָאָה (lâʼâh, law-aw'): to tire; (figuratively) to be (or make) disgusted. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: faint, grieve, lothe, (be, make) weary (selves).

H3812 לֵאָה (Lêʼâh, lay-aw'): Leah, a wife of Jacob. Origin: from H3811 (לָאָה); weary; KJV: Leah.

H3813 לָאַט (lâʼaṭ, law-at'): to muffle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover.

H3814 לָאט (lâʼṭ, lawt): properly, muffled, i.e. silently. Origin: from H3813 (לָאַט) (or perhaps for active participle of H3874 (לוּט)); KJV: softly.

H3815 לָאֵל (Lâʼêl, law-ale'): Lael an Israelite. Origin: from the prepositional prefix and H410 (אֵל); (belonging) to God; KJV: Lael.

H3816 לְאֹם (lᵉʼôm, leh-ome'): a community. Origin: or לְאוֹם; from an unused root meaning to gather; KJV: nation, people.

H3817 לְאֻמִּים (Lᵉʼummîym, leh-oom-meem'): Leum mim, an Arabian. Origin: plural of H3816 (לְאֹם); communities; KJV: Leummim.

H3818 לֹא עַמִּי (Lôʼ ʻAmmîy, lo am-mee'): Lo-Ammi, the symbolic name of a son of Hosea. Origin: from H3808 (לֹא) and H5971 (עַם) with pronominal suffix; not my people; KJV: Lo-ammi.

H3819 לֹא רֻחָמָה (Lôʼ Ruchâmâh, lo roo-khaw-maw'): Lo-Ruchamah, the symbolic name of a son of Hosea. Origin: from H3808 (לֹא) and H7355 (רָחַם); not pitied; KJV: Lo-ruhamah.

H3820 לֵב (lêb, labe): the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything. Origin: a form of H3824 (לֵבָב); KJV: [phrase] care for, comfortably, consent, [idiom] considered, courag(-eous), friend(-ly), ((broken-), (hard-), (merry-), (stiff-), (stout-), double) heart(-ed), [idiom] heed, [idiom] I, kindly, midst, mind(-ed), [idiom] regard(-ed), [idiom] themselves, [idiom] unawares, understanding, [idiom] well, willingly, wisdom.

H3821 לֵב (lêb, labe): {the heart; also used (figuratively) very widely for the feelings, the will and even the intellect; likewise for the centre of anything}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3820 (לֵב) KJV: heart.

H3822 לְבָאוֹת (Lᵉbâʼôwth, leb-aw-oth'): Lebaoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H3833 (לָבִיא); lionesses; KJV: Lebaoth. See also H1034 (בֵּית לְבָאוֹת).

H3823 לָבַב (lâbab, law-bab'): (in a good sense) transport (with love), or (in a bad sense) stultify; to make cakes. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to be enclosed (as if with fat); by implication (as denominative from H3824 (לֵבָב)); to unheart; also as denominative from H3834 (לָבִיבָה) i.e. KJV: make cakes, ravish, be wise.

H3824 לֵבָב (lêbâb, lay-bawb'): the heart (as the most interior organ). Origin: from H3823 (לָבַב); used also like H3820 (לֵב) KJV: [phrase] bethink themselves, breast, comfortably, courage, ((faint), (tender-) heart(-ed), midst, mind, [idiom] unawares, understanding.

H3825 לְבַב (lᵉbab, leb-ab'): {the heart (as the most interior organ);}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3824 (לֵבָב) KJV: heart.
