H3826 לִבָּה (libbâh, lib-baw'): the heart. Origin: feminine of H3820 (לֵב); KJV: heart.

H3827 לַבָּה (labbâh, lab-baw'): flame. Origin: for H3852 (לֶהָבָה); KJV: flame.

H3828 לְבוֹנָה (lᵉbôwnâh, leb-o-naw'): frankincense (from its whiteness or perhaps that of its smoke). Origin: or לְבֹנָה; from H3836 (לָבָן); KJV: (frank-) incense.

H3829 לְבוֹנָה (Lᵉbôwnâh, leb-o-naw'): Lebonah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3828 (לְבוֹנָה); KJV: Lebonah.

H3830 לְבוּשׁ (lᵉbûwsh, leb-oosh'): a garment (literally or figuratively); by implication (euphemistically) a wife. Origin: or לְבֻשׁ; from H3847 (לָבַשׁ); KJV: apparel, clothed with, clothing, garment, raiment, vestment, vesture.

H3831 לְבוּשׁ (lᵉbûwsh, leb-oosh'): {a garment (literally or figuratively); by implication (euphemistically) a wife}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3830 (לְבוּשׁ) KJV: garment.

H3832 לָבַט (lâbaṭ, law-bat'): to overthrow; intransposed, to fall. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fall.

H3833 לָבִיא (lâbîyʼ, law-bee'): to roar; a lion (properly, a lioness as the fiercer (although not a roarer;)). Origin: or (Ezekiel 19:2) לְבִיָּא; irregular masculine plural לְבָאִים; irregular feminine plural לְבָאוֹת; from an unused root meaning; compare H738 (אֲרִי) KJV: (great, old, stout) lion, lioness, young (lion).

H3834 לָבִיבָה (lâbîybâh, law-bee-baw'): a cake (either as fried or turned). Origin: or rather לְבִבָה; from H3823 (לָבַב) in its original sense of fatness (or perhaps of folding); KJV: cake.

H3835 לָבַן (lâban, law-ban'): to be (or become) white; to make bricks. Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative from H3843 (לְבֵנָה) KJV: make brick, be (made, make) white(-r).

H3836 לָבָן (lâbân, law-bawn'): white. Origin: or (Genesis 49:12) לָבֵן; from H3835 (לָבַן); KJV: white.

H3837 לָבָן (Lâbân, law-bawn'): Laban, a Mesopotamian; also a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H3836 (לָבָן); KJV: Laban.

H3838 לְבָנָא (Lᵉbânâʼ, leb-aw-naw'): Lebana or Lebanah, one of the Nethinim. Origin: or לְבָנָה; the same as H3842 (לְבָנָה); KJV: Lebana, Lebanah.

H3839 לִבְנֶה (libneh, lib-neh'): some sort of whitish tree, perhaps the storax. Origin: from H3835 (לָבַן); KJV: poplar.

H3840 לִבְנָה (libnâh, lib-naw'): properly, whiteness, i.e. (by implication) transparency. Origin: from H3835 (לָבַן); KJV: paved.

H3841 לִבְנָה (Libnâh, lib-naw'): Libnah, a place in the Desert and one in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3839 (לִבְנֶה); KJV: Libnah.

H3842 לְבָנָה (lᵉbânâh, leb-aw-naw'): properly, (the) white, i.e. the moon. Origin: from H3835 (לָבַן); KJV: moon. See also H3838 (לְבָנָא).

H3843 לְבֵנָה (lᵉbênâh, leb-ay-naw'): a brick (from the whiteness of the clay). Origin: from H3835 (לָבַן); KJV: (altar of) brick, tile.

H3844 לְבָנוֹן (Lᵉbânôwn, leb-aw-nohn'): Lebanon, a mountain range in Palestine. Origin: from H3825 (לְבַב); (the) white mountain (from its snow); KJV: Lebanon.

H3845 לִבְנִי (Libnîy, lib-nee'): Libni, an Israelite. Origin: from H3835 (לָבַן); white; KJV: Libni.

H3846 לִבְנִי (Libnîy, lib-nee'): a Libnite or descendants of Libni (collectively). Origin: patronymically from H3845 (לִבְנִי); KJV: Libnites.

H3847 לָבַשׁ (lâbash, law-bash'): properly, wrap around, i.e. (by implication) to put on agarment or clothe (oneself, or another), literally or figuratively. Origin: or לָבֵשׁ; a primitive root; KJV: (in) apparel, arm, array (self), clothe (self), come upon, put (on, upon), wear.

H3848 לְבַשׁ (lᵉbash, leb-ash'): {properly, wrap around, i.e. (by implication) to put on agarment or clothe (oneself, or another), literally or figuratively}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3847 (לָבַשׁ) KJV: clothe.

H3849 לֹג (lôg, lohg): a log or measure forliquids. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to deepen or hollow (like H3537 (כַּד)); KJV: log (of oil).

H3850 לֹד (Lôd, lode): Lod, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain signification; KJV: Lod.

H3851 לַהַב (lahab, lah'-hab): a flash; figuratively, a sharply polished blade or point of aweapon. Origin: from an usused root meaning to gleam; KJV: blade, bright, flame, glittering.

H3852 לֶהָבָה (lehâbâh, leh-aw-baw'): {a flash; figuratively, a sharply polished blade or point of aweapon}. Origin: or לַהֶבֶת; feminine of H3851 (לַהַב), and meaning the same KJV: flame(-ming), head (of a spear).

H3853 לְהָבִים (Lᵉhâbîym, leh-haw-beem'): Lehabim, a son of Mizraim, and his descendants. Origin: plural of H3851 (לַהַב); flames; KJV: Lehabim.

H3854 לַהַג (lahag, lah'-hag): intense mental application. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be eager; KJV: study.

H3855 לַהַד (Lahad, lah'-had): Lahad, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to glow (compare H3851 (לַהַב)) or else to be earnest (compare H3854 (לַהַג)); KJV: Lahad.

H3856 לָהַהּ (lâhahh, law-hah'): to be rabid (figuratively, insane); also (from the exhaustion of frenzy) to languish. Origin: a primitive root meaning properly, to burn, i.e. (by implication) KJV: faint, mad.

H3857 לָהַט (lâhaṭ, law-hat'): properly, to lick, i.e. (by implication) to blaze. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn (up), set on fire, flaming, kindle.

H3858 לַהַט (lahaṭ, lah'-hat): a blaze; also (from the idea of enwrapping) magic (as covert). Origin: from H3857 (לָהַט); KJV: flaming, enchantment.

H3859 לָהַם (lâham, law-ham'): properly, to burn in, i.e. (figuratively) to rankle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wound.

H3860 לָהֵן (lâhên, law-hane'): popularly for if; hence, therefore. Origin: from the prepositional prefix meaning to or for and H2005 (הֵן); KJV: for them (by mistake for prepositional suffix).

H3861 לָהֵן (lâhên, law-hane'): therefore; also except. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3860 (לָהֵן); KJV: but, except, save, therefore, wherefore.

H3862 לַהֲקָה (lahăqâh, lah-hak-aw'): an assembly. Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to gather; KJV: company.

H3863 לוּא (lûwʼ, loo): a conditional particle; if; by implication (interj. as a wish) would that!. Origin: or לֻא; or לוּ; KJV: if (haply), peradventure, I pray thee, though, I would, would God (that).

H3864 לוּבִי (Lûwbîy, loo-bee'): a Libyan or inhabitant of interior Africa (only in plural). Origin: or לֻבִּי; (Daniel 11:43), partrial from a name probably derived from an unused root meaning to thirst, i.e. a dry region; apparently KJV: Lubim(-s), Libyans.

H3865 לוּד (Lûwd, lood): Lud, the name of two nations. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Lud, Lydia.

H3866 לוּדִי (Lûwdîy, loo-dee'): a Ludite or inhabitants of Lud (only in plural). Origin: or לוּדִיִּי; patrial from H3865 (לוּד); KJV: Ludim. Lydians.

H3867 לָוָה (lâvâh, law-vaw'): properly, to twine, i.e. (by implication) to unite, to remain; also to borrow (as a form of obligation) or (caus.) to lend. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abide with, borrow(-er), cleave, join (self), lend(-er).

H3868 לוּז (lûwz, looz): to turn aside , i.e. (literally) to depart, (figuratively) be perverse. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H3867 (לָוָה), H3874 (לוּט) and H3885 (לוּן)) KJV: depart, froward, perverse(-ness).

H3869 לוּז (lûwz, looz): some kind of nuttree, perhaps the almond. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: hazel.

H3870 לוּז (Lûwz, looz): Luz, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: probably from H3869 (לוּז) (as growing there); KJV: Luz.

H3871 לוּחַ (lûwach, loo'-akh): probably meaning to glisten; a tablet (as polished), of stone, wood or metal. Origin: or לֻחַ; from a primitive root; KJV: board, plate, table.

H3872 לוּחִית (Lûwchîyth, loo-kheeth'): Luchith, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: or לֻחוֹת; (Jeremiah 48:5), from the same as H3871 (לוּחַ); floored; KJV: Luhith.

H3873 לוֹחֵשׁ (Lôwchêsh, lo-khashe'): Lochesh, an Israelite. Origin: active participle of H3907 (לָחַשׁ); (the) enchanter; KJV: Hallohesh, Haloshesh (includ. the article).

H3874 לוּט (lûwṭ, loot): to wrap up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast, wrap.

H3875 לוֹט (lôwṭ, lote): a veil. Origin: from H3874 (לוּט); KJV: covering.

H3876 לוֹט (Lôwṭ, lote): Lot, Abraham's nephew. Origin: the same as H3875 (לוֹט); KJV: Lot.

H3877 לוֹטָן (Lôwṭân, lo-tawn'): Lotan, an Idumaean. Origin: from H3875 (לוֹט); covering; KJV: Lotan.

H3878 לֵוִי (Lêvîy, lay-vee'): Levi, a son of Jacob. Origin: from H3867 (לָוָה); attached; KJV: Levi. See also H3879 (לֵוִי), H3881 (לֵוִיִּי).

H3879 לֵוִי (Lêvîy, lay-vee'): {something attached, i.e. a wreath}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3880 (לִוְיָה) KJV: Levite.

H3880 לִוְיָה (livyâh, liv-yaw'): something attached, i.e. a wreath. Origin: from H3867 (לָוָה); KJV: ornament.

H3881 לֵוִיִּי (Lêvîyîy, lay-vee-ee'): a Levite or descendant of Levi. Origin: or לֵוִי; patronymically from H3878 (לֵוִי); KJV: Leviite.

H3882 לִוְיָתָן (livyâthân, liv-yaw-thawn'): a wreathed animal, i.e. a serpent (especially the crocodile or some other large sea-monster); figuratively, the constellation of the dragon; also as a symbol of Babylon. Origin: from H3867 (לָוָה); KJV: leviathan, mourning.

H3883 לוּל (lûwl, lool): a spiral step. Origin: from an unused root meaning to fold back; KJV: winding stair. Compare H3924 (לֻלָאָה).

H3884 לוּלֵא (lûwlêʼ, loo-lay'): if not. Origin: or לוּלֵי; from H3863 (לוּא) and H3808 (לֹא); KJV: except, had not, if (...not), unless, were it not that.

H3885 לוּן (lûwn, loon): to stop (usually over night); by implication, to stay permanently; hence (in a bad sense) to be obstinate (especially in words, to complain). Origin: or לִין; a primitive root; KJV: abide (all night), continue, dwell, endure, grudge, be left, lie all night, (cause to) lodge (all night, in, -ing, this night), (make to) murmur, remain, tarry (all night, that night).

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H3886 to H4020
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H3886 לוּעַ (lûwaʻ, loo'-ah): to gulp; figuratively, to be rash. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: swallow down (up).

H3887 לוּץ (lûwts, loots): properly, to make mouths at, i.e. to scoff; hence (from the effort to pronounce a foreign language) to interpret, or (generally) intercede. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: ambassador, have in derision, interpreter, make a mock, mocker, scorn(-er, -ful), teacher.

H3888 לוּשׁ (lûwsh, loosh): to knead. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: knead.

H3889 לוּשׁ (Lûwsh, loosh): Lush, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3888 (לוּשׁ); kneading; KJV: Laish (from the margin). Compare H3919 (לַיִשׁ).

H3890 לְוָת (lᵉvâth, lev-awth'): properly, adhesion, i.e. (as preposition) with. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H3867 (לָוָה); KJV: [idiom] thee.

H3891 לְזוּת (lᵉzûwth, lez-ooth'): perverseness. Origin: from H3868 (לוּז); KJV: perverse.

H3892 לַח (lach, lakh): fresh, i.e. unused or undried. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be new; KJV: green, moist.

H3893 לֵחַ (lêach, lay'-akh): freshness, i.e. vigor. Origin: from the same as H3892 (לַח); KJV: natural force.

H3894 לָחוּם (lâchûwm, law-khoom'): properly, eaten, i.e. food; also flesh, i.e. body. Origin: or לָחֻם; passive participle of H3898 (לָחַם); KJV: while...is eating, flesh.

H3895 לְחִי (lᵉchîy, lekh-ee'): the cheek (from its fleshiness); hence, the jaw-bone. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be soft; KJV: cheek (bone), jaw (bone).

H3896 לֶחִי (Lechîy, lekh'-ee): Lechi, a place in Palestine. Origin: a form of H3895 (לְחִי); KJV: Lehi. Compare also H7437 (רָמַת לֶחִי).

H3897 לָחַךְ (lâchak, law-khak'): to lick. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lick (up).

H3898 לָחַם (lâcham, law-kham'): to feed on; figuratively, to consume; by implication, to battle (as destruction). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: devour, eat, [idiom] ever, fight(-ing), overcome, prevail, (make) war(-ring).

H3899 לֶחֶם (lechem, lekh'-em): food (for man or beast), especially bread, or grain (for making it). Origin: from H3898 (לָחַם); See also H1036 (בֵּית לְעַפְרָה) KJV: (shew-) bread, [idiom] eat, food, fruit, loaf, meat, victuals.

H3900 לְחֶם (lᵉchem, lekh-em'): {(for man or beast), especially bread, or grain (for making it)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3899 (לֶחֶם) KJV: feast.

H3901 לָחֶם (lâchem, law-khem'): battle. Origin: from H3898 (לָחַם), KJV: war.

H3902 לַחְמִי (Lachmîy, lakh-mee'): Lachmi, an Israelite; or rather probably a brief form. Origin: from H3899 (לֶחֶם); foodful; (or perhaps erroneous transcription) for H1022 (בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי) KJV: Lahmi. See also H3433 (יָשֻׁבִי לֶחֶם).

H3903 לַחְמָס (Lachmâç, lakh-maws'): Lachmam or Lachmas, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably by erroneous transcription for לַחְמָם; from H3899 (לֶחֶם); food-like; KJV: Lahmam.

H3904 לְחֵנָה (lᵉchênâh, lekh-ay-naw'): a concubine. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: concubine.

H3905 לָחַץ (lâchats, law-khats'): properly, to press, i.e. (figuratively) to distress. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: afflict, crush, force, hold fast, oppress(-or), thrust self.

H3906 לַחַץ (lachats, lakh'-ats): distress. Origin: from H3905 (לָחַץ); KJV: affliction, oppression.

H3907 לָחַשׁ (lâchash, law-khash'): to whisper; by implication, to mumble aspell (as a magician). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: charmer, whisper (together).

H3908 לַחַשׁ (lachash, lakh'-ash): properly, a whisper, i.e. by implication, (in a good sense) a private prayer, (in a bad one) an incantation; concretely, an amulet. Origin: from H3907 (לָחַשׁ); KJV: charmed, earring, enchantment, orator, prayer.

H3909 לָט (lâṭ, lawt): properly, covered, i.e. secret; by implication, incantation; also secrecy or (adverb) covertly. Origin: a form of H3814 (לָאט) or else participle from H3874 (לוּט); KJV: enchantment, privily, secretly, softly.

H3910 לֹט (lôṭ, lote): a gum (from its sticky nature), probably ladanum. Origin: probably from H3874 (לוּט); KJV: myrrh.

H3911 לְטָאָה (lᵉṭâʼâh, let-aw-aw'): a kind of lizard (from its covert habits). Origin: from an unused root meaning to hide; KJV: lizard.

H3912 לְטוּשִׁם (Lᵉṭûwshim, let-oo-sheem'): Letushim, an Arabian tribe. Origin: masculine plural of passive participle of H3913 (לָטַשׁ); hammered (i.e. oppressed) ones; KJV: Letushim.

H3913 לָטַשׁ (lâṭash, law-tash'): properly, to hammer out (an edge), i.e. to sharpen. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: instructer, sharp(-en), whet.

H3914 לֹיָה (lôyâh, lo-yaw'): a wreath. Origin: a form of H3880 (לִוְיָה); KJV: addition.

H3915 לַיִל (layil, lah'-yil): properly, a twist (away of the light), i.e. night; figuratively, adversity. Origin: or (Isaiah 21:11) לֵיל; also לַיְלָה; from the same as H3883 (לוּל); KJV: (mid-)night (season).

H3916 לֵילְיָא (lêylᵉyâʼ, lay-leh-yaw'): {Lael an Israelite}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3815 (לָאֵל) KJV: night.

H3917 לִילִית (lîylîyth, lee-leeth'): a night spectre. Origin: from H3915 (לַיִל); KJV: screech owl.

H3918 לַיִשׁ (layish, lah'-yish): a lion (from his destructive blows). Origin: from H3888 (לוּשׁ) in the sense of crushing; KJV: (old) lion.

H3919 לַיִשׁ (Layish, lah'-yish): Laish, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3918 (לַיִשׁ); KJV: Laish. Compare H3889 (לוּשׁ).

H3920 לָכַד (lâkad, law-kad'): to catch (in a net, trap or pit); generally, to capture or occupy; also to choose (by lot); figuratively, to cohere. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, catch (self), be frozen, be holden, stick together, take.

H3921 לֶכֶד (leked, leh'ked): something to capture with, i.e. a noose. Origin: from H3920 (לָכַד); KJV: being taken.

H3922 לֵכָה (lêkâh, lay-kaw'): Lekah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3212 (יָלַךְ); a journey; KJV: Lecah.

H3923 לָכִישׁ (Lâkîysh, law-keesh'): Lakish, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: Lachish.

H3924 לֻלָאָה (lulâʼâh, loo-law-aw'): a loop. Origin: from the same as H3883 (לוּל); KJV: loop.

H3925 לָמַד (lâmad, law-mad'): properly, to goad, i.e. (by implication) to teach (the rod being an Oriental incentive). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (un-) accustomed, [idiom] diligently, expert, instruct, learn, skilful, teach(-er, -ing).

H3926 לְמוֹ (lᵉmôw, lem-o'): to or for. Origin: a prolonged and separable form of the prepositional prefix; KJV: at, for, to, upon.

H3927 לְמוּאֵל (Lᵉmûwʼêl, lem-oo-ale'): Lemuel or Lemoel, a symbolic name of Solomon. Origin: or לְמוֹאֵל; from H3926 (לְמוֹ) and H410 (אֵל); (belonging) to God; KJV: Lemuel.

H3928 לִמּוּד (limmûwd, lim-mood'): instructed. Origin: or לִמֻּד; from H3925 (לָמַד); KJV: accustomed, disciple, learned, taught, used.

H3929 לֶמֶךְ (Lemek, leh'-mek): Lemek, the name of two antediluvian patriarchs. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: Lamech.

H3930 לֹעַ (lôaʻ, lo'ah): the gullet. Origin: from H3886 (לוּעַ); KJV: throat.

H3931 לָעַב (lâʻab, law-ab'): to deride. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mock.

H3932 לָעַג (lâʻag, law-ag'): to deride; by implication (as if imitating a foreigner) to speak unintelligibly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have in derision, laugh (to scorn), mock (on), stammering.

H3933 לַעַג (laʻag, lah'-ag): derision, scoffing. Origin: from H3932 (לָעַג); KJV: derision, scorn (-ing).

H3934 לָעֵג (lâʻêg, law-ayg'): a buffoon; also a foreigner. Origin: from H3932 (לָעַג); KJV: mocker, stammering.

H3935 לַעְדָּה (Laʻdâh, lah-daw'): Ladah, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: Laadah.

H3936 לַעְדָּן (Laʻdân, lah-dawn'): Ladan, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from the same as H3935 (לַעְדָּה); KJV: Laadan.

H3937 לָעַז (lâʻaz, law-az'): to speak in a foreign tongue. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: strange language.

H3938 לָעַט (lâʻaṭ, law-at'): to swallow greedily; causatively, to feed. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: feed.

H3939 לַעֲנָה (laʻănâh, lah-an-aw'): wormwood (regarded as poisonous, and therefore accursed). Origin: from an unused root supposed to mean to curse; KJV: hemlock, wormwood.

H3940 לַפִּיד (lappîyd, lap-peed'): a flambeau, lamp or flame. Origin: or לַפִּד; from an unused root probably meaning to shine; KJV: (fire-) brand, (burning) lamp, lightning, torch.

H3941 לַפִּידוֹת (Lappîydôwth, lap-pee-doth'): Lappidoth, the husband of Deborah. Origin: feminine plural of H3940 (לַפִּיד); KJV: Lappidoth.

H3942 לִפְנַי (liphnay, lif-nah'ee): anterior. Origin: from the prepositional prefix (to or for) and H6440 (פָּנִים); KJV: before.

H3943 לָפַת (lâphath, law-fath'): properly, to bend, i.e. (by implication) to clasp; also (reflexively) to turn around or aside. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: take hold, turn aside (self).

H3944 לָצוֹן (lâtsôwn, law-tsone'): derision. Origin: from H3887 (לוּץ); KJV: scornful(-ning).

H3945 לָצַץ (lâtsats, law-tsats'): to deride. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: scorn.

H3946 לַקּוּם (Laqqûwm, lak-koom'): Lakkum, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root thought to mean to stop up by a barricade; perhaps fortification; KJV: Lakum.

H3947 לָקַח (lâqach, law-kakh'): to take (in the widest variety of applications). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: accept, bring, buy, carry away, drawn, fetch, get, infold, [idiom] many, mingle, place, receive(-ing), reserve, seize, send for, take (away, -ing, up), use, win.

H3948 לֶקַח (leqach, leh'-kakh): properly, something received, i.e. (mentally) instruction (whether on the part of the teacher or hearer); also (in an active and sinister sense) inveiglement. Origin: from H3947 (לָקַח); KJV: doctrine, learning, fair speech.

H3949 לִקְחִי (Liqchîy, lik-khee'): Likchi, an Israelite. Origin: from H3947 (לָקַח); learned; KJV: Likhi.

H3950 לָקַט (lâqaṭ, law-kat'): properly, to pick up, i.e. (generally) to gather; specifically, to glean. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather (up), glean.

H3951 לֶקֶט (leqeṭ, leh'-ket): the gleaning. Origin: from H3950 (לָקַט); KJV: gleaning.

H3952 לָקַק (lâqaq, law-kak'): to lick or lap. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lap, lick.

H3953 לָקַשׁ (lâqash, law-kash'): to gather the after crop. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather.

H3954 לֶקֶשׁ (leqesh, leh'-kesh): the after crop. Origin: from H3953 (לָקַשׁ); KJV: latter growth.

H3955 לְשַׁד (lᵉshad, lesh-ad'): (figuratively) vigor; also a sweet or fat cake. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; apparently juice, i.e. KJV: fresh, moisture.

H3956 לָשׁוֹן (lâshôwn, law-shone'): the tongue (of man or animals), used literally (as the instrument of licking, eating, or speech), and figuratively (speech, an ingot, a fork of flame, a cove of water). Origin: or לָשֹׁן; also (in plural) feminine לְשֹׁנָה; from H3960 (לָשַׁן); KJV: [phrase] babbler, bay, [phrase] evil speaker, language, talker, tongue, wedge.

H3957 לִשְׁכָּה (lishkâh, lish-kaw'): a room in a building (whether for storage, eating, or lodging). Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: chamber, parlour. Compare H5393 (נִשְׁכָּה).

H3958 לֶשֶׁם (leshem, leh'-shem): a gem, perhaps the jacinth. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: ligure.

H3959 לֶשֶׁם (Leshem, leh'-shem): Leshem, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H3958 (לֶשֶׁם); KJV: Leshem.

H3960 לָשַׁן (lâshan, law-shan'): to wag the tongue, i.e. to calumniate. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to lick; but used only as a denominative from H3956 (לָשׁוֹן); KJV: accuse, slander.

H3961 לִשָּׁן (lishshân, lish-shawn'): speech, i.e. a nation. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3956 (לָשׁוֹן); KJV: language.

H3962 לֶשַׁע (Leshaʻ, leh'-shah): Lesha, a place probably East of the Jordan. Origin: from an unused root thought to mean to break through; a boiling spring; KJV: Lasha.

H3963 לֶתֶךְ (lethek, leh'-thek): a measure for things dry. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: half homer. m

H3964 מָא (mâʼ, maw): (as indefinitely) that. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4100 (מָה); KJV: [phrase] what.

H3965 מַאֲבוּס (maʼăbûwç, mah-ab-ooce'): a granary. Origin: from H75 (אָבַס); KJV: storehouse.

H3966 מְאֹד (mᵉʼôd, meh-ode'): properly, vehemence, i.e. (with or without preposition) vehemently; by implication, wholly, speedily, etc. (often with other words as an intensive or superlative; especially when repeated). Origin: from the same as H181 (אוּד); KJV: diligently, especially, exceeding(-ly), far, fast, good, great(-ly), [idiom] louder and louder, might(-ily, -y), (so) much, quickly, (so) sore, utterly, very ([phrase] much, sore), well.

H3967 מֵאָה (mêʼâh, may-aw'): a hundred; also as a multiplicative and a fraction. Origin: or מֵאיָה; properly, a primitive numeral KJV: hundred((-fold), -th), [phrase] sixscore.

H3968 מֵאָה (Mêʼâh, may-aw'): Meah, a tower in Jerusalem. Origin: the same as H3967 (מֵאָה); KJV: Meah.

H3969 מְאָה (mᵉʼâh, meh-aw'): a hundred; also as a multiplicative and a fraction}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3967 (מֵאָה); properly, a primitive numeral KJV: hundred.

H3970 מַאֲוַי (maʼăvay, mah-av-ah'ee): a desire. Origin: from H183 (אָוָה); KJV: desire.

H3971 מאוּם (mʼûwm, moom): to stain; a blemish (physically or morally). Origin: usually מוּם; as if passive participle from an unused root probably meaning KJV: blemish, blot, spot.

H3972 מְאוּמָה (mᵉʼûwmâh, meh-oo'-maw): properly, a speck or point, i.e. (by implication) something; with negative, nothing. Origin: apparently a form of H3971 (מאוּם); KJV: fault, [phrase] no(-ught), ought, somewhat, any (no-)thing.

H3973 מָאוֹס (mâʼôwç, maw-oce'): refuse. Origin: from H3988 (מָאַס); KJV: refuse.

H3974 מָאוֹר (mâʼôwr, maw-ore'): properly, a luminous body or luminary, i.e. (abstractly) light (as an element); figuratively, brightness, i.e.cheerfulness; specifically, a chandelier. Origin: or מָאֹר; also (in plural) feminine מְאוֹרָה; or מְאֹרָה; from H215 (אוֹר); KJV: bright, light.

H3975 מְאוּרָה (mᵉʼûwrâh, meh-oo-raw'): something lighted, i.e. an aperture; by implication, a crevice or hole (of a serpent). Origin: feminine passive participle of H215 (אוֹר); KJV: den.

H3976 מֹאזֵן (môʼzên, mo-zane'): (only in the dual) a pair of scales. Origin: from H239 (אָזַן); KJV: balances.

H3977 מֹאזֵן (môʼzên, mo-zane'): {(only in the dual) a pair of scales}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3976 (מֹאזֵן) KJV: balances.

H3978 מַאֲכָל (maʼăkâl, mah-ak-awl'): an eatable (includ. provender, flesh and fruit). Origin: from H398 (אָכַל); KJV: food, fruit, (bake-)meat(-s), victual.

H3979 מַאֲכֶלֶת (maʼăkeleth, mah-ak-eh'-leth): something to eat with,i.e. a knife. Origin: from H398 (אָכַל); KJV: knife.

H3980 מַאֲכֹלֶת (maʼăkôleth, mah-ak-o'-leth): something eaten (by fire), i.e. fuel. Origin: from H398 (אָכַל); KJV: fuel.

H3981 מַאֲמָץ (maʼămâts, mah-am-awts'): strength, i.e. (plural) resources. Origin: from H553 (אָמַץ); KJV: force.

H3982 מַאֲמַר (maʼămar, mah-am-ar'): something (authoritatively) said, i.e. an edict. Origin: from H559 (אָמַר); KJV: commandment, decree.

H3983 מֵאמַר (mêʼmar, may-mar'): {something (authoritatively) said, i.e. an edict}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H3982 (מַאֲמַר) KJV: appointment, word.

H3984 מָאן (mâʼn, mawn): a utensil. Origin: (Aramaic) probably from a root corresponding to H579 (אָנָה) in the sense of an inclosure by sides; KJV: vessel.

H3985 מָאֵן (mâʼên, maw-ane'): to refuse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: refuse, [idiom] utterly.

H3986 מָאֵן (mâʼên, maw-ane'): unwilling. Origin: from H3985 (מָאֵן); KJV: refuse.

H3987 מֵאֵן (mêʼên, may-ane'): refractory. Origin: from H3985 (מָאֵן); KJV: refuse.

H3988 מָאַס (mâʼaç, maw-as'): to spurn; also (intransitively) to disappear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor, cast away (off), contemn, despise, disdain, (become) loathe(some), melt away, refuse, reject, reprobate, [idiom] utterly, vile person.

H3989 מַאֲפֶה (maʼăpheh, mah-af-eh'): something baked, i.e. a batch. Origin: from H644 (אָפָה); KJV: baken.

H3990 מַאֲפֵל (maʼăphêl, mah-af-ale'): something opaque. Origin: from the same as H651 (אָפֵל); KJV: darkness.

H3991 מַאְפֵלְיָה (maʼphêlᵉyâh, mah-af-ay-leh-yaw'): opaqueness. Origin: prolonged feminine of H3990 (מַאֲפֵל); KJV: darkness.

H3992 מָאַר (mâʼar, maw-ar'): to be bitter or (causatively) to embitter, i.e. be painful. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fretting, picking.

H3993 מַאֲרָב (maʼărâb, mah-ar-awb'): an ambuscade. Origin: from H693 (אָרַב); KJV: lie in ambush, ambushment, lurking place, lying in wait.

H3994 מְאֵרָה (mᵉʼêrâh, meh-ay-raw'): an execration. Origin: from H779 (אָרַר); KJV: curse.

H3995 מִבְדָּלָה (mibdâlâh, mib-daw-law'): a separation, i.e. (concretely) a separate place. Origin: from H914 (בָּדַל); KJV: separate.

H3996 מָבוֹא (mâbôwʼ, maw-bo'): an entrance (the place or the act); specifically sunset or the west; also (adverb with preposition) towards. Origin: from H935 (בּוֹא); (with or without H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ)) KJV: by which came, as cometh, in coming, as men enter into, entering, entrance into, entry, where goeth, going down, [phrase] westward. Compare H4126 (מוֹבָא).

H3997 מְבוֹאָה (mᵉbôwʼâh, meb-o-aw'): a haven. Origin: feminine of H3996 (מָבוֹא); KJV: entry.

H3998 מְבוּכָה (mᵉbûwkâh, meb-oo-kaw'): perplexity. Origin: from H943 (בּוּךְ); KJV: perplexity.

H3999 מַבּוּל (mabbûwl, mab-bool'): a deluge. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל) in the sense of flowing; KJV: flood.

H4000 מָבוֹן (mâbôwn, maw-bone'): instructing. Origin: from H995 (בִּין); KJV: taught.

H4001 מְבוּסָה (mᵉbûwçâh, meb-oo-saw'): a trampling. Origin: from H947 (בּוּס); KJV: treading (trodden) down (under foot).

H4002 מַבּוּעַ (mabbûwaʻ, mab-boo'-ah): a fountain. Origin: from H5042 (נָבַע); KJV: fountain, spring.

H4003 מְבוּקָה (mᵉbûwqâh, meb-oo-kah'): emptiness. Origin: from the same as H950 (בּוּקָה); KJV: void.

H4004 מִבְחוֹר (mibchôwr, mib-khore'): select, i.e. well fortified. Origin: from H977 (בָּחַר); KJV: choice.

H4005 מִבְחָר (mibchâr, mib-khawr'): select, i.e. best. Origin: from H977 (בָּחַר); KJV: choice(-st), chosen.

H4006 מִבְחָר (Mibchâr, mib-khawr'): Mibchar, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4005 (מִבְחָר); KJV: Mibhar.

H4007 מַבָּט (mabbâṭ, mab-bawt'): something expected, i.e. (abstractly) expectation. Origin: or מֶבָּט; from H5027 (נָבַט); KJV: expectation.

H4008 מִבְטָא (mibṭâʼ, mib-taw'): a rash utterance (hasty vow). Origin: from H981 (בָּטָא); KJV: (that which...) uttered (out of).

H4009 מִבְטָח (mibṭâch, mib-tawkh'): properly, a refuge, i.e. (objective) security, or (subjective) assurance. Origin: from H982 (בָּטַח); KJV: confidence, hope, sure, trust.

H4010 מַבְלִיגִית (mablîygîyth, mab-leeg-eeth'): desistance (or rather desolation). Origin: from H1082 (בָּלַג); KJV: comfort self.

H4011 מִבְנֶה (mibneh, mib-neh'): a building. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: frame.

H4012 מְבֻנַּי (Mᵉbunnay, meb-oon-hah'-ee): Mebunnai, an Israelite. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); built up; KJV: Mebunnai.

H4013 מִבְצָר (mibtsâr, mib-tsawr'): a fortification, castle, or fortified city; figuratively, a defender. Origin: also (in plural) feminine (Daniel 11:l5) מִבְצָרָה; from H1219 (בָּצַר); KJV: (de-, most) fenced, fortress, (most) strong (hold).

H4014 מִבְצָר (Mibtsâr, mib-tsawr'): Mibtsar, an Idumaean. Origin: the same as H4013 (מִבְצָר); KJV: Mibzar.

H4015 מִבְרָח (mibrâch, mib-rawkh'): a refugee. Origin: from H1272 (בָּרַח); KJV: fugitive.

H4016 מָבֻשׁ (mâbush, maw-boosh'): (plural) the (male) pudenda. Origin: from H954 (בּוּשׁ); KJV: secrets.

H4017 מִבְשָׂם (Mibsâm, mib-sawm'): Mibsam, the name of an Ishmaelite and of an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H1314 (בֶּשֶׂם); fragrant; KJV: Mibsam.

H4018 מְבַשְּׁלָה (mᵉbashshᵉlâh, meb-ash-shel-aw'): a cooking hearth. Origin: from H1310 (בָּשַׁל); KJV: boiling-place.

H4019 מַגְבִּישׁ (Magbîysh, mag-beesh'): Magbish, an Israelite, or a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H1378 (גָּבִישׁ); stiffening; KJV: Magbish.

H4020 מִגְבָּלָה (migbâlâh, mig-baw-law'): a border. Origin: from H1379 (גָּבַל); KJV: end.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4021 to H4144
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4021 מִגְבָּעָה (migbâʻâh, mig-baw-aw'): a cap (as hemispherical). Origin: from the same as H1389 (גִּבְעָה); KJV: bonnet.

H4022 מֶגֶד (meged, meh'-ghed): properly, a distinguished thing; hence something valuable, as aproduct or fruit. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to be eminent; KJV: pleasant, precious fruit (thing).

H4023 מְגִדּוֹן (Mᵉgiddôwn, meg-id-done'): Megiddon or Megiddo, a place in Palestine. Origin: (Zechariah H12 (אַבְדָן)) or מְגִדּוֹ; from H1413 (גָּדַד); rendezvous; KJV: Megiddo, Megiddon.

H4024 מִגְדּוֹל (Migdôwl, mig-dole'): Migdol, a place in Egypt. Origin: or מִגְדֹּל; probably of Egyptian origin; KJV: Migdol, tower.

H4025 מַגְדִּיאֵל (Magdîyʼêl, mag-dee-ale'): Magdiel, an Idumaean. Origin: from H4022 (מֶגֶד) and H410 (אֵל); preciousness of God; KJV: Magdiel.

H4026 מִגְדָּל (migdâl, mig-dawl'): a tower (from its size or height); by analogy, a rostrum; figuratively, a (pyramidal) bed of flowers. Origin: also (in plural) feminine מִגְדָּלָה; from H1431 (גָּדַל); KJV: castle, flower, tower. Compare the names following.

H4027 מִגְדַּל־אֵל (Migdal-ʼÊl, mig-dal-ale'): Migdal-El, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4026 (מִגְדָּל) and H410 (אֵל); tower of God; KJV: Migdal-el.

H4028 מִגְדַּל־גָּד (Migdal-Gâd, migdal-gawd'): Migdal-Gad, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4026 (מִגְדָּל) and H1408 (גַּד); tower of Fortune; KJV: Migdal-gad.

H4029 מִגְדַּל־עֵדֶר (Migdal-ʻÊder, mig-dal'-ay'-der): Migdal-Eder, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4026 (מִגְדָּל) and H5739 (עֵדֶר); tower of a flock; KJV: Migdal-eder, tower of the flock.

H4030 מִגְדָּנָה (migdânâh, mig-daw-naw'): preciousness, i.e. a gem. Origin: from the same as H4022 (מֶגֶד); KJV: precious thing, present.

H4031 מָגוֹג (Mâgôwg, maw-gogue'): Magog, a son of Japheth; also a barbarous northern region. Origin: from H1463 (גּוֹג); KJV: Magog.

H4032 מָגוֹר (mâgôwr, maw-gore'): a fright (objective or subjective). Origin: or (Lamentations 2:22) מָגוּר; from H1481 (גּוּר) in the sense of fearing; KJV: fear, terror. Compare H4036 (מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב).

H4033 מָגוּר (mâgûwr, maw-goor'): a temporary abode; by extension, a permanent residence. Origin: or מָגֻר; from H1481 (גּוּר) in the sense of lodging; KJV: dwelling, pilgrimage, where sojourn, be a stranger. Compare H4032 (מָגוֹר).

H4034 מְגוֹרַה (mᵉgôwrah, meg-o-raw'): affright. Origin: feminine of H4032 (מָגוֹר); KJV: fear.

H4035 מְגוּרָה (mᵉgûwrâh, meg-oo-raw'): a fright; also a granary. Origin: feminine of H4032 (מָגוֹר) or of H4033 (מָגוּר); KJV: barn, fear.

H4036 מָגוֹר מִסָּבִיב (Mâgôwr miç-Çâbîyb, maw-gore' mis-saw-beeb'): Magor-mis-Sabib, a symbolic name of Pashur. Origin: from H4032 (מָגוֹר) and H5439 (סָבִיב) with the preposition inserted; affright from around; KJV: Magormissabib.

H4037 מַגְזֵרָה (magzêrâh, mag-zay-raw'): a cutting implement, i.e. a blade. Origin: from H1504 (גָּזַר); KJV: axe.

H4038 מַגָּל (maggâl, mag-gawl'): a sickle. Origin: from an unused root meaning to reap; KJV: sickle.

H4039 מְגִלָּה (mᵉgillâh, meg-il-law'): a roll. Origin: from H1556 (גָּלַל); KJV: roll, volume.

H4040 מְגִלָּה (mᵉgillâh, meg-il-law'): {a roll}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4039 (מְגִלָּה) KJV: roll.

H4041 מְגַמָּה (mᵉgammâh, meg-am-maw'): properly, accumulation, i.e. impulse or direction. Origin: from the same as H1571 (גַּם); KJV: sup up.

H4042 מָגַן (mâgan, maw-gan'): properly, to shield; encompass with; figuratively, to rescue, to hand safely over (i.e. surrender). Origin: a denominative from H4043 (מָגֵן); KJV: deliver.

H4043 מָגֵן (mâgên, maw-gane'): a shield (i.e. the small one or buckler); figuratively, a protector; also the scaly hide of the crocodile. Origin: also (in plural) feminine מְגִנָּה; from H1598 (גָּנַן); KJV: [idiom] armed, buckler, defence, ruler, [phrase] scale, shield.

H4044 מְגִנָּה (mᵉginnâh, meg-in-naw'): a covering (in a bad sense), i.e. blindness or obduracy. Origin: from H4042 (מָגַן); KJV: sorrow. See also H4043 (מָגֵן).

H4045 מִגְעֶרֶת (migʻereth, mig-eh'-reth): reproof (i.e. curse). Origin: from H1605 (גָּעַר); KJV: rebuke.

H4046 מַגֵּפָה (maggêphâh, mag-gay-faw'): a pestilence; by analogy, defeat. Origin: from H5062 (נָגַף); KJV: ([idiom] be) plague(-d), slaughter, stroke.

H4047 מַגְפִּיעָשׁ (Magpîyʻâsh, mag-pee-awsh'): Magpiash, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H1479 (גּוּף) or H5062 (נָגַף) and H6211 (עָשׁ); exterminator of (the) moth; KJV: Magpiash.

H4048 מָגַר (mâgar, maw-gar'): to yield up; intensively, to precipitate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast down, terror.

H4049 מְגַר (mᵉgar, meg-ar'): to overthrow. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4048 (מָגַר); KJV: destroy.

H4050 מְגֵרָה (mᵉgêrâh, meg-ay-raw'): a saw. Origin: from H1641 (גָּרַר); KJV: axe, saw.

H4051 מִגְרוֹן (Migrôwn, mig-rone'): Migron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4048 (מָגַר); precipice; KJV: Migron.

H4052 מִגְרָעָה (migrâʻâh, mig-raw-aw'): a ledge or offset. Origin: from H1639 (גָּרַע); KJV: narrowed rest.

H4053 מִגְרָפָה (migrâphâh, mig-raw-faw'): something thrown off (by the spade), i.e. a clod. Origin: from H1640 (גָּרַף); KJV: clod.

H4054 מִגְרָשׁ (migrâsh, mig-rawsh'): a suburb (i.e. open country whither flocks are driven from pasture); hence, the area around abuilding, or the margin of the sea. Origin: also (in plural) feminine (Ezekiel 27:28) מִגְרָשָׁה; from H1644 (גָּרַשׁ); KJV: cast out, suburb.

H4055 מַד (mad, mad): properly, extent, i.e. height; also a measure; by implication, a vesture (as measured); also a carpet. Origin: or מֵד; from H4058 (מָדַד); KJV: armour, clothes, garment, judgment, measure, raiment, stature.

H4056 מַדְבַּח (madbach, mad-bakh'): a sacrificial altar. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1684 (דְּבַח); KJV: altar.

H4057 מִדְבָּר (midbâr, mid-bawr'): a pasture (i.e. open field, whither cattle are driven); by implication, a desert; also speech (including its organs). Origin: from H1696 (דָבַר) in the sense of driving; KJV: desert, south, speech, wilderness.

H4058 מָדַד (mâdad, maw-dad'): properly, to stretch; by implication, to measure (as if by stretching a line); figuratively, to be extended. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: measure, mete, stretch self.

H4059 מִדַּד (middad, mid-dad'): flight. Origin: from H5074 (נָדַד); KJV: be gone.

H4060 מִדָּה (middâh, mid-daw'): properly, extension, i.e. height or breadth; also a measure (including its standard); hence a portion (as measured) or a vestment; specifically, tribute (as measured). Origin: feminine of H4055 (מַד); KJV: garment, measure(-ing, meteyard, piece, size, (great) stature, tribute, wide.

H4061 מִדָּה (middâh, mid-daw'): tribute in money. Origin: (Aramaic) or מִנְדָּה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H4060 (מִדָּה); KJV: toll, tribute.

H4062 מַדְהֵבָה (madhêbâh, mad-hay-baw'): goldmaking, i.e. exactness. Origin: perhaps from the equivalent of H1722 (דְּהַב); KJV: golden city.

H4063 מֶדֶו (medev, meh'-dev): properly, extent, i.e. measure; by implication, a dress (as measured). Origin: from an unused root meaning to stretch; KJV: garment.

H4064 מַדְוֶה (madveh, mad-veh'): sickness. Origin: from H1738 (דָּוָה); KJV: disease.

H4065 מַדּוּחַ (maddûwach, mad-doo'akh): seduction. Origin: from H5080 (נָדַח); KJV: cause of banishment.

H4066 מָדוֹן (mâdôwn, maw-dohn'): a contest or quarrel. Origin: from H1777 (דִּין); KJV: brawling, contention(-ous), discord, strife. Compare H4079 (מִדְיָן), H4090 (מְדָן).

H4067 מָדוֹן (mâdôwn, maw-dohn'): extensiveness, i.e. height. Origin: from the same as H4063 (מֶדֶו); KJV: stature.

H4068 מָדוֹן (Mâdôwn, maw-dohn'): Madon, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H4067 (מָדוֹן); KJV: Madon.

H4069 מַדּוּעַ (maddûwaʻ, mad-doo'-ah): what (is) known?; i.e. (by implication) (adverbially) why?. Origin: or מַדֻּעַ; from H4100 (מָה) and the passive participle of H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: how, wherefore, why.

H4070 מְדוֹר (mᵉdôwr, med-ore'): a dwelling. Origin: (Aramaic) or מְדֹר; (Aramaic), or מְדָר; (Aramaic), from H1753 (דּוּר); KJV: dwelling.

H4071 מְדוּרָה (mᵉdûwrâh, med-oo-raw'): a pile of fuel. Origin: or מְדֻרָה; from H1752 (דּוּר) in the sense of accumulation; KJV: pile (for fire).

H4072 מִדְחֶה (midcheh, mid-kheh'): overthrow. Origin: from H1760 (דָּחָה); KJV: ruin.

H4073 מְדַחְפָה (mᵉdachphâh, med-akh-faw'): a push, i.e. ruin. Origin: from H1765 (דָּחַף); KJV: overthrow.

H4074 מָדַי (Mâday, maw-dah'-ee): Madai, a country of central Asia. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Madai, Medes, Media.

H4075 מָדַי (Mâday, maw-dah'-ee): a Madian or native of Madai. Origin: patrial from H4074 (מָדַי); KJV: Mede.

H4076 מָדַי (Mâday, maw-dah'-ee): {Madai, a country of central Asia}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4074 (מָדַי) KJV: Mede(-s).

H4077 מָדַי (Mâday, maw-dah'-ee): {a Madian or native of Madai}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4075 (מָדַי) KJV: Median.

H4078 מַדַּי (madday, mad-dah'-ee): what (is) enough, i.e. sufficiently. Origin: from H4100 (מָה) and H1767 (דַּי); KJV: sufficiently.

H4079 מִדְיָן (midyân, mid-yawn'): {a contest or quarrel}. Origin: a variation for H4066 (מָדוֹן) KJV: brawling, contention(-ous).

H4080 מִדְיָן (Midyân, mid-yawn'): Midjan, a son of Abraham; also his country and (collectively) his descendants. Origin: the same as H4079 (מִדְיָן); KJV: Midian, Midianite.

H4081 מִדִּין (Middîyn, mid-deen'): {Midjan, a son of Abraham; also his country and (collectively) his descendants}. Origin: a variation for H4080 (מִדְיָן) KJV: Middin.

H4082 מְדִינָה (mᵉdîynâh, med-ee-naw'): properly, a judgeship, i.e. jurisdiction; by implication, a district (as ruled by a judge); generally, a region. Origin: from H1777 (דִּין); KJV: ([idiom] every) province.

H4083 מְדִינָה (mᵉdîynâh, med-ee-naw'): {properly, a judgeship, i.e. jurisdiction; by implication, a district (as ruled by a judge); generally, a region}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4082 (מְדִינָה) KJV: province.

H4084 מִדְיָנִי (Midyânîy, mid-yaw-nee'): a Midjanite or descendant (native) of Midjan. Origin: patronymical or patrial from H4080 (מִדְיָן); KJV: Midianite. Compare H4092 (מְדָנִי).

H4085 מְדֹכָה (mᵉdôkâh, med-o-kaw'): a mortar. Origin: from H1743 (דּוּךְ); KJV: mortar.

H4086 מַדְמֵן (Madmên, mad-mane'): Madmen, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H1828 (דֹּמֶן); dunghill; KJV: Madmen.

H4087 מַדְמֵנָה (madmênâh, mad-may-naw'): a dunghill. Origin: feminine from the same as H1828 (דֹּמֶן); KJV: dunghill.

H4088 מַדְמֵנָה (Madmênâh, mad-may-naw'): Madmenah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H4087 (מַדְמֵנָה); KJV: Madmenah.

H4089 מַדְמַנָּה (Madmannâh, mad-man-naw'): Madmannah, a place in Palestine. Origin: a variation for H4087 (מַדְמֵנָה); KJV: Madmannah.

H4090 מְדָן (mᵉdân, med-awn'): {a contest or quarrel}. Origin: a form of H4066 (מָדוֹן) KJV: discord, strife.

H4091 מְדָן (Mᵉdân, med-awn'): Medan, a son of Abraham. Origin: the same as H4090 (מְדָן); KJV: Medan.

H4092 מְדָנִי (Mᵉdânîy, med-aw-nee'): {a Midjanite or descendant (native) of Midjan}. Origin: a variation of H4084 (מִדְיָנִי) KJV: Midianite.

H4093 מַדָּע (maddâʻ, mad-daw'): intelligence or consciousness. Origin: or מַדַּע; from H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: knowledge, science, thought.

H4094 מַדְקָרָה (madqârâh, mad-kaw-raw'): a wound. Origin: from H1856 (דָּקַר); KJV: piercing.

H4095 מַדְרֵגָה (madrêgâh, mad-ray-gaw'): properly, a step; by implication, a steep or inaccessible place. Origin: from an unused root meaning to step; KJV: stair, steep place.

H4096 מִדְרָךְ (midrâk, mid-rawk'): a treading, i.e. a place for stepping on. Origin: from H1869 (דָּרַךְ); KJV: (foot-) breadth.

H4097 מִדְרָשׁ (midrâsh, mid-rawsh'): properly, an investigation, i.e. (by implication) a treatise or elaborate compilation. Origin: from H1875 (דָּרַשׁ); KJV: story.

H4098 מְדֻשָּׁה (mᵉdushshâh, med-oosh-shaw'): a threshing, i.e. (concretely and figuratively) down-trodden people. Origin: from H1758 (דּוּשׁ); KJV: threshing.

H4099 מְדָתָא (Mᵉdâthâʼ, med-aw-thaw'): Medatha, the father of Haman. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Hammedatha (including the article).

H4100 מָה (mâh, maw): properly, interrogative what? (including how? why? when?); but also exclamation, what! (including how!), or indefinitely what (including whatever, and even relatively, that which); often used with prefixes in various adverbial or conjunctive senses. Origin: or מַה; or מָ; or מַ; also מֶה; a primitive particle; KJV: how (long, oft, (-soever)), (no-) thing, what (end, good, purpose, thing), whereby(-fore, -in, -to, -with), (for) why.

H4101 מָה (mâh, maw): {properly, interrogative what? (including how? why? when?); but also exclamation, what! (including how!), or indefinitely what}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4100 (מָה) KJV: how great (mighty), that which, what(-soever), why.

H4102 מָהַהּ (mâhahh, maw-hah'): properly, to question or hesitate, i.e. (by implication) to be reluctant. Origin: apparently a denominative from H4100 (מָה); KJV: delay, linger, stay selves, tarry.

H4103 מְהוּמָה (mᵉhûwmâh, meh-hoo-maw'): confusion or uproar. Origin: from H1949 (הוּם); KJV: destruction, discomfiture, trouble, tumult, vexation, vexed.

H4104 מְהוּמָן (Mᵉhûwmân, meh-hoo-mawn'): Mehuman, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Mehuman.

H4105 מְהֵיטַבְאֵל (Mᵉhêyṭabʼêl, meh-hay-tab-ale'): Mehetabel, the name of an Edomitish man and woman. Origin: from H3190 (יָטַב) (augmented) and H410 (אֵל); bettered of God; KJV: Mehetabeel, Mehetabel.

H4106 מָהִיר (mâhîyr, maw-here'): quick; hence, skilful. Origin: or מָהִר; from H4116 (מָהַר); KJV: diligent, hasty, ready.

H4107 מָהַל (mâhal, maw-hal'): properly, to cut down or reduce, i.e. by implication, to adulterate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mixed.

H4108 מַהְלֵךְ (mahlêk, mah-lake'): a walking (plural collectively), i.e. access. Origin: from H1980 (הָלַךְ); KJV: place to walk.

H4109 מַהֲלָךְ (mahălâk, mah-hal-awk'): a walk, i.e. a passage or a distance. Origin: from H1980 (הָלַךְ); KJV: journey, walk.

H4110 מַהֲלָל (mahălâl, mah-hal-awl'): fame. Origin: from H1984 (הָלַל); KJV: praise.

H4111 מַהֲלַלְאֵל (Mahălalʼêl, mah-hal-al-ale'): Mahalalel, the name of an antediluvian patriarch and of an Israelite. Origin: from H4110 (מַהֲלָל) and H410 (אֵל); praise of God; KJV: Mahalaleel.

H4112 מַהֲלֻמָּה (mahălummâh, mah-hal-oom-maw'): a blow. Origin: from H1986 (הָלַם); KJV: stripe, stroke.

H4113 מַהֲמֹרָה (mahămôrâh, mah-ham-o-raw'): perhaps an abyss. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: deep pit.

H4114 מַהְפֵּכָה (mahpêkâh, mah-pay-kaw'): a destruction. Origin: from H2015 (הָפַךְ); KJV: when...overthrew, overthrow(-n).

H4115 מַהְפֶּכֶת (mahpeketh, mah-peh'-keth): a wrench, i.e. the stocks. Origin: from H2015 (הָפַךְ); KJV: prison, stocks.

H4116 מָהַר (mâhar, maw-har'): properly, to be liquid or flow easily, i.e. (by implication); to hurry (in a good or a bad sense); often used (with another verb) adverbially, promptly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be carried headlong, fearful, (cause to make, in, make) haste(-n, -ily), (be) hasty, (fetch, make ready) [idiom] quickly, rash, [idiom] shortly, (be so) [idiom] soon, make speed, [idiom] speedily, [idiom] straightway, [idiom] suddenly, swift.

H4117 מָהַר (mâhar, maw-har'): to bargain (for a wife), i.e. to wed. Origin: a primitive root (perhaps rather the same as H4116 (מָהַר) through the idea of readiness in assent); KJV: endow, [idiom] surely.

H4118 מַהֵר (mahêr, mah-hare'): properly, hurrying; hence (adverbially) in ahurry. Origin: from H4116 (מָהַר); KJV: hasteth, hastily, at once, quickly, soon, speedily, suddenly.

H4119 מֹהַר (môhar, mo'-har): a price (for a wife). Origin: from H4117 (מָהַר); KJV: dowry.

H4120 מְהֵרָה (mᵉhêrâh, meh-hay-raw'): properly, a hurry; hence (adverbially) promptly. Origin: feminine of H4118 (מַהֵר); KJV: hastily, quickly, shortly, soon, make (with) speed(-ily), swiftly.

H4121 מַהֲרַי (Mahăray, mah-har-ah'-ee): Maharai, an Israelite. Origin: from H4116 (מָהַר); hasty; KJV: Maharai.

H4122 מַהֵר שָׁלָל חָשׁ בַּז (Mahêr Shâlâl Châsh Baz, mah-hare' shaw-lawl' khawsh baz): Maher-Shalal-Chash-Baz; the symbolical name of the son of Isaiah. Origin: from H4118 (מַהֵר) and H7998 (שָׁלָל) and H2363 (חוּשׁ) and H957 (בַּז); hasting (is he (the enemy) to the) booty, swift (to the) prey; KJV: Maher-sha-lal-bash-baz.

H4123 מַהֲתַלָּה (mahăthallâh, mah-hath-al-law'): a delusion. Origin: from H2048 (הָתַל); KJV: deceit.

H4124 מוֹאָב (Môwʼâb, mo-awb): Moab, an incestuous son of Lot; also his territory and descendants. Origin: from a prolonged form of the prepositional prefix m-and H1 (אָב); from (her (the mother's)) father; KJV: Moab.

H4125 מוֹאָבִי (Môwʼâbîy, mo-aw-bee'): a Moabite or Moabitess, i.e. a descendant from Moab. Origin: feminine מוֹאָבִיָּה; or מוֹאָבִיתxlit Môwâbîyth corrected to Môwʼâbîyth; patronymical from H4124 (מוֹאָב); KJV: (woman) of Moab, Moabite(-ish, -ss).

H4126 מוֹבָא (môwbâʼ, mo-baw'): an entrance. Origin: by transp. for H3996 (מָבוֹא); KJV: coming.

H4127 מוּג (mûwg, moog): to melt, i.e. literally (to soften, flow down, disappear), or figuratively (to fear, faint). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consume, dissolve, (be) faint(-hearted), melt (away), make soft.

H4128 מוּד (mûwd, mood): to shake. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: measure.

H4129 מוֹדַע (môwdaʻ, mo-dah'): an acquaintance. Origin: or rather מֹדָע; from H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: kinswoman.

H4130 מוֹדַעַת (môwdaʻath, mo-dah'-ath): acquaintance. Origin: from H3045 (יָדַע); KJV: kindred.

H4131 מוֹט (môwṭ, mote): to waver; by implication, to slip, shake, fall. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be carried, cast, be out of course, be fallen in decay, [idiom] exceedingly, fall(-ing down), be (re-) moved, be ready, shake, slide, slip.

H4132 מוֹט (môwṭ, mote): a wavering, i.e. fall; by implication, a pole (as shaking); hence, a yoke (as essentially a bent pole). Origin: from H4131 (מוֹט); KJV: bar, be moved, staff, yoke.

H4133 מוֹטָה (môwṭâh, mo-taw'): a pole; by implication, an ox-bow; hence, a yoke (either literal or figurative). Origin: feminine of H4132 (מוֹט); KJV: bands, heavy, staves, yoke.

H4134 מוּךְ (mûwk, mook): to become thin, i.e. (figuratively) be impoverished. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (waxen) poor(-er).

H4135 מוּל (mûwl, mool): to cut short, i.e. curtail (specifically the prepuce, i.e. to circumcise); by implication, to blunt; figuratively, to destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: circumcise(-ing), selves), cut down (in pieces), destroy, [idiom] must needs.

H4136 מוּל (mûwl, mool): properly, abrupt, i.e. a precipice; by implication, the front; used only adverbially (with prepositional prefix) opposite. Origin: or מוֹל; (Deuteronomy 1:1), or מוֹאל; (Nehemiah 12:38), or מֻל; (Numbers 22:5), from H4135 (מוּל); KJV: (over) against, before, (fore-) front, from, (God-) ward, toward, with.

H4137 מוֹלָדָה (Môwlâdâh, mo-law-daw'): Moladah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3205 (יָלַד); birth; KJV: Moladah.

H4138 מוֹלֶדֶת (môwledeth, mo-leh'-deth): nativity (plural birth-place); by implication, lineage, native country; also offspring, family. Origin: from H3205 (יָלַד); KJV: begotten, born, issue, kindred, native(-ity).

H4139 מוּלָה (mûwlâh, moo-law'): circumcision. Origin: from H4135 (מוּל); KJV: circumcision.

H4140 מוֹלִיד (Môwlîyd, mo-leed'): Molid, an Israelite. Origin: from H3205 (יָלַד); genitor; KJV: Molid.

H4141 מוּסָב (mûwçâb, moo-sawb'): a turn, i.e. circuit (of a building). Origin: from H5437 (סָבַב); KJV: winding about.

H4142 מוּסַבָּה (mûwçabbâh, moo-sab-baw'): a reversal, i.e. the backside (of a gem), fold (of a double-leaved door), transmutation (of a name). Origin: or מֻסַבָּה; feminine of H4141 (מוּסָב); KJV: being changed, inclosed, be set, turning.

H4143 מוּסָד (mûwçâd, moo-sawd'): a foundation. Origin: from H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: foundation.

H4144 מוֹסָד (môwçâd, mo-sawd'): a foundation. Origin: from H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: foundation.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4145 to H4271
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4145 מוּסָדָה (mûwçâdâh, moo-saw-daw'): a foundation; figuratively, an appointment. Origin: feminine of H4143 (מוּסָד); KJV: foundation, grounded. Compare H4328 (מְיֻסָּדָה).

H4146 מוֹסָדָה (môwçâdâh, mo-saw-daw'): a foundation. Origin: or מֹסָדָה; feminine of H4144 (מוֹסָד); KJV: foundation.

H4147 מוֹסֵר (môwçêr, mo-sare'): properly, chastisement, i.e. (by implication) a halter; figuratively, restraint. Origin: also (in plural) feminine מוֹסֵרָה; or מֹסְרָה; from H3256 (יָסַר); KJV: band, bond.

H4148 מוּסָר (mûwçâr, moo-sawr'): properly, chastisement; figuratively, reproof, warning or instruction; also restraint. Origin: from H3256 (יָסַר); KJV: bond, chastening(-eth), chastisement, check, correction, discipline, doctrine, instruction, rebuke.

H4149 מוֹסֵרָה (Môwçêrâh, mo-say-raw'): Moserah or Moseroth, a place in the Desert. Origin: or (plural) מֹסְרוֹת feminine of H4147 (מוֹסֵר); correction or corrections; KJV: Mosera, Moseroth.

H4150 מוֹעֵד (môwʻêd, mo-ade'): properly, an appointment, i.e. a fixed time or season; specifically, a festival; conventionally ayear; by implication, an assembly (as convened for a definite purpose); technically the congregation; by extension, the place of meeting; also a signal (as appointed beforehand). Origin: or מֹעֵד; or (feminine) מוֹעָדָה; (2 Chronicles 8:13), from H3259 (יָעַד); KJV: appointed (sign, time), (place of, solemn) assembly, congregation, (set, solemn) feast, (appointed, due) season, solemn(-ity), synogogue, (set) time (appointed).

H4151 מוֹעָד (môwʻâd, mo-awd'): properly, an assembly figuratively, a troop. Origin: from H3259 (יָעַד); (as in H4150 (מוֹעֵד)); KJV: appointed time.

H4152 מוּעָדָה (mûwʻâdâh, moo-aw-daw'): an appointed place, i.e. asylum. Origin: from H3259 (יָעַד); KJV: appointed.

H4153 מוֹעַדְיָה (Môwʻadyâh, mo-ad-yaw'): Moadjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H4151 (מוֹעָד) and H3050 (יָהּ); assembly of Jah; KJV: Moadiah. Compare H4573 (מַעֲדְיָה).

H4154 מוּעֶדֶת (mûwʻedeth, moo-ay'-deth): properly, made to slip, i.e. dislocated. Origin: feminine passive participle of H4571 (מָעַד); KJV: out of joint.

H4155 מוּעָף (mûwʻâph, moo-awf'): properly, covered, i.e. dark; abstractly, obscurity, i.e. distress. Origin: from H5774 (עוּף); KJV: dimness.

H4156 מוֹעֵצָה (môwʻêtsâh, mo-ay-tsaw'): a purpose. Origin: from H3289 (יָעַץ); KJV: counsel, device.

H4157 מוּעָקָה (mûwʻâqâh, moo-aw-kaw'): pressure, i.e. (figuratively) distress. Origin: from H5781 (עוּק); KJV: affliction.

H4158 מוֹפַעַת (Môwphaʻath, mo-fah'-ath): Mophaath or Mephaath, a place in Palestine. Origin: (Jeremiah 48:21) or מֵיפַעַת; or מֵפַעַת; from H3313 (יָפַע); illuminative; KJV: Mephaath.

H4159 מוֹפֵת (môwphêth, mo-faith'): a miracle; by implication, a token or omen. Origin: or מֹפֵת; from H3302 (יָפָה) in the sense of conspicuousness; KJV: miracle, sign, wonder(-ed at).

H4160 מוּץ (mûwts, moots): to press, i.e. (figuratively) to oppress. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: extortioner.

H4161 מוֹצָא (môwtsâʼ, mo-tsaw'): a going forth, i.e. (the act) an egress, or (the place) an exit; hence, a source or product; specifically, dawn, the rising of the sun (the East), exportation, utterance, a gate, a fountain, a mine, a meadow (as producing grass). Origin: or מֹצָאxlit môtsâ corrected to môtsâʼ; from H3318 (יָצָא); KJV: brought out, bud, that which came out, east, going forth, goings out, that which (thing that) is gone out, outgoing, proceeded out, spring, vein, (water-) course (springs).

H4162 מוֹצָא (môwtsâʼ, mo-tsaw'): Motsa, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H4161 (מוֹצָא); KJV: Moza.

H4163 מוֹצָאָה (môwtsâʼâh, mo-tsaw-aw'): a family descent; also a sewer. Origin: feminine of H4161 (מוֹצָא); (marg.; compare H6675 (צוֹאָה)) KJV: draught house; going forth.

H4164 מוּצַק (mûwtsaq, moo-tsak'): narrowness; figuratively, distress. Origin: or מוּצָק; from H3332 (יָצַק); KJV: anguish, is straitened, straitness.

H4165 מוּצָק (mûwtsâq, moo-tsawk'): properly, fusion, i.e. literally, a casting (of metal); figuratively, a mass (of clay). Origin: from H5694 (עָגִיל); KJV: casting, hardness.

H4166 מוּצָקָה (mûwtsâqâh, moo-tsaw-kaw'): properly, something poured out, i.e. a casting (of metal); by implication, a tube (as cast). Origin: or מֻצָקָה; from H3332 (יָצַק); KJV: when it was cast, pipe.

H4167 מוּק (mûwq, mook): to jeer, i.e. (intens.) blaspheme. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be corrupt.

H4168 מוֹקֵד (môwqêd, mo-kade'): a fire or fuel; abstractly, a conflagration. Origin: from H3344 (יָקַד); KJV: burning, hearth.

H4169 מוֹקְדָה (môwqᵉdâh, mo-ked-aw'): fuel. Origin: feminine of H4168 (מוֹקֵד); KJV: burning.

H4170 מוֹקֵשׁ (môwqêsh, mo-kashe'): a noose (for catching animals) (literally or figuratively); by implication, a hook (for the nose). Origin: or מֹקֵשׁ; from H3369 (יָקֹשׁ); KJV: be ensnared, gin, (is) snare(-d), trap.

H4171 מוּר (mûwr, moor): to alter; by implication, to barter, to dispose of. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, (ex-) change, remove.

H4172 מוֹרָא (môwrâʼ, mo-raw'): fear; by implication, a fearful thing or deed. Origin: or מֹרָא; or מוֹרָהxlit môrâh corrected to môwrâh; (Psalm 9:20), from H3372 (יָרֵא); KJV: dread, (that ought to be) fear(-ed), terribleness, terror.

H4173 מוֹרַג (môwrag, mo-rag'): a threshing sledge. Origin: or מֹרַג; from an unused root meaning to triturate; KJV: threshing instrument.

H4174 מוֹרָד (môwrâd, mo-rawd'): a descent; as architecture, an ornamental appendage, perhaps a festoon. Origin: from H3381 (יָרַד); KJV: going down, steep place, thin work.

H4175 מוֹרֶה (môwreh, mo-reh'): an archer; also teacher or teaching; also the early rain. Origin: from H3384 (יָרָה); (see H3138 (יוֹרֶה)) KJV: (early) rain.

H4176 מוֹרֶה (Môwreh, mo-reh'): Moreh, a Canaanite; also a hill (perhaps named from him). Origin: or מֹרֶה; the same as H4175 (מוֹרֶה); KJV: Moreh.

H4177 מוֹרָה (môwrâh, mo-raw'): a razor. Origin: from H4171 (מוּר) in the sense of shearing; KJV: razor.

H4178 מוֹרָט (môwrâṭ, mo-rawt'): obstinate, i.e. independent. Origin: from H3399 (יָרַט); KJV: peeled.

H4179 מוֹרִיָּה (Môwrîyâh, mo-ree-yaw'): Morijah, a hill in Palestine. Origin: or מֹרִיָּה; from H7200 (רָאָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); seen of Jah; KJV: Moriah.

H4180 מוֹרָשׁ (môwrâsh, mo-rawsh'): a possession; figuratively, delight. Origin: from H3423 (יָרַשׁ); KJV: possession, thought.

H4181 מוֹרָשָׁה (môwrâshâh, mo-raw-shaw'): a possession. Origin: feminine of H4180 (מוֹרָשׁ); KJV: heritage, inheritance, possession.

H4182 מוֹרֶשֶׁת גַּת (Môwresheth Gath, mo-reh'-sheth gath): Moresheth-Gath, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3423 (יָרַשׁ) and H1661 (גַּת); possession of Gath; KJV: Moresheth-gath.

H4183 מוֹרַשְׁתִּי (Môwrashtîy, mo-rash-tee'): a Morashtite or inhabitant of Moresheth-Gath. Origin: patrial from H4182 (מוֹרֶשֶׁת גַּת); KJV: Morashthite.

H4184 מוּשׁ (mûwsh, moosh): to touch. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: feel, handle.

H4185 מוּשׁ (mûwsh, moosh): to withdraw (both literally and figuratively, whether intransitive or transitive). Origin: a primitive root (perhaps rather the same as H4184 (מוּשׁ) through the idea of receding by contact); KJV: cease, depart, go back, remove, take away.

H4186 מוֹשָׁב (môwshâb, mo-shawb'): a seat; figuratively, a site; abstractly, a session; by extension an abode (the place or the time); by implication, population. Origin: or מֹשָׁב; from H3427 (יָשַׁב); KJV: assembly, dwell in, dwelling(-place), wherein (that) dwelt (in), inhabited place, seat, sitting, situation, sojourning.

H4187 מוּשִׁי (Mûwshîy, moo-shee'): Mushi, a Levite. Origin: or מֻשִּׁי; from H4184 (מוּשׁ); sensitive; KJV: Mushi.

H4188 מוּשִׁי (Mûwshîy, moo-shee'): a Mushite (collectively) or descendants of Mushi. Origin: patronymical from H4187 (מוּשִׁי); KJV: Mushites.

H4189 מוֹשְׁכָה (môwshᵉkâh, mo-shek-aw'): something drawing, i.e. (figuratively) a cord. Origin: act participle feminine of H4900 (מָשַׁךְ); KJV: band.

H4190 מוֹשָׁעָה (môwshâʻâh, mo-shaw-aw'): deliverance. Origin: from H3467 (יָשַׁע); KJV: salvation.

H4191 מוּת (mûwth, mooth): to die (literally or figuratively); causatively, to kill. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, [idiom] crying, (be) dead (body, man, one), (put to, worthy of) death, destroy(-er), (cause to, be like to, must) die, kill, necro(-mancer), [idiom] must needs, slay, [idiom] surely, [idiom] very suddenly, [idiom] in (no) wise.

H4192 מוּת (Mûwth, mooth): 'To die for the son', probably the title of a popular song. Origin: (Psalm H48 (אֲבִירָם) or מוּת לַבֵּן; from H4191 (מוּת) and H1121 (בֵּן) with the preposition and article interposed; KJV: death, Muthlabben.

H4193 מוֹת (môwth, mohth): death. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4194 (מָוֶת); KJV: death.

H4194 מָוֶת (mâveth, maw'-veth): death (natural or violent); concretely, the dead, their place or state (hades); figuratively, pestilence, ruin. Origin: from H4191 (מוּת); KJV: (be) dead(-ly), death, die(-d).

H4195 מוֹתָר (môwthâr, mo-thar'): literally gain; figuratively, superiority. Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); KJV: plenteousness, preeminence, profit.

H4196 מִזְבֵּחַ (mizbêach, miz-bay'-akh): an altar. Origin: from H2076 (זָבַח); KJV: altar.

H4197 מֶזֶג (mezeg, meh'-zeg): tempered wine. Origin: from an unused root meaning to mingle (water with wine); KJV: liquor.

H4198 מָזֶה (mâzeh, maw-zeh'): exhausted. Origin: from an unused root meaning to suck out; KJV: burnt.

H4199 מִזָּה (Mizzâh, miz-zaw'): Mizzah, an Edomite. Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to faint with fear; terror; KJV: Mizzah.

H4200 מֶזֶו (mezev, meh'-zev): a granary. Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to gather in; KJV: garner.

H4201 מְזוּזָה (mᵉzûwzâh, mez-oo-zaw'): a door-post (as prominent). Origin: or מְזֻזָה; from the same as H2123 (זִיז); KJV: (door, side) post.

H4202 מָזוֹן (mâzôwn, maw-zone'): food. Origin: from H2109 (זוּן); KJV: meat, victual.

H4203 מָזוֹן (mâzôwn, maw-zone'): {food}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4202 (מָזוֹן) KJV: meat.

H4204 מָזוֹר (mâzôwr, maw-zore'): treachery, i.e. a plot. Origin: from H2114 (זוּר) in the sense of turning aside from truth; KJV: wound.

H4205 מָזוֹר (mâzôwr, maw-zore'): a bandage, i.e. remedy; hence, a sore (as needing a compress). Origin: or מָזֹר; from H2115 (זוּר) in the sense of binding up; KJV: bound up, wound.

H4206 מָזִיחַ (mâzîyach, maw-zee'-akh): a belt (as movable). Origin: or מֵזַח; from H2118 (זָחַח); KJV: girdle, strength.

H4207 מַזְלֵג (mazlêg, maz-layg'): a fork. Origin: or (feminine) מִזְלָגָה; from an unused root meaning to draw up; KJV: fleshhook.

H4208 מַזָּלָה (mazzâlâh, maz-zaw-law'): a constellation, i.e. Zodiacal sign (perhaps as affecting the weather). Origin: apparently from H5140 (נָזַל) in the sense of raining; KJV: planet. Compare H4216 (מַזָּרָה).

H4209 מְזִמָּה (mᵉzimmâh, mez-im-maw'): a plan, usually evil (machination), sometimes good (sagacity). Origin: from H2161 (זָמַם); KJV: (wicked) device, discretion, intent, witty invention, lewdness, mischievous (device), thought, wickedly.

H4210 מִזְמוֹר (mizmôwr, miz-more'): properly, instrumental music; by implication, a poem set to notes. Origin: from H2167 (זָמַר); KJV: psalm.

H4211 מַזְמֵרָה (mazmêrâh, maz-may-raw'): a pruningknife. Origin: from H2168 (זָמַר); KJV: pruning-hook.

H4212 מְזַמְּרָה (mᵉzammᵉrâh, mez-am-mer-aw'): a tweezer (only in the plural). Origin: from H2168 (זָמַר); KJV: snuffers.

H4213 מִזְעָר (mizʻâr, miz-awr'): fewness; by implication, as superl. diminutiveness. Origin: from the same as H2191 (זְעֵיר)xlit zeʻêyr corrected to zᵉʻêyr; KJV: few, [idiom] very.

H4214 מִזְרֶה (mizreh, miz-reh'): a winnowing shovel (as scattering the chaff). Origin: from H2219 (זָרָה); KJV: fan.

H4215 מְזָרֶה (mᵉzâreh, mez-aw-reh'): properly, a scatterer, i.e. the north wind (as dispersing clouds; only in plural). Origin: apparently from H2219 (זָרָה); KJV: north.

H4216 מַזָּרָה (mazzârâh, maz-zaw-raw'): some noted constellation (only in the plural), perhaps collectively, the zodiac. Origin: apparently from H5144 (נָזַר) in the sense of distinction; KJV: Mazzoroth. Compare H4208 (מַזָּלָה).

H4217 מִזְרָח (mizrâch, miz-rawkh'): sunrise, i.e. the east. Origin: from H2224 (זָרַח); KJV: east (side, -ward), (sun-) rising (of the sun).

H4218 מִזְרָע (mizrâʻ, miz-raw'): a planted field. Origin: from H2232 (זָרַע); KJV: thing sown.

H4219 מִזְרָק (mizrâq, miz-rawk'): a bowl (as if for sprinkling). Origin: from H2236 (זָרַק); KJV: bason, bowl.

H4220 מֵחַ (mêach, may'-akh): fat; figuratively, rich. Origin: from H4229 (מָחָה) in the sense of greasing; KJV: fatling (one).

H4221 מֹחַ (môach, mo'-akh): fat, i.e. marrow. Origin: from the same as H4220 (מֵחַ); KJV: marrow.

H4222 מָחָא (mâchâʼ, maw-khaw'): to rub or strike the hands together (in exultation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: clap.

H4223 מְחָא (mᵉchâʼ, mekh-aw'): to strike in pieces; also to arrest; specifically to impale. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4222 (מָחָא); KJV: hang, smite, stay.

H4224 מַחֲבֵא (machăbêʼ, makh-ab-ay'): a refuge. Origin: or מַחֲבֹא; from H2244 (חָבָא); KJV: hiding (lurking) place.

H4225 מַחְבֶּרֶת (machbereth, makh-beh'-reth): a junction, i.e. seam or sewed piece. Origin: from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: coupling.

H4226 מְחַבְּרָה (mᵉchabbᵉrâh, mekh-ab-ber-aw'): a joiner, i.e. brace or cramp. Origin: from H2266 (חָבַר); KJV: coupling, joining.

H4227 מַחֲבַת (machăbath, makh-ab-ath'): a pan for baking in. Origin: from the same as H2281 (חָבֵת); KJV: pan.

H4228 מַחֲגֹרֶת (machăgôreth, makh-ag-o'-reth): a girdle. Origin: from H2296 (חָגַר); KJV: girding.

H4229 מָחָה (mâchâh, maw-khaw'): properly, to stroke or rub; by implication, to erase; also to smooth (as if with oil), i.e. grease or make fat; also to touch, i.e. reach to. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abolish, blot out, destroy, full of marrow, put out, reach unto, [idiom] utterly, wipe (away, out).

H4230 מְחוּגָה (mᵉchûwgâh, mekk-oo-gaw'): an instrument for marking a circle, i.e. compasses. Origin: from H2328 (חוּג); KJV: compass.

H4231 מָחוֹז (mâchôwz, maw-khoze'): a harbor (as shut in by the shore). Origin: from an unused root meaning to enclose; KJV: haven.

H4232 מְחוּיָאֵל (Mᵉchûwyâʼêl, mekh-oo-yaw-ale'): Mechujael or Mechijael, an antediluvian patriarch. Origin: or מְחִיּיָאֵל; from H4229 (מָחָה) and H410 (אֵל); smitten of God; KJV: Mehujael.

H4233 מַחֲוִים (Machăvîym, makh-av-eem'): a Machavite or inhabitant of some place named Machaveh. Origin: apparently a patrial, but from an unknown place (in the plural only for a singular); KJV: Mahavite.

H4234 מָחוֹל (mâchôwl, maw-khole'): a (round) dance. Origin: from H2342 (חוּל); KJV: dance(-cing).

H4235 מָחוֹל (Mâchôwl, maw-khole'): Machol, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4234 (מָחוֹל); dancing; KJV: Mahol.

H4236 מַחֲזֶה (machăzeh, makh-az-eh'): a vision. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: vision.

H4237 מֶחֱזָה (mechĕzâh, mekh-ez-aw'): a window. Origin: from H2372 (חָזָה); KJV: light.

H4238 מַחֲזִיאוֹת (Machăzîyʼôwth, makh-az-ee-oth'): Machazioth, an Israelite. Origin: feminine plural from H2372 (חָזָה); visions; KJV: Mahazioth.

H4239 מְחִי (mᵉchîy, mekh-ee'): a stroke, i.e. battering-ram. Origin: from H4229 (מָחָה); KJV: engines.

H4240 מְחִידָא (Mᵉchîydâʼ, mek-ee-daw'): Mechida, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from H2330 (חוּד); junction; KJV: Mehida.

H4241 מִחְיָה (michyâh, mikh-yaw'): preservation of life; hence, sustenance; also the live flesh, i.e. the quick. Origin: from H2421 (חָיָה); KJV: preserve life, quick, recover selves, reviving, sustenance, victuals.

H4242 מְחִיר (mᵉchîyr, mekk-eer'): price, payment, wages. Origin: from an unused root meaning to buy; KJV: gain, hire, price, sold, worth.

H4243 מְחִיר (Mᵉchîyr, mekh-eer'): Mechir, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4242 (מְחִיר); price; KJV: Mehir.

H4244 מַחְלָה (Machlâh, makh-law'): Machlah, the name apparently of two Israelitesses. Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); sickness; KJV: Mahlah.

H4245 מַחֲלֶה (machăleh, makh-al-eh'): sickness. Origin: or (feminine) מַחֲלָה; from H2470 (חָלָה); KJV: disease, infirmity, sickness.

H4246 מְחֹלָה (mᵉchôlâh, mek-o-law'): a dance. Origin: feminine of H4234 (מָחוֹל); KJV: company, dances(-cing).

H4247 מְחִלָּה (mᵉchillâh, mekh-il-law'): a cavern (as if excavated). Origin: from H2490 (חָלַל); KJV: cave.

H4248 מַחְלוֹן (Machlôwn, makh-lone'): Machlon, an Israelite. Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); sick; KJV: Mahlon.

H4249 מַחְלִי (Machlîy, makh-lee'): Machli, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); sick; KJV: Mahli.

H4250 מַחְלִי (Machlîy, makh-lee'): a Machlite or (collectively) descendants of Machli. Origin: patronymical from H4249 (מַחְלִי); KJV: Mahlites.

H4251 מַחְלֻי (machluy, makh-loo'-ee): a disease. Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); KJV: disease.

H4252 מַחֲלָף (machălâph, makh-al-awf'): a (sacrificial) knife (as gliding through the flesh). Origin: from H2498 (חָלַף); KJV: knife.

H4253 מַחְלָפָה (machlâphâh, makh-law-faw'): a ringlet of hair (as gliding over each other). Origin: from H2498 (חָלַף); KJV: lock.

H4254 מַחֲלָצָה (machălâtsâh, makh-al-aw-tsaw'): a mantle (as easily drawn off). Origin: from H2502 (חָלַץ); KJV: changeable suit of apparel, change of raiment.

H4255 מַחְלְקָה (machlᵉqâh, makh-lek-aw'): a section (of the Levites). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4256 (מַחֲלֹקֶת); KJV: course.

H4256 מַחֲלֹקֶת (machălôqeth, makh-al-o'-keth): a section (of Levites, people or soldiers). Origin: from H2505 (חָלַק); KJV: company, course, division, portion. See also H5555 (סֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת).

H4257 מַחֲלַת (machălath, makh-al-ath'): 'Machalath', probably the title (initial word) of a popular song. Origin: from H2470 (חָלָה); sickness; KJV: Mahalath.

H4258 מַחֲלַת (Machălath, makh-al-ath'): Machalath, the name of an Ishmaelitess and of an Israelitess. Origin: the same as H4257 (מַחֲלַת); sickness; KJV: Mahalath.

H4259 מְחֹלָתִי (Mᵉchôlâthîy, mekh-o-law-thee'): a Mecholathite or inhabitant of Abel-Mecholah. Origin: patrial from H65 (אָבֵל מְחוֹלָה); KJV: Mecholathite.

H4260 מַחֲמָאָה (machămâʼâh, makh-am-aw-aw'): something buttery (i.e. unctuous and pleasant), as (figuratively) flattery. Origin: a denominative from H2529 (חֶמְאָה); KJV: [idiom] than butter.

H4261 מַחְמָד (machmâd, makh-mawd'): delightful; hence, a delight, i.e. object of affection or desire. Origin: from H2530 (חָמַד); KJV: beloved, desire, goodly, lovely, pleasant (thing).

H4262 מַחְמֻד (machmud, makh-mood'): desired; hence, a valuable. Origin: or מַחְמוּד; from H2530 (חָמַד); KJV: pleasant thing.

H4263 מַחְמָל (machmâl, makh-mawl'): properly, sympathy. Origin: from H2550 (חָמַל); (by paronomasia with H4261 (מַחְמָד)) delight KJV: pitieth.

H4264 מַחֲנֶה (machăneh, makh-an-eh'): an encampment (of travellers or troops); hence, an army, whether literal (of soldiers) or figurative (of dancers, angels, cattle, locusts, stars; or even the sacred courts). Origin: from H2583 (חָנָה); KJV: army, band, battle, camp, company, drove, host, tents.

H4265 מַחֲנֵה־דָן (Machănêh-Dân, makh-an-ay'-dawn): Machaneh-Dan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4264 (מַחֲנֶה) and H1835 (דָּן); camp of Dan; KJV: Mahaneh-dan.

H4266 מַחֲנַיִם (Machănayim, makh-an-ah'-yim): Machanajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of H4264 (מַחֲנֶה); double camp; KJV: Mahanaim.

H4267 מַחֲנַק (machănaq, makh-an-ak'): choking. Origin: from H2614 (חָנַק); KJV: strangling.

H4268 מַחֲסֶה (machăçeh, makh-as-eh'): a shelter (literally or figuratively). Origin: or מַחְסֶה; from H2620 (חָסָה); KJV: hope, (place of) refuge, shelter, trust.

H4269 מַחְסוֹם (machçôwm, makh-sohm'): a muzzle. Origin: from H2629 (חָסַם); KJV: bridle.

H4270 מַחְסוֹר (machçôwr, makh-sore'): deficiency; hence, impoverishment. Origin: or מַחְסֹר; from H2637 (חָסֵר); KJV: lack, need, penury, poor, poverty, want.

H4271 מַחְסֵיָה (Machçêyâh, makh-say-yaw'): Machsejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H4268 (מַחֲסֶה) and H3050 (יָהּ); refuge of (i.e. in) Jah; KJV: Maaseiah.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4272 to H4396
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4272 מָחַץ (mâchats, maw-khats'): to dash asunder; by implication, to crush, smash or violently plunge; figuratively, to subdue or destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dip, pierce (through), smite (through), strike through, wound.

H4273 מַחַץ (machats, makh'-ats): a contusion. Origin: from H4272 (מָחַץ); KJV: stroke.

H4274 מַחְצֵב (machtsêb, makh-tsabe'): properly, a hewing; concretely, a quarry. Origin: from H2672 (חָצַב); KJV: hewed(-n).

H4275 מֶחֱצָה (mechĕtsâh, mekh-ets-aw'): a halving. Origin: from H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; KJV: half.

H4276 מַחֲצִית (machătsîyth, makh-ats-eeth'): a halving or the middle. Origin: from H2673 (חָצָה)lemma חָעָה ayin, corrected to חָצָה; KJV: half (so much), mid(-day).

H4277 מָחַק (mâchaq, maw-khak'): to crush. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: smite off.

H4278 מֶחְקָר (mechqâr, mekh-kawr'): properly, scrutinized, i.e. (by implication) a recess. Origin: from H2713 (חָקַר); KJV: deep place.

H4279 מָחָר (mâchâr, maw-khar'): properly, deferred, i.e. the morrow; usually (adverbially) tomorrow; indefinitely, hereafter. Origin: probably from H309 (אָחַר); KJV: time to come, tomorrow.

H4280 מַחֲרָאָה (machărâʼâh, makh-ar-aw-aw'): a sink. Origin: from the same as H2716 (חֶרֶא); KJV: draught house.

H4281 מַחֲרֵשָׁה (machărêshâh, makh-ar-ay-shaw'): probably a pick-axe. Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: mattock.

H4282 מַחֲרֶשֶׁת (machăresheth, makh-ar-eh'-sheth): probably a hoe. Origin: from H2790 (חָרַשׁ); KJV: share.

H4283 מׇחֳרָת (mochŏrâth, mokh-or-awth'): the morrow or (adverbially) tomorrow. Origin: or מׇחֳרָתָם; (1 Samuel 30:17), feminine from the same as H4279 (מָחָר); KJV: morrow, next day.

H4284 מַחֲשָׁבָה (machăshâbâh, makh-ash-aw-baw'): a contrivance, i.e. (concretely) a texture, machine, or (abstractly) intention, plan (whether bad, a plot; or good, advice). Origin: or מַחֲשֶׁבֶת; from H2803 (חָשַׁב); KJV: cunning (work), curious work, device(-sed), imagination, invented, means, purpose, thought.

H4285 מַחְשָׁךְ (machshâk, makh-shawk'): darkness; concretely, a dark place. Origin: from H2821 (חָשַׁךְ); KJV: dark(-ness, place).

H4286 מַחְשֹׂף (machsôph, makh-sofe'): a peeling. Origin: from H2834 (חָשַׂף); KJV: made appear.

H4287 מַחַת (Machath, makh'-ath): Machath, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably from H4229 (מָחָה); erasure; KJV: Mahath.

H4288 מְחִתָּה (mᵉchittâh, mekh-it-taw'): properly, a dissolution; concretely, a ruin, or (abstractly) consternation. Origin: from H2846 (חָתָה); KJV: destruction, dismaying, ruin, terror.

H4289 מַחְתָּה (machtâh, makh-taw'): a pan for live coals. Origin: the same as H4288 (מְחִתָּה) in the sense of removal; KJV: censer, firepan, snuffdish.

H4290 מַחְתֶּרֶת (machtereth, makh-teh'-reth): a burglary; figuratively, unexpected examination. Origin: from H2864 (חָתַר); KJV: breaking up, secret search.

H4291 מְטָא (mᵉṭâʼ, met-aw'): to arrive, extend or happen. Origin: (Aramaic) or מְטָה; (Aramaic), apparently corresponding to H4672 (מָצָא) in the intransitive sense of being found present; KJV: come, reach.

H4292 מַטְאֲטֵא (maṭʼăṭêʼ, mat-at-ay'): a broom (as removing dirt (compare English 'to dust', i.e. remove dust)). Origin: apparently a denominative from H2916 (טִיט); KJV: besom.

H4293 מַטְבֵּחַ (maṭbêach, mat-bay'-akh): slaughter. Origin: from H2873 (טָבַח); KJV: slaughter.

H4294 מַטֶּה (maṭṭeh, mat-teh'): a branch (as extending); figuratively, a tribe; also a rod, whether for chastising (figuratively, correction), ruling (a sceptre), throwing (a lance), or walking (a staff; figuratively, a support of life, e.g. bread). Origin: or (feminine) מַטָּה; from H5186 (נָטָה); KJV: rod, staff, tribe.

H4295 מַטָּה (maṭṭâh, mat'-taw): downward, below or beneath; often adverbially with or without prefixes. Origin: from H5786 (עָוַר) with directive enclitic appended; KJV: beneath, down(-ward), less, very low, under(-neath).

H4296 מִטָּה (miṭṭâh, mit-taw'): a bed (as extended) forsleeping or eating; by analogy, a sofa, litter or bier. Origin: from H5186 (נָטָה); KJV: bed(-chamber), bier.

H4297 מֻטֶּה (muṭṭeh, moot-teh'): a stretching, i.e. distortion (figuratively, iniquity). Origin: from H5186 (נָטָה); KJV: perverseness.

H4298 מֻטָּה (muṭṭâh, moot-taw'): expansion. Origin: from H5186 (נָטָה); KJV: stretching out.

H4299 מַטְוֶה (maṭveh, mat-veh'): something spun. Origin: from H2901 (טָוָה); KJV: spun.

H4300 מְטִיל (mᵉṭîyl, met-eel'): an iron bar (as forged). Origin: from H2904 (טוּל) in the sense of hammering out; KJV: bar.

H4301 מַטְמוֹן (maṭmôwn, mat-mone'): a secret storehouse; hence, a secreted valuable (buried); generally money. Origin: or מַטְמֹן; or מַטְמֻן; from H2934 (טָמַן); KJV: hidden riches, (hid) treasure(-s).

H4302 מַטָּע (maṭṭâʻ, mat-taw'): something planted, i.e. the place (a garden or vineyard), or the thing (a plant, figuratively or men); by implication, the act, planting. Origin: from H5193 (נָטַע); KJV: plant(-ation, -ing).

H4303 מַטְעַם (maṭʻam, mat-am'): a delicacy. Origin: or (feminine) מַטְעַמָּה; from H2938 (טָעַם); KJV: dainty (meat), savoury meat.

H4304 מִטְפַּחַת (miṭpachath, mit-pakh'-ath): a wide cloak (for a woman). Origin: from H2946 (טָפַח); KJV: vail, wimple.

H4305 מָטַר (mâṭar, maw-tar'): to rain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) rain (upon).

H4306 מָטַר (mâṭar, maw-tawr'): rain. Origin: from H4305 (מָטַר); KJV: rain.

H4307 מַטָּרָא (maṭṭârâʼ, mat-taw-raw'): a jail (as a guard-house); also an aim (as being closely watched). Origin: or מַטָּרָה; from H5201 (נָטַר); KJV: mark, prison.

H4308 מַטְרֵד (Maṭrêd, mat-rade'): Matred, an Edomitess. Origin: from H2956 (טָרַד); propulsive; KJV: Matred.

H4309 מַטְרִי (Maṭrîy, mat-ree'): Matri, an Israelite. Origin: from H4305 (מָטַר); rainy; KJV: Matri.

H4310 מִי (mîy, me): who? (occasionally, by a peculiar idiom, of things); also (indefinitely) whoever; often used in oblique construction with prefix or suffix. Origin: an interrogative pronoun of persons, as H4100 (מָה) is of things, KJV: any (man), [idiom] he, [idiom] him, [phrase] O that! what, which, who(-m, -se, -soever), [phrase] would to God.

H4311 מֵידְבָא (Mêydᵉbâʼ, may-deb-aw'): Medeba, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4325 (מַיִם) and H1679 (דֹּבֶא); water of quiet; KJV: Medeba.

H4312 מֵידָד (Mêydâd, may-dawd'): Medad, an Israelite. Origin: from H3032 (יָדַד) in the sense of loving; affectionate; KJV: Medad.

H4313 מֵי הַיַּרְקוֹן (Mêy hay-Yarqôwn, may hah'-ee-yar-kone'): Me-haj-Jarkon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H4325 (מַיִם) and H3420 (יֵרָקוֹן) with the art. interposed; water of the yellowness; KJV: Me-jarkon.

H4314 מֵי זָהָב (Mêy Zâhâb, may zaw-hawb'): Me-Zahab, an Edomite. Origin: from H4325 (מַיִם) and H2091 (זָהָב), water of gold; KJV: Mezahab.

H4315 מֵיטָב (mêyṭâb, may-tawb'): the best part. Origin: from H3190 (יָטַב); KJV: best.

H4316 מִיכָא (Mîykâʼ, mee-kaw'): Mica, the name of two Israelites. Origin: a variation for H4318 (מִיכָה); KJV: Micha.

H4317 מִיכָאֵל (Mîykâʼêl, me-kaw-ale'): Mikael, the name of an archangel and of nine Israelites. Origin: from H4310 (מִי) and (the prefix derivative from) H3588 (כִּי) and H410 (אֵל); who (is) like God?; KJV: Michael.

H4318 מִיכָה (Mîykâh, mee-kaw'): Micah, the name of seven Israelites. Origin: an abbreviated form of H4320 (מִיכָיָה); KJV: Micah, Micaiah, Michah.

H4319 מִיכָהוּ (Mîykâhûw, me-kaw'-hoo): Mikehu, an Israelite prophet. Origin: a contr. for H4321 (מִיכָיְהוּ); KJV: Micaiah (2 Chronicles 18:8).

H4320 מִיכָיָה (Mîykâyâh, me-kaw-yaw'): Micajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H4310 (מִי) and (the prefix derivative from) H3588 (כִּי) and H3050 (יָהּ); who (is) like Jah?; KJV: Micah, Michaiah. Compare H4318 (מִיכָה).

H4321 מִיכָיְהוּ (Mîykâyᵉhûw, me-kaw-yeh-hoo'): Mikajah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: or מִכָיְהוּ; (Jeremiah 36:11), abbreviated form for H4322 (מִיכָיָהוּ); KJV: Micah, Micaiah, Michaiah.

H4322 מִיכָיָהוּ (Mîykâyâhûw, me-kaw-yaw'-hoo): Mikajah, the name of an Israelite and an Israelitess. Origin: for H4320 (מִיכָיָה); KJV: Michaiah.

H4323 מִיכָל (mîykâl, me-kawl'): properly, a container, i.e. a streamlet. Origin: from H3201 (יָכֹל); KJV: brook.

H4324 מִיכָל (Mîykâl, me-kawl'): Mikal, Saul's daughter. Origin: apparently the same as H4323 (מִיכָל); revulet; KJV: Michal.

H4325 מַיִם (mayim, mah'-yim): water; figuratively, juice; by euphemism, urine, semen. Origin: dual of a primitive noun (but used in a singular sense); KJV: [phrase] piss, wasting, water(-ing, (-course, -flood, -spring)).

H4326 מִיָּמִן (Mîyâmin, me-yaw-meem'): Mijamin, the name of three Israelites. Origin: a form for H4509 (מִנְיָמִין); KJV: Miamin, Mijamin.

H4327 מִין (mîyn, meen): a sort, i.e. species. Origin: from an unused root meaning to portion out; KJV: kind. Compare H4480 (מִן).

H4328 מְיֻסָּדָה (mᵉyuççâdâh, meh-yoos-saw-daw'): something founded, i.e. a foundation. Origin: properly, feminine passive participle of H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: foundation.

H4329 מֵיסָךְ (mêyçâk, may-sawk'): a portico (as covered). Origin: from H5526 (סָכַךְ); KJV: covert.

H4330 מִיץ (mîyts, meets): pressure. Origin: from H4160 (מוּץ); KJV: churning, forcing, wringing.
