H4331 מֵישָׁא (Mêyshâʼ, may-shaw'): Mesha, a place in Arabia; also an Israelite. Origin: from H4185 (מוּשׁ); departure; KJV: Mesha.

H4332 מִישָׁאֵל (Mîyshâʼêl, mee-shaw-ale'): Mishael, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H4310 (מִי) and H410 (אֵל) with the abbreviated form insep. relatively (see H834 (אֲשֶׁר)) interposed; who (is) what God (is) ?; KJV: Mishael.

H4333 מִישָׁאֵל (Mîyshâʼêl, mee-shaw-ale'): Mishael, an Israelite. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4332 (מִישָׁאֵל); KJV: Mishael.

H4334 מִישׁוֹר (mîyshôwr, mee-shore'): a level, i.e. a plain (often used (with the article prefix) as a proper name of certain districts); figuratively, concord; also straightness, i.e. (figuratively) justice (sometimes adverbially, justly). Origin: or מִישֹׁר; from H3474 (יָשַׁר); KJV: equity, even place, plain, right(-eously), (made) straight, uprightness.

H4335 מֵישַׁךְ (Mêyshak, may-shak'): Meshak, an Israelite. Origin: borrowed from H4336 (מֵישַׁךְ); KJV: Meshak.

H4336 מֵישַׁךְ (Mêyshak, may-shak'): Meshak, the Babylonian. Origin: (Aramaic) of foreign origin and doubtful significance; name of H4333 (מִישָׁאֵל) KJV: Meshak.

H4337 מֵישָׁע (Mêyshâʻ, may-shah'): Mesha, an Israelite. Origin: from H3467 (יָשַׁע); safety; KJV: Mesha.

H4338 מֵישַׁע (Mêyshaʻ, may-shaw'): Mesha, a Moabite. Origin: a variation for H4337 (מֵישָׁע); safety; KJV: Mesha.

H4339 מֵישָׁר (mêyshâr, may-shawr'): evenness, i.e. (figuratively) prosperity or concord; also straightness, i.e. (figuratively) rectitude (only in plural with singular sense; often adverbially). Origin: from H3474 (יָשַׁר); KJV: agreement, aright, that are equal, equity, (things that are) right(-eously, things), sweetly, upright(-ly, -ness).

H4340 מֵיתָר (mêythâr, may-thar'): a cord (of a tent); or the string (of a bow). Origin: from H3498 (יָתַר); (compare H3499 (יֶתֶר)) KJV: cord, string.

H4341 מַכְאֹב (makʼôb, mak-obe'): anguish or (figuratively) affliction. Origin: sometimes מַכְאוֹב; also (feminine Isaiah 53:3) מַכְאֹבָה; from H3510 (כָּאַב); KJV: grief, pain, sorrow.

H4342 מַכְבִּיר (makbîyr, mak-beer'): plenty. Origin: transitive participle of H3527 (כָּבַר); KJV: abundance.

H4343 מַכְבֵּנָא (Makbênâʼ, mak-bay-naw'): Macbena, a place in Palestine settled by him. Origin: from the same as H3522 (כַּבּוֹן); knoll; KJV: Machbenah.

H4344 מַכְבַּנַּי (Makbannay, mak-ban-nah'-ee): a Macbannite or native of Macbena. Origin: patrial from H4343 (מַכְבֵּנָא); KJV: Machbanai.

H4345 מַכְבֵּר (makbêr, mak-bare'): a grate. Origin: from H3527 (כָּבַר) in the sense of covering (compare H3531 (כְּבָרָה)); KJV: grate.

H4346 מַכְבָּר (makbâr, mak-bawr'): a cloth (as netted). Origin: from H3527 (כָּבַר) in the sense of covering; (compare H4345 (מַכְבֵּר)) KJV: thick cloth.

H4347 מַכָּה (makkâh, mak-kaw'): a wound; figuratively, carnage, also pestilence. Origin: or (masculine) מַכֶּה; (plural only) from H5221 (נָכָה); a blow (in 2 Chronicles 2:10, of the flail); by implication, KJV: beaten, blow, plague, slaughter, smote, [idiom] sore, stripe, stroke, wound(-ed).

H4348 מִכְוָה (mikvâh, mik-vaw'): a burn. Origin: from H3554 (כָּוָה); KJV: that burneth, burning.

H4349 מָכוֹן (mâkôwn, maw-kone'): properly, a fixture, i.e. a basis; generally a place, especially as an abode. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); KJV: foundation, habitation, (dwelling-, settled) place.

H4350 מְכוֹנָה (mᵉkôwnâh, mek-o-naw'): a pedestal, also a spot. Origin: or מְכֹנָה; feminine of H4349 (מָכוֹן); KJV: base.

H4351 מְכוּרָה (mᵉkûwrâh, mek-oo-raw'): origin (as if a mine). Origin: or מְכֹרָה; from the same as H3564 (כּוּר) in the sense of dipping; KJV: birth, habitation, nativity.

H4352 מָכִי (Mâkîy, maw-kee'): Maki, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H4134 (מוּךְ); pining; KJV: Machi.

H4353 מָכִיר (Mâkîyr, maw-keer'): Makir, an Israelite. Origin: from H4376 (מָכַר); salesman; KJV: Machir.

H4354 מָכִירִי (Mâkîyrîy, maw-kee-ree'): a Makirite or descendant of Makir. Origin: patronymical from H4353 (מָכִיר); KJV: of Machir.

H4355 מָכַךְ (mâkak, maw-kak'): to tumble (in ruins); figuratively, to perish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be brought low, decay.

H4356 מִכְלָאָה (miklâʼâh, mik-law-aw'): a pen (for flocks). Origin: or מִכְלָה; from H3607 (כָּלָא); KJV: (sheep-)fold. Compare H4357 (מִכְלָה).

H4357 מִכְלָה (miklâh, mik-law'): completion (in plural concrete adverbial, wholly). Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: perfect. Compare H4356 (מִכְלָאָה).

H4358 מִכְלוֹל (miklôwl, mik-lole'): perfection (i.e. concrete adverbial, splendidly). Origin: from H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: most gorgeously, all sorts.

H4359 מִכְלָל (miklâl, mik-lawl'): perfection (of beauty). Origin: from H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: perfection.

H4360 מִכְלֻל (miklul, mik-lool'): something perfect, i.e. a splendid garment. Origin: from H3634 (כָּלַל); KJV: all sorts.

H4361 מַכֹּלֶת (makkôleth, mak-ko'-leth): nourishment. Origin: from H398 (אָכַל); KJV: food.

H4362 מִכְמַן (mikman, mik-man'): treasure (as hidden). Origin: from the same as H3646 (כַּמֹּן) in the sense of hiding; KJV: treasure.

H4363 מִכְמָס (Mikmâç, mik-maws'): Mikmas or Mikmash, a place in Palestine. Origin: (Ezra 2:2 or מִכְמָשׁ; or מִכְמַשׁ; (Nehemiah 11:31), from H3647 (כָּמַס); hidden; KJV: Mikmas, Mikmash.

H4364 מַכְמָר (makmâr, mak-mawr'): a (hunter's) net (as dark from concealment). Origin: or מִכְמֹר; from H3648 (כָּמַר) in the sense of blackening by heat; KJV: net.

H4365 מִכְמֶרֶת (mikmereth, mik-meh'-reth): a (fisher's) net. Origin: or מִכְמֹרֶת; feminine of H4364 (מַכְמָר); KJV: drag, net.

H4366 מִכְמְתָת (Mikmᵉthâth, mik-meth-awth'): Mikmethath, a place in Palestine. Origin: apparently from an unused root meaning to hide; concealment; KJV: Michmethath.

H4367 מַכְנַדְבַי (Maknadbay, mak-nad-bah'-ee): Maknadbai, an Israelite. Origin: from H4100 (מָה) and H5068 (נָדַב) with a particle interposed; what (is) like (a) liberal (man) ?; KJV: Machnadebai.

H4368 מְכֹנָה (Mᵉkônâh, mek-o-naw'): Mekonah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H4350 (מְכוֹנָה); a base; KJV: Mekonah.

H4369 מְכֻנָה (mᵉkunâh, mek-oo-naw'): a spot. Origin: the same as H4350 (מְכוֹנָה); KJV: base.

H4370 מִכְנָס (miknâç, mik-nawce'): (only in dual) drawers (from concealing the private parts). Origin: from H3647 (כָּמַס) in the sense of hiding; KJV: breeches.

H4371 מֶכֶס (mekeç, meh'-kes): an assessment (as based upon a census). Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to enumerate; KJV: tribute.

H4372 מִכְסֶה (mikçeh, mik-seh'): a covering, i.e. weatherboarding. Origin: from H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: covering.

H4373 מִכְסָה (mikçâh, mik-saw'): an enumeration; by implication, a valuation. Origin: feminine of H4371 (מֶכֶס); KJV: number, worth.

H4374 מְכַסֶּה (mᵉkaççeh, mek-as-seh'): a covering, i.e. garment; specifically, a coverlet (for a bed), an awning (from the sun); also the omentum (as covering the intestines). Origin: from H3680 (כָּסָה); KJV: clothing, to cover, that which covereth.

H4375 מַכְפֵּלָה (Makpêlâh, mak-pay-law'): Makpelah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3717 (כָּפַל); a fold; KJV: Machpelah.

H4376 מָכַר (mâkar, maw-kar'): to sell, literally (as merchandise, a daughter in marriage, into slavery), or figuratively (to surrender). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, sell (away, -er, self).

H4377 מֶכֶר (meker, meh'-ker): merchandise; also value. Origin: from H4376 (מָכַר); KJV: pay, price, ware.

H4378 מַכָּר (makkâr, mak-kawr'): an acquaintance. Origin: from H5234 (נָכַר); KJV: acquaintance.

H4379 מִכְרֶה (mikreh, mik-reh'): a pit (for salt). Origin: from H3738 (כָּרָה); KJV: (salt-) pit.

H4380 מְכֵרָה (mᵉkêrâh, mek-ay-raw'): a sword. Origin: probably from the same as H3564 (כּוּר) in the sense of stabbing; KJV: habitation.

H4381 מִכְרִי (Mikrîy, mik-ree'): Mikri, an Israelite. Origin: from H4376 (מָכַר); salesman; KJV: Michri.

H4382 מְכֵרָתִי (Mᵉkêrâthîy, mek-ay-raw-thee'): a Mekerathite, or inhabitant of Mekerah. Origin: patrial from an unused name (the same as H4380 (מְכֵרָה)) of a place in Palestine; KJV: Mecherathite.

H4383 מִכְשׁוֹל (mikshôwl, mik-shole'): a stumbling-block, literally or figuratively (obstacle, enticement (specifically an idol), scruple). Origin: or מִכְשֹׁל; masculine from H3782 (כָּשַׁל); KJV: caused to fall, offence, [idiom] (no-) thing offered, ruin, stumbling-block.

H4384 מַכְשֵׁלָה (makshêlâh, mak-shay-law'): a stumbling-block, but only figuratively (fall, enticement (idol)). Origin: feminine from H3782 (כָּשַׁל); KJV: ruin, stumbling-block.

H4385 מִכְתָּב (miktâb, mik-tawb'): a thing written, the characters, or a document (letter, copy, edict, poem). Origin: from H3789 (כָּתַב); KJV: writing.

H4386 מְכִתָּה (mᵉkittâh, mek-it-taw'): a fracture. Origin: from H3807 (כָּתַת); KJV: bursting.

H4387 מִכְתָּם (miktâm, mik-tawm'): an engraving, i.e. (techn.) a poem. Origin: from H3799 (כָּתַם); KJV: Michtam.

H4388 מַכְתֵּשׁ (maktêsh, mak-taysh'): a mortar; by analogy, a socket (of a tooth). Origin: from H3806 (כָּתַשׁ); KJV: hollow place, mortar.

H4389 מַכְתֵּשׁ (Maktêsh, mak-taysh'): dell; the Maktesh, a place in Jerusalem. Origin: the same as H4388 (מַכְתֵּשׁ); KJV: Maktesh.

H4390 מָלֵא (mâlêʼ, maw-lay'): to fill or (intransitively) be full of, in a wide application (literally and figuratively). Origin: or מָלָא; (Esther 7:5), a primitive root; KJV: accomplish, confirm, [phrase] consecrate, be at an end, be expired, be fenced, fill, fulfil, (be, become, [idiom] draw, give in, go) full(-ly, -ly set, tale), (over-) flow, fulness, furnish, gather (selves, together), presume, replenish, satisfy, set, space, take a (hand-) full, [phrase] have wholly.

H4391 מְלָא (mᵉlâʼ, mel-aw'): to fill. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4390 (מָלֵא); KJV: fill, be full.

H4392 מָלֵא (mâlêʼ, maw-lay'): full (literally or figuratively) or filling (literally); also (concretely) fulness; adverbially, fully. Origin: from H4390 (מָלֵא); KJV: [idiom] she that was with child, fill(-ed, -ed with), full(-ly), multitude, as is worth.

H4393 מְלֹא (mᵉlôʼ, mel-o'): fulness (literally or figuratively). Origin: rarely מְלוֹא; or מְלוֹ; (Ezekiel [41:8), from H4390 (מָלֵא); KJV: [idiom] all along, [idiom] all that is (there-) in, fill, ([idiom] that whereof...was) full, fulness, (hand-) full, multitude.

H4394 מִלֻּא (milluʼ, mil-loo'): a fulfilling (only in plural), i.e. (literally) a setting (of gems), or (technically) consecration (also concretely, a dedicatory sacrifice). Origin: from H4390 (מָלֵא); KJV: consecration, be set.

H4395 מְלֵאָה (mᵉlêʼâh, mel-ay-aw'): something fulfilled, i.e. abundance (of produce). Origin: feminine of H4392 (מָלֵא); KJV: (first of ripe) fruit, fulness.

H4396 מִלֻּאָה (milluʼâh, mil-loo-aw'): a filling, i.e. setting (of gems). Origin: feminine of H4394 (מִלֻּא); KJV: enclosing, setting.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4397 to H4524
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4397 מֲלְאָךְ (mălʼâk, mal-awk'): a messenger; specifically, of God, i.e. an angel (also a prophet, priest or teacher). Origin: from an unused root meaning to despatch as a deputy; KJV: ambassador, angel, king, messenger.

H4398 מַלְאַךְ (malʼak, mal-ak'): an angel. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4397 (מֲלְאָךְ); KJV: angel.

H4399 מְלָאכָה (mᵉlâʼkâh, mel-aw-kaw'): properly, deputyship, i.e. ministry; generally, employment (never servile) or work (abstractly or concretely); also property (as the result of labor). Origin: from the same as H4397 (מֲלְאָךְ); KJV: business, [phrase] cattle, [phrase] industrious, occupation, ([phrase] -pied), [phrase] officer, thing (made), use, (manner of) work((-man), -manship).

H4400 מַלְאֲכוּת (malʼăkûwth, mal-ak-ooth'): a message. Origin: from the same as H4397 (מֲלְאָךְ); KJV: message.

H4401 מַלְאָכִי (Malʼâkîy, mal-aw-kee'): Malaki, a prophet. Origin: from the same as H4397 (מֲלְאָךְ); ministrative; KJV: Malachi.

H4402 מִלֵּאת (millêʼth, mil-layth'): fulness, i.e. (concretely) a plump socket (of the eye). Origin: from H4390 (מָלֵא); KJV: [idiom] fitly.

H4403 מַלְבּוּשׁ (malbûwsh, mal-boosh'): a garment, or (collectively) clothing. Origin: or מַלְבֻּשׁ; from H3847 (לָבַשׁ); KJV: apparel, raiment, vestment.

H4404 מַלְבֵּן (malbên, mal-bane'): a brickkiln. Origin: from H3835 (לָבַן) (denominative); KJV: brickkiln.

H4405 מִלָּה (millâh, mil-law'): a word; collectively, a discourse; figuratively, a topic. Origin: from H4448 (מָלַל) (plural masculine as if from מִלֶּה; KJV: [phrase] answer, by-word, matter, any thing (what) to say, to speak(-ing), speak, talking, word.

H4406 מִלָּה (millâh, mil-law'): a word, command, discourse, or subject. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4405 (מִלָּה); KJV: commandment, matter, thing. word.

H4407 מִלּוֹא (millôwʼ, mil-lo'): a rampart (as filled in), i.e. the citadel. Origin: or מִלֹּא; (2 Kings 12:20), from H4390 (מָלֵא); KJV: Millo. See also H1037 (בֵּית מִלּוֹא).

H4408 מַלּוּחַ (mallûwach, mal-loo'-akh): sea-purslain (from its saltness). Origin: from H4414 (מָלַח); KJV: mallows.

H4409 מַלּוּךְ (Mallûwk, mal-luke'): Malluk, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or מַלּוּכִי; (Nehemiah 12:14), from H4427 (מָלַךְ); remnant; KJV: Malluch, Melichu (from the margin).

H4410 מְלוּכָה (mᵉlûwkâh, mel-oo-kaw'): something ruled, i.e. a realm. Origin: feminine passive participle of H4427 (מָלַךְ); KJV: kingsom, king's, [idiom] royal.

H4411 מָלוֹן (mâlôwn, maw-lone'): a lodgment, i.e. caravanserai or encampment. Origin: from H3885 (לוּן); KJV: inn, place where...lodge, lodging (place).

H4412 מְלוּנָה (mᵉlûwnâh, mel-oo-naw'): a hut, a hammock. Origin: feminine from H3885 (לוּן); KJV: cottage, lodge.

H4413 מַלּוֹתִי (Mallôwthîy, mal-lo'-thee): Mallothi, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H4448 (מָלַל); I have talked (i.e. loquacious) KJV: Mallothi.

H4414 מָלַח (mâlach, maw-lakh'): properly, to rub to pieces or pulverize; intransitively, to disappear as dust; to salt whether internally (to season with salt) or externally (to rub with salt). Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative from H4417 (מֶלַח) KJV: [idiom] at all, salt, season, temper together, vanish away.

H4415 מְלַח (mᵉlach, mel-akh'): to eat salt, i.e. (generally) subsist. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4414 (מָלַח); KJV: [phrase] have maintenance.

H4416 מְלַח (mᵉlach, mel-akh'): salt. Origin: (Aramaic) from H4415 (מְלַח); KJV: [phrase] maintenance, salt.

H4417 מֶלַח (melach, meh'-lakh): properly, powder, i.e. (specifically) salt (as easily pulverized and dissolved). Origin: from H4414 (מָלַח); KJV: salt(-pit).

H4418 מָלָח (mâlâch, maw-lawkh'): a rag or old garment. Origin: from H4414 (מָלַח) in its original sense; KJV: rotten rag.

H4419 מַלָּח (mallâch, mal-lawkh'): a sailor (as following 'the salt'). Origin: from H4414 (מָלַח) in its second. sense; KJV: mariner.

H4420 מְלֵחָה (mᵉlêchâh, mel-ay-khaw'): properly, salted (i.e. land), i.e. a desert. Origin: from H4414 (מָלַח) (in its denominative sense); understood as land (H776 (אֶרֶץ)) KJV: barren land(-ness), salt (land).

H4421 מִלְחָמָה (milchâmâh, mil-khaw-maw'): a battle (i.e. the engagement); generally, war (i.e. warfare). Origin: from H3898 (לָחַם) (in the sense of fighting); KJV: battle, fight(-ing), war(-rior).

H4422 מָלַט (mâlaṭ, maw-lat'): properly, to be smooth, i.e. (by implication) to escape (as if by slipperiness); causatively, to release or rescue; specifically, to bring forth young, emit sparks. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deliver (self), escape, lay, leap out, let alone, let go, preserve, save, [idiom] speedily, [idiom] surely.

H4423 מֶלֶט (meleṭ, meh'-let): cement (from its plastic smoothness). Origin: from H4422 (מָלַט), KJV: clay.

H4424 מְלַטְיָה (Mᵉlaṭyâh, mel-at-yaw'): Melatjah, a Gibeonite. Origin: from H4423 (מֶלֶט) and H3050 (יָהּ); (whom) Jah has delivered; KJV: Melatiah.

H4425 מְלִילָה (mᵉlîylâh, mel-ee-law'): a head of grain (as cut off). Origin: from H4449 (מְלַל) (in the sense of cropping (compare H4135 (מוּל))); KJV: ear.

H4426 מְלִיצָה (mᵉlîytsâh, mel-ee-tsaw'): an aphorism; also a satire. Origin: from H3887 (לוּץ); KJV: interpretation, taunting.

H4427 מָלַךְ (mâlak, maw-lak'): to reign; inceptively, to ascend the throne; causatively, to induct into royalty; hence (by implication) to take counsel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consult, [idiom] indeed, be (make, set a, set up) king, be (make) queen, (begin to, make to) reign(-ing), rule, [idiom] surely.

H4428 מֶלֶךְ (melek, meh'-lek): a king. Origin: from H4427 (מָלַךְ); KJV: king, royal.

H4429 מֶלֶךְ (Melek, meh'-lek): Melek, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); king; KJV: Melech, Hammelech (by including the article).

H4430 מֶלֶךְ (melek, meh'-lek): a king. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); KJV: king, royal.

H4431 מְלַךְ (mᵉlak, mel-ak'): advice. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H4427 (מָלַךְ) in the sense of consultation; KJV: counsel.

H4432 מֹלֶךְ (Môlek, mo'-lek): Molek (i.e. king), the chief deity of the Ammonites. Origin: from H4427 (מָלַךְ); KJV: Molech. Compare H4445 (מַלְכָּם).

H4433 מַלְכָּא (malkâʼ, mal-kaw'): a queen. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4436 (מַלְכָּה); KJV: queen.

H4434 מַלְכֹּדֶת (malkôdeth, mal-ko'-deth): a snare. Origin: from H3920 (לָכַד); KJV: trap.

H4435 מִלְכָּה (Milkâh, mil-kaw'): Milcah, the name of a Hebrewess and of an Israelite. Origin: a form of H4436 (מַלְכָּה); queen; KJV: Milcah.

H4436 מַלְכָּה (malkâh, mal-kaw'): a queen. Origin: feminine of H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); KJV: queen.

H4437 מַלְכוּ (malkûw, mal-koo'): dominion (abstractly or concretely). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4438 (מַלְכוּת); KJV: kingdom, kingly, realm, reign.

H4438 מַלְכוּת (malkûwth, mal-kooth'): a rule; concretely, a dominion. Origin: or מַלְכֻת; or (in plural) מַלְכֻיָּה; from H4427 (מָלַךְ); KJV: empire, kingdom, realm, reign, royal.

H4439 מַלְכִּיאֵל (Malkîyʼêl, mal-kee-ale'): Malkiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H4428 (מֶלֶךְ) and H410 (אֵל); king of (i.e. appointed by) God; KJV: Malchiel.

H4440 מַלְכִּיאֵלִי (Malkîyʼêlîy, mal-kee-ay-lee'): a Malkielite or descendant of Malkiel. Origin: patronymical from H4439 (מַלְכִּיאֵל); KJV: Malchielite.

H4441 מַלְכִּיָּה (Malkîyâh, mal-kee-yaw'): Malkijah, the name of ten Israelites. Origin: or מַלְכִּיָּהוּlemma מַלְכִּיָהוּ missing dagesh, corrected to מַלְכִּיָּהוּ; (Jeremiah [38:6), from H4428 (מֶלֶךְ) and H3050 (יָהּ); king of (i.e. appointed by) Jah; KJV: Malchiah, Malchijah.

H4442 מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק (Malkîy-Tsedeq, mal-kee-tseh'-dek): Malki-Tsedek, an early king in Palestine. Origin: from H4428 (מֶלֶךְ) and H6664 (צֶדֶק); king of right; KJV: Melchizedek.

H4443 מַלְכִּירָם (Malkîyrâm, mal-kee-rawm'): Malkiram, an Israelite. Origin: from H4428 (מֶלֶךְ) and H7311 (רוּם); king of a high one (i.e. of exaltation); KJV: Malchiram.

H4444 מַלְכִּישׁוּעַ (Malkîyshûwaʻ, mal-kee-shoo'-ah): Malkishua, an Israelite. Origin: from H4428 (מֶלֶךְ) and H7769 (שׁוּעַ); king of wealth; KJV: Malchishua.

H4445 מַלְכָּם (Malkâm, mal-kawm'): Malcam or Milcom, the national idol of the Ammonites. Origin: or מִלְכּוֹם; from H4428 (מֶלֶךְ) for H4432 (מֹלֶךְ); KJV: Malcham, Milcom.

H4446 מְלֶכֶת (mᵉleketh, mel-eh'-keth): a queen. Origin: from H4427 (מָלַךְ); KJV: queen.

H4447 מֹלֶכֶת (Môleketh, mo-leh'-keth): Moleketh, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine active participle of H4427 (מָלַךְ); queen; KJV: Hammoleketh (including the article).

H4448 מָלַל (mâlal, maw-lal'): to speak (mostly poetical) or say. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: say, speak, utter.

H4449 מְלַל (mᵉlal, mel-al'): to speak. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4448 (מָלַל); KJV: say, speak(-ing).

H4450 מִלֲלַי (Milălay, mee-lal-ah'-ee): Milalai, an Israelite. Origin: from H4448 (מָלַל); talkative; KJV: Milalai.

H4451 מַלְמָד (malmâd, mal-mawd'): a goad for oxen. Origin: from H3925 (לָמַד); KJV: goad.

H4452 מָלַץ (mâlats, maw-lats'): to be smooth, i.e. (figuratively) pleasant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be sweet.

H4453 מֶלְצָר (meltsâr, mel-tsawr'): the butler or other officer in the Babylonian court. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Melzar.

H4454 מָלַק (mâlaq, maw-lak'): to crack a joint; by implication, to wring the neck of afowl (without separating it). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wring off.

H4455 מַלְקוֹחַ (malqôwach, mal-ko'-akh): transitively (in dual) the jaws (as taking food); intransitively, spoil (and captives) (as taken). Origin: from H3947 (לָקַח); KJV: booty, jaws, prey.

H4456 מַלְקוֹשׁ (malqôwsh, mal-koshe'): the spring rain; figuratively, eloquence. Origin: from H3953 (לָקַשׁ); (compare H3954 (לֶקֶשׁ)) KJV: latter rain.

H4457 מֶלְקָח (melqâch, mel-kawkh'): (only in dual) tweezers. Origin: or מַלְקָח; from H3947 (לָקַח); KJV: snuffers, tongs.

H4458 מֶלְתָּחָה (meltâchâh, mel-taw-khaw'): a wardrobe (i.e. room where clothing is spread). Origin: from an unused root meaning to spread out; KJV: vestry.

H4459 מַלְתָּעָה (maltâʻâh, mal-taw-aw'): a grinder, i.e. back tooth. Origin: transp. for H4973 (מְתַלְּעָה); KJV: great tooth.

H4460 מַמְּגֻרָה (mammᵉgurâh, mam-meg-oo-raw'): a granary. Origin: from H4048 (מָגַר) (in the sense of depositing); KJV: barn.

H4461 מֵמַד (mêmad, may-mad'): a measure. Origin: from H4058 (מָדַד); KJV: measure.

H4462 מְמוּכָן (Mᵉmûwkân, mem-oo-kawn'): Memucan or Momucan, a Persian satrap. Origin: or (transp.) מוֹמֻכָן; (Esther 1:16), of Persian derivation; KJV: Memucan.

H4463 מָמוֹת (mâmôwth, maw-mothe'): a mortal disease; concretely, a corpse. Origin: from H4191 (מוּת); KJV: death.

H4464 מַמְזֵר (mamzêr, mam-zare'): a mongrel, i.e. born of aJewish father and aheathen mother. Origin: from an unused root meaning to alienate; KJV: bastard.

H4465 מִמְכָּר (mimkâr, mim-kawr'): merchandise; abstractly, a selling. Origin: from H4376 (מָכַר); KJV: [idiom] ought, (that which cometh of) sale, that which...sold, ware.

H4466 מִמְכֶּרֶת (mimkereth, mim-keh'-reth): a sale. Origin: feminine of H4465 (מִמְכָּר); KJV: [phrase] sold as.

H4467 מַמְלָכָה (mamlâkâh, mam-law-kaw'): dominion, i.e. (abstractly) the estate (rule) or (concretely) the country (realm). Origin: from H4427 (מָלַךְ); KJV: kingdom, king's, reign, royal.

H4468 מַמְלָכוּת (mamlâkûwth, mam-law-kooth'): {dominion, i.e. (abstractly) the estate (rule) or (concretely) the country (realm)}. Origin: a form of H4467 (מַמְלָכָה) and equiv. to it KJV: kingdom, reign.

H4469 מַמְסָךְ (mamçâk, mam-sawk'): mixture, i.e. (specifically) wine mixed (with water or spices). Origin: from H4537 (מָסַךְ); KJV: drink-offering, mixed wine.

H4470 מֶמֶר (memer, meh'-mer): sorrow. Origin: from an unused root meaning to grieve; KJV: bitterness.

H4471 מַמְרֵא (Mamrêʼ, mam-ray'): Mamre, an Amorite. Origin: from H4754 (מָרָא)(in the sense of vigor); lusty; KJV: Mamre.

H4472 מַמְרֹר (mamrôr, mam-rore'): a bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) calamity. Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: bitterness.

H4473 מִמְשַׁח (mimshach, mim-shakh'): outspread (i.e. with outstretched wings). Origin: from H4886 (מָשַׁח), in the sense of expansion; KJV: anointed.

H4474 מִמְשָׁל (mimshâl, mim-shawl'): a ruler or (abstractly) rule. Origin: from H4910 (מָשַׁל); KJV: dominion, that ruled.

H4475 מֶמְשָׁלָה (memshâlâh, mem-shaw-law'): rule; also (concretely in plural) a realm or a ruler. Origin: feminine of H4474 (מִמְשָׁל); KJV: dominion, government, power, to rule.

H4476 מִמְשָׁק (mimshâq, mim-shawk'): a possession. Origin: from the same as H4943 (מֶשֶׁק); KJV: breeding.

H4477 מַמְתַּק (mamtaq, mam-tak'): something sweet (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H4985 (מָתַק); KJV: (most) sweet.

H4478 מָן (mân, mawn): literally a whatness (so to speak), i.e. manna (so called from the question about it). Origin: from H4100 (מָה); KJV: manna.

H4479 מָן (mân, mawn): who or what (properly, interrogatively, hence, also indefinitely and relatively). Origin: (Aramaic) from H4101 (מָה); KJV: what, who(-msoever, [phrase] -so).

H4480 מִן (min, min): properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of in many senses. Origin: or מִנִּי; or מִנֵּי; (constructive plural) (Isaiah 30:11); for H4482 (מֵן); KJV: above, after, among, at, because of, by (reason of), from (among), in, [idiom] neither, [idiom] nor, (out) of, over, since, [idiom] then, through, [idiom] whether, with.

H4481 מִן (min, min): {properly, a part of; hence (prepositionally), from or out of}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4480 (מִן) KJV: according, after, [phrase] because, [phrase] before, by, for, from, [idiom] him, [idiom] more than, (out) of, part, since, [idiom] these, to, upon, [phrase] when.

H4482 מֵן (mên, mane): a musical chord (as parted into strings). Origin: from an unused root meaning to apportion; a part; hence, KJV: in (the same) (Psalm 68:23), stringed instrument (Psalm 150:4), whereby (Psalm 45:8 (defective plural)).

H4483 מְנָא (mᵉnâʼ, men-aw'): to count, appoint. Origin: (Aramaic) or מְנָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H4487 (מָנָה); KJV: number, ordain, set.

H4484 מְנֵא (mᵉnêʼ, men-ay'): numbered. Origin: (Aramaic) passive participle of H4483 (מְנָא); KJV: Mene.

H4485 מַנְגִּינָה (mangîynâh, man-ghee-naw'): a satire. Origin: from H5059 (נָגַן); KJV: music.

H4486 מַנְדַּע (mandaʻ, man-dah'): wisdom or intelligence. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4093 (מַדָּע); KJV: knowledge, reason, understanding.

H4487 מָנָה (mânâh, maw-naw'): properly, to weigh out; by implication, to allot or constitute officially; also to enumerate or enroll. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, count, number, prepare, set, tell.

H4488 מָנֶה (mâneh, maw-neh'): properly, a fixed weight or measured amount, i.e. (techn.) a maneh or mina. Origin: from H4487 (מָנָה); KJV: maneh, pound.

H4489 מֹנֶה (môneh, mo-neh'): properly, something weighed out, i.e. (figuratively) a portion of time, i.e. an instance. Origin: from H4487 (מָנָה); KJV: time.

H4490 מָנָה (mânâh, maw-naw'): properly, something weighed out, i.e. (generally) a division; specifically (of food) a ration; also a lot. Origin: from H4487 (מָנָה); KJV: such things as belonged, part, portion.

H4491 מִנְהָג (minhâg, min-hawg'): the driving (of a chariot). Origin: from H5090 (נָהַג); KJV: driving.

H4492 מִנְהָרָה (minhârâh, min-haw-raw'): properly, a channel or fissure, i.e. (by implication) a cavern. Origin: from H5102 (נָהַר); KJV: den.

H4493 מָנוֹד (mânôwd, maw-node'): a nodding or toss (of the head in derision). Origin: from H5110 (נוּד) KJV: shaking.

H4494 מָנוֹחַ (mânôwach, maw-no'-akh): quiet, i.e. (concretely) a settled spot, or (figuratively) a home. Origin: from H5117 (נוּחַ); KJV: (place of) rest.

H4495 מָנוֹחַ (Mânôwach, maw-no'-akh): Manoach, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4494 (מָנוֹחַ); rest; KJV: Manoah.

H4496 מְנוּחָה (mᵉnûwchâh, men-oo-khaw'): repose or (adverbially) peacefully; figuratively, consolation (specifically, matrimony); hence (concretely) an abode. Origin: or מְנֻחָה; feminine of H4495 (מָנוֹחַ); KJV: comfortable, ease, quiet, rest(-ing place), still.

H4497 מָנוֹן (mânôwn, maw-nohn'): a continuator, i.e. heir. Origin: from H5125 (נוּן); KJV: son.

H4498 מָנוֹס (mânôwç, maw-noce'): a retreat (literally or figuratively); abstractly, a fleeing. Origin: from H5127 (נוּס); KJV: [idiom] apace, escape, way to flee, flight, refuge.

H4499 מְנוּסָה (mᵉnûwçâh, men-oo-saw'): retreat. Origin: or מְנֻסָה; feminine of H4498 (מָנוֹס); KJV: fleeing, flight.

H4500 מָנוֹר (mânôwr, maw-nore'): a yoke (properly, for plowing), i.e. the frame of aloom. Origin: from H5214 (נִיר); KJV: beam.

H4501 מְנוֹרָה (mᵉnôwrâh, men-o-raw'): a chandelier. Origin: or מְנֹרָה; feminine of H4500 (מָנוֹר) (in the original sense of H5216 (נִיר)); KJV: candlestick.

H4502 מִנְּזָר (minnᵉzâr, min-ez-awr'): a prince. Origin: from H5144 (נָזַר); KJV: crowned.

H4503 מִנְחָה (minchâh, min-khaw'): a donation; euphemistically, tribute; specifically a sacrificial offering (usually bloodless and voluntary). Origin: from an unused root meaning to apportion, i.e. bestow; KJV: gift, oblation, (meat) offering, present, sacrifice.

H4504 מִנְחָה (minchâh, min-khaw'): a sacrificial offering. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4503 (מִנְחָה); KJV: oblation, meat offering.

H4505 מְנַחֵם (Mᵉnachêm, men-akh-ame'): Menachem, an Israelite. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); comforter; KJV: Menahem.

H4506 מָנַחַת (Mânachath, maw-nakh'-ath): Manachath, the name of an Edomite and of a place in Moab. Origin: from H5117 (נוּחַ); rest; KJV: Manahath.

H4507 מְנִי (Mᵉnîy, men-ee'): the Apportioner, i.e. Fate (as an idol). Origin: from H4487 (מָנָה); KJV: number.

H4508 מִנִּי (Minnîy, min-nee'): Minni, an Armenian province. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Minni.

H4509 מִנְיָמִין (Minyâmîyn, min-yaw-meen'): Minjamin, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H4480 (מִן) and H3225 (יָמִין); from (the) right hand; KJV: Miniamin. Compare H4326 (מִיָּמִן).

H4510 מִנְיָן (minyân, min-yawn'): enumeration. Origin: (Aramaic) from H4483 (מְנָא); KJV: number.

H4511 מִנִּית (Minnîyth, min-neeth'): Minnith, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from the same as H4482 (מֵן); enumeration; KJV: Minnith.

H4512 מִנְלֶה (minleh, min-leh'): completion, i.e. (in produce) wealth. Origin: from H5239 (נָלָה); KJV: perfection.

H4513 מָנַע (mânaʻ, maw-nah'): to debar (negatively or positively) from benefit or injury. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deny, keep (back), refrain, restrain, withhold.

H4514 מַנְעוּל (manʻûwl, man-ool'): a bolt. Origin: or מַנְעֻל; from H5274 (נָעַל); KJV: lock.

H4515 מִנְעָל (minʻâl, man-awl'): a bolt. Origin: from H5274 (נָעַל); KJV: shoe.

H4516 מַנְעַם (manʻam, man-am'): a delicacy. Origin: from H5276 (נָעֵם); KJV: dainty.

H4517 מְנַעְנַע (mᵉnaʻnaʻ, men-ah-ah'): a sistrum (so called from its rattling sound). Origin: from H5128 (נוּעַ); KJV: cornet.

H4518 מְנַקִּית (mᵉnaqqîyth, men-ak-keeth'): a sacrificial basin (for holding blood). Origin: from H5352 (נָקָה); KJV: bowl.

H4519 מְנַשֶּׁה (Mᵉnashsheh, men-ash-sheh'): Menashsheh, a grandson of Jacob, also the tribe descended from him, and its territory. Origin: from H5382 (נָשָׁה); causing to forget; KJV: Manasseh.

H4520 מְנַשִּׁי (Mᵉnashshîy, men-ash-shee'): a Menashshite or descendant of Menashsheh. Origin: from H4519 (מְנַשֶּׁה); KJV: of Manasseh, Manassites.

H4521 מְנָת (mᵉnâth, men-awth'): an allotment (by courtesy, law or providence). Origin: from H4487 (מָנָה); KJV: portion.

H4522 מַס (maç, mas): properly, a burden (as causing to faint), i.e. a tax in the form of forced labor. Origin: or מִס; from H4549 (מָסַס); KJV: discomfited, levy, task(-master), tribute(-tary).

H4523 מָס (mâç, mawce): fainting, i.e. (figuratively) disconsolate. Origin: from H4549 (מָסַס); KJV: is afflicted.

H4524 מֵסַב (mêçab, may-sab'): a divan (as enclosing the room); abstractly (adverbial) around. Origin: plural masculine מְסִבִּים; or feminine מְסִבּוֹת; from H5437 (סָבַב); KJV: that compass about, (place) round about, at table.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4525 to H4651
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4525 מַסְגֵּר (maçgêr, mas-gare'): a fastener, i.e. (of a person) a smith, (of a thing) a prison. Origin: from H5462 (סָגַר); KJV: prison, smith.

H4526 מִסְגֶּרֶת (miçgereth, mis-gheh'-reth): something enclosing, i.e. a margin (of a region, of a panel); concretely, a stronghold. Origin: from H5462 (סָגַר); KJV: border, close place, hole.

H4527 מַסַּד (maççad, mas-sad'): a foundation. Origin: from H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: foundation.

H4528 מִסְדְּרוֹן (miçdᵉrôwn, mis-der-ohn'): a colonnade or internal portico (from its rows of pillars). Origin: from the same as H5468 (סֶדֶר); KJV: porch.

H4529 מָסָה (mâçâh, maw-saw'): to dissolve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make to consume away, (make to) melt, water.

H4530 מִסָּה (miççâh, mis-saw'): abundance, i.e. (adverbially) liberally. Origin: from H4549 (מָסַס) (in the sense of flowing); KJV: tribute.

H4531 מַסָּה (maççâh, mas-saw'): a testing, of men (judicial) or of God (querulous). Origin: from H5254 (נָסָה); KJV: temptation, trial.

H4532 מַסָּה (Maççâh, mas-saw'): Massah, a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H4531 (מַסָּה); KJV: Massah.

H4533 מַסְוֶה (maçveh, mas-veh'): a veil. Origin: apparently from an unused root meaning to cover; KJV: vail.

H4534 מְסוּכָה (mᵉçûwkâh, mes-oo-kaw'): a hedge. Origin: for H4881 (מְשׂוּכָה); KJV: thorn hedge.

H4535 מַסָּח (maççâch, mas-sawkh'): a cordon, (adverbially) or (as a) military barrier. Origin: from H5255 (נָסַח) in the sense of staving off; KJV: broken down.

H4536 מִסְחָר (miçchâr, mis-khawr'): trade. Origin: from H5503 (סָחַר); KJV: traffic.

H4537 מָסַךְ (mâçak, maw-sak'): to mix, especially wine (with spices). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mingle.

H4538 מֶסֶךְ (meçek, meh'-sek): a mixture, i.e. of wine with spices. Origin: from H4537 (מָסַךְ); KJV: mixture.

H4539 מָסָךְ (mâçâk, maw-sawk'): a cover, i.e. veil. Origin: from H5526 (סָכַךְ); KJV: covering, curtain, hanging.

H4540 מְסֻכָּה (mᵉçukkâh, mes-ook-kaw'): a covering, i.e. garniture. Origin: from H5526 (סָכַךְ); KJV: covering.

H4541 מַסֵּכָה (maççêkâh, mas-say-kaw'): properly, a pouring over, i.e. fusion of metal (especially a cast image); by implication, a libation, i.e. league; concretely a coverlet (as if poured out). Origin: from H5258 (נָסַךְ); KJV: covering, molten (image), vail.

H4542 מִסְכֵּן (miçkên, mis-kane'): indigent. Origin: from H5531 (סִכְלוּת); KJV: poor (man).

H4543 מִסְכְּנָה (miçkᵉnâh, mis-ken-aw'): a magazine. Origin: by transp. from H3664 (כָּנַס); KJV: store(-house), treasure.

H4544 מִסְכֵּנֻת (miçkênuth, mis-kay-nooth'): indigence. Origin: from H4542 (מִסְכֵּן); KJV: scarceness.

H4545 מַסֶּכֶת (maççeketh, mas-seh'-keth): something expanded, i.e. the warp in aloom (as stretched out to receive the woof). Origin: from H5259 (נָסַךְ) in the sense of spreading out; KJV: web.

H4546 מְסִלָּה (mᵉçillâh, mes-il-law'): a thoroughfare (as turnpiked), literally or figuratively; specifically a viaduct, a staircase. Origin: from H5549 (סָלַל); KJV: causeway, course, highway, path, terrace.

H4547 מַסְלוּל (maçlûwl, mas-lool'): a thoroughfare (as turnpiked). Origin: from H5549 (סָלַל); KJV: highway.

H4548 מַסְמֵר (maçmêr, mas-mare'): a peg (as bristling from the surface). Origin: or מִסְמֵר; also (feminine) מַסְמְרָה; or מִסְמְרָה; or even מַשְׂמְרָה; (Ecclesiastes 12:11), from H5568 (סָמַר); KJV: nail.

H4549 מָסַס (mâçaç, maw-sas'): to liquefy; figuratively, to waste (with disease), to faint (with fatigue, fear or grief). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: discourage, faint, be loosed, melt (away), refuse, [idiom] utterly.

H4550 מַסַּע (maççaʻ, mas-sah'): a departure (from striking the tents), i.e. march (not necessarily a single day's travel); by implication, a station (or point of departure). Origin: from H5265 (נָסַע); KJV: journey(-ing).

H4551 מַסָּע (maççâʻ, mas-saw'): a missile (spear or arrow); also a quarry (whence stones are, as it were, ejected). Origin: from H5265 (נָסַע) in the sense of projecting; KJV: before it was brought, dart.

H4552 מִסְעָד (miçʻâd, mis-awd'): a balustrade (for stairs). Origin: ' from H5582 (סָעַד); KJV: pillar.

H4553 מִסְפֵּד (miçpêd, mis-pade'): a lamentation. Origin: from H5594 (סָפַד); KJV: lamentation, one mourneth, mourning, wailing.

H4554 מִסְפּוֹא (miçpôwʼ, mis-po'): fodder. Origin: from an unused root meaning to collect; KJV: provender.

H4555 מִסְפָּחָה (miçpâchâh, mis-paw-khaw'): a veil (as spread out). Origin: from H5596 (סָפַח); KJV: kerchief.

H4556 מִסְפַּחַת (miçpachath, mis-pakh'-ath): scruf (as spreading over the surface). Origin: from H5596 (סָפַח); KJV: scab.

H4557 מִסְפָּר (miçpâr, mis-pawr'): a number, definite (arithmetical) or indefinite (large, innumerable; small, a few); also (abstractly) narration. Origin: from H5608 (סָפַר); KJV: [phrase] abundance, account, [idiom] all, [idiom] few, (in-) finite, (certain) number(-ed), tale, telling, [phrase] time.

H4558 מִסְפָּר (Miçpâr, mis-pawr'): Mispar, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4457 (מֶלְקָח); number; KJV: Mizpar. Compare H4559 (מִסְפֶּרֶת).

H4559 מִסְפֶּרֶת (Miçpereth, mis-peh'-reth): Mispereth, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H4437 (מַלְכוּ); enumeration; KJV: Mispereth. Compare H4458 (מֶלְתָּחָה).

H4560 מָסַר (mâçar, maw-sar'): to sunder, i.e. (transitively) set apart, or (reflex.) apostatize. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: commit, deliver.

H4561 מֹסָר (môçâr, mo-sawr'): admonition. Origin: from H3256 (יָסַר); KJV: instruction.

H4562 מָסֹרֶת (mâçôreth, maw-so'-reth): a band. Origin: from H631 (אָסַר); KJV: bond.

H4563 מִסְתּוֹר (miçtôwr, mis-tore'): a refuge. Origin: from H5641 (סָתַר); KJV: covert.

H4564 מַסְתֵּר (maçtêr, mas-tare'): properly, a hider, i.e. (abstractly) a hiding, i.e. aversion. Origin: from H5641 (סָתַר); KJV: hid.

H4565 מִסְתָּר (miçtâr, mis-tawr'): properly, a concealer, i.e. a covert. Origin: from H5641 (סָתַר); KJV: secret(-ly, place).

H4566 מַעְבָּד (maʻbâd, mah-bawd'): an act. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: work.

H4567 מַעְבָד (maʻbâd, mah-bawd'): an act. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4566 (מַעְבָּד); KJV: work.

H4568 מַעֲבֶה (maʻăbeh, mah-ab-eh'): properly, compact (part of soil), i.e. loam. Origin: from H5666 (עָבָה); KJV: clay.

H4569 מַעֲבָר (maʻăbâr, mah-ab-awr'): a crossing-place (of a river, a ford; of a mountain, a pass); abstractly, a transit, i.e. (figuratively) overwhelming. Origin: or feminine מַעֲבָרָה; from H5674 (עָבַר); KJV: ford, place where...pass, passage.

H4570 מַעְגָּל (maʻgâl, mah-gawl'): a track (literally or figuratively); also a rampart (as circular). Origin: or feminine מַעְגָּלָה; from the same as H5696 (עָגֹל); KJV: going, path, trench, way(-side).

H4571 מָעַד (mâʻad, maw-ad'): to waver. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make to shake, slide, slip.

H4572 מַעֲדַי (Maʻăday, mah-ad-ah'-ee): Maadai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5710 (עָדָה); ornamental; KJV: Maadai.

H4573 מַעֲדְיָה (Maʻădyâh, mah-ad-yaw'): Maadjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H5710 (עָדָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); ornament of Jah; KJV: Maadiah. Compare H4153 (מוֹעַדְיָה).

H4574 מַעֲדָן (maʻădân, mah-ad-awn'): a delicacy or (abstractly) pleasure (adverbially, cheerfully). Origin: or (feminine) מַעֲדַנָּה; from H5727 (עָדַן); KJV: dainty, delicately, delight.

H4575 מַעֲדַנָּה (maʻădannâh, mah-ad-an-naw'): a bond, i.e. group. Origin: by transitive from H6029 (עָנַד); KJV: influence.

H4576 מַעְדֵּר (maʻdêr, mah-dare'): a (weeding) hoe. Origin: from H5737 (עֲדַר); KJV: mattock.

H4577 מְעָה (mᵉʻâh, meh-aw'): only in plural the bowels. Origin: (Aramaic) or מְעָא; (Aramaic), corresponding to H4578 (מֵעֶה)xlit mêʻâh corrected to mêʻeh; KJV: belly.

H4578 מֵעֶה (mêʻeh, may-aw'): used only in plural the intestines, or (collectively) the abdomen, figuratively, sympathy; by implication, a vest; by extension the stomach, the uterus (or of men, the seat of generation), the heart (figuratively). Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to be soft; KJV: belly, bowels, [idiom] heart, womb.

H4579 מֵעָה (mêʻâh, may-aw'): the belly, i.e. (figuratively) interior. Origin: feminine of H4578 (מֵעֶה)xlit mêʻâh corrected to mêʻeh; KJV: gravel.

H4580 מָעוֹג (mâʻôwg, maw-ogue'): a cake of bread; parasite. Origin: from H5746 (עוּג); also with H3934 (לָעֵג) a table-buffoon, i.e. KJV: cake, feast.

H4581 מָעוֹז (mâʻôwz, maw-oze'): a fortified place; figuratively, a defence. Origin: (also מָעוּז ); or מָעֹז (also מָעֻז; from H5810 (עָזַז); KJV: force, fort(-ress), rock, strength(-en), ([idiom] most) strong (hold).

H4582 מָעוֹךְ (Mâʻôwk, maw-oke'): Maok, a Philistine. Origin: from H4600 (מָעַךְ); oppressed; KJV: Maoch.

H4583 מָעוֹן (mâʻôwn, maw-ohn'): an abode, of God (the Tabernacle or the Temple), men (their home) or animals (their lair); hence, a retreat (asylum). Origin: or מָעִין; (1 Chronicles 4:41), from the same as H5772 (עוֹנָה); KJV: den, dwelling((-) place), habitation.

H4584 מָעוֹן (Mâʻôwn, maw-ohn'): Maon, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H4583 (מָעוֹן); a residence; KJV: Maon, Maonites. Compare H1010 (בֵּית בַּעַל מְעוֹן), H4586 (מְעוּנִי)lemma מְעוּנָי third vowel, corrected to מְעוּנִי.

H4585 מְעוֹנָה (mᵉʻôwnâh, meh-o-naw'): {an abode, of God (the Tabernacle or the Temple), men (their home) or animals (their lair); hence, a retreat (asylum)}. Origin: or מְעֹנָה; feminine of H4583 (מָעוֹן), and meaning the same KJV: den, habitation, (dwelling) place, refuge.

H4586 מְעוּנִי (Mᵉʻûwnîy, meh-oo-nee'): a Meunite, or inhabitant of Maon (only in plural). Origin: or מְעִינִי; probably patrial from H4584 (מָעוֹן); KJV: Mehunim(-s), Meunim.

H4587 מְעוֹנֹתַי (Mᵉʻôwnôthay, meh-o-no-thah'-ee): Meonothai, an Israelite. Origin: plural of H4585 (מְעוֹנָה); habitative; KJV: Meonothai.

H4588 מָעוּף (mâʻûwph, maw-off'): darkness. Origin: from H5774 (עוּף) in the sense of covering with shade (compare H4155 (מוּעָף)); KJV: dimness.

H4589 מָעוֹר (mâʻôwr, maw-ore'): nakedness, i.e. (in plural) the pudenda. Origin: from H5783 (עוּר); KJV: nakedness.

H4590 מַעַזְיָה (Maʻazyâh, mah-az-yaw'): Maazjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or מַעַזְיָהוּ; probably from H5756 (עוּז) (in the sense of protection) and H3050 (יָהּ); rescue of Jah; KJV: Maaziah.

H4591 מָעַט (mâʻaṭ, maw-at'): properly, to pare off, i.e. lessen; intransitively, to be (or causatively, to make) small or few (or figuratively, ineffective). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: suffer to decrease, diminish, (be, [idiom] borrow a, give, make) few (in number, -ness), gather least (little), be (seem) little, ([idiom] give the) less, be minished, bring to nothing.

H4592 מְעַט (mᵉʻaṭ, meh-at'): a little or few (often adverbial or compar.). Origin: or מְעָט; from H4591 (מָעַט); KJV: almost (some, very) few(-er, -est), lightly, little (while), (very) small (matter, thing), some, soon, [idiom] very.

H4593 מָעֹט (mâʻôṭ, maw-ote'): thinned (as to the edge), i.e. sharp. Origin: passive adjective of H4591 (מָעַט); KJV: wrapped up.

H4594 מַעֲטֶה (maʻăṭeh, mah-at-eh'): a vestment. Origin: from H5844 (עָטָה); KJV: garment.

H4595 מַעֲטָפָה (maʻăṭâphâh, mah-at-aw-faw'): a cloak. Origin: from H5848 (עָטַף); KJV: mantle.

H4596 מְעִי (mᵉʻîy, meh-ee'): a pile of rubbish (as contorted), i.e. a ruin. Origin: from H5753 (עָוָה); (compare H5856 (עִי)) KJV: heap.

H4597 מָעַי (Mâʻay, maw-ah'-ee): Maai, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H4578 (מֵעֶה)xlit mêʻâh corrected to mêʻeh; sympathetic; KJV: Maai.

H4598 מְעִיל (mᵉʻîyl, meh-eel'): a robe (i.e. upper and outer garment). Origin: from H4603 (מָעַל) in the sense of covering; KJV: cloke, coat, mantle, robe.

H4599 מַעְיָן (maʻyân, mah-yawn'): a fountain (also collectively), figuratively, a source (of satisfaction). Origin: or מַעְיְנוֹ; (Psalm 114:8), or (feminine) מַעְיָנָה; from H5869 (עַיִן) (as a denominative in the sense of a spring); KJV: fountain, spring, well.

H4600 מָעַךְ (mâʻak, maw-ak'): to press, i.e. to pierce, emasculate, handle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bruised, stuck, be pressed.

H4601 מַעֲכָה (Maʻăkâh, mah-ak-aw'): Maakah (or Maakath), the name of a place in Syria, also of a Mesopotamian, of three Israelites, and of four Israelitesses and one Syrian woman. Origin: or מַעֲכָת; (Joshua 13:13), from H4600 (מָעַךְ); depression; KJV: Maachah, Maachathites. See also H1038 (בֵּית מַעֲכָה).

H4602 מַעֲכָתִי (Maʻăkâthîy, mah-ak-aw-thee'): a Maakathite, or inhabitant of Maakah. Origin: patrial from H4601 (מַעֲכָה); KJV: Maachathite.

H4603 מָעַל (mâʻal, maw-al'): properly, to cover up; used only figuratively, to act covertly, i.e. treacherously. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: transgress, (commit, do a) trespass(-ing).

H4604 מַעַל (maʻal, mah'-al): treachery, i.e. sin. Origin: from H4603 (מָעַל); KJV: falsehood, grievously, sore, transgression, trespass, [idiom] very.

H4605 מַעַל (maʻal, mah'al): properly, the upper part, used only adverbially with prefix upward, above, overhead, from the top, etc. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: above, exceeding(-ly), forward, on ([idiom] very) high, over, up(-on, -ward), very.

H4606 מֵעָל (mêʻâl, may-awl'): (only in plural as singular) the setting (of the sun). Origin: (Aramaic) from H5954 (עֲלַל); KJV: going down.

H4607 מֹעַל (môʻal, mo'-al): a raising (of the hands). Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: lifting up.

H4608 מַעֲלֶה (maʻăleh, mah-al-eh'): an elevation, i.e. (concretely) acclivity or platform; abstractly (the relation or state) a rise or (figuratively) priority. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: ascent, before, chiefest, cliff, that goeth up, going up, hill, mounting up, stairs.

H4609 מַעֲלָה (maʻălâh, mah-al-aw'): elevation, i.e. the act (literally, a journey to a higher place, figuratively, a thought arising), or (concretely) the condition (literally, a step or grademark, figuratively, a superiority of station); specifically a climactic progression (in certain Psalms). Origin: feminine of H4608 (מַעֲלֶה); KJV: things that come up, (high) degree, deal, go up, stair, step, story.

H4610 מַעֲלֵה עַקְרַבִּים (Maʻălêh ʻAqrabbîym, mah-al-ay' ak-rabbeem'): Steep of Scorpions, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H4608 (מַעֲלֶה) and (the plural of) H6137 (עַקְרָב); KJV: Maaleh-accrabim, the ascent (going up) of Akrabbim.

H4611 מַעֲלָל (maʻălâl, mah-al-awl'): an act (good or bad). Origin: from H5953 (עָלַל); KJV: doing, endeavour, invention, work.

H4612 מַעֲמָד (maʻămâd, mah-am-awd'): (figuratively) a position. Origin: from H5975 (עָמַד); KJV: attendance, office, place, state.

H4613 מׇעֳמָד (moʻŏmâd, moh-om-awd'): literally a foothold. Origin: from H5975 (עָמַד); KJV: standing.

H4614 מַעֲמָסָה (maʻămâçâh, mah-am-aw-saw'): burdensomeness. Origin: from H6006 (עָמַס); KJV: burdensome.

H4615 מַעֲמָק (maʻămâq, mah-am-awk'): a deep. Origin: from H6009 (עָמַק); KJV: deep, depth.

H4616 מַעַן (maʻan, mah'-an): properly, heed, i.e. purpose; used only adverbially, on account of (as a motive or an aim), teleologically, in order that. Origin: from H6030 (עָנָה); KJV: because of, to the end (intent) that, for (to,... 's sake), [phrase] lest, that, to.

H4617 מַעֲנֶה (maʻăneh, mah-an-eh'): a reply (favorable or contradictory). Origin: from H6030 (עָנָה); KJV: answer, [idiom] himself.

H4618 מַעֲנָה (maʻănâh, mah-an-aw'): a furrow. Origin: from H6031 (עָנָה), in the sense of depression or tilling; KJV: [phrase] acre, furrow.

H4619 מַעַץ (Maʻats, mah'-ats): Maats, an Israelite. Origin: from H6095 (עָצָה); closure; KJV: Maaz.

H4620 מַעֲצֵבָה (maʻătsêbâh, mah-ats-ay-baw'): anguish. Origin: from H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: sorrow.

H4621 מַעֲצָד (maʻătsâd, mah-ats-awd'): an axe. Origin: from an unused root meaning to hew; KJV: ax, tongs.

H4622 מַעְצוֹר (maʻtsôwr, mah-tsore'): objectively, a hindrance. Origin: from H6113 (עָצָר); KJV: restraint.

H4623 מַעְצָר (maʻtsâr, mah-tsawr'): subjectively, control. Origin: from H6113 (עָצָר); KJV: rule.

H4624 מַעֲקֶה (maʻăqeh, mah-ak-eh'): a parapet. Origin: from an unused root meaning to repress; KJV: battlement.

H4625 מַעֲקָשׁ (maʻăqâsh, mah-ak-awsh'): a crook (in a road). Origin: from H6140 (עָקַשׁ); KJV: crooked thing.

H4626 מַעַר (maʻar, mah'-ar): a nude place, i.e. (literally) the pudenda, or (figuratively) a vacant space. Origin: from H6168 (עָרָה); KJV: nakedness, proportion.

H4627 מַעֲרָב (maʻărâb, mah-ar-awb'): traffic; by implication, mercantile goods. Origin: from H6148 (עָרַב), in the sense of trading; KJV: market, merchandise.

H4628 מַעֲרָב (maʻărâb, mah-ar-awb'): the west (as a region of the evening sun). Origin: or (feminine) מַעֲרָבָה; from H6150 (עָרַב), in the sense of shading; KJV: west.

H4629 מַעֲרֶה (maʻăreh, mah-ar-eh'): a nude place, i.e. a common. Origin: from H6168 (עָרָה); KJV: meadows.

H4630 מַעֲרָה (maʻărâh, mah-ar-aw'): an open spot. Origin: feminine of H4629 (מַעֲרֶה); KJV: army (from the margin).

H4631 מְעָרָה (mᵉʻârâh, meh-aw-raw'): a cavern (as dark). Origin: from H5783 (עוּר); KJV: cave, den, hole.

H4632 מְעָרָה (Mᵉʻârâh, meh-aw-raw'): Mearah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H4631 (מְעָרָה); cave; KJV: Mearah.

H4633 מַעֲרָךְ (maʻărâk, mah-ar-awk'): an arrangement, i.e. (figuratively) mental disposition. Origin: from H6186 (עָרַךְ); KJV: preparation.

H4634 מַעֲרָכָה (maʻărâkâh, mah-ar-aw-kaw'): an arrangement; concretely, a pile; specifically a military array. Origin: feminine of H4633 (מַעֲרָךְ); KJV: army, fight, be set in order, ordered place, rank, row.

H4635 מַעֲרֶכֶת (maʻăreketh, mah-ar-eh'-keth): an arrangement, i.e. (concretely) a pile (of loaves). Origin: from H6186 (עָרַךְ); KJV: row, shewbread.

H4636 מַעֲרֹם (maʻărôm, mah-ar-ome'): bare. Origin: from H6191 (עָרַם), in the sense of stripping; KJV: naked.

H4637 מַעֲרָצָה (maʻărâtsâh, mah-ar-aw-tsaw'): violence. Origin: from H6206 (עָרַץ); KJV: terror.

H4638 מַעֲרָת (Maʻărâth, mah-ar-awth'): Maarath, a place in Palestine. Origin: a form of H4630 (מַעֲרָה); waste; KJV: Maarath.

H4639 מַעֲשֶׂה (maʻăseh, mah-as-eh'): an action (good or bad); generally, a transaction; abstractly, activity; by implication, a product (specifically, a poem) or (generally) property. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה); KJV: act, art, [phrase] bakemeat, business, deed, do(-ing), labor, thing made, ware of making, occupation, thing offered, operation, possession, [idiom] well, (handy-, needle-, net-) work(ing, -manship), wrought.

H4640 מַעֲשַׂי (Maʻăsay, mah-as-ah'ee): Maasai, an Israelite. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה); operative; KJV: Maasiai.

H4641 מַעֲשֵׂיָה (Maʻăsêyâh, mah-as-ay-yaw'): Maasejah, the name of sixteen Israelites. Origin: or מַעֲשֵׂיָהוּ; from H4639 (מַעֲשֶׂה) and H3050 (יָהּ); work of Jah; KJV: Maaseiah.

H4642 מַעֲשַׁקָּה (maʻăshaqqâh, mah-ash-ak-kaw'): oppression. Origin: from H6231 (עָשַׁק); KJV: oppression, [idiom] oppressor.

H4643 מַעֲשֵׂר (maʻăsêr, mah-as-ayr'): a tenth; especially a tithe. Origin: or מַעֲשַׂר; and (in plural) feminine מַעַשְׂרָה; from H6240 (עָשָׂר); KJV: tenth (part), tithe(-ing).

H4644 מֹף (Môph, mofe): Moph, the capital of Lower Egypt. Origin: of Egyptian origin; KJV: Memphis. Compare H5297 (נֹף).

H4645 מִפְגָּע (miphgâʻ, mif-gaw'): an object of attack. Origin: from H6293 (פָּגַע); KJV: mark.

H4646 מַפָּח (mappâch, map-pawkh'): a breathing out (of life), i.e. expiring. Origin: from H5301 (נָפַח); KJV: giving up.

H4647 מַפֻּחַ (mappuach, map-poo'-akh): the bellows (i.e. blower) of aforge. Origin: from H5301 (נָפַח); KJV: bellows.

H4648 מְפִיבֹשֶׁת (Mᵉphîybôsheth, mef-ee-bo'-sheth): Mephibosheth, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or מְפִבֹשֶׁת; probably from H6284 (פָּאָה) and H1322 (בֹּשֶׁת); dispeller of shame (i.e. of Baal); KJV: Mephibosheth.

H4649 מֻפִּים (Muppîym, moop-peem'): Muppim, an Israelite. Origin: a plural apparently from H5130 (נוּף); wavings; KJV: Muppim. Compare H8206 (שֻׁפִּים).

H4650 מֵפִיץ (mêphîyts, may-feets'): a breaker, i.e. mallet. Origin: from H6327 (פּוּץ); KJV: maul.

H4651 מַפָּל (mappâl, map-pawl'): a falling off, i.e. chaff; also something pendulous, i.e. a flap. Origin: from H5307 (נָפַל); KJV: flake, refuse.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4652 to H4773
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4652 מִפְלָאָה (miphlâʼâh, mif-law-aw'): a miracle. Origin: from H6381 (פָּלָא); KJV: wondrous work.

H4653 מִפְלַגָּה (miphlaggâh, mif-lag-gaw'): a classification. Origin: from H6385 (פָּלַג); KJV: division.

H4654 מַפָּלָה (mappâlâh, map-paw-law'): something fallen, i.e. a ruin. Origin: or מַפֵּלָה; from H5307 (נָפַל); KJV: ruin(-ous).

H4655 מִפְלָט (miphlâṭ, mif-lawt'): an escape. Origin: from H6403 (פָּלַט); KJV: escape.

H4656 מִפְלֶצֶת (miphletseth, mif-leh'-tseth): a terror, i.e. an idol. Origin: from H6426 (פָּלַץ); KJV: idol.

H4657 מִפְלָשׂ (miphlâs, mif-lawce'): a poising. Origin: from an unused root meaning to balance; KJV: balancing.

H4658 מַפֶּלֶת (mappeleth, map-peh'-leth): fall, i.e. decadence; concretely, a ruin; specifically a carcase. Origin: from H5307 (נָפַל); KJV: carcase, fall, ruin.

H4659 מִפְעָל (miphʻâl, mif-awl'): a performance. Origin: or (feminine) מִפְעָלָה; from H6466 (פָּעַל); KJV: work.

H4660 מַפָּץ (mappâts, map-pawts'): a smiting to pieces. Origin: from H5310 (נָפַץ); KJV: slaughter.

H4661 מַפֵּץ (mappêts, map-pates'): a smiter, i.e. a war club. Origin: from H5310 (נָפַץ); KJV: battle ax.

H4662 מִפְקָד (miphqâd, mif-kawd'): an appointment, i.e. mandate; concretely, a designated spot; specifically, a census. Origin: from H6485 (פָּקַד); KJV: appointed place, commandment, number.

H4663 מִפְקָד (Miphqâd, mif-kawd'): Miphkad, the name of a gate in Jerusalem. Origin: the same as H4662 (מִפְקָד); assignment; KJV: Miphkad.

H4664 מִפְרָץ (miphrâts, mif-rawts'): a break (in the shore), i.e. a haven. Origin: from H6555 (פָּרַץ)lemma פּרַץ missing vowel, corrected to פָּרַץ; KJV: breach.

H4665 מִפְרֶקֶת (miphreqeth, mif-reh'-keth): properly, a fracture, i.e. joint (vertebrae) of the neck. Origin: from H6561 (פָּרַק); KJV: neck.

H4666 מִפְרָשׂ (miphrâs, mif-rawce'): an expansion. Origin: from H6566 (פָּרַשׂ); KJV: that which...spreadest forth, spreading.

H4667 מִפְשָׂעָה (miphsâʻâh, mif-saw-aw'): a stride, i.e. (by euphemism) the crotch. Origin: from H6585 (פָּשַׂע); KJV: buttocks.

H4668 מַפְתֵּחַ (maphtêach, maf-tay'-akh): an opener, i.e. a key. Origin: from H6605 (פָּתַח); KJV: key.

H4669 מִפְתָּח (miphtâch, mif-tawkh'): an aperture, i.e. (figuratively) utterance. Origin: from H6605 (פָּתַח); KJV: opening.

H4670 מִפְתָּן (miphtân, mif-tawn'): a stretcher, i.e. a sill. Origin: from the same as H6620 (פֶּתֶן); KJV: threshold.

H4671 מֹץ (môts, motes): chaff (as pressed out, i.e. winnowed or (rather) threshed loose). Origin: or מוֹץ; (Zephaniah 2:2), from H4160 (מוּץ); KJV: chaff.

H4672 מָצָא (mâtsâʼ, maw-tsaw'): properly, to come forth to, i.e. appear or exist; transitively, to attain, i.e. find or acquire; figuratively, to occur, meet or be present. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [phrase] be able, befall, being, catch, [idiom] certainly, (cause to) come (on, to, to hand), deliver, be enough (cause to) find(-ing, occasion, out), get (hold upon), [idiom] have (here), be here, hit, be left, light (up-) on, meet (with), [idiom] occasion serve, (be) present, ready, speed, suffice, take hold on.

H4673 מַצָּב (matstsâb, mats-tsawb'): a fixed spot; figuratively, an office, a military post. Origin: from H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: garrison, station, place where...stood.

H4674 מֻצָּב (mutstsâb, moots-tsawb'): a station, i.e. military post. Origin: from H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: mount.

H4675 מַצָּבָה (matstsâbâh, mats-tsaw-baw'): a military guard. Origin: or מִצָּבָה; feminine of H4673 (מַצָּב); KJV: army, garrison.

H4676 מַצֵּבָה (matstsêbâh, mats-tsay-baw'): something stationed, i.e. a column or (memorial stone); by analogy, an idol. Origin: feminine (causatively) participle of H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: garrison, (standing) image, pillar.

H4677 מְצֹבָיָה (Mᵉtsôbâyâh, mets-o-baw-yaw'): Metsobajah, a place in Palestine. Origin: apparently from H4672 (מָצָא) and H3050 (יָהּ); found of Jah; KJV: Mesobaite.

H4678 מַצֶּבֶת (matstsebeth, mats-tseh'-beth): something stationary, i.e. a monumental stone; also the stock of atree. Origin: from H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: pillar, substance.

H4679 מְצַד (mᵉtsad, mets-ad'): a fastness (as a covert of ambush). Origin: or מְצָד; or (feminine) מְצָדָה; from H6679 (צוּד); KJV: castle, fort, (strong) hold, munition.

H4680 מָצָה (mâtsâh, maw-tsaw'): to suck out; by implication, to drain, to squeeze out. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: suck, wring (out).

H4681 מֹצָה (Môtsâh, mo-tsaw'): Motsah, a place in Palestine. Origin: active participle feminine of H4680 (מָצָה); drained; KJV: Mozah.

H4682 מַצָּה (matstsâh, mats-tsaw'): properly, sweetness; concretely, sweet (i.e. not soured or bittered with yeast); specifically, an unfermented cake or loaf, or (elliptically) the festival of Passover (because no leaven was then used). Origin: from H4711 (מָצַץ) in the sense of greedily devouring for sweetness; KJV: unleaved (bread, cake), without leaven.

H4683 מַצָּה (matstsâh, mats-tsaw'): a quarrel. Origin: from H5327 (נָצָה); KJV: contention, debate, strife.

H4684 מַצְהָלָה (matshâlâh, mats-haw-law'): a whinnying (through impatience for battle or lust). Origin: from H6670 (צָהַל); KJV: neighing.

H4685 מָצוֹד (mâtsôwd, maw-tsode'): a net (for capturing animals or fishes); afastness or (beseiging) tower. Origin: or (feminine) מְצוֹדָה; or מצֹדָה; from H6679 (צוּד); also (by interchange for H4679 (מְצַד)) KJV: bulwark, hold, munition, net, snare.

H4686 מָצוּד (mâtsûwd, maw-tsood'): a net, or (abstractly) capture; also a fastness. Origin: or (feminine) מְצוּדָה; or מְצֻדָה; for H4685 (מָצוֹד); KJV: castle, defense, fort(-ress), (strong) hold, be hunted, net, snare, strong place.

H4687 מִצְוָה (mitsvâh, mits-vaw'): a command, whether human or divine (collectively, the Law). Origin: from H6680 (צָוָה); KJV: (which was) commanded(-ment), law, ordinance, precept.

H4688 מְצוֹלָה (mᵉtsôwlâh, mets-o-law'): a deep place (of water or mud). Origin: or מְצֹלָה; also מְצוּלָה; or מְצֻלָה; from the same as H6683 (צוּלָה); KJV: bottom, deep, depth.

H4689 מָצוֹק (mâtsôwq, maw-tsoke'): a narrow place, i.e. (abstractly and figuratively) confinement or disability. Origin: from H6693 (צוּק); KJV: anguish, distress, straitness.

H4690 מָצוּק (mâtsûwq, maw-tsook'): something narrow, i.e. a column or hilltop. Origin: or מָצֻק; from H6693 (צוּק); KJV: pillar, situate.

H4691 מְצוּקָה (mᵉtsûwqâh, mets-oo-kaw'): narrowness, i.e. (figuratively) trouble. Origin: or מְצֻקָה; feminine of H4690 (מָצוּק); KJV: anguish, distress.

H4692 מָצוֹר (mâtsôwr, maw-tsore'): something hemming in, i.e. (objectively) a mound (of besiegers), (abstractly) a siege, (figuratively) distress; or (subjectively) a fastness. Origin: or מָצוּר; from H6696 (צוּר); KJV: besieged, bulwark, defence, fenced, fortress, siege, strong (hold), tower.

H4693 מָצוֹר (mâtsôwr, maw-tsore'): Egypt (as the border of Palestine). Origin: the same as H4692 (מָצוֹר) in the sense of a limit; KJV: besieged places, defense, fortified.

H4694 מְצוּרָה (mᵉtsûwrâh, mets-oo-raw'): a hemming in, i.e. (objectively) a mound (of siege), or (subjectively) a rampart (of protection), (abstractly) fortification. Origin: or מְצֻרָה; feminine of H4692 (מָצוֹר); KJV: fenced (city, fort, munition, strong hold.

H4695 מַצּוּת (matstsûwth, mats-tsooth'): a quarrel. Origin: from H5327 (נָצָה); KJV: that contended.

H4696 מֵצַח (mêtsach, may'-tsakh): the forehead (as open and prominent). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be clear, i.e. conspicuous; KJV: brow, forehead, [phrase] impudent.

H4697 מִצְחָה (mitschâh, mits-khaw'): a shinpiece of armor (as prominent), only plural. Origin: from the same as H4696 (מֵצַח); KJV: greaves.

H4698 מְצִלָּה (mᵉtsillâh, mets-il-law'): a tinkler, i.e. a bell. Origin: from H6750 (צָלַל); KJV: bell.

H4699 מְצֻלָּה (mᵉtsullâh, mets-ool-law'): shade. Origin: from H6751 (צָלַל); KJV: bottom.

H4700 מְצֵלֶת (mᵉtsêleth, mets-ay'-leth): (only dual) double tinklers, i.e. cymbals. Origin: from H6750 (צָלַל); KJV: cymbals.

H4701 מִצְנֶפֶת (mitsnepheth, mits-neh'-feth): a tiara, i.e. official turban (of a king or high priest). Origin: from H6801 (צָנַף); KJV: diadem, mitre.

H4702 מַצָּע (matstsâʻ, mats-tsaw'): a couch. Origin: from H3331 (יַצַע); KJV: bed.

H4703 מִצְעָד (mitsʻâd, mits-awd'): a step; figuratively, companionship. Origin: from H6805 (צָעַד); KJV: going, step.

H4704 מִצְּעִירָה (mitstsᵉʻîyrâh, mits-tseh-ee-raw'): properly, littleness; concretely, diminutive. Origin: feminine of H4705 (מִצְעָר); KJV: little.

H4705 מִצְעָר (mitsʻâr, mits-awr'): petty (in size or number); adverbially, a short (time). Origin: from H6819 (צָעַר); KJV: little one (while), small.

H4706 מִצְעָר (Mitsʻâr, mits-awr'): Mitsar, a peak of Lebanon. Origin: the same as H4705 (מִצְעָר); KJV: Mizar.

H4707 מִצְפֶּה (mitspeh, mits-peh'): an observatory, especially formilitary purposes. Origin: from H6822 (צָפָה); KJV: watch tower.

H4708 מִצְפֶּה (Mitspeh, mits-peh'): Mitspeh, the name of five places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H4707 (מִצְפֶּה); KJV: Mizpeh, watch tower. Compare H4709 (מִצְפָּה).

H4709 מִצְפָּה (Mitspâh, mits-paw'): Mitspah, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H4708 (מִצְפֶּה); KJV: Mitspah. (This seems rather to be only an orthographic variation of H4708 (מִצְפֶּה) when 'in pause'.)

H4710 מִצְפֻּן (mitspun, mits-poon'): a secret (place or thing, perhaps, treasure). Origin: from H6845 (צָפַן); KJV: hidden thing.

H4711 מָצַץ (mâtsats, maw-tsats'): to suck. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: milk.

H4712 מֵצַר (mêtsar, may-tsar'): something tight, i.e. (figuratively) trouble. Origin: from H6896 (קֵבָה); KJV: distress, pain, strait.

H4713 מִצְרִי (Mitsrîy, mits-ree'): a Mitsrite, or inhabitant of Mitsrajim. Origin: from H4714 (מִצְרַיִם); KJV: Egyptian, of Egypt.

H4714 מִצְרַיִם (Mitsrayim, mits-rah'-yim): Mitsrajim, i.e. Upper and Lower Egypt. Origin: dual of H4693 (מָצוֹר); KJV: Egypt, Egyptians, Mizraim.

H4715 מִצְרֵף (mitsrêph, mits-rafe'): a crucible. Origin: from H6884 (צָרַף); KJV: fining pot.

H4716 מַק (maq, mak): properly, a melting, i.e. putridity. Origin: from H4743 (מָקַק); KJV: rottenness, stink.

H4717 מַקָּבָה (maqqâbâh, mak-kaw-baw'): properly, a perforatrix, i.e. a hammer (as piercing). Origin: from H5344 (נָקַב); KJV: hammer.

H4718 מַקֶּבֶת (maqqebeth, mak-keh'-beth): properly, a perforator, i.e. a hammer (as piercing); also (intransitively) a perforation, i.e. a quarry. Origin: from H5344 (נָקַב); KJV: hammer, hole.

H4719 מַקֵּדָה (Maqqêdâh, mak-kay-daw'): Makkedah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H5348 (נָקֹד) in the denominative sense of herding (compare H5349 (נֹקֵד)); fold; KJV: Makkedah.

H4720 מִקְדָּשׁ (miqdâsh, mik-dawsh'): a consecrated thing or place, especially, a palace, sanctuary (whether of Jehovah or of idols) or asylum. Origin: or מִקְּדָשׁ; (Exodus 15:17), from H6942 (קָדַשׁ); KJV: chapel, hallowed part, holy place, sanctuary.

H4721 מַקְהֵל (maqhêl, mak-hale'): an assembly. Origin: or (feminine) מַקְהֵלָה; from H6950 (קָהַל); KJV: congregation.

H4722 מַקְהֵלֹת (Maqhêlôth, mak-hay-loth'): Makheloth, a place in the Desert. Origin: plural of H4721 (מַקְהֵל) (feminine); assemblies; KJV: Makheloth.

H4723 מִקְוֶה (miqveh, mik-veh'): something waited for, i.e. confidence (objective or subjective); also a collection, i.e. (of water) a pond, or (of men and horses) a caravan or drove. Origin: or מִקְוֵה; (1 Kings 10:28), or מִקְוֵאlemma מִּקְוֵא extra dagesh, corrected to מִקְוֵא; (2 Chronicles 1:16), from H6960 (קָוָה); KJV: abiding, gathering together, hope, linen yarn, plenty (of water), pool.

H4724 מִקְוָה (miqvâh, mik-vaw'): a collection, i.e. (of water) a reservoir. Origin: feminine of H4723 (מִקְוֶה); KJV: ditch.

H4725 מָקוֹם (mâqôwm, maw-kome'): properly, a standing, i.e. a spot; but used widely of a locality (general or specific); also (figuratively) of a condition (of body or mind). Origin: or מָקֹם; also (feminine) מְקוֹמָה; or מְקֹמָה; from H6965 (קוּם); KJV: country, [idiom] home, [idiom] open, place, room, space, [idiom] whither(-soever).

H4726 מָקוֹר (mâqôwr, maw-kore'): properly, something dug, i.e. a (general) source (of water, even when naturally flowing; also of tears, blood (by euphemism, of the female pudenda); figuratively, of happiness, wisdom, progeny). Origin: or מָקֹר; from H6979 (קוּר); KJV: fountain, issue, spring, well(-spring).

H4727 מִקָּח (miqqâch, mik-kawkh'): reception. Origin: from H3947 (לָקַח); KJV: taking.

H4728 מַקָּחָה (maqqâchâh, mak-kaw-khaw'): something received, i.e. merchandise (purchased). Origin: from H3947 (לָקַח); KJV: ware.

H4729 מִקְטָר (miqṭâr, mik-tawr'): something to fume (incense) on i.e. a hearth place. Origin: from H6999 (קָטַר); KJV: to burn...upon.

H4730 מִקְטֶרֶת (miqṭereth, mik-teh'-reth): something to fume (incense) in, i.e. a coal-pan. Origin: feminine of H4729 (מִקְטָר); KJV: censer.

H4731 מַקֵּל (maqqêl, mak-kale): a shoot, i.e. stick (with leaves on, or for walking, striking, guiding, divining). Origin: or (feminine) מַקְּלָה; from an unused root meaning apparently to germinate; KJV: rod, (hand-)staff.

H4732 מִקְלוֹת (Miqlôwth, mik-lohth'): Mikloth, a place in the Desert. Origin: (or perhaps mik-kel-ohth') plural of (feminine) H4731 (מַקֵּל); rods; KJV: Mikloth.

H4733 מִקְלָט (miqlâṭ, mik-lawt'): an asylum (as a receptacle). Origin: from H7038 (קָלַט) in the sense of taking in; KJV: refuge.

H4734 מִקְלַעַת (miqlaʻath, mik-lah'-ath): a sculpture (probably in bas-relief). Origin: from H7049 (קָלַע); KJV: carved (figure), carving, graving.

H4735 מִקְנֶה (miqneh, mik-neh'): something bought, i.e. property, but only livestock; abstractly, acquisition. Origin: from H7069 (קָנָה); KJV: cattle, flock, herd, possession, purchase, substance.

H4736 מִקְנָה (miqnâh, mik-naw'): properly, a buying, i.e. acquisition; concretely, a piece of property (land or living); also the sum paid. Origin: feminine of H4735 (מִקְנֶה); KJV: (he that is) bought, possession, piece, purchase.

H4737 מִקְנֵיָהוּ (Miqnêyâhûw, mik-nay-yaw'-hoo): Miknejah, an Israelite. Origin: from H4735 (מִקְנֶה) and H3050 (יָהּ); possession of Jah; KJV: Mikneiah.

H4738 מִקְסָם (miqçâm, mik-sawn'): an augury. Origin: from H7080 (קָסַם); KJV: divination.

H4739 מָקַץ (Mâqats, maw-kats'): Makats, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7112 (קָצַץ); end; KJV: Makaz.

H4740 מַקְצוֹעַ (maqtsôwaʻ, mak-tso'-ah): an angle or recess. Origin: or מַקְצֹעַ; or (feminine) מַקְצֹעָה; from H7106 (קָצַע) in the denominative sense of bending; KJV: corner, turning.

H4741 מַקְצֻעָה (maqtsuʻâh, mak-tsoo-aw'): a scraper, i.e. a carving chisel. Origin: from H7106 (קָצַע); KJV: plane.

H4742 מְקֻצְעָה (mᵉqutsʻâh, mek-oots-aw'): an angle. Origin: from H7106 (קָצַע) in the denominative sense of bending; KJV: corner.

H4743 מָקַק (mâqaq, maw-kak'): to melt; figuratively, to flow, dwindle, vanish. Origin: ' a primitive root; KJV: consume away, be corrupt, dissolve, pine away.

H4744 מִקְרָא (miqrâʼ, mik-raw'): something called out, i.e. a public meeting (the act, the persons, or the place); also a rehearsal. Origin: from H7121 (קָרָא); KJV: assembly, calling, convocation, reading.

H4745 מִקְרֶה (miqreh, mik-reh'): something met with, i.e. an accident or fortune. Origin: from H7136 (קָרָה); KJV: something befallen, befalleth, chance, event, hap(-peneth).

H4746 מְקָרֶה (mᵉqâreh, mek-aw-reh'): properly, something meeting, i.e. a frame (of timbers). Origin: from H7136 (קָרָה); KJV: building.

H4747 מְקֵרָה (mᵉqêrâh, mek-ay-raw'): a cooling off. Origin: from the same as H7119 (קַר); KJV: [idiom] summer.

H4748 מִקְשֶׁה (miqsheh, mik-sheh'): something turned (rounded), i.e. a curl (of tresses). Origin: from H7185 (קָשָׁה) in the sense of knotting up round and hard; KJV: [idiom] well (set) hair.

H4749 מִקְשָׁה (miqshâh, mik-shaw'): rounded work, i.e. moulded by hammering (repousse). Origin: feminine of H4748 (מִקְשֶׁה); KJV: beaten (out of one piece, work), upright, whole piece.

H4750 מִקְשָׁה (miqshâh, mik-shaw'): literally a cucumbered field, i.e. a cucumber patch. Origin: denominative from H7180 (קִשֻּׁא); KJV: garden of cucumbers.

H4751 מַר (mar, mar): bitter (literally or figuratively); also (as noun) bitterness, or (adverbially) bitterly. Origin: or (feminine) מָרָה; from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: [phrase] angry, bitter(-ly, -ness), chafed, discontented, [idiom] great, heavy.

H4752 מַר (mar, mar): a drop. Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר) in its original sense of distillation; KJV: drop.

H4753 מֹר (môr, more): myrrh (as distilling in drops, and also as bitter). Origin: or מוֹר; from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: myrrh.

H4754 מָרָא (mârâʼ, maw-raw'): to rebel; hence (through the idea of maltreating) to whip, i.e. lash (self with wings, as the ostrich in running). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be filthy, lift up self.

H4755 מָרָא (Mârâʼ, maw-raw'): Mara, a symbolic name of Naomi. Origin: for H4751 (מַר) feminine; bitter; KJV: Mara.

H4756 מָרֵא (mârêʼ, maw-ray'): a master. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H4754 (מָרָא) in the sense of domineering; KJV: lord, Lord.

H4757 מְרֹאדַךְ בַּלְאָדָן (Mᵉrôʼdak Balʼâdân, mer-o-dak' bal-awdawn'): Merodak-Baladan, a Babylonian king. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Merodach-baladan. Compare H4781 (מְרֹדָךְ).

H4758 מַרְאֶה (marʼeh, mar-eh'): a view (the act of seeing); also an appearance (the thing seen), whether (real) a shape (especially if handsome, comeliness; often plural the looks), or (mental) a vision. Origin: from H7200 (רָאָה); KJV: [idiom] apparently, appearance(-reth), [idiom] as soon as beautiful(-ly), countenance, fair, favoured, form, goodly, to look (up) on (to), look(-eth), pattern, to see, seem, sight, visage, vision.

H4759 מַרְאָה (marʼâh, mar-aw'): a vision; also (causatively) a mirror. Origin: feminine of H4758 (מַרְאֶה); KJV: looking glass, vision.

H4760 מֻרְאָה (murʼâh, moor-aw'): something conspicuous, i.e. the craw of abird (from its prominence). Origin: apparently feminine passive causative participle of H7200 (רָאָה); KJV: crop.

H4761 מַרְאָשָׁה (marʼâshâh, mar-aw-shaw'): properly, headship, i.e. (plural for collective) dominion. Origin: denominative from H7218 (רֹאשׁ); KJV: principality.

H4762 מַרְאֵשָׁה (Marʼêshâh, mar-ay-shaw'): Mareshah, the name of two Israelites and of a place in Palestine. Origin: or מַרֵשָׁה; formed like H4761 (מַרְאָשָׁה); summit; KJV: Mareshah.

H4763 מְרַאֲשָׁה (mᵉraʼăshâh, mer-ah-ash-aw'): properly, a headpiece, i.e. (plural for adverbial) at (or as) the head-rest (or pillow). Origin: formed like H4761 (מַרְאָשָׁה); KJV: bolster, head, pillow. Compare H4772 (מַרְגְלָה).

H4764 מֵרָב (Mêrâb, may-rawb'): Merab, a daughter of Saul. Origin: from H7231 (רָבַב); increase; KJV: Merab.

H4765 מַרְבַד (marbad, mar-bad'): a coverlet. Origin: from H7234 (רָבַד); KJV: covering of tapestry.

H4766 מַרְבֶה (marbeh, mar-beh'): properly, increasing; as noun, greatness, or (adverbially) greatly. Origin: from H7235 (רָבָה); KJV: great, increase.

H4767 מִרְבָּה (mirbâh, meer-baw'): abundance, i.e. a great quantity. Origin: from H7235 (רָבָה); KJV: much.

H4768 מַרְבִּית (marbîyth, mar-beeth'): a multitude; also offspring; specifically interest (on capital). Origin: from H7235 (רָבָה); KJV: greatest part, greatness, increase, multitude.

H4769 מַרְבֵּץ (marbêts, mar-bates'): a reclining place, i.e. fold (for flocks). Origin: from H7257 (רָבַץ); KJV: couching place, place to lie down.

H4770 מַרְבֵּק (marbêq, mar-bake'): a stall (for cattle). Origin: from an unused root meaning to tie up; KJV: [idiom] fat(-ted), stall.

H4771 מַרְגּוֹעַ (margôwaʻ, mar-go'-ah): a resting place. Origin: from H7280 (רָגַע); KJV: rest.

H4772 מַרְגְלָה (margᵉlâh, mar-ghel-aw'): (plural for collective) a footpiece, i.e. (adverbially) at the foot, or (direct.) the foot itself. Origin: denominative from H7272 (רֶגֶל); KJV: feet. Compare H4763 (מְרַאֲשָׁה).

H4773 מַרְגֵּמָה (margêmâh, mar-gay-maw'): a stone-heap. Origin: from H7275 (רָגַם); KJV: sling.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4774 to H4909
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4774 מַרְגֵּעָה (margêʻâh, mar-gay-aw'): rest. Origin: from H7280 (רָגַע); KJV: refreshing.

H4775 מָרַד (mârad, maw-rad'): to rebel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: rebel(-lious).

H4776 מְרַד (mᵉrad, mer-ad'): rebellion. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H4775 (מָרַד); KJV: rebellion.

H4777 מֶרֶד (mered, meh'-red): rebellion. Origin: from H4775 (מָרַד); KJV: rebellion.

H4778 מֶרֶד (Mered, meh'-red): Mered, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4777 (מֶרֶד); KJV: Mered.

H4779 מָרָד (mârâd, maw-rawd'): rebellious. Origin: (Aramaic) from the same as H4776 (מְרַד); KJV: rebellious.

H4780 מַרְדּוּת (mardûwth, mar-dooth'): rebelliousness. Origin: from H4775 (מָרַד); KJV: [idiom] rebellious.

H4781 מְרֹדָךְ (Mᵉrôdâk, mer-o-dawk'): Merodak, a Babylonian idol. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Merodach. Compare H4757 (מְרֹאדַךְ בַּלְאָדָן).

H4782 מׇרְדְּכַי (Mordᵉkay, mor-dek-ah'-ee): Mordecai, an Israelite. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Mordecai.

H4783 מֻרְדָּף (murdâph, moor-dawf'): persecuted. Origin: from H7291 (רָדַף); KJV: persecuted.

H4784 מָרָה (mârâh, maw-raw'): to be (causatively, make) bitter (or unpleasant); (figuratively) to rebel (or resist; causatively, to provoke). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bitter, change, be disobedient, disobey, grievously, provocation, provoke(-ing), (be) rebel (against, -lious).

H4785 מָרָה (Mârâh, maw-raw'): Marah, a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H4751 (מַר) feminine; bitter; KJV: Marah.

H4786 מֹרָה (môrâh, mo-raw'): bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) trouble. Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: grief.

H4787 מׇרָּה (morrâh, mor-raw'): trouble. Origin: a form of H4786 (מֹרָה); KJV: bitterness.

H4788 מָרוּד (mârûwd, maw-rood'): an outcast; (abstractly) destitution. Origin: from H7300 (רוּד) in the sense of maltreatment; KJV: cast out, misery.

H4789 מֵרוֹז (Mêrôwz, may-roze'): Meroz, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Meroz.

H4790 מְרוֹחַ (mᵉrôwach, mer-o-akh'): bruised, i.e. emasculated. Origin: from H4799 (מָרַח); KJV: broken.

H4791 מָרוֹם (mârôwm, maw-rome'): altitude, i.e. concretely (an elevated place), abstractly (elevation, figuratively (elation), or adverbially (aloft). Origin: from H7311 (רוּם); KJV: (far) above, dignity, haughty, height, (most, on) high (one, place), loftily, upward.

H4792 מֵרוֹם (Mêrôwm, may-rome'): Merom, a lake in Palestine. Origin: formed like H4791 (מָרוֹם); height; KJV: Merom.

H4793 מֵרוֹץ (mêrôwts, may-rotes'): a run (the trial of speed). Origin: from H7323 (רוּץ); KJV: race.

H4794 מְרוּצָה (mᵉrûwtsâh, mer-oo-tsaw'): a race (the act), whether the manner or the progress. Origin: or מְרֻצָה; feminine of H4793 (מֵרוֹץ); KJV: course, running. Compare H4835 (מְרֻצָה).

H4795 מָרוּק (mârûwq, maw-rook'): properly, rubbed; but used abstractly, a rubbing (with perfumery). Origin: from H4838 (מָרַק); KJV: purification.

H4796 מָרוֹת (Mârôwth, maw-rohth'): Maroth, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H4751 (מַר) feminine; bitter springs; KJV: Maroth.

H4797 מִרְזַח (mirzach, meer-zakh'): a cry, i.e. (of job), a revel. Origin: from an unused root meaning to scream; KJV: banquet.

H4798 מַרְזֵחַ (marzêach, mar-zay'-akh): a cry, i.e. (of grief) a lamentation. Origin: formed like H4797 (מִרְזַח); KJV: mourning.

H4799 מָרַח (mârach, maw-rakh'): properly, to soften by rubbing or pressure; hence (medicinally) to apply as an emollient. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lay for a plaister.

H4800 מֶרְחָב (merchâb, mer-khawb'): enlargement, either literally (an open space, usually in a good sense), or figuratively (liberty). Origin: from H7337 (רָחַב); KJV: breadth, large place (room).

H4801 מֶרְחָק (merchâq, mer-khawk'): remoteness, i.e. (concretely) a distant place; often (adverbially) from afar. Origin: ; from H7368 (רָחַק); KJV: (a-, dwell in, very) far (country, off). See also H1023 (בֵּית הַמֶּרְחָק).

H4802 מַרְחֶשֶׁת (marchesheth, mar-kheh'-sheth): a stewpan. Origin: from H7370 (רָחַשׁ); KJV: fryingpan.

H4803 מָרַט (mâraṭ, maw-rat'): to polish; by implication, to make bald (the head), to gall (the shoulder); also, to sharpen. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bright, furbish, (have his) hair (be) fallen off, peeled, pluck off (hair).

H4804 מְרַט (mᵉraṭ, mer-at'): to pull off. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4803 (מָרַט); KJV: be plucked.

H4805 מְרִי (mᵉrîy, mer-ee'): bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) rebellion; concretely, bitter, or rebellious. Origin: from H4784 (מָרָה); KJV: bitter, (most) rebel(-lion, -lious).

H4806 מְרִיא (mᵉrîyʼ, mer-ee'): stall-fed; often (as noun) a beeve. Origin: from H4754 (מָרָא) in the sense of grossness, through the idea of domineering (compare H4756 (מָרֵא)); KJV: fat (fed) beast (cattle, -ling).

H4807 מְרִיב בַּעַל (Mᵉrîyb Baʻal, mer-eeb' bah'-al): quarreller of Baal, Merib-Baal, an epithet of Gideon. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב) and H1168 (בַּעַל); KJV: Merib-baal. Compare H4810 (מְרִי בַעַל).

H4808 מְרִיבָה (mᵉrîybâh, mer-ee-baw'): quarrel. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב); KJV: provocation, strife.

H4809 מְרִיבָה (Mᵉrîybâh, mer-ee-baw'): Meribah, the name of two places in the Desert. Origin: the same as H4808 (מְרִיבָה); KJV: Meribah.

H4810 מְרִי בַעַל (Mᵉrîy Baʻal, mer-ee' bah'-al): Meri-Baal, an epithet of Gideon. Origin: from H4805 (מְרִי) and H1168 (בַּעַל); rebellion of (i.e. against) Baal; KJV: Meri-baal. Compare H4807 (מְרִיב בַּעַל).

H4811 מְרָיָה (Mᵉrâyâh, mer-aw-yaw'): Merajah, an Israelite. Origin: from H4784 (מָרָה); rebellion; KJV: Meraiah. Compare H3236 (יִמְרָה).

H4812 מְרָיוֹת (Mᵉrâyôwth, mer-aw-yohth'): Merajoth, the name of two Israelites. Origin: plural of H4811 (מְרָיָה); rebellious; KJV: Meraioth.

H4813 מִרְיָם (Miryâm, meer-yawm'): Mirjam, the name of two Israelitesses. Origin: from H4805 (מְרִי); rebelliously; KJV: Miriam.

H4814 מְרִירוּת (mᵉrîyrûwth, mer-ee-rooth'): bitterness, i.e. (figuratively) grief. Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: bitterness.

H4815 מְרִירִי (mᵉrîyrîy, mer-ee-ree'): bitter, i.e. poisonous. Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: bitter.

H4816 מֹרֶךְ (môrek, mo'-rek): softness, i.e. (figuratively) fear. Origin: perhaps from H7401 (רָכַךְ); KJV: faintness.

H4817 מֶרְכָּב (merkâb, mer-kawb'): a chariot; also a seat (in a vehicle). Origin: from H7392 (רָכַב); KJV: chariot, covering, saddle.

H4818 מֶרְכָּבָה (merkâbâh, mer-kaw-baw'): a chariot. Origin: feminine of H4817 (מֶרְכָּב); KJV: chariot. See also H1024 (בֵּית הַמַּרְכָּבוֹת).

H4819 מַרְכֹּלֶת (markôleth, mar-ko'-leth): a mart. Origin: from H7402 (רָכַל); KJV: merchandise.

H4820 מִרְמָה (mirmâh, meer-maw'): fraud. Origin: from H7411 (רָמָה) in the sense of deceiving; KJV: craft, deceit(-ful, -fully), false, feigned, guile, subtilly, treachery.

H4821 מִרְמָה (Mirmâh, meer-maw'): Mirmah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4820 (מִרְמָה); KJV: Mirma.

H4822 מְרֵמוֹת (Mᵉrêmôwth, mer-ay-mohth'): Meremoth, the name of two Israelites. Origin: plural from H7311 (רוּם); heights; KJV: Meremoth.

H4823 מִרְמָס (mirmâç, meer-mawce'): abasement (the act or the thing). Origin: from H7429 (רָמַס); KJV: tread (down) -ing, (to be) trodden (down) under foot.

H4824 מֵרֹנֹתִי (Mêrônôthîy, may-ro-no-thee'): a Meronothite, or inhabitant of some (otherwise unknown) Meronoth. Origin: patrial from an unused noun; KJV: Meronothite.

H4825 מֶרֶס (Mereç, meh'-res): Meres, a Persian. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Meres.

H4826 מַרְסְנָא (Marçᵉnâʼ, mar-sen-aw'): Marsena, a Persian. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Marsena.

H4827 מֵרַע (mêraʻ, may-rah'): used as (abstract) noun, wickedness. Origin: from H7489 (רָעַע); KJV: do mischief.

H4828 מֵרֵעַ (mêrêaʻ, may-ray'-ah): a friend. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה) in the sense of companionship; KJV: companion, friend.

H4829 מִרְעֶה (mirʻeh, meer-eh'): pasture (the place or the act); also the haunt of wild animals. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה) in the sense of feeding; KJV: feeding place, pasture.

H4830 מִרְעִית (mirʻîyth, meer-eeth'): pasturage; concretely, a flock. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה) in the sense of feeding; KJV: flock, pasture.
