H4831 מַרְעֲלָה (Marʻălâh, mar-al-aw'): Maralah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7477 (רָעַל); perhaps, earthquake; KJV: Maralah.

H4832 מַרְפֵּא (marpêʼ, mar-pay'): properly, curative, i.e. literally (concretely) a medicine, or (abstractly) a cure; figuratively (concretely) deliverance, or (abstractly) placidity. Origin: from H7495 (רָפָא); KJV: (in-)cure(-able), healing(-lth), remedy, sound, wholesome, yielding.

H4833 מִרְפָּשׂ (mirpâs, meer-paws'): muddled water. Origin: from H7515 (רָפַשׂ); KJV: that which...have fouled.

H4834 מָרַץ (mârats, maw-rats'): properly, to press, i.e. (figuratively) to be pungent or vehement; to irritate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: embolden, be forcible, grievous, sore.

H4835 מְרֻצָה (mᵉrutsâh, mer-oo-tsaw'): oppression. Origin: from H7533 (רָצַץ); KJV: violence. See also H4794 (מְרוּצָה).

H4836 מַרְצֵעַ (martsêaʻ, mar-tsay'-ah): an awl. Origin: from H7527 (רָצַע); KJV: aul.

H4837 מַרְצֶפֶת (martsepheth, mar-tseh'-feth): a pavement. Origin: from H7528 (רָצַף); KJV: pavement.

H4838 מָרַק (mâraq, maw-rak'): to polish; by implication, to sharpen; also to rinse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bright, furbish, scour.

H4839 מָרָק (mârâq, maw-rawk'): soup (as if a rinsing). Origin: from H4838 (מָרַק); KJV: broth. See also H6564 (פָּרָק).

H4840 מֶרְקָח (merqâch, mer-kawkh'): a spicy herb. Origin: from H7543 (רָקַח); KJV: [idiom] sweet.

H4841 מֶרְקָחָה (merqâchâh, mer-kaw-khaw'): abstractly, a seasoning (with spicery); concretely, an unguentkettle (for preparing spiced oil). Origin: feminine of H4840 (מֶרְקָח); KJV: pot of ointment, [idiom] well.

H4842 מִרְקַחַת (mirqachath, meer-kakh'-ath): an aromatic unguent; also an unguent-pot. Origin: from H7543 (רָקַח); KJV: prepared by the apothecaries' art, compound, ointment.

H4843 מָרַר (mârar, maw-rar'): to be (causatively, make) bitter (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to trickle (see H4752 (מַר)); but used only as a denominative from H4751 (מַר); KJV: (be, be in, deal, have, make) bitter(-ly, -ness), be moved with choler, (be, have sorely, it) grieved(-eth), provoke, vex.

H4844 מְרֹר (mᵉrôr, mer-ore'): a bitter herb. Origin: or מְרוֹר; from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: bitter(-ness).

H4845 מְרֵרָה (mᵉrêrâh, mer-ay-raw'): bile (from its bitterness). Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: gall.

H4846 מְרֹרָה (mᵉrôrâh, mer-o-raw'): properly, bitterness; concretely, a bitter thing; specifically bile; also venom (of a serpent). Origin: or מְרוֹרָה; from H4843 (מָרַר); KJV: bitter (thing), gall.

H4847 מְרָרִי (Mᵉrârîy, mer-aw-ree'): Merari, an Israelite. Origin: from H4843 (מָרַר); bitter; KJV: Merari. See also H4848 (מְרָרִי).

H4848 מְרָרִי (Mᵉrârîy, mer-aw-ree'): a Merarite (collectively), or decendants of Merari. Origin: from H4847 (מְרָרִי); KJV: Merarites.

H4849 מִרְשַׁעַת (mirshaʻath, meer-shah'-ath): a female wicked doer. Origin: from H7561 (רָשַׁע); KJV: wicked woman.

H4850 מְרָתַיִם (Mᵉrâthayim, mer-aw-thah'-yim): Merathajim, an epithet of Babylon. Origin: dual of H4751 (מַר) feminine; double bitterness; KJV: Merathaim.

H4851 מַשׁ (Mash, mash): Mash, a son of Aram, and the people descended from him. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Mash.

H4852 מֵשָׁא (Mêshâʼ, may-shaw'): Mesha, a place in Arabia. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Mesha.

H4853 מַשָּׂא (massâʼ, mas-saw'): a burden; specifically, tribute, or (abstractly) porterage; figuratively, an utterance, chiefly adoom, especially singing; mental, desire. Origin: from H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: burden, carry away, prophecy, [idiom] they set, song, tribute.

H4854 מַשָּׂא (Massâʼ, mas-saw'): Massa, a son of Ishmael. Origin: the same as H4853 (מַשָּׂא); burden; KJV: Massa.

H4855 מַשָּׁא (mashshâʼ, mash-shaw'): a loan; by implication, interest on adebt. Origin: from H5383 (נָשָׁה); KJV: exaction, usury.

H4856 מַשֹּׂא (massôʼ, mas-so'): partiality (as a lifting up). Origin: from H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: respect.

H4857 מַשְׁאָב (mashʼâb, mash-awb'): a trough for cattle to drink from. Origin: from H7579 (שָׁאַב); KJV: place of drawing water.

H4858 מַשָּׂאָה (massâʼâh, mas-saw-aw'): a conflagration (from the rising of smoke). Origin: from H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: burden.

H4859 מַשָּׁאָה (mashshâʼâh, mash-shaw-aw'): a loan. Origin: feminine of H4855 (מַשָּׁא); KJV: [idiom] any(-thing), debt.

H4860 מַשָּׁאוֹן (mashshâʼôwn, mash-shaw-ohn'): dissimulation. Origin: from H5377 (נָשָׁא); KJV: deceit.

H4861 מִשְׁאָל (Mishʼâl, mish-awl'): Mishal, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7592 (שָׁאַל); request; KJV: Mishal, Misheal. Compare H4913 (מָשָׁל).

H4862 מִשְׁאָלָה (mishʼâlâh, mish-aw-law'): a request. Origin: from H7592 (שָׁאַל); KJV: desire, petition.

H4863 מִשְׁאֶרֶת (mishʼereth, mish-eh'-reth): a kneading-trough (in which the dough rises). Origin: from H7604 (שָׁאַר) in the original sense of swelling; KJV: kneading trough, store.

H4864 מַשְׂאֵת (masʼêth, mas-ayth'): properly, (abstractly) a raising (as of the hands in prayer), or rising (of flame); figuratively, an utterance; concretely, a beacon (as raised); a present (as taken), mess, or tribute; figuratively, a reproach (as a burden). Origin: from H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: burden, collection, sign of fire, (great) flame, gift, lifting up, mess, oblation, reward.

H4865 מִשְׁבְּצָה (mishbᵉtsâh, mish-bets-aw'): a brocade; by analogy, a (reticulated) setting of agem. Origin: from H7660 (שָׁבַץ); KJV: ouch, wrought.

H4866 מִשְׁבֵּר (mishbêr, mish-bare'): the orifice of the womb (from which the fetus breaks forth). Origin: from H7665 (שָׁבַר); KJV: birth, breaking forth.

H4867 מִשְׁבָּר (mishbâr, mish-bawr'): a breaker (of the sea). Origin: from H7665 (שָׁבַר); KJV: billow, wave.

H4868 מִשְׁבָּת (mishbâth, mish-bawth'): cessation, i.e. destruction. Origin: from H7673 (שָׁבַת); KJV: sabbath.

H4869 מִשְׂגָּב (misgâb, mis-gawb'): defence, high fort (tower), refuge, Misgab, a place in Moab. Origin: from H7682 (שָׂגַב); properly, a cliff (or other lofty or inaccessible place); abstractly, altitude; figuratively, a refuge KJV: Misgab.

H4870 מִשְׁגֶּה (mishgeh, mish-gay'): an error. Origin: from H7686 (שָׁגָה); KJV: oversight.

H4871 מָשָׁה (mâshâh, maw-shaw'): to pull out (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: draw(out).

H4872 מֹשֶׁה (Môsheh, mo-sheh'): Mosheh, the Israelite lawgiver. Origin: from H4871 (מָשָׁה); drawing out (of the water), i.e. rescued; KJV: Moses.

H4873 מֹשֶׁה (Môsheh, mo-sheh'): {Mosheh, the Israelite lawgiver}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4872 (מֹשֶׁה) KJV: Moses.

H4874 מַשֶּׁה (mashsheh, mash-sheh'): a debt. Origin: from H5383 (נָשָׁה); KJV: [phrase] creditor.

H4875 מְשׁוֹאָה (mᵉshôwʼâh, meh-o-aw'): (a) ruin, abstractly (the act) or concretely (the wreck). Origin: or מְשֹׁאָה; from the same as H7722 (שׁוֹא); KJV: desolation, waste.

H4876 מַשּׁוּאָה (mashshûwʼâh, mash-shoo-aw'): ruin. Origin: or מַשֻּׁאָה; for H4875 (מְשׁוֹאָה); KJV: desolation, destruction.

H4877 מְשׁוֹבָב (Mᵉshôwbâb, mesh-o-bawb'): Meshobab, an Israelite. Origin: from H7725 (שׁוּב); returned; KJV: Meshobab.

H4878 מְשׁוּבָה (mᵉshûwbâh, mesh-oo-baw'): apostasy. Origin: or מְשֻׁבָה; from H7725 (שׁוּב); KJV: backsliding, turning away.

H4879 מְשׁוּגָה (mᵉshûwgâh, mesh-oo-gaw'): mistake. Origin: from an unused root meaning to stray; KJV: error.

H4880 מָשׁוֹט (mâshôwṭ, maw-shote'): an oar. Origin: or מִשּׁוֹט; from H7751 (שׁוּט); KJV: oar.

H4881 מְשׂוּכָה (mᵉsûwkâh, mes-oo-kaw'): a hedge. Origin: or מְשֻׂכָה; from H7753 (שׂוּךְ); KJV: hedge.

H4882 מְשׁוּסָה (mᵉshûwçâh, mesh-oo-saw'): spoilation. Origin: from an unused root meaning to plunder; KJV: spoil.

H4883 מַשּׂוֹר (massôwr, mas-sore'): a saw. Origin: from an unused root meaning to rasp; KJV: saw.

H4884 מְשׂוּרָה (mᵉsûwrâh, mes-oo-raw'): a measure (for liquids). Origin: from an unused root meaning apparently to divide; KJV: measure.

H4885 מָשׂוֹשׂ (mâsôws, maw-soce'): delight, concretely (the cause or object) or abstractly (the feeling). Origin: from H7797 (שׂוּשׂ); KJV: joy, mirth, rejoice.

H4886 מָשַׁח (mâshach, maw-shakh'): to rub with oil, i.e. to anoint; by implication, to consecrate; also to paint. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: anoint, paint.

H4887 מְשַׁח (mᵉshach, mesh-akh'): oil. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H4886 (מָשַׁח); KJV: oil.

H4888 מִשְׁחָה (mishchâh, meesh-khaw'): unction (the act); by implication, a consecratory gift. Origin: or מׇשְׁחָה; from H4886 (מָשַׁח); KJV: (to be) anointed(-ing), ointment.

H4889 מַשְׁחִית (mashchîyth, mash-kheeth'): destructive, i.e. (as noun) destruction, literally (specifically a snare) or figuratively (corruption). Origin: from H7843 (שָׁחַת); KJV: corruption, (to) destroy(-ing), destruction, trap, [idiom] utterly.

H4890 מִשְׂחַק (mischaq, mis-khawk'): a laughing-stock. Origin: from H7831 (שַׁחֲצוֹם); KJV: scorn.

H4891 מִשְׁחָר (mishchâr, mish-khawr'): dawn. Origin: from H7836 (שָׁחַר) in the sense of day breaking; KJV: morning.

H4892 מַשְׁחֵת (mashchêth, mash-khayth'): destruction. Origin: for H4889 (מַשְׁחִית); KJV: destroying.

H4893 מִשְׁחָת (mishchâth, mish-khawth'): disfigurement. Origin: or מׇשְׁחָת; from H7843 (שָׁחַת); KJV: corruption, marred.

H4894 מִשְׁטוֹחַ (mishṭôwach, mish-to'-akh): a spreading-place. Origin: or מִשְׁטַח; from H7849 (שָׁטַח); KJV: (to) spread (forth, -ing, upon).

H4895 מַשְׂטֵמָה (masṭêmâh, mas-tay-maw'): enmity. Origin: from the same as H7850 (שֹׁטֵט); KJV: hatred.

H4896 מִשְׁטָר (mishṭâr, mish-tawr'): jurisdiction. Origin: from H7860 (שֹׁטֵר); KJV: dominion.

H4897 מֶשִׁי (meshîy, meh'-shee): silk (as drawn from the cocoon). Origin: from H4871 (מָשָׁה); KJV: silk.

H4898 מְשֵׁיזַבְאֵל (Mᵉshêyzabʼêl, mesh-ay-zab-ale'): Meshezabel, an Israelite. Origin: from an equiv. to H7804 (שְׁזַב) and H410 (אֵל); delivered of God; KJV: Meshezabeel.

H4899 מָשִׁיחַ (mâshîyach, maw-shee'-akh): anointed; usually a consecrated person (as a king, priest, or saint); specifically, the Messiah. Origin: from H4886 (מָשַׁח); KJV: anointed, Messiah.

H4900 מָשַׁךְ (mâshak, maw-shak'): to draw, used in a great variety of applications (including to sow, to sound, to prolong, to develop, to march, to remove, to delay, to be tall, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: draw (along, out), continue, defer, extend, forbear, [idiom] give, handle, make (pro-, sound) long, [idiom] sow, scatter, stretch out.

H4901 מֶשֶׁךְ (meshek, meh'shek): a sowing; also a possession. Origin: from H4900 (מָשַׁךְ); KJV: precious, price.

H4902 מֶשֶׁךְ (Meshek, meh'-shek): Meshek, a son of Japheth, and the people descended from him. Origin: the same in form as H4901 (מֶשֶׁךְ), but probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Mesech, Meshech.

H4903 מִשְׁכַּב (mishkab, mish-kab'): a bed. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4904 (מִשְׁכָּב); KJV: bed.

H4904 מִשְׁכָּב (mishkâb, mish-kawb'): a bed (figuratively, a bier); abstractly, sleep; by euphemism, carnal intercourse. Origin: from H7901 (שָׁכַב); KJV: bed(-chamber), couch, lieth (lying) with.

H4905 מַשְׂכִּיל (maskîyl, mas-keel'): instructive, i.e. a didactic poem. Origin: from H7919 (שָׂכַל); KJV: Maschil.

H4906 מַשְׂכִּית (maskîyth, mas-keeth'): a figure (carved on stone, the wall, or any object); figuratively, imagination. Origin: from the same as H7906 (שֵׂכוּ); KJV: conceit, image(-ry), picture, [idiom] wish.

H4907 מִשְׁכַּן (mishkan, mish-kan'): residence. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4908 (מִשְׁכָּן); KJV: habitation.

H4908 מִשְׁכָּן (mishkân, mish-kawn'): a residence (including a shepherd's hut, the lair of animals, figuratively, the grave; also the Temple); specifically, the Tabernacle (properly, its wooden walls). Origin: from H7931 (שָׁכַן); KJV: dwelleth, dwelling (place), habitation, tabernacle, tent.

H4909 מַשְׂכֹּרֶת (maskôreth, mas-koh'-reth): wages or a reward. Origin: from H7936 (שָׂכַר); KJV: reward, wages.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H4910 to H5031
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H4910 מָשַׁל (mâshal, maw-shal'): to rule. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (have, make to have) dominion, governor, [idiom] indeed, reign, (bear, cause to, have) rule(-ing, -r), have power.

H4911 מָשַׁל (mâshal, maw-shal'): to liken, i.e. (transitively) to use figurative language (an allegory, adage, song or the like); intransitively, to resemble. Origin: denominative from H4912 (מָשָׁל); KJV: be(-come) like, compare, use (as a) proverb, speak (in proverbs), utter.

H4912 מָשָׁל (mâshâl, maw-shawl'): properly, a pithy maxim, usually of metaphorical nature; hence, a simile (as an adage, poem, discourse). Origin: apparently from H4910 (מָשַׁל) in some original sense of superiority in mental action; KJV: byword, like, parable, proverb.

H4913 מָשָׁל (Mâshâl, maw-shawl'): Mashal, a place in Palestine. Origin: for H4861 (מִשְׁאָל); KJV: Mashal.

H4914 מְשֹׁל (mᵉshôl, mesh-ol'): a satire. Origin: from H4911 (מָשַׁל); KJV: byword.

H4915 מֹשֶׁל (môshel, mo'-shel): empire; a parallel. Origin: (1) from H4910 (מָשַׁל); (2) from H4911 (מָשַׁל); KJV: dominion, like.

H4916 מִשְׁלוֹחַ (mishlôwach, mish-lo'-akh): a sending out, i.e. (abstractly) presentation (favorable), or seizure (unfavorable); also (concretely) a place of dismissal, or a business to be discharged. Origin: or מִשְׁלֹחַ; also מִשְׁלָח; from H7971 (שָׁלַח); KJV: to lay, to put, sending (forth), to set.

H4917 מִשְׁלַחַת (mishlachath, mish-lakh'-ath): a mission, i.e. (abstractly and favorable) release, or (concretely and unfavorable) an army. Origin: feminine of H4916 (מִשְׁלוֹחַ); KJV: discharge, sending.

H4918 מְשֻׁלָּם (Mᵉshullâm, mesh-ool-lawm'): Meshullam, the name of seventeen Israelites. Origin: from H7999 (שָׁלַם); allied; KJV: Meshullam.

H4919 מְשִׁלֵּמוֹת (Mᵉshillêmôwth, mesh-il-lay-mohth'): Meshillemoth, an Israelite. Origin: plural from H7999 (שָׁלַם); reconciliations KJV: Meshillemoth. Compare H4921 (מְשִׁלֵּמִית).

H4920 מְשֶׁלֶמְיָה (Mᵉshelemyâh, mesh-eh-lem-yaw'): Meshelemjah, an Israelite. Origin: or מְשֶׁלֶמְיָהוּ; from H7999 (שָׁלַם) and H3050 (יָהּ); ally of Jah; KJV: Meshelemiah.

H4921 מְשִׁלֵּמִית (Mᵉshillêmîyth, mesh-il-lay-meeth'): Meshillemith, an Israelite. Origin: from H7999 (שָׁלַם); reconciliation; KJV: Meshillemith. Compare H4919 (מְשִׁלֵּמוֹת).

H4922 מְשֻׁלֶּמֶת (Mᵉshullemeth, mesh-ool-leh'-meth'): Meshullemeth, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine of H4918 (מְשֻׁלָּם); KJV: Meshullemeth.

H4923 מְשַׁמָּה (mᵉshammâh, mesh-am-maw'): a waste or amazement. Origin: from H8074 (שָׁמֵם); KJV: astonishment, desolate.

H4924 מַשְׁמָן (mashmân, mash-mawn'): fat, i.e. (literally and abstractly) fatness; but usually (figuratively and concretely) a rich dish, a fertile field, a robust man. Origin: from H8080 (שָׁמַן); KJV: fat (one, -ness, -test, -test place).

H4925 מִשְׁמַנָּה (Mishmannâh, mish-man-naw'): Mashmannah, an Israelite. Origin: from H8080 (שָׁמַן); fatness; KJV: Mishmannah.

H4926 מִשְׁמָע (mishmâʻ, mish-maw'): a report. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע); KJV: hearing.

H4927 מִשְׁמָע (Mishmâʻ, mish-maw'): Mishma, the name of a son of Ishmael, and of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4926 (מִשְׁמָע); KJV: Mishma.

H4928 מִשְׁמַעַת (mishmaʻath, mish-mah'-ath): audience, i.e. the royal court; also obedience, i.e. (concretely) a subject. Origin: feminine of H4926 (מִשְׁמָע); KJV: bidding, guard, obey.

H4929 מִשְׁמָר (mishmâr, mish-mawr'): a guard (the man, the post or the prison); a deposit (figuratively); also (as observed) a usage (abstractly), or an example (concretely). Origin: from H8104 (שָׁמַר); KJV: diligence, guard, office, prison, ward, watch.

H4930 מַשְׂמְרָה (masmᵉrâh, mas-mer-aw'): a peg. Origin: for H4548 (מַסְמֵר) fem.; KJV: nail.

H4931 מִשְׁמֶרֶת (mishmereth, mish-mer'-reth): watch, i.e. the act (custody), or (concretely) the sentry, the post; objectively preservation, or (concretely) safe; figuratively observance, i.e. (abstractly) duty or (objectively) a usage or party. Origin: feminine of H4929 (מִשְׁמָר); KJV: charge, keep, or to be kept, office, ordinace, safeguard, ward, watch.

H4932 מִשְׁנֶה (mishneh, mish-neh'): properly, a repetition, i.e. a duplicate (copy of a document), or a double (in amount); by implication, a second (in order, rank, age, quality or location). Origin: from H8138 (שָׁנָה); KJV: college, copy, double, fatlings, next, second (order), twice as much.

H4933 מְשִׁסָּה (mᵉshiççâh, mesh-is-saw'): plunder. Origin: from H8155 (שָׁסַס); KJV: booty, spoil.

H4934 מִשְׁעוֹל (mishʻôwl, mish-ole'): a hollow, i.e. a narrow passage. Origin: from the same as H8168 (שֹׁעַל); KJV: path.

H4935 מִשְׁעִי (mishʻîy, mish-ee'): inspection. Origin: probably from H8159 (שָׁעָה); KJV: to supple.

H4936 מִשְׁעָם (Mishʻâm, mish-awm'): Misham, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H8159 (שָׁעָה); inspection; KJV: Misham.

H4937 מִשְׁעֵן (mishʻên, mish-ane'): a support (concretely), i.e. (figuratively) a protector or sustenance. Origin: or מִשְׁעָן; from H8172 (שָׁעַן); KJV: stay.

H4938 מִשְׁעֵנָה (mishʻênâh, mish-ay-naw'): support (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) sustenance or (concretely) a walking-stick. Origin: or מִשְׁעֶנֶת; feminine of H4937 (מִשְׁעֵן); KJV: staff.

H4939 מִשְׂפָּח (mispâch, mis-pawkh'): slaughter. Origin: from H5596 (סָפַח); KJV: oppression.

H4940 מִשְׁפָּחָה (mishpâchâh, mish-paw-khaw'): a family, i.e. circle of relatives; figuratively, a class (of persons), a species (of animals) or sort (of things); by extension a tribe or people. Origin: from H8192 (שָׁפָה) (compare H8198 (שִׁפְחָה)); KJV: family, kind(-red).

H4941 מִשְׁפָּט (mishpâṭ, mish-pawt'): properly, a verdict (favorable or unfavorable) pronounced judicially, especially a sentence or formal decree (human or (participant's) divine law, individual or collective), including the act, the place, the suit, the crime, and the penalty; abstractly, justice, including a participant's right or privilege (statutory or customary), or even a style. Origin: from H8199 (שָׁפַט); KJV: [phrase] adversary, ceremony, charge, [idiom] crime, custom, desert, determination, discretion, disposing, due, fashion, form, to be judged, judgment, just(-ice, -ly), (manner of) law(-ful), manner, measure, (due) order, ordinance, right, sentence, usest, [idiom] worthy, [phrase] wrong.

H4942 מִשְׁפָּת (mishpâth, mish-pawth'): a stall for cattle (only dual). Origin: from H8192 (שָׁפָה); KJV: burden, sheepfold.

H4943 מֶשֶׁק (mesheq, meh'-shek): possession. Origin: from an unused root meaning to hold; KJV: [phrase] steward.

H4944 מַשָּׁק (mashshâq, mash-shawk'): a traversing, i.e. rapid motion. Origin: from H8264 (שָׁקַק); KJV: running to and fro.

H4945 מַשְׁקֶה (mashqeh, mash-keh'): properly, causing to drink, i.e. a butler; by implication (intransitively), drink (itself); figuratively, a well-watered region. Origin: from H8248 (שָׁקָה); KJV: butler(-ship), cupbearer, drink(-ing), fat pasture, watered.

H4946 מִשְׁקוֹל (mishqôwl, mish-kole'): weight. Origin: from H8254 (שָׁקַל); KJV: weight.

H4947 מַשְׁקוֹף (mashqôwph, mash-kofe'): a lintel. Origin: from H8259 (שָׁקַף) in its original sense of overhanging; KJV: lintel.

H4948 מִשְׁקָל (mishqâl, mish-kawl'): weight (numerically estimated); hence, weighing (the act). Origin: from H8254 (שָׁקַל); KJV: (full) weight.

H4949 מִשְׁקֶלֶת (mishqeleth, mish-keh'-leth): a weight, i.e. a plummet (with line attached). Origin: or מִשְׁקֹלֶת; feminine of H4948 (מִשְׁקָל) or H4947 (מַשְׁקוֹף); KJV: plummet.

H4950 מִשְׁקָע (mishqâʻ, mish-kaw'): a settling place (of water), i.e. a pond. Origin: from H8257 (שָׁקַע); KJV: deep.

H4951 מִשְׂרָה (misrâh, mis-raw'): empire. Origin: from H8280 (שָׂרָה); KJV: government.

H4952 מִשְׁרָה (mishrâh, mish-raw'): maceration, i.e. steeped juice. Origin: from H8281 (שָׁרָה) in the sense of loosening; KJV: liquor.

H4953 מַשְׁרוֹקִי (mashrôwqîy, mash-ro-kee'): a (musical) pipe (from its whistling sound). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H8319 (שָׁרַק); KJV: flute.

H4954 מִשְׁרָעִי (Mishrâʻîy, mish-raw-ee'): a Mishraite, or inhabitant (collectively) of Mishra. Origin: patrial from an unused noun from an unused root; probably meaning to stretch out; extension; KJV: Mishraites.

H4955 מִשְׂרָפָה (misrâphâh, mis-raw-faw'): combustion, i.e. cremation (of a corpse), or calcination (of lime). Origin: from H8313 (שָׂרַף); KJV: burning.

H4956 מִשְׂרְפוֹת מַיִם (Misrᵉphôwth mayim, mis-ref-ohth' mah'-yim): Misrephoth-Majim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the plural of H4955 (מִשְׂרָפָה) and H4325 (מַיִם); burnings of water; KJV: Misrephoth-mayim.

H4957 מַשְׂרֵקָה (Masrêqâh, mas-ray-kaw'): Masrekah, a place in Idumaea. Origin: a form for H7796 (שׂוֹרֵק) used denominatively; vineyard; KJV: Masrekah.

H4958 מַשְׂרֵת (masrêth, mas-rayth'): a pan. Origin: apparently from an unused root meaning to perforate, i.e. hollow out; KJV: pan.

H4959 מָשַׁשׁ (mâshash, maw-shash'): to feel of; by implication, to grope. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: feel, grope, search.

H4960 מִשְׁתֶּה (mishteh, mish-teh'): drink, by implication, drinking (the act); also (by implication) a banquet or (generally) feast. Origin: from H8354 (שָׁתָה); KJV: banquet, drank, drink, feast((-ed), -ing).

H4961 מִשְׁתֶּה (mishteh, mish-teh'): a banquet. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4960 (מִשְׁתֶּה); KJV: banquet.

H4962 מַת (math, math): properly, an adult (as of full length); by implication, a man (only in the plural). Origin: from the same as H4970 (מָתַי); KJV: [phrase] few, [idiom] friends, men, persons, [idiom] small.

H4963 מַתְבֵּן (mathbên, math-bane'): straw in the heap. Origin: denominative from H8401 (תֶּבֶן); KJV: straw.

H4964 מֶתֶג (metheg, meh-theg): a bit. Origin: from an unused root meaning to curb; KJV: bit, bridle.

H4965 מֶתֶג הָאַמָּה (Metheg hâ-ʼAmmâh, meh'-theg haw-am-maw'): Metheg-ha-Ammah, an epithet of Gath. Origin: from H4964 (מֶתֶג) and H520 (אַמָּה) with the art. interposed; bit of the metropolis; KJV: Metheg-ammah.

H4966 מָתוֹק (mâthôwq, maw-thoke'): sweet. Origin: or מָתוּק; from H4985 (מָתַק); KJV: sweet(-er, -ness).

H4967 מְתוּשָׁאֵל (Mᵉthûwshâʼêl, meth-oo-shaw-ale'): Methusael, an antediluvian patriarch. Origin: from H4962 (מַת) and H410 (אֵל), with the relative interposed; man who (is) of God; KJV: Methusael.

H4968 מְתוּשֶׁלַח (Mᵉthûwshelach, meth-oo-sheh'-lakh): Methushelach, an antediluvian patriarch. Origin: from H4962 (מַת) and H7973 (שֶׁלַח); man of a dart; KJV: Methuselah.

H4969 מָתַח (mâthach, maw-thakh'): to stretch out. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: spread out.

H4970 מָתַי (mâthay, maw-thah'ee): properly, extent (of time); but used only adverbially (especially with other particle prefixes), when (either relative or interrogative). Origin: from an unused root meaning to extend; KJV: long, when.

H4971 מַתְכֹנֶת (mathkôneth, math-ko'-neth): proportion (in size, number or ingredients). Origin: or מַתְכֻנֶת; from H8505 (תָּכַן) in the transferred sense of measuring; KJV: composition, measure, state, tale.

H4972 מַתְּלָאָה (mattᵉlâʼâh, mat-tel-aw-aw'): what a trouble!. Origin: from H4100 (מָה) and H8513 (תְּלָאָה); KJV: what a weariness.

H4973 מְתַלְּעָה (mᵉthallᵉʻâh, meth-al-leh-aw'): properly, a biter, i.e. a tooth. Origin: contr. from H3216 (יָלַע); KJV: cheek (jaw) tooth, jaw.

H4974 מְתֹם (mᵉthôm, meth-ohm'): wholesomeness; also (adverb) completely. Origin: from H8552 (תָּמַם); KJV: men (by reading H4962 (מַת)), soundness.

H4975 מֹתֶן (môthen, mo'-then): properly, the waist or small of the back; only in plural the loins. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be slender; KJV: [phrase] greyhound, loins, side.

H4976 מַתָּן (mattân, mat-tawn'): a present. Origin: from H5414 (נָתַן); KJV: gift, to give, reward.

H4977 מַתָּן (Mattân, mat-tawn'): Mattan, the name of a priest of Baal, and of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H4976 (מַתָּן); KJV: Mattan.

H4978 מַתְּנָא (mattᵉnâʼ, mat-ten-aw'): {a present; specifically (in a good sense), a sacrificial offering, (in a bad sense) a bribe}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H4979 (מַתָּנָה) KJV: gift.

H4979 מַתָּנָה (mattânâh, mat-taw-naw'): a present; specifically (in a good sense), a sacrificial offering, (in a bad sense) a bribe. Origin: feminine of H4976 (מַתָּן); KJV: gift.

H4980 מַתָּנָה (Mattânâh, mat-taw-naw'): Mattanah, a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H4979 (מַתָּנָה); KJV: Mattanah.

H4981 מִתְנִי (Mithnîy, mith-nee'): a Mithnite, or inhabitant of Methen. Origin: probably patrial from an unused noun meaning slenderness; KJV: Mithnite.

H4982 מַתְּנַי (Mattᵉnay, mat-ten-ah'ee): Mattenai, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H4976 (מַתָּן); liberal; KJV: Mattenai.

H4983 מַתַּנְיָה (Mattanyâh, mat-tan-yaw'): Mattanjah, the name of ten Israelites. Origin: or מַתַּנְיָהוּ; from H4976 (מַתָּן) and H3050 (יָהּ); gift of Jah; KJV: Mattaniah.

H4984 מִתְנַשֵּׂא (mithnassêʼ, mith-nas-say'): (used as abstractly) supreme exaltation. Origin: from H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: exalted.

H4985 מָתַק (mâthaq, maw-thak'): to suck, by implication, to relish, or (intransitively) be sweet. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (made, [idiom] take) sweet.

H4986 מֶתֶק (metheq, meh'-thek): figuratively, pleasantness (of discourse). Origin: from H4985 (מָתַק); KJV: sweetness.

H4987 מֹתֶק (môtheq, mo'-thek): sweetness. Origin: from H4985 (מָתַק); KJV: sweetness.

H4988 מָתָק (mâthâq, maw-thawk'): a dainty, i.e. (generally) food. Origin: from H4985 (מָתַק); KJV: feed sweetly.

H4989 מִתְקָה (Mithqâh, mith-kaw'): Mithkah, a place in the Desert. Origin: feminine of H4987 (מֹתֶק); sweetness; KJV: Mithcah.

H4990 מִתְרְדָת (Mithrᵉdâth, mith-red-awth'): Mithredath, the name of two Persians. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Mithredath.

H4991 מַתָּת (mattâth, mat-tawth'): a present. Origin: feminine of H4976 (מַתָּן) abbreviated form; KJV: gift.

H4992 מַתַּתָּה (Mattattâh, mat-tat-taw'): Mattattah, an Israelite. Origin: for H4993 (מַתִּתְיָה); gift of Jah; KJV: Mattathah.

H4993 מַתִּתְיָה (Mattithyâh, mat-tith-yaw'): Mattithjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or מַתִּתְיָהוּ; from H4991 (מַתָּת) and H3050 (יָהּ); gift of Jah; KJV: Mattithiah. n

H4994 נָא (nâʼ, naw): 'I pray', 'now', or 'then'; added mostly to verbs (in the Imperative or Future), or to interjections, occasionally to an adverb or conjunction. Origin: a primitive particle of incitement and entreaty, which may usually be rendered; KJV: I beseech (pray) thee (you), go to, now, oh.

H4995 נָא (nâʼ, naw): properly, tough, i.e. uncooked (flesh). Origin: apparently from H5106 (נוּא) in the sense of harshness from refusal; KJV: raw.

H4996 נֹא (Nôʼ, no): No (i.e. Thebes), the capital of Upper Egypt. Origin: of Egyptian origin; KJV: No. Compare H528 (אָמוֹן).

H4997 נֹאד (nôʼd, node): a (skin or leather) bag (for fluids). Origin: or נאוֹדlemma נֹאוד vowel, corrected to נאוֹדxlit nôʼwd corrected to nʼôwd; also (feminine) נֹאדָה; from an unused root of uncertain signification; KJV: bottle.

H4998 נָאָה (nâʼâh, naw-aw'): properly, to be at home, i.e. (by implication) to be pleasant (or suitable), i.e. beautiful. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be beautiful, become, be comely.

H4999 נָאָה (nâʼâh, naw-aw'): a home; figuratively, a pasture. Origin: from H4998 (נָאָה); KJV: habitation, house, pasture, pleasant place.

H5000 נָאוֶה (nâʼveh, naw-veh'): suitable, or beautiful. Origin: from H4998 (נָאָה) or H5116 (נָוֶה); KJV: becometh, comely, seemly.

H5001 נָאַם (nâʼam, naw-am'): properly, to whisper, i.e. (by implication) to utter as aoracle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: say.

H5002 נְאֻם (nᵉʼum, neh-oom'): an oracle. Origin: from H5001 (נָאַם); KJV: (hath) said, saith.

H5003 נָאַף (nâʼaph, naw-af'): to commit adultery; figuratively, to apostatize. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: adulterer(-ess), commit(-ing) adultery, woman that breaketh wedlock.

H5004 נִאֻף (niʼuph, nee-oof'): adultery. Origin: from H5003 (נָאַף); KJV: adultery.

H5005 נַאֲפוּף (naʼăphûwph, nah-af-oof'): adultery. Origin: from H5003 (נָאַף); KJV: adultery.

H5006 נָאַץ (nâʼats, naw-ats'): to scorn. Origin: a primitive root; in Ecclesiastes 12:5, by interchange for H5132 (נוּץ), to bloom KJV: abhor, (give occasion to) blaspheme, contemn, despise, flourish, [idiom] great, provoke.

H5007 נְאָצָה (nᵉʼâtsâh, neh-aw-tsaw'): scorn. Origin: or נֶאָצָה; from H5006 (נָאַץ); KJV: blasphemy.

H5008 נָאַק (nâʼaq, naw-ak'): to groan. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: groan.

H5009 נְאָקָה (nᵉʼâqâh, neh-aw-kaw'): a groan. Origin: from H5008 (נָאַק); KJV: groaning.

H5010 נָאַר (nâʼar, naw-ar'): to reject. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor, make void.

H5011 נֹב (Nôb, nobe): Nob, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5108 (נוֹב); fruit; KJV: Nob.

H5012 נָבָא (nâbâʼ, naw-baw'): to prophesy, i.e. speak (or sing) by inspiration (in prediction or simple discourse). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: prophesy(-ing), make self a prophet.

H5013 נְבָא (nᵉbâʼ, neb-aw'): {to prophesy, i.e. speak (or sing) by inspiration (in prediction or simple discourse) to prophesy, i.e. speak (or sing) by inspiration (in prediction or simple discourse)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5012 (נָבָא) KJV: prophesy.

H5014 נָבַב (nâbab, naw-bab'): to pierce; to be hollow, or (figuratively) foolish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hollow, vain.

H5015 נְבוֹ (Nᵉbôw, neb-o'): Nebo, the name of a Babylonian deity, also of a mountain in Moab, and of a place in Palestine. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Nebo.

H5016 נְבוּאָה (nᵉbûwʼâh, neb-oo-aw'): a prediction (spoken or written). Origin: from H5012 (נָבָא); KJV: prophecy.

H5017 נְבוּאָה (nᵉbûwʼâh, neb-oo-aw): inspired teaching. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5016 (נְבוּאָה); KJV: prophesying.

H5018 נְבוּזַרְאֲדָן (Nᵉbûwzarʼădân, neb-oo-zar-ad-awn'): Nebuzaradan, a Babylonian general. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Nebuzaradan.

H5019 נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר (Nᵉbûwkadneʼtstsar, neb-oo-kad-nets-tsar'): Nebukadnetstsar (or -retstsar, or -retstsor), king of Babylon. Origin: or נְבֻּכַדְנֶאצַּר; (2 Kings 24:1,10), or נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר; (Esther 2:6; Daniel 1:18), or נְבוּכַדְרֶאצַּר; or נְבוּכַדְרֶאצּוֹר; (Ezra 2:1; Jeremiah 49:28), or foreign derivation; KJV: Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuchadrezzar.

H5020 נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר (Nᵉbûwkadnetstsar, neb-oo-kad-nets-tsar'): {Nebukadnetstsar (or -retstsar, or -retstsor), king of Babylon}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5019 (נְבוּכַדְנֶאצַּר) KJV: Nebuchadnezzar.

H5021 נְבוּשַׁזְבָּן (Nᵉbûwshazbân, neb-oo-shaz-bawn'): Nebushazban, Nebuchadnezzar's chief eunuch. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Nebushazban.

H5022 נָבוֹת (Nâbôwth, naw-both'): Naboth, an Israelite. Origin: feminine plural from the same as H5011 (נֹב); fruits; KJV: Naboth.

H5023 נְבִזְבָּה (nᵉbizbâh, neb-iz-baw'): a largess. Origin: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; KJV: reward.

H5024 נָבַח (nâbach, naw-bakh'): to bark (as a dog). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bark.

H5025 נֹבַח (Nôbach, no'-bach): Nobach, the name of an Israelite, and of a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H5024 (נָבַח); a bark; KJV: Nobah.

H5026 נִבְחַז (Nibchaz, nib-khaz'): Nibchaz, a deity of the Avites. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Nibhaz.

H5027 נָבַט (nâbaṭ, naw-bat'): to scan, i.e. look intently at; by implication, to regard with pleasure, favor or care. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) behold, consider, look (down), regard, have respect, see.

H5028 נְבָט (Nᵉbâṭ, neb-awt'): Nebat, the father of Jeroboam I. Origin: from H5027 (נָבַט); regard; KJV: Nebat.

H5029 נְבִיא (nᵉbîyʼ, neb-ee'): a prophet. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5030 (נָבִיא); KJV: prophet.

H5030 נָבִיא (nâbîyʼ, naw-bee'): a prophet or (generally) inspired man. Origin: from H5012 (נָבָא); KJV: prophecy, that prophesy, prophet.

H5031 נְבִיאָה (nᵉbîyʼâh, neb-ee-yaw'): a prophetess or (generally) inspired woman; by implication, a poetess; by association a prophet's wife. Origin: feminine of H5030 (נָבִיא); KJV: prophetess.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5032 to H5140
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5032 נְבָיוֹת (Nᵉbâyôwth, neb-aw-yoth'): Nebajoth, a son of Ismael, and the country settled by him. Origin: or נְבָיֹת; feminine plural from H5107 (נוּב); fruitfulnesses; KJV: Nebaioth, Nebajoth.

H5033 נֵבֶךְ (nêbek, nay'-bek): a fountain. Origin: from an unused root meaning to burst forth; KJV: spring.

H5034 נָבֵל (nâbêl, naw-bale'): to wilt; generally, to fall away, fail, faint; figuratively, to be foolish or (morally) wicked; causatively, to despise, disgrace. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: disgrace, dishounour, lightly esteem, fade (away, -ing), fall (down, -ling, off), do foolishly, come to nought, [idiom] surely, make vile, wither.

H5035 נֶבֶל (nebel, neh'-bel): a skin-bag for liquids (from collapsing when empty); hence, a vase (as similar in shape when full); also a lyre (as having a body of like form). Origin: or נֵבֶל; from H5034 (נָבֵל); KJV: bottle, pitcher, psaltery, vessel, viol.

H5036 נָבָל (nâbâl, naw-bawl'): stupid; wicked (especially impious). Origin: from H5034 (נָבֵל); KJV: fool(-ish, -ish man, -ish woman), vile person.

H5037 נָבָל (Nâbâl, naw-bawl'): Nabal, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H5036 (נָבָל); dolt; KJV: Nabal.

H5038 נְבֵלָה (nᵉbêlâh, neb-ay-law'): a flabby thing, i.e. a carcase or carrion (human or bestial, often collectively); figuratively, an idol. Origin: from H5034 (נָבֵל); KJV: (dead) body, (dead) carcase, dead of itself, which died, (beast) that (which) dieth of itself.

H5039 נְבָלָה (nᵉbâlâh, neb-aw-law'): foolishness, i.e. (morally) wickedness; concretely, a crime; by extension, punishment. Origin: feminine of H5036 (נָבָל); KJV: folly, vile, villany.

H5040 נַבְלוּת (nablûwth, nab-looth'): properly, disgrace, i.e. the (female) pudenda. Origin: from H5036 (נָבָל); KJV: lewdness.

H5041 נְבַלָּט (Nᵉballâṭ, neb-al-lawt'): Neballat, a place in Palestine. Origin: apparently from H5036 (נָבָל) and H3909 (לָט); foolish secrecy; KJV: Neballat.

H5042 נָבַע (nâbaʻ, naw-bah'): to gush forth; figuratively, to utter (good or bad words); specifically, to emit (a foul odor). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: belch out, flowing, pour out, send forth, utter (abundantly).

H5043 נֶבְרְשָׁא (nebrᵉshâʼ, neb-reh-shaw'): a light; plural (collectively) a chandelier. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root meaning to shine; KJV: candlestick.

H5044 נִבְשָׁן (Nibshân, nib-shawn'): Nibshan, a place in Palestine. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Nibshan.

H5045 נֶגֶב (negeb, neh'-gheb): the south (from its drought); specifically, the Negeb or southern district of Judah, occasionally, Egypt (as south to Palestine). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be parched; KJV: south (country, side, -ward).

H5046 נָגַד (nâgad, naw-gad'): properly, to front, i.e. stand boldly out opposite; by implication (causatively), to manifest; figuratively, to announce (always by word of mouth to one present); specifically, to expose, predict, explain, praise. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bewray, [idiom] certainly, certify, declare(-ing), denounce, expound, [idiom] fully, messenger, plainly, profess, rehearse, report, shew (forth), speak, [idiom] surely, tell, utter.

H5047 נְגַד (nᵉgad, neg-ad'): to flow (through the idea of clearing the way). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5046 (נָגַד); KJV: issue.

H5048 נֶגֶד (neged, neh'-ghed): a front, i.e. part opposite; specifically a counterpart, or mate; usually (adverbial, especially with preposition) over against or before. Origin: from H5046 (נָגַד); KJV: about, (over) against, [idiom] aloof, [idiom] far (off), [idiom] from, over, presence, [idiom] other side, sight, [idiom] to view.

H5049 נֶגֶד (neged, neh'-ghed): opposite. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5048 (נֶגֶד); KJV: toward.

H5050 נָגַהּ (nâgahh, naw-gah'): to glitter; causatively, to illuminate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (en-) lighten, (cause to) shine.

H5051 נֹגַהּ (nôgahh, no'-gah): brilliancy (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H5050 (נָגַהּ); KJV: bright(-ness), light, (clear) shining.

H5052 נֹגַהּ (Nôgahh, no'-gah): Nogah, a son of David. Origin: the same as H5051 (נֹגַהּ); KJV: Nogah.

H5053 נֹגַהּ (nôgahh, no'-gah): dawn. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5051 (נֹגַהּ); KJV: morning.

H5054 נְגֹהָה (nᵉgôhâh, neg-o-haw'): splendor. Origin: feminine of H5051 (נֹגַהּ); KJV: brightness.

H5055 נָגַח (nâgach, naw-gakh'): to butt with the horns; figuratively, to war against. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gore, push (down, -ing).

H5056 נַגָּח (naggâch, nag-gawkh'): butting, i.e. vicious. Origin: from H5055 (נָגַח); KJV: used (wont) to push.

H5057 נָגִיד (nâgîyd, naw-gheed'): a commander (as occupying the front), civil, military or religious; generally (abstractly, plural), honorable themes. Origin: or נָגִד; from H5046 (נָגַד); KJV: captain, chief, excellent thing, (chief) governor, leader, noble, prince, (chief) ruler.

H5058 נְגִינָה (nᵉgîynâh, neg-ee-naw'): properly, instrumental music; by implication, a stringed instrument; by extension, a poem set to music; specifically, an epigram. Origin: or נְגִינַת; (Psalm 61:title), from H5059 (נָגַן); KJV: stringed instrument, musick, Neginoth (plural), song.

H5059 נָגַן (nâgan, naw-gan'): properly, to thrum, i.e. beat atune with the fingers; expectation. to play on astringed instrument; hence (generally), to make music. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: player on instruments, sing to the stringed instruments, melody, ministrel, play(-er, -ing).

H5060 נָגַע (nâgaʻ, naw-gah'): properly, to touch, i.e. lay the hand upon (for any purpose; euphemistically, to lie with a woman); by implication, to reach (figuratively, to arrive, acquire); violently, to strike (punish, defeat, destroy, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat, ([idiom] be able to) bring (down), cast, come (nigh), draw near (nigh), get up, happen, join, near, plague, reach (up), smite, strike, touch.

H5061 נֶגַע (negaʻ, neh'-gah): a blow (figuratively, infliction); also (by implication) a spot (concretely, a leprous person or dress). Origin: from H5060 (נָגַע); KJV: plague, sore, stricken, stripe, stroke, wound.

H5062 נָגַף (nâgaph, naw-gaf'): to push, gore, defeat, stub (the toe), inflict (a disease). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat, dash, hurt, plague, slay, smite (down), strike, stumble, [idiom] surely, put to the worse.

H5063 נֶגֶף (negeph, neh'-ghef): a trip (of the foot); figuratively, an infliction (of disease). Origin: from H5062 (נָגַף); KJV: plague, stumbling.

H5064 נָגַר (nâgar, naw-gar'): to flow; figuratively, to stretch out; causatively, to pour out or down; figuratively, to deliver over. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fall, flow away, pour down (out), run, shed, spilt, trickle down.

H5065 נָגַשׂ (nâgas, naw-gas'): to drive (an animal, a workman, a debtor, an army); by implication, to tax, harass, tyrannize. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: distress, driver, exact(-or), oppress(-or), [idiom] raiser of taxes, taskmaster.

H5066 נָגַשׁ (nâgash, naw-gash'): to be or come (causatively, bring) near (for any purpose); euphemistically, to lie with a woman; as an enemy, to attack; religious to worship; causatively, to present; figuratively, to adduce an argument; by reversal, to stand back. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make to) approach (nigh), bring (forth, hither, near), (cause to) come (hither, near, nigh), give place, go hard (up), (be, draw, go) near (nigh), offer, overtake, present, put, stand.

H5067 נֵד (nêd, nade): a mound, i.e. wave. Origin: from H5110 (נוּד) in the sense of piling up; KJV: heap.

H5068 נָדַב (nâdab, naw-dab'): to impel; hence, to volunteer (as a soldier), to present spontaneously. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: offer freely, be (give, make, offer self) willing(-ly).

H5069 נְדַב (nᵉdab, ned-ab'): be (or give) liberal(-ly). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5068 (נָדַב); KJV: (be minded of...own) freewill (offering), offer freely (willingly).

H5070 נָדָב (Nâdâb, naw-dawb'): Nadab, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H5068 (נָדַב); liberal; KJV: Nadab.

H5071 נְדָבָה (nᵉdâbâh, ned-aw-baw'): properly (abstractly) spontaneity, or (adjectively) spontaneous; also (concretely) a spontaneous or (by inference, in plural) abundant gift. Origin: from H5068 (נָדַב); KJV: free(-will) offering, freely, plentiful, voluntary(-ily, offering), willing(-ly), offering).

H5072 נְדַבְיָה (Nᵉdabyâh, ned-ab-yaw'): Nedabjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H5068 (נָדַב) and H3050 (יָהּ); largess of Jah; KJV: Nedabiah.

H5073 נִדְבָּךְ (nidbâk, nid-bawk'): a layer (of building materials). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root meaning to stick; KJV: row.

H5074 נָדַד (nâdad, naw-dad'): properly, to wave to and fro (rarely to flap up and down); figuratively, to rove, flee, or (causatively) to drive away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: chase (away), [idiom] could not, depart, flee ([idiom] apace, away), (re-) move, thrust away, wander (abroad, -er, -ing).

H5075 נְדַד (nᵉdad, ned-ad'): to depart. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5074 (נָדַד); KJV: go from.

H5076 נָדֻד (nâdud, naw-dood'): properly, tossed; abstractly, a rolling (on the bed). Origin: passive participle of H5074 (נָדַד); KJV: tossing to and fro.

H5077 נָדָה (nâdâh, naw-daw'): properly, to toss; figuratively, to exclude, i.e. banish, postpone, prohibit. Origin: or נָדָא; (2 Kings 17:21), a primitive root; KJV: cast out, drive, put far away.

H5078 נֵדֶה (nêdeh, nay'-deh): a bounty (for prostitution). Origin: from H5077 (נָדָה) in the sense of freely flinging money; KJV: gifts.

H5079 נִדָּה (niddâh, nid-daw'): properly, rejection; by implication, impurity, especially personal (menstruation) or moral (idolatry, incest). Origin: from H5074 (נָדַד); KJV: [idiom] far, filthiness, [idiom] flowers, menstruous (woman), put apart, [idiom] removed (woman), separation, set apart, unclean(-ness, thing, with filthiness).

H5080 נָדַח (nâdach, naw-dakh'): to push off; used in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (to expel, mislead, strike, inflict, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: banish, bring, cast down (out), chase, compel, draw away, drive (away, out, quite), fetch a stroke, force, go away, outcast, thrust away (out), withdraw.

H5081 נָדִיב (nâdîyb, naw-deeb'): properly, voluntary, i.e. generous; hence, magnanimous; as noun, a grandee (sometimes a tyrant). Origin: from H5068 (נָדַב); KJV: free, liberal (things), noble, prince, willing (hearted).

H5082 נְדִיבָה (nᵉdîybâh, ned-ee-baw'): properly, nobility, i.e. reputation. Origin: feminine of H5081 (נָדִיב); KJV: soul.

H5083 נָדָן (nâdân, naw-dawn'): a present (for prostitution). Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to give; KJV: gift.

H5084 נָדָן (nâdân, naw-dawn'): a sheath (of a sword). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: sheath.

H5085 נִדְנֶה (nidneh, nid-neh'): a sheath; figuratively, the body (as the receptacle of the soul). Origin: (Aramaic) from the same as H5084 (נָדָן); KJV: body.

H5086 נָדַף (nâdaph, naw-daf'): to shove asunder, i.e. disperse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drive (away, to and fro), thrust down, shaken, tossed to and fro.

H5087 נָדַר (nâdar, naw-dar'): to promise (pos., to do or give something to God). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make a) vow.

H5088 נֶדֶר (neder, neh'-der): a promise (to God); also (concretely) a thing promised. Origin: or נֵדֶר; from H5087 (נָדַר); KJV: vow(-ed).

H5089 נֹהַּ (nôahh, no'-ah): lamentation. Origin: from an unused root meaning to lament; KJV: wailing.

H5090 נָהַג (nâhag, naw-hag'): to drive forth (a person, an animal or chariot), i.e. lead, carry away; reflexively, to proceed (i.e. impel or guide oneself); also (from the panting induced by effort), to sigh. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: acquaint, bring (away), carry away, drive (away), lead (away, forth), (be) guide, lead (away, forth).

H5091 נָהָה (nâhâh, naw-haw'): to groan, i.e. bewail; hence (through the idea of crying aloud), to assemble (as if on proclamation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lament, wail.

H5092 נְהִי (nᵉhîy, neh-hee'): an elegy. Origin: from H5091 (נָהָה); KJV: lamentation, wailing.

H5093 נִהְיָה (nihyâh, nih-yaw'): lamentation. Origin: feminine of H5092 (נְהִי); KJV: doleful.

H5094 נְהִיר (nᵉhîyr, neh-heere'): illumination, i.e. (figuratively) wisdom. Origin: (Aramaic) or נְהִירוּ; (Aramaic), from the same as H5105 (נְהָרָה); KJV: light.

H5095 נָהַל (nâhal, naw-hal'): properly, to run with asparkle, i.e. flow; hence (transitively), to conduct, and (by inference) to protect, sustain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: carry, feed, guide, lead (gently, on).

H5096 נַהֲלָל (Nahălâl, nah-hal-awl'): Nahalal or Nahalol, a place in Palestine. Origin: or נַהֲלֹל; the same as H5097 (נַהֲלֹל); KJV: Nahalal, Nahallal, Nahalol.

H5097 נַהֲלֹל (nahălôl, nah-hal-ole'): pasture. Origin: from H5095 (נָהַל); KJV: bush.

H5098 נָהַם (nâham, naw-ham'): to growl. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mourn, roar(-ing).

H5099 נַהַם (naham, nah'-ham): a snarl. Origin: from H5098 (נָהַם); KJV: roaring.

H5100 נְהָמָה (nᵉhâmâh, neh-haw-maw'): snarling. Origin: feminine of H5099 (נַהַם); KJV: disquietness, roaring.

H5101 נָהַק (nâhaq, naw-hak'): to bray (as an ass), scream (from hunger). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bray.

H5102 נָהַר (nâhar, naw-har'): to sparkle, i.e. (figuratively) be cheerful; hence (from the sheen of a running stream) to flow, i.e. (figuratively) assemble. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: flow (together), be lightened.

H5103 נְהַר (nᵉhar, neh-har'): a river, especially the Euphrates. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5102 (נָהַר); KJV: river, stream.

H5104 נָהָר (nâhâr, naw-hawr'): a stream (including the sea; expectation the Nile, Euphrates, etc.); figuratively, prosperity. Origin: from H5102 (נָהַר); KJV: flood, river.

H5105 נְהָרָה (nᵉhârâh, neh-haw-raw'): daylight. Origin: from H5102 (נָהַר) in its original sense; KJV: light.

H5106 נוּא (nûwʼ, noo): to refuse, forbid, dissuade, or neutralize. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break, disallow, discourage, make of none effect.

H5107 נוּב (nûwb, noob): to germinate, i.e. (figuratively) to (causatively, make) flourish; also (of words), to utter. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring forth (fruit), make cheerful, increase.

H5108 נוֹב (nôwb, nobe): produce, literally or figuratively. Origin: or נֵיב; from H5107 (נוּב); KJV: fruit.

H5109 נוֹבַי (Nôwbay, no-bah'ee): Nobai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5108 (נוֹב); fruitful; KJV: Nebai (from the margin).

H5110 נוּד (nûwd, nood): to nod, i.e. waver; figuratively, to wander, flee, disappear; also (from shaking the head in sympathy), to console, deplore, or (from tossing the head in scorn) taunt. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bemoan, flee, get, mourn, make to move, take pity, remove, shake, skip for joy, be sorry, vagabond, way, wandering.

H5111 נוּד (nûwd, nood): to flee. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5116 (נָוֶה); KJV: get away.

H5112 נוֹד (nôwd, node): exile. Origin: (only defective נֹד ); from H5110 (נוּד); KJV: wandering.

H5113 נוֹד (Nôwd, node): Nod, the land of Cain. Origin: the same as H5112 (נוֹד)lemma נוֹדּ extra dagesh, corrected to נוֹד; vagrancy; KJV: Nod.

H5114 נוֹדָב (Nôwdâb, no-dawb'): Nodab, an Arab tribe. Origin: from H5068 (נָדַב); noble; KJV: Nodab.

H5115 נָוָה (nâvâh, naw-vaw'): to rest (as at home); causatively (through the implied idea of beauty ), to celebrate (with praises). Origin: a primitive root; (compare H5116 (נָוֶה)) KJV: keept at home, prepare an habitation.

H5116 נָוֶה (nâveh, naw-veh'): (adjectively) at home; hence (by implication of satisfaction) lovely; also (noun) a home, of God (temple), men (residence), flocks (pasture), or wild animals (den). Origin: or (feminine) נָוָה; from H5115 (נָוָה); KJV: comely, dwelling (place), fold, habitation, pleasant place, sheepcote, stable, tarried.

H5117 נוּחַ (nûwach, noo'-akh): to rest, i.e. settle down; used in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, intransitive, transitive and causative (to dwell, stay, let fall, place, let alone, withdraw, give comfort, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease, be confederate, lay, let down, (be) quiet, remain, (cause to, be at, give, have, make to) rest, set down. Compare H3241 (יָנִים).

H5118 נוּחַ (nûwach, noo'-akh): quiet. Origin: or נוֹחַ; from H5117 (נוּחַ); KJV: rest(-ed, -ing place).

H5119 נוֹחָה (Nôwchâh, no-chaw'): Nochah, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H5118 (נוּחַ); quietude; KJV: Nohah.

H5120 נוּט (nûwṭ, noot): to quake. KJV: be moved.

H5121 נָוִית (Nâvîyth, naw-veeth'): Navith, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5115 (נָוָה); residence; KJV: Naioth (from the margin).

H5122 נְוָלוּ (nᵉvâlûw, nev-aw-loo'): a sink. Origin: (Aramaic) or נְוָלִי; (Aramaic), from an unused root probably meaning to be foul; KJV: dunghill.

H5123 נוּם (nûwm, noom): to slumber (from drowsiness). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sleep, slumber.

H5124 נוּמָה (nûwmâh, noo-maw'): sleepiness. Origin: from H5123 (נוּם); KJV: drowsiness.

H5125 נוּן (nûwn, noon): to resprout, i.e. propagate by shoots; figuratively, to be perpetual. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be continued.

H5126 נוּן (Nûwn, noon): Nun or Non, the father of Joshua. Origin: or נוֹן; (1 Chronicles 7:27), from H5125 (נוּן); perpetuity, KJV: Non, Nun.

H5127 נוּס (nûwç, noos): to flit, i.e. vanish away (subside, escape; causatively, chase, impel, deliver). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] abate, away, be displayed, (make to) flee (away, -ing), put to flight, [idiom] hide, lift up a standard.

H5128 נוּעַ (nûwaʻ, noo'-ah): to waver, in a great variety of applications, literally and figuratively (as subjoined). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: continually, fugitive, [idiom] make, to (go) up and down, be gone away, (be) move(-able, -d), be promoted, reel, remove, scatter, set, shake, sift, stagger, to and fro, be vagabond, wag, (make) wander (up and down).

H5129 נוֹעַדְיָה (Nôwʻadyâh, no-ad-yaw'): Noadjah, the name of an Israelite, and a false prophetess. Origin: from H3259 (יָעַד) and H3050 (יָהּ); convened of Jah; KJV: Noadiah.

H5130 נוּף (nûwph, noof): to quiver (i.e. vibrate up and down, or rock to and fro); used in a great variety of applications (including sprinkling, beckoning, rubbing, bastinadoing, sawing, waving, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lift up, move, offer, perfume, send, shake, sift, strike, wave.

H5131 נוֹף (nôwph, nofe): elevation. Origin: from H5130 (נוּף); KJV: situation. Compare H5297 (נֹף).

H5132 נוּץ (nûwts, noots): properly, to flash; hence, to blossom (from the brilliancy of color); also, to fly away (from the quickness of motion). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: flee away, bud (forth).

H5133 נוֹצָה (nôwtsâh, no-tsaw'): a pinion (or wing feather); often (collectively) plumage. Origin: or נֹצָה; feminine active participle of H5327 (נָצָה) in the sense of flying; KJV: feather(-s), ostrich.

H5134 נוּק (nûwq, nook): to suckle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: nurse.

H5135 נוּר (nûwr, noor): fire. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root (corresponding to that of H5216 (נִיר)) meaning to shine; KJV: fiery, fire.

H5136 נוּשׁ (nûwsh, noosh): to be sick, i.e. (figuratively) distressed. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be full of heaviness.

H5137 נָזָה (nâzâh, naw-zaw'): to spirt, i.e. besprinkle (especially in expiation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sprinkle.

H5138 נָזִיד (nâzîyd, naw-zeed'): something boiled, i.e. soup. Origin: from H2102 (זוּד); KJV: pottage.

H5139 נָזִיר (nâzîyr, naw-zeer'): separate, i.e. consecrated (as prince, a Nazirite); hence (figuratively from the latter) an unpruned vine (like an unshorn Nazirite). Origin: or נָזִר; from H5144 (נָזַר); KJV: Nazarite (by a false alliteration with Nazareth), separate(-d), vine undressed.

H5140 נָזַל (nâzal, naw-zal'): to drip, or shed by trickling. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: distil, drop, flood, (cause to) flow(-ing), gush out, melt, pour (down), running water, stream.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5141 to H5263
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5141 נֶזֶם (nezem, neh'-zem): a nose-ring. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: earring, jewel.

H5142 נְזַק (nᵉzaq, nez-ak'): to suffer (causatively, inflict) loss. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of H5143 (נֵזֶק); KJV: have (en-) damage, hurt(-ful).

H5143 נֵזֶק (nêzeq, nay'zek): loss. Origin: from an unused root meaning to injure; KJV: damage.

H5144 נָזַר (nâzar, naw-zar'): to hold aloof, i.e. (intransitivey) abstain (from food and drink, from impurity, and even from divine worship (i.e. apostatize)); specifically, to set apart (to sacred purposes), i.e. devote. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consecrate, separate(-ing, self).

H5145 נֶזֶר (nezer, neh'-zer): properly, something set apart, i.e. (abstractly) dedication (of a priet or Nazirite); hence (concretely) unshorn locks; also (by implication) a chaplet (especially of royalty). Origin: or נֵזֶר; from H5144 (נָזַר); KJV: consecration, crown, hair, separation.

H5146 נֹחַ (Nôach, no'-akh): Noach, the patriarch of the flood. Origin: the same as H5118 (נוּחַ); rest; KJV: Noah.

H5147 נַחְבִּי (Nachbîy, nakh-bee'): Nachbi, an Israelite. Origin: from H2247 (חָבָה); occult; KJV: Nakbi.

H5148 נָחָה (nâchâh, naw-khaw'): to guide; by implication, to transport (into exile, or as colonists). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bestow, bring, govern, guide, lead (forth), put, straiten.

H5149 נְחוּם (Nᵉchûwm, neh-khoom'): Nechum, an Israelite. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); comforted; KJV: Nehum.

H5150 נִחוּם (nichûwm, nee-khoom'): properly, consoled; abstractly, solace. Origin: or נִחֻם; from H5162 (נָחַם); KJV: comfort(-able), repenting.

H5151 נַחוּם (Nachûwm, nakh-oom'): Nachum, an Israelite prophet. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); comfortable; KJV: Nahum.

H5152 נָחוֹר (Nâchôwr, naw-khore'): Nochor, the name of the grandfather and a brother of Abraham. Origin: from the same as H5170 (נַחַר); snorer; KJV: Nahor.

H5153 נָחוּשׁ (nâchûwsh, naw-khoosh'): coppery, i.e. (figuratively) hard. Origin: apparently passive participle of H5172 (נָחַשׁ) (perhaps in the sense of ringing), i.e. bell-metal; or from the red color of the throat of a serpent (H5175 (נָחָשׁ), as denominative) when hissing); KJV: of brass.

H5154 נְחוּשָׁה (nᵉchûwshâh, nekh-oo-shaw'): copper. Origin: or נְחֻשָׁה; feminine of H5153 (נָחוּשׁ); KJV: brass, steel. Compare H5176 (נָחָשׁ).

H5155 נְחִילָה (nᵉchîylâh, nekh-ee-law'): a flute. Origin: probably denominative from H2485 (חָלִיל); KJV: (plural) Nehiloth.

H5156 נְחִיר (nᵉchîyr, nekh-eer'): a nostril. Origin: from the same as H5170 (נַחַר); KJV: (dual) nostrils.

H5157 נָחַל (nâchal, naw-khal'): to inherit (as a (figurative) mode of descent), or (generally) to occupy; causatively, to bequeath, or (generally) distribute, instate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: divide, have (inheritance), take as a heritage, (cause to, give to, make to) inherit, (distribute for, divide (for, for an, by), give for, have, leave for, take (for)) inheritance, (have in, cause to, be made to) possess(-ion).

H5158 נַחַל (nachal, nakh'-al): a stream, especially a winter torrent; (by implication) a (narrow) valley (in which a brook runs); also a shaft (of a mine). Origin: or (feminine) נַחְלָה; (Psalm 124:4), or נַחֲלָה; (Ezekiel 47:19; Ezekiel 48:28), from H5157 (נָחַל) in its original sense; KJV: brook, flood, river, stream, valley.

H5159 נַחֲלָה (nachălâh, nakh-al-aw'): properly, something inherited, i.e. (abstractly) occupancy, or (concretely) an heirloom; generally an estate, patrimony or portion. Origin: from H5157 (נָחַל) (in its usual sense); KJV: heritage, to inherit, inheritance, possession. Compare H5158 (נַחַל).

H5160 נַחֲלִיאֵל (Nachălîyʼêl, nakh-al-ee-ale'): Nachaliel, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H5158 (נַחַל) and H410 (אֵל); valley of God; KJV: Nahaliel.

H5161 נֶחֱלָמִי (Nechĕlâmîy, nekh-el-aw-mee'): a Nechelamite, or descendant of Nechlam. Origin: apparently a patronymic from an unused name (apparently passive participle of H2492 (חָלַם)); dreamed; KJV: Nehelamite.

H5162 נָחַם (nâcham, naw-kham'): properly, to sigh, i.e. breathe strongly; by implication, to be sorry, i.e. (in a favorable sense) to pity, console or (reflexively) rue; or (unfavorably) to avenge (oneself). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: comfort (self), ease (one's self), repent(-er,-ing, self).

H5163 נַחַם (Nacham, nakh'-am): Nacham, an Israelite. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); consolation; KJV: Naham.

H5164 נֹחַם (nôcham, no'-kham): ruefulness, i.e. desistance. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); KJV: repentance.

H5165 נֶחָמָה (nechâmâh, nekh-aw-maw'): consolation. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); KJV: comfort.

H5166 נְחֶמְיָה (Nᵉchemyâh, nekh-em-yaw'): Nechemjah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם) and H3050 (יָהּ); consolation of Jah; KJV: Nehemiah.

H5167 נַחֲמָנִי (Nachămânîy, nakh-am-aw-nee'): Nachamani, an Israelite. Origin: from H5162 (נָחַם); consolatory; KJV: Nahamani.

H5168 נַחְנוּ (nachnûw, nakh-noo'): we. Origin: for H587 (אֲנַחְנוּ); KJV: we.

H5169 נָחַץ (nâchats, naw-khats'): to be urgent. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: require haste.

H5170 נַחַר (nachar, nakh'-ar): a snorting. Origin: and (feminine) נַחֲרָה; from an unused root meaning to snort or snore; KJV: nostrils, snorting.

H5171 נַחֲרַי (Nachăray, nakh-ar-ah'-ee): Nacharai or Nachrai, an Israelite. Origin: or נַחְרַי; from the same as H5170 (נַחַר); snorer; KJV: Naharai, Nahari.

H5172 נָחַשׁ (nâchash, naw-khash'): properly, to hiss, i.e. whisper a (magic) spell; generally, to prognosticate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] certainly, divine, enchanter, (use) [idiom] enchantment, learn by experience, [idiom] indeed, diligently observe.

H5173 נַחַשׁ (nachash, nakh'-ash): an incantation or augury. Origin: from H5172 (נָחַשׁ); KJV: enchantment.

H5174 נְחָשׁ (nᵉchâsh, nekh-awsh'): copper. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5154 (נְחוּשָׁה); KJV: brass.

H5175 נָחָשׁ (nâchâsh, naw-khawsh'): a snake (from its hiss). Origin: from H5172 (נָחַשׁ); KJV: serpent.

H5176 נָחָשׁ (Nâchâsh, naw-khawsh'): Nachash, the name of two persons apparently non-Israelite. Origin: the same as H5175 (נָחָשׁ); KJV: Nahash.

H5177 נַחְשׁוֹן (Nachshôwn, nakh-shone'): Nachshon, an Israelite. Origin: from H5172 (נָחַשׁ); enchanter; KJV: Naashon, Nahshon.

H5178 נְחֹשֶׁת (nᵉchôsheth, nekh-o'-sheth): copper, hence, something made of that metal, i.e. coin, a fetter; figuratively, base (as compared with gold or silver). Origin: for H5154 (נְחוּשָׁה); KJV: brasen, brass, chain, copper, fetter (of brass), filthiness, steel.

H5179 נְחֻשְׁתָּא (Nᵉchushtâʼ, nekh-oosh-taw'): Nechushta, an Israelitess. Origin: from H5178 (נְחֹשֶׁת); copper; KJV: Nehushta.

H5180 נְחֻשְׁתָּן (Nᵉchushtân, nekh-oosh-tawn'): something made of copper, i.e. the copper serpent of the Desert. Origin: from H5178 (נְחֹשֶׁת); KJV: Nehushtan.

H5181 נָחַת (nâchath, naw-khath'): to sink, i.e. descend; causatively, to press or lead down. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be broken, (cause to) come down, enter, go down, press sore, settle, stick fast.

H5182 נְחַת (nᵉchath, nekh-ath'): to descend; causatively, to bring away, deposit, depose. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5181 (נָחַת); KJV: carry, come down, depose, lay up, place.

H5183 נַחַת (Nachath, nakh'-ath): a descent, i.e. imposition, unfavorable (punishment) or favorable (food); restfulness. Origin: from H5182 (נְחַת); also (intransitively; perhaps from H5117 (נוּחַ)) KJV: lighting down, quiet(-ness), to rest, be set on.

H5184 נַחַת (Nachath, nakh'-ath): Nachath, the name of an Edomite and of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H5183 (נַחַת); quiet; KJV: Nahath.

H5185 נָחֵת (nâchêth, naw-khayth'): descending. Origin: from H5181 (נָחַת); KJV: come down.

H5186 נָטָה (nâṭâh, naw-taw'): to stretch or spread out; by implication, to bend away (including moral deflection); used in a great variety of application. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [phrase] afternoon, apply, bow (down, -ing), carry aside, decline, deliver, extend, go down, be gone, incline, intend, lay, let down, offer, outstretched, overthrown, pervert, pitch, prolong, put away, shew, spread (out), stretch (forth, out), take (aside), turn (aside, away), wrest, cause to yield.

H5187 נְטִיל (nᵉṭîyl, net-eel'): laden. Origin: from H5190 (נָטַל); KJV: that bear.

H5188 נְטִיפָה (nᵉṭîyphâh, net-ee-faw'): a pendant for the ears (especially of pearls). Origin: from H5197 (נָטַף); KJV: chain, collar.

H5189 נְטִישָׁה (nᵉṭîyshâh, net-ee-shaw'): a tendril (as an offshoot). Origin: from H5203 (נָטַשׁ); KJV: battlement, branch, plant.

H5190 נָטַל (nâṭal, naw-tal'): to lift; by implication, to impose. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear, offer, take up.

H5191 נְטַל (nᵉṭal, net-al'): to raise. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5190 (נָטַל); KJV: take up.

H5192 נֵטֶל (nêṭel, nay'-tel): a burden. Origin: ; from H5190 (נָטַל); KJV: weighty.

H5193 נָטַע (nâṭaʻ, naw-tah'): properly, to strike in, i.e. fix; specifically, to plant (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fastened, plant(-er).

H5194 נֶטַע (neṭaʻ, neh'-tah): a plant; collectively, a plantation; abstractly, a planting. Origin: from H5193 (נָטַע); KJV: plant.

H5195 נָטִיעַ (nâṭîyaʻ, naw-tee'-ah): a plant. Origin: from H5193 (נָטַע); KJV: plant.

H5196 נְטָעִים (Nᵉṭâʻîym, net-aw-eem'): Netaim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H5194 (נֶטַע); KJV: plants.

H5197 נָטַף (nâṭaph, naw-taf'): to ooze, i.e. distil gradually; by implication, to fall in drops; figuratively, to speak by inspiration. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drop(-ping), prophesy(-et).

H5198 נָטָף (nâṭâph, naw-tawf'): a drop; specifically, an aromatic gum (probably stacte). Origin: from H5197 (נָטַף); KJV: drop, stacte.

H5199 נְטֹפָה (Nᵉṭôphâh, net-o-faw'): Netophah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5197 (נָטַף); distillation; KJV: Netophah.

H5200 נְטֹפָתִי (Nᵉṭôphâthîy, net-o-faw-thee'): a Netophathite, or inhabitant of Netophah. Origin: patronymic from H5199 (נְטֹפָה); KJV: Netophathite.

H5201 נָטַר (nâṭar, naw-tar'): to guard; figuratively, to cherish (anger). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear grudge, keep(-er), reserve.

H5202 נְטַר (nᵉṭar, net-ar'): to retain. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5201 (נָטַר); KJV: keep.

H5203 נָטַשׁ (nâṭash, naw-tash'): properly, to pound, i.e. smite; by implication (as if beating out, and thus expanding) to disperse; also, to thrust off, down, out or upon (inclusively, reject, let alone, permit, remit, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast off, drawn, let fall, forsake, join (battle), leave (off), lie still, loose, spread (self) abroad, stretch out, suffer.

H5204 נִי (nîy, nee): lamentation. Origin: a doubtful word; apparently from H5091 (נָהָה); KJV: wailing.

H5205 נִיד (nîyd, need): motion (of the lips in speech). Origin: from H5110 (נוּד); KJV: moving.

H5206 נִידָה (nîydâh, nee-daw'): removal, i.e. exile. Origin: feminine of H5205 (נִיד); KJV: removed.

H5207 נִיחוֹחַ (nîychôwach, nee-kho'-akh): properly, restful, i.e. pleasant; abstractly, delight. Origin: or נִיחֹחַ; from H5117 (נוּחַ); KJV: sweet (odour).

H5208 נִיחוֹחַ (nîychôwach, nee-kho'-akh): pleasure. Origin: (Aramaic) or נִיחֹחַ; (shorter) (Aramaic), corresponding to H5207 (נִיחוֹחַ); KJV: sweet odour (savour).

H5209 נִין (nîyn, neen): progeny. Origin: from H5125 (נוּן); KJV: son.

H5210 נִינְוֵה (Nîynᵉvêh, nee-nev-ay'): Nineveh, the capital of Assyria. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Nineveh.

H5211 נִיס (nîyç, neece): fugitive. Origin: from H5127 (נוּס); KJV: that fleeth.

H5212 נִיסָן (Nîyçân, nee-sawn'): Nisan, the first month of the Jewish sacred year. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Nisan.

H5213 נִיצוֹץ (nîytsôwts, nee-tsotes'): a spark. Origin: from H5340 (נָצַץ); KJV: spark.

H5214 נִיר (nîyr, neer): to till the soil. Origin: a root probably identical with that of H5216 (נִיר), through the idea of the gleam of a fresh furrow; KJV: break up.

H5215 נִיר (nîyr, neer): properly, plowing, i.e. (concretely) freshly plowed land. Origin: or נִר; from H5214 (נִיר); KJV: fallow ground, plowing, tillage.

H5216 נִיר (nîyr, neer): a lamp (i.e. the burner) or light (literally or figuratively). Origin: or נִר; also נֵיר; or נֵר; or (feminine) נֵרָה; from a primitive root (see H5214 (נִיר); H5135 (נוּר)) properly, meaning to glisten; KJV: candle, lamp, light.

H5217 נָכָא (nâkâʼ, naw-kaw'): to smite, i.e. drive away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be viler.

H5218 נָכֵא (nâkêʼ, naw-kay'): smitten, i.e. (figuratively) afflicted. Origin: or נָכָא; from H5217 (נָכָא); KJV: broken, stricken, wounded.

H5219 נְכֹאת (nᵉkôʼth, nek-ohth'): properly, a smiting, i.e. (concretely) an aromatic gum (perhaps styrax) (as powdered). Origin: from H5218 (נָכֵא); KJV: spicery(-ces).

H5220 נֶכֶד (neked, neh'-ked): offspring. Origin: from an unused root meaning to propagate; KJV: nephew, son's son.

H5221 נָכָה (nâkâh, naw-kaw'): to strike (lightly or severely, literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat, cast forth, clap, give (wounds), [idiom] go forward, [idiom] indeed, kill, make (slaughter), murderer, punish, slaughter, slay(-er, -ing), smite(-r, -ing), strike, be stricken, (give) stripes, [idiom] surely, wound.

H5222 נֵכֶה (nêkeh, nay-keh'): a smiter, i.e. (figuratively) traducer. Origin: from H5221 (נָכָה); KJV: abject.

H5223 נָכֶה (nâkeh, naw-keh'): smitten, i.e. (literally) maimed, or (figuratively) dejected. KJV: contrite, lame.

H5224 נְכוֹ (Nᵉkôw, nek-o'): Neko, an Egyptian king. Origin: probably of Egyptian origin; KJV: Necho. Compare H6549 (פַּרְעֹה נְכֹה).

H5225 נָכוֹן (Nâkôwn, naw-kone'): Nakon, probably an Israelite. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); prepared; KJV: Nachon.

H5226 נֵכַח (nêkach, nay'-kakh): properly, the fore part; used adverbially, opposite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be straightforward; KJV: before, over against.

H5227 נֹכַח (nôkach, no'-kakh): properly, the front part; used adverbially (especially with preposition), opposite, in front of, forward, in behalf of. Origin: from the same as H5226 (נֵכַח); KJV: (over) against, before, direct(-ly), for, right (on).

H5228 נָכֹחַ (nâkôach, naw-ko'-akh): straightforward, i.e. (figuratively), equitable, correct, or (abstractly), integrity. Origin: from the same as H5226 (נֵכַח); KJV: plain, right, uprightness.

H5229 נְכֹחָה (nᵉkôchâh, nek-o-khaw'): properly, straightforwardness, i.e. (figuratively) integrity, or (concretely) a truth. Origin: feminine of H5228 (נָכֹחַ); KJV: equity, right (thing), uprightness.

H5230 נָכַל (nâkal, naw-kal'): to defraud, i.e. act treacherously. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beguile, conspire, deceiver, deal subtilly.

H5231 נֵכֶל (nêkel, nay'-kel): deceit. Origin: from H5230 (נָכַל); KJV: wile.

H5232 נְכַס (nᵉkaç, nek-as'): {treasure}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5233 (נֶכֶס) KJV: goods.

H5233 נֶכֶס (nekeç, neh'-kes): treasure. Origin: from an unused root meaning to accumulate; KJV: riches, wealth.

H5234 נָכַר (nâkar, naw-kar'): properly, to scrutinize, i.e. look intently at; hence (with recognition implied), to acknowledge, be acquainted with, care for, respect, revere, or (with suspicion implied), to disregard, ignore, be strange toward, reject, resign, dissimulate (as if ignorant or disowning). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: acknowledge, [idiom] could, deliver, discern, dissemble, estrange, feign self to be another, know, take knowledge (notice), perceive, regard, (have) respect, behave (make) self strange(-ly).

H5235 נֶכֶר (neker, neh'-ker): something strange, i.e. unexpected calamity. Origin: or נֹכֶר; from H5234 (נָכַר); KJV: strange.

H5236 נֵכָר (nêkâr, nay-kawr'): foreign, or (concretely) a foreigner, or (abstractly) heathendom. Origin: ' from H5234 (נָכַר); KJV: alien, strange ([phrase] -er).

H5237 נׇכְרִי (nokrîy, nok-ree'): strange, in a variety of degrees and applications (foreign, non-relative, adulterous, different, wonderful). Origin: from H5235 (נֶכֶר) (second form); KJV: alien, foreigner, outlandish, strange(-r, woman).

H5238 נְכֹת (nᵉkôth, nek-oth'): spicery, i.e. (generally) valuables. Origin: probably for H5219 (נְכֹאת); KJV: precious things.

H5239 נָלָה (nâlâh, naw-law'): to complete. Origin: apparently a primitive root; KJV: make an end.

H5240 נְמִבְזֶה (nᵉmibzeh, nem-ib-zeh'): despised. Origin: from H959 (בָּזָה), KJV: vile.

H5241 נְמוּאֵל (Nᵉmûwʼêl, nem-oo-ale'): Nemuel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: apparently for H3223 (יְמוּאֵל); KJV: Nemuel.

H5242 נְמוּאֵלִי (Nᵉmûwʼêlîy, nem-oo-ay-lee'): a Nemuelite, or descendant of Nemuel. Origin: from H5241 (נְמוּאֵל); KJV: Nemuelite.

H5243 נָמַל (nâmal, naw-mal'): to become clipped or (specifically) circumcised. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (branch to) be cut down (off), circumcise.

H5244 נְמָלָה (nᵉmâlâh, nem-aw-law'): an ant (probably from its almost bisected form). Origin: feminine from H5243 (נָמַל); KJV: ant.

H5245 נְמַר (nᵉmar, nem-ar'): {a leopard (from its stripes)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5246 (נָמֵר) KJV: leopard.

H5246 נָמֵר (nâmêr, naw-mare'): a leopard (from its stripes). Origin: from an unused root meaning properly, to filtrate, i.e. be limpid (comp H5247 (נִמְרָה) and H5249 (נִמְרִים)); and thus to spot or stain as if by dripping; KJV: leopard.

H5247 נִמְרָה (Nimrâh, nim-raw'): Nimrah, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from the same as H5246 (נָמֵר); clear water; KJV: Nimrah. See also H1039 (בֵּית נִמְרָה), H5249 (נִמְרִים).

H5248 נִמְרוֹד (Nimrôwd, nim-rode'): Nimrod, a son of Cush. Origin: or נִמְרֹד; probably of foreign origin; KJV: Nimrod.

H5249 נִמְרִים (Nimrîym, nim-reem'): Nimrim, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: plural of a masculine corresponding to H5247 (נִמְרָה); clear waters; KJV: Nimrim. Compare H1039 (בֵּית נִמְרָה).

H5250 נִמְשִׁי (Nimshîy, nim-shee'): Nimshi, the (grand-) father of Jehu. Origin: probably from H4871 (מָשָׁה); extricated; KJV: Nimshi.

H5251 נֵס (nêç, nace): a flag; also a sail; by implication, a flagstaff; generally a signal; figuratively, a token. Origin: from H5264 (נָסַס); KJV: banner, pole, sail, (en-) sign, standard.

H5252 נְסִבָּה (nᵉçibbâh, nes-ib-baw'): properly, an environment, i.e. circumstance or turn of affairs. Origin: feminine participle passive of H5437 (סָבַב); KJV: cause.

H5253 נָסַג (nâçag, naw-sag'): to retreat. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: departing away, remove, take (hold), turn away.

H5254 נָסָה (nâçâh, naw-saw'): to test; by implication, to attempt. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: adventure, assay, prove, tempt, try.

H5255 נָסַח (nâçach, naw-sakh'): to tear away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destroy, pluck, root.

H5256 נְסַח (nᵉçach, nes-akh'): {to tear away}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5255 (נָסַח) KJV: pull down.

H5257 נְסִיךְ (nᵉçîyk, nes-eek'): properly, something poured out, i.e. a libation; also a molten image; by implication, a prince (as anointed). Origin: from H5258 (נָסַךְ); KJV: drink offering, duke, prince(-ipal).

H5258 נָסַךְ (nâçak, naw-sak'): to pour out, especially a libation, or to cast (metal); by analogy, to anoint aking. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover, melt, offer, (cause to) pour (out), set (up).

H5259 נָסַךְ (nâçak, naw-sak'): to interweave, i.e. (figuratively) to overspread. Origin: a primitive root (probably identical with H5258 (נָסַךְ) through the idea of fusion); KJV: that is spread.

H5260 נְסַךְ (nᵉçak, nes-ak'): to pour out a libation. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5258 (נָסַךְ); KJV: offer.

H5261 נְסַךְ (nᵉçak, nes-ak'): a libation. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5262 (נֶסֶךְ); KJV: drink offering.

H5262 נֶסֶךְ (neçek, neh'-sek): a libation; also a cast idol. Origin: or נֵסֶךְ; from H5258 (נָסַךְ); KJV: cover, drink offering, molten image.

H5263 נָסַס (nâçaç, naw-sas'): to wane, i.e. be sick. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: faint.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5264 to H5380
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5264 נָסַס (nâçaç, naw-sas'): to raise a beacon. Origin: a primitive root; to gleam from afar, i.e. to be conspicuous as a signal; or rather perhaps a denominative from H5251 (נֵס) (and identical with H5263 (נָסַס), through the idea of a flag as fluttering in the wind); KJV: lift up as an ensign.

H5265 נָסַע (nâçaʻ, naw-sah'): properly, to pull up, especially the tent-pins, i.e. start on ajourney. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cause to blow, bring, get, (make to) go (away, forth, forward, onward, out), (take) journey, march, remove, set aside (forward), [idiom] still, be on his (go their) way.

H5266 נָסַק (nâçaq, naw-sak'): to go up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: ascend.

H5267 נְסַק (nᵉçaq, nes-ak'): {to go up}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5266 (נָסַק) KJV: take up.

H5268 נִסְרֹךְ (Niçrôk, nis-roke'): Nisrok, a Babylonian idol. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Nisroch.

H5269 נֵעָה (Nêʻâh, nay-aw'): Neah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5128 (נוּעַ); motion; KJV: Neah.

H5270 נֹעָה (Nôʻâh, no-aw'): Noah, an Israelitess. Origin: from H5128 (נוּעַ); movement; KJV: Noah.

H5271 נָעוּר (nâʻûwr, naw-oor'): (only in plural collectively or emphatic form) youth, the state (juvenility) or the persons (young people). Origin: or נָעֻר; and (feminine) נְעֻרָה; properly, passive participle from H5288 (נַעַר) as denominative; KJV: childhood, youth.

H5272 נְעִיאֵל (Nᵉʻîyʼêl, neh-ee-ale'): Neiel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5128 (נוּעַ) and H410 (אֵל); moved of God; KJV: Neiel.

H5273 נָעִים (nâʻîym, naw-eem'): delightful (objective or subjective, literal or figurative). Origin: from H5276 (נָעֵם); KJV: pleasant(-ure), sweet.

H5274 נָעַל (nâʻal, naw-al'): properly, to fasten up, i.e. with abar or cord; hence, to sandal, i.e. furnish with slippers. Origin: a primitive root; also denominative from H5275 (נַעַל) KJV: bolt, inclose, lock, shoe, shut up.

H5275 נַעַל (naʻal, nah'-al): properly, a sandal tongue; by extension a sandal or slipper (sometimes as a symbol of occupancy, a refusal to marry, or of something valueless). Origin: or (feminine) נַעֲלָה; from H5274 (נָעַל); KJV: dryshod, (pair of) shoe((-latchet), -s).

H5276 נָעֵם (nâʻêm, naw-ame'): to be agreeable (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pass in beauty, be delight, be pleasant, be sweet.

H5277 נַעַם (Naʻam, nah'-am): Naam, an Israelite. Origin: from H5276 (נָעֵם); pleasure; KJV: Naam.

H5278 נֹעַם (nôʻam, no'-am): agreeableness, i.e. delight, suitableness, splendor or grace. Origin: from H5276 (נָעֵם); KJV: beauty, pleasant(-ness).

H5279 נַעֲמָה (Naʻămâh, nah-am-aw'): Naamah, the name of an antediluvian woman, of an Ammonitess, and of a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H5277 (נַעַם); pleasantness; KJV: Naamah.

H5280 נַעֲמִי (Naʻămîy, nah-am-ee'): a Naamanite, or descendant of Naaman (collectively). Origin: patronymic from H5283 (נַעֲמָן); KJV: Naamites.

H5281 נׇעֳמִי (Noʻŏmîy, no-om-ee'): Noomi, an Israelitess. Origin: from H5278 (נֹעַם); pleasant; KJV: Naomi.

H5282 נַעֲמָן (naʻămân, nah-am-awn'): pleasantness (plural as concrete). Origin: from H5276 (נָעֵם); KJV: pleasant.

H5283 נַעֲמָן (Naʻămân, nah-am-awn'): Naaman, the name of an Israelite and of a Damascene. Origin: the same as H5282 (נַעֲמָן); KJV: Naaman.

H5284 נַעֲמָתִי (Naʻămâthîy, nah-am-aw-thee'): a Naamathite, or inhabitant of Naamah. Origin: patrial from a place corresponding in name (but not identical) with H5279 (נַעֲמָה); KJV: Naamathite.

H5285 נַעֲצוּץ (naʻătsûwts, nah-ats-oots'): probably a brier; by implication, a thicket of thorny bushes. Origin: from an unused root meaning to prick; KJV: thorn.

H5286 נָעַר (nâʻar, naw-ar'): to growl. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: yell.

H5287 נָעַר (nâʻar, naw-ar'): to tumble about. Origin: a primitive root (probably identical with H5286 (נָעַר), through the idea of the rustling of mane, which usually accompanies the lion's roar); KJV: shake (off, out, self), overthrow, toss up and down.

H5288 נַעַר (naʻar, nah'-ar): (concretely) a boy (as active), from the age of infancy to adolescence; by implication, a servant; also (by interch. of sex), a girl (of similar latitude in age). Origin: from H5287 (נָעַר); KJV: babe, boy, child, damsel (from the margin), lad, servant, young (man).

H5289 נַעַר (naʻar, nah'-ar): a wanderer. Origin: from H5287 (נָעַר) in its derivative sense of tossing about; KJV: young one.

H5290 נֹעַר (nôʻar, no'-ar): (abstractly) boyhood. Origin: from H5287 (נָעַר); (compare H5288 (נַעַר)) KJV: child, youth.

H5291 נַעֲרָה (naʻărâh, nah-ar-aw'): a girl (from infancy to adolescence). Origin: feminine of H5288 (נַעַר); KJV: damsel, maid(-en), young (woman).

H5292 נַעֲרָה (Naʻărâh, nah-ar-aw'): Naarah, the name of an Israelitess, and of a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5291 (נַעֲרָה); KJV: Naarah, Naarath.

H5293 נַעֲרַי (Naʻăray, nah-ar-ah'-ee): Naarai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5288 (נַעַר); youthful; KJV: Naarai.

H5294 נְעַרְיָה (Nᵉʻaryâh, neh-ar-yaw'): Nearjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5288 (נַעַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); servant of Jah; KJV: Neariah.

H5295 נַעֲרָן (Naʻărân, nah-ar-awn'): Naaran, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5288 (נַעַר); juvenile; KJV: Naaran.

H5296 נְעֹרֶת (nᵉʻôreth, neh-o'-reth): something shaken out, i.e. tow (as the refuse of flax). Origin: from H5287 (נָעַר); KJV: tow.

H5297 נֹף (Nôph, nofe): Noph, the capital of Upper Egypt. Origin: a variation of H4644 (מֹף); KJV: Noph.

H5298 נֶפֶג (Nepheg, neh'-feg): Nepheg, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to spring forth; a sprout; KJV: Nepheg.

H5299 נָפָה (nâphâh, naw-faw'): a height; also a sieve. Origin: from H5130 (נוּף) in the sense of lifting; KJV: border, coast, region, sieve.

H5300 נְפוּשְׁסִים (Nᵉphûwshᵉçîym, nef-oo-shes-eem'): Nephushesim, a Temple-servant. Origin: for H5304 (נְפִיסִים); KJV: Nephisesim (from the margin).

H5301 נָפַח (nâphach, naw-fakh'): to puff, in various applications (literally, to inflate, blow hard, scatter, kindle, expire; figuratively, to disesteem). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: blow, breath, give up, cause to lose (life), seething, snuff.

H5302 נֹפַח (Nôphach, no'-fakh): Nophach, a place in Moab. Origin: from H5301 (נָפַח); a gust; KJV: Nophah.

H5303 נְפִיל (nᵉphîyl, nef-eel'): properly, a feller, i.e. a bully or tyrant. Origin: or נְפִל; from H5307 (נָפַל); KJV: giant.

H5304 נְפִיסִים (Nᵉphîyçîym, nef-ee-seem'): Nephisim, a Temple-servant. Origin: plural from an unused root meaning to scatter; expansions; KJV: Nephusim (from the margin).

H5305 נָפִישׁ (Nâphîysh, naw-feesh'): Naphish, a son of Ishmael, and his posterity. Origin: from H5314 (נָפַשׁ); refreshed; KJV: Naphish.

H5306 נֹפֶךְ (nôphek, no'-fek): shining; a gem, probably the garnet. Origin: from an unused root meaning to glisten; KJV: emerald.

H5307 נָפַל (nâphal, naw-fal'): to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative).
