Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be accepted, cast (down, self, (lots), out), cease, die, divide (by lot), (let) fail, (cause to, let, make, ready to) fall (away, down, -en, -ing), fell(-ing), fugitive, have (inheritance), inferior, be judged (by mistake for H6419 (פָּלַל)), lay (along), (cause to) lie down, light (down), be ([idiom] hast) lost, lying, overthrow, overwhelm, perish, present(-ed, -ing), (make to) rot, slay, smite out, [idiom] surely, throw down.

H5308 נְפַל (nᵉphal, nef-al'): {to fall, in a great variety of applications (intransitive or causative, literal or figurative)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5307 (נָפַל) KJV: fall (down), have occasion.

H5309 נֶפֶל (nephel, neh'-fel): something fallen, i.e. an abortion. Origin: or נֵפֶל; from H5307 (נָפַל); KJV: untimely birth.

H5310 נָפַץ (nâphats, naw-fats'): to dash to pieces, or scatter. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be beaten in sunder, break (in pieces), broken, dash (in pieces), cause to be discharged, dispersed, be overspread, scatter.

H5311 נֶפֶץ (nephets, neh'-fets): a storm (as dispersing). Origin: from H5310 (נָפַץ); KJV: scattering.

H5312 נְפַק (nᵉphaq, nef-ak'): to issue; causatively, to bring out. Origin: (Aramaic) a primitive root; KJV: come (go, take) forth (out).

H5313 נִפְקָא (niphqâʼ, nif-kaw'): an outgo, i.e. expense. Origin: (Aramaic) from H5312 (נְפַק); KJV: expense.

H5314 נָפַשׁ (nâphash, naw-fash'): to breathe; passively, to be breathed upon , i.e. (figuratively) refreshed (as if by a current of air). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) refresh selves (-ed).

H5315 נֶפֶשׁ (nephesh, neh'-fesh): properly, a breathing creature, i.e. animal of (abstractly) vitality; used very widely in a literal, accommodated or figurative sense (bodily or mental). Origin: from H5314 (נָפַשׁ); KJV: any, appetite, beast, body, breath, creature, [idiom] dead(-ly), desire, [idiom] (dis-) contented, [idiom] fish, ghost, [phrase] greedy, he, heart(-y), (hath, [idiom] jeopardy of) life ([idiom] in jeopardy), lust, man, me, mind, mortally, one, own, person, pleasure, (her-, him-, my-, thy-) self, them (your) -selves, [phrase] slay, soul, [phrase] tablet, they, thing, ([idiom] she) will, [idiom] would have it.

H5316 נֶפֶת (nepheth, neh'-feth): a height. Origin: for H5299 (נָפָה); KJV: country.

H5317 נֹפֶת (nôpheth, no'-feth): a dripping i.e. of honey (from the comb). Origin: from H5130 (נוּף) in the sense of shaking to pieces; KJV: honeycomb.

H5318 נֶפְתּוֹחַ (Nephtôwach, nef-to'-akh): Nephtoach, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6605 (פָּתַח); opened, i.e. a spring; KJV: Neptoah.

H5319 נַפְתּוּל (naphtûwl, naf-tool'): properly, wrestled; but used (in the plural) transitively, a struggle. Origin: from H6617 (פָּתַל); KJV: wrestling.

H5320 נַפְתֻּחִים (Naphtuchîym, naf-too-kheem): Naphtuchim, an Egyptian tribe. Origin: plural of foreign origin, KJV: Naptuhim.

H5321 נַפְתָּלִי (Naphtâlîy, naf-taw-lee'): Naphtali, a son of Jacob, with the tribe descended from him, and its territory. Origin: from H6617 (פָּתַל); my wrestling; KJV: Naphtali.

H5322 נֵץ (nêts, nayts): a flower (from its brilliancy); also a hawk (from it flashing speed). Origin: from H5340 (נָצַץ); KJV: blossom, hawk.

H5323 נָצָא (nâtsâʼ, naw-tsaw'): to go away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: flee.

H5324 נָצַב (nâtsab, naw-tsab'): to station, in various applications (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appointed, deputy, erect, establish, [idiom] Huzzah (by mistake for a proper name), lay, officer, pillar, present, rear up, set (over, up), settle, sharpen, establish, (make to) stand(-ing, still, up, upright), best state.

H5325 נִצָּב (nitstsâb, nits-twawb'): fixed, i.e. a handle. Origin: passive participle of H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: haft.

H5326 נִצְבָּה (nitsbâh, nits-baw'): fixedness, i.e. firmness. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: strength.

H5327 נָצָה (nâtsâh, naw-tsaw'): properly, to go forth, i.e. (by implication) to be expelled, and (consequently) desolate; causatively, to lay waste; also (specifically), to quarrel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be laid waste, runinous, strive (together).

H5328 נִצָּה (nitstsâh, nits-tsaw'): a blossom. Origin: feminine of H5322 (נֵץ); KJV: flower.

H5329 נָצַח (nâtsach, naw-tsakh'): properly, to glitter from afar, i.e. to be eminent (as a superintendent, especially of the Temple services and its music); to be permanent. Origin: a primitive root; also as denominative from H5331 (נֶצַח) KJV: excel, chief musician (singer), oversee(-r), set forward.

H5330 נְצַח (nᵉtsach, nets-akh'): to become chief. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5329 (נָצַח); KJV: be preferred.

H5331 נֶצַח (netsach, neh'-tsakh): properly, a goal, i.e. the bright object at adistance travelled towards; hence (figuratively), splendor, or (subjectively) truthfulness, or (objectively) confidence; but usually (adverbially), continually (i.e. to the most distant point of view). Origin: or נֵצַח; from H5329 (נָצַח); KJV: alway(-s), constantly, end, ([phrase] n-) ever(more), perpetual, strength, victory.

H5332 נֵצַח (Nêtsach, nay'-tsakh): juice of the grape (as blood red). Origin: probably identical with H5331 (נֶצַח), through the idea of brilliancy of color; KJV: blood, strength.

H5333 נְצִיב (nᵉtsîyb, nets-eeb'): something stationary, i.e. a prefect, a military post, a statue. Origin: or נְצִב; from H5324 (נָצַב); KJV: garrison, officer, pillar.

H5334 נְצִיב (Nᵉtsîyb, nets-eeb'): Netsib, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5333 (נְצִיב); station; KJV: Nezib.

H5335 נְצִיחַ (nᵉtsîyach, nets-ee'-akh): Netsiach, a Temple-servant. Origin: from H5329 (נָצַח); conspicuous; KJV: Neziah.

H5336 נָצִיר (nâtsîyr, naw-tsere'): properly, conservative; but used passively, delivered. Origin: from H5341 (נָצַר); KJV: preserved.

H5337 נָצַל (nâtsal, naw-tsal'): to snatch away, whether in a good or a bad sense. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, defend, deliver (self), escape, [idiom] without fail, part, pluck, preserve, recover, rescue, rid, save, spoil, strip, [idiom] surely, take (out).

H5338 נְצַל (nᵉtsal, nets-al'): to extricate. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5337 (נָצַל); KJV: deliver, rescue.

H5339 נִצָּן (nitstsân, nits-tsawn'): a blossom. Origin: from H5322 (נֵץ); KJV: flower.

H5340 נָצַץ (nâtsats, naw-tsats'): to glare, i.e. be bright-colored. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sparkle.

H5341 נָצַר (nâtsar, naw-tsar'): to guard, in a good sense (to protect, maintain, obey, etc.) or a bad one (to conceal, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: besieged, hidden thing, keep(-er, -ing), monument, observe, preserve(-r), subtil, watcher(-man).

H5342 נֵצֶר (nêtser, nay'-tser): a shoot; figuratively, a descendant. Origin: from H5341 (נָצַר) in the sense of greenness as a striking color; KJV: branch.

H5343 נְקֵא (nᵉqêʼ, nek-ay'): clean. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5352 (נָקָה); KJV: pure.

H5344 נָקַב (nâqab, naw-kab'): to puncture, literally (to perforate, with more or less violence) or figuratively (to specify, designate, libel). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, blaspheme, bore, curse, express, with holes, name, pierce, strike through.

H5345 נֶקֶב (neqeb, neh'keb): a bezel (for a gem). KJV: pipe.

H5346 נֶקֶב (Neqeb, neh'-keb): Nekeb, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5345 (נֶקֶב); dell; KJV: Nekeb.

H5347 נְקֵבָה (nᵉqêbâh, nek-ay-baw'): female (from the sexual form). Origin: from H5344 (נָקַב); KJV: female.

H5348 נָקֹד (nâqôd, naw-kode'): spotted. Origin: from an unused root meaning to mark (by puncturing or branding); KJV: speckled.

H5349 נֹקֵד (nôqêd, no-kade'): a spotter (of sheep or cattle), i.e. the owner or tender (who thus marks them). Origin: active participle from the same as H5348 (נָקֹד); KJV: herdman, sheepmaster.

H5350 נִקֻּד (niqqud, nik-kood'): a crumb (as broken to spots); also a biscuit (as pricked). Origin: from the same as H5348 (נָקֹד); KJV: cracknel, mouldy.

H5351 נְקֻדָּה (nᵉquddâh, ned-ood-daw'): a boss. Origin: feminine of H5348 (נָקֹד); KJV: stud.

H5352 נָקָה (nâqâh, naw-kaw'): to be (or make) clean (literally or figuratively); by implication (in an adverse sense) to be bare, i.e. extirpated. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: acquit [idiom] at all, [idiom] altogether, be blameless, cleanse, (be) clear(-ing), cut off, be desolate, be free, be (hold) guiltless, be (hold) innocent, [idiom] by no means, be quit, be (leave) unpunished, [idiom] utterly, [idiom] wholly.

H5353 נְקוֹדָא (Nᵉqôwdâʼ, nek-o-daw'): Nekoda, a Temple-servant. Origin: feminine of H5348 (נָקֹד) (in the figurative sense of marked); distinction; KJV: Nekoda.

H5354 נָקַט (nâqaṭ, naw-kat'): to loathe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: weary.

H5355 נָקִי (nâqîy, naw-kee'): innocent. Origin: or נָקִיא; (Joel 4:19; Jonah [1:14), from H5352 (נָקָה); KJV: blameless, clean, clear, exempted, free, guiltless, innocent, quit.

H5356 נִקָּיוֹן (niqqâyôwn, nik-kaw-yone'): clearness (literally or figuratively). Origin: or נִקָּיֹן; from H5352 (נָקָה); KJV: cleanness, innocency.

H5357 נָקִיק (nâqîyq, naw-keek'): a cleft. Origin: from an unused root meaning to bore; KJV: hole.

H5358 נָקַם (nâqam, naw-kam'): to grudge, i.e. avenge or punish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: avenge(-r, self), punish, revenge (self), [idiom] surely, take vengeance.

H5359 נָקָם (nâqâm, naw-kawm'): revenge. Origin: from H5358 (נָקַם); KJV: [phrase] avenged, quarrel, vengeance.

H5360 נְקָמָה (nᵉqâmâh, nek-aw-maw'): avengement, whether the act of the passion. Origin: feminine of H5359 (נָקָם); KJV: [phrase] avenge, revenge(-ing), vengeance.

H5361 נָקַע (nâqaʻ, naw-kah'): to feel aversion. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be alienated.

H5362 נָקַף (nâqaph, naw-kaf'): to strike with more or less violence (beat, fell, corrode); by implication (of attack) to knock together, i.e. surround or circulate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: compass (about, -ing), cut down, destroy, go round (about), inclose, round.

H5363 נֹקֶף (nôqeph, no'-kef): a threshing (of olives). Origin: from H5362 (נָקַף); KJV: shaking.

H5364 נִקְפָּה (niqpâh, nik-paw'): probably a rope (as encircling). Origin: from H5362 (נָקַף); KJV: rent.

H5365 נָקַר (nâqar, naw-kar'): to bore (penetrate, quarry). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dig, pick out, pierce, put (thrust) out.

H5366 נְקָרָה (nᵉqârâh, nek-aw-raw'): {to bore (penetrate, quarry)}. Origin: from H5365 (נָקַר), a fissure KJV: cleft, clift.

H5367 נָקַשׁ (nâqash, naw-kash'): to entrap (with a noose), literally or figuratively. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: catch (lay a) snare.

H5368 נְקַשׁ (nᵉqash, nek-ash'): to knock. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5367 (נָקַשׁ); used in the sense of H5362 (נָקַף); KJV: smote.

H5369 נֵר (Nêr, nare): Ner, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H5216 (נִיר); lamp; KJV: Ner.

H5370 נֵרְגַּל (Nêrᵉgal, nare-gal'): Nergal, a Cuthite deity. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Nergal.

H5371 נֵרְגַּל שַׁרְאֶצֶר (Nêrᵉgal Sharʼetser, nare-gal' shar-eh'-tser): Nergal-Sharetser, the name of two Babylonians. Origin: from H5370 (נֵרְגַּל) and H8272 (שַׁרְאֶצֶר); KJV: Nergal-sharezer.

H5372 נִרְגָּן (nirgân, neer-gawn'): a slanderer. Origin: from an unused root meaning to roll to pieces; KJV: talebearer, whisperer.

H5373 נֵרְדְּ (nêrd, nayrd): nard, an aromatic. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: spikenard.

H5374 נֵרִיָּה (Nêrîyâh, nay-ree-yaw'): Nerijah, an Israelite. Origin: or נֵרִיָּהוּ; from H5216 (נִיר) and H3050 (יָהּ); light of Jah; KJV: Neriah.

H5375 נָשָׂא (nâsâʼ, naw-saw'): to lift, in a great variety of applications, literal and figurative, absolute and relative. Origin: or נָסָה; (Psalm 4:6 (H7 (אֲבַד))), a primitive root; KJV: accept, advance, arise, (able to, (armor), suffer to) bear(-er, up), bring (forth), burn, carry (away), cast, contain, desire, ease, exact, exalt (self), extol, fetch, forgive, furnish, further, give, go on, help, high, hold up, honorable ([phrase] man), lade, lay, lift (self) up, lofty, marry, magnify, [idiom] needs, obtain, pardon, raise (up), receive, regard, respect, set (up), spare, stir up, [phrase] swear, take (away, up), [idiom] utterly, wear, yield.

H5376 נְשָׂא (nᵉsâʼ, nes-aw'): {to lift}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5375 (נָשָׂא) KJV: carry away, make insurrection, take.

H5377 נָשָׁא (nâshâʼ, naw-shaw'): to lead astray, i.e. (mentally) to delude, or (morally) to seduce. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beguile, deceive, [idiom] greatly, [idiom] utterly.

H5378 נָשָׁא (nâshâʼ, naw-shaw'): to lend on interest; by implication, to dun fordebt. Origin: a primitive root (perhaps identical with H5377 (נָשָׁא), through the idea of imposition); KJV: [idiom] debt, exact, giver of usury.

H5379 נִשֵּׂאת (nissêʼth, nis-sayth'): something taken, i.e. a present. Origin: passive participle feminine of H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: gift.

H5380 נָשַׁב (nâshab, naw-shab'): to blow; by implication, to disperse. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) blow, drive away.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5381 to H5510
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5381 נָשַׂג (nâsag, naw-sag'): to reach (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: ability, be able, attain (unto), (be able to, can) get, lay at, put, reach, remove, wax rich, [idiom] surely, (over-) take (hold of, on, upon).

H5382 נָשָׁה (nâshâh, naw-shaw'): to forget; figuratively, to neglect; causatively, to remit, remove. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: forget, deprive, exact.

H5383 נָשָׁה (nâshâh, naw-shaw'): to lend or (by reciprocity) borrow on security or interest. Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H5382 (נָשָׁה), in the sense of H5378 (נָשָׁא)); KJV: creditor, exact, extortioner, lend, usurer, lend on (taker on) usury.

H5384 נָשֶׁה (nâsheh, naw-sheh'): rheumatic or crippled (from the incident to Jacob). Origin: from H5382 (נָשָׁה), in the sense of failure; KJV: which shrank.

H5385 נְשׂוּאָה (nᵉsûwʼâh, nes-oo-aw'): something borne, i.e. a load. Origin: or rather, נְשֻׂאָה; feminine. passive participle of H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: carriage.

H5386 נְשִׁי (nᵉshîy, nesh-ee'): a debt. Origin: from H5383 (נָשָׁה); KJV: debt.

H5387 נָשִׂיא (nâsîyʼ, naw-see'): properly, an exalted one, i.e. a king or sheik; also a rising mist. Origin: or נָשִׂא; from H5375 (נָשָׂא); KJV: captain, chief, cloud, governor, prince, ruler, vapour.

H5388 נְשִׁיָּה (nᵉshîyâh, nesh-ee-yaw'): oblivion. Origin: from H5382 (נָשָׁה); KJV: forgetfulness.

H5389 נָשִׁין (nâshîyn, naw-sheen'): {a man}. Origin: (Aramaic) irregular plural feminine of H606 (אֱנָשׁ) KJV: women.

H5390 נְשִׁיקָה (nᵉshîyqâh, nesh-ee-kaw'): a kiss. Origin: from H5401 (נָשַׁק); KJV: kiss.

H5391 נָשַׁךְ (nâshak, naw-shak'): to strike with a sting (as a serpent); figuratively, to oppress with interest on a loan. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bite, lend upon usury.

H5392 נֶשֶׁךְ (neshek, neh'-shek): interest on a debt. Origin: from H5391 (נָשַׁךְ); KJV: usury.

H5393 נִשְׁכָּה (nishkâh, nish-kaw'): a cell. Origin: for H3957 (לִשְׁכָּה); KJV: chamber.

H5394 נָשַׁל (nâshal, naw-shal'): to pluck off, i.e. divest, eject or drop. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast (out), drive, loose, put off (out), slip.

H5395 נָשַׁם (nâsham, naw-sham'): properly, to blow away, i.e. destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destroy.

H5396 נִשְׁמָא (nishmâʼ, nish-maw'): vital breath. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5397 (נְשָׁמָה); KJV: breath.

H5397 נְשָׁמָה (nᵉshâmâh, nesh-aw-maw'): a puff, i.e. wind, angry or vital breath, divine inspiration, intellect. or (concretely) an animal. Origin: from H5395 (נָשַׁם); KJV: blast, (that) breath(-eth), inspiration, soul, spirit.

H5398 נָשַׁף (nâshaph, naw-shaf'): to breeze, i.e. blow up fresh (as the wind). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: blow.

H5399 נֶשֶׁף (nesheph, neh'-shef): properly, a breeze, i.e. (by implication) dusk (when the evening breeze prevails). Origin: from H5398 (נָשַׁף); KJV: dark, dawning of the day (morning), night, twilight.

H5400 נָשַׂק (nâsaq, naw-sak'): to catch fire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn, kindle.

H5401 נָשַׁק (nâshaq, naw-shak'): to kiss, literally or figuratively (touch); also (as a mode of attachment), to equip with weapons. Origin: a primitive root (identical with H5400 (נָשַׂק), through the idea of fastening up; compare H2388 (חָזַק), H2836 (חָשַׁק)); KJV: armed (men), rule, kiss, that touched.

H5402 נֶשֶׁק (nesheq, neh'-shek): military equipment, i.e. (collectively) arms (offensive or defensive), or (concretely) an arsenal. Origin: or נֵשֶׁק; from H5401 (נָשַׁק); KJV: armed men, armour(-y), battle, harness, weapon.

H5403 נְשַׁר (nᵉshar, nesh-ar'): an eagle. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5404 (נֶשֶׁר); KJV: eagle.

H5404 נֶשֶׁר (nesher, neh'-sher): the eagle (or other large bird of prey). Origin: from an unused root meaning to lacerate; KJV: eagle.

H5405 נָשַׁת (nâshath, naw-shath'): properly, to eliminate, i.e. (intransitively) to dry up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fail.

H5406 נִשְׁתְּוָן (nishtᵉvân, nish-tev-awn'): an epistle. Origin: probably of Persian origin; KJV: letter.

H5407 נִשְׁתְּוָן (nishtᵉvân, nish-tev-awn'): {an epistle}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5406 (נִשְׁתְּוָן) KJV: letter.

H5408 נָתַח (nâthach, naw-thakh'): to dismember. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut (in pieces), divide, hew in pieces.

H5409 נֵתַח (nêthach, nay'-thakh): a fragment. Origin: from H5408 (נָתַח); KJV: part, piece.

H5410 נָתִיב (nâthîyb, naw-theeb'): a (beaten) track. Origin: or (feminine) נְתִיבָה; or נְתִבָה; (Jeremiah 6:16), from an unused root meaning to tramp; KJV: path(-way), [idiom] travel(-ler), way.

H5411 נָתִין (Nâthîyn, naw-theen'): the Nethinim, or Temple-servants (as given to that duty). Origin: or נָתוּן (Ezra 8:17), (the proper form as passive participle), from H5414 (נָתַן); one given, i.e. (in the plural only) KJV: Nethinims.

H5412 נְתִין (Nᵉthîyn, netheen'): {the Nethinim, or Temple-servants (as given to that duty)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5411 (נָתִין) KJV: Nethinims.

H5413 נָתַךְ (nâthak, naw-thak'): to flow forth (literally or figuratively); by implication, to liquify. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drop, gather (together), melt, pour (forth, out).

H5414 נָתַן (nâthan, naw-than'): to give, used with greatest latitude of application (put, make, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: add, apply, appoint, ascribe, assign, [idiom] avenge, [idiom] be (healed), bestow, bring (forth, hither), cast, cause, charge, come, commit, consider, count, [phrase] cry, deliver (up), direct, distribute, do, [idiom] doubtless, [idiom] without fail, fasten, frame, [idiom] get, give (forth, over, up), grant, hang (up), [idiom] have, [idiom] indeed, lay (unto charge, up), (give) leave, lend, let (out), [phrase] lie, lift up, make, [phrase] O that, occupy, offer, ordain, pay, perform, place, pour, print, [idiom] pull, put (forth), recompense, render, requite, restore, send (out), set (forth), shew, shoot forth (up), [phrase] sing, [phrase] slander, strike, (sub-) mit, suffer, [idiom] surely, [idiom] take, thrust, trade, turn, utter, [phrase] weep, [phrase] willingly, [phrase] withdraw, [phrase] would (to) God, yield.

H5415 נְתַן (nᵉthan, neth-an'): give. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5414 (נָתַן); KJV: bestow, give pay.

H5416 נָתָן (Nâthân, naw-thawn'): Nathan, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H5414 (נָתַן); given; KJV: Nathan.

H5417 נְתַנְאֵל (Nᵉthanʼêl, neth-an-ale'): Nethanel, the name of ten Israelites. Origin: from H5414 (נָתַן) and H410 (אֵל); given of God; KJV: Nethaneel.

H5418 נְתַנְיָה (Nᵉthanyâh, neth-an-yaw'): Nethanjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or נְתַנְיָהוּ; from H5414 (נָתַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); given of Jah; KJV: Nethaniah.

H5419 נְתַן־מֶלֶךְ (Nᵉthan-Melek, neth-an' meh'-lek): Nethan-Melek, an Israelite. Origin: from H5414 (נָתַן) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); given of (the) king; KJV: Nathanmelech.

H5420 נָתָס (nâthâç, naw-thas'): to tear up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mar.

H5421 נָתַע (nâthaʻ, naw-thah'): to tear out. Origin: for H5422 (נָתַץ); KJV: break.

H5422 נָתַץ (nâthats, naw-thats'): to tear down. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beat down, break down (out), cast down, destroy, overthrow, pull down, throw down.

H5423 נָתַק (nâthaq, naw-thak'): to tear off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break (off), burst, draw (away), lift up, pluck (away, off), pull (out), root out.

H5424 נֶתֶק (netheq, neh'-thek): scurf. Origin: from H5423 (נָתַק); KJV: (dry) scall.

H5425 נָתַר (nâthar, naw-thar'): to jump, i.e. be violently agitated; causatively, to terrify, shake off, untie. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drive asunder, leap, (let) loose, [idiom] make, move, undo.

H5426 נְתַר (nᵉthar, neth-ar'): {to jump, i.e. be violently agitated; causatively, to terrify, shake off, untie}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5425 (נָתַר) KJV: shake off.

H5427 נֶתֶר (nether, neh'-ther): mineral potash (so called from effervescing with acid). Origin: from H5425 (נָתַר); KJV: nitre.

H5428 נָתַשׁ (nâthash, naw-thash'): to tear away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destroy, forsake, pluck (out, up, by the roots), pull up, root out (up), [idiom] utterly. s

H5429 סְאָה (çᵉʼâh, seh-aw'): a seah, or certain measure (as determinative) forgrain. Origin: from an unused root meaning to define; KJV: measure.

H5430 סְאוֹן (çᵉʼôwn, seh-own'): perhaps a military boot (as aprotection from mud. Origin: from H5431 (סָאַן); KJV: battle.

H5431 סָאַן (çâʼan, saw-an'): to shoe, i.e. (active participle) a soldier shod. Origin: a primitive root; to be miry; used only as denominative from H5430 (סְאוֹן); KJV: warrior.

H5432 סַאסְּאָה (çaʼçᵉʼâh, sah-seh-aw'): measurement, i.e. moderation. Origin: for H5429 (סְאָה); KJV: measure.

H5433 סָבָא (çâbâʼ, saw-baw'): to quaff to satiety, i.e. become tipsy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drunkard, fill self, Sabean, (wine-) bibber.

H5434 סְבָא (Çᵉbâʼ, seb-aw'): Seba, a son of Cush, and the country settled by him. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Seba.

H5435 סֹבֶא (çôbeʼ, so'-beh): potation, concretely (wine), or abstractly (carousal). Origin: from H5433 (סָבָא); KJV: drink, drunken, wine.

H5436 סְבָאִי (Çᵉbâʼîy, seb-aw-ee'): a Sebaite, or inhabitant of Seba. Origin: patrial from H5434 (סְבָא); KJV: Sabean.

H5437 סָבַב (çâbab, saw-bab'): to revolve, surround, or border; used in various applications, literally and figuratively. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring, cast, fetch, lead, make, walk, [idiom] whirl, [idiom] round about, be about on every side, apply, avoid, beset (about), besiege, bring again, carry (about), change, cause to come about, [idiom] circuit, (fetch a) compass (about, round), drive, environ, [idiom] on every side, beset (close, come, compass, go, stand) round about, inclose, remove, return, set, sit down, turn (self) (about, aside, away, back).

H5438 סִבָּה (çibbâh, sib-baw'): a (providential) turn (of affairs). Origin: from H5437 (סָבַב); KJV: cause.

H5439 סָבִיב (çâbîyb, saw-beeb'): (as noun) a circle, neighbour, or environs; but chiefly (as adverb, with or without preposition) around. Origin: or (feminine) סְבִיבָה; from H5437 (סָבַב); KJV: (place, round) about, circuit, compass, on every side.

H5440 סָבַךְ (çâbak, saw-bak'): to entwine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fold together, wrap.

H5441 סֹבֶךְ (çôbek, so'-bek): a copse. Origin: from H5440 (סָבַךְ); KJV: thicket.

H5442 סְבָךְ (çᵉbâk, seb-awk'): a copse. Origin: from H5440 (סָבַךְ), KJV: thick(-et).

H5443 סַבְּכָא (çabbᵉkâʼ, sab-bek-aw'): a lyre. Origin: (Aramaic) or שַׂבְּכָא; (Aramaic), from a root corresponding to H5440 (סָבַךְ); KJV: sackbut.

H5444 סִבְּכַי (Çibbᵉkay, sib-bek-ah'-ee): Sibbecai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5440 (סָבַךְ); copse-like; KJV: Sibbecai, Sibbechai.

H5445 סָבַל (çâbal, saw-bal'): to carry (literally or figuratively), or (reflexively) be burdensome; specifically, to be gravid. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear, be a burden, carry, strong to labour.

H5446 סְבַל (çᵉbal, seb-al'): to erect. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5445 (סָבַל); KJV: strongly laid.

H5447 סֵבֶל (çêbel, say'-bel): a load (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H5445 (סָבַל); KJV: burden, charge.

H5448 סֹבֶל (çôbel, so'-bel): a load (figuratively). Origin: (only in the form סֻבָּל; from H5445 (סָבַל); KJV: burden.

H5449 סַבָּל (çabbâl, sab-bawl'): a porter. Origin: from H5445 (סָבַל); KJV: (to bear, bearer of) burden(-s).

H5450 סְבָלָה (çᵉbâlâh, seb-aw-law'): porterage. Origin: from H5447 (סֵבֶל); KJV: burden.

H5451 סִבֹּלֶת (çibbôleth, sib-bo'-leth): an ear of grain. Origin: for H7641 (שִׁבֹּל); KJV: Sibboleth.

H5452 סְבַר (çᵉbar, seb-ar'): to bear in mind, i.e. hope. Origin: (Aramaic) a primitive root; KJV: think.

H5453 סִבְרַיִם (Çibrayim, sib-rah'-yim): Sibrajim, a place in Syria. Origin: dual from a root corresponding to H5452 (סְבַר); double hope; KJV: Sibraim.

H5454 סַבְתָּא (Çabtâʼ, sab-taw'): Sabta or Sabtah, the name of a son of Cush, and the country occupied by his posterity. Origin: or סַבְתָּה; probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Sabta, Sabtah.

H5455 סַבְתְּכָא (Çabtᵉkâʼ, sab-tek-aw'): Sabteca, the name of a son of Cush, and the region settled by him. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Sabtecha, Sabtechah.

H5456 סָגַד (çâgad, saw-gad'): to prostrate oneself (in homage). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fall down.

H5457 סְגִד (çᵉgid, seg-eed'): {to prostrate oneself (in homage)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5456 (סָגַד) KJV: worship.

H5458 סְגוֹר (çᵉgôwr, seg-ore'): properly, shut up, i.e. the breast (as enclosing the heart); also gold (as generally shut up safely). Origin: from H5462 (סָגַר); KJV: caul, gold.

H5459 סְגֻלָּה (çᵉgullâh, seg-ool-law'): wealth (as closely shut up). Origin: feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to shut up; KJV: jewel, peculiar (treasure), proper good, special.

H5460 סְגַן (çᵉgan, seg-an'): {a prefect of aprovince}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5461 (סָגָן) KJV: governor.

H5461 סָגָן (çâgân, saw-gawn'): a prefect of a province. Origin: from an unused root meaning to superintend; KJV: prince, ruler.

H5462 סָגַר (çâgar, saw-gar'): to shut up; figuratively, to surrender. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: close up, deliver (up), give over (up), inclose, [idiom] pure, repair, shut (in, self, out, up, up together), stop, [idiom] straitly.

H5463 סְגַר (çᵉgar, seg-ar'): {to shut up; figuratively, to surrender}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5462 (סָגַר) KJV: shut up.

H5464 סַגְרִיד (çagrîyd, sag-reed'): a pouring rain. Origin: probably from H5462 (סָגַר) in the sense of sweeping away; KJV: very rainy.

H5465 סַד (çad, sad): the stocks. Origin: from an unused root meaning to estop; KJV: stocks.

H5466 סָדִין (çâdîyn, saw-deen'): a wrapper, i.e. shirt. Origin: from an unused root meaning to envelop; KJV: fine linen, sheet.

H5467 סְדֹם (Çᵉdôm, sed-ome'): Sedom, a place near the Dead Sea. Origin: from an unused root meaning to scorch; burnt (i.e. volcanic or bituminous) district; KJV: Sodom.

H5468 סֶדֶר (çeder, seh'-der): order. Origin: from an unused root meaning to arrange; KJV: order.

H5469 סַהַר (çahar, cah'-har): roundness. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be round; KJV: round.

H5470 סֹהַר (çôhar, so'-har): a dungeon (as surrounded by walls). Origin: from the same as H5469 (סַהַר); KJV: prison.

H5471 סוֹא (Çôwʼ, so): So, an Egyptian king. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: So.

H5472 סוּג (çûwg, soog): properly, to flinch, i.e. (by implication) to go back, literally (to retreat) or figuratively (to apostatize). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: backslider, drive, go back, turn (away, back).

H5473 סוּג (çûwg, soog): to hem in, i.e. bind. Origin: a primitive root (probably rather identical with H5472 (סוּג) through the idea of shrinking from a hedge; compare H7735 (שׂוּג)); KJV: set about.

H5474 סוּגַר (çûwgar, soo-gar'): an inclosure, i.e. cage (for an animal). Origin: from H5462 (סָגַר); KJV: ward.

H5475 סוֹד (çôwd, sode): a session, i.e. company of persons (in close deliberation); by implication, intimacy, consultation, a secret. Origin: from H3245 (יָסַד); KJV: assembly, consel, inward, secret (counsel).

H5476 סוֹדִי (Çôwdîy, so-dee'): Sodi, an Israelite. Origin: from H5475 (סוֹד); a confidant; KJV: Sodi.

H5477 סוּחַ (Çûwach, soo'-akh): Suach, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to wipe away; sweeping; KJV: Suah.

H5478 סוּחָה (çûwchâh, soo-khaw'): something swept away, i.e. filth. Origin: from the same as H5477 (סוּחַ); KJV: torn.

H5479 סוֹטַי (Çôwṭay, so-tah'-ee): Sotai, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from H7750 (שׂוּט); roving; KJV: Sotai.

H5480 סוּךְ (çûwk, sook): properly, to smear over (with oil), i.e. anoint. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: anoint (self), [idiom] at all.

H5481 סוּמְפּוֹנְיָה (çûwmᵉpôwnᵉyâh, soom-po-neh-yaw'): a bagpipe (with a double pipe). Origin: (Aramaic) or סוּמְפֹּנְיָה; (Aramaic), or סִיפֹנְיָא; (Daniel 3:10) (Aramaic), of Greek origin; KJV: dulcimer.

H5482 סְוֵנֵה (Çᵉvênêh, sev-ay-nay'): Seven, a place in Upper Egypt. Origin: (rather to be written סְוֵנָה; for סְוֵן; i.e to Seven); of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Syene.

H5483 סוּס (çûwç, soos): a horse (as leaping); also a swallow (from its rapid flight). Origin: or סֻס; from an unused root meaning to skip (properly, for joy); KJV: crane, horse (-back, -hoof). Compare H6571 (פָּרָשׁ).

H5484 סוּסָה (çûwçâh, soo-saw'): a mare. Origin: feminine of H5483 (סוּס); KJV: company of horses.

H5485 סוּסִי (Çûwçîy, soo-see'): Susi, an Israelite. Origin: from H5483 (סוּס); horse-like; KJV: Susi.

H5486 סוּף (çûwph, soof): to snatch away, i.e. terminate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consume, have an end, perish, [idiom] be utterly.

H5487 סוּף (çûwph, soof): to come to an end. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5486 (סוּף); KJV: consume, fulfill.

H5488 סוּף (çûwph, soof): a reed, especially the papyrus. Origin: probably of Egyptian origin; KJV: flag, Red (sea), weed. Compare H5489 (סוּף).

H5489 סוּף (Çûwph, soof): the Reed (Sea). Origin: for H5488 (סוּף) (by ellipsis of H3220 (יָם)); KJV: Red Sea.

H5490 סוֹף (çôwph, sofe): a termination. Origin: from H5486 (סוּף); KJV: conclusion, end, hinder participle

H5491 סוֹף (çôwph, sofe): {a termination}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5490 (סוֹף) KJV: end.

H5492 סוּפָה (çûwphâh, soo-faw'): a hurricane. Origin: from H5486 (סוּף); KJV: Red Sea, storm, tempest, whirlwind, Red sea.

H5493 סוּר (çûwr, soor): to turn off (literal or figurative). Origin: or שׂוּר; (Hosea 9:12), a primitive root; KJV: be(-head), bring, call back, decline, depart, eschew, get (you), go (aside), [idiom] grievous, lay away (by), leave undone, be past, pluck away, put (away, down), rebel, remove (to and fro), revolt, [idiom] be sour, take (away, off), turn (aside, away, in), withdraw, be without.

H5494 סוּר (çûwr, soor): turned off, i.e. deteriorated. Origin: probably passive participle of H5493 (סוּר); KJV: degenerate.

H5495 סוּר (Çûwr, soor): Sur, a gate of the temple. Origin: the same as H5494 (סוּר); KJV: Sur.

H5496 סוּת (çûwth, sooth): properly, to prick, i.e. (figuratively) stimulate; by implication, to seduce. Origin: perhaps denominative from H7898 (שַׁיִת); KJV: entice, move, persuade, provoke, remove, set on, stir up, take away.

H5497 סוּת (çûwth, sooth): covering, i.e. clothing. Origin: probably from the same root as H4533 (מַסְוֶה); KJV: clothes.

H5498 סָחַב (çâchab, saw-khab'): to trail along. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: draw (out), tear.

H5499 סְחָבָה (çᵉchâbâh, seh-khaw-baw'): a rag. Origin: from H5498 (סָחַב); KJV: cast clout.

H5500 סָחָה (çâchâh, saw-khaw'): to sweep away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: scrape.

H5501 סְחִי (çᵉchîy, seh-khee'): refuse (as swept off). Origin: from H5500 (סָחָה); KJV: offscouring.

H5502 סָחַף (çâchaph, saw-khaf'): to scrape off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sweep (away).

H5503 סָחַר (çâchar, saw-khar'): to travel round (specifically as a pedlar); intensively, to palpitate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: go about, merchant(-man), occupy with, pant, trade, traffick.

H5504 סַחַר (çachar, sakh'-ar): profit (from trade). Origin: from H5503 (סָחַר); KJV: merchandise.

H5505 סָחַר (çâchar, saw-khar'): an emporium; abstractly, profit (from trade). Origin: from H5503 (סָחַר); KJV: mart, merchandise.

H5506 סְחֹרָה (çᵉchôrâh, sekh-o-raw'): traffic. Origin: from H5503 (סָחַר); KJV: merchandise.

H5507 סֹחֵרָה (çôchêrâh, so-khay-raw'): something surrounding the person, i.e. a shield. Origin: properly, active participle feminine of H5503 (סָחַר); KJV: buckler.

H5508 סֹחֵרֶת (çôchêreth, so-kheh'-reth): probably a (black) tile (or tessara) forlaying borders with. Origin: similar to H5507 (סֹחֵרָה); KJV: black marble.

H5509 סִיג (çîyg, seeg): scoria. Origin: or סוּג; (Ezekiel 22:18), from H5472 (סוּג) in the sense of refuse; KJV: dross.

H5510 סִיוָן (Çîyvân, see-vawn'): Sivan, the third Hebrew month. Origin: probably of Persian origin; KJV: Sivan.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5511 to H5644
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5511 סִיחוֹן (Çîychôwn, see-khone'): Sichon, an Amoritish king. Origin: or סִיחֹן; from the same as H5477 (סוּחַ); tempestuous; KJV: Sihon.

H5512 סִין (Çîyn, seen): Sin the name of an Egyptian town and (probably) desert adjoining. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Sin.

H5513 סִינִי (Çîynîy, see-nee'): a Sinite, or descendant of one of the sons of Canaan. Origin: from an otherwise unknown name of a man; KJV: Sinite.

H5514 סִינַי (Çîynay, see-nah'-ee): Sinai, mountain of Arabia. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Sinai.

H5515 סִינִים (Çîynîym, see-neem'): Sinim, a distant Oriental region. Origin: plural of an otherwise unknown name; KJV: Sinim.

H5516 סִיסְרָא (Çîyçᵉrâʼ, see-ser-aw'): Sisera, the name of a Canaanitish king and of one of the Nethinim. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Sisera.

H5517 סִיעָא (Çîyʻâʼ, see-ah'): Sia or Siaha, one of the Nethinim. Origin: or סִיעֲהָא; from an unused root meaning to converse; congregation; KJV: Sia, Siaha.

H5518 סִיר (çîyr, seer): a pot; also a thorn (as springing up rapidly); by implication, a hook. Origin: or (feminine) סִירָה; or סִרָה; (Jeremiah 52:18), from a primitive root meaning to boil up; KJV: caldron, fishhook, pan, (wash-)pot, thorn.

H5519 סָךְ (çâk, sawk): properly, a thicket of men, i.e. a crowd. Origin: from H5526 (סָכַךְ); KJV: multitude.

H5520 סֹךְ (çôk, soke): a hut (as of entwined boughs); also a lair. Origin: from H5526 (סָכַךְ); KJV: covert, den, pavilion, tabernacle.

H5521 סֻכָּה (çukkâh, sook-kaw'): a hut or lair. Origin: feminine of H5520 (סֹךְ); KJV: booth, cottage, covert, pavilion, tabernacle, tent.

H5522 סִכּוּת (çikkûwth, sik-kooth'): an (idolatrous) booth. Origin: feminine of H5519 (סָךְ); KJV: tabernacle.

H5523 סֻכּוֹת (Çukkôwth, sook-kohth'): Succoth, the name of a place in Egypt and of three in Palestine. Origin: or סֻכֹּת; plural of H5521 (סֻכָּה); booths; KJV: Succoth.

H5524 סֻכּוֹת בְּנוֹת (Çukkôwth bᵉnôwth, sook-kohth' ben-ohth'): booths of (the) daughters; brothels, i.e. idoalatrous tents forimpure purpose. Origin: from H5523 (סֻכּוֹת) and the (irregular) plural of H1323 (בַּת); KJV: Succothbenoth.

H5525 סֻכִּי (Çukkîy, sook-kee'): a Sukkite, or inhabitant of some place near Egypt (i.e. hut-dwellers). Origin: patrial from an unknown name (perhaps H5520 (סֹךְ)); KJV: Sukkiims.

H5526 סָכַךְ (çâkak, saw-kak'): properly, to entwine as ascreen; by implication, to fence in, cover over, (figuratively) protect. Origin: or שָׂכַךְ; (Exodus 33:22), a primitive root; KJV: cover, defence, defend, hedge in, join together, set, shut up.

H5527 סְכָכָה (Çᵉkâkâh, sek-aw-kaw'): Secacah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5526 (סָכַךְ); inclosure; KJV: Secacah.

H5528 סָכַל (çâkal, saw-kal'): to be silly. Origin: for H3688 (כָּסַל); KJV: do (make, play the, turn into) fool(-ish, -ishly, -ishness).

H5529 סֶכֶל (çekel, seh'-kal): silliness; concretely and collectively, dolts. Origin: from H5528 (סָכַל); KJV: folly.

H5530 סָכָל (çâkâl, saw-kawl'): silly. Origin: from H5528 (סָכַל); KJV: fool(-ish), sottish.

H5531 סִכְלוּת (çiklûwth, sik-looth'): silliness. Origin: or שִׂכְלוּת; (Ecclesiastes 1:17), from H5528 (סָכַל); KJV: folly, foolishness.

H5532 סָכַן (çâkan, saw-kan'): to be familiar with; by implication, to minister to, be serviceable to, be customary. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: acquaint (self), be advantage, [idiom] ever, (be, (un-)) profit(-able), treasurer, be wont.

H5533 סָכַן (çâkan, saw-kan'): properly, to cut, i.e. damage; also to grow (causatively, make) poor. Origin: probably a denominative from H7915 (שַׂכִּין); KJV: endanger, impoverish.

H5534 סָכַר (çâkar, saw-kar'): to shut up; by implication, to surrender. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: stop, give over. See also H5462 (סָגַר), H7936 (שָׂכַר).

H5535 סָכַת (çâkath, saw-kath'): by implication, to observe quietly. Origin: a primitive root to be silent; KJV: take heed.

H5536 סַל (çal, sal): properly, a willow twig (as pendulous), i.e. an osier; but only as woven into abasket. Origin: from H5549 (סָלַל); KJV: basket.

H5537 סָלָא (çâlâʼ, saw-law'): to suspend in a balance, i.e. weigh. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: compare.

H5538 סִלָּא (Çillâʼ, sil-law'): Silla, a place in Jerusalem. Origin: from H5549 (סָלַל); an embankment; KJV: Silla.

H5539 סָלַד (çâlad, saw-lad'): probably to leap (with joy), i.e. exult. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: harden self.

H5540 סֶלֶד (Çeled, seh'-led): Seled, an Israelite. Origin: from H5539 (סָלַד); exultation; KJV: Seled.

H5541 סָלָה (çâlâh, saw-law'): to hang up, i.e. weigh, or (figuratively) contemn. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tread down (under foot), value.

H5542 סֶלָה (çelâh, seh'-law): suspension (of music), i.e. pause. Origin: from H5541 (סָלָה); KJV: Selah.

H5543 סַלּוּ (Çallûw, sal-loo'): Sallu or Sallai, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or סַלּוּא; or סָלוּא; or סַלַּי; from H5541 (סָלָה); weighed; KJV: Sallai, Sallu, Salu.

H5544 סִלּוֹן (çillôwn, sil-lone'): a prickle (as if pendulous). Origin: or סַלּוֹן; from H5541 (סָלָה); KJV: brier, thorn.

H5545 סָלַח (çâlach, saw-lakh'): to forgive. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: forgive, pardon, spare.

H5546 סַלָּח (çallâch, saw-lawkh'): placable. Origin: from H5545 (סָלַח); KJV: ready to forgive.

H5547 סְלִיחָה (çᵉlîychâh, sel-ee-khaw'): pardon. Origin: from H5545 (סָלַח); KJV: forgiveness, pardon.

H5548 סַלְכָה (Çalkâh, sal-kaw'): Salcah, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from an unused root. meaning to walk; walking; KJV: Salcah, Salchah.

H5549 סָלַל (çâlal, saw-lal'): to mound up (especially a turnpike); figurative, to exalt; reflexively, to oppose (as by a dam). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast up, exalt (self), extol, make plain, raise up.

H5550 סֹלְלָה (çôlᵉlâh, so-lel-aw'): a military mound, i.e. rampart of besiegers. Origin: or סוֹלְלָה; active participle feminine of H5549 (סָלַל), but used passively; KJV: bank, mount.

H5551 סֻלָּם (çullâm, sool-lawm'): a stair-case. Origin: from H5549 (סָלַל); KJV: ladder.

H5552 סַלְסִלָּה (çalçillâh, sal-sil-law'): a twig (as pendulous). Origin: from H5541 (סָלָה); KJV: basket.

H5553 סֶלַע (çelaʻ, seh'-lah): a craggy rock, literally or figuratively (a fortress). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be lofty; KJV: (ragged) rock, stone(-ny), strong hold.

H5554 סֶלַע (Çelaʻ, seh'-lah): Sela, the rock-city of Idumaea. Origin: the same as H5553 (סֶלַע); KJV: rock, Sela(-h).

H5555 סֶלַע הַמַּחְלְקוֹת (Çelaʻ ham-machlᵉqôwth, seh'-lah hammakh-lek-oth'): Sela-ham-Machlekoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5553 (סֶלַע) and the plural of H4256 (מַחֲלֹקֶת) with the article interposed; rock of the divisions; KJV: Sela-hammalekoth.

H5556 סׇלְעָם (çolʻâm, sol-awm'): a kind of locust (from its destructiveness). Origin: apparently from the same as H5553 (סֶלַע) in the sense of crushing as with a rock, i.e. consuming; KJV: bald locust.

H5557 סָלַף (çâlaph, saw-laf'): properly, to wrench, i.e. (figuratively) to subvert. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: overthrow, pervert.

H5558 סֶלֶף (çeleph, seh'-lef): distortion, i.e. (figuratively) viciousness. Origin: from H5557 (סָלַף); KJV: perverseness.

H5559 סְלִק (çᵉliq, sel-eek'): to ascend. Origin: (Aramaic) a primitive root; KJV: come (up).

H5560 סֹלֶת (çôleth, so'-leth): flour (as chipped off). Origin: from an unused root meaning to strip; KJV: (fine) flour, meal.

H5561 סַם (çam, sam): an aroma. Origin: from an unused root meaning to smell sweet; KJV: sweet (spice).

H5562 סַמְגַּר נְבוֹ (Çamgar Nᵉbôw, sam-gar' neb-o'): Samgar-Nebo, a Babylonian general. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Samgar-nebo.

H5563 סְמָדַר (çᵉmâdar, sem-aw-dar'): a vine blossom; used also adverbially, abloom. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: tender grape.

H5564 סָמַךְ (çâmak, saw-mak'): to prop (literally or figuratively); reflexively, to lean upon or take hold of (in a favorable or unfavorable sense). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear up, establish, (up-) hold, lay, lean, lie hard, put, rest self, set self, stand fast, stay (self), sustain.

H5565 סְמַכְיָהוּ (Çᵉmakyâhûw, sem-ak-yaw'-hoo): Semakjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H5564 (סָמַךְ) and H3050 (יָהּ); supported of Jah; KJV: Semachiah.

H5566 סֶמֶל (çemel, seh'-mel): a likeness. Origin: or סֵמֶל; from an unused root meaning to resemble; KJV: figure, idol, image.

H5567 סָמַן (çâman, saw-man'): to designate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appointed.

H5568 סָמַר (çâmar, saw-mar'): to be erect, i.e. bristle as hair. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: stand up, tremble.

H5569 סָמָר (çâmâr, saw-mar'): bristling, i.e. shaggy. Origin: from H5568 (סָמַר); KJV: rough.

H5570 סְנָאָה (Çᵉnâʼâh, sen-aw-aw'): Senaah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root meaning to prick; thorny; KJV: Senaah, Hassenaah (with the article).

H5571 סַנְבַלַּט (Çanballaṭ, san-bal-lat'): Sanballat, a Persian satrap of Samaria. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Sanballat.

H5572 סְנֶה (çᵉneh, sen-eh'): a bramble. Origin: from an unused root meaning to prick; KJV: bush.

H5573 סֶנֶה (Çeneh, seh-neh'): Seneh, a crag in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5572 (סְנֶה); thorn; KJV: Seneh.

H5574 סְנוּאָה (Çᵉnûwʼâh, sen-oo-aw'): pointed; (used with the article as a proper name) Senuah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or סְנֻאָה from the same as H5570 (סְנָאָה); KJV: Hasenuah (including the art), Senuah.

H5575 סַנְוֵר (çanvêr, san-vare'): (in plural) blindness. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: blindness.

H5576 סַנְחֵרִיב (Çanchêrîyb, san-khay-reeb'): Sancherib, an Assyrian king. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Sennacherib.

H5577 סַנְסִן (çançin, san-seen'): a twig (as tapering). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be pointed; KJV: bough.

H5578 סַנְסַנָּה (Çançannâh, san-san-naw'): Sansannah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of a form of H5577 (סַנְסִן); a bough; KJV: Sansannah.

H5579 סְנַפִּיר (çᵉnappîyr, sen-ap-peer'): a fin (collectively). Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: fins.

H5580 סָס (çâç, sawce): a moth (from the agility of the fly). Origin: from the same as H5483 (סוּס); KJV: moth.

H5581 סִסְמַי (Çiçmay, sis-mah'-ee): Sismai, an Israelite. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Sisamai.

H5582 סָעַד (çâʻad, saw-ad'): to suport (mostly figurative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: comfort, establish, hold up, refresh self, strengthen, be upholden.

H5583 סְעַד (çᵉʻad, seh-ad'): to aid. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5582 (סָעַד); KJV: helping.

H5584 סָעָה (çâʻâh, saw-aw'): to rush. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: storm.

H5585 סָעִיף (çâʻîyph, saw-eef'): a fissure (of rocks); also a bough (as subdivided). Origin: from H5586 (סָעַף); KJV: (outmost) branch, clift, top.

H5586 סָעַף (çâʻaph, saw-af'): to disbranch (a tree). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to divide up; but used only as denominative from H5585 (סָעִיף), KJV: top.

H5587 סָעִף (çâʻiph, saw-eef'): divided (in mind), i.e. (abstractly) a sentiment. Origin: or שָׂעִף; from H5586 (סָעַף); KJV: opinion.

H5588 סֵעֵף (çêʻêph, say-afe'): divided (in mind), i.e. (concretely) a skeptic. Origin: from H5586 (סָעַף); KJV: thought.

H5589 סְעַפָּה (çᵉʻappâh, seh-ap-paw'): a twig. Origin: feminine of H5585 (סָעִיף); KJV: bough, branch. Compare H5634 (סַרְעַפָּה).

H5590 סָעַר (çâʻar, saw-ar'): to rush upon; by implication, to toss (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (toss with) tempest(-uous), be sore, troubled, come out as a (drive with the, scatter with a) whirlwind.

H5591 סַעַר (çaʻar, sah'-ar): a hurricane. Origin: or (feminine) סְעָרָה; from H5590 (סָעַר); KJV: storm(-y), tempest, whirlwind.

H5592 סַף (çaph, saf): a vestibule (as a limit); also a dish (for holding blood or wine). Origin: from H5605 (סָפַף), in its original sense of containing; KJV: bason, bowl, cup, door (post), gate, post, threshold.

H5593 סַף (Çaph, saf): Saph, a Philistine. Origin: the same as H5592 (סַף); KJV: Saph. Compare H5598 (סִפַּי).

H5594 סָפַד (çâphad, saw-fad'): properly, to tear the hair and beat the breasts (as Orientals do in grief); generally to lament; by implication, to wail. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lament, mourn(-er), wail.

H5595 סָפָה (çâphâh, saw-faw'): properly, to scrape (literally, to shave; but usually figuratively) together (i.e. to accumulate or increase) or away (i.e. to scatter, remove, or ruin; intransitively, to perish). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: add, augment, consume, destroy, heap, join, perish, put.

H5596 סָפַח (çâphach, saw-fakh'): properly, to scrape out, but in certain peculiar senses (of removal or association). Origin: or שָׂפַח; (Isaiah 3:17), a primitive root; KJV: abiding, gather together, cleave, smite with the scab.

H5597 סַפַּחַת (çappachath, sap-pakh'-ath): the mange (as making the hair fall off). Origin: from H5596 (סָפַח); KJV: scab.

H5598 סִפַּי (Çippay, sip-pah'-ee): Sippai, a Philistine. Origin: from H5592 (סַף); bason-like; KJV: Sippai. Compare H5593 (סַף).

H5599 סָפִיחַ (çâphîyach, saw-fee'-akh): something (spontaneously) falling off, i.e. a self-sown crop; figuratively, a freshet. Origin: from H5596 (סָפַח); KJV: (such) things as (which) grow (of themselves), which groweth of its own accord (itself).

H5600 סְפִינָה (çᵉphîynâh, sef-ee-naw'): a (sea-going) vessel (as ceiled with a deck). Origin: from H5603 (סָפַן); KJV: ship.

H5601 סַפִּיר (çappîyr, sap-peer'): a gem (perhaps used for scratching other substances), probably the sapphire. Origin: from H5608 (סָפַר); KJV: sapphire.

H5602 סֵפֶל (çêphel, say'-fel): a basin (as deepened out). Origin: from an unused root meaning to depress; KJV: bowl, dish.

H5603 סָפַן (çâphan, saw-fan'): to hide by covering; specifically, to roof (passive participle as noun, a roof) or wainscot; figuratively, to reserve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cieled, cover, seated.

H5604 סִפֻּן (çippun, sip-poon'): a wainscot. Origin: from H5603 (סָפַן); KJV: cieling.

H5605 סָפַף (çâphaph, saw-faf'): to wait at the threshold. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to snatch away, i.e. terminate; but used only as denominative from H5592 (סַף) (in the sense of a vestibule), KJV: be a doorkeeper.

H5606 סָפַק (çâphaq, saw-fak'): to clap the hands (in token of compact, derision, grief, indignation, or punishment); by implication of satisfaction, to be enough; by implication of excess, to vomit. Origin: or שָׂפַק; (1 Kings 20:10; Job 27:23; Isaiah 2:6), a primitive root; KJV: clap, smite, strike, suffice, wallow.

H5607 סֵפֶק (çêpheq, say'-fek): chastisement; also satiety. Origin: or שֶׂפֶק; (Job 20:22; Job 36:18), from H5606 (סָפַק); KJV: stroke, sufficiency.

H5608 סָפַר (çâphar, saw-far'): properly, to score with a mark as a tally or record, i.e. (by implication) to inscribe, and also to enumerate; intensively, to recount, i.e. celebrate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: commune, (ac-) count; declare, number, [phrase] penknife, reckon, scribe, shew forth, speak, talk, tell (out), writer.

H5609 סְפַר (çᵉphar, sef-ar'): a book. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5608 (סָפַר); KJV: book, roll.

H5610 סְפָר (çᵉphâr, sef-awr'): a census. Origin: from H5608 (סָפַר); KJV: numbering.

H5611 סְפָר (Çᵉphâr, sef-awr'): Sephar, a place in Arabia. Origin: the same as H5610 (סְפָר); KJV: Sephar.

H5612 סֵפֶר (çêpher, say'-fer): properly, writing (the art or a document); by implication, a book. Origin: or (feminine) סִפְרָה; (Psalm 56:8 (H9 (אֲבֵדָה))), from H5608 (סָפַר); KJV: bill, book, evidence, [idiom] learn(-ed) (-ing), letter, register, scroll.

H5613 סָפֵר (çâphêr, saw-fare'): a scribe (secular or sacred). Origin: (Aramaic) from the same as H5609 (סְפַר); KJV: scribe.

H5614 סְפָרָד (Çᵉphârâd, sef-aw-rawd'): Sepharad, a region of Assyria. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Sepharad.

H5615 סְפֹרָה (çᵉphôrâh, sef-o-raw'): a numeration. Origin: from H5608 (סָפַר); KJV: number.

H5616 סְפַרְוִי (Çᵉpharvîy, sef-ar-vee'): a Sepharvite or inhabitant of Sepharvain. Origin: patrial from H5617 (סְפַרְוַיִם); KJV: Sepharvite.

H5617 סְפַרְוַיִם (Çᵉpharvayim, sef-ar-vah'-yim): Sepharvites. Origin: (dual)

H5618 סֹפֶרֶת (Çôphereth, so-feh'-reth): Sophereth, a temple servant. Origin: feminine active participle of H5608 (סָפַר); a scribe (properly, female); KJV: Sophereth.

H5619 סָקַל (çâqal, saw-kal'): properly, to be weighty; but used only in the sense of lapidation or its contrary (as if a delapidation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cast, gather out, throw) stone(-s), [idiom] surely.

H5620 סַר (çar, sar): peevish. Origin: contracted from H5637 (סָרַר); KJV: heavy, sad.

H5621 סָרָב (çârâb, saw-rawb'): a thistle. Origin: from an unused root meaning to sting; KJV: brier.

H5622 סַרְבַּל (çarbal, sar-bal'): a cloak. Origin: (Aramaic) of uncertain derivation; KJV: coat.

H5623 סַרְגּוֹן (Çargôwn, sar-gone'): Sargon, an Assyrian king. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Sargon.

H5624 סֶרֶד (Çered, seh'-red): Sered, an Israelite. Origin: from a primitive root meaning to tremble; trembling; KJV: Sered.

H5625 סַרְדִּי (Çardîy, sar-dee'): a Seredite (collectively) or descendants of Sered. Origin: patron from H5624 (סֶרֶד); KJV: Sardites.

H5626 סִרָה (Çirâh, see-raw'): Sirah, a cistern so-called. Origin: from H5493 (סוּר); departure; KJV: Sirah. See also H5518 (סִיר).

H5627 סָרָה (çârâh, saw-raw'): apostasy, crime; figuratively, remission. Origin: from H5493 (סוּר); KJV: [idiom] continual, rebellion, revolt(-ed), turn away, wrong.

H5628 סָרַח (çârach, saw-rakh'): to extend (even to excess). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: exceeding, hand, spread, stretch self, banish.

H5629 סֶרַח (çerach, seh'-rakh): a redundancy. Origin: from H5628 (סָרַח); KJV: remnant.

H5630 סִרְיֹן (çiryôn, sir-yone'): a coat of mail. Origin: for H8302 (שִׁרְיוֹן); KJV: brigandine.

H5631 סָרִיס (çârîyç, saw-reece'): a eunuch; by implication, valet (especially of the female apartments), and thus, a minister of state. Origin: or סָרִס; from an unused root meaning to castrate; KJV: chamberlain, eunuch, officer. Compare H7249 (רַב־סָרִיס).

H5632 סָרֵךְ (çârêk, saw-rake'): an emir. Origin: (Aramaic) of foreign origin; KJV: president.

H5633 סֶרֶן (çeren, seh'-ren): an axle; figuratively, a peer. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: lord, plate.

H5634 סַרְעַפָּה (çarʻappâh, sar-ap-paw'): a twig. Origin: for H5589 (סְעַפָּה); KJV: bough.

H5635 סָרַף (çâraph, saw-raf'): to cremate, i.e. to be (near) of kin (such being privileged to kindle the pyre). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn.

H5636 סַרְפָּד (çarpâd, sar-pawd'): a nettle (as stinging like a burn). Origin: from H5635 (סָרַף); KJV: brier.

H5637 סָרַר (çârar, saw-rar'): to turn away, i.e. (morally) be refractory. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] away, backsliding, rebellious, revolter(-ing), slide back, stubborn, withdrew.

H5638 סְתָו (çᵉthâv, seth-awv'): winter (as the dark season). Origin: from an unused root meaning to hide; KJV: winter.

H5639 סְתוּר (Çᵉthûwr, seth-oor'): Sethur, an Israelite. Origin: from H5641 (סָתַר); hidden; KJV: Sethur.

H5640 סָתַם (çâtham, saw-tham'): to stop up; by implication, to repair; figuratively, to keep secret. Origin: or שָׂתַם; (Numbers 24:15), a primitive root; KJV: closed up, hidden, secret, shut out (up), stop.

H5641 סָתַר (çâthar, saw-thar'): to hide (by covering), literally or figuratively. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be absent, keep close, conceal, hide (self), (keep) secret, [idiom] surely.

H5642 סְתַר (çᵉthar, seth-ar'): to conceal; figuratively, to demolish. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5641 (סָתַר); KJV: destroy, secret thing.

H5643 סֵתֶר (çêther, say'-ther): a cover (in a good or a bad, a literal or a figurative sense). Origin: or (feminine) סִתְרָה; (Deuteronomy [32:38), from H5641 (סָתַר); KJV: backbiting, covering, covert, [idiom] disguise(-th), hiding place, privily, protection, secret(-ly, place).

H5644 סִתְרִי (Çithrîy, sith-ree'): Sithri, an Israelite. Origin: from H5643 (סֵתֶר); protective; KJV: Zithri. [

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5645 to H5765
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5645 עָב (ʻâb, awb): properly, an envelope, i.e. darkness (or density, 2 Chronicles 4:17); specifically, a (scud) cloud; also a copse. Origin: (masculine and feminine); from H5743 (עוּב); KJV: clay, (thick) cloud, [idiom] thick, thicket. Compare H5672 (עֲבִי).

H5646 עָב (ʻâb, awb): an architrave (as shading the pillars). Origin: or עֹב; from an unused root meaning to cover; properly, equivalent to H5645 (עָב); but used only as an architectural term, KJV: thick (beam, plant).

H5647 עָבַד (ʻâbad, aw-bad'): to work (in any sense); by implication, to serve, till, (causatively) enslave, etc. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] be, keep in bondage, be bondmen, bond-service, compel, do, dress, ear, execute, [phrase] husbandman, keep, labour(-ing man, bring to pass, (cause to, make to) serve(-ing, self), (be, become) servant(-s), do (use) service, till(-er), transgress (from margin), (set a) work, be wrought, worshipper,

H5648 עֲבַד (ʻăbad, ab-bad'): to do, make, prepare, keep, etc. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: [idiom] cut, do, execute, go on, make, move, work.

H5649 עֲבַד (ʻăbad, ab-bad'): a servant. Origin: (Aramaic) from H5648 (עֲבַד); KJV: servant.

H5650 עֶבֶד (ʻebed, eh'-bed): a servant. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: [idiom] bondage, bondman, (bond-) servant, (man-) servant.

H5651 עֶבֶד (ʻEbed, eh'-bed): Ebed, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H5650 (עֶבֶד); KJV: Ebed.

H5652 עֲבָד (ʻăbâd, ab-awd'): a deed. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: work.

H5653 עַבְדָּא (ʻAbdâʼ, ab-daw'): Abda, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); work; KJV: Abda

H5654 עֹבֵד אֱדוֹם (ʻÔbêd ʼĔdôwm, o-bade' ed-ome'): Obed-Edom, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from the active participle of H5647 (עָבַד) and H123 (אֱדֹם); worker of Edom; KJV: Obed-edom.

H5655 עַבְדְּאֵל (ʻAbdᵉʼêl, ab-deh-ale'): Abdeel, an Israelite. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד) and H410 (אֵל); serving God; KJV: Abdeel. Compare H5661 (עַבְדִיאֵל).

H5656 עֲבֹדָה (ʻăbôdâh, ab-o-daw'): work of any kind. Origin: or עֲבוֹדָה; from H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: act, bondage, [phrase] bondservant, effect, labour, ministering(-try), office, service(-ile, -itude), tillage, use, work, [idiom] wrought.

H5657 עֲבֻדָּה (ʻăbuddâh, ab-ood-daw'): something wrought, i.e. (concretely) service. Origin: passive participle of H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: household, store of servants.

H5658 עַבְדוֹן (ʻAbdôwn, ab-dohn'): Abdon, the name of a place in Palestine and of four Israelites. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); servitude; KJV: Abdon. Compare H5683 (עֶבְרֹן).

H5659 עַבְדוּת (ʻabdûwth, ab-dooth'): servitude. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); KJV: bondage.

H5660 עַבְדִּי (ʻAbdîy, ab-dee'): Abdi, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5647 (עָבַד); serviceable; KJV: Abdi.

H5661 עַבְדִיאֵל (ʻAbdîyʼêl, ab-dee-ale'): Abdiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H5650 (עֶבֶד) and H410 (אֵל); servant of God; KJV: Abdiel. Compare H5655 (עַבְדְּאֵל).

H5662 עֹבַדְיָה (ʻÔbadyâh, o-bad-yaw'): Obadjah, the name of thirteen Israelites. Origin: or עֹבַדְיָהוּ; active participle of H5647 (עָבַד) and H3050 (יָהּ); serving Jah; KJV: Obadiah.

H5663 עֶבֶד מֶלֶךְ (ʻEbed Melek, eh'-bed meh'-lek): Ebed-Melek, a eunuch of Zedekeah. Origin: from H5650 (עֶבֶד) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); servant of a king; KJV: Ebed-melech.

H5664 עֲבֵד נְגוֹ (ʻĂbêd Nᵉgôw, ab-ade' neg-o'): Abed-Nego, the Babylonian name of one of Daniel's companions. Origin: the same as H5665 (עֲבֵד נְגוֹא); KJV: Abed-nego.

H5665 עֲבֵד נְגוֹא (ʻĂbêd Nᵉgôwʼ, ab-ade' neg-o'): Abed-Nego, the name of Azariah. Origin: (Aramaic) of foreign origin; KJV: Abed-nego.

H5666 עָבָה (ʻâbâh, aw-baw'): to be dense. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (grow) thick(-er).

H5667 עֲבוֹט (ʻăbôwṭ, ab-ote'): a pawn. Origin: or עֲבֹט; from H5670 (עָבַט); KJV: pledge.

H5668 עָבוּר (ʻâbûwr, aw-boor'): properly, crossed, i.e. (abstractly) transit; used only adverbially, on account of, in order that. Origin: or עָבֻר; passive participle of H5674 (עָבַר); KJV: because of, for (...'s sake), (intent) that, to.

H5669 עָבוּר (ʻâbûwr, aw-boor'): passed, i.e. kept over; used only of stored grain. Origin: the same as H5668 (עָבוּר); KJV: old corn.

H5670 עָבַט (ʻâbaṭ, aw-bat'): to pawn; causatively, to lend (on security); figuratively, to entangle. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: borrow, break (ranks), fetch (a pledge), lend, [idiom] surely.

H5671 עַבְטִיט (ʻabṭîyṭ, ab-teet'): something pledged, i.e. (collectively) pawned goods. Origin: from H5670 (עָבַט); KJV: thick clay (by a false etym.).

H5672 עֲבִי (ʻăbîy, ab-ee'): density, i.e. depth or width. Origin: or עֳבִי]; from H5666 (עָבָה); KJV: thick(-ness). Compare H5645 (עָב).

H5673 עֲבִידָה (ʻăbîydâh, ab-ee-daw'): labor or business. Origin: (Aramaic) from H5648 (עֲבַד); KJV: affairs, service, work.

H5674 עָבַר (ʻâbar, aw-bar'): to cross over; used very widely of any transition (literal or figurative; transitive, intransitive, intensive, causative); specifically, to cover (in copulation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: alienate, alter, [idiom] at all, beyond, bring (over, through), carry over, (over-) come (on, over), conduct (over), convey over, current, deliver, do away, enter, escape, fail, gender, get over, (make) go (away, beyond, by, forth, his way, in, on, over, through), have away (more), lay, meddle, overrun, make partition, (cause to, give, make to, over) pass(-age, along, away, beyond, by, -enger, on, out, over, through), (cause to, make) [phrase] proclaim(-amation), perish, provoke to anger, put away, rage, [phrase] raiser of taxes, remove, send over, set apart, [phrase] shave, cause to (make) sound, [idiom] speedily, [idiom] sweet smelling, take (away), (make to) transgress(-or), translate, turn away, (way-) faring man, be wrath.

H5675 עֲבַר (ʻăbar, ab-ar'): {properly, a region across; but used only adverbially (with or without a preposition) on the opposite side (especially of the Jordan; ususally meaning the east)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5676 (עֵבֶר) KJV: beyond, this side.

H5676 עֵבֶר (ʻêber, ay'-ber): properly, a region across; but used only adverbially (with or without a preposition) on the opposite side (especially of the Jordan; ususally meaning the east). Origin: from H5674 (עָבַר); KJV: [idiom] against, beyond, by, [idiom] from, over, passage, quarter, (other, this) side, straight.

H5677 עֵבֵר (ʻÊbêr, ay'-ber): Eber, the name of two patriarchs and four Israelites. Origin: the same as H5676 (עֵבֶר); KJV: Eber, Heber.

H5678 עֶבְרָה (ʻebrâh, eb-raw'): an outburst of passion. Origin: feminine of H5676 (עֵבֶר); KJV: anger, rage, wrath.

H5679 עֲבָרָה (ʻăbârâh, ab-aw-raw'): a crossing-place. Origin: from H5674 (עָבַר); KJV: ferry, plain (from the margin).

H5680 עִבְרִי (ʻIbrîy, ib-ree'): an Eberite (i.e. Hebrew) or descendant of Eber. Origin: patronymic from H5677 (עֵבֵר); KJV: Hebrew(-ess, woman).

H5681 עִבְרִי (ʻIbrîy, ib-ree'): Ibri, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H5680 (עִבְרִי); KJV: Ibri.

H5682 עֲבָרִים (ʻĂbârîym, ab-aw-reem'): Abarim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H5676 (עֵבֶר); regions beyond; KJV: Abarim, passages.

H5683 עֶבְרֹן (ʻEbrôn, eb-rone'): Ebron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5676 (עֵבֶר); transitional; KJV: Hebron. Perhaps a clerical error for H5658 (עַבְדוֹן).

H5684 עֶבְרֹנָה (ʻEbrônâh, eb-raw-naw'): Ebronah, place in the Desert. Origin: feminine of H5683 (עֶבְרֹן); KJV: Ebronah.

H5685 עָבַשׁ (ʻâbash, aw-bash'): to dry up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be rotten.

H5686 עָבַת (ʻâbath, aw-bath'): to interlace, i.e. (figuratively) to pervert. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wrap up.

H5687 עָבֹת (ʻâbôth, aw-both'): intwined, i.e. dense. Origin: or עָבוֹת; from H5686 (עָבַת); KJV: thick.

H5688 עֲבֹת (ʻăbôth, ab-oth'): something intwined, i.e. a string, wreath or foliage. Origin: or עֲבוֹת; or (feminine) עֲבֹתָה; the same as H5687 (עָבֹת); KJV: band, cord, rope, thick bough (branch), wreathen (chain).

H5689 עֲגַב (ʻăgab, aw-gab'): to breathe after, i.e. to love (sensually). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dote, lover.

H5690 עֶגֶב (ʻegeb, eh'-gheb): love (concretely), i.e. amative words. Origin: from H5689 (עֲגַב); KJV: much love, very lovely.

H5691 עֲגָבָה (ʻăgâbâh, ag-aw-baw'): love (abstractly), i.e. amorousness. Origin: from H5689 (עֲגַב); KJV: inordinate love.

H5692 עֻגָּה (ʻuggâh, oog-gaw'): an ash-cake (as round). Origin: from H5746 (עוּג); KJV: cake (upon the hearth).

H5693 עָגוּר (ʻâgûwr, aw-goor'): probably the swallow. Origin: passive part (but with active sense) of an unused root meaning to twitter; KJV: swallow.

H5694 עָגִיל (ʻâgîyl, aw-gheel'): something round, i.e. a ring (for the ears). Origin: from the same as H5696 (עָגֹל); KJV: earring.

H5695 עֵגֶל (ʻêgel, ay-ghel): a (male) calf (as frisking round), especially one nearly grown (i.e. a steer). Origin: from the same as H5696 (עָגֹל); KJV: bullock, calf.

H5696 עָגֹל (ʻâgôl, aw-gole'): circular. Origin: or עָגוֹל; from an unused root meaning to revolve, KJV: round.

H5697 עֶגְלָה (ʻeglâh, eg-law'): a (female) calf, especially one nearly grown (i.e. a heifer). Origin: feminine of H5695 (עֵגֶל); KJV: calf, cow, heifer.

H5698 עֶגְלָה (ʻEglâh, eg-law'): Eglah, a wife of David. Origin: the same as H5697 (עֶגְלָה); KJV: Eglah.

H5699 עֲגָלָה (ʻăgâlâh, ag-aw-law'): something revolving, i.e. a wheeled vehicle. Origin: from the same as H5696 (עָגֹל); KJV: cart, chariot, wagon

H5700 עֶגְלוֹן (ʻEglôwn, eg-lawn'): Eglon, the name of a place in Palestine and of a Moabitish king. Origin: from H5695 (עֵגֶל); vituline; KJV: Eglon.

H5701 עָגַם (ʻâgam, aw-gam'): to be sad. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: grieve.

H5702 עָגַן (ʻâgan, aw-gan'): to debar, i.e. from marriage. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: stay.

H5703 עַד (ʻad, ad): properly, a (peremptory) terminus, i.e. (by implication) duration, in the sense of advance or perpetuity (substantially as a noun, either with or without a preposition). Origin: from H5710 (עָדָה); KJV: eternity, ever(-lasting, -more), old, perpetually, [phrase] world without end.

H5704 עַד (ʻad, ad): as far (or long, or much) as, whether of space (even unto) or time (during, while, until) or degree (equally with). Origin: properly, the same as H5703 (עַד) (used as a preposition, adverb or conjunction; especially with a preposition); KJV: against, and, as, at, before, by (that), even (to), for(-asmuch as), (hither-) to, [phrase] how long, into, as long (much) as, (so) that, till, toward, until, when, while, ([phrase] as) yet.

H5705 עַד (ʻad, ad): {as far (or long, or much) as, whether of space (even unto) or time (during, while, until) or degree (equally with)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5704 (עַד) KJV: [idiom] and, at, for, (hither-) to, on till, (un-) to, until, within.

H5706 עַד (ʻad, ad): booty. Origin: the same as H5703 (עַד) in the sense of the aim of an attack; KJV: prey.

H5707 עֵד (ʻêd, ayd): concretely, a witness; abstractly, testimony; specifically, a recorder, i.e. prince. Origin: contracted from H5749 (עוּד); KJV: witness.

H5708 עֵד (ʻêd, ayd): the menstrual flux (as periodical); by implication (in plural) soiling. Origin: from an unused root meaning to set a period (compare H5710 (עָדָה), H5749 (עוּד)); KJV: filthy.

H5709 עֲדָא (ʻădâʼ, ad-aw'): {to advance, i.e. pass on or continue; causatively, to remove; specifically, to bedeck (i.e. bring an ornament upon)}. Origin: (Aramaic) or עֲדָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H5710 (עָדָה) KJV: alter, depart, pass (away), remove, take (away).

H5710 עָדָה (ʻâdâh, aw-daw'): to advance, i.e. pass on or continue; causatively, to remove; specifically, to bedeck (i.e. bring an ornament upon). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: adorn, deck (self), pass by, take away.

H5711 עָדָה (ʻÂdâh, aw-daw'): Adah, the name of two women. Origin: from H5710 (עָדָה); ornament; KJV: Adah.

H5712 עֵדָה (ʻêdâh, ay-daw'): a stated assemblage (specifically, a concourse, or generally, a family or crowd). Origin: feminine of H5707 (עֵד) in the original sense of fixture; KJV: assembly, company, congregation, multitude, people, swarm. Compare H5713 (עֵדָה).

H5713 עֵדָה (ʻêdâh, ay-daw'): testimony. Origin: feminine of H5707 (עֵד) in its techn. sense; KJV: testimony, witness. Compare H5712 (עֵדָה).

H5714 עִדּוֹ (ʻIddôw, id-do'): Iddo (or Iddi), the name of five Israelites. Origin: or עִדּוֹא; or עִדִּיא; from H5710 (עָדָה); timely; KJV: Iddo. Compare H3035 (יִדּוֹ), H3260 (יֶעְדִּי).

H5715 עֵדוּת (ʻêdûwth, ay-dooth'): testimony. Origin: feminine of H5707 (עֵד); KJV: testimony, witness.

H5716 עֲדִי (ʻădîy, ad-ee'): finery; generally an outfit; specifically, a headstall. Origin: from H5710 (עָדָה) in the sense of trappings; KJV: [idiom] excellent, mouth, ornament.

H5717 עֲדִיאֵל (ʻĂdîyʼêl, ad-ee-ale'): Adiel, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H5716 (עֲדִי) and H410 (אֵל); ornament of God; KJV: Adiel.

H5718 עֲדָיָה (ʻĂdâyâh, ad-aw-yaw'): Adajah, the name of eight Israelites. Origin: or עֲדָיָהוּ; from H5710 (עָדָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has adorned; KJV: Adaiah.

H5719 עָדִין (ʻâdîyn, aw-deen'): voluptuous. Origin: from H5727 (עָדַן); KJV: given to pleasures.

H5720 עָדִין (ʻÂdîyn, aw-deen'): Adin, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H5719 (עָדִין); KJV: Adin.

H5721 עֲדִינָא (ʻĂdîynâʼ, ad-ee-naw'): Adina, an Israelite. Origin: from H5719 (עָדִין); effeminacy; KJV: Adina.

H5722 עֲדִינוֹ (ʻădîynôw, ad-ee-no'): his spear. Origin: probably from H5719 (עָדִין) in the original sense of slender (i.e. a spear); KJV: Adino.

H5723 עֲדִיתַיִם (ʻĂdîythayim, ad-ee-thah'-yim): Adithajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of a feminine of H5706 (עַד); double prey; KJV: Adithaim.

H5724 עַדְלַי (ʻAdlay, ad-lah'-ee): Adlai, an Israelite. Origin: probably from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: Adlai.

H5725 עֲדֻלָּם (ʻĂdullâm, ad-ool-lawm'): Adullam, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from the passive participle of the same as H5724 (עַדְלַי); KJV: Adullam.

H5726 עֲדֻלָּמִי (ʻĂdullâmîy, ad-ool-law-mee'): an Adullamite or native of Adullam. Origin: patrial from H5725 (עֲדֻלָּם); KJV: Adullamite.

H5727 עָדַן (ʻâdan, aw-dan'): to be soft or pleasant; figuratively and reflexively, to live voluptuously. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: delight self.

H5728 עֲדֶן (ʻăden, ad-en'): till now. Origin: or עֲדֶנָּה; from H5704 (עַד) and H2004 (הֵן); KJV: yet.

H5729 עֶדֶן (ʻEden, eh'-den): Eden, a place in Mesopotamia. Origin: from H5727 (עָדַן); pleasure; KJV: Eden.

H5730 עֵדֶן (ʻêden, ay'-den): pleasure. Origin: or (feminine) עֶדְנָה; from H5727 (עָדַן); KJV: delicate, delight, pleasure. See also H1040 (בֵּית עֵדֶן).

H5731 עֵדֶן (ʻÊden, ay'-den): Eden, the region of Adam's home. Origin: the same as H5730 (עֵדֶן) (masculine); KJV: Eden.

H5732 עִדָּן (ʻiddân, id-dawn'): a set time; technically, a year. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of H5708 (עֵד); KJV: time.

H5733 עַדְנָא (ʻAdnâʼ, ad-naw'): Adna, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5727 (עָדַן); pleasure; KJV: Adna.

H5734 עַדְנָה (ʻAdnâh, ad-naw'): Adnah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5727 (עָדַן); pleasure; KJV: Adnah.

H5735 עֲדְעָדָה (ʻĂdʻâdâh, ad-aw-daw'): Adadah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5712 (עֵדָה); festival; KJV: Adadah.

H5736 עֲדַף (ʻădaph, aw-daf'): to be (causatively, have) redundant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be more, odd number, be (have) over (and above), overplus, remain.

H5737 עֲדַר (ʻădar, aw-dar'): to arrange as a battle, a vineyard (to hoe); hence, to muster and so to miss (or find wanting). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dig, fail, keep (rank), lack.

H5738 עֶדֶר (ʻEder, eh'-der): Eder, an Israelite. Origin: from H5737 (עֲדַר); an arrangement (i.e. drove); KJV: Ader.

H5739 עֵדֶר (ʻêder, ay'-der): an arrangement, i.e. muster (of animals). Origin: from H5737 (עֲדַר); KJV: drove, flock, herd.

H5740 עֵדֶר (ʻÊder, ay'-der): Eder, the name of an Israelite and of two places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5739 (עֵדֶר); KJV: Edar, Eder.

H5741 עַדְרִיאֵל (ʻAdrîyʼêl, ad-ree-ale'): Adriel, an Israelite. Origin: from H5739 (עֵדֶר) and H410 (אֵל); flock of God; KJV: Adriel.

H5742 עָדָשׁ (ʻâdâsh, aw-dawsh'): a lentil. Origin: from an unused root of uncertain meaning; KJV: lentile.

H5743 עוּב (ʻûwb, oob): to be dense or dark, i.e. to becloud. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover with a cloud.

H5744 עוֹבֵד (ʻÔwbêd, o-bade'): Obed, the name of five Israelites. Origin: active participle of H5647 (עָבַד); serving; KJV: Obed.

H5745 עוֹבָל (ʻÔwbâl, o-bawl'): Obal, a son of Joktan. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Obal.

H5746 עוּג (ʻûwg, oog): to bake (round cakes on the hearth). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to gyrate; but used only as a denominative from H5692 (עֻגָּה), KJV: bake.

H5747 עוֹג (ʻÔwg, ogue): Og, a king of Bashan. Origin: probably from H5746 (עוּג); round; KJV: Og.

H5748 עוּגָב (ʻûwgâb, oo-gawb'): a reed-instrument of music. Origin: or עֻגָּב; from H5689 (עֲגַב) in the original sense of breathing; KJV: organ.

H5749 עוּד (ʻûwd, ood): to duplicate or repeat; by implication, to protest, testify (as by reiteration); intensively, to encompass, restore (as a sort of reduplication). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: admonish, charge, earnestly, lift up, protest, call (take) to record, relieve, rob, solemnly, stand upright, testify, give warning, (bear, call to, give, take to) witness.

H5750 עוֹד (ʻôwd, ode): properly, iteration or continuance; used only adverbially (with or without preposition), again, repeatedly, still, more. Origin: or עֹד; from H5749 (עוּד); KJV: again, [idiom] all life long, at all, besides, but, else, further(-more), henceforth, (any) longer, (any) more(-over), [idiom] once, since, (be) still, when, (good, the) while (having being), (as, because, whether, while) yet (within).

H5751 עוֹד (ʻôwd, ode): {properly, iteration or continuance; used only adverbially (with or without preposition), again, repeatedly, still, more}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5750 (עוֹד) KJV: while.

H5752 עוֹדֵד (ʻÔwdêd, o-dade'): Oded, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or עֹדֵד; from H5749 (עוּד); reiteration; KJV: Oded.

H5753 עָוָה (ʻâvâh, aw-vaw'): to crook, literally or figuratively. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: do amiss, bow down, make crooked, commit iniquity, pervert, (do) perverse(-ly), trouble, [idiom] turn, do wickedly, do wrong.

H5754 עַוָּה (ʻavvâh, av-vaw'): overthrow. Origin: intensive from H5753 (עָוָה) abbreviated; KJV: [idiom] overturn.

H5755 עִוָּה (ʻIvvâh, iv-vaw'): Ivvah or Avva, a region of Assyria. Origin: or עַוָּא; (2 Kings 17:24), for H5754 (עַוָּה); KJV: Ava, Ivah.

H5756 עוּז (ʻûwz, ooz): to be strong; causatively, to stregthen, i.e. (figuratively) to save (by flight). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather (self, self to flee), retire.

H5757 עַוִּי (ʻAvvîy, av-vee'): an Avvite or native of Avvah (only plural). Origin: patrial from H5755 (עִוָּה); KJV: Avims, Avites.

H5758 עִוְיָא (ʻivyâʼ, iv-yaw'): perverseness. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5753 (עָוָה); KJV: iniquity.

H5759 עֲוִיל (ʻăvîyl, av-eel'): a babe. Origin: from H5764 (עוּל); KJV: young child, little one.

H5760 עֲוִיל (ʻăvîyl, av-eel'): perverse (morally). Origin: from H5765 (עֲוַל); KJV: ungodly.

H5761 עַוִּים (ʻAvvîym, av-veem'): Avvim (as inhabited by Avvites), a place in Palestine (with the article prefix). Origin: plural of H5757 (עַוִּי); KJV: Avim.

H5762 עֲוִית (ʻĂvîyth, av-veeth'): Avvith (or Avvoth), a place in Palestine. Origin: or perhaps (עַיּוֹת (as if plural of H5857 (עַי)) (עַיוּת; from H5753 (עָוָה); ruin; KJV: Avith.

H5763 עוּל (ʻûwl, ool): to suckle, i.e. give milk. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: milch, (ewe great) with young.

H5764 עוּל (ʻûwl, ool): a babe. Origin: from H5763 (עוּל); KJV: sucking child, infant.

H5765 עֲוַל (ʻăval, aw-val'): to distort (morally). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deal unjustly, unrighteous.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5766 to H5892
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5766 עֶוֶל (ʻevel, eh'-vel): (moral) evil. Origin: or עָוֶל; and (feminine) עַוְלָה; or עוֹלָה; or עֹלָה; from H5765 (עֲוַל); KJV: iniquity, perverseness, unjust(-ly), unrighteousness(-ly); wicked(-ness).

H5767 עַוָּל (ʻavvâl, av-vawl'): evil (morally). Origin: intensive from H5765 (עֲוַל); KJV: unjust, unrighteous, wicked.

H5768 עוֹלֵל (ʻôwlêl, o-lale'): a suckling. Origin: or עֹלָל; from H5763 (עוּל); KJV: babe, (young) child, infant, little one.

H5769 עוֹלָם (ʻôwlâm, o-lawm'): properly, concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always. Origin: or עֹלָם; from H5956 (עָלַם); KJV: alway(-s), ancient (time), any more, continuance, eternal, (for, (n-)) ever(-lasting, -more, of old), lasting, long (time), (of) old (time), perpetual, at any time, (beginning of the) world ([phrase] without end). Compare H5331 (נֶצַח), H5703 (עַד).

H5770 עָוַן (ʻâvan, aw-van'): to watch (with jealosy). Origin: denominative from H5869 (עַיִן); KJV: eye.

H5771 עָוֺן (ʻâvôn, aw-vone'): perversity, i.e. (moral) evil. Origin: or עָווֹן; (2 Kings 7:9; Psalm 51:5 (H7 (אֲבַד))), from H5753 (עָוָה); KJV: fault, iniquity, mischeif, punishment (of iniquity), sin.

H5772 עוֹנָה (ʻôwnâh, o-naw'): sexual (cohabitation). Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to dwell together; KJV: duty of marriage.

H5773 עַוְעֶה (ʻavʻeh, av-eh'): perversity. Origin: from H5753 (עָוָה); KJV: [idiom] perverse.

H5774 עוּף (ʻûwph, oof): to fly; also (by implication of dimness) to faint (from the darkness of swooning). Origin: a primitive root; to cover (with wings or obscurity); hence (as denominative from H5775 (עוֹף)) KJV: brandish, be (wax) faint, flee away, fly (away), [idiom] set, shine forth, weary.

H5775 עוֹף (ʻôwph, ofe): a bird (as covered with feathers, or rather as covering with wings), often collectively. Origin: from H5774 (עוּף); KJV: bird, that flieth, flying, fowl.

H5776 עוֹף (ʻôwph, ofe): {a bird (as covered with feathers, or rather as covering with wings), often collectively}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5775 (עוֹף) KJV: fowl.

H5777 עוֹפֶרֶת (ʻôwphereth, o-feh'-reth): lead (from its dusty color). Origin: or עֹפֶרֶת; feminine participle active of H6080 (עָפַר); KJV: lead.

H5778 עוֹפַי (ʻÔwphay, o-fah'-ee): Ephai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5775 (עוֹף); birdlike; KJV: Ephai (from margin).

H5779 עוּץ (ʻûwts, oots): to consult. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: take advice ((counsel) together).

H5780 עוּץ (ʻÛwts, oots): Uts, a son of Aram, also a Seirite, and the regions settled by them. Origin: apparently from H5779 (עוּץ); consultation; KJV: Uz.

H5781 עוּק (ʻûwq, ook): to pack. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be pressed.

H5782 עוּר (ʻûwr, oor): to wake (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with through the idea of opening the eyes); KJV: (a-) wake(-n, up), lift up (self), [idiom] master, raise (up), stir up (self).

H5783 עוּר (ʻûwr, oor): to (be) bare. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be made naked.

H5784 עוּר (ʻûwr, oor): chaff (as the naked husk). Origin: (Aramaic) KJV: chaff.

H5785 עוֹר (ʻôwr, ore): skin (as naked); by implication, hide, leather. Origin: from H5783 (עוּר); KJV: hide, leather, skin.

H5786 עָוַר (ʻâvar, aw-var'): to blind. Origin: a primitive root (rather denominatively from H5785 (עוֹר) through the idea of a film over the eyes); KJV: blind, put out. See also H5895 (עַיִר).

H5787 עִוֵּר (ʻivvêr, iv-vare'): blind (literally or figuratively). Origin: intensive from H5786 (עָוַר); KJV: blind (men, people).

H5788 עִוָּרוֹן (ʻivvârôwn, iv-vaw-rone'): blindness. Origin: and (feminine) עַוֶּרֶת; from H5787 (עִוֵּר); KJV: blind(-ness).

H5789 עוּשׁ (ʻûwsh, oosh): to hasten. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: assemble self.

H5790 עוּת (ʻûwth, ooth): to hasten, i.e. succor. Origin: for H5789 (עוּשׁ); KJV: speak in season.

H5791 עָוַת (ʻâvath, aw-vath'): to wrest. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bow self, (make) crooked., falsifying, overthrow, deal perversely, pervert, subvert, turn upside down.

H5792 עַוָּתָה (ʻavvâthâh, av-vaw-thaw'): oppression. Origin: from H5791 (עָוַת); KJV: wrong.

H5793 עוּתַי (ʻÛwthay, oo-thah'-ee): Uthai, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5790 (עוּת); succoring; KJV: Uthai.

H5794 עַז (ʻaz, az): strong, vehement, harsh. Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז); KJV: fierce, [phrase] greedy, mighty, power, roughly, strong.

H5795 עֵז (ʻêz, aze): a she-goat (as strong), but masculine in plural (which also is used elliptically for goat's hair). Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז); KJV: (she) goat, kid.

H5796 עֵז (ʻêz, aze): {a she-goat (as strong), but masculine in plural (which also is used elliptically for goat's hair)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5795 (עֵז) KJV: goat.

H5797 עֹז (ʻôz, oze): strength in various applications (force, security, majesty, praise). Origin: or (fully) עוֹז; from H5810 (עָזַז); KJV: boldness, loud, might, power, strength, strong.

H5798 עֻזָּא (ʻUzzâʼ, ooz-zaw'): Uzza or Uzzah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or עֻזָּה; feminine of H5797 (עֹז); strength; KJV: Uzza, Uzzah.

H5799 עֲזָאזֵל (ʻăzâʼzêl, az-aw-zale'): goat of departure; the scapegoat. Origin: from H5795 (עֵז) and H235 (אָזַל); KJV: scapegoat.

H5800 עָזַב (ʻâzab, aw-zab'): to loosen, i.e. relinquish, permit, etc. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: commit self, fail, forsake, fortify, help, leave (destitute, off), refuse, [idiom] surely.

H5801 עִזָּבוֹן (ʻizzâbôwn, iz-zaw-bone'): trade, i.e. the place (mart) or the payment (revenue). Origin: from H5800 (עָזַב) in the sense of letting go (for a price, i.e. selling); KJV: fair, ware.

H5802 עַזְבּוּק (ʻAzbûwq, az-book'): Azbuk, an Israelite. Origin: from H5794 (עַז) and the root of H950 (בּוּקָה); stern depopulator; KJV: Azbuk.

H5803 עַזְגָּד (ʻAzgâd, az-gawd'): Azgad, an Israelite. Origin: from H5794 (עַז) and H1409 (גָּד); stern troop; KJV: Azgad.
