H5804 עַזָּה (ʻAzzâh, az-zaw'): Azzah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H5794 (עַז); strong; KJV: Azzah, Gaza.

H5805 עֲזוּבָה (ʻăzûwbâh, az-oo-baw'): desertion (of inhabitants). Origin: feminine passive participle of H5800 (עָזַב); KJV: forsaking.

H5806 עֲזוּבָה (ʻĂzûwbâh, az-oo-baw'): Azubah, the name of two Israelitesses. Origin: the same as H5805 (עֲזוּבָה); KJV: Azubah.

H5807 עֱזוּז (ʻĕzûwz, ez-ooz'): forcibleness. Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז); KJV: might, strength.

H5808 עִזּוּז (ʻizzûwz, iz-zooz'): forcible; collectively and concretely, an army. Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז); KJV: power, strong.

H5809 עַזּוּר (ʻAzzûwr, az-zoor'): Azzur, the name of three Israelites. Origin: or עַזֻּר; from H5826 (עָזַר); helpful; KJV: Azur, Azzur.

H5810 עָזַז (ʻâzaz, aw-zaz'): to be stout (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: harden, impudent, prevail, strengthen (self), be strong.

H5811 עָזָז (ʻÂzâz, aw-zawz'): Azaz, an Israelite. Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז); strong; KJV: Azaz.

H5812 עֲזַזְיָהוּ (ʻĂzazyâhûw, az-az-yaw'-hoo): Azazjah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has strengthened; KJV: Azaziah.

H5813 עֻזִּי (ʻUzzîy, ooz-zee'): Uzzi, the name of six Israelites. Origin: from H5810 (עָזַז); forceful; KJV: Uzzi.

H5814 עֻזִּיָּא (ʻUzzîyâʼ, ooz-zee-yaw'): Uzzija, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps for H5818 (עֻזִּיָּה); KJV: Uzzia.

H5815 עֲזִיאֵל (ʻĂzîyʼêl, az-ee-ale'): Aziel, an Israelite. Origin: from H5756 (עוּז) and H410 (אֵל); strengthened of God; KJV: Aziel. Compare H3268 (יַעֲזִיאֵל).

H5816 עֻזִּיאֵל (ʻUzzîyʼêl, ooz-zee-ale'): Uzziel, the name of six Israelites. Origin: from H5797 (עֹז) and H410 (אֵל); strength of God; KJV: Uzziel.

H5817 עׇזִּיאֵלִי (ʻOzzîyʼêlîy, oz-zee-ay-lee'): an Uzzielite (collectively) or descendants of Uzziel. Origin: patronymically from H5816 (עֻזִּיאֵל); KJV: Uzzielites.

H5818 עֻזִּיָּה (ʻUzzîyâh, ooz-zee-yaw'): Uzzijah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: or עֻזִּיָּהוּ; from H5797 (עֹז) and H3050 (יָהּ); strength of Jah; KJV: Uzziah.

H5819 עֲזִיזָא (ʻĂzîyzâʼ, az-ee-zaw'): Aziza, an Israelite. Origin: from H5756 (עוּז); strengthfulness; KJV: Aziza.

H5820 עַזְמָוֶת (ʻAzmâveth, az-maw'-veth): Azmaveth, the name of three Israelites and of a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5794 (עַז) and H4194 (מָוֶת); strong one of death; KJV: Azmaveth. See also H1041 (בֵּית עַזְמָוֶת).

H5821 עַזָּן (ʻAzzân, az-zawn'): Azzan, an Israelite. Origin: from H5794 (עַז); strong one; KJV: Azzan.

H5822 עׇזְנִיָּה (ʻoznîyâh, oz-nee-yaw'): probably the sea-eagle (from its strength). Origin: probably feminine of H5797 (עֹז); KJV: ospray.

H5823 עָזַק (ʻâzaq, aw-zak'): to grub over. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fence about.

H5824 עִזְקָא (ʻizqâʼ, iz-kaw'): a signet-ring (as engraved). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5823 (עָזַק); KJV: signet.

H5825 עֲזֵקָה (ʻĂzêqâh, az-ay-kaw'): Azekah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5823 (עָזַק); tilled; KJV: Azekah.

H5826 עָזַר (ʻâzar, aw-zar'): to surround, i.e. protect or aid. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: help, succour.

H5827 עֶזֶר (ʻEzer, eh'-zer): Ezer, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5826 (עָזַר); help; KJV: Ezer. Compare H5829 (עֵזֶר).

H5828 עֵזֶר (ʻêzer, ay'-zer): aid. Origin: from H5826 (עָזַר); KJV: help.

H5829 עֵזֶר (ʻÊzer, ay'-zer): Ezer, the name of four Israelites. Origin: the same as H5828 (עֵזֶר); KJV: Ezer. Compare H5827 (עֶזֶר).

H5830 עֶזְרָא (ʻEzrâʼ, ez-raw'): Ezra, an Israelite. Origin: a variation of H5833 (עֶזְרָה); KJV: Ezra.

H5831 עֶזְרָא (ʻEzrâʼ, ez-raw'): Ezra, an Israelite. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5830 (עֶזְרָא); KJV: Ezra.

H5832 עֲזַרְאֵל (ʻĂzarʼêl, az-ar-ale'): Azarel, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H5826 (עָזַר) and H410 (אֵל); God has helped; KJV: Azarael, Azareel.

H5833 עֶזְרָה (ʻezrâh, ez-raw'): aid. Origin: or עֶזְרָת; (Psalm 60:11 (13); Psalm 108:12 (13)), feminine of H5828 (עֵזֶר); KJV: help(-ed, -er).

H5834 עֶזְרָה (ʻEzrâh, ez-raw'): Ezrah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H5833 (עֶזְרָה); KJV: Ezrah.

H5835 עֲזָרָה (ʻăzârâh, az-aw-raw'): an inclosure; also a border. Origin: from H5826 (עָזַר) in its original meaning of surrounding; KJV: court, settle.

H5836 עֶזְרִי (ʻEzrîy, ez-ree'): Ezri, an Israelite. Origin: from H5828 (עֵזֶר); helpful; KJV: Ezri.

H5837 עַזְרִיאֵל (ʻAzrîyʼêl, az-ree-ale'): Azriel, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H5828 (עֵזֶר) and H410 (אֵל); help of God; KJV: Azriel.

H5838 עֲזַרְיָה (ʻĂzaryâh, az-ar-yaw'): Azarjah, the name of nineteen Israelites. Origin: or עֲזַרְיָהוּ; from H5826 (עָזַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has helped; KJV: Azariah.

H5839 עֲזַרְיָה (ʻĂzaryâh, az-ar-yaw'): Azarjah, one of Daniel's companions. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5838 (עֲזַרְיָה); KJV: Azariah.

H5840 עַזְרִיקָם (ʻAzrîyqâm, az-ree-kawm'): Azrikam, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H5828 (עֵזֶר) and active participle of H6965 (קוּם); help of an enemy; KJV: Azrikam.

H5841 עַזָּתִי (ʻAzzâthîy, az-zaw-thee'): an Azzathite or inhabitant of Azzah. Origin: patrial from H5804 (עַזָּה); KJV: Gazathite, Gazite.

H5842 עֵט (ʻêṭ, ate): a stylus or marking stick. Origin: from H5860 (עִיט) (contracted) in the sense of swooping, i.e. side-long stroke; KJV: pen.

H5843 עֵטָא (ʻêṭâʼ, ay-taw'): prudence. Origin: (Aramaic) from H3272 (יְעַט); KJV: counsel.

H5844 עָטָה (ʻâṭâh, aw-taw'): to wrap, i.e. cover, veil, cloth, or roll. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: array self, be clad, (put a) cover (-ing, self), fill, put on, [idiom] surely, turn aside.

H5845 עֲטִין (ʻăṭîyn, at-een'): a receptacle (for milk, i.e. pail; figuratively, breast). Origin: from an unused root meaning apparently to contain; KJV: breast.

H5846 עֲטִישָׁה (ʻăṭîyshâh, at-ee-shaw'): sneezing. Origin: from an unused root meaning to sneeze; KJV: sneezing.

H5847 עֲטַלֵּף (ʻăṭallêph, at-al-lafe'): a bat. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: bat.

H5848 עָטַף (ʻâṭaph, aw-taf'): to shroud, i.e. clothe (whether transitive or reflex.); hence (from the idea of darkness) to languish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover (over), fail, faint, feebler, hide self, be overwhelmed, swoon.

H5849 עָטַר (ʻâṭar, aw-tar'): to encircle (for attack or protection); especially to crown (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: compass, crown.

H5850 עֲטָרָה (ʻăṭârâh, at-aw-raw'): a crown. Origin: from H5849 (עָטַר); KJV: crown.

H5851 עֲטָרָה (ʻĂṭârâh, at-aw-raw'): Atarah, an Israelitess. Origin: the same as H5850 (עֲטָרָה); KJV: Atarah.

H5852 עֲטָרוֹת (ʻĂṭârôwth, at-aw-roth'): Ataroth, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine. Origin: or עֲטָרֹת; plural of H5850 (עֲטָרָה); KJV: Ataroth.

H5853 עַטְרוֹת אַדָּר (ʻAṭrôwth ʼAddâr, at-roth' ad-dawr'): Atroth-Addar, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H5852 (עֲטָרוֹת) and H146 (אַדָּר); crowns of Addar; KJV: Ataroth-adar(-addar).

H5854 עַטְרוֹת בֵּית יוֹאָב (ʻAṭrôwth bêyth Yôwʼâb, at-roth' bayth yoawb'): Atroth-beth-Joab, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H5852 (עֲטָרוֹת) and H1004 (בַּיִת) and H3097 (יוֹאָב); crowns of the house of Joab; KJV: Ataroth the house of Joab.

H5855 עַטְרוֹת שׁוֹפָן (ʻAṭrôwth Shôwphân, at-roth' sho-fawn'): Atroth-Shophan, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H5852 (עֲטָרוֹת) and a name otherwise unused (being from the same as H8226 (שָׂפַן)) meaning hidden; crowns of Shophan; KJV: Atroth, Shophan (as if two places).

H5856 עִי (ʻîy, ee): a ruin (as if overturned). Origin: from H5753 (עָוָה); KJV: heap.

H5857 עַי (ʻAy, ah'ee): Ai, Aja or Ajath, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (feminine) עַיָּא; (Nehemiah 11:31), or עַיָּת; (Isaiah 10:28), for H5856 (עִי); KJV: Ai, Aija, Aijath, Hai.

H5858 עֵיבָל (ʻÊybâl, ay-bawl'): Ebal, a mountain of Palestine. Origin: perhaps from an unused root probably meaning to be bald; bare; KJV: Ebal.

H5859 עִיּוֹן (ʻÎyôwn, ee-yone'): Ijon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5856 (עִי); ruin; KJV: Ijon.

H5860 עִיט (ʻîyṭ, eet): to swoop down upon (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fly, rail.

H5861 עַיִט (ʻayiṭ, ah'-yit): a hawk or other bird of prey. Origin: from H5860 (עִיט); KJV: bird, fowl, ravenous (bird).

H5862 עֵיטָם (ʻÊyṭâm, ay-tawm'): Etam, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5861 (עַיִט); hawk-ground; KJV: Etam.

H5863 עִיֵּי הָעֲבָרִים (ʻÎyêy hâ-ʻĂbârîym, ee-yay' haw-ab-aw-reem'): Ije-ha-Abarim, a place near Palestine. Origin: from the plural of H5856 (עִי) and the plural of the active participle of H5674 (עָבַר) with the article interposed; ruins of the passers; KJV: Ije-abarim.

H5864 עִיִּים (ʻÎyîym, ee-yeem'): Ijim, a place in the Desert. Origin: plural of H5856 (עִי); ruins; KJV: Iim.

H5865 עֵילוֹם (ʻêylôwm, ay-lome'): {concealed, i.e. the vanishing point; generally, time out of mind (past or future), i.e. (practically) eternity; frequentatively, adverbial (especially with prepositional prefix) always}. Origin: for H5769 (עוֹלָם) KJV: ever.

H5866 עִילַי (ʻÎylay, ee-lah'-ee): Ilai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); elevated; KJV: Ilai.

H5867 עֵילָם (ʻÊylâm, ay-lawm'): Elam, a son of Shem and his descendants, with their country; also of six Israelites. Origin: or עוֹלָם; (Ezra 10:2; Jeremiah 49:36), probably from H5956 (עָלַם); hidden, i.e. distant; KJV: Elam.

H5868 עֲיָם (ʻăyâm, ah-yawm'): probably meaning strength. Origin: of doubtful origin and authenticity; KJV: mighty.

H5869 עַיִן (ʻayin, ah'-yin): an eye (literally or figuratively); by analogy, a fountain (as the eye of the landscape). Origin: probably a primitive word; KJV: affliction, outward appearance, [phrase] before, [phrase] think best, colour, conceit, [phrase] be content, countenance, [phrase] displease, eye((-brow), (-d), -sight), face, [phrase] favour, fountain, furrow (from the margin), [idiom] him, [phrase] humble, knowledge, look, ([phrase] well), [idiom] me, open(-ly), [phrase] (not) please, presence, [phrase] regard, resemblance, sight, [idiom] thee, [idiom] them, [phrase] think, [idiom] us, well, [idiom] you(-rselves).

H5870 עַיִן (ʻayin, ah'-yin): an eye. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5869 (עַיִן); KJV: eye.

H5871 עַיִן (ʻAyin, ah'-yin): Ajin, the name (thus simply) of two places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5869 (עַיִן); fountain; KJV: Ain.

H5872 עֵין גֶּדִי (ʻÊyn Gedîy, ane geh'-dee): En-Gedi, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and H1423 (גְּדִי); fountain of a kid; KJV: En-gedi.

H5873 עֵין גַּנִּים (ʻÊyn Gannîym, ane gan-neem'): En-Gannim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and the plural of H1588 (גַּן); fountain of gardens; KJV: En-gannim.

H5874 עֵין־דֹּאר (ʻÊyn-Dôʼr, ane-dore'): En-Dor, a place in Palestine. Origin: or עֵין דּוֹר; or עֵין־דֹּר; from H5869 (עַיִן) and H1755 (דּוֹר); fountain of dwelling; KJV: En-dor.

H5875 עֵין הַקּוֹרֵא (ʻÊyn haq-Qôwrêʼ, ane-hak-ko-ray'): En-hak-Kore, a place near Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and the active participle of H7121 (קָרָא); fountain of One calling; KJV: En-hakhore.

H5876 עֵין חַדָּה (ʻÊyn Chaddâh, ane khad-daw'): En-Chaddah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and the feminine of a derivative from H2300 (חָדַד); fountain of sharpness; KJV: En-haddah.

H5877 עֵין חָצוֹר (ʻÊyn Châtsôwr, ane khaw-tsore'): En-Chatsor, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and the same as H2674 (חָצוֹר); fountain of a village; KJV: En-hazor.

H5878 עֵין חֲרֹד (ʻÊyn Chărôd, ane khar-ode'): En-Charod, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and a derivative of H2729 (חָרַד); fountain of trembling; KJV: well of Harod.

H5879 עֵינַיִם (ʻÊynayim, ay-nah'-yim): Enajim or Enam, a place in Palestine. Origin: or עֵינָם; dual of H5869 (עַיִן); double fountain; KJV: Enaim, openly (Genesis 38:21).

H5880 עֵין מִשְׁפָּט (ʻÊyn Mishpâṭ, ane mish-pawt'): En-Mishpat, a place near Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and H4941 (מִשְׁפָּט); fountain of judgment; KJV: En-mishpat.

H5881 עֵינָן (ʻÊynân, ay-nawn'): Enan, an Israelite. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן); having eyes; KJV: Enan. Compare H2704 (חֲצַר עֵינָן).

H5882 עֵין עֶגְלַיִם (ʻÊyn ʻEglayim, ane eg-lah'-yim): En-Eglajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: עַיִן and the dual of H5695 (עֵגֶל); fountain of two calves; KJV: En-eglaim.

H5883 עֵין רֹגֵל (ʻÊyn Rôgêl, ane ro-gale'): En-Rogel, a place near Jerusalem. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and the active participle of H7270 (רָגַל); fountain of a traveller; KJV: En-rogel.

H5884 עֵין רִמּוֹן (ʻÊyn Rimmôwn, ane rim-mone'): En-Rimmon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and H7416 (רִמּוֹן); fountain of a pomegranate; KJV: En-rimmon.

H5885 עֵין שֶׁמֶשׁ (ʻÊyn Shemesh, ane sheh'-mesh): En-Shemesh, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); fountain of the sun; KJV: Enshemesh.

H5886 עֵין תַּנִּים (ʻÊyn Tannîym, ane tan-neem'): En-Tannim, a pool near Jerusalem. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and the plural of H8565 (תַּן); fountain of jackals; KJV: dragon well.

H5887 עֵין תַּפּוּחַ (ʻÊyn Tappûwach, ane tap-poo'-akh): En-Tappuach, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5869 (עַיִן) and H8598 (תַּפּוּחַ); fountain of an apple-tree; KJV: En-tappuah.

H5888 עָיֵף (ʻâyêph, aw-yafe'): to languish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be wearied.

H5889 עָיֵף (ʻâyêph, aw-yafe'): languid. Origin: from H5888 (עָיֵף); KJV: faint, thirsty, weary.

H5890 עֵיפָה (ʻêyphâh, ay-faw'): obscurity (as if from covering). Origin: feminine from H5774 (עוּף); KJV: darkness.

H5891 עֵיפָה (ʻÊyphâh, ay-faw'): Ephah, the name of a son of Midian, and of the region settled by him; also of an Israelite and of an Israelitess. Origin: the same as H5890 (עֵיפָה); KJV: Ephah.

H5892 עִיר (ʻîyr, eer): a city (a place guarded by waking or a watch) in the widest sense (even of a mere encampment or post). Origin: or (in the plural) עָר; or עָיַר; (Judges 10:4), from H5782 (עוּר) KJV: Ai (from margin), city, court (from margin), town.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H5893 to H6012
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H5893 עִיר (ʻÎyr, eer): Ir, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H5892 (עִיר); KJV: Ir.

H5894 עִיר (ʻîyr, eer): a watcher, i.e. an angel (as guardian). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H5782 (עוּר); KJV: watcher.

H5895 עַיִר (ʻayir, ah'-yeer): properly, a young ass (as just broken to a load); hence an ass-colt. Origin: from H5782 (עוּר) in the sense of raising (i.e. bearing a burden); KJV: (ass) colt, foal, young ass.

H5896 עִירָא (ʻÎyrâʼ, ee-raw'): Ira, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H5782 (עוּר); wakefulness; KJV: Ira.

H5897 עִירָד (ʻÎyrâd, ee-rawd'): Irad, an antediluvian. Origin: from the same as H6166 (עֲרָד); fugitive; KJV: Irad.

H5898 עִיר הַמֶּלַח (ʻÎyr ham-Melach, eer ham-meh'-lakh): Irham-Melach, a place near Palestine. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר) and H4417 (מֶלַח) with the article of substance interp.; city of (the) salt; KJV: the city of salt.

H5899 עִיר הַתְּמָרִים (ʻÎyr hat-Tᵉmârîym, eer hat-tem-aw-reem'): Ir-hat-Temarim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר) and the plural of H8558 (תָּמָר) with the article interpolated; city of the palmtrees; KJV: the city of palmtrees.

H5900 עִירוּ (ʻÎyrûw, ee-roo'): Iru, an Israelite. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר); a citizen; KJV: Iru.

H5901 עִירִי (ʻÎyrîy, ee-ree'): Iri, an Israelite. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר); urbane; KJV: Iri.

H5902 עִירָם (ʻÎyrâm, ee-rawm'): Iram, an Idumaean. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר); city-wise; KJV: Iram.

H5903 עֵירֹם (ʻêyrôm, ay-rome'): nudity. Origin: or עֵרֹם; from H6191 (עָרַם); KJV: naked(-ness).

H5904 עִיר נָחָשׁ (ʻÎyr Nâchâsh, eer naw-khawsh'): Ir-Nachash, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר) and H5175 (נָחָשׁ); city of a serpent; KJV: Irnahash.

H5905 עִיר שֶׁמֶשׁ (ʻÎyr Shemesh, eer sheh'-mesh): Ir-Shemesh, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5892 (עִיר) and H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); city of the sun; KJV: Irshemesh.

H5906 עַיִשׁ (ʻAyish, ah'-yish): the constellation of the Great Bear (perhaps from its migration through the heavens). Origin: or עָשׁ; from H5789 (עוּשׁ); KJV: Arcturus.

H5907 עַכְבּוֹר (ʻAkbôwr, ak-bore'): Akbor, the name of an Idumaean and of two Israelites. Origin: probably for H5909 (עַכְבָּר); KJV: Achbor.

H5908 עַכָּבִישׁ (ʻakkâbîysh, ak-kaw-beesh'): a spider (as weaving a network). Origin: probably from an unused root in the literal sense of entangling; KJV: spider.

H5909 עַכְבָּר (ʻakbâr, ak-bawr'): a mouse (as nibbling). Origin: probably from the same as H5908 (עַכָּבִישׁ) in the secondary sense of attacking; KJV: mouse.

H5910 עַכּוֹ (ʻAkkôw, ak-ko'): Akko (from its situation on a bay). Origin: apparently from an unused root meaning to hem in; KJV: Accho.

H5911 עָכוֹר (ʻÂkôwr, aw-kore'): Akor, the name of a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5916 (עָכַר); troubled; KJV: Achor.

H5912 עָכָן (ʻÂkân, aw-kawn'): Akan, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to trouble; troublesome; KJV: Achan. Compare H5917 (עָכָר).

H5913 עָכַס (ʻâkaç, aw-kas'): to put on anklets. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to tie, specifically, with fetters; but used only as denominative from H5914 (עֶכֶס); KJV: make a tinkling ornament.

H5914 עֶכֶס (ʻekeç, eh'-kes): a fetter; hence, an anklet. Origin: from H5913 (עָכַס); KJV: stocks, tinkling ornament.

H5915 עַכְסָה (ʻAkçâh, ak-saw'): Aksah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine of H5914 (עֶכֶס); anklet; KJV: Achsah.

H5916 עָכַר (ʻâkar, aw-kar'): properly, to roil water; figuratively, to disturb or affict. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: trouble, stir.

H5917 עָכָר (ʻÂkâr, aw-kawr'): Akar, an Israelite. Origin: from H5916 (עָכַר); troublesome; KJV: Achar. Compare H5912 (עָכָן).

H5918 עׇכְרָן (ʻOkrân, ok-rawn'): Okran, an Israelite. Origin: from H5916 (עָכַר); muddler; KJV: Ocran.

H5919 עַכְשׁוּב (ʻakshûwb, ak-shoob'): an asp (from lurking coiled up). Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to coil; KJV: adder.

H5920 עַל (ʻal, al): properly, the top; specifically, the highest (i.e. God); also (adverb) aloft, to Jehovah. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: above, high, most High.

H5921 עַל (ʻal, al): above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications. Origin: properly, the same as H5920 (עַל) used as a preposition (in the singular or plural often with prefix, or as conjunction with a particle following); KJV: above, according to(-ly), after, (as) against, among, and, [idiom] as, at, because of, beside (the rest of), between, beyond the time, [idiom] both and, by (reason of), [idiom] had the charge of, concerning for, in (that), (forth, out) of, (from) (off), (up-) on, over, than, through(-out), to, touching, [idiom] with.

H5922 עַל (ʻal, al): {above, over, upon, or against (yet always in this last relation with a downward aspect) in a great variety of applications}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5921 (עַל) KJV: about, against, concerning, for, (there-) fore, from, in, [idiom] more, of, (there-, up-) on, (in-) to, [phrase] why with.

H5923 עֹל (ʻôl, ole): a yoke (as imposed on the neck), literally or figuratively. Origin: or עוֹל; from H5953 (עָלַל); KJV: yoke.

H5924 עֵלָּא (ʻêllâʼ, ale-law'): above. Origin: (Aramaic) from H5922 (עַל); KJV: over.

H5925 עֻלָּא (ʻUllâʼ, ool-law'): Ulla, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H5923 (עֹל); burden; KJV: Ulla.

H5926 עִלֵּג (ʻillêg, il-layg'): stuttering. Origin: from an unused root meaning to stutter; KJV: stammerer.

H5927 עָלָה (ʻâlâh, aw-law'): to ascend, intransitively (be high) or actively (mount); used in a great variety of senses, primary and secondary, literal and figurative. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: arise (up), (cause to) ascend up, at once, break (the day) (up), bring (up), (cause to) burn, carry up, cast up, [phrase] shew, climb (up), (cause to, make to) come (up), cut off, dawn, depart, exalt, excel, fall, fetch up, get up, (make to) go (away, up); grow (over) increase, lay, leap, levy, lift (self) up, light, (make) up, [idiom] mention, mount up, offer, make to pay, [phrase] perfect, prefer, put (on), raise, recover, restore, (make to) rise (up), scale, set (up), shoot forth (up), (begin to) spring (up), stir up, take away (up), work.

H5928 עֲלָה (ʻălâh, al-law'): a holocaust. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5930 (עֹלָה); KJV: burnt offering.

H5929 עָלֶה (ʻâleh, aw-leh'): a leaf (as coming up on a tree); collectively, foliage. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: branch, leaf.

H5930 עֹלָה (ʻôlâh, o-law'): a step or (collectively, stairs, as ascending); usually a holocaust (as going up in smoke). Origin: or עוֹלָה; feminine active participle of H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: ascent, burnt offering (sacrifice), go up to. See also H5766 (עֶוֶל).

H5931 עִלָּה (ʻillâh, il-law'): a pretext (as arising artificially). Origin: (Aramaic) feminine from a root corresponding to H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: occasion.

H5932 עַלְוָה (ʻalvâh, al-vaw'): moral perverseness. Origin: for H5766 (עֶוֶל); KJV: iniquity.

H5933 עַלְוָה (ʻAlvâh, al-vaw'): Alvah or Aljah, an Idumaean. Origin: or עַליָה; the same as H5932 (עַלְוָה); KJV: Aliah, Alvah.

H5934 עָלוּם (ʻâlûwm, aw-loom'): (only in plural as abstract) adolescence; figuratively, vigor. Origin: passive participle of H5956 (עָלַם) in the denominative sense of H5958 (עֶלֶם); KJV: youth.

H5935 עַלְוָן (ʻAlvân, al-vawn'): Alvan or Aljan, an Idumaean. Origin: or עַלְיָן; from H5927 (עָלָה); lofty; KJV: Alian, Alvan.

H5936 עֲלוּקָה (ʻălûwqâh, al-oo-kaw'): the leech. Origin: feminine passive participle of an unused root meaning to suck; KJV: horse-leech.

H5937 עָלַז (ʻâlaz, aw-laz'): to jump for joy, i.e. exult. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be joyful, rejoice, triumph.

H5938 עָלֵז (ʻâlêz, aw-laze'): exultant. Origin: from H5937 (עָלַז); KJV: that rejoiceth.

H5939 עֲלָטָה (ʻălâṭâh, al-aw-taw'): dusk. Origin: feminine from an unused root meaning to cover; KJV: dark, twilight.

H5940 עֱלִי (ʻĕlîy, el-ee'): a pestle (as lifted). Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: pestle.

H5941 עֵלִי (ʻÊlîy, ay-lee'): Eli, an Israelite highpriest. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); lofty; KJV: Eli.

H5942 עִלִּי (ʻillîy, il-lee'): high; i.e. comparative. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: upper.

H5943 עִלַּי (ʻillay, il-lah'-ee): supreme (i.e. God). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5942 (עִלִּי); KJV: (most) high.

H5944 עֲלִיָּה (ʻălîyâh, al-ee-yaw'): something lofty, i.e. a stair-way; also a second-story room (or even one on the roof); figuratively, the sky. Origin: feminine from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: ascent, (upper) chamber, going up, loft, parlour.

H5945 עֶלְיוֹן (ʻelyôwn, el-yone'): an elevation, i.e. (adj.) lofty (compar.); as title, the Supreme. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: (Most, on) high(-er, -est), upper(-most).

H5946 עֶלְיוֹן (ʻelyôwn, el-yone'): the Supreme. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5945 (עֶלְיוֹן); KJV: Most high.

H5947 עַלִּיז (ʻallîyz, al-leez'): exultant. Origin: from H5937 (עָלַז); KJV: joyous, (that) rejoice(-ing)

H5948 עֲלִיל (ʻălîyl, al-eel'): probably a crucible (as working over the metal). Origin: from H5953 (עָלַל) in the sense of completing; KJV: furnace.

H5949 עֲלִילָה (ʻălîylâh, al-ee-law'): an exploit (of God), or a performance (of man, often in a bad sense); by implication, an opportunity. Origin: or עֲלִלָה; from H5953 (עָלַל) in the sense of effecting; KJV: act(-ion), deed, doing, invention, occasion, work.

H5950 עֲלִילִיָּה (ʻălîylîyâh, al-ee-lee-yaw'): (miraculous) execution. Origin: for H5949 (עֲלִילָה); KJV: work.

H5951 עֲלִיצוּת (ʻălîytsûwth, al-ee-tsooth'): exultation. Origin: from H5970 (עָלַץ); KJV: rejoicing.

H5952 עַלִּית (ʻallîyth, al-leeth'): a second-story room. Origin: from H5927 (עָלָה); KJV: chamber. Compare H5944 (עֲלִיָּה).

H5953 עָלַל (ʻâlal, aw-lal'): to effect thoroughly; specifically, to glean (also figuratively); by implication (in a bad sense) to overdo, i.e. maltreat, be saucy to, pain, impose (also literal). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abuse, affect, [idiom] child, defile, do, glean, mock, practise, thoroughly, work (wonderfully).

H5954 עֲלַל (ʻălal, al-al'): to enter; causatively, to introduce. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5953 (עָלַל) (in the sense of thrusting oneself in), KJV: bring in, come in, go in.

H5955 עֹלֵלָה (ʻôlêlâh, o-lay-law'): only in plural gleanings; by extension gleaning-time. Origin: feminine active participle of H5953 (עָלַל); KJV: (gleaning) (of the) grapes, grapegleanings.

H5956 עָלַם (ʻâlam, aw-lam'): to veil from sight, i.e. conceal (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] any ways, blind, dissembler, hide (self), secret (thing).

H5957 עָלַם (ʻâlam, aw-lam'): remote time, i.e. the future or past indefinitely; often adverb, forever. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5769 (עוֹלָם); KJV: for (n-)ever (lasting), old.

H5958 עֶלֶם (ʻelem, eh'-lem): properly, something kept out of sight, i.e. a lad. Origin: from H5956 (עָלַם); (compare H5959 (עַלְמָה)) KJV: young man, stripling.

H5959 עַלְמָה (ʻalmâh, al-maw'): a lass (as veiled or private). Origin: feminine of H5958 (עֶלֶם); KJV: damsel, maid, virgin.

H5960 עַלְמוֹן (ʻAlmôwn, al-mone'): Almon, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5956 (עָלַם); hidden; See also H5963 (עַלְמֹן דִּבְלָתָיְמָה).

H5961 עֲלָמוֹת (ʻĂlâmôwth, al-aw-moth'): properly, girls, i.e. the soprano or female voice, perhaps falsetto. Origin: plural of H5959 (עַלְמָה); KJV: Alamoth.

H5962 עַלְמִי (ʻAlmîy, al-mee'): an Elamite or inhabitant of Elam. Origin: (Aramaic) patrial from a name corresponding to H5867 (עֵילָם) contracted; KJV: Elamite.

H5963 עַלְמֹן דִּבְלָתָיְמָה (ʻAlmôn Diblâthâyᵉmâh, al-mone' dib-lawthaw'-yem-aw): Almon-Diblathajemah, a place in Moab. Origin: from the same as H5960 (עַלְמוֹן) and the dual of H1960 (הֻיְּדָה) (compare H1015 (בֵּית דִּבְלָתַיִם)) with enclitic of direction; Almon towards Diblathajim; KJV: Almondilathaim.

H5964 עָלֶמֶת (ʻÂlemeth, aw-leh'-meth): Alemeth, the name of a place in Palestine and of two Israelites. Origin: from H5956 (עָלַם); a covering; KJV: Alameth, Alemeth.

H5965 עָלַס (ʻâlaç, aw-las'): to leap for joy, i.e. exult, wave joyously. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] peacock, rejoice, solace self.

H5966 עָלַע (ʻâlaʻ, aw-lah'): to sip up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: suck up.

H5967 עֲלַע (ʻălaʻ, al-ah'): a rib. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6763 (צֵלָע); KJV: rib.

H5968 עָלַף (ʻâlaph, aw-laf'): to veil or cover; figuratively, to be languid. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: faint, overlaid, wrap self.

H5969 עֻלְפֶּה (ʻulpeh, ool-peh'): an envelope, i.e. (figuratively) mourning. Origin: from H5968 (עָלַף); KJV: fainted.

H5970 עָלַץ (ʻâlats, aw-lats'): to jump for joy, i.e. exult. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be joyful, rejoice, triumph.

H5971 עַם (ʻam, am): a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock. Origin: from H6004 (עָמַם); KJV: folk, men, nation, people.

H5972 עַם (ʻam, am): {a people (as a congregated unit); specifically, a tribe (as those of Israel); hence (collectively) troops or attendants; figuratively, a flock}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5971 (עַם) KJV: people.

H5973 עִם (ʻim, eem): adverb or preposition, with (i.e. in conjunction with), in varied applications; specifically, equally with; often with prepositional prefix (and then usually unrepresented in English). Origin: from H6004 (עָמַם); KJV: accompanying, against, and, as ([idiom] long as), before, beside, by (reason of), for all, from (among, between), in, like, more than, of, (un-) to, with(-al).

H5974 עִם (ʻim, eem): {adverb or preposition, with (i.e. in conjunction with), in varied applications; specifically, equally with; often with prepositional prefix (and then usually unrepresented in English)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H5973 (עִם) KJV: by, from, like, to(-ward), with.

H5975 עָמַד (ʻâmad, aw-mad'): to stand, in various relations (literal and figurative, intransitive and transitive). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abide (behind), appoint, arise, cease, confirm, continue, dwell, be employed, endure, establish, leave, make, ordain, be (over), place, (be) present (self), raise up, remain, repair, [phrase] serve, set (forth, over, -tle, up), (make to, make to be at a, with-) stand (by, fast, firm, still, up), (be at a) stay (up), tarry.

H5976 עָמַד (ʻâmad, aw-mad'): to shake. Origin: for H4571 (מָעַד); KJV: be at a stand.

H5977 עֹמֶד (ʻômed, o'-med): a spot (as being fixed). Origin: from H5975 (עָמַד); KJV: place, ([phrase] where) stood, upright.

H5978 עִמָּד (ʻimmâd, im-mawd'): along with. Origin: prolonged for H5973 (עִם); KJV: against, by, from, [phrase] me, [phrase] mine, of, [phrase] that I take, unto, upon, with(-in.)

H5979 עֶמְדָּה (ʻemdâh, em-daw'): a station, i.e. domicile. Origin: from H5975 (עָמַד); KJV: standing.

H5980 עֻמָּה (ʻummâh, oom-maw'): conjunction, i.e. society; mostly adverb or preposition (with prepositional prefix), near, beside, along with. Origin: from H6004 (עָמַם); KJV: (over) against, at, beside, hard by, in points.

H5981 עֻמָּה (ʻUmmâh, oom-maw'): Ummah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H5980 (עֻמָּה); association; KJV: Ummah.

H5982 עַמּוּד (ʻammûwd, am-mood'): a column (as standing); also a stand, i.e. platform. Origin: or עַמֻּד; from H5975 (עָמַד); KJV: [idiom] apiece, pillar.

H5983 עַמּוֹן (ʻAmmôwn, am-mone'): Ammon, a son of Lot; also his posterity and their country. Origin: from H5971 (עַם); tribal, i.e. inbred; KJV: Ammon, Ammonites.

H5984 עַמּוֹנִי (ʻAmmôwnîy, am-mo-nee'): an Ammonite or (the adjective) Ammonitish. Origin: patronymically from H5983 (עַמּוֹן); KJV: Ammonite(-s).

H5985 עַמּוֹנִית (ʻAmmôwnîyth, am-mo-neeth'): an Ammonitess. Origin: feminine of H5984 (עַמּוֹנִי); KJV: Ammonite(-ss).

H5986 עָמוֹס (ʻÂmôwç, aw-moce'): Amos, an Israelite prophet. Origin: from H6006 (עָמַס); burdensome; KJV: Amos.

H5987 עָמוֹק (ʻÂmôwq, aw-moke'): Amok, an Israelite. Origin: from H6009 (עָמַק); deep; KJV: Amok.

H5988 עַמִּיאֵל (ʻAmmîyʼêl, am-mee-ale'): Ammiel, the name of three or four Israelites. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H410 (אֵל); people of God; KJV: Ammiel.

H5989 עַמִּיהוּד (ʻAmmîyhûwd, am-mee-hood'): Ammihud, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H1935 (הוֹד); people of splendor; KJV: Ammihud.

H5990 עַמִּיזָבָד (ʻAmmîyzâbâd, am-mee-zaw-bawd'): Ammizabad, an Israelite. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H2064 (זָבַד); people of endowment; KJV: Ammizabad.

H5991 עַמִּיחוּר (ʻAmmîychûwr, am-mee-khoor'): Ammichur, a Syrian prince. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H2353 (חוּר); people of nobility; KJV: Ammihud (from the margin).

H5992 עַמִּינָדָב (ʻAmmîynâdâb, am-mee-naw-dawb'): Amminadab, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H5068 (נָדַב); people of liberality; KJV: Amminadab.

H5993 עַמִּי נָדִיב (ʻAmmîy Nâdîyb, am-mee' naw-deeb'): Ammi-Nadib, probably an Israelite. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H5081 (נָדִיב); my people (is) liberal; KJV: Amminadib.

H5994 עֲמִיק (ʻămîyq, am-eek'): profound, i.e. unsearchable. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6012 (עָמֵק); KJV: deep.

H5995 עָמִיר (ʻâmîyr, aw-meer'): a bunch of grain. Origin: from H6014 (עָמַר); KJV: handful, sheaf.

H5996 עַמִּישַׁדַּי (ʻAmmîyshadday, am-mee-shad-dah'ee): Ammishaddai, an Israelite. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H7706 (שַׁדַּי); people of (the) Almighty; KJV: Ammishaddai.

H5997 עָמִית (ʻâmîyth, aw-meeth'): companionship; hence (concretely) a comrade or kindred man. Origin: from a primitive root meaning to associate; KJV: another, fellow, neighbour.

H5998 עָמַל (ʻâmal, aw-mal'): to toil, i.e. work severely and with irksomeness. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (take) labour (in).

H5999 עָמָל (ʻâmâl, aw-mawl'): toil, i.e. wearing effort; hence, worry, wheth. of body or mind. Origin: from H5998 (עָמַל); KJV: grievance(-vousness), iniquity, labour, mischief, miserable(-sery), pain(-ful), perverseness, sorrow, toil, travail, trouble, wearisome, wickedness.

H6000 עָמָל (ʻÂmâl, aw-mawl'): Amal, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H5999 (עָמָל); KJV: Amal.

H6001 עָמֵל (ʻâmêl, aw-male'): toiling; concretely, a laborer; figuratively, sorrowful. Origin: from H5998 (עָמַל); KJV: that laboureth, that is a misery, had taken (labour), wicked, workman.

H6002 עֲמָלֵק (ʻĂmâlêq, am-aw-lake'): Amalek, a descendant of Esau; also his posterity and their country. Origin: probably of foreign origin; KJV: Amalek.

H6003 עֲמָלֵקִי (ʻĂmâlêqîy, am-aw-lay-kee'): an Amalekite (or collectively the Amalekites) or descendants of Amalek. Origin: patronymically from H6002 (עֲמָלֵק); KJV: Amalekite(-s).

H6004 עָמַם (ʻâmam, aw-mam'): to associate; by implication, to overshadow (by huddling together). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: become dim, hide.

H6005 עִמָּנוּאֵל (ʻImmânûwʼêl, im-maw-noo-ale'): Immanuel, a type name of Isaiah's son. Origin: from H5973 (עִם) and with a pronominal suffix inserted; with us (is) God; KJV: Immanuel.

H6006 עָמַס (ʻâmaç, aw-mas'): to load, i.e. impose aburden (or figuratively, infliction). Origin: or עָמַשׂ; a primitive root; KJV: be borne, (heavy) burden (self), lade, load, put.

H6007 עֲמַסְיָה (ʻĂmaçyâh, am-as-yaw'): Amasjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H6006 (עָמַס) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has loaded; KJV: Amasiah.

H6008 עַמְעָד (ʻAmʻâd, am-awd'): Amad, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H5971 (עַם) and H5703 (עַד); people of time; KJV: Amad.

H6009 עָמַק (ʻâmaq, aw-mak'): to be (causatively, make) deep (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be, have, make, seek) deep(-ly), depth, be profound.

H6010 עֵמֶק (ʻêmeq, ay'-mek): a vale (i.e. broad depression). Origin: from H6009 (עָמַק); KJV: dale, vale, valley (often used as a part of proper names). See also H1025 (בֵּית הָעֵמֶק).

H6011 עֹמֶק (ʻômeq, o'-mek): depth. Origin: from H6009 (עָמַק); KJV: depth.

H6012 עָמֵק (ʻâmêq, aw-make'): deep (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H6009 (עָמַק); KJV: deeper, depth, strange.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6013 to H6141
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6013 עָמֹק (ʻâmôq, aw-moke'): deep (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H6009 (עָמַק); KJV: ([idiom] exceeding) deep (thing).

H6014 עָמַר (ʻâmar, aw-mar'): to gather grain. Origin: a primitive root; properly, apparently to heap; figuratively, to chastise (as if piling blows); specifically (as denominative from H6016 (עֹמֶר)) KJV: bind sheaves, make merchandise of.

H6015 עֲמַר (ʻămar, am-ar'): wool. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6785 (צֶמֶר); KJV: wool.

H6016 עֹמֶר (ʻômer, o'-mer): properly, a heap, i.e. a sheaf; also an omer, as a dry measure. Origin: from H6014 (עָמַר); KJV: omer, sheaf.

H6017 עֲמֹרָה (ʻĂmôrâh, am-o-raw'): Amorah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6014 (עָמַר); a (ruined) heap; KJV: Gomorrah.

H6018 עׇמְרִי (ʻOmrîy, om-ree'): Omri, an Israelite. Origin: from H6014 (עָמַר); heaping; KJV: Omri.

H6019 עַמְרָם (ʻAmrâm, am-rawm'): Amram, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably from H5971 (עַם) and H7311 (רוּם); high people; KJV: Amram.

H6020 עַמְרָמִי (ʻAmrâmîy, am-raw-mee'): an Amramite or descendant of Amram. Origin: from H6019 (עַמְרָם); KJV: Amramite.

H6021 עֲמָשָׂא (ʻĂmâsâʼ, am-aw-saw'): Amasa, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6006 (עָמַס); burden; KJV: Amasa.

H6022 עֲמָשַׂי (ʻĂmâsay, am-aw-sah'-ee): Amasai, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H6006 (עָמַס); burdensome; KJV: Amasai.

H6023 עֲמַשְׁסַי (ʻĂmashçay, am-ash-sah'-ee): Amashsay, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H6006 (עָמַס); burdensome; KJV: Amashai.

H6024 עֲנָב (ʻĂnâb, an-awb'): Anab, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H6025 (עֵנָב); fruit; KJV: Anab.

H6025 עֵנָב (ʻênâb, ay-nawb'): a grape. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to bear fruit; KJV: (ripe) grape, wine.

H6026 עָנַג (ʻânag, aw-nag'): to be soft or pliable, i.e. (figuratively) effeminate or luxurious. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: delicate(-ness), (have) delight (self), sport self.

H6027 עֹנֶג (ʻôneg, o'-neg): luxury. Origin: from H6026 (עָנַג); KJV: delight, pleasant.

H6028 עָנֹג (ʻânôg, aw-nogue'): luxurious. Origin: from H6026 (עָנַג); KJV: delicate.

H6029 עָנַד (ʻânad, aw-nad'): to lace fast. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind, tie.

H6030 עָנָה (ʻânâh, aw-naw'): properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extension to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: give account, afflict (by mistake for H6031 (עָנָה)), (cause to, give) answer, bring low (by mistake for H6031 (עָנָה)), cry, hear, Leannoth, lift up, say, [idiom] scholar, (give a) shout, sing (together by course), speak, testify, utter, (bear) witness. See also H1042 (בֵּית עֲנוֹת), H1043 (בֵּית עֲנָת).

H6031 עָנָה (ʻânâh, aw-naw'): to depress literally or figuratively, transitive or intransitive (in various applications, as follows). Origin: a primitive root (possibly rather identical with H6030 (עָנָה) through the idea of looking down or browbeating); KJV: abase self, afflict(-ion, self), answer (by mistake for H6030 (עָנָה)), chasten self, deal hardly with, defile, exercise, force, gentleness, humble (self), hurt, ravish, sing (by mistake for H6030 (עָנָה)), speak (by mistake for H6030 (עָנָה)), submit self, weaken, [idiom] in any wise.

H6032 עֲנָה (ʻănâh, an-aw'): {properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extension to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6030 (עָנָה) KJV: answer, speak.

H6033 עֲנָה (ʻănâh, an-aw'): {to depress literally or figuratively, transitive or intransitive (in various applications, as follows)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6031 (עָנָה) KJV: poor.

H6034 עֲנָה (ʻĂnâh, an-aw'): Anah, the name of two Edomites and one Edomitess. Origin: probably from H6030 (עָנָה); an answer; KJV: Anah.

H6035 עָנָו (ʻânâv, aw-nawv'): depressed (figuratively), in mind (gentle) or circumstances (needy, especially saintly). Origin: or (by intermixture with H6041 (עָנִי)) עָנָיו; from H6031 (עָנָה); KJV: humble, lowly, meek, poor. Compare H6041 (עָנִי).

H6036 עָנוּב (ʻÂnûwb, aw-noob'): Anub, an Israelite. Origin: passive participle from the same as H6025 (עֵנָב); borne (as fruit); KJV: Anub.

H6037 עַנְוָה (ʻanvâh, an-vaw'): mildness (royal); also (concretely) oppressed. Origin: feminine of H6035 (עָנָו); KJV: gentleness, meekness.

H6038 עֲנָוָה (ʻănâvâh, an-aw-vaw'): condescension, human and subjective (modesty), or divine and objective (clemency). Origin: from H6035 (עָנָו); KJV: gentleness, humility, meekness.

H6039 עֱנוּת (ʻĕnûwth, en-ooth'): affliction. Origin: from H6031 (עָנָה); KJV: affliction.

H6040 עֳנִי (ʻŏnîy, on-ee'): depression, i.e. misery. Origin: from H6031 (עָנָה); KJV: afflicted(-ion), trouble.

H6041 עָנִי (ʻânîy, aw-nee'): depressed, in mind or circumstances. Origin: from H6031 (עָנָה); (practically the same as H6035 (עָנָו), although the margin constantly disputes this, making H6035 (עָנָו) subjective and objective); KJV: afflicted, humble, lowly, needy, poor.

H6042 עֻנִּי (ʻUnnîy, oon-nee'): Unni, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6031 (עָנָה); afflicted; KJV: Unni.

H6043 עֲנָיָה (ʻĂnâyâh, an-aw-yaw'): Anajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6030 (עָנָה); Jah has answered; KJV: Anaiah.

H6044 עָנִים (ʻÂnîym, aw-neem'): Anim, a place in Palestine. Origin: for plural of H5869 (עַיִן); fountains; KJV: Anim.

H6045 עִנְיָן (ʻinyân, in-yawn'): ado, i.e. (generally) employment or (specifically) an affair. Origin: from H6031 (עָנָה); KJV: business, travail.

H6046 עָנֵם (ʻÂnêm, aw-name'): Anem, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the dual of H5869 (עַיִן); two fountains; KJV: Anem.

H6047 עֲנָמִים (ʻĂnâmîym, an-aw-meem'): Anamim, a son of Mizraim and his descendants, with their country. Origin: as if plural of some Egyptian word; KJV: Anamim.

H6048 עֲנַמֶּלֶךְ (ʻĂnammelek, an-am-meh'-lek): Anammelek, an Assyrian deity. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Anammelech.

H6049 עָנַן (ʻânan, aw-nan'): figuratively, to act covertly, i.e. practise magic. Origin: a primitive root; to cover; used only as a denominative from H6051 (עָנָן), to cloud over; KJV: [idiom] bring, enchanter, Meonemin, observe(-r of) times, soothsayer, sorcerer.

H6050 עֲנַן (ʻănan, an-an'): {a cloud (as covering the sky), i.e. the nimbus or thunder-cloud}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6051 (עָנָן) KJV: cloud.

H6051 עָנָן (ʻânân, aw-nawn'): a cloud (as covering the sky), i.e. the nimbus or thunder-cloud. Origin: from H6049 (עָנַן); KJV: cloud(-y).

H6052 עָנָן (ʻÂnân, aw-nawn'): Anan, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H6051 (עָנָן); cloud; KJV: Anan.

H6053 עֲנָנָה (ʻănânâh, an-aw-naw'): cloudiness. Origin: feminine of H6051 (עָנָן); KJV: cloud.

H6054 עֲנָנִי (ʻĂnânîy, an-aw-nee'): Anani, an Israelite. Origin: from H6051 (עָנָן); cloudy; KJV: Anani.

H6055 עֲנַנְיָה (ʻĂnanyâh, an-an-yaw'): Ananjah, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6049 (עָנַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has covered; KJV: Ananiah.

H6056 עֲנַף (ʻănaph, an-af'): {a twig (as covering the limbs)}. Origin: (Aramaic) or עֶנֶף; (Aramaic), corresponding to H6057 (עָנָף) KJV: bough, branch.

H6057 עָנָף (ʻânâph, aw-nawf'): a twig (as covering the limbs). Origin: from an unused root meaning to cover; KJV: bough, branch.

H6058 עָנֵף (ʻânêph, aw-nafe'): branching. Origin: from the same as H6057 (עָנָף); KJV: full of branches.

H6059 עָנַק (ʻânaq, aw-nak'): to collar, i.e. adorn with anecklace; figuratively, to fit out with supplies. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to choke; used only as denominative from H6060 (עָנָק), KJV: compass about as a chain, furnish, liberally.

H6060 עָנָק (ʻânâq, aw-nawk'): a necklace (as if strangling). Origin: from H6059 (עָנַק); KJV: chain.

H6061 עָנָק (ʻÂnâq, aw-nawk'): Anak, a Canaanite. Origin: the same as H6060 (עָנָק); KJV: Anak.

H6062 עֲנָקִי (ʻĂnâqîy, an-aw-kee'): an Anakite or descendant of Anak. Origin: patronymically from H6061 (עָנָק); KJV: Anakim.

H6063 עָנֵר (ʻÂnêr, aw-nare'): Aner, a Amorite, also a place in Palestine. Origin: probably for H5288 (נַעַר); KJV: Aner.

H6064 עָנַשׁ (ʻânash, aw-nash'): properly, to urge; by implication, to inflict apenalty, specifically, to fine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: amerce, condemn, punish, [idiom] surely.

H6065 עֲנַשׁ (ʻănash, an-ash'): a mulct. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6066 (עֹנֶשׁ); KJV: confiscation.

H6066 עֹנֶשׁ (ʻônesh, o'-nesh): a fine. Origin: from H6064 (עָנַשׁ); KJV: punishment, tribute.

H6067 עֲנָת (ʻĂnâth, an-awth'): Anath, an Israelite. Origin: from H6030 (עָנָה); answer; KJV: Anath.

H6068 עֲנָתוֹת (ʻĂnâthôwth, an-aw-thoth'): Anathoth, the name of two Israelites, also of a place in Pal. Origin: plural of H6067 (עֲנָת); KJV: Anathoth.

H6069 עַנְתֹתִי (ʻAnthôthîy, an-tho-thee'): a Antothite or inhabitant of Anathoth. Origin: or עַנְּתוֹתִי; patrial from H6068 (עֲנָתוֹת); KJV: of Anathoth, Anethothite, Anetothite, Antothite.

H6070 עַנְתֹתִיָּה (ʻAnthôthîyâh, an-tho-thee-yaw'): Anthothijah, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H6068 (עֲנָתוֹת) and H3050 (יָהּ); answers of Jah; KJV: Antothijah.

H6071 עָסִיס (ʻâçîyç, aw-sees'): must or fresh grape-juice (as just trodden out). Origin: from H6072 (עָסַס); KJV: juice, new (sweet) wine.

H6072 עָסַס (ʻâçaç, aw-sas'): to squeeze out juice; figuratively, to trample. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tread down.

H6073 עֳפֶא (ʻŏpheʼ, of-eh'): a bough (as covering the tree). Origin: from an unused root meaning to cover; KJV: branch.

H6074 עֳפִי (ʻŏphîy, of-ee'): a twig; bough, i.e. (collectively) foliage. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6073 (עֳפֶא); KJV: leaves.

H6075 עָפַל (ʻâphal, aw-fal'): to swell; figuratively, be elated. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be lifted up, presume.

H6076 עֹפֶל (ʻôphel, o'-fel): a tumor; also a mound, i.e. fortress. Origin: from H6075 (עָפַל); KJV: emerod, fort, strong hold, tower.

H6077 עֹפֶל (ʻÔphel, o'-fel): Ophel, a ridge in Jerusalem. Origin: the same as H6076 (עֹפֶל); KJV: Ophel.

H6078 עׇפְנִי (ʻOphnîy, of-nee'): an Ophnite (collectively) or inhabitants of Ophen. Origin: from an unused noun (denoting a place in Palestine; from an unused root of uncertain meaning); KJV: Ophni.

H6079 עַפְעַף (ʻaphʻaph, af-af'): an eyelash (as fluttering); figuratively, morning ray. Origin: from H5774 (עוּף); KJV: dawning, eye-lid.

H6080 עָפַר (ʻâphar, aw-far'): to be dust. Origin: ; a primitive root; meaning either to be gray or perhaps rather to pulverize; used only as denominative from H6083 (עָפָר), KJV: cast (dust).

H6081 עֵפֶר (ʻÊpher, ay'-fer): Epher, the name of an Arabian and of two Israelites. Origin: probably a variation of H6082 (עֹפֶר); gazelle; KJV: Epher.

H6082 עֹפֶר (ʻôpher, o'-fer): a fawn (from the dusty color). Origin: from H6080 (עָפַר); KJV: young roe (hart).

H6083 עָפָר (ʻâphâr, aw-fawr'): dust (as powdered or gray); hence, clay, earth, mud. Origin: from H6080 (עָפַר); KJV: ashes, dust, earth, ground, morter, powder, rubbish.

H6084 עׇפְרָה (ʻOphrâh, of-raw'): Ophrah, the name of an Israelite and of two places in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H6082 (עֹפֶר); female fawn; KJV: Ophrah.

H6085 עֶפְרוֹן (ʻEphrôwn, ef-rone'): Ephron, the name of a Canaanite and of two places in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H6081 (עֵפֶר); fawn-like; KJV: Ephron, Ephrain (from the margin).

H6086 עֵץ (ʻêts, ates): a tree (from its firmness); hence, wood (plural sticks). Origin: from H6095 (עָצָה); KJV: [phrase] carpenter, gallows, helve, [phrase] pine, plank, staff, stalk, stick, stock, timber, tree, wood.

H6087 עָצַב (ʻâtsab, aw-tsab'): properly, to carve, i.e. fabricate or fashion; hence (in a bad sense) to worry, pain or anger. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: displease, grieve, hurt, make, be sorry, vex, worship, wrest.

H6088 עֲצַב (ʻătsab, ats-ab'): to afflict. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: lamentable.

H6089 עֶצֶב (ʻetseb, eh'-tseb): an earthen vessel; usually (painful) toil; also a pang (whether of body or mind). Origin: from H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: grievous, idol, labor, sorrow.

H6090 עֹצֶב (ʻôtseb, o'-tseb): an idol (as fashioned); also pain (bodily or mental). Origin: a variation of H6089 (עֶצֶב); KJV: idol, sorrow, [idiom] wicked.

H6091 עָצָב (ʻâtsâb, aw-tsawb'): an (idolatrous) image. Origin: from H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: idol, image.

H6092 עָצֵב (ʻâtsêb, aw-tsabe'): a (hired) workman. Origin: from H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: labour.

H6093 עִצָּבוֹן (ʻitstsâbôwn, its-tsaw-bone'): worrisomeness, i.e. labor or pain. Origin: from H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: sorrow, toil.

H6094 עַצֶּבֶת (ʻatstsebeth, ats-tseh'-beth): a idol; also, a pain or wound. Origin: from H6087 (עָצַב); KJV: sorrow, wound.

H6095 עָצָה (ʻâtsâh, aw-tsaw'): properly, to fasten (or make firm), i.e. to close (the eyes). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shut.

H6096 עָצֶה (ʻâtseh, aw-tseh'): the spine (as giving firmness to the body). Origin: from H6095 (עָצָה); KJV: backbone.

H6097 עֵצָה (ʻêtsâh, ay-tsaw'): timber. Origin: feminine of H6086 (עֵץ); KJV: trees.

H6098 עֵצָה (ʻêtsâh, ay-tsaw'): advice; by implication, plan; also prudence. Origin: from H3289 (יָעַץ); KJV: advice, advisement, counsel(l-(or)), purpose.

H6099 עָצוּם (ʻâtsûwm, aw-tsoom'): powerful (specifically, a paw); by implication, numerous. Origin: or עָצֻם; passive participle of H6105 (עָצַם); KJV: [phrase] feeble, great, mighty, must, strong.

H6100 עֶצְיוֹן גֶּבֶר (ʻEtsyôwn Geber, ets-yone' gheh'ber): Etsjon-Geber, a place on the Red Sea. Origin: from H6096 (עָצֶה) and H1397 (גֶּבֶר); backbone-like of a man; KJV: Ezion-geber.

H6101 עָצַל (ʻâtsal, aw-tsal'): to lean idly, i.e. to be indolent or slack. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be slothful.

H6102 עָצֵל (ʻâtsêl, aw-tsale'): indolent. Origin: from H6101 (עָצַל); KJV: slothful, sluggard.

H6103 עַצְלָה (ʻatslâh, ats-law'): (as abstractly) indolence. Origin: feminine of H6102 (עָצֵל); KJV: slothfulness.

H6104 עַצְלוּת (ʻatslûwth, ats-looth'): indolence. Origin: from H6101 (עָצַל); KJV: idleness.

H6105 עָצַם (ʻâtsam, aw-tsam'): to bind fast, i.e. close (the eyes); intransitively, to be (causatively, make) powerful or numerous; to crunch the bones. Origin: a primitive root; also denominatively (from H6106 (עֶצֶם)) KJV: break the bones, close, be great, be increased, be (wax) mighty(-ier), be more, shut, be(-come, make) strong(-er).

H6106 עֶצֶם (ʻetsem, eh'tsem): a bone (as strong); by extension, the body; figuratively, the substance, i.e. (as pron.) selfsame. Origin: from H6105 (עָצַם); KJV: body, bone, [idiom] life, (self-) same, strength, [idiom] very.

H6107 עֶצֶם (ʻEtsem, eh'-tsem): Etsem, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6106 (עֶצֶם); bone; KJV: Azem, Ezem.

H6108 עֹצֶם (ʻôtsem, o'-tsem): power; hence, body. Origin: from H6105 (עָצַם); KJV: might, strong, substance.

H6109 עׇצְמָה (ʻotsmâh, ots-maw'): powerfulness; by extension, numerousness. Origin: feminine of H6108 (עֹצֶם); KJV: abundance, strength.

H6110 עַצֻּמָה (ʻatstsumâh, ats-tsoo-maw'): a bulwark, i.e. (figuratively) argument. Origin: feminine of H6099 (עָצוּם); KJV: strong.

H6111 עַצְמוֹן (ʻAtsmôwn, ats-mone'): Atsmon, a place near Palestine. Origin: or עַצְמֹן; from H6107 (עֶצֶם); bone-like; KJV: Azmon.

H6112 עֵצֶן (ʻêtsen, ay'-tsen): a spear. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be sharp or strong; KJV: Eznite (from the margin).

H6113 עָצָר (ʻâtsâr, aw-tsar'): to inclose; by analogy, to hold back; also to maintain, rule, assemble. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] be able, close up, detain, fast, keep (self close, still), prevail, recover, refrain, [idiom] reign, restrain, retain, shut (up), slack, stay, stop, withhold (self).

H6114 עֶצֶר (ʻetser, eh'-tser): restraint. Origin: from H6113 (עָצָר); KJV: [phrase] magistrate.

H6115 עֹצֶר (ʻôtser, o'-tser): closure; also constraint. Origin: from H6113 (עָצָר); KJV: [idiom] barren, oppression, [idiom] prison.

H6116 עֲצָרָה (ʻătsârâh, ats-aw-raw'): an assembly, especially on afestival or holiday. Origin: or עֲצֶרֶת; from H6113 (עָצָר); KJV: (solemn) assembly (meeting).

H6117 עָקַב (ʻâqab, aw-kab'): to seize by the heel; figuratively, to circumvent (as if tripping up the heels); also to restrain (as if holding by the heel). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to swell out or up; used only as denominative from H6119 (עָקֵב), KJV: take by the heel, stay, supplant, [idiom] utterly.

H6118 עֵקֶב (ʻêqeb, ay'-keb): a heel, i.e. (figuratively) the last of anything (used adverbially, for ever); also result, i.e. compensation; and so (adverb with preposition or relatively) on account of. Origin: from H6117 (עָקַב) in the sense of H6119 (עָקֵב); KJV: [idiom] because, by, end, for, if, reward.

H6119 עָקֵב (ʻâqêb, aw-kabe'): a heel (as protuberant); hence, a track; figuratively, the rear (of an army). Origin: or (feminine) עִקְּבָה; from H6117 (עָקַב); KJV: heel, (horse-) hoof, last, lier in wait (by mistake for H6120 (עָקֵב)), (foot-) step.

H6120 עָקֵב (ʻâqêb, aw-kabe'): a lier in wait. Origin: from H6117 (עָקַב) in its denominative sense; KJV: heel (by mistake for H6119 (עָקֵב)).

H6121 עָקֹב (ʻâqôb, aw-kobe'): (transitive) fraudulent or (intransitive) tracked. Origin: from H6117 (עָקַב); in the original sense, a knoll (as swelling up); in the denominative sense KJV: crooked, deceitful, polluted.

H6122 עׇקְבָה (ʻoqbâh, ok-baw'): trickery. Origin: feminine of an unused form from H6117 (עָקַב) meaning a trick; KJV: subtilty.

H6123 עָקַד (ʻâqad, aw-kad'): to tie with thongs. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind.

H6124 עָקֹד (ʻâqôd, aw-kode'): striped (with bands). Origin: from H6123 (עָקַד); KJV: ring straked.

H6125 עָקָה (ʻâqâh, aw-kaw'): constraint. Origin: from H5781 (עוּק); KJV: oppression.

H6126 עַקּוּב (ʻAqqûwb, ak-koob'): Akkub, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H6117 (עָקַב); insidious; KJV: Akkub.

H6127 עָקַל (ʻâqal, aw-kal'): to wrest. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wrong.

H6128 עֲקַלְקַל (ʻăqalqal, ak-al-kal'): winding. Origin: from H6127 (עָקַל); KJV: by(-way), crooked way.

H6129 עֲקַלָּתוֹן (ʻăqallâthôwn, ak-al-law-thone'): tortuous. Origin: from H6127 (עָקַל); KJV: crooked.

H6130 עָקָן (ʻÂqân, aw-kawn'): Akan, an Idummaean. Origin: from an unused root meaning to twist; tortuous; KJV: Akan. Compare H3292 (יַעֲקָן).

H6131 עָקַר (ʻâqar, aw-kar'): to pluck up (especially by the roots); specifically, to hamstring; figuratively, to exterminate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dig down, hough, pluck up, root up.

H6132 עֲקַר (ʻăqar, ak-ar'): {to pluck up (especially by the roots); specifically, to hamstring; figuratively, to exterminate}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6131 (עָקַר) KJV: pluck up by the roots.

H6133 עֵקֶר (ʻêqer, ay'-ker): figuratively, a transplanted person, i.e. naturalized citizen. Origin: from H6131 (עָקַר); KJV: stock.

H6134 עֵקֶר (ʻÊqer, ay'-ker): Eker, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H6133 (עֵקֶר); KJV: Eker.

H6135 עָקָר (ʻâqâr, aw-kawr'): sterile (as if extirpated in the generative organs). Origin: from H6131 (עָקַר); KJV: ([idiom] male or female) barren (woman).

H6136 עִקַּר (ʻiqqar, ik-kar'): a stock. Origin: (Aramaic) from H6132 (עֲקַר); KJV: stump.

H6137 עַקְרָב (ʻaqrâb, ak-rawb'): a scorpion; figuratively, a scourge or knotted whip. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: scorpion.

H6138 עֶקְרוֹן (ʻEqrôwn, ek-rone'): Ekron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6131 (עָקַר); eradication; KJV: Ekron.

H6139 עֶקְרוֹנִי (ʻEqrôwnîy, ek-ro-nee'): an Ekronite or inhabitant of Ekron. Origin: or עֶקְרֹנִי; patrial from H6138 (עֶקְרוֹן); KJV: Ekronite.

H6140 עָקַשׁ (ʻâqash, aw-kash'): to knot or distort; figuratively, to pervert (act or declare perverse). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make crooked, (prove, that is) perverse(-rt).

H6141 עִקֵּשׁ (ʻiqqêsh, ik-kashe'): distorted; hence, false. Origin: from H6140 (עָקַשׁ); KJV: crooked, froward, perverse.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6142 to H6264
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6142 עִקֵּשׁ (ʻIqqêsh, ik-kashe'): Ikkesh, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H6141 (עִקֵּשׁ); perverse; KJV: Ikkesh.

H6143 עִקְּשׁוּת (ʻiqqᵉshûwth, ik-kesh-ooth'): perversity. Origin: from H6141 (עִקֵּשׁ); KJV: [idiom] froward.

H6144 עָר (ʻÂr, awr): Ar, a place in Moab. Origin: the same as H5892 (עִיר); a city; KJV: Ar.

H6145 עָר (ʻâr, awr): a foe (as watchful for mischief). Origin: from H5782 (עוּר); KJV: enemy.

H6146 עָר (ʻâr, awr): {a foe (as watchful for mischief)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6145 (עָר) KJV: enemy.

H6147 עֵר (ʻÊr, ayr): Er, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5782 (עוּר); watchful; KJV: Er.

H6148 עָרַב (ʻârab, aw-rab'): to braid, i.e. intermix; technically, to traffic (as if by barter); also or give to be security (as a kind of exchange). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: engage, (inter-) meddle (with), mingle (self), mortgage, occupy, give pledges, be(-come, put in) surety, undertake.

H6149 עָרֵב (ʻârêb, aw-rabe'): to be agreeable. Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H6148 (עָרַב) through the idea of close association); KJV: be pleasant(-ing), take pleasure in, be sweet.

H6150 עָרַב (ʻârab, aw-rab'): to grow dusky at sundown. Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H6148 (עָרַב) through the idea of covering with a texture); KJV: be darkened, (toward) evening.

H6151 עֲרַב (ʻărab, ar-ab'): to commingle. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6148 (עָרַב); KJV: mingle (self), mix.

H6152 עֲרָב (ʻĂrâb, ar-awb'): Arab (i.e. Arabia), a country East of Palestine. Origin: or עֲרַב; from H6150 (עָרַב) in the figurative sense of sterility; KJV: Arabia.

H6153 עֶרֶב (ʻereb, eh'-reb): dusk. Origin: from H6150 (עָרַב); KJV: [phrase] day, even(-ing, tide), night.

H6154 עֵרֶב (ʻêreb, ay'-reb): the web (or transverse threads of cloth); also a mixture, (or mongrel race). Origin: or עֶרֶב; (1 Kings 10:15), (with the article [prefix), from H6148 (עָרַב); KJV: Arabia, mingled people, mixed (multitude), woof.

H6155 עָרָב (ʻârâb, aw-rawb'): a willow (from the use of osiers as wattles). Origin: from H6148 (עָרַב); KJV: willow.

H6156 עָרֵב (ʻârêb, aw-rabe'): pleasant. Origin: from H6149 (עָרֵב); KJV: sweet.

H6157 עָרֹב (ʻârôb, aw-robe'): a mosquito (from its swarming). Origin: from H6148 (עָרַב); KJV: divers sorts of flies, swarm.

H6158 עֹרֵב (ʻôrêb, o-rabe'): a raven (from its dusky hue). Origin: or עוֹרֵב; from H6150 (עָרַב); KJV: raven.

H6159 עֹרֵב (ʻÔrêb, o-rabe'): Oreb, the name of a Midianite and of the cliff near the Jordan. Origin: or עוֹרֵב; the same as H6158 (עֹרֵב); KJV: Oreb.

H6160 עֲרָבָה (ʻărâbâh, ar-aw-baw'): a desert; especially (with the article prefix) the (generally) sterile valley of the Jordan and its continuation to the Red Sea. Origin: from H6150 (עָרַב) (in the sense of sterility); KJV: Arabah, champaign, desert, evening, heaven, plain, wilderness. See also H1026 (בֵּית הָעֲרָבָה).

H6161 עֲרֻבָּה (ʻărubbâh, ar-oob-baw'): something given as security, i.e. (literally) a token (of safety) or (metaphorically) a bondsman. Origin: feminine passive participle of H6048 (עֲנַמֶּלֶךְ) in the sense of a bargain or exchange; KJV: pledge, surety.

H6162 עֲרָבוֹן (ʻărâbôwn, ar-aw-bone'): a pawn (given as security). Origin: from H6148 (עָרַב) (in the sense of exchange); KJV: pledge.

H6163 עֲרָבִי (ʻĂrâbîy, ar-aw-bee'): an Arabian or inhabitant of Arab (i.e. Arabia). Origin: or עַרְבִי; patrial from H6152 (עֲרָב); KJV: Arabian.

H6164 עַרְבָתִי (ʻArbâthîy, ar-baw-thee'): an Arbathite or inhabitant of (Beth-) Arabah. Origin: patrial from H1026 (בֵּית הָעֲרָבָה); KJV: Arbahite.

H6165 עָרַג (ʻârag, aw-rag'): to long for. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cry, pant.

H6166 עֲרָד (ʻĂrâd, ar-awd'): Arad, the name of a place near Palestine, also of a Canaanite and an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to sequester itself; fugitive; KJV: Arad.

H6167 עֲרָד (ʻărâd, ar-awd'): an onager. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6171 (עָרוֹד); KJV: wild ass.

H6168 עָרָה (ʻârâh, aw-raw'): to be (causatively, make) bare; hence, to empty, pour out, demolish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: leave destitute, discover, empty, make naked, pour (out), rase, spread self, uncover.

H6169 עָרָה (ʻârâh, aw-raw'): a naked (i.e. level) plot. Origin: feminine from H6168 (עָרָה); KJV: paper reed.

H6170 עֲרוּגָה (ʻărûwgâh, ar-oo-gaw'): something piled up (as if (figuratively) raised by mental aspiration), i.e. a paterre. Origin: or עֲרֻגָה; feminine passive participle of H6165 (עָרַג); KJV: bed, furrow.

H6171 עָרוֹד (ʻârôwd, aw-rode'): an onager (from his lonesome habits). Origin: from the same as H6166 (עֲרָד); KJV: wild ass.

H6172 עֶרְוָה (ʻervâh, er-vaw'): nudity, literally (especially the pudenda) or figuratively (disgrace, blemish). Origin: from H6168 (עָרָה); KJV: nakedness, shame, unclean(-ness).

H6173 עַרְוָה (ʻarvâh, ar-vaw'): nakedness, i.e. (figuratively) impoverishment. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6172 (עֶרְוָה); KJV: dishonor.

H6174 עָרוֹם (ʻârôwm, aw-rome'): nude, either partially or totally. Origin: or עָרֹם; from H6191 (עָרַם) (in its original sense); KJV: naked.

H6175 עָרוּם (ʻârûwm, aw-room'): cunning (usually in a bad sense). Origin: passive participle of H6191 (עָרַם); KJV: crafty, prudent, subtil.

H6176 עֲרוֹעֵר (ʻărôwʻêr, ar-o-ayr'): a juniper (from its nudity of situation). Origin: or עַרְעָר; from H6209 (עָרַר) reduplicated; KJV: health.

H6177 עֲרוֹעֵר (ʻĂrôwʻêr, ar-o-ayr'): Aroer, the name of three places in or near Palestine. Origin: or עֲרֹעֵר; or עַרְעוֹר; the same as H6176 (עֲרוֹעֵר); nudity of situation; KJV: Aroer.

H6178 עָרוּץ (ʻârûwts, aw-roots'): feared, i.e. (concretely) a horrible place or chasm. Origin: passive participle of H6206 (עָרַץ); KJV: cliffs.

H6179 עֵרִי (ʻÊrîy, ay-ree'): Eri, an Israelite. Origin: from H5782 (עוּר); watchful; KJV: Eri.

H6180 עֵרִי (ʻÊrîy, ay-ree'): a Erite (collectively) or descendants of Eri. Origin: patronymically of H6179 (עֵרִי); KJV: Erites.

H6181 עֶרְיָה (ʻeryâh, er-yaw'): nudity. Origin: for H6172 (עֶרְוָה); KJV: bare, naked, [idiom] quite.

H6182 עֲרִיסָה (ʻărîyçâh, ar-ee-saw'): meal. Origin: from an unused root meaning to comminute; KJV: dough.

H6183 עָרִיף (ʻârîyph, aw-reef'): the sky (as dropping at the horizon). Origin: from H6201 (עָרַף); KJV: heaven.

H6184 עָרִיץ (ʻârîyts, aw-reets'): fearful, i.e. powerful or tyrannical. Origin: from H6206 (עָרַץ); KJV: mighty, oppressor, in great power, strong, terrible, violent.

H6185 עֲרִירִי (ʻărîyrîy, ar-e-ree'): bare, i.e. destitute (of children). Origin: from H6209 (עָרַר); KJV: childless.

H6186 עָרַךְ (ʻârak, aw-rak'): to set in a row, i.e. arrange, put in order (in a very wide variety of applications). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: put (set) (the battle, self) in array, compare, direct, equal, esteem, estimate, expert (in war), furnish, handle, join (battle), ordain, (lay, put, reckon up, set) (in) order, prepare, tax, value.

H6187 עֵרֶךְ (ʻêrek, eh'rek): a pile, equipment, estimate. Origin: from H6186 (עָרַךְ); KJV: equal, estimation, (things that are set in) order, price, proportion, [idiom] set at, suit, taxation, [idiom] valuest.

H6188 עָרֵל (ʻârêl, aw-rale'): to expose or remove the prepuce, whether literal (to go naked) or figurative (to refrain from using). Origin: a primitive root; properly, to strip; but used as denominative from H6189 (עָרֵל); KJV: count uncircumcised, foreskin to be uncovered.

H6189 עָרֵל (ʻârêl, aw-rale'): uncircumcised (i.e. still having the prepuce uncurtailed). Origin: from H6188 (עָרֵל); properly, exposed, i.e. projecting loose (as to the prepuce); used only technically, KJV: uncircumcised (person).

H6190 עׇרְלָה (ʻorlâh, or-law'): the prepuce. Origin: feminine of H6189 (עָרֵל); KJV: foreskin, [phrase] uncircumcised.

H6191 עָרַם (ʻâram, aw-ram'): properly, to be (or make) bare; but used only in the derivative sense (through the idea perhaps of smoothness) to be cunning (usually in a bad sense). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] very, beware, take crafty (counsel), be prudent, deal subtilly.

H6192 עָרַם (ʻâram, aw-ram'): to pile up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather together.

H6193 עֹרֶם (ʻôrem, o'-rem): a stratagem. Origin: from H6191 (עָרַם); KJV: craftiness.

H6194 עָרֵם (ʻârêm, aw-rame'): a heap; specifically, a sheaf. Origin: (Jeremiah 50:26) or (feminine) עֲרֵמָה; from H6192 (עָרַם); KJV: heap (of corn), sheaf.

H6195 עׇרְמָה (ʻormâh, or-maw'): trickery; or (in a good sense) discretion. Origin: feminine of H6193 (עֹרֶם); KJV: guile, prudence, subtilty, wilily, wisdom.

H6196 עַרְמוֹן (ʻarmôwn, ar-mone'): the plane tree (from its smooth and shed bark). Origin: probably from H6191 (עָרַם); KJV: chestnut tree.

H6197 עֵרָן (ʻÊrân, ay-rawn'): Eran, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H5782 (עוּר); watchful; KJV: Eran.

H6198 עֵרָנִי (ʻÊrânîy, ay-raw-nee'): an Eranite or descendant (collectively) of Eran. Origin: patronymically from H6197 (עֵרָן); KJV: Eranites.

H6199 עַרעָר (ʻarʻâr, ar-awr'): naked, i.e. (figuratively) poor. Origin: from H6209 (עָרַר); KJV: destitute. See also H6176 (עֲרוֹעֵר).

H6200 עֲרֹעֵרִי (ʻĂrôʻêrîy, ar-o-ay-ree'): an Aroerite or inhabitant of Aroer. Origin: patronymically from H6177 (עֲרוֹעֵר); KJV: Aroerite.

H6201 עָרַף (ʻâraph, aw-raf'): to droop; hence, to drip. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: drop (down).

H6202 עָרַף (ʻâraph, aw-raf'): to break the neck; hence (figuratively) to destroy. Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of sloping); properly, to bend downward; but used only as a denominative from H6203 (עֹרֶף), KJV: that is beheaded, break down, break (cut off, strike off) neck.

H6203 עֹרֶף (ʻôreph, o-ref'): the nape or back of the neck (as declining); hence, the back generally (whether literal or figurative). Origin: from H6202 (עָרַף); KJV: back ((stiff-) neck((-ed).

H6204 עׇרְפָּה (ʻOrpâh, or-paw'): Orpah, a Moabites. Origin: feminine of H6203 (עֹרֶף); mane; KJV: Orpah.

H6205 עֲרָפֶל (ʻărâphel, ar-aw-fel'): gloom (as of a lowering sky). Origin: probably from H6201 (עָרַף); KJV: (gross, thick) dark (cloud, -ness).

H6206 עָרַץ (ʻârats, aw-rats'): to awe or (intransitive) to dread; hence, to harass. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be affrighted (afraid, dread, feared, terrified), break, dread, fear, oppress, prevail, shake terribly.

H6207 עָרַק (ʻâraq, aw-rak'): to gnaw, i.e. (figuratively) eat (by hyberbole); also (participle) a pain. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fleeing, sinew.

H6208 עַרְקִי (ʻArqîy, ar-kee'): an Arkite or inhabitant of Erek. Origin: patrial from an unused name meaning a tush; KJV: Arkite.

H6209 עָרַר (ʻârar, aw-rar'): to bare; figuratively, to demolish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make bare, break, raise up (perhaps by clerical error for raze), [idiom] utterly.

H6210 עֶרֶשׂ (ʻeres, eh'res): a couch (properly, with a canopy). Origin: from an unused root meaning perhaps to arch; KJV: bed(-stead), couch.

H6211 עָשׁ (ʻâsh, awsh): a moth. Origin: from H6244 (עָשֵׁשׁ); KJV: moth. See also H5906 (עַיִשׁ).

H6212 עֶשֶׂב (ʻeseb, eh'seb): grass (or any tender shoot). Origin: from an unused root meaning to glisten (or be green); KJV: grass, herb.

H6213 עָשָׂה (ʻâsâh, aw-saw'): to do or make, in the broadest sense and widest application. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: accomplish, advance, appoint, apt, be at, become, bear, bestow, bring forth, bruise, be busy, [idiom] certainly, have the charge of, commit, deal (with), deck, [phrase] displease, do, (ready) dress(-ed), (put in) execute(-ion), exercise, fashion, [phrase] feast, (fight-) ing man, [phrase] finish, fit, fly, follow, fulfill, furnish, gather, get, go about, govern, grant, great, [phrase] hinder, hold (a feast), [idiom] indeed, [phrase] be industrious, [phrase] journey, keep, labour, maintain, make, be meet, observe, be occupied, offer, [phrase] officer, pare, bring (come) to pass, perform, pracise, prepare, procure, provide, put, requite, [idiom] sacrifice, serve, set, shew, [idiom] sin, spend, [idiom] surely, take, [idiom] thoroughly, trim, [idiom] very, [phrase] vex, be (warr-) ior, work(-man), yield, use.

H6214 עֲשָׂהאֵל (ʻĂsâhʼêl, as-aw-ale'): Asahel, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה) and H410 (אֵל); God has made; KJV: Asahel.

H6215 עֵשָׂו (ʻÊsâv, ay-sawv'): Esav, a son of Isaac, including his posterity. Origin: apparently a form of the passive participle of H6213 (עָשָׂה) in the original sense of handling; rough (i.e. sensibly felt); KJV: Esau.

H6216 עָשׁוֹק (ʻâshôwq, aw-shoke'): oppressive (as noun, a tyrant). Origin: from H6231 (עָשַׁק); KJV: oppressor.

H6217 עָשׁוּק (ʻâshûwq, aw-shook'): used in plural masculine as abstractly, tyranny. Origin: or עָשֻׁק; passive participle of H6231 (עָשַׁק); KJV: oppressed(-ion). (Doubtful.)

H6218 עָשׂוֹר (ʻâsôwr, aw-sore'): ten; by abbreviated form ten strings, and so a decachord. Origin: or עָשֹׂר; from H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: (instrument of) ten (strings, -th).

H6219 עָשׁוֹת (ʻâshôwth, aw-shoth'): shining, i.e. polished. Origin: from H6245 (עָשַׁת); KJV: bright.

H6220 עַשְׁוָת (ʻAshvâth, ash-vawth'): Ashvath, an Israelite. Origin: for H6219 (עָשׁוֹת); bright; KJV: Ashvath.

H6221 עֲשִׂיאֵל (ʻĂsîyʼêl, as-ee-ale'): Asiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה) and H410 (אֵל); made of God; KJV: Asiel.

H6222 עֲשָׂיָה (ʻĂsâyâh, aw-saw-yaw'): Asajah, the name of three or four Israelites. Origin: from H6213 (עָשָׂה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has made; KJV: Asaiah.

H6223 עָשִׁיר (ʻâshîyr, aw-sheer'): rich, whether literal or figurative (noble). Origin: from H6238 (עָשַׁר); KJV: rich (man).

H6224 עֲשִׂירִי (ʻăsîyrîy, as-ee-ree'): tenth; by abbreviation, tenth month or (feminine) part. Origin: from H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: tenth (part).

H6225 עָשַׁן (ʻâshan, aw-shan'): to smoke, whether literal or figurative. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be angry (be on a) smoke.

H6226 עָשֵׁן (ʻâshên, aw-shane'): smoky. Origin: from H6225 (עָשַׁן); KJV: smoking.

H6227 עָשָׁן (ʻâshân, aw-shawn'): smoke, literally or figuratively (vapor, dust, anger). Origin: from H6225 (עָשַׁן); KJV: smoke(-ing).

H6228 עָשָׁן (ʻÂshân, aw-shawn'): Ashan, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6227 (עָשָׁן); KJV: Ashan.

H6229 עָשַׂק (ʻâsaq, aw-sak): to press upon, i.e. quarrel. Origin: a primitive root (identical with H6231 (עָשַׁק)); KJV: strive with.

H6230 עֵשֶׂק (ʻêseq, ay'sek): strife. Origin: from H6229 (עָשַׂק); KJV: Esek.

H6231 עָשַׁק (ʻâshaq, aw-shak'): to press upon, i.e. oppress, defraud, violate, overflow. Origin: a primitive root (compare H6229 (עָשַׂק)); KJV: get deceitfully, deceive, defraud, drink up, (use) oppress(-ion), -or), do violence (wrong).

H6232 עֵשֶׁק (ʻÊsheq, ay-shek'): Eshek, an Israelite. Origin: from H6231 (עָשַׁק); oppression; KJV: Eshek.

H6233 עֹשֶׁק (ʻôsheq, o'-shek): injury, fraud, (subjectively) distress, (concretely) unjust gain. Origin: from H6231 (עָשַׁק); KJV: cruelly, extortion, oppression, thing (deceitfully gotten).

H6234 עׇשְׁקָה (ʻoshqâh, osh-kaw'): anguish. Origin: feminine of H6233 (עֹשֶׁק); KJV: oppressed.

H6235 עֶשֶׂר (ʻeser, eh'ser): ten (as an accumulation to the extent of the digits). Origin: masculine of term עֲשָׂרָה; from H6237 (עָשַׂר); KJV: ten, (fif-, seven-) teen.

H6236 עֲשַׂר (ʻăsar, as-ar'): ten. Origin: (Aramaic) masculine עֲשְׂרָה (Aramaic); corresponding to H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: ten, [phrase] twelve.

H6237 עָשַׂר (ʻâsar, aw-sar'): to tithe, i.e. to take or give atenth. Origin: a primitive root (identical with H6238 (עָשַׁר)); to accumulate; but used only as denominative from H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: [idiom] surely, give (take) the tenth, (have, take) tithe(-ing, -s), [idiom] truly.

H6238 עָשַׁר (ʻâshar, aw-shar'): properly, to accumulate; chiefly (specifically) to grow (causatively, make) rich. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be(-come, en-, make, make self, wax) rich, make (1 Kings 22:48 marg). See H6240 (עָשָׂר).

H6239 עֹשֶׁר (ʻôsher, o'-sher): wealth. Origin: from H6238 (עָשַׁר); KJV: [idiom] far (richer), riches.

H6240 עָשָׂר (ʻâsâr, aw-sawr'): ten (only in combination), i.e. -teen; also (ordinal) -teenth. Origin: for H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: (eigh-, fif-, four-, nine-, seven-, six-, thir-) teen(-th), [phrase] eleven(-th), [phrase] sixscore thousand, [phrase] twelve(-th).

H6241 עִשָּׂרוֹן (ʻissârôwn, is-saw-rone'): (fractional) a tenth part. Origin: or עִשָּׂרֹן; from H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: tenth deal.

H6242 עֶשְׂרִים (ʻesrîym, es-reem'): twenty; also (ordinal) twentieth. Origin: from H6235 (עֶשֶׂר); KJV: (six-) score, twenty(-ieth).

H6243 עֶשְׂרִין (ʻesrîyn, es-reen'): {twenty; also (ordinal) twentieth}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6242 (עֶשְׂרִים) KJV: twenty.

H6244 עָשֵׁשׁ (ʻâshêsh, aw-shaysh'): probably to shrink, i.e. fail. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be consumed.

H6245 עָשַׁת (ʻâshath, aw-shath'): probably to be sleek, i.e. glossy; hence (through the idea of polishing) to excogitate (as if forming in the mind). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shine, think.

H6246 עֲשִׁת (ʻăshith, ash-eeth'): to purpose. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6245 (עָשַׁת); KJV: think.

H6247 עֶשֶׁת (ʻesheth, eh'-sheth): a fabric. Origin: from H6245 (עָשַׁת); KJV: bright.

H6248 עַשְׁתּוּת (ʻashtûwth, ash-tooth'): cogitation. Origin: from H6245 (עָשַׁת); KJV: thought.

H6249 עַשְׁתֵּי (ʻashtêy, ash-tay'): eleven or (ordinal) eleventh. Origin: apparently masculine plural construction of H6247 (עֶשֶׁת) in the sense of an afterthought (used only in connection with H6240 (עָשָׂר) in lieu of H259 (אֶחָד)) KJV: [phrase] eleven(-th).

H6250 עֶשְׁתֹּנָה (ʻeshtônâh, esh-to-naw'): thinking. Origin: from H6245 (עָשַׁת); KJV: thought.

H6251 עַשְׁתְּרָה (ʻashtᵉrâh, ash-ter-aw'): increase. Origin: probably from H6238 (עָשַׁר); KJV: flock.

H6252 עַשְׁתָּרוֹת (ʻAshtârôwth, ash-taw-roth'): Ashtaroth, the name of a Sidonian deity, and of a place East of the Jordan. Origin: or עַשְׁתָּרֹת; plural of H6251 (עַשְׁתְּרָה); KJV: Asharoth, Astaroth. See also H1045 (בֵּית עַשְׁתָּרוֹת), H6253 (עַשְׁתֹּרֶת), H6255 (עַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם).

H6253 עַשְׁתֹּרֶת (ʻAshtôreth, ash-to'reth): Ashtoreth, the Phoenician goddess of love (and increase). Origin: probably for H6251 (עַשְׁתְּרָה); KJV: Ashtoreth.

H6254 עַשְׁתְּרָתִי (ʻAshtᵉrâthîy, ash-ter-aw-thee'): an Ashterathite or inhabitant of Ashtaroth. Origin: patrial from H6252 (עַשְׁתָּרוֹת); KJV: Ashterathite.

H6255 עַשְׁתְּרֹת קַרְנַיִם (ʻAshtᵉrôth Qarnayim, ash-ter-oth' kar-nah'-yim): Ashteroth-Karnaim, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H6252 (עַשְׁתָּרוֹת) and the dual of H7161 (קֶרֶן); Ashtaroth of (the) double horns (a symbol of the deity); KJV: Ashtoreth Karnaim.

H6256 עֵת (ʻêth, ayth): time, especially (adverb with preposition) now, when, etc. Origin: from H5703 (עַד); KJV: [phrase] after, (al-) ways, [idiom] certain, [phrase] continually, [phrase] evening, long, (due) season, so (long) as, (even-, evening-, noon-) tide, (meal-), what) time, when.

H6257 עָתַד (ʻâthad, aw-thad'): to prepare. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make fit, be ready to become.

H6258 עַתָּה (ʻattâh, at-taw'): at this time, whether adverb, conjunction or expletive. Origin: from H6256 (עֵת); KJV: henceforth, now, straightway, this time, whereas.

H6259 עָתוּד (ʻâthûwd, aw-thood'): prepared. Origin: passive participle of H6257 (עָתַד); KJV: ready.

H6260 עַתּוּד (ʻattûwd, at-tood'): prepared, i.e. full grown; spoken only (in plural) of he-goats, or (figuratively) leaders of the people. Origin: or עַתֻּד; from H6257 (עָתַד); KJV: chief one, (he) goat, ram.

H6261 עִתִּי (ʻittîy, it-tee'): timely. Origin: from H6256 (עֵת); KJV: fit.

H6262 עַתַּי (ʻAttay, at-tah'ee): Attai, the name of three Israelites. Origin: for H6261 (עִתִּי); KJV: Attai.

H6263 עֲתִיד (ʻăthîyd, ath-eed'): prepared. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6264 (עָתִיד); KJV: ready.

H6264 עָתִיד (ʻâthîyd, aw-theed'): prepared; by implication, skilful; feminine plural the future; also treasure. Origin: from H6257 (עָתַד); KJV: things that shall come, ready, treasures.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6265 to H6394
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6265 עֲתָיָה (ʻĂthâyâh, ath-aw-yaw'): Athajah, an Israelite. Origin: from H5790 (עוּת) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has helped; KJV: Athaiah.

H6266 עָתִיק (ʻâthîyq, aw-theek'): properly, antique, i.e. venerable or splendid. Origin: from H6275 (עָתַק); KJV: durable.

H6267 עַתִּיק (ʻattîyq, at-teek'): removed, i.e. weaned; also antique. Origin: from H6275 (עָתַק); KJV: ancient, drawn.

H6268 עַתִּיק (ʻattîyq, at-teek'): venerable. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6267 (עַתִּיק); KJV: ancient.

H6269 עֲתָךְ (ʻĂthâk, ath-awk'): Athak, a place in Palestine. Origin: from an unused root meaning to sojourn; lodging; KJV: Athach.

H6270 עַתְלַי (ʻAthlay, ath-lah'ee): Athlai, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to compress; constringent; KJV: Athlai.

H6271 עֲתַלְיָה (ʻĂthalyâh, ath-al-yaw'): Athaljah, the name of an Israelitess and two Israelites. Origin: or עֲתַלְיָהוּ; from the same as H6270 (עַתְלַי) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has constrained; KJV: Athaliah.

H6272 עָתַם (ʻâtham, aw-tham): probably to glow, i.e. (figuratively) be desolated. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be darkened.

H6273 עׇתְנִי (ʻOthnîy, oth-nee'): Othni, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to force; forcible; KJV: Othni.

H6274 עׇתְנִיאֵל (ʻOthnîyʼêl, oth-nee-ale'): Othniel, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H6273 (עׇתְנִי) and H410 (אֵל); force of God; KJV: Othniel.

H6275 עָתַק (ʻâthaq, aw-thak'): to remove (intransitive or transitive) figuratively, to grow old; specifically, to transcribe. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: copy out, leave off, become (wax) old, remove.

H6276 עָתֵק (ʻâthêq, aw-thake'): antique, i.e. valued. Origin: from H6275 (עָתַק); KJV: durable.

H6277 עָתָק (ʻâthâq, aw-thawk'): impudent. Origin: from H6275 (עָתַק) in the sense of license; KJV: arrogancy, grievous (hard) things, stiff.

H6278 עֵת קָצִין (ʻÊth Qâtsîyn, ayth kaw-tseen'): Eth-Katsin, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6256 (עֵת) and H7011 (קַיָּם); time of a judge; KJV: Ittahkazin (by including directive enclitic).

H6279 עָתַר (ʻâthar, aw-thar'): to burn incense in worship, i.e. intercede (reciprocally, listen to prayer). Origin: a primitive root (rather denominative from H6281 (עֶתֶר)); KJV: intreat, (make) pray(-er).

H6280 עָתַר (ʻâthar, aw-thar'): to be (causatively, make) abundant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deceitful, multiply.

H6281 עֶתֶר (ʻEther, eh'ther): Ether, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6280 (עָתַר); abundance; KJV: Ether.

H6282 עָתָר (ʻâthâr, aw-thawr'): incense (as increasing to a volume of smoke); hence a worshipper. Origin: from H6280 (עָתַר); also compare H6279 (עָתַר) KJV: suppliant, thick.

H6283 עֲתֶרֶת (ʻăthereth, ath-eh'-reth): copiousness. Origin: from H6280 (עָתַר); KJV: abundance. p

H6284 פָּאָה (pâʼâh, paw-aw'): to puff, i.e. blow away. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: scatter into corners.

H6285 פֵּאָה (pêʼâh, pay-aw'): properly, mouth in a figurative sense, i.e. direction, region, extremity. Origin: feminine of H6311 (פֹּה); KJV: corner, end, quarter, side.

H6286 פָּאַר (pâʼar, paw-ar'): to gleam, i.e. (causatively) embellish; figuratively, to boast; also to explain (i.e. make clear) oneself; to shake a tree. Origin: a primitive root; also denominative from H6288 (פְּאֹרָה), KJV: beautify, boast self, go over the boughs, glorify (self), glory, vaunt self.

H6287 פְּאֵר (pᵉʼêr, peh-ayr'): an embellishment, i.e. fancy head-dress. Origin: from H6286 (פָּאַר); KJV: beauty, bonnet, goodly, ornament, tire.

H6288 פְּאֹרָה (pᵉʼôrâh, peh-o-raw'): properly, ornamentation, i.e. (plural) foliage (including the limbs) as bright green. Origin: or פֹּרָאה; or פֻּארָה; from H6286 (פָּאַר); KJV: bough, branch, sprig.

H6289 פָּארוּר (pâʼrûwr, paw-roor'): properly, illuminated, i.e. a glow; as noun, a flush (of anxiety). Origin: from H6286 (פָּאַר); KJV: blackness.

H6290 פָּארָן (Pâʼrân, paw-rawn'): Paran, a desert of Arabia. Origin: from H6286 (פָּאַר); ornamental; KJV: Paran.

H6291 פַּג (pag, pag): crude; an unripe fig. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be torpid, i.e. KJV: green figuratively

H6292 פִּגּוּל (piggûwl, pig-gool'): properly, fetid, i.e. (figuratively) unclean (ceremonially). Origin: or פִּגֻּל; from an unused root meaning to stink; KJV: abominable(-tion, thing).

H6293 פָּגַע (pâgaʻ, paw-gah'): to impinge, by accident or violence, or (figuratively) by importunity. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: come (betwixt), cause to entreat, fall (upon), make intercession, intercessor, intreat, lay, light (upon), meet (together), pray, reach, run.

H6294 פֶּגַע (pegaʻ, peh'-gah): impact (casual). Origin: from H6293 (פָּגַע); KJV: chance, occurent.

H6295 פַּגְעִיאֵל (Pagʻîyʼêl, pag-ee-ale'): Pagiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H6294 (פֶּגַע) and H410 (אֵל); accident of God; KJV: Pagiel.

H6296 פָּגַר (pâgar, paw-gar'): to relax, i.e. become exhausted. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be faint.
