H6297 פֶּגֶר (peger, peh'gher): a carcase (as limp), whether of man or beast; figuratively, an idolatrous image. Origin: from H6296 (פָּגַר); KJV: carcase, corpse, dead body.

H6298 פָּגַשׁ (pâgash, paw-gash'): to come in contact with, whether by accident or violence; figuratively, to concur. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: meet (with, together).

H6299 פָּדָה (pâdâh, paw-daw'): to sever, i.e. ransom; gener. to release, preserve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, deliver, [idiom] by any means, ransom, (that are to be, let be) redeem(-ed), rescue, [idiom] surely.

H6300 פְּדַהְאֵל (Pᵉdahʼêl, ped-ah-ale'): Pedahel, an Israelite. Origin: from H6299 (פָּדָה) and H410 (אֵל); God has ransomed; KJV: Pedahel.

H6301 פְּדָהצוּר (Pᵉdâhtsûwr, ped-aw-tsoor'): Pedahtsur, an Israelite. Origin: from H6299 (פָּדָה) and H6697 (צוּר); a rock (i.e. God) has ransomed; KJV: Pedahzur.

H6302 פָּדוּי (pâdûwy, paw-doo'ee): as abstractly (in plural masculine) a ransom. Origin: passive participle of H6299 (פָּדָה). ransomed (and so occurring under H6299 (פָּדָה)); KJV: (that are) to be (that were) redeemed.

H6303 פָּדוֹן (Pâdôwn, paw-done'): Padon, one of the Nethinim. Origin: from H6299 (פָּדָה); ransom; KJV: Padon.

H6304 פְּדוּת (pᵉdûwth, ped-ooth'): distinction; also deliverance. Origin: or פְּדֻת; from H6929 (קֵדְמָה)lemma קדְמָה missing vowel, corrected to קֵדְמָה; KJV: division, redeem, redemption.

H6305 פְּדָיָה (Pᵉdâyâh, ped-aw-yaw'): Pedajah, the name of six Israelites. Origin: or פְּדָיָהוּ; from H6299 (פָּדָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has ransomed; KJV: Pedaiah.

H6306 פִּדְיוֹם (pidyôwm, pid-yome'): a ransom. Origin: or פִּדְיֹם; also פִּדְיוֹן; or פִּדְיֹן; from H6299 (פָּדָה); KJV: ransom, that were redeemed, redemption.

H6307 פַּדָּן (Paddân, pad-dawn'): Paddan or Paddan-Aram, a region of Syria. Origin: from an unused root meaning to extend; a plateau; or פַּדַּן אֲרָם; from the same and H758 (אֲרָם); the table-land of Aram; KJV: Padan, Padan-aram.

H6308 פָּדַע (pâdaʻ, paw-dah'): to retrieve. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deliver.

H6309 פֶּדֶר (peder, peh'der): suet. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be greasy; KJV: fat.

H6310 פֶּה (peh, peh): the mouth (as the means of blowing), whether literal or figurative (particularly speech); specifically edge, portion or side; adverbially (with preposition) according to. Origin: from H6284 (פָּאָה); KJV: accord(-ing as, -ing to), after, appointment, assent, collar, command(-ment), [idiom] eat, edge, end, entry, [phrase] file, hole, [idiom] in, mind, mouth, part, portion, [idiom] (should) say(-ing), sentence, skirt, sound, speech, [idiom] spoken, talk, tenor, [idiom] to, [phrase] two-edged, wish, word.

H6311 פֹּה (pôh, po): this place (French ici), i.e. here or hence. Origin: or פֹּא; (Job 38:11), or פּוֹ; probably from a primitive inseparable particle 'p' (of demonstrative force) and H1931 (הוּא); KJV: here, hither, the one (other, this, that) side.

H6312 פּוּאָה (Pûwʼâh, poo-aw'): Puah or Puvvah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or פֻּוָּה; from H6284 (פָּאָה); a blast; KJV: Phuvah, Pua, Puah.

H6313 פּוּג (pûwg, poog): to be sluggish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease, be feeble, faint, be slacked.

H6314 פּוּגָה (pûwgâh, poo-gaw'): intermission. Origin: from H6313 (פּוּג); KJV: rest.

H6315 פּוּחַ (pûwach, poo'akh): to puff, i.e. blow with the breath or air; hence, to fan (as a breeze), to utter, to kindle (a fire), to scoff. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: blow (upon), break, puff, bring into a snare, speak, utter.

H6316 פּוּט (Pûwṭ, poot): Put, a son of Ham, also the name of his descendants or their region, and of a Persian tribe. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Phut, Put.

H6317 פּוּטִיאֵל (Pûwṭîyʼêl, poo-tee-ale'): Putiel, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root (probably meaning to disparage) and H410 (אֵל); contempt of God; KJV: Putiel.

H6318 פּוֹטִיפַר (Pôwṭîyphar, po-tee-far'): Potiphar, an Egyptian. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Potiphar.

H6319 פּוֹטִי פֶרַע (Pôwṭîy Pheraʻ, po-tee feh'-rah): Poti-Phera, an Egyptian. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Poti-pherah.

H6320 פּוּךְ (pûwk, pook): dye (specifically, stibium for the eyes). Origin: from an unused root meaning to paint; KJV: fair colours, glistering, paint(-ed) (-ing).

H6321 פּוֹל (pôwl, pole): a bean (as plump). Origin: from an unused root meaning to be thick; KJV: beans.

H6322 פּוּל (Pûwl, pool): Pul, the name of an Assyrian king and of an Ethiopian tribe. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Pul.

H6323 פּוּן (pûwn, poon): be perplexed. Origin: a primitive root meaning to turn, i.e. KJV: be distracted.

H6324 פּוּנִי (Pûwnîy, poo-nee'): a Punite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Pun. Origin: patronymically from an unused name meaning a turn; KJV: Punites.

H6325 פּוּנֹן (Pûwnôn, poo-none'): Punon, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H6323 (פּוּן); perplexity; KJV: Punon.

H6326 פּוּעָה (Pûwʻâh, poo-aw'): Puah, an Israelitess. Origin: from an unused root meaning to glitter; brilliancy; KJV: Puah.

H6327 פּוּץ (pûwts, poots): to dash in pieces, literally or figuratively (especially to disperse). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break (dash, shake) in (to) pieces, cast (abroad), disperse (selves), drive, retire, scatter (abroad), spread abroad.

H6328 פּוּק (pûwq, pook): to waver. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: stumble, move.

H6329 פּוּק (pûwq, pook): to issue, i.e. furnish; causatively, to secure; figuratively, to succeed. Origin: a primitive root (identical with H6328 (פּוּק) through the idea of dropping out; compare H5312 (נְפַק)); KJV: afford, draw out, further, get, obtain.

H6330 פּוּקָה (pûwqâh, poo-kaw'): a stumbling-block. Origin: from H6328 (פּוּק); KJV: grief.

H6331 פּוּר (pûwr, poor): to crush. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break, bring to nought, [idiom] utterly take.

H6332 פּוּר (Pûwr, poor): a lot (as by means of a broken piece). Origin: also (plural) פּוּרִים; or פֻּרִים; from H6331 (פּוּר); KJV: Pur, Purim.

H6333 פּוּרָה (pûwrâh, poo-raw'): a wine-press (as crushing the grapes). Origin: from H6331 (פּוּר); KJV: winepress.

H6334 פּוֹרָתָא (Pôwrâthâʼ, po-raw-thaw'): Poratha, a son of Haman. Origin: of Persian origin; KJV: Poratha.

H6335 פּוּשׁ (pûwsh, poosh): to spread; figuratively, act proudly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: grow up, be grown fat, spread selves, be scattered.

H6336 פּוּתִי (Pûwthîy, poo-thee'): a Puthite (collectively) or descendants of an unknown Puth. Origin: patronymically from an unused name meaning a hinge; KJV: Puhites (as if from H6312 (פּוּאָה)).

H6337 פָּז (pâz, pawz): pure (gold); hence, gold itself (as refined). Origin: from H6338 (פָּזַז); KJV: fine (pure) gold.

H6338 פָּזַז (pâzaz, paw-zaz'): to refine (gold). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: best (gold).

H6339 פָּזַז (pâzaz, paw-zaz'): to solidify (as if by refining); also to spring (as if separating the limbs). Origin: a primitive root (identical with H6338 (פָּזַז)); KJV: leap, be made strong.

H6340 פָּזַר (pâzar, paw-zar'): to scatter, whether in enmity or bounty. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: disperse, scatter (abroad).

H6341 פַּח (pach, pakh): a (metallic) sheet (as pounded thin); also a spring net (as spread out like a lamina). Origin: from H6351 (פָּחַח); KJV: gin, (thin) plate, snare.

H6342 פָּחַד (pâchad, paw-kkad'): to be startled (by a sudden alarm); hence, to fear in general. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be afraid, stand in awe, (be in) fear, make to shake.

H6343 פַּחַד (pachad, pakh'-ad): a (sudden) alarm (properly, the object feared, by implication, the feeling). Origin: from H6342 (פָּחַד); KJV: dread(-ful), fear, (thing) great (fear, -ly feared), terror.

H6344 פַּחַד (pachad, pakh'-ad): a testicle (as a cause of shame akin to fear). Origin: the same as H6343 (פַּחַד); KJV: stone.

H6345 פַּחְדָּה (pachdâh, pakh-daw'): alarm (i.e. awe). Origin: feminine of H6343 (פַּחַד); KJV: fear.

H6346 פֶּחָה (pechâh, peh-khaw'): a prefect (of a city or small district). Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: captain, deputy, governor.

H6347 פֶּחָה (pechâh, peh-khaw'): {a prefect (of a city or small district)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6346 (פֶּחָה) KJV: captain, governor.

H6348 פָּחַז (pâchaz, paw-khaz'): to bubble up or froth (as boiling water), i.e. (figuratively) to be unimportant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: light.

H6349 פַּחַז (pachaz, pakh'-az): ebullition, i.e. froth (figuratively, lust). Origin: from H6348 (פָּחַז); KJV: unstable.

H6350 פַּחֲזוּת (pachăzûwth, pakh-az-ooth'): frivolity. Origin: from H6348 (פָּחַז); KJV: lightness.

H6351 פָּחַח (pâchach, paw-khakh'): to spread a net. Origin: a primitive root; to batter out; but used only as denominative from H6341 (פַּח), KJV: be snared.

H6352 פֶּחָם (pechâm, peh-khawm'): a coal, whether charred or live. Origin: perhaps from an unused root probably meaning to be black; KJV: coals.

H6353 פֶּחָר (pechâr, peh-khawr'): a potter. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root probably meaning to fashion; KJV: potter.

H6354 פַּחַת (pachath, pakh'-ath): a pit, especially forcatching animals. Origin: probably from an unused root apparently meaning to dig; KJV: hole, pit, snare.

H6355 פַּחַת מוֹאָב (Pachath Môwʼâb, pakh'-ath mo-awb'): Pachath-Moab, an Israelite. Origin: from H6354 (פַּחַת) and H4124 (מוֹאָב); pit of Moab; KJV: Pahathmoab.

H6356 פְּחֶתֶת (pᵉchetheth, pekh-eh'-theth): a hole (by mildew in a garment). Origin: from the same as H6354 (פַּחַת); KJV: fret inward.

H6357 פִּטְדָה (piṭdâh, pit-daw'): a gem, probably the topaz. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: topaz.

H6358 פָּטוּר (pâṭûwr, paw-toor'): opened, i.e. (as noun) a bud. Origin: passive participle of H6362 (פָּטַר); KJV: open.

H6359 פָּטִיר (pâṭîyr, paw-teer'): open, i.e. unoccupied. Origin: from H6362 (פָּטַר); KJV: free.

H6360 פַּטִּישׁ (paṭṭîysh, pat-teesh'): a hammer. Origin: intensively from an unused root meaning to pound; KJV: hammer.

H6361 פַּטִּישׁ (paṭṭîysh, pat-teesh'): a gown (as if hammered out wide). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to that of H6360 (פַּטִּישׁ); KJV: hose.

H6362 פָּטַר (pâṭar, paw-tar'): to cleave or burst through, i.e. (causatively) to emit, whether literal or figurative (gape). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dismiss, free, let (shoot) out, slip away.

H6363 פֶּטֶר (peṭer, peh'-ter): a fissure, i.e. (concretely) firstling (as opening the matrix). Origin: or פִּטְרָה; from H6362 (פָּטַר); KJV: firstling, openeth, such as open.

H6364 פִּי־בֶסֶת (Pîy-Beçeth, pee beh'-seth): Pi-Beseth, a place in Egypt. Origin: of Egyptian origin; KJV: Pi-beseth.

H6365 פִּיד (pîyd, peed): (figuratively) misfortune. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to pierce; KJV: destruction, ruin.

H6366 פֵּיָה (pêyâh, pay-aw'): an edge. Origin: or פִּיָּה; feminine of H6310 (פֶּה); KJV: (two-) edge(-d).

H6367 פִּי הַחִירֹת (Pîy ha-Chîyrôth, pee hah-khee-roth'): Pi-ha-Chiroth, a place in Egypt. Origin: from H6310 (פֶּה) and the feminine plural of a noun (from the same root as H2356 (חוֹר)), with the article interpolated; mouth of the gorges; KJV: Pi-hahiroth. (In Numbers 14:19 without Pi-.)

H6368 פִּיחַ (pîyach, pee'-akh): a powder (as easily puffed away), i.e. ashes or dust. Origin: from H6315 (פּוּחַ); KJV: ashes.

H6369 פִּיכֹל (Pîykôl, pee-kole'): Picol, a Philistine. Origin: apparently from H6310 (פֶּה) and H3605 (כֹּל); mouth of all; KJV: Phichol.

H6370 פִּילֶגֶשׁ (pîylegesh, pee-leh'-ghesh): a concubine; also (masculine) a paramour. Origin: or פִּלֶגֶשׁ; of uncertain derivation; KJV: concubine, paramour.

H6371 פִּימָה (pîymâh, pee-maw'): obesity. Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to be plump; KJV: collops.

H6372 פִּינְחָס (Pîynᵉchâç, pee-nekh-aws'): Pinechas, the name of three Israelites. Origin: apparently from H6310 (פֶּה) and a variation of H5175 (נָחָשׁ); mouth of a serpent; KJV: Phinehas.

H6373 פִּינֹן (pîynôn, pee-none'): Pinon, an Idumaean. Origin: probably the same as H6325 (פּוּנֹן); KJV: Pinon.

H6374 פִּיפִיָּה (pîyphîyâh, pee-fee-yaw'): an edge or tooth. Origin: for H6366 (פֵּיָה); KJV: tooth, [idiom] two-edged.

H6375 פִּיק (pîyq, peek): a tottering. Origin: from H6329 (פּוּק); KJV: smite together.

H6376 פִּישׁוֹן (Pîyshôwn, pee-shone'): Pishon, a river of Eden. Origin: from H6335 (פּוּשׁ); dispersive; KJV: Pison.

H6377 פִּיתוֹן (Pîythôwn, pee-thone'): Pithon, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the same as H6596 (פֹּת); expansive; KJV: Pithon.

H6378 פַּךְ (pak, pak): a flask (from which a liquid may flow). Origin: from H6379 (פָּכָה); KJV: box, vial.

H6379 פָּכָה (pâkâh, paw-kaw'): to pour. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: run out.

H6380 פֹּכֶרֶת צְבָיִים (Pôkereth Tsᵉbâyîym, po-keh'-reth tseb-awyeem'): Pokereth-Tsebajim, one of the 'servants of Solomon'. Origin: from the active participle (of the same form as the first word) feminine of an unused root (meaning to entrap) and plural of H6643 (צְבִי); trap of gazelles; KJV: Pochereth of Zebaim.

H6381 פָּלָא (pâlâʼ, paw-law'): properly, perhaps to separate, i.e. distinguish (literally or figuratively); by implication, to be (causatively, make) great, difficult, wonderful. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: accomplish, (arise...too, be too) hard, hidden, things too high, (be, do, do a, shew) marvelous(-ly, -els, things, work), miracles, perform, separate, make singular, (be, great, make) wonderful(-ers, -ly, things, works), wondrous (things, works, -ly).

H6382 פֶּלֶא (peleʼ, peh'-leh): a miracle. Origin: from H6381 (פָּלָא); KJV: marvellous thing, wonder(-ful, -fully).

H6383 פִּלְאִי (pilʼîy, pil-ee'): remarkable. Origin: or פָּלִיא; from H6381 (פָּלָא); KJV: secret, wonderful.

H6384 פַּלֻּאִי (Palluʼîy, pal-loo-ee'): a Palluite (collectively) or descendants of Pallu. Origin: patronymically from H6396 (פַּלּוּא); KJV: Palluites.

H6385 פָּלַג (pâlag, paw-lag'): to split (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: divide.

H6386 פְּלַג (pᵉlag, pel-ag'): {to split (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6385 (פָּלַג) KJV: divided.

H6387 פְּלַג (pᵉlag, pel-ag'): a half. Origin: (Aramaic) from H6386 (פְּלַג); KJV: dividing.

H6388 פֶּלֶג (peleg, peh'-leg): a rill (i.e. small channel of water, as in irrigation). Origin: from H6385 (פָּלַג); KJV: river, stream.

H6389 פֶּלֶג (Peleg, peh'-leg): Peleg, a son of Shem. Origin: the same as H6388 (פֶּלֶג); earthquake; KJV: Peleg.

H6390 פְּלַגָּה (pᵉlaggâh, pel-ag-gaw'): a runlet, i.e. gully. Origin: from H6385 (פָּלַג); KJV: division, river.

H6391 פְּלֻגָּה (pᵉluggâh, pel-oog-gaw'): a section. Origin: from H6385 (פָּלַג); KJV: division.

H6392 פְּלֻגָּה (pᵉluggâh, pel-oog-gaw'): {a section}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6391 (פְּלֻגָּה) KJV: division.

H6393 פְּלָדָה (pᵉlâdâh, pel-aw-daw'): a cleaver, i.e. iron armature (of a chariot). Origin: from an unused root meaning to divide; KJV: torch.

H6394 פִּלְדָּשׁ (Pildâsh, pil-dawsh'): Pildash, a relative of Abraham. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Pildash.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6395 to H6523
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6395 פָּלָה (pâlâh, paw-law'): to distinguish (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: put a difference, show marvellous, separate, set apart, sever, make wonderfully.

H6396 פַּלּוּא (Pallûwʼ, pal-loo'): Pallu, an Israelite. Origin: from H6395 (פָּלָה); distinguished; KJV: Pallu, Phallu.

H6397 פְּלוֹנִי (Pᵉlôwnîy, pel-o-nee'): a Pelonite or inhabitant of an unknown Palon. Origin: patronymically from an unused name (from H6395 (פָּלָה)) meaning separate; KJV: Pelonite.

H6398 פָּלַח (pâlach, paw-lakh'): to slice, i.e. break open or pierce. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring forth, cleave, cut, shred, strike through.

H6399 פְּלַח (pᵉlach, pel-akh'): to serve or worship. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6398 (פָּלַח); KJV: minister, serve.

H6400 פֶּלַח (pelach, peh'-lakh): a slice. Origin: from H6398 (פָּלַח); KJV: piece.

H6401 פִּלְחָא (Pilchâʼ, pil-khaw'): Pilcha, an Israelite. Origin: from H6400 (פֶּלַח); slicing; KJV: Pilcha.

H6402 פׇּלְחָן (polchân, pol-khawn'): worship. Origin: (Aramaic) from H6399 (פְּלַח); KJV: service.

H6403 פָּלַט (pâlaṭ, paw-lat'): to slip out, i.e. escape; causatively, to deliver. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: calve, carry away safe, deliver, (cause to) escape.

H6404 פֶּלֶט (Peleṭ, peh'-let): Pelet, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6403 (פָּלַט); escape; KJV: Pelet. See also H1046 (בֵּית פֶּלֶט).

H6405 פַּלֵּט (pallêṭ, pal-late'): escape. Origin: from H6403 (פָּלַט); KJV: deliverance, escape.

H6406 פַּלְטִי (Palṭîy, pal-tee'): Palti, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6403 (פָּלַט); delivered; KJV: Palti, Phalti.

H6407 פַּלְטִי (Palṭîy, pal-tee'): a Paltite or descendant of Palti. Origin: patronymically from H6406 (פַּלְטִי); KJV: Paltite.

H6408 פִּלְטַי (Pilṭay, pil-tah'-ee): Piltai, an Israelite. Origin: for H6407 (פַּלְטִי); KJV: Piltai.

H6409 פַּלְטִיאֵל (Palṭîyʼêl, pal-tee-ale'): Paltiel, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from the same as H6404 (פֶּלֶט) and H410 (אֵל); deliverance of God; KJV: Paltiel, Phaltiel.

H6410 פְּלַטְיָה (Pᵉlaṭyâh, pel-at-yaw'): Pelatjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or פְּלַטְיָהוּ; from H6403 (פָּלַט) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has delivered; KJV: Pelatiah.

H6411 פְּלָיָה (Pᵉlâyâh, pel-aw-yaw'): Pelajah, the name of three Israelites. Origin: or פְּלָאיָה; from H6381 (פָּלָא) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has distinguished; KJV: Pelaiah.

H6412 פָּלִיט (pâlîyṭ, paw-leet'): a refugee. Origin: or פָּלֵיט; or פָּלֵט; from H6403 (פָּלַט); KJV: (that have) escape(-d, -th), fugitive.

H6413 פְּלֵיטָה (pᵉlêyṭâh, pel-ay-taw'): deliverance; concretely, an escaped portion. Origin: or פְּלֵטָה; feminine of H6412 (פָּלִיט); KJV: deliverance, (that is) escape(-d), remnant.

H6414 פָּלִיל (pâlîyl, paw-leel'): a magistrate. Origin: from H6419 (פָּלַל); KJV: judge.

H6415 פְּלִילָה (pᵉlîylâh, pel-ee-law'): justice. Origin: feminine of H6414 (פָּלִיל); KJV: judgment.

H6416 פְּלִילִי (pᵉlîylîy, pel-ee-lee'): judicial. Origin: from H6414 (פָּלִיל); KJV: judge.

H6417 פְּלִילִיָּה (pᵉlîylîyâh, pel-ee-lee-yaw'): judicature. Origin: feminine of H6416 (פְּלִילִי); KJV: judgment.

H6418 פֶּלֶךְ (pelek, peh'-lek): a circuit (i.e. district); also a spindle (as whirled); hence, a crutch. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be round; KJV: (di-) staff, participle

H6419 פָּלַל (pâlal, paw-lal'): to judge (officially or mentally); by extension, to intercede, pray. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: intreat, judge(-ment), (make) pray(-er, -ing), make supplication.

H6420 פָּלָל (Pâlâl, paw-lawl'): Palal, an Israelite. Origin: from H6419 (פָּלַל); judge; KJV: Palal.

H6421 פְּלַלְיָה (Pᵉlalyâh, pel-al-yaw'): Pelaljah, an Israelite. Origin: from H6419 (פָּלַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has judged; KJV: Pelaliah.

H6422 פַּלְמוֹנִי (palmôwnîy, pal-mo-nee'): a certain one, i.e. so-and-so. Origin: probably for H6423 (פְּלֹנִי); KJV: certain.

H6423 פְּלֹנִי (pᵉlônîy, pel-o-nee'): such a one, i.e. a specified person. Origin: from H6395 (פָּלָה); KJV: such.

H6424 פָּלַס (pâlaç, paw-las'): properly, to roll flat, i.e. prepare (a road); also to revolve, i.e. weigh (mentally). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make, ponder, weigh.

H6425 פֶּלֶס (peleç, peh'-les): a balance. Origin: from H6424 (פָּלַס); KJV: scales, weight.

H6426 פָּלַץ (pâlats, paw-lats'): properly, perhaps to rend, i.e. (by implication) to quiver. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tremble.

H6427 פַּלָּצוּת (pallâtsûwth, pal-law-tsooth'): affright. Origin: from H6426 (פָּלַץ); KJV: fearfulness, horror, trembling.

H6428 פָּלַשׁ (pâlash, paw-lash'): to roll (in dust). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: roll (wallow) self.

H6429 פְּלֶשֶׁת (Pᵉlesheth, pel-eh'-sheth): Pelesheth, a region of Syria. Origin: from H6428 (פָּלַשׁ); rolling, i.e. migratory; KJV: Palestina, Palestine, Philistia, Philistines.

H6430 פְּלִשְׁתִּי (Pᵉlishtîy, pel-ish-tee'): a Pelishtite or inhabitant of Pelesheth. Origin: patrial from H6429 (פְּלֶשֶׁת); KJV: Philistine.

H6431 פֶּלֶת (Peleth, peh'-leth): Peleth, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from an unused root meaning to flee; swiftness; KJV: Peleth.

H6432 פְּלֵתִי (Pᵉlêthîy, pel-ay-thee'): a courier (collectively) or official messenger. Origin: from the same form as H6431 (פֶּלֶת); KJV: Pelethites.

H6433 פֻּם (pum, poom): the mouth (literally or figuratively). Origin: (Aramaic) probably for H6310 (פֶּה); KJV: mouth.

H6434 פֵּן (pên, pane): an angle (of a street or wall). Origin: from an unused root meaning to turn; KJV: corner.

H6435 פֵּן (pên, pane): properly, removal; used only (in the construction) adverb as conjunction, lest. Origin: from H6437 (פָּנָה); KJV: (lest) (peradventure), that...not.

H6436 פַּנַּג (pannag, pan-nag'): probably pastry. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Pannag.

H6437 פָּנָה (pânâh, paw-naw'): to turn; by implication, to face, i.e. appear, look, etc. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appear, at (even-) tide, behold, cast out, come on, [idiom] corner, dawning, empty, go away, lie, look, mark, pass away, prepare, regard, (have) respect (to), (re-) turn (aside, away, back, face, self), [idiom] right (early).

H6438 פִּנָּה (pinnâh, pin-naw'): an angle; by implication, a pinnacle; figuratively, a chieftain. Origin: feminine of H6434 (פֵּן); KJV: bulwark, chief, corner, stay, tower.

H6439 פְּנוּאֵל (Pᵉnûwʼêl, pen-oo-ale'): Penuel or Peniel, a place East of Jordan; also (as Penuel) the name of two Israelites. Origin: or (more properly,) פְּנִיאֵל; from H6437 (פָּנָה) and H410 (אֵל); face of God; KJV: Peniel, Penuel.

H6440 פָּנִים (pânîym, paw-neem'): the face (as the part that turns); used in a great variety of applications (literally and figuratively); also (with prepositional prefix) as a preposition (before, etc.). Origin: plural (but always as singular) of an unused noun פָּנֶה; from H6437 (פָּנָה)); KJV: [phrase] accept, a-(be-) fore(-time), against, anger, [idiom] as (long as), at, [phrase] battle, [phrase] because (of), [phrase] beseech, countenance, edge, [phrase] employ, endure, [phrase] enquire, face, favour, fear of, for, forefront(-part), form(-er time, -ward), from, front, heaviness, [idiom] him(-self), [phrase] honourable, [phrase] impudent, [phrase] in, it, look(-eth) (-s), [idiom] me, [phrase] meet, [idiom] more than, mouth, of, off, (of) old (time), [idiom] on, open, [phrase] out of, over against, the partial, person, [phrase] please, presence, propect, was purposed, by reason of, [phrase] regard, right forth, [phrase] serve, [idiom] shewbread, sight, state, straight, [phrase] street, [idiom] thee, [idiom] them(-selves), through ([phrase] -out), till, time(-s) past, (un-) to(-ward), [phrase] upon, upside ([phrase] down), with(-in, [phrase] -stand), [idiom] ye, [idiom] you.

H6441 פְּנִימָה (pᵉnîymâh, pen-ee'-maw): faceward, i.e. indoors. Origin: from H6440 (פָּנִים) with directive enclitic; KJV: (with-) in(-ner part, -ward).

H6442 פְּנִימִי (pᵉnîymîy, pen-ee-mee'): interior. Origin: from H6440 (פָּנִים); KJV: (with-) in(-ner, -ward).

H6443 פָּנִין (pânîyn, paw-neen'): probably a pearl (as round). Origin: or פָּנִי; from the same as H6434 (פֵּן); KJV: ruby.

H6444 פְּנִנָּה (Pᵉninnâh, pen-in-naw'): Peninnah, an Israelitess. Origin: probably feminine from H6443 (פָּנִין) contr.; KJV: Peninnah.

H6445 פָּנַק (pânaq, paw-nak'): to enervate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring up.

H6446 פַּס (paç, pas): a long and sleeved tunic (perhaps simply a wide one; from the original sense of the root, i.e. of many breadths). Origin: from H6461 (פָּסַס); properly, the palm (of the hand) or sole (of the foot) (compare H6447 (פַּס)); by implication (plural) KJV: (divers) colours.

H6447 פַּס (paç, pas): the palm (of the hand, as being spread out). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H6461 (פָּסַס); KJV: participle

H6448 פָּסַג (pâçag, paw-sag'): to cut up, i.e. (figuratively) contemplate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consider.

H6449 פִּסְגָּה (Piçgâh, pis-gaw'): Pisgah, a Mountain East of Jordan. Origin: from H6448 (פָּסַג); a cleft; KJV: Pisgah.

H6450 פַּס דַּמִּים (Paç Dammîym, pas dam-meem'): Pas-Dammim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6446 (פַּס) and the plural of H1818 (דָּם); palm (i.e. dell) of bloodshed; KJV: Pas-dammim. Compare H658 (אֶפֶס דַּמִּים).

H6451 פִּסָּה (piççâh, pis-saw'): expansion, i.e. abundance. Origin: from H6461 (פָּסַס); KJV: handful.

H6452 פָּסַח (pâçach, paw-sakh'): to hop, i.e. (figuratively) skip over (or spare); by implication, to hesitate; also (literally) to limp, to dance. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: halt, become lame, leap, pass over.

H6453 פֶּסַח (peçach, peh'-sakh): a pretermission, i.e. exemption; used only techically of the Jewish Passover (the festival or the victim). Origin: from H6452 (פָּסַח); KJV: passover (offering).

H6454 פָּסֵחַ (Pâçêach, paw-say'-akh): Paseach, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6452 (פָּסַח); limping; KJV: Paseah, Phaseah.

H6455 פִּסֵּחַ (piççêach, pis-say'-akh): lame. Origin: from H6452 (פָּסַח); KJV: lame.

H6456 פְּסִיל (pᵉçîyl, pes-eel'): an idol. Origin: from H6458 (פָּסַל); KJV: carved (graven) image, quarry.

H6457 פָּסַךְ (Pâçak, paw-sak'): Pasak, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to divide; divider; KJV: Pasach.

H6458 פָּסַל (pâçal, paw-sal'): to carve, whether wood or stone. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: grave, hew.

H6459 פֶּסֶל (peçel, peh'-sel): an idol. Origin: from H6458 (פָּסַל); KJV: carved (graven) image.

H6460 פְּסַנְטֵרִין (pᵉçanṭêrîyn, pes-an-tay-reen'): psalterion; a lyre. Origin: (Aramaic) or פְּסַנְתֵּרִין; a transliteration of the Greek, KJV: psaltery.

H6461 פָּסַס (pâçaç, paw-sas'): probably to disperse, i.e. (intransitive) disappear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cease.

H6462 פִּסְפָּה (Piçpâh, pis-paw'): Pispah, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H6461 (פָּסַס); dispersion; KJV: Pispah.

H6463 פָּעָה (pâʻâh, paw-aw'): to scream. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cry.

H6464 פָּעוּ (Pâʻûw, paw-oo'): Pau or Pai, a place in Edom. Origin: or פָּעִי; from H6463 (פָּעָה); screaming; KJV: Pai, Pau.

H6465 פְּעוֹר (Pᵉʻôwr, peh-ore'): Peor, a mountain East of Jordan; Baal Peor, (for a deity worshipped there. Origin: from H6473 (פָּעַר); a gap; also H1187 (בַּעַל פְּעוֹר)) KJV: Peor. See also H1047 (בֵּית פְּעוֹר).

H6466 פָּעַל (pâʻal, paw-al'): to do or make (systematically and habitually), especially to practise. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: commit, (evil-) do(-er), make(-r), ordain, work(-er).

H6467 פֹּעַל (pôʻal, po'-al): an act or work (concretely). Origin: from H6466 (פָּעַל); KJV: act, deed, do, getting, maker, work.

H6468 פְּעֻלָּה (pᵉʻullâh, peh-ool-law'): (abstractly) work. Origin: feminine passive participle of H6466 (פָּעַל); KJV: labour, reward, wages, work.

H6469 פְּעֻלְּתַי (Pᵉʻullᵉthay, peh-ool-leh-thah'-ee): Peullethai, an Israelite. Origin: from H6468 (פְּעֻלָּה); laborious; KJV: Peulthai.

H6470 פָּעַם (pâʻam, paw-am'): to tap, i.e. beat regularly; hence (generally) to impel or agitate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: move, trouble.

H6471 פַּעַם (paʻam, pah'-am): a stroke, literally or figuratively (in various applications, as follow). Origin: or (feminine) פַּעֲמָה; from H6470 (פָּעַם); KJV: anvil, corner, foot(-step), going, (hundred-) fold, [idiom] now, (this) [phrase] once, order, rank, step, [phrase] thrice, (often-), second, this, two) time(-s), twice, wheel.

H6472 פַּעֲמֹן (paʻămôn, pah-am-one'): a bell (as struck). Origin: from H6471 (פַּעַם); KJV: bell.

H6473 פָּעַר (pâʻar, paw-ar'): to yawn, i.e. open wide (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gape, open (wide).

H6474 פַּעֲרַי (Paʻăray, pah-ar-ah'-ee): Paarai, an Israelite. Origin: from H6473 (פָּעַר); yawning; KJV: Paarai.

H6475 פָּצָה (pâtsâh, paw-tsaw'): to rend, i.e. open (especially the mouth). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: deliver, gape, open, rid, utter.

H6476 פָּצַח (pâtsach, paw-tsakh'): to break out (in joyful sound). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break (forth, forth into joy), make a loud noise.

H6477 פְּצִירָה (pᵉtsîyrâh, pets-ee-raw'): bluntness. Origin: from H6484 (פָּצַר); KJV: [phrase] file.

H6478 פָּצַל (pâtsal, paw-tsal'): to peel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pill.

H6479 פְּצָלָה (pᵉtsâlâh, pets-aw-law'): a peeling. Origin: from H6478 (פָּצַל); KJV: strake.

H6480 פָּצַם (pâtsam, paw-tsam'): to rend (by earthquake). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break.

H6481 פָּצַע (pâtsaʻ, paw-tsah'): to split, i.e. wound. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wound.

H6482 פֶּצַע (petsaʻ, peh'-tsah): a wound. Origin: from H6481 (פָּצַע); KJV: wound(-ing).

H6483 פִּצֵּץ (Pitstsêts, pits-tsates'): Pitstsets, a priest. Origin: from an unused root meaning to dissever; dispersive; KJV: Apses (including the article).

H6484 פָּצַר (pâtsar, paw-tsar'): to peck at, i.e. (figuratively) stun or dull. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: press, urge, stubbornness.

H6485 פָּקַד (pâqad, paw-kad'): to visit (with friendly or hostile intent); by analogy, to oversee, muster, charge, care for, miss, deposit, etc. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, [idiom] at all, avenge, bestow, (appoint to have the, give a) charge, commit, count, deliver to keep, be empty, enjoin, go see, hurt, do judgment, lack, lay up, look, make, [idiom] by any means, miss, number, officer, (make) overseer, have (the) oversight, punish, reckon, (call to) remember(-brance), set (over), sum, [idiom] surely, visit, want.

H6486 פְּקֻדָּה (pᵉquddâh, pek-ood-daw'): visitation (in many senses, chiefly official). Origin: feminine passive participle of H6485 (פָּקַד); KJV: account, (that have the) charge, custody, that which...laid up, numbers, office(-r), ordering, oversight, [phrase] prison, reckoning, visitation.

H6487 פִּקָּדוֹן (piqqâdôwn, pik-kaw-done'): a deposit. Origin: from H6485 (פָּקַד); KJV: that which was delivered (to keep), store.

H6488 פְּקִדֻת (pᵉqiduth, pek-ee-dooth'): supervision. Origin: from H6496 (פָּקִיד); KJV: ward.

H6489 פְּקוֹד (Pᵉqôwd, pek-ode'): Pekod, a symbolic name for Babylon. Origin: from H6485 (פָּקַד); punishment; KJV: Pekod.

H6490 פִּקּוּד (piqqûwd, pik-kood'): properly, appointed, i.e. a mandate (of God; plural only, collectively, for the Law). Origin: or פִּקֻּד; from H6485 (פָּקַד); KJV: commandment, precept, statute.

H6491 פָּקַח (pâqach, paw-kakh'): to open (the senses, especially the eyes); figuratively, to be observant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: open.

H6492 פֶּקַח (Peqach, peh'-kakh): Pekach, an Israelite king. Origin: from H6491 (פָּקַח); watch; KJV: Pekah.

H6493 פִּקֵּחַ (piqqêach, pik-kay'-akh): clear-sighted; figuratively, intelligent. Origin: from H6491 (פָּקַח); KJV: seeing, wise.

H6494 פְּקַחְיָה (Pᵉqachyâh, pek-akh-yaw'): Pekachjah, an Israelite king. Origin: from H6491 (פָּקַח) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has observed; KJV: Pekahiah.

H6495 פְּקַח־קוֹחַ (pᵉqach-qôwach, pek-akh-ko'-akh): opening (of a dungeon), i.e. jail-delivery (figuratively, salvation for sin). Origin: from H6491 (פָּקַח) redoubled; KJV: opening of the prison.

H6496 פָּקִיד (pâqîyd, paw-keed'): a superintendent (civil, military or religious). Origin: from H6485 (פָּקַד); KJV: which had the charge, governor, office, overseer, (that) was set.

H6497 פֶּקַע (peqaʻ, peh'-kah): a semi-globe. Origin: from an unused root meaning to burst; only used as an architectural term of an ornament similar to H6498 (פַּקֻּעָה), KJV: knop.

H6498 פַּקֻּעָה (paqquʻâh, pak-koo-aw'): the wild cucumber (from splitting open to shed its seeds). Origin: from the same as H6497 (פֶּקַע); KJV: gourd.

H6499 פַּר (par, par): a bullock (apparently as breaking forth in wild strength, or perhaps as dividing the hoof). Origin: or פָּר; from H6565 (פָּרַר); KJV: ([phrase] young) bull(-ock), calf, ox.

H6500 פָּרָא (pârâʼ, paw-raw'): to bear fruit. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be fruitful.

H6501 פֶּרֶא (pereʼ, peh'-reh): the onager. Origin: or פֶּרֶה; (Jeremiah 2:24), from H6500 (פָּרָא) in the secondary sense of running wild; KJV: wild (ass).

H6502 פִּרְאָם (Pirʼâm, pir-awm'): Piram, a Canaanite. Origin: from H6501 (פֶּרֶא); wildly; KJV: Piram.

H6503 פַּרְבָּר (Parbâr, par-bawr'): Parbar or Parvar, a quarter of Jerusalem. Origin: or פַּרְוָר; of foreign origin; KJV: Parbar, suburb.

H6504 פָּרַד (pârad, paw-rad'): to break through, i.e. spread or separate (oneself). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: disperse, divide, be out of joint, part, scatter (abroad), separate (self), sever self, stretch, sunder.

H6505 פֶּרֶד (pered, peh'-red): a mule (perhaps from his lonely habits). Origin: from H6504 (פָּרַד); KJV: mule.

H6506 פִּרְדָּה (pirdâh, pir-daw'): a she-mule. Origin: feminine of H6505 (פֶּרֶד); KJV: mule.

H6507 פְּרֻדָה (pᵉrudâh, per-oo-daw'): something separated, i.e. a kernel. Origin: feminine passive participle of H6504 (פָּרַד); KJV: seed.

H6508 פַּרְדֵּס (pardêç, par-dace'): a park. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: forest, orchard.

H6509 פָּרָה (pârâh, paw-raw'): to bear fruit (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear, bring forth (fruit), (be, cause to be, make) fruitful, grow, increase.

H6510 פָּרָה (pârâh, paw-raw'): a heifer. Origin: feminine of H6499 (פַּר); KJV: cow, heifer, kine.

H6511 פָּרָה (Pârâh, paw-raw'): Parah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6510 (פָּרָה); KJV: Parah.

H6512 פֵּרָה (pêrâh, pay-raw'): a hole (as broken, i.e. dug). Origin: from H6331 (פּוּר); KJV: [phrase] mole. Compare H2661 (חֲפֹר).

H6513 פֻּרָה (Purâh, poo-raw'): Purah, an Israelite. Origin: for H6288 (פְּאֹרָה); foliage; KJV: Phurah.

H6514 פְּרוּדָא (Pᵉrûwdâʼ, per-oo-daw'): Peruda or Perida, one of 'Solomon's servants'. Origin: or פְּרִידָא; from H6504 (פָּרַד); dispersion; KJV: Perida, Peruda.

H6515 פָּרוּחַ (Pârûwach, paw-roo'-akh): Paruach, an Israelite. Origin: passive participle of H6524 (פָּרַח); blossomed; KJV: Paruah.

H6516 פַּרְוַיִם (Parvayim, par-vah'-yim): Parvajim, an Oriental region. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: Parvaim.

H6517 פָּרוּר (pârûwr, paw-roor'): a skillet (as flat or deep). Origin: passive participle of H6565 (פָּרַר) in the sense of spreading out (compare H6524 (פָּרַח)); KJV: pan, pot.

H6518 פָּרָז (pârâz, paw-rawz'): decide; a chieftain. Origin: from an unused root meaning to separate, i.e. KJV: village.

H6519 פְּרָזָה (pᵉrâzâh, per-aw-zaw'): an open country. Origin: from the same as H6518 (פָּרָז); KJV: (unwalled) town (without walls), unwalled village.

H6520 פְּרָזוֹן (pᵉrâzôwn, per-aw-zone'): magistracy, i.e. leadership (also concretely, chieftains). Origin: from the same as H6518 (פָּרָז); KJV: village.

H6521 פְּרָזִי (pᵉrâzîy, per-aw-zee'): a rustic. Origin: or פְּרוֹזִי; from H6519 (פְּרָזָה); KJV: village.

H6522 פְּרִזִּי (Pᵉrizzîy, per-iz-zee'): a Perizzite, one of the Canaanitish tribes. Origin: for H6521 (פְּרָזִי); inhabitant of the open country; KJV: Perizzite.

H6523 פַּרְזֶל (parzel, par-zel'): iron. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H1270 (בַּרְזֶל); KJV: iron.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6524 to H6655
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6524 פָּרַח (pârach, paw-rakh'): to break forth as a bud, i.e. bloom; generally, to spread; specifically, to fly (as extending the wings); figuratively, to flourish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] abroad, [idiom] abundantly, blossom, break forth (out), bud, flourish, make fly, grow, spread, spring (up).

H6525 פֶּרַח (perach, peh'-rakh): a calyx (natural or artificial); generally, bloom. Origin: from H6524 (פָּרַח); KJV: blossom, bud, flower.

H6634 צְבָא (tsᵉbâʼ, tseb-aw'): to please. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6623 (פִּתְרוֹן) in the figurative sense of summoning one's wishes; KJV: will, would.

H6635 צָבָא (tsâbâʼ, tsaw-baw'): a mass of persons (or figuratively, things), especially reg. organized forwar (an army); by implication, a campaign, literally or figuratively (specifically, hardship, worship). Origin: or (feminine) צְבָאָה; from H6633 (צָבָא); KJV: appointed time, ([phrase]) army, ([phrase]) battle, company, host, service, soldiers, waiting upon, war(-fare).

H6636 צְבֹאִים (Tsᵉbôʼîym, tseb-o-eem'): Tseboim or Tsebijim, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (more correctly) צְבִיִּים; or צְבִיִּם; plural of H6643 (צְבִי); gazelles; KJV: Zeboiim, Zeboim.

H6637 צֹבֵבָה (Tsôbêbâh, tso-bay-baw'): Tsobebah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine active participle of the same as H6632 (צָב); the canopier (with the article); KJV: Zobebah.

H6638 צָבָה (tsâbâh, tsaw-baw'): to amass, i.e. grow turgid; specifically, to array an army against. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fight swell.

H6639 צָבֶה (tsâbeh, tsaw-beh'): turgid. Origin: from H6638 (צָבָה); KJV: swell.

H6640 צְבוּ (tsᵉbûw, tseb-oo'): properly, will; concretely, an affair (as a matter of determination). Origin: (Aramaic) from H6634 (צְבָא); KJV: purpose.

H6641 צָבוּעַ (tsâbûwaʻ, tsaw-boo'-ah): dyed (in stripes), i.e. the hyena. Origin: passive participle of the same as H6648 (צֶבַע); KJV: speckled.

H6642 צָבַט (tsâbaṭ, tsaw-bat'): to grasp, i.e. hand out. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: reach.

H6643 צְבִי (tsᵉbîy, tseb-ee'): splendor (as conspicuous); also a gazelle (as beautiful). Origin: from H6638 (צָבָה) in the sense of prominence; KJV: beautiful(-ty), glorious (-ry), goodly, pleasant, roe(-buck).

H6644 צִבְיָא (Tsibyâʼ, tsib-yaw'): Tsibja, an Israelite. Origin: for H6645 (צִבְיָּה); KJV: Zibia.

H6645 צִבְיָּה (Tsibyâh, tsib-yaw'): Tsibjah, an Israelite. Origin: for H6646 (צְבִיָּה); KJV: Zibiah.

H6646 צְבִיָּה (tsᵉbîyâh, tseb-ee-yaw'): a female gazelle. Origin: feminine of H6643 (צְבִי); KJV: roe.

H6647 צְבַע (tsᵉbaʻ, tseb-ah'): to dip. Origin: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to that of H6648 (צֶבַע); KJV: wet.

H6648 צֶבַע (tsebaʻ, tseh'-bah): a dye. Origin: from an unused root meaning to dip (into coloring fluid); KJV: divers, colours.

H6649 צִבְעוֹן (Tsibʻôwn, tsib-one'): Tsibon, an Idumaean. Origin: from the same as H6648 (צֶבַע); variegated; KJV: Zibeon.

H6650 צְבֹעִים (Tsᵉbôʻîym, tseb-o-eem'): Tseboim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H6641 (צָבוּעַ); hyenas; KJV: Zeboim.

H6651 צָבַר (tsâbar, tsaw-bar'): to aggregate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather (together), heap (up), lay up.

H6652 צִבֻּר (tsibbur, tsib-boor'): a pile. Origin: from H6551 (פַּרְעֹשׁ); KJV: heap.

H6653 צֶבֶת (tsebeth, tseh'-beth): a lock of stalks. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to grip; KJV: handful.

H6654 צַד (tsad, tsad): a side; figuratively, an adversary. Origin: contr. from an unused root meaning to sidle off; KJV: (be-) side.

H6655 צַד (tsad, tsad): used adverbially (with preposition) at or upon the side of. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6654 (צַד); KJV: against, concerning.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6656 to H6782
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6656 צְדָא (tsᵉdâʼ, tsed-aw'): a (sinister) design. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root corresponding to H6658 (צָדָה) in the sense of intentness; KJV: true.

H6657 צְדָד (Tsᵉdâd, tsed-awd'): Tsedad, a place near Palestine. Origin: from the same as H6654 (צַד); a siding; KJV: Zedad.

H6658 צָדָה (tsâdâh, tsaw-daw'): to chase; by implication, to desolate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destroy, hunt, lie in wait.

H6659 צָדוֹק (Tsâdôwq, tsaw-doke'): Tsadok, the name of eight or nine Israelites. Origin: from H6663 (צָדַק); just; KJV: Zadok.

H6660 צְדִיָּה (tsᵉdîyâh, tsed-ee-yaw'): design. Origin: from H6658 (צָדָה); (compare H6656 (צְדָא)) KJV: lying in wait.

H6661 צִדִּים (Tsiddîym, tsid-deem'): Tsiddim (with the article), a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H6654 (צַד); sides; KJV: Ziddim.

H6662 צַדִּיק (tsaddîyq, tsad-deek'): just. Origin: from H6663 (צָדַק); KJV: just, lawful, righteous (man).

H6663 צָדַק (tsâdaq, tsaw-dak'): to be (causatively, make) right (in a moral or forensic sense). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cleanse, clear self, (be, do) just(-ice, -ify, -ify self), (be turn to) righteous(-ness).

H6664 צֶדֶק (tsedeq, tseh'-dek): the right (natural, moral or legal); also (abstractly) equity or (figuratively) prosperity. Origin: from H6663 (צָדַק); KJV: [idiom] even, ([idiom] that which is altogether) just(-ice), (un-)right(-eous) (cause, -ly, -ness).

H6665 צִדְקָה (tsidqâh, tsid-kaw'): beneficence. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6666 (צְדָקָה); KJV: righteousness.

H6666 צְדָקָה (tsᵉdâqâh, tsed-aw-kaw'): rightness (abstractly), subjectively (rectitude), objectively (justice), morally (virtue) or figuratively (prosperity). Origin: from H6663 (צָדַק); KJV: justice, moderately, right(-eous) (act, -ly, -ness).

H6667 צִדְקִיָּה (Tsidqîyâh, tsid-kee-yaw'): Tsidkijah, the name of six Israelites. Origin: or צִדְקִיָּהוּ; from H6664 (צֶדֶק) and H3050 (יָהּ); right of Jah; KJV: Zedekiah, Zidkijah.

H6668 צָהַב (tsâhab, tsaw-hab'): to glitter, i.e. be golden in color. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] fine.

H6669 צָהֹב (tsâhôb, tsaw-obe'): golden in color. Origin: from H6668 (צָהַב); KJV: yellow.

H6670 צָהַל (tsâhal, tsaw-hal'): to gleam, i.e. (figuratively) be cheerful; by transference to sound clear (of various animal or human expressions). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bellow, cry aloud (out), lift up, neigh, rejoice, make to shine, shout.

H6671 צָהַר (tsâhar, tsaw-har'): to press out oil. Origin: a primitive root; to glisten; used only as denominative from H3323 (יִצְהָר), KJV: make oil.

H6672 צֹהַר (tsôhar, tso'-har): a light (i.e. window); dual double light, i.e. noon. Origin: from H6671 (צָהַר); KJV: midday, noon(-day, -tide), window.

H6673 צַו (tsav, tsav): an injunction. Origin: or צָו; from H6680 (צָוָה); KJV: commandment, precept.

H6674 צוֹא (tsôwʼ, tso): soiled (as if excrementitious). Origin: or צֹא; from an unused root meaning to issue; KJV: filthy.

H6675 צוֹאָה (tsôwʼâh, tso-aw'): excrement; generally, dirt; figuratively, pollution. Origin: or צֹאָה ; feminine of H6674 (צוֹא); KJV: dung, filth(-iness). Marg. for H2716 (חֶרֶא).

H6676 צַוַּאר (tsavvaʼr, tsav-var'): {the back of the neck (as that on which burdens are bound)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6677 (צַוָּאר) KJV: neck.

H6677 צַוָּאר (tsavvâʼr, tsav-vawr'): the back of the neck (as that on which burdens are bound). Origin: or צַוָּר; (Nehemiah 3:5), or צַוָּרֹןlemma צַוָּרן missing vowel, corrected to צַוָּרֹן; (Song of Solomon 4:9), or (feminine) צַוָּארָה; (Micah 2:3), intensively from H6696 (צוּר) in the sense of binding; KJV: neck.

H6678 צוֹבָא (Tsôwbâʼ, tso-baw'): Zoba or Zobah, a region of Syria. Origin: or צוֹבָה; or צֹבָה; from an unused root meaning to station; a station; KJV: Zoba, Zobah.

H6679 צוּד (tsûwd, tsood): to lie alongside (i.e. in wait); by implication, to catch an animal (figuratively, men); to victual (for a journey). Origin: a primitive root; also denominative from H6718 (צַיִד) KJV: chase, hunt, sore, take (provision).

H6680 צָוָה (tsâvâh, tsaw-vaw'): (intensively) to constitute, enjoin. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, (for-) bid, (give a) charge, (give a, give in, send with) command(-er, -ment), send a messenger, put, (set) in order.

H6681 צָוַח (tsâvach, tsaw-vakh'): to screech (exultingly). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shout.

H6682 צְוָחָה (tsᵉvâchâh, tsev-aw-khaw'): a screech (of anguish). Origin: from H6681 (צָוַח); KJV: cry(-ing).

H6683 צוּלָה (tsûwlâh, tsoo-law'): an abyss (of the sea). Origin: from an unused root meaning to sink; KJV: deep.

H6684 צוּם (tsûwm, tsoom): to cover over (the mouth), i.e. to fast. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, fast.

H6685 צוֹם (tsôwm, tsome): a fast. Origin: or צֹם; from H6684 (צוּם); KJV: fast(-ing).

H6686 צוּעָר (Tsûwʻâr, tsoo-awr'): Tsuar, an Israelite. Origin: from H6819 (צָעַר); small; KJV: Zuar.

H6687 צוּף (tsûwph, tsoof): to overflow. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (make to over-) flow, swim.

H6688 צוּף (tsûwph, tsoof): comb of honey (from dripping). Origin: from H6687 (צוּף); KJV: honeycomb.

H6689 צוּף (Tsûwph, tsoof): Tsuph or Tsophai or Tsiph, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. Origin: or צוֹפַי; or צִיף; from H6688 (צוּף); honey-comb; KJV: Zophai, Zuph.

H6690 צוֹפַח (Tsôwphach, tso-fakh'): Tsophach, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to expand, breadth; KJV: Zophah.

H6691 צוֹפַר (Tsôwphar, tso-far'): Tsophar, a friend of Job. Origin: from H6852 (צָפַר); departing; KJV: Zophar.

H6692 צוּץ (tsûwts, tsoots): to twinkle, i.e. glance; by analogy, to blossom (figuratively, flourish). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bloom, blossom, flourish, shew self.

H6693 צוּק (tsûwq, tsook): to compress, i.e. (figuratively) oppress, distress. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: constrain, distress, lie sore, (op-) press(-or), straiten.

H6694 צוּק (tsûwq, tsook): to pour out, i.e. (figuratively) smelt, utter. Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of narrowness (of orifice)); KJV: be molten, pour.

H6695 צוֹק (tsôwq, tsoke): a strait, i.e. (figuratively) distress. Origin: or (feminine) צוּקָה; from H6693 (צוּק); KJV: anguish, [idiom] troublous.

H6696 צוּר (tsûwr, tsoor): to cramp, i.e. confine (in many applications, literally and figuratively, formative or hostile). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: adversary, assault, beset, besiege, bind (up), cast, distress, fashion, fortify, inclose, lay siege, put up in bags.

H6697 צוּר (tsûwr, tsoor): properly, a cliff (or sharp rock, as compressed); generally, a rock or boulder; figuratively, a refuge; also an edge (as precipitous). Origin: or צֻר; from H6696 (צוּר); KJV: edge, [idiom] (mighty) God (one), rock, [idiom] sharp, stone, [idiom] strength, [idiom] strong. See also H1049 (בֵּית צוּר).

H6698 צוּר (Tsûwr, tsoor): Tsur, the name of a Midianite and of an Israelite. Origin: the same as H6697 (צוּר); rock; KJV: Zur.

H6699 צוּרָה (tsûwrâh, tsoo-raw'): a rock (Job 28:10); also a form (as if pressed out). Origin: feminine of H6697 (צוּר); KJV: form, rock.

H6700 צוּרִיאֵל (Tsûwrîyʼêl, tsoo-ree-ale'): Tsuriel, an Israelite. Origin: from H6697 (צוּר) and H410 (אֵל); rock of God; KJV: Zuriel.

H6701 צוּרִישַׁדַּי (Tsûwrîyshadday, tsoo-ree-shad-dah'-ee): Tsurishaddai, an Israelite. Origin: from H6697 (צוּר) and H7706 (שַׁדַּי); rock of (the) Almighty; KJV: Zurishaddai.

H6702 צוּת (tsûwth, tsooth): to blaze. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn.

H6703 צַח (tsach, tsakh): dazzling, i.e. sunny, bright, (figuratively) evident. Origin: from H6705 (צָחַח); KJV: clear, dry, plainly, white.

H6704 צִחֶה (tsicheh, tsee-kheh'): parched. Origin: from an unused root meaning to glow; KJV: dried up.

H6705 צָחַח (tsâchach, tsaw-khakh'): to glare, i.e. be dazzling white. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be whiter.

H6706 צְחִיחַ (tsᵉchîyach, tsekh-ee'-akh): glaring, i.e. exposed to the bright sun. Origin: from H6705 (צָחַח); KJV: higher place, top.

H6707 צְחִיחָה (tsᵉchîychâh, tsekh-ee-khaw'): a parched region, i.e. the desert. Origin: feminine of H6706 (צְחִיחַ); KJV: dry land.

H6708 צְחִיחִי (tsᵉchîychîy, tsekh-ee-khee'): bare spot, i.e. in the glaring sun. Origin: from H6706 (צְחִיחַ); KJV: higher place.

H6709 צַחֲנָה (tsachănâh, tsakh-an-aw'): stench. Origin: from an unused root meaning to putrefy; KJV: ill savour.

H6710 צַחְצָחָה (tsachtsâchâh, tsakh-tsaw-khaw'): a dry place, i.e. desert. Origin: from H6705 (צָחַח); KJV: drought.

H6711 צָחַק (tsâchaq, tsaw-khak'): to laugh outright (in merriment or scorn); by implication, to sport. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: laugh, mock, play, make sport.

H6712 צְחֹק (tsᵉchôq, tsekh-oke'): laughter (in pleasure or derision). Origin: from H6711 (צָחַק); KJV: laugh(-ed to scorn).

H6713 צַחַר (tsachar, tsakh'-ar): sheen, i.e. whiteness. Origin: from an unused root meaning to dazzle; KJV: white.

H6714 צֹחַר (Tsôchar, tso'-khar): Tsochar, the name of a Hittite and of an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H6713 (צַחַר); whiteness; KJV: Zohar. Compare H3328 (יִצְחַר).

H6715 צָחֹר (tsâchôr, tsaw-khore'): white. Origin: from the same as H6713 (צַחַר); KJV: white.

H6716 צִי (tsîy, tsee): a ship (as a fixture). Origin: from H6680 (צָוָה); KJV: ship.

H6717 צִיבָא (Tsîybâʼ, tsee-baw'): Tsiba, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H6678 (צוֹבָא); station; KJV: Ziba.

H6718 צַיִד (tsayid, tsah'-yid): the chase; also game (thus taken); (generally) lunch (especially for a journey). Origin: from a form of H6679 (צוּד) and meaning the same; KJV: [idiom] catcheth, food, [idiom] hunter, (that which he took in) hunting, venison, victuals.

H6719 צַיָּד (tsayâd, tsah'-yawd): a huntsman. Origin: from the same as H6718 (צַיִד); KJV: hunter.

H6720 צֵידָה (tsêydâh, tsay-daw'): food. Origin: or צֵדָה; feminine of H6718 (צַיִד); KJV: meat, provision, venison, victuals.

H6721 צִידוֹן (Tsîydôwn, tsee-done'): Tsidon, the name of a son of Canaan, and of a place in Palestine. Origin: or צִידֹן; from H6679 (צוּד) in the sense of catching fish; fishery; KJV: Sidon, Zidon.

H6722 צִידֹנִי (Tsîydônîy, tsee-do-nee'): a Tsidonian or inhabitant of Tsidon. Origin: patrial from H6721 (צִידוֹן); KJV: Sidonian, of Sidon, Zidonian.

H6723 צִיָּה (tsîyâh, tsee-yaw'): aridity; concretely, a desert. Origin: from an unused root meaning to parch; KJV: barren, drought, dry (land, place), solitary place, wilderness.

H6724 צִיוֹן (tsîyôwn, tsee-yone'): a desert. Origin: from the same as H6723 (צִיָּה); KJV: dry place.

H6725 צִיּוּן (tsîyûwn, tsee-yoon'): a monumental or guiding pillar. Origin: from the same as H6723 (צִיָּה) in the sense of conspicuousness (compare H5329 (נָצַח)); KJV: sign, title, waymark.

H6726 צִיּוֹן (Tsîyôwn, tsee-yone'): Tsijon (as a permanent capital), a mountain of Jerusalem. Origin: the same (regularly) as H6725 (צִיּוּן)lemma צִיוּן missing dagesh, corrected to צִיּוּן; KJV: Zion.

H6727 צִיחָא (Tsîychâʼ, tsee-khaw'): Tsicha, the name of two Nethinim. Origin: or צִחָא; as if feminine of H6704 (צִחֶה); drought; KJV: Ziha.

H6728 צִיִּי (tsîyîy, tsee-ee'): a desert-dweller, i.e. nomad or wild beast. Origin: from the same as H6723 (צִיָּה); KJV: wild beast of the desert, that dwell in (inhabiting) the wilderness.

H6729 צִינֹק (tsîynôq, tsee-noke'): the pillory. Origin: from an unused root meaning to confine; KJV: stocks.

H6730 צִיעֹר (Tsîyʻôr, tsee-ore'): Tsior, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6819 (צָעַר); small; KJV: Zior.

H6731 צִיץ (tsîyts, tseets): properly, glistening, i.e. a burnished plate; also a flower (as bright-colored); a wing (as gleaming in the air). Origin: or צִץ; from H6692 (צוּץ); KJV: blossom, flower, plate, wing.

H6732 צִיץ (Tsîyts, tseets): Tsits, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6731 (צִיץ); bloom; KJV: Ziz.

H6733 צִיצָה (tsîytsâh, tsee-tsaw'): a flower. Origin: feminine of H6731 (צִיץ); KJV: flower.

H6734 צִיצִת (tsîytsith, tsee-tseeth'): a floral or wing-like projection, i.e. a forelock of hair, a tassel. Origin: feminine of H6731 (צִיץ); KJV: fringe, lock.

H6735 צִיר (tsîyr, tseer): a hinge (as pressed in turning); also a throe (as a phys. or mental pressure); also a herald or erranddoer (as constrained by the principal). Origin: from H6696 (צוּר); KJV: ambassador, hinge, messenger, pain, pang, sorrow. Compare H6736 (צִיר).

H6736 צִיר (tsîyr, tseer): a form (of beauty; as if pressed out, i.e. carved); hence, an (idolatrous) image. Origin: the same as H6735 (צִיר); KJV: beauty, idol.

H6737 צָיַר (tsâyar, tsaw-yar'): to make an errand, i.e. betake oneself. Origin: a denominative from H6735 (צִיר) in the sense of ambassador; KJV: make as if...had been ambassador.

H6738 צֵל (tsêl, tsale): shade, whether literal or figurative. Origin: from H6751 (צָלַל); KJV: defence, shade(-ow).

H6739 צְלָא (tsᵉlâʼ, tsel-aw'): pray. Origin: (Aramaic) probably corresponding to H6760 (צָלַע) in the sense of bowing; KJV: pray.

H6740 צָלָה (tsâlâh, tsaw-law'): to roast. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: roast.

H6741 צִלָּה (Tsillâh, tsil-law'): Tsillah, an antediluvian woman. Origin: feminine of H6738 (צֵל); KJV: Zillah.

H6742 צְלוּל (tsᵉlûwl, tsel-ool'): a (round or flattened) cake. Origin: from H6749 (צָלַל) in the sense of rolling; KJV: cake.

H6743 צָלַח (tsâlach, tsaw-lakh'): to push forward, in various senses (literal or figurative, transitive or intransitive). Origin: or צָלֵחַ; a primitive root; KJV: break out, come (mightily), go over, be good, be meet, be profitable, (cause to, effect, make to, send) prosper(-ity, -ous, -ously).

H6744 צְלַח (tsᵉlach, tsel-akh'): to advance (transitive or intransitive). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6743 (צָלַח); KJV: promote, prosper.

H6745 צֵלָחָה (tsêlâchâh, tsay-law-khaw'): something protracted or flattened out, i.e. a platter. Origin: from H6743 (צָלַח); KJV: pan.

H6746 צְלֹחִית (tsᵉlôchîyth, tsel-o-kheeth'): something prolonged or tall, i.e. a vial or salt-cellar. Origin: from H6743 (צָלַח); KJV: cruse.

H6747 צַלַּחַת (tsallachath, tsal-lakh'-ath): something advanced or deep, i.e. a bowl; figuratively, the bosom. Origin: from H6743 (צָלַח); KJV: bosom, dish.

H6748 צָלִי (tsâlîy, tsaw-lee'): roasted. Origin: passive participle of H6740 (צָלָה); KJV: roast.

H6749 צָלַל (tsâlal, tsaw-lal'): properly, to tumble down, i.e. settle by awaving motion. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sink. Compare H6750 (צָלַל), H6751 (צָלַל).

H6750 צָלַל (tsâlal, tsaw-lal'): to tinkle, i.e. rattle together (as the ears in reddening with shame, or the teeth in chattering with fear). Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of vibration); KJV: quiver, tingle.

H6751 צָלַל (tsâlal, tsaw-lal'): to shade, as twilight or an opaque object. Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of hovering over (compare H6754 (צֶלֶם))); KJV: begin to be dark, shadowing.

H6752 צֵלֶל (tsêlel, tsay'-lel): shade. Origin: from H6751 (צָלַל); KJV: shadow.

H6753 צְלֶלְפּוֹנִי (Tsᵉlelpôwnîy, tsel-el-po-nee'): Tselelponi, an Israelitess. Origin: from H6752 (צֵלֶל) and the active participle of H6437 (פָּנָה); shade-facing; KJV: Hazelelponi (including the article).

H6754 צֶלֶם (tselem, tseh'-lem): a phantom, i.e. (figuratively) illusion, resemblance; hence, a representative figure, especially an idol. Origin: from an unused root meaning to shade; KJV: image, vain shew.

H6755 צֶלֶם (tselem, tseh'-lem): an idolatrous figure. Origin: (Aramaic) or צְלֶם; (Aramaic), corresponding to H6754 (צֶלֶם); KJV: form, image.

H6756 צַלְמוֹן (Tsalmôwn, tsal-mone'): Tsalmon, the name of a place in Palestine and of an Israelite. Origin: from H6754 (צֶלֶם); shady; KJV: Zalmon.

H6757 צַלְמָוֶת (tsalmâveth, tsal-maw'-veth): shade of death, i.e. the grave (figuratively, calamity). Origin: from H6738 (צֵל) and H4194 (מָוֶת); KJV: shadow of death.

H6758 צַלְמֹנָה (Tsalmônâh, tsal-mo-naw'): Tsalmonah, a place in the Desert. Origin: feminine of H6757 (צַלְמָוֶת); shadiness; KJV: Zalmonah.

H6759 צַלְמֻנָּע (Tsalmunnâʻ, tsal-moon-naw'): Tsalmunna, a Midianite. Origin: from H6738 (צֵל) and H4513 (מָנַע); shade has been denied; KJV: Zalmunna.

H6760 צָלַע (tsâlaʻ, tsaw-lah'): to limp (as if one-sided). Origin: a primitive root; probably to curve; used only as denominative from H6763 (צֵלָע), KJV: halt.

H6761 צֶלַע (tselaʻ, tseh'-lah): a limping or full (figuratively). Origin: from H6760 (צָלַע); KJV: adversity, halt(-ing).

H6762 צֶלַע (Tselaʻ, tseh'-lah): Tsela, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6761 (צֶלַע); KJV: Zelah.

H6763 צֵלָע (tsêlâʻ, tsay-law'): a rib (as curved), literally (of the body) or figuratively (of a door, i.e. leaf); hence, a side, literally (of a person) or figuratively (of an object or the sky, i.e. quarter); architecturally, a (especially floor or ceiling) timber or plank (single or collective, i.e. a flooring). Origin: or (feminine) צַלְעָה; from H6760 (צָלַע); KJV: beam, board, chamber, corner, leaf, plank, rib, side (chamber).

H6764 צָלָף (Tsâlâph, tsaw-lawf'): Tsalaph, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root of unknown meaning; KJV: Zalaph.

H6765 צְלׇפְחָד (Tsᵉlophchâd, tsel-of-chawd'): Tselophchad, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H6764 (צָלָף) and H259 (אֶחָד); KJV: Zelophehad.

H6766 צֶלְצַח (Tseltsach, tsel-tsakh'): Tseltsach, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6738 (צֵל) and H6703 (צַח); clear shade; KJV: Zelzah.

H6767 צְלָצַל (tsᵉlâtsal, tsel-aw-tsal'): a clatter, i.e. (abstractly) whirring (of wings); (concretely) a cricket; also a harpoon (as rattling), a cymbal (as clanging). Origin: from H6750 (צָלַל) reduplicated; KJV: cymbal, locust, shadowing, spear.

H6768 צֶלֶק (Tseleq, tseh'-lek): Tselek, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to split; fissure; KJV: Zelek.

H6769 צִלְּתַי (Tsillᵉthay, tsil-leth-ah'-ee): Tsillethai, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from the feminine of H6738 (צֵל); shady; KJV: Zilthai.

H6770 צָמֵא (tsâmêʼ, tsaw-may'): to thirst (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be a-, suffer) thirst(-y).

H6771 צָמֵא (tsâmêʼ, tsaw-may'): thirsty (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H6770 (צָמֵא); KJV: (that) thirst(-eth, -y).

H6772 צָמָא (tsâmâʼ, tsaw-maw'): thirst (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H6770 (צָמֵא); KJV: thirst(-y).

H6773 צִמְאָה (tsimʼâh, tsim-aw'): thirst (figuratively, of libidinousnes). Origin: feminine of H6772 (צָמָא); KJV: thirst.

H6774 צִמָּאוֹן (tsimmâʼôwn, tsim-maw-one'): a thirsty place, i.e. desert. Origin: from H6771 (צָמֵא); KJV: drought, dry ground, thirsty land.

H6775 צָמַד (tsâmad, tsaw-mad'): to link, i.e. gird; figuratively, to serve, (mentally) contrive. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fasten, frame, join (self).

H6776 צֶמֶד (tsemed, tseh'-med): hence, an acre (i.e. day's task for a yoke of cattle to plough). Origin: a yoke or team (i.e. pair); KJV: acre, couple, [idiom] together, two (donkeys), yoke (of oxen).

H6777 צַמָּה (tsammâh, tsam-maw'): a veil. Origin: from an unused root meaning to fasten on; KJV: locks.

H6778 צַמּוּק (tsammûwq, tsam-mook'): a cake of dried grapes. Origin: from H6784 (צָמַק); KJV: bunch (cluster) of raisins.

H6779 צָמַח (tsâmach, tsaw-makh'): to sprout (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear, bring forth, (cause to, make to) bud (forth), (cause to, make to) grow (again, up), (cause to) spring (forth, up).

H6780 צֶמַח (tsemach, tseh'-makh): a sprout (usually concrete), literal or figurative. Origin: from H6779 (צָמַח); KJV: branch, bud, that which (where) grew (upon), spring(-ing).

H6781 צָמִיד (tsâmîyd, tsaw-meed'): a bracelet or arm-clasp; generally, a lid. Origin: or צָמִד; from H6775 (צָמַד); KJV: bracelet, covering.

H6782 צַמִּים (tsammîym, tsam-meem'): a noose (as fastening); figuratively, destruction. Origin: from the same as H6777 (צַמָּה); KJV: robber.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6783 to H6919
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6783 צְמִיתֻת (tsᵉmîythuth, tsem-ee-thooth'): excision, i.e. destruction; used only (adverbially) with prepositional prefix to extinction, i.e. perpetually. Origin: or צְמִתֻת; from H6789 (צָמַת); KJV: ever.

H6784 צָמַק (tsâmaq, tsaw-mak'): to dry up. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dry.

H6785 צֶמֶר (tsemer, tseh'-mer): wool. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to be shaggy; KJV: wool(-len).

H6786 צְמָרִי (Tsᵉmârîy, tsem-aw-ree'): a Tsemarite or branch of the Canaanites. Origin: patrial from an unused name of a place in Palestine; KJV: Zemarite.

H6787 צְמָרַיִם (Tsᵉmârayim, tsem-aw-rah'-yim): Tsemarajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of H6785 (צֶמֶר); double fleece; KJV: Zemaraim.

H6788 צַמֶּרֶת (tsammereth, tsam-meh'-reth): fleeciness, i.e. foliage. Origin: from the same as H6785 (צֶמֶר); KJV: highest branch, top.

H6789 צָמַת (tsâmath, tsaw-math'): to extirpate (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: consume, cut off, destroy, vanish.

H6790 צִן (Tsin, tseen): Tsin, a part of the Desert. Origin: from an unused root meaning to prick; a crag; KJV: Zin.

H6791 צֵן (tsên, tsane): a thorn; hence, a cactus-hedge. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be prickly; KJV: thorn.

H6792 צֹנֵא (tsônêʼ, tso-nay'): a flock. Origin: or צֹנֶה; for H6629 (צֹאן); KJV: sheep.

H6793 צִנָּה (tsinnâh, tsin-naw'): a hook (as pointed); also a (large) shield (as if guarding by prickliness); also cold (as piercing). Origin: feminine of H6791 (צֵן); KJV: buckler, cold, hook, shield, target.

H6794 צִנּוּר (tsinnûwr, tsin-noor'): a culvert. Origin: from an unused root perhaps meaning to be hollow; KJV: gutter, water-spout.

H6795 צָנַח (tsânach, tsaw-nakh'): to alight; (transitive) to cause to descend, i.e. drive down. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fasten, light (from off).

H6796 צָנִין (tsânîyn, tsaw-neen'): a thorn. Origin: or צָנִן; from the same as H6791 (צֵן); KJV: thorn.

H6797 צָנִיף (tsânîyph, tsaw-neef'): a head-dress (i.e. piece of cloth wrapped around). Origin: or צָנוֹף; or (feminine) צָנִיפָה; from H6801 (צָנַף); KJV: diadem, hood, mitre.

H6798 צָנַם (tsânam, tsaw-nam'): to blast or shrink. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: withered.

H6799 צְנָן (Tsᵉnân, tsen-awn'): Tsenan, a place near Palestine. Origin: probably for H6630 (צַאֲנָן); KJV: Zenan.

H6800 צָנַע (tsânaʻ, tsaw-nah'): to humiliate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: humbly, lowly.

H6801 צָנַף (tsânaph, tsaw-naf'): to wrap, i.e. roll or dress. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be attired, [idiom] surely, violently turn.

H6802 צְנֵפָה (tsᵉnêphâh, tsen-ay-faw'): a ball. Origin: from H6801 (צָנַף); KJV: [idiom] toss.

H6803 צִנְצֶנֶת (tsintseneth, tsin-tseh'-neth): a vase (probably a vial tapering at the top). Origin: from the same as H6791 (צֵן); KJV: pot.

H6804 צַנְתָּרָה (tsantârâh, tsan-taw-raw'): a tube. Origin: probably from the same as H6794 (צִנּוּר); KJV: pipe.

H6805 צָעַד (tsâʻad, tsaw-ad'): to pace, i.e. step regularly; (upward) to mount; (along) to march; (down and causatively) to hurl. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring, go, march (through), run over.

H6806 צַעַד (tsaʻad, tsah'-ad): a pace or regular step. Origin: from H6804 (צַנְתָּרָה); KJV: pace, step.

H6807 צְעָדָה (tsᵉʻâdâh, tseh-aw-daw'): a march; (concretely) an (ornamental) ankle-chain. Origin: feminine of H6806 (צַעַד); KJV: going, ornament of the legs.

H6808 צָעָה (tsâʻâh, tsaw-aw'): to tip over (for the purpose of spilling or pouring out), i.e. (figuratively) depopulate; by implication, to imprison or conquer; (reflexive) to lie down (for coitus). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: captive exile, travelling, (cause to) wander(-er).

H6809 צָעִיף (tsâʻîyph, tsaw-eef'): a veil. Origin: from an unused root meaning to wrap over; KJV: vail.

H6810 צָעִיר (tsâʻîyr, tsaw-eer'): little; (in number) few; (in age) young, (in value) ignoble. Origin: or צָעוֹר; from H6819 (צָעַר); KJV: least, little (one), small (one), [phrase] young(-er, -est).

H6811 צָעִיר (Tsâʻîyr, tsaw-eer'): Tsair, a place in Idumaea. Origin: the same as H6810 (צָעִיר); KJV: Zair.

H6812 צְעִירָה (tsᵉʻîyrâh, tseh-ee-raw'): smallness (of age), i.e. juvenility. Origin: feminine of H6810 (צָעִיר); KJV: youth.

H6813 צָעַן (tsâʻan, tsaw-an'): to load up (beasts), i.e. to migrate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be taken down.

H6814 צֹעַן (Tsôʻan, tso'-an): Tsoan, a place in Egypt. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Zoan.

H6815 צַעֲנַנִּים (Tsaʻănannîym, tsah-an-an-neem'): Tsaanannim or Tsaanajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (dual) צַעֲנַיִם; plural from H6813 (צָעַן); removals; KJV: Zaannannim, Zaanaim.

H6816 צַעְצֻעַ (tsaʻtsuaʻ, tsah-tsoo'-ah): sculpture. Origin: from an unused root meaning to bestrew with carvings; KJV: image (work).

H6817 צָעַק (tsâʻaq, tsaw-ak'): to shriek; (by implication) to proclaim (an assembly). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, call together, cry (out), gather (selves) (together).

H6818 צַעֲקָה (tsaʻăqâh, tsah-ak-aw'): a shriek. Origin: from H6817 (צָעַק); KJV: cry(-ing).

H6819 צָעַר (tsâʻar, tsaw-ar'): to be small, i.e. (figuratively) ignoble. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be brought low, little one, be small.

H6820 צֹעַר (Tsôʻar, tso'ar): Tsoar, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H6819 (צָעַר); little; KJV: Zoar.

H6821 צָפַד (tsâphad, tsaw-fad'): to adhere. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cleave.

H6822 צָפָה (tsâphâh, tsaw-faw'): properly, to lean forward, i.e. to peer into the distance; by implication, to observe, await. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: behold, espy, look up (well), wait for, (keep the) watch(-man).

H6823 צָפָה (tsâphâh, tsaw-faw'): to sheet over (especially with metal). Origin: a primitive root (probably identical with H6822 (צָפָה) through the idea of expansion in outlook, transferring to action); KJV: cover, overlay.

H6824 צָפָה (tsâphâh, tsaw-faw'): an inundation (as covering). Origin: from H6823 (צָפָה); KJV: [idiom] swimmest.

H6825 צְפוֹ (Tsᵉphôw, tsef-o'): Tsepho or Tsephi, an Idumaean. Origin: or צְפִי; from H6822 (צָפָה); observant; KJV: Zephi, Zepho.

H6826 צִפּוּי (tsippûwy, tsip-poo'-ee): encasement (with metal). Origin: from H6823 (צָפָה); KJV: covering, overlaying.

H6827 צְפוֹן (Tsᵉphôwn, tsef-one'): Tsephon, an Israelite. Origin: probably for H6837 (צִפְיוֹן); KJV: Zephon.

H6828 צָפוֹן (tsâphôwn, tsaw-fone'): properly, hidden, i.e. dark; used only of the north as aquarter (gloomy and unknown). Origin: or צָפֹן; from H6845 (צָפַן); KJV: north(-ern, side, -ward, wind).

H6829 צָפוֹן (Tsâphôwn, tsaw-fone'): Tsaphon, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6828 (צָפוֹן); boreal; KJV: Zaphon.

H6830 צְפוֹנִי (tsᵉphôwnîy, tsef-o-nee'): northern. Origin: from H6828 (צָפוֹן); KJV: northern.

H6831 צְפוֹנִי (Tsᵉphôwnîy, tsef-o-nee'): a Tsephonite, or (collectively) descendants of Tsephon. Origin: patronymically from H6827 (צְפוֹן); KJV: Zephonites.

H6832 צְפוּעַ (tsᵉphûwaʻ, tsef-oo'-ah): excrement (as protruded). Origin: from the same as H6848 (צֶפַע); KJV: dung.

H6833 צִפּוֹר (tsippôwr, tsip-pore'): a little bird (as hopping). Origin: or צִפֹּר; from H6852 (צָפַר); KJV: bird, fowl, sparrow.

H6834 צִפּוֹר (Tsippôwr, tsip-pore'): Tsippor, a Moabite. Origin: the same as H6833 (צִפּוֹר); KJV: Zippor.

H6835 צַפַּחַת (tsappachath, tsap-pakh'-ath): a saucer (as flat). Origin: from an unused root meaning to expand; KJV: cruse.

H6836 צְפִיָּה (tsᵉphîyâh, tsef-ee-yaw'): watchfulness. Origin: from H6822 (צָפָה); KJV: watching.

H6837 צִפְיוֹן (Tsiphyôwn, tsif-yone'): Tsiphjon, an Israelite. Origin: from H6822 (צָפָה); watch-tower; KJV: Ziphion. Compare H6827 (צְפוֹן).

H6838 צַפִּיחִת (tsappîychith, tsap-pee-kheeth'): a flat thin cake. Origin: from the same as H6835 (צַפַּחַת); KJV: wafer.

H6839 צֹפִים (Tsôphîym, tso-feem'): Tsophim, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: plural of active participle of H6822 (צָפָה); watchers; KJV: Zophim.

H6840 צָפִין (tsâphîyn, tsaw-feen'): a treasure (as hidden). Origin: from H6845 (צָפַן); KJV: hid.

H6841 צְפִיר (tsᵉphîyr, tsef-eer'): a he-goat. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6842 (צָפִיר); KJV: he (goat).

H6842 צָפִיר (tsâphîyr, tsaw-feer'): a male goat (as prancing). Origin: from H6852 (צָפַר); KJV: (he) goat.

H6843 צְפִירָה (tsᵉphîyrâh, tsef-ee-raw'): a crown (as encircling the head); also a turn of affairs (i.e. mishap). Origin: feminine formed like H6842 (צָפִיר); KJV: diadem, morning.

H6844 צָפִית (tsâphîyth, tsaw-feeth'): a sentry. Origin: from H6822 (צָפָה); KJV: watchtower.

H6845 צָפַן (tsâphan, tsaw-fan'): to hide (by covering over); by implication, to hoard or reserve; figuratively to deny; specifically (favorably) to protect, (unfavorably) to lurk. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: esteem, hide(-den one, self), lay up, lurk (be set) privily, (keep) secret(-ly, place).

H6846 צְפַנְיָה (Tsᵉphanyâh, tsef-an-yaw'): Tsephanjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or צְפַנְיָהוּ; from H6845 (צָפַן) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has secreted; KJV: Zephaniah.

H6847 צׇפְנַת פַּעְנֵחַ (Tsophnath Paʻnêach, tsof-nath' pah-nay'-akh): Tsophnath-Paneach, Joseph's Egyptian name. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Zaphnath-paaneah.

H6848 צֶפַע (tsephaʻ, tseh'-fah or tsiphoniy tsif-o-nee'): a viper (as thrusting out the tongue, i.e. hissing). Origin: from an unused root meaning to extrude; KJV: adder, cockatrice.

H6849 צְפִעָה (tsᵉphiʻâh, tsef-ee-aw'): an outcast thing. Origin: feminine from the same as H6848 (צֶפַע); KJV: issue.

H6850 צָפַף (tsâphaph, tsaw-faf'): to coo or chirp (as a bird). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: chatter, peep, whisper.

H6851 צַפְצָפָה (tsaphtsâphâh, tsaf-tsaw-faw'): a willow (as growing in overflowed places). Origin: from H6687 (צוּף); KJV: willow tree.

H6852 צָפַר (tsâphar, tsaw-far'): to skip about, i.e. return. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: depart early.

H6853 צְפַר (tsᵉphar, tsef-ar'): a bird. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6833 (צִפּוֹר); KJV: bird.

H6854 צְפַרְדֵּעַ (tsᵉphardêaʻ, tsef-ar-day'-ah): a marsh-leaper, i.e. frog. Origin: from H6852 (צָפַר) and a word elsewhere unused meaning a swamp; KJV: frog.

H6855 צִפֹּרָה (Tsippôrâh, tsip-po-raw'): Tsipporah, Moses' wife. Origin: feminine of H6833 (צִפּוֹר); bird; KJV: Zipporah.

H6856 צִפֹּרֶן (tsippôren, tsip-po'-ren): properly, a claw, i.e. (human) nail; also the point of astyle (or pen, tipped with adamant). Origin: from H6852 (צָפַר) (in the denominative sense (from H6833 (צִפּוֹר)) of scratching); KJV: nail, point.

H6857 צְפַת (Tsᵉphath, tsef-ath'): Tsephath, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6822 (צָפָה); watch-tower; KJV: Zephath.

H6858 צֶפֶת (tsepheth, tseh'-feth): a capital of a column. Origin: from an unused root meaning to encircle; KJV: chapiter.

H6859 צְפָתָה (Tsᵉphâthâh, tsef-aw'-thaw): Tsephathah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6857 (צְפַת); KJV: Zephathah.

H6860 צִקְלַג (Tsiqlag, tsik-lag'): Tsiklag or Tsikelag, a place in Palestine. Origin: or צִיקלַג; (1 Chronicles 12:1,20), of uncertain derivation; KJV: Ziklag.

H6861 צִקְלֹן (tsiqlôn, tsik-lone'): a sack (as tied at the mouth). Origin: from an unused root meaning to wind; KJV: husk.

H6862 צַר (tsar, tsar): narrow; (as a noun) a tight place (usually figuratively, i.e. trouble); also a pebble ; (transitive) an opponent (as crowding). Origin: or צָר; from H6887 (צָרַר); compare as in H6864 (צֹר) KJV: adversary, afflicted(-tion), anguish, close, distress, enemy, flint, foe, narrow, small, sorrow, strait, tribulation, trouble.

H6863 צֵר (Tsêr, tsare): Tser, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6887 (צָרַר); rock; KJV: Zer.

H6864 צֹר (tsôr, tsore): a stone (as if pressed hard or to a point); (by implication, of use) a knife. Origin: from H6696 (צוּר); KJV: flint, sharp stone.

H6865 צֹר (Tsôr, tsore): Tsor, a place in Palestine. Origin: or צוֹר; the same as H6864 (צֹר); a rock; KJV: Tyre, Tyrus.

H6866 צָרַב (tsârab, tsaw-rab'): to burn. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: burn.

H6867 צָרֶבֶת (tsârebeth, tsaw-reh'-beth): conflagration (of fire or disease). Origin: from H6686 (צוּעָר); KJV: burning, inflammation.

H6868 צְרֵדָה (Tsᵉrêdâh, tser-ay-daw'): Tseredah, a place in Palestine. Origin: or צְרֵדָתָה; apparently from an unused root meaning to pierce; puncture; KJV: Zereda, Zeredathah.

H6869 צָרָה (tsârâh, tsaw-raw'): tightness (i.e. figuratively, trouble); transitively, a female rival. Origin: feminine of H6862 (צַר); KJV: adversary, adversity, affliction, anguish, distress, tribulation, trouble.

H6870 צְרוּיָה (Tsᵉrûwyâh, tser-oo-yaw'): Tserujah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine passive participle from the same as H6875 (צְרִי); wounded; KJV: Zeruiah.

H6871 צְרוּעָה (Tsᵉrûwʻâh, tser-oo-aw'): Tseruah, an Israelitess. Origin: feminine passive participle of H6879 (צָרַע); leprous; KJV: Zeruah.

H6872 צְרוֹר (tsᵉrôwr, tser-ore'): a parcel (as packed up); also a kernel or particle (as if a package). Origin: or (shorter) צְרֹר; from H6887 (צָרַר); KJV: bag, [idiom] bendeth, bundle, least grain, small stone.

H6873 צָרַח (tsârach, tsaw-rakh'): to be clear (in tone, i.e. shrill), i.e. to whoop. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cry, roar.

H6874 צְרִי (Tsᵉrîy, tser-ee'): Tseri, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H6875 (צְרִי); KJV: Zeri. Compare H3340 (יִצְרִי).

H6875 צְרִי (tsᵉrîy, tser-ee'): distillation, i.e. balsam. Origin: or צֳרִי; from an unused root meaning to crack (as by pressure), hence, to leak; KJV: balm.

H6876 צֹרִי (Tsôrîy, tso-ree'): a Tsorite or inhabitant of Tsor (i.e. Syrian). Origin: patrial from H6865 (צֹר); KJV: (man) of Tyre.

H6877 צְרִיחַ (tsᵉrîyach, tser-ee'-akh): a citadel. Origin: from H6873 (צָרַח) in the sense of clearness of vision; KJV: high place, hold.

H6878 צֹרֶךְ (tsôrek, tso'-rek): need. Origin: from an unused root meaning to need; KJV: need.

H6879 צָרַע (tsâraʻ, tsaw-rah'): to scourge, i.e. (intransitive and figurative) to be stricken with leprosy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: leper, leprous.

H6880 צִרְעָה (tsirʻâh, tsir-aw'): a wasp (as stinging). Origin: from H6879 (צָרַע); KJV: hornet.

H6881 צׇרְעָה (Tsorʻâh, tsor-aw'): Tsorah, a place in Palestine. Origin: apparently another form for H6880 (צִרְעָה); KJV: Zareah, Zorah, Zoreah.

H6882 צׇרְעִי (Tsorʻîy, tsor-ee'): a Tsorite or Tsorathite, i.e. inhabitants of Tsorah. Origin: or צׇרְעָתִי; patrial from H6881 (צׇרְעָה); KJV: Zorites, Zareathites, Zorathites.

H6883 צָרַעַת (tsâraʻath, tsaw-rah'-ath): leprosy. Origin: from H6879 (צָרַע); KJV: leprosy.

H6884 צָרַף (tsâraph, tsaw-raf'): to fuse (metal), i.e. refine (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast, (re-) fine(-er), founder, goldsmith, melt, pure, purge away, try.

H6885 צֹרְפִי (Tsôrᵉphîy, tso-ref-ee'): Tsorephi (with the article), an Israelite. Origin: from H6884 (צָרַף); refiner; KJV: goldsmith's.

H6886 צָרְפַת (Tsârᵉphath, tsaq-ref-ath'): Tsarephath, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6884 (צָרַף); refinement; KJV: Zarephath.

H6887 צָרַר (tsârar, tsaw-rar'): to cramp, literally or figuratively, transitive or intransitive. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: adversary, (be in) afflict(-ion), beseige, bind (up), (be in, bring) distress, enemy, narrower, oppress, pangs, shut up, be in a strait (trouble), vex.

H6888 צְרֵרָה (Tsᵉrêrâh, tser-ay-raw'): Tsererah for Tseredah. Origin: apparently by erroneous transcription for H6868 (צְרֵדָה); KJV: Zererath.

H6889 צֶרֶת (Tsereth, tseh'-reth): Tsereth, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H6671 (צָהַר); splendor; KJV: Zereth.

H6890 צֶרֶת הַשַּׁחַר (Tsereth hash-Shachar, tseh'-reth hash-shakh'-ar): Tsereth-hash-Shachar, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H6889 (צֶרֶת) and H7837 (שַׁחַר) with the article interposed; splendor of the dawn; KJV: Zareth-shahar.

H6891 צָרְתָן (Tsârᵉthân, tsaw-reth-awn'): Tsarethan, a place in Palestine. Origin: perhaps for H6868 (צְרֵדָה); KJV: Zarthan. q

H6892 קֵא (qêʼ, kay): vomit. Origin: or קִיא; from H6958 (קוֹא); KJV: vomit.

H6893 קָאַת (qâʼath, kaw-ath'): probably the pelican (from vomiting). Origin: from H6958 (קוֹא); KJV: cormorant.

H6894 קַב (qab, kab): a hollow, i.e. vessel used as a (dry) measure. Origin: from H6895 (קָבַב); KJV: cab.

H6895 קָבַב (qâbab, kaw-bab'): to scoop out, i.e. (figuratively) to malign or execrate (i.e. stab with words). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, curse.

H6896 קֵבָה (qêbâh, kay-baw'): the paunch (as a cavity) or first stomach of ruminants. Origin: from H6895 (קָבַב); KJV: maw.

H6897 קֹבָה (qôbâh, ko'-baw): the abdomen (as a cavity). Origin: from H6895 (קָבַב); KJV: belly.

H6898 קֻבָּה (qubbâh, koob-baw'): a pavilion (as a domed cavity). Origin: from H6895 (קָבַב); KJV: tent.

H6899 קִבּוּץ (qibbûwts, kib-boots'): a throng. Origin: from H6908 (קָבַץ); KJV: company.

H6900 קְבוּרָה (qᵉbûwrâh, keb-oo-raw'): sepulture; (concretely) a sepulchre. Origin: or קְבֻרָה; feminine passive participle of H6912 (קָבַר); KJV: burial, burying place, grave, sepulchre.

H6901 קָבַל (qâbal, kaw-bal'): to admit, i.e. take (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: choose, (take) hold, receive, (under-) take.

H6902 קְבַל (qᵉbal, keb-al'): to acquire. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6901 (קָבַל); KJV: receive, take.

H6903 קְבֵל (qᵉbêl, keb-ale'): (adverbially) in front of; usually (with other particles) on account of, so as, since, hence. Origin: (Aramaic) or קֳבֵל; (Aramaic), (corresponding to H6905 (קָבָל); KJV: [phrase] according to, [phrase] as, [phrase] because, before, [phrase] for this cause, [phrase] forasmuch as, [phrase] by this means, over against, by reason of, [phrase] that, [phrase] therefore, [phrase] though, [phrase] wherefore.

H6904 קֹבֶל (qôbel, ko'-bel): a battering-ram. Origin: from H6901 (קָבַל) in the sense of confronting (as standing opposite in order to receive); KJV: war.

H6905 קָבָל (qâbâl, kaw-bawl'): the presence, i.e. (adverbially) in front of. Origin: from H6901 (קָבַל) in the sense of opposite (see H6904 (קֹבֶל)); KJV: before.

H6906 קָבַע (qâbaʻ, kaw-bah'): to cover, i.e. (figuratively) defraud. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: rob, spoil.

H6907 קֻבַּעַת (qubbaʻath, koob-bah'-ath): a goblet (as deep like a cover). Origin: from H6906 (קָבַע); KJV: dregs.

H6908 קָבַץ (qâbats, kaw-bats'): to grasp, i.e. collect. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: assemble (selves), gather (bring) (together, selves together, up), heap, resort, [idiom] surely, take up.

H6909 קַבְצְאֵל (Qabtsᵉʼêl, kab-tseh-ale'): Kabtseel, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6908 (קָבַץ) and H410 (אֵל); God has gathered; KJV: Kabzeel. Compare H3343 (יְקַבְצְאֵל).

H6910 קְבֻצָה (qᵉbutsâh, keb-oo-tsaw'): a hoard. Origin: feminine passive participle of H6908 (קָבַץ); KJV: [idiom] gather.

H6911 קִבְצַיִם (Qibtsayim, kib-tsah'-yim): Kibtsajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual from H6908 (קָבַץ); a double heap; KJV: Kibzaim.

H6912 קָבַר (qâbar, kaw-bar'): to inter. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] in any wise, bury(-ier).

H6913 קֶבֶר (qeber, keh'-ber): a sepulchre. Origin: or (feminine) קִבְרָה; from H6912 (קָבַר); KJV: burying place, grave, sepulchre.

H6914 קִבְרוֹת הַתַּאֲוָה (Qibrôwth hat-Taʼă-vâh, kib-roth' hat-tahav-aw'): Kibroth-hat-Taavh, a place in the Desert. Origin: from the feminine plural of H6913 (קֶבֶר) and H8378 (תַּאֲוָה) with the article interposed; graves of the longing; KJV: Kibroth-hattaavah.

H6915 קָדַד (qâdad, kaw-dad'): to shrivel up, i.e. contract or bend the body (or neck) in deference. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bow (down) (the) head, stoop.

H6916 קִדָּה (qiddâh, kid-daw'): cassia bark (as in shrivelled rolls). Origin: from H6915 (קָדַד); KJV: cassia.

H6917 קָדוּם (qâdûwm, kaw-doom'): a pristine hero. Origin: passive participle of H6923 (קָדַם); KJV: ancient.

H6918 קָדוֹשׁ (qâdôwsh, kaw-doshe'): sacred (ceremonially or morally); (as noun) God (by eminence), an angel, a saint, a sanctuary. Origin: or קָדֹשׁ; from H6942 (קָדַשׁ); KJV: holy (One), saint.

H6919 קָדַח (qâdach, kaw-dakh'): to inflame. Origin: a primitive root to inflame KJV: burn, kindle.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H6920 to H7044
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H6920 קַדַּחַת (qaddachath, kad-dakh'-ath): inflammation, i.e. febrile disease. Origin: from H6919 (קָדַח); KJV: burning ague, fever.
