H6921 קָדִים (qâdîym, kaw-deem'): the fore or front part; hence (by orientation) the East (often adverbially, eastward, for brevity the east wind). Origin: or קָדִם; from H6923 (קָדַם); KJV: east(-ward, wind).

H6922 קַדִּישׁ (qaddîysh, kad-deesh'): {sacred (ceremonially or morally); (as noun) God (by eminence), an angel, a saint, a sanctuary}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6918 (קָדוֹשׁ). KJV: holy (One), saint.

H6923 קָדַם (qâdam, kaw-dam'): to project (one self), i.e. precede; hence, to anticipate, hasten, meet (usually for help). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: come (go, (flee)) before, [phrase] disappoint, meet, prevent.

H6924 קֶדֶם (qedem, keh'-dem): the front, of place (absolutely, the fore part, relatively the East) or time (antiquity); often used adverbially (before, anciently, eastward). Origin: or קֵדְמָה; from H6923 (קָדַם); KJV: aforetime, ancient (time), before, east (end, part, side, -ward), eternal, [idiom] ever(-lasting), forward, old, past. Compare H6926 (קִדְמָה).

H6925 קֳדָם (qŏdâm, kod-awm'): before. Origin: (Aramaic) or קְדָם; (Aramaic) (Daniel 7:13), corresponding to H6924 (קֶדֶם); KJV: before, [idiom] from, [idiom] I (thought), [idiom] me, [phrase] of, [idiom] it pleased, presence.

H6926 קִדְמָה (qidmâh, kid-maw'): the forward part (or relatively) East (often adverbially, on the east or in front). Origin: feminine of H6924 (קֶדֶם); KJV: east(-ward).

H6927 קַדְמָה (qadmâh, kad-maw'): priority (in time); also used adverbially (before). Origin: from H6923 (קָדַם); KJV: afore, antiquity, former (old) estate.

H6928 קַדְמָה (qadmâh, kad-maw'): former time. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6927 (קַדְמָה); KJV: afore(-time), ago.

H6929 קֵדְמָה (Qêdᵉmâh, kayd'-maw): Kedemah, a son of Ishmael. Origin: from H6923 (קָדַם); precedence; KJV: Kedemah.

H6930 קַדְמוֹן (qadmôwn, kad-mone'): eastern. Origin: from H6923 (קָדַם); KJV: east.

H6931 קַדְמוֹנִי (qadmôwnîy, kad-mo-nee'): (of time) anterior or (of place) oriental. Origin: or קַדְמֹנִי; from H6930 (קַדְמוֹן); KJV: ancient, they that went before, east, (thing of) old.

H6932 קְדֵמוֹת (Qᵉdêmôwth, ked-ay-mothe'): Kedemoth, a place in eastern Palestine. Origin: from H6923 (קָדַם); beginnings; KJV: Kedemoth.

H6933 קַדְמַי (qadmay, kad-mah'-ee): first. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H6923 (קָדַם); KJV: first.

H6934 קַדְמִיאֵל (Qadmîyʼêl, kad-mee-ale'): Kadmiel, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H6924 (קֶדֶם) and H410 (אֵל); presence of God; KJV: Kadmiel.

H6935 קַדְמֹנִי (Qadmônîy, kad-mo-nee'): Kadmonite (collectively), the name of a tribe in Palestine. Origin: the same as H6931 (קַדְמוֹנִי); ancient, i.e. aboriginal; KJV: Kadmonites.

H6936 קׇדְקֹד (qodqôd, kod-kode'): the crown of the head (as the part most bowed). Origin: from H6915 (קָדַד); KJV: crown (of the head), pate, scalp, top of the head.

H6937 קָדַר (qâdar, kaw-dar'): to be ashy, i.e. darkcolored; by implication, to mourn (in sackcloth or sordid garments). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be black(-ish), be (make) dark(-en), [idiom] heavily, (cause to) mourn.

H6938 קֵדָר (Qêdâr, kay-dawr'): Kedar, a son of Ishmael; also (collectively) Bedouin (as his descendants or representatives). Origin: from H6937 (קָדַר); dusky (of the skin or the tent); KJV: Kedar.

H6939 קִדְרוֹן (Qidrôwn, kid-rone'): Kidron, a brook near Jerusalem. Origin: from H6937 (קָדַר); dusky place; KJV: Kidron.

H6940 קַדְרוּת (qadrûwth, kad-rooth'): duskiness. Origin: from H6937 (קָדַר); KJV: blackness.

H6941 קְדֹרַנִּית (qᵉdôrannîyth, ked-o-ran-neeth'): blackish ones (i.e. in sackcloth); used adverbially, in mourning weeds. Origin: adverb from H6937 (קָדַר); KJV: mournfully.

H6942 קָדַשׁ (qâdash, kaw-dash'): to be (causatively, make, pronounce or observe as) clean (ceremonially or morally). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, bid, consecrate, dedicate, defile, hallow, (be, keep) holy(-er, place), keep, prepare, proclaim, purify, sanctify(-ied one, self), [idiom] wholly.

H6943 קֶדֶשׁ (Qedesh, keh'-desh): Kedesh, the name of four places in Palestine. Origin: from H6942 (קָדַשׁ); a sanctum; KJV: Kedesh.

H6944 קֹדֶשׁ (qôdesh, ko'-desh): a sacred place or thing; rarely abstract, sanctity. Origin: from H6942 (קָדַשׁ); KJV: consecrated (thing), dedicated (thing), hallowed (thing), holiness, ([idiom] most) holy ([idiom] day, portion, thing), saint, sanctuary.

H6945 קָדֵשׁ (qâdêsh, kaw-dashe'): a (quasi) sacred person, i.e. (technically) a (male) devotee (by prostitution) to licentious idolatry. Origin: from H6942 (קָדַשׁ); KJV: sodomite, unclean.

H6946 קָדֵשׁ (Qâdêsh, kaw-dashe'): Kadesh, a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H6945 (קָדֵשׁ); sanctuary; KJV: Kadesh. Compare H6947 (קָדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ).

H6947 קָדֵשׁ בַּרְנֵעַ (Qâdêsh Barnêaʻ, kaw-dashe' bar-nay'-ah): Kadesh-Barnea, a place in the Desert. Origin: from the same as H6946 (קָדֵשׁ) and an otherwise unused word (apparently compounded of a correspondent to H1251 (בַּר) and a derivative of H5128 (נוּעַ)) meaning desert of a fugitive; Kadesh of (the) Wilderness of Wandering; KJV: Kadeshbarnea.

H6948 קְדֵשָׁה (qᵉdêshâh, ked-ay-shaw'): a female devotee (i.e. prostitute). Origin: feminine of H6945 (קָדֵשׁ); KJV: harlot, whore.

H6949 קָהָה (qâhâh, kaw-haw'): to be dull. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be set on edge, be blunt.

H6950 קָהַל (qâhal, 'kaw-hal'): to convoke. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: assemble (selves) (together), gather (selves) (together).

H6951 קָהָל (qâhâl, kaw-hawl'): assemblage (usually concretely). Origin: from H6950 (קָהַל); KJV: assembly, company, congregation, multitude.

H6952 קְהִלָּה (qᵉhillâh, keh-hil-law'): an assemblage. Origin: from H6950 (קָהַל); KJV: assembly, congregation.

H6953 קֹהֶלֶת (qôheleth, ko-heh'-leth): a (female) assembler (i.e. lecturer); abstractly, preaching (used as a 'nom de plume', Koheleth). Origin: feminine of active participle from H6950 (קָהַל); KJV: preacher.

H6954 קְהֵלָתָה (Qᵉhêlâthâh, keh-hay-law'-thaw): Kehelathah, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H6950 (קָהַל); convocation; KJV: Kehelathah.

H6955 קְהָת (Qᵉhâth, keh-hawth'): Kehath, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to ally oneself; allied; KJV: Kohath.

H6956 קֳהָתִי (Qŏhâthîy, ko-haw-thee'): a Kohathite (collectively) or descendants of Kehath. Origin: patronymically from H6955 (קְהָת); KJV: Kohathites.

H6957 קַו (qav, kav): a cord (as connecting), especially formeasuring; figuratively, a rule; also a rim, a musical string or accord. Origin: or קָו; from H6960 (קָוָה) (compare H6961 (קָוֶה)); KJV: line. Compare H6978 (קַו־קַו)lemma קַו־קַי yod, corrected to קַו־קַו.

H6958 קוֹא (qôwʼ, ko): to vomit. Origin: or קָיָה; (Jeremiah 25:27), a primitive root; KJV: spue (out), vomit (out, up, up again).

H6959 קוֹבַע (qôwbaʻ, ko'-bah or ko-bah'): a helmet. Origin: a form collateral to H3553 (כּוֹבַע); KJV: helmet.

H6960 קָוָה (qâvâh, kaw-vaw'): to bind together (perhaps by twisting), i.e. collect; (figuratively) to expect. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather (together), look, patiently, tarry, wait (for, on, upon).

H6961 קָוֶה (qâveh, kaw-veh'): a (measuring) cord (as if for binding). Origin: from H6960 (קָוָה); KJV: line.

H6962 קוּט (qûwṭ, koot): properly, to cut off, i.e. (figuratively) detest. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: begrieved, loathe self.

H6963 קוֹל (qôwl, kole): a voice or sound. Origin: or קֹל; from an unused root meaning to call aloud; KJV: [phrase] aloud, bleating, crackling, cry ([phrase] out), fame, lightness, lowing, noise, [phrase] hold peace, (pro-) claim, proclamation, [phrase] sing, sound, [phrase] spark, thunder(-ing), voice, [phrase] yell.

H6964 קוֹלָיָה (Qôwlâyâh, ko-law-yaw'): Kolajah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H6963 (קוֹל) and H3050 (יָהּ); voice of Jah; KJV: Kolaiah.

H6965 קוּם (qûwm, koom): to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abide, accomplish, [idiom] be clearer, confirm, continue, decree, [idiom] be dim, endure, [idiom] enemy, enjoin, get up, make good, help, hold, (help to) lift up (again), make, [idiom] but newly, ordain, perform, pitch, raise (up), rear (up), remain, (a-) rise (up) (again, against), rouse up, set (up), (e-) stablish, (make to) stand (up), stir up, strengthen, succeed, (as-, make) sure(-ly), (be) up(-hold, -rising).

H6966 קוּם (qûwm, koom): {to rise (in various applications, literal, figurative, intensive and causative)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6965 (קוּם) KJV: appoint, establish, make, raise up self, (a-) rise (up), (make to) stand, set (up).

H6967 קוֹמָה (qôwmâh, ko-maw'): height. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); KJV: [idiom] along, height, high, stature, tall.

H6968 קוֹמְמִיּוּת (qôwmᵉmîyûwth, ko-mem-ee-yooth'): elevation, i.e. (adverbially) erectly (figuratively). Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); KJV: upright.

H6969 קוּן (qûwn, koon): to strike a musical note, i.e. chant or wail (at a funeral). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lament, mourning woman.

H6970 קוֹעַ (Qôwaʻ, ko'-ah): Koa, a region of Babylon. Origin: probably from H6972 (קוּץ) in the original sense of cutting off; curtailment; KJV: Koa.

H6971 קוֹף (qôwph, kofe): a monkey. Origin: or קֹף; of foreign origin, KJV: ape.

H6972 קוּץ (qûwts, koots): to spend the harvest season. Origin: a primitive root; to clip off; used only as denominative from H7019 (קַיִץ); KJV: summer.

H6973 קוּץ (qûwts, koots): to be (causatively, make) disgusted or anxious. Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of severing oneself from (compare H6962 (קוּט))); KJV: abhor, be distressed, be grieved, loathe, vex, be weary.

H6974 קוּץ (qûwts, koots): to awake (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of abruptness in starting up from sleep (compare H3364 (יָקַץ))); KJV: arise, (be) (a-) wake, watch.

H6975 קוֹץ (qôwts, kotse): a thorn. Origin: or קֹץ; from H6972 (קוּץ) (in the sense of pricking); KJV: thorn.

H6976 קוֹץ (Qôwts, kotse): Kots, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H6975 (קוֹץ); KJV: Koz, Hakkoz (including the article).

H6977 קְוֻצָּה (qᵉvutstsâh, kev-oots-tsaw'): a forelock (as shorn). Origin: feminine passive participle of H6972 (קוּץ) in its original sense; KJV: lock.

H6978 קַו־קַו (qav-qav, kav-kav'): stalwart. Origin: from H6957 (קַו) (in the sense of a fastening); KJV: [idiom] meted out.

H6979 קוּר (qûwr, koor): to trench; by implication, to throw forth; to wall up, whether literal (to build a wall) or figurative (to estop). Origin: a primitive root; also denominative from H7023 (קִיר) KJV: break down, cast out, destroy, dig.

H6980 קוּר (qûwr, koor): (only plural) trenches, i.e. a web (as if so formed). Origin: from H6979 (קוּר); KJV: web.

H6981 קוֹרֵא (Qôwrêʼ, ko-ray'): Kore, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or קֹרֵא; (1 Chronicles 26:1), active participle of H7121 (קָרָא); crier; KJV: Kore.

H6982 קוֹרָה (qôwrâh, ko-raw'): a rafter (forming trenches as it were); by implication, a roof. Origin: or קֹרָה; from H6979 (קוּר); KJV: beam, roof.

H6983 קוֹשׁ (qôwsh, koshe): to set a trap. Origin: a primitive root; to bend; used only as denominative for H3369 (יָקֹשׁ), KJV: lay a snare.

H6984 קוּשָׁיָהוּ (qûwshâyâhûw, koo-shaw-yaw'-hoo): Kushajah, an Israelite. Origin: from the passive participle of H6983 (קוֹשׁ) and H3050 (יָהּ); entrapped of Jah; KJV: Kushaiah.

H6985 קַט (qaṭ, kat): a little, i.e. (adverbially) merely. Origin: from H6990 (קָטַט) in the sense of abbreviation; KJV: very.

H6986 קֶטֶב (qeṭeb, keh'-teb): ruin. Origin: from an unused root meaning to cut off; KJV: destroying, destruction.

H6987 קֹטֶב (qôṭeb, ko'-teb): extermination. Origin: from the same as H6986 (קֶטֶב); KJV: destruction.

H6988 קְטוֹרָה (qᵉṭôwrâh, ket-o-raw'): perfume. Origin: from H6999 (קָטַר); KJV: incense.

H6989 קְטוּרָה (Qᵉṭûwrâh, ket-oo-raw'): Keturah, a wife of Abraham. Origin: feminine passive participle of H6999 (קָטַר); perfumed; KJV: Keturah.

H6990 קָטַט (qâṭaṭ, kaw-tat'): to clip off, i.e. (figuratively) destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be cut off.

H6991 קָטַל (qâṭal, kaw-tal'): properly, to cut off, i.e. (figuratively) put to death. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: kill, slay.

H6992 קְטַל (qᵉṭal, ket-al'): to kill. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6991 (קָטַל); KJV: slay.

H6993 קֶטֶל (qeṭel, keh'-tel): a violent death. Origin: from H6991 (קָטַל); KJV: slaughter.

H6994 קָטֹן (qâṭôn, kaw-tone'): to diminish, i.e. be (causatively, make) diminutive or (figuratively) of no account. Origin: a primitive root (rather denominative from H6996 (קָטָן)); KJV: be a (make) small (thing), be not worthy.

H6995 קֹטֶן (qôṭen, ko'-ten): a pettiness, i.e. the little finger. Origin: from H6994 (קָטֹן); KJV: little finger.

H6996 קָטָן (qâṭân, kaw-tawn'): abbreviated, i.e. diminutive, literally (in quantity, size or number) or figuratively (in age or importance). Origin: or קָטֹן; from H6962 (קוּט); KJV: least, less(-er), little (one), small(-est, one, quantity, thing), young(-er, -est).

H6997 קָטָן (Qâṭân, kaw-tawn'): Katan, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H6996 (קָטָן); small; KJV: Hakkatan (including the article).

H6998 קָטַף (qâṭaph, kaw-taf'): to strip off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: crop off, cut down (up), pluck.

H6999 קָטַר (qâṭar, kaw-tar'): to smoke, i.e. turn into fragrance by fire (especially as an act of worship). Origin: a primitive root (identical with through the idea of fumigation in a close place and perhaps thus driving out the occupants); KJV: burn (incense, sacrifice) (upon), (altar for) incense, kindle, offer (incense, a sacrifice).

H7000 קָטַר (qâṭar, kaw-tar'): to inclose. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: join.

H7001 קְטַר (qᵉṭar, ket-ar'): a knot (as tied up), i.e. (figuratively) a riddle; also a vertebra (as if a knot). Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H7000 (קָטַר); KJV: doubt, joint.

H7002 קִטֵּר (qiṭṭêr, kit-tare'): perfume. Origin: from H6999 (קָטַר); KJV: incense.

H7003 קִטְרוֹן (Qiṭrôwn, kit-rone'): Kitron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6999 (קָטַר); fumigative; KJV: Kitron.

H7004 קְטֹרֶת (qᵉṭôreth, ket-o'-reth): a fumigation. Origin: from H6999 (קָטַר); KJV: (sweet) incense, perfume.

H7005 קַטָּת (Qaṭṭâth, kat-tawth'): Kattath, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H6996 (קָטָן); littleness; KJV: Kattath.

H7006 קָיָה (qâyâh, kaw-yaw'): to vomit. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: spue.

H7007 קַיִט (qayiṭ, kah'-yit): harvest. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7019 (קַיִץ); KJV: summer.

H7008 קִיטוֹר (qîyṭôwr, kee-tore'): a fume, i.e. cloud. Origin: or קִיטֹר; from H6999 (קָטַר); KJV: smoke, vapour.

H7009 קִים (qîym, keem): an opponent (as rising against one), i.e. (collectively) enemies. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); KJV: substance.

H7010 קְיָם (qᵉyâm, keh-yawm'): an edict (as arising in law). Origin: (Aramaic) from H6966 (קוּם); KJV: decree, statute.

H7011 קַיָּם (qayâm, kah-yawm'): permanent (as rising firmly). Origin: (Aramaic) from H6966 (קוּם); KJV: stedfast, sure.

H7012 קִימָה (qîymâh, kee-maw'): an arising. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); KJV: rising up.

H7013 קַיִן (qayin, kah'-yin): a lance (as striking fast). Origin: from H6969 (קוּן) in the original sense of fixity; KJV: spear.

H7014 קַיִן (Qayin, kah'-yin): Kajin, the name of the first child, also of a place in Palestine, and of an Oriental tribe. Origin: the same as H7013 (קַיִן) (with a play upon the affinity to H7069 (קָנָה)); KJV: Cain, Kenite(-s).

H7015 קִינָה (qîynâh, kee-naw'): a dirge (as accompanied by beating the breasts or on instruments). Origin: from H6969 (קוּן); KJV: lamentation.

H7016 קִינָה (Qîynâh, kee-naw'): Kinah, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H7015 (קִינָה); KJV: Kinah.

H7017 קֵינִי (Qêynîy, kay-nee'): a Kenite or member of the tribe of Kajin. Origin: or קִינִי; (1 Chronicles 2:55), patronymic from H7014 (קַיִן); KJV: Kenite.

H7018 קֵינָן (Qêynân, kay-nawn'): Kenan, an antediluvian. Origin: from the same as H7064 (קֵן); fixed; KJV: Cainan, Kenan.

H7019 קַיִץ (qayits, kah'-yits): harvest (as the crop), whether the product (grain or fruit) or the (dry) season. Origin: from H6972 (קוּץ); KJV: summer (fruit, house).

H7020 קִיצוֹן (qîytsôwn, kee-tsone'): terminal. Origin: from H6972 (קוּץ); KJV: out-(utter-) most.

H7021 קִיקָיוֹן (qîyqâyôwn, kee-kaw-yone'): the gourd (as nauseous). Origin: perhaps from H7006 (קָיָה); KJV: gourd.

H7022 קִיקָלוֹן (qîyqâlôwn, kee-kaw-lone'): intense disgrace. Origin: from H7036 (קָלוֹן); KJV: shameful spewing.

H7023 קִיר (qîyr, keer): a wall (as built in a trench). Origin: or קִר; (Isaiah 22:5), or (feminine) קִירָה; from H6979 (קוּר); KJV: [phrase] mason, side, town, [idiom] very, wall.

H7024 קִיר (Qîyr, keer): Kir, a place in Assyrian; also one in Moab. Origin: the same as H7023 (קִיר); fortress; KJV: Kir. Compare H7025 (קִיר חֶרֶשׂ).

H7025 קִיר חֶרֶשׂ (Qîyr Cheres, keer kheh'-res): Kir-Cheres or Kir-Chareseth, a place in Moab. Origin: or (feminine of the latter word) קִיר חֲרֶשֶׂת; from H7023 (קִיר) and H2789 (חֶרֶשׂ); fortress of earthenware; KJV: Kir-haraseth, Kir-hareseth, Kirharesh, Kir-heres.

H7026 קֵירֹס (Qêyrôç, kay-roce'): Keros, one of the Nethinim. Origin: or קֵרֹס; from the same as H7166 (קַרְסֹל); ankled; KJV: Keros.

H7027 קִישׁ (Qîysh, keesh): Kish, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H6983 (קוֹשׁ); a bow; KJV: Kish.

H7028 קִישׁוֹן (Qîyshôwn, kee-shone'): Kishon, a river of Palestine. Origin: from H6983 (קוֹשׁ); winding; KJV: Kishon, Kison.

H7029 קִישִׁי (Qîyshîy, kee-shee'): Kishi, an Israelite. Origin: from H6983 (קוֹשׁ); bowed; KJV: Kishi.

H7030 קִיתָרֹס (qîythârôç, kee-thaw-roce'): a lyre. Origin: (Aramaic) of Greek origin; KJV: harp.

H7031 קַל (qal, kal): light; (by implication) rapid (also adverbial). Origin: contracted from H7043 (קָלַל); KJV: light, swift(-ly).

H7032 קָל (qâl, kawl): {a voice or sound}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H6963 (קוֹל) KJV: sound, voice.

H7033 קָלָה (qâlâh, kaw-law'): to toast, i.e. scorch partially or slowly. Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H7034 (קָלָה) through the idea of shrinkage by heat); KJV: dried, loathsome, parch, roast.

H7034 קָלָה (qâlâh, kaw-law'): to be light (as implied in rapid motion), but figuratively, only (be (causatively, hold) in contempt). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: base, contemn, despise, lightly esteem, set light, seem vile.

H7035 קָלַהּ (qâlahh, kaw-lah'): to assemble. Origin: for H6950 (קָהַל); KJV: gather together.

H7036 קָלוֹן (qâlôwn, kaw-lone'): disgrace; (by implication) the pudenda. Origin: from H7034 (קָלָה); KJV: confusion, dishonour, ignominy, reproach, shame.

H7037 קַלַּחַת (qallachath, kal-lakh'-ath): a kettle. Origin: apparently but a form for H6747 (צַלַּחַת); KJV: caldron.

H7038 קָלַט (qâlaṭ, kaw-lat'): to maim. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lacking in his parts.

H7039 קָלִי (qâlîy, kaw-lee'): roasted ears of grain. Origin: or קָלִיא; from H7033 (קָלָה); KJV: parched corn.

H7040 קַלַּי (Qallay, kal-lah'-ee): Kallai, an Israelite. Origin: from H7043 (קָלַל); frivolous; KJV: Kallai.

H7041 קֵלָיָה (Qêlâyâh, kay-law-yaw'): Kelajah, an Israelite. Origin: from H7034 (קָלָה); insignificance; KJV: Kelaiah.

H7042 קְלִיטָא (Qᵉlîyṭâʼ, kel-ee-taw'): Kelita, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H7038 (קָלַט); maiming; KJV: Kelita.

H7043 קָלַל (qâlal, kaw-lal'): to be (causatively, make) light, literally (swift, small, sharp, etc.) or figuratively (easy, trifling, vile, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abate, make bright, bring into contempt, (ac-) curse, despise, (be) ease(-y, -ier), (be a, make, make somewhat, move, seem a, set) light(-en, -er, -ly, -ly afflict, -ly esteem, thing), [idiom] slight(-ly), be swift(-er), (be, be more, make, re-) vile, whet.

H7044 קָלָל (qâlâl, kaw-lawl'): brightened (as if sharpened). Origin: from H7043 (קָלַל); KJV: burnished, polished.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H7045 to H7164
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H7045 קְלָלָה (qᵉlâlâh, kel-aw-law'): vilification. Origin: from H7043 (קָלַל); KJV: (ac-) curse(-d, -ing).

H7046 קָלַס (qâlaç, kaw-las'): to disparage, i.e. ridicule. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: mock, scoff, scorn.

H7047 קֶלֶס (qeleç, keh'-les): a laughing-stock. Origin: from H7046 (קָלַס); KJV: derision.

H7048 קַלָּסָה (qallâçâh, kal-law-saw'): ridicule. Origin: intensive from H7046 (קָלַס); KJV: mocking.

H7049 קָלַע (qâlaʻ, kaw-lah'): to sling; also to carve (as if a circular motion, or into light forms). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: carve, sling (out).

H7050 קֶלַע (qelaʻ, keh'-lah): a sling; also a (door) screen (as if slung across), or the valve (of the door) itself. Origin: from H7049 (קָלַע); KJV: hanging, leaf, sling.

H7051 קַלָּע (qallâʻ, kal-law'): a slinger. Origin: intensive from H7049 (קָלַע); KJV: slinger.

H7052 קְלֹקֵל (qᵉlôqêl, kel-o-kale'): insubstantial. Origin: from H7043 (קָלַל); KJV: light.

H7053 קִלְּשׁוֹן (qillᵉshôwn, kil-lesh-one'): a prong, i.e. hay-fork. Origin: from an unused root meaning to prick; KJV: fork.

H7054 קָמָה (qâmâh, kuw-maw'): something that rises, i.e. a stalk of grain. Origin: feminine of active participle of H6965 (קוּם); KJV: (standing) corn, grown up, stalk.

H7055 קְמוּאֵל (Qᵉmûwʼêl, kem-oo-ale'): Kemuel, the name of a relative of Abraham, and of two Israelites. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם) and H410 (אֵל); raised of God; KJV: Kemuel.

H7056 קָמוֹן (Qâmôwn, kaw-mone'): Kamon, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H6965 (קוּם); an elevation; KJV: Camon.

H7057 קִמּוֹשׁ (qimmôwsh, kim-moshe'): a prickly plant. Origin: or קִימוֹשׁ; from an unused root meaning to sting; KJV: nettle. Compare H7063 (קִמָּשׁוֹן).

H7058 קֶמַח (qemach, keh'-makh): flour. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to grind; KJV: flour, meal.

H7059 קָמַט (qâmaṭ, kaw-mat'): to pluck, i.e. destroy. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut down, fill with wrinkles.

H7060 קָמַל (qâmal, kaw-mal'): to wither. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hew down, wither.

H7061 קָמַץ (qâmats, kaw-mats'): to grasp with the hand. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: take an handful.

H7062 קֹמֶץ (qômets, ko'mets): a grasp, i.e. handful. Origin: from H7061 (קָמַץ); KJV: handful.

H7063 קִמָּשׁוֹן (qimmâshôwn, kim-maw-shone'): a prickly plant. Origin: from the same as H7057 (קִמּוֹשׁ); KJV: thorn.

H7064 קֵן (qên, kane): a nest (as fixed), sometimes including the nestlings; figuratively, a chamber or dwelling. Origin: contracted from H7077 (קָנַן); KJV: nest, room.

H7065 קָנָא (qânâʼ, kaw-naw'): to be (causatively, make) zealous, i.e. (in a bad sense) jealous or envious. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) envy(-ious), be (move to, provoke to) jealous(-y), [idiom] very, (be) zeal(-ous).

H7066 קְנָא (qᵉnâʼ, ken-aw'): to purchase. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7069 (קָנָה); KJV: buy.

H7067 קַנָּא (qannâʼ, kan-naw'): jealous. Origin: from H7065 (קָנָא); KJV: jealous. Compare H7072 (קַנּוֹא).

H7068 קִנְאָה (qinʼâh, kin-aw'): jealousy or envy. Origin: from H7065 (קָנָא); KJV: envy(-ied), jealousy, [idiom] sake, zeal.

H7069 קָנָה (qânâh, kaw-naw'): to erect, i.e. create; by extension, to procure, especially by purchase (causatively, sell); by implication to own. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: attain, buy(-er), teach to keep cattle, get, provoke to jealousy, possess(-or), purchase, recover, redeem, [idiom] surely, [idiom] verily.

H7070 קָנֶה (qâneh, kaw-neh'): a reed (as erect); by resemblance a rod (especially for measuring), shaft, tube, stem, the radius (of the arm), beam (of a steelyard). Origin: from H7069 (קָנָה); KJV: balance, bone, branch, calamus, cane, reed, [idiom] spearman, stalk.

H7071 קָנָה (Qânâh, kaw-naw'): Kanah, the name of a stream and of a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine of H7070 (קָנֶה); reediness; KJV: Kanah.

H7072 קַנּוֹא (qannôwʼ, kan-no'): jealous or angry. Origin: for H7067 (קַנָּא); KJV: jealous.

H7073 קְנַז (Qᵉnaz, ken-az'): Kenaz, the name of an Edomite and of two Israelites. Origin: probably from an unused root meaning to hunt; hunter; KJV: Kenaz.

H7074 קְנִזִּי (Qᵉnizzîy, ken-iz-zee'): a Kenizzite or descendant of Kenaz. Origin: patronymic from H7073 (קְנַז), KJV: Kenezite, Kenizzites.

H7075 קִנְיָן (qinyân, kin-yawn'): creation, i.e. (concretely) creatures; also acquisition, purchase, wealth. Origin: from H7069 (קָנָה); KJV: getting, goods, [idiom] with money, riches, substance.

H7076 קִנָּמוֹן (qinnâmôwn, kin-naw-mone'): cinnamon bark (as in upright rolls). Origin: from an unused root (meaning to erect); KJV: cinnamon.

H7077 קָנַן (qânan, kaw-nan'): to nestle, i.e. build or occupy as anest. Origin: a primitive root; to erect; but used only as denominative from H7064 (קֵן); KJV: make...nest.

H7078 קֶנֶץ (qenets, keh'-nets): perversion. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to wrench; KJV: end.

H7079 קְנָת (Qᵉnâth, ken-awth'): Kenath, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H7069 (קָנָה); possession; KJV: Kenath.

H7080 קָסַם (qâçam, kaw-sam'): properly, to distribute, i.e. determine by lot or magical scroll; by implication, to divine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: divine(-r, -ation), prudent, soothsayer, use (divination).

H7081 קֶסֶם (qeçem, keh'-sem): a lot; also divination (including its fee), oracle. Origin: from H7080 (קָסַם); KJV: (reward of) divination, divine sentence, witchcraft.

H7082 קָסַס (qâçaç, kaw-sas'): to lop off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut off.

H7083 קֶסֶת (qeçeth, keh'-seth): properly, a cup, i.e. an ink-stand. Origin: from the same as H3563 (כּוֹס) (or as H7185 (קָשָׁה)); KJV: inkhorn.

H7084 קְעִילָה (Qᵉʻîylâh, keh-ee-law'): Keilah, a place in Palestine. Origin: perhaps from H7049 (קָלַע) in the sense of enclosing; citadel; KJV: Keilah.

H7085 קַעֲקַע (qaʻăqaʻ, kah-ak-ah'): an incision or gash. Origin: from the same as H6970 (קוֹעַ); KJV: [phrase] mark.

H7086 קְעָרָה (qᵉʻârâh, keh-aw-raw'): a bowl (as cut out hollow). Origin: probably from H7167 (קָרַע); KJV: charger, dish.

H7087 קָפָא (qâphâʼ, kaw-faw'): to shrink, i.e. thicken (as unracked wine, curdled milk, clouded sky, frozen water). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: congeal, curdle, dark, settle.

H7088 קָפַד (qâphad, kaw-fad'): to contract, i.e. roll together. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut off.

H7089 קְפָדָה (qᵉphâdâh, kef-aw-daw'): shrinking, i.e., terror. Origin: from H7088 (קָפַד); KJV: destruction.

H7090 קִפּוֹד (qippôwd, kip-pode'): a species of bird, perhaps the bittern (from its contracted form). Origin: or קִפֹּדlemma קִכֹּד kaf, corrected to קִפֹּד; from H7088 (קָפַד); KJV: bittern.

H7091 קִפּוֹז (qippôwz, kip-poze'): spring forward; an arrow-snake (as darting on its prey). Origin: from an unused root meaning to contract, i.e. KJV: great owl.

H7092 קָפַץ (qâphats, kaw-fats'): to draw together, i.e. close; by implication, to leap (by contracting the limbs); specifically, to die (from gathering up the feet). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: shut (up), skip, stop, take out of the way.

H7093 קֵץ (qêts, kates): an extremity; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after. Origin: contracted from H7112 (קָצַץ); KJV: [phrase] after, (utmost) border, end, (in-) finite, [idiom] process.

H7094 קָצַב (qâtsab, kaw-tsab'): to clip, or (generally) chop. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut down, shorn.

H7095 קֶצֶב (qetseb, keh'-tseb): shape (as if cut out); base (as if there cut off). Origin: from H7094 (קָצַב); KJV: bottom, size.

H7096 קָצָה (qâtsâh, kaw-tsaw'): to cut off; (figuratively) to destroy; (partially) to scrape off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut off, cut short, scrape (off).

H7097 קָצֶה (qâtseh, kaw-tseh'): an extremity. Origin: or (negative only) קֵצֶה; from H7096 (קָצָה); (used in a great variety of applications and idioms; compare H7093 (קֵץ)) KJV: [idiom] after, border, brim, brink, edge, end, (in-) finite, frontier, outmost coast, quarter, shore, (out-) side, [idiom] some, ut(-ter-) most (part).

H7098 קָצָה (qâtsâh, kaw-tsaw'): a termination. Origin: feminine of H7097 (קָצֶה); (used like H7097 (קָצֶה)) KJV: coast, corner, (selv-) edge, lowest, (uttermost) participle

H7099 קֶצֶו (qetsev, keh'-tsev): a limit. Origin: and (feminine) קִצְוָה; from H7096 (קָצָה); (used like H7097 (קָצֶה), but with less variety) KJV: end, edge, uttermost participle

H7100 קֶצַח (qetsach, keh'-tsakh): fennelflower (from its pungency). Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to incise; KJV: fitches.

H7101 קָצִין (qâtsîyn, kaw-tseen'): a magistrate (as deciding) or other leader. Origin: from H7096 (קָצָה) in the sense of determining; KJV: captain, guide, prince, ruler. Compare H6278 (עֵת קָצִין).

H7102 קְצִיעָה (qᵉtsîyʻâh, kets-ee-aw'): cassia (as peeled; plural the bark). Origin: from H7106 (קָצַע); KJV: cassia.

H7103 קְצִיעָה (Qᵉtsîyʻâh, kets-ee-aw'): Ketsiah, a daughter of Job. Origin: the same as H7102 (קְצִיעָה); KJV: Kezia.

H7104 קְצִיץ (Qᵉtsîyts, kets-eets'): Keziz, a valley in Palestine. Origin: from H7112 (קָצַץ); abrupt; KJV: Keziz.

H7105 קָצִיר (qâtsîyr, kaw-tseer'): severed, i.e. harvest (as reaped), the crop, the time, the reaper, or figuratively; also a limb (of a tree, or simply foliage). Origin: from H7114 (קָצַר); KJV: bough, branch, harvest (man).

H7106 קָצַע (qâtsaʻ, kaw-tsah'): to strip off, i.e. (partially) scrape; by implication, to segregate (as an angle). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cause to scrape, corner.

H7107 קָצַף (qâtsaph, kaw-tsaf'): to crack off, i.e. (figuratively) burst out in rage. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) anger(-ry), displease, fret self, (provoke to) wrath (come), be wroth.

H7108 קְצַף (qᵉtsaph, kets-af'): to become enraged. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7107 (קָצַף); KJV: be furious.

H7109 קְצַף (qᵉtsaph, kets-af'): rage. Origin: (Aramaic) from H7108 (קְצַף); KJV: wrath.

H7110 קֶצֶף (qetseph, keh'-tsef): a splinter (as chipped off); figuratively, rage or strife. Origin: from H7107 (קָצַף); KJV: foam, indignation, [idiom] sore, wrath.

H7111 קְצָפָה (qᵉtsâphâh, kets-aw-faw'): a fragment. Origin: from H7107 (קָצַף); KJV: bark(-ed).

H7112 קָצַץ (qâtsats, kaw-tsats'): to chop off (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut (asunder, in pieces, in sunder, off), [idiom] utmost.

H7113 קְצַץ (qᵉtsats, kets-ats'): {to chop off (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7112 (קָצַץ) KJV: cut off.

H7114 קָצַר (qâtsar, kaw-tsar'): to dock off, i.e. curtail (transitive or intransitive, literal or figurative); especially to harvest (grass or grain). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] at all, cut down, much discouraged, grieve, harvestman, lothe, mourn, reap(-er), (be, wax) short(-en, -er), straiten, trouble, vex.

H7115 קֹצֶר (qôtser, ko'-tser): shortness (of spirit), i.e. impatience. Origin: from H7114 (קָצַר); KJV: anguish.

H7116 קָצֵר (qâtsêr, kaw-tsare'): short (whether in size, number, life, strength or temper). Origin: from H7114 (קָצַר); KJV: few, hasty, small, soon.

H7117 קְצָת (qᵉtsâth, kets-awth'): a termination (literally or figuratively); also (by implication) a portion; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after. Origin: from H7096 (קָצָה); KJV: end, part, [idiom] some.

H7118 קְצָת (qᵉtsâth, kets-awth'): {a termination (literally or figuratively); also (by implication) a portion; adverbially (with prepositional prefix) after}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7117 (קְצָת) KJV: end, partly.

H7119 קַר (qar, kar): cool; figuratively, quiet. Origin: contracted from an unused root meaning to chill; KJV: cold, excellent (from the margin).

H7120 קֹר (qôr, kore): cold. Origin: from the same as H7119 (קַר); KJV: cold.

H7121 קָרָא (qârâʼ, kaw-raw'): to call out to (i.e. properly, address by name, but used in a wide variety of applications). Origin: a primitive root (rather identical with H7122 (קָרָא) through the idea of accosting a person met); KJV: bewray (self), that are bidden, call (for, forth, self, upon), cry (unto), (be) famous, guest, invite, mention, (give) name, preach, (make) proclaim(-ation), pronounce, publish, read, renowned, say.

H7122 קָרָא (qârâʼ, kaw-raw'): to encounter, whether accidentally or in a hostile manner. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: befall, (by) chance, (cause to) come (upon), fall out, happen, meet.

H7123 קְרָא (qᵉrâʼ, ker-aw'): {to call out to (i.e. properly, address by name, but used in a wide variety of applications)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7121 (קָרָא) KJV: call, cry, read.

H7124 קֹרֵא (qôrêʼ, ko-ray'): a caller, i.e. partridge (from its cry). Origin: properly, active participle of H7121 (קָרָא); KJV: partridge. See also H6981 (קוֹרֵא).

H7125 קִרְאָה (qirʼâh, keer-aw'): an encountering, accidental, friendly or hostile (also adverbially, opposite). Origin: from H7122 (קָרָא); KJV: [idiom] against (he come), help, meet, seek, [idiom] to, [idiom] in the way.

H7126 קָרַב (qârab, kaw-rab'): to approach (causatively, bring near) for whatever purpose. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to) approach, (cause to) bring (forth, near), (cause to) come (near, nigh), (cause to) draw near (nigh), go (near), be at hand, join, be near, offer, present, produce, make ready, stand, take.

H7127 קְרֵב (qᵉrêb, ker-abe'): {to approach (causatively, bring near) for whatever purpose}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7126 (קָרַב) KJV: approach, come (near, nigh), draw near.

H7128 קְרָב (qᵉrâb, ker-awb'): hostile encounter. Origin: from H7126 (קָרַב); KJV: battle, war.

H7129 קְרָב (qᵉrâb, ker-awb'): {hostile encounter}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7128 (קְרָב) KJV: war.

H7130 קֶרֶב (qereb, keh'-reb): properly, the nearest part, i.e. the center, whether literal, figurative or adverbial (especially with preposition). Origin: from H7126 (קָרַב); KJV: [idiom] among, [idiom] before, bowels, [idiom] unto charge, [phrase] eat (up), [idiom] heart, [idiom] him, [idiom] in, inward ([idiom] -ly, part, -s, thought), midst, [phrase] out of, purtenance, [idiom] therein, [idiom] through, [idiom] within self.

H7131 קָרֵב (qârêb, kaw-rabe'): near. Origin: from H7126 (קָרַב); KJV: approach, come (near, nigh), draw near.

H7132 קְרָבָה (qᵉrâbâh, ker-aw-baw'): approach. Origin: from H7126 (קָרַב); KJV: approaching, draw near.

H7133 קׇרְבָּן (qorbân, kor-bawn'): something brought near the altar, i.e. a sacrificial present. Origin: or קֻרְבָּן; from H7126 (קָרַב); KJV: oblation, that is offered, offering.

H7134 קַרְדֹּם (qardôm, kar-dome'): an axe. Origin: perhaps from H6923 (קָדַם) in the sense of striking upon; KJV: ax.

H7135 קָרָה (qârâh, kaw-raw'): coolness. Origin: feminine of H7119 (קַר); KJV: cold.

H7136 קָרָה (qârâh, kaw-raw'): to light upon (chiefly by accident); causatively, to bring about; specifically, to impose timbers (for roof or floor). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appoint, lay (make) beams, befall, bring, come (to pass unto), floor, (hap) was, happen (unto), meet, send good speed.

H7137 קָרֶה (qâreh, kaw-reh'): an (unfortunate) occurrence, i.e. some accidental (ceremonial) disqualification. Origin: from H7136 (קָרָה); KJV: uncleanness that chanceth.

H7138 קָרוֹב (qârôwb, kaw-robe'): near (in place, kindred or time). Origin: or קָרֹב; from H7126 (קָרַב); KJV: allied, approach, at hand, [phrase] any of kin, kinsfold(-sman), (that is) near (of kin), neighbour, (that is) next, (them that come) nigh (at hand), more ready, short(-ly).

H7139 קָרַח (qârach, kaw-rakh'): to depilate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make (self) bald.

H7140 קֶרַח (qerach, keh'-rakh): ice (as if bald, i.e. smooth); hence, hail; by resemblance, rock crystal. Origin: or קֹרַח; from H7139 (קָרַח); KJV: crystal, frost, ice.

H7141 קֹרַח (Qôrach, ko'rakh): Korach, the name of two Edomites and three Israelites. Origin: from H7139 (קָרַח); ice; KJV: Korah.

H7142 קֵרֵחַ (qêrêach, kay-ray'-akh): bald (on the back of the head). Origin: from H7139 (קָרַח); KJV: bald (head).

H7143 קָרֵחַ (Qârêach, kaw-ray'-akh): Kareach, an Israelite. Origin: from H7139 (קָרַח); bald; KJV: Careah, Kareah.

H7144 קׇרְחָה (qorchâh, kor-khaw'): baldness. Origin: or קׇרְחָא; (Ezekiel 27:31), from H7139 (קָרַח); KJV: bald(-ness), [idiom] utterly.

H7145 קׇרְחִי (Qorchîy, kor-khee'): a Korchite (collectively) or descendants of Korach. Origin: patronymic from H7141 (קֹרַח); KJV: Korahite, Korathite, sons of Kore, Korhite.

H7146 קָרַחַת (qârachath, kaw-rakh'-ath): a bald spot (on the back of the head); figuratively, a threadbare spot (on the back side of the cloth). Origin: from H7139 (קָרַח); KJV: bald head, bare within.

H7147 קְרִי (qᵉrîy, ker-ee'): hostile encounter. Origin: from H7136 (קָרָה); KJV: contrary.

H7148 קָרִיא (qârîyʼ, kaw-ree'): called, i.e. select. Origin: from H7121 (קָרָא); KJV: famous, renowned.

H7149 קִרְיָא (qiryâʼ, keer-yaw'): {building; a city}. Origin: (Aramaic) or קִרְיָה; (Aramaic), corresponding to H7151 (קִרְיָה) KJV: city.

H7150 קְרִיאָה (qᵉrîyʼâh, ker-ee-aw'): a proclamation. Origin: from H7121 (קָרָא); KJV: preaching.

H7151 קִרְיָה (qiryâh, kir-yaw'): building; a city. Origin: from H7136 (קָרָה) in the sense of flooring, i.e. KJV: city.

H7152 קְרִיּוֹת (Qᵉrîyôwth, ker-ee-yoth'): Kerioth, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: plural of H7151 (קִרְיָה); buildings; KJV: Kerioth, Kirioth.

H7153 קִרְיַת אַרְבַּע (Qiryath ʼArbaʻ, keer-yath' ar-bah'): Kirjath-Arba or Kirjath-ha-Arba, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (with the article interposed) קִרְיַת הָאַרְבַּע; (Nehemiah 11:25), from H7151 (קִרְיָה) and H704 (אַרְבַּע) or H702 (אַרְבַּע); city of Arba, or city of the four (giants); KJV: Kirjath-arba.

H7154 קִרְיַת בַּעַל (Qiryath Baʻal, keer-yath' bah'-al): Kirjath-Baal, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7151 (קִרְיָה) and H1168 (בַּעַל); city of Baal; KJV: Kirjathbaal.

H7155 קִרְיַת חֻצוֹת (Qiryath Chutsôwth, keer-yath' khoo-tsoth'): Kirjath-Chutsoth, a place in Moab. Origin: from H7151 (קִרְיָה) and the feminine plural of H2351 (חוּץ); city of streets; KJV: Kirjath-huzoth.

H7156 קִרְיָתַיִם (Qiryâthayim, keer-yaw-thah'-yim): Kirjathaim, the name of two placed in Palestine. Origin: dual of H7151 (קִרְיָה); double city; KJV: Kiriathaim, Kirjathaim.

H7157 קִרְיַת יְעָרִים (Qiryath Yᵉʻârîym, keer-yath' yeh-aw-reem'): Kirjath-Jearim or Kirjath-Arim, a place in Palestine. Origin: or (Jeremiah 26:20) with the article interposed; or (Joshua 18:28) simply the former part of the word; or קִרְיַת עָרִים; from H7151 (קִרְיָה) and the plural of H3293 (יַעַר) or H5892 (עִיר); city of forests, or city of towns; KJV: Kirjath, Kirjath-jearim, Kirjath-arim.

H7158 קִרְיַת סַנָּה (Qiryath Çannâh, keer-yath' san-naw'): Kirjath-Sannah or Kirjath-Sepher, a place in Palestine. Origin: or קִרְיַת סֵפֶר; from H7151 (קִרְיָה) and a simpler feminine from the same as H5577 (סַנְסִן), or (for the latter name) H5612 (סֵפֶר); city of branches, or of a book; KJV: Kirjath-sannah, Kirjath-sepher.

H7159 קָרַם (qâram, kaw-ram'): to cover. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cover.

H7160 קָרַן (qâran, kaw-ran'): to shoot out horns; figuratively, rays. Origin: a primitive root; to push or gore; used only as denominative from H7161 (קֶרֶן), KJV: have horns, shine.

H7161 קֶרֶן (qeren, keh'-ren): a horn (as projecting); by implication, a flask, cornet; by resemblance. an elephant's tooth (i.e. ivory), a corner (of the altar), a peak (of a mountain), a ray (of light); figuratively, power. Origin: from H7160 (קָרַן); KJV: [idiom] hill, horn.

H7162 קֶרֶן (qeren, keh'-ren): a horn (literally or for sound). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7161 (קֶרֶן); KJV: horn, cornet.

H7163 קֶרֶן הַפּוּךְ (qeren hap-pûwk, keh'-ren hap-pook'): Keren-hap-Puk, one of Job's daughters. Origin: from H7161 (קֶרֶן) and H6320 (פּוּךְ); horn of cosmetic; KJV: Keren-happuch.

H7164 קָרַס (qâraç, kaw-ras'): to hunch, i.e. be hump-backed. Origin: a primitive root; properly, to protrude; used only as denominative from H7165 (קֶרֶס) (for alliteration with H7167 (קָרַע)), KJV: stoop.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H7165 to H7281
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H7165 קֶרֶס (qereç, keh'-res): a knob or belaying-pin (from its swelling form). Origin: from H7164 (קָרַס); KJV: tache.

H7166 קַרְסֹל (qarçôl, kar-sole'): an ankle (as a protuberance or joint). Origin: from H7164 (קָרַס); KJV: foot.

H7167 קָרַע (qâraʻ, kaw-rah'): to rend, literally or figuratively (revile, paint the eyes, as if enlarging them). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut out, rend, [idiom] surely, tear.

H7168 קֶרַע (qeraʻ, keh'-rah): a rag. Origin: from H7167 (קָרַע); KJV: piece, rag.

H7169 קָרַץ (qârats, kaw-rats'): to pinch, i.e. (partially) to bite the lips, blink the eyes (as a gesture of malice), or (fully) to squeeze off (a piece of clay in order to mould a vessel from it). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: form, move, wink.

H7170 קְרַץ (qᵉrats, ker-ats'): chew him up (figuratively) by slander. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7171 (קֶרֶץ) in the sense of a bit (to 'eat the morsels of' any one, i.e. KJV: [phrase] accuse.

H7171 קֶרֶץ (qerets, keh'-rets): extirpation (as if by constriction). Origin: from H7169 (קָרַץ); KJV: destruction.

H7172 קַרְקַע (qarqaʻ, kar-kah'): floor (as if a pavement of pieces or tesseroe), of abuilding or the sea. Origin: from H7167 (קָרַע); KJV: bottom, ([idiom] one side of the) floor.

H7173 קַרְקַע (Qarqaʻ, kar-kah'): Karka (with the article prefix), a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H7172 (קַרְקַע); ground-floor; KJV: Karkaa.

H7174 קַרְקֹר (Qarqôr, kar-kore'): Karkor, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: from H6979 (קוּר); foundation; KJV: Karkor.

H7277 רִגְמָה (rigmâh, rig-maw'): a pile (of stones), i.e. (figuratively) a throng. Origin: feminine of the same as H7276 (רֶגֶם); KJV: council.

H7278 רֶגֶם מֶלֶךְ (Regem Melek, reh'-gem meh'-lek): Regem-Melek, an Israelite. Origin: from H7276 (רֶגֶם) and H4428 (מֶלֶךְ); king's heap; KJV: Regem-melech.

H7279 רָגַן (râgan, raw-gan'): to grumble, i.e. rebel. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: murmur.

H7280 רָגַע (râgaʻ, raw-gah'): properly, to toss violently and suddenly (the sea with waves, the skin with boils); figuratively (in a favorable manner) to settle, i.e. quiet; specifically, to wink (from the motion of the eye-lids). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break, divide, find ease, be a moment, (cause, give, make to) rest, make suddenly.

H7281 רֶגַע (regaʻ, reh'-gah): a wink (of the eyes), i.e. a very short space of time. Origin: from H7280 (רָגַע). KJV: instant, moment, space, suddenly.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H7282 to H7413
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H7282 רָגֵעַ (râgêaʻ, raw-gay'-ah): restful, i.e. peaceable. Origin: from H7280 (רָגַע); KJV: that are quiet.

H7283 רָגַשׁ (râgash, raw-gash'): to be tumultuous. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: rage.

H7284 רְגַשׁ (rᵉgash, reg-ash'): to gather tumultuously. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7283 (רָגַשׁ); KJV: assemble (together).

H7285 רֶגֶשׁ (regesh, reh'-ghesh): a tumultuous crowd. Origin: or (feminine) רִגְשָׁה; from H7283 (רָגַשׁ); KJV: company, insurrection.

H7286 רָדַד (râdad, raw-dad'): to tread in pieces, i.e. (figuratively) to conquer, or (specifically) to overlay. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: spend, spread, subdue.

H7287 רָדָה (râdâh, raw-daw'): to tread down, i.e. subjugate; specifically, to crumble off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (come to, make to) have dominion, prevail against, reign, (bear, make to) rule,(-r, over), take.

H7288 רַדַּי (Radday, rad-dah'-ee): Raddai, an Israelite. Origin: intensive from H7287 (רָדָה); domineering; KJV: Raddai.

H7289 רָדִיד (râdîyd, raw-deed'): a veil (as expanded). Origin: from H7286 (רָדַד) in the sense of spreading; KJV: vail, veil.

H7290 רָדַם (râdam, raw-dam'): to stun, i.e. stupefy (with sleep or death). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be fast a-, be in a deep, cast into a dead, that) sleep(-er, -eth).

H7291 רָדַף (râdaph, raw-daf'): to run after (usually with hostile intent; figuratively (of time) gone by). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: chase, put to flight, follow (after, on), hunt, (be under) persecute(-ion, -or), pursue(-r).

H7292 רָהַב (râhab, raw-hab'): to urge severely, i.e. (figuratively) importune, embolden, capture, act insolently. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: overcome, behave self proudly, make sure, strengthen.

H7293 רַהַב (rahab, rah'-hab): bluster(-er). Origin: from H7292 (רָהַב), KJV: proud, strength.

H7294 רַהַב (Rahab, rah'-hab): Rahab (i.e. boaster), an epithet of Egypt. Origin: the same as H7293 (רַהַב); KJV: Rahab.

H7295 רָהָב (râhâb, raw-hawb'): insolent. Origin: from H7292 (רָהַב); KJV: proud.

H7296 רֹהָב (rôhâb, ro'-hab): pride. Origin: from H7292 (רָהַב); KJV: strength.

H7297 רָהָה (râhâh, raw-haw'): to fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be afraid.

H7298 רַהַט (rahaṭ, rah'-hat): a channel or watering-box; by resemblance a ringlet of hair (as forming parallel lines). Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to hollow out; KJV: gallery, gutter, trough.

H7299 רֵו (rêv, rave): aspect. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H7200 (רָאָה); KJV: form.

H7300 רוּד (rûwd, rood): to tramp about, i.e. ramble (free or disconsolate). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have the dominion, be lord, mourn, rule.

H7301 רָוָה (râvâh, raw-vaw'): to slake the thirst (occasionally of other appetites). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bathe, make drunk, (take the) fill, satiate, (abundantly) satisfy, soak, water (abundantly).

H7302 רָוֶה (râveh, raw-veh'): sated (with drink). Origin: from H7301 (רָוָה); KJV: drunkenness, watered.

H7303 רוֹהֲגָה (Rôwhăgâh, ro-hag-aw'): Rohagah, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root probably meaning to cry out; outcry; KJV: Rohgah.

H7304 רָוַח (râvach, raw-vakh'): properly, to breathe freely, i.e. revive; by implication, to have ample room. Origin: a primitive root (identical with H7306 (רוּחַ)); KJV: be refreshed, large.

H7305 רֶוַח (revach, reh'-vakh): room, literally (an interval) or figuratively (deliverance). Origin: from H7304 (רָוַח); KJV: enlargement, space.

H7306 רוּחַ (rûwach, roo'-akh): properly, to blow, i.e. breathe; only (literally) to smell or (by implication, perceive (figuratively, to anticipate, enjoy). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: accept, smell, [idiom] touch, make of quick understanding.

H7307 רוּחַ (rûwach, roo'-akh): wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension, a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit, but only of a rational being (including its expression and functions). Origin: from H7306 (רוּחַ); KJV: air, anger, blast, breath, [idiom] cool, courage, mind, [idiom] quarter, [idiom] side, spirit(-ual), tempest, [idiom] vain, (whirl-) wind(-y).

H7308 רוּחַ (rûwach, roo'-akh): {wind; by resemblance breath, i.e. a sensible (or even violent) exhalation; figuratively, life, anger, unsubstantiality; by extension, a region of the sky; by resemblance spirit, but only of a rational being (including its expression and functions)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7307 (רוּחַ) KJV: mind, spirit, wind.

H7309 רְוָחָה (rᵉvâchâh, rev-aw-khaw'): relief. Origin: feminine of H7305 (רֶוַח); KJV: breathing, respite.

H7310 רְוָיָה (rᵉvâyâh, rev-aw-yaw'): satisfaction. Origin: from H7301 (רָוָה); KJV: runneth over, wealthy.

H7311 רוּם (rûwm, room): to be high actively, to rise or raise (in various applications, literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring up, exalt (self), extol, give, go up, haughty, heave (up), (be, lift up on, make on, set up on, too) high(-er, one), hold up, levy, lift(-er) up, (be) lofty, ([idiom] a-) loud, mount up, offer (up), [phrase] presumptuously, (be) promote(-ion), proud, set up, tall(-er), take (away, off, up), breed worms.

H7312 רוּם (rûwm, room): (literally) elevation or (figuratively) elation. Origin: or רֻם; from H7311 (רוּם); KJV: haughtiness, height, [idiom] high.

H7313 רוּם (rûwm, room): {to be high actively, to rise or raise (in various applications, literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7311 (רוּם); KJV: extol, lift up (self), set up.

H7314 רוּם (rûwm, room): (literally) altitude. Origin: (Aramaic) from H7313 (רוּם); KJV: height.

H7315 רוֹם (rôwm, rome): elevation, i.e. (adverbially) aloft. Origin: from H7311 (רוּם); KJV: on high.

H7316 רוּמָה (Rûwmâh, roo-maw'): Rumah, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7311 (רוּם); height; KJV: Rumah.

H7317 רוֹמָה (rôwmâh, ro-maw'): elation, i.e. (adverbially) proudly. Origin: feminine of H7315 (רוֹם); KJV: haughtily.

H7318 רוֹמָם (rôwmâm, ro-mawm'): exaltation, i.e. (figuratively and specifically) praise. Origin: from H7426 (רָמַם); KJV: be extolled.

H7319 רוֹמְמָה (rôwmᵉmâh, ro-mem-aw'): exaltation, i.e. praise. Origin: feminine active participle of H7426 (רָמַם); KJV: high.

H7320 רוֹמַמְתִּי עֶזֶר (Rôwmamtîy ʻEzer, ro-mam'-tee eh'-zer): Romamti-Ezer, an Israelite. Origin: (or Romam from H7311 (רוּם) and H5828 (עֵזֶר); I have raised up a help; KJV: Romamti-ezer.

H7321 רוּעַ (rûwaʻ, roo-ah'): to mar (especially by breaking); figuratively, to split the ears (with sound), i.e. shout (for alarm or joy). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: blow an alarm, cry (alarm, aloud, out), destroy, make a joyful noise, smart, shout (for joy), sound an alarm, triumph.

H7322 רוּף (rûwph, roof): properly, to triturate (in a mortar), i.e. (figuratively) to agitate (by concussion). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tremble.

H7323 רוּץ (rûwts, roots): to run (for whatever reason, especially to rush). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: break down, divide speedily, footman, guard, bring hastily, (make) run (away, through), post.

H7324 רוּק (rûwq, rook): to pour out (literally or figuratively), i.e. empty. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] arm, cast out, draw (out), (make) empty, pour forth (out).

H7325 רוּר (rûwr, roor): to slaver (with spittle), i.e. (by analogy) to emit afluid (ulcerous or natural). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: run.

H7326 רוּשׁ (rûwsh, roosh): to be destitute. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lack, needy, (make self) poor (man).

H7327 רוּת (Rûwth, rooth): Ruth, a Moabitess. Origin: probably for H7468 (רְעוּת); friend; KJV: Ruth.

H7328 רָז (râz, rawz): to attenuate, i.e. (figuratively) hide; a mystery. Origin: (Aramaic) from an unused root probably meaning KJV: secret.

H7329 רָזָה (râzâh, raw-zaw'): to emaciate, i.e. make (become) thin (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: famish, wax lean.

H7330 רָזֶה (râzeh, raw-zeh'): thin. Origin: from H7329 (רָזָה); KJV: lean.

H7331 רְזוֹן (Rᵉzôwn, rez-one'): Rezon, a Syrian. Origin: from H7336 (רָזַן); prince; KJV: Rezon.

H7332 רָזוֹן (râzôwn, raw-zone'): thinness. Origin: from H7329 (רָזָה); KJV: leanness, [idiom] scant.

H7333 רָזוֹן (râzôwn, raw-zone'): a dignitary. Origin: from H7336 (רָזַן); KJV: prince.

H7334 רָזִי (râzîy, raw-zee'): thinness. Origin: from H7329 (רָזָה); KJV: leanness.

H7335 רָזַם (râzam, raw-zam'): to twinkle the eye (in mockery). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wink.

H7336 רָזַן (râzan, raw-zan'): probably to be heavy, i.e. (figuratively) honorable. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: prince, ruler.

H7337 רָחַב (râchab, raw-khab'): to broaden (intransitive or transitive, literal or figurative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be an en-(make) large(-ing), make room, make (open) wide.

H7338 רַחַב (rachab, rakh'-ab): a width. Origin: from H7337 (רָחַב); KJV: breadth, broad place.

H7339 רְחֹב (rᵉchôb, rekh-obe'): a width, i.e. (concretely) avenue or area. Origin: or רְחוֹב; from H7337 (רָחַב); KJV: broad place (way), street. See also H1050 (בֵּית רְחוֹב).

H7340 רְחֹב (Rᵉchôb, rekh-obe'): Rechob, the name of a place in Syria, also of a Syrian and an Israelite. Origin: or רְחוֹב; the same as H7339 (רְחֹב); KJV: Rehob.

H7341 רֹחַב (rôchab, ro'-khab): width (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H7337 (רָחַב); KJV: breadth, broad, largeness, thickness, wideness.

H7342 רָחָב (râchâb, raw-khawb'): roomy, in any (or every) direction, literally or figuratively. Origin: from H7337 (רָחַב); KJV: broad, large, at liberty, proud, wide.

H7343 רָחָב (Râchâb, raw-khawb'): Rachab, a Canaanitess. Origin: the same as H7342 (רָחָב); proud; KJV: Rahab.

H7344 רְחֹבוֹת (Rᵉchôbôwth, rekh-o-both'): Rechoboth, a place in Assyria and one in Palestine. Origin: or רְחֹבֹת; plural of H7339 (רְחֹב); streets; KJV: Rehoboth.

H7345 רְחַבְיָה (Rᵉchabyâh, rekh-ab-yaw'): Rechabjah, an Israelite. Origin: or רְחַבְיָהוּ; from H7337 (רָחַב) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has enlarged; KJV: Rehabiah.

H7346 רְחַבְעָם (Rᵉchabʻâm, rekh-ab-awm'): Rechabam, an Israelite king. Origin: from H7337 (רָחַב) and H5971 (עַם); a people has enlarged; KJV: Rehoboam.

H7347 רֵחֶה (rêcheh, ray-kheh'): a mill-stone. Origin: from an unused root meaning to pulverize; KJV: mill (stone).

H7348 רְחוּם (Rᵉchûwm, rekh-oom'): Rechum, the name of a Persian and of three Israelites. Origin: a form of H7349 (רַחוּם); KJV: Rehum.

H7349 רַחוּם (rachûwm, rakh-oom'): compassionate. Origin: from H7355 (רָחַם); KJV: full of compassion, merciful.

H7350 רָחוֹק (râchôwq, raw-khoke'): remote, literally or figuratively, of place or time; specifically, precious; often used adverbially (with preposition). Origin: or רָחֹק; from H7368 (רָחַק); KJV: (a-) far (abroad, off), long ago, of old, space, great while to come.

H7351 רְחִיט (rᵉchîyṭ, rekh-eet'): a panel (as resembling a trough). Origin: from the same as H7298 (רַהַט); KJV: rafter.

H7352 רַחִיק (rachîyq, rakh-eek'): {remote, literally or figuratively, of place or time; specifically, precious; often used adverbially (with preposition)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7350 (רָחוֹק) KJV: far.

H7353 רָחֵל (râchêl, raw-kale'): a ewe (the females being the predominant element of a flock) (as a good traveller). Origin: from an unused root meaning to journey; KJV: ewe, sheep.

H7354 רָחֵל (Râchêl, raw-khale'): Rachel, a wife of Jacob. Origin: the same as H7353 (רָחֵל); KJV: Rachel.

H7355 רָחַם (râcham, raw-kham'): to fondle; by implication, to love, especially to compassionate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have compassion (on, upon), love, (find, have, obtain, shew) mercy(-iful, on, upon), (have) pity, Ruhamah, [idiom] surely.

H7356 רַחַם (racham, rakh'-am): compassion (in the plural); by extension, the womb (as cherishing the fetus); by implication, a maiden. Origin: from H7355 (רָחַם); KJV: bowels, compassion, damsel, tender love, (great, tender) mercy, pity, womb.

H7357 רַחַם (Racham, rakh'-am): Racham, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H7356 (רַחַם); pity; KJV: Raham.

H7358 רֶחֶם (rechem, rekh'-em): the womb. Origin: from H7355 (רָחַם); (compare H7356 (רַחַם)) KJV: matrix, womb.

H7359 רְחֵם (rᵉchêm, rekh-ame'): (plural) pity. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7356 (רַחַם); KJV: mercy.

H7360 רָחָם (râchâm, raw-khawm'): a kind of vulture (supposed to be tender towards its young). Origin: or (feminine) רָחָמָה; from H7355 (רָחַם); KJV: gier-eagle.

H7361 רַחֲמָה (rachămâh, rakh-am-aw'): a maiden. Origin: feminine of H7356 (רַחַם); KJV: damsel.

H7362 רַחְמָנִי (rachmânîy, rakh-maw-nee'): compassionate. Origin: from H7355 (רָחַם); KJV: pitiful.

H7363 רָחַף (râchaph, raw-khaf'): to brood; by implication, to be relaxed. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: flutter, move, shake.

H7364 רָחַץ (râchats, raw-khats'): to lave (the whole or a part of a thing). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bathe (self), wash (self).

H7365 רְחַץ (rᵉchats, rekh-ats'): to attend upon. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7364 (רָחַץ) (probably through the accessory idea of ministering as a servant at the bath); KJV: trust.

H7366 רַחַץ (rachats, rakh'-ats): a bath. Origin: from H7364 (רָחַץ); KJV: wash(-pot).

H7367 רַחְצָה (rachtsâh, rakh-tsaw'): a bathing place. Origin: feminine of H7366 (רַחַץ); KJV: washing.

H7368 רָחַק (râchaq, raw-khak'): to widen (in any direction), i.e. (intransitively) recede or (transitively) remove (literally or figuratively, of place or relation). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (a-, be, cast, drive, get, go, keep (self), put, remove, be too, (wander), withdraw) far (away, off), loose, [idiom] refrain, very, (be) a good way (off).

H7369 רָחֵק (râchêq, raw-khake'): remote. Origin: from H7368 (רָחַק); KJV: that are far.

H7370 רָחַשׁ (râchash, raw-khash'): to gush. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: indite.

H7371 רַחַת (rachath, rakh'-ath): a winnowing-fork (as blowing the chaff away). Origin: from H7306 (רוּחַ); KJV: shovel.

H7372 רָטַב (râṭab, raw-tab'): to be moist. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be wet.

H7373 רָטֹב (râṭôb, raw-tobe'): moist (with sap). Origin: from H7372 (רָטַב); KJV: green.

H7374 רֶטֶט (reṭeṭ, reh'-tet): terror. Origin: from an unused root meaning to tremble; KJV: fear.

H7375 רֻטֲפַשׁ (ruṭăphash, roo-taf-ash'): to be rejuvenated. Origin: a root compounded from H7373 (רָטֹב) and H2954 (טָפַשׁ); KJV: be fresh.

H7376 רָטָשׁ (râṭâsh, raw-tash'): to dash down. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dash (in pieces).

H7377 רִי (rîy, ree): irrigation, i.e. a shower. Origin: from H7301 (רָוָה); KJV: watering.

H7378 רִיב (rîyb, reeb): properly, to toss, i.e. grapple; mostly figuratively, to wrangle, i.e. hold a controversy; (by implication) to defend. Origin: or רוּב; a primitive root; KJV: adversary, chide, complain, contend, debate, [idiom] ever, [idiom] lay wait, plead, rebuke, strive, [idiom] thoroughly.

H7379 רִיב (rîyb, reeb): a contest (personal or legal). Origin: or רִב; from H7378 (רִיב); KJV: [phrase] adversary, cause, chiding, contend(-tion), controversy, multitude (from the margin), pleading, strife, strive(-ing), suit.

H7380 רִיבַי (Rîybay, ree-bah'-ee): Ribai, an Israelite. Origin: from H7378 (רִיב); contentious; KJV: Ribai.

H7381 רֵיחַ (rêyach, ray'-akh): odor (as if blown). Origin: from H7306 (רוּחַ); KJV: savour, scent, smell.

H7382 רֵיחַ (rêyach, ray'-akh): {odor (as if blown)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7381 (רֵיחַ) KJV: smell.

H7383 רִיפָה (rîyphâh, ree-faw'): (only plural), grits (as pounded). Origin: or רִפָה; from H7322 (רוּף); KJV: ground corn, wheat.

H7384 רִיפַת (Rîyphath, ree-fath'): Riphath, a grandson of Japheth and his descendants. Origin: or (probably by orthographical error) דִּיפַת; of foreign origin; KJV: Riphath.

H7385 רִיק (rîyq, reek): emptiness; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain. Origin: from H7324 (רוּק); KJV: empty, to no purpose, (in) vain (thing), vanity.

H7386 רֵיק (rêyq, rake): empty; figuratively, worthless. Origin: or (shorter) רֵק; from H7324 (רוּק); KJV: emptied(-ty), vain (fellow, man).

H7387 רֵיקָם (rêyqâm, ray-kawm'): emptily; figuratively (objective) ineffectually, (subjective) undeservedly. Origin: from H7386 (רֵיק); KJV: without cause, empty, in vain, void.

H7388 רִיר (rîyr, reer): saliva; by resemblance, broth. Origin: from H7325 (רוּר); KJV: spittle, white (of an egg).

H7389 רֵישׁ (rêysh, raysh): poverty. Origin: or רֵאשׁ; or רִישׁ; from H7326 (רוּשׁ); KJV: poverty.

H7390 רַךְ (rak, rak): tender (literally or figuratively); by implication, weak. Origin: from H7401 (רָכַךְ); KJV: faint((-hearted), soft, tender ((-hearted), one), weak.

H7391 רֹךְ (rôk, roke): softness (figuratively). Origin: from H7401 (רָכַךְ); KJV: tenderness.

H7392 רָכַב (râkab, raw-kab'): to ride (on an animal or in a vehicle); causatively, to place upon (for riding or generally), to despatch. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring (on (horse-) back), carry, get (oneself) up, on (horse-) back, put, (cause to, make to) ride (in a chariot, on, -r), set.

H7393 רֶכֶב (rekeb, reh'-keb): a vehicle; by implication, a team; by extension, cavalry; by analogy a rider, i.e. the upper millstone. Origin: from H7392 (רָכַב); KJV: chariot, (upper) millstone, multitude (from the margin), wagon.

H7394 רֵכָב (Rêkâb, ray-kawb'): Rekab, the name of two Arabs and of two Israelites. Origin: from H7392 (רָכַב); rider; KJV: Rechab.

H7395 רַכָּב (rakkâb, rak-kawb'): a charioteer. Origin: from H7392 (רָכַב); KJV: chariot man, driver of a chariot, horseman.

H7396 רִכְבָּה (rikbâh, rik-baw'): a chariot (collectively). Origin: feminine of H7393 (רֶכֶב); KJV: chariots.

H7397 רֵכָה (Rêkâh, ray-kaw'): Rekah, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably feminine from H7401 (רָכַךְ); softness; KJV: Rechah.

H7398 רְכוּב (rᵉkûwb, rek-oob'): a vehicle (as ridden on). Origin: from passive participle of H7392 (רָכַב); KJV: chariot.

H7399 רְכוּשׁ (rᵉkûwsh, rek-oosh'): property (as gathered). Origin: or רְכֻשׁ; from passive participle of H7408 (רָכַשׁ); KJV: good, riches, substance.

H7400 רָכִיל (râkîyl, raw-keel'): a scandal-monger (as travelling about). Origin: from H7402 (רָכַל) KJV: slander, carry tales, talebearer.

H7401 רָכַךְ (râkak, raw-kak'): to soften (intransitively or transitively), used figuratively. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (be) faint(-hearted), mollify, (be, make) soft(-er), be tender.

H7402 רָכַל (râkal, raw-kal'): to travel for trading. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (spice) merchant.

H7403 רָכָל (Râkâl, raw-kawl'): Rakal, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7402 (רָכַל); merchant; KJV: Rachal.

H7404 רְכֻלָּה (rᵉkullâh, rek-ool-law'): trade (as peddled). Origin: feminine passive participle of H7402 (רָכַל); KJV: merchandise, traffic.

H7405 רָכַס (râkaç, raw-kas'): to tie. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind.

H7406 רֶכֶס (rekeç, reh'-kes): a mountain ridge (as of tied summits). Origin: from H7405 (רָכַס); KJV: rough place.

H7407 רֹכֶס (rôkeç, ro'-kes): a snare (as of tied meshes). Origin: from H7405 (רָכַס); KJV: pride.

H7408 רָכַשׁ (râkash, raw-kash'): to lay up, i.e. collect. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gather, get.

H7409 רֶכֶשׁ (rekesh, reh'-kesh): a relay of animals on a post-route (as stored up for that purpose); by implication, a courser. Origin: from H7408 (רָכַשׁ); KJV: dromedary, mule, swift beast.

H7410 רָם (Râm, rawm): Ram, the name of an Arabian and of an Israelite. Origin: active participle of H7311 (רוּם); high; KJV: Ram. See also H1027 (בֵּית הָרָם).

H7411 רָמָה (râmâh, raw-maw'): to hurl; specifically, to shoot; figuratively, to delude or betray (as if causing to fall). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beguile, betray, (bow-) man, carry, deceive, throw.

H7412 רְמָה (rᵉmâh, rem-aw'): to throw, set, (figuratively) assess. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7411 (רָמָה); KJV: cast (down), impose.

H7413 רָמָה (râmâh, raw-maw'): a height (as a seat of idolatry). Origin: feminine active participle of H7311 (רוּם); KJV: high place.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H7414 to H7540
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H7414 רָמָה (Râmâh, raw-maw'): Ramah, the name of four places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H7413 (רָמָה); KJV: Ramah.

H7415 רִמָּה (rimmâh, rim-maw'): a maggot (as rapidly bred), literally or figuratively. Origin: from H7426 (רָמַם) in the sense of breeding (compare H7311 (רוּם)); KJV: worm.

H7416 רִמּוֹן (rimmôwn, rim-mone'): a pomegranate, the tree (from its upright growth) or the fruit (also an artificial ornament). Origin: or רִמֹּן; from H7426 (רָמַם); KJV: pomegranate.

H7417 רִמּוֹן (Rimmôwn, rim-mone'): Rimmon, the name of a Syrian deity, also of five places in Palestine. Origin: or (shorter) (רִמֹּן; or רִמּוֹנוֹ; (1 Chronicles 6:62 (H77 (אֶבֶץ))), the same as H7416 (רִמּוֹן); in Joshua 19:13: הַמְּתֹאָר is mistaken for part of a name; article with the passive participle of H8388 (תָּאַר); the (one) marked off, i.e. which pertains). KJV: Remmon, Rimmon.

H7418 רָמוֹת (Râmôwth, raw-moth): Ramoth-Negeb or Ramath-Negeb, a place in Palestine. Origin: or רָמַת נֶגֶב; from the plural or construct form of H7413 (רָמָה) and H5045 (נֶגֶב); heights (or height) of the South; KJV: south Ramoth, Ramath of the south.

H7419 רָמוּת (râmûwth, raw-mooth'): a heap (of carcases). Origin: from H7311 (רוּם); KJV: height.

H7420 רֹמַח (rômach, ro'-makh): a lance (as thrown); especially the iron point. Origin: from an unused root meaning to hurl; KJV: buckler, javelin, lancet, spear.

H7421 רַמִּי (rammîy, ram-mee'): a Ramite, i.e. Aramaean. Origin: for H761 (אֲרַמִּי); KJV: Syrian.

H7422 רַמְיָה (Ramyâh, ram-yaw'): Ramjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H7311 (רוּם) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has raised; KJV: Ramiah.

H7423 רְמִיָּה (rᵉmîyâh, rem-ee-yaw'): remissness, treachery. Origin: from H7411 (רָמָה); KJV: deceit(-ful, -fully), false, guile, idle, slack, slothful.

H7424 רַמָּךְ (rammâk, ram-mawk'): a brood mare. Origin: of foreign origin; KJV: dromedary.

H7425 רְמַלְיָהוּ (Rᵉmalyâhûw, rem-al-yaw'-hoo): Remaljah, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root and H3050 (יָהּ) (perhaps meaning to deck); Jah has bedecked; KJV: Remaliah.

H7426 רָמַם (râmam, raw-mam'): to rise (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: exalt, get (oneself) up, lift up (self), mount up.

H7427 רֹמֵמֻת (rômêmuth, ro-may-mooth'): exaltation. Origin: from the active participle of H7426 (רָמַם); KJV: lifting up of self.

H7428 רִמֹּן פֶּרֶץ (Rimmôn Perets, rim-mone' peh'-rets): Rimmon-Perets, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H7416 (רִמּוֹן) and H6556 (פֶּרֶץ); pomegranate of the breach; KJV: Rimmon-parez.

H7429 רָמַס (râmaç, raw-mas'): to tread upon (as a potter, in walking or abusively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: oppressor, stamp upon, trample (under feet), tread (down, upon).

H7430 רָמַשׂ (râmas, raw-mas'): properly, to glide swiftly, i.e. to crawl or move with short steps; by analogy to swarm. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: creep, move.

H7431 רֶמֶשׂ (remes, reh'-mes): a reptile or any other rapidly moving animal. Origin: from H7430 (רָמַשׂ); KJV: that creepeth, creeping (moving) thing.

H7432 רֶמֶת (Remeth, reh'-meth): Remeth, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7411 (רָמָה); height; KJV: Remeth.

H7433 רָמֹת גִּלעָד (Râmôth Gilʻâd, raw-moth' gil-awd'): Ramoth-Gilad, a place East of the Jordan. Origin: or רָמוֹת גִּלעָד; (2 Chronicles 22:5), from the plural of H7413 (רָמָה) and H1568 (גִּלְעָד); heights of Gilad; KJV: Ramoth-gilead, Ramoth in Gilead. See also H7216 (רָאמוֹת).

H7434 רָמַת הַמִּצְפֶּה (Râmath ham-Mit-speh, raw-math' ham-mitspeh'): Ramath-ham-Mitspeh, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7413 (רָמָה) and H4707 (מִצְפֶּה) with the article interpolated; height of the watch-tower; KJV: Ramath-mizpeh.

H7435 רָמָתִי (Râmâthîy, raw-maw-thee'): a Ramathite or inhabitant of Ramah. Origin: patronymic of H7414 (רָמָה); KJV: Ramathite.

H7436 רָמָתַיִם צוֹפִים (Râmâthayim Tsôwphîym, raw-maw-thah'-yim tso-feem'): Ramathajim-Tsophim, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the dual of H7413 (רָמָה) and the plural of the active participle of H6822 (צָפָה); double height of watchers; KJV: Ramathaimzophim.

H7437 רָמַת לֶחִי (Râmath Lechîy, raw'-math lekh'-ee): Ramath-Lechi, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H7413 (רָמָה) and H3895 (לְחִי); height of a jaw-bone; KJV: Ramath-lehi.

H7438 רֹן (rôn, rone): a shout (of deliverance). Origin: from H7442 (רָנַן); KJV: song.

H7439 רָנָה (rânâh, raw-naw'): to whiz. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: rattle.

H7440 רִנָּה (rinnâh, rin-naw'): properly, a creaking (or shrill sound), i.e. shout (of joy or grief). Origin: from H7442 (רָנַן); KJV: cry, gladness, joy, proclamation, rejoicing, shouting, sing(-ing), triumph.

H7441 רִנָּה (Rinnâh, rin-naw'): Rinnah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H7440 (רִנָּה); KJV: Rinnah.

H7442 רָנַן (rânan, raw-nan'): properly, to creak (or emit a stridulous sound), i.e. to shout (usually for joy). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: aloud for joy, cry out, be joyful (greatly, make to) rejoice, (cause to) shout (for joy), (cause to) sing (aloud, for joy, out), triumph.

H7443 רֶנֶן (renen, reh'-nen): an ostrich (from its wail). Origin: from H7442 (רָנַן); KJV: [idiom] goodly.

H7444 רַנֵּן (rannên, ran-nane'): shouting (for joy). Origin: intensive from H7442 (רָנַן); KJV: singing.

H7445 רְנָנָה (rᵉnânâh, ren-aw-naw'): a shout (for joy). Origin: from H7442 (רָנַן); KJV: joyful (voice), singing, triumphing.

H7446 רִסָּה (Riççâh, ris-saw'): Rissah, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H7450 (רָסַס); a ruin (as dripping to pieces); KJV: Rissah.

H7447 רָסִיס (râçîyç, raw-sees'): properly, dripping to pieces, i.e. a ruin; also a dew-drop. Origin: from H7450 (רָסַס); KJV: breach, drop.

H7448 רֶסֶן (reçen, reh'-sen): a halter (as restraining); by implication, the jaw. Origin: from an unused root meaning to curb; KJV: bridle.

H7449 רֶסֶן (Reçen, reh'-sen): Resen, a place in Assyrian. Origin: the same as H7448 (רֶסֶן); KJV: Resen.

H7450 רָסַס (râçaç, raw-sas'): to moisten (with drops). Origin: a primitive root; to comminute; used only as denominative from H7447 (רָסִיס), KJV: temper.

H7451 רַע (raʻ, rah): bad or (as noun) evil (natural or moral). Origin: from H7489 (רָעַע); KJV: adversity, affliction, bad, calamity, [phrase] displease(-ure), distress, evil((-favouredness), man, thing), [phrase] exceedingly, [idiom] great, grief(-vous), harm, heavy, hurt(-ful), ill (favoured), [phrase] mark, mischief(-vous), misery, naught(-ty), noisome, [phrase] not please, sad(-ly), sore, sorrow, trouble, vex, wicked(-ly, -ness, one), worse(-st), wretchedness, wrong. (Incl. feminine raaah; as adjective or noun.).

H7452 רֵעַ (rêaʻ, ray'-ah): a crash (of thunder), noise (of war), shout (of joy). Origin: from H7321 (רוּעַ); KJV: [idiom] aloud, noise, shouted.

H7453 רֵעַ (rêaʻ, ray'-ah): an associate (more or less close). Origin: or רֵיעַ; from H7462 (רָעָה); KJV: brother, companion, fellow, friend, husband, lover, neighbour, [idiom] (an-) other.

H7454 רֵעַ (rêaʻ, ray'-ah): a thought (as association of ideas). Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה); KJV: thought.

H7455 רֹעַ (rôaʻ, ro'-ah): badness (as marring), physically or morally. Origin: from H7489 (רָעַע); KJV: [idiom] be so bad, badness, ([idiom] be so) evil, naughtiness, sadness, sorrow, wickedness.

H7456 רָעֵב (râʻêb, raw-abe'): to hunger. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (suffer to) famish, (be, have, suffer, suffer to) hunger(-ry).

H7457 רָעֵב (râʻêb, raw-abe'): hungry (more or less intensely). Origin: from H7456 (רָעֵב); KJV: hunger bitten, hungry.

H7458 רָעָב (râʻâb, raw-awb'): hunger (more or less extensive). Origin: from H7456 (רָעֵב); KJV: dearth, famine, [phrase] famished, hunger.

H7459 רְעָבוֹן (rᵉʻâbôwn, reh-aw-bone'): famine. Origin: from H7456 (רָעֵב); KJV: famine.

H7460 רָעַד (râʻad, raw-ad'): to shudder (more or less violently). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: tremble.

H7461 רַעַד (raʻad, rah'-ad): a shudder. Origin: or (feminine) רְעָדָהxlit rᵉâdâh corrected to rᵉʻâdâh; from H7460 (רָעַד); KJV: trembling.

H7462 רָעָה (râʻâh, raw-aw'): to tend a flock; i.e. pasture it; intransitively, to graze (literally or figuratively); generally to rule; by extension, to associate with (as a friend). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] break, companion, keep company with, devour, eat up, evil entreat, feed, use as a friend, make friendship with, herdman, keep (sheep) (-er), pastor, [phrase] shearing house, shepherd, wander, waste.

H7463 רֵעֶה (rêʻeh, ray-eh'): a (male) companion. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה); KJV: friend.

H7464 רֵעָה (rêʻâh, ray'-aw): a female associate. Origin: feminine of H7453 (רֵעַ); KJV: companion, fellow.

H7465 רֹעָה (rôʻâh, ro-aw'): breakage. Origin: for H7455 (רֹעַ); KJV: broken, utterly.

H7466 רְעוּ (Rᵉʻûw, reh-oo'): Reu, a postdiluvian patriarch. Origin: for H7471 (רְעִי) in the sense of H7453 (רֵעַ); friend; KJV: Reu.

H7467 רְעוּאֵל (Rᵉʻûwʼêl, reh-oo-ale'): Reuel, the name of Moses' father-in-law, also of an Edomite and an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H7466 (רְעוּ) and H410 (אֵל); friend of God; KJV: Raguel, Reuel.

H7468 רְעוּת (rᵉʻûwth, reh-ooth'): a female associate; generally an additional one. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה) in the sense of H7453 (רֵעַ); KJV: [phrase] another, mate, neighbour.

H7469 רְעוּת (rᵉʻûwth, reh-ooth'): a feeding upon, i.e. grasping after. Origin: probably from H7462 (רָעָה); KJV: vexation.

H7470 רְעוּת (rᵉʻûwth, reh-ooth'): desire. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7469 (רְעוּת); KJV: pleasure, will.

H7471 רְעִי (rᵉʻîy, reh-ee'): pasture. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה); KJV: pasture.

H7472 רֵעִי (Rêʻîy, ray-ee'): Rei, an Israelite. Origin: from H7453 (רֵעַ); social; KJV: Rei.

H7473 רֹעִי (rôʻîy, ro-ee'): pastoral; as noun, a shepherd. Origin: from active participle of H7462 (רָעָה); KJV: shipherd.

H7474 רַעְיָה (raʻyâh, rah-yaw'): a female associate. Origin: feminine of H7453 (רֵעַ); KJV: fellow, love.

H7475 רַעְיוֹן (raʻyôwn, rah-yone'): desire. Origin: from H7462 (רָעָה) in the sense of H7469 (רְעוּת); KJV: vexation.

H7476 רַעְיוֹן (raʻyôwn, rah-yone'): a grasp. i.e. (figuratively) mental conception. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7475 (רַעְיוֹן); KJV: cogitation, thought.

H7477 רָעַל (râʻal, raw-al'): to reel, i.e. (figuratively) to brandish. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: terribly shake.

H7478 רַעַל (raʻal, rah'-al): a reeling (from intoxication). Origin: from H7477 (רָעַל); KJV: trembling.

H7479 רַעֲלָה (raʻălâh, rah-al-aw'): a long veil (as fluttering). Origin: feminine of H7478 (רַעַל); KJV: muffler.

H7480 רְעֵלָיָה (Rᵉʻêlâyâh, reh-ay-law-yaw'): Reelajah, an Israelite. Origin: from H7477 (רָעַל) and H3050 (יָהּ); made to tremble (i.e. fearful) of Jah; KJV: Reeliah.

H7481 רָעַם (râʻam, raw-am'): to tumble, i.e. be violently agitated; specifically, to crash (of thunder); figuratively, to irritate (with anger). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make to fret, roar, thunder, trouble.

H7482 רַעַם (raʻam, rah'am): a peal of thunder. Origin: from H7481 (רָעַם); KJV: thunder.

H7483 רַעְמָה (raʻmâh, rah-maw'): the mane of a horse (as quivering in the wind). Origin: feminine of H7482 (רַעַם); KJV: thunder.

H7484 רַעְמָה (Raʻmâh, rah-maw'): Ramah, the name of a grandson of Ham, and of a place (perhaps founded by him). Origin: the same as H7483 (רַעְמָה); KJV: Raamah.

H7485 רַעַמְיָה (Raʻamyâh, rah-am-yaw'): Raamjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H7481 (רָעַם) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has shaken; KJV: Raamiah.

H7486 רַעְמְסֵס (Raʻmᵉçêç, rah-mes-ace'): Rameses or Raamses, a place in Egypt. Origin: or רַעַמְסֵס; of Egyptian origin; KJV: Raamses, Rameses.

H7487 רַעֲנַן (raʻănan, rah-aw-nan'): green, i.e. (figuratively) prosperous. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7488 (רַעֲנָן); KJV: flourishing.

H7488 רַעֲנָן (raʻănân, rah-an-awn'): verdant; by analogy, new; figuratively, prosperous. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be green; KJV: green, flourishing.

H7489 רָעַע (râʻaʻ, raw-ah'): properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good fornothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: afflict, associate selves (by mistake for H7462 (רָעָה)), break (down, in pieces), [phrase] displease, (be, bring, do) evil (doer, entreat, man), show self friendly (by mistake for H7462 (רָעָה)), do harm, (do) hurt, (behave self, deal) ill, [idiom] indeed, do mischief, punish, still, vex, (do) wicked (doer, -ly), be (deal, do) worse.

H7490 רְעַע (rᵉʻaʻ, reh-ah'): {properly, to spoil (literally, by breaking to pieces); figuratively, to make (or be) good fornothing, i.e. bad (physically, socially or morally)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7489 (רָעַע) KJV: break, bruise.

H7491 רָעַף (râʻaph, raw-af'): to drip. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: distil, drop (down).

H7492 רָעַץ (râʻats, raw-ats'): to break in pieces; figuratively, harass. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: dash in pieces, vex.

H7493 רָעַשׁ (râʻash, raw-ash): to undulate (as the earth, the sky, etc.; also a field of grain), particularly through fear; specifically, to spring (as a locust). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make afraid, (re-) move, quake, (make to) shake, (make to) tremble.

H7494 רַעַשׁ (raʻash, rah'-ash): vibration, bounding, uproar. Origin: from H7493 (רָעַשׁ); KJV: commotion, confused noise, earthquake, fierceness, quaking, rattling, rushing, shaking.

H7495 רָפָא (râphâʼ, raw-faw'): properly, to mend (by stitching), i.e. (figuratively) to cure. Origin: or רָפָה; a primitive root; KJV: cure, (cause to) heal, physician, repair, [idiom] thoroughly, make whole. See H7503 (רָפָה).

H7496 רָפָא (râphâʼ, raw-faw'): properly, lax, i.e. (figuratively) a ghost (as dead; in plural only). Origin: from H7495 (רָפָא) in the sense of H7503 (רָפָה); KJV: dead, deceased.

H7497 רָפָא (râphâʼ, raw-faw'): a giant. Origin: or רָפָה; from H7495 (רָפָא) in the sense of invigorating; KJV: giant, Rapha, Rephaim(-s). See also H1051 (בֵּית רָפָא).

H7498 רָפָא (Râphâʼ, raw-faw'): Rapha or Raphah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or רָפָה; probably the same as H7497 (רָפָא); giant; KJV: Rapha.

H7499 רְפֻאָה (rᵉphuʼâh, ref-oo-aw'): a medicament. Origin: feminine passive participle of H7495 (רָפָא); KJV: heal(-ed), medicine.

H7500 רִפְאוּת (riphʼûwth, rif-ooth'): a cure. Origin: from H7495 (רָפָא); KJV: health.

H7501 רְפָאֵל (Rᵉphâʼêl, ref-aw-ale'): Rephael, an Israelite. Origin: from H7495 (רָפָא) and H410 (אֵל); God has cured; KJV: Rephael.

H7502 רָפַד (râphad, raw-fad'): to spread (a bed); by implication, to refresh. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: comfort, make (a bed), spread.

H7503 רָפָה (râphâh, raw-faw'): to slacken (in many applications, literal or figurative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abate, cease, consume, draw (toward evening), fail, (be) faint, be (wax) feeble, forsake, idle, leave, let alone (go, down), (be) slack, stay, be still, be slothful, (be) weak(-en). See H7495 (רָפָא).

H7504 רָפֶה (râpheh, raw-feh'): slack (in body or mind). Origin: from H7503 (רָפָה); KJV: weak. raphah, Raphah. See H7497 (רָפָא), H7498 (רָפָא). riphah. See H7383 (רִיפָה).

H7505 רָפוּא (Râphûwʼ, raw-foo'): Raphu, an Israelite. Origin: passive participle of H7495 (רָפָא); cured; KJV: Raphu.

H7506 רֶפַח (Rephach, reh'-fakh): Rephach, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root apparently meaning to sustain; support; KJV: Rephah.

H7507 רְפִידָה (rᵉphîydâh, ref-ee-daw'): a railing (as spread along). Origin: from H7502 (רָפַד); KJV: bottom.

H7508 רְפִידִים (Rᵉphîydîym, ref-ee-deem'): Rephidim, a place in the Desert. Origin: plural of the masculine of the same as H7507 (רְפִידָה); ballusters; KJV: Rephidim.

H7509 רְפָיָה (Rᵉphâyâh, ref-aw-yaw'): Rephajah, the name of five Israelites. Origin: from H7495 (רָפָא) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has cured; KJV: Rephaiah.

H7510 רִפְיוֹן (riphyôwn, rif-yone'): slackness. Origin: from H7503 (רָפָה); KJV: feebleness.

H7511 רָפַס (râphaç, raw-fas'): to trample, i.e. prostrate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: humble self, submit self.

H7512 רְפַס (rᵉphaç, ref-as'): {to trample, i.e. prostrate}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7511 (רָפַס) KJV: stamp.

H7513 רַפְסֹדָה (raphçôdâh, raf-so-daw'): a raft (as flat on the water). Origin: from H7511 (רָפַס); KJV: flote.

H7514 רָפַק (râphaq, raw-fak'): to recline. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lean.

H7515 רָפַשׂ (râphas, raw-fas'): to trample, i.e. roil water. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: foul, trouble.

H7516 רֶפֶשׁ (rephesh, reh'-fesh): mud (as roiled). Origin: from H7515 (רָפַשׂ); KJV: mire.

H7517 רֶפֶת (repheth, reh'-feth): a stall for cattle (from their resting there). Origin: probably from H7503 (רָפָה); KJV: stall.

H7518 רַץ (rats, rats): a fragment. Origin: contracted from H7533 (רָצַץ); KJV: piece.
