H8010 שְׁלֹמֹה (Shᵉlômôh, shel-o-mo'): Shelomah, David's successor. Origin: from H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); peaceful; KJV: Solomon.

H8011 שִׁלֻּמָה (shillumâh, shil-loo-maw'): retribution. Origin: feminine of H7966 (שִׁלּוּם); KJV: recompense.

H8012 שַׂלְמוֹן (Salmôwn, sal-mone'): Salmon, an Israelite. Origin: from H8008 (שַׂלְמָה); investiture; KJV: Salmon. Compare H8009 (שַׂלְמָה).

H8013 שְׁלֹמוֹת (Shᵉlômôwth, shel-o-moth'): Shelomoth, the name of two Israelites. Origin: feminine plural of H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); pacifications; KJV: Shelomith (from the margin), Shelomoth. Compare H8019 (שְׁלֹמִית).

H8014 שַׂלְמַי (Salmay, sal-mah'-ee): Salmai, an Israelite. Origin: from H8008 (שַׂלְמָה); clothed; KJV: Shalmai.

H8015 שְׁלֹמִי (Shᵉlômîy, shel-o-mee'): Shelomi, an Israelite. Origin: from H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); peaceable; KJV: Shelomi.

H8016 שִׁלֵּמִי (Shillêmîy, shil-lay-mee'): a Shilemite (collectively) or descendants of Shillem. Origin: patronymically from H8006 (שִׁלֵּם); KJV: Shillemites.

H8017 שְׁלֻמִיאֵל (Shᵉlumîyʼêl, shel-oo-mee-ale'): Shelumiel, an Israelite. Origin: from H7965 (שָׁלוֹם) and H410 (אֵל); peace of God; KJV: Shelumiel.

H8018 שֶׁלֶמְיָה (Shelemyâh, shel-em-yaw'): Shelemjah, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: or שֶׁלֶמְיָהוּ; from H8002 (שֶׁלֶם) and H3050 (יָהּ); thankoffering of Jah; KJV: Shelemiah.

H8019 שְׁלֹמִית (Shᵉlômîyth, shel-o-meeth'): Shelomith, the name of five Israelites and three Israelitesses. Origin: or שׁלוֹמִית; (Ezra 8:10), from H7965 (שָׁלוֹם); peaceableness; KJV: Shelomith.

H8020 שַׁלְמַן (Shalman, shal-man'): Shalman, a king apparently of Assyria. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Shalman. Compare H8022 (שַׁלְמַנְאֶסֶר).

H8021 שַׁלְמֹן (shalmôn, shal-mone'): a bribe. Origin: from H7999 (שָׁלַם); KJV: reward.

H8022 שַׁלְמַנְאֶסֶר (Shalmanʼeçer, shal-man-eh'-ser): Shalmaneser, an Assyrian king. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Shalmaneser. Comp H8020 (שַׁלְמַן).

H8023 שִׁלֹנִי (Shilônîy, shee-lo-nee'): Shiloni, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H7888 (שִׁילוֹנִי); KJV: Shiloni.

H8024 שֵׁלָנִי (Shêlânîy, shay-law-nee'): a Shelanite (collectively), or descendants of Shelah. Origin: from H7956 (שֵׁלָה); KJV: Shelanites.

H8025 שָׁלַף (shâlaph, saw-laf'): to pull out, up or off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: draw (off), grow up, pluck off.

H8026 שֶׁלֶף (sheleph, sheh'-lef): Sheleph, a son of Jokthan. Origin: from H8025 (שָׁלַף); extract; KJV: Sheleph.

H8027 שָׁלַשׁ (shâlash, shaw-lash'): to be (causatively, make) triplicate (by restoration, in portions, strands, days or years). Origin: a primitive root perhaps originally to intensify, i.e. treble; but apparently used only as denominative from H7969 (שָׁלוֹשׁ), KJV: do the third time, (divide into, stay) three (days, -fold, parts, years old).

H8028 שֶׁלֶשׁ (Shelesh, sheh'-lesh): Shelesh, an Israelite. Origin: from H8027 (שָׁלַשׁ); triplet; KJV: Shelesh.

H8029 שִׁלֵּשׁ (shillêsh, shil-laysh'): a descendant of the third degree, i.e. great grandchild. Origin: from H8027 (שָׁלַשׁ); KJV: third (generation).

H8030 שִׁלְשָׁה (Shilshâh, shil-shaw'): Shilshah, an Israelite. Origin: feminine from the same as H8028 (שֶׁלֶשׁ); triplication; KJV: Shilshah.

H8031 שָׁלִשָׁה (Shâlishâh, shaw-lee-shaw'): Shalishah, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine from H8027 (שָׁלַשׁ); trebled land; KJV: Shalisha.

H8032 שִׁלְשׁוֹם (shilshôwm, shil-shome'): trebly, i.e. (in time) day before yesterday. Origin: or שִׁלְשֹׁם; from the same as H8028 (שֶׁלֶשׁ); KJV: [phrase] before (that time, -time), excellent things (from the margin), [phrase] heretofore, three days, [phrase] time past.

H8033 שָׁם (shâm, shawm): there (transferring to time) then; often thither, or thence. Origin: a primitive particle (rather from the relative pronoun, H834 (אֲשֶׁר)); KJV: in it, [phrase] thence, there (-in, [phrase] of, [phrase] out), [phrase] thither, [phrase] whither.

H8034 שֵׁם (shêm, shame): an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character. Origin: a primitive word (perhaps rather from through the idea of definite and conspicuous position; compare H8064 (שָׁמַיִם)); KJV: [phrase] base, (in-) fame(-ous), named(-d), renown, report.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H8035 to H8155
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H8035 שֵׁם (Shêm, shame): Shem, a son of Noah (often includ. his posterity). Origin: the same as H8034 (שֵׁם); name; KJV: Sem, Shem.

H8036 שֻׁם (shum, shoom): {an appellation, as amark or memorial of individuality; by implication honor, authority, character}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8034 (שֵׁם) KJV: name.

H8037 שַׁמָּא (Shammâʼ, sham-maw'): Shamma, an Israelite. Origin: from H8074 (שָׁמֵם); desolation; KJV: Shamma.

H8038 שֶׁמְאֵבֶר (Shemʼêber, shem-ay'-ber): Shemeber, a king of Zeboim. Origin: apparently from H8034 (שֵׁם) and H83 (אֵבֶר); name of pinion, i.e. illustrious; KJV: Shemeber.

H8039 שִׁמְאָה (Shimʼâh, shim-aw'): Shimah, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps for H8093 (שִׁמְעָה); KJV: Shimah. Compare H8043 (שִׁמְאָם).

H8040 שְׂמֹאול (sᵉmôʼwl, sem-ole'): properly, dark (as enveloped), i.e. the north; hence (by orientation), the left hand. Origin: or שְׂמֹאל; a primitive word (rather perhaps from the same as H8071 (שִׂמְלָה) (by insertion of the aleph) through the idea of wrapping up); KJV: left (hand, side).

H8041 שָׂמַאל (sâmaʼl, saw-mal'): to use the left hand or pass in that direction). Origin: a primitive root (denominative from H8040 (שְׂמֹאול)); KJV: (go, turn) (on the, to the) left.

H8042 שְׂמָאלִי (sᵉmâʼlîy, sem-aw-lee'): situated on the left side. Origin: from H8040 (שְׂמֹאול); KJV: left.

H8043 שִׁמְאָם (Shimʼâm, shim-awm'): Shimam, an Israelite. Origin: for H8039 (שִׁמְאָה) (compare H38 (אֲבִיָּם)); KJV: Shimeam.

H8044 שַׁמְגַּר (Shamgar, sham-gar'): Shamgar, an Israelite judge. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: Shamgar.

H8045 שָׁמַד (shâmad, shaw-mad'): to desolate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: destory(-uction), bring to nought, overthrow, perish, pluck down, [idiom] utterly.

H8046 שְׁמַד (shᵉmad, shem-ad'): {to desolate}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8045 (שָׁמַד) KJV: consume.

H8047 שַׁמָּה (shammâh, sham-maw'): ruin; by implication, consternation. Origin: from H8074 (שָׁמֵם); KJV: astonishment, desolate(-ion), waste, wonderful thing.

H8048 שַׁמָּה (Shammâh, sham-maw'): Shammah, the name of an Edomite and four Israelites. Origin: the same as H8047 (שַׁמָּה); KJV: Shammah.

H8049 שַׁמְהוּת (Shamhûwth, sham-hooth'): Shamhuth, an Israelite. Origin: for H8048 (שַׁמָּה); desolation; KJV: Shamhuth.

H8050 שְׁמוּאֵל (Shᵉmûwʼêl, sehm-oo-ale'): Shemuel, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from the passive participle of H8085 (שָׁמַע) and H410 (אֵל); heard of God; KJV: Samuel, Shemuel.

H8051 שַׁמּוּעַ (Shammûwaʻ, sham-moo'-ah): Shammua, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H8074 (שָׁמֵם); renowned; KJV: Shammua, Shammuah.

H8052 שְׁמוּעָה (shᵉmûwʻâh, sehm-oo-aw'): something heard, i.e. an announcement. Origin: feminine passive participle of H8074 (שָׁמֵם); KJV: bruit, doctrine, fame, mentioned, news, report, rumor, tidings.

H8053 שָׁמוּר (Shâmûwr, shaw-moor'): Shamur, an Israelite. Origin: passive participle of H8103 (שִׁמְצָה); observed; KJV: Shamir (from the margin).

H8054 שַׁמּוֹת (Shammôwth, sham-moth'): Shammoth, an Israelite. Origin: plural of H8047 (שַׁמָּה); ruins; KJV: Shamoth.

H8055 שָׂמַח (sâmach, saw-makh'): probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cheer up, be (make) glad, (have, make) joy(-ful), be (make) merry, (cause to, make to) rejoice, [idiom] very.

H8056 שָׂמֵחַ (sâmêach, saw-may'-akh): blithe or gleeful. Origin: from H8055 (שָׂמַח); KJV: (be) glad, joyful, (making) merry((-hearted), -ily), rejoice(-ing).

H8057 שִׂמְחָה (simchâh, sim-khaw'): blithesomeness or glee, (religious or festival). Origin: from H8056 (שָׂמֵחַ); KJV: [idiom] exceeding(-ly), gladness, joy(-fulness), mirth, pleasure, rejoice(-ing).

H8058 שָׁמַט (shâmaṭ, shaw-mat'): to fling down; incipiently to jostle; figuratively, to let alone, desist, remit. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: discontinue, overthrow, release, let rest, shake, stumble, throw down.

H8059 שְׁמִטָּה (shᵉmiṭṭâh, shem-it-taw'): remission (of debt) or suspension of labor). Origin: from H8058 (שָׁמַט); KJV: release.

H8060 שַׁמַּי (Shammay, sham-mah'-ee): Shammai, the name of three Israelites. Origin: from H8073 (שַׁמְלַי); destructive; KJV: Shammai.

H8061 שְׁמִידָע (Shᵉmîydâʻ, shem-ee-daw'): Shemida, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H8034 (שֵׁם) and H3045 (יָדַע); name of knowing; KJV: Shemida, Shemidah.

H8062 שְׁמִידָעִי (Shᵉmîydâʻîy, shem-ee-daw-ee'): a Shemidaite (collectively) or descendants of Shemida. Origin: patronymically from H8061 (שְׁמִידָע); KJV: Shemidaites.

H8063 שְׂמִיכָה (sᵉmîykâh, sem-ee-kaw'): a run (as sustaining the Oriental sitter). Origin: from H5564 (סָמַךְ); KJV: mantle.

H8064 שָׁמַיִם (shâmayim, shaw-mah'-yim): the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve). Origin: dual of an unused singular שָׁמֶה; from an unused root meaning to be lofty; KJV: air, [idiom] astrologer, heaven(-s).

H8065 שָׁמַיִן (shâmayin, shaw-mah'-yin): {the sky (as aloft; the dual perhaps alluding to the visible arch in which the clouds move, as well as to the higher ether where the celestial bodies revolve)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8064 (שָׁמַיִם) KJV: heaven.

H8066 שְׁמִינִי (shᵉmîynîy, shem-ee-nee'): eight. Origin: from H8083 (שְׁמֹנֶה); KJV: eight.

H8067 שְׁמִינִית (shᵉmîynîyth, shem-ee-neeth'): probably an eight-stringed lyre. Origin: feminine of H8066 (שְׁמִינִי); KJV: Sheminith.

H8068 שָׁמִיר (shâmîyr, shaw-meer'): a thorn; also (from its keenness for scratching) a gem, probably the diamond. Origin: from H8104 (שָׁמַר) in the original sense of pricking; KJV: adamant (stone), brier, diamond.

H8069 שָׁמִיר (Shâmîyr, shaw-meer'): Shamir, the name of two places in Palestine. Origin: the same as H8068 (שָׁמִיר); KJV: Shamir. Compare H8053 (שָׁמוּר).

H8070 שְׁמִירָמוֹת (Shᵉmîyrâmôwth, shem-ee-raw-moth'): Shemiramoth, the name of two Israelites. Origin: or שְׁמָרִימוֹת; probably from H8034 (שֵׁם) and plural of H7413 (רָמָה); name of heights; KJV: Shemiramoth.

H8071 שִׂמְלָה (simlâh, sim-law'): a dress, especially a mantle. Origin: perhaps by permutation for the feminine of H5566 (סֶמֶל) (through the idea of a cover assuming the shape of the object beneath); KJV: apparel, cloth(-es, -ing), garment, raiment. Compare H8008 (שַׂלְמָה).

H8072 שַׂמְלָה (Samlâh, sam-law'): Samlah, an Edomite. Origin: probably for the same as H8071 (שִׂמְלָה); KJV: Samlah.

H8073 שַׁמְלַי (Shamlay, sham-lah'-ee): Shamlai, one of the Nethinim. Origin: for H8014 (שַׂלְמַי); KJV: Shalmai (from the margin).

H8074 שָׁמֵם (shâmêm, shaw-mame'): to stun (or intransitively, grow numb), i.e. devastate or (figuratively) stupefy (both usually in a passive sense). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: make amazed, be astonied, (be an) astonish(-ment), (be, bring into, unto, lay, lie, make) desolate(-ion, places), be destitute, destroy (self), (lay, lie, make) waste, wonder.

H8075 שְׁמַם (shᵉmam, shem-am'): {to stun (or intransitively, grow numb), i.e. devastate or (figuratively) stupefy (both usually in a passive sense)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8074 (שָׁמֵם) KJV: be astonied.

H8076 שָׁמֵם (shâmêm, shaw-mame'): ruined. Origin: from H8074 (שָׁמֵם); KJV: desolate.

H8077 שְׁמָמָה (shᵉmâmâh, shem-aw-maw'): devastation; figuratively, astonishment. Origin: or שִׁמָמָה; feminine of H8076 (שָׁמֵם); KJV: (laid, [idiom] most) desolate(-ion), waste.

H8078 שִׁמָּמוֹן (shimmâmôwn, shim-maw-mone'): stupefaction. Origin: from H8074 (שָׁמֵם); KJV: astonishment.

H8079 שְׂמָמִית (sᵉmâmîyth, sem-aw-meeth'): a lizard (from the superstition of its noxiousness). Origin: probably from H8074 (שָׁמֵם) (in the sense of poisoning); KJV: spider.

H8080 שָׁמַן (shâman, shaw-man'): to shine, i.e. (by analogy) be (causatively, make) oily or gross. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: become (make, wax) fat.

H8081 שֶׁמֶן (shemen, sheh'-men): grease, especially liquid (as from the olive, often perfumed); figuratively, richness. Origin: from H8080 (שָׁמַן); KJV: anointing, [idiom] fat (things), [idiom] fruitful, oil(-ed), ointment, olive, [phrase] pine.

H8082 שָׁמֵן (shâmên, shaw-mane'): greasy, i.e. gross; figuratively, rich. Origin: from H8080 (שָׁמַן); KJV: fat, lusty, plenteous.

H8083 שְׁמֹנֶה (shᵉmôneh, shem-o-neh'): a cardinal number, eight (as if a surplus above the 'perfect' seven); also (as ordinal) eighth. Origin: or שְׁמוֹנֶה; feminine שְׁמֹנָה; or שְׁמוֹנָה; apparently from H8082 (שָׁמֵן) through the idea of plumpness; KJV: eight(-een, -eenth), eighth.

H8084 שְׁמֹנִים (shᵉmônîym, shem-o-neem'): eighty, also eightieth. Origin: or שְׁמוֹנִים; multiple from H8083 (שְׁמֹנֶה); KJV: eighty(-ieth), fourscore.

H8085 שָׁמַע (shâmaʻ, shaw-mah'): to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] attentively, call (gather) together, [idiom] carefully, [idiom] certainly, consent, consider, be content, declare, [idiom] diligently, discern, give ear, (cause to, let, make to) hear(-ken, tell), [idiom] indeed, listen, make (a) noise, (be) obedient, obey, perceive, (make a) proclaim(-ation), publish, regard, report, shew (forth), (make a) sound, [idiom] surely, tell, understand, whosoever (heareth), witness.

H8086 שְׁמַע (shᵉmaʻ, shem-ah'): {to hear intelligently (often with implication of attention, obedience, etc.; causatively, to tell, etc.)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8085 (שָׁמַע) KJV: hear, obey.

H8087 שֶׁמַע (Shemaʻ, sheh'-mah): Shema, the name of a place in Palestine and of four Israelites. Origin: for the same as H8088 (שֵׁמַע); KJV: Shema.

H8088 שֵׁמַע (shêmaʻ, shay'-mah): something heard, i.e. a sound, rumor, announcement; abstractly, audience. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע); KJV: bruit, fame, hear(-ing), loud, report, speech, tidings.

H8089 שֹׁמַע (shômaʻ, sho'-mah): a report. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע); KJV: fame.

H8090 שְׁמָע (Shᵉmâʻ, shem-aw'): Shema, a place in Palestine. Origin: for H8087 (שֶׁמַע); KJV: Shema.

H8091 שָׁמָע (Shâmâʻ, shaw-maw'): Shama, an Israelite. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע); obedient; KJV: Shama.

H8092 שִׁמְעָא (Shimʻâʼ, shim-aw'): Shima, the name of four Israelites. Origin: for H8093 (שִׁמְעָה); KJV: Shimea, Shimei, Shamma.

H8093 שִׁמְעָה (Shimʻâh, shim-aw'): Shimah, an Israelite. Origin: feminine of H8088 (שֵׁמַע); annunciation; KJV: Shimeah.

H8094 שְׁמָעָה (Shᵉmâʻâh, shem-aw-aw'): Shemaah, an Israelite. Origin: for H8093 (שִׁמְעָה); KJV: Shemaah.

H8095 שִׁמְעוֹן (Shimʻôwn, shim-one'): Shimon, one of Jacob's sons, also the tribe descended from him. Origin: from H8085 (שָׁמַע); hearing; KJV: Simeon.

H8096 שִׁמְעִי (Shimʻîy, shim-ee'): Shimi, the name of twenty Israelites. Origin: from H8088 (שֵׁמַע); famous; KJV: Shimeah (from the margin), Shimei, Shimhi, Shimi.

H8097 שִׁמְעִי (Shimʻîy, shim-ee'): a Shimite (collectively) or descendants of Shimi. Origin: patronymically from H8096 (שִׁמְעִי); KJV: of Shimi, Shimites.

H8098 שְׁמַעְיָה (Shᵉmaʻyâh, shem-aw-yaw'): Shemajah, the name of twenty-five Israelites. Origin: or שְׁמַעְיָהוּ; from H8085 (שָׁמַע) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has heard; KJV: Shemaiah.

H8099 שִׁמְעֹנִי (Shimʻônîy, shim-o-nee'): a Shimonite (collectively) or descendants of Shimon. Origin: patronymically from H8095 (שִׁמְעוֹן); KJV: tribe of Simeon, Simeonites.

H8100 שִׁמְעַת (Shimʻath, shim-awth'): Shimath, an Ammonitess. Origin: feminine of H8088 (שֵׁמַע); annunciation; KJV: Shimath.

H8101 שִׁמְעָתִי (Shimʻâthîy, shim-aw-thee'): a Shimathite (collectively) or descendants of Shimah. Origin: patronymically from H8093 (שִׁמְעָה); KJV: Shimeathites.

H8102 שֶׁמֶץ (shemets, sheh'-mets): an inkling. Origin: from an unused root meaning to emit a sound; KJV: a little.

H8103 שִׁמְצָה (shimtsâh, shim-tsaw'): scornful whispering (of hostile spectators). Origin: feminine of H8102 (שֶׁמֶץ); KJV: shame.

H8104 שָׁמַר (shâmar, shaw-mar'): properly, to hedge about (as with thorns), i.e. guard; generally, to protect, attend to, etc. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: beward, be circumspect, take heed (to self), keep(-er, self), mark, look narrowly, observe, preserve, regard, reserve, save (self), sure, (that lay) wait (for), watch(-man).

H8105 שֶׁמֶר (shemer, sheh'-mer): something preserved, i.e. the settlings (plural only) of wine. Origin: from H8104 (שָׁמַר); KJV: dregs, (wines on the) lees.

H8106 שֶׁמֶר (Shemer, sheh'-mer): Shemer, the name of three Israelites. Origin: the same as H8105 (שֶׁמֶר); KJV: Shamer, Shemer.

H8107 שִׁמֻּר (shimmur, shim-moor'): an observance. Origin: from H8104 (שָׁמַר); KJV: [idiom] be (much) observed.

H8108 שׇׁמְרָה (shomrâh, shom-raw'): watchfulness. Origin: feminine of an unused noun from H8104 (שָׁמַר) meaning a guard; KJV: watch.

H8109 שְׁמֻרָה (shᵉmurâh, shem-oo-raw'): something guarded, i.e. an eye-lid. Origin: feminine of passive participle of H8104 (שָׁמַר); KJV: waking.

H8110 שִׁמְרוֹן (Shimrôwn, shim-rone'): Shimron, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine. Origin: from H8105 (שֶׁמֶר) in its original sense; guardianship; KJV: Shimron.

H8111 שֹׁמְרוֹן (Shômᵉrôwn, sho-mer-one'): Shomeron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the active participle of H8104 (שָׁמַר); watch-station; KJV: Samaria.

H8112 שִׁמְרוֹן מְראוֹן (Shimrôwn Mᵉrʼôwn, shim-rone' mer-one'): Shimron-Meron, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H8110 (שִׁמְרוֹן) and a derivative of H4754 (מָרָא); guard of lashing; KJV: Shimon-meron.

H8113 שִׁמְרִי (Shimrîy, shim-ree'): Shimri, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H8105 (שֶׁמֶר) in its original sense; watchful; KJV: Shimri.

H8114 שְׁמַרְיָה (Shᵉmaryâh, shem-ar-yaw'): Shemarjah, the name of four Israelites. Origin: or שְׁמַרְיָהוּ; from H8104 (שָׁמַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has guarded; KJV: Shamariah, Shemariah.

H8115 שׇׁמְרַיִן (Shomrayin, shom-rah'-yin): Shomrain, a place in Palestine. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8111 (שֹׁמְרוֹן); KJV: Samaria.

H8116 שִׁמְרִית (Shimrîyth, shim-reeth'): Shimrith, a Moabitess. Origin: feminine of H8113 (שִׁמְרִי); female guard; KJV: Shimrith.

H8117 שִׁמְרֹנִי (Shimrônîy, shim-ro-nee'): a Shimronite (collectively) or descendants of Shimron. Origin: patronymically from H8110 (שִׁמְרוֹן); KJV: Shimronites.

H8118 שֹׁמרֹנִי (Shômrônîy, sho-mer-o-nee'): a Shomeronite (collectively) or inhabitants of Shomeron. Origin: patrial from H8111 (שֹׁמְרוֹן); KJV: Samaritans.

H8119 שִׁמְרָת (Shimrâth, shim-rawth'): Shimrath, an Israelite. Origin: from H8104 (שָׁמַר); guardship; KJV: Shimrath.

H8120 שְׁמַשׁ (shᵉmash, shem-ash'): to serve. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to the root of H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ) through the idea of activity implied in day-light; KJV: minister.

H8121 שֶׁמֶשׁ (shemesh, sheh'-mesh): the sun; by implication, the east; figuratively, a ray, i.e. (architectural) a notched battlement. Origin: from an unused root meaning to be brilliant; KJV: [phrase] east side(-ward), sun (rising), [phrase] west(-ward), window. See also H1053 (בֵּית שֶׁמֶשׁ).

H8122 שֶׁמֶשׁ (shemesh, sheh'-mesh): the sun. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); KJV: sun.

H8123 שִׁמְשׁוֹן (Shimshôwn, shim-shone'): Shimshon, an Israelite. Origin: from H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); sunlight; KJV: Samson.

H8124 שִׁמְשַׁי (Shimshay, shim-shah'-ee): Shimshai, a Samaritan. Origin: (Aramaic) from H8122 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); sunny; KJV: Shimshai.

H8125 שַׁמְשְׁרַי (Shamshᵉray, sham-sher-ah'-ee): Shamsherai, an Israelite. Origin: apparently from H8121 (שֶׁמֶשׁ); sunlike; KJV: Shamsherai.

H8126 שֻׁמָתִי (Shumâthîy, shoo-maw-thee'): a Shumathite (collectively) or descendants of Shumah. Origin: patronymically from an unused name from H7762 (שׁוּם) probably meaning garlic-smell; KJV: Shumathites.

H8127 שֵׁן (shên, shane): a tooth (as sharp); specifically ivory; figuratively, a cliff. Origin: from H8150 (שָׁנַן); compare H8143 (שֶׁנְהַבִּים) KJV: crag, [idiom] forefront, ivory, [idiom] sharp, tooth.

H8128 שֵׁן (shên, shane): a tooth. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8127 (שֵׁן); KJV: tooth.

H8129 שֵׁן (Shên, shane): Shen, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H8127 (שֵׁן); crag; KJV: Shen.

H8130 שָׂנֵא (sânêʼ, saw-nay'): to hate (personally). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: enemy, foe, (be) hate(-ful, -r), odious, [idiom] utterly.

H8131 שְׂנֵא (sᵉnêʼ, sen-ay'): {to hate (personally)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8130 (שָׂנֵא) KJV: hate.

H8132 שָׁנָא (shânâʼ, shaw-naw'): to alter. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: change.

H8133 שְׁנָא (shᵉnâʼ, shen-aw'): {to alter}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8132 (שָׁנָא) KJV: alter, change, (be) diverse.

H8134 שִׁנְאָב (Shinʼâb, shin-awb'): Shinab, a Canaanite. Origin: probably from H8132 (שָׁנָא) and H1 (אָב); a father has turned; KJV: Shinab.

H8135 שִׂנְאָה (sinʼâh, sin-aw'): hate. Origin: from H8130 (שָׂנֵא); KJV: [phrase] exceedingly, hate(-ful, -red).

H8136 שִׁנְאָן (shinʼân, shin-awn'): change, i.e. repetition. Origin: from H8132 (שָׁנָא); KJV: [idiom] angels.

H8137 שֶׁנְאַצַּר (Shenʼatstsar, shen-ats-tsar'): Shenatstsar, an Israelite. Origin: apparently of Babylonian origin; KJV: Senazar.

H8138 שָׁנָה (shânâh, shaw-naw'): to fold, i.e. duplicate (literally or figuratively); by implication, to transmute (transitive or intransitive). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: do (speak, strike) again, alter, double, (be given to) change, disguise, (be) diverse, pervert, prefer, repeat, return, do the second time.

H8139 שְׁנָה (shᵉnâh, shen-aw'): {sleep}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8142 (שֵׁנָה) KJV: sleep.

H8140 שְׁנָה (shᵉnâh, shen-aw'): {a year (as a revolution of time)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8141 (שָׁנֶה) KJV: year.

H8141 שָׁנֶה (shâneh, shaw-neh'): a year (as a revolution of time). Origin: (in plural or (feminine) שָׁנָה; from H8138 (שָׁנָה); KJV: [phrase] whole age, [idiom] long, [phrase] old, year([idiom] -ly).

H8142 שֵׁנָה (shênâh, shay-naw'): sleep. Origin: or שֵׁנָא; (Psalm 127:2), from H3462 (יָשֵׁן); KJV: sleep.

H8143 שֶׁנְהַבִּים (shenhabbîym, shen-hab-beem'): probably, tooth of elephants, i.e. ivory tusk. Origin: from H8127 (שֵׁן) and the plural apparently of a foreign word; KJV: ivory.

H8144 שָׁנִי (shânîy, shaw-nee'): crimson, properly, the insect or its color, also stuff dyed with it. Origin: of uncertain derivation; KJV: crimson, scarlet (thread).

H8145 שֵׁנִי (shênîy, shay-nee'): properly, double, i.e. second; also adverbially, again. Origin: from H8138 (שָׁנָה); KJV: again, either (of them), (an-) other, second (time).

H8146 שָׂנִיא (sânîyʼ, saw-nee'): hated. Origin: from H8130 (שָׂנֵא); KJV: hated.

H8147 שְׁנַיִם (shᵉnayim, shen-ah'-yim): two; also (as ordinal) twofold. Origin: dual of H8145 (שֵׁנִי); feminine שְׁתַּיִם; KJV: both, couple, double, second, twain, [phrase] twelfth, [phrase] twelve, [phrase] twenty (sixscore) thousand, twice, two.

H8148 שְׁנִינָה (shᵉnîynâh, shen-ee-naw'): something pointed, i.e. a gibe. Origin: from H8150 (שָׁנַן); KJV: byword, taunt.

H8149 שְׁנִיר (Shᵉnîyr, shen-eer'): Shenir or Senir, a summit of Lebanon. Origin: or שְׂנִיר; from an unused root meaning to be pointed; peak; KJV: Senir, Shenir.

H8150 שָׁנַן (shânan, shaw-nan'): to point (transitive or intransitive); intensively, to pierce; figuratively, to inculcate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: prick, sharp(-en), teach diligently, whet.

H8151 שָׁנַס (shânaç, shaw-nas'): to compress (with a belt). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: gird up.

H8152 שִׁנְעָר (Shinʻâr, shin-awr'): Shinar, a plain in Babylonia. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Shinar.

H8153 שְׁנָת (shᵉnâth, shen-awth'): sleep. Origin: from H3462 (יָשֵׁן); KJV: sleep.

H8154 שָׁסָה (shâçâh, shaw-saw'): to plunder. Origin: or שָׁשָׂה; (Isaiah 10:13), a primitive root; KJV: destroyer, rob, spoil(-er).

H8155 שָׁסַס (shâçaç, shaw-sas'): to plunder. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: rifle, spoil.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H8156 to H8284
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H8156 שָׁסַע (shâçaʻ, shaw-sah'): to split or tear; figuratively, to upbraid. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cleave, (be) cloven (footed), rend, stay.

H8157 שֶׁסַע (sheçaʻ, sheh'-sah): a fissure. Origin: from H8156 (שָׁסַע); KJV: cleft, clovenfooted.

H8158 שָׁסַף (shâçaph, shaw-saf'): to cut in pieces, i.e. slaughter. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hew in pieces.

H8159 שָׁעָה (shâʻâh, shaw-aw'): to gaze at or about (properly, for help); by implication, to inspect, consider, compassionate, be nonplussed (as looking around in amazement) or bewildered. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: depart, be dim, be dismayed, look (away), regard, have respect, spare, turn.

H8160 שָׁעָה (shâʻâh, shaw-aw'): properly, a look, i.e. a moment. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H8159 (שָׁעָה); KJV: hour.

H8161 שַׁעֲטָה (shaʻăṭâh, shah'-at-aw): a clatter (of hoofs). Origin: feminine from an unused root meaning to stamp; KJV: stamping.

H8162 שַׁעַטְנֵז (shaʻaṭnêz, shah-at-naze'): linsey-woolsey, i.e. cloth of linen and wool carded and spun together. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: garment of divers sorts, linen and wollen.

H8163 שָׂעִיר (sâʻîyr, saw-eer'): shaggy; as noun, a he-goat; by analogy, a faun. Origin: or שָׂעִר; from H8175 (שָׂעַר); KJV: devil, goat, hairy, kid, rough, satyr.

H8164 שָׂעִיר (sâʻîyr, saw-eer'): a shower (as tempestuous). Origin: formed the same as H8163 (שָׂעִיר); KJV: small rain.

H8165 שֵׂעִיר (Sêʻîyr, say-eer'): Seir, a mountain of Idumaea and its aboriginal occupants, also one in Palestine. Origin: formed like H8163 (שָׂעִיר); rough; KJV: Seir.

H8166 שְׂעִירָה (sᵉʻîyrâh, seh-ee-raw'): a she-goat. Origin: feminine of H8163 (שָׂעִיר); KJV: kid.

H8167 שְׂעִירָה (Sᵉʻîyrâh, seh-ee-raw'): Seirah, a place in Palestine. Origin: formed as H8166 (שְׂעִירָה); roughness; KJV: Seirath.

H8168 שֹׁעַל (shôʻal, sho'-al): the palm; by extension, a handful. Origin: from an unused root meaning to hollow out; KJV: handful, hollow of the hand.

H8169 שַׁעַלְבִים (Shaʻalbîym, shah-al-beem'): Shaalbim or Shaalabbin, a place in Palestine. Origin: or שַׁעֲלַבִּין; plural from H7776 (שׁוּעָל); fox-holes; KJV: Shaalabbin, Shaalbim.

H8170 שַׁעַלְבֹנִי (Shaʻalbônîy, shah-al-bo-nee'): a Shaalbonite or inhabitant of Shaalbin. Origin: patrial from H8169 (שַׁעַלְבִים); KJV: Shaalbonite.

H8171 שַׁעֲלִים (Shaʻălîym, shah-al-eem'): Shaalim, a place in Palestine. Origin: plural of H7776 (שׁוּעָל); foxes; KJV: Shalim.

H8172 שָׁעַן (shâʻan, shaw-an'): to support one's self. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: lean, lie, rely, rest (on, self), stay.

H8173 שָׁעַע (shâʻaʻ, shaw-ah'): (in a good acceptation) to look upon (with complacency), i.e. fondle, please or amuse (self); (in a bad one) to look about (in dismay), i.e. stare. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cry (out) (by confusion with H7768 (שָׁוַע)), dandle, delight (self), play, shut.

H8174 שַׁעַף (Shaʻaph, shah'-af): Shaaph, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H5586 (סָעַף); fluctuation; KJV: Shaaph.

H8175 שָׂעַר (sâʻar, saw-ar'): to storm; by implication, to shiver, i.e. fear. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be (horribly) afraid, fear, hurl as a storm, be tempestuous, come like (take away as with) a whirlwind.

H8176 שָׁעַר (shâʻar, shaw-ar'): to act as gatekeeper; (figuratively) to estimate. Origin: a primitive root; to split or open, i.e. (literally, but only as denominative from H8179 (שַׁעַר)); compare see H7778 (שׁוֹעֵר) KJV: think.

H8177 שְׂעַר (sᵉʻar, seh-ar'): hair. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8181 (שֵׂעָר); KJV: hair.

H8178 שַׂעַר (saʻar, sah'-ar): a tempest; also a terror. Origin: from H8175 (שָׂעַר); KJV: affrighted, [idiom] horribly, [idiom] sore, storm. See H8181 (שֵׂעָר).

H8179 שַׁעַר (shaʻar, shah'-ar): an opening, i.e. door or gate. Origin: from H8176 (שָׁעַר) in its original sense; KJV: city, door, gate, port ([idiom] -er).

H8180 שַׁעַר (shaʻar, shah'-ar): a measure (as a section). Origin: from H8176 (שָׁעַר); KJV: (hundred-) fold.

H8181 שֵׂעָר (sêʻâr, say-awr'): hair (as if tossed or bristling). Origin: or שַׂעַר; (Isaiah 7:20), from H8175 (שָׂעַר) in the sense of dishevelling; KJV: hair(-y), [idiom] rough.

H8182 שֹׁעָר (shôʻâr, sho-awr'): harsh or horrid, i.e. offensive. Origin: from H8176 (שָׁעַר); KJV: vile.

H8183 שְׂעָרָה (sᵉʻârâh, seh-aw-raw'): a hurricane. Origin: feminine of H8178 (שַׂעַר); KJV: storm, tempest.

H8184 שְׂעֹרָה (sᵉʻôrâh, seh-o-raw'): barley (as villose). Origin: or שְׂעוֹרָה (feminine meaning the plant); and (masculine meaning the grain); also שְׂעֹר; or שְׂעוֹר; from H8175 (שָׂעַר) in the sense of roughness; KJV: barley.

H8185 שַׂעֲרָה (saʻărâh, sah-ar-aw'): hairiness. Origin: feminine of H8181 (שֵׂעָר); KJV: hair.

H8186 שַׁעֲרוּרָה (shaʻărûwrâh, shah-ar-oo-raw'): something fearful. Origin: or שַׁעֲרִירִיָּה; or שַׁעֲרֻרִת; feminine from H8176 (שָׁעַר) in the sense of H8175 (שָׂעַר); KJV: horrible thing.

H8187 שְׁעַרְיָה (Shᵉʻaryâh, sheh-ar-yaw'): Shearjah, an Israelite. Origin: from H8176 (שָׁעַר) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has stormed; KJV: Sheariah.

H8188 שְׂעֹרִים (Sᵉʻôrîym, seh-o-reem'): Seorim, an Israelite. Origin: masculine plural of H8184 (שְׂעֹרָה); barley grains; KJV: Seorim.

H8189 שַׁעֲרַיִם (Shaʻărayim, shah-ar-ah'-yim): Shaarajim, a place in Palestine. Origin: dual of H8179 (שַׁעַר); double gates; KJV: Shaaraim.

H8190 שַׁעַשְׁגַּז (Shaʻashgaz, shah-ash-gaz'): Shaashgaz, a eunuch of Xerxes. Origin: of Persian derivation; KJV: Shaashgaz.

H8191 שַׁעְשֻׁעַ (shaʻshuaʻ, shah-shoo'-ah): enjoyment. Origin: from H8173 (שָׁעַע); KJV: delight, pleasure.

H8192 שָׁפָה (shâphâh, shaw-faw'): to abrade, i.e. bare. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: high, stick out.

H8193 שָׂפָה (sâphâh, saw-faw'): the lip (as a natural boundary); by implication, language; by analogy, a margin (of a vessel, water, cloth, etc.). Origin: or (in dual and plural) שֶׂפֶת; probably from H5595 (סָפָה) or H8192 (שָׁפָה) through the idea of termination (compare H5490 (סוֹף)); KJV: band, bank, binding, border, brim, brink, edge, language, lip, prating, (sea-)shore, side, speech, talk, (vain) words.

H8194 שָׁפָה (shâphâh, shaw-faw'): a cheese (as strained from the whey). Origin: from H8192 (שָׁפָה) in the sense of clarifying; KJV: cheese.

H8195 שְׁפוֹ (Shᵉphôw, shef-o'): Shepho or Shephi, an Idumaean. Origin: or שְׁפִי; from H8192 (שָׁפָה); baldness (compare H8205 (שְׁפִי)); KJV: Shephi, Shepho.

H8196 שְׁפוֹט (shᵉphôwṭ, shef-ote'): a judicial sentence, i.e. punishment. Origin: or שְׁפוּט; from H8199 (שָׁפַט); KJV: judgment.

H8197 שְׁפוּפָם (Shᵉphûwphâm, shef-oo-fawm'): Shephupham or Shephuphan, an Israelite. Origin: or שְׁפוּפָן; from the same as H8207 (שְׁפִיפֹן); serpent-like; KJV: Shephuphan, Shupham.

H8198 שִׁפְחָה (shiphchâh, shif-khaw'): a female slave (as a member of the household). Origin: feminine from an unused root meaning to spread out (as a family; see H4940 (מִשְׁפָּחָה)); KJV: (bond-, hand-) maid(-en, -servant), wench, bondwoman, womanservant.

H8199 שָׁפַט (shâphaṭ, shaw-fat'): to judge, i.e. pronounce sentence (for or against); by implication, to vindicate or punish; by extenssion, to govern; passively, to litigate (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [phrase] avenge, [idiom] that condemn, contend, defend, execute (judgment), (be a) judge(-ment), [idiom] needs, plead, reason, rule.

H8200 שְׁפַט (shᵉphaṭ, shef-at'): to judge. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8199 (שָׁפַט); KJV: magistrate.

H8201 שֶׁפֶט (shepheṭ, sheh'-fet): a sentence, i.e. infliction. Origin: from H8199 (שָׁפַט); KJV: judgment.

H8202 שָׁפָט (Shâphâṭ, shaw-fawt'): Shaphat, the name of four Israelites. Origin: from H8199 (שָׁפַט); judge; KJV: Shaphat.

H8203 שְׁפַטְיָה (Shᵉphaṭyâh, shef-at-yaw'): Shephatjah, the name of ten Israelites. Origin: or שְׁפַטְיָהוּ; from H8199 (שָׁפַט) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has judged; KJV: Shephatiah.

H8204 שִׁפְטָן (Shiphṭân, shif-tawn'): Shiphtan, an Israelite. Origin: from H8199 (שָׁפַט); judge-like; KJV: Shiphtan.

H8205 שְׁפִי (shᵉphîy, shef-ee'): bareness; concretely, a bare hill or plain. Origin: from H8192 (שָׁפָה); KJV: high place, stick out.

H8206 שֻׁפִּים (Shuppîym, shoop-peem'): Shuppim, an Israelite. Origin: plural of an unused noun from the same as H8207 (שְׁפִיפֹן) and meaning the same; serpents; KJV: Shuppim.

H8207 שְׁפִיפֹן (shᵉphîyphôn, shef-ee-fone'): a kind of serpent (as snapping), probably the cerastes or horned adder. Origin: from an unused root meaning the same as H7779 (שׁוּף); KJV: adder.

H8208 שָׁפִיר (Shâphîyr, shaf-eer'): Shaphir, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H8231 (שָׁפַר); beautiful; KJV: Saphir.

H8209 שַׁפִּיר (shappîyr, shap-peer'): beautiful. Origin: (Aramaic) intensive of a form corresponding to H8208 (שָׁפִיר); KJV: fair.

H8210 שָׁפַךְ (shâphak, shaw-fak'): to spill forth (blood, a libation, liquid metal; or even a solid, i.e. to mound up); also (figuratively) to expend (life, soul, complaint, money, etc.); intensively, to sprawl out. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cast (up), gush out, pour (out), shed(-der, out), slip.

H8211 שֶׁפֶךְ (shephek, sheh'-fek): an emptying place, e.g. an ash-heap. Origin: from H8210 (שָׁפַךְ); KJV: are poured out.

H8212 שׇׁפְכָה (shophkâh, shof-kaw'): a pipe (for pouring forth, e.g. wine), i.e. the penis. Origin: feminine of a derivative from H8210 (שָׁפַךְ); KJV: privy member.

H8213 שָׁפֵל (shâphêl, shaw-fale'): to depress or sink (expectation figuratively, to humiliate, intransitive or transitive). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abase, bring (cast, put) down, debase, humble (self), be (bring, lay, make, put) low(-er).

H8214 שְׁפַל (shᵉphal, shef-al'): {to depress or sink (expectation figuratively, to humiliate, intransitive or transitive)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8213 (שָׁפֵל) KJV: abase, humble, put down, subdue.

H8215 שְׁפַל (shᵉphal, shef-al'): low. Origin: (Aramaic) from H8214 (שְׁפַל); KJV: basest.

H8216 שֶׁפֶל (shephel, shay'-fel): an humble rank. Origin: from H8213 (שָׁפֵל); KJV: low estate (place).

H8217 שָׁפָל (shâphâl, shaw-fawl'): depressed, literally or figuratively. Origin: from H8213 (שָׁפֵל); KJV: base(-st), humble, low(-er, -ly).

H8218 שִׁפְלָה (shiphlâh, shif-law'): depression. Origin: feminine of H8216 (שֶׁפֶל); KJV: low place.

H8219 שְׁפֵלָה (shᵉphêlâh, shef-ay-law'): Lowland, i.e. (with the article) the maritime slope of Palestine. Origin: from H8213 (שָׁפֵל); KJV: low country, (low) plain, vale(-ley).

H8220 שִׁפְלוּת (shiphlûwth, shif-looth'): remissness. Origin: from H8213 (שָׁפֵל); KJV: idleness.

H8221 שְׁפָם (Shᵉphâm, shef-awm'): Shepham, a place in or near Palestine. Origin: probably from H8192 (שָׁפָה); bare spot; KJV: Shepham.

H8222 שָׂפָם (sâphâm, saw-fawm'): the beard (as a lippiece). Origin: from H8193 (שָׂפָה); KJV: beard, (upper) lip.

H8223 שָׁפָם (Shâphâm, shaw-fawm'): Shapham, an Israelite. Origin: formed like H8221 (שְׁפָם); baldly; KJV: Shapham.

H8224 שִׂפְמוֹת (Siphmôwth, sif-moth'): Siphmoth, a place in Palestine. Origin: feminine plural of H8221 (שְׁפָם); KJV: Siphmoth.

H8225 שִׁפְמִי (Shiphmîy, shif-mee'): a Shiphmite or inhabitant of Shepham. Origin: patrial from H8221 (שְׁפָם); KJV: Shiphmite.

H8226 שָׂפַן (sâphan, saw-fan'): to conceal (as a valuable). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: treasure.

H8227 שָׁפָן (shâphân, shaw-fawn'): a species of rockrabbit (from its hiding), i.e. probably the hyrax. Origin: from H8226 (שָׂפַן); KJV: coney.

H8228 שֶׁפַע (shephaʻ, sheh'-fah): resources. Origin: from an unused root meaning to abound; KJV: abundance.

H8229 שִׁפְעָה (shiphʻâh, shif-aw'): copiousness. Origin: feminine of H8228 (שֶׁפַע); KJV: abundance, company, multitude.

H8230 שִׁפְעִי (Shiphʻîy, shif-ee'): Shiphi, an Israelite. Origin: from H8228 (שֶׁפַע); copious; KJV: Shiphi.

H8231 שָׁפַר (shâphar, shaw-far'): to glisten, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) fair. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] goodly.

H8232 שְׁפַר (shᵉphar, shef-ar'): to be beautiful. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8231 (שָׁפַר); KJV: be acceptable, please, [phrase] think good.

H8233 שֶׁפֶר (shepher, sheh'-fer): beauty. Origin: from H8231 (שָׁפַר); KJV: [idiom] goodly.

H8234 שֶׁפֶר (Shepher, sheh'-fer): Shepher, a place in the Desert. Origin: the same as H8233 (שֶׁפֶר); KJV: Shapper.

H8235 שִׁפְרָה (shiphrâh, shif-raw'): brightness. Origin: from H8231 (שָׁפַר); KJV: garnish.

H8236 שִׁפְרָה (Shiphrâh, shif-raw'): Shiphrah, an Israelitess. Origin: the same as H8235 (שִׁפְרָה); KJV: Shiphrah.

H8237 שַׁפְרוּר (shaphrûwr, shaf-roor'): splendid, i.e. a tapestry or canopy. Origin: from H8231 (שָׁפַר); KJV: royal pavilion.

H8238 שְׁפַרְפַר (shᵉpharphar, shef-ar-far'): the dawn (as brilliant with aurora). Origin: (Aramaic) from H8231 (שָׁפַר); KJV: [idiom] very early in the morning.

H8239 שָׁפַת (shâphath, shaw-fath'): to locate, i.e. (generally) hang on or (figuratively) establish, reduce. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bring, ordain, set on.

H8240 שָׁפָת (shâphâth, shaw-fawth'): a (double) stall (for cattle); also a (two-pronged) hook (for flaying animals on). Origin: from H8239 (שָׁפַת); KJV: hook, pot.

H8241 שֶׁצֶף (shetseph, sheh'-tsef): an outburst (of anger). Origin: from H7857 (שָׁטַף) (for alliteration with H7110 (קֶצֶף)); KJV: little.

H8242 שַׂק (saq, sak): properly, a mesh (as allowing a liquid to run through), i.e. coarse loose cloth or sacking (used in mourning and for bagging); hence, a bag (for grain, etc.). Origin: from H8264 (שָׁקַק); KJV: sack(-cloth, -clothes).

H8243 שָׁק (shâq, shawk): the leg. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7785 (שׁוֹק); KJV: leg.

H8244 שָׂקַד (sâqad, saw-kad'): to fasten. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bind.

H8245 שָׁקַד (shâqad, shaw-kad'): to be alert, i.e. sleepless; hence to be on the lookout (whether for good or ill). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hasten, remain, wake, watch (for).

H8246 שָׁקַד (shâqad, shaw-kad'): to be (intensively, make) almond-shaped. Origin: a denominative from H8247 (שָׁקֵד); KJV: make like (unto, after the fashion of) almonds.

H8247 שָׁקֵד (shâqêd, shaw-kade'): the almond (tree or nut; as being the earliest in bloom). Origin: from H8245 (שָׁקַד); KJV: almond (tree).

H8248 שָׁקָה (shâqâh, shaw-kaw'): to quaff, i.e. (causatively) to irrigate or furnish apotion to. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cause to (give, give to, let, make to) drink, drown, moisten, water. See H7937 (שָׁכַר), H8354 (שָׁתָה).

H8249 שִׁקֻּו (shiqquv, shif-koov'): (plural collective) a draught. Origin: from H8248 (שָׁקָה); KJV: drink.

H8250 שִׁקּוּי (shiqqûwy, shik-koo'-ee): a beverage; moisture, i.e. (figuratively) refreshment. Origin: from H8248 (שָׁקָה); KJV: drink, marrow.

H8251 שִׁקּוּץ (shiqqûwts, shik-koots'): disgusting, i.e. filthy; especially idolatrous or (concretely) an idol. Origin: or שִׁקֻּץ; from H8262 (שָׁקַץ); KJV: abominable filth (idol, -ation), detestable (thing).

H8252 שָׁקַט (shâqaṭ, shaw-kat'): to repose (usually figurative). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appease, idleness, (at, be at, be in, give) quiet(-ness), (be at, be in, give, have, take) rest, settle, be still.

H8253 שֶׁקֶט (sheqeṭ, sheh'-ket): tranquillity. Origin: from H8252 (שָׁקַט); KJV: quietness.

H8254 שָׁקַל (shâqal, shaw-kal'): to suspend or poise (especially in trade). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: pay, receive(-r), spend, [idiom] throughly, weigh.

H8255 שֶׁקֶל (sheqel, sheh'-kel): probably a weight; used as a commercial standard. Origin: from H8254 (שָׁקַל); KJV: shekel.

H8256 שִׁקְמָה (shiqmâh, shik-maw'): a sycamore (usually the tree). Origin: or (feminine) שִׁקְמָה; of uncertain derivation; KJV: sycamore (fruit, tree).

H8257 שָׁקַע (shâqaʻ, shaw-kah'): to subside; by implication, to be overflowed, cease; causatively, to abate, subdue. Origin: (abbreviated Amos 8:8); a primitive root; KJV: make deep, let down, drown, quench, sink.

H8258 שְׁקַעְרוּרָה (shᵉqaʻrûwrâh, shek-ah-roo-raw'): a depression. Origin: from H8257 (שָׁקַע); KJV: hollow strake.

H8259 שָׁקַף (shâqaph, shaw-kaf'): properly, to lean out (of a window), i.e. (by implication) peep or gaze (passively, be a spectacle). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: appear, look (down, forth, out).

H8260 שֶׁקֶף (sheqeph, sheh'-kef): a loophole (for looking out), to admit light and air. Origin: from H8259 (שָׁקַף); KJV: window.

H8261 שָׁקֻף (shâquph, shaw-koof'): an embrasure or opening with bevelled jam. Origin: passive participle of H8259 (שָׁקַף); (compare H8260 (שֶׁקֶף)) KJV: light, window.

H8262 שָׁקַץ (shâqats, shaw-kats'): to be filthy, i.e. (intensively) to loathe, pollute. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: abhor, make abominable, have in abomination, detest, [idiom] utterly.

H8263 שֶׁקֶץ (sheqets, sheh'-kets): filth, i.e. (figuratively and specifically) an idolatrous object. Origin: from H8262 (שָׁקַץ); KJV: abominable(-tion).

H8264 שָׁקַק (shâqaq, shaw-kak'): to course (like a beast of prey); by implication, to seek greedily. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have appetite, justle one against another, long, range, run (to and fro).

H8265 שָׂקַר (sâqar, saw-kar'): to ogle, i.e. blink coquettishly. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wanton.

H8266 שָׁקַר (shâqar, shaw-kar'): to cheat, i.e. be untrue (usually in words). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: fail, deal falsely, lie.

H8267 שֶׁקֶר (sheqer, sheh'-ker): an untruth; by implication, a sham (often adverbial). Origin: from H8266 (שָׁקַר); KJV: without a cause, deceit(-ful), false(-hood, -ly), feignedly, liar, [phrase] lie, lying, vain (thing), wrongfully.

H8268 שֹׁקֶת (shôqeth, sho'-keth): a trough (for watering). Origin: from H8248 (שָׁקָה); KJV: trough.

H8269 שַׂר (sar, sar): a head person (of any rank or class). Origin: from H8323 (שָׂרַר); KJV: captain (that had rule), chief (captain), general, governor, keeper, lord,(-task-)master, prince(-ipal), ruler, steward.

H8270 שֹׁר (shôr, shore): a string (as twisted ), i.e. (specifically) the umbilical cord (also figuratively, as the centre of strength). Origin: from H8324 (שָׁרַר); (compare H8306 (שָׁרִיר)) KJV: navel.

H8271 שְׁרֵא (shᵉrêʼ, sher-ay'): to free, separate; figuratively, to unravel, commence; by implication (of unloading beasts) to reside. Origin: (Aramaic) a root corresponding to that of H8293 (שֵׁרוּת); KJV: begin, dissolve, dwell, loose.

H8272 שַׁרְאֶצֶר (Sharʼetser, shar-eh'-tser): Sharetser, the name of an Assyrian and an Israelite. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Sharezer.

H8273 שָׁרָב (shârâb, shaw-rawb'): quivering glow (of the air), expectation. the mirage. Origin: from an unused root meaning to glare; KJV: heat, parched ground.

H8274 שֵׁרֵבְיָה (Shêrêbᵉyâh, shay-rayb-yaw'): Sherebjah, the name of two Israelites. Origin: from H8273 (שָׁרָב) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has brought heat; KJV: Sherebiah.

H8275 שַׁרְבִיט (sharbîyṭ, shar-beet'): a rod of empire. Origin: for H7626 (שֵׁבֶט); KJV: sceptre.

H8276 שָׂרַג (sârag, saw-rag'): to intwine. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: wrap together, wreath.

H8277 שָׂרַד (sârad, saw-rad'): properly, to puncture, i.e. (figuratively through the idea of slipping out) to escape or survive. Origin: a primitive root; (compare H8279 (שֶׂרֶד)) KJV: remain.

H8278 שְׂרָד (sᵉrâd, ser-awd'): stitching (as pierced with a needle). Origin: from H8277 (שָׂרַד); KJV: service.

H8279 שֶׂרֶד (sered, seh'-red): a (carpenter's) scribing-awl (for pricking or scratching measurements). Origin: from H8277 (שָׂרַד); KJV: line.

H8280 שָׂרָה (sârâh, saw-raw'): to prevail. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have power (as a prince).

H8281 שָׁרָה (shârâh, shaw-raw'): to free. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: direct.

H8282 שָׂרָה (sârâh, saw-raw'): a mistress, i.e. female noble. Origin: feminine of H8269 (שַׂר); KJV: lady, princess, queen.

H8283 שָׂרָה (Sârâh, saw-raw'): Sarah, Abraham's wife. Origin: the same as H8282 (שָׂרָה); KJV: Sarah.

H8284 שָׁרָה (shârâh, shaw-raw'): a fortification (literally or figuratively). Origin: probably feminine of H7791 (שׁוּר); KJV: sing (by mistake for H7891 (שִׁיר)), wall.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H8285 to H8419
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H8285 שֵׁרָה (shêrâh, shay-raw'): a wrist-band (as compact or clasping). Origin: from H8324 (שָׁרַר) in its original sense of pressing; KJV: bracelet.

H8286 שְׂרוּג (Sᵉrûwg, ser-oog'): Serug, a postdiluvian patriarch. Origin: from H8276 (שָׂרַג); tendril; KJV: Serug.

H8287 שָׁרוּחֶן (Shârûwchen, shaw-roo-khen'): Sharuchen, a place in Palestine. Origin: probably from H8281 (שָׁרָה) (in the sense of dwelling (compare H8271 (שְׁרֵא)) and H2580 (חֵן); abode of pleasure; KJV: Sharuhen.

H8288 שְׂרוֹךְ (sᵉrôwk, ser-oke'): a thong (as laced or tied). Origin: from H8308 (שָׂרַךְ); KJV: (shoe-)latchet.

H8289 שָׁרוֹן (Shârôwn, shaw-rone'): plain, Sharon, the name of a place in Palestine. Origin: probably abridged from H3474 (יָשַׁר); KJV: Lasharon, Sharon.

H8290 שָׁרוֹנִי (Shârôwnîy, shaw-ro-nee'): a Sharonite or inhabitant of Sharon. Origin: patrial from H8289 (שָׁרוֹן); KJV: Sharonite.

H8291 שָׂרוּק (sârûwq, sar-ook'): a grapevine. Origin: passive participle from the same as H8321 (שֹׂרֵק); KJV: principal plant. See H8320 (שָׂרֻק), H8321 (שֹׂרֵק).

H8292 שְׁרוּקָה (shᵉrûwqâh, sher-oo-kaw'): a whistling (in scorn); by analogy, a piping. Origin: or (by permutation) שְׁרִיקָה; feminine passive participle of H8319 (שָׁרַק); KJV: bleating, hissing.

H8293 שֵׁרוּת (shêrûwth, shay-rooth'): freedom. Origin: from H8281 (שָׁרָה) abbreviated; KJV: remnant.

H8294 שֶׂרַח (Serach, seh'-rakh): Serach, an Israelitess. Origin: by permutation for H5629 (סֶרַח); superfluity; KJV: Sarah, Serah.

H8295 שָׂרַט (sâraṭ, saw-rat'): to gash. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut in pieces, make (cuttings) pieces.

H8296 שֶׂרֶט (sereṭ, seh'-ret): an incision. Origin: and שָׂרֶטֶת; from H8295 (שָׂרַט); KJV: cutting.

H8297 שָׂרַי (Sâray, saw-rah'-ee): Sarai, the wife of Abraham. Origin: from H8269 (שַׂר); dominative; KJV: Sarai.

H8298 שָׁרַי (Shâray, shaw-rah'-ee): Sharay, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H8324 (שָׁרַר); hostile; KJV: Sharai.

H8299 שָׂרִיג (sârîyg, saw-reeg'): a tendril (as entwining). Origin: from H8276 (שָׂרַג); KJV: branch.

H8300 שָׂרִיד (sârîyd, saw-reed'): a survivor. Origin: from H8277 (שָׂרַד); KJV: [idiom] alive, left, remain(-ing), remnant, rest.

H8301 שָׂרִיד (Sârîyd, suw-reed'): Sarid, a place in Palestine. Origin: the same as H8300 (שָׂרִיד); KJV: Sarid.

H8302 שִׁרְיוֹן (shiryôwn, shir-yone'): a corslet (as if twisted). Origin: or שִׁרְיֹן; and שִׁרְיָן; also (feminine) שִׁרְיָה; and שִׁרְיֹנָה; from H8281 (שָׁרָה) in the original sense of turning; KJV: breastplate, coat of mail, habergeon, harness. See H5630 (סִרְיֹן).

H8303 שִׁרְיוֹן (Shiryôwn, shir-yone'): Shirjon or Sirjon, a peak of the Lebanon. Origin: and שִׂרְיֹן; the same as H8304 (שְׂרָיָה) (i.e. sheeted with snow); KJV: Sirion.

H8304 שְׂרָיָה (Sᵉrâyâh, ser-aw-yaw'): Serajah, the name of nine Israelites. Origin: or שְׂרָיָהוּ; from H8280 (שָׂרָה) and H3050 (יָהּ); Jah has prevailed; KJV: Seraiah.

H8305 שְׂרִיקָה (sᵉrîyqâh, ser-ee-kaw'): hetchelling (or combing flax), i.e. (concretely) tow (by extension, linen cloth). Origin: from the same as H8321 (שֹׂרֵק) in the original sense of piercing; KJV: fine.

H8306 שָׁרִיר (shârîyr, shaw-reer'): a cord, i.e. (by analogy) sinew. Origin: from H8324 (שָׁרַר) in the original sense as in H8270 (שֹׁר) (compare H8326 (שֹׁרֶר)); KJV: navel.

H8307 שְׁרִירוּת (shᵉrîyrûwth, sher-ee-rooth'): obstinacy. Origin: from H8324 (שָׁרַר) in the sense of twisted, i.e. firm; KJV: imagination, lust.

H8308 שָׂרַךְ (sârak, saw-rak'): to interlace. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: traverse.

H8309 שְׁרֵמָה (shᵉrêmâh, sher-ay-maw'): a common. Origin: probably by an orthographical error for H7709 (שְׁדֵמָה); KJV: field.

H8310 שַׂרְסְכִים (Sarçᵉkîym, sar-seh-keem'): Sarsekim, a Babylonian general. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Sarsechim.

H8311 שָׂרַע (sâraʻ, saw-rah'): to prolong, i.e. (reflex) be deformed by excess of members. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: stretch out self, (have any) superfluous thing.

H8312 שַׂרְעַף (sarʻaph, sar-af'): cogitation. Origin: for H5587 (סָעִף); KJV: thought.

H8313 שָׂרַף (sâraph, saw-raf'): to be (causatively, set) on fire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (cause to, make a) burn((-ing), up) kindle, [idiom] utterly.

H8314 שָׂרָף (sârâph, saw-rawf'): burning, i.e. (figuratively) poisonous (serpent); specifically, a saraph or symbolical creature (from their copper color). Origin: from H8313 (שָׂרַף); KJV: fiery (serpent), seraph.

H8315 שָׂרָף (Sârâph, saw-raf'): Saraph, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H8314 (שָׂרָף); KJV: Saraph.

H8316 שְׂרֵפָה (sᵉrêphâh, ser-ay-faw'): cremation. Origin: from H8313 (שָׂרַף); KJV: burning.

H8317 שָׁרַץ (shârats, shaw-rats'): to wriggle, i.e. (by implication) swarm or abound. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: breed (bring forth, increase) abundantly (in abundance), creep, move.

H8318 שֶׁרֶץ (sherets, sheh'-rets): a swarm, i.e. active mass of minute animals. Origin: from H8317 (שָׁרַץ); KJV: creep(-ing thing), move(-ing creature).

H8319 שָׁרַק (shâraq, shaw-rak'): properly, to be shrill, i.e. to whistle or hiss (as a call or in scorn). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: hiss.

H8320 שָׂרֻק (sâruq, saw-rook'): bright red (as piercing to the sight), i.e. bay. Origin: from H8319 (שָׁרַק); KJV: speckled. See H8291 (שָׂרוּק).

H8321 שֹׂרֵק (sôrêq, so-rake'): a vine stock (properly, one yielding purple grapes, the richest variety). Origin: or שׂוֹרֵק; and (feminine) שֹׂרֵקָה; from H8319 (שָׁרַק) in the sense of redness (compare H8320 (שָׂרֻק)); KJV: choice(-st, noble) wine. Compare H8291 (שָׂרוּק).

H8322 שְׁרֵקָה (shᵉrêqâh, sher-ay-kaw'): a derision. Origin: from H8319 (שָׁרַק); KJV: hissing.

H8323 שָׂרַר (sârar, saw-rar'): to have (transitively, exercise; reflexively, get) dominion. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] altogether, make self a prince, (bear) rule.

H8324 שָׁרַר (shârar, shaw-rar'): to be hostile (only active participle an opponent). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: enemy.

H8325 שָׁרַר (Shârar, shaw-rawr'): Sharar, an Israelite. Origin: from H8324 (שָׁרַר); hostile; KJV: Sharar.

H8326 שֹׁרֶר (shôrer, sho'-rer): the umbilical cord, i.e. (by extension) a bodice. Origin: from H8324 (שָׁרַר) in the sense of twisting (compare H8270 (שֹׁר)); KJV: navel.

H8327 שָׁרַשׁ (shârash, shaw-rash'): to root, i.e. strike into the soil, or (by implication) to pluck from it. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: (take, cause to take) root (out).

H8328 שֶׁרֶשׁ (sheresh, sheh'-resh): a root (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H8327 (שָׁרַשׁ); KJV: bottom, deep, heel, root.

H8329 שֶׁרֶשׁ (Sheresh, sheh'-resh): Sheresh, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H8328 (שֶׁרֶשׁ); KJV: Sharesh.

H8330 שֹׁרֶשׁ (shôresh, sho'-resh): {a root (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8328 (שֶׁרֶשׁ) KJV: root.

H8331 שַׁרְשָׁה (sharshâh, shar-shaw'): a chain (as rooted, i.e. linked). Origin: from H8327 (שָׁרַשׁ); KJV: chain. Compare H8333 (שַׁרְשְׁרָה).

H8332 שְׁרֹשׁוּ (shᵉrôshûw, sher-o-shoo'): eradication, i.e. (figuratively) exile. Origin: (Aramaic) from a root corresponding to H8327 (שָׁרַשׁ); KJV: banishment.

H8333 שַׁרְשְׁרָה (sharshᵉrâh, shar-sher-aw'): a chain; (architectural) probably a garland. Origin: from H8327 (שָׁרַשׁ) (compare H8331 (שַׁרְשָׁה)); KJV: chain.

H8334 שָׁרַת (shârath, shaw-rath'): to attend as a menial or worshipper; figuratively, to contribute to. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: minister (unto), (do) serve(-ant, -ice, -itor), wait on.

H8335 שָׁרֵת (shârêth, shaw-rayth'): service (in the Temple). Origin: infinitive of H8334 (שָׁרַת); KJV: minister(-ry).

H8336 שֵׁשׁ (shêsh, shaysh): bleached stuff, i.e. white linen or (by analogy) marble. Origin: or (for alliteration with H4897 (מֶשִׁי)) שְׁשִׁי; for H7893 (שַׁיִשׁ); KJV: [idiom] blue, fine (twined) linen, marble, silk.

H8337 שֵׁשׁ (shêsh, shaysh): six (as an overplus beyond five or the fingers of the hand); as ord. sixth. Origin: masculine שִׁשָּׁה; a primitive number; compare H7797 (שׂוּשׂ) KJV: six(-teen, -teenth), sixth.

H8338 שָׁשָׁא (shâshâʼ, shaw-shaw'): to annihilate. Origin: a primitive root; apparently, KJV: leave by the sixth part (by confusion with H8341 (שָׁשָׁה)).

H8339 שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר (Shêshᵉbatstsar, shaysh-bats-tsar'): Sheshbatstsar, Zerubbabel's Persian name. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Sheshbazzar.

H8340 שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר (Shêshᵉbatstsar, shaysh-bats-tsar'): {Sheshbatstsar, Zerubbabel's Persian name}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8339 (שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּר) KJV: Sheshbazzar.

H8341 שָׁשָׁה (shâshâh, shaw-shaw'): to sixth or divide into sixths. Origin: a denominative from H8337 (שֵׁשׁ); KJV: give the sixth participle

H8342 שָׂשׂוֹן (sâsôwn, saw-sone'): cheerfulness; specifically, welcome. Origin: or שָׂשֹׂן; from H7797 (שׂוּשׂ); KJV: gladness, joy, mirth, rejoicing.

H8343 שָׁשַׁי (Shâshay, shaw-shah'-ee): Shashai, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H8336 (שֵׁשׁ); whitish; KJV: Shashai.

H8344 שֵׁשַׁי (Shêshay, shay-shah'-ee): Sheshai, a Canaanite. Origin: probably for H8343 (שָׁשַׁי); KJV: Sheshai.

H8345 שִׁשִּׁי (shishshîy, shish-shee'): sixth, ord. or (feminine) fractional. Origin: from H8337 (שֵׁשׁ); KJV: sixth (part).

H8346 שִׁשִּׁים (shishshîym, shish-sheem'): sixty. Origin: multiple of H8337 (שֵׁשׁ); KJV: sixty, three score.

H8347 שֵׁשַׁךְ (Shêshak, shay-shak'): Sheshak, a symbolic name of Babylon. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Sheshach.

H8348 שֵׁשָׁן (Shêshân, shay-shawn'): Sheshan, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps for H7799 (שׁוּשַׁן); lily; KJV: Sheshan.

H8349 שָׁשַׁק (Shâshaq, shaw-shak'): Shashak, an Israelite. Origin: probably from the base of H7785 (שׁוֹק); pedestrian; KJV: Shashak.

H8350 שָׁשַׁר (shâshar, shaw-shar'): red ochre (from its piercing color). Origin: perhaps from the base of H8324 (שָׁרַר) in the sense of that of H8320 (שָׂרֻק); KJV: vermillion.

H8351 שֵׁת (shêth, shayth): tumult. Origin: (Numbers from H7582 (שָׁאָה); KJV: Sheth.

H8352 שֵׁת (Shêth, shayth): Sheth, third son of Adam. Origin: from H7896 (שִׁית); put, i.e. substituted; KJV: Seth, Sheth.

H8353 שֵׁת (shêth, shayth): {six}. Origin: (Aramaic) or שִׁת; (Aramaic), corresponding to H8337 (שֵׁשׁ); KJV: six(-th).

H8354 שָׁתָה (shâthâh, shaw-thaw'): to imbibe (literally or figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: [idiom] assuredly, banquet, [idiom] certainly, drink(-er, -ing), drunk ([idiom] -ard), surely. (Prop. intensive of H8248 (שָׁקָה).)

H8355 שְׁתָה (shᵉthâh, sheth-aw'): {to imbibe (literally or figuratively)}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8354 (שָׁתָה) KJV: drink.

H8356 שָׁתָה (shâthâh, shaw-thaw'): a basis, i.e. (figuratively) political or moral support. Origin: from H7896 (שִׁית); KJV: foundation, purpose.

H8357 שֵׁתָה (shêthâh, shay-thaw'): the seat (of the person). Origin: from H7896 (שִׁית); KJV: buttock.

H8358 שְׁתִי (shᵉthîy, sheth-ee'): intoxicaion. Origin: from H8354 (שָׁתָה); KJV: drunkenness.

H8359 שְׁתִי (shᵉthîy, sheth-ee'): a fixture, i.e. the warp in weaving. Origin: from H7896 (שִׁית); KJV: warp.

H8360 שְׁתִיָּה (shᵉthîyâh, sheth-ee-yaw'): potation. Origin: feminine of H8358 (שְׁתִי); KJV: drinking.

H8361 שִׁתִּין (shittîyn, shit-teen'): sixty. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8346 (שִׁשִּׁים) (compare H8353 (שֵׁת)); KJV: threescore.

H8362 שָׁתַל (shâthal, shaw-thal'): to transplant. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: plant.

H8363 שְׁתִל (shᵉthil, sheth-eel'): a sprig (as if transplanted), i.e. sucker. Origin: from H8362 (שָׁתַל); KJV: plant.

H8364 שֻׁתַלְחִי (Shuthalchîy, shoo-thal-kee'): a Shuthalchite (collectively) or descendants of Shuthelach. Origin: patronymically from H7803 (שׁוּתֶלַח); KJV: Shuthalhites.

H8365 שָׁתַם (shâtham, shaw-tham'): to unveil (figuratively). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be open.

H8366 שָׁתַן (shâthan, shaw-than'): (causatively) to make water, i.e. urinate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: piss.

H8367 שָׁתַק (shâthaq, shaw-thak'): to subside. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be calm, cease, be quiet.

H8368 שָׂתַר (sâthar, saw-thar'): to break out (as an eruption). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: have in (one's) secret parts.

H8369 שֵׁתָר (Shêthâr, shay-thawr'): Shethar, a Persian satrap. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Shethar.

H8370 שְׁתַר בּוֹזְנַי (Shᵉthar Bôwzᵉnay, sheth-ar' bo-zen-ah'-ee): Shethar-Bozenai, a Persian officer. Origin: of foreign derivation; KJV: Shetharboznai.

H8371 שָׁתַת (shâthath, shaw-thath'): to place, i.e. array; reflex. to lie. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be laid, set. t

H8372 תָּא (tâʼ, taw): a room (as circumscribed). Origin: and (feminine) תָּאָה; (Ezekiel 40:12), from (the base of) H8376 (תָּאָה); KJV: (little) chamber.

H8373 תָּאַב (tâʼab, taw-ab'): to desire. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: long.

H8374 תָּאַב (tâʼab, taw-ab'): to loathe (morally). Origin: a primitive root (probably identical with H8373 (תָּאַב) through the idea of puffing disdainfully at; compare H340 (אָיַב)); KJV: abhor.

H8375 תַּאֲבָה (taʼăbâh, tah-ab-aw'): desire. Origin: from H8374 (תָּאַב) (compare H15 (אָבֶה)); KJV: longing.

H8376 תָּאָה (tâʼâh, taw-aw'): to mark off, i.e. (intensively) designate. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: point out.

H8377 תְּאוֹ (tᵉʼôw, teh-o'): a species of antelope (probably from the white stripe on the cheek). Origin: and תּוֹא; (the original form), from H8376 (תָּאָה); KJV: wild bull (ox).

H8378 תַּאֲוָה (taʼăvâh, tah-av-aw'): a longing; by implication, a delight (subjectively, satisfaction, objectively, a charm). Origin: from H183 (אָוָה) (abbreviated); KJV: dainty, desire, [idiom] exceedingly, [idiom] greedily, lust(ing), pleasant. See also H6914 (קִבְרוֹת הַתַּאֲוָה).

H8379 תַּאֲוָה (taʼăvâh, tah-av-aw'): a limit, i.e. full extent. Origin: from H8376 (תָּאָה); KJV: utmost bound.

H8380 תָּאוֹם (tâʼôwm, taw-ome'): a twin (in plural only), literally or figuratively. Origin: or תָּאֹם; from H8382 (תָּאַם); KJV: twins.

H8381 תַּאֲלָה (taʼălâh, tah-al-aw'): an imprecation. Origin: from H422 (אָלָה); KJV: curse.

H8382 תָּאַם (tâʼam, taw-am'): to be (causatively, make) twinned, i.e. (figuratively) duplicate or (architectural) jointed. Origin: a primitive root; to be complete; but used only as denominative from H8380 (תָּאוֹם), KJV: coupled (together), bear twins.

H8383 תְּאֻן (tᵉʼun, teh-oon'): naughtiness, i.e. toil. Origin: from H205 (אָוֶן); KJV: lie.

H8384 תְּאֵן (tᵉʼên, teh-ane'): the fig (tree or fruit). Origin: or (in the singular, feminine) תְּאֵנָה; perhaps of foreign derivation KJV: fig (tree).

H8385 תַּאֲנָה (taʼănâh, tah-an-aw'): an opportunity or (subjectively) purpose. Origin: or תֹּאֲנָה; from H579 (אָנָה); KJV: occasion.

H8386 תַּאֲנִיָּה (taʼănîyâh, tah-an-ee-yaw'): lamentation. Origin: from H578 (אָנָה); KJV: heaviness, mourning.

H8387 תַּאֲנַת שִׁלֹה (Taʼănath Shilôh, tah-an-ath' shee-lo'): Taanath-Shiloh, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H8385 (תַּאֲנָה) and H7887 (שִׁילֹה); approach of Shiloh; KJV: Taanath-shiloh.

H8388 תָּאַר (tâʼar, taw-ar'): to delineate; reflex. to extend. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: be drawn, mark out, (Rimmon-) methoar (by union with H7417 (רִמּוֹן)).

H8389 תֹּאַר (tôʼar, to'-ar): outline, i.e. figure or appearance. Origin: from H8388 (תָּאַר); KJV: [phrase] beautiful, [idiom] comely, countenance, [phrase] fair, [idiom] favoured, form, [idiom] goodly, [idiom] resemble, visage.

H8390 תַּאֲרֵעַ (Taʼărêaʻ, tah-ar-ay'-ah): Taarea, an Israelite. Origin: perhaps from H772 (אֲרַע); KJV: Tarea. See H8475 (תַּחְרֵעַ).

H8391 תְּאַשּׁוּר (tᵉʼashshûwr, teh-ash-shoor'): a species of cedar (from its erectness). Origin: from H833 (אָשַׁר); KJV: box (tree).

H8392 תֵּבָה (têbâh, tay-baw'): a box. Origin: perhaps of foreign derivation; KJV: ark.

H8393 תְּבוּאָה (tᵉbûwʼâh, teb-oo-aw'): income, i.e. produce (literally or figuratively). Origin: from H935 (בּוֹא); KJV: fruit, gain, increase, revenue.

H8394 תָּבוּן (tâbûwn, taw-boon'): intelligence; by implication, an argument; by extension, caprice. Origin: and (feminine) תְּבוּנָה; or תּוֹבֻנָה; from H995 (בִּין); KJV: discretion, reason, skilfulness, understanding, wisdom.

H8395 תְּבוּסָה (tᵉbûwçâh, teb-oo-saw'): a treading down, i.e. ruin. Origin: from H947 (בּוּס); KJV: destruction.

H8396 תָּבוֹר (Tâbôwr, taw-bore'): Tabor, a mountain in Palestine, also a city adjacent. Origin: from a root corresponding to H8406 (תְּבַר); broken region; KJV: Tabor.

H8397 תֶּבֶל (tebel, teh'-bel): mixture, i.e. unnatural bestiality. Origin: apparently from H1101 (בָּלַל); KJV: confusion.

H8398 תֵּבֵל (têbêl, tay-bale'): the earth (as moist and therefore inhabited); by extension, the globe; by implication, its inhabitants; specifically, a particular land, as Babylonia, Palestine. Origin: from H2986 (יָבַל); KJV: habitable part, world.

H8399 תַּבְלִית (tablîyth, tab-leeth'): consumption. Origin: from H1086 (בָּלָה); KJV: destruction.

H8400 תְּבַּלֻּל (tᵉballul, teb-al-lool'): a cataract (in the eye). Origin: from H1101 (בָּלַל) in the original sense of flowing; KJV: blemish.

H8401 תֶּבֶן (teben, teh'-ben): properly, material, i.e. (specifically) refuse haum or stalks of grain (as chopped in threshing and used for fodder). Origin: probably from H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: chaff, straw, stubble.

H8402 תִּבְנִי (Tibnîy, tib-nee'): Tibni, an Israelite. Origin: from H8401 (תֶּבֶן); strawy; KJV: Tibni.

H8403 תַּבְנִית (tabnîyth, tab-neeth'): structure; by implication, a model, resemblance. Origin: from H1129 (בָּנָה); KJV: figure, form, likeness, pattern, similitude.

H8404 תַּבְעֵרָה (Tabʻêrâh, tab-ay-raw'): Taberah, a place in the Desert. Origin: from H1197 (בָּעַר); burning; KJV: Taberah.

H8405 תֵּבֵץ (Têbêts, tay-bates'): Tebets, a place in Palestine. Origin: from the same as H948 (בּוּץ); whiteness; KJV: Thebez.

H8406 תְּבַר (tᵉbar, teb-ar'): to be fragile (figuratively). Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7665 (שָׁבַר); KJV: broken.

H8407 תִּגְלַת פִּלְאֶסֶר (Tiglath Pilʼeçer, tig-lath' pil-eh'-ser): Tiglath-Pileser or Tilgath-pilneser, an Assyryrian king. Origin: or תִּגְלַת פְּלֶסֶר; or תִּלְגַּת פִּלְנְאֶסֶר or תִּלְגַּת פִּלְנֶסֶר; of foreign derivation; KJV: Tiglath-pileser, Tilgath-pilneser.

H8408 תַּגְמוּל (tagmûwl, tag-mool'): a bestowment. Origin: from H1580 (גָּמַל); KJV: benefit.

H8409 תִּגְרָה (tigrâh, tig-raw'): strife, i.e. infliction. Origin: from H1624 (גָּרָה); KJV: blow.

H8410 תִּדְהָר (tidhâr, tid-hawr'): enduring; a species of hard-wood or lasting tree (perhaps oak). Origin: apparently from H1725 (דָּהַר); KJV: pine (tree).

H8411 תְּדִירָא (tᵉdîyrâʼ, ted-ee-raw'): permanence, i.e. (adverb) constantly. Origin: (Aramaic) from H1753 (דּוּר) in the original sense of enduring; KJV: continually.

H8412 תַּדְמֹר (Tadmôr, tad-more'): Tadmor, a place near Palestine. Origin: or תַּמֹּר; (1 Kings 9:18), apparently from H8558 (תָּמָר); palm-city; KJV: Tadmor.

H8413 תִּדְעָל (Tidʻâl, tid-awl'): Tidal, a Canaanite. Origin: perhaps from H1763 (דְּחַל); fearfulness; KJV: Tidal.

H8414 תֹּהוּ (tôhûw, to'-hoo): a desolation (of surface), i.e. desert; figuratively, a worthless thing; adverbially, in vain. Origin: from an unused root meaning to lie waste; KJV: confusion, empty place, without form, nothing, (thing of) nought, vain, vanity, waste, wilderness.

H8415 תְּהוֹם (tᵉhôwm, teh-home'): an abyss (as a surging mass of water), especially the deep (the main sea or the subterranean watersupply). Origin: or תְּהֹם; (usually feminine) from H1949 (הוּם); KJV: deep (place), depth.

H8416 תְּהִלָּה (tᵉhillâh, teh-hil-law'): laudation; specifically (concretely) a hymn. Origin: from H1984 (הָלַל); KJV: praise.

H8417 תׇּהֳלָה (tohŏlâh, to-hol-aw'): braggadocio, i.e. (by implication) fatuity. Origin: feminine of an unused noun (apparently from H1984 (הָלַל)) meaning bluster; KJV: folly.

H8418 תַּהֲלֻכָה (tahălukâh, tah-hal-oo-kaw'): a procession. Origin: from H1980 (הָלַךְ); KJV: [idiom] went.

H8419 תַּהְפֻּכָה (tahpukâh, tah-poo-kaw'): a perversity or fraud. Origin: from H2015 (הָפַךְ); KJV: (very) froward(-ness, thing), perverse thing.

title: Strong's Hebrew Dictionary, H8420 to H8543
source: James Strong, A Concise Dictionary of the Words in the Hebrew Bible (1894), public domain; JSON edition by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA). Each entry: Strong number, Hebrew word, Latin reading, meaning, origin, how the KJV renders it.
body:
H8420 תָּו (tâv, tawv): a mark; by implication, a signature. Origin: from H8427 (תָּוָה); KJV: desire, mark.

H8421 תּוּב (tûwb, toob): specifically (transitive and ellip.) to reply. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H7725 (שׁוּב), to come back; KJV: answer, restore, return (an answer).

H8422 תּוּבַל (Tûwbal, too-bal'): Tubal, a postdiluvian patriarch and his posterity. Origin: or תֻּבַל; probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Tubal.

H8423 תּוּבַל קַיִן (Tûwbal Qayin, too-bal' kah'-yin): Tubal-Kajin, an antidiluvian patriarch. Origin: apparently from H2986 (יָבַל) (compare H2981 (יְבוּל)) and H7014 (קַיִן); offspring of Cain; KJV: Tubal-cain.

H8424 תּוּגָה (tûwgâh, too-gaw'): depression (of spirits); concretely a grief. Origin: from H3013 (יָגָה); KJV: heaviness, sorrow.

H8425 תּוֹגַרְמָה (Tôwgarmâh, to-gar-maw'): Togarmah, a son of Gomer and his posterity. Origin: or תֹּגַרְמָה; probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Togarmah.

H8426 תּוֹדָה (tôwdâh, to-daw'): properly, an extension of the hand, i.e. (by implication) avowal, or (usually) adoration; specifically, a choir of worshippers. Origin: from H3034 (יָדָה); KJV: confession, (sacrifice of) praise, thanks(-giving, offering).

H8427 תָּוָה (tâvâh, taw-vaw'): to mark out, i.e. (primitive) scratch or (definite) imprint. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: scrabble, set (a mark).

H8428 תָּוָה (tâvâh, taw-vaw'): to grieve. Origin: a primitive root (or perhaps identical with H8427 (תָּוָה) through a similar idea from scraping to pieces); KJV: limit (by confusion with H8427 (תָּוָה)).

H8429 תְּוַהּ (tᵉvahh, tev-ah'): to amaze, i.e. (reflex. by implication) take alarm. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8539 (תָּמַהּ) or perhaps to H7582 (שָׁאָה) through the idea of sweeping to ruin (compare H8428 (תָּוָה)); KJV: be astonied.

H8430 תּוֹחַ (Tôwach, to'-akh): Toach, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to depress; humble; KJV: Toah.

H8431 תּוֹחֶלֶת (tôwcheleth, to-kheh'-leth): expectation. Origin: from H3176 (יָחַל); KJV: hope.

H8432 תָּוֶךְ (tâvek, taw'-vek): a bisection, i.e. (by implication) the centre. Origin: from an unused root meaning to sever; KJV: among(-st), [idiom] between, half, [idiom] (there-, where-), in(-to), middle, mid(-night), midst (among), [idiom] out (of), [idiom] through, [idiom] with(-in).

H8433 תּוֹכֵחָה (tôwkêchâh, to-kay-khaw'): chastisement; figuratively (by words) correction, refutation, proof (even in defence). Origin: and תּוֹכַחַת; from H3198 (יָכַח); KJV: argument, [idiom] chastened, correction, reasoning, rebuke, reproof, [idiom] be (often) reproved.

H8434 תּוֹלָד (Tôwlâd, to-lawd'): Tolad, a place in Palestine. Origin: from H3205 (יָלַד); posterity; KJV: Tolad. Compare H513 (אֶלְתּוֹלַד).

H8435 תּוֹלְדָה (tôwlᵉdâh, to-led-aw'): (plural only) descent, i.e. family; (figuratively) history. Origin: or תֹּלְדָה; from H3205 (יָלַד); KJV: birth, generations.

H8436 תּוּלוֹן (Tûwlôwn, too-lone'): Tulon, an Israelite. Origin: from H8524 (תָּלַל); suspension; KJV: Tilon (from the margin).

H8437 תּוֹלָל (tôwlâl, to-lawl'): causing to howl, i.e. an oppressor. Origin: from H3213 (יָלַל); KJV: that wasted.

H8438 תּוֹלָע (tôwlâʻ, to-law'): the crimson-grub, but used only (in this connection) of the colorfrom it, and cloths dyed therewith. Origin: and (feminine) תּוֹלֵעָה; or תּוֹלַעַת; or תֹּלַעַת; from H3216 (יָלַע); a maggot (as voracious); specifically (often with ellipsis of H8144 (שָׁנִי)) KJV: crimson, scarlet, worm.

H8439 תּוֹלָע (Tôwlâʻ, to-law'): Tola, the name of two Israelites. Origin: the same as H8438 (תּוֹלָע); worm; KJV: Tola.

H8440 תּוֹלָעִי (Tôwlâʻîy, to-law-ee'): a Tolaite (collectively) or descendants of Tola. Origin: patronymically from H8439 (תּוֹלָע); KJV: Tolaites.

H8441 תּוֹעֵבַה (tôwʻêbah, to-ay-baw'): properly, something disgusting (morally), i.e. (as noun) an abhorrence; especially idolatry or (concretely) an idol. Origin: or תֹּעֵבַה; feminine active participle of H8581 (תַּעָב); KJV: abominable (custom, thing), abomination.

H8442 תּוֹעָה (tôwʻâh, to-aw'): mistake, i.e. (morally) impiety, or (political) injury. Origin: feminine active participle of H8582 (תָּעָה); KJV: error, hinder.

H8443 תּוֹעָפָה (tôwʻâphâh, to-aw-faw'): (only in plural collective) weariness, i.e. (by implication) toil (treasure so obtained) or speed. Origin: from H3286 (יָעַף); KJV: plenty, strength.

H8444 תּוֹצָאָה (tôwtsâʼâh, to-tsaw-aw'): (only in plural collective) exit, i.e. (geographical) boundary, or (figuratively) deliverance, (actively) source. Origin: or תֹּצָאָה; from H3318 (יָצָא); KJV: border(-s), going(-s) forth (out), issues, outgoings.

H8445 תּוֹקַהַת (Tôwqahath, to-kah'-ath): Tokahath, an Israelite. Origin: from the same as H3349 (יִקָּהָה); obedience; KJV: Tikvath (by correction for H8616 (תִּקְוָה)).

H8446 תּוּר (tûwr, toor): to meander (causatively, guide) about, especially fortrade or reconnoitring. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: chap(-man), sent to descry, be excellent, merchant(-man), search (out), seek, (e-) spy (out).

H8447 תּוֹר (tôwr, tore): a succession, i.e. a string or (abstractly) order. Origin: or תֹּר; from H8446 (תּוּר); KJV: border, row, turn.

H8448 תּוֹר (tôwr, tore): a manner (as a sort of turn). Origin: probably the same as H8447 (תּוֹר); KJV: estate.

H8449 תּוֹר (tôwr, tore): a ring-dove, often (figuratively) as a term of endearment. Origin: or תֹּר; probably the same as H8447 (תּוֹר); KJV: (turtle) dove.

H8450 תּוֹר (tôwr, tore): a bull. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding (by permutation) to H7794 (שׁוֹר); KJV: bullock, ox.

H8451 תּוֹרָה (tôwrâh, to-raw'): a precept or statute, especially the Decalogue or Pentateuch. Origin: or תֹּרָה; from H3384 (יָרָה); KJV: law.

H8452 תּוֹרָה (tôwrâh, to-raw'): a custom. Origin: probably feminine of H8448 (תּוֹר); KJV: manner.

H8453 תּוֹשָׁב (tôwshâb, to-shawb'): resident alien. Origin: or תֹּשָׁב; (1 Kings 17:1), from H3427 (יָשַׁב); a dweller (but not outlandish (H5237 (נׇכְרִי))); especially (as distinguished from a native citizen (active participle of H3427 (יָשַׁב)) and a temporary inmate (H1616 (גֵּר)) or mere lodger (H3885 (לוּן))) KJV: foreigner, inhabitant, sojourner, stranger.

H8454 תּוּשִׁיָּה (tûwshîyâh, too-shee-yaw'): support or (by implication) ability, i.e. (direct) help, (in purpose) an undertaking, (intellectual) understanding. Origin: or תֻּשִׁיָּה; from an unused root probably meaning to substantiate; KJV: enterprise, that which (thing as it) is, substance, (sound) wisdom, working.

H8455 תּוֹתָח (tôwthâch, to-thawkh'): a club. Origin: from an unused root meaning to smite; KJV: darts.

H8456 תָּזַז (tâzaz, taw-zaz'): to lop off. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: cut down.

H8457 תַּזְנוּת (taznûwth, taz-nooth'): harlotry, i.e. (figuratively) idolatry. Origin: or תַּזְנֻת; from H2181 (זָנָה); KJV: fornication, whoredom.

H8458 תַּחְבֻּלָה (tachbulâh, takh-boo-law'): (only in plural) properly, steerage (as a management of ropes), i.e. (figuratively) guidance or (by implication) a plan. Origin: or תַּחְבּוּלָה; from H2254 (חָבַל) as denominative from H2256 (חֶבֶל); KJV: good advice, (wise) counsels.

H8459 תֹּחוּ (Tôchûw, to'-khoo): Tochu, an Israelite. Origin: from an unused root meaning to depress; abasement; KJV: Tohu.

H8460 תְּחוֹת (tᵉchôwth, tekh-oth'): beneath. Origin: (Aramaic) or תּחֹת; (Aramaic), corresponding to H8478 (תַּחַת); KJV: under.

H8461 תַּחְכְּמֹנִי (Tachkᵉmônîy, takh-kem-o-nee'): Tachkemoni, an Israelite. Origin: probably for H2453 (חַכְמוֹנִי); sagacious; KJV: Tachmonite.

H8462 תְּחִלָּה (tᵉchillâh, tekh-il-law'): a commencement; rel. original (adverb, -ly). Origin: from H2490 (חָלַל) in the sense of opening; KJV: begin(-ning), first (time).

H8463 תַּחֲלוּא (tachălûwʼ, takh-al-oo'): a malady. Origin: or תַּחֲלֻא; from H2456 (חָלָא); KJV: disease, [idiom] grievous, (that are) sick(-ness).

H8464 תַּחְמָס (tachmâç, takh-mawce'): a species of unclean bird (from its violence), perhaps an owl. Origin: from H2554 (חָמַס); KJV: night hawk.

H8465 תַּחַן (Tachan, takh'-an): Tachan, the name of two Israelites. Origin: probably from H2583 (חָנָה); station; KJV: Tahan.

H8466 תַּחֲנָה (tachănâh, takh-an-aw'): (only plural collectively) an encampment. Origin: from H2583 (חָנָה); KJV: camp.

H8467 תְּחִנָּה (tᵉchinnâh, tekh-in-naw'): graciousness; causatively, entreaty. Origin: from H2603 (חָנַן); KJV: favour, grace, supplication.

H8468 תְּחִנָּה (Tᵉchinnâh, tekh-in-naw'): Techinnah, an Israelite. Origin: the same as H8467 (תְּחִנָּה); KJV: Tehinnah.

H8469 תַּחֲנוּן (tachănûwn, takh-an-oon'): earnest prayer. Origin: or (feminine) תַּחֲנוּנָה; from H2603 (חָנַן); KJV: intreaty, supplication.

H8470 תַּחֲנִי (Tachănîy, takh-an-ee'): a Tachanite (collectively) or descendants of Tachan. Origin: patronymically from H8465 (תַּחַן); KJV: Tahanites.

H8471 תַּחְפַּנְחֵס (Tachpanchêç, takh-pan-khace'): Tachpanches, Techaphneches or Tachpenes, a place in Egypt. Origin: or תְּחַפְנְחֵס; (Ezekiel 30:18), or תַּחְפְּנֵס; (Jeremiah 2:16), of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Tahapanes, Tahpanhes, Tehaphnehes.

H8472 תַּחְפְּנֵיס (Tachpᵉnêyç, takh-pen-ace'): Tachpenes, an Egyptian woman. Origin: of Egyptian derivation; KJV: Tahpenes.

H8473 תַּחֲרָא (tachărâʼ, takh-ar-aw'): a linen corslet (as white or hollow). Origin: from H2734 (חָרָה) in the original sense of H2352 (חוּר) or H2353 (חוּר); KJV: habergeon.

H8474 תַּחָרָה (tachârâh, takh-aw-raw'): to vie with a rival. Origin: a facitious root from H2734 (חָרָה) through the idea of the heat of jealousy; KJV: close, contend.

H8475 תַּחְרֵעַ (Tachrêaʻ, takh-ray'-ah): Tachrea, an Israelite. Origin: for H8390 (תַּאֲרֵעַ); KJV: Tahrea.

H8476 תַּחַשׁ (tachash, takh'-ash): a (clean) animal with fur, probably a species of antelope. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: badger.

H8477 תַּחַשׁ (Tachash, takh'-ash): Tachash, a relative of Abraham. Origin: the same as H8476 (תַּחַשׁ); KJV: Thahash.

H8478 תַּחַת (tachath, takh'-ath): the bottom (as depressed); only adverbially, below (often with prepositional prefix underneath), in lieu of, etc. Origin: from the same as H8430 (תּוֹחַ); KJV: as, beneath, [idiom] flat, in(-stead), (same) place (where...is), room, for...sake, stead of, under, [idiom] unto, [idiom] when...was mine, whereas, (where-) fore, with.

H8479 תַּחַת (tachath, takh'-ath): {the bottom (as depressed); only adverbially, below (often with prepositional prefix underneath), in lieu of, etc.}. Origin: (Aramaic) corresponding to H8478 (תַּחַת) KJV: under.

H8480 תַּחַת (Tachath, takh'-ath): Tachath, the name of a place in the Desert, also of three Israelites. Origin: the same as H8478 (תַּחַת); KJV: Tahath.

H8481 תַּחְתּוֹן (tachtôwn, takh-tone'): bottommost. Origin: or תַּחְתֹּן; from H8478 (תַּחַת); KJV: lower(-est), nether(-most).

H8482 תַּחְתִּי (tachtîy, takh-tee'): lowermost; as noun (feminine plural) the depths (figuratively, a pit, the womb). Origin: from H8478 (תַּחַת); KJV: low (parts, -er, -er parts, -est), nether (part).

H8483 תַּחְתִּים חׇדְשִׁי (Tachtîym Chodshîy, takh-teem' khod-shee'): Tachtim-Chodshi, a place in Palestine. Origin: apparently from the plural masculine of H8482 (תַּחְתִּי) or H8478 (תַּחַת) and H2320 (חֹדֶשׁ); lower (ones) monthly; KJV: Tahtim-hodshi.

H8484 תִּיכוֹן (tîykôwn, tee-kone'): central. Origin: or תִּיכֹן; from H8432 (תָּוֶךְ); KJV: middle(-most), midst.

H8485 תֵּימָא (Têymâʼ, tay-maw'): Tema, a son of Ishmael, and the region settled by him. Origin: or תֵּמָא; probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Tema.

H8486 תֵּימָן (têymân, tay-mawn'): the south (as being on the right hand of a person facing the east). Origin: or תֵּמָן; denominative from H3225 (יָמִין); KJV: south (side, -ward, wind).

H8487 תֵּימָן (Têymân, tay-mawn'): Teman, the name of two Edomites, and of the region and descendant of one of them. Origin: or תֵּמָן; the same as H8486 (תֵּימָן); KJV: south, Teman.

H8488 תֵּימְנִי (Têymᵉnîy, tay-men-ee'): Temeni, an Israelite. Origin: probably for H8489 (תֵּימָנִי); KJV: Temeni.

H8489 תֵּימָנִי (Têymânîy, tay-maw-nee'): a Temanite or descendant of Teman. Origin: patronymically from H8487 (תֵּימָן); KJV: Temani, Temanite.

H8490 תִּימָרָה (tîymârâh, tee-maw-raw'): a column, i.e. cloud. Origin: or תִּמָרָה; from the same as H8558 (תָּמָר); KJV: pillar.

H8491 תִּיצִי (Tîytsîy, tee-tsee'): a Titsite or descendant or inhabitant of an unknown Tits. Origin: patrial or patronymically from an unused noun of uncertain meaning; KJV: Tizite.

H8492 תִּירוֹשׁ (tîyrôwsh, tee-roshe'): must or fresh grape-juice (as just squeezed out); by implication (rarely) fermented wine. Origin: or תִּירֹשׁ; from H3423 (יָרַשׁ) in the sense of expulsion; KJV: (new, sweet) wine.

H8493 תִּירְיָא (Tîyrᵉyâʼ, tee-reh-yaw'): fearful, Tirja, an Israelite. Origin: probably from H3372 (יָרֵא); KJV: Tiria.

H8494 תִּירָס (Tîyrâç, tee-rawce'): Tiras, a son of Japheth. Origin: probably of foreign derivation; KJV: Tiras.

H8495 תַּיִשׁ (tayish, tah'-yeesh): a buck or he-goat (as given to butting). Origin: from an unused root meaning to butt; KJV: he goat.

H8496 תֹּךְ (tôk, toke): oppression. Origin: or תּוֹך; (Psalm 72:14), from the same base as H8432 (תָּוֶךְ) (in the sense of cutting to pieces); KJV: deceit, fraud.

H8497 תָּכָה (tâkâh, taw-kaw'): to strew, i.e. encamp. Origin: a primitive root; KJV: sit down.

H8498 תְּכוּנָה (tᵉkûwnâh, tek-oo-naw'): adjustment, i.e. structure; by implication, equipage. Origin: feminine passive participle of H8505 (תָּכַן); KJV: fashion, store.

H8499 תְּכוּנָה (tᵉkûwnâh, tek-oo-naw'): something arranged or fixed, i.e. a place. Origin: from H3559 (כּוּן); or probably identical with H8498 (תְּכוּנָה); KJV: seat.

H8500 תֻּכִּי (tukkîy, took-kee'): probably of foreign derivation; some imported creature, probably a peacock. Origin: or תּוּכִּי; KJV: peacock.

H8501 תָּכָךְ (tâkâk, taw-kawk'): to dissever, i.e. crush. Origin: from an unused root meaning KJV: deceitful.

H8502 תִּכְלָה (tiklâh, tik-law'): completeness. Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: perfection.

H8503 תַּכְלִית (taklîyth, tak-leeth'): completion; by implication, an extremity. Origin: from H3615 (כָּלָה); KJV: end, perfect(-ion).

H8504 תְּכֵלֶת (tᵉkêleth, tek-ay'-leth): the cerulean mussel, i.e. the color (violet) obtained therefrom or stuff dyed therewith. Origin: probably for H7827 (שְׁחֶלֶת); KJV: blue.

H8505 תָּכַן (tâkan, taw-kan'): to balance, i.e. measure out (by weight or dimension); figuratively, arrange, equalize, through the idea of levelling (ment. estimate, test). Origin: a primitive root; KJV: bear up, direct, be (un-)equal, mete, ponder, tell, weigh.

H8506 תֹּכֶן (tôken, to'-ken): a fixed quantity. Origin: from H8505 (תָּכַן); KJV: measure, tale.
